paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 43: the source R’ Tzadok cites for the teaching that the three levels of the soul — nefesh, ruach, and neshamah — are drawn from the three lower worlds: nefesh from Asiyah (the world of the spheres, galgalim), ruach from Yetzirah (the world of the angels), and neshamah from Beriah (the world of the Throne of Glory). Because Beriah, the world of the Throne, is “mostly good,” the neshamah — which corresponds to the thought of the mind — remains essentially pure, as we declare each morning, “the soul You placed within me is pure.” The corruption of sin therefore lodges not in the neshamah but in the heart, the seat of the yetzer.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Dover Tzedek, Eruvin §3): “There are five levels in the soul — nefesh, ruach, neshamah, chayah, yechidah; and nefesh, ruach, neshamah are deed, speech, and thought: the deed corresponds to the liver, which is full of blood, and ‘the blood is the soul’; speech to the heart — ‘and speaks truth in his heart’ — the seat of the ‘spirit of life’ (so Onkelos renders it ‘a speaking spirit,’ for speech is in the ruach); and the neshamah is thought.” Exactly the se’if’s structure: the neshamah — the mind’s thought — is the highest, drawn from the “Throne,” above the reach of deed.

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar 15:39: the verse of tzitzis — “וְהָיָה לָכֶם לְצִיצִת וּרְאִיתֶם אֹתוֹ וּזְכַרְתֶּם אֶת כָּל מִצְוֹת ה׳ וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֹתָם, וְלֹא תָתוּרוּ אַחֲרֵי לְבַבְכֶם וְאַחֲרֵי עֵינֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם זֹנִים אַחֲרֵיהֶם” — “and it shall be for you as a fringe, that you may look upon it and remember all the commandments of Hashem and perform them; and you shall not stray after your heart and after your eyes, after which you go astray.” Rashi explains that the heart and the eyes are “the spies of the body” (meraglim la-guf), the go-betweens for sin: the eye sees, the heart covets, and the body commits the transgression. R’ Tzadok builds on this that the root of sin lies in the heart — the dwelling-place of the yetzer hara — and hence that the thought of teshuvah in the heart is the beginning of rectification.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §144): “In the place where a person’s thought is — there is the whole person; for the essence of the person is not the body but the nefesh, and the nefesh is nothing but the power of thinking, reflecting, and desiring within a man; and the place to which his thought cleaves — such is the entire form of the person at that moment.” This is the very hinge of §2-1: because “the thought is the essence of the person” and “wherever a man thinks, there he is entirely,” a thought of teshuvah does not merely settle the future — it relocates the whole man to the pure neshamah above, and so “reaches the Throne” and heals even the past.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 34:10: “הרשעים הן ברשות לבן ... אבל הצדיקים לבן ברשותן” — “The wicked are under the authority of their heart ... but the righteous have their heart under their authority.” R’ Tzadok draws the inference that the mind is the person’s essence, and that the righteous person’s heart follows the mind. Compare Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 12:5, speaking of the beinoni: “כי המוח שליט על הלב ... בתולדתו וטבע יצירתו, שכך נוצר האדם בתולדתו, שכל אדם יכול ברצונו שבמוחו להתאפק ולמשול ברוח תאותו שבלבו” — “For the mind rules over the heart ... by its inborn nature and the nature of its creation, for man was so formed at birth that every person can, through the will in his mind, restrain himself and govern the spirit of desire in his heart.” This supplies a direct parallel for the mind’s power to govern the heart; Tanya’s category of beinoni should be distinguished from its category of tzaddik.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 86a: “אמר רבי לוי: גדולה תשובה שמגעת עד כסא הכבוד, שנאמר: שובה ישראל עד ה׳ אלהיך” — “R’ Levi said: Great is teshuvah, for it reaches the Throne of Glory, as it says: Return, Israel, unto Hashem your God.” Compare Maharal, Netivos Olam, Netiv HaTeshuvah 2:16: “כי כאשר החוטא שב בתשובה, מסלק עצמו מן המדריגה החמרית שהיה בו החטא, ומגיע עד המדריגה הנבדלת. ומפני כך נחשב לו חטאו — מצד התשובה שעתה עומד בו — שגגה” — “For when the sinner returns in repentance, he removes himself from the material level in which the sin existed and reaches the separated level. Therefore his sin is considered, from the standpoint of the repentance in which he now stands, inadvertent.” This directly parallels R’ Tzadok’s explanation that the return of wisdom repairs the past, so the former sin no longer draws another sin after it.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: “Reaching the Throne of Glory” is the healing of the past as well. The neshamah — the mind’s thought — stays essentially pure; the seat of sin is the heart. By persisting in teshuvah until the rectification reaches the mind, which is the person’s essence, the heart comes under his control, and only then is the past itself rectified.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §240): “The Torah is a tavlin to the yetzer, as the Sages said; and even one whose heart is not yet wholly clean of the yetzer — if he is filled with Torah as much as he needs, the yetzer itself is ‘spiced’ into a fitting thing; therefore they said (Pesachim 49b) that a talmid chacham may eat meat, but not an am ha’aretz.” This deepens §2-2’s “spice against the yetzer”: Torah does not only fence the heart off from evil — it tempers the yetzer’s own force into something usable, so that the mind’s wisdom, drawing the heart after it, turns the very drive that sinned into an instrument of service.

paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 16a: “ברא הקדוש ברוך הוא יצר הרע, ברא לו תורה תבלין” — Hashem created the evil inclination and created Torah as its antidote. Kiddushin 30b: “אם פגע בך מנוול זה, משכהו לבית המדרש; אם אבן הוא נימוח, ואם ברזל הוא מתפוצץ” — If this contemptible one confronts you, draw him to the study hall; if he is stone, he dissolves, and if iron, he bursts apart. The same discussion explains that Torah was created as the antidote to the inclination; by engaging in Torah one is not surrendered to its power. Rav Tzadok uses both teachings to show how the mind’s study of Torah directs the heart and subdues its inclination.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 31b: “דומה לגזבר שמסרו לו מפתחות הפנימיות ומפתחות החיצונות לא מסרו לו — בהי עייל?” — “He resembles a treasurer to whom the inner keys were handed, but the outer keys were not handed: by what means can he enter?” This is said of one who possesses Torah but lacks fear of Heaven. It directly supports R’ Tzadok’s point that wisdom cannot be entered without yirah. The following saying of R’ Yannai, “חבל על דלית ליה דרתא ותרעא לדרתא עביד” — “Pity one who has no courtyard and makes a gate for his courtyard” — supplies a complementary image of study without its required end.

It directly supports R’ Tzadok’s point that wisdom cannot be entered without yirah. paragraphs.text: Yoma 72b expounds Mishlei 17:16, “למה זה מחיר ביד כסיל לקנות חכמה ולב אין” — “Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom when there is no heart?”: “אוי להם לשונאיהן של תלמידי חכמים, שעוסקין בתורה ואין בהן יראת שמים” — “Woe to the enemies of Torah scholars a euphemism for the scholars themselves, who engage in Torah and have no fear of Heaven.” The passage continues: “חבל על דלית ליה דרתא ותרעא לדרתיה עביד” — “Pity one who has no courtyard and makes a gate for his courtyard.” These sayings establish the failure of Torah study without inward yirah; R’ Tzadok then explains the mutual dependence of wisdom and fear.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Kometz HaMinchah I §61: “אבל בלימוד תורה אם מסיתו היצר הרע ע״ז גופה שלא לקיים מה יש תבלין לכך שפיר מועלת התפילה הערב נא” — “But in Torah study, if the evil inclination incites him against this very thing, not to fulfill it, what antidote is there for that? Therefore the prayer ‘Make pleasant, please’ properly helps.” This clarifies why one prays for Torah’s sweetness even though choice is entrusted to the person: the yetzer can obstruct access to the very Torah that is its remedy.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Torah is the mind’s study of wisdom, drawing the heart after it — this is “the spice against the yetzer hara.” Yirah is the gate to that courtyard: without it a spirit of folly enters and a man’s own wisdom misleads him. Hence “if there is no yirah there is no chochmah” — and yirah is complete only when it arrives, through itself, at chochmah.

p: (ג) וְהַמַּלְאָכִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם יֵצֶר הָרָע
And the angels, who do not possess an evil inclination,
הֵם בְּתַכְלִית תּוֹקֶף הַיִּרְאָה
are at the absolute pinnacle of fear and awe,
וְכָל עִנְיָנָם בְּאֵימָה וְיִרְאָה
and their entire essence exists in dread and reverence;
וְזֶהוּ "תַּרְעָא לְדָרְתָּא דְּחָכְמְתָא",
and this is the very 'gate to the courtyard of wisdom',
וְחָשְׁכוּ לִכָּנֵס גַּם לִפְנִים לְהַשָּׂגַת חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה
and they sought to enter further inward to comprehend the wisdom of the Torah.
בְּטַעֲנָה שֶׁהָאָדָם מָלֵא יֵצֶר רַע וְאֵין בּוֹ יִרְאָה
with the argument that man is filled with the evil inclination and lacks pure fear.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "שֶׁמָּא יִשְׂרְפוּנִי בְּהֶבֶל שֶׁבְּפִיהֶם"
And concerning this, Moses said: “Lest they consume me with the breath of their mouth?” (Shabbat 88b),
פֵּירוּשׁ, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא (שַׁבָּת קי״ט סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳):
the explanation being along the lines of what is stated in Shabbat (119b):
"אֵין דּוֹמֶה הֶבֶל פֶּה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֵטְא לְהֶבֶל פֶּה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ חֵטְא".
“Breath of the mouth in which there is sin does not compare to breath of the mouth in which there is no sin.”
וְגַם שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיִּרְאָה – "זֶה הַשַּׁעַר לַה' צַדִּיקִים יָבֹאוּ בוֹ",
Furthermore, the root of reverence—'This is the gate of Hashem, into which the righteous shall enter' (Psalms 118:20)—
הוּא מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת פֶּה
– is the attribute of Malchut (Sovereignty), which is the mouth—
תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ" כַּנּוֹדָע
for 'we call it the Oral Torah', as is known.
וְגַם שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמַּלְאָכִים בָּאִים מִכֹּחַ הַדִּבּוּר פֶּה
Moreover, the source of the angels derives from the power of spoken utterance through the mouth,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ק״ה עַמּוּד ב׳):
and as they stated in Sanhedrin (105b): "'
וַיָּשֶׂם ה' דָּבָר בְּפִי בִלְעָם' – רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: מַלְאָךְ",
“'And Hashem put a thing in the mouth of Balaam'—Rabbi Elazar says: an angel,”.
עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּמַהַרְשָׁ״א בְּחִדּוּשֵׁי אַגָּדוֹת
examine there in the Maharsha in Chiddushei Aggadot.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת עִיקַּר תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהִיא מוֹרָה דֶּרֶךְ,
Yet in truth, the essential purpose of the Torah, which teaches the path,
הוּא רַק לְמִי שֶׁיָּכוֹל לִתְעוֹת
is specifically for one capable of going astray;
וְיִתְרוֹן הַחָכְמָה הוּא רַק מִן הַסִּכְלוּת
and the superiority of wisdom emerges solely out of folly,
כְּיִתְרוֹן הָאוֹר שֶׁהוּא רַק מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ,
just as the preeminence of light emerges solely out of darkness.
וּמִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ סִכְלוּת מְעַט דְּיֵצֶר הָרָע אֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְחָכְמָה
and one who lacks that touch of folly of the evil inclination has no genuine connection to wisdom.
וְהַמַּלְאָכִים צוֹעֲקִים "אַיֵּה מְקוֹם כְּבוֹדוֹ",
And the angels cry out, “Where is the place of His glory?”.
אֲבָל הָאָדָם מְאוֹחָז בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
whereas man holds fast to the very Throne of Glory.
כִּי "כֹּל פָּעַל ה' לַמַּעֲנֵהוּ" – לְקִילוּסוֹ,
For 'Hashem made everything for His purpose' (Proverbs 16:4)—meaning for His praise,
וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית הַבְּרִיאָה: גִּילּוּי כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and this is the ultimate purpose of Creation: the revelation of His glory, blessed be He.
וְתַכְלִית הַבְּרִיאָה הוּא הָאָדָם
And the ultimate objective of Creation is man,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית גִּילּוּי הַכָּבוֹד
for this constitutes the zenith of the revelation of glory:
כַּאֲשֶׁר יֵשׁ אָדָם בַּעַל בְּחִירָה וְגוּפוֹ נוֹטֶה לִמְקוֹם טֻמְאָה
when there exists a person endowed with free will whose body gravitates toward defilement,
וְעִם כָּל זֶה כּוֹפֶה יִצְרוֹ וְתַאֲווֹתָיו בִּשְׁבִיל כְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם
yet despite all this, he subjugates his inclination and physical desires for the honor of Heaven—,
זֶהוּ עִיקַּר מְקוֹם כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים
this is the primary locus of the glory of the King of kings.
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַמַּלְאָכִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם יֵצֶר הָרָע לְהַשִּׂיגוֹ כְּלָל, רַק הָאָדָם
which is impossible for angels lacking an evil inclination to grasp at all, but reserved solely for man.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הוּא זוֹכֶה וּמַשִּׂיג לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ,
And when he merits and attains to this spiritual level,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּכָל מַעֲשָׂיו גִּילּוּי כְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם עַד שֶׁהוּא מְאוֹחָז בְּכִסֵּא כְּבוֹדוֹ,
such that in all his deeds the honor of Heaven is revealed until he holds fast to the Throne of His glory,
אָז יוּכַל לְהַחֲזִיר לָהֶם תְּשׁוּבָה
then he is empowered to return a decisive response to them;
כִּי אַדְּרַבָּה, עַל יְדֵי יֵצֶר הָרָע מַדְרֵגָתוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגָתָם
for on the contrary, by overcoming the evil inclination his station ascends higher than theirs,
וְרַק עַל יְדֵי זֶה יֵשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לַתּוֹרָה וְחָכְמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and only through this does he possess a true bond with the Torah and the wisdom of Hashem, blessed be He.
וְדָבָר זֶה אֵין בְּכֹחַ אָדָם לְבַד לְהַגִּיעַ לִכְפִיַּת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע בְּתַכְלִית
Yet to achieve this absolute subjugation of the evil inclination is not within human power alone,
עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ חוֹפֵף עָלָיו וְנִגְלֶה מִכָּל פְּרָטֵי עִנְיָנָיו
to the point where His glory, blessed be He, hovers over him and is revealed through every detail of his life,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין שָׁם (ל׳ עַמּוּד ב׳):
and as they stated in Kiddushin there (30b):
"אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ – אֵין יָכוֹל לוֹ".
“Were the Holy One, blessed be He, not to assist him, he could not overcome it.”
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָמַר לוֹ זֶה: "",
Therefore the text notes that the Holy One, blessed be He, instructed Moses: “Grasp (the Throne of My glory), etc.” (Shabbat 88b).
וְלוּלֵי זֶה לֹא הָיָה יָכוֹל לֶאֱחוֹז
and without this divine aid he would never have been able to grasp it.
וְכֵן הוּא מַאֲמַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא
And similarly, the declaration of Hashem, blessed be He, arrives via an awakening from Above: ",
שׁוּבָה יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ" וְגוֹמֵר
“Return, O Israel, unto Hashem your God, etc.” (Hosea 14:2);
מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ דִּתְשׁוּבָה לְהַגִּיעַ עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
for this lofty level of repentance—to reach all the way up to the Throne of Glory—
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לִבּוֹ בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ,
which means that his heart be entirely within his mastery,
זֶהוּ רַק עַל יְדֵי עֵזֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּילֵיהּ שֶׁשּׁוֹלֵחַ לְלִבּוֹ.
is possible solely through the assistance of Hashem, blessed be He, through His own awakening that He dispatches into the heart.
וְ"עַד ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ" הַיְינוּ כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
And “unto Hashem your God” denotes the Throne of Glory,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ גַּם כֵּן בְּפֶרֶק שׁוֹאֵל שָׁם (שַׁבָּת קנ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
as they stated likewise in the chapter Sho'el there (Shabbat 152b).
מִקְּרָא דְּ"צְרוּרָה בִּצְרוֹר הַחַיִּים אֵת ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ", עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִׁ״י
from the verse 'bound in the bundle of life with Hashem your God' (I Samuel 25:29), examine there in Rashi.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּמַה שֶּׁה' הוּא אֱלֹהֶיךָ,
And that is: the reality that Hashem is 'your God',
שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית הַכָּרַת הָאָדָם שֶׁה' הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים
which is the absolute apex of human perception that Hashem is God,
וּבוֹ פָּתְחָה תּוֹרָה: "אָנֹכִי ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ", "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים",
with which the Torah opened: 'I am Hashem your God', 'You shall have no other gods',
זֶה לְבַד שָׁמַעְנוּ מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה
this alone we heard directly from the mouth of the Almighty (Makkot 24a),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַמְּכֻוָּון מִכָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ: לְהַגִּיעַ לְהִתְגַּלּוּת דָּבָר זֶה
this being the focal intent of the entire Torah: to arrive at the revelation of this reality;
שֶׁעַל זֶה הָיָה הַמְּכֻוָּון בַּבְּרִיאָה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת כְּבוֹד אֱלֹהוּתוֹ,
since this was the grand design in Creation: in the revelation of the glory of His Divinity,
וְזֶהוּ הַכִּסֵּא וּמִשְׁכַּן מְקוֹם כְּבוֹדוֹ.
and this is the Throne and the sanctuary of the place of His glory.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 119b: Reish Lakish taught in the name of R’ Yehudah Nesi’ah that “the world endures only for the sake of the breath hevel of the schoolchildren” — the Torah of little children who bear no sin. When Rav Pappa asked Abaye, “and what of my Torah and yours?” he answered, “the breath in which there is sin is not like the breath in which there is no sin” (eino domeh hevel she-yesh bo chet le-hevel she-ein bo chet). R’ Tzadok applies this to Moshe’s fear of the angels — “lest they consume me with the breath of their mouths”: the sinless breath of the angels would overpower the breath of one who has sinned.

). R’ Tzadok applies this to Moshe’s fear of the angels — “lest they consume me with the breath of their mouths”: the sinless breath of the angels would overpower the breath of one who has sinned.

The Torah is the antidote for this garment, making it a linen garment like that of the ministering angels.” This directly explains why Torah is given to embodied man, whose inclination requires its remedy. The relevant Talmudic discussion of the soul, body, and beginning of the inclination is Sanhedrin 91b.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §219): “In accordance with the increase of da’as and chochmah in a person, so do the false imaginings intensify against them in his mind and heart — as in ‘he who adds knowledge adds pain’ (Koheles 1:18); and the Tree of Knowledge is ‘good and evil’ — for through the entry of good da’as, its opposite enters too, as they said (Sotah 21b) ‘wisdom entered, cunning entered.’” This is why §2-3 rules that reaching the ultimate subduing of the yetzer “is not in a person’s power alone”: the very ascent toward the chochmah of Torah rouses a correspondingly greater yetzer against him (Sukkah 52a, “whoever is greater than his fellow, his yetzer is greater than his”) — so that man, unlike the angels, cannot prevail “unless His glory hovers over him.”

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 30b: R’ Shimon ben Levi taught, “a person’s yetzer overpowers him every day and seeks to slay him, as it says, ‘the wicked one watches the righteous and seeks to slay him’ (Tehillim 37:32); and were the Holy One, blessed be He, not to help him, he could not prevail against it, as it says, ‘Hashem will not abandon him in his hand’ (Tehillim 37:33).” R’ Tzadok draws from this that the ultimate subduing of the yetzer lies beyond a person’s own power — it comes only when God’s glory “hovers over him” and He helps him; and so the Holy One told Moshe, “grip My Throne of Glory.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Tzidkas HaTzadik §129: “מיד שאדם רוצה לשוב הרי הוא בא לטהר והמשפט לסייע אותו ... וכשמסייעין אז ממילא ניתוסף בו רוח טהרה והוא מוסיף לבוא לטהר ואז חוזר הסיוע מלמעלה ביתר שאת ... עד שמפתח כחודו של מחט נעשה כפתחו של אולם” — “As soon as a person wishes to return, he is coming to purify himself, and the rule is to assist him ... When they assist him, a spirit of purity is naturally added to him, and he further comes to purify himself; then the assistance from Above returns with greater strength ... until an opening like the point of a needle becomes like the entrance of a hall.” This directly illuminates the divine assistance that enables the person’s return beyond what he could accomplish alone.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §187): “Words of Torah are oz might to a person — ‘and wisdom gives strength’ (Koheles 7:19), and ‘who is mighty? he who subdues his yetzer’ — for through it he overcomes his yetzer, as it says (Kiddushin 30b) ‘drag him to the beis midrash,’ and ‘I created the yetzer hara, I created the Torah as its antidote’ — and this is the meaning of ‘were the Holy One not to help him he could not withstand it’: the help and the assistance come through words of Torah.” R’ Tzadok here reads §2-3’s very proof-text (Kiddushin 30b, “were the Holy One not to help him”) exactly as the se’if does — the “help from Above” by which alone the yetzer is subdued is the Torah itself, the God-given oz that lets flesh-and-blood attain what belongs by nature to the angels.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The angels, having no yetzer, are the utmost of yirah and hold that gate — but they cannot enter beyond it. Man alone, a creature of choice whose body inclines to impurity and who subdues it for Heaven’s glory, is himself the place of the King’s glory. And even he cannot reach that subduing by his own power: God’s own call, “Return, Israel,” is the arousal sent into his heart.

p: (ד) וְעַל הַשָּׂגָה זוֹ אָמַר "אֱלֹהֶיךָ" לְשׁוֹן יָחִיד
And concerning this perception Scripture says “your God” (Elohekha) in the singular,
כִּי הוּא תַּכְלִית הַשָּׂגַת הָאֱלֹהוּת וְהַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכַח דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for this is the ultimate comprehension of Divinity and recognition of the immediate Presence of Hashem, blessed be He,
הַמּוּשֶּׂגֶת לְלִבּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
that is grasped within the hearts of the children of Israel,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּזֶה חִלּוּק בִּפְרָטֵי נְפָשׁוֹת
wherein distinctions exist among individual souls,
שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד טוֹעֵם כְּפִי חֶלְקוֹ,
each person tasting according to his unique portion,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר עַל פָּסוּק "נוֹדָע בַּשְּׁעָרִים בַּעְלָהּ"
– and as they expounded in the Zohar (Part I, 103b) on the verse 'Her husband is known in the gates (she'arim)'—
בְּשִׁעוּרִין דִּילֵיהּ, כָּל חַד לְפוּם מַה דִּמְשַׁעֵר בְּלִבֵּיהּ.
according to each one's estimation (shiurin), each person according to what he estimates and measures in his heart.
וְזֶהוּ כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
And this is the Throne of Glory,
דְּעוֹלַם הַכִּסֵּא דִּבְרִיאָה שָׁם הַתְחָלַת עָלְמָא דְּפֵירוּדָא
for the World of the Throne (Beriah) marks the starting point of the Realm of Differentiation.
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חִלּוּקִים וּפֵירוּד פְּרָטֵי נִבְרָאִים שׁוֹנִים
wherein distinctions and divisions among different specific creatures exist.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּאֲצִילוּת כּוּלֵיהּ חַד
In contrast, in Atzilut everything is absolute oneness;
הַיְינוּ בְּחֶלְקֵי חַיָּה יְחִידָה שֶׁהֵם בִּבְחִינַת מַקִּיף לָאָדָם
that is, within the soul-levels of Chayah and Yechidah that encompass man from without.
הַשָּׂגָה דְּשָׁם אֵין חִלּוּק
and within that apprehension there is no differentiation.
וְנִקְרָא "אֱלֹהִים",
And it is designated by the Name Elohim,
כִּי הַמַּקִּיף הוּא בִּבְחִינַת עִגּוּלִים
for the encompassing realm is in the aspect of Circles (Iggulim),
וְדָבָר עָגֹל אֵין בּוֹ חִלּוּק מַדְרֵגוֹת
and in a circular reality there is no hierarchy of levels,
כִּי לֹא נוֹדַע מְקוֹם הָרֹאשׁ וְסוֹף כְּלָל
since neither head nor end is distinguishable at all.
רַק בִּבְחִינַת יוֹשֶׁר שֶׁהוּא הַנְּשָׁמָה הַנִּכְנֶסֶת תּוֹךְ הַגּוּף
unlike the aspect of Linearity (Yosher), which is the soul entering directly within the physical body.
וּמִצַּד הָאֱמוּנָה שֶׁהוּא מַה שֶּׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל מַאֲמִינִים דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל
And from the perspective of faith, which is what Israel believes generally,
בְּלֹא הַכָּרָה בְּרוּרָה כְּאִלּוּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹכְחוֹ מַמָּשׁ שֶׁיִּצְדַּק לְשׁוֹן "אֱלֹהֶיךָ",
without that tangible, vivid recognition as though Hashem, blessed be He, were directly facing him so as to fully justify the address “your God”,
רַק בְּהֶעְלֵם הַשָּׂגָה גְּלוּיָה
but rather in the concealment of manifest revelation,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מַאֲמִין גַּם בְּמַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ מַשִּׂיג כְּלָל
a person nevertheless believes also in that which he does not consciously comprehend at all;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ גֶּדֶר הָאֱמוּנָה
which is the very definition of faith,
וּכְטַעַם "וֶאֱמוּנָתְךָ בַּלֵּילוֹת",
and mirroring 'and Your faithfulness in the nights' (Psalms 92:3).
דְּהַיְינוּ בַּחֲשֵׁיכָה וְהֶעְלֵם הָאוֹר הַבָּהִיר שֶׁאָז מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁים בֶּאֱמוּנָה
meaning in darkness and in the absence of radiant light, when we rely upon faith.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּשַׁחֲרִית "אֱמֶת וְיַצִּיב",
In contrast, in the morning we proclaim “True and Certain”,
כִּי אֱמֶת הוּא דָּבָר הַמְּבוֹרָר אֵלָיו לְגַמְרֵי
for Truth is a reality fully clarified to him.
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִטְעוֹן נֶגְדּוֹ בִּהְיוֹתוֹ גָּלוּי לָעַיִן
against which no counterargument can be brought, being completely visible to the eye.
וְהוּא מִצַּד הַשָּׂגַת הַחָכְמָה
And this stems from the comprehension of wisdom,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): "אֵין אֱמֶת אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה",
as they stated in Berakhot (5b): “There is no truth other than Torah,”
שֶׁהוּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב מִדַּת יוֹם
which is the Written Torah, the attribute of day,
אוֹר הַבָּהִיר בַּשְּׁחָקִים הַמֵּאִיר בְּכָל דָּבָר לִהְיוֹת נִגְלֶה לָעַיִן
the clear radiant light in the skies that illuminates everything so that it is revealed to sight;
שֶׁבָּזֶה יֵשׁ חִלּוּק, כָּל אֶחָד נִכְוֶה מֵהַשָּׂגָתוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ —
in which there is differentiation, where each one is singed by the spiritual canopy of his fellow (Bava Batra 75a),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק הָרוֹאֶה (בִּבְרָכוֹת נ״ח עַמּוּד א׳):
and as they said in the chapter HaRoeh (Berakhot 58a):
שֶׁאֵין דַּעְתָּן שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם דּוֹמָה זֶה לָזֶה
that the minds of human beings are not identical to one another.
אֲבָל הָאֱמוּנָה שֶׁבְּהֶעְלֵם, בָּהּ אֵין חִלּוּק מַדְרֵגוֹת
However, regarding faith which abides in concealment, there is no hierarchy of levels,
וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל מַאֲמִינִים
and all Israel are faithful believers,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (צ״ז עַמּוּד א׳),
as they stated in Shabbat (97a),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
for this is the essential root of Knesset Yisrael.
וּכְלַל הַכְּנֵסִיָּה מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם אֱמוּנָה
and the entire collective of the children of Israel possesses this inherent faith.
וְזֶה דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And this is the spiritual rung of King David, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ הַהֶעְלֵם הַשָּׁוֶה בַּכֹּל
which is the inception of repentance emerging from that concealed realm equal in all;
וְכָל הַשָּׁב מִיָּד זוֹכֶה לִסְלִיחָה וּרְפוּאַת נֶפֶשׁ.
and anyone who repents immediately merits forgiveness and the healing of the soul.
אֲבָל הַהַגָּעָה עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
However, arriving all the way up to the Throne of Glory,
הוּא הַגָּעַת הַתִּיקּוּן עַד שׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתוֹ הַמְּאוֹחָז בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
is the ascension of rectification unto the innermost root of his soul attached to the Throne of Glory;
הוּא דַּרְגָּא דִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which is the lofty rung of King Solomon, peace be upon him,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: "וַיֵּשֶׁב (שְׁלֹמֹה) עַל כִּסֵּא ה' לְמֶלֶךְ",
concerning whom it is said: 'And Solomon sat on the throne of Hashem as king' (I Chronicles 29:23);
וְכִסֵּא ה' הוּא כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד וְעוֹלַם הַכִּסֵּא
and the throne of Hashem is the Throne of Glory and the World of the Throne (Beriah),
שֶׁהוּא שָׁרְשֵׁי כָּל הַנְּשָׁמוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
which is the collective root of all souls of Israel,
שֶׁהֵם הֵן כִּסֵּא כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
which themselves constitute the very Throne of His glory, blessed be He.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §177): “As they said (Avos d’Rabbi Nasan 37), ‘two who eat from one dish — each tastes according to his deeds,’ for the taste is not the same in all; and this is called a ‘secret’ sod, which cannot be conveyed at all — for whatever can be told, once told is known to another, so how is it a secret? — as it says, ‘the secret of Hashem is to those who fear Him.’” Exactly the se’if’s face-to-face recognition: each Jewish heart tastes the Godhead according to its own portion, an apprehension that cannot be transferred.

Zohar (on “her husband is known in the gates,” Mishlei 31:23): “noda ba’she’arim — each one according to what he apprehends measures, me’sha’er in his heart”; the Divine “Husband” is “known” to each soul in the measure of that soul’s own vessel. R’ Tzadok: hence the singular “your God” — the graded, individual apprehension of the “world of separation” (the Throne, Beriah). Izhbitz-Radzin and the individualized measure of Divine apprehension. Beis Yaakov, Vayechi 24:1, emphasizes that the illumination of bechirah and da'as is not identical in every soul or at every time: what is "day" for one soul may be "night" for another, and even within a single Jew the clarity of da'as can expand and contract. The avodah established in the clear hour must therefore carry the person through periods when the light of choice and understanding is hidden. This is closely related to "לפום מה דמשער בלביה": the Divine truth is one, but the vessel through which it is presently received is particular.

The point protects R' Tzadok's language from being read as relativism. Each soul has its own shiur, not its own Torah. The same Hashem is "known in the gates" according to the measure of the heart, while halachic obligation remains objective. The individualized apprehension concerns the depth, taste, and inner recognition with which the common Torah is lived.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 58a: the Sages taught that one who sees multitudes of Israel (six hundred thousand) recites, “Blessed is He who knows all secrets chacham ha-razim” — for “their minds are not alike one to another, and their faces are not alike one to another,” and He who knows all secrets knows what lies in each of their hearts. R’ Tzadok cites this for the principle that in the revealed apprehension of Godhead there is a genuine difference among individual souls, each one tasting according to his portion — as opposed to emunah, the concealed faith shared alike by all Israel.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §227): “All Israel possess a complete emunah in Hashem — in His existence, His oneness, and His providence — as it says (Shabbos 97a) that they are ‘believers, the children of believers’; and this is called the nefesh of the holiness of Bnei Yisrael. And when one merits more, they grant him ruach — that is, when the heart is further refined, until he feels it in the heart and passes from the rung of emunah to the rung of emes truth.” This is exactly §2-4’s two tiers: the general emunah by which “Israel believe, without clear apprehension” — believing even what is not grasped at all — and, above it, the face-to-face “recognition granted to the hearts of Israel,” where emunah has ripened into felt emes.

paragraphs.text:
Shabbos 97a: “Israel are believers, the children of believers” — and one who suspects the worthy is stricken; faith is the shared root of Knesses Yisrael. R’ Tzadok: because faith operates in “concealment,” it admits no gradation — every Jew equally believes; this equal-in-all concealment is David’s rung of teshuvah. Izhbitz-Radzin on emunah that remains when da'as is concealed. Beis Yaakov, Vayechi 24:1, explains that there are times when "אור הבחירה" and the person's felt da'as are hidden; therefore Chazal fixed Krias Shema and tefillah each morning so that the prior acceptance of Malchus Shamayim surrounds and carries him even through the later hours of concealment. This gives a practical form to R' Tzadok's distinction between emunah and revealed apprehension. The equal root-faith of Israel is not a lesser substitute for knowledge but the covenantal hold that persists when individualized spiritual clarity recedes.

That is why David's rung can be associated with concealment without being a defect. Davidic emunah means the ability to remain attached precisely where the visible proof is absent — the spiritual condition in which teshuvah begins, before the person's past has been openly transfigured.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: “Your God” marks a face-to-face recognition granted to each heart according to its portion — the Throne of Glory, the world of separation, in which levels genuinely differ. Faith is shared by all Israel without gradation; revealed apprehension is graded. David’s teshuvah works from the concealment shared by all, while reaching the Throne itself is Shlomo’s rung.

p: (ה) וּמַלְכוּת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמְרוּ עָלָיו מֵהַאי קְרָא בִּמְגִלָּה (י״א עַמּוּד ב׳):
And regarding the kingdom of King Solomon, peace be upon him, they deduced from this verse in Megillah (11b):
"שֶׁמָּלַךְ עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנִים וְעַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים".
“that he reigned over the upper beings and over the lower beings.”,
וּמִלַּת "וְעַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים" לִכְאוֹרָה מְיוּתָּר לָעִנְיָן
And the phrase “and over the lower beings” is seemingly redundant to the point,
דְּאָתוּ עֲלָהּ דְּהַמִּילְּתָא אַחֲרִיתָא דַּהֲוָה בֵּיהּ,
since they come to explain the unique, exceptional matter that was found in him,
הוּא מַה דְּמָלַךְ עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנִים
which is that he reigned over the celestial beings.
וְגַם מִקְּרָא דְּ"כִסֵּא ה'" נָפֵיק רַק זֶה
and also from the verse citing “the throne of Hashem” only this celestial dominion is derived.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אִם הָיָה זֶה דְּמָלַךְ עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנִים רַק תּוֹסֶפֶת בְּמַלְכוּתוֹ,
However in truth, had this fact that he reigned over the upper beings been merely an added bonus in his monarchy,
אִם כֵּן עֲדַיִן הַקֻּשְׁיָא בִּמְקוֹמָהּ:
if so, the difficulty remains in full force:
וּמַה בְּכָךְ דְּמָלַךְ גַּם עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנִים
what of it that he also reigned over celestial beings?
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מָלַךְ גַּם עַל כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ כְּמוֹהֶם
nonetheless he also reigned over the entire terrestrial world just like the other global monarchs!
וְהָיָה לוֹ לְחוֹשְׁבוֹ בִּכְלַל הַמּוֹלְכִים בְּכִיפָּה
and the Gemara should have numbered him among those who ruled over the entire dome of the earth!
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ אָמַר דְּמִילְּתָא אַחֲרִיתָא הֲוָה בִּכְלַל מַלְכוּתוֹ,
Perforce you must say that a fundamentally different quality permeated his entire kingship;
כִּי כָּל מֶלֶךְ הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הָאֻמָּה
for every king is the essential root of his entire nation,
שֶׁעַל כֵּן נִמְשַׁל מֶלֶךְ בָּעוֹלָם כְּלֵב בַּגּוּף
which is why a king in the world is compared to the heart in the body,
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַגּוּף וּמִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים לְכָל הָאֵבָרִים
which is the life-source of the body, from which flow the conduits of life to all the limbs.
וְכֵן הַמֶּלֶךְ, אֲפִילּוּ מַלְכֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
and likewise the king, even among the kings of the nations of the world.
וּבִזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל תַּחַת מֶמְשַׁלְתָּם הוּא גָּלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה
And during times when Israel is subjugated under their rule, this constitutes the exile of the Shechinah.
שֶׁהִיא מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם שֶׁמִּתְלַבֶּשֶׁת בָּהֶם לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יָדָם
which is the Sovereignty of Heaven enclothing itself within them to channel divine sustenance to Israel through their hands.
וּכְשֶׁהוּא אֵין מַכִּיר זֶה שֶׁרַק מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה
And when the gentile monarch fails to recognize that His Sovereignty, blessed be He, alone rules over all,
וְאֵין מוֹרָא שָׁמַיִם עָלָיו
and bears no fear of Heaven upon himself,
נִקְרָא גָּלוּת: "כְּאִישׁ נוֹדֵד מִמְּקוֹמוֹ".
it is termed exile, mirroring: “Like a man who wanders from his place” (Proverbs 27:8).
שֶׁהוּא הַיִּרְאָה אֵצֶל מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
Whereas fear is the hallmark found by the kings of Israel,
שֶׁמְּבָרְכִין עֲלֵיהֶם "שֶׁחָלַק מִכְּבוֹדוֹ לִירֵאָיו",
over whom we recite the blessing: “Who has imparted of His glory to those who fear Him,”
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק הָרוֹאֶה (בְּרָכוֹת נ״ח עַמּוּד א׳),
as they stated in the chapter HaRoeh (Berakhot 58a).
שֶׁבָּהֶם תַּכְלִית הַיִּרְאָה בְּתוֹקֶף
for within them exists the absolute pinnacle of awe in all its might.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת לד רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב)
As they taught (Berakhot 34b):
"מֶלֶךְ, כֵּיוָן שֶׁכּוֹרֵעַ שׁוּב אֵינוֹ זוֹקֵף",
“A king, once he bows, does not straighten up again (until the prayer concludes),”
וְזֶה מִפְּנֵי תּוֹקֶף הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁעָלָיו
and this is due to the formidable intensity of the fear resting upon him,
וּמִפְּנֵי שְׁמִי נָחַת הוּא
and “because of My Name he was humbled,”
כִּי מִדַּת מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם, שֶׁהִיא מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה, נוֹסְסָה בּוֹ,
for the attribute of the Sovereignty of Heaven, which is the attribute of Fear, is raised as a banner within him,
וְאָז מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת בִּמְקוֹמוֹ.
and then the attribute of Malchut is properly situated in its place.
וּמִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה הִיא הַתַּרְעָא לְדָרְתָּא (הַשַּׁעַר לַדִּירָה),
And the attribute of Fear is the outer gate to the inner dwelling,
וְהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם רֹאשׁ לְמַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
and this is the spiritual rung of King David, peace be upon him, head of the kings of Israel,
וְהוּא עָשָׂה הַשְּׁעָרִים לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
and he constructed the gates for the Holy Temple.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל פָּסוּק "טָבְעוּ בָאָרֶץ שְׁעָרֶיהָ",
And our Sages of blessed memory expounded on the verse (Lamentations 2:9): “Her gates have sunk into the ground,”.
שֶׁלֹּא שָׁלְטוּ אוֹיְבִים בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו
that enemies held no destructive power over the handiwork of his hands.
כִּי הַשְּׁלִיטָה הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר יֵשׁ לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ,
For dominion can occur only when the foes possess some intrinsic affinity to that specific spiritual force;
וְיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּיָּדוּעַ,
and the fear of Heaven of King David, peace be upon him, who is the root of the Congregation of Israel as is known,
"לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי",
“He did not do so unto any other nation,” (Psalms 147:20),
וְנִשְׁבַּע לָהֶם שֶׁלֹּא יַחֲלִיפֵם בְּאֻמָּה אַחֶרֶת
and He swore unto them that He would never exchange them for another people,
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת לֹא יָמוּשׁ,
and the bedrock of Jewish identity shall never depart,
וְכֹחַ זֶה לְעוֹלָם נָטוּעַ בִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד
and this power is planted eternally within the Congregation of Israel alone.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם
only that it exists in concealment.
כִּי עִיקַּר הַיִּרְאָה הוּא בֵּין בְּטִיבוּ בֵּין בְּעָקוּ,
For authentic fear abides whether in benevolence or in acute distress,
לֹא כְּמִנְהַג אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם: "כִּי יִרְעַב וְהִתְקַצַּף וְקִלֵּל בְּמַלְכּוֹ וּבֵאלֹהָיו".
not like the practice of the pagan nations: “when he shall be hungry, he shall fret himself, and curse his king and his God” (Isaiah 8:21).
כִּי הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁבְּהֶעְלֵם הִיא יִרְאָה תַּתָּאָה
For the fear in concealment is the lower fear (Yirah Tata'ah),
הִיא יִרְאַת הָעוֹנֶשׁ הַמִּתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ;
which is the fear of punishment that spreads throughout the entire world;
אֲבָל אֵצֶל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵין זֶה קָרוּי יִרְאָה כְּלָל
yet among the nations of the world this is not termed true fear at all,
שֶׁהֲרֵי אִם יַגִּיעֵם הָעוֹנֶשׁ וְלֹא יִמָּלְטוּ יִבְעֲטוּ בוֹ,
for if the punishment overtakes them and they cannot escape, they kick and rebel against Him.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אֵצֶל יִשְׂרָאֵל
which is not so with Israel.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
And as they stated in Rosh Hashanah (4a),
לְחַלֵּק כֵּן בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
to distinguish thus between Israel and the nations of the world.
עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִׁ״י דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּשֶׁמְּרִיעִין לוֹ אֵין קוֹרֵא תַּגָּר
see there in Rashi, that an Israelite, even when suffering is brought upon him, does not challenge divine justice.
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא צַדִּיק גָּמוּר גַּם בְּיִרְאַת הָעוֹנֶשׁ שֶׁלָּהֶם
Therefore an Israelite is termed completely righteous even within his baseline fear of punishment.
שֶׁגַּם בָּהּ גָּנוּז יִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת
since within it there is also concealed the lofty awe of divine transcendence.
וְזֶהוּ הַטְּבִיעָה בָּאָרֶץ שְׁעָרֶיהָ:
And this is the mystical meaning of the sinking of her gates into the earth:
יִרְאָה הַגְּמוּרָה, שֶׁהִיא הַשַּׁעַר לַה', טְבוּעָה וּגְנוּזָה בָּאָרֶץ
the absolute, authentic Fear, which is the Gate to Hashem, is deeply sunk and concealed within the earth,
שֶׁהִיא יִרְאָה תַּתָּאָה
which is this lower, foundational fear,
וְהַיְינוּ בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
meaning rooted within the Land of Israel and the Congregation of Israel;
וְלֹא שָׁלְטָה בָּהֶם יְדֵי אוֹיְבִים מֵאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
and the hands of enemies from the nations held no dominion over them.
דְּהֵם בְּיִרְאַת עוֹנֶשׁ שֶׁלָּהֶם נִקְרָאִים רְשָׁעִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם
since the nations, within their own selfish fear of punishment, are classified as wicked, as they stated there.

This is §2-5’s premise made explicit: “every king is the root of his whole nation,” so that his dominion over “the lower” is no mere addendum — the nation is comprised within him at the root, and to rule its members is to rule what is already folded into his own soul.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §68): “All the services of the body’s limbs, and the mitzvos performed through them, are only to straighten the heart; and the essence is the heart, for there is the dwelling-place of Hashem — as the Sages said (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2), ‘the Holy One is the heart of Israel,’ as it says, ‘the Rock of my heart’ (Tehillim 73:26).” This is precisely the image §2-5 invokes — “a king is likened to the heart in the body”: the limbs (the nation) exist to serve and actualize the heart (the king), the single root-organ that is the seat of vitality and of the bond with God, and from which all the rest draws its life.

paragraphs.text: Eicha 2:9: “טָבְעוּ בָאָרֶץ שְׁעָרֶיהָ, אִבַּד וְשִׁבַּר בְּרִיחֶיהָ, מַלְכָּהּ וְשָׂרֶיהָ בַגּוֹיִם אֵין תּוֹרָה, גַּם נְבִיאֶיהָ לֹא מָצְאוּ חָזוֹן מֵה׳” — “Her gates have sunk into the ground, He has ruined and shattered her bars; her king and her officers are among the nations, there is no Torah; her prophets, too, find no vision from Hashem.” Rashi, citing the Sages (Sotah 9a), explains that the Temple gates David had wrought sank into the earth rather than fall to the enemy — “they were the handiwork of David, and therefore the enemies had no power over them”; and Eichah Rabbah adds that the gates had once done honor to the Aron, saying “lift up your heads, O gates” (Tehillim 24:7). R’ Tzadok reads this as the mark of David’s rung: his yiras shamayim, the root of Knesses Yisrael, gives the nations no purchase, so his handiwork can never come under their rule.

paragraphs.text: Yeshayah 8:21: “וְעָבַר בָּהּ נִקְשֶׁה וְרָעֵב, וְהָיָה כִי יִרְעַב וְהִתְקַצַּף וְקִלֵּל בְּמַלְכּוֹ וּבֵאלֹהָיו וּפָנָה לְמָעְלָה” — “And he shall pass through it hard-pressed and hungry; and it shall be, when he is hungry, that he shall rage and curse his king and his god, and turn his face upward.” Rashi explains that this speaks of those who forsake the Holy One and rely on the kings of Egypt: when famine and siege overtake them, “he curses the calves and the baalim they had worshipped, and turns upward to beseech Hashem — who will not listen, for the decree has been sealed.” R’ Tzadok contrasts this fickle fear with Israel’s: the nations cling to their god only in good times and blaspheme in distress, whereas Israel’s yirah endures “whether in His goodness or in affliction,” and a Jew, when he is stricken, does not “cry out in complaint” (Rosh Hashanah 4a).

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Every king is the root of his whole nation, as the heart is to the body. The malchus of Israel’s kings is the yiras shamayim that rests upon them, over which one blesses “who apportioned of His glory to those who fear Him.” Enemies never ruled over David’s handiwork, for yiras shamayim gives them no purchase — and Israel’s fear holds in affliction as in good.

p: אֲבָל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִדָּה אַחֶרֶת הָיְתָה בּוֹ,
However, regarding King Solomon, peace be upon him, a different divine attribute was manifest in him:
הוּא מִדַּת הַחָכְמָה
namely, the attribute of Wisdom,
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה הָיְתָה מַלְכוּתוֹ;
and from this dimension his royal sovereignty emanated;
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (כ״א עַמּוּד ב׳):
which is why they stated in Rosh Hashanah (21b):
"בִּמְלָכִים קָם",
“among kings he did arise,”
רָצָה לוֹמַר בְּמִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁהָיְתָה לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
meaning that he arose in that dimension of kingship that belonged to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהָיָה רַק מִפְּנֵי מַעֲלַת חָכְמָתוֹ,
which emerged purely on account of the transcendent supremacy of his wisdom.
דְּעַל כֵּן מָלַךְ עַל דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר, דּוֹר דֵּעָה
which is why Moses ruled over the generation of the wilderness, the generation of profound knowledge.
וְגַם לְאִידָךְ מַאן דְּאָמַר שָׁם
And also according to the other authority cited there,
מַה דְּבִקֵּשׁ לִהְיוֹת כְּמֹשֶׁה הוּא מִן הַצַּד הַזֶּה
what Solomon sought—to attain the spiritual stature of Moses—stemmed from this perspective,
וְיָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל: "וְלֹא קָם וְגוֹמֵר".
and a Heavenly Voice came forth proclaiming: “And there arose not (a prophet in Israel like Moses), etc.” (Deuteronomy 34:10).
כִּי כָּל חָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה הָיְתָה טְפֵלָה לִנְבוּאָתוֹ וְנִמְשֶׁכֶת מִמֶּנָּה
For all the wisdom of Moses was secondary to his prophecy and directly drawn from it,
שֶׁהוּא חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב שֶׁכֻּלָּהּ נְבוּאָה מִפִּי ה
', which is the wisdom of the Written Torah that is entirely prophecy directly from the mouth of Hashem,
שֶׁהוּא בִּרְאִיָּה גְּמוּרָה וּבְאַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא הַמְּאִירָה
which exists in clear sight and through the luminous looking-glass.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן חָכְמַת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא חָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה
in contrast, the wisdom of King Solomon, peace be upon him, was lower wisdom (Chokhmah Tata'ah).
דְּעַל כֵּן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מָלַךְ בַּמִּדְבָּר עַל אוֹכְלֵי מָן
Therefore Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, reigned in the wilderness over eaters of manna,
שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהֶם חֵלֶק בָּאָרֶץ וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל
who held no practical share in the physical land or mundane affairs of this world at all;
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא מָלַךְ גַּם כֵּן עַל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
and therefore he likewise did not reign over the gentile nations of the world,
שֶׁחָכְמָתוֹ הִיא חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה
since his wisdom was Supernal Wisdom,
שֶׁלֹּא מִצַּד הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתָהּ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים
not from the perspective of its downward extension into the lower earthly realms.
הַיְינוּ בְּחָכְמָתָן שֶׁל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִיא חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
meaning through the rational-spiritual wisdom of the children of Israel which constitutes the Oral Torah.
אֲבָל חָכְמַת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא גִּימֶ״ל סְפָרִים שֶׁעָשָׂה
However, the wisdom of King Solomon, peace be upon him, is embodied in the three sacred books he authored (Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, Song of Songs),
שֶׁהֵם בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ לְבַד
which were composed through Ruach HaKodesh (Divine Inspiration) alone.
שֶׁהוּא נְבוּאַת הַחֲכָמִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ן (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא י״ב עַמּוּד א׳), עַיֵּין שָׁם
which is the subtle prophetic inspiration of sages, as the Ramban wrote in Bava Batra (12a), see there.
וְהוּא כֹּחַ הַחָכְמָה הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים
And it is the power of wisdom that extends downward into the terrestrial realms,
שֶׁהִיא מִתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת גַּם בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
which expands even into the nations of the world,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה  עַל פָּסוּק: "וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי חֲכָמִים מֵאֱדוֹם":
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Eichah Rabbah 2:13) on the verse: “And I will destroy the wise men out of Edom” (Obadiah 1:8):
"הָאוֹמֵר יֵשׁ חָכְמָה בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם – תַּאֲמֵן".
“If one says to you: There is wisdom among the nations of the world—believe it.”
וְכֵן אִיתָא בִּמְגִלָּה (ט״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
And so it is brought in Megillah (16a);
דְּגַם בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם נִקְרָא חָכָם
that even among the gentile nations one can be designated as wise;
וּבְפֶרֶק הָרוֹאֶה דִּמְבָרְכִין "שֶׁנָּתַן מֵחָכְמָתוֹ" עַל חַכְמֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
and in the chapter HaRoeh (Berakhot 58a) it is taught that we recite the blessing: “Who has given of His wisdom” over gentile sages,
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין אוֹמֵר "לִירֵאָיו",
except that the blessing omits the words “to those who fear Him,”
דִּלְיִרְאָה אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת
for with awe and fear of God they have no authentic connection.
אֲבָל לְחָכְמָה יֵשׁ לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת
yet to wisdom they certainly possess an affinity.
עַל כֵּן שָׁלְטוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו שֶׁל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
Therefore foreign foes were able to hold dominion over the physical handiwork of King Solomon, peace be upon him;
וְגַם זֶה רַק מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and even this occurred only from the vantage point of this transient world,
דִּלְעָתִיד נֶאֱמַר: "וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר",
for in the ultimate future it is declared: “And I will destroy (the wise men out of Edom), etc.”,
וְאֵין עִיקַּר חָכְמָה אֶלָּא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
and the essential, enduring core of wisdom exists nowhere except in Israel,
שֶׁשּׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתָם שֶׁבְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
for the root of their soul anchored within the Throne of Glory.
הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ שֶׁל כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
is the primordial fountainhead of the wisdom that resides in the brain of every single Jew.
וְזֶהוּ כִּסֵּא ה' וְהַמְּלוּכָה בָּעֶלְיוֹנִים
And this is the throne of Hashem and kingship over the celestial beings,
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבְּעוֹלַם הַכִּסֵּא
which is the supreme root of wisdom rooted within the World of the Throne (Beriah),
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מָלַךְ גַּם עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים
and through this foundation he reigned over the terrestrial beings as well,
שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן עַל כִּסֵּא ה
'. which is likewise seated upon the throne of Hashem.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים אֵינוֹ מְיוּחָד בָּהֶם
Just as the expansion of the glory of His divine kingship, blessed be He, in the lower realms is not isolated or confined to them,
רַק נִמְשָׁךְ מִצַּד הִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתוֹ בָּעֶלְיוֹנִים
but is rather drawn forth via the descending cascade of His manifest expanse in the supernal realms.
כֵּן אֶצְלוֹ הַכֹּל הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת מַלְכוּת אַחַת מֵרֹאשׁ וְעַד סוֹף
so too with Solomon, his entire domain was one single continuum of kingship from summit to base.
וְזֶהוּ הַמִּילְּתָא אַחֲרִינָא דַּהֲוָה בֵּיהּ גַּם בְּמַלְכוּתוֹ עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים
And this is the distinct, unique reality that existed within him regarding his kingship over the lower realm as well:
שֶׁלֹּא מָלַךְ בְּכִיפָּה
that he did not merely reign 'under the dome',
דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר עוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ שֶׁתַּחַת הַשָּׁמַיִם הַדּוֹמִים לְכִיפָּה
which denotes the terrestrial earth beneath the heavens that curve like a vaulted dome,
דְּשָׁם הוּא מַלְכוּתָם לִהְיוֹת שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְכָל הָעַמִּים
where the worldly emperors reign, serving as earthly roots for physical nations,
שֶׁכָּל זֶה רַק מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְתַחַת הַכִּיפָּה לְבַד
all of which exists strictly from the earthly perspective and beneath the physical dome alone.
אֲבָל הוּא, שׁוֹרֶשׁ מַלְכוּתוֹ הָיְתָה מֵעַל הַכִּיפָּה וְלֹא בְּכִיפָּה
however, regarding Solomon, the foundational root of his monarchy transcended above the cosmic dome and was not confined within the dome.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 21b presents two readings. One says: “בקש קהלת להיות כמשה, יצתה בת קול ואמרה לו ... ולא קם נביא עוד בישראל כמשה” — “Koheles sought to be like Moshe; a heavenly voice went out and said to him ... ‘No prophet again arose in Israel like Moshe.’” The other says: “בנביאים לא קם, במלכים קם” — “Among prophets none arose; among kings one arose,” and interprets Koheles’ rejected request as the wish to judge inner intentions without witnesses or warning. R’ Tzadok identifies the royal comparison with the dimension of wisdom, while distinguishing Moshe’s wisdom, which flowed from prophecy, from Shlomo’s lower wisdom.

paragraphs.text: Eichah Rabbah 2:13: on “her king and her officers are among the nations, there is no Torah” (Eicha 2:9), the Midrash teaches: “If a person says to you, ‘there is wisdom chochmah among the nations,’ believe it — as it is written, ‘I will destroy the wise from Edom and understanding from the mount of Esav’ (Ovadiah 1:8); but if he says, ‘there is Torah among the nations,’ do not believe it, as it is written, ‘her king and her officers are among the nations — there is no Torah.’” This is R’ Tzadok’s source that the lower chochmah — the order of wisdom belonging to Shlomo — spreads even among the nations, whereas Torah and yiras shamayim are the portion of Israel alone.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 58a: the Sages taught that one who sees the sages of Israel recites, “Blessed is He who apportioned chalak of His wisdom to those who fear Him,” whereas over the sages of the nations one recites, “Blessed is He who gave natan of His wisdom to flesh and blood.” R’ Tzadok draws his distinction from the wording of the blessings: the nations are given wisdom, but the blessing does not add “to those who fear Him” — for they have a connection to chochmah but not to yirah; only over the sages of Israel, in whom wisdom and fear are joined, does one say “who apportioned of His wisdom to those who fear Him.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Tzidkas HaTzadik §226: “כל אחד יכול להשיג חכמה וד״ת ואע״פ שאין לו יראת חטא הקודמת ואתעדל״ת שמתעורר ללימוד והשגת התורה בשביל כבוד שמו ית׳ ומכיר שהוא תורת ה׳. מ״מ הש״י מוכן להשפיע תמיד ד״ת אף בלא אתעדל״ת” — “Everyone can attain wisdom and words of Torah, even though he lacks prior fear of sin and an awakening from below that moves him to study and attain Torah for the honor of His blessed Name, recognizing it as God’s Torah. inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Shlomo’s kingship came from a different side — the middah of chochmah. Moshe’s wisdom was subordinate to his prophecy, the clear vision of the Written Torah; Shlomo’s is the lower wisdom of ruach ha-kodesh. That lower wisdom spreads even among the nations, which is why they did rule over Shlomo’s handiwork — the root wisdom being Israel’s alone.

p: (ז) וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (ל׳ עַמּוּד א׳):
And this is what they stated in Shabbat (30a):
"בְּחַיֵּי שְׁלֹמֹה בִּנְךָ אֲנִי מוֹדִיעַ וְכוּלֵי",
“In the lifetime of Solomon your son I will make it known, etc.”;
וּבֵירוּר מַעֲלַת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיְתָה בִּפְתִיחַת שְׁעָרִים
and the decisive validation of the sublime status of King David, peace be upon him, occurred at the opening of the Temple gates.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד (יִרְאָה) כַּנִּזְכָּר
which is the spiritual rung of David (Reverence/Gate), as mentioned.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הַהוֹדָעָה הַזּוֹ, שֶׁהוּא בֵּירוּר תִּיקּוּן הַקּוֹדֵם
And nevertheless, this public disclosure, which constitutes the definitive clarification that the past had been completely rectified
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל סִימָן א׳),
(as I wrote above in Section 1),
זֶה הָיָה רַק בְּחַיֵּי שְׁלֹמֹה
this could occur only in the lifetime of Solomon,
שֶׁהוּא הַמַּגִּיעַ בִּתְשׁוּבָתוֹ עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
who is the one who ascends in his repentance all the way to the Throne of Glory,
דְּיָשַׁב עַל כִּסֵּא ה
', for he sat enthroned upon the throne of Hashem,
וְאָז אֵין חֵטְא כְּלָל
and at that celestial altitude sin has no existence whatsoever,
כְּטַעַם: "גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי".
mirroring the verse (Psalms 23:4): “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me.”
"אַתָּה" הוּא הַכָּרַת נוֹכַח דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
“You” denotes the immediate, face-to-face perception of Hashem, blessed be He;
זֶהוּ "עִמָּדִי" מַמָּשׁ בְּעוֹלַם הַכִּסֵּא
and this is literally “with me” in the World of the Throne,
שֶׁנִּקְרָא "אֵת ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ" כַּנִּזְכָּר
which is termed “with Hashem your God,” as mentioned earlier;
אָז "גַּם כִּי וְגוֹמֵר"
at that pinnacle, “even though (I walk in deepest darkness)”,
וְאֶעֱשֶׂה מַה שֶּׁאֶעֱשֶׂה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
and whatever actions I may find myself doing, Heaven forbid,
אֵין כָּאן יִרְאַת רָע
there is no fear of evil here,
דְּ"לֹא יְגֻרְךָ רָע" כְּתִיב
for it is written (Psalms 5:5): “Evil cannot abide with You,”.
וְאֵין דָּבָר רָע יוֹרֵד מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
and no evil ever descends directly from Heaven.
וְהַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכַח הַיְינוּ דִּ"מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ" גַּם כֵּן
And the perception of His immediate Presence reveals that “the fullness of the whole earth is His glory” as well.

paragraphs.text:
Divrei HaYamim I 29:23: “וַיֵּשֶׁב שְׁלֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּא ה׳ לְמֶלֶךְ תַּחַת דָּוִיד אָבִיו וַיַּצְלַח, וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ אֵלָיו כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל” — “And Shlomo sat upon the Throne of Hashem as king in place of David his father, and he prospered, and all Israel heeded him.” Scripture uniquely calls Israel’s royal throne “the Throne of Hashem,” for the kingship of the House of David is the earthly embodiment of the kingship of Heaven — as the Gemara puts it, “earthly kingship is a likeness of the heavenly kingship” (Berachos 58a). R’ Tzadok therefore assigns to Shlomo the rung of reaching the Throne of Glory itself, in contrast to David’s rung — the teshuvah that rises from the concealment shared by all Israel. Maharal and the symbolism of the Kisei. Gevuros Hashem ch. 70, in explaining the seven things created before the world, identifies the Kisei HaKavod with absolute elevation and with malchus: "כסא" signifies kingship, the level at which Hashem is revealed as exalted over the created order. Teshuvah and the Kisei are both pre-worldly realities in that sugya. R' Tzadok's assignment of Shlomo to the second rung can therefore be read with precision: "וישב שלמה על כסא ה'" is not merely a royal metaphor but an earthly appearance of the level to which teshuvah reaches.

For David the forgiveness is real while its final vindication remains hidden; under Shlomo, the gates open and the truth of David's past is publicly disclosed. The transition from David to Shlomo thus mirrors the movement from concealed teshuvah to the Kisei's revealed malchus.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 23:4: “גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי, שִׁבְטְךָ וּמִשְׁעַנְתֶּךָ הֵמָּה יְנַחֲמֻנִי” — “Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff — they comfort me.” In its plain sense (Rashi; Metzudat David), David declares that even when passing through places dark as death’s shadow he fears no harm, for Hashem is at his side, and even the “rod” of affliction is for his good and consoles him. R’ Tzadok reads “for You are with me” as the face-to-face recognition of Hashem “in the world of the Throne” — the rung of Shlomo, “he sat on the Throne of Hashem” — at which one “fears no evil at all,” since evil has no independent standing before that presence.

paragraphs.text: Koheles Rabbah 1:13 says that Shlomo knew how to sweeten mustard and the bitter lupines (tormusin). The standard Midrash does NOT say that he knew how to “heal the past.” Rav Tzadok separately records a received reading concerning ha-kodem, “the past,” which should not be presented as the standard Midrash text. His comparison is interpretive: just as bitterness is sweetened, the bitterness of sin can be transformed through teshuvah. He associates this with “evil and bitter is your forsaking Hashem” (Yirmeyah 2:19) — the bitter itself ultimately becoming sweet through repentance from love.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: David attained the opening of the gates; the manifest rectification of the past came only in Shlomo’s lifetime, who reached “up to the Throne of Glory.” At that rung there is no sin at all — “I shall fear no evil, for You are with me.” This accounts for conduct of his that looks like walking in the valley of the shadow, and for the answer given to those who questioned it.

p: (ח) וְלֵיכָּא מִידֵּי דְּלָא רְמִיזֵי בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא
And there is nothing that is not alluded to in the Torah,
כִּי כְּבָר נִגְלָה הַכֹּל לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
for everything was already revealed to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him,
רַק שֶׁאָז עֲדַיִן הָיָה בְּהֶעְלֵם וּבְרֶמֶז
except that at that era it remained in concealment and subtle allusion.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת
and only later did it emerge into open manifestation.
וְגַם זוֹ הַמַּדְרֵגָה, שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַתּוֹרָה
And this lofty level as well, which is the foundational threshold of the Torah,
נִגְלָה תְּחִלָּתוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּרֶמֶז
was initially revealed to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, in allusion.
בַּהַמְתָּקַת מֵי מָרָה שֶׁהָיְתָה עַל יְדֵי הַשְׁלָכַת עֵץ
at the sweetening of the bitter waters of Marah, which took place through casting in a tree.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "אֵין עֵץ אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה",
And our Sages of blessed memory expounded: “Tree refers to nothing other than Torah,”
שֶׁהוּא תַּבְלִין לַיֵּצֶר
which is the curative spice against the evil inclination,
וְעַל יָדָהּ הוּא הִתְהַפְּכוּת הַמַּר לְמָתוֹק
and through it occurs the complete transmutation of bitter into sweet;
וְזֶה לְשׁוֹן "וַיּוֹרֵהוּ", וְתִרְגֵּם אוּנְקְלוֹס "וְאַלְּפֵיהּ",
and this is the meaning of “And He instructed him (vayorehu),” which Onkelos translates as “and He taught him,”.
וְהוּא מִלְּשׁוֹן תּוֹרָה
which derives from the very root of Torah (instruction).
וְשָׁם הָיְתָה הַתְחָלַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּצְטַוּוּ עַל מִקְצָת מִצְווֹת
And there was the inception of the Torah, where they were commanded concerning several initial mitzvot,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר שָׁם: "שָׁם שָׂם לוֹ חֹק וּמִשְׁפָּט".
as it is stated there (Exodus 15:25): “There He made for them a statute and an ordinance.”,
וּמִשְׁפָּט הַיְינוּ דִּינִין דְּאִיפַּקּוּד שָׁם
And “ordinance” (mishpat) refers to the civil laws they were instructed there,
דַּרְגָּא דְּיִצְחָק שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה
which is the spiritual rung of Isaac who is the source-root of the Torah,
דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה נָפְקַת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים
for the Torah emerges from the side of Gevurah (Might/Discipline), as stated in the Zohar numerous times;
וּלְשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא בְּמַכּוֹת (כג עַמּוּד ב)
and matching the wording of the Gemara in Makkot (24a):
עַל "אָנֹכִי" וְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה" מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה שְׁמַעֲנוּם
regarding the commandments “I am” and “You shall have no other gods,” that we heard them directly from the mouth of the Almighty (Gevurah).
וְהַהַכָּרָה דְּ"אָנֹכִי ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ" הוּא הַהַכָּרָה דְּ"אַתָּה עִמָּדִי",
And the recognition that “I am Hashem your God” is identical to the perception that “You are with me”;
וְזֶהוּ מִסִּטְרָא דְּיִצְחָק
and this originates from the side of Isaac,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (פ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳):
just as they stated in Shabbat (89b):
"מַחְוֵי לְהוּ יִצְחָק הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ",
“Isaac will point out the Holy One, blessed be He, before their very eyes,”.
דְּהָרְאִיָּה הַגְּמוּרָה לְנוֹכַח הָעַיִן הוּא עַל יְדֵי יִצְחָק
for the complete, undeniable direct vision before the eye is attained through Isaac.
דְּהַשָּׂגָה זוֹ הַבְּרוּרָה לָעַיִן וּבְחִלּוּק מַדְרֵגוֹת
For this comprehension, crystal-clear to the eye yet differentiated by spiritual levels,
הוּא מִצַּד מִדַּת הַצִּמְצוּם הַמְּצַמְצֶמֶת הַהַשָּׂגָה לְשִׁיעוּרִין וּמַדְרֵגוֹת
stems from the attribute of Tzimtzum (Contraction/Focus) which contracts comprehension into precise measures and distinct ranks;
שֶׁהוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן הַנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה
for Isaac was the first to be circumcised on the eighth day,
שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְקַן שָׁרְשׁוֹ לִהְיוֹת טוֹב מִתּוֹלָדָה
such that his essential root was already rectified to be pure and good from birth,
וְטֶרֶם יֵדַע מָאוֹס בָּרָע וּבָחוֹר בַּטּוֹב
and before he even knew how to refuse the evil and choose the good
כְּבָר הוּא נִימּוֹל וְנִרְשָׁם בִּבְרִית חוֹתָמוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
he was already circumcised and inscribed in the covenant of the seal of Hashem, blessed be He,
שֶׁשַּׁיָּיךְ לְחֶלְקוֹ וְגוֹרָלוֹ וְלֹא יִירָא רָע כְּלָל
signifying that he belongs intrinsically to His portion and destiny and shall fear no evil at all.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִמְתַּק הַמַּר
and through this the bitter is sweetened.

paragraphs.text: Shemos 15:25: at Marah — “וַיִּצְעַק אֶל ה׳ וַיּוֹרֵהוּ ה׳ עֵץ וַיַּשְׁלֵךְ אֶל הַמַּיִם וַיִּמְתְּקוּ הַמָּיִם, שָׁם שָׂם לוֹ חֹק וּמִשְׁפָּט וְשָׁם נִסָּהוּ” — “and he cried out to Hashem, and Hashem showed him a tree; he cast it into the water, and the water turned sweet. There He set for them a statute and an ordinance, and there He tested them.” Rashi (from Sanhedrin 56b): “‘there He set for them’ — at Marah He gave them a few passages of the Torah to occupy themselves with: Shabbos, the red heifer, and civil law dinin.” R’ Tzadok reads the tree that sweetened the bitter waters as the Torah — “there is no ‘tree’ but Torah,” the spice for the yetzer — and the “chok u-mishpat” as the beginning of the Torah’s dinim, the rung of Yitzchak and the side of Gevurah from which the Torah issues; and “va’yorehu and He showed him,” which Onkelos renders “and He taught him,” is of the very root of “Torah.”

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Shlomo’s wisdom included knowing how to heal the past and to “sweeten the lupine” — turning the bitter itself sweet. All of it was already hinted to Moshe: the waters of Marah were sweetened through a tree, and there is no “tree” but Torah, the spice for the yetzer. The recognition “I am Hashem your God” belongs to the side of Yitzchak — the graded, contracted vision.

p: (ט) אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵצֶל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה בַּמַּיִם
Only that with Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, the sweetening occurred within water,
וְאֵין מַיִם אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה
and water is nothing other than Torah,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ גַּם כֵּן סַמָּא דְּמוֹתָא לַמַּשְׂמְאִילִים (לַלּוֹמְדִים שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ),
which can also become a potion of death to those who turn to the left (learning Torah not for its own sake),
וְנִמְתַּק עַל יְדֵי עֵץ הַחַיִּים
and was sweetened through the Tree of Life;
וְהַיְינוּ קִלְקוּלִים שֶׁבַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה וּבַחָכְמָה
which refers to corruptions residing in thought and intellect.
שֶׁבָּהּ נִשְׁקְעוּ בְּמִצְרַיִם בְּחָכְמַת מִצְרַיִם
in which they had sunk while in Egypt through pagan Egyptian occult philosophies.
וְדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר נִקְרָא דּוֹר דֵּעָה
And the generation of the wilderness was called the Generation of Knowledge,
שֶׁכָּל עֵסֶק וּמַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עִמָּם הָיָה בְּעֵין הַדַּעַת וְהַמַּחֲשָׁבָה לְבַד
whose entire spiritual engagement and interaction with Hashem was judged solely in the refined dimension of knowledge and thought.
וְכָל הָעֳנָשִׁים שֶׁלָּהֶם הָיוּ כְּפִי הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה
and all their severe punishments corresponded strictly to subtle flaws in thought.
וְזֶהוּ רַק לָהֶם מִצַּד מַעֲלָתָם
Yet this applied strictly to them by virtue of their lofty stature,
אֲבָל בְּעָלְמָא קַיְימָא לָן בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּ
whereas for the rest of the world we hold in the first chapter of Kiddushin (40a):
"מַחֲשָׁבָה רָעָה אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְצָרְפָהּ לְמַעֲשֶׂה".
“A bad thought the Holy One, blessed be He, does not combine with action.”,
וְהַמְתָּקַת הַמַּר שֶׁבְּמַעֲשֶׂה וּבַפּוֹעַל לֹא נִתְגַּלָּה עַד שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And the sweetening of the bitterness within physical deed and action was not openly revealed until King Solomon, peace be upon him,
שֶׁיָּדַע הַמְתָּקַת הַתֻּרְמוֹס
– who knew the secret of sweetening the lupine—.
דָּבָר גַּשְׁמִי הָרוֹמֵז לְמַעֲשֶׂה וּפְעֻלָּה גַּשְׁמִית
a physical, material food that alludes to earthly deed and concrete physical action.
וְכָל סֵפֶר מִשְׁלֵי מְיוּסָּד עַל זֶה
And the entire Book of Proverbs is founded upon this principle:
"לָדַעַת חָכְמָה וּמוּסָר וְגוֹמֵר",
“To know wisdom and discipline, etc.” (Proverbs 1:2);
חָכְמָה הוּא הַכָּרָה הַבְּרוּרָה
“wisdom” denotes lucid, unambiguous cognition,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded in Sanhedrin (7b)
עַל פָּסוּק "אֱמֹר לַחָכְמָה אֲחֹתִי אָתְּ":
on the verse (Proverbs 7:4): “Say unto wisdom: You are my sister”:
אִם בָּרוּר לְךָ הַדָּבָר כַּאֲחוֹתְךָ וְכוּלֵי
if the matter is as clearly certain to you as the prohibition of your sister, proclaim it, etc.
וּמוּסָר רָצָה לוֹמַר: הַמְיַסֶּרֶת לָאָדָם וּפוֹעֶלֶת בַּלֵּב לַהֲסִירוֹ מִדֶּרֶךְ רָע עַל יְדֵי זֶה
And “discipline” (mussar) denotes that which rebukes man and acts directly upon the heart to turn him away from the path of evil through it.
לֹא כְּחָכְמָה הַמְּצוּיָה גַּם בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁאֵינָהּ מוּסָר וְאֵין בָּהּ תַּבְלִין לְיֵצֶר הָרָע
unlike that theoretical wisdom found among the nations of the world which contains no moral discipline and provides no seasoning to overcome the evil inclination.
וְאָמַר: "לָתֵת לִפְתָאיִם"
And Scripture says (Proverbs 1:4): “To give to the simple (peta'im)”—
הֵם הַנִּפְתִּים בְּיִצְרָם
who are those seduced by their base inclination.
עָרְמָה", אֵיךְ לְהִנָּצֵל מִמֶּנָּה עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין
“prudence / craftiness,” how to be delivered from it through the Torah which serves as a curative spice.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עָרְמָה שֶׁדּוֹמֶה מַר וְאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִתְמַתֵּק
this being the holy cunning that appears bitter on the surface yet in truth is being sweetened.
וְאָמַר: "יִשְׁמַע חָכָם וְיוֹסֶף לֶקַח",
And Scripture says (Proverbs 1:5): “A wise man will hear, and will increase learning (lekach),”
כִּי הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
for this is the root-source of the wisdom of the Oral Torah.
שֶׁהִיא הוֹלֶכֶת וּמִתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת בְּלֵב חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד אֵין קֵץ
which broadens and expands continuously within the hearts of the sages of Israel without end.
וְכֵן רְפוּאַת הַקּוֹדֵם
And likewise the healing of the past,
עַל יְדֵי הַחָכְמָה וְהַכָּרָה גְּמוּרָה דְּ"אַתָּה עִמָּדִי" וְהַכֹּל מֵאִתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
through wisdom and the complete perception that “You are with me” and all is from Him, blessed be He,
הוּא הַשָּׂגָה חֲלוּקָה בְּמַדְרֵגוֹת הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
is an illumination differentiated according to the individualized rungs of the souls of Israel.
וְעַל כֵּן הִיא מִתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת וּמְקַבֶּלֶת הַתּוֹסֶפֶת כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא רָאוּי לְחָכְמַת כָּל נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִי
and therefore it spreads and receives expansion commensurate with what is appropriate to the unique wisdom of each specific soul.
וְאָמַר בָּזֶה מִלַּת "לֶקַח",
And concerning this Solomon employed the word “lekach” (learning/appropriation),
כְּטַעַם: "וְלָקַחְתִּי אֶתְכֶם לִי לְעָם",
mirroring the verse (Exodus 6:7): “And I will take you to Me for a people,”
שֶׁהַלְּקִיחָה בָּאָדָם הוּא הִשְׁתַּנּוּת הַדֵּעָה וּרְצוֹן הַלֵּב בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ לְגַמְרֵי
for true “taking” within a human being is the total transformation of conscious outlook and the heart’s will at its very foundation,
כְּמוֹ הִשְׁתַּנּוּת עַל יְדֵי לְקִיחָה גַּשְׁמִית שֶׁהוּא הִשְׁתַּנּוּת גָּמוּר
just as the transfer effected through a physical acquisition constitutes a complete, legally binding change of status.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַחָכְמָה פּוֹעֵל הִשְׁתַּנּוּת בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁזֶּהוּ רְפוּאַת הַקּוֹדֵם
and through divine wisdom a person effects a profound transformation at the essential root, which constitutes the true healing of the past.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: With Moshe the sweetening was in water — Torah, which is also “a drug of death” for those who go to its left. The corruptions at issue were of thought and wisdom, in which Israel had sunk in Egypt; sweetening the bitter in deed awaited Shlomo. All of Mishlei is founded on this: chochmah is clear recognition, mussar is what works upon the heart, and this healing is graded to each soul.

sections.en: Great is teshuvah, for it overrides a Torah prohibition

items.h: Great is teshuvah, for it overrides a Torah prohibition
גדולה תשובה שדוחה לא תעשה שבתורה.

p: (א), — גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁדּוֹחָה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
Great is repentance, for it overrides a negative commandment in the Torah,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּתְקַבֶּלֶת וּמוֹעִילָה גַּם כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ בַּמִּשְׁפָּט שֶׁיּוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה
meaning that it is accepted and efficacious even when it is not according to strict legal justice that repentance should avail,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קג עַמּוּד א) בִּמְנַשֶּׁה
and along the lines of that which is taught in Sanhedrin (103a) regarding King Menashe,
שֶׁעָשָׂה לוֹ כְּמִין מַחְתֶּרֶת וְכוּלֵי
that He carved out for him a sort of hidden subterranean breach under the Throne of Glory, etc.
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ בִּפְסָחִים (קיט עַמּוּד א) עַל פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
and similarly in Pesachim (119a) concerning the transgressors of Israel.
וּבָזֶה טָעָה אַחֵר
And regarding this error, Acher (Elisha ben Avuyah) erred,
כְּשֶׁשָּׁמַע אוֹתוֹ בַּת קוֹל כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּ
when he heard that heavenly voice (bat kol) as our Sages recounted in Chagigah (15a);
לֹא יָדַע שֶׁיָּדוֹ כִּבְיָכוֹל פְּשׁוּטָה לְקַבֵּל הַשָּׁבִים
he did not comprehend that His hand, as it were, is outstretched to welcome the penitent.
אַף נֶגֶד שׁוּרַת הַדִּין
even in direct contravention of the strict measure of the law.
וְכָל עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים הַמְּעַכְּבִים הַתְּשׁוּבָה
And all twenty-four matters that impede repentance
אֵין מוֹנְעִין לְקַבֵּל לְגַמְרֵי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם
do not absolutely block reception forever, as Maimonides (Rambam) wrote,
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר עוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה
for in truth, nothing can stand in the path of repentance;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה אֵין לְקַבְּלָהּ,
and even though according to the strict juridical code of the Torah one ought not to receive it.
זֶהוּ גְּדוּלָּתָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁפּוֹרֶצֶת גֶּדֶר דִּין הַתּוֹרָה
this is the very grandeur of repentance: that it breaches the strict perimeter of the Torah's legal sentence.
וּבְעִיקַּר קַבָּלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה אָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי (פֶּרֶק ב דְּמַכּוֹת, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּיָפֶה מַרְאֶה הַגִּירְסָא):
And concerning the fundamental acceptance of repentance, they taught in the Jerusalem Talmud (Makkot, ch. 2, see there in Yafeh Mareh for the textual reading):
שָׁאֲלוּ לַחָכְמָה וְכוּלֵי, לַתּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי, לַנְּבוּאָה וְכוּלֵי
They asked Wisdom, etc. they asked the Torah, etc. they asked Prophecy, etc.
עַד לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, אָמַר יַעֲשֶׂה תְּשׁוּבָה
until they reached the Holy One, blessed be He, Who answered: Let him do teshuva and be atoned.
וּשְׁלֹשֶׁת אֵלּוּ עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ג עַמּוּד ב):
And these three correspond to what our Sages said in Berakhot (3b):
יוֹעֲצִין בַּאֲחִיתֹפֶל, וְנִמְלָכִין בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין, וְשׁוֹאֲלִין בְּאוּרִים וְתוּמִים
They consult with Achitophel, take counsel with the Sanhedrin, and inquire of the Urim VeTumim.
שֶׁהֵם חָכְמָה, תּוֹרָה, וּנְבוּאָה כִּמְבוֹאָר
which correspond precisely to Wisdom, Torah, and Prophecy, as elucidated.
וְשָׁלֹשׁ עֵצוֹת אֵלּוּ צָרִיךְ לְכָל דָּבָר
And these three counsels are needed for every single undertaking.
וְאָמַר "שָׁאֲלוּ" וְלֹא אָמַר מִי הַשּׁוֹאֵל
And the Midrash stated 'they asked' without specifying who was asking,
רַק רָצָה לוֹמַר כִּי הַתְחָלַת כָּל דָּבָר עַל כָּרְחֲךָ הוּא נִשְׁאָל וְנִמְלָךְ לִפְנֵי שְׁלֹשֶׁת יוֹעֲצִים אֵלּוּ אֵיךְ יַעֲשֶׂה
meaning to indicate that perforce the inception of any matter is deliberated and inquired before these three counselors as to how to proceed.
שֶׁיֶּשְׁנָם בִּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
which exist within the collective nation of Israel.
וְכֵן הֵם בְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִית גַּם כֵּן
And likewise, they are present within every individual soul as well:
שָׁלֹשׁ דַּרְכֵי הִתְבּוֹנְנוּת הַלָּלוּ בְּכָל דָּבָר
these three distinct modes of contemplation in every matter:
מִצַּד חָכְמָה אֱנוֹשִׁית, וְחָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה, וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
from the vantage point of human wisdom, the wisdom of the Torah, and the Holy Spirit,
דְּהַיְינוּ הַשָּׂגַת חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּנְבוּאָה אוֹ אוּרִים וְתוּמִים וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ.
which is the spiritual perception of the sages of Israel through prophecy, Urim VeTumim, or divine inspiration.
וּשְׁלֹשֶׁת אֵלּוּ הֵם יוֹעֲצִים וּמַנְהִיגִים כָּל דָּבָר בַּעֲצָתָם
And these three act as counselors, directing every human affair through their guidance.
וְהַתְּשׁוּבָה הִיא לְמַעְלָה מֵהֶם
Yet repentance transcends them all,
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲמוֹד עָלֶיהָ בְּשׁוּם עֵצָה אֱנוֹשִׁית
so that it is impossible to fathom its inner mechanism by any human intellect,
אֲפִילּוּ נְבוּאָה דְּהוּא הַשָּׂגַת אָדָם מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
even through prophecy, which represents mortal perception received from the Blessed Creator.
וְכֵן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
And likewise the Torah, though originating directly from Heaven,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מֵאַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר נִמְסְרָה לִבְנֵי אָדָם וְלֹא בַּשָּׁמַיִם הִיא
nevertheless, since it has already been transmitted to mortal beings and 'is not in heaven,'.
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲמוֹד מִצִּידָּהּ גַּם כֵּן עַל עֹמֶק מַעֲלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה
it is likewise impossible to comprehend the profound depth of the virtue of repentance from its bounded perspective alone.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 86b: “R’ Yochanan said: Great is teshuvah, for it overrides a negative commandment of the Torah, as it says, ‘Saying: if a man sends away his wife and she goes from him and becomes another man’s, shall he return to her again? Would not that land be utterly defiled? Yet you have played the harlot with many companions; and return to Me, says Hashem’ (Yirmeyah 3:1)” — though a remarried divorcée is forbidden to return to her first husband, God says “return to Me.” R’ Tzadok: teshuvah avails even where the Torah’s own law would bar it. Maharal, Netivos Olam, Netiv HaTeshuvah ch. 2 (§13 in Sefaria's segmentation), comments on these two statements of R' Yochanan together: "גדולה תשובה שמגעת עד כסא הכבוד" and "גדולה תשובה שדוחה את לא תעשה שבתורה." Their juxtaposition is conceptually exact. The Torah's prohibition marks the order appropriate to a world in which a broken marital bond cannot simply be restored after a second union. Teshuvah, however, reaches the Kisei HaKavod — the source above the ordinary created order — and therefore the prophetic "ושובו אלי" can disclose a relationship whose possibility cannot be generated by the legal structure alone. This does not mean halachah is suspended for human beings; the divorced wife remains prohibited by Torah law. Rather, the mashal teaches the transcendent nature of the Divine reception of teshuvah: Hashem can restore the sinner to a closeness that the finite legal analogy would declare irrecoverable. Maharal, Netivos Olam, Netiv HaTeshuvah ch. 2, §§13–14, discusses R’ Levi’s teaching about reaching the Throne of Glory together with R’ Yochanan’s teaching about overriding the Torah prohibition. He explains: “התשובה הוא שחוזר אל התחלתו, והתחלת האדם מן תחת כסא, כי משם הנשמה חצובה” — “Repentance means returning to one’s beginning, and a person’s beginning is beneath the Throne, for the soul is hewn from there.” He then distinguishes the individual from the community: an individual’s repentance reaches the Throne, whereas the community’s greater removal from sin reaches “עד השם יתברך — עד ועד בכלל” — “to Hashem Himself — up to and including.” The comparison illuminates repentance’s return to a source beyond its present damaged form. The prohibition on a remarried divorcée remains binding; the prophetic analogy describes Divine reception of repentance.

This supplies a THEMATIC comparison for his present discussion of Menasheh’s accepted teshuvah, while Sanhedrin 103a remains the direct source for the homily about God making a “tunnel” to receive him. The two passages should not be conflated into one quotation.  —  Source: Yisrael Kedoshim 8:9
