paragraphs.text:
Sanhedrin 103a: Menasheh did teshuvah. The biblical wording is “vayei’ater lo” — “He accepted his entreaty”; “va-yeichater lo” is the Gemara’s homiletical reading of the verse in Divrei HaYamim II 33:13, teaching that the Holy One made for him a kind of tunnel machteres in the firmament, to receive him in teshuvah, past the Attribute of Justice. Pesachim 119a: “‘the hands of a man beneath their wings’ (Yechezkel 1:8) — it is written yado His hand, the hand of the Holy One spread beneath the wings of the chayos, to receive penitents from the hand of the Attribute of Justice.” Chagigah 15a: after Acher sinned, a bas kol announced “‘Return, wayward children’ — except for Acher”; hearing this, he despaired of being received, and gave himself over to sin. R’ Tzadok: Acher failed to grasp that the “hand” receives even against the strict law. The Ishbitzer's reading of Menasheh gives a remarkable inner background to the "machteres." Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Prophets, II Kings 21:1, says Menasheh was born with an overwhelming yirah that human strength could scarcely bear. His sin, in the Izhbitzer's formulation, began from seeking ways to remove that overpowering awe "בכדי שיהיה בעל בחירה" — so that he would possess a felt field of choice — because the intensity of the yirah seemed to take choice away from him. Whether or not one translates every detail of this daring teaching into R' Tzadok's system, its relevance is clear: Menasheh's corruption is not treated as proof that no holy root existed. The very point that became distorted had an original holy form.

That makes the tunnel beneath the Kisei especially meaningful. Teshuvah does not merely negotiate with the externally visible record of Menasheh's reign; it reaches beneath it to the buried root from which even the distorted search for "bechirah" had emerged. The Middas HaDin, judging the acts in their revealed form, has no argument for such a return. The Holy One "digs" beneath that plane and receives the soul from its deeper source. This is a characteristically Ishbitz-Radzin way of understanding why even the architect of the churban can become a baal teshuvah: the shoresh and the revealed history are not identical.

paragraphs.text: Yerushalmi Makkos 2:6: The standard text (Yerushalmi Makkos 2:6:9) asks Wisdom, Prophecy, and the Holy One what should happen to the sinner. Wisdom answers that evil pursues sinners; Prophecy answers that the soul which sins shall die; the Holy One answers that the person should repent and be forgiven. It does not include a separate question to the Torah. An expanded version in Pesikta DeRav Kahana 24:7 does ask the Torah, whose answer is to bring a guilt-offering and receive atonement. Rav Tzadok also refers to Yefeh Mar’eh for a textual version that includes the additional Torah question; the expanded wording must not be quoted as the standard Yerushalmi text.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Sichas Malachei HaShareis §2): On the Yerushalmi (Makkos ch. 2) — “they asked the Torah… they asked the Holy One, and He said, ‘let him do teshuvah’” — R’ Tzadok explains: “by the measure of the Torah and chochmah, through the sin a blemish has been made in his soul, and with what shall that blemish be atoned? It requires something that atones. But by the measure of the Holy One — who alludes to the perfect Unity, the clear sensation that ‘Hashem is One’ and that He ‘fills the whole earth with His glory,’ with nothing else here at all — teshuvah itself suffices.” This is exactly §3-1’s “overriding a prohibition of the Torah”: Torah and wisdom must reckon a residue that demands payment, but from the vantage of God’s own Oneness the sinner simply returns — teshuvah is the remedy above the Torah’s own accounting.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: “Overriding a Torah prohibition” means teshuvah is accepted even where, by strict law, it should not avail — as with Menasheh, for whom God burrowed a tunnel beneath His Throne. Acher erred exactly here, not grasping that God’s hand is stretched out to receive penitents even against the line of the law. In the Yerushalmi, Wisdom, Torah and Prophecy were each asked the sinner’s remedy, and only the Holy One answered “let him do teshuvah” — for teshuvah stands above all three.

p: (ב) — וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא בִּבְרָכוֹת (לד עַמּוּד ב):
And along the lines of that which is taught in Berakhot (34b):
מְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין אֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים יְכוֹלִין לַעֲמוֹד
In the place where penitents stand, even the completely righteous cannot stand,
כִּי מְקוֹם הַצַּדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים הוּא הַמַּגִּיעַ לָהֶם כְּפִי מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם
for the spiritual station of the completely righteous is that which is accorded to them strictly commensurate with their deeds,
שֶׁהוּא עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה וְהַנְּבוּאָה וְהַחָכְמָה וְלֹא יָצְאוּ מִגִּדְרָם
which is bounded by the parameters of the Torah, Prophecy, and Wisdom, never having deviated from their ordained perimeter:
וְהֵם בַּעֲלֵי גֶּדֶר וּגְבוּל
and they are people oriented around borders and demarcations:
אֶת זֶה תַּעֲשֶׂה וְזֶה לֹא, וְעַד פֹּה תָבוֹא וְלֹא תוֹסִיף
this you shall do and this you shall not do; thus far shall you come and no further.
אֲבָל בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה הוּא שֶׁכְּבָר פָּרַץ גִּדְרוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַנִּגְדָּר עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה וְהַנְּבִיאִים וְהַחֲכָמִים
However, the penitent is one who has already ruptured the moral boundaries of the world constructed by the Torah, the Prophets, and the Sages.
וְנִשְׁקַע בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁנִּשְׁקַע
and sank into whatever dark abyss he sank into.
וּכְשֶׁחוֹזֵר לָשׁוּב אֶל ה' וּלְתַקֵּן הַקּוֹדֵם בְּהַכָּרָה בְּרוּרָה דְּ"אַתָּה עִמָּדִי",
And when he turns back to return to Hashem and rectify his past through the lucid awareness that 'You are with me,'
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ,
and that in whatever spiritual condition he finds himself, there is none besides Him,
זוֹכֶה לְנַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
he merits the boundless inheritance of our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהוּא נַחֲלָה בְּלֹא מְצָרִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קיח עַמּוּד ב),
which is a heritage without borders, as our Sages stated in Shabbat (118b).
וְזֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דִּילֵיהּ שֶׁהָיְתָה מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה
and this was his unique spiritual level: that his bed was whole, entirely devoid of spiritual blemishes.
דְּיִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, אַף שֶׁכְּבָר הָיָה מְתוּקָּן מִשָּׁרְשׁוֹ,
For Isaac our father, peace be upon him, although thoroughly rectified from his supernal root,
וְאַף עֵשָׂו הַנּוֹלָד מִמֶּנּוּ נִקְרָא בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּ "יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר",
and even Esau who descended from him is initially termed in the first chapter of Kiddushin (18a) 'an apostate Israelite',
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּבָר הָיָה יָכוֹל לְהַמִּיר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמֶּנּוּ
nonetheless, he was ultimately able to strip the identity of Israel from himself,
וְלִהְיוֹת כְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם וְעוֹד גָּרוּעַ מֵהֶם
and become like all other nations, and even worse than them,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (עֹבַדְיָה א, ב): "קָטֹן נְתַתִּיךָ בַּגּוֹיִם בָּזוּי מְאֹד",
as it is written (Obadiah 1:2): 'Behold, I have made you small among the nations; you are greatly despised,'
דְּמַה שֶּׁהַנָּבִיא קוֹרֵא קָטָן וּבָזוּי אֵינוֹ מִצַּד הַחֲשִׁיבוּת בְּעֵינֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם
for when the prophet terms someone small and despised, it is not evaluated by mortal social esteem.
רַק מִצַּד אֲמִיתַּת עִנְיָנָם
rather from the perspective of their essential spiritual reality.
וְזֶהוּ הַפְּסֹלֶת שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ,
And this was the spiritual dross that was cast out from him;
כִּי מִצַּד מִדַּת הַצִּמְצוּם יֵשׁ גְּבוּל וְגֶדֶר
for from the side of the attribute of divine contraction (Tzimtzum) there exist limits and borders.
וּמִסִּטְרָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא הַמְגַדֶּרֶת הָאָדָם בְּפִקּוּדִין דַּעֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
and from the side of the Torah, which hedges man around with positive and negative commandments.
וְאַף הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁהִיא אַחַת מִמִּצְווֹת הַתּוֹרָה הִיא מְצוּמְצֶמֶת בִּגְבוּל
And even repentance, when considered one of the specific commandments of the Torah, is restricted within boundaries.
שֶׁלֹּא יוֹעִיל חוּץ מֵאוֹתוֹ גְּבוּל
such that it does not avail beyond that circumscribed limit.
וְכֵן שׁוֹרֶשׁ טוֹב בְּתוֹלָדָה שֶׁזָּכָה לוֹ יִצְחָק
And likewise, the root of goodness from birth that Isaac attained,
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ עִנְיַן יִשְׂרָאֵל, הוּא מוּגְבָּל בִּגְבוּל
which is the primal root of the Israelite essence, is circumscribed by boundary,
וְאִם יִפְרוֹץ גֶּדֶר וּגְבוּל זֶה
and if one breaches this fence and border.
הֲרֵי זֶה נֶעֱקָר מִשֵּׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנַעֲשֶׂה כְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם
he is uprooted from the name of Israel and becomes like all other gentiles.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הִיא בְּלֹא מְצָרִים
In contrast, the spiritual heritage of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, is boundless,
שֶׁאֵין שָׁם גְּבוּל הַמַּגְדִּיר כְּלָל
harboring no defining restriction whatsoever;
וַאֲפִילּוּ הִגְדִּיל מֵאָה עֲווֹנוֹת זֶה לְמַעְלָה מִזֶּה
and even if a person piles up a hundred sins one atop another,
לֹא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמֶּנּוּ לְכָל דָּבָר
the name of Israel is never completely uprooted from him in any halachic respect,
דְּקִדּוּשָׁיו קִדּוּשִׁין וְגִטּוֹ גֵּט כַּיָּדוּעַ.
for his betrothal remains valid and his bill of divorce remains effective, as is known.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (מד עַמּוּד א):
And as our Sages stated in Sanhedrin (44a):
"אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא – יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא",
'Even though he has sinned, he remains Israel,'
דְּזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְנַתֵּק וְלַעֲקוֹר מִזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
for it is impossible to sever or uproot from the offspring of Jacob our father, peace be upon him.
הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מִיַּעֲקֹב שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ פְּסֹלֶת כְּלָל
that inner essence deriving from Jacob, which contains no dross whatsoever.
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת נִפְסָל וְנֶעֱקָר עַל יְדֵי שׁוּם דָּבָר
And it is impossible for him to be invalidated or uprooted by anything.
מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה דָּבָר הַמַּגְבִּיל כְּלָל
since there is no limiting factor that can constrain this root.

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 18a (first chapter): R’ Chiya bar Avin said in the name of R’ Yochanan that a gentile inherits from his father by Torah law, “for it is written, ‘I have given Mount Se’ir to Esav as an inheritance’ (Devarim 2:5)”; the Gemara objects, “ve-dilma Yisrael meshumad shani? — but perhaps an apostate Jew is different,” i.e. Esav was no gentile at all but an apostate Jew, so his inheriting proves nothing about gentiles (the point is instead proven from the descendants of Lot). The objection reads “וְדִלְמָא יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשׁוּמָּד שָׁאנֵי?” — “But perhaps an apostate Israelite is different?” R’ Tzadok cites Esav’s classification at the Yitzchak stage and then distinguishes it from the root inherited through Yaakov: the former is still described here as bounded and capable of being uprooted, whereas the latter cannot be severed by any sin. For the halachic survival of Israelite status after apostasy, compare Yevamos 47b: “יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשׁוּמָּד קָרֵינָא בֵּיהּ, וְקִידּוּשָׁיו קִידּוּשִׁין” — “We call him an apostate Israelite, and his betrothals are valid.” The author’s statement about valid betrothal and divorce belongs to this indestructible Yaakov root, expressed by Sanhedrin 44a: “even though he has sinned, he is still Israel.”

Berachos 34b: R’ Abbahu taught, “in the place where baalei teshuvah stand, the wholly righteous do not stand,” deriving it from “peace, peace to the far and to the near” (Yeshayah 57:19) — peace is extended first to “the far one” (the penitent) and only afterward to “the near one” (the ever-righteous). This follows the discussion there of R’ Yochanan, “all the prophets prophesied only for baalei teshuvah, but of the wholly righteous it is said ‘no eye has seen’” — though R’ Yochanan himself reads the verse oppositely (the “far one” is the tzaddik, ever-distant from sin; the “near one” is the penitent, once near to sin). R’ Tzadok builds on R’ Abbahu: the “place” of the wholly righteous is bounded — what accrues to them by their deeds, measured by Torah, prophecy, and wisdom, and they never left their bounds — whereas the baal teshuvah, having breached the fence and returned, reaches the boundless “inheritance of Yaakov,” where the “masters of limit” cannot stand. Sefas Emes repeatedly explains "במקום שבעלי תשובה עומדין" as access to a new path drawn from above the ordinary order. In Pekudei 12:3 he writes that after the sin and teshuvah, "ע"י תשובה נתקן דרך חדש" — through teshuvah a new way was repaired — and that baalei teshuvah have a share in the derech of the future. In Acharei Mos 19:2, the entrance "lifnai ve-lifnim" on Yom Kippur becomes the image of the same principle: a gate from the upper world is opened specifically for baalei teshuvah. And in Vayishlach 13:3 he connects the ma'amar directly to "teshuvah reaches the Kisei HaKavod," describing teshuvah as return to the point from which the person's future good is destined to grow.

These passages deepen R' Tzadok's language of "place." The baal teshuvah does not simply receive a larger reward than the tzaddik for the same route. His fall and return open a derech chadash — a route that did not exist within the bounded map of his earlier avodah. That is why the tzaddik gamur cannot "stand" there: it is not a higher rung on the tzaddik's unchanged ladder but a place generated by the movement of return itself.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: “In the place where baalei teshuvah stand, the completely righteous cannot stand.” The righteous never left their bounds — they are masters of fence and border; the baal teshuvah has already breached the world’s fence and returned from where he sank. Rectifying the past with the clear recognition of “You are with me,” he merits the inheritance of Yaakov — an inheritance without borders, a root that nothing can sever.

p: (ג), — וְדַרְגָּא זוֹ דִּתְשׁוּבָה שֶׁמִּצִּידּוֹ, הַפּוֹרֶצֶת וְדוֹחָה כָּל גְּבוּלֵי הַתּוֹרָה
And this spiritual level of repentance stemming from his vantage point, which breaches and transcends all statutory boundaries of the Torah,
הוּא הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁאֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים בַּעֲלֵי גְּבוּל יְכוֹלִין לַעֲמוֹד בּוֹ,
is the very locus where completely righteous individuals, whose lives are framed by borders, cannot stand.
כִּי כֹּחַ הַצִּמְצוּם וְהַמַּגְבִּיל הוּא הֵיפֶךְ כֹּחַ הַבִּלְתִּי בַּעַל גְּבוּל
because the faculty of contraction and delimitation is the polar opposite of the boundless divine power.
כִּי מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא נֶגֶד שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה
For the attribute of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, corresponds to the ineffable Name Havayah,
שֶׁהוּא הַמָּקוֹר שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִתְפָּס בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל
which is the primordial Source that cannot be apprehended within this physical world at all,
דְּעַל כֵּן אֵינוֹ נֶהֱגֶה
which is why it is not pronounced as written;
כִּי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא בִּגְבוּל
because this world is governed by boundaries,
וְהַשָּׂגָה זוֹ הוּא בְּלֹא גְּבוּל
whereas this spiritual comprehension is entirely without boundaries.
דְּכָךְ מַשְׁמָעוּתוֹ: שֶׁהָיָה, הֹוֶה, וְיִהְיֶה בְּלֹא רֵאשִׁית וְלֹא תַכְלִית
for such is its meaning: He was, is, and will be without beginning and without end.
וּמִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, גַּם דִּבְרֵי הַמַּאן דְּאָמַר שָׁם דְּ"כָל הַנְּבִיאִים לֹא נִתְנַבְּאוּ אֶלָּא לְבַעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵי" הוּא אֱמֶת
And from the perspective of this world, the opinion of that sage who maintains there that 'all the prophets prophesied only concerning penitents, etc.' is also true.
דְּאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים
for 'both these and those are the words of the living God.',
וּמִצַּד הַהַשָּׂגָה הַמּוּשֶּׂגֶת לַנְּבִיאִים, מַדְרֵגַת הַבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה פְּחוּתָה מִצַּדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים
And from the perspective of the prophetic perception attainable by prophets, the level of penitents is inferior to completely righteous people,
כִּי דַּרְגָּא זוֹ דִּתְשׁוּבָה אֵינוֹ מוּשָּׂג מִצַּד הַנְּבוּאָה כְּלָל
because this higher dimension of repentance cannot be comprehended through prophecy at all,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר שָׁם רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן עַצְמוֹ:
just as Rabbi Yochanan himself stated there:
כָּל הַנְּבִיאִים לֹא נִתְנַבְּאוּ אֶלָּא לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ,
All the prophets prophesied only regarding the days of the Messiah,
אֲבָל לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא וְכוּלֵי, "עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה אֱלֹהִים זוּלָתְךָ" וְגוֹמֵר
but regarding the World to Come, 'no eye has seen, O God, beside You, etc.',
וְזֶהוּ מַדְרֵגַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁשָּׁאֲלוּ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ.
and this corresponds to the supreme level of repentance that they asked of the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself.
וְהַפְּלוּגְתָּא הִיא רַק בְּעִנְיַן תְּפִיסַת וְהַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבִיאִים
And their dispute concerns solely the grasp and perceptual framework of the prophets,
וְגַם בָּזֶה דִּבְרֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת
and in this too the words of both are truth,
כִּי מִצַּד מִשְׁפַּט הַנְּבוּאָה הַמּוּשָּׂג בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין זֶה מוּשָּׂג
for according to the prophetic standard accessible in this world, this dimension cannot be apprehended,
דְּהַשָּׂגַת עוֹלָם הַבָּא "עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה",
since the comprehension of the World to Come is beyond what 'any eye has seen',
אֲבָל זֶהוּ דֶּרֶךְ רְאִיַּת עַיִן
yet this limitation applies specifically to visual perception.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַשָּׂגַת נְבוּאָה אֲשֶׁר יִקָּרֵא לְפָנִים "הָרוֹאֶה", שֶׁהוּא כְּרוֹאֶה בָּעַיִן
which is the nature of prophecy, whose practitioner was formerly called 'the seer,' being like one who beholds with the eye.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַשָּׂגָה דֶּרֶךְ חָכְמָה וַהֲבָנָה
In contrast, perception that comes through wisdom and abstract comprehension
יְכוֹלִים לְהַשִּׂיג גַּם מַה שֶּׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵשִׁיב
can comprehend both what the Holy One, blessed be He, answers,
וְגַם מַה שֶּׁיִּהְיֶה לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
and what will transpire in the World to Come,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁגִּילּוּ לָנוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה מִזֶּה דְּבָרִים הַרְבֵּה
as our Sages of blessed memory revealed to us regarding this in numerous teachings,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא דֶּרֶךְ הַשָּׂגָה נֶעְלֶמֶת מַה שֶּׁיִּהְיֶה
only that it is perceived through an intuitive, concealed mode of apprehension regarding what will be.
וְלֹא בְּרוֹאֶה בָּעַיִן מַה שֶּׁלְּנוֹכַח עֵינָיו
and not as one seeing tangibly with the eye that which stands directly before him.
וּלְאִידָךְ מַאן דְּאָמַר (רַבִּי אַבָּהוּ)
And according to the other authority (Rabbi Abbahu),
נִמְצָא גַּם הַשָּׂגָה כָּזוֹ בַּנְּבִיאִים
such a profound mode of perception was also found among the prophets;
אֲבָל גּוּף הָעִנְיָן עַצְמוֹ הַכֹּל דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים
yet regarding the substantive essence of the matter itself, everything is the words of the living God,
וְאֵין מַחֲלוֹקֶת כְּלָל
and there is no disagreement at all.
וְאָנוּ דָּנִין בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַכֹּל כְּמִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה
and in this world, we adjudicate all matters strictly in accordance with the law of the Torah.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §8): “…whereas the baal teshuvah breaches every kind of boundary poretz kol minei hagdaros, and in a single hour, in one instant, he can acquire his entire world — and more, they call him ‘Rabbi,’ as with R’ Elazar ben Durdaya (Avodah Zarah 17a).” This is §3-3’s very claim that teshuvah “from its own side breaches and overrides all the boundaries of the Torah”: the tzaddik, “master of limit,” acquires his portion measure by measure, but the penitent’s power is limitless — it bursts every bound and wins the world “in one instant,” a place where the bounded righteous cannot stand.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §7): “‘In the place where baalei teshuvah stand, the completely righteous cannot stand’ (Berachos 34b) — and through the sin, when he afterward merits teshuvah, he reaches a greater level than before.” R’ Tzadok makes explicit why the baal teshuvah’s place exceeds the tzaddik’s in §3-2: it is the sin itself, once returned upon, that carries him past the fixed bounds of the righteous — the fall becomes the very rung on which he now stands higher, in the “inheritance without borders.”

paragraphs.text: Yeshayah 64:3: “וּמֵעוֹלָם לֹא שָׁמְעוּ לֹא הֶאֱזִינוּ, עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה אֱלֹקִים זוּלָתְךָ, יַעֲשֶׂה לִמְחַכֵּה לוֹ” — “From of old none has heard, none has given ear; no eye has seen a God besides You, who acts for the one who waits for Him” — from Yeshayah’s plea for redemption (ch. 63–64). Rashi gives both the plain sense — no other people’s god ever did for its devotees what You do for those who hope in You — and the reading of the Sages (Berachos 34b): “no prophet’s eye has seen what the Holy One will do for the one who waits for Him, except Your eyes, O God” — the reward of the World to Come lies beyond all prophetic vision. R’ Tzadok uses this distinction to explain R’ Yochanan’s judgment from the perspective of prophetic apprehension in this world. He then distinguishes it from concealed intellectual apprehension: “הַשָּׂגָה נֶעְלֶמֶת ... וְלֹא בְּרוֹאֶה בָּעַיִן” — “a concealed apprehension ... rather than seeing with the eye.” Such understanding can apprehend even what will be in the World to Come. R’ Abbahu holds that this mode is found among prophets too; the dispute concerns their mode of apprehension, while the reality itself is not disputed.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 34b: “R’ Chiya bar Abba said in the name of R’ Yochanan: All the prophets prophesied only for the days of Mashiach, but of the World to Come, ‘no eye has seen a God besides You’ (Yeshayah 64:3). And R’ Chiya bar Abba said in the name of R’ Yochanan: All the prophets prophesied only for baalei teshuvah, but of the completely righteous, ‘no eye has seen a God besides You’ — and this disputes R’ Abbahu, who said, ‘in the place where baalei teshuvah stand, the completely righteous do not stand.’” R’ Tzadok distinguishes the visible mode of prophecy from concealed understanding, which can apprehend even what will be in the World to Come. R’ Yochanan’s judgment concerns the former mode; R’ Abbahu holds that the latter is found among prophets too. paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Likkutei Maamarim, Chodashim u-Moadim §9): in explaining Shabbos as a gift beyond one’s labor, he invokes “a king breaches a fence and none may protest” (Yevamos 76b) and Amatzyah’s words, “הַלְיוֹעֵץ לַמֶּלֶךְ נְתַנּוּךָ” — “Have we appointed you a counselor to the king?” He immediately qualifies the gift: “מצד עולם הזה הרי צריך הגדרה בשבת בלא תעשה ועשה דזכור ושמור” — “From the perspective of this world, Shabbos still requires limitation through the negative and positive commands of ‘Remember’ and ‘Guard.’” This illuminates the author’s two levels here: repentance reaches beyond finite boundaries, while our conduct in this world is judged according to Torah law.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: This rung breaches every boundary of the Torah, and therefore the “masters of limit” cannot stand in it — for contraction is the opposite of the limitless. It answers to the Name that is not grasped in this world at all, and so it is not apprehended by prophecy either. Hence the view that the prophets prophesied only for baalei teshuvah; the dispute concerns the prophets’ grasp, and both are the words of the living God.

p: (ד), — וְהִנֵּה עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה, אַף דְּהִיא וְכָל הַנְּבִיאִים הִזְהִירוּ עַל הַתְּשׁוּבָה
And behold, according to the Torah, although it and all the prophets urgently admonished regarding repentance,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין זֶה מוֹעִיל לְבַטֵּל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
nevertheless, this does not operate to overturn the codified rulings of the Torah.
דְּהַיְינוּ לִפְטוֹר מִמִּיתַת בֵּית דִּין וּמַלְקוּת בְּמֵזִיד וְקָרְבָּן בְּשׁוֹגֵג
namely to exempt an intentional offender from judicial execution by court or lashes, or an inadvertent sinner from a sin-offering.
אֲפִילּוּ שָׁב בְּכָל לִבּוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת
Even if he repented with all his heart in complete sincerity,
(וְלֹא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ קְצָת אַחֲרוֹנִים בָּזֶה מֵחֲשַׁשׁ רַמָּאוּת וְשֶׁלֹּא שָׁב בֶּאֱמֶת)
and not as some later commentators suggested, that court penalties persist merely out of suspicion of deception and insincerity,
לֹא נִפְטַר מִמִּשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה
he is not exempted from the Torah's legal sentence.
שֶׁמִּצַּד מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה אֵין הַתְּשׁוּבָה מוֹעֶלֶת לִפְטוֹרוֹ מִמִּשְׁפָּטָהּ עַל אוֹתוֹ עָווֹן
because from the perspective of the Torah's jurisprudence, repentance is not halachically effective in absolving him of its sentence for that specific transgression.
וַאֲפִילּוּ בָּעֳנָשִׁים שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שָׁנִינוּ בְּיוֹמָא (פו עַמּוּד א) — אַרְבַּע חִלּוּקֵי כַּפָּרָה
And even with respect to celestial punishments inflicted in this world, we learned in Yoma (86a) the four divisions of atonement,
וְעָבַר עַל כְּרֵיתוֹת וּמִיתַת בֵּית דִּין אֲפִילּוּ תְּשׁוּבָה עִם יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים אֵין מְהַנֵּי לִפְטוֹרוֹ לְגַמְרֵי
such that if one transgressed sins incurring spiritual excision (karet) or capital execution, even repentance combined with Yom Kippur does not suffice to release him entirely.
וְצָרִיךְ גַּם כֵּן לְיִסּוּרִין מְמָרְקִין הָעֹנֶשׁ דְּכָרֵת וּמִיתָה
and he furthermore requires afflictions to scour away the sentence of excision and death.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אַחַר הַמִּיתָה מִתְמָרֵק לְגַמְרֵי בְּכֹחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה
Nonetheless, after bodily death everything is entirely scoured and atoned for through the power of repentance.
אֲפִילּוּ עֲווֹן חִלּוּל הַשֵּׁם הֶחָמוּר מִכּוּלָּם
even the sin of desecrating the Divine Name (chillul Hashem), the gravest of all.
דְּכָל מַה שֶּׁאֵין תְּשׁוּבָה מוֹעִילָה לְמָרֵק לְגַמְרֵי הוּא רַק מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
For all that repentance does not fully cleanse is strictly from the perspective of this earthly world.
דִּתְשׁוּבָה הוּא מִכֹּחַ הַבִּינָה
For repentance derives from the supernal faculty of Binah (Understanding),
דְּ"לְבָבוֹ יָבִין וְשָׁב",
as in the verse 'and his heart understands, and he returns,'
שֶׁהוּא סוֹד עָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי (הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא) כַּנּוֹדָע
which is the mystical secret of the World to Come, as is known;
וּמִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל גְּבוּל וְתַכְלִית גַּם לַתְּשׁוּבָה יֵשׁ גְּבוּל מַה בְּכֹחָהּ לְמָרֵק
and from the perspective of this physical world, which is bounded and finite, repentance too has a functional boundary as to what it can cleanse,
וְהַחֲמוּרוֹת אֵינָהּ מְמָרֶקֶת עֲדַיִן
so that the severe sins it does not scour immediately;
אֲבָל אַחַר הַמִּיתָה בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא אֵין עוֹד שׁוּם עֹנֶשׁ מִשֶּׁשָּׁב
yet after physical death, in the World to Come, there is no punishment whatsoever for one who has repented.
אֲפִילּוּ הַחֲמוּרָה שֶׁבַּחֲמוּרוֹת
even for the most severe of all transgressions.
וְכֵן מִצַּד הַנְּבוּאָה דְּהֵשִׁיבָה "הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַחֹטֵאת הִיא תָמוּת",
And likewise from the perspective of Prophecy, which replied 'The soul that sins, it shall die,'
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִשֶּׁמֵּת נִתְכַּפֵּר לוֹ מִיהַת
nonetheless, once the sinner has died, he is at least atoned for,
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין נִגְאֶלֶת וְנִצֶּלֶת מִן הַמִּיתָה
except that the soul is not redeemed or spared from death itself.
כְּטַעַם: וְכִי הַנְּבִיאִים לְעוֹלָם יִחְיוּ?
mirroring the challenge: 'And do the prophets live forever?'.
דְּנֶגֶד כָּל הָעֳנָשִׁים יֵשׁ פְּדוּת לַנְּבִיאִים עַל פִּי כֹּחַ הַנְּבוּאָה וּמִשְׁפָּטָהּ לְהַצִּיל מִיִּסּוּרִין מְמָרְקִין
For against ordinary punishments, prophets possess redemption via the power and law of prophecy to deliver a penitent from scouring afflictions.
כִּי מַדְרֵגַת הַנְּבוּאָה הוּא תַּכְלִית הַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכַח דְּ"אַתָּה עִמָּדִי",
Because the spiritual attainment of prophecy represents the pinnacle of direct second-person awareness that 'You are with me,'
עַד כִּי רוּחַ ה' דִּבֶּר בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ לוֹמַר "כֹּה אָמַר ה
'", to the extent that the spirit of Hashem literally speaks through him to pronounce 'Thus said the Lord,'.
שֶׁזּוֹ הַכָּרָה גְּלוּיָה יוֹתֵר מֵהַהַכָּרָה שֶׁעַל פִּי חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה
which is a far more tangible, explicit perception than that derived through the wisdom of the Torah.
דְּאַף דְּ"חָכָם עָדִיף מִנָּבִיא" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (יב עַמּוּד א),
For although 'a sage is superior to a prophet' as our Sages stated in Bava Batra (12a),
הַיְינוּ מִצַּד הָעֹמֶק
that applies specifically regarding conceptual depth.
אֲבָל גִּלּוּי וּרְאִיָּה חוּשִׁית הוּא אֵצֶל הַנָּבִיא יוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל
yet vivid disclosure and tangible sensory vision are far greater in the prophet.
וְעִיקַּר תִּיקּוּן הַקּוֹדֵם הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַגִּלּוּי הַבָּרוּר דְּ"אַתָּה עִמָּדִי",
And the primary rectification of the past is effected specifically through the lucid revelation that 'You are with me,'
כְּעִנְיַן דִּ"מְחַוֵּי לְהוּ בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ" בְּשַׁבָּת (פט עַמּוּד ב),
as in the account of Yitzchak showing them the Holy One before their very eyes, in Shabbat (89b),
עַד שֶׁיּוּכַל לְדַבֵּר לְנוֹכַח כְּמַרְאֶה בְּאֶצְבַּע – אַתָּה עִמָּדִי
until he can speak directly to the Almighty as though pointing with a finger: 'You are with me,'.
וּמִצַּד הַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבוּאָה הוּא תַּכְלִית תִּיקּוּן זֶה
and from the perspective of prophetic apprehension this rectification reaches its zenith.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ מַצִּיל אֶלָּא מֵעָנְשֵׁי יִסּוּרִין הַמַּגִּיעִין לָאָדָם מִצַּד חֲטָאֵי עַצְמוֹ,
Yet nonetheless, it rescues him only from punitive afflictions incurred through his own personal sins,
וּמְתַקֵּן שָׁרְשׁוֹ מִתּוֹלַדְתּוֹ;
rectifying his root as an individual from his birth;
אֲבָל אֵין מוֹעִיל לְתַקֵּן שָׁרְשׁוֹ בְּאֵיפֹה שֶׁהָיָה תָּלוּי בְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
yet it does not avail to rectify his soul's root where it was bound up with Adam the First.
וּלְתַקֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ חֵטְא דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּגְזַר עֲבוּרוֹ מִיתָה לַדּוֹרוֹת
and to rectify the root of Adam's sin, for which physical mortality was decreed upon all future generations.
דְּעַל דָּבָר זֶה נִסְגַּר בַּעֲדוֹ דַּלְתֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה
For regarding this universal decree, the gates of repentance were shut,
כְּפִי הַנִּרְאֶה מִדִּבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּ
as appears from the words of our Sages in Eruvin (18b),
דְּמֵאָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה יָשַׁב בְּתַעֲנִית וְהֶעֱלָה זַרְזֵי תְאֵנָה וְכוּלֵי
that for one hundred and thirty years Adam fasted and wore belts of fig leaves, etc.
וַהֲרֵי חָזַר בִּתְשׁוּבָה וְלֹא הוֹעִיל לוֹ.
and though he repented, it did not annul the decree of physical death.
וּכְבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה כב) דְּאָמַר לוֹ קַיִן: עָשִׂיתִי תְשׁוּבָה וְנִתְפַּשַּׁרְתִּי
And as taught in Bereishit Rabbah (end of Parashah 22), where Cain said to Adam: 'I repented and was granted a compromise,'
אָמַר: כָּךְ כֹּחָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵי
whereupon Adam exclaimed: 'Is such the power of repentance?! etc.'
וְלֹא נִגְלָה לָהֶם כֹּחָהּ רַק לְפַשֵּׁר לֹא לְכַפֵּר לְגַמְרֵי
Its power was revealed to them only to bring a compromise, not to atone completely.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §49): “as the Sages said, ‘teshuvah suspends and afflictions purge’ teshuvah tolah ve-yissurin memarkin — for the afflictions are only the completion, and atone for a half, and the other half is through teshuvah (which likewise atones a half, as in Vayikra Rabbah), which comes of itself through the afflictions.” This is §3-4’s ruling in R’ Tzadok’s own hand: by the Torah’s measure, wholehearted teshuvah does not by itself discharge the debt — it “suspends,” while the sentence (afflictions, and the graver levels) must still “purge” and complete what teshuvah alone leaves outstanding — the very reckoning of the “four levels of atonement.”

paragraphs.text: Yoma 86a: the four levels of atonement. “One who transgressed a positive commandment and repented — is forgiven at once. One who transgressed a prohibition and repented — teshuvah suspends and Yom Kippur atones. One who committed sins bearing kareis or court-death and repented — teshuvah and Yom Kippur suspend, and sufferings scour memarkin. But one who has chillul Hashem in his hand — teshuvah has no power to suspend, nor Yom Kippur to atone, nor sufferings to scour; rather, all of them suspend and death scours.” R’ Tzadok: for the graver categories, teshuvah alone does not complete the cleansing — that limitation belongs only to “this world.”

Tanya, Iggeres HaTeshuvah ch. 1, opens with the baraisa: “עבר על מצות עשה ושב — אינו זז משם עד שמוחלין לו; עבר על מצות לא תעשה ושב — תשובה תולה, ויום הכפורים מכפר ... עבר על כריתות ומיתות בית דין — תשובה ויום הכפורים תולין, ויסורין ממרקין” — “If one transgressed a positive commandment and repented, he does not move from there before he is forgiven; if he transgressed a prohibition and repented, repentance suspends and Yom Kippur atones ... for sins carrying excision or judicial death, repentance and Yom Kippur suspend, and afflictions cleanse.” Regarding a missed positive commandment, he explains that although the punishment for rebelling against God’s kingship is forgiven, “מכל מקום האור נעדר” — “nevertheless, the light is absent”: the light that performance of that commandment would have drawn down has not been supplied by the pardon. This gives a precise example of forgiveness and restoration being distinct. The opening of Tanya, Iggeres HaTeshuvah, is especially useful for R' Tzadok's distinction between selichah and complete restoration. The Alter Rebbe first cites the four-fold baraisa of Yoma and then insists that the essential Torah mitzvah of teshuvah is the wholehearted abandonment of sin; the subsequent categories describe what is still required for full kapparah and cleansing of the blemish. Thus immediate forgiveness and the remaining need for Yom Kippur or yissurin are not contradictions. A person may already be a genuine baal teshuvah while the spiritual effect of the past has not yet been fully cleared.

That structure parallels the architecture of Takanas HaShavin: the earliest rung makes the person "healed" from now on, while later rungs address the harder question of the former reality itself. The Chabad formulation and R' Tzadok's formulation are not identical, but both refuse to reduce teshuvah to a single undifferentiated event.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §128): “A baal teshuvah, even though ‘willful sins become merits,’ nonetheless requires afflictions and fasts for atonement, because they are no better than ‘a transgression for its own sake.’ On this it says (Bava Kamma 50a), ‘whoever says the Holy One waives punishment is mistaken’ — for on everything a person did he is exacted the fixed punishment and is fit for it, only that there are many remedies in His mercy.” He adds: “וגם על ידי המרירות בתשובתו זה ממש עונשי גיהנם” — “And through the bitterness of his repentance itself, these are truly the punishments of Gehinnom.” Exactly the se’if: by Torah-law teshuvah does not exempt from the punishments — court-death, lashes, korban, and the scouring sufferings — within this world; the author then distinguishes the complete cleansing after death.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Poked Akarim §6): “the sins and deficiencies — death purges them misah memarkasan, and they go on being consumed until nothing at all remains of them; and only the good remains, fixed in all hearts.” In context, he explains how each generation’s Torah and mitzvos remain in the hearts of later generations, while its sins and deficiencies pass away. This is a parallel to the author’s distinction between the remaining this-world consequences and the eventual cleansing of the deficiency: the dross is removed while the good remains.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: By Torah-law teshuvah does not nullify the Torah’s own consequences — not court-death, not lashes, not a korban. The four levels of atonement grade what teshuvah alone gains, what Yom Kippur completes, what sufferings scour, and what only death scours. Yet all of that holds only from the side of this bounded world: after death even chillul Hashem is scoured, for teshuvah draws from binah, the secret of the World to Come.

p: (ה) — וְעִנְיַן הַפְּשָׁר בְּחֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
And the nature of the compromise regarding the sin of Adam the First,
הוּא לְתַקֵּן מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא
was to effect rectification from now and onward.
וְלֹא לַעֲקוֹר לְמַפְרֵעַ לְגַמְרֵי, לִהְיוֹת כְּמִי שֶׁלֹּא חָטָא
and not to uproot the past retroactively and entirely, so as to be regarded as one who never sinned at all.
וְעַל כֵּן עוֹנֶשׁ מִיתָה שֶׁנִּגְזַר עָלָיו עַל זֶה
Therefore, the punishment of mortality decreed upon him on account of this,
לֹא נִתְכַּפֵּר כְּמִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה
was not expiated, according to the strict juridical sentence of the Torah,
דְּאֵין הַתְּשׁוּבָה מַצֶּלֶת מֵהָעוֹנֶשׁ,
for within the legal framework of Torah, repentance does not rescue from the statutory penalty;
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג, כב): "וְעַתָּה פֶּן יִשְׁלַח יָדוֹ וְלָקַח גַּם מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים וְגוֹמֵר".
and concerning this Scripture states (Genesis 3:22): "And now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever, etc."
וּמַה שֶּׁנִּקְרָא בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב "חַיִּים",
And that which Scripture designates as 'life',
הַיְינוּ וַדַּאי חַיֵּי עוֹלָם וְחַיִּים נִצְחִיִּים
assuredly refers to eternal life and everlasting existence.
שֶׁפּוֹעֵל בַּנֶּפֶשׁ תִּיקּוּן הַקִּלְקוּל וּגְזֵירַת מִיתָה שֶׁגָּרַם עֵץ הַדַּעַת
which effects within the soul the rectification of the ruin and the decree of mortality caused by the Tree of Knowledge.
וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה כא, ו) אָמַר
And in Bereishit Rabbah (Parashah 21:6) it is stated:
אֵין "וְעַתָּה" אֶלָּא תְשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵי
'And now' implies nothing other than repentance, etc.?!
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם סִיֵּים: "וְהוּא אָמַר פֶּן, וְאֵין פֶּן אֶלָּא לָאו",
and see there where it concludes: 'yet he said 'lest' (pen), and 'lest' denotes nothing other than a negative prohibition?!'
וְצָרִיךְ לוֹמַר דְּאָז בְּגַן עֵדֶן הוּא שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה לָשׁוּב
and one must say that at that moment in Gan Eden Adam refused to repent,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִמְלַךְ וְשָׁב
and only subsequently reconsidered and repented;
אֲבָל אֶפְשָׁר דְּהֵן מִדְרָשׁוֹת חֲלוּקוֹת
or it is possible that these are differing midrashic traditions,
אוֹ דְּגַם כַּוָּונַת מִדְרָשׁ זֶה "וְהוּא אָמַר" – עַל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַצְמוֹ,
or even that the intent of this Midrash in saying 'and he said' refers to Hashem Himself.
שֶׁפָּתַח לוֹ פֶּתַח לִתְשׁוּבָה, אֲבָל לֹא לְגַמְרֵי
Who opened an aperture for him to repent, yet not entirely.
וְעֵץ הַחַיִּים זוֹ תּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (פֶּרֶק א),
And 'the Tree of Life' refers to the Torah, as they stated in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 1),
וְהוּא הַמְּתַבֵּל הַיֵּצֶר
which is the seasoning that spices and refines the evil inclination,
לְתַקֵּן הַקּוֹדֵם גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה בְּצֵירוּף הַתּוֹרָה
– so as to rectify the past as well through repentance combined with the Torah—
זֶה נִמְנַע מִמֶּנּוּ.
and this was withheld from him.
וְגַם הַנְּבִיאִים שֶׁזָּכוּ לִצְפּוֹת בַּפַּרְדֵּס וּבַמַּרְאוֹת הָעֶלְיוֹנוֹת וְטָעֲמוּ מֵהֶם
And even the prophets, who merited gazing into the Orchard (Pardes) and supernal visions and tasted of them.
לֹא זָכוּ עֲדַיִן לִטְעוֹם מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים לִחְיוֹת לְעוֹלָם
still did not merit tasting of the Tree of Life so as to live forever.
שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ מִצַּד מַדְרֵגַת הַנְּבוּאָה
For this level does not proceed from the station of prophecy,
שֶׁהוּא שֶׁהָאָדָם נִבְדָּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
wherein mortal man remains separate from Hashem, blessed be He,
וּמְקַבֵּל שֶׁפַע נְבוּאָתוֹ וְדִבּוּרוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ לְבַד
and merely receives the influx of His prophecy and speech from Him alone;
אֲבָל חַיֵּי עוֹלָם הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַדְּבֵיקוּת הַגָּמוּר בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
whereas eternal life is attained through absolute cleaving (devekut) unto Him, blessed be He,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים ד, ד): "וְאַתֶּם הַדְּבֵקִים בַּה' אֱלֹהֵיכֶם חַיִּים כֻּלְּכֶם הַיּוֹם".
along the lines of that which is said (Deuteronomy 4:4): 'And you who cleave unto Hashem your God are alive every one of you this day.':
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קו עַמּוּד א) עַל לֶעָתִיד
And as it is taught in Sanhedrin (106a) regarding the ultimate future:
מִי מֵשִׂים כְּסוּתוֹ בֵּין לָבִיא וּלְבִיאָה כְּשֶׁנִּזְקָקִין זֶה לָזֶה
'Who dares place his garment between a lion and a lioness when they unite with one another?!'.
שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגַת הַנְּבוּאָה
which is elevated far above the spiritual grade of prophecy.
וְאָז יְבוּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח
And then death will be swallowed up forever,
וְיִשְׁתַּלְּמוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּצֶלֶם וּדְמוּת לְגַמְרֵי
and mankind will thereby become perfected in divine image and likeness completely,
עַד שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (עה עַמּוּד ב):
to the extent that they stated in Bava Batra (75b):
עֲתִידִים צַדִּיקִים שֶׁיִּקָּרְאוּ בִּשְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
the righteous are destined to be called by the very Name of the Holy One, blessed be He.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פרשה ח):
And that aligns with what they said in Bereishit Rabbah (Parashah 8):
דְּמֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם אֵין עוֹשֶׂה אַחֵר כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ,
that an earthly king of flesh and blood does not make another like unto himself,
אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה צַדִּיקִים כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ.
yet the Holy One, blessed be He, fashions the righteous to be like Himself.
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה אָמַר בִּיצִירַת הָאָדָם "בְּצַלְמֵנוּ" וּ"בְצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים",
And from this vantage point Scripture stated regarding the creation of man 'in our image' and 'in the image of God,'.
שֶׁהוּא כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ כִּבְיָכוֹל
signifying that he is, as it were, like unto Him.
אֶלָּא שֶׁאַחַר הַחֵטְא
However, following the sin,
מִלְּבַד דְּנִשְׁתַּנָּה זִיווֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
in addition to his countenance having changed, as our Sages of blessed memory noted,
הִנֵּה גְּזֵירַת הַמִּיתָה עַצְמָהּ גּוֹרֶמֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵעַתָּה כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ בָּזֶה עַל כָּל פָּנִים דְּאֵין חַי לְעוֹלָם
the very decree of physical death caused that from then on he is not like unto Him at least in this respect, being mortal;
וְעַל כֵּן אֵין הַצֶּלֶם שָׁלֵם
and consequently the divine image is not complete.
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִקְרָאוֹ בִּשְׁמוֹ כִּבְיָכוֹל
and it is impossible for him to be called by His Name, as it were.
רַק אָז שֶׁיִּקָּרְאוּ בִּשְׁמוֹ, שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגַת נְבוּאָה
Only then in the future, when they will be called by His Name—which transcends the level of prophecy—,
רַק מִצַּד מַדְרֵגַת הַדִּבּוּק הַגָּמוּר
proceeding solely from the realm of total cleaving,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה (ה, ב):
and in the manner brought in Shir HaShirim Rabbah (5:2):
תַּמָּתִי" – תְּיוֹמָתִי
my perfect one (tammati)—my twin (tiyomati):
לֹא אֲנִי גָּדוֹל מִכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא הִיא גְּדוֹלָה מִמֶּנִּי
neither am I greater than the Congregation of Israel, nor is she greater than Me.
וְדָבָר זֶה, אִלְמָלֵא אֲמָרוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ כִּבְיָכוֹל: "נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בְּצַלְמֵנוּ וְגוֹמֵר",
And this matter, were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself declared, as it were: 'Let us make man in our image, etc.',
אֵין כֹּחַ בַּפֶּה לְאָמְרוֹ.
no mortal mouth would possess the audacity or strength to utter it.
וְאָמְרוּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (יז עַמּוּד ב):
And they expounded in Rosh Hashanah (17b): ",
ה' ה'" – אֲנִי הוּא קוֹדֶם שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא הָאָדָם, וַאֲנִי הוּא לְאַחַר שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא וְיַעֲשֶׂה תְשׁוּבָה
'Hashem, Hashem'—I am He before man sins, and I am He after he sins and repents.
וּמַשְׁמָע גַּם לְאַחַר הַחֵטְא מַמָּשׁ כְּמִקֶּדֶם
implying that even following sin and repentance, he is restored literally to his primal state.

Bereishis Rabbah 21:6: “‘And now ve-atah, lest he stretch out his hand and take also of the tree of life’ — R’ Abba bar Kahana said: this teaches that the Holy One opened for him an opening of teshuvah, for ‘and now ve-atah’ is always an expression of teshuvah; but he Adam said ‘pen lest,’ and ‘pen’ is always a negation.” R’ Tzadok considers several readings: Adam refused in Gan Eden but repented later; the midrashim differ; or “he said pen” refers to Hashem, who opened a partial path of repentance. In the last reading, the opening did not fully undo the death-decree — the “tree of life” remained withheld. A striking Izhbitz parallel makes the phrase "tree of life" almost a definition of the higher teshuvah discussed here. Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Bereishis 6, on "ועץ החיים בתוך הגן," writes explicitly: "ועץ החיים הוא תשובה אמיתיות שמרפאות את הקודם" - the Tree of Life is true teshuvah that heals what came before. He then associates the river Peras with baalei teshuvah and explains that teshuvah "מגיע למקורו הראשון," reaches the person's first source. This is precisely the distinction of the present se'if: ordinary compromise heals from now on, whereas access to the Tree of Life would mean reaching back to the first source and curing the prior deficiency itself.

R' Tzadok himself supplies an essential safeguard in Pri Tzaddik, Shelach §6. He explains that teshuvah can transform the Tree of Knowledge into "very good," so that even deliberate sins become merits; but the mekoshesh erred by imagining that this might make it desirable to spoil first and repent afterward. The higher reading of the past is available only after a real fall has occurred and a real teshuvah has transformed it. It can never be used prospectively to authorize what the Torah forbids. Thus the Izhbitz-Radzin language of healing the original source intensifies moral responsibility rather than weakening it.

6, on "ועץ החיים בתוך הגן," writes explicitly: "ועץ החיים הוא תשובה אמיתיות שמרפאות את הקודם" - the Tree of Life is true teshuvah that heals what came before. He then associates the river Peras with baalei teshuvah and explains that teshuvah "מגיע למקורו הראשון," reaches the person's first source. This is precisely the distinction of the present se'if: ordinary compromise heals from now on, whereas access to the Tree of Life would mean reaching back to the first source and curing the prior deficiency itself.

R' Tzadok himself supplies an essential safeguard in

. He explains that teshuvah can transform the Tree of Knowledge into "very good," so that even deliberate sins become merits; but the mekoshesh erred by imagining that this might make it desirable to spoil first and repent afterward. The higher reading of the past is available only after a real fall has occurred and a real teshuvah has transformed it. It can never be used prospectively to authorize what the Torah forbids. Thus the Izhbitz-Radzin language of healing the original source intensifies moral responsibility rather than weakening it.

paragraphs.text:
Rosh Hashanah 17b: expounding the doubled Divine Name of the Thirteen Attributes — “Hashem, Hashem” — the Gemara teaches, “I am He before a person sins, and I am He after a person sins and does teshuvah,” for God does not hold the earlier sins against him, being ever “merciful and gracious.” The same passage is the source that “great is teshuvah, for it tears up a person’s sentence gzar din,” derived from “and he shall return and be healed” (Yeshayah 6:10) — “what is it that requires healing? — say, that is a sealed decree.” R’ Tzadok fastens on the wording “I am He after he sins and repents”: the penitent is restored to God exactly as before the sin, with no trace remaining — the full retroactive rectification of the past, the rung that (like the tree of life) awaits the future. Sod Yesharim, Shabbos Chol HaMoed Sukkos 33:1 (Izhbitz-Radzin), develops the doubled Name in a way that closely matches R' Tzadok's "exactly as before." After citing "ה' ה' - אני הוא קודם שיחטא אדם ואני הוא לאחר שיחטא האדם ויעשה תשובה," it explains that the latter Name means that after sin and teshuvah Hashem illuminates the person "ממקום היותר נעלה" - from a still higher place. It further says that there remains a hidden point of connection that is concealed even from the heavenly hosts, and that "יכול רק השי"ת לבדו להראות התיקון איך שמעולם לא נפסק מזה האדם החיבור אף בשעת החטא" - only Hashem Himself can reveal the rectification, namely how at the deepest level the bond was never severed even during the sin.

This is not a denial of the sin on the revealed plane; the same teaching distinguishes what can be seen by the created order from what Hashem alone discloses after teshuvah. It therefore gives unusually exact content to R' Tzadok's use of "אני הוא לאחר שיחטא": the restored identity is not merely a new relationship built after the break. Teshuvah can uncover a deeper, hidden continuity of the covenantal bond that the sin never reached, and from that hidden point the revealed rupture can itself be healed.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The “compromise” granted after Adam’s sin rectifies going forward, not retroactively — which is why the death-decree was not annulled. “Lest he stretch out his hand and take also of the tree of life” is the withholding of that fuller rectification; and the tree of life is Torah, the spice for the yetzer. Even the prophets did not taste of it, for it belongs not to prophecy but to complete cleaving — and only in the future will the righteous be “called by the Name of the Holy One.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, Large Beis and Small Beis §2): “at first He and His Name were one, and His simple Oneness spread without end or limit; and when it arose in His simple will to reveal His kingship and to create beings the differentiation began.” This gives §3-6 its ground: the wholeness of the Name is its original, undivided state — “He and His Name were one” before creation — which sin fractures and teshuvah mends, and which the World to Come restores, when “Hashem is One and His Name One” stands wholly revealed.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: This is the rung of the shem Havayah, the middah of Yaakov — a Name that sin alters, so that it is “not read as it is written,” and that teshuvah restores. In the World to Come His Name is one, read as written: that is after teshuvah, according to the force of a rung whose root reaches there. And when the question was put to the Holy One Himself, He answered “I am He” — atonement utterly, greater than all the wisdom this world contains.

p: (ז), — אוּלָם זֶהוּ מַדְרֵגַת הָאָבוֹת מִצַּד עַצְמָן
However, this represents the level of the Patriarchs from their own intrinsic perspective,
דְּהַיְינוּ כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר קוֹדֶם שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא
namely, in line with how God made man upright before he fell into sin;
אֲבָל לְאַחַר שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא
yet following sin,
רֹאשׁ הַמַּדְרֵגָה בְּקַבָּלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה הוּא דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
the vanguard of the rung in receiving repentance is King David, peace be upon him,
רֶגֶל רְבִיעִית שֶׁבַּמֶּרְכָּבָה שֶׁהֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה
the fourth leg of the divine Chariot, who raised the yoke of repentance.
וְהָאֲבָהָן דִּבְכָל שְׁאָר שֶׁבַע הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת כְּלוּלוֹת בּוֹ בִּפְרָטָיו
and the Patriarchs across all other seven sefirotic rungs are integrated within him in his various details.
וְהוּא רֹאשׁ וּתְחִלַּת הֲקָמָתָהּ בְּתַרְעָא לְדַרְתָּא
And he is the head and inception of its raising at the outer gate leading into the courtyard,
דְּהוּא נֶגֶד הֵ"א אַחֲרוֹנָה
which corresponds to the final Hei of the Tetragrammaton,
וְסִיּוּמוֹ בְּמָשִׁיחַ שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד הֵ"א רִאשׁוֹנָה
and its culmination is in the Messiah who corresponds to the first Hei,
שֶׁהוּא הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב
which is Binah (Understanding) within the heart,
שֶׁבּוֹ שְׁלֵימוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה לְגַמְרֵי
in whom resides the absolute perfection of repentance,
וְעָלָיו נֶאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה נב, יג): "יָרוּם וְנִשָּׂא וְגָבַהּ מְאֹד",
and concerning him it is said (Isaiah 52:13): 'He shall be exalted and lifted up, and shall be very high,'.
וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּתַנְחוּמָא (תּוֹלְדוֹת יד) עַל הָאָבוֹת שֶׁיִּגְדַּל מֵהֶם
which our Sages of blessed memory expounded in Tanchuma (Toldot 14) as referring to the Patriarchs, that he shall tower greater than they.
כִּי חָכְמָה, תּוֹרָה, וּנְבוּאָה הֵם שְׁלֹשָׁה דַּרְגִּין דְּאַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק, וְיַעֲקֹב
For Wisdom, Torah, and Prophecy are the three rungs of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
דְּחָכְמָה – יָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (טז עַמּוּד ב):
For concerning Wisdom—it is known what they stated in Bava Batra (16b):
אִצְטַגְנִינוּת גְּדוֹלָה הָיְתָה בְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְכוּלֵי
a great astrological wisdom was in the heart of Abraham our father, peace be upon him, etc.
וּשְׁתֵּי כִלְיוֹתָיו נַעֲשׂוּ כִּשְׁתֵּי מַעְיָנוֹת וְלִמְּדוּהוּ חָכְמָה (אָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן פֶּרֶק לג, א).
and his two kidneys became like two springs and taught him wisdom (Avot DeRabbi Natan 33:1).
וּתְחִלַּת הִתְקָרְבוּתוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיְתָה מִצַּד חָכְמָה אֱנוֹשִׁית
And the inception of his drawing near to Hashem, blessed be He, occurred through sanctified human wisdom?
שֶׁהָיָה יוֹשֵׁב וְחָקַר: כְּלוּם אֶפְשָׁר לַבִּירָה זוֹ בְּלֹא מַנְהִיג
in that he sat and contemplated: Is it conceivable that this castle should lack a governor?
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (לט, א).
as they taught in Bereishit Rabbah (39:1).
אֲבָל אוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה
However, Torah is from the side of Gevurah (Isaac),
וְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת יִצְחָק לֹא הָיְתָה עוֹד מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ וְחָכְמָה אֱנוֹשִׁית
and the awakening of Isaac was no longer through his own subjective mortal inquiry.
שֶׁכְּבָר קִבֵּל תּוֹרָה מֵאָבִיו
since he had already received the revealed tradition of Torah from his father.
וּנְבוּאָה מִסִּטְרָא דְּיַעֲקֹב
And Prophecy stems from the aspect of Jacob,
דִּכְתִיב (בְּרֵאשִׁית כח, יג): "וְהִנֵּה ה' נִצָּב עָלָיו".
as it is written (Genesis 28:13): 'And behold, Hashem stood over him.'

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: That boundless rung belongs to the Avos from their own side, as man was before he sinned. After the sin, the head of the rung in the receiving of teshuvah is David — fourth leg of the Chariot, “who raised up the yoke of teshuvah” — and its consummation is in Mashiach. Wisdom, Torah and prophecy are the three rungs of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, each marking how its bearer first drew near.

p: (ח) — וּגְדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁדּוֹחָה מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה וְהַחֲכָמִים וּפוֹרֶצֶת הַגְּבוּלִים שֶׁקָּבְעוּ,
And great is repentance, for it overrides the judicial measure of the Torah and the Sages, breaching the statutory boundaries they established;
וַאֲפִילּוּ כָּל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים וּמְפוֹרָשׁ בַּנְּבִיאִים וּבַתּוֹרָה שֶׁאֵין תְּשׁוּבָה מוֹעֶלֶת
and even regarding all that the Sages declared, and is made explicit in the Prophets and the Torah, that repentance does not avail—
מִצַּד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ,
from the perspective of the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself,
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הַדִּיבּוּק הַגָּמוּר בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד
which is realized through absolute cleaving unto Him, blessed be He, as will be in the World to Come.
הוּא אוֹמֵר: יַעֲשֶׂה תְּשׁוּבָה וְנִתְכַּפֵּר הַכֹּל לְגַמְרֵי
He declares: Let him do teshuva, and everything is atoned for completely.
וּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ דְּמִקּוֹדֶם שָׁאֲלוּ לַחָכְמָה, לַתּוֹרָה, וְלַנְּבוּאָה
And that which they taught, that initially they addressed the question to Wisdom, Torah, and Prophecy,
אֵין זֶה שִׂיחָה בְּטֵלָה וְדֶרֶךְ מְלִיצָה
is neither idle chatter nor mere poetic metaphor.
רַק כָּךְ הוּא הַשּׁוּרָה הָרְאוּיָה וְסֵדֶר הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁאָל לָהֶם קוֹדֶם
rather such is the proper order and ontological hierarchy of levels to be inquired of first.
וַעֲדַיִן לֹא הִגִּיעַ הַשְּׁאֵלָה לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וְשֶׁיְּבוּלַּע הַמָּוֶת
And the inquiry has not yet reached the Holy One Himself to consummate the swallowing up of death,
עַד שֶׁיָּבוֹא מָשִׁיחַ הַשּׁוֹאֵל זֶה מֵהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
until the Messiah arrives, who asks this directly of the Holy One, blessed be He,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (תְּהִלִּים כא, ה): "חַיִּים שָׁאַל מִמְּךָ נָתַתָּה לּוֹ וְגוֹמֵר",
as it is stated (Psalms 21:5): 'He asked life of You, and You gave it him, even length of days forever and ever,'.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּ
and as they expounded in Sukkah (52a).
וְעַד מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
And up until the Giving of the Torah,
שֶׁהוּא עַד הַתְחָלַת שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה מֵ"אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ בְחָרָן" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ט עַמּוּד א),
which represents the dawn of the two thousand years of Torah inaugurated from 'the souls they made in Haran' as stated in Avodah Zarah (9a),
הוּא הַזְּמַן דְּשָׁאֲלוּ לַחָכְמָה, וֶהֱשִׁיבָה: "חַטָּאִים תְּרַדֵּף רָעָה",
was the historical epoch when they asked Wisdom, which answered: 'Evil pursues sinners' (Proverbs 13:21).
כִּי אֵין תְּשׁוּבָה לַגּוֹיִם כְּלָל
for there is no metaphysical teshuva for the pagan nations whatsoever.
וּבְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הִתְחִילָה תּוֹרָה וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת
And with Abraham our father, peace be upon him, began the Torah and the primal root of Jewishness,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְצִיאוּת כַּפָּרָה לַחֵטְא עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה
signifying that there is a genuine possibility of atonement for sin through repentance,
וְצָרִיךְ רַק קָרְבָּן לְכַפֵּר
and one merely requires a sacrificial offering to atone;
וְזֶהוּ סֵדֶר קָרְבָּנוֹת שֶׁאָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַעֲנִית (כז עַמּוּד ב).
and this corresponds to the order of sacrifices that the Holy One conveyed to Abraham our father, as they stated in Ta'anit (27b).
וּבְאוֹתוֹ מַעֲמָד בָּחַר לוֹ אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם גַּם כֵּן הַגָּלִיּוֹת
And at that visionary Covenant, Abraham our father also selected the exiles,
שֶׁהֵן הַיִּסּוּרִין הַמְּמָרְקִין
which are the scouring afflictions;
דְּאֵין תְּשׁוּבָה מְמָרֶקֶת לְגַמְרֵי עַל פִּי מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה כְּפִי אַרְבַּע חִלּוּקֵי כַּפָּרָה
since repentance does not fully cleanse according to the statutory ruling of the Torah, commensurate with the four divisions of atonement.
וְעַל זֶה רָמַז הַקָּרְבָּן לְכַוֵּון כְּאִלּוּ נַעֲשָׂה הַיִּסּוּרִין בּוֹ כַּנּוֹדָע
and upon this hinted the sacrifice: that one mentally intend as though those purgative suffering were inflicted upon himself, as is known.
וְזֶהוּ עַד אַחַר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁהִתְחִיל זְמַן דְּשָׁאֲלוּ לַנְּבוּאָה
And this stage extended until after the Giving of the Torah, when began the epoch when they asked Prophecy;
וְדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר זָכוּ כֻּלָּם לִנְבוּאָה בִּשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
and the Wilderness Generation all attained prophecy at the Giving of the Torah.
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בִּפְסָחִים (סו עַמּוּד א): אִם אֵינָן נְבִיאִים – בְּנֵי נְבִיאִים הֵן
which is why our Sages stated in Pesachim (66a): 'If they are not prophets, they are the children of prophets.',
וּמִצַּד הַשָּׂגַת "אָנֹכִי ה' וְגוֹמֵר", דְּשָׁמְעוּ כֻּלָּם מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה
And from the vantage point of apprehending 'I am Hashem, etc.' which they all heard directly from the Almighty,
הִתְחִיל הַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבוּאָה
began the era of prophetic comprehension,
שֶׁהוּא דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל הַהַשָּׂגָה דְּ"אַתָּה עִמָּדִי",
which is broadly the direct second-person realization that 'You are with me,'.
שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְתַקֵּן הַקּוֹדֵם וּלְהַצִּיל מִיִּסּוּרִין גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה
empowering them to rectify the past and be rescued from afflictions through repentance as well.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין נִתְקָן לְגַמְרֵי לְהַצִּיל גַּם מֵהַמִּיתָה
Yet nonetheless, matters are not rectified so entirely as to deliver them from physical mortality,
וּתְשׁוּבָתָם: "הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַחֹטֵאת הִיא תָמוּת" כַּנִּזְכָּר
and its prophetic response remains: 'The soul that sins, it shall die,' as mentioned;
וְזֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ וְהוֹלֵךְ עַד מָשִׁיחַ.
and this ongoing dynamic extends uninterruptedly until the Messiah.
דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּמִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה
For although this underlying prophetic reality is rooted in Jacob our father whose bed was whole,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין זֶה נִגְלֶה עֲדַיִן
nevertheless in this physical world this is not yet openly manifest;
וְהַרְבֵּה מְשׁוּמָּדִים וְכוֹפְרִים יֵשׁ בַּעֲווֹנוֹתֵינוּ הָרַבִּים מִזֶּרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל
for there are many apostates and deniers, due to our abundant sins, stemming from the biological seed of Israel;
אֶלָּא שֶׁהִבְטִיחָנוּ יִתְבָּרַךְ דְּ"לֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח"
except that the Blessed Creator promised us that 'none of them shall be utterly cast out' (II Samuel 14:14),
וּכְשֶׁיְּקַבֵּץ נִדָּחֵינוּ מֵאַרְבַּע כַּנְפוֹת יְבוֹרַר לָעַיִן דָּבָר זֶה
and when He gathers our dispersed from the four corners of the earth, this reality will be visibly confirmed to every eye:
דְּשׁוּם זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא נִדְחָה כְּלָל
that not a single soul of the seed of Jacob our father was ever discarded.
אָז יִהְיֶה שְׁלֵימוּת דַּרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and then the spiritual stature of Jacob our father will reach utter completion.
וְהַהַשְׁלָמָה הַגְּמוּרָה יִהְיֶה לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ,
And the consummate perfection will occur in the days of the Messiah,
שֶׁאָז יִתְבָּרֵר גְּדוּלָּה זוֹ דִּתְשׁוּבָה שֶׁדּוֹחָה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
wherein this supreme greatness of repentance that overrides a negative Torah prohibition will be fully revealed:
הוּא לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה רִאשׁוֹנָה דְּ"פֶּן יִשְׁלַח יָדוֹ וְגוֹמֵר",
which refers to that very first negative prohibition: 'lest he put forth his hand, etc.',
דְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "פֶּן" הוּא לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
for wherever 'lest' (pen) is stated it constitutes a negative commandment.
וְזֶהוּ שְׁלֵימוּת הַמַּעֲלָה
and this constitutes the pinnacle of perfection.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Soferim §6): “one is called alive only when the vitality is cleaving to him davuk bo and not severed… the righteous, even in their death, are called ‘alive’ — this is ‘alive’ in the absolute sense, for there is no true vitality except that which is drawn from Hashem.” This is the inner force of §3-8’s “complete cleaving to Him”: teshuvah that overrides even what the Torah and sages ruled unavailing works precisely by re-attaching the person to the Source of life — the sinner, “severed,” is as dead, and by cleaving wholly to God he is drawn back into the vitality that flows straight from Him, above every bound.

paragraphs.text: Rav Tzadok makes this the culminating rung: only with Mashiach does the request reach the Holy One Himself, after the epochs of asking Wisdom, Torah, and Prophecy. Only then is the promise “death shall be swallowed up forever” fulfilled — the utter, retroactive rectification that no earlier rung could attain. This is Rav Tzadok’s development of the verse and the Gemara’s account.

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 9a: “The world exists six thousand years: two thousand of chaos tohu, two thousand of Torah, two thousand the days of Mashiach. From when are the ‘two thousand of Torah’ counted? From ‘the souls they made in Charan’ (Bereishis 12:5)” — when Avraham began teaching Torah and bringing souls to faith. R’ Tzadok aligns the epochs with “asking Wisdom” (until Torah), “asking Prophecy” (from Sinai), and “asking the Holy One” (Mashiach).

paragraphs.text: Taanis 27b: “Avraham said before the Holy One: Master of the Universe, perhaps Israel will sin before You and You will do to them as to the generation of the Flood? He said: No. He said: How shall I know I will inherit it? He said: Take Me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old goat, and a three-year-old ram (Bereishis 15:9) the covenant of the pieces. He said: This is well while the Temple stands — when it does not stand, what will be of them? He said: I have already established for them the order of sacrifices; whenever they read them before Me I will regard it as if they offered them, and I forgive them all their sins.” R’ Tzadok: with Avraham begins atonement-through-korban (and he “chose the exiles” — the scouring sufferings — since teshuvah alone does not fully scour).

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 66b: “Hillel said: ‘leave it to Israel: if they are not prophets, they are the children of prophets.’” R’ Tzadok: the desert generation attained prophecy at Sinai (hearing “I am Hashem” from the Almighty) — the epoch of “asking Prophecy,” the general “You are with me,” which rectifies the past and saves from sufferings, though not yet from death.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Poked Akarim 2:7): “for the Torah is ‘from Heaven,’ given through the apprehension of prophecy — and all Israel merited, at the standing of Har Sinai, the apprehension of prophecy then, ‘and they heard Anochi and Lo Yihyeh from the mouth of the Almighty’; therefore it is ‘an inheritance for all the congregations of Yaakov,’ and all are destined to attain this in the future.” This parallel concerns the opening of prophecy at Sinai and its inheritance by Israel. R’ Tzadok here expressly distinguishes that stage from the final answer of “the Holy One Himself”: prophecy can repair the past and save from sufferings, but the answer “the sinning soul shall die” remains until Mashiach. The two stages should not be identified. The maxim “if they are not prophets, they are children of prophets” appears in Pesachim 66a and is repeated on 66b.

R’ Tzadok here expressly distinguishes that stage from the final answer of “the Holy One Himself”: prophecy can repair the past and save from sufferings, but the answer “the sinning soul shall die” remains until Mashiach. Shmuel II 14:14: the wise woman of Teko’a, pleading with David to bring back the banished Avshalom, says — “כִּי מוֹת נָמוּת וְכַמַּיִם הַנִּגָּרִים אַרְצָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא יֵאָסֵפוּ, וְלֹא יִשָּׂא אֱלֹקִים נֶפֶשׁ, וְחָשַׁב מַחֲשָׁבוֹת לְבִלְתִּי יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח” — “for we must surely die, and are like water spilled on the ground that cannot be gathered; yet God does not take away a soul, but devises means that the banished one not be cast out from Him.” Rashi: “‘God does not spare a man’ from death — therefore the king should devise means machashavos that his outcast not remain banished.” R’ Tzadok takes “lo yidach mimenu nidach” as God’s own assurance that no member of Yaakov’s seed is ever finally cast off: though in this world there are apostates and deniers among Israel, at the future ingathering it will be “clarified to the eye” that no seed of Yaakov is rejected at all. Two major Chassidic traditions make R' Tzadok's use of "לא ידח ממנו נדח" especially concrete. Tanya, Likkutei Amarim ch. 39 (39:20 in Sefaria), explains the assurance that even Torah learned shelo lishmah will ultimately rise: a Jew's end is certainly to do teshuvah, in this gilgul or another, "כי לא ידח ממנו נדח." The Alter Rebbe thus reads the verse not merely as a promise that God will not abandon the person, but as a promise that the person's own buried Torah and avodah will eventually return with him when he returns.

Sha'ar HaEmunah VeYesod HaChasidut, Entrance to the Gate of Beit Yaakov 23:11, gives the Izhbitz-Radzin side of the same promise. The believer trusts that Hashem "חושב מחשבות לבלתי ידח ממנו נדח" and that whatever passes over him can ultimately be shown to have been for his good. Even events that presently seem impossible to reconcile can, through a clarity Hashem later opens in the mind, become the very ground of consolation. This is not a claim that every present act is good in its revealed form. It is a statement about the final Divine "machashavos" that refuse to let a Jewish soul's history end in banishment.

Cf. Resisei Layla §35: even the consciously "nidachim" - those who know they are Jews yet have been driven far from the knowledge of Hashem - are promised awakening by the great shofar, because "לא ידח ממנו נדח." This sharpens the se'if's future tense: the fact that the root cannot be finally expelled will only be fully "clarified to the eye" when the outcasts actually return.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Teshuvah overrides even what the sages, the prophets and the Torah declared unavailing — because it comes from the side of the Holy One Himself. The order in which Wisdom, Torah and Prophecy were asked is no figure of speech but the sequence of the epochs: wisdom until matan Torah, prophecy after it, and the question reaching the Holy One only with Mashiach. Then the first prohibition — “lest he stretch out his hand” — is itself nullified.

p: (ט), — וְהַתְחָלָתָהּ הָיְתָה כְּבָר בִּימֵי חִזְקִיָּה
And its inception was already glimpsed in the days of King Hezekiah,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (צד עַמּוּד א) דְּבִקֵּשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ מָשִׁיחַ,
concerning whom they stated in Sanhedrin (94a) that the Holy One sought to make him the Messiah,
שֶׁהוּא כְּבָר הִתְחִיל לְגַלּוֹת מַעֲלָה זוֹ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה
since he had already begun unveiling this supreme virtue of repentance.
שֶׁהִיא לְמַעְלָה מִמִּשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה וְהַנְּבוּאָה
which transcends both the judicial verdicts of Torah and Prophecy.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (י עַמּוּד א):
And as our Sages recounted in Berakhot (10a):
דְּאָמַר לִישַׁעְיָה: "כַּלֵּה נְבוּאָתְךָ וְצֵא, כָּךְ מְקֻבְּלַנִי מִבֵּית אֲבִי אַבָּא: אֲפִילּוּ חֶרֶב חַדָּה מוּנַּחַת עַל צַוָּארוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם אַל יִמְנַע עַצְמוֹ מִן הָרַחֲמִים" וְכוּלֵי

where he told the prophet Isaiah: 'Conclude your prophecy and depart! For thus have I received from the house of my ancestor: Even if a sharp sword rests upon a man's neck, let him not refrain from seeking mercy, etc.',
דְּאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר הָעוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי בַּקָּשַׁת רַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם
For nothing can withstand the plea for Heavenly mercy.
דְּגָדוֹל כֹּחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה לְמַעְלָה מִכָּל הַמִּשְׁפָּטִים
inasmuch as the power of repentance is exalted far above all statutory legal measures.
וְחֶטְאוֹ הָיָה דְּלָא נְסֵיב
And his error lay in not marrying,
לְפִי שֶׁרָאָה שֶׁיֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ מְנַשֶּׁה שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא
because he foresaw through prophecy that Menashe would emerge from him who would sin.
וְיָדַע שֶׁיַּפְלִיג לַחֲטוֹא עַד שֶׁמִּן הַדִּין לֹא יִהְיֶה שֶׁיְּקוּבַּל בִּתְשׁוּבָה
and he knew he would sin so outrageously that strictly by law he could not be received in repentance.
וּמִיָּד שֶׁגִּילָּה דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁל "כַּלֵּה נְבוּאָתְךָ וְכוּלֵי",
Yet the moment Hezekiah disclosed this principle of 'conclude your prophecy, etc.',
שֶׁאֵין לְהַשְׁגִּיחַ גַּם בִּנְבוּאָה
demonstrating that one does not surrender even before prophetic decree,
בָּזֶה נִתְגַּלָּה לוֹ מִמֵּילָא
there was automatically revealed unto him.
שֶׁגַּם לִמְנַשֶּׁה יוֹעִיל חֲתִירָה לְקַבְּלוֹ בִּתְשׁוּבָה
that for Menashe too an underground tunnel would avail to receive him in repentance.
וַחֲכָמִים שֶׁמְּנָאוּהוּ בִּכְלַל שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
And as for the Sages who counted Menashe among those who have no portion in the World to Come,
הַיְינוּ מִצַּד מִשְׁפַּט הַחֲכָמִים
that was strictly according to the judicial vantage point of the Sages,
אֲבָל לֹא מִצַּד מִשְׁפַּט הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
yet not from the sovereign prerogative of the Holy One, blessed be He,
שֶׁהוּא קִבְּלוֹ בְּמַחְתֶּרֶת וּבְהֶעְלֵם מֵעֵינֵי כָּל חֲכָמִים וּנְבִיאִים גַּם כֵּן
Who accepted him through a secret breach hidden even from the eyes of all sages and prophets.
דְּהוּא הָאוֹמֵר דִּתְשׁוּבָה מוֹעֶלֶת בְּכָל עִנְיָן
for He is the One Who affirms that repentance avails in every circumstance.
וְדוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קד עַמּוּד ב) דָּרְשׁוּ עַל כֻּלָּם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
And the interpreters of esoteric traces (dorshei reshumot) in Sanhedrin (104b) expounded concerning all of them that they possess a portion in the World to Come,
וְהַיְינוּ מִצַּד שֶׁהֵם זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּמִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה וְ"לֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח",
namely, from the intrinsic reality that they stem from the seed of Jacob whose bed was whole and 'none of them shall be cast out';
וְדָבָר זֶה לֹא נִגְלָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and this mystery is not overtly manifest in this physical world.
אֶלָּא רְשִׁימוּ מִמֶּנּוּ נִרְמַז וְנוֹדַע לְדוֹרְשֵׁי הָרְשׁוּמוֹת
save that a subtle trace of it was hinted and unveiled to the expounders of scriptural allusions.
אֲבָל מִשְׁפַּט חַכְמֵי הַמִּשְׁנָה, כְּפִי מִשְׁפַּט הַחָכְמָה הַמְּסוּרָה בְּיָדֵיהֶם וּגְלוּיָה לַחֲכָמִים, לֹא הָיָה כֵן
However, the legal judgment of the Tannaitic sages, according to the normative wisdom transmitted into their hands and revealed to mortal sages, could not be so.
וְחִזְקִיָּה הוּא הַמַּתְחִיל לְעוֹרֵר דָּבָר זֶה גַּם כֵּן בְּנִיצּוּחַ סַנְחֵרִיב
And Hezekiah was the one who began awakening this transcendent power in the defeat of Sennacherib as well,
שֶׁהוּא אָמַר: "הַבִּלְעֲדֵי ה' עָלִיתִי וְגוֹמֵר" (מְלָכִים ב יח, כה),
who had arrogantly boasted: 'Have I now come up without Hashem against this place, etc.'
כִּי הוּא הָיָה שֵׁבֶט אַפּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁלָחוֹ גַּם לִירוּשָׁלַיִם
for Sennacherib was indeed the rod of His wrath, and Hashem had dispatched him against Jerusalem.
אֲבָל חִזְקִיָּה הָיָה גָּנוּז בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה
Yet within Hezekiah this supernal root was concealed,
שֶׁהָיָה רָאוּי לַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ מָשִׁיחַ,
rendering him worthy of being made the Messiah;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ כֹּחַ הִתְעוֹרְרוּת שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה כָּל כָּךְ
meaning that he possessed such an intense awakening of repentance
לְעוֹרֵר עַל יְדֵי זֶה רַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם
as to stir Heavenly mercy through it.
לִשְׁבּוֹר כָּל מַאֲמָרֵי ה' גַּם כֵּן
so as to shatter even harsh prophetic decrees of Hashem.

Berachos 10a: Yeshayahu told the ailing Chizkiyahu, “‘set your house in order, for you shall die and not live’ (Melachim II 20:1) — you shall die in this world and not live in the World to Come,” because he had not engaged in procreation (foreseeing wicked offspring). Chizkiyahu answered, “Son of Amotz, finish your prophecy and go: thus I have received from the house of my father’s father — even if a sharp sword rests on a man’s neck, let him not withhold himself from mercy.” R’ Tzadok: this is the revelation that nothing — not even a prophetic decree — stands before the request for Heaven’s mercy. R' Tzadok returns to this very Chizkiyahu-Menasheh episode in Pri Tzaddik, Bo §9. Chizkiyahu saw that a "ben delo ma'ali" would issue from him, yet Yeshayahu answered "בהדי כבשי דרחמנא למה לך"; and R' Tzadok adds that when Hashem gives children, the hidden outcome is necessarily toward good - for from Menasheh came the chain of Mashiach ben David, and even regarding Menasheh himself the dorshei reshumos found a share in the World to Come. What Chizkiyahu saw prophetically was true, but it was not the whole truth of the future chain.

Likkutei Torah, Pinchas 3:22, places "כבשי דרחמנא" in a still broader Chassidic frame: the "secret of the world" is the hidden dimension of Torah and of the Divine will, drawing from a level described there as Atik, beyond what the revealed order can display. This helps define the limit R' Tzadok is drawing. Prophecy may reveal what a future child will do; it does not thereby give the prophet jurisdiction over why that soul must exist or what ultimate tikkun will emerge through generations. The command belongs to the revealed Torah; the hidden accounting belongs to Hashem.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Ohr Zarua LaTzadik §6): “‘that which you were commanded, you should do — but with the secrets of the Merciful, why meddle?’ — and this is what Moshe Rabbeinu intends, the Written Torah; yet there are times of ‘a time to act for Hashem, they have annulled Your Torah.’” The distinction here is between obeying a command and the possibility that repentance and prayer overturn a prophetic sentence. In Berachos 10a, Chizkiyahu accepts the demand to marry and asks for Yeshayahu’s daughter; he then refuses to give up hope in mercy when told that his death has already been decreed. R’ Tzadok applies that refusal of despair to Menasheh’s eventual acceptance in repentance. It does not turn Chizkiyahu’s earlier refusal to marry into a permitted breach of the command.

, Chizkiyahu accepts the demand to marry and asks for Yeshayahu’s daughter; he then refuses to give up hope in mercy when told that his death has already been decreed. R’ Tzadok applies that refusal of despair to Menasheh’s eventual acceptance in repentance. It does not turn Chizkiyahu’s earlier refusal to marry into a permitted breach of the command.
