inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The beginning of this appeared already with Chizkiyahu, whom the Holy One wished to make Mashiach. His “finish your prophecy and go” — that one must not withhold himself from asking mercy even against a prophet’s word — was itself the disclosure that a tunnel would be opened even for Menasheh. The sages who excluded Menasheh judged from the side of the sages’ own judgment; from the side of the Holy One he was received.

p: (י) — וּבֵירֵר זֶה בְּיִחוּד בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמַר "כַּלֵּה נְבוּאָתְךָ וְכוּלֵי",
And he established this uniquely in his pronouncement 'Conclude your prophecy, etc.',
וְאָז נָתַן לוֹ יְשַׁעְיָה בִּתּוֹ לְהוֹלִיד מְנַשֶּׁה
and then Isaiah gave him his daughter in marriage in order to father Menashe,
שֶׁכְּבָר הִמְצִיא וְהֵבִיא גִּלּוּי אוֹר זֶה הַמְּחוּדָּשׁ שֶׁל מַעֲלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה
for he had already revealed and brought forth this novel illumination of the primacy of teshuva,
כָּל כָּךְ נֶגֶד שֵׂכֶל הַתּוֹרָה וּנְבוּאָה
so powerfully contrary to the standard intellect of Torah and Prophecy.
עַד שֶׁיּוֹעִיל גַּם לִמְנַשֶּׁה
that it would avail even for a sinner like Menashe.
אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁלַם אָז עֲדַיִן הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים
Except that the full expansion of the attribute of a boundless heritage was not yet completed then,
לִהְיוֹת בֶּאֱמֶת עַד אֵין קֵץ
so as to extend in ultimate truth without end,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִמְחָל לְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לְגַמְרֵי עַד שֶׁיְּבוּלַּע הַמָּוֶת
such that the entire universe would be completely forgiven until death be abolished,
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מָשִׁיחַ.
namely, that the Messianic era be fully inaugurated.
וְאָמַר עַל זֶה (יְשַׁעְיָה כד, טז): "רָזִי לִי רָזִי לִי",
And concerning this Isaiah lamented (Isaiah 24:16): 'My secret is mine, my secret is mine!',
שֶׁהוּא מֵהַנִּסְתָּרוֹת לַה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְכִבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא
which belongs to the hidden things of Hashem our God and the profound mysteries of the Merciful One;
דְּאוֹר זֶה שֶׁל מַעֲלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה כְּבָר נִתְגַּלָּה וְנִתְבָּרֵר עַל יְדֵי חִזְקִיָּה
for though this illumination of teshuva was disclosed and established through Hezekiah.
דְּאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר עוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה
proving that nothing can withstand repentance,
וְדוֹרוֹ דּוֹר דֵּעָה וּבַעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה
and his generation was a generation of deep knowledge and penitence,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּשְׁבַח דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל חִזְקִיָּה בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (צד עַמּוּד ב).
as our Sages of blessed memory noted in praise of the generation of Hezekiah in Sanhedrin (94b).
רַק שֶׁהוּא "רָזִי לִי",
Yet it remained 'my secret is mine'—,
רָצָה לוֹמַר: יָדוּעַ לוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לְבַד וְלֹא לִבְרִיָּה בָּעוֹלָם
meaning: known to Him alone, blessed be He, and to no mortal creature in the universe;
כִּי אֵין שׁוּם בְּרִיָּה שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה
because no created being can independently grasp this transcendent level of repentance,
שֶׁהוּא רַק מִצַּד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ,
which exists solely from the vantage point of the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself;
וְעַל כֵּן אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲמוֹד עַל סוֹדוֹתֶיהָ וְסֵדֶר גִּילּוּיָהּ.
and therefore it is impossible to fully comprehend its mysteries and the timetable of its disclosure.
וּכְבָר יְשַׁעְיָה גִּילָּה זֶה לְחִזְקִיָּה דְּיֵשׁ כִּבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת שָׁם
And Isaiah had already conveyed this to Hezekiah that there are impenetrable divine secrets, as they stated in Berakhot there:
דְּיֵשׁ סוֹדוֹת שֶׁאֵין נִגְלִים לִבְרִיָּה, כְּמוֹ לֵידַת רָשָׁע כִּמְנַשֶּׁה
that there are esoteric secrets never revealed to any creature, such as the mysterious purpose behind the birth of a wicked figure like Menashe.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁלֵּידָתוֹ הוּא מִסּוֹד ה
', And by virtue of the fact that his birth was rooted in the divine secret of Hashem,
מִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ לוֹ תְּשׁוּבָה וְתִיקּוּן גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד סוֹד ה' שֶׁרָצָה בְּכָךְ,
he automatically possesses repentance and rectification through that very divine mystery which willed it so,
כַּאֲשֶׁר יִתְגַּלֶּה לֶעָתִיד סוֹדוֹ.
when His hidden purpose will be revealed in the ultimate future.
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהַדָּבָר הָיָה מְסוּדָּר כָּךְ מִכִּבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא
And at all events, since the matter was thus orchestrated from the depths of the divine mysteries,
אֵין כָּאן עוֹד חֵטְא שֶׁהוּא הַיְצִיאָה מֵהַסֵּדֶר וּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
there is ultimately no 'sin' in the sense of a deviation from the absolute master plan and will of Hashem,
וַהֲרֵי זֶה כָּךְ יִסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
for Hashem Himself thus founded reality;
אִם כֵּן אֵין כָּל הַחֵטְא אֶלָּא מִצִּידּוֹ,
if so, the entire sinful nature exists solely from the human subject's perspective,
שֶׁהוּא לֹא יָדַע דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁל סוֹד ה
' in that he was ignorant of this hidden divine mystery,
וְחָשַׁב שֶׁהוּא מַמְרֶה פְּנֵי ה' בַּחֲטָאָיו
and imagined that he was defying Hashem through his transgressions;
אֲבָל עַל הָאֱמֶת, הֲרֵי אֵין כָּאן חֵטְא מֵעִיקָּרוֹ.
yet according to the ultimate truth, there was no sin at its core.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה הֵם כָּל הַדְּחִיּוֹת סֵדֶר מִשְׁפְּטֵי הַתּוֹרָה עַל יְדֵי מַעֲלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה זוֹ שֶׁגִּילָּה חִזְקִיָּה וִישַׁעְיָה בָּזֶה
And along these lines operate all overrides of the normative legal framework of the Torah through this sublime teshuva revealed by Hezekiah and Isaiah:
דְּיֵשׁ כִּבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא וְסוֹד וָרָז שֶׁנִּגְלָה לוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לְבַד
that there exist divine mysteries and a hidden secret revealed to Him alone, blessed be He;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגּוּף הַסּוֹד לֹא נִתְגַּלָּה
and even though the substantive essence of the mystery has not been unveiled.
מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִתְגַּלָּה דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ סוֹד
nonetheless the meta-fact that such a mystery exists was indeed revealed.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִמֵּילָא, אַף שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּסוֹתֵר מִשְׁפְּטֵי הַתּוֹרָה
And through this, even though it appears superficially to contradict the rulings of the Torah,
אֵין כָּאן סְתִירָה עַל הָאֱמֶת
there is no genuine contradiction in absolute truth;
כִּי מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה הוּא מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבְנֵי אָדָם
because the jurisprudence of the Torah reflects reality as it is revealed to mortal men.
אֲבָל מִצַּד הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה לֶעָתִיד לֹא הָיָה חֵטְא כְּלָל
whereas from the perspective of the hidden depths to be disclosed in the future, it was not a sin at all.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (פט עַמּוּד ב):
And concerning this our Sages stated in Shabbat (89b):
אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית
if your sins are like these solar years which have been arranged and advancing systematically since the six days of Creation,
דְּהַיְינוּ מִצַּד כִּבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא
namely stemming from the supernal divine mysteries.
אָז כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ לְגַמְרֵי שֶׁאֵין חֵטְא כְּלָל
then 'they shall be white as snow' completely, revealing that no sin existed at all.

Yeshayah 24:16: “מִכְּנַף הָאָרֶץ זְמִרֹת שָׁמַעְנוּ, צְבִי לַצַּדִּיק, וָאֹמַר רָזִי לִי רָזִי לִי אוֹי לִי” — “From the corner of the earth we have heard songs, ‘Glory to the righteous!’; but I said, ‘My secret is mine, my secret is mine, woe is me!’” Rashi: the prophet heard from behind the heavenly Curtain that in the future songs would rise “from the corner of the earth” — the raising-up of the righteous; “‘razi li’ — woe is me that two secrets have been revealed to me, the secret of retribution and the secret of salvation,” for the redemption is delayed until wave upon wave of oppressors has come. R’ Tzadok takes “razi li” as the mark that the highest rung of teshuvah — already revealed to Chizkiyahu, that “nothing stands before teshuvah” — is one of the kivshei d’Rachmana, “known to Him alone and to no creature.” The continuation in Sha'ar HaEmunah VeYesod HaChasidut, Entrance to the Gate of Beit Yaakov 23:11, sheds light on Yeshayahu's "razi li." Faith in Hashem's hidden "machashavos" includes trust that a person can eventually be given a da'as in which what was formerly unbearable is understood and consoled - "הצרות ישובו נחמות." Until that da'as is opened, however, the secret remains secret. The believer does not manufacture an explanation for the hidden decree; he continues in emunah while leaving its resolution to Hashem.

This is a useful Izhbitz-Radzin complement to R' Tzadok's distinction here between the revelation that teshuvah always remains possible and the still-concealed order by which that possibility works. Chizkiyahu could reveal the rule "do not despair of mercy"; neither he nor Yeshayahu thereby possessed the complete map of how Menasheh, destruction, exile, and the Davidic chain would be woven into redemption.

Devarim 29:28: “הַנִּסְתָּרֹת לַה׳ אֱלֹקֵינוּ, וְהַנִּגְלֹת לָנוּ וּלְבָנֵינוּ עַד עוֹלָם, לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת כָּל דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת” — “The hidden things belong to Hashem our God, but the revealed things belong to us and to our children forever, to carry out all the words of this Torah.” In its plain sense the verse divides jurisdiction over sin: what is hidden is left to Heaven, and only the revealed is given to the human court to punish (Rashi notes the dots over “lanu u-le-vaneinu,” teaching that Israel was not held answerable for the revealed sins of individuals until it had crossed the Jordan and taken on mutual responsibility). R’ Tzadok reads “ha-nistaros la-Hashem” as the kivshei d’Rachmana — the hidden counsels known to God alone — from whose side the great rung of teshuvah operates, overriding the Torah’s revealed judgments with no true contradiction. Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Nitzavim 3, reads "הנסתרות לה' אלקינו והנגלות לנו ולבנינו... לעשות" as a direct rule for the boundary between hidden causation and human bechirah. A person may be tempted to say that a corrupt impulse did not truly come from him but from the spiritual atmosphere into which he was placed. The Izhbitzer answers from this verse: "ישתדל האדם לבער הרע מקרבו ולבדוק עד מקום שידו מגעת בנגלות, והשי"ת יעזור לו בנסתרות" - the human task is to uproot evil as far as his hand reaches in the revealed realm; Hashem will deal with and help him in the hidden realm.

This is one of the clearest guardrails for reading the present se'if and, more broadly, the Izhbitz-Radzin discussions of foreknowledge and choice. Only Hashem can disclose afterward how the hidden dimension was woven through the story. Thus "razi li" protects, rather than dissolves, the boundary of halachic responsibility.

paragraphs.text:
Berachos 10a: the Gemara recounts that when Yeshayahu told the ailing Chizkiyahu “you shall die and not live” — because he had not fulfilled the mitzvah of procreation — Chizkiyahu explained that he had foreseen through ruach hakodesh that unworthy children (Menasheh) would issue from him. Yeshayahu answered: “bahadei kivshei d’Rachmana lamah lach — why do you involve yourself with the secret counsels of the Merciful One? What you are commanded, you must do; and what is pleasing before the Holy One, let Him do.” R’ Tzadok builds his whole se’if on this: the very existence of a Menasheh is from the kivshei d’Rachmana, and therefore his teshuvah and rectification are likewise from that hidden secret — so that teshuvah’s “overriding” of the Torah’s judgments is no contradiction, but a matter reserved to God alone, to be revealed in the future. The Chassidic application of "בהדי כבשי דרחמנא למה לך" is especially important because it prevents a deterministic misreading of the entire discussion. The revealed command to Chizkiyahu was peru u'revu; his knowledge of a future Menasheh did not allow him to calculate his way out of that command. R' Tzadok states the principle in Tzidkas HaTzadik §78 with exceptional force: had Menasheh not been born, the entire holy chain culminating in Mashiach ben David would, God forbid, have been lost - even though Menasheh stood among those whom the revealed Mishnah lists as having no share in the World to Come. The hidden good of a future outcome is therefore not something a person can calculate in advance.

This is fully consonant with the Mei HaShiloach on Nitzavim cited above: the hidden things belong to Hashem, while man's obligation is to work within the revealed Torah. The paradox is deliberate. Divine foreknowledge can contain a redemptive end that prophecy itself does not encompass, while human bechirah remains accountable precisely because the person is commanded to act only on the revealed word.

Shabbos 89b: “‘Though your sins be like shanim scarlet, they shall be white as snow’ (Yeshayah 1:18) — Rabbi Yitzchak said: read ka-shanim like the years shanim that are ordered and come from the six days of creation, yet ‘they shall be white as snow.’” R’ Tzadok: sins that are, in truth, “ordered from the six days of creation” (from the kivshei d’Rachmana) are, from the hidden side, no sin at all — hence utterly whitened. R' Tzadok's own Pri Tzaddik, Vayechi §4, gives a fuller explanation of this difficult derashah of "כשנים." On the human side, he says, a stain that has penetrated through and through cannot simply be washed away: "מצד האדם אי אפשר לטהר א"ע מהחטא." Therefore the promise "כשלג ילבינו" requires a purification from Hashem Himself, from the hidden supernal source. He then reads "כשנים הללו שסדורות ובאות מששת ימי בראשית" as pointing to that concealed root which will be revealed in the future. The whiteness is not produced by calling the red stain white; it is produced by a Divine purification that reaches deeper than the layer in which the stain took hold.

Sefas Emes, Purim 29:3, expresses the same transformation tersely: "אם יהיו חטאיכם כשנים כשלג ילבינו" - the sins are turned into merits, and the Purim reversal is a foretaste of the future, when the entire structure raised by Haman becomes the cause of his own fall. This offers a concrete model for R' Tzadok's language: the past is whitened when the very sequence that embodied danger becomes, through teshuvah and Divine reversal, the instrument of redemption. Again, the transformation is retrospective; it does not render the original wrong permissible.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Resisei Layla §42, cautions: “על ידי ההכרה שהכל מהשם יתברך הנה יוכל לבוא על ידי זה לקלות ראש ולפריקת עול ... ויחשוב אדם שיעשה כל התועבות וגם זה הכל מהשם יתברך” — “Through the recognition that everything is from Hashem, a person can come through this to frivolity and casting off the yoke ... and think that he may do every abomination, and that this too is all from Hashem.” He connects this error with Yeravam, while adding: “רק שהוא מישראל ויש לו תיקון אצל דורשי רשומות” — “Yet he is of Israel and has rectification among the expounders of allusions.” This directly parallels the distinction here between responsibility within revealed Torah and the hidden rectification known to God.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Yeshayahu’s “my secret is mine” marks this as belonging to the kivshei d’Rachmana, the hidden counsels known to Him alone. The light of teshuvah’s greatness was revealed through Chizkiyahu, but not the order of its working, which no creature can fathom. And since the matter is founded in that hidden will, there is no sin at its root — what appears to contradict the Torah’s judgments is only the difference between the revealed and the hidden.

p: (א), — שֶׁמְּקָרֶבֶת אוֹ מְבִיאָה גְּאוּלָּה לָעוֹלָם
that it hastens or brings redemption to the world,
וְזֶהוּ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת מִדַּת "מְבִיאָה רְפוּאָה",
and this is an extension of the attribute that 'it brings healing',
דְּאֵלּוּ שָׁלֹשׁ הַקּוֹדְמוֹת מוֹלִידוֹת עוֹד שָׁלֹשׁ מַעֲלוֹת אַחֵרוֹת
for those first three virtues generate three further virtues,
מִצַּד הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת וְהַמְשָׁכַת שִׁפְעָם
by way of the expansion and continuation of their spiritual influx;
כְּמִדָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל דָּבָר טוֹב
as is His trait, blessed be He, in every good matter.
וְהַגְּאוּלָּה הוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַתִּיקּוּן לְהַבָּא יוֹתֵר מֵרְפוּאָה
and redemption is the expansion of rectification for the future to a greater degree than healing.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּיָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בִּבְרָכוֹת (יז עַמּוּד א):
And that is based on that which is known from what was said in Berakhot (17a).
רְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנָךְ, וּמִי מְעַכֵּב – שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת
'It is our will to perform Your will, and what hinders us? The leaven in the dough and subjugation to the kingdoms.',
וְהַיְינוּ רָצוֹן הָאֲמִיתִּי הַנֶּעְלָם שֶׁבְּנֶפֶשׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי, זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
Which means that the true, hidden will in the soul of the Israelite, the seed of our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
אֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְשׁוּם חֵטְא
has no intrinsic connection to any sin whatsoever,
שֶׁהֵם רַק כְּהוּצֵי הַסּוֹבְבִים לְאָסָא
these sins being merely like the briars encircling the myrtle.
מֵרְצוֹנוֹת זָרוֹת הַנִּמְשָׁכוֹת לַלֵּב עַל יְדֵי יֵצֶר הָרָע וְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
arising from alien desires drawn into the heart through the evil inclination and the nations of the world.
הַיְינוּ מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שׁוֹכֵן בְּלִבּוֹ,
Namely, from his own internal aspect in that the evil inclination dwells in his heart.
וּמִצַּד אֲחֵרִים הַגּוֹרְמִים שֶׁלּוֹמֵד מִמַּעֲשֵׂיהֶם, וְהֵם הָאוּמּוֹת שֶׁשָּׁרְשָׁם רָע
and from external agents who cause it, as he learns from their deeds, namely the nations whose very root is evil.
וּרְפוּאָה הוּא לַחוֹלִי שֶׁבַּנֶּפֶשׁ עַצְמוֹ
And 'healing' is directed toward the sickness within the soul itself,
לְהִנָּצֵל מֵהַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה עַצְמָהּ,
to be rescued from the leaven in the dough itself.
וּגְאוּלָּה הוּא מִשִּׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת
while 'redemption' is deliverance from subjugation to the foreign kingdoms.
וְזֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא הַגּוֹאֵל הָרִאשׁוֹן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
And this is the spiritual rung of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who is the first redeemer of Israel.
וּבְעֵת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּתְקַן הַקּוֹדֵם
And at the time of the Giving of the Torah, when the past was fully rectified,
נַעֲשָׂה חֵירוּת לְגַמְרֵי מִמַּלְכֻיּוֹת וּמִיֵּצֶר הָרָע
there was achieved total liberation from the foreign kingdoms and from the evil inclination.
וְגַם מִמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד
and even from the Angel of Death, just as will be in the World to Come.
אֲבָל זֶה הָיָה קוֹדֶם שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא
However, this state occurred prior to sin,
דְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם לֹא הָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל חֵטְא
for the exile in Egypt did not occur on account of sin,
שֶׁהֲרֵי עֲדַיִן לֹא נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה חֵטְא
since the Torah had not yet been given such that there could be formal sin.
רַק הָיָה הֲכָנָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
rather it served as the preparation for the Giving of the Torah.
וּלְאַחַר הַחֵטְא, שֶׁיּוֹעִיל הַתְּשׁוּבָה לְהַחֲזִיר לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ
– Yet after sin, that repentance should avail to restore one to this exalted rung—.
זֶה לֹא הָיָה עֲדַיִן
this had not yet emerged.
כִּי הֲקָמַת עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
For the raising of the yoke of repentance was achieved through King David, peace be upon him,
וּמִזַּרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו הֵם הַמְגַלִּים וּמְעוֹרְרִים מַעֲלוֹת וּמַדְרֵיגוֹת הַתְּשׁוּבָה אַחַת לְאַחַת
and his descendants after him are the ones who disclose and awaken the virtues and gradations of repentance one by one.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר מִשְּׁלֹמֹה וְחִזְקִיָּה
as was elucidated concerning Solomon and Hezekiah.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 86b: “R’ Yonatan said: Great is teshuvah, for it brings the redemption nearer, as it says, ‘and a redeemer shall come to Zion, and to those of Yaakov who turn from transgression’ (Yeshayah 59:20) — why does ‘a redeemer come to Zion’? Because there are ‘those of Yaakov who turn from transgression.’” R’ Tzadok: redemption is the outward spreading of teshuvah’s rectification-going-forward — deliverance from the enslaving kingdoms, as healing is from the inner “leaven.” The Zohar makes the connection between teshuvah and geulah even more structural. Zohar, Nasso 4:29, explains that sin distances the final heh of the Divine Name from the vav; this separation is expressed below in the destruction of the Mikdash and Israel's exile among the nations. Consequently, "כל מאן דעביד תשובה, גרים לאחזרא ה' לאת ו', ופורקנא בדא תלייא" - whoever performs teshuvah causes the heh to return to the vav, and redemption depends upon this. It concludes: "הכל תלוי בתשובה... ואין הדבר תלוי אלא בתשובה, דאיהו שלימו דשמיה" - everything depends on teshuvah, for teshuvah is the completion of His Name. Thus the Gemara's language that teshuvah "brings the redemption" is not only causal in the ordinary sense. In the Zohar's language, the inner repair accomplished by teshuvah and the historical repair called geulah are two expressions of the same reunion: what is restored within the Divine Name is manifest outwardly as the return of Israel and the rebuilding of the place from which they were exiled. This also supplies a bridge to the earlier simanim. There the higher teshuvah was described as restoring the Divine Name "as before"; here the same restoration spreads out into history. The personal and national processes are therefore not separate topics. The inward healing of the relationship becomes, when it reaches its full extension, the redemption of the community and the world.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 17a: “R’ Alexandri would say after his prayer: Master of the Universe, it is revealed before You that our will is to do Your will — and what prevents? The leaven in the dough se’or she-ba’isah, the yetzer and the enslavement to the kingdoms.” R’ Tzadok: healing addresses the “leaven” within; redemption addresses the “enslavement to kingdoms” without. Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Talmud, Pesachim 104a:1, quotes this very prayer - "רצוננו לעשות רצונך ומי מעכב, שאור שבעיסה ושעבוד מלכיות" - and uses it to define the inner identity of a Jew. In explaining havdalah, the Izhbitzer says that beneath the external "form and garment" there is an immense holiness fixed in the heart of every Jew: "אבל באמת הוקבע בלב כל אחד מישראל קדושה עצומה." The se'or and the foreign rule obscure what is already present; they do not create a second, equally authentic will. This fits R' Tzadok's division exactly: the leaven is the internal obstruction that healing removes, while the kingdoms are the external obstruction that redemption removes. In both cases what emerges is not a newly manufactured Jewish will, but the will that was present underneath the obstruction all along. Sefas Emes, Pesach 27:2, places the two obstructions in one chain. The admixture of good and evil introduced through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge is "שאור שבעיסה," and "מזה בא כל הגלות" - from this comes the entire exile; therefore, he says, Chazal regularly place "שאור שבעיסה ושעבוד מלכיות" together. On Pesach the matzah represents a momentary Divine suspension of that admixture: before the dough could become leavened, the light of holiness appeared and Israel went free. He adds that the first Exodus is the preparation and continuing power for the last redemption: "יציאת מצרים שהי' ראשית הגאולה, בכח זה יכולין לעורר תמיד הגאולה." R' Tzadok's sequence - healing first, geulah as its spreading outward - is almost diagrammed by this Sefas Emes: the inner admixture generates the outer exile, and its clarification opens the road to redemption. Tanya, Likkutei Amarim ch. 14, gives the same point from the side of avodah. The beinoni can tell himself that he does not truly wish to become a rasha or be separated from Hashem, because of the hidden love "כמו בלב כללות ישראל"; even the lightest Jew can surrender his life for Kiddush Hashem, and ordinary sin occurs only because a "ruach shtus" makes him imagine that the act does not sever that bond. This is a useful Chabad parallel to the Izhbitz formulation: the deepest will belongs to holiness, while the obstructing layer is real and must be fought, but is not the soul's final identity.

The leaven in the dough” — the inner will of the seed of Yaakov is wholly for God, and the se’or is only the alien intruder; the Torah given at Sinai is what disarms it, so the hidden will can act unhindered.

paragraphs.text: Healing and redemption remove different obstacles to the heart’s will

paragraphs.text: The hidden will to serve God remains beneath the obstruction of the inclination and subjugation. Healing addresses the wound within the soul; redemption extends the repair into freedom from the external power.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Machshavot Charutz 11:2: “Likewise, someone who is wicked in actual deed is so only through the inclination; it does not come from his heart. As written in Berakhot: “It is revealed and known that our will is to do Your will; what prevents us? The leaven in the dough,” and so forth. This is also the well-known explanation of Maimonides in chapter two of the Laws of Divorce for “they compel him until he says, ‘I am willing.’” Although he sins in deed and is consequently called wicked, nevertheless “even the sinners of Israel are full of remorse.” A thought of regret in the heart suffices for someone to be called wholly righteous, as stated in Kiddushin. There is no Israelite sinner who does not regret for some moment after the pleasure has passed and the inclination is no longer inciting him, because of the depth of good within his heart. Therefore, “Even though he has sinned, he is Israel”: that depth of good cannot be severed from him.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Machshavot Charutz describes how the hidden good becomes recognizable: actual sin does not erase the depth of the heart, and remorse can emerge after the attraction has passed. This gives a psychological expression to Takanat HaShavin’s distinction between the true will and the obstacles surrounding it. Healing can therefore uncover a will that remains present, while the section’s further stage of redemption removes the external conditions that impede its expression.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: “Bringing redemption to the world” is the spreading-out of “bringing healing” — the later praises issuing from the earlier. Healing addresses the illness within the soul, “the leaven in the dough”; redemption addresses the enslavement to the kingdoms. This is the rung of Moshe, first redeemer of Israel — but that was before the sin, and the teshuvah that restores it afterward began only with David.

p: (ב) — וּמַעֲלָה זוֹ הָרְבִיעִית, אַף שֶׁשְּׁלֵימוּתָהּ הוּא לֶעָתִיד
And as for this fourth virtue, although its ultimate perfection belongs to the future,
כְּשֶׁיִּהְיֶה גְּאוּלָּה הַשְּׁלֵימָה עַל יְדֵי הַמָּשִׁיחַ מִזֶּרַע דָּוִד
when there will be the complete redemption through the Messiah of the seed of David,
שֶׁהוּא יְבָרֵר וִיגַלֶּה כָּל מַדְרֵיגוֹת הַתְּשׁוּבָה כּוּלָּם עַל שְׁלֵימוּתָם הָרָאוּי
who will clarify and reveal all the gradations of repentance in their fitting perfection,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּבָר הִתְחִילָה גִּלּוּי אוֹר מַעֲלָה זוֹ
nonetheless, the disclosure of the light of this virtue already began.
עַל יְדֵי זְרֻבָּבֶל בֶּן שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל שֶׁהוּא מִזֶּרַע דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
through Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, who was of the lineage of King David, peace be upon him.
וְהוּא נְחֶמְיָה בֶּן חֲכַלְיָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (לח עַמּוּד א),
And he is Nehemiah the son of Hachaliah, as is taught in Sanhedrin (38a),
וְנִקְרָא זְרֻבָּבֶל שֶׁנִּזְרַע בְּבָבֶל
and he was named Zerubbabel because he was sown (conceived) in Babylon.
וְהַיְינוּ לִהְיוֹת הוּא עִיקַּר הַגּוֹאֵל מִבָּבֶל
which is because he was the primary redeemer from Babylon.
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל פָּסוּק (יְשַׁעְיָה כז, י): "שָׁם יִרְעֶה עֵגֶל"
– And this is in line with what they expounded on the verse (Isaiah 27:10): 'There the calf shall feed'—,
עַל מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁגָּדַל עִמָּהֶם בַּמְּדִינָה
referring to the Messiah who grows up alongside them in their land.
כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּפְלָטִין דְּמִצְרָיִם
just as Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, grew in the palace of Egypt.
דִּלְעוֹלָם הַגּוֹאֵל הוּא מִגִּידּוּלֵי מְדִינַת הַגָּלוּת דַּוְוקָא
For the redeemer consistently emerges specifically from among those reared in the land of exile,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (לט עַמּוּד ב):
in accordance with what is taught in Sanhedrin (39b):
"מִינֵיהּ וּבֵיהּ אַבָּא נֵיזִיל בֵּיהּ נַרְגָּא".
'From the forest itself comes the handle for the axe to chop it down.'
וְשָׁם בְּעֹבַדְיָה הוּא מִינֵיהּ עַצְמוֹ,
And there concerning Obadiah, it was literally from Edom itself;
דְּהוּא לֹא הָיָה הַגּוֹאֵל רַק נִתְנַבֵּא עַל מַפַּלְתָּם
for he was not the redeemer, but merely prophesied over their downfall;
אֲבָל גּוֹאֵל בְּהֶכְרֵחַ לִהְיוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל וּ"מִקֶּרֶב אַחֶיךָ",
yet a redeemer must necessarily be from Israel and 'from among your brethren'.
וּמִתְקַיֵּים "מִינֵיהּ וּבֵיהּ" בַּמַּה שֶּׁגָּדַל שָׁם
and 'from the forest itself' is fulfilled in that he was raised there.
וּזְרֻבָּבֶל שֶׁנִּזְרַע שָׁם
And Zerubbabel was conceived there,
וְהַיְינוּ דְּעִיקַּר הַזְרָעָתוֹ הָיָה עַל יְדֵי מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל עַצְמוֹ,
meaning that the essential cause of his conception was brought about through the king of Babylon himself,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה
as they taught in Vayikra Rabbah:
פִּיְּיסוּ לַגְּדֻלַּת, וּגְדֻלַּת לַמַּלְכָּה, וּמַלְכָּה לַמֶּלֶךְ,
they appeased the court attendant, and the attendant appeased the queen, and the queen appeased the king to grant Jehoiachin conjugal visitation.
וּלְכָךְ נִטְפַּל לוֹ הַשֵּׁם זְרֻבָּבֶל
and therefore the name Zerubbabel was permanently attached to him.
וְלֹא הוּא לְבַדּוֹ שֶׁהָיָה נִזְרַע בְּבָבֶל
Now, he was not the only one conceived in Babylon,
שֶׁהֲרֵי כָּל בְּנֵי הַדּוֹר הַהוּא נִזְרְעוּ וְנוֹלְדוּ שָׁם
for indeed all the members of that generation were conceived and born there;
רַק שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר מַעֲלָתוֹ וְכֹחוֹ הָיָה מִצַּד הַזֶּה
rather, his primary distinction and power derived from this unique facet,
וְעַל כֵּן נַעֲשָׂה לוֹ זֶה שֵׁם תּוֹאַר הַמּוֹרֶה תֹּאַר מַעֲלָתוֹ.
and therefore this became his titular name indicating the nature of his spiritual greatness.
וְהַהַזְרָעָה רָצָה לוֹמַר שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתְחָלַת הַיְצִירָה
And 'conception' denotes the very root and inception of formation,
דִּיכָנְיָה כְּבָר נִגְזַר עָלָיו (יִרְמְיָה כב, ל): "כִּתְבוּ אֶת הָאִישׁ הַזֶּה עֲרִירִי וְגוֹמֵר",
for regarding Jeconiah it had already been decreed (Jeremiah 22:30): 'Inscribe this man childless, etc.',
אֶלָּא שֶׁבָּבֶל גָּרְמָה לוֹ, דְּהַגָּלוּת כִּפֵּר כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (לז עַמּוּד ב).
except that Babylon occasioned his forgiveness, since the exile atoned for him, as they stated in Sanhedrin (37b).
וְהַזְרָעָתוֹ הָיָה מוֹרֶה שֶׁכְּבָר פָּעַל גָּלוּת בָּבֶל פְּעֻלָּתוֹ
And his conception indicated that the Babylonian exile had already accomplished its atoning function,
וּמִמֵּילָא מַתְחִיל מִמֶּנּוּ הַגְּאוּלָּה
and automatically from him the redemption begins to unfold;
בְּאוֹפֶן דְּשֵׁם זֶה מוֹרֶה עַל מַעֲלָתוֹ, שֶׁהַגְּאוּלָּה נִצְמַח עַל יָדוֹ.
so that this name denotes his virtue: that redemption sprouted through him.
וְרָאוּי הָיָה לִהְיוֹת אָז גְּאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה
And it was fitting for there to have been a complete redemption at that time,
אֶלָּא שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ד עַמּוּד א).
were it not that sin brought about the impediment, as they stated in Berakhot (4a).

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 38a: “‘And the sons of Yechanyah: Asir, She’altiel his son’ (Divrei HaYamim I 3:17); another explanation: ‘She’altiel’ — that God was asked nish’al concerning the oath against Yechanyah’s line (Sanhedrin 38a itself does not say that a Heavenly Court was consulted); ‘Zerubavel’ — that he was sown in Bavel nizra b’Bavel. And what was his real name? Nechemyah ben Chachalyah.” R’ Tzadok: Zerubavel/Nechemyah, of David’s seed, is the redeemer who sprouts within the exile. Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Prophets, Zechariah 4:1, takes the prophecy addressed to Zerubavel - "לא בחיל ולא בכח כי אם ברוחי" - as a prophecy of the very end of redemption. He contrasts Avraham and Yitzchak, whose service shook the worlds through mighty human exertion, with Yaakov, who said "האלקים הרועה אותי מעודי" and would not make even a small movement until Hashem took him by the hand and led him like a sheep after its shepherd. That, the Izhbitzer says, is "נחלת יעקב": looking and waiting for Hashem's salvation with such complete dependence that one never departs from His will. "וזהו יהיה סוף וקץ הגאולה, שיתמעטו כל הכחות מפעולות אדם, רק השי"ת יעזור את בית יעקב" - this will be the end and completion of redemption: the powers attributed to human action will recede and Hashem Himself will help the house of Yaakov. Hence Zechariah's word specifically to Zerubavel, "not by army and not by strength, but by My spirit." This is an especially close Izhbitz-Radzin companion to R' Tzadok's choice of Zerubavel as the first disclosure of this fourth rung. Zerubavel is not merely a political figure who happens to arise in Bavel. His very prophetic sign is that redemption germinates where visible power is weakest, so that the redeemer's emergence from the place of exile becomes a demonstration that the saving force was hidden there from Hashem from the beginning. The point must not be read as passivity in the revealed duties of Torah; the same Ishbitz tradition insists that a person must do what is commanded. It is, rather, the final interpretation of the success: even the strength with which one acted is recognized as "כי אם ברוחי.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Et HaOchel §13): “it is known that on Tisha b’Av Mashiach ben David was born — and this is the oil that issues from the olive only when crushed; the yesod, the olive and its fruit joined to malchus, is oil, and therefore it alludes to chochmah.” This is §4-2’s “complete redemption through Mashiach of David’s seed”: the redeemer who “will clarify and reveal all the rungs of teshuvah” is born precisely on the day of the destruction, from the crushed olive — the wisdom-oil pressed out of the very lowest, so that the fullest revelation rises out of the deepest fall.

paragraphs.text: Yirmeyah 22:30 decrees against Yechanyah: “כתבו את האיש הזה ערירי ... כי לא יצלח מזרעו איש ישב על כסא דוד ומושל עוד ביהודה” — “Record this man as childless ... for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting on David’s throne and ruling again in Yehudah.” Sanhedrin 37b brings this as proof that “גלות מכפרת על הכל” — “Exile atones for everything”: “ובתר דגלה כתיב: ובני יכניה אסר שאלתיאל בנו” — “Yet after he was exiled it is written: ‘The sons of Yechanyah: Asir, She’altiel his son.’” Vayikra Rabbah 19:6 records the intercession through the court attendant, queen, and Babylonian king that reunited him with his wife, followed by their observance of marital purity and the forgiveness of his sins. R’ Tzadok reads the resulting birth as evidence that exile had accomplished its atoning work, so that the redemptive seed could emerge from Bavel itself.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 1:2: “The matter follows what is written in the holy Zohar: “Go for yourself—to put yourself right, to put your own level right,” and so forth. God was telling him that, although he was born to Terah, an idolater, in a place immersed in idolatry, he should not fear this. On the contrary, from that very situation he could advance and reach his level. This resembles “From there you shall seek the Lord your God, and you shall find Him,” which follows “The Lord will scatter you among the peoples.” Do not lose heart and despair, fearing that, God forbid, you will become completely corrupted. On the contrary, precisely “from there you shall seek”: the exile will bring about “when you seek Him with all your heart and all your soul,” and thereby “you shall seek and find.” So too, the blessed God told our father Abraham: “Go for yourself”—to put your own level right—“from your land and your birthplace,” having been born in a degraded, lowly place, “and from your father’s house,” Terah having been an idolater. From that very situation you can put your level right.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Peri Tzadik states the inward form of the movement illustrated by Zerubbabel: “from there” means that distance and exile can themselves awaken wholehearted seeking. Takanat HaShavin supplies a historical pattern for that reading—the place of exile can bring forth the very person through whom release begins. Both passages preserve a real process of change; the Babylonian beginning is not confused with the complete redemption that sin delayed.

paragraphs.text: A direct parallel is Beit Yaakov, Vayeshev 19:3: “אך אור מלכות בית דוד היה מאיר עוד אור מצומצם, זרובבל פחת יהודה היה ראש בישראל” — “Yet the light of the kingship of the House of David still shone in a contracted light; Zerubavel, governor of Yehudah, was the head of Israel.” He explains that the Second Temple’s earlier light was revealed during the sacred service, rather than fixed openly in the body. This directly illuminates R’ Tzadok’s real but incomplete beginning of redemption through Zerubavel. Compare Resisei Layla §21, specifically on Purim: “נס דפורים היה בהעלם מלובש בדרכי הטבע ... נס גמור וגאולה שלימה אבל לא היה בגילוי גמור לעין כל בשר” — “The miracle of Purim was concealed, clothed in the ways of nature ... a complete miracle and a complete redemption, but it was not completely revealed to the eyes of all flesh.” This is an analogy for a real redemption whose disclosure remains concealed. Chiddushei HaRim, Vayigash 2, describes the future completion: “שנראה למפרע שכל עניני הגלות היה לטובתינו, ויתברר איך ומה כל פרט ופרט” — “We will see retrospectively that all the matters of exile were for our benefit, and how and what every detail was will be clarified.”

rich.text: : “אך אור מלכות בית דוד היה מאיר עוד אור מצומצם, זרובבל פחת יהודה היה ראש בישראל” — “Yet the light of the kingship of the House of David still shone in a contracted light; Zerubavel, governor of Yehudah, was the head of Israel.” He explains that the Second Temple’s earlier light was revealed during the sacred service, rather than fixed openly in the body. This directly illuminates R’ Tzadok’s real but incomplete beginning of redemption through Zerubavel. Compare

paragraphs.text: Berachos 4a: “ראויים היו ישראל ליעשות להם נס בימי עזרא כדרך שנעשה להם בימי יהושע בן נון, אלא שגרם החטא” — “Israel were worthy that a miracle be performed for them in Ezra’s days, as one was performed for them in the days of Yehoshua bin Nun, but sin caused its prevention.” This is the direct source for R’ Tzadok’s qualification that the return associated with Zerubavel was fit to become a complete redemption but did not attain that completion because of sin.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The completion of this fourth level awaits Mashiach, yet its light already began with Zerubavel of David’s seed — “sown in Bavel,” the redeemer from within the place of exile. Redeemers are always raised among the great ones of the land of exile, as Moshe was in Pharaoh’s palace. A complete redemption would fittingly have come then, but the sin caused otherwise.

p: (ג), — וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הִתְחִיל אָז עִנְיַן גְּאוּלָּה עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה
Nonetheless, there began at that point the dynamic of redemption through repentance,
דִּגְאוּלַּת מִצְרַיִם לֹא הָיְתָה עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה כְּלָל
for the Exodus from Egypt was not through repentance at all.
רַק עַל יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁרָאָה שֶׁעֲתִידִים לְקַבֵּל הַתּוֹרָה
rather solely because He foresaw that they were destined to receive the Torah.
וְכֵן נָתַן לָהֶם שְׁתֵּי מִצְווֹת – דַּם פֶּסַח וְדַם מִילָה שֶׁיָּגֵנּוּ עֲלֵיהֶם
And likewise He granted them two commandments—the blood of the Passover lamb and the blood of circumcision—to shield them.
כִּי עִיקַּר הַגָּלוּת גַּם כֵּן הָיָה רַק בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה
For the primary purpose of the exile was also exclusively for this,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ה עַמּוּד א):
as they taught in Berakhot (5a).
שֶׁמַּתְּנַת הַתּוֹרָה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי יִסּוּרִין, וְהֵם יִסּוּרֵי גָּלוּת מִצְרָיִם
that the gift of the Torah was conferred through suffering, and those were the afflictions of the Egyptian exile.
אֲבָל גָּלוּת בָּבֶל הוּא גָּלוּת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁהָיְתָה בִּשְׁבִיל הַחֵטְא
However, the Babylonian exile was the first exile that occurred on account of sin.
וּגְאוּלָתוֹ הוּא גְּאוּלָּה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁהָיְתָה עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמְּבִיאָה גְּאוּלָּה
and its redemption was the first redemption brought about through repentance, which ushers in redemption.
וְזֶה נֶגֶד מִדַּת הַנֶּצַח, הַיְינוּ נִיצּוּחַ,
And this corresponds to the attribute of Netzach, which denotes victory/conquest,
שֶׁכָּל גְּאוּלָּה הוּא נִיצּוּחַ הָאוּמָּה הַמְשַׁעְבֶּדֶת
for every redemption is the conquest over the subjugating empire.
שֶׁכָּל כֹּחַ שִׁעְבּוּדָהּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִצַּד הַחֵטְא שֶׁהוּא בַּפּוֹעַל
since the empire's entire power to subjugate Israel stems from the sin that was committed in actuality.
וְעַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמְּתַקֵּן מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא לְבַד
And through repentance that rectifies from this point forward alone,
דְּנִתְבַּטֵּל מַעֲשֵׂה הַחֵטְא בַּפּוֹעַל אַף שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַן הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דִּלְמַפְרֵעַ,
wherein the actual sinful deed is nullified in practice even though the retroactive root has not been rectified,
וַעֲדַיִן אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיַּחֲזוֹר לְקִלְקוּלוֹ,
and it remains possible that he could revert to his corruption,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה אָז שֶׁגָּלוּ שֵׁנִית
just as indeed occurred then when they were exiled a second time;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד כֹּחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה בְּתִיקּוּן דִּלְהַבָּא
nonetheless, through the power of repentance in rectifying for the future,
שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר בְּסִימָן א בְּהַבָּאַת רְפוּאָה
as was elucidated in Section 1 regarding the bringing of healing,
דְּהוּא גַּם כֵּן אַף שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַן בְּהֶחְלֵט
that it operates even if the root was not definitively corrected.
הָכִי נַמֵּי הֲבָאַת גְּאוּלָּה עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה
so too does the bringing of redemption operate along these same lines.
כִּי אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַבִּיט בָּזֶה אֶלָּא עַל מַה שֶּׁהוּא אוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה
For Hashem, blessed be He, looks in this regard only upon a person's standing at that very moment;
רַק צָרִיךְ לָזֶה תְּשׁוּבָה בְּתוֹקֶף יוֹתֵר שֶׁיּוֹעִיל לְנַצֵּחַ הָאוּמָּה
only that this requires a more potent repentance to prevail over the oppressing nation.
שֶׁכְּבָר נִמְסְרוּ לְיָדָן בְּסִבַּת הַחֵטְא
since they had already been handed over into their power on account of the sin.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עַל דֶּרֶךְ: "עֲבֵירָה גּוֹרֶרֶת עֲבֵירָה" וּ"בָּא לִיטַּמֵּא פּוֹתְחִין לוֹ",
For this operates on the principle: 'one sin draws another sin' and 'he who comes to defile himself, an opening is made for him',
שֶׁהֲרֵי שִׁעְבּוּדָם גּוֹרֵם לַחֲטוֹא עוֹד יוֹתֵר
since their subjugation causes them to sin even further,
וְזֶה מִצַּד שֶׁנִּכְתַּם הֶעָווֹן
and this is because the iniquity became so deeply ingrained.
עַד שֶׁפָּעַל כְּבָר גְּזֵירַת הַגָּלוּת עַל יָדוֹ וְהִמְצִיא הַגְּזֵירָה לַפּוֹעַל
that it already effected the decree of exile through it and brought the decree into actualization.
וְאִם כֵּן, אֲפִילּוּ יוֹעִיל לְרַפֵּא עַצְמָם
If so, even if repentance avails to heal themselves internally,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כֵּיוָן שֶׁכְּבָר נִמְסְרוּ לְאוֹתָהּ אוּמָּה
nevertheless, since they have already been delivered into the hands of that empire,
צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָהֶם עוֹד זְכוּת עַל זֶה
they must possess an additional merit for this,
שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ הַמִּשְׁפָּט לְהוֹצִיא בִּלְעוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתָהּ אוּמָּה מִתּוֹךְ פִּיהָ.
so that strict justice dictates that the swallowed prey of that nation be extracted from its mouth.
וְאָמְרוּ בִּפְסָחִים (קיח עַמּוּד ב):
And they said in Pesachim (118b):
דִּכְלוּם יֵשׁ עֶבֶד שֶׁרַבּוֹ נוֹתֵן לוֹ מַתָּנָה וְחוֹזֵר וְנוֹטְלָהּ מִמֶּנּוּ?
'Is there any servant whose master gives him a gift and then turns around and reclaims it from him?',
וְאַף דְּגָלוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל חָלִילָה לֹא הָיָה דֶּרֶךְ מַתָּנָה כְּלָל כְּהַאי דְּהָתָם
And though Israel's exile was, Heaven forbid, not at all by way of a gift as in that case there,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֲרֵי לְפִי שָׁעָה מִיהַת נִגְזַר לִהְיוֹת תַּחַת יָדָם
nevertheless, at least temporarily it was decreed that they be under their hand;
וְצָרִיךְ עַל זֶה מִשְׁפָּט בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְנַצְּחָם וְלָצֵאת מִתַּחַת יָדָם
and this demands a distinct judicial verdict to enable them to conquer them and escape from their control.
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כֹּחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה בְּתִיקּוּנָהּ דִּלְהַבָּא
and this is achieved through the expansion of the power of repentance in its forward rectification.
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתְּשׁוּבָה דְּהוּא הַחֲרָטָה מֵהַחֵטְא וּשְׁמִירָה מִמֶּנּוּ לְהַבָּא
And the root of repentance, which is remorse over the sin and vigilance against it in the future—,
הִנֵּה קַבָּלַת הַשְּׁמִירָה מִגּוּף הַחֵטְא עַצְמוֹ מֵבִיא רְפוּאָה לְמַכַּת הַחֵטְא
the acceptance of vigilance against the core transgression itself brings healing to the wound of sin,
וְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתוֹ הוּא קַבָּלַת גְּדֵרִים וּסְיָיגִים עַל עֶצֶם הַדָּבָר שֶׁסְּבִיבוֹת הַחֵטְא
while its expansion consists of adopting safeguards and protective fences around the periphery of the sin,
שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹא לִידֵי חֵטְא
– so that one does not come near to sin—,
זֶהוּ הַגּוֹרֵם גְּאוּלָּה וְנִיצּוּחַ לָאוּמָּה הַמְשַׁעְבֶּדֶת
and this is what effects redemption and victory over the subjugating empire.
בִּהְיוֹתוֹ מִתְרַחֵק עַל יְדֵי זֶה מֵהַחֵטְא לְגַמְרֵי
inasmuch as he distances himself through this from the sin entirely.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §9): “as soon as Moshe Rabbeinu came and aroused them, they immediately believed in Hashem — and by the merit of emunah they were redeemed; that is, through this the light was aroused, little by little, within their hearts, until they merited to go out from darkness to a great light, for emunah is the beginning of the apprehension of the light of His Shechinah.” This is §4-3’s ruling that “the Egyptian redemption was not through teshuvah at all”: it turned on faith, not repentance — the bare belief that opened them to the light of the Torah they were “yet to receive,” redemption granted on the credit of a will not yet acted upon. Sefas Emes, Shemos 15:5, gives a particularly apt explanation of the faith that preceded the Egyptian redemption. On "ויאמן העם וישמעו" he asks why the verse does not first say that they heard and only then believed. He answers that this is like Israel's "נעשה ונשמע": the good middah is already rooted in Jewish souls, and it accompanies them even in exile, only there it exists in the form of emunah. "גם קודם השמיעה היו מאמינים ומצפים לישועת ה'... רק בגלות עיקר העבודה באמונה" - even before the hearing they believed and waited for Hashem's salvation; in exile the essential avodah is faith. After redemption that hidden quality becomes revealed action. This sharply illuminates R' Tzadok's distinction here between the redemption from Egypt and the later redemptions that follow sin and require teshuvah. Egypt was the birth of the nation before the Torah's regime of transgression and repair had been established. What existed was the latent holy orientation of Israel expressed as faith and expectation; the Exodus carried that hidden emunah into revelation, preparing "na'aseh ve-nishma" at Sinai. In this sense the first geulah is not yet the fruit of teshuvah but the revelation of the root from which later teshuvah becomes possible.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §79): “As the Sages said, that He gave them the blood of the Pesach and the blood of circumcision so that they might be redeemed.” Exactly the se’if: the Egyptian redemption was not through teshuvah at all, but by the merit of two mitzvos — the blood of the Pesach and the blood of milah — given to shield them, for the exile itself was only a preparation for the giving of the Torah.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Likkutei Maamarim §11): “each one came to his particular holiness through the blood of the Pesach and the blood of milah — for from this comes the birth of yetzias Mitzrayim, that is, the emergence of the particular holiness into actuality; and these are the crowns of matan Torah, that each one had a crown and a special exaltation.” This unfolds §4-3’s “two mitzvos… to shield them”: lacking teshuvah and even deeds of their own, Israel were carried out of Egypt by the two bloods alone — the sheer birth of their latent holiness into the open — which then became the “crowns” they received when the Torah was given.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 5a: “Three good gifts the Holy One gave Israel, and all of them only through sufferings: Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come.” R’ Tzadok: the Egyptian exile’s sufferings were the “birth-pangs” of the gift of Torah — not a punishment for sin (there being no Torah yet to transgress) — unlike the Bavel exile, the first to come for sin.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 118b: God tells the angel of the sea, “פלוט אותן ליבשה” — “Cast them out onto dry land.” The sea answers: “כלום יש עבד שנותן לו רבו מתנה וחוזר ונוטל ממנו?” — “Is there a slave whose master gives him a gift and then takes it back from him?” The gift here is the Egyptians surrendered to the sea. R’ Tzadok adapts the principle while expressly distinguishing exile from a literal gift: once Israel has been handed over to a nation by judgment, a distinct judgment is needed to release them. This is achieved by the extension of repentance’s repair for the future.

paragraphs.text: Repentance extends from stopping a sin to guarding its surroundings. Repentance can bring real release before the past has been completely repaired. Extending restraint to the conditions around a sin prevents renewed descent and gives the work of return greater strength.

paragraphs.text:
Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Kometz HaMinchah 2:16:1: “It is known that the repair of character traits consists in raising them to their source. Then the repair of strength belonging to the shell is through strength in holiness: zeal against those who transgress His will. The repair of desire belonging to the shell is through desire in holiness: longing for God. Victory, however, comes through the opposite; this use of the same powers for holiness is for someone who has already won. So it is written in Tanya, chapter twenty-seven: it is only for a completely righteous person, whose foreign thoughts come to him solely from others; see there. Someone entering battle opposes his adversary: if the adversary lights a fire against him, he applies water and extinguishes it. But someone who has already won, and has taken possession, repairs for his own use everything the enemy made to fight against him, so that those same things serve his purposes.”

Explanation: Kometz HaMinchah distinguishes the stage of resistance from the later use of an opposing power for holiness. That distinction clarifies why the repentance described here requires safeguards even though it already brings a measure of redemption: Takanat HaShavin expressly says that the root of the past has not yet been completely repaired. The boundaries belong to the active struggle that prevents renewed sin, while a further transformation remains possible.

paragraphs.text:
Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 6: “It is written, “Through Me kings reign.” At the plain level it could have said, “Through Me there reign kings.” But this hints that the Holy One, blessed be He, appoints as king only someone who can first rule himself; that person He appoints over others as well. This accords with “Who is mighty? One who conquers his inclination.” Thus, “Through Me kings reign” means: someone who rules himself, whose intellect governs his desire, will then “reign”—he will be king over all. He need not attend to what opposes him, since his entire intention is for the sake of Heaven. This is “Melchizedek, king of Salem”: first he was a righteous king, ruling himself through his righteousness, and afterward “king of Salem,” which is Jerusalem. This is why Nisan is the new year for kings. It would have been fitting for it to be the first of Sivan, when Torah was given to Israel, of which it is written, “Through Me kings,” and so forth. But because it first says “Through Me kings” and afterward “reign,” one must first be king over oneself. This occurs in Nisan, when Israel restrict themselves to eating bread of poverty and accept the Creator’s yoke: eating dry bread without flavor from His hand, rather than delicacies beneath the yoke of flesh and blood. In Egypt they actually had much good, as it is written, “When we sat,” and so forth. Through this they “reign,” over the whole world. This occurs in Sivan through the Torah given then.”

Explanation: Mei HaShiloach makes inward self-rule a condition for the wider rule symbolized by kingship. His sequence from restrained eating in Nisan to Torah in Sivan gives an illuminating form to Takanat HaShavin’s movement from governing the conditions of sin to overcoming an external power. Both passages locate freedom in accepting divine service and ordering desire, with the wider victory growing from that inward work.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The Egyptian redemption came not through teshuvah at all, but by the merit of two mitzvos; Bavel is the first exile that came on account of sin, and its redemption the first that came through teshuvah. This answers to Netzach — nitzuach, overcoming — for a nation’s power over Israel rests on the sin that stands in act. Once Israel were handed over, a further merit was needed to extract the swallowed prey, and that comes through teshuvah spreading out into fences and safeguards.

p: (ד), — וּנְחֶמְיָה הוּא הָיָה הָרִאשׁוֹן לְחַדֵּשׁ גְּזֵירוֹת וּסְיָיגוֹת חֲדָשׁוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
And Nehemiah was the first to institute new decrees and safeguards in Israel,
וְהוּא כְּפִי הַנִּרְאֶה הָיָה הַמַּתְחִיל בָּזֶה
and he apparently was the initiator in this.
וּכְנִזְכָּר בְּסִפְרוֹ קַבָּלַת אִיסּוּר מוּקְצֶה וּמַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן בְּשַׁבָּת
and as recorded in his book, the acceptance of the prohibition of muktzeh and commerce on Shabbat.
וְכֵן אַחֲרָיו כָּל חֲבֵירָיו אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה הֵם בַּעֲלֵי הַתַּקָּנוֹת וְהַסְּיָיגוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
And likewise after him, all his colleagues, the Men of the Great Assembly, were the authors of enactments and fences in Israel,
וְהִזְהִירוּ עַל זֶה בְּפֵירוּשׁ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּאָבוֹת: "וַעֲשׂוּ סְיָג לַתּוֹרָה".
and they expressly admonished regarding this in the three maxims they stated in the first chapter of Avot: 'And make a fence around the Torah.'
וּמוֹסִיף עֲלֵיהֶם נְחֶמְיָה בַּעֲשִׂיַּת סְיָיג דִּלְצוֹרֶךְ שָׁעָה
And Nehemiah added beyond them in constructing a safeguard for the need of the hour,
אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לְהִתְקַיֵּים לְעוֹלָם
even one not intended to endure forever,
שֶׁהֲרֵי בְּמוּקְצֶה הִתִּירוּ וְחָזְרוּ וְהִתִּירוּ.
for regarding muktzeh the Sages later permitted and repeatedly relaxed it.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קכג עַמּוּד ב): "בִּימֵי נְחֶמְיָה בֶּן חֲכַלְיָה נִשְׁנֵית מִשְׁנָה זוֹ",
And as they stated in Shabbat (123b): 'In the days of Nehemiah the son of Hachaliah this mishnah was taught,'.
וְהַכֹּל כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁרָאָה צוֹרֶךְ לִגְדּוֹר הַדּוֹר שֶׁלֹּא יָשׁוּבוּ לְכִסְלָה
and it was all according to what he deemed necessary to wall in the generation lest they return to folly.
אַף הוּא חִדֵּשׁ עִנְיַן חֲזָרַת קַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה
He also innovated the reaffirmation of the acceptance of the Torah,
שֶׁבָּאוּ עַל הֶחָתוּם בְּאָלָה וּשְׁבוּעָה לִשְׁמוֹר תּוֹרַת ה' כַּכָּתוּב בְּסִפְרוֹ.
in that they affixed their signature with an oath and a curse to observe the law of God, as recorded in his book.
וּמִבֵּית אֲבוֹתָיו לְמָדָהּ,
And from his ancestral house he learned it,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (תְּהִלִּים קיט, קו): "נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי וָאֲקַיֵּמָה וְגוֹמֵר",
as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 119:106): 'I have sworn, and I will perform it, etc.',
וְלָמְדוּ מִזֶּה בִּנְדָרִים (ח עַמּוּד א) דְּנִשְׁבָּעִין לְקַיֵּם הַמִּצְוָה לְזָרוֹזֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ.
and they derived from this in Nedarim (8a) that one may take an oath to fulfill a mitzvah in order to spur oneself on.
וְאַף הוּא קִבְּלָהּ מִזְּקֵינוֹ בֹּעַז שֶׁאָמַר : "חַי ה' שִׁכְבִי עַד הַבֹּקֶר",
And he too received it from his ancestor Boaz who said (Ruth 3:13): 'As Hashem lives, lie down until morning,'.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּסִפְרֵי (בְּהַעֲלֹתְךָ פח): לְיִצְרוֹ נִשְׁבַּע
and our Sages of blessed memory expounded in Sifrei (Beha'alotekha 88): he swore against his evil inclination.
וּבָא נְחֶמְיָה וּפִרְסְמָהּ לְעֵצָה זוֹ בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל
And Nehemiah came and publicized this counsel throughout all Israel,
וְכָל עִנְיָנָיו וּמַעֲשָׂיו הָיָה בְּעִנְיָן זֶה
and all his affairs and deeds were focused on this matter:
לְהוֹסִיף גְּדֵרִים וְזֵירוּזִים אַלְּהַבָּא שֶׁלֹּא יַעַבְרוּ עוֹד
to add fences and exhortations for the future so that they would transgress no more.
וְעִנְיָן זֶה דִּתְשׁוּבָה הוּא הַמֵּבִיא גְּאוּלָּה
and this dimension of repentance is what brings redemption.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר בְּעֵין יַעֲקֹב מִקְרָא דְּ"שִׁמְרוּ מִשְׁפָּט",
And this is what the Ein Yaakov cited on the verse 'Keep justice' (Isaiah 56:1).
עַיֵּין שָׁם בָּרִי"ף שֶׁהֵעִיר בָּזֶה
see there in the Rif (Rabbi Yoshiyahu Pinto) who commented on this.
וְנִרְאֶה דְּדָרְשִׁינַן עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא בִּמְגִילָּה (טו עַמּוּד ב)
And it appears that we expound this in line with what is taught in Megillah (15b)
עַל פָּסוּק (יְשַׁעְיָה כח, ו): "וּלְרוּחַ מִשְׁפָּט" – זֶה הַדָּן אֶת יִצְרוֹ,
on the verse (Isaiah 28:6): ''And for a spirit of judgment'—this refers to one who judges his evil inclination,'
פֵּירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י: כּוֹפֵהוּ לָשׁוּב בִּתְשׁוּבָה וּמִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִצְרוֹ וְאֵינוֹ הוֹלֵךְ אַחֲרָיו לַעֲבוֹר עֲבֵירָה, עַד כָּאן לְשׁוֹנוֹ;
which Rashi explains: he coerces it to return in repentance, subdues his inclination, and does not follow it to commit sin, until here is his phrasing.
וְדָבָר זֶה דִּשְׁפִיטַת הַיֵּצֶר הוּא הַמְקָרֵב גְּאוּלָּה
and this matter of judging and restraining the inclination is what brings near the redemption.
וּלְגַבֵּי קֵירוּב אָמַר לְשׁוֹן "לָעוֹלָם",
And regarding bringing near, the Talmud used the expression 'to the world',
שֶׁכֵּן סִיֵּים הַכָּתוּב שָׁם (יְשַׁעְיָה נו, ג): "וְאַל יֹאמַר בֶּן הַנֵּכָר הַנִּלְוָה וְגוֹמֵר",
for Scripture there concludes (Isaiah 56:3): 'Neither let the alien that has joined himself, etc. speak',
כִּי לְעִנְיַן הַקֵּירוּב מוֹעִיל לְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ.
for with respect to drawing near, it avails for the entire world.
אֲבָל גַּבֵּי "מְבִיאָה גְּאוּלָּה" לֹא אָמַר לְשׁוֹן "לָעוֹלָם",
However, regarding 'it brings redemption' it did not state the expression 'to the world',
וְגַם לְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב הוּא (שָׁם נט, כ): "וּבָא לְצִיּוֹן גּוֹאֵל" דַּוְוקָא
and that is also the wording of Scripture (ibid. 59:20): 'And a redeemer shall come to Zion' specifically,
וְכֵן עַל הַתְּשׁוּבָה אָמַר: "וּלְשָׁבֵי פֶשַׁע בְּיַעֲקֹב".
and likewise concerning repentance it states: 'and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob'.
כִּי הֲבָאַת הַגְּאוּלָּה לְגַמְרֵי הוּא תִּיקּוּן גָּמוּר עַל הַקּוֹדֵם גַּם כֵּן
For the bringing of redemption entirely represents total rectification for the past as well,
וְזֶה "לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי".
and this 'He has not done so to any nation' (Psalms 147:20).
וְעַל זְמַן הַגְּאוּלָּה הַשְּׁלֵימָה נֶאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים לב, יב): "ה' בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ וְגוֹמֵר",
And regarding the time of the ultimate redemption it is said (Deuteronomy 32:12): 'Hashem alone did lead him, etc.'
וְאֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת גְּאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה בִּפְדוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כְּלָל
and complete redemption in terms of spiritual redemption of the soul has no application to the nations of the world at all.
וְרַק לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
And only for the Messianic era did our Sages of blessed memory state,
דְּהַמָּשִׁיחַ יָבוֹא לִיתֵּן מִצְווֹת לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
that the Messiah will come to assign commandments to the nations of the world,
וְהֵם "בֶּן הַנֵּכָר הַנִּלְוָה"
and they are 'the alien that has joined himself' –,
לֹא שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר, דִּבְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכוּנֶּה
not that he converts, for then he would be called by the name of Israel,
וּבִכְלַל אוֹנָאַת הַגֵּר הוּא לִקְרוֹתוֹ בֶּן הַנֵּכָר
and it constitutes oppression of a convert to call him an alien,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (נט עַמּוּד ב) דְּאָסוּר לוֹמַר לוֹ זְכוֹר מַעֲשֵׂה אֲבוֹתֶיךָ,
as they said in Bava Metzia (59b) that it is forbidden to say to him: remember the deeds of your ancestors,
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ דִּבְבֶן נֵכָר מַמָּשׁ קָאֵי
so perforce it refers to an actual foreigner,

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef explains a positive purpose served by boundaries under concealment: they make a person’s connection with God perceptible in conduct. This illuminates Nehemiah’s practical program in Takanat HaShavin. Renewed commitment becomes particular acts of restraint that sustain the relationship during the work of return, while Rav Tzadok also retains the need to fit a safeguard to its generation and, where appropriate, to its temporary purpose.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 119:106: “נשבעתי ואקימה לשמר משפטי צדקך” — “I have sworn, and I will fulfill it, to keep Your righteous ordinances.” Nedarim 8a derives that one may swear to fulfill a mitzvah in order to spur oneself on, despite already being sworn from Sinai. Ran ad loc. explains: “מנין שדבר הגון הוא להשבע לקיים את המצוה ואפי׳ כשרים שנמנעין משבועה נשבעין הן בכך ... שהרי דוד היה עושה כן” — “From where do we know that it is a proper thing to swear to fulfill a mitzvah, and that even upright people who refrain from oaths swear in this way? ... For David would do so.” Ran does not deny all additional legal force: he expressly notes its force regarding bal yachel, while distinguishing sacrificial liability. R’ Tzadok traces Nechemyah’s public covenant of renewed Torah observance to this ancestral practice of strengthening future obedience.

paragraphs.text: Rus 3:13: “לִינִי הַלַּיְלָה, … אִם יִגְאָלֵךְ טוֹב יִגְאָל, וְאִם לֹא יַחְפֹּץ לְגָאֳלֵךְ וּגְאַלְתִּיךְ אָנֹכִי, חַי ה׳; שִׁכְבִי עַד הַבֹּקֶר” — Boaz to Rus on the threshing floor: “Stay the night… if he will redeem you, good, let him redeem; but if he does not wish to redeem you, then I will redeem you myself, as Hashem lives; lie down until morning.” In its plain sense (Rashi) Boaz swears to act as redeemer rather than dismissing her with mere words. R’ Tzadok relies on the aggadic reading (cited in the sefer as Sifrei; the extant midrashic locus is Vayikra Rabbah 23:11, and cf. Rus Rabbah): that all that night Boaz was assailed by his yetzer, and his oath “chai Hashem” was sworn against his yetzer — “he swore to his yetzer” that he would not touch her unlawfully. This is the ancestral root (Boaz → David → Nechemyah) of “swearing to fulfill a mitzvah” and to subdue the yetzer — binding oneself by oath as a fence against sin, the very counsel Nechemyah publicized throughout Israel. Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Matos 2, treats the very phenomenon R' Tzadok cites here - swearing in order to overcome the yetzer - as a specific Torah remedy for the moment when ordinary counsel no longer works. The Izhbitzer distinguishes the advice of Avos, "look at three things and you will not come to sin," which operates before desire surges, from the crisis "בעידנא דיצר הרע לית מאן דמדכר ליצר טוב," when the yetzer suddenly overwhelms a person. For that hour the Torah gives the counsel of neder: "חי ה' אם אעשה זאת לעבור על רצון השי"ת חס ושלום." He then cites precisely David and Boaz, "שליצרם נשבעו," and joins to them the nazir of Shimon HaTzaddik who swore, at the moment his vanity flared, to shave his beautiful hair for Heaven. This directly explains the oath as an additional safeguard when desire suddenly overwhelms ordinary counsel. Nechemyah’s communal covenant gives public form to the same practice of strengthening obedience that David and Boaz used within themselves.

paragraphs.text: Yeshayah 59:20: “וּבָא לְצִיּוֹן גּוֹאֵל, וּלְשָׁבֵי פֶשַׁע בְּיַעֲקֹב, נְאֻם ה׳” — “And a redeemer shall come to Zion, and to those of Yaakov who turn from transgression, says Hashem” — from Yeshayah’s prophecy of the redemption. The Gemara (Yoma 86b): the redeemer comes to Zion for the sake of “shavei fesha,” those who turn back from sin. This is the Gemara’s very proof (Yoma 86b) that “great is teshuvah, for it brings the redemption nearer” — the go’el comes because of the ba’alei teshuvah. R’ Tzadok binds the complete redemption to “shavei fesha be-Yaakov” specifically: it comes through the turning-from-sin of the seed of Yaakov, and “be-Yaakov” precisely — for “He did not do so for any other nation”; the complete rectification of the soul belongs to Israel and not to the nations of the world.

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: וְעַל זְמַן הַגְּאוּלָּה הַשְּׁלֵימָה נֶאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים לב, יב): "ה' בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ וְגוֹמֵר",

paragraphs.text: Devarim 32:12: “ה׳ בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ, וְאֵין עִמּוֹ אֵל נֵכָר” — “Hashem alone did guide him, and there was no foreign god with Him” — from Shiras Ha’azinu, of God’s lone guidance of Israel. Rashi: “Hashem badad yanchenu — He guided them securely, alone, in the wilderness, with no foreign god’s aid; and so is He destined to settle them, dwelling alone and secure”; “ve-ein imo el nechar — none of the gods of the nations had any power to display strength and wage war against Him” (cf. Onkelos). “Badad” bespeaks Israel’s singular separateness and security under God alone (cf. “am levadad yishkon,” Bamidbar 23:9). R’ Tzadok reads it of the complete redemption: “Hashem badad yanchenu” — Israel alone, with no admixture of the nations and “no foreign god with Him” — for the nations have no portion or existence in the ultimate redemption of the soul, which is “badad,” Israel’s alone; as against the days of Mashiach, when the nations still retain “some joining” so long as they have existence. Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Ha'azinu 5, comments on this exact verse, "ה' בדד ינחנו ואין עמו אל נכר," that in this world many created things can appear as aids to Torah - wealth, possessions, and the conditions that broaden the mind - "אבל לעתיד לא יהיה שום כח רק השי"ת לבדו": in the future there will be no power at all except Hashem alone. This brings the siman's final contrast into unusually sharp focus. The complete geulah is not only that hostile powers cease to rule; even helpful secondary powers cease to claim independent standing. "Badad" means that the redemptive order is experienced directly as Hashem's guidance with no rival or auxiliary power beside Him. Taken together with the Mei HaShiloach on Zechariah cited above - "לא בחיל ולא בכח כי אם ברוחי" - the Ishbitz picture forms a single arc. Zerubavel inaugurates a redemption whose secret is already that human force is not the final cause; in the complete future that truth is totally manifest, "ה' בדד ינחנו." This is why R' Tzadok can describe the fourth rung as a spreading-out of teshuvah: the same recognition that, after return, uncovers Hashem's presence within the individual's story ultimately expands until the national story itself contains no alien power standing outside His guidance.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Nechemyah was the first to institute new decrees and safeguards in Israel, and after him the Men of the Great Assembly, who warned “make a fence for the Torah.” He also renewed the re-accepting of the Torah by oath, a counsel he learned from David and from Boaz, who “swore to his yetzer.” It is this judging of the yetzer, and the fences that follow from it, that hastens the redemption.

sections.en: Great is teshuvah, for willful sins become as errors — or as merits

items.h: Great is teshuvah, for willful sins become as errors — or as merits
גדולה תשובה שזדונות נעשות כשגגות או זכויות.

p: (א), — שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוּ כִּשְׁגָגוֹת אוֹ כִּזְכִיּוֹת
that willful transgressions are transformed into inadvertent sins or into merits.
וְהוּא תִּיקּוּן הֶעָבָר בְּמַעֲשִׂים שֶׁיָּצְאוּ לַפּוֹעַל כְּבָר
and this is the rectification of the past regarding actions that have already emerged into physical actuality.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַהַגָּעָה בִּתְשׁוּבָתוֹ שֶׁבַּלֵּב
And through reaching in his heartfelt repentance
עַד שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ,
up to the very root of the soul situated in the brain,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
which corresponds to ascending up to the Throne of Glory,
מִמֶּנּוּ נִמְשָׁךְ וּמִתְפַּשֵּׁט גַּם כֵּן
from there is drawn down and expanded likewise.
תִּיקּוּן יְצִיאַת הַמַּעֲשִׂים לַפּוֹעַל
the rectification of the actualized emergence of those deeds.
וְטַעַם "כִּשְׁגָגוֹת" עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה מִיִּרְאָה
And the rationale for becoming 'like inadvertent sins' through repentance out of fear,
הַיְינוּ דְּהָוֵי כְּנִתְכַּוֵּין לֶאֱכֹל בְּשַׂר חֲזִיר וְעָלָה בְּיָדוֹ בְּשַׂר טָלֶה
is that it resembles one who intended to eat swine's flesh yet inadvertently partook of lamb's flesh,
דִּמְדַמֶּה בְּנָזִיר (כג עַמּוּד א) לִשְׁגָגוֹת לְעִנְיַן סְלִיחָה וְכַפָּרָה
which the Talmud in Nazir (23a) likens to inadvertent sins regarding forgiveness and atonement.
דַּהֲרֵי הוּא מִיהָא לְאִיסּוּרָא אִיכַּוֵּין
for he at least harbored illicit intent.
וְאִם כֵּן, אַף שֶׁנִּתְקַן הַקּוֹדֵם לִהְיוֹת נַעֲשֶׂה הַכֹּל זְכִיּוֹת
If so, even though the past is rectified such that all is transformed into merits,
דְּהַכֹּל רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְאֵין רַע כְּלָל כִּי "אַתָּה עִמָּדִי",
inasmuch as everything is Hashem's will and no true evil exists because 'You are with me,';
מִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם כְּשֶׁעָלָה בְּיָדוֹ זְכִיּוֹת, אִם הוּא לְאִיסּוּרָא אִיכַּוֵּין נֶחְשָׁב שְׁגָגוֹת
nevertheless, even when merits ultimately emerge in his hand, if he intended an illicit prohibition it is still deemed an inadvertent sin;
וְצָרִיךְ לְתַקֵּן כָּל כָּךְ לְמַפְרֵעַ,
and one must rectify so thoroughly retroactively,
עַד שֶׁיּוּכַל לַחְשׁוֹב גַּם כַּוָּונָתוֹ שֶׁלְּמַפְרֵעַ שֶׁהָיְתָה לִזְכוּת וְלֹא לְאִיסּוּרָא כְּלָל
until he can regard even his retroactive intention as having been for holy merit and not for forbidden transgression at all,
אַף שֶׁאָנוּ יוֹדְעִים שֶׁהוּא כִּיוֵּון אָז לְהָזִיד וּלְהַרְשִׁיעַ.
even though we know full well that he intended at that moment to act willfully and wickedly.
וְזֶה לִכְאוֹרָה נֶגֶד הַשֵּׂכֶל כְּלָל
And this seemingly defies human reason entirely,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּאֶפְשָׁרוּת לְהַגִּיעַ לְתִיקּוּן כָּזֶה כְּלָל
that it should ever be possible to arrive at such a radical rectification?!
דְּאֵיךְ נַעֲשֶׂה בְּנַפְשֵׁינוּ שֶׁקֶר לוֹמַר שֶׁכִּיוֵּון לִזְכוּת, וְהוּא הָיָה אָז חוֹטֵא וְרָשָׁע
for how could we fabricate a falsehood within our soul to claim that he intended merit, when in truth he was then a sinner and a wicked man?!
וּקְרָא דְּ"שׁוּבָה" שֶׁאָמַר בּוֹ "עַד ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ" (הוֹשֵׁעַ יד, ב),
And the verse in Shuvah which proclaims 'unto Hashem your God' (Hosea 14:2),
דְּהַיְינוּ עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
meaning up to the Throne of Glory;
מְסַיֵּים "כִּי כָשַׁלְתָּ", דְּהוּא רַק כִּשְׁגָגוֹת
concludes 'for you have stumbled,' which denotes only inadvertent stumbling;
אַף דְּהוּא עַתָּה מַגִּיעַ עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד דְּאֵין שָׁם רַע כְּלָל
for even though he now reaches the Throne of Glory where no evil resides at all.
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד כַּוָּונָתוֹ אָז נֶחְשָׁב לוֹ לְמִכְשׁוֹל עַל כָּל פָּנִים
nonetheless, from the perspective of his intention at that time, it is at least reckoned unto him as an obstacle.
רַק בִּקְרָא דְּ"וּבְשׁוּב" שֶׁאָמַר (יְחֶזְקֵאל לג, יט): "וְעָשָׂה מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה",
Only in the verse of 'And when he turns' where it states (Ezekiel 33:19): 'and does justice and righteousness,'
מְסַיֵּים: "עֲלֵיהֶם הוּא יִחְיֶה".
does it conclude: 'he shall live by them'—transforming them into actual merits.
וְזֶהוּ הַחִלּוּק בֵּין מֵאַהֲבָה לְיִרְאָה
And this is the fundamental distinction between repentance out of love and out of fear,
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּאַהֲבָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְ"קוּם וַעֲשֵׂה",
as is known that love is the root of active positive commandments ('arise and do'),
וְיִרְאָה לְ"שֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה";
and fear is the root of passive restraint ('sit and do not do');
וְעַל כֵּן "וְעָשָׂה צְדָקָה וּמִשְׁפָּט וְגוֹמֵר" מַשְׁמָע מֵאַהֲבָה
and therefore 'and does righteousness and justice, etc.' implies repentance out of love,
דְּעַל יְדֵי יִרְאָה הוּא רַק שְׁבִיתַת לֵב וָמוֹחַ מֵהִתְעוֹרְרוּת לְרַע
since through fear there occurs merely the cessation of heart and mind from awakening toward evil.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מְתַקֵּן רַק מַעֲשֵׂה הָאִיסּוּר שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה נֶחְשָׁב לְזָדוֹן
and through this he rectifies only the forbidden deed so that it will not be reckoned as willful transgression.
כִּי כָּל זְכִיּוֹת שֶׁל הָעוֹשֶׂה מִיִּרְאָה הוּא רַק מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צִיוָּוה לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן
For all merits of one who acts out of fear exist solely because Hashem, blessed be He, commanded to do so;
וְיָרֵא לְהַמְרוֹת צִיוּוּיוֹ, וּמִפְּנֵי כֵן הוּא עוֹשֶׂה
and he fears defying His command, and on account of that he acts:
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי, פֶּרֶק ט דִּבְרָכוֹת
and as they stated in the Jerusalem Talmud (Berakhot 9:5).
עֲשֵׂה מִיִּרְאָה, שֶׁאִם בָּאתָ לִבְעוֹט דַּע שֶׁאַתָּה יָרֵא וְאֵין יָרֵא בּוֹעֵט
'Act out of fear, for if you come to rebel, know that you are in awe, and one who fears does not kick.',
וְזֶה כֹּחַ הַיִּרְאָה – לִמְנוֹעַ מִלִּבְעוֹט
And this is the power of fear—to restrain from rebelling,
וְהַיְינוּ לַעֲבוֹר עַל רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
namely from transgressing the will of Hashem, blessed be He,
וְעִיקָּרוֹ בְּ"שֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה",
and its primary expression is in passive restraint;
וְגַם בְּ"קוּם וַעֲשֵׂה" הַיְינוּ רַק שֶׁלֹּא לִבְעוֹט בְּצִיוּוּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and even in active observance, it is directed merely toward not defying the commandment of Hashem.
וְאִם כֵּן, הָעֲבֵירָה, אַף דְּמַכִּיר עַתָּה דְּ"אַתָּה עִמָּדִי"
If so, regarding the transgression, even though he now recognizes that 'You are with me'
וְהַכֹּל הָיָה בִּרְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and all unfolded within His supernal will,
וְכֵיוָן דְּכָךְ רָצָה יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא זְכִיּוֹת
and since Hashem so willed it, it is fundamentally merits—
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא לֹא הָיָה מַכְנִיס עַצְמוֹ לָזֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן
nonetheless he would never have entered into this to act thus
אֲפִילּוּ הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ אָז דְּכָךְ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
even had he known then that such was the concealed will of Hashem,
כֵּיוָן דְּצִיוּוּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתּוֹרָה הוּא אַדְּרַבָּה לְהֵיפֶךְ
inasmuch as Hashem's explicit command in the Torah is quite the contrary;
וְנֶעֱנָשׁ עַל מַעֲשֶׂה זֶה
and one is penalized for this deed;
אַף דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה וְיֵעָנֵשׁ,
and though Hashem willed that he commit it and incur the penalty,
מִצַּד הַיִּרְאָה אֵין עוֹשֶׂה אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא לִבְעוֹט בְּצִיוּוּיוֹ,
from the vantage point of fear he acts solely to avoid defying His explicit command,
וְלֹא לַחְקוֹר אַחַר מַעֲמַקֵּי רְצוֹנוֹ וְלַעֲשׂוֹת דָּבָר שֶׁהֵיפֶךְ צִיוּוּיוֹ.
and not to probe behind the depths of His hidden will so as to perform an act contrary to His revealed mandate.
אֲבָל הָאוֹהֵב – כָּל חֶשְׁקוֹ וְתַאֲוָותוֹ לְמַלֹּאות רְצוֹן אֲהוּבוֹ
However, the lover—his entire desire and passion is to fulfill the will of his Beloved
וְלַעֲשׂוֹת מַה שֶּׁיִּהְיֶה לְרָצוֹן לְפָנָיו, בֵּין צִיוָּוהוּ בֵּין לֹא צִיוָּוהוּ,
and to accomplish whatever is pleasing before Him, whether He commanded him or did not command him,
שֶׁכָּל מְגַמָּתוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת דָּבָר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ לְנַחַת רוּחַ.
for his sole objective is to perform that which brings Him contentment.
וְזֶה מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And this is the attribute of Abraham our father, peace be upon him,
שֶׁקִּיֵּים כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִיתְּנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (כח עַמּוּד ב),
who fulfilled the entire Torah before it was given, as our Sages stated in Yoma (28b).
וּמַה שֶּׁקִּיְּמוּ שְׁאָר אָבוֹת הוּא מַה שֶּׁהוּא צִיוָּה בָנָיו וּבֵיתוֹ אַחֲרָיו
and what the other Patriarchs fulfilled derived from that which he commanded his children and his household after him.
וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה מא, ח): "אַבְרָהָם אֹהֲבִי",
And therefore Scripture declares (Isaiah 41:8): 'Abraham, My lover,'
כִּי מֵרוֹב הָאַהֲבָה כָּל עִסְקוֹ הָיָה לַחְקוֹר וְלִדְרוֹשׁ
for out of immense love, his entire occupation was to investigate and discern,
אֵיזֶה דָבָר יִהְיֶה לְרָצוֹן לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיַעֲשֶׂנָּה
what matter would be pleasing before Him, blessed be He, that he might perform it,
וְאֵיזֶה דָבָר שָׂנוּי וְלֹא יַעֲשֶׂה
and what matter was repugnant that he might avoid it,
עַד שֶׁעָמַד עַל כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ.
until he comprehended the entire Torah in its entirety.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 4:2): “this is the end-deed and this is the beginning-of-thought — Esav only said it in his heart, while Haman brought the decree out into act; and Kayin, and Gog and Magog, are likewise ‘the end-deed that was in thought first.’” This gives §5-1 its mechanism: every deed’s origin lies in the thought — “the end of the deed is in the thought first” — so when teshuvah “reaches the root of the soul in the mind,” it takes hold of the deed at its very beginning; the act that “already emerged into act” is rectified from the thought-root out of which it first came.  —  Verified source: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 4:2

paragraphs.text: Yoma 86b: “Reish Lakish said: Great is teshuvah, for willful sins become for him as inadvertent ones, as it says, ‘Return, Israel, unto Hashem your God, for you have stumbled kashalta in your iniquity’ (Hoshea 14:2) — ‘iniquity’ is willful, yet it is called a ‘stumbling’ inadvertent. But Reish Lakish also said: Great is teshuvah, for willful sins become for him as merits, as it says, ‘and when the wicked turns from his wickedness and does justice and righteousness, by them he shall live’ (Yechezkel 33:19)! — It is not difficult: here merits from love, there inadvertent from fear.” R’ Tzadok builds the whole siman on this ahavah/yirah distinction.

paragraphs.text: Yerushalmi Berachos 9:5: “עֲשֵׂה מֵאַהֲבָה וַעֲשֵׂה מִיִּרְאָה. עֲשֵׂה מֵאַהֲבָה — שֶׁאִם בָּאתָ לִשְׂנֹא, דַּע כִּי אַתָּה אוֹהֵב, וְאֵין אוֹהֵב שׂוֹנֵא. עֲשֵׂה מִיִּרְאָה — שֶׁאִם בָּאתָ לִבְעֹט, דַּע שֶׁאַתָּה יָרֵא, וְאֵין יָרֵא בּוֹעֵט” — “Serve from love and serve from fear. Serve from love — for if you come to hate, know that you are one who loves, and a lover does not hate. Serve from fear — for if you come to kick rebel, know that you are one who fears, and one who fears does not kick.” This is the exact source (parallel in Yerushalmi Sotah 5:5): it stands in the sugya expounding “and you shall love Hashem your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might” (on the Mishnah, “a person is obligated to bless over the bad as he blesses over the good”), the same passage that lists the “seven types of perushim” and crowns them with “the parush of love, like Avraham” (over against “the parush of fear, like Iyov”). Meforshim (Korban HaEidah, Pnei Moshe): fear is a real but lower rung — since fear restrains, one who genuinely fears will not “kick,” i.e. throw off the yoke. R’ Tzadok builds on this: fear can only still the heart from arousal to evil — “one who fears does not kick” — so it rectifies the deed (that the sin be reckoned only “as inadvertent,” not willful), but not the intent; the transformation of the past into outright merits belongs to love.
