paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Machshavos Charutz §5, on Shaul’s sparing Amalek’s property: “ואף על פי שהשם יתברך אמר בפירוש להחרים הכל חשב הוא זה על דבר עבירה לשמה לקלוט השורש טוב ממנו ... והתחכמו להקריב מהצאן לד׳ ... עד שאמר לו שמואל הלא שמוע וגו׳ הפצר פירוש הפצר הוא עקשות להתחכם יותר נגד הש״י.” — “Although Hashem, blessed be He, explicitly said to destroy everything, he thought of this as a transgression for its own sake, to absorb its good root. ... They devised offering the sheep to Hashem. ... Until Shmuel told him, ‘Surely, to listen,’ and so forth: ‘insistence’ means stubbornly trying to be wiser in opposition to Hashem.” The source describes a rejected inference from hidden good, sharpening the present distinction between the revealed command and a person’s attempt to act on a supposed hidden will.

paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah I §39 considers a proposed reason Nadav and Avihu did not marry: “או יאמר דלא נסיבו דלא חזו מינייהו בנין דמעלי כמו שהאמת רק בהדי כבשי דרחמנא למ"ל.” — “Or one could say that they did not marry because they foresaw that worthy children would not issue from them, as indeed was the truth; but what business have you with the hidden counsels of the Merciful One?” It then observes: “והנה הם לא הורו רק לעצמם עשו מעשה” — “They did not issue a ruling; they acted only for themselves.” That observation does not exempt them: “רק אי דרשינן טעמא דקרא משום כבוד הרב גם זה אסור וממ"נ חייבים.” — “But if we interpret the reason of the verse as respect for the teacher, even this is prohibited, and either way they are liable.” This parallel illuminates the boundary here: an appeal to hidden purposes, or a decision to act only for oneself, does not by itself override the revealed command.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: This is the rectification of the past, in deeds already carried out into act. Reaching, in the heart’s teshuvah, up to the soul’s root in the mind spreads the rectification down into the deeds themselves. “As inadvertent ones” comes through teshuvah from fear, which stills the heart but leaves the earlier intent standing — the difference between love, the root of “arise and do,” and fear, the root of “sit and do not.”

p: (ב) — וּמִצַּד הָאַהֲבָה יוּכַל לְהַכְנִיס עַצְמוֹ לְעִנְיָן כָּזֶה
And from the perspective of love, a person can enter into such a matter,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ "עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ" דְּיָעֵל
in the manner of 'a transgression for Heaven's sake' committed by Yael;
וְלֹא מָצִינוּ בְּפֵירוּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה מוּתָּר
and we do not find explicitly in the written Torah that such an act is permissible.
רַק מֵהָתָם הוּא דְּיָלְפִינַן
rather it is from that historical episode alone that our Sages derived it.
וְהִיא, מֵרוֹב חֶשְׁקָהּ וְאַהֲבָתָהּ לְהַצָּלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל
And she, out of the intensity of her yearning and love for the salvation of Israel,
וּלְבַעֵר צוֹרֵר וְאוֹיֵב ה' כָּמוֹהוּ מִן הָעוֹלָם
and to eradicate an oppressor and enemy of Hashem such as Sisera from the world,
לֹא הִבִּיטָה עַל הָעֲבֵירָה וְעַל הַזּוּהֲמָא שֶׁהֵטִיל
did not gaze upon the technical transgression nor upon the defilement that he cast into her,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּנָזִיר (כג עַמּוּד ב) שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה רָעָה הוּא אֶצְלָהּ;
as they stated in Nazir (23b) that this matter was an absolute torment to her;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הִפְקִירָה גַּם נַפְשָׁהּ בִּשְׁבִיל דָּבָר זֶה
nonetheless she surrendered even her soul for the sake of this outcome,
שֶׁחָשְׁבָה: אֲפִילּוּ אֵין שׁוּם הֶיתֵּר לְדָבָר זֶה וְהִיא תֵּעָנֵשׁ עַל זֶה
reasoning: even if there is no halakhic dispensation for this act and she will be punished for it.
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מוּטָב תֹּאבַד הִיא וְיֹאבַד צוֹרֵר ה' מִן הָעוֹלָם
nevertheless it is better that she perish and that this oppressor of Hashem be eradicated from the world.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה עָשְׂתָה אֶסְתֵּר
And in this very manner acted Queen Esther
בַּמַּה שֶּׁאָמְרָה : "וְכַאֲשֶׁר אָבַדְתִּי אָבָדְתִּי",
in declaring (Esther 4:16): 'and if I perish, I perish,'
הַיְינוּ גַּם עַל אֲבֵידַת הַנֶּפֶשׁ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
meaning even regarding the loss of her eternal soul, Heaven forbid.
עַל יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁעָשְׂתָה עֲבֵירָה בְּרָצוֹן לְהַצָּלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל
through submitting to a forbidden relationship willingly for the salvation of Israel.
וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁאָמַר שִׁמְשׁוֹן (שׁוֹפְטִים טז, ל): "תָּמוֹת נַפְשִׁי עִם פְּלִשְׁתִּים",
And likewise that which Samson declared (Judges 16:30): 'Let my soul die with the Philistines,'
לְשׁוֹן "תָּמוֹת נַפְשִׁי" אֵינוֹ מוֹרֶה מִיתַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְבַד
the phrase 'let my soul die' does not indicate physical death in this world alone,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִיתַת גּוּף לְבַד וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ תָּשׁוּב אֶל הָאֱלֹהִים
for that is merely the death of the body while the soul returns to God;
וּמִיתַת נֶפֶשׁ הַיְינוּ בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא
rather spiritual death of the soul pertains to the World to Come.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל פָּסוּק "תָּמֹת נַפְשִׁי מוֹת יְשָׁרִים" דְּבִלְעָם
just as I have written elsewhere on the verse 'Let my soul die the death of the upright' uttered by Balaam.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּמַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵי דְּאִינָשֵׁי
And it is well known to be common among the people to say,
דְּהַמְאַבֵּד עַצְמוֹ לָדַעַת אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
that one who commits suicide has no share in the World to Come;
וְיֵשׁ לוֹ קְצָת רֶמֶז לַדָּבָר מֵהָא דְּגִיטִּין (נז עַמּוּד ב)
and there is a subtle allusion to this from the incident in Gittin (57b)?
דְּשָׁאֲלוּ: אִם אָנוּ טוֹבְעִים בַּיָּם אָנוּ בָּאִים לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא
where the captive children asked: 'If we drown in the sea, do we attain the life of the World to Come?',
וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּכַוָּונַת הַשְּׁאֵלָה עַל הַהַטְבָּעָה עַצְמָם בַּיָּדַיִם
And I have heard that the focus of their question was concerning drowning themselves with their own hands.
כֵּיוָן דְּהָיָה לְהַצָּלַת נַפְשָׁם מֵעֲבֵירוֹת
even though it was intended to rescue their souls from severe transgressions.
וְשִׁמְשׁוֹן הֵמִית עַצְמוֹ לֹא לְהַצָּלַת נַפְשׁוֹ מֵעֲבֵירוֹת וְלֹא לְהַצָּלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל
Yet Samson brought death upon himself neither to save his soul from transgressions nor to rescue Israel from immediate danger,
רַק כְּדֵי לְהָמִית פְּלִשְׁתִּים הַרְבֵּה וְלִנְקוֹם נִקְמָתוֹ,
rather solely to slay many Philistines and avenge himself;
וְעַל זֶה הָיָה חוֹשֵׁב דְּאֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ דִּין מְאַבֵּד עַצְמוֹ לָדַעַת דְּאֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
and regarding this he reasoned that it was possible he would incur the status of a suicide who has no share in the World to Come;
אֲבָל נִתְרַצָּה גַּם בָּזֶה כְּדֵי לְהָמִית הַרְבֵּה מֵאוֹיְבֵי ה
', yet he consented even to this spiritual fate in order to destroy many of the enemies of Hashem,
דְּ"בַּאֲבֹד רְשָׁעִים רִנָּה" (מִשְׁלֵי יא, י).
for 'when the wicked perish there is jubilation' (Proverbs 11:10).
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר: "תָּמוֹת נַפְשִׁי עִם פְּלִשְׁתִּים",
And therefore he declared: 'Let my soul die with the Philistines,'
כְּאִלּוּ חֶלְקוֹ עִמָּהֶם יַחַד בְּמִיתַת הַנֶּפֶשׁ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם גַּם כֵּן
as if his portion were bound with theirs in spiritual demise, Heaven forbid, as well;
דְּלֹא חָשׁ לְכָל זֶה
for he paid no heed to all this,
כְּדֵי לִמְנוֹעַ חִלּוּל שְׁמוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
solely to avert the desecration of His Name, blessed be He,
שֶׁהָיָה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁתְּפָסוּהוּ,
which occurred through their capturing him;
וּלְאַבֵּד אוֹיְבֵי ה' וְיִשְׂרָאֵל
and to destroy the enemies of Hashem and Israel;
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי תּוֹקֶף הָאַהֲבָה לוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and such extraordinary sacrifice is possible only through the supreme intensity of love for Him, blessed be He.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Pri Tzaddik, Parshas Zachor §12: “וכמו כן יש לומר בענין רע״ק ורחב״ת שהיו מקהילין קהילות ברבים ועוסקין בתורה דאיפשר דלא היו רשאין מדין מאבד עצמו לדעת והיו צריכין להטמין עצמם ... רק רע״ק השיבו ומה במקום חיותנו אנו מתיראין כו׳ מפני שהרגיש בנפשו שנצרך שיבא לידו שתצא נשמתו באחד וזהו עיקר חיותו והתעלות נפשו כנ״ל. ... וממילא גם במעשה זו דהיה כעין עבירה לשמה היה הספק אם ע״ז בעצמו יגיע שכר לעולם הבא.” — “Likewise one may explain concerning Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon, who gathered public assemblies and engaged in Torah, that it is possible they were not permitted to do so under the law of knowingly taking one’s life, and should have concealed themselves. ... Only, Rabbi Akiva answered him: ‘If we are afraid in the place of our life,’ and so forth, because he felt within himself that it was necessary for this to come to him, that his soul depart at ‘One’; and this was the essence of his life and the elevation of his soul, as stated above. ... Consequently, even in this act, which resembled a transgression for its own sake, there was doubt whether reward in the World to Come would accrue for this act itself.” This directly parallels the present account’s willingness to surrender even reward, rather than treating an inner perception as ordinary permission.

paragraphs.text: Shimshon and the Plishtim — background: Shimshon (Shoftim chs. 13–16), of the tribe of Dan, was the last of the great Shoftim and a nazir from the womb (his mother so instructed by the angel), of whom it was foretold “he shall begin to save Israel from the hand of the Plishtim.” The Plishtim were Israel’s dominant oppressors in his day, and his superhuman strength was bound up with his uncut Nazirite hair. He judged Israel twenty years; Delilah, at the Plishtim chieftains’ bidding, drew out his secret; they seized him, put out his eyes, and bound him to grind in the prison-house at Azzah (Gaza). At the temple of their god Dagon, his hair regrown, he prayed “remember me and strengthen me only this once,” grasped the two central pillars, and cried “tamos nafshi im Plishtim — let my soul die with the Plishtim” (Shoftim 16:30), bringing the house down upon the assembled lords — “so that the dead he slew at his death were more than those he slew in his life.” On this the Sages (Sotah 9b–10a) expound his whole career, and rule that “Shimshon judged Israel like the Father in Heaven.” R’ Tzadok reads “tamos nafshi” at its depth: Shimshon feared he might be judged a me’abed atzmo la-da’as (one who knowingly takes his own life, who forfeits even his share in the World to Come) — for he died to avenge himself and slay God’s enemies, not to save his soul from sin or to save Israel — yet out of sheer love for God, to prevent the chillul Hashem of his capture, he consented even to that.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Divrei Chalomot §22: “והקב״ה ממתיק המר במר שכאשר מראה שיש בעשיית חטא כזה דבר גדול גם כן ועבירה לשמה הגדול כמצוה שלא לשמה (כמ״ש שם) ועל ידי זה נעשים החטאים כשנים וכשלג כמו שכתבתי במקום אחר.” — “The Holy One, blessed be He, sweetens bitterness with bitterness: when He shows that even in the doing of such a sin there is something great, and the great transgression for its own sake is like a mitzvah not for its own sake, as stated there, through this sins red as crimson become like snow, as I have written elsewhere.” This is the same Sisera/Yael setting; the comparison follows Nazir23b’s corrected conclusion, ‘like,’ rather than its initial ‘greater than.’ Izhbitz on exceptional action and the limits of bechirah. Mei HaShiloach I, Pinchas §2, is an unusually close — and deliberately dangerous — parallel to the category R’ Tzadok is discussing. The Izhbitzer distinguishes levels in which a person progressively exhausts his ability to escape a temptation, culminating in a case where, after genuine resistance, he understands the event as bound up with a hidden Divine will; he applies this to Zimri while simultaneously presenting Pinchas’s opposite judgment as valid and accepted by Heaven. The point is therefore not a prospective license to transgress. On the contrary, the passage dramatizes how little a person can know, before the fact, whether he has truly reached such a boundary of bechirah. This sharpens R’ Tzadok’s treatment of Yael, Esther, and Shimshon: an aveirah lishmah is not the ordinary suspension of halachah by subjective inspiration, but an extreme case of self-surrender in which personal benefit is absent and the actor is prepared even to bear punishment. The Izhbitz parallel is especially useful here because it places the question precisely at the fault-line between human choice and the hidden Divine ordering that can be recognized, if at all, only after the deed has been fully clarified.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: From the side of love a person can enter even an aveirah lishmah, as Yael did — a heter nowhere explicit in the Torah. Out of her longing to save Israel she disregarded both the transgression and the defilement it cast upon her, forfeiting even her own soul. Esther’s “and if I perish, I perish” and Shimshon’s “let my soul die with the Plishtim” are of the same order — a surrender possible only through the intensity of love for Him.

p: (ג) — וְעַל זֶה אָמַר בְּמִצְוַת הָאַהֲבָה (דְּבָרִים ו, ה): "בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ",
And regarding this Scripture states in the commandment of love (Deuteronomy 6:5): 'with all your soul,'
דִּפְשׁוּטוֹ הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ:
the plain meaning of which is as our Sages expounded:
לִמְסוֹר נַפְשׁוֹ וְנִשְׁמָתוֹ גַּם כֵּן בִּשְׁבִיל אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
to surrender one's vital soul and spiritual essence likewise out of love for Hashem, blessed be He.
וְהִקְדִּים "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ",
And Scripture preceded this with 'with all your heart,'
שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרָכוֹת (נד עַמּוּד א): בִּשְׁנֵי יְצָרֶיךָ,
concerning which our Sages taught in Berakhot (54a): with both of your inclinations;
דְּזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן מִמִּידַּת הָאַהֲבָה
for this too derives from the attribute of love:
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי, פֶּרֶק ט דִּבְרָכוֹת
and as they stated in the Jerusalem Talmud (Berakhot 9:5):
אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עָשָׂה יֵצֶר רָע טוֹב
Abraham our father, peace be upon him, transformed the evil inclination into good,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (נְחֶמְיָה ט, ח): "וּמָצָאתָ אֶת לְבָבוֹ נֶאֱמָן לְפָנֶיךָ".
as it is written (Nehemiah 9:8): 'And You found his heart faithful before You.'
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא הָיָה יָכוֹל לַעֲמוֹד בּוֹ וַהֲרָגוֹ,
Whereas King David, peace be upon him, could not endure it and slew it through fasting;
כִּי מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת הוּא תּוֹקֶף הַיִּרְאָה
for the attribute of Malchut represents the intense rigor of fear,
"מִשֶּׁכָּרַע אֵינוֹ זוֹקֵף" (בִּ),
'once he has bowed he does not straighten up' (Berakhot 34b),
וְהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּ"אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה
'", which is the spiritual rung of 'a woman that fears Hashem' (Proverbs 31:30),
וְהִיא מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה לִכְבּוֹשׁ יִצְרוֹ וּלְאַכְפַּיָּא
and it embodies the attribute of Gevurah to conquer one's inclination and subdue it;
וּלְפִיכָךְ מִצַּד מִדָּתוֹ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאַכְפַּיָּא לְגַמְרֵי דֶּרֶךְ כְּבִישָׁה
and therefore from his attribute's perspective it is impossible to fully overpower it merely by force,
כִּי עִיקַּר הָאֲחִיזָה בְּסִטְרָא דְּנוּקְבָא כַּיָּדוּעַ,
since the primary grip of the adversary is on the feminine side (Nukva) as is known.
הוּכְרַח לַהֲרָגוֹ לְגַמְרֵי וּלְהַאֲבִידוֹ מִמְּצִיאוּת
so he was compelled to slay it entirely and obliterate it from existence.
אֲבָל מִצַּד מִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה וְתוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
However, from the perspective of love and the burning yearning for Hashem, blessed be He,
יוּכַל לְאַהְפָּכָא וְלַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ טוֹב
one is capable of transmuting it (le'ahpacha) and turning it into good,
כַּיָּדוּעַ מִמְּשַׁל הַזּוֹנָה הַמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, קסג עַמּוּד א),
as is known from the parable of the harlot brought in the Zohar (Part II, 163a),
דְּעִיקַּר בְּרִיָּיתוֹ הָיָה בִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
that its very creation was rooted in the primordial will of Hashem.
וְכֵן בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ט, ז):
And so too in Bereishit Rabbah (Parashah 9:7): ",
טוֹב" – זֶה יֵצֶר טוֹב, "מְאֹד" – זֶה יֵצֶר רָע
'Good'—this is the good inclination; 'very'—this is the evil inclination;
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת "טוֹב מְאֹד".
for through its transformation it can become 'very good.',
כִּי עִיקַּר שֵׁם "יֵצֶר" הוּא עַל חֵשֶׁק הַלֵּב
For the foundational term yetzer denotes the passionate desire of the heart;
וְיֵצֶר רָע הוּא עַל חֵשֶׁק הָרַע
and the evil inclination designates desire channeled toward evil;
אֲבָל מִי שֶׁבְּתוֹקֶף אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
yet one who abides in the intense love of Hashem, blessed be He,
דְּכָל חֶשְׁקוֹ וְתַאֲווֹתָיו הוּא לִמְצוֹא דָּבָר לְנַחַת רוּחַ לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ,
such that his whole yearning and passion are to discover that which brings contentment before Him,
גַּם כְּשֶׁיִּזְדַּמְּנוּ לְפָנָיו חֶשְׁקֵי וְתַאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
even when the appetites and passions of this world present themselves before him,
אֵין צָרִיךְ לְהִתְגַּבֵּר נֶגְדָּם וּלְאַכְפַּיָּא לְהוּ,
he does not even need to struggle against them or forcefully suppress them;
כִּי מִי שֶׁלִּבּוֹ בּוֹעֵר בְּאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for one whose heart blazes with the love of Hashem, blessed be He,
כָּל אֲהָבוֹת אֲחֵרוֹת בְּטֵלוֹת לְגַבֵּיהּ.
all other competing loves become completely nullified in comparison.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָנוּ רוֹאִין בְּאַהֲבוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּמָמוֹן וְכַיּוֹצֵא
Just as we observe with earthly loves such as wealth and the like,
שֶׁמִּי שֶׁשָּׁקוּעַ וְשׁוֹקֵד לְמַלֹּאות אַהֲבָתוֹ וְתַאֲוָותוֹ בְּדָבָר זֶה
that one who is deeply immersed and diligent in satisfying his love and desire for this pursuit.
גַּם אִם יִמְצָא וְיִפְגַּע בַּאֲהָבוֹת אֲחֵרוֹת לֹא יִפֶן לָהֶם
even if he encounters other attractions along the way, he pays no attention to them.
וְאֵין חִלּוּק אֵלָיו בְּלֶכְתּוֹ לְהַרְוִיחַ מָמוֹן הַרְבֵּה
And it makes no difference to him when he goes to amass substantial wealth,
אִם אוֹכֵל מַעֲדַנִּים אוֹ לֶחֶם צַר
whether he eats delicacies or meager bread;
וְלֹא יַטְרִיד עַצְמוֹ אֲפִילּוּ רֶגַע מוּעֶטֶת בִּשְׁבִיל אֲכִילַת מַעֲדַנֵּי עוֹלָם
nor will he distract himself even for a brief moment for the sake of worldly fine dining
אִם יַפְסִיד עַל יְדֵי זֶה רֶוַוח הֶעָצוּם שֶׁשּׁוֹקֵד לְהַרְוִיחַ;
if he would thereby lose the tremendous profit he is striving to gain;
וְגַם כְּשֶׁאוֹכֵל אֵין לִבּוֹ פּוֹנֶה לְעִידּוּן הַמַּאֲכָל וּמִילּוּי תַּאֲוָה זוֹ,
and even while eating, his heart does not turn to savor the food's delicacy or indulge that bodily desire.
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלִּבּוֹ שָׁקוּעַ וּבוֹעֵר לְמַלְּאָהּ בְּתַאֲוָה אַחֶרֶת
so long as his heart remains consumed and burning to satisfy another overarching ambition.
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן בְּאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And how much more so regarding the love of Hashem, blessed be He,
דִּמְעַט מֵהָאוֹר שֶׁמְּאִירִים עֵינָיו עַל יְדֵי זֶה דּוֹחֶה הַרְבֵּה מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ,
wherein a little of the light that illuminates his eyes through this dispels vast darkness.
וְכָל תַּאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה מְאוּסִים בְּעֵינָיו לְגַמְרֵי
and all pleasures of this world become utterly repugnant in his eyes.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהָאוֹהֵב הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכָל חֶשְׁקוֹ לִמְצוֹא אֵיזֶה דָּבָר לַעֲשׂוֹת נַחַת רוּחַ לְפָנָיו
Rather, one who loves Hashem, blessed be He, and whose whole desire is to find any avenue to bring Him gratification,
הִנֵּה הוּא מוֹצֵא גַּם בְּתַאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה מַה שֶּׁיִּהְיֶה לְנַחַת רוּחַ לְפָנָיו
he discovers even within the physical appetites of this world that which will bring contentment before Him;
דְּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהוּא יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרָא דָּבָר זֶה וְחֵשֶׁק זֶה בָּעוֹלָם
for since He, blessed be He, created this physical entity and this natural appetite in the world,
וַדַּאי יֵשׁ בּוֹ צוֹרֶךְ וְתוֹעֶלֶת לִקְדוּשָּׁה
there is assuredly a vital purpose and utility in it for sanctity.
וְלִהְיוֹת לוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כֵּן נַחַת רוּחַ מִזֶּה
so that He, blessed be He, may derive sacred contentment from it as well.
וְזֶה כָּל עֲבוֹדַת הָאוֹהֵב ה' בְּעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And this is the entire divine service of one who loves Hashem amidst the affairs of this world:
שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ לְהִתְאַמֵּץ לְאַכְפַּיָּא
that he does not need to strain himself merely to suppress (le'akpaya),
רַק לְאַהְפָּכָא, שֶׁיִּמְצָא בָּהֶם דַּרְכֵי עֲבוֹדַת ה
'. rather to transmute (le'ahpacha), discovering within them elevated paths of serving Hashem.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם טוֹב
And this is how Abraham our father, peace be upon him, transformed it into good,
וְהוּא נִקְרָא "טוֹב מְאֹד".
and it is titled 'very good.'
כַּיָּדוּעַ הַמָּשָׁל מִבֶּן מֶלֶךְ שֶׁהָיָה בְּשִׁבְיָה בְּיַד אוֹיְבִים וֶהֱבִיאוּהוּ לוֹ,
As is known from the parable of a king's son who was held in captivity by enemies and whom they returned to him,
דְּיוֹתֵר שִׂמְחָה הוּא לְפָנָיו בּוֹ לְאֵין עֵרֶךְ מִמַּה שֶּׁשָּׂמַח בְּבָנָיו הָאֲחֵרִים שֶׁהֵם לְפָנָיו תָּמִיד
that the king feels incomparably greater rejoicing over him than over his other children who stand before him continually.
וַאֲפִילּוּ יִהְיֶה זֶה הַבֵּן פְּחוּת הַמַּעֲלָה הַרְבֵּה מֵהֶם
even if this returning son is far inferior in stature compared to them.
וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁמּוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל בַּעֲבוֹדַת ה
' And likewise, what a person extracts precious from the vile in serving Hashem,
בְּעִנְיְנֵי תַּאֲווֹת וְחֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
within the physical desires and delights of this world,
הַמְעַט בָּזֶה לְרַב וּלְ"טוֹב מְאֹד" יֵחָשֵׁב לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ.
even a small measure of this is considered vast and 'very good' before Him, blessed be He.

paragraphs.text: Nechemyah 9:8: “וּמָצָאתָ אֶת לְבָבוֹ נֶאֱמָן לְפָנֶיךָ, וְכָרוֹת עִמּוֹ הַבְּרִית לָתֵת אֶת אֶרֶץ הַכְּנַעֲנִי … לָתֵת לְזַרְעוֹ, וַתָּקֶם אֶת דְּבָרֶיךָ כִּי צַדִּיק אָתָּה” — “And You found his heart faithful before You, and made the covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanite… to give it to his seed; and You fulfilled Your words, for You are righteous.” The verse is from the great confession-prayer of the Leviim at the teshuvah-assembly of Ezra and Nechemyah’s generation (Nechemyah 9), which retells God’s kindnesses from creation onward — here, His choosing Avram, bringing him out of Ur Kasdim, renaming him Avraham, and “finding his heart faithful.” Meforshim: the “faithful heart” is Avraham’s steadfastness proven through his trials (the Ten Nisyonos). The Yerushalmi (Berachos 9:5 — see the note there) presses “u-matzasa es levavo ne’eman” one degree further: Avraham “made even his yetzer hara faithful good,” so that his whole heart — both inclinations — was faithful before God; whereas of David it says “ve-libi chalal be-kirbi” (Tehillim 109:22), that he “slew” his yetzer within him. On this rests R’ Tzadok’s contrast: Avraham (love) transformed the yetzer; David (kingship / fear) could only kill it.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 34b: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani reports Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s explanation: “הַמֶּלֶךְ — כֵּיוָן שֶׁכָּרַע שׁוּב אֵינוֹ זוֹקֵף, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְהִי כְּכַלּוֹת שְׁלֹמֹה לְהִתְפַּלֵּל וְגוֹ׳ קָם מִלִּפְנֵי מִזְבַּח ה׳ מִכְּרֹעַ עַל בִּרְכָּיו״.” — “The king, once he has bowed, does not straighten up, as it is stated: ‘When Shlomo finished praying … he arose from before the altar of Hashem, from kneeling upon his knees.’” The king’s continuous bowing supplies Rav Tzadok’s emblem of the submission of kingship; his application to David’s fear and the killing of the inclination is the exposition developed here.

R’ Tzadok invokes it to show the yetzer’s root is itself holy.

Is the evil inclination ‘very good’?! — Yes, for were it not for the evil inclination a man would not build a house, marry, beget children, or engage in commerce.” R’ Tzadok: the lover of God does not merely suppress the yetzer but transforms it — finding in the desires of this world themselves a means of serving God (“very good”).

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Chalomot §25): “through the tzimtzum contraction of desire, which is the middah of Yitzchak our father — ‘dwelling in the land of the Negev,’ dried of all the desire and craving of this world.” This is a parallel description of the restrictive pole of Divine service: Yitzchak’s contraction of worldly desire. It clarifies the contrast developed here between fear’s subduing of desire and Avraham’s loving transformation of that same desire into service.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The mitzvah of love says “with all your soul” — plainly, to give over one’s life — and prefaces it with “with all your heart,” which the Sages read as “with your two inclinations.” Avraham made the yetzer hara good; David, whose middah is the intensity of fear, could not, and killed it outright. From the side of love the yetzer is not subdued but transformed, so that through it a person becomes “very good.”

p: (ד). — וְזֶהוּ "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ" – הַיְינוּ אֲפִילּוּ בְּאַהֲבוֹת וְתַאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And this is 'with all your heart'—meaning even within the loves and desires of this physical world.
וּ"בְכָל נַפְשְׁךָ" הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּפֶרֶק הָרוֹאֶה (בִּבְרָכוֹת סג עַמּוּד א):
And 'with all your soul' operates in line with what is taught in the chapter HaRoeh (Berakhot 63a): ",
בְּכָל דְּרָכֶיךָ דָעֵהוּ" – וַאֲפִילּוּ לִדְבַר עֲבֵירָה
'In all your ways acknowledge Him'—even regarding a matter of transgression.
שֶׁהַכַּוָּונָה כְּעִנְיַן "עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ" הַנִּזְכָּר
wherein the intention points to the concept of 'a transgression for Heaven's sake' mentioned above.
וּ"בְכָל מְאֹדֶךָ", דְּקָאֵי אַמָּמוֹן כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (נד עַמּוּד א);
And 'with all your might (me'odekha)', which refers to money, as they stated in Berakhot (54a);
וְהַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן דָּבָר אַחֵר דְּשָׁם: "בְּכָל מִדָּה שֶׁמּוֹדֵד לְךָ הֱוֵי מוֹדֶה לוֹ",
and that is likewise the alternative interpretation there: 'with whatever measure (middah) He metes out to you, be thankful to Him,'.
דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר אֲפִילּוּ בְּעָאקוּ (בְּצַעַר) רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן
meaning even in acute suffering (tzá'ar), may the Merciful One preserve us.
וְעִיקַּר יִסּוּרִין דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא בְּמָמוֹן
And the primary suffering of this world is financial,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: חֶסְרוֹן כִּיס קָשֶׁה מִכּוּלָּם
as our Sages of blessed memory stated: monetary loss is the harshest of all;
וּמְפוֹרָשׁ בְּאִיּוֹב (לו, כא): "כִּי עַל זֹאת בָּחַרְתָּ מֵעֹנִי",
and it is stated explicitly in Job (36:21): 'for this have you chosen rather than affliction/poverty,'
וְיָדוּעַ דְּיִסּוּרֵי אִיּוֹב הֵם תַּכְלִית תּוֹקֶף הַיִּסּוּרִין שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר בַּמְּצִיאוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and it is known that the afflictions of Job represent the utmost apex of suffering possible in this world;
עֹנִי הוּא יוֹתֵר מִזֶּה
yet crushing poverty is even greater than that.
וְעַל כֵּן לְעִנְיַן עָאקוּ רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן נָקַט מָמוֹן
and therefore concerning dire affliction, may the Merciful One preserve us, the Mishnah cited wealth.
וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית בֵּירוּר הָאַהֲבָה
And this represents the ultimate testing and clarification of love,
כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַרְאֶה לוֹ כְּנֶגֶד פָּנִים מַסְבִּירוֹת
for when Hashem, blessed be He, displays a welcoming, shining countenance toward a person,
גַּם כֵּן אֵין הָאַהֲבָה רְבוּתָא כָּל כָּךְ,
such love is not so extraordinary a wonder,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם הָאוֹהֲבִים זֶה לָזֶה "כַּמַּיִם הַפָּנִים לַפָּנִים וְכוּלֵי",
mirroring the manner of human beings who love one another where 'as in water face reflects face, etc.',
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּסִפְרֵי (דְּבָרִים א, כז):
and as our Sages of blessed memory expounded in Sifrei (Deuteronomy 1:27).
מַה דִּבְלִבָּךְ עַל רְחִימָךְ וְכוּלֵי גַּם כְּלַפֵּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כֵּן
what is in your heart toward your friend, etc. so is it likewise toward Hashem, blessed be He.
וּבִתְחִלַּת כְּנִיסַת הָאָדָם לְמִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה
And at the initial entry of a person into the attribute of love,
אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵבִיא עָלָיו נִסְיוֹנוֹת עֲדַיִן
Hashem does not bring harsh trials upon him yet;
רַק אַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְבָּרֵר בִּשְׁתֵּי הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת דְּ"כָל לְבָבְךָ" וְ"כָל נַפְשְׁךָ",
only after he has already been verified in the two gradations of 'all your heart' and 'all your soul'.
אָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְנַסֵּהוּ בְּיִסּוּרִין רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן
does Hashem test him through afflictions, may the Merciful One preserve us.
וּבֶאֱמֶת "אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶאֱהַב ה' יוֹכִיחַ" (מִשְׁלֵי ג, יב),
And in truth, 'whom Hashem loves He rebukes' (Proverbs 3:12),
וְגַם זֶה מִצַּד תּוֹקֶף אַהֲבָתוֹ אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ
and this too proceeds from the sheer intensity of his love for Him, blessed be He,
רוֹצֶה כִּבְיָכוֹל לְבָרֵר שֶׁלֹּא בְּחִנָּם אוֹהֲבוֹ;
in that He wishes, as it were, to demonstrate that not without reason does He love him;
כִּי הֲגַם שֶׁהוּא מַרְאֶה לוֹ פָּנִים זוֹעֲמוֹת רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן
for even though He displays a stern, frowning countenance, may the Merciful One preserve us,
עִם כָּל זֶה הוּא לֹא נִיתַּק מֵאַהֲבָתוֹ,
despite all that he is never severed from his love.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת הָאַהֲבָה
which is the absolute pinnacle of love's perfection.
כִּי הוּא דָּבוּק בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבוֹ בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For he is bound in the innermost depths of his heart unto Him, blessed be He,
אֲשֶׁר "מַיִם רַבִּים לֹא יוּכְלוּ לְכַבּוֹת אֶת הָאַהֲבָה" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ח, ז),
where 'many waters cannot quench the love' (Song of Songs 8:7),
וְדָבוּק בְּמַעֲמַקָּיו יִתְבָּרַךְ אֲשֶׁר הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת אוֹהֲבוֹ.
and cleaved to His profound essence, knowing that He truly loves him.
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא כְּתִיב בַּפָּרָשָׁה שְׁנִיָּה דִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע "בְּכָל מְאֹדְכֶם",
Therefore, in the second paragraph of the Shema (Vehaya Im Shamoa) it does not write 'with all your might (me'odkhem)',
כִּי אֵין הַנִּסְיוֹנוֹת לַצִּיבּוּר וּלִכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
because such crushing trials are not inflicted upon the collective public and all Israel,
רַק לִשְׂרִידִים וִיחִידִים הַיְכוֹלִים לַעֲמוֹד בַּנִּסָּיוֹן
rather only upon select individuals capable of enduring the trial,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה לב, ג):
as our Sages taught in Bereishit Rabbah (Parashah 32:3).
שֶׁאֵין מְנַסֶּה אֶלָּא קַנְקַנִּים חֲזָקִים
that a potter does not strike to test any vessels except the strongest jars.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Eikev §19): "“though I walk in the valley of the shadow of death, I shall fear no evil, for You are with me” — the matter is according to what they said Berachos 63a on “in all your ways know Him,” and “He shall straighten your paths.”" Exactly the se’if: “in all your ways know Him — even in a matter of transgression” is the same verse by which one walks unafraid through the valley itself, because He is there too.

paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah II §34: “אבל דבר זה צריך להיות מקודם שהשמאל ואימינה שבכל מיני שמאלית יהיה הוא לימין אז יוכל לסמוך על עצמו גם לעבור על ד"ת” — “But this requires, beforehand, ‘if you go left, I shall go right’: in every kind of leftwardness he must be on the right; only then can he rely on himself even to transgress words of Torah.” The example is “כאליהו בהר הכרמל שמוחזק לנביא ומחזיק בימין צדקו” — “like Eliyahu on Mount Carmel, who is established as a prophet and holds firmly to his righteous right hand.” The passage expressly excludes “וחוץ מע"ז, רצה לומר שיחשוב לשם שמים אף שאין רצון השם יתברך באמת כך זה נקרא ע"ז” — “idolatry; that is, to think something is for the sake of Heaven when God’s will is not in truth so—this is called idolatry.” It then explains Berachos 63a’s “even in a matter of transgression”: “שימסור עצמו להשם יתברך אף לאבד גם כל חלקו מעוה"ב כשרצון השם יתברך כך וכמו ששמעתי על נסיון העקידה.” — “That he should surrender himself to God, even to lose his entire portion in the World to Come when God’s will is so, as I heard concerning the trial of the Binding.” The parallel illuminates exceptional surrender to God’s actual will, including surrender of one’s own reward.

paragraphs.text: Iyov 36:21: “הִשָּׁמֶר אַל תֵּפֶן אֶל אָוֶן כִּי עַל זֶה בָּחַרְתָּ מֵעֹנִי.” — “Beware; do not turn to wrongdoing, for you have preferred this to poverty.” Rashi ad loc. explicitly explains: “כִּי עַל הַיִּסּוּרִין הַלָּלוּ יֵשׁ לִבְחֹר יוֹתֵר מֵעֲנִיּוּת” — “For these afflictions are to be preferred to poverty”; and, citing Midrash Tanchuma, concludes: “כִּי נוֹחִין הָיוּ יִסּוּרֵי אִיּוֹב מִיִּסּוּרֵי עֲנִיּוּת.” — “For Job’s afflictions were easier than the afflictions of poverty.” This is the very comparative reading Rav Tzadok invokes to explain the special weight of loss of money.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 54a (Mishnah Berachos 9:5): the same Mishnah continues: “‘and with all your might me’odecha’ — with all your money mamoncha; another interpretation: with every measure middah that He metes out to you, thank Him exceedingly modeh lo me’od me’od.” Rashi: “me’odecha” is expounded “with all your money,” for there are people to whom their money is dearer than their body; and the “middah” reading — bless Him for the measure of bad as one blesses for the measure of good. (The Yerushalmi, ad loc., records both readings identically.) R’ Tzadok draws the §4 point from here: loving God “with all your might” means loving Him even in distress and loss of money — the ultimate proof of love, which is shown not when He “shows a pleasant face” but when one loves Him in his affliction; and these are the “sufferings of love.”

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 32:3: “‘Hashem tests the righteous’ (Tehillim 11:5) — the potter does not test flawed vessels, which he could not strike once without breaking; rather he tests strong vessels kankanim, which he strikes many times and they do not break. So the Holy One tests the righteous.” R’ Tzadok: the “sufferings of love” (the highest trial, “with all your might”) are given only to the “strong vessels” — the individuals who can withstand them — not to the community, hence “b’chol me’odchem” is absent from the second paragraph of Shema.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: “With all your heart” reaches even the desires of this world; “with all your soul,” even a matter of transgression; “with all your might,” one’s money. The essence of this world’s suffering is in money, and to love Him in distress is the ultimate clarification of love. These are the “sufferings of love” — brought only after a person has been clarified in the first two rungs, which is why “with all your might” is absent from the second paragraph of Shema.

p: (ה), — וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן לַנִּסְיוֹנוֹת
And Abraham our father, peace be upon him, was the first regarding trials,
כִּי הוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁבֵּירֵר מִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה בְּכָל תּוֹקֶף
for he was the first who clarified the attribute of love in its full intensity;
עַד שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה כַּנּוֹדָע
until he became the chariot for the attribute of love, as is known;
דְּכָל נִסְיוֹנוֹת מִצַּד יִסּוּרֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּרוֹב נִסְיוֹנוֹת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
for regarding all trials stemming from worldly tribulations, like the majority of the trials of Abraham our father, peace be upon him,
מִצַּד הַיִּרְאָה אֵינוֹ רְבוּתָא
from the perspective of awe/fear this is not an extraordinary novelty,
דְּאַדְּרַבָּה, יוֹתֵר יִרְאָה יֵשׁ עַל הָאָדָם כַּאֲשֶׁר רוֹאֶה מִדַּת הַדִּין חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מְתוּחָה
for, on the contrary, greater fear falls upon man when he sees the attribute of strict justice stretched out, Heaven forbid,
שֶׁהִיא הַמַּטִילָה יִרְאָה עַל הָאָדָם
which is what casts awe and dread upon man.
וּמִדַּת חֲסָדָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ מְבִיאָה אַהֲבָה לִבְנֵי אָדָם
whereas the attribute of His lovingkindness, blessed be He, draws out love among human beings.
אֲבָל אִם הוּא אוֹהֵב גַּם בְּעָאקוּ רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן
However, if one loves even in the midst of crushing distress (áku), may the Merciful One preserve us;
זֶהוּ בֵּירוּר עַל שְׁלֵימוּת הָאַהֲבָה
this serves as the definitive clarification of the completeness of love;
וְאֵלּוּ הַיִּסּוּרִין הֵן הַנִּקְרָאִין "יִסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה",
and these tribulations are what are designated as 'chastisements of love',
שֶׁגַּם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵין מְבִיאָן עַל הָאָדָם אֶלָּא מֵאַהֲבָתוֹ אוֹתוֹ,
for Hashem, blessed be He, likewise brings them upon man solely out of His love for him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (מִשְׁלֵי ג, יב): "כִּי אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶאֱהַב ה' יוֹכִיחַ וְגוֹמֵר",
as it is stated (Proverbs 3:12): 'For whom Hashem loves He rebukes, etc.',
וְנֶאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה נג, י): "וַה' חָפֵץ דַּכְּאוֹ הֶחֱלִי וְגוֹמֵר",
and it is stated (Isaiah 53:10): 'Yet it pleased Hashem to crush him; He has put him to grief, etc.'
וְדָרְשׁוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ה עַמּוּד א): מִי שֶׁחָפֵץ בּוֹ, עַיֵּין שָׁם
which they expounded in Berakhot (5a): 'he in whom Hashem delights', see there.
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּ"כַּמַּיִם הַפָּנִים לַפָּנִים וְגוֹמֵר",
As is known that 'as in water face reflects face, etc.' (Proverbs 27:19);
וְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא וְדִלְעֵילָּא מְעוֹרְרִים זֶה אֶת זֶה
and the lower awakening and the supernal awakening stimulate each other;
רַק שֶׁאָנוּ אוֹמְרִים (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים א, ד): "מָשְׁכֵנִי אַחֲרֶיךָ נָּרוּצָה",
only that we plead (Song of Songs 1:4): 'Draw me, after You we will run,'
וְ"הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ ה' אֵלֶיךָ וְנָשׁוּבָה וְגוֹמֵר" (אֵיכָה ה, כא),
and 'Turn us back to You, Hashem, and we shall return, etc.' (Lamentations 5:21),
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא קוֹדֶמֶת לְעוֹרְרֵינוּ,
asking that the supernal arousal from Above precede to awaken us.
וְאָנוּ נִמְשׁוֹךְ וְנָרוּץ אַחֲרָיו אַחַר כָּךְ בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא
and then we will be drawn and run after Him afterward through the lower awakening from below.
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹמֵר בְּהֵיפֶךְ : "שׁוּבוּ אֵלַי וְאָשׁוּבָה אֲלֵיכֶם",
Yet Hashem, blessed be He, says the reverse (Malachi 3:7): 'Return unto Me, and I will return unto you,'
וְעַל זֶה הוּא כָּל אֹרֶךְ הַגָּלוּת
and upon this tension hinges the entire duration of the exile;
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוֹצֶה שֶׁנְּעוֹרֵר אֲנַחְנוּ בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא
for Hashem, blessed be He, desires that we initiate the arousal from below.
וְאִם יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂים תְּשׁוּבָה – מִיָּד נִגְאָלִים
and if Israel repents, they are redeemed immediately.
וּבְ"בְּעִתָּהּ" נֶאֱמַר (יְחֶזְקֵאל כ, לג): "בְּיָד חֲזָקָה וּבִזְרוֹעַ נְטוּיָה וּבְחֵמָה שְׁפוּכָה אֶמְלוֹךְ עֲלֵיכֶם",
And regarding the predetermined time ('in its time' / be'itah) it is stated (Ezekiel 20:33): 'with a strong hand, and with an outstretched arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you,'.
וְ"עָשִׂיתִי אֵת אֲשֶׁר בְּחֻקַּי תֵּלֵכוּ" (שָׁם לו, כז) בְּלִי שׁוּם אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא
and 'I will cause you to walk in My statutes' (ibid. 36:27) without any lower awakening whatsoever.
אֲבָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ אֶלָּא אוֹצָר שֶׁל יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם בִּלְבַד (בִּבְרָכוֹת לג עַמּוּד ב),
However, in this present world the Holy One, blessed be He, has in His world only a storehouse of the fear of Heaven alone (Berakhot 33b);
הַיִּרְאָה הִיא הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא כַּיָּדוּעַ,
fear being the lower awakening from below, as is known,
דְּעָלָיו נֶאֱמַר (תְּהִלִּים קיח, כ): "זֶה הַשַּׁעַר לַה' וְגוֹמֵר",
concerning which it is said (Psalms 118:20): 'This is the gate of Hashem, etc.'
דְּהִיא תַּרְעָא לְאַעֲלָא גּוֹ מְהֵימְנוּתָא (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק א, יא עַמּוּד ב).
it being 'the gate to enter into faith' (Zohar Part I, 11b).
דִּבִּתְחִלַּת כְּנִיסַת הָאָדָם לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא עַל יְדֵי יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
For man's initial entry into the service of Hashem, blessed be He, occurs through the fear of Heaven,
שֶׁהִיא "רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה" (תְּהִלִּים קיא, י),
which is 'the beginning of wisdom' (Psalms 111:10),
רָצָה לוֹמַר הַתְחָלַת הַכָּרַת הָאָדָם
meaning the dawn of man's conscious perception
(דְּכֵן "חָכָם" בַּאֲרַמִּי רָצָה לוֹמַר הַכָּרָה)
(for similarly 'chakam' in Aramaic signifies recognition)
שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְצִיאוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
that Hashem exists,
מִיָּד יַגִּיעַ אֵלָיו הַיִּרְאָה וְהַהַכְנָעָה וְכוּלֵי כִּלְשׁוֹן רַמָ"א בְּרֵישׁ שֻׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ אֹרַח חַיִּים (סִימָן א, א).
fear and submissiveness immediately reach him, etc. in the words of Rema at the beginning of the Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayyim 1:1.
וְנֶאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים י, יב): "מָה ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ שֹׁאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה",
And it is said (Deuteronomy 10:12): 'What does Hashem your God ask of you, but to fear,'.
דְּאֵין הַמְּבוּקָּשׁ מֵהָאָדָם רַק מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה
showing that what is directly demanded from man is solely the attribute of awe.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Dover Tzedek, Likutim §3): “These are the ten trials with which Avraham Avinu was tested, and he was found whole in all of them, that they did not move him even a hair’s breadth — and then he merited the name ‘Eisan,’ and at once also the title ‘HaEzrachi’; and this is the trial of the Akeidah, and it is known in the Zohar that then Avraham and Yitzchak were ‘incorporated’ one in the other.” The se’if’s Avraham: through the ten trials, culminating in the Akeidah, he “became a Chariot for the middah of love.”

rich.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Dover Tzedek, Likutim §3): “These are the ten trials with which Avraham Avinu was tested, and he was found whole in all of them, that they did not move him even a hair’s breadth — and then he merited the name ‘Eisan,’ and at once also the title ‘HaEzrachi’; and this is the trial of the Akeidah, and it is known in the Zohar that then Avraham and Yitzchak were ‘incorporated’ one in the other.” The se’if’s Avraham: through the ten trials, culminating in the Akeidah, he “became a Chariot for the middah of love.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Chayei Sarah §9): “‘coming with days’ — that they had already come to be clarified in the supernal days; and Binah too is the World to Come, as it says in the Zohar; and Chochmah and Binah are likewise called ‘days.’” The discourse explains that Avraham’s tenth trial completed his clarification in all the attributes, so that “Hashem blessed Avraham in everything” also means that He would no longer test him. This supplies a further account of the process described here: Avraham’s trials culminate in an established spiritual stature.

paragraphs.text: Mishlei 3:12: “כִּי אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶאֱהַב ה׳ יוֹכִיחַ, וּכְאָב אֶת בֵּן יִרְצֶה” — “For whom Hashem loves He rebukes, as a father the son in whom he delights” — from Shlomo’s exhortation (Mishlei 3) not to despise the mussar of Hashem nor recoil from His reproof. Meforshim: God’s chastisements are the very mark of His love, as a father who loves his son corrects him. From this verse (with others) the Gemara (Berachos 5a) establishes the category of “yissurin shel ahavah,” sufferings of love. R’ Tzadok applies it precisely: the trials God brings upon the lover — the sufferings that clarify his love — are brought “only out of His love for him,” as it says, “whom Hashem loves, He rebukes.”

paragraphs.text: Berachos 5a: “אִם רוֹאֶה אָדָם שֶׁיִּסּוּרִין בָּאִין עָלָיו — יְפַשְׁפֵּשׁ בְּמַעֲשָׂיו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״נַחְפְּשָׂה דְרָכֵינוּ וְנַחְקֹרָה וְנָשׁוּבָה עַד ה׳״. פִּשְׁפֵּשׁ וְלֹא מָצָא — יִתְלֶה בְּבִטּוּל תּוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַשְׁרֵי הַגֶּבֶר אֲשֶׁר תְּיַסְּרֶנּוּ יָּהּ וּמִתּוֹרָתְךָ תְלַמְּדֶנּוּ״. וְאִם תָּלָה וְלֹא מָצָא — בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁיִּסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה הֵם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶאֱהַב ה׳ יוֹכִיחַ״.” — “If a person sees sufferings coming upon him, he should examine his deeds, as it is stated: ‘Let us search and examine our ways and return to Hashem.’ If he examined and found nothing, he should attribute them to neglect of Torah, as it is stated: ‘Happy is the man whom You discipline, God, and whom You teach from Your Torah.’ If he attributed them and found nothing, it is known that they are sufferings of love, as it is stated: ‘For whom Hashem loves He chastises.’” The passage continues: “אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כׇּל שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חָפַץ בּוֹ — מְדַכְּאוֹ בְּיִסּוּרִין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַה׳ חָפֵץ דַּכְּאוֹ הֶחֱלִי״. יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ לֹא קִבְּלָם מֵאַהֲבָה? — תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִם תָּשִׂים אָשָׁם נַפְשׁוֹ״, מָה אָשָׁם לְדַעַת, אַף יִסּוּרִין — לְדַעַת.” — “Rava said in the name of Rav Sechora, in the name of Rav Huna: Whoever the Holy One, blessed is He, desires, He crushes with sufferings, as it is stated: ‘Hashem desired to crush him with illness.’ Might this apply even if he did not accept them lovingly? Scripture says: ‘If his soul makes itself a guilt-offering’: just as a guilt-offering is brought willingly, so sufferings must be accepted willingly.” Rav Tzadok applies this category to the lover whose fidelity is proved through the trial.

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim 1:4: “מָשְׁכֵנִי אַחֲרֶיךָ נָּרוּצָה, הֱבִיאַנִי הַמֶּלֶךְ חֲדָרָיו” — “Draw me, we will run after You; the King has brought me into His chambers.” Shir HaShirim is read as the allegory of the love of the Holy One and Knesses Yisrael — “all the Writings are holy, but Shir HaShirim is the Holy of Holies” (Mishnah Yadayim 3:5; Rashi). Meforshim: “mashcheni” — Israel asks God to draw her, for the first arousal must come from Him. R’ Tzadok’s use: “mashcheni acharecha narutza” (and, in prayer, “hashiveinu Hashem eilecha ve-nashuvah,” Eichah 5:21) express that love and return depend on the drawing from Above; a person’s “running” follows only after God draws — it is not in his power to awaken love by his own striving.

paragraphs.text: Rema (R’ Moshe Isserles, c. 1530–1572), in his gloss at the very opening of Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chayim 1:1, teaches on the verse “I have set Hashem before me always” (Tehillim 16:8) that “this is a great principle in the Torah and among the virtues of the righteous who walk before God”; for a person’s sitting, movements, and dealings when he is alone in his house are not like his sitting, movements, and dealings when he stands before a great king. And when a person takes to heart that the great King, the Holy One, blessed is He, whose glory fills the whole earth, stands over him and sees his deeds, “immediately the awe and the submission in the fear of Him reach him” (the Rema there citing Rambam, Moreh Nevuchim III:52). R’ Tzadok invokes this to show that the very recognition that God exists draws down yirah of itself.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Chalomot §14): “‘what does Hashem ask of you but to fear,’ and ‘the end of the matter… fear God, for this is the whole of man’ — and therefore this mitzvah is set on Rosh Hashanah, to bring the fear into the heart for all the days of the year.” This is precisely the rung §5-5 measures Avraham against: fear is “the whole of man,” the baseline every person can reach — so enduring the world’s sufferings “is no great feat from the side of fear.” Avraham’s greatness lay elsewhere — in the love that a fear-trial can never disclose.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Avraham is the first of those tested, the first to clarify the middah of love until he became a Chariot for it. Trials of worldly suffering are no great feat from the side of fear; it is loving Him in distress that proves love complete. The whole length of the exile hangs on this: God wills that the arousal come first from below — “Return to Me” — though we ask that His arousal precede ours.

p: (ו), — אֲבָל הָאַהֲבָה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיעַ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם
However, love cannot be attained through mortal human exertion,
כִּי אֵין אַהֲבָה אֶלָּא בֵּין הַדּוֹמִים
for authentic love exists only between those who share affinity and resemblance,
וְאֵיךְ יִתְפָּאֵר הַגַּרְזֶן עַל הַחוֹצֵב לוֹמַר שֶׁאוֹהֲבוֹ —
and how could the axe ever boast over the one who hews with it (Isaiah 10:15) to say that it loves him?!
רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרוֹב רַחֲמָיו וַחֲסָדָיו קוֹרֵא לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל: "אֲחֹתִי" וְ"תַמָּתִי – תְּיוֹמָתִי",
Rather, Hashem in His abundant mercy and kindness calls the Congregation of Israel: 'My sister' and 'my undefiled—my twin' (Song of Songs 5:2),
וְאוֹמֵר : "אָהַבְתִּי אֶתְכֶם וְגוֹמֵר",
and declares (Malachi 1:2): 'I have loved you, etc.',
וּכְשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹהֵב הָאָדָם, מִמֵּילָא הָאָדָם אוֹהֲבוֹ גַּם כֵּן
and when Hashem loves a person, that person automatically loves Him as well.
וְהָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא קוֹדֶמֶת בָּזֶה לְעוֹלָם
so the awakening from Above eternally precedes in this regard.
וּלְכָךְ, מִצַּד עַבְדוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהוּא בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, הַיִּרְאָה קוֹדֶמֶת
Therefore, from the perspective of Israel's divine service, which proceeds through the lower awakening from below, fear comes first;
אֲבָל מִצַּד מִדּוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ יָדוּעַ דְּאַהֲבָה קוֹדֶמֶת
yet from the perspective of His divine attributes, it is known that love precedes;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כט, יא): "לְךָ ה' הַגְּדֻלָּה וְהַגְּבוּרָה", גְּדֻלָּה קוֹדֶמֶת
and as it is stated (I Chronicles 29:11): 'Yours, Hashem, is the Greatness (Chesed/Love) and the Might (Gevurah/Fear),' Greatness taking precedence.
וְכֵן בָּאָבוֹת שֶׁהֵן הַמֶּרְכָּבָה: אַבְרָהָם הוֹלִיד אֶת יִצְחָק
and likewise among the Patriarchs who form the Chariot: Abraham fathered Isaac.
דְּרַק בַּעֲבוֹדַת פְּרָטֵי הַנְּפָשׁוֹת אַחַר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
For only in the personal service of individual souls after the Giving of the Torah,
שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ קִנְיָן לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּרְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
who became an acquired possession unto Hashem and His will;
שׁוֹאֵל מֵהֶם לְיִרְאָה וּלְעוֹרֵר בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא
does He ask of them to fear and to arouse from below;
אֲבָל הָאָבוֹת שֶׁהֵם בִּנְיַן כְּלַל הַכְּנֵסִיָּה וְשָׁרְשָׁהּ וּמְקוֹרָהּ,
yet the Patriarchs, who are the very foundation, root, and origin of the entire collective assembly,
וַדַּאי בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא לְבַד
certainly emerged through the awakening from Above alone,
כְּמוֹ תְּחִלַּת בְּרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁהָיָה רַק בְּמַאֲמָרוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ "יְהִי אוֹר",
just like the primordial creation of the world which unfolded solely by His divine utterance 'Let there be light',
וּבְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא לְבַד
and through supernal arousal alone.
דְּאָדָם אֵין לַעֲבוֹד בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא
for there was no man yet to work through an awakening from below.
וְכֵן זְרִיחַת אוֹרוֹ דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִתּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ נֶאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה מא, ב): "מִי הֵעִיר מִמִּזְרָח וְגוֹמֵר",
And so regarding the shining forth of the light of Abraham our father, peace be upon him, out of the darkness, it is said (Isaiah 41:2): 'Who raised up the righteous one from the east, etc.'
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֱעִירוֹ וְעוֹרְרוֹ לָזֶה
signifying that Hashem, blessed be He, awakened him and stirred him to this.
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד מִדַּת אַהֲבָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And this stems from the attribute of His love, blessed be He,
שֶׁמִּטֶּבַע הַטּוֹב וְאִישׁ הַחֶסֶד לְהֵיטִיב חַסְדּוֹ
for it is the intrinsic nature of the Good and the Master of Lovingkindness to bestow His benevolence;
מִבְּלִי שֶׁיְּקַדְּמֶנּוּ הַלָּה לְבַקְּשׁוֹ עַל זֶה כְּלָל
without the recipient having to precede in petitioning Him for it at all;
וְאַךְ מִצַּד מִדָּה זוֹ הוּא שֶׁבָּא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא הַקּוֹדֶמֶת לְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא
and solely from this attribute comes the supernal awakening preceding the awakening from below.
וְכָל אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא הַקּוֹדֶמֶת הִיא הַמְּעוֹרֶרֶת מִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה
and any prior supernal awakening is what awakens the attribute of love.
כִּי הָאַהֲבָה מְעוֹרֶרֶת אַהֲבָה
For love awakens love,
שֶׁהָאַהֲבָה הוּא בִּדְבָרִים הַדּוֹמִים
since love exists between harmonious entities.
וְהוּא שָׁוֶה בִּשְׁנֵיהֶם
and is symmetrical and equal in both of them.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Ki Seitzei §8): "“just as a dove, from the hour she recognizes her mate, does not exchange him for another — so Israel”; and as they said Eruvin 100b, “had the Torah not been given we would have learned sexual fidelity from the dove.”" Exactly the se’if: love holds between a pair that answer one another — which is why He calls Knesses Yisrael “My twin,” a like recognizing its like and never exchanging it.

paragraphs.text: Divrei HaYamim I 29:11: “לְךָ ה׳ הַגְּדֻלָּה וְהַגְּבוּרָה וְהַתִּפְאֶרֶת וְהַנֵּצַח וְהַהוֹד, כִּי כֹל בַּשָּׁמַיִם וּבָאָרֶץ, לְךָ ה׳ הַמַּמְלָכָה” — “Yours, Hashem, is the greatness and the might and the splendor and the eternity and the majesty…” — from David HaMelech’s public blessing of Hashem before the whole assembly at the gathering for the building of the Beis HaMikdash. This is the classic scriptural enumeration of the seven lower middos/sefiros (Gedulah = Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferes, Netzach, Hod, “ki chol” = Yesod, and ha-mamlachah = Malchus). R’ Tzadok reads the order: “ha-gedulah (Chesed) ve-ha-gevurah” — Chesed (love) named before Gevurah (fear) — as showing that from God’s side love precedes fear; and correspondingly among the Avos, who “are the Merkavah (Chariot)” (Bereishis Rabbah 47:6, 82:6), “Avraham begot Yitzchak” (Bereishis 25:19) — Avraham (Chesed) before Yitzchak (Gevurah).

paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah II §25: “ומכל מקום צריך לטרוח בבישול המאכלים בע"ש אבל מי שלא טרח בע"ש מה יאכל בשבת” — “Nevertheless, one must labor at preparing the food on the eve of Shabbos; one who did not labor on the eve of Shabbos—what will he eat on Shabbos?” It explains: “שאינו בא מעצמו אור הזה לאדם. וכן נר שבת צריך להדליק מע"ש אבל בשבת אין עוד זמן לעורר היראה אז כי כולו אהבה ודביקות בד' והדלקת הנר סמוכה לשבת” — “For this light does not come to a person by itself. Similarly, the Shabbos lamp must be kindled on the eve of Shabbos; on Shabbos there is no longer time then to awaken fear, for it is wholly love and attachment to God, and the lamp is kindled close to Shabbos.” The reason is “כי לעולם הדביקות ואהבה תכופה אחר היראה” — “for attachment and love always follow closely after fear.” This parallel illuminates fear as the preparation for received love.

paragraphs.text: Yeshayah 41:2: “מִי הֵעִיר מִמִּזְרָח, צֶדֶק יִקְרָאֵהוּ לְרַגְלוֹ, יִתֵּן לְפָנָיו גּוֹיִם וּמְלָכִים יַרְדְּ, יִתֵּן כֶּעָפָר חַרְבּוֹ כְּקַשׁ נִדָּף קַשְׁתּוֹ” — “Who roused one from the east, calling righteousness to his feet? He delivers up nations before him and makes him tread down kings; his sword makes them as dust, his bow as driven chaff.” From Yeshayah’s prophecy of consolation (ch. 41), in which God summons the nations to judgment and asks “who aroused he’ir” the victor from the east. Rashi and the Sages apply “mi he’ir mimizrach” to Avraham — whom God “roused” from the east (Ur Kasdim / Aram), “calling righteousness to his feet,” and before whom He delivered up the four kings (Bereishis 14). R’ Tzadok reads the verb “he’ir” as the point: it was God who first aroused Avraham — Avraham’s light shining “out of the darkness” came not by his own initiative but by God’s love preceding him, the “arousal from Above” (is’aruta di-le’eila) that always precedes love. (The received text reads Yeshayah 41:2.)

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Sichas Shedim §1): “when a person is made whole in the middah of Yaakov, the Holy One calls him ‘My twin te’omasi’ — that both are equal; and ‘He did not budge from cherishing her until He called her My mother’ — as though she were even greater than He, generating, as it were, the beginning-of-thought that is His.” This is §5-6’s astonishing claim exactly: love needs equals, and God Himself confers the equality — calling Knesses Yisrael “My twin,” then raising her past even that, to “My mother,” so that the love has its “like” on both sides.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Love cannot be reached by a person’s own effort, for “there is no love except between equals” — how shall the axe boast over the one who hews with it? It is God who confers the equality, calling Knesses Yisrael “My twin.” Hence from the side of Israel’s service fear comes first, but from the side of His own middos love precedes — as Chesed precedes Gevurah, and Avraham begot Yitzchak.

p: (ז) — מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַיִּרְאָה
– In contrast, awe/fear—,
מִמִּי שֶׁהוּא מִתְיָירֵא עַל כָּרְחֲךָ אֵינָם דּוֹמִים
with respect to the One of Whom one is in awe, perforce they are not alike,
וְאֵין הַמִּדָּה שָׁוָה בִּשְׁנֵיהֶם
and the attribute is not symmetrical between the two.
שֶׁזֶּה מִתְיָירֵא וְזֶה מַטִיל וְנוֹתֵן הַמּוֹרָא
for this one is afraid, while That One casts and imparts the dread.
וּלְכָךְ, בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּת מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה
Therefore, upon the stirring of the supernal attribute of Gevurah Above,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מוֹלִיד הַיִּרְאָה בִּלְבַב הָאָדָם
which consequently engenders fear within the heart of man,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא: כְּשֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה דִּין בָּרְשָׁעִים הוּא מִתְיָרֵא וְכוּלֵי
in the manner taught: when the Holy One executes judgment upon the wicked He is feared, etc.
אֵין זֶה נִקְרָא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא הַקּוֹדֶמֶת לְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא
this is not defined as an awakening from Above preceding an awakening from below.
שֶׁאֵין שְׁנֵיהֶם עִנְיָן אֶחָד
because the two experiences are not of the identical nature.
וּלְכָךְ, אַף דְּגַם הַיִּרְאָה אֵינוֹ מִצַּד הָאָדָם
And therefore, even though fear too does not originate autonomously from man,
וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר (אִיּוֹב מא, ג): "מִי הִקְדִּימַנִי וַאֲשַׁלֵּם",
and concerning this it is written (Job 41:3): 'Who has preceded Me, that I should repay him?',
דְּגַם בָּזֶה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמַּקְדִּים לְהָבִיא אֵלָיו דָּבָר הַמְּעוֹרֵר הַיִּרְאָה
since in this as well Hashem, blessed be He, is the One Who initiates bringing upon him the factor that evokes awe,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְרָא שֶׁבָּא בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא
nevertheless it is termed as coming via an awakening from below,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵין אוֹתוֹ דָבָר מְעוֹרֵר בַּפּוֹעַל בֵּירוּר כְּמוֹ אַהֲבָה הַמּוֹלִיד אַהֲבָה
inasmuch as that external factor does not stimulate directly and unmistakably the identical state, unlike love which automatically begets love,
וּכְטַעַם "מָשְׁכֵנִי אַחֲרֶיךָ נָּרוּצָה" וְ"הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ וְגוֹמֵר".
and mirroring 'Draw me, after You we will run' and 'Turn us back, etc.',
וְעַל כֵּן זֶה לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ רַק בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
And therefore this dynamic pertains solely to Israel,
דְּ"אָהַבְתִּי אֶתְכֶם אָמַר ה'" מִצַּד שֶׁהֵם קְרוּיִים "תְּיוֹמָתִי" כִּבְיָכוֹל
for 'I have loved you, says Hashem' is spoken because they are designated 'My twin,' as it were,
וְשַׁיָּיךְ אַהֲבָה גַּבַּיְיהוּ.
and authentic mutual love applies to them.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה הוּא גַּם בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
In contrast, the attribute of fear exists among the nations of the world as well,
רַק שֶׁהִיא יִרְאָה תַּתָּאָה בְּיוֹתֵר, שֶׁיְּרֵאִים מֵעָנְשָׁיו יִתְבָּרַךְ,
except that it is the lowest form of dread, being afraid of His punishments, blessed be He;
כִּי עַל כָּל פָּנִים בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּת מִדַּת גְּבוּרָה מוֹלִיד יִרְאָה
for at any rate the awakening of Gevurah engenders fear.
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינָהּ נִמְשֶׁכֶת אַחֲרֶיהָ בְּבֵירוּר
yet it does not follow after it consistently.
שֶׁהֲרֵי בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם נֶאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה ח, כא): "וְהָיָה כִי יִרְעַב וְהִתְקַצַּף וְקִלֵּל בְּמַלְכּוֹ וּבֵאלֹהָיו",
For regarding the nations of the world it is said (Isaiah 8:21): 'And it shall come to pass that when they are hungry, they shall fret themselves, and curse by their king and by their God,'
שֶׁהִתְעוֹרְרוּת מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה וְזַעַם, אִם מוֹלִיד בְּלִבּוֹ גַּם כֵּן
in that the stirring of Gevurah and divine wrath, if it awakens in a gentile heart,
הוּא אַדְּרַבָּה גַּם כֵּן חָפֵץ לְהִתְגַּבֵּר וְלִזְעוֹם וּלְהִתְקַצֵּף וְלִמְרוֹד כִּבְיָכוֹל בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
it conversely prompts him to become defiant, wrathful, furious, and rebel, as it were, against Hashem, blessed be He.
וְזֶהוּ בְּאוֹתָן שֶׁהֵן מִפְּסֹלֶת וְזוּהֲמַת מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה וּשְׁמָרֶיהָ בְּזֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה
And this occurs in those who stem from the dross and defilement of Gevurah and its sediment in the cosmic balance of opposites;
וְאַף בְּאוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם כֹּחַ הַמֶּרֶד וְנוֹפֶלֶת עֲלֵיהֶם יִרְאָה מֵעוֹנֶשׁ וְזַעַף
and even in those who lack the boldness to rebel and upon whom falls dread of punishment and wrath,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֶפְשָׁר דְּאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא יִרְאָה גְּרוּעָה וְתַחְתּוֹנָה
it may still be only an inferior, lower fear,
וְאֵינָהּ קְרוּיָה "יִרְאַת ה
'". and is not dignified by the name 'the fear of Hashem.'
רַק אוֹתָם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהֶם (נְחֶמְיָה א, יא): "הַחֲפֵצִים לְיִרְאָה אֶת שְׁמֶךָ",
Only those concerning whom it is said (Nehemiah 1:11): 'who desire to fear Your Name,'
וְהַמְחַפְּשִׂים כַּמַּטְמוֹנִים לְהָבִין יִרְאַת ה' – הֵם יִמְצָאוּהָ.
and who seek it like hidden treasures to understand the fear of Hashem (Proverbs 2:4–5)—they alone shall find it.
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא
Therefore it is designated as the lower awakening from below;
וְזֶה כָּל עִנְיַן הַתּוֹרָה, דְּמִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה נָפְקָא
and this is the entire essence of the Torah, which emanates from the side of Gevurah,
הַמְצַוָּוה וּמַזְהֶרֶת לָאָדָם לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל לִבְחוֹר בַּטּוֹב בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּילֵיהּ.
commanding and cautioning man to exert himself to choose good through his own active initiative.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §24): “One greets his fellow out of love and joining; but fear is from the side of ‘derech eretz’ toward a man who is great and separate from him. And by Hashem, both are together, and one without the other does not suffice — for fear alone brings folly (‘is not your fear your folly?’), and joy alone brings frivolity.” The se’if’s point: fear, unlike love, is not between equals — it is toward “one great and separate,” who “casts and gives the dread.”

paragraphs.text: Iyov 41:3: “מִי הִקְדִּימַנִי וַאֲשַׁלֵּם, תַּחַת כָּל הַשָּׁמַיִם לִי הוּא” — “Who has preceded Me, that I should repay him? Whatever is under the whole heaven is Mine.” From God’s answer to Iyov out of the whirlwind (the Livyasan passage, ch. 41), asserting His absolute sovereignty. Rashi gives a distinct plain reading: “מִי הִקְדִּימַנִי. וּמִי הוּא אֲשֶׁר הִקְדִּים פָּנַי בְּהַקְבָּלָתוֹ, לְעָבְדֵנִי וְלִשְׁמֹר מִצְוֹתַי, וַאֲשַׁלֵּם לוֹ שְׂכָרוֹ?” — “Who preceded Me? Who is the one who first came before Me, receiving Me by serving Me and keeping My commandments, that I should pay him his reward?” He continues: “כָּל אֲשֶׁר בַּשָּׁמַיִם לִי הוּא, וּבְיָדִי לִפְרֹעַ לוֹ שְׂכָרוֹ וּפְעֻלָּתוֹ וּמַעֲבָדוֹ” — “Everything in heaven is Mine, and it is in My hand to pay him his reward, his recompense, and his labor.” This assures God’s ability to reward; the interpretation that His gifts precede every mitzvah is the following Midrash’s exposition. The Sages apply “mi hikdimani va-ashalem” to the mitzvos: none can “precede” God and put Him in his debt, since He Himself first provides the very means of the mitzvah (a house before its mezuzah, a garment before its tzitzis — Vayikra Rabbah 27:2, and the like). R’ Tzadok’s use: even fear is not purely from the person’s own side — “who has preceded Me?” — for God Himself precedes to bring him the thing that rouses fear; yet it is still called “an arousal from below,” since (unlike love) that thing does not rouse “in clear act.”

paragraphs.text: Malachi 1:2: “אָהַבְתִּי אֶתְכֶם אָמַר ה׳, וַאֲמַרְתֶּם בַּמָּה אֲהַבְתָּנוּ, הֲלוֹא אָח עֵשָׂו לְיַעֲקֹב נְאֻם ה׳, וָאֹהַב אֶת יַעֲקֹב” — “‘I have loved you,’ says Hashem; yet you say, ‘How have You loved us?’ — Was not Esav a brother to Yaakov, declares Hashem, yet I loved Yaakov.” The opening of Malachi, last of the prophets. Rashi/Radak: God’s love for Israel is unconditional and rooted in the Avos, shown by His choosing Yaakov over his very brother Esav. R’ Tzadok’s use: this love applies uniquely to Israel — “I have loved you, says Hashem” — for Israel alone is called, as it were, God’s “twin,” and love (unlike fear) obtains only between equals; God’s love (the arousal from Above) precedes and evokes Israel’s love in return.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Fear is not between equals: this one fears, and the Other casts and gives the dread. So even when Gevurah is aroused above and begets fear below, this is not called an arousal from Above preceding one from below, for the two are not one matter. Love, which begets love, is therefore Israel’s alone; fear reaches the nations too, but only as dread of punishment, never drawn after it in clear truth.

p: (ח), — וְאַחַר שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בָּאַהֲבָה הַגְּמוּרָה בַּנִּסָּיוֹן הָעֲשִׂירִי דַּעֲקֵידָה
And after Abraham our father, peace be upon him, was clarified in absolute love during the tenth trial of the Binding of Isaac,
שֶׁהָיָה לְגַבֵּיו תַּכְלִית תּוֹקֶף דְּ"בְכָל מְאֹדֶךָ",
which represented for him the supreme pinnacle of 'with all your might',
נֶאֱמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית כב, יב): "עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה",
it was said (Genesis 22:12): 'Now I know that you are a God-fearing man,'.
דְּאִתְכְּלִיל אָז בְּמִדַּת יִצְחָק
for he was then integrated into the attribute of Isaac (Gevurah/Fear).
כִּי זֶהוּ שְׁלֵימוּת הָאַהֲבָה דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה מִדָּתוֹ אַהֲבָה לְבַד
For this was the consummation of the love of Abraham our father whose sole innate attribute was love,
שֶׁהִיא מֵאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא
which originates from the awakening from Above;
רַק שֶׁהוּא הוֹסִיף אֹמֶץ וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת מְרוּבָּה עַל יְדֵי הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא שֶׁקְּדָמַתּוּ,
except that he added fortitude and immense personal striving by virtue of the supernal awakening that had preceded him,
עַד שֶׁזָּכָה לִהְיוֹת נִקְרָא עַל שְׁמוֹ כְּאִלּוּ הוּא הַמְּעוֹרֵר
until he merited that it be credited to his own name as though he himself were the initiator.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה
which is the attribute of fear.
וְהָאַהֲבָה הַבָּאָה עַל יְדֵי הַיִּרְאָה
And the love that emerges through the conduit of fear
נֶחְשָׁב שֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּילֵיהּ,
is considered to have arrived through his own lower awakening,

because he aroused himself to awe, through this “a spirit draws forth a spirit” of love above.
וְנִתְעוֹרֵר אַחַר כָּךְ לְאַהֲבָה
and was subsequently awakened to divine love.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּאַבְרָהָם שֶׁ"בְּחָרוֹ אֲבָל לֹא קֵרְבוֹ, רַק הוּא קֵירֵב אֶת עַצְמוֹ" (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יד, ב);
And this is what is taught concerning Abraham, that Hashem 'chose him but did not draw him near, rather he drew himself near' (Bemidbar Rabbah 14:2);
פֵּירוּשׁ: תְּחִלַּת הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא שֶׁהָיָה עָלָיו
meaning: the initial supernal awakening that rested upon him,
וְנִבְחַר הוּא מִכָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לְעוֹרְרוֹ לְאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
wherein he was chosen out of the entire world to be stirred toward the love of Hashem, blessed be He,
זֶהוּ מֵה' שֶׁ"בָּחַרְתָּ בְּאַבְרָם וְהוֹצֵאתוֹ וְכוּלֵי" (נְחֶמְיָה ט, ז);
this came from Hashem Who 'chose Abram and brought him forth, etc.' (Nehemiah 9:7).
אֲבָל אַחַר כָּךְ נִתְנַסָּה בְּנִסְיוֹנוֹת
yet subsequently he was tested with trials.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּמִסְפַּר עֶשֶׂר הוּא מִסְפָּר כּוֹלֵל וּמִדַּת קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה
And it is known that the number ten is an all-inclusive number and the measure of a complete spiritual stature.
הַיְינוּ שֶׁתַּכְלִית כָּל עִנְיַן הַנִּסְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁיִּסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְשֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּמְּצִיאוּת בָּעוֹלָם הֵבִיא עָלָיו
meaning that the consummate scope of all trials established by Hashem and existing in the universe were brought upon him.
וְכָל עִנְיַן הַנִּסָּיוֹן יָדוּעַ, דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַרְאֶה עַצְמוֹ מְרוּחָק מִמֶּנּוּ בְּתַכְלִית
And the essence of a trial is known: namely that Hashem, blessed be He, portrays Himself as utterly distant from him.
וְהוּא צָרִיךְ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְלוּתוֹ לְקָרֵב אֶת עַצְמוֹ אֵלָיו
and he must, through his own striving, draw himself near unto Him:
וְכָךְ רָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And thus did Hashem desire with Abraham our father, peace be upon him:
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא בָּחַר בּוֹ וְעוֹרְרוֹ,
that even though He chose him and awakened him,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא קֵרְבוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִצְטָרֵךְ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת
nonetheless He did not bring him near in a manner that would eliminate the need for effort.
רַק רָצָה שֶׁבְּהִשְׁתַּדְלוּתוֹ יַגִּיעַ לָזֶה
rather He willed that through his own exertion he arrive at this.
כִּי זֶה יְסוֹד הָאוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית
For this is the foundational pillar of the Jewish nation:
לָתֵת מָקוֹם לַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא הַמַּזְהֶרֶת בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם
to afford room for the Torah, which admonishes and guides mortal human effort,
וּמֵאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא שֶׁהִתְחִיל שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה .
and from Abraham our father began the two thousand years of Torah (Avodah Zarah 9a).
וְאַף יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל, "בְּחָרוֹ וְלֹא קֵרְבוֹ",
And even Jacob our father, who is the root of the name Israel, Hashem 'chose him but did not draw him near unearned',
כִּי יְסוֹד בִּנְיַן הָאוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא לְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לְקָרֵב אֶת עַצְמוֹ,
for the foundation of the Jewish people in this world is exertion to draw oneself near.
וְרַק בְּעֵת קֵץ אָז הוּא יְקָרְבֵם
and only at the time of the End of Days will He draw them close unilaterally.
וְנִשְׁתּוֹקֵק לָזֶה דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (תְּהִלִּים סה, ה): "אַשְׁרֵי תִּבְחַר וּתְקָרֵב",
And King David, peace be upon him, yearned for this (Psalms 65:5): 'Happy is the one You choose and bring near',
דְּגַם הוּא בְּחָרוֹ וְלֹא קֵרְבוֹ,
for him too He chose, but did not bring near without labor,
דְּהוּא רַק הֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה
in that David merely raised the yoke of repentance.
אֲבָל לֹא הִשְׁלִימָהּ עֲדַיִן לְגַמְרֵי
yet did not consummate it entirely.
דִּשְׁלֵימוּתָהּ עַל יְדֵי מָשִׁיחַ,
For its ultimate completion will be through the Messiah,
שֶׁיְּתוּקַּן כָּל הַקּוֹדֵם גַּם חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
wherein all the past will be rectified, including the sin of Adam the First;
דְּיִתְהַפֵּךְ הַכֹּל לִזְכִיּוֹת
such that everything will be transmuted into merits;
זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק עַל יְדֵי הִתְגַּלּוּת הַקֵּירוּב הַגָּמוּר מִמֶּנּוּ יִתְבָּרַךְ
this being impossible except through the overt disclosure of absolute closeness from Him, blessed be He,
וַהֲסָרַת הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לְגַמְרֵי
and the total cessation of mortal striving,
כִּי יִתְבָּרֵר דְּגַם כָּל מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵינוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂינוּ (יְשַׁעְיָה כו, יב): "פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ"
for it will become manifest that even all our thoughts and deeds 'You have wrought for us',
וְהַכֹּל מִמֶּנּוּ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and everything originated from Him, blessed be He:
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (עד, יז) בַּאֲחֵי יוֹסֵף
Along the lines of what is taught in Bereishit Rabbah (74:17) regarding Joseph's brothers.
כְּשֶׁרָצִיתָ נָתַתָּ בְּלִבָּם לֶאֱהוֹב, וּכְשֶׁרָצִיתָ וְכוּלֵי
'When You willed, You placed in their hearts to love; and when You willed, etc.',
וְכָךְ רָצָה יִתְבָּרַךְ לָתֵת בְּלֵב הָאָדָם לִשְׂנוֹא
And likewise Hashem willed to place hatred in man's heart;
וְגַם זֶה מֵאִתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁרָצָה לְקָרְבוֹ עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה
and this too stems from Him, having willed to draw him near through this course;
וְהָרִיחוּקִים הַכֹּל הֵם קֵירוּבִים
and all apparent distancings are in truth intimate drawings near.
כְּעִנְיַן יִסּוּרִים שֶׁל אַהֲבָה
akin to the dynamic of chastisements of love.
שֶׁהֲרֵי הַיִּסּוּר הוּא רִיחוּק וְהֵיפֶךְ הָאַהֲבָה
For tribulation appears to be distance and the very antithesis of love,
וּבִשְׁעַת מַעֲשֶׂה כִּסְבוּרִים אָנוּ שֶׁהוּא רִיחוּק
and at the moment of the event we assume that it is alienation,
וּבֶאֱמֶת אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא קֵירוּב וְתוֹקֶף אַהֲבָה
yet in truth it is nothing other than closeness and the utmost intensity of love,
וְ"אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶאֱהַב ה' יוֹכִיחַ"
and 'whom Hashem loves He rebukes'.
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְבָּרֵר תּוֹקֶף אַהֲבַת אָדָם
for through this is clarified the unshakeable depth of man's love.
וְכֵן כָּל הָעֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁהֵבִיאוּ הָאָדָם לָשׁוּב
And so too all transgressions that ultimately brought a person to repent,
וְלִזְכּוֹת לְמַדְרֵגַת בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה
and to merit the lofty station of the ba'al teshuva,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרָכוֹת (לד עַמּוּד ב) שֶׁאֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים יְכוֹלִים לַעֲמוֹד
concerning which our Sages stated in Berakhot (34b) that completely righteous people cannot stand.
הֲרֵי הָרִיחוּק הוּא סִבַּת קֵירוּב
behold, the distancing itself served as the direct catalyst for supreme closeness.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §10): “the modes of service are love, fear, and deveikus; love and fear are the two wings and the two arms of the world — and they are the two Avos, Avraham and Yitzchak; and deveikus is ‘the one who grasps the body of the King,’ the form of Yaakov engraved on the Throne.” This is the structure behind §5-8’s “now I know that you fear God”: love and fear are the two wings on which one rises, and neither flies alone — so Avraham’s love reached its height only when, at the Akeidah, it was joined to Yitzchak’s fear, the two wings become one.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §21): “Avraham and Yitzchak are love and fear: love is the root of the positive commandments — the distancing from envy, through the chesed of Avraham, by actively doing good; and fear is the foundation of the negative commandments — the distancing from desire.” This is §5-8 exactly: Avraham’s love was made whole only when it was “included in the middah of Yitzchak,” for love and fear are the two roots of all avodah — the “doing good” of Avraham and the “turning from evil” of Yitzchak — and the complete servant, like Avraham at the Akeidah, holds both.

paragraphs.text: Yeshayah 26:12: “ה׳ תִּשְׁפֹּת שָׁלוֹם לָנוּ, כִּי גַּם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ” — “Hashem, You will establish peace for us, for You have also wrought all our deeds for us.” From the “song” of the future redemption sung in the land of Yehudah (Yeshayah 26). The commentators explain the verse differently. Rashi reads “כִּי גַם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ” as “הָרָעִים” — “For all our deeds”—“the evil ones”; on “פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ” he writes “כְּנֶגְדָּם לָקַחְנוּ מִיָּדְךָ בְּכָל חַטֹּאתֵינוּ” — “Corresponding to them we received from Your hand, for all our sins.” Radak writes “מה שקרה לנו ממעשה העולם הן טוב הן רע אתה פעלת הכל ולא היה בדרך מקרה” — “Whatever happened to us among the world’s events, whether good or bad, You wrought it all; it did not happen by chance.” The reading of all our thoughts and actions as God’s activity is Rav Tzadok’s exposition here, and should not be attributed to these commentaries as a statement specifically about every good deed. R’ Tzadok’s use: the ultimate rectification (through Mashiach) requires the removal of “striving” and the revelation that “gam kol ma’aseinu pa’alta lanu” — all is from Him; and then even the past sins turn to merits, for the “distancings” themselves were, in truth, His drawings-near. Izhbitz-Radzin and Ger on the future revelation that “all our deeds You wrought for us.” Mei HaShiloach II, Zechariah 4:1, reads “לא בחיל ולא בכח כי אם ברוחי” as the future state in which the powers of human action are progressively effaced and the inheritance of Yaakov is revealed: Yaakov describes himself as one who does nothing, even in the smallest matter, until God “takes him by the hand and leads him like sheep after the shepherd.” That is a striking complement to R’ Tzadok’s use of Yeshayah 26:12 here: the final repair comes when the very framework of self-authored hishtadlus is removed and it is disclosed that “all is from Him.” Chiddushei HaRim, Vayigash §2, states the same point retrospectively: at the complete redemption it will be seen “למפרע שכל עניני הגלות היה לטובתינו,” and every detail of the exile will be clarified as part of the good; he therefore describes the descent itself as carrying its ascent within it, “אנכי ארד עמך… אעלך גם עלה.” These are not denials of the Torah’s present demand for bechirah; they describe the eschatological disclosure R’ Tzadok is speaking about — what becomes visible only when the work of human striving has reached its end.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 84:18 (74:17 in the supplied Har Bracha body citation), on the sale of Yosef, applies Yeshayah63:17 and says: “כְּשֶׁרָצִיתָ נָתַתָּ בְּלִבָּם לֶאֱהֹב וּכְשֶׁרָצִיתָ נָתַתָּ בְּלִבָּם לִשְׂנֹא” — “When You willed, You placed in their hearts to love; when You willed, You placed in their hearts to hate.” The continuation still assigns the brothers consequences for the sale. Rav Tzadok invokes the providential dimension and develops it toward the eventual rectification in which estrangement leads to a fuller return; the Midrash does not erase the deed’s accountability in its present setting.
