inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Daniel’s “my Hod was turned within me to ruin” marks the kingdoms that caused Hod to become daveh. Rome, the seed of Esav, is the dross of that spreading-out — the reverse of Aharon who loved peace, yet making itself appear otherwise. Every nation seeks to resemble Knesses Yisrael precisely in what it most inverts, “like an ape that walks after a man.”

p: (טז) וּמַתִּתְיָהוּ דְּנִצְּחָם, יָדוּעַ בְּסֵפֶר פְּרִי עֵץ חַיִּים שֶׁ״תִּיקֵּן הַהוֹד״, דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרִינַן ״עַל הַנִּסִּים״ בְּהוֹדָאָה, עַיֵּן שָׁם; וְהוּא כֹּהֵן, וְזָכוּ זַרְעוֹ לַמַּלְכוּת אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנֶּעֶנְשׁוּ עַל זֶה — לְפִי שֶׁהֵם כֹּהֲנִים וְנָטְלוּ מְלוּכָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַמְבַּ"ן (פָּרָשַׁת וַיְחִי) עַל פָּסוּק ״לֹא יָסוּר שֵׁבֶט״

And Matisyahu, who overcame them, it is known in Sefer Pri Etz Chaim that he repaired the Hod — therefore we say “for the miracles” in the blessing of thanksgiving Hoda’ah; and he was a priest, and his seed merited the kingship, even though they were punished for it — because they were priests and took the monarchy, as the Ramban wrote Parashas Vayechi on the verse “the scepter shall not depart from Yehudah.”

וְהַיְינוּ דְּעִנְיַן הַמַּלְכוּת אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא ״חֲלוּקַת כָּבוֹד״, שֶׁכֵּן מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו ״שֶׁחָלַק מִכְּבוֹדוֹ״, וְאֵין הַכָּבוֹד מִפְּאַת עַצְמוּתוֹ רַק מִפְּאַת זִיו הוֹד מֶלֶךְ הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט מִמֶּנּוּ

And this is because the matter of monarchy is nothing but an apportioning of honor — as one blesses over him “who apportioned of His honor” — and the honor is not from the essence of the person, but from the radiance of the King’s Hod that spreads from him.

וְעַל כֵּן זָכָה יְהוּדָה, שֶׁתָּפַס בְּפֶלֶךְ הוֹדָיָה, מִדַּת הוֹד לַמַּלְכוּת — וְהַיְינוּ ״שֵׁבֶט מוֹשְׁלִים״ שֶׁהוּא הוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְזֶהוּ מַלְכוּת דָּוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ ״וַיֵּשֶׁב עַל כִּסֵּא ה’״; וּמִדַּת הוֹד דְּאַהֲרֹן הוּא הוֹד דְּנֻקְבָּא — מִדַּת הַבּוּשָׁה כַּנִּזְכָּר

And therefore Yehudah, who grasped “the spindle of Hoda’ah,” merited the middah of Hod for the monarchy — the “scepter of rulers,” which is the Hod of His kingship; and this is the monarchy of David and Shlomo, of whom it says “he sat on the Throne of Hashem”; and the middah of Hod of Aharon is the Hod of the nukva — the middah of shame, as mentioned.

וְנֶאֱמַר ״הֵן יוֹרוּ מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ לְיַעֲקֹב ״, וְגַם הוּא הוֹד מַלְכוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּגִיטִּין סב. ) ״מַאן מַלְכֵי? רַבָּנָן״, וְנֶאֱמַר ״כָּבוֹד חֲכָמִים יִנְחָלוּ ״ — אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא מַלְכוּת בְּלֹא ״שֵׁבֶט מוֹשְׁלִים״, שֶׁאֵין הַמֶּמְשָׁלָה אֶלָּא לְאִישׁ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְהוּא יִמְשֹׁל״

And it says, “they shall teach Your ordinances to Yaakov” (Devarim 33:10), and this too is a Hod of kingship, as they said Gittin 62a, “who are the kings? The Rabbis,” and it says “the wise shall inherit honor” (Mishlei 3:35) — only that it is a monarchy without a “scepter of rulers,” for rulership belongs to the man, as it says “and he shall rule.”

וְגַם בִּיהוּדָה נֶאֱמַר ״וּמְחוֹקֵק מִבֵּין רַגְלָיו״, וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין ה. ) עַל נְשִׂיאֵי אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם מִנֻּקְבְּתָא דְּבֵית דָּוִד, דְּאֵין לָהֶם ״שֵׁבֶט״ לִרְדּוֹת בְּמַקֵּל, רַק הֵם מַלְכֵי דְּרַבָּנָן — דְּזֶהוּ עִיקָּר בְּכֹהֲנִים כַּמְפֹרָשׁ בִּקְרָא בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת

And of Yehudah too it says “and a lawgiver from between his feet,” which the Sages expounded Sanhedrin 5a of the Nesi’im of Eretz Yisrael, who are of the female line of the House of David, who have no “scepter” to rule with the rod — rather they are the “kings of the Rabbis,” which is the essential kingship in priests, as is explicit in Scripture in several places.

וְהַחַשְׁמוֹנָאִים שֶׁתִּיקְּנוּ מִדַּת הַהוֹד זָכוּ לַמַּלְכוּת, רַק לְפִי שֶׁהֵם לְקָחוּהָ בְּ״שֵׁבֶט מוֹשְׁלִים״ נֶעֶנְשׁוּ. וּבֶאֱמֶת בִּימֵי בַּיִת שֵׁנִי, שֶׁהָיָה ״פְּקִידָה בְּעָלְמָא״, לֹא הָיָה רָאוּי מַלְכוּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְעַל כֵּן לֹא מָלַךְ מֶלֶךְ מִבֵּית דָּוִד

And the Chashmona’im, who repaired the middah of Hod, merited the monarchy — only that, since they took it with a “scepter of rulers,” they were punished; and in truth, in the days of the Second Temple, which was but a “remembrance,” monarchy was not fitting for Israel — and therefore no king of the House of David reigned.

וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁהֵם לָקְחוּ מַלְכוּת דְּמֶמְשָׁלָה לְעַצְמָם וְלֹא עַל פִּי נָבִיא, נֶעֶנְשׁוּ עַל יְדֵי הוֹרְדּוֹס שֶׁהֶאֱבִיד כָּל זֵכֶר לָמוֹ, וּבָא הַמַּלְכוּת לַעֲבָדִים שֶׁאֵין רְאוּיִים לַמַּלְכוּת כְּלָל; וְאָז נִבְחַר הִלֵּל, שֶׁהוּא מִנֻּקְבְּתָא דְּבֵית דָּוִד, לְנָשִׂיא

And because they took the ruling monarchy for themselves and not through a prophet, they were punished by Hordos, who destroyed all their memory, and the monarchy came to slaves not fit for it at all; and then Hillel — who is of the female line of the House of David — was chosen as Nasi.
שֶׁהָיָה בִּתְחִלַּת מַלְכוּת הוֹרְדוֹס, שֶׁהָיְתָה מֵאָה וְשָׁלוֹשׁ שָׁנִים בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת,
This was at the beginning of the reign of Hordos, which began one hundred and three years before the destruction of the Temple;
וְהִלֵּל וּבָנָיו מֵאָה בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת טו.).
and Hillel and his descendants held office for one hundred years before the destruction, as our Sages of blessed memory said (Shabbat 15a).
וּבְסֵפֶר עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת כָּתַב דְּעָשׂוּ זֶה לְמַלֹּאות מְקוֹם הַמַּלְכוּת,
And in Sefer Asarah Maamaros he wrote that they established this to fill the place of the monarchy;
וְעַל כֵּן יָרְשׁוּ בָנָיו אַחֲרָיו כְּמִשְׁפַּט הַמְּלוּכָה, עַיֵּן שָׁם.
therefore his descendants inherited the office after him according to the law of kingship; see there.
וְהֵם מִמַּלְכֵי רַבָּנָן, כִּי הִלֵּל רֹאשׁ לְחַכְמֵי הַמִּשְׁנָה,
And they are among the kings who are the Sages, for Hillel is foremost among the Sages of the Mishnah.
וְאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין יא. דְּהָיָה רָאוּי שֶׁתִּשְׁרֶה עָלָיו שְׁכִינָה כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And they said in Sanhedrin 11a that he was worthy for the Shechinah to rest upon him as upon Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him;
וְעַיֵּן שָׁם בְּמַהַרְשָׁ״א בְּחִדּוּשֵׁי אַגָּדוֹת הַטַּעַם.
and see there in Maharsha, Chiddushei Aggados, for the reason.
וְהִסְפִּידוּהוּ שָׁם: תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁל עֶזְרָא,
And there they eulogized him as a disciple of Ezra,
כִּי גַּם אַעֶזְרָא אָמְרוּ שָׁם (כא סוֹף עַמּוּד ב) דְּהָיָה רָאוּי שֶׁתִּנָּתֵן תּוֹרָה עַל יָדוֹ כְּמֹשֶׁה —
for concerning Ezra too they said (Sanhedrin 21b, near the end) that he was worthy for the Torah to be given through him, as through Moshe.
וּשְׁנֵיהֶם, עֶזְרָא וְהִלֵּל, יִסְּדוּ תוֹרָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל אַחַר שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּכְּחָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּסֻכָּה כ.),
And both Ezra and Hillel re-established Torah in Eretz Yisrael after it had been forgotten, as they said in Sukkah 20a, near the end.
אֶלָּא שֶׁעֶזְרָא עִיקַּר מַה שֶּׁיִּסֵּד הָיָה תוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, עַל כֵּן אָמַר שֶׁתִּנָּתֵן תּוֹרָה.
However, Ezra primarily re-established the Written Torah; therefore it says that the Torah should be given through him.
אֲבָל הִלֵּל עִיקַּר יְסוֹדוֹ הָיָה תוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, עַל כֵּן אָמַר שֶׁתִּשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָה,
Hillel, however, primarily established the Oral Torah; therefore it says that the Shechinah should rest upon him,
דְּגִילּוּי תוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה,
for the revelation of the Oral Torah comes through the resting of the Shechinah;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְגַּלָּה לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כָּל מַה שֶּׁתַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ.
and through this there was revealed to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, everything that a seasoned disciple would one day bring forth as a novel Torah insight.
וְעֶזְרָא הָיָה עִם נְחֶמְיָה יַחַד רָאשֵׁי הַדּוֹר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין לו.),
And Ezra and Nechemyah together were the leaders of the generation, as they said in Sanhedrin 36a;
וּשְׁנֵיהֶם רָאשֵׁי אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה וְרָאשֵׁי מְבִיאֵי גְאֻלָּה דְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי לָעוֹלָם,
and both were heads of the Men of the Great Assembly and foremost among those who brought the redemption of the Second Temple into the world,
שֶׁהוּא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא דְּהוֹפָעַת אוֹר הַגְּאֻלָּה הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל סִימָן ד.
which is the arousal from below that brings forth the light of redemption mentioned above in Siman 4.
וְכָל עִנְיַן נְחֶמְיָה כָּלוּל בְּעֶזְרָא, דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא סֵפֶר נְחֶמְיָה עַל שֵׁם עֶזְרָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּחֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין צג:).
And the entire matter of Nechemyah is included in Ezra; therefore the book of Nechemyah is called by the name of Ezra, as they said in the chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 93b).
אַף דְּשָׁם נָתַן טַעַם עַל זֶה לְעוֹנֶשׁ דִּנְחֶמְיָה,
Although there the Gemara gives a reason for this as a punishment of Nechemyah,
סוֹף סוֹף הֲרֵי כָּלוּל כָּל סִפְרוֹ, שֶׁהוּא חֲקִיקַת דִּבְרֵי חָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁחִדֵּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם, עַל שֵׁם עֶזְרָא, וַהֲרֵי כָּלוּל בּוֹ.
ultimately his entire book—the inscription of the words of wisdom that he introduced into the world—is included under the name of Ezra, and thus is included within him.
וְעַל כֵּן עָשׂוּ עֶזְרָא לְעִיקָּר בְּכָל מָקוֹם לִנְתִינַת הַתּוֹרָה עַל יָדוֹ וּלְיַחֵס הִלֵּל לְתַלְמִידוֹ.
Therefore they consistently treated Ezra as the principal figure, both for the giving of the Torah through him and for identifying Hillel as his disciple.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §51): “kingship is drawn from His kingship, as we bless ‘shechalak mikevodo’ who apportioned of His honor; and to the nations of the world it is only ‘to His creatures,’ since they do not recognize this — only perforce, ‘the heart of kings is in the hand of Hashem, like an axe in the hand of the hewer.’” This is §5-16’s very definition of monarchy: the honor “is not from the essence of the person, but from the radiance of the King’s Hod that spreads from him” — apportioned, shechalak mikevodo; and Israel’s kings recognize the Source, while the nations are but “His creatures,” drawn after Him against their will.

paragraphs.text: Devarim 33:10: “יוֹרוּ מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ לְיַעֲקֹב וְתוֹרָתְךָ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, יָשִׂימוּ קְטוֹרָה בְּאַפֶּךָ וְכָלִיל עַל מִזְבְּחֶךָ” — “they shall teach Your ordinances to Yaakov and Your Torah to Israel; they shall place incense before You and whole-offerings on Your altar.” From Moshe’s blessing of the tribe of Levi (Vezos HaBerachah). The verse assigns to Levi and the kohanim both the teaching of Torah and the avodah of the altar. R’ Tzadok’s use: “yoru mishpatecha le-Yaakov” shows that the priestly line, too, bears a Hod of kingship — the majesty of Torah instruction — which is the “kingship of the Rabbis,” a rule by Torah authority rather than by the “scepter of rulers.”

paragraphs.text: Mishlei 3:35: “כָּבוֹד חֲכָמִים יִנְחָלוּ, וּכְסִילִים מֵרִים קָלוֹן” — “the wise shall inherit honor, but fools carry off shame.” From the close of Mishlei ch. 3, contrasting the destinies of the wise and the foolish. Meforshim: kavod (honor) is the enduring inheritance of the wise, whereas the fool’s “elevation” is only disgrace. R’ Tzadok’s use: “kavod chachamim yinchalu” is the Hod — the honor and majesty — that the Torah-sages inherit, the “kings of the Rabbis,” over-against the fool who “raises up kalon (shame),” the counterfeit of the true bushah.

paragraphs.text: Gittin62a reports that Geniva greeted the sages as kings. Asked for his basis, he answered: “מְנָא לָךְ דְּרַבָּנַן אִיקְּרוּ מְלָכִים? אֲמַר לְהוּ: דִּכְתִיב: ״בִּי מְלָכִים יִמְלוֹכוּ וְגוֹ׳״.” — “‘From where do you know that the rabbis are called kings?’ He said to them: ‘For it is written, “Through me kings reign,” and so forth.’” The proof is Mishlei8:15, spoken by wisdom. Rav Tzadok develops this rabbinic kingship as the honor of Torah instruction and distinguishes it from the civil “scepter of rulers.”

paragraphs.text: Asarah Ma’amaros (R’ Menachem Azaryah of Fano): since there is, in principle, no inheritance of the office of Torah-leadership (rabbanus), the fact that Hillel’s descendants inherited the Nesi’us “as by the law of kingship” shows that, after the Chashmona’i servants and Hordos usurped an unfit monarchy, the court instituted that “the crown of Torah complete the crown of kingship,” seating the son on his father’s throne — with Divine approval (Hillel’s line being of great pedigree).

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Matisyahu repaired the Hod — hence “for the miracles” is fixed in the blessing of Hoda’ah. His seed took the kingship and were punished for it, since monarchy belongs to Yehudah, who “grasped the spindle of Hoda’ah.” For kingship is nothing but an apportioning of honor — the radiance of the King’s Hod spreading from its bearer; and the crown of the Sages is a kingship without a ruler’s scepter.

p: (יז) וְהִנֵּה הִלֵּל הֵיפֶךְ עֶזְרָא וְאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁשָּׁקְדוּ לְהוֹסִיף סְיָיגוֹת וְהִזְהִירוּ עַל זֶה (כַּנַ"ל סִימָן ד’); אֲבָל הִלֵּל לֹא הָיָה רוֹצֶה בְּרִיבּוּי הַסְּיָיגוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ לְעִנְיַן שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה דָּבָר, עַיֵּן שַׁבָּת (יז עַמּוּד א) וּבְתוֹסָפוֹת שָׁם (יד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב), מֵהַתּוֹסֶפְתָּא.

Now Hillel was the reverse of Ezra and the Men of the Great Assembly, who diligently added safeguards and warned of it as above, Siman 4; but Hillel did not want a multitude of safeguards, as they said regarding the “eighteen matters” Shabbos 17a. And see Tosafos there (Shabbat 14b, near the end), citing the Tosefta.

וְעַיֵּין (שָׁם קנג:) וּבְרַשִׁ"י דִּפְלוּגְתָּא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְעִנְיַן שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה דָּבָר: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר — ״שַׁמּוּתִי״ מִתַּלְמִידֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ תוֹסָפוֹת שָׁם (קל עַמּוּד ב, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל ״דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר״) — אָמַר עַל זֶה לְשֶׁבַח (״גָּדְשׁוּ סְאָה״), אֲבָל רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִבֵּית הִלֵּל אָמַר לִגְנַאי (״מָחֲקוּ סְאָה״ עַל יְדֵי רִיבּוּי סְיָיגוֹת), וְכֵן בְּכָל מָקוֹם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְקֻלָּא

And see Shabbos 153b and Rashi on the dispute of R’ Eliezer and R’ Yehoshua about the eighteen matters: R’ Eliezer — “Shammuti,” of the disciples of Beis Shammai, as Tosafos writes there (Shabbat 130b, s.v. “DeRabbi Eliezer”) — spoke of it in praise “they heaped up the measure”, but R’ Yehoshua, of Beis Hillel, spoke of it in blame “they wiped away the measure,” through a multitude of safeguards; and so in every place Beis Hillel rule leniently.

ואע"פ שֶׁהוּא נִקְרָא ״תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁל עֶזְרָא״, וְלֹא לָמַד לְפָנָיו, רַק שֶׁהָיָה הוֹלֵךְ בְּעִקְבוֹתָיו — וְהַיְינוּ בְּעִנְיַן הָעֲנָוָה וְהַחֲסִידוּת שֶׁתְּאָרוּהוּ שָׁם; וְכָל אֶחָד לְפִי דּוֹרוֹ: בְּדוֹר עֶזְרָא הָיוּ צְרִיכִים לְהַרְבּוֹת סְיָיגוֹת, וּבָזֶה הָיָה חֲסִידוּתוֹ גַּם עַנְוְותוֹ — שֶׁאֵין מַסְפִּיק לְפִי שִׁפְלוּתָם מִצְוֹת הַתּוֹרָה לְבַד, וְזֶהוּ תִּיקּוּן הַבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה דִּלְהַבָּא

And though he is called “the disciple of Ezra,” he did not learn before him, only that he followed in his footsteps — namely in the matter of humility and piety with which they described him; and each one acted according to his generation: in the generation of Ezra they needed to multiply safeguards, and in this lay his piety and also his humility — that the mitzvos of the Torah alone did not suffice for their lowliness — and this is the rectification of the baal teshuvah going forward.

אֲבָל אַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁמַּתִּתְיָהוּ תִּיקֵּן הַהוֹד, וְאַחֲרָיו בָּא הִלֵּל מִזַּרְעָא דְּדָוִד שֶׁהֵקִים עֻלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, וְעוֹרֵר תִּיקּוּן מִדַּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה מִצַּד תִּיקּוּן הַהוֹד וְהַזִּיו הַמֵּאִיר בָּהּ — שֶׁהוּא הַתִּיקּוּן דִּלְשֶׁעָבַר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה זְדוֹנוֹת כִּזְכִיּוֹת — אֵין צָרִיךְ עוֹד לְרִיבּוּי סְיָיגוֹת מֵעַתָּה לִשְׁמִירָה דִּלְהַבָּא

But afterward, once Matisyahu repaired the Hod, and after him came Hillel of the seed of David, “who raised up the yoke of teshuvah,” and aroused the rectification of the middah of teshuvah from the side of the repaired Hod and radiance that shines within it — which is the rectification of the past, that willful sins become as merits — there is no longer need for a multitude of safeguards for guarding-going-forward,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁגַּם הַזְּדוֹנוֹת שֶׁבּוֹ זְכִיּוֹת וְנִתְקַן לְשֶׁעָבַר גַּם כֵּן; וְעַל כֵּן בְּהוֹפָעַת אוֹר הַזֶּה עַל יָדוֹ אָז לֹא הֻצְרַךְ עוֹד לְרִיבּוּי סְיָיגִים
since even the willful sins in him are merits, and the past too is rectified; and therefore, in the shining of this light through him, there was no longer need for a multitude of fences.

וְנִמְשְׁכוּ תַּלְמִידֵי הִלֵּל הַנִּקְרָאִים ״בֵּית הִלֵּל״, שֶׁהֵם כְּ״אַנְשֵׁי בֵּיתוֹ״ הַנִּמְשָׁכִים אַחֲרָיו, עַד הַחֻרְבָּן — שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי הַקָּטָן שֶׁבְּתַלְמִידָיו עֲדַיִין קַיָּים וְנָשִׂיא אַחַר כָּךְ; וְנִמְצָא כָּל הָאַרְבַּע דּוֹרוֹת עַד רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַנֶּהֱרָג , שֶׁהָיוּ נְשִׂיאִים עַד הַחֻוֽרְבָּן, כֻּלָּם עַל שֵׁם הִלֵּל יִקְרְאוּ, כִּי עֲדַיִין בֵּיתוֹ קַיָּים

And the disciples of Hillel, called “Beis Hillel,” who are like the “men of his house” drawn after him, continued until the Destruction — for R’ Yochanan ben Zakkai, the youngest of his disciples, was still alive and became Nasi afterward; and thus all the four generations — down to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel who was slain — who were Nesi’im until the Destruction, are all called by the name of Hillel, for his “house” still endured.

paragraphs.text: Mishnah Shabbos1:4 recounts the vote for the eighteen decrees when BeisShammai outnumbered BeisHillel in Chananyah benChizkiyah’s upper chamber. Shabbos17a states: “וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם הָיָה הִלֵּל כָּפוּף וְיוֹשֵׁב לִפְנֵי שַׁמַּאי כְּאֶחָד מִן הַתַּלְמִידִים. וְהָיָה קָשֶׁה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּיוֹם שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה בּוֹ הָעֵגֶל.” — “That day Hillel sat bowed before Shammai like one of the students, and it was as hard for Israel as the day the Calf was made.” Tosafos14b discusses the chronology and distinguishes two events; the contrasting evaluations occur explicitly in Shabbos153b: “תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם גָּדְשׁוּ סְאָה. רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם מָחֲקוּ סְאָה.” — “It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says, On that day they heaped up the measure. Rabbi Yehoshua says, On that day they leveled off the measure.” Rashi explains the second image as excessive decrees that people cannot sustain, leading them to transgress. Rav Tzadok gives the approaches their generation-specific place: Ezra’s forward protection, and the later light of rectifying the past.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 153b (and 17a): “R’ Eliezer says: On that day when the eighteen decrees were enacted in the upper chamber of Chananyah ben Chizkiyah they heaped up the measure gadshu se’ah — praise; R’ Yehoshua says: On that day they wiped away the measure machaku se’ah — blame.” Rashi: over-decreeing produces fences the community cannot bear, leading them to transgress. R’ Tzadok: R’ Eliezer (“Shammuti,” of Beis Shammai) praised the multiplication of fences; R’ Yehoshua (Beis Hillel) blamed it — for once Hod was repaired, the emphasis shifts from forward-guarding fences to the teshuvah that rectifies the past.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Hillel was the reverse of Ezra and the Men of the Great Assembly, who diligently multiplied safeguards: he did not want a multitude of them, and Beis Hillel rule leniently throughout. Each acted according to his generation — Ezra’s needed those fences, and in that lay his piety and his humility. Once Matisyahu had repaired the Hod, Hillel, of David’s seed, could arouse the rectification of that middah instead.

p: (יח) וְהֵם גִּילּוּ אוֹר זֶה עַד רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וַחֲבֵרָיו ״עֲשָׂרָה הֲרוּגֵי מְלוּכָה״ מִגְּדוֹלֵי הַתַּנָּאִים, שֶׁבֵּירְרוּ ״דְּיֵשׁ מִיתָה בְּלֹא חֵטְא, רַק כָּךְ עָלָה בְּמַחְשָׁבָה לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרֵךְ״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בִּמְנָחוֹת כט: ) בְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא

And they revealed this light down to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and his colleagues, the “Ten Martyrs of the kingdom,” of the greatest of the Tannaim — who clarified that “there is death without sin, but rather so it arose in His thought before Him,” as they said Menachos 29b of R’ Akiva,

שֶׁהוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ רָצָה בְּכָךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת סא: ) ״מָתַי יָבוֹא (לְיָדִי וַאֲקַיְּימֶנּוּ)״ כו’; וְהַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁרָצָה לְבָרֵר תֹּקֶף אַהֲבָתוֹ לוֹ יִתְבָּרֵךְ בְּ״כָל נֶפֶשׁ״, והשי"ת מִלֵּא רְצוֹנוֹ

who himself desired it, as they said Berachos 61b, “when will this verse come to my hand, that I may fulfill it?”; and this is what he wished — to clarify the intensity of his love for Him “with all his soul” — and Hashem fulfilled his will.

וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים הֲרֵי מָצִינוּ מִיתָה לֹא לְעֹנֶשׁ, רַק לִזְכוּת אוֹ מִכְּבָשַׂי דְּרַחֲמָנָא; וַהֲרֵי ״הוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע הוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא טז. , אִם כֵּן כָּךְ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הָעֲבֵירָה וְהַזָּדוֹן שֶׁל יֵצֶר הָרָע: יֵשׁ שֶׁהוּא כָּךְ, אוֹ שֶׁהוּא מִכְּבָשַׂי דְּרַחֲמָנָא שֶׁכָּךְ עָלָה בִּרְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרֵךְ

And at all events, we have found death that is not for punishment but for a merit, or of the kivshei d’Rachmana; and behold, “the yetzer hara is the Angel of Death,” as they said in Bava Basra 16a — if so, so too with the deed of transgression and willfulness of the yetzer hara: there are cases in which it too is for merit, or that it is of the kivshei d’Rachmana, that so it arose in His will.

וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהַמַּעֲשֶׂה כִּרְצוֹן ה’ הוּא זְכִיּוֹת — אֶלָּא דְּכַוָּנָתוֹ לְאִיסּוּר עוֹשֵׂהוּ כִּשְׁגָגוֹת, אוֹ שֶׁמִּתֹּקֶף אַהֲבָה הוֹפְכוֹ לִזְכִיּוֹת, שֶׁהַחֵטְא הָיָה לְבֵירוּר תֹּקֶף אַהֲבָתוֹ

And since the deed is according to God’s will, it is merits — only that his intent to the forbidden makes it “as inadvertent,” or, from the intensity of love, that love turns it to merits, the sin having been for the clarification of the intensity of his love.

(וּכְמוֹ הַמִּיתָה לְבָרֵר ״בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ״ כִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ, כֵּן הַחֵטְא שֶׁהוּא אַחַר הַתִּיקּוּן כַּ״עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ״ — דְּהַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן ״בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ״ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל) שֶׁהוּא גּוֹבֶרֶת יוֹתֵר עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁאַחַר הַחֵטְא כַּנִּזְכָּר

and just as death clarifies “with all your soul” in its plain sense, so the sin, which after rectification is like an aveirah lishmah — which is likewise “with all your soul,” as mentioned above — which prevails the more through the teshuvah that comes after the sin, as mentioned.

(וְגַם עַל יְדֵי תֹּקֶף הָאַהֲבָה הַמְּעוֹרֶרֶת כֹּחַ הַתְּנוּעָה בַּמּוֹחַ וָלֵב לְהֵיטִיב — דְּהַהִתְעוֹרְרוּת לִפְעֹל טוֹב בָּא עַל יְדֵי אַהֲבָה שֶׁהִיא שֹׁרֶשׁ לְ״קוּם וַעֲשֵׂה״ — עַל יְדֵי זֶה מְתַקֵּן גַּם כַּוָּנַת מוֹחַ וָלֵב הַקּוֹדֶמֶת, לִהְיוֹת מִתְמַתֶּקֶת וּמִתְהַפֶּכֶת וּמִתְבַּטֶּלֶת, וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁאֵינָהּ לְרָע)

And also through the intensity of the love that arouses the power of motion in the mind and heart toward good — for the arousal to act for the good comes through love, which is the root of “arise and do” — thereby he rectifies even the earlier intent of mind and heart, so that it is sweetened and transformed and nullified; and all the more that it is not to evil.

paragraphs.text: Menachos 29b: Moshe saw R’ Akiva expounding “heaps of laws” from the crowns of the letters, then saw R’ Akiva’s flesh “weighed out in the market” his martyrdom. “He said: Master of the Universe, this is Torah and this is its reward? He said: Be silent — so it arose in My thought kach alah be-machashavah lefanai.” Berachos 61b: as they raked R’ Akiva’s flesh with iron combs at the hour of Kerias Shema, he accepted the yoke of Heaven, saying, “All my days I was troubled by this verse, ‘with all your soul’ — even if He takes your soul — I said, when will it come to my hand that I may fulfill it? And now that it has come, shall I not fulfill it?” He prolonged “Echad” until his soul departed. R’ Tzadok: the martyrs clarified that death can be “without sin” — a merit or a kivshei d’Rachmana — and, since “the yetzer hara is the Angel of Death” (Bava Basra 16a), so too a sin can be, at root, God’s own will — hence “merits.”

paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 16a: Reish Lakish taught, “He is the Satan, he is the yetzer hara, he is the Angel of Death” — one and the same adversary under three names: he entices to sin (as the yetzer / Satan), ascends to accuse, and then descends to take the soul (as the Angel of Death). Rashi: the single power that seduces a person to sin is the very one that brings his death. R’ Tzadok’s use: since “the yetzer hara is the Angel of Death,” then just as the Sages found death without sin — “so it arose in His thought,” a matter of the kivshei d’Rachmana rather than punishment — so too the deed of the yetzer’s transgression may be of the kivshei d’Rachmana, “so it arose in His will”; and since the deed accords with God’s will, it is merits (only that the intent to the forbidden reckons it “as inadvertent,” or love transforms it to merit).

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Resisei Layla §27: “ואחר התשובה גמורה דזדונות כזכיות אף הוא מפעולת השם יתברך רק הוא כענין דבר שאינו מתכוין או מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. וזדונות כשגגות היינו כמתעסק בעלמא.” — “After complete teshuvah, when willful sins are like merits, it too is from the action of Hashem, blessed be He, only in the manner of an unintentional act or a labor not needed for its own purpose. Willful sins as inadvertent ones means like one merely occupied in an act without awareness.” The two comparisons should not be collapsed. The present siman distinguishes the retrospectively clarified deed from the person’s earlier forbidden intention, which love must itself rectify.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: This light was revealed down to the Ten Martyrs, who clarified that there is death without sin — rather “so it arose in thought” before Him. R’ Akiva himself desired it, asking when “with all your soul” would come to his hand that he might fulfill it. And since the yetzer hara is itself the Angel of Death, the same holds for the deed of transgression: where it belongs to the kivshei d’Rachmana, the deed is His will, and therefore merits.

sections.en: Great is teshuvah, for it lengthens a person's years

items.h: Great is teshuvah, for it lengthens a person's years
גדולה תשובה שמאחדת שנותיו של אדם.

p: (א) שֶׁמַּאֲרֶכֶת שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם,
That repentance lengthens a person’s years,
הוּא עַל יְדֵי הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת מַדְרֵגַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּלֹא מֵת,
comes through the extension of the level of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, who did not die,
שֶׁזָּכָה לָהּ חִזְקִיָּה בַּהֲאָרָכַת חַיִּים דְּ״וְהוֹסַפְתִּי עַל יָמֶיךָ״ וְגוֹמֵר
which Chizkiyahu merited through the extension of life expressed in “and I will add to your days,” etc.
עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ בְּתֹקֶף כָּל כָּךְ
through the awakening of his teshuvah with such force,
לִפְרֹץ כָּל הַגְּדֵרִים וְהַגְּזֵרוֹת וְהַגְּבוּלִים לְחַיָּיו ״עַד פֹּה תָּבוֹא״
as to burst through all the fences, decrees, and boundaries set upon his life — that is, the fixed limit of “until here you shall come and no further” (cf. Iyov 38:11) —
רַק בְּנַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב בְּלֹא מְצָרִים —
dwelling rather within the inheritance of Yaakov, which is without straits — “an inheritance without boundaries” (Shabbos 118a) —
דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא מֵת
and it is for this reason that he does not die.
כִּי הַמִּיתָה הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַגְּבוּל שֶׁשָּׂם הַבּוֹרֵא לְחַיֵּי הָאָדָם
For death comes about only by means of the boundary that the Creator set upon the life of man;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּלֹא מֵצָרִים
whereas when one stands without straits,
לֹא שַׁיָּךְ מִיתָה
death has no relevance to him.
וּמִיתָתוֹ הָיָה רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן
And Yaakov’s “death” was only in this world, to the perception of the eye,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּתַעֲנִית ה: ) ״מִקְרָא אֲנִי דּוֹרֵשׁ״ כו׳, ״מַקִּישׁ הוּא לְזַרְעוֹ״ כו׳
as they said in Taanis 5b, “I am expounding a verse; he is likened to his offspring”
רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר: אַתָּה מֵבִיא לִי מֵעֵדוּת הַכָּתוּב עַל מַה שֶּׁרָאוּ בְּמוּחָשׁ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
meaning: you bring me the testimony of Scripture concerning what people perceived tangibly in this world,
אֲבָל אֲנִי דּוֹרֵשׁ הַמִּקְרָא
but I expound the verse.
שֶׁהַדְּרָשׁ הוּא הַשָּׂגַת הָעֹמֶק הַנֶּעְלָם מֵהַפְּשָׁט
For the derashah is the apprehension of the hidden depth that lies beyond the plain sense;
וִידִיעַת הַדָּבָר לַאֲמִתּוֹ, הַנֶּעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
and knowledge of the matter as it truly is, which is concealed in this world,
הוּא הַדְּרָשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם תּוֹךְ הַכְּתָב שֶׁהוּא הַנִּגְלֶה לַכֹּל
is precisely the hidden derashah contained within the written text, which is itself revealed to all.
וְעִנְיַן חִיּוּתוֹ הוּא ״מַקִּישׁ הוּא לְזַרְעוֹ״ כו׳
And the matter of his vitality is captured in, “he is likened to his offspring,” etc:
פְּשׁוּטוֹ הַכַּוָּנָה דְּחִיּוּת שֶׁבְּזַרְעוֹ הַיְינוּ חִיּוּתוֹ
its plain intent is that the vitality present in his offspring is his own vitality,
דְּשֹׁרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹת כָּל דּוֹר וָדוֹר בִּכְלָל הוּא נֶפֶשׁ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע״ה
for the root of the souls of each and every generation collectively is the soul of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him.

paragraphs.text: Yeshayahu 38:5: “הָלוֹךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ אֶל חִזְקִיָּהוּ, כֹּה אָמַר ה׳ אֱלֹקֵי דָּוִד אָבִיךָ: שָׁמַעְתִּי אֶת תְּפִלָּתֶךָ, רָאִיתִי אֶת דִּמְעָתֶךָ, הִנְנִי יוֹסִף עַל יָמֶיךָ חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה” — “Go and say to Chizkiyahu: Thus says Hashem, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears; behold, I am adding onto your days fifteen years.” Context: Chizkiyahu HaMelech, mortally ill, “turned his face to the wall” and prayed; Yeshayahu — who had told him “you shall die and not live” (a sealed decree; cf. Berachos 10a) — is sent back with this reprieve. Rashi: the fifteen years granted after his prayer. R’ Tzadok’s use: Chizkiyahu’s teshuvah, awakened “with such force as to burst through all the fences, decrees, and boundaries set upon his life,” drew down the deathless vitality of Yaakov — the very model of how teshuvah “lengthens a person’s years.”

R’ Tzadok’s use: Chizkiyahu’s teshuvah, awakened “with such force as to burst through all the fences, decrees, and boundaries set upon his life,” drew down the deathless vitality of Yaakov — the very model of how teshuvah “lengthens a person’s years.”

paragraphs.text: Iyov 38:11: “וָאֹמַר עַד פֹּה תָבוֹא וְלֹא תֹסִיף, וּפֹא יָשִׁית בִּגְאוֹן גַּלֶּיךָ” — “and I said: until here you shall come and no further; and here shall your proud waves be stayed.” From God’s answer to Iyov out of the whirlwind, of the sea whose bounds He fixed at creation. Meforshim (Rashi): God set a limit (gevul) upon the sea, that it not overflow the dry land. paragraphs.text: Shabbos 118a: “R’ Yochanan said in the name of R’ Yosi: Whoever delights in the Shabbos is given a boundless inheritance nachalah bli metzarim, as it says (Yeshayahu 58:14), ‘Then you shall delight upon Hashem, and I will cause you to ride upon the high places of the earth, and I will feed you the inheritance of Yaakov your father’ — not the inheritance of Avraham, of whom it is written ‘arise, walk the land, to its length and to its breadth’ a bounded measure, nor of Yitzchak, of whom it is written ‘for to you and to your seed I will give all these lands,’ but the inheritance of Yaakov, of whom it is written (Bereishis 28:14), ‘and you shall spread forth to the west and to the east, to the north and to the south’ without limit.” (Yaakov’s inheritance alone is ‘without straits’ — the boundlessness the se’if identifies with his deathlessness.)

paragraphs.text: Taanis 5b: R’ Yochanan said: Yaakov Avinu did not die. Rav Nachman objected, “was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed, and the buriers buried him?!” He replied, “I am expounding a verse — as it says (Yirmeyah 30), ‘and you, fear not, My servant Yaakov, says Hashem — for behold I save you from afar and your offspring from the land of their captivity’ — Scripture likens him to his offspring: just as his offspring are alive, so too is he alive.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzadik, Lag BaOmer §3): “Yaakov did not die, but was only as one asleep — as it is written, ‘Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust’ (Yeshayah 26:19); and as expounded in the Gemara (Taanis 5b), ‘He likens him to his offspring — just as his offspring are alive, so is he alive.’ And since ‘there is no partial analogy,’ He likewise likens his offspring to him: that all the seed of Yaakov will in the end be clarified to stand in the level of ‘Yaakov did not die.’ And when each one is roused from his sleep, he will remember all the words of Torah; and concerning this we plead, ‘let us not be forgotten by You — neither in this world nor in the World to Come.’”

paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah 2:40: “ההשארה לעד אומה שלימה מפרסמים אחדותו נגד אמת ליעקב כי אמת הוא הקיום לעד ... כל חשקות יעקב ועבודתו להוליד בנים ונקראת כל האומה על שמו ואז״ל (תענית) יעקב אבינו לא מת מקיש הוא לזרעו ... כי מצד מדרגות אברהם ויצחק שהוא רק בקשת אהבת השם יתברך ויראתו בתכלית הבירור לא הי׳ מחייבת ההצלה מאור כשדים רק מצד מדרגת יעקב שהוא החפץ להעמיד אומה שלימה והשארה לעד מהכרת כבוד ד׳ מזה נמשך הפדיון לבל ימות ואבד שמו” — “The endurance forever of a whole nation proclaiming His unity corresponds to truth for Yaakov, for truth is enduring existence forever … All Yaakov’s desire and service were to beget children, and the whole nation is named for him; the Sages said, “Yaakov our father did not die”—Scripture compares him to his offspring … The levels of Avraham and Yitzchak, seeking love and fear of Hashem in their utmost clarity, would not themselves have required the rescue from Ur Kasdim. Rather, Yaakov’s level—the desire to establish a whole nation and the perpetual endurance of the recognition of Hashem’s glory—drew forth the redemption, so that he should not die and his name be lost.” This closely parallels the author’s account of Yaakov’s life enduring in the whole people. Chassidic parallel - Sefat Emet, Vayechi 22:3 and 4:3: Sefat Emet gives an especially close Chassidic formulation of the life of Yaakov that R. Tzadok is invoking here. On "Yaakov Avinu lo meis," he explains that Yaakov "left all of his power within Klal Yisrael," so that his force can be awakened in Israel in every generation; elsewhere in Vayechi he explains that Yaakov drew the hidden vitality of Torah even into Egypt, and that through the middah of emes one can find life within the concealment of galus itself. This complements R. Tzadok's use of Taanis 5b: the "lengthening of years" produced by teshuvah is not merely an extension of biological time. Teshuvah reconnects the individual to the undying root of Yaakov, whose life persists in his descendants and can be reawakened within them. In that sense, the penitent's renewed life is a participation in a life that was never severed by death in the first place. The Sefat Emet also helps explain why R. Tzadok immediately moves from Yaakov himself to his seed: Yaakov's immortality is revealed precisely through the continuity of the souls and avodah of Israel.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Teshuvah lengthens a person’s life by drawing down the deathless level of Yaakov Avinu — the root-soul of every Jewish generation.

p: (ב) וְהִנֵּה , שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר תּוֹלְדוֹתָיו
And behold, “the offspring of Yaakov is Yosef” (Bereishis 37:2) — meaning that he is his essential offspring.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה  דְּזִיו אִיקוֹנִין דּוֹמֶה לוֹ.
and the Sages said (Bereishis Rabbah 84:8) that the radiance of Yosef’s countenance resembled his father’s.
וְנוֹדָע דְּכַוָּנַת דְּבָרָיו אֵינוֹ בְּאִיקוֹנִין דְּגוּף שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁהוּא דָּבָר שֶׁלְּשָׁעָה,
And it is known that his meaning is not the countenance of the body in this world, which is something temporary,
רַק בְּאִיקוֹנִין דְּנֶפֶשׁ וְצֶלֶם אֱלֹקִים דְּנִשְׁמַת חַיִּים,
but the countenance of the soul and the divine image of the living soul,
שֶׁהוּא דָּבָר הַקַּיָּם לָעַד, וְזֶה הָיָה דּוֹמֶה לוֹ.
which is something that endures forever; in this he resembled him.
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל שְׁמוֹ ״שְׁאֵרִית יוֹסֵף״
And therefore Israel is called by his name, “the remnant of Yosef” (Amos 5:15),
כִּי גַּם הוּא כּוֹלֵל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל דּוֹר. וְהַיְינוּ דְּיָדוּעַ דְּהוּא נִקְרָא יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, דְּזֶהוּ מִדָּתוֹ,
for he too encompasses the souls of Israel in every generation. This is the meaning of his familiar designation, Yosef HaTzaddik, for this is his attribute;
וְנֶאֱמַר ״וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים ״, שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִדַּת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and it says, “and your people are all tzaddikim” (Yeshayahu 60:21) — this being the middah of all Israel;
״כֻּלָּם״ הַיְינוּ אֲפִילּוּ פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּרְשָׁעִים גְּמוּרִים
“all of them” — meaning even the transgressors of Israel and the wholly wicked,
דְּעִיקַּר שֵׁם ״צַדִּיק״ יָדוּעַ דְּרוֹצֶה לוֹמַר שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית כְּיוֹסֵף.
for the essential meaning of the title “tzaddik” is a guardian of the covenant, like Yosef.
וַהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ בִּ דְּאֵין הָעָרְלָה נִקְרֵאת אֶלָּא עַל שֵׁם אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
And they said in Nedarim 31b that the designation “uncircumcised” applies only to the nations of the world,
וַאֲפִילּוּ עַרְלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים ״מוּלִים״
and even the “uncircumcised” of Israel are essentially called “circumcised.”
וּבְפֶרֶק עוֹשִׂין פַּסִּין  אָמְרוּ דְּבוֹעֵל אֲרַמִּית מִימַשְׁכָא עָרְלָתוֹ וְלָא מְבַשְׁקַר לֵיהּ,
And in the chapter Osin Passin (Eruvin 19a) they said that the foreskin of one who cohabits with a gentile woman is drawn over, and Avraham does not recognize him;
הַיְינוּ דְּאֵינוֹ מַכִּיר לְבַד, לֹא שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת עָרֵל, דַּהֲרֵי הַמָּשׁוּךְ אֵינוֹ עָרֵל, רַק מִדְּרַבָּנָן מִפְּנֵי מַרְאִית הָעַיִן צָרִיךְ לְתַקֵּן.

meaning only that he does not recognize him, not that he is truly uncircumcised. For one whose circumcision is drawn over is not uncircumcised, but must repair it by rabbinic law because of its outward appearance.
וְהַיְינוּ מַרְאִית הָעַיִן דְּלָא מְבַשְׁקַר: לְפִי רְאוּת הָעַיִן וְהַנִּגְלֶה נִרְאֶה דְּקִלְקֵל הַבְּרִית, הֵיפֶךְ יוֹסֵף,
And this is the outward appearance expressed by “he does not recognize him”: to the eye and on the revealed level, he appears to have corrupted the covenant, the opposite of Yosef,
שֶׁבָּזֶה עִיקַּר נִסְיוֹן שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית, שֶׁהוּא לְאַכְפְּיָא בְּדַרְגָּא דְּצַדִּיק בְּצִמְצוּם,
for in this lies the essential trial of guarding the covenant: subduing the inclination at the level of the tzaddik, through restraint;
הוּא בַּאֲרַמִּית, דְּאֵין לָהּ שַׁיָּכוּת עִם זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל.
it is tested precisely with a gentile woman, who has no connection to the seed of Israel.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן נִסָּיוֹן דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה בְּיִשְׂרְאֵלִית לֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדוֹ
whereas the trial of David HaMelech with a Jewish woman did not succeed for him,
שֶׁשָּׁם הַנִּסָּיוֹן הָיָה לְאַהְפְּכָא לֹא לְכַפְיָיא
for the trial there was one of “transforming,” rather than “subduing,”
דְּבֶאֱמֶת רְאוּיָה הִיא לוֹ וְאֵין זֶה דַּרְגָּא דְּיוֹסֵף
since in truth she was fitting for him, and this is not the level of Yosef.
וְעִיקַּר הַהַבְדָּלָה בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים הוּא בְּאוֹת הַבְּרִית, דְּעַל כֵּן הָעָרְלָה נִקְרֵאת עַל שֵׁם אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
And the essential distinction between Israel and the nations is in the sign of the covenant — which is why “orlah” is named for the nations.
וְרוֹצֶה לוֹמַר בִּקְדֻשַּׁת שֹׁרֶשׁ הַתּוֹלָדָה
And he means the distinction lies in the holiness of the root of one’s birth,
כִּי בְּמַעֲשֶׂה אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם שָׁוִים
for in deed it is possible that both are alike,
רַק זֶה שָׁרְשׁוֹ טוֹב
but this one’s root is good;
וְעַל כֵּן אֲפִילּוּ פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּכְלַל ״שְׁאֵרִית יוֹסֵף״ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים
and therefore even the transgressors of Israel are included in “the remnant of Yosef — all of them tzaddikim.”
וַאֲפִילּוּ חֲסִידֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לָזֶה
And even the pious of the nations have no share in this,
כִּי הַמְשָׁכַת מְקוֹר חִיּוּתָם מִמְּקוֹם טֻמְאָה וְעׇרְלָה
for the drawing of the source of their vitality is from a place of impurity and “orlah”;

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֹׁרֶשׁ חִיּוּתָם מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם. וְעַל כֵּן עִיקַּר תּוֹלְדוֹתָיו יוֹסֵף, לוֹמַר דְּזַרְעוֹ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים מִצַּד הוֹלָדָתוֹ אוֹתָם, דְּעִיקַּר תּוֹלְדוֹתָיו הוּא כֵן מִשָּׁרְשָׁם.

The Children of Israel, however, derive the root of their vitality from Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him. Therefore his essential offspring is Yosef, expressing that all his offspring are righteous through his begetting them, for this is the essential nature of his offspring at their root.
דְּכָל עִנְיַן יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע״ה ״מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה״
For the whole matter of Yaakov Avinu, “his bed was whole” (Pesachim 56a; Vayikra Rabbah 36:5),
הַיְינוּ שֶׁכָּל הוֹלְדוֹתָיו בִּקְדֻשָּׁה
means that all his offspring were conceived in holiness,
כִּי הוּא שְׁלֵימוּת תִּיקּוּן חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁהָיָה בְּתַאֲוָה
for he is the completion of the rectification of Adam’s sin, which was rooted in desire.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ עַל יִשַׁי שֶׁמֵּת בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ
And therefore they said of Yishai that he died “through the counsel of the serpent” —
הַיְינוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ הֲסָתַת הַנָּחָשׁ בְּחֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן, דִּ״בְעָווֹן מָלֵא״ — אֲפִילּוּ חָסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים וְכוּלֵי, דְּהָיָה בוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ שֶׁל כַּוָּנָה לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ.

meaning the root of the serpent’s incitement in Adam’s sin: the word “be’avon” (in iniquity) is written in full—even the most pious of the pious, etc.—for there was in him a root of intent for his own pleasure.
וּמִזֶּה נִמְשְׁכָה הַבּוּשָׁה לְאָדָם וּלְאִשְׁתּוֹ אַחַר הַחֵטְא, כְּשֶׁהִכִּירוּ שֶׁהֵם עֵירוּמִּים,
And from this was drawn the shame of Adam and his wife after the sin, when they recognized that they were naked —
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהִרְגִּישׁוּ בַּהֲנָאָה גּוּפָנִית
because they felt bodily pleasure;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִקּוֹדֶם נֶאֱמַר ״וְלֹא יִתְבֹּשָׁשׁוּ״
whereas beforehand it says, “and they were not ashamed” (Bereishis 2:25).
וְכֵן יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר ״הָבָה אֶת״ וְגוֹמֵר, מַה דְּקַל שֶׁבַּקַּלִּים אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר כֵּן מִפְּנֵי הַבּוּשָׁה שֶׁבָּאָה אַחַר חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
And likewise Yaakov Avinu said, “Give me my wife” — a phrasing that even the coarsest of the coarse would not use, on account of the shame that came after Adam’s sin —
רַק הוּא דְּלֹא הִרְגִּישׁ בְּשׁוּם הֲנָאָה גּוּפָנִית
but he felt no bodily pleasure whatever,
רַק לְהַעֲמִיד תּוֹלָדוֹת לְבַד נִתְכַּוֵּון
intending solely to establish offspring.
וּכְמוֹ לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא דְּאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל פָּסוּק ״לֵב בָּשָׂר״ — לֵב לְהוֹצִיא בָּשָׂר,
And as concerning the future, when they expounded the verse “a heart of flesh”: a heart to bring forth flesh, meaning to beget offspring,
הֲרֵי זֶה אֶצְלוֹ כַּהֲנָחַת תְּפִלִּין וְכָל מִצְוֹת הַתּוֹרָה, וְלֹא שַׁיָּךְ בּוּשָׁה.
so that the marital act is to him like the donning of tefillin and all the mitzvos of the Torah, and no shame applies.
וְעַל כֵּן ״מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה״, דְּ״שׁוֹמֵר מִצְוָה לֹא יֵדַע דָּבָר רָע״
And therefore “his bed was whole,” for “one who guards a mitzvah knows no evil thing” (Koheles 8:5),
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלָל שֶׁיָּבוֹא מִמִּצְוָה עֲבֵירָה וְדָבָר רָע ח״ו
and it is entirely impossible that a sin or evil thing should issue from a mitzvah, Heaven forbid.
רַק יְצִיאַת הַפְּסֹלֶת הוּא עַל יְדֵי עִרְבּוּב הֲנָאוֹת גּוּפָנִיּוֹת הַנִּמְשָׁכוֹת מֵעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ, שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵב עַל יְדֵי חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּכָל זַרְעוֹ.

Rather, the emergence of “dross” in one’s offspring comes about only through the admixture of bodily pleasures drawn from “the counsel of the serpent,” which became intermingled through Adam’s sin into all his seed.
וְהָאָבוֹת הֵם שֶׁבָּאוּ לְתַקֵּן זֶה, וּגְמַר הַתִּיקּוּן הָיָה בְּיַעֲקֹב
And the Avos are those who came to rectify this, and the completion of the rectification was in Yaakov,
דְּאָמְרִי עֲלֵיהּ ״אֲשֶׁר פָּדָה אֶת אַבְרָהָם״
of whom they expound, “Yaakov, who redeemed Avraham” (Yeshayahu 29:22; cf. Sanhedrin 19b).
וְגַם אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק נִקְרְאוּ ״יַעֲקֹב״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה,
And Avraham and Yitzchak too are retroactively “called Yaakov,”
הַיְינוּ אַחַר שֶׁבָּא הוּא לָעוֹלָם נִתְבָּרְרוּ גַּם הֵם
meaning that once he came into the world, they too were “clarified,”
דְּאֵין נִקְרָא זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל אָבוֹת אֶלָּא יַעֲקֹב בִּלְבַד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּנְדָרִים (לא עַמּוּד א).
for in the fullest sense only Yaakov is called “the seed” of the Avos, as they said in Nedarim.
וְנִמְצָא גַּם מִטָּתָם הָיְתָה שְׁלֵימָה
It follows that their “beds,” too, were whole,
שֶׁהֲרֵי הַפְּסֹלֶת אֵינוֹ זַרְעָם כְּלָל
for the “dross” (Yishmael, Esav) is not their true seed at all,
כִּי לֹא הָיָה זֶה מִצִּדָּם
since it did not come from their side.
וּכְמוֹ דְּאֵצֶל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵמָה, אַף שֶׁנִּרְאֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ אֵיזֶה פְּסֹלֶת לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן, בֶּאֱמֶת אֵינוֹ פְּסֹלֶת כְּלָל,
And just as Yaakov Avinu’s bed is whole—although to the eye there appears to be some dross, in truth it is no dross at all—
כֵּן אֶצְלָם, אַף דְּלְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן הָיָה נִרְאֶה אֵיזֶה פְּסֹלֶת מֵהֶם, בֶּאֱמֶת אֵינוֹ שֶׁלָּהֶם כְּלָל.
so too with them: although to the eye it appeared that some dross emerged from them, in truth it is not theirs at all.
דְּזֶה כָּל כֹּחַ יַעֲקֹב — ״נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים״
For this is the entire power of Yaakov — “an inheritance without boundaries” (Shabbos 118a):
הַיְינוּ גְּבוּלֵי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁהוּא כְּפִי הַהִתְגַּלּוּת לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן, דְּבָזֶה הֵם הַגְּבוּלִים.
that is, the boundaries of this world, which exist only according to the revealed appearance to the eye — that is where the “boundaries” lie.
וְזֶהוּ דְּחִיַּת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה הַנִּזְכָּר בְּסִימָן ג,
And this is the “pushing-aside of a negative commandment” of the Torah, mentioned in Siman 3,
שֶׁזּוֹכִין לָהּ בַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה בְּעוֹמֶק תְּשׁוּבָתָם
which the baalei teshuvah merit in the depth of their teshuvah.
וְצַדִּיק גָּמוּר הוּא בְּהִיפּוּךְ מִזֶּה
The perfect tzaddik is the reverse of this:
שֶׁנִּשְׁמָר שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲבֹר עַל שׁוּם דָּבָר מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
he guards himself from transgressing anything of the words of Torah —
וְהוּא זִיו אִיקוֹנִין שֶׁל יוֹסֵף, שֶׁהוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב ע״ה בְּזַרְעוֹ שֶׁבַּחַיִּים בְּכָל דּוֹר
and he is the “radiance of the countenance of Yosef,” which is the spreading-forth of the middah of Yaakov Avinu among his living offspring in every generation.

paragraphs.text: Yeshayahu 60:21: “וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים, לְעוֹלָם יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ, נֵצֶר מַטָּעַי מַעֲשֵׂה יָדַי לְהִתְפָּאֵר” — “and your people are all tzaddikim; they shall inherit the land forever; the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to glory.” From Yeshaya’s prophecy of Zion’s future glory. Meforshim: in the future all Israel will be found righteous (the Mishnah, Sanhedrin 90a, opens “all Israel have a share in the World to Come” from this verse). R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the middah of all Israel — “kulam,” even the transgressors and the wholly wicked — for the essential meaning of “tzaddik” is a guardian of the covenant like Yosef; every Jew’s root is holy, whatever appears to the eye.

paragraphs.text: Amos 5:15: “שִׂנְאוּ רָע וְאֶהֱבוּ טוֹב וְהַצִּיגוּ בַשַּׁעַר מִשְׁפָּט, אוּלַי יֶחֱנַן ה׳ אֱלֹקֵי צְבָאוֹת שְׁאֵרִית יוֹסֵף” — “hate evil and love good, and establish justice in the gate; perhaps Hashem, God of Hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Yosef.” From Amos’s call to repentance. Meforshim: “she’eris Yosef” is the remnant of Israel, called by Yosef’s name. R’ Tzadok’s use: Israel is called “the remnant of Yosef” because Yosef, the guardian of the covenant, “comprises the souls of Israel in every generation” — and therefore even the transgressors of Israel are included in “the remnant of Yosef — all of them tzaddikim.”

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 56a (and Vayikra Rabbah 36:5) — “mittaso shleimah”: the Gemara relates that as Yaakov lay dying he feared there might be a blemish in his “bed” (as Avraham had produced Yishmael, and Yitzchak, Esav); his sons declared, “Shema Yisrael, Hashem Elokeinu Hashem echad — just as in your heart there is but One, so in ours,” whereupon Yaakov responded “Baruch shem kevod malchuso le-olam va’ed.” The Sages conclude that Yaakov’s bed was whole mittaso shleimah — all his offspring were worthy, none cast off (so too Vayikra Rabbah 36:5). R’ Tzadok’s use: “mittaso shleimah” means all his offspring were conceived in holiness, for Yaakov completed the rectification of Adam’s sin (which was rooted in desire); hence no true “dross” issues from him — and the same holds of all Israel, his seed.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 118a — “nachalah bli metzarim”: R’ Yochanan said in the name of R’ Yosi, whoever delights in the Shabbos is granted “a boundless inheritance nachalah bli metzarim,” as it says (Yeshaya 58:14), “then you shall delight in Hashem… and I will feed you the inheritance of Yaakov your father” — not the bounded inheritance promised to Avraham (“arise, walk the length and breadth of the land”) or to Yitzchak, but the unbounded inheritance of Yaakov, of whom it says “u-faratzta — you shall spread out to the west and east, north and south” (Bereishis 28:14). R’ Tzadok’s use (recurring from §1): the whole “power of Yaakov” is this “inheritance without boundaries”; the “boundaries” of this world exist only “according to the revealed appearance to the eye,” but in the inward truth the seed of Yaakov is beyond all straits — so that any apparent “dross” among the poshei Yisrael is only external. Izhbitz-Radzin and Sefat Emet parallel - Mei HaShiloach, Anthology, Collectanea, Siddur 1; Sefat Emet, Vayera 30:3: The Izhbitz-Radzin tradition sharply supports the distinction in this se'if between the holy root of the Jewish soul and the external corruption produced by sin. Mei HaShiloach teaches on "Neshamah shenasata bi tehorah hi" that the neshamah itself is never reached by cheit or pegam; nefesh remains joined to the body, while ruach signifies the faculty of bechirah through which a person chooses good and rejects evil. Thus sin is terribly real at the level of choice and embodied life, but it does not rewrite the deepest origin of the neshamah. Sefat Emet, Vayera 30:3, develops the complementary side: Israel are "zera emes" because their souls extend from beginning to end, and the bris is meant to bring the body itself into correspondence with the holy neshamah. This illuminates R. Tzadok's insistence that even poshei Yisrael retain the name and root of tzaddikim. The dross can cover, distort, and damage the vessel, but it is not the essential identity of the soul. Teshuvah therefore does not manufacture a new Jewish essence; it uncovers and re-aligns the embodied person with the holy root that remained intact beneath the concealment.

This illuminates R. Tzadok's insistence that even poshei Yisrael retain the name and root of tzaddikim. The dross can cover, distort, and damage the vessel, but it is not the essential identity of the soul. Teshuvah therefore does not manufacture a new Jewish essence; it uncovers and re-aligns the embodied person with the holy root that remained intact beneath the concealment.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Yosef is Yaakov’s essential “offspring” — the guarding of the bris — which is why even the poshei Yisrael are called “kulam tzaddikim.” The root of every Jewish soul is holy, so any apparent “dross” is only external; Yaakov’s “bed was whole.”

p: (ג) וּמִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע״ה עַצְמוֹ דְּלֹא מֵת כְּלָל
And as for the measure of Yaakov Avinu himself, that he did not die at all — the deathless level in its own right, not merely its extension through descendants —
זֶה לֹא נִתְגַּלָּה עֲדַיִן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עַד שֶׁיְבוּלַּע הַמָּוֶת —
this has not yet been revealed in this world, until death shall be swallowed up forever (Yeshayahu 25:8); for a world still ruled by death cannot yet contain an openly deathless man.
אֲבָל לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן גַּם אוֹתוֹ קָבְרוּ קַבְרַיָּא וַחֲנָטוּ כו׳
but to the eye’s perception, him too “the buriers buried and the embalmers embalmed,” etc. — the outward “death” that this world’s concealment requires.
רַק הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא בְּחִיּוּת זַרְעוֹ
Rather, the present spreading-forth in this world is only in the vitality of his offspring — his deathless life shows itself here not as his own continued life but as the living-on of his seed;
וְזֶה נִקְרָא יוֹסֵף לְשׁוֹן הוֹסָפָה
and this is called “Yosef,” a term of “addition,” the name itself (from asaf/yosef, “to add”) pointing to this mode of survival-through-increase,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתּוֹסְפוּ נְפָשׁוֹת רַבּוֹת דְּזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר
for through it many souls of the seed of Israel are added in each and every generation.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה עַמּוּד א): אַלְמָלֵא אֲבוֹתֵינוּ חָטְאוּ אָנוּ לֹא בָּאנוּ, (אוֹ כְּמִי שֶׁלֹּא בָּאנוּ) —

And along the lines of what they said in Avodah Zarah 5a: “Had our ancestors not sinned, we would not have come into the world,” or “we would be as those who never came,” — a striking teaching: it is precisely the sin and its consequent mortality that made room for each later soul to be born as its own person;
שֶׁהָיִינוּ כְּלוּלִים בָּהֶם וְלֹא הָיָה מָקוֹם לְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ

for we would have been subsumed within them, and there would have been no place for each soul to spread forth as an entity of its own — all later generations remaining folded, undifferentiated, within the first.
וְהִנֵּה הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת זֶה הוּא גוֹרֵם הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת וְהִתְרַבּוּת נַחֲלַת וְנֶפֶשׁ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע״ה עַצְמוֹ
And behold, this very spreading-forth is what causes the spreading and increase of the portion and soul of Yaakov Avinu himself,
שֶׁהוּא עֶצֶם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
for he is the very essence of the souls of Israel — so that every soul added below is, at root, more of him.
וְנִמְצָא הֶעְלֵם חִיּוּתוֹ, שֶׁכִּסְבוּרִין אָנוּ שֶׁהוּא מִיעוּט חִיּוּת, אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא רִיבּוּי וְהוֹסָפַת חִיּוּת
It emerges that the concealment of his vitality, which we imagine to be a diminishment of vitality, is in fact a multiplication and addition of vitality,
שֶׁנִּתְרַחֵב וְנִתּוֹסֵף בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַרְבֵּה יוֹתֵר
which has broadened and increased through this spreading-forth all the more.
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן הוֹסָפַת יָמִים עַל יָמָיו דְּחִזְקִיָּה אַחַר שֶׁקִּבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ לִינְסַב וְיוֹלִיד זֶרַע —
And this too is the matter of the addition of days to the days of Chizkiyahu, after he accepted upon himself to marry and beget offspring (cf. Berachos 10a),
שֶׁיִּהְיוּ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת חִיּוּתוֹ לְדוֹרוֹת
so that his vitality would spread forth into future generations.
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּכָל הַצֶּאֱצָאִים גְּנוּזִים בַּאֲבוֹתָם, שֶׁהֲרֵי מֵהֶם יָצְאוּ —
As is known, all offspring are stored away within their forebears, for they emerged from them,
וּבַהוֹלָדָה הֵם יוֹצְאִים מֵהֶעְלֵם לְגִילּוּי וּמֵהַצִּמְצוּם לְהִתְרַחֲבוּת
and in birth they emerge from concealment to revelation, from contraction to expansion;
וְזֶה גּוֹרֵם גַּם כֵּן הִתְרַחֲבוּת וְהוֹסָפָה בְּחִיּוּתוֹ וְיָמָיו, עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁאַחַר הַחֵטְא בָּזֶה
and this too brings about expansion and addition in his vitality and days, through the teshuvah that follows the sin.
וְהוּא הָיָה מִצַּד הַתְחָלַת מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ, דַּרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע״ה, שֶׁהוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
But he Chizkiyahu was only at the beginning of this level — the rung of Yaakov Avinu — which as yet is concealed in this world.
וְעַל כֵּן אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר  דְּרַק הִשְׁלִימוּ לוֹ וּמִשֶּׁלּוֹ נָתְנוּ לוֹ
Therefore there is an opinion in Yevamos 50a that they merely “completed” his allotted years and “gave him from his own,”
וְאֵין כָּאן עֲדַיִין הָאֲרָכָה גְּמוּרָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and there is here as yet no true lengthening of life in this world.
וְגַם לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הוֹסִיפוּ לוֹ, לֹא הֶאֱרִיךְ יָמִים יוֹתֵר מִשְּׁאָר בְּנֵי הַדּוֹר
And even according to the one who holds that they “added” to him, he did not live longer than the rest of his generation,
וְאֵין כָּאן עֲדַיִין מַדְרֵגַת מַאֲרֶכֶת יָמָיו, רַק מַה שֶּׁנִּדְחָה הַגְּזֵרָה וְהַגְּבוּל מִיָּמָיו
and there is here as yet no level of “lengthening his years,” only that the decree and the boundary were pushed off from his days.
וְזֶהוּ רַק כִּדְחִיַּית לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וּגְזֵרַת הַתּוֹרָה
And this is only like the “pushing-aside” of a negative precept, a decree of the Torah;
אֲבָל כַּאֲשֶׁר יַעֲמִיק יוֹתֵר בִּתְשׁוּבָתוֹ וּבִדְבֵיקוּתוֹ בֵּאלֹקִים חַיִּים
but when a person delves deeper in his teshuvah and in his cleaving to the living God,
יִזְכֶּה לְחַיִּים וְהָאֲרָכַת יָמִים, עַל יְדֵי שׁוּבוֹ מֵרִשְׁעָתוֹ — עַל יְדֵי זֶה יִחְיֶה
he will merit life and length of days; through his return from his wickedness — “through this he shall live.”
כִּי יוֹסֵף שֶׁהָיָה צַדִּיק גָּמוּר, וְהוּא עִיקַּר דַּרְגָּא דְּהוֹסָפָה
For Yosef, who was a perfect tzaddik and is the essential rung of “addition,”
אָמְרוּ ז״ל  דְּאַדְּרַבָּא נִפְחֲתוּ לוֹ עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים בִּשְׁבִיל חֵטְא דְּשָׁמַע ״עַבְדְּךָ אָבִינוּ״

the Sages said (Sotah 13b) that, on the contrary, ten years were subtracted from his life on account of the “sin” of hearing his brothers say “your servant our father” ten times, without protesting — so that the very embodiment of “addition” was himself diminished, teaching that this rung is precarious.
הָעִנְיַן דְּהוֹסָפָה הֲרֵי נִרְאֶה כְּמוֹסִיף וּמַעֲדִיף עַל הָעִיקַּר
The matter is that “addition” appears as though it adds and exceeds beyond the essential root — and whatever seems to stand “above” its source invites the illusion of independent worth,
וְצָרִיךְ בָּזֶה שְׁמִירָה יְתֵירָה שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹא לְהִתְגָּאוֹת וְלַחְשֹׁב שֶׁהוּא בֶּאֱמֶת טוֹב יוֹתֵר
and this requires extra guarding, lest one come to haughtiness and think that he is truly better.
וְעַל זֶה הוּזְהֲרוּ ״אַל תֹּאמַר בְּצִדְקָתְךָ וּבְיֹשֶׁר לְבָבְךָ ״ וְגוֹמֵר
Regarding this they were warned: “Do not say — ‘through my righteousness and the uprightness of my heart’ Hashem has brought me in,’ etc.” (Devarim 9:4–5–5),
וְאַזְהָרָה זוֹ הוּא לְמִי שֶׁהוּא צַדִּיק גָּמוּר
and this warning is addressed precisely to one who is a perfect tzaddik,
וְזֶה עָלוּל לִטְעוֹת, וּבָזֶה יוּכַל לְהַחְשִׁיב עַצְמוֹ טוֹב יוֹתֵר מֵעִילָּתוֹ וְשָׁרְשׁוֹ
for such a one is liable to err, and might come to consider himself better than his Cause and his Root,
וְאֵין מַכִּיר שֶׁעִיקַּר מַה שֶּׁהוּא טוֹב הוּא רַק מִמֶּנּוּ
not recognizing that the essence of whatever good he has is only from Him.

paragraphs.text: Yeshayahu 25:8: “בִּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח, וּמָחָה אֲדֹנָי ה׳ דִּמְעָה מֵעַל כָּל פָּנִים” — “He will swallow up death forever, and the Lord God will wipe away tears from every face.” From Yeshaya’s prophecy of the end of days (ch. 25). Meforshim (Rashi; and the Sages, Kesuvos 111b) take “bila ha-maves la-netzach” to mean that death — decreed on mankind through Adam’s sin — is abolished in the World to Come. R’ Tzadok’s use here: the measure of Yaakov Avinu himself, “that he did not die at all,” cannot yet be revealed in this world until death is swallowed up — a world still ruled by death cannot contain an openly deathless man; therefore “him too the buriers buried and the embalmers embalmed,” the outward “death” that this world’s concealment requires. (The verse is treated also at Siman 3 §5.)

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 30:24 (the name Yosef): “וַתִּקְרָא אֶת שְׁמוֹ יוֹסֵף לֵאמֹר, יֹסֵף ה׳ לִי בֵּן אַחֵר” — “and she called his name Yosef, saying, ‘May Hashem add yosef to me another son.’” Rachel, upon bearing Yosef (Vayeitzei). Rashi: the name is from the root y-s-f, “to add” — her prayer for an additional son. R’ Tzadok’s use: the name itself — “Yosef, a term of addition hosafah” — expresses the very mode by which Yaakov’s deathless vitality persists in this world: not as his own continued life, but as the adding of ever more souls of the seed of Israel in each generation.

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 5a: Reish Lakish: “come, let us be grateful to our ancestors — for had they not sinned, we would not have come into the world.” The Gemara concludes that had Israel not sinned they would not have died; and R’ Yosi taught, “Israel accepted the Torah only so that the Angel of Death should not rule over them,” as it says “I said, you are angelic beings, sons of the Most High, all of you — (yet) you corrupted your deeds, therefore you shall die like Adam” (Tehillim 82:6–7). The sugya qualifies the initial formulation: “לא תימא אנו לא באנו לעולם, אלא כמי שלא באנו לעולם” — “Do not say that we would not have come into the world, but that we would have been as though we had not come into the world.” This is the qualification the author develops through inclusion in the ancestors.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 10a: When Yeshayahu told Chizkiyahu “you shall die and not live” (Yeshayahu 38:1) — because “you did not engage in the mitzvah of procreation” — Chizkiyahu answered that he had seen by ru’ach ha-kodesh that unworthy children would issue from him. Yeshayahu replied: “What have you to do with the secrets of the Merciful One? What you are commanded, you are obligated to do.” Chizkiyahu said: “Then give me your daughter — perhaps my merit together with yours will cause worthy children to issue from me.” (Only after he accepted to marry and beget were his years lengthened.)

paragraphs.text: Yevamos 50a: It was taught: “‘the number of your days I will fill’ (Shemos 23) — these are the years preordained to a person at birth. If he merits, they complete the full span for him; if he does not merit, they reduce it — the words of R’ Akiva. And the Sages say: if he merits, they add to him; if not, they reduce.” They said to R’ Akiva: does it not say (II Melachim 20), “I will add to your days fifteen years” to Chizkiyahu? Rashi: they inherit it through the wickedness of the nations and the merit of the Avos — not their own righteousness. R’ Tzadok’s use: this admonition is addressed precisely to the perfect tzaddik — the “addition” / Yosef rung — who is liable to the illusion that he is “better than his Cause and his Root,” failing to recognize that “the essence of whatever good he has is only from Him.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Korach §6): “he was not aware of this at all, and held no credit to himself — he looked only to Hashem who chose him, and not to his own power at all, as it says, ‘and what is Aharon that you murmur against him?’” This is §6-3’s tzaddik who does not stumble into the pride the se’if warns of: the rung of “addition” tempts one to “think he is truly better,” but Aharon — the very embodiment of drawing-near — took no credit, seeing all his good as flowing from the One who chose him. Chassidic parallel - Chiddushei HaRim on Torah, Chayei Sara 1; Sefat Emet, Vayechi 4:3: Chiddushei HaRim makes the relation between teshuvah and "length of days" unusually explicit. Commenting on Sarah's years, he notes the Zoharic principle that through teshuvah "in one hour and in one moment" a person can repair days that have already passed as though those days had been filled with mitzvos and good deeds; this is the deeper meaning of willful sins becoming merits. The point closely complements R. Tzadok's distinction here between merely postponing a decree of death and true arichus yamim. A penitent does not only receive additional days at the end of life; teshuvah can restore content and holiness to days already spent. Sefat Emet, Vayechi 4:3, adds that Yaakov drew a hidden current of life even into Egypt and that "Yaakov Avinu did not die" can be found by seeking the concealed Torah-life within exile. Read together, these sources sharpen R. Tzadok's claim: genuine lengthening of life reaches backward as well as forward. It is the recovery of the life concealed in apparently lost time, rooted in Yaakov's deathless emes rather than simply an extension of the calendar.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Yaakov’s own deathlessness is not yet revealed in this world; here it appears as “Yosef” — addition through offspring. Chizkiyahu’s extra years were only the lower rung (the decree pushed off), not true length-of-life; the deeper rung comes through the depth of teshuvah. And the “addition”/tzaddik level carries a danger of haughtiness.

p: (ד), — וְיָדוּעַ דִּשְׁלֹשֶׁת שָׁרְשֵׁי הַטֻּמְאָה דְּיֵצֶר רָע
And it is known that the three roots of impurity of the evil inclination,
זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה לִשְׁלוֹשָׁה אֲבָהָן
standing one opposite the other facing the three Patriarchs:
הֵם קִנְאָה וְתַאֲוָה וְכָבוֹד
are envy, lust, and the pursuit of honor (Avot 4:21):
שֶׁהוּא כַּעַס הַבָּא מִפְּסֹלֶת הַגְּבוּרָה דְּיִצְחָק
envy being wrath that emerges from the dross of Isaac's Gevurah,
וְתַאֲוָה מִפְּסֹלֶת הַחֶסֶד דְּאַבְרָהָם
and lust from the dross of Abraham's Chesed,
שֶׁהֵם שָׁרְשֵׁי הָרַע שֶׁבָּאוּמּוֹת
which are the roots of evil within the archetypal nations.
אֱדוֹם וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל – בִּרְצִיחָה וְנִיאוּף
Edom and Ishmael—expressed through murder and illicit sexual immorality.
וְגַאֲוָה הוּא נֶגֶד מִדַּת אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ עֲנָוָה
And pride/arrogance stands opposite the attribute of truth belonging to Jacob whose true trait is humility, (,
דַּרְגָּא דִּנְחֹשֶׁת נֶגֶד כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב
(the spiritual rung of copper versus silver and gold,
שֶׁהֵם רוֹמְזִים לִשְׁלֹשָׁה אֲבָהָן כַּיָּדוּעַ).
which allude to the three Patriarchs as is known).
כִּי הַגֵּיאוּת הוּא שֶׁקֶר
For pride is an absolute falsehood,
דַּאֲפִילּוּ אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נֶאֱמַר (תְּהִלִּים צג, א): "גֵּאוּת לָבֵשׁ"
since even regarding Hashem, blessed be He, it is stated: 'He is robed in majesty (ge'ut),'
רַק דֶּרֶךְ לְבוּשׁ,
meaning merely by way of an outward garment,
וּ"מִתְגָּאֶה עַל גֵּיוְותָנָא" ;
and 'He exalts Himself over the arrogant' (Chagigah 13b);
אֲבָל (מִשְׁלֵי ג, לד): "וְלַעֲנָוִים יִתֶּן חֵן" וְכָבוֹד
yet 'unto the humble He gives favor' and honor,
וּבִמְקוֹם גְּדוּלָּתוֹ אַתָּה מוֹצֵא עַנְוְותָנוּתוֹ .
and wherever you find His greatness, there you find His humility (Megillah 31a).
וְנִמְצָא צוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁחֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד —
And this is the form of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, which is engraved upon the Throne of Glory (Chullin 91b),
(יְשַׁעְיָה נז, טו): "דְּמָרוֹם וְקָדוֹשׁ אֶשְׁכּוֹן, וְאֶת דַּכָּא וּשְׁפַל רוּחַ",
as in (Isaiah 57:15): 'I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit,'
וְהָיוּ הַמַּלְאָכִים מַבִּיטִים לְמַעְלָה וְרוֹאִים צוּרָתוֹ, וְכֵן לְמַטָּה
and the angels gazed above and saw his form, and likewise below,
דְּהָיוּ עוֹלִים וְיוֹרְדִים בּוֹ,
for 'they were ascending and descending on him' (Genesis 28:12),
דְּהַיְינוּ מְקוֹם גְּדוּלָּתוֹ וְעַנְוְותָנוּתוֹ.
which embodies the synthesis of the place of his greatness and his humility.
וְכֵן הוּא צוּרַת אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם
And such is the structure of man in the universe,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (חֲגִיגָה יג עַמּוּד ב)
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Chagigah 13b),
דְּגָאֶה בְּכֻלָּם אָדָם שֶׁמִּתְגָּאֶה עַל הַכֹּל
that the most exalted among all creations is man, who exalts himself over everything,
וְעִיקַּר הַשֵּׁם מוֹרֶה פְּחִיתוּת
yet the primary name Adam actually indicates lowliness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה (ה עַמּוּד א)
as they noted in Sotah (5a).
דְּמוֹרֶה: אֵפֶר, דָּם, מָרָה
that Adam
(אד"ם)
alludes by acronym to: efer (ashes), dam (blood), marah (gall).
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת מוּרְכָּב
And this is because he is truly a composite:
מִנֶּפֶשׁ הַחֲצוּבָה מֵעוֹלַם הַכִּסֵּא לְמַעְלָה מִמַּלְאָכִים
of a divine soul hewn from the world of the Throne of Glory far above the angels.
וְגוּף עָפָר מִן הָאֲדָמָה שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַשִּׁפְלוּת
and a body of dust from the earth which is the ultimate nadir of lowliness.
וְנֶפֶשׁ הוּא חֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמַּעַל
And the soul is an actual portion of God from Above,
וּמִצִּידָּהּ הוּא הַדְּבֵיקוּת בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and from its perspective arises cleaving unto Hashem, blessed be He,
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר בִּיהוֹשָׁפָט (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ב יז, ו): "וַיִּגְבַּהּ לִבּוֹ בְּדַרְכֵי ה
'". and concerning this it is said of Jehoshaphat (II Chronicles 17:6): 'And his heart was lifted up in the ways of Hashem.'
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל לְהַכְנִיס בּוֹ יֵצֶר רָע גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ,
Yet through this very dynamic the evil inclination can inject arrogant haughtiness into him,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּתַעֲנִית (כ עַמּוּד ב)
along the lines of what is taught in Ta'anit (20b)
בְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁלָּמַד תּוֹרָה הַרְבֵּה וְזָחָה דַּעְתּוֹ,
concerning Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon who had studied much Torah and whose mind grew haughty.

paragraphs.text: Michah 7:20: “תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב, חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם, אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתָּ לַאֲבֹתֵינוּ מִימֵי קֶדֶם” — “You will grant truth to Yaakov, kindness to Avraham, which You swore to our fathers from days of old” — the sealing verse of Michah’s prophecy of pardon. Rashi: God will fulfill the oath of emes toward Yaakov and chesed toward Avraham. The Sages pair each Patriarch with a middah — Avraham = Chesed, Yitzchak = Gevurah/Pachad, Yaakov = Emes/Tiferes. R’ Tzadok’s use: “emes le-Yaakov” — truth is Yaakov’s middah, and its lived trait is anavah (humility), the opposite of gaavah (haughtiness, which is itself falsehood); therefore haughtiness stands “this-opposite-that” to Yaakov, the third of the three roots of impurity (envy, desire, honor) over against the three Avos.

R’ Tzadok’s use: gaavah is falsehood — for even of Hashem “majesty” is spoken only “as a garment”; “He shows Himself lofty over the lofty, but to the lowly He gives grace and honor” (cf. Mishlei 3:34, “to the humble He gives grace”), and “in the place of His greatness, there you find His humility” (Megillah 31a). True greatness is thus inseparable from humility — the middah of Yaakov.

paragraphs.text: Iyov 31:2: “וּמֶה חֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמָּעַל וְנַחֲלַת שַׁדַּי מִמְּרֹמִים” — “And what is the portion from God above, and the inheritance from Shaddai on high?” In context (31:1–4), Iyov asks rhetorically about the recompense allotted by Heaven in relation to moral conduct; compare Rashi on Iyov 31:2 (“שגמלני כך”). Iyov does not there directly define the soul as a part of God. Rather, the wording “חֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמָּעַל” is applied to the soul in later mystical teaching: Tanya, Likutei Amarim, ch. 2: “וְנֶפֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִית בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא חֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמַּעַל מַמָּשׁ.” Rav Tzadok employs this interpretive sense to contrast the soul’s lofty spiritual root and capacity for deveikus with the body’s earth-born lowliness, before warning that awareness of spiritual elevation may give rise to pride. Thus the verse supplies an allusive expression, not a direct proof from Iyov’s plain contextual meaning.

paragraphs.text: Divrei HaYamim II 17:6: “וַיִּגְבַּהּ לִבּוֹ בְּדַרְכֵי ה׳, וְעוֹד הֵסִיר אֶת הַבָּמוֹת וְאֶת הָאֲשֵׁרִים מִיהוּדָה” — “and his heart was elevated in the ways of Hashem, and he further removed the high places and the Asherim from Yehudah” — of the righteous King Yehoshafat. Meforshim (Rashi, Metzudos): his heart was raised up — emboldened and exalted — in the service of God, a praiseworthy “loftiness of heart” (as opposed to sinful pride). R’ Tzadok’s use: there is a legitimate elevation of heart, from the side of the soul (the “portion of God from above”), which is the true cleaving to Hashem — yet “through this very loftiness the yetzer can insinuate coarseness of spirit,” turning genuine spiritual height into self-importance (as befell R. Elazar b’R. Shimon with his Torah).

paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah 2:29: “וקומה נגד יעקב קו אמצעי בהתפארות דקדושה נגד רדיפת כבוד והגבהת קומה ... כדרך שאמרו ביהושפט ויגבה לבו בדרכי (וגו׳) שצריך על ידי זה להתרחק מפחיתות” — “Height corresponds to Yaakov, the middle line, in holy self-glory, opposite the pursuit of honor and self-exaltation … As they said of Yehoshafat, “his heart was elevated in the ways of Hashem”: through this one must distance oneself from baseness.” This provides a precise parallel for the legitimate elevation that the author then distinguishes from the evil inclination’s pride.

paragraphs.text: Taanis 20a–b: R’ Elazar b’Rabbi Shimon, returning from his teacher’s house riding on a donkey by a riverbank, was in high spirits and conceited over how much Torah he had learned. A strikingly ugly man greeted him, “peace upon you, Rebbi,” but he did not return the greeting, saying, “Empty one! how ugly is that man — are all the people of your town as ugly as you?” The man replied, “I do not know; but go and tell the Craftsman who made me, ‘how ugly is this vessel You have made!’” Realizing he had sinned, he dismounted and prostrated himself before him in apology.

paragraphs.text: Yirmeyah 1:5: “בְּטֶרֶם אֶצָּרְךָ בַבֶּטֶן יְדַעְתִּיךָ, וּבְטֶרֶם תֵּצֵא מֵרֶחֶם הִקְדַּשְׁתִּיךָ, נָבִיא לַגּוֹיִם נְתַתִּיךָ” — “Before I formed you in the belly I knew you, and before you emerged from the womb I sanctified you; a prophet to the nations I appointed you” — God’s word to Yirmeyahu at his calling. Rashi: he was designated for prophecy from before his birth. R’ Tzadok’s use: this seals the lesson of the “ugly man” and of Avos 2:8 — “if you have learned much Torah, do not hold the credit to yourself… for it is for this that you were fashioned notzarta”: whatever a person is and attains is “from the Craftsman who made him,” fixed already “before I formed you in the belly,” so the tzaddik must not suppose that his own striving is the cause — “the essence of whatever good he has is only from Him.” Maharal parallel - Netivot Olam, Netiv HaAnavah 3:2 and 7:2: Maharal's analysis of ga'avah clarifies why R. Tzadok places kavod and self-importance among the root forces opposed to Yaakov. In Netiv HaAnavah 3, Maharal describes pride as an improper "addition" to the person and compares the baal ga'avah to an asherah that grows upward as a foreign, idolatrous excrescence; ga'avah is thus bound to avodah zarah because the person gives independent weight and elevation to the self. In ch. 7 he adds a subtler warning: Torah itself is genuinely elevated, and a talmid chacham may therefore be exposed to a refined residue of pride precisely because of the objective greatness of Torah. The corrective is to be "soft like a reed": the higher the reed grows, the more it bends. This complements R. Tzadok's pairing of Yaakov's emes with anavah. Yaakov's greatness is not self-negation born of worthlessness, but the refusal to treat any excellence as self-generated. The more truth a person receives, the less room remains for autonomous self-glorification.
