inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The three roots of tumah — kinah, taavah, kavod (envy, desire, honor) — stand opposite the three Avos. Gaavah (haughtiness) opposes Yaakov’s middah of emes/anavah; man’s greatness and lowliness are joined in the “form of Yaakov” engraved on the Throne, and Torah-pride is the yetzer’s opening — as in the story of R. Elazar b’R. Shimon and the “ugly man.”

p: (ה), — וְאַף דְּהַכֹּל בִּבְחִירָה
And even though everything is governed by free choice,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ גַּם כֵּן בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (טז עַמּוּד א):
nonetheless they also stated in Bava Batra (16a):
"בָּרָאתָ צַדִּיקִים, בָּרָאתָ רְשָׁעִים".
'You created righteous individuals, You created wicked individuals.'
וְכֵן בְּבִרְכַּת רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנֶה (בִּבְרָכוֹת כח עַמּוּד ב):
And likewise in the blessing of Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKaneh (Berakhot 28b):
עַל שֶׁשַּׂמְתָּ חֶלְקִי מִיּוֹשְׁבֵי בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ,
upon 'having set my portion among those who sit in the study hall,'
דְּעַל הָאֱמֶת הַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
for in ultimate truth, everything originates from Hashem, blessed be He.
וְכַיָּדוּעַ מִסּוֹד הַיְדִיעָה וְהַבְּחִירָה שֶׁנִּתְקַשָּׁה בּוֹ הָרַמְבַּ"ם
And as is known from the mystery of divine Foreknowledge versus Free Choice with which Maimonides wrestled
(פֶּרֶק ה מֵהִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה הֲלָכָה ה),
(Laws of Repentance 5:5),
וְגִילָּה שָׁם תַּכְלִית יְדִיעָתוֹ
and he disclosed there the absolute peak of mortal comprehension,
בַּמַּה שֶּׁאָמַר שֶׁלֹּא יָדַע תֵּירוּץ עַל זֶה
in stating that one cannot know the resolution to this,
כִּי אֵין יְדִיעָתֵנוּ כִּידִיעָתוֹ;
because our mode of knowledge is not like His Knowledge;
וְהוּא הַתֵּירוּץ הָאֲמִיתִּי עַל קוּשְׁיָא זוֹ,
and this is the authentic resolution to this paradox.
וְלֹא כְּהָרַאֲבָ"ד שֶׁכָּתַב שֶׁהִנִּיחָהּ בְּקוּשְׁיָא
and not as the Ra'avad critically contended, that the Rambam left the matter unresolved.
וְסוֹדוֹ יָדוּעַ בְּתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר חָדָשׁ וּבְסֵפֶר אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף מֵהָאֲרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
And its esoteric secret is known in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash and in the book Arba Me'ot Shekel Kesef by the holy Ari, of blessed memory.
וְתוֹרֶף הָעִנְיָן
And the crux of the matter is:
דִּבִּמְקוֹם הַיְדִיעָה אֵין בְּחִירָה
that in the realm of Foreknowledge there is no free choice,
וּבִמְקוֹם הַבְּחִירָה אֵין הַשָּׂגָה לִידִיעָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and in the realm of Free Choice there is no comprehension of His Foreknowledge, blessed be He.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּהַבְּחִירָה הוּא רַק מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
Which means that choice exists solely from the vantage point of this physical world,
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁעֲדַיִן דָּבוּק בְּחָמְרִיּוּת וְאֵינוֹ דָּבוּק לְגַמְרֵי בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and so long as a person is attached to materiality and not completely cleaved unto Him, blessed be He;
וְאָז אֵינוֹ בְּתַכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת הַבְּחִירָה עֲדַיִן
and then he has not yet attained the ultimate fruition of choice,
שֶׁהוּא לִידָּבֵק בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים לְגַמְרֵי
which is to cling completely to the living God;
דְּאָז כְּשֶׁיַּגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ
for when he ascends to that supreme rung,
מַשִּׂיג הָאֱמֶת שֶׁאֵין בְּחִירָה
he apprehends the ultimate truth that there is no independent choice
וְאֵינוֹ בְּצִדְקָתוֹ וּבְיוֹשֶׁר לְבָבוֹ.
and that he did not achieve this by his own self-righteousness or uprightness of heart.
וְהַגֵּיאוּת הוּא מִצַּד הַשִּׁפְלוּת וְהַחֹמֶר שֶׁבּוֹ,
And pride originates directly from the baseness and materiality within him,
וְאָז גַּם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְרוֹמָם מִמֶּנּוּ;
and at that stage Hashem, blessed be He, is perceived as distant and exalted above him;
שֶׁאִלּוּ הָיָה מַכִּיר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עִמּוֹ וְשֶׁהַכֹּל מִמֶּנּוּ
– for had he truly perceived that Hashem is with him and that everything is from Him—,
אֵין מָקוֹם לְגֵיאוּת
there would be no conceivable room for pride;
דְּאָז הוּא בִּמְקוֹם גְּדוּלָּתוֹ וְשָׁם עַנְוְותָנוּתוֹ,
for then he abides in the place of His greatness where His humility resides,
וְנִמְצָא הָעֲנָוָה הוּא הַגַּדְלוּת דְּאָדָם
and it emerges that true humility is the genuine greatness of man,
כַּאֲשֶׁר נַפְשׁוֹ דְּבוּקָה בִּמְקוֹרָהּ.
whenever his soul is cleaving to its supernal Source.
וְהַגֵּיאוּת הוּא מִצַּד הַגּוּף הַמְרוּחָק מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁמִּצִּידּוֹ הַבְּחִירָה
Whereas pride stems from the body which is distant from Hashem, whence choice operates.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא הַגֵּיאוּת כְּאִלּוּ הוּא הַמִּשְׁתַּדֵּל וּבוֹחֵר בַּטּוֹב
and through this arises pride as if he himself were the sole agent exerting and choosing good.
וְכָל בַּקָּשַׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית כח, כ): "אִם יִהְיֶה אֱלֹהִים עִמָּדִי וּשְׁמָרַנִי בַּדֶּרֶךְ הַזֶּה וְגוֹמֵר",
And the entire prayer of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, was (Genesis 28:20): 'If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way, etc.',
אָז (שָׁם, כא): "וְהָיָה ה' לִי לֵאלֹהִים".
only then: 'shall Hashem be my God.'
דְּיָדַע שֶׁאִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ אֵין יָכוֹל לוֹ ,
For he knew that were it not that the Holy One helps him, he could not overcome it (Kiddushin 30b),
רַק אִם הוּא יִהְיֶה עִמָּדִי וְיִשְׁמְרֵנִי אָז יִהְיֶה וְכוּלֵי
only if He will be with me and preserve me, then will it be so, etc.
וְהַמַּצֵּבָה יִהְיֶה בֵּית אֱלֹהִים שֶׁאוּכַל לְעָבְדוֹ.
and 'this pillar shall be God's house' so that I can serve Him.
וְזֶה מִדָּה יְתֵירָה שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מִבְּגֵרִים
And this is the superior virtue of Israel over converts,
שֶׁאִיתָא בְּפֶרֶק עֲשָׂרָה יוּחֲסִין :
which is brought in chapter Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 70b):
דְּמִקּוֹדֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לָהֶם לֵאלֹהִים, וַהֲדַר וְהֵם וְכוּלֵי
that first Hashem is God unto them, and only afterward are they His people, etc.

paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 16a: Rava said: Iyov sought to exempt the whole world from judgment. He said before Him, “Master of the world — You created the ox with cloven hooves and the donkey with closed hooves; You created Gan Eden and You created Gehinnom; You created the righteous and You created the wicked the latter by way of the evil inclination — who can stop You?” i.e., since God made the yetzer hara, the sinner is as though compelled — an argument the Gemara rejects, though it reflects that “all is from Him.”

paragraphs.text: Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 5:5: the Rambam confronts the classic difficulty — if the Holy One foreknows whether a person will be righteous or wicked, how can his choice be free? He answers that God and His knowledge are one (His knowing is not something added to His essence), and therefore “it is not within the power of the human mind to grasp this matter clearly”; His manner of knowing is utterly unlike ours (“ein yedi’aseinu ki-yedi’aso”) — yet, he insists, “without doubt a person’s deeds are in his own hand,” and free choice is a firm foundation of the Torah. R’ Tzadok’s use: the Rambam’s very acknowledgment that he had “no full resolution” — for our knowing is not like His — is itself the true resolution: Divine knowledge and human choice occupy different “places,” and both are real.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar Chadash and Arba Me’os Shekel Kesef: the “secret” of yedi’ah (Divine knowledge) and bechirah (free choice) is expounded in the Kabbalah — in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, and in Arba Me’os Shekel Kesef, a work of the Arizal’s Kabbalah (its title drawn from “four hundred silver shekels,” Bereishis 23:16). There the two are set on different planes of the supernal roots: from the side of God’s knowledge (the higher unity) there is no independent “choice,” while free choice belongs to the “place” of this lower world — so that the two do not contradict. R’ Tzadok points to these as the mystical ground of the principle that “in the place of knowledge there is no choice, and in the place of choice there is no grasp of His knowledge.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §47): “The attainment of the heart comes only through wholeheartedness, and without recklessly ascending toward Hashem by inquiry into what lies beyond the intellect’s grasp. For with the human intellect it is impossible to grasp the truth of this matter fully, as is known — as the Rambam wrote concerning the difficulty of Divine foreknowledge and human free choice. Only the Children of Israel, upon whom the light of Torah — ‘in which truth is written’ — has shone, grasp this: the Torah-scholars, called by the name ‘Israel,’ grasp it by way of chochmah — and this is what the name ‘Israel’ denotes, from ‘for you have striven with the Divine and with men and have prevailed’ (Bereishis 32:29), that he became a ‘prince’ over the angels — and this is from the complete cleaving to the ultimate truth.” And Tzidkas HaTzaddik (os 40) puts it most pointedly — citing the very same source adduced here, the Arizal at the end of Arba Me’os Shekel Kesef: “The essence of teshuvah is that Hashem so illumine a person’s eyes that the willful sins become as merits — that is, that he recognize and understand that all he sinned was, too, by the will of Hashem… and this is the matter of yedi’ah and bechirah that the Arizal explained at the end of Arba Me’os Shekel Kesef: that both are true, each in its own place — in the place of choice there is no place for His knowledge, and in the place of His knowledge there is in truth no place for choice. And when one attains this tremendous light, then all his willful sins are seen never to have departed from the depth of Hashem’s knowledge — He, His knowing, and His will being all One; and since Hashem willed it so, all is indeed merits, and one attains the complete atonement of Yom Kippur.”

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim 1:4: “מָשְׁכֵנִי אַחֲרֶיךָ נָּרוּצָה” — “Draw me after You, we will run” (treated more fully at Siman 5 §5). In the love-allegory of the Holy One and Knesses Yisrael, Israel asks God to draw her first, and only then does she “run” after Him — the initial arousal must come from Above. R’ Tzadok’s use here: this is Israel’s superiority over converts — for Israel, Scripture places Hashem “as a God to them” first and “they a people to Me” only afterward (Kiddushin 70b); Israel apprehends that God alone directs “every detail of a person’s thoughts,” so the drawing precedes — whereas the convert reckons that his own effort came first. Izhbitz-Radzin parallel - Mei HaShiloach, Korach 2; Beit Yaakov on Torah, Bereshit 69:1: This se'if's yedi'ah-bechirah tension is central to Izhbitz, and the school itself supplies an important boundary against misunderstanding it. Mei HaShiloach, Korach 2, explains Korach's claim that at the deepest level "everything is in the hands of Heaven, even fear of Heaven." The teaching then says that Hashem specifically conceals this depth in olam ha-zeh so that human beings experience themselves as baalei bechirah and avodah can exist; if Divine direction were fully transparent, no meaningful human service would grow. Beit Yaakov, Bereshit 69:1, develops the same point through Kayin. Kayin argues "hashomer achi anochi" as though the overwhelming anger that led to Hevel's death proved that he had no choice. Hashem rejects that defense: the crying blood demonstrates that the deficiency lay in Kayin and that he did possess bechirah. These sources are a precise complement to R. Tzadok. "In truth all is from Hashem" is a truth disclosed from the deeper Divine perspective and, ultimately, after the avodah and teshuvah; it is not a practical heter before the act. Within the lived world of Torah, a person must treat the choice before him as real, binding, and his responsibility.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Though all is in one’s free choice, “in truth all is from Hashem” — the secret of yedi’ah and bechirah (Divine knowledge and free will). Where there is [Divine] knowledge there is no [creaturely] choice, and where there is choice there is no grasp of His knowledge; true humility is a person’s real greatness — recognizing that Hashem is with him and all is from Him. This is Israel’s superiority over converts.

paragraphs.text: Devarim 4:35: “אַתָּה הָרְאֵתָ לָדַעַת כִּי ה׳ הוּא הָאֱלֹקִים, אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ” — “You have been shown, to know, that Hashem is the God; there is nothing else besides Him.” From Moshe’s recollection of the Revelation (Devarim 4). Rashi: at Sinai the Holy One opened the seven heavens to show Israel that He alone is God. The Kabbalists take “ein od milvado” at its ultimate depth — that there is no true existence apart from Him. R’ Tzadok’s use: Yaakov’s whole endeavor was to clarify “that all is from Him, and there is nothing else besides Him” — this is his middah, the trait of deveikus (cleaving), the recognition that leaves no room for the illusion of independent choice or self-attainment.

Meforshim read “akeres ha-bayis” both as the once-barren woman akarah and, homiletically, as the mainstay of the house ikar ha-bayis; and the Sages apply the barren-turned-joyful mother to the Matriarchs, Rachel foremost (Bereishis Rabbah 71:2). paragraphs.text: Zohar, Vayeitzei (on “and Hashem saw that Leah was hated”): the editor adduces this passage for the importance of the matter — why was she hated? surely the children of a hated wife are not worthy children, yet we see that all the good sons issued from Leah! Rather, Leah corresponds to the concealed upper world (the Yovel / Binah / the world of teshuvah), all of whose matters are hidden; therefore her doings were hidden from Yaakov. Rachel corresponds to the revealed lower world (Malchus), the beginning of the ascent through the rungs. Yaakov cleaved by his outward will to the revealed (Rachel), in the secret of “and he shall cleave to his wife” — yet the “good sons” issue from the hidden root (Leah); for Yaakov corresponds to Zeir Anpin, son of Imma Ila’ah (Binah), and Rachel to the Nukva of Zeir Anpin (Malchus), called “daughter” to the supernal Abba and Imma.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Likkutei Maamarim §10): “this is from the side of the Binah in the heart — ‘his heart shall understand and he shall repent’ — it is the portion of the clarifying of the eight rungs of teshuvah.” This is §6-6’s Leah exactly — “the trait of Binah, ‘his heart shall understand and repent,’ the rung of the baal teshuvah, which stands higher than the perfect tzaddikim”: the return that reaches, through Binah, into a hidden depth that the never-fallen tzaddik, for all his perfection, never has cause to touch.

paragraphs.text: Mishlei 28:13: “מְכַסֶּה פְשָׁעָיו לֹא יַצְלִיחַ, וּמוֹדֶה וְעֹזֵב יְרֻחָם” — “one who conceals his transgressions shall not succeed, but one who confesses and forsakes shall be granted mercy.” Meforshim: the essence of teshuvah is viduy (confession) joined to the abandonment of the sin. R’ Tzadok’s use: Leah and all her offspring “grasped the distaff of hoda’ah” (thanksgiving / confession) — “for this is the essence of teshuvah: one who confesses and forsakes shall be granted mercy”; hers is the rung of Binah, the baal teshuvah, higher than the perfect tzaddik — and from her line came Reuven, “the first to open with teshuvah,” and Hoshea.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 84:19: On “וַיָּשָׁב רְאוּבֵן אֶל הַבּוֹר” (Bereishis 37:29), the Midrash asks where Reuven had been, and answers that he was occupied “בְּשַׂקּוֹ וּבְתַעֲנִיתוֹ” — in his sackcloth and fasting, doing teshuvah for the matter of Bilhah (Bereishis 35:22). The Holy One said to him: “מֵעוֹלָם לֹא חָטָא אָדָם לְפָנַי וְעָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה, וְאַתָּה פָּתַחְתָּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה תְּחִלָּה — never has a person sinned before Me and repented, and you are the first to open with teshuvah; by your life, a descendant of yours will arise and be the first to open with teshuvah” — and who is that? Hoshea, as it says, “שׁוּבָה יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד ה׳ אֱלֹקֶיךָ” (Hoshea 14:2). The Yefe To’ar notes that Hoshea would be the first to teach teshuvah me-ahavah — repentance from love, whereby willful sins become as merits. R’ Tzadok’s use: Leah’s firstborn Reuven, and Hoshea of his line, are those who “grasp the distaff of hoda’ah / teshuvah” — the rung of Binah, the baal teshuvah who stands higher than the perfect tzaddik. Izhbitz-Radzin parallel - Shem MiShmuel, Vayetzei 9:15; Sha'ar HaEmunah VeYesod HaChasidut, Entrance to the Gate of Beit Yaakov 24:3-4: Shem MiShmuel explicitly identifies Rachel with alma d'isgalya and Leah with alma d'iskasya, and explains that their differing modes of avodah correspond to revealed and concealed spiritual attainment: Rachel's side is more readily expressed through revealed "aseh tov," while Leah's hidden heights are reached through the inward work of "sur mera." This closely fits R. Tzadok's contrast between the externally beautiful, revealed tzaddik-rung of Rachel and Leah's Binah/teshuvah, whose beauty is initially hidden. Sha'ar HaEmunah deepens the identification of teshuvah with Binah: complete teshuvah returns a person to the place of Binah and thereby reaches "above time," where past, present, and future are not divided in the ordinary way and the past can be healed. The work explicitly links this to "u-miBnei Yissachar yodei binah la'itim" - those who know how to heal the time. The hidden world is therefore not merely less visible than Rachel's world; it is the level from which a person's apparently fixed history can be reread and repaired.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Yaakov’s whole endeavor was to clarify that “all is from Him.” Rachel is the revealed world (alma d’isgalya) — the perfected tzaddikim, comely in deed; Leah is the concealed world (alma d’iskasya) — Binah, the rung of the baal teshuvah, higher than the perfect tzaddik. Leah and her offspring “grasped the domain of hoda’ah” — the essence of teshuvah (Reuven, and Hoshea from his line).

p: (ז) — וְזֶהוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, לא): "וַיַּרְא ה' כִּי שְׂנוּאָה לֵאָה וַיִּפְתַּח אֶת רַחְמָהּ",
And this is (Genesis 29:31): 'And Hashem saw that Leah was hated, and He opened her womb,'
דְּחָלִילָה שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹר יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עַל (וַיִּקְרָא יט, יז): "לֹא תִשְׂנָא אֶת אָחִיךָ בִּלְבָבֶךָ" וְעַל לֹא דָבָר
for Heaven forbid that our father Jacob, peace be upon him, should violate 'You shall not hate your brother in your heart' over nothing,
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן בִּהְיוֹתָהּ אִשְׁתּוֹ,
and all the more so seeing that she was his wife,
וְיִהְיֶה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בְּנֵי שְׂנוּאָה .
and that her offspring should, Heaven forbid, be considered children of a hated wife (Nedarim 20b).
וְעַל כֵּן דָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (קכג עַמּוּד א):
Therefore our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded in Bava Batra (123a):
שֶׁשְּׂנוּאִים מַעֲשֵׂה עֵשָׂו בְּעֵינֶיהָ.
that the deeds of Esau were hateful in her eyes.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, אֵין מִקְרָא יוֹצֵא מִידֵי פְּשׁוּטוֹ גַּם כֵּן
Nonetheless, a biblical verse does not lose its literal meaning entirely either,
כִּי מַעֲשֵׂה עֵשָׂו בִּרְצִיחָה
for the practice of Esau is bloodshed,
וְיִצְרָא דְּכַעַס הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ מִיִּצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁאִבְּדוּ אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה
and the impulse of wrath is the root of the inclination for idolatry which the Men of the Great Assembly destroyed,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, כז עַמּוּד ב):
as they stated in the Zohar (Part I, 27b):
כָּל הַכּוֹעֵס כְּאִלּוּ עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
whoever loses his temper is as though he served idols.
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּשֵׁם אֱלֹהִים הוּא לְשׁוֹן אַיִל, כֹּחַ וּגְבוּרָה
For as is known, the Name Elohim denotes strength, power, and might,
שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל הַכֹּחוֹת כֻּלָּם
being the Master of all cosmic forces;
וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁהוּא הַכּוֹבֵשׁ יִצְרוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּאָבוֹת (פֶּרֶק ד מִשְׁנָה א),
and this is the holy attribute of Gevurah, wherein one conquers his inclination as our Sages taught in Avot (4:1),
וּמִמֶּנּוּ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת דֶּ"אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים" בְּ"זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה אֱלֹהִים",
and from it stems the expansion of 'other gods' in the principle of 'God made one corresponding to the other'.
וּמֵהֶם מִתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה הָרָעָה בְּכַעַס וּרְצִיחָה
and from them expands the corrupt attribute of Gevurah in rage and bloodshed.
וְעַל כֵּן "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם עֲמָלֵק" (בַּמִּדְבָּר כד, כ),
Therefore 'Amalek is first among the nations' (Numbers 24:20),
שֶׁהוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ מִכָּל מִינֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל כָּל שִׁבְעִים אוּמּוֹת
being the seminal root of all varieties of idolatry across all seventy nations,
דְּכָל אוּמָּה יֵשׁ לָהּ כֹּחַ מְיוּחָד שֶׁבּוֹ מִתְפָּאֲרִים (דְּבָרִים ח, יז): "כֹּחִי וְעֹצֶם יָדִי עָשָׂה לִי אֶת הַחַיִל הַזֶּה".
for each nation possesses a distinct power regarding which they boast: 'My power and the might of my hand has gotten me this wealth.',
וְזֶהוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלָּהֶם
And this self-worship is their idolatry,
דְּכָל עִנְיַן עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הַיְינוּ שֶׁמַּפְרִיד אֵיזֶה כֹּחַ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for the whole concept of idolatry is that one isolates a power from Hashem, blessed be He,
וְאוֹמֵר שֶׁהוּא שַׁלִּיט וּבַעַל כֹּחַ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
and asserts that it is an autonomous ruler and sovereign force in its own right.
וַעֲמָלֵק הוּא הָרֵאשִׁית וְהַמָּקוֹר שֶׁבְּכֻלָּם
And Amalek is the primal beginning and wellspring of them all,
כִּי הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ פְּסֹלֶת מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה, דַּרְגָּא דֶּ"אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים".
for he is the root of the dross of Gevurah, the rung of 'other gods.'
וְאֵינוֹ נוֹפֵל אֶלָּא בְּיַד זַרְעָהּ שֶׁל רָחֵל (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכג עַמּוּד ב),
And he falls only at the hand of the offspring of Rachel (Bava Batra 123b),
שֶׁהֵם הָאוֹחֲזִים בְּמִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה דִּקְדוּשָּׁה לִכְבּוֹשׁ אֶת יִצְרָם
who hold fast to the holy attribute of Gevurah to conquer their inclination;
וְיָבוֹא מִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מב, יח): "אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים אֲנִי יָרֵא" – דַּרְגָּא דְּיִצְחָק
and let him of whom it is said (Genesis 42:18): 'I fear God'—the spiritual rung of Isaac—come
וְיִפָּרַע מִמִּי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ (דְּבָרִים כה, יח): "וְלֹא יָרֵא אֱלֹהִים".
and exact retribution from him concerning whom it is written (Deuteronomy 25:18): 'and he feared not God.',
דְּאַף דְּזֶה נֶאֱמַר עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
For although this phrase was spoken concerning the weak among Israel,
הַיְינוּ דַּעֲמָלֵק פָּגַע בָּהֶם בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה
the meaning is that Amalek attacked them on account of this flaw,
כִּי הוּא שָׁרְשׁוֹ מִצַּד אוֹתוֹ פְּסֹלֶת דְּיִצְחָק
since his spiritual root originates from that very dross of Isaac;
וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁרוֹאֶה גַּם יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַרְאִית עַיִן כֵּן
and therefore when he observes Israelites behaving superficially thus.
יֵשׁ לוֹ טַעֲנָה לְקַטְרֵג חַס וְשָׁלוֹם עֲלֵיהֶם
he has grounds to prosecute accusations, Heaven forbid, against them.
וְהַבְּרִיּוֹת הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים: הַגְּדוֹלָה לַגָּדוֹל (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכג עַמּוּד א),
And the people used to say: The older daughter (Leah) belongs to the older son (Esau), (Bava Batra 123a),
דְּמִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת הָיָה נִרְאֶה כְּאִלּוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם דּוֹמֵית אֵלָיו
because from the perspective of external appearances it seemed as though she, Heaven forbid, resembled him,
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת: שְׂנוּאִים מַעֲשֵׂה עֵשָׂו בְּעֵינֶיהָ.
yet in internal truth: the deeds of Esau were utterly hateful in her eyes.
וּבָזֶה נִתְעַלֵּית הִיא עַל רָחֵל
And in this she was elevated above Rachel:
דְּזַרְעָהּ הֵם רַק שִׂטְנוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו
in that Rachel's descendants are merely the adversary (satno) of Esau,
הַיְינוּ מְקַטְרְגִים בִּהְיוֹת הֵם טוֹבִים וְהוּא רַע
meaning they accuse him by virtue of their being overtly good while he is wicked,
אֲבָל אִם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם יֶחֱטָא הָאָדָם הֲרֵי חַס וְשָׁלוֹם נִרְאֶה דּוֹמֶה לוֹ;
yet if an individual sins, Heaven forbid, he superficially appears similar to him;

paragraphs.text: The Name Elokim as a term of “power/might”: the grammarians and the Kuzari derive Elokim / E-l from the root of “ayil” — strength, ram, mighty one (cf. “אֵילֵי הָאָרֶץ,” Yechezkel 17:13, “the mighty of the land”). Ibn Ezra and Radak (Sefer HaShorashim, root אול/איל) explain E-l as denoting power; the Kuzari (IV:1–3) treats Elokim as “the Master of all the forces” — the Governor of all the powers of nature. R’ Tzadok’s use: because Elokim is the “baal ha-kochos,” it is the Name of Gevurah — holy might, the conquering of the yetzer (Avos 4:1); and when a single “power” is “severed off” from Him and declared independent, that same term becomes “Elohim acheirim,” the root of idolatry and of the evil Gevurah of anger and bloodshed.

paragraphs.text: Genesis 42:18: “את האלהים אני ירא” — “I fear God.” The paired phrase is “ולא ירא אלהים” — “and he did not fear God” (Devarim 25:18). The author invokes Yosef’s holy fear as the opposite of Amalek’s corrupted might, then expressly qualifies his reading: even though the latter phrase is applied here to Israel, Amalek encountered them because of that lack of fear and can accuse them when their outward deeds resemble his. The comparison therefore includes both the contrast with Amalek and the warning about Israel’s apparent resemblance to him.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 13a: “כָּל הַכּוֹפֵר בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה נִקְרָא יְהוּדִי” — “whoever repudiates idolatry is called a Yehudi.” The Gemara asks why Mordechai, a Binyaminite, is called “אִישׁ יְהוּדִי” (Esther 2:5), and answers that anyone who denies avodah zarah is called by the name Yehudi (after Yehudah). R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the very root of Yehudah, son of Leah — the inward denial, “in the heart,” of every “power” set up against Hashem; Leah’s whole superiority lies in this root-level repudiation of idolatry, deeper than and prior to any outward deed.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Chag HaPesach §14): “(Shabbos 105b) ‘the el zar in a person’s body — this is the yetzer hara,’ that is, it is a foreign power — this is ‘a foreign god’; and the matter of the erasure of Amalek is to empty the evil from the heart.” This is the flip side of §6-7’s “denier of idolatry is called a Yehudi”: Amalek is the “foreign god” lodged within man, and Leah’s root — the heart that “utterly rejects the thing” — is the erasing of that foreign power, the inward Yehudah who holds “no belief in any power against Hashem.” Tanya and Maharal parallel - Tanya, Iggeret HaKodesh 25; Maharal, Netivot Olam, Netiv HaAnavah 3:2: Tanya's treatment of anger gives a strong conceptual parallel to R. Tzadok's association here of anger, avodah zarah, and the failure to recognize Divine rule. Iggeret HaKodesh 25 explains the dictum that one who becomes angry is "as though he serves idolatry": in ordinary worldly matters, anger arises when a person loses sight of the fact that the event confronting him has come through Divine providence. At the same time, Tanya carefully preserves the realm of yiras Shamayim and the obligation to prevent issur; the recognition of providence does not erase Torah responsibility. Maharal similarly describes ga'avah as an idolatrous growth, an asherah-like elevation of the self. Together they illuminate R. Tzadok's Leah-Esav contrast. Leah's hatred of "ma'aseh Esav" is rejection of the inner posture that grants independent ultimacy to force, rage, or self. Her teshuvah-root is therefore the opposite of avodah zarah: it acknowledges both the reality of human responsibility and the deeper truth that no power, including one's own anger or strength, possesses independent being before Hashem.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: “Hashem saw that Leah was hated” — not that Yaakov hated her, but that the deeds of Esav were hateful in her eyes. Anger is the root of idolatry; Amalek is the root-“dross” of Gevurah and of all avodah zarah (declaring a power independent of Hashem). Leah’s superiority: her rejection of evil is at the root, in the heart — the trait of Yehudah, who “denies idolatry.”

p: (ח) — וְזֶה שׁוֹרֶשׁ דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (תְּהִלִּים קט, ד): "וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה",
And this is the root of the spiritual rung of King David, peace be upon him (Psalms 109:4): 'and I am prayer',
לְהַכִּיר שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
to recognize that everything originates from Hashem, blessed be He,
וְאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁמְּקַבֵּל מִמֶּנּוּ בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ.
and that he possesses nothing other than what he receives from Him through his prayer.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף עָמַד יָרָבְעָם שֶׁחִדֵּשׁ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
In contrast, from the seed of Joseph arose Jeroboam who reinstituted idolatry in Israel.
וּבֶאֱמֶת גַּם הוּא לֹא הֶאֱמִין בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
Yet in truth he too did not genuinely believe in idolatry,
כִּי גַּם כָּל בֵּית יוֹסֵף נִקְרָאִים יְהוּדִים
for the entire House of Joseph is likewise called Yehudim,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁגַּם כָּל בֵּית יְהוּדָה נִקְרָאִים "שְׁאֵרִית יוֹסֵף",
just as the entire House of Judah is called 'the remnant of Joseph',
דְּכָל הַשְּׁבָטִים כְּלוּלִים זֶה בָּזֶה בְּמַעֲלוֹתֵיהֶם
for all the tribes are integrated within one another in their spiritual virtues.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פרשה צט, ד) דְּחָזַר וּכְלָלָן בְּבִרְכוֹתֵיהֶם
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Bereishit Rabbah 99:4) that Jacob returned and included them together in their blessings.
וְעִיקַּר כַּוָּונָתוֹ הָיָה מִצַּד הַגֵּיאוּת וְהַכָּבוֹד
And his primary motivation stemmed from pride and honor:
כְּשֶׁיִּרְאוּ רְחַבְעָם יוֹשֵׁב וְהוּא עוֹמֵד כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק .
when the people would see Rehoboam seated and himself standing, as our Sages stated in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 101b).
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ דְּלֹא רָצָה לָשׁוּב בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: בֶּן יִשַׁי בָּרֹאשׁ (שָׁם קב עַמּוּד א),
And likewise they recounted that he refused to repent because Hashem told him: 'The son of Jesse shall walk at the head' (ibid. 102a),
וְזֶה הֱבִיאוֹ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
and this pride brought him to idolatry,
כִּי כָּל הַמִּתְגָּאֶה כְּאִלּוּ עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה .
for whoever behaves haughtily is as though he served idols (Sotah 4b).
וְהַיְינוּ דְּרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה חָשְׁבוּ רַק שְׁנֵי יְצָרִים: דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וּדְעֲרָיוֹת ,
And this explains why our Rabbis enumerated essentially only two primary inclinations: that of idolatry and that of licentiousness (Yoma 69b).
כִּי רַק מֵאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק יָצְאוּ פְּסֹלֶת דְּעֵשָׂו וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל
for from Abraham and Isaac issued the respective dross of Ishmael and Esau.
וְעֵשָׂו הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כַּנִּזְכָּר
And Esau is the root of idolatry as noted.
דְּכַעַס וְגַאֲוָה הֵם עַנְפֵי יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
since anger and pride are the primary branches of the inclination for idolatry.
(וְשָׁמַעְתִּי עַל פָּסוּק (מְלָכִים א יא, כו): "וְשֵׁם אִמּוֹ צְרוּעָה",
(And I have heard expounded on the verse (I Kings 11:26): 'and his mother's name was Tzeruah (a leper),'
דְּעִנְיַן טֻמְאַת צָרַעַת בָּא מִמִּדַּת הַכַּעַס
that the defilement of leprosy stems from the attribute of anger,
וְשָׁרְשׁוֹ דְּיָרָבְעָם אַגַּב אִמֵּיהּ הָיָה מִמִּדַּת הַכַּעַס
and the spiritual root of Jeroboam via his mother was drawn from the trait of wrath,
דְּבָזֶה הָיָה הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁלּוֹ.
for herein lay his foundational flaw.
וְהוּא נָכוֹן גַּם כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי
And this is accurate likewise according to what I have written:
דְּהַגֵּאוּת נִמְשָׁךְ מֵהַכַּעַס וּגְבוּרָה דְּרַע
that pride is drawn from anger and the corrupted Gevurah,
שֶׁחָפֵץ לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל הַכֹּל).
wherein one lusts to assert dominion over everything).
וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן חֲלוּקִים שְׁנֵי יְצָרִים אֵלּוּ בְּזַרְעָא דְּרָחֵל וְזַרְעָא דְּלֵאָה
And within Israel too these two inclinations are apportioned between the seed of Rachel and the seed of Leah;
וּלְכָךְ שִׂנְאַת מַעֲשֵׂה עֵשָׂו הוּא רַק אֵצֶל לֵאָה
and therefore the hatred of Esau's conduct is located uniquely within Leah,
שֶׁהִיא הַהֵיפֶךְ מִמֶּנּוּ מַמָּשׁ, וְלֹא שִׂטְנוֹ.
for she is his absolute intrinsic opposite, and not merely his external adversary.
וּבְאִתְגַּלְיָא הָיוּ הַבְּרִיּוֹת אוֹמְרִים דִּרְאוּיָה לוֹ,
And in manifest appearances people said that she was fitting for him;
הַיְינוּ דְּיָדוּעַ דְּהַשְּׁנֵי יְצָרִים הֵם זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה
meaning, as is known, that the two inclinations function as masculine and feminine:
וְעֵשָׂו הָיָה דְּכוּרָא בְּיִצְרָא דְּכַעַס וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
and Esau was the masculine aspect in the inclination for wrath and idolatry,
וְחָשְׁבוּ כְּאִלּוּ הִיא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם נוּקְבָא בְּיִצְרָא דַּעֲרָיוֹת לְעֵשָׂו
and they mistakenly assumed that she was, Heaven forbid, the feminine counterpart in the inclination of lust for Esau,
שֶׁהוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּרַע
who is the root of evil,
וַדַּאי זִיוּוּגוֹ הָרָאוּי לוֹ הוּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהִיא גַּם כֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּרַע וּמִיִּצְרָא דַּעֲרָיוֹת
reasoning that his fitting match would be one who was likewise a root of evil from the inclination of lust.
וְהִיא מָחֲלַת בַּת יִשְׁמָעֵאל
which was in truth Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael (Genesis 28:9).
אֲבָל לֵאָה הִיא שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדוּשָּׁה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד מִדַּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה
However, Leah is the primordial root of the supernal holiness of the Community of Israel through the attribute of Teshuva,
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ יֶחֶטְאוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם וְיַגְדִּילוּ עֲווֹנוֹת
in that even if they sin, Heaven forbid, and multiply transgressions,
עִם כָּל זֶה שָׁרְשָׁם דָּבוּק בֵּאלֹהִים
nevertheless their root remains cleaving to God,
שֶׁשְּׂנוּאִים מַעֲשֵׂה עֵשָׂו בְּעֵינֵיהֶם וְכוֹפְרִים בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
for the deeds of Esau are repulsive in their eyes and they deny idolatry,
וְכָל הַחֲטָאִים רַק כְּהוֹצִים הַסּוֹבְבִים לְאָסָא
and all sins are merely like thorns encircling the myrtle (Sanhedrin 44a).
רַק לְפִי שֶׁהַגּוֹיִם אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לִתְשׁוּבָה
Only because the gentile nations have no intrinsic connection to repentance,
עַל כֵּן לֹא יָדְעוּ מִזֶּה
they therefore could not grasp this;
דְּבֶאֱמֶת הַכִּיעוּר שֶׁבְּלֵאָה, דְּ"עֵינֵי לֵאָה רַכּוֹת" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, יז),
for in truth the apparent imperfection in Leah, that 'Leah's eyes were weak' (Genesis 29:17),
דְּזֶהוּ כִּמְסַפֵּר בִּגְנוּתָהּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ע, טז):
which seemingly speaks to her disparagement, as our Sages of blessed memory noted in Bereishit Rabbah (70:16):
אֲפִילּוּ בִּגְנוּת בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה לֹא דִּבֵּר הַכָּתוּב
even concerning the blemish of an unclean beast Scripture avoided speaking negatively.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיְתָה בּוֹכָה וְכוּלֵי
except that her eyes were tender because she was constantly weeping in prayer, etc.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 109:4: “תַּחַת אַהֲבָתִי יִשְׂטְנוּנִי, וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה” — “In return for my love they accuse me, but I am all prayer.” Rashi: “וַאֲנִי מִתְפַּלֵּל אֵלֶיךָ תָּמִיד” — “I pray to You always.” Radak / Metzudos: even as they persecute him, David turns himself wholly to prayer. R’ Tzadok takes “va-ani tefillah” as David’s very rung — he made himself into prayer, the paradigm of one who knows “he has nothing except what he receives from Hashem.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the exact antithesis of Yerovam’s haughtiness — David’s recognition that “all is from Hashem,” the rung of the King Mashiach (see the Resisei Layla parallel that follows).

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Nisan §2): “"the word of Hashem" — this is halachah; it is called "dibbur" speech. And here it said "in sichah" and not "in dibbur" — for we have said that words of Torah are called dibbur, unlike sichah conversation.” Here sichah means sacred conversation, especially prayer, rather than words handed to the outer forces. R’ Tzadok connects David’s “Hashem, open my lips” to the mouth of Malchus and explains that the twelve middle blessings express the recognition that everything comes from Hashem. This is a precise parallel to §8’s completed claim that David’s rung is prayer and the recognition that he receives everything from Hashem through it. The source states: “שעיקר התפלה שנפתח הפה לומר תהלת ה׳ שכל י״ב ברכות אמצעיות ההכרה שהכל מהשי״ת כמו שבא נוסח הברכות בלשון הווה” — “The essence of prayer is that the mouth is opened to speak Hashem’s praise, for all twelve middle blessings express the recognition that everything comes from Hashem, as their wording is in the present tense.”

The source states: “שעיקר התפלה שנפתח הפה לומר תהלת ה׳ שכל י״ב ברכות אמצעיות ההכרה שהכל מהשי״ת כמו שבא נוסח הברכות בלשון הווה” — “The essence of prayer is that the mouth is opened to speak Hashem’s praise, for all twelve middle blessings express the recognition that everything comes from Hashem, as their wording is in the present tense.”

paragraphs.text: The two “root” inclinations — idolatry and arayos: the Men of the Great Assembly first captured the yetzer of avodah zarah and confined it in a lead vessel, and then prayed that the yetzer of arayos (illicit relations) be delivered into their hands as well; they temporarily imprisoned the latter and ultimately blinded its eyes (Yoma 69b; cf. Sanhedrin 63b–64a). These are the two “great” inclinations that Chazal single out. R’ Tzadok’s use: precisely two — “for it was only from Avraham and Yitzchak that the ‘dross’ emerged” (Yishmael, the root of arayos; Esav, the root of avodah zarah, whose branches are anger and haughtiness); from Yaakov, the third Patriarch, no such “dross” issued.

paragraphs.text: Maharal and Tanya parallel — Maharal, Netivot Olam, Netiv HaAnavah 3:2; Tanya, Iggeret HaKodesh 25: R. Tzadok's contrast between David's "va-ani tefillah" and Yeravam's fall through kavod is sharpened by Maharal and Tanya. Maharal writes that the baal ga'avah is comparable to an asherah: pride is an alien growth because it treats the self as possessing an independent height. This is why Chazal can compare ga'avah itself to avodah zarah. Tanya makes the related point with anger: when a person experiences the human cause in front of him as an autonomous power, he forgets the Divine source of the event and enters the logic of idolatry. David's "I am prayer" represents the reverse posture. Tefillah is the admission that life, kingship, success, and even the power to serve are received rather than possessed. The more a king knows that his authority is a shefa entrusted to him, the more his malchus becomes a vessel for Malchus Shamayim; the more he claims the honor as his own, the more kingship becomes an idol of self. Thus R. Tzadok's two root-inclinations are opposite answers to the question: from where does one's power come?

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 28:9: “וַיֵּלֶךְ עֵשָׂו אֶל יִשְׁמָעֵאל, וַיִּקַּח אֶת מָחֲלַת בַּת יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן אַבְרָהָם אֲחוֹת נְבָיוֹת עַל נָשָׁיו לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה” — “And Esav went to Yishmael and took Machalas the daughter of Yishmael… in addition to his other wives, as a wife.” (Bereishis Rabbah 67:13 reads Machalas as “nimchalu — his sins were pardoned” on his wedding day.) R’ Tzadok’s use: Esav’s truly fitting mate — the “female” of the inclination of arayos, matching his “male” of anger and idolatry — was Machalas, of Yishmael’s line (the root of arayos), not Leah; the crowd’s saying “the elder Leah for the elder Esav” mistook Leah’s inward loathing of evil for kinship with it.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas Shabbos §4): “‘the sins are like the thorn that surrounds the lettuce — and not in the root’; and this is from the side that our root is from Yitzchak… and thereby Israel becomes an actual merkavah, ‘children of the living God.’” This is §6-8’s Leah, “the root of the supernal holiness of Knesses Yisrael”: even should they “multiply iniquities,” the sins are only “thorns that encircle the myrtle” — peripheral, never the root — so that their inmost heart stays bound to God, and they remain “children of the living God.”

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 44a: “אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא — יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא” — “even though he has sinned, he remains Yisrael.” R’ Abba explained it by the folk-saying: “a myrtle that stands among thorns chalfei — its name is still ‘myrtle,’ and people still call it a myrtle.” R’ Tzadok’s use: Israel’s sins are “but like thorns that encircle the myrtle” — the hotzim surround and prick the surface but never reach the fragrant myrtle-essence within, whose root “stays bound to God”; this is Leah’s trait of teshuvah, whereby even multiplied iniquities cannot sever the root that loathes Esav’s deeds and denies idolatry. (The same Gemara is cited at Siman 1.)

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: David’s rung is “va-ani tefillah” — all is received from Hashem. Yerovam (of Yosef’s line) introduced avodah zarah out of kavod — “whoever is haughty is as one who serves idols.” The two root-inclinations (avodah zarah, arayos) come from the “dross” of Esav and Yishmael; within Israel they split between Rachel’s and Leah’s seed. Leah is the root of Knesses Yisrael’s teshuvah — whose sins are “but thorns around the myrtle.”

p: (ט), — וְעִנְיַן הַגְּנוּת דְּעֵינַיִם הוּא עִיקָּר בְּאִשָּׁה
And the concept of a flaw in the eyes is paramount regarding a woman,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ד, ג) עַל פָּסוּק (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ד, א): "מִבַּעַד לְצַמָּתֵךְ":
as they expounded in Shir HaShirim Rabbah (4:3) on the verse: 'behind your veil':
כָּל כַּלָּה שֶׁעֵינֶיהָ יָפוֹת – אֵין כָּל גּוּפָהּ צָרִיךְ בְּדִיקָה (תַּעֲנִית כד עַמּוּד א).
every bride whose eyes are beautiful requires no examination of the rest of her body (Ta'anit 24a).
וְהוּא כְּעִנְיַן (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ו, ה): "הָסֵבִּי עֵינַיִךְ מִנֶּגְדִּי שֶׁהֵם הִרְהִיבֻנִי",
And this parallels: 'Turn away your eyes from me, for they have overcome me',
וְאָמַר "הָסֵבִּי וְגוֹמֵר" שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה בְּכָךְ,
and the Lover says 'turn away, etc.' showing He does not desire them thus.
לְפִי שֶׁ"הֵם הִרְהִיבֻנִי" – הִכְנִיסוּ בִי גַּדְלוּת וְגֵיאוּת
because 'they have overcome me'—they introduced haughtiness and pride into me.
כַּיָּדוּעַ: עַיִן רוֹאָה וְלֵב חוֹמֵד (רַשִּׁ"י בַּמִּדְבָּר טו, לט),
As is known: the eye sees and the heart covets (Rashi, Numbers 15:39),
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הַתְחָלַת הַתַּאֲוָה
from which begins the arousal of desire,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג, ו): "וְתַאֲוָה הִיא לָעֵינַיִם".
and as it is stated (Genesis 3:6): 'and that it was a delight to the eyes.'
וְעַל כֵּן בְּזַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף נֶאֱמַר (שָׁם מט, כב): "עֲלֵי עָיִן",
Therefore concerning the seed of Joseph it is said (ibid. 49:22): 'above the eye (alei ayin)',
וּמִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה אֵין הָעַיִן שׁוֹלֵט בָּהֶם (בְּרָכוֹת כ עַמּוּד א).
and measure for measure the evil eye holds no dominion over them (Berakhot 20a).
וְעִיקַּר הַיּוֹפִי הוּא בִּכְבִישַׁת הַתַּאֲווֹת
And true beauty lies in the conquest of bodily passions,
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בִּנְדָרִים (כ עַמּוּד ב):
and concerning this they taught in Nedarim (20b):
מִפְּנֵי מָה בָּנֶיךָ יְפֵיפִיִּין? שֶׁכְּשֶׁהוּא מְסַפֵּר וְכוּלֵי
Why are your children so exceptionally handsome? Because when he converses with his wife, etc.
בִּשְׁבִיל הַקְּדוּשָּׁה בְּלֵידָתָם
on account of the intense holiness present at their conception.
וּמִי שֶׁהוּא גִּבּוֹר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ יִצְרוֹ בְּתַאֲוָה, אֵין כָּל גּוּפוֹ צָרִיךְ בְּדִיקָה
And one who is a mighty hero conquering his inclination in lust, his entire body requires no inspection,
דְּזֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּיִרְאַת ה
', for this is the spiritual stature of the fear of Hashem,
וְ"אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה' הִיא תִתְהַלָּל" (מִשְׁלֵי לא, ל),
and 'a woman that fears Hashem, she shall be praised' (Proverbs 31:30),
וְהוּא תַּרְעָא לְאַעֲלָא גּוֹ מְהֵימְנוּתָא
and this serves as 'the gateway to enter into faith'.
וּמָה ה' שׁוֹאֵל כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה
and what does Hashem ask of you but to fear.
אֲבָל מִי שֶׁעֵינֶיהָ כְּעוּרוֹת – כָּל גּוּפָהּ צָרִיךְ בְּדִיקָה
However, one whose eyes are blemished requires examination of her entire body.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם בִּבְדִיקָה מִיהַת מְהַנֵּי
Nevertheless, examination at least proves effective.
שֶׁאֵין לְהַשְׁגִּיחַ עוֹד בִּגְנוּת הָעֵינַיִם
so that one no longer pays heed to the external defect of the eyes.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי יֵשׁ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּעֶצֶם
And this is because there is a blemish that is not essential;
וּבְלֵאָה הָיָה אַדְּרַבָּה לִשְׁבָח לְפִי שֶׁהָיְתָה בּוֹכָה וְכוּלֵי
and in Leah it was, on the contrary, for supreme praise, since she was weeping in prayer, etc.
כִּי אַחַר הַתְּשׁוּבָה וְהַתִּיקּוּן
For after repentance and rectification,
בְּאוֹתוֹ אֵיבָר שֶׁבּוֹ הַקִּלְקוּל נַעֲשָׂה אַדְּרַבָּה אוֹתוֹ אֵיבָר מְשׁוּבָּח יוֹתֵר
in the very limb wherein the spiritual flaw occurred, that limb becomes on the contrary far more exalted,
וְהַגְּנַאי עַצְמוֹ שָׁב לִהְיוֹת שְׁבָח כְּטַעַם "זְדוֹנוֹת כִּזְכִיּוֹת",
and the disparagement itself turns into glory, mirroring 'willful sins become merits',
וּבְשִׁבְחָהּ דִּבֶּר הַכָּתוּב, לֹא בִּגְנוּתָהּ,
and Scripture in truth spoke of her praise, not her blemish;
דְּמַה שֶּׁעֵינֶיהָ רַכּוֹת הָיָה מִצַּד שֶׁשְּׂנוּאִים מַעֲשֵׂה עֵשָׂו בְּעֵינֶיהָ,
for that her eyes were tender was because the deeds of Esau were hateful in her eyes.
דְּיָדוּעַ דְּכַעַס וְתַאֲוָה הֵם שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים
since it is known that anger and lust are two direct opposites.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן כְּפִי הַנִּגְלֶה בִּפְשַׁט הַכָּתוּב נִרְאֶה כִּגְנוּת וְכִיעוּר
Yet to outward sight, according to what is manifest in the plain verse, it appears as a blemish and ugliness;
וְכֵן כְּפִי פְּשַׁט לְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב "שְׂנוּאָה לֵאָה" מוּסָב עָלֶיהָ,
and likewise according to the simple reading of the text 'Leah was hated' is applied directly unto her,
דְּעַל יְדֵי שֶׁשְּׂנוּאִים מַעֲשֵׂה וְכוּלֵי עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִגְרַם לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן דְּהִיא שְׂנוּאָה
in that because the deeds of Esau were hateful, this caused her to appear to outward sight as though she were hated,
רָצָה לוֹמַר שְׂנוּאָה בְּמַעֲשֶׂיהָ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
meaning hated on account of her actions, Heaven forbid,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (סח עַמּוּד א) עַל פָּסוּק (דְּבָרִים כא, טו): "וְאַחַת שְׂנוּאָה".
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded in Kiddushin (68a) on the verse: 'and the other hated.'
וְהוּא מִצַּד הָרְאִיָּה דְּ"וַיַּרְא ה
'", And this stems from the divine vantage point of 'And Hashem saw',
כְּטַעַם (בְּרֵאשִׁית לח, ז): "וַיְהִי עֵר בְּכוֹר יְהוּדָה רַע בְּעֵינֵי ה
'". mirroring (Genesis 38:7): 'And Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of Hashem.',
כִּי קִלְקוּל הַבְּרִית הוּא כִּיעוּר הָעֵינַיִם
For corrupting the Covenant is the essential ugliness of the eyes,
וְגוֹרֵם גַּם כֵּן בְּעֵינִין דִּלְעֵילָּא כִּבְיָכוֹל לִהְיוֹת רַע בְּעֵינֵי ה
'. and causes likewise in the supernal Eyes, as it were, to appear wicked in the eyes of Hashem.
וְ"יִרְאַת ה' שִׂנְאַת רָע" (מִשְׁלֵי ח, יג),
And 'The fear of Hashem is to hate evil' (Proverbs 8:13),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ דַּרְגָּא דִּירֵא ה' הַכּוֹבֵשׁ יִצְרוֹ לִהְיוֹת שׂוֹנֵא רָע
which is the rung of one who fears Hashem and conquers his inclination so as to hate evil.
שֶׁהוּא מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית כַּיָּדוּעַ בַּזֹּהַר מִקְּרָא דְּעֵר
which is one who fails to guard the Covenant, as known in the Zohar from the verse concerning Er.
וּ"רְאִיָּה" אוֹתִיּוֹת "יִרְאָה",
And re'iyah (
רְאִיָּה
/ sight) contains the identical letters of yir'ah (
יִרְאָה
/ awe),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִצַּד רְאִיַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
– for this pertains to the vision of Hashem, blessed be He—,
הַיְינוּ הִסְתַּכְּלוּתוֹ בְּעָלְמָא דְּאִתְגַּלְיָא
namely His gaze within the Revealed World,
דְּהַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם חוּץ מִיִּרְאַת שָׁמַיִם (בְּרָכוֹת לג עַמּוּד ב),
wherein 'all is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven' (Berakhot 33b).
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עֵסֶק הָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא עוֹלַם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
which is man's specific occupation in this world, the World of Action.

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim 6:5: “הָסֵבִּי עֵינַיִךְ מִנֶּגְדִּי שֶׁהֵם הִרְהִיבֻנִי” — “Turn your eyes away from Me, for they have overwhelmed Me.” In the love-song of the Holy One and Knesses Yisrael, God, as it were, says that her gazing “overwhelms” Him. Rashi: “hirhivuni” — they have emboldened Me, stirred a rush of feeling within Me. R’ Tzadok reads “hirhivuni” as “they brought into Me an aspect of greatness and loftiness gadlus ve-geius” — the “eye” being the wellspring of both desire and pride, which is why He says “hasebi” (turn them away).

paragraphs.text: Yerushalmi Berachos 1:5: “לִיבָּא וְעֵינָא תְּרֵין סַרְסוֹרֵי דַחֲטָאָה” — “the heart and the eye are the two agents of sin.” It discusses “and you shall not go about after your heart and after your eyes” (Bamidbar 15:39). paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:1 (on “עֵינַיִךְ יוֹנִים מִבַּעַד לְצַמָּתֵךְ” — “your eyes are doves from behind your veil”): “כָּל כַּלָּה שֶׁעֵינֶיהָ יָפוֹת — אֵין כָּל גּוּפָהּ צָרִיךְ בְּדִיקָה; וְשֶׁעֵינֶיהָ כְּעוּרוֹת — כָּל גּוּפָהּ צְרִיכָה בְּדִיקָה” — “any bride whose eyes are beautiful, her whole body needs no examination she is surely fit; but one whose eyes are ugly, her whole body requires examination.” (The Midrash applies the “eyes” to the Sanhedrin — the seeing “eyes” of the congregation.) R’ Tzadok’s use: the eyes are “the essential point in a woman,” for they disclose the inner state — hence the whole se’if turns on the meaning of Leah’s “tender eyes.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev §3): “בְּשֵׁינָה צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם שְׁמִירָה” — “In sleep a person requires guarding”; “והשי״ת שומרו באור מקיף והוא סומך לכל הנופלים” — “Hashem guards him with an encompassing light, and He is ‘the Supporter of all the fallen.’” The passage then applies that support to the imagery of beauty and covenantal purity: “ובתורה נקרא יוסף הצדיק יפה תואר ויפה מראה והיינו שהיה לו גוף נקי דנטיר ברית” — “In the Torah Yosef the righteous is called ‘beautiful of form and beautiful of appearance’: he had a pure body, because he guarded the covenant.” Conversely, its image of one who is dark and not beautiful represents one who has already damaged the covenant. Yet the source concludes: “שאף אם קלקל כבר יוכל לתקן ע״י תשובה והשי״ת סומך לכל הנופלים” — “Even if he has already caused damage, he can repair it through repentance, and Hashem supports all the fallen.” This illuminates the completed movement here from beauty as covenantal restraint to Leah’s apparent blemish becoming praise through repentance; the source does not say that a person’s beauty simply survives his lapses unchanged.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Shemos §4): “דטוב מורה על קדושת הברית כמה שנאמר אמרו צדיק כי טוב והוא היפך הפוגם ח״ו שנקרא רע בעיני ה׳” — “‘Good’ indicates the holiness of the covenant, as it says, ‘Say of the righteous that it is good’; it is the opposite of one who, God forbid, damages it, who is called ‘evil in the eyes of Hashem.’” This directly illuminates the author’s completed interpretation here of “evil in the eyes of Hashem” in relation to covenantal purity. The source also teaches: “שומר שבת מחללו ושומר ידו מעשות כל רע ודרשו במכילתא ... שמשומר מן העבירה ונראה שמרמז ביחוד על פגם זה שנקרא רע” — “‘One who guards Shabbos from profaning it, and guards his hand from doing any evil’: the Mechilta expounds that he is guarded from transgression, and it appears that this alludes particularly to this blemish, which is called ‘evil.’” It continues that Shabbos repairs the past as well as guarding the future, and earlier develops repentance’s power to repair this covenantal fault.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 33b: “R’ Chanina said: Everything is in the hands of Heaven except for the fear of Heaven ha-kol biydei shamayim chutz mi-yiras shamayim, as it says (Devarim 10:12), ‘and now, Israel, what does Hashem your God ask of you, but to fear Him.’”Sefat Emet parallel - Eikev 24:3: Sefat Emet offers a striking parallel to R. Tzadok's equation of sight, fear, and the rectification of the eyes. On "mah Hashem Elokecha sho'el me'imach ki im le-yirah," he writes that the inward bond with Hashem is already planted in the souls of Israel, but materiality covers it; yirah opens that hidden interior. He then states explicitly, "yirah otiyot re'iyah": fear and seeing are composed of the same letters, because through yirah a person becomes able to see truth, and the Divine power concealed in the Jewish soul is revealed. He connects this to the opening of both moach and lev. This beautifully complements R. Tzadok's use of "the eye sees and the heart desires." The problem of sight is not solved merely by closing the eyes; it is rectified by transforming seeing itself. Unrectified re'iyah awakens taavah and draws the heart outward. Holy re'iyah, born of yirah, pierces the material covering and allows the heart to perceive Divine reality within what it sees. Leah's "tender eyes" can therefore become not a defect but the very place in which a higher seeing is formed through tears, fear, and teshuvah.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The “eyes” are the essence of a woman’s beauty — the eye sees and the heart desires. True beauty is kevishas ha-taavah (mastering desire). Leah’s “tender eyes” seem a disgrace, but after teshuvah the very flawed limb becomes praiseworthy — “zdonos become zechuyos.” Re’iyah (seeing) is the letters of yirah; “all is in Heaven’s hands except the fear of Heaven.”

p: (י) — וְכָל עֵסֶק קְדוּשַׁת לֵאָה וְזַרְעָהּ הוּא בְּטָהֳרַת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה
And the entire focus of the sanctity of Leah and her offspring lies in the purity of thought,
וְשֶׁלֹּא לְהַשְׁגִּיחַ בַּמַּעֲשֶׂה אִם לֹא כֵן
and not to look at the external deed if it appears otherwise;
וְהוּא הַדְּבֵיקוּת בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
and this is cleaving to His divine thought, blessed be He,
כְּטַעַם: יִשְׂרָאֵל עָלוּ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה א, ד).
mirroring the principle: Israel arose in the Primordial Thought (Bereishit Rabbah 1:4).
וְאוּכְמָא הוּא לְגַבֵּי מַדְרֵגוֹת שֶׁלְּמַטָּה הֵימֶנּוּ,
And it appears dark and obscure (ukhmá) relative to the levels that exist below it.
וְשָׂנוּא לְגַבֵּי מַדְרֵיגַת הָרְאִיָּה
and 'hated' in relation to the perceptible level of vision.
אֲבָל זֶה גָּרַם לִפְתִיחַת הָרַחַם
Yet this very quality caused the opening of the womb,
שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּלֹא דָּם וְטֻמְאָה דְּלֵידָה
which never occurs without the blood and ritual impurity of childbirth;
כִּי כָּל לֵידָה וְהוֹסָפַת קְדוּשָּׁה יְתֵירָה וְרִיבּוּי בִּנְפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
for every birth, addition of extra sanctity, and multiplication of Jewish souls,
אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה הַבָּאָה אַחַר הַחֵטְא וְהָרִיחוּק
occurs solely through repentance that follows sin and alienation;
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְגַּדֵּל וְנִתְרַבָּה מַעֲלָתוֹ
since through this a person's stature is elevated and amplified.
וְנִתְרַחֵב חֶלְקוֹ וְגוֹרָלוֹ שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִתְרַבּוֹת הַרְבֵּה יוֹתֵר מִכְּפִי גְּבוּלוֹ הַנִּקְצָב
and his portion and lot are expanded so that he can increase far beyond his strictly apportioned boundary.
דְּזֶהוּ מִדַּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה: לִפְרוֹץ מְצָרִים וּגְבוּלִים
For this is the defining trait of teshuva: to breach boundaries and borders.
וְלַעֲשׂוֹת זְכִיּוֹת חֲדָשׁוֹת מִזְּדוֹנוֹת
and to fashion new merits out of willful transgressions.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן צַדִּיק גָּמוּר שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא הוֹלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ הַתּוֹרָה הַקָּצוּב וְהַמּוּגְבָּל וְאֵין בּוֹ הוֹסָפָה
In contrast to the completely righteous person who merely walks in the measured and bounded path of the Torah without generating expansion;
וְעַל כֵּן רָחֵל עֲקָרָה
and therefore Rachel was barren,
וְכֵן יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן הַגָּדוֹל מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף לָא הֲוֵי לֵיהּ בְּנִין .
and likewise Joshua son of Nun, the great figure from Joseph's seed, had no sons (Megillah 16b).
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר דָּוִד (תְּהִלִּים נא, ז): "הֵן בְּעָווֹן חוֹלָלְתִּי וּבְחֵטְא יֶחֱמַתְנִי אִמִּי וְגוֹמֵר",
And therefore David declared (Psalms 51:7): 'Behold, I was shapen in iniquity, and in sin did my mother conceive me, etc.',
וְעִיקַּר הַהוֹלָדָה מִנְּפָשׁוֹת יְקָרוֹת וּמְשׁוּבָּחוֹת כְּשִׁבְטֵי יָ"הּ וְהַדּוֹמֶה
and the primary procreation of precious and exalted souls such as the tribes of God and the like—
אוֹתָן שֶׁצַּדִּיקִים כְּרָחֵל וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן מִתְאַוִּים לָהֶם לֹא כְּבָנִים דְּעָלְמָא
– those which tzaddikim like Rachel and Joshua yearn for, not like ordinary children—.
אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי דַּרְגָּא דִּתְשׁוּבָה שֶׁהִיא אִימָּא עִילָּאָה – אֵם הַבָּנִים
occurs solely through the rung of Teshuva, which is Imma Ila'ah (the Supernal Mother)—the mother of children.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן רָחֵל, מִדַּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַנִּקְרֵאת בְּרַתָּא וּבַת
In contrast, Rachel embodies the attribute of the Community of Israel called the daughter (brata / bat),
(תְּהִלִּים מה, יא): "שִׁמְעִי בַת וּרְאִי",
(Psalms 45:11): 'Hear, O daughter, and consider,'
וְאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה :
and they expounded in the beginning of the chapter of the stubborn and rebellious son (Sanhedrin 68b): ",
בֵּן" – וְלֹא הָרָאוּי לִיקָּרֵא אָב
'a son'—and not one already fit to be called a father.
הָכִי נַמֵּי: "בַּת" – וְלֹא הָרְאוּיָה לִיקָּרֵא אֵם
so too: 'a daughter'—and not one fit to be called a mother.
וְנִקְרָא רַק אִימָּא תַּתָּאָה
And she is termed merely the Lower Mother (Imma Tata'ah).
רָצָה לוֹמַר מִצַּד הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים וְעָלְמָא דְּאִתְגַּלְיָא גַּם זֶה נִקְרָא אֵם
meaning from the perspective of the lower beings and the Revealed World this too is called a mother.
כִּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אַדְּרַבָּה צַדִּיק גָּמוּר חָשׁוּב יוֹתֵר מִבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה
For in this world, on the contrary, the completely righteous person appears more esteemed than the penitent,
כִּי הָאָדָם יִרְאֶה לַעֵינַיִם מִי שֶׁעֵינֶיהָ יָפוֹת
for man looks on the outward appearance, unto one whose eyes are beautiful,
וַה' יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב לְטָהֳרַת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה וְהַמַּעֲמַקִּים שֶׁבּוֹ .
while Hashem looks on the heart, unto the purity of thought and the inner depths within it (I Samuel 16:7).
וְשָׁם אָמַר "יִרְאֶה" לְשׁוֹן עָתִיד – הָרְאִיָּה גַּם כֵּן לַלֵּבָב
And there Scripture says 'yir'eh' in the future tense—that divine vision is directed toward the heart (,
וְזֶה הָיָה בְּעֵת בְּחִירַת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
(and this occurred during the choosing of King David, peace be upon him,
הַגֶּבֶר אֲשֶׁר הֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁתְּלוּיָה בַּלֵּב
the man who raised the yoke of repentance which depends upon the heart,
דְּ"לְבָבוֹ יָבִין וְשָׁב",
as in 'and his heart understands, and he returns',
וְעִיקַּר הִסְתַּכְּלוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בּוֹ לַלֵּבָב
and Hashem's primary gaze upon him was toward the heart,
אַף דְּהוּא הָיָה יְפֵה עֵינַיִם גַּם כֵּן)
even though David was also of beautiful eyes),
כִּי כָּל לְשׁוֹן עָתִיד מוֹרֶה עַל הַשָּׂגָה דִּלְעָתִיד לָבוֹא
for every future-tense phrasing points to the spiritual comprehension of the World to Come,
כְּטַעַם: אֵין "וְהָיָה" אֶלָּא שִׂמְחָה שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן עָתִיד, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן "וַיְהִי" (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה מב, ג).
mirroring the adage: 've-haya' implies joy because it denotes the future, whereas 'va-yehi' implies sorrow (Bereishit Rabbah 42:3).
וְכָאן "וַיַּרְא ה'" לְשׁוֹן עָבָר הוּא רְאִיָּה בְּעָלְמָא דְּאִתְגַּלְיָא
And here 'And Hashem saw' (vayyar) in the past tense represents sight within the Revealed World,
וּלְפִי שֶׁמַּפְתֵּחַ שֶׁל עֲקָרוּת בְּיָדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ (תַּעֲנִית ב עַמּוּד א, עַיֵּין שָׁם),
and because the key of barrenness is held exclusively in His hand, blessed be He (Ta'anit 2a, see there),
וְלָמְדוּ מִמִּקְרָא הַזֶּה דְּ"וַיִּפְתַּח"
and our Sages deduced this from this very verse of 'and He opened (her womb)',
דְּלֹא הָיָה הוֹלָדָה טִבְעִית כְּכָל לֵידַת בָּנִים דְּעָלְמָא
that this was no ordinary biological birth like all mundane human procreation,
רַק הוֹלָדַת נְפָשׁוֹת יְקָרוֹת מִיָּדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ כְּפִי מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם הָרָאוּי לָהֶם
– rather the generation of exalted souls directly from His hand, blessed be His Name, commensurate with their fitting deeds—.
הָיָה הַמִּשְׁפָּט רַק לְלֵאָה
the divine decree was accorded exclusively to Leah.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §39): “The essential holiness of thought kedushas ha-machshavah comes only from habit and from the effort of ‘the commandment of men learned by rote’ mitzvas anashim melumadah — which, though it accomplishes nothing in the heart, is the more beneficial for the purity of the thought. For from a feeling in the heart comes such enthusiasm that one can scarcely act with composure; but from the recognition of the intellect in thought, one is not over-inflamed, and it works properly, with a settled mind.” (Thus Leah’s rung — “purity of thought,” at which every steady increase of holiness in Israel is achieved — is reached precisely through disciplined, unspectacular toil.)

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 122:4: “שֶׁשָּׁם עָלוּ שְׁבָטִים, שִׁבְטֵי יָהּ, עֵדוּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, לְהֹדוֹת לְשֵׁם ה׳” — “for there the tribes went up, the tribes of Kah, a testimony for Israel, to give thanks to the Name of Hashem.” Rashi: they are called “shivtei Kah” because the Divine Name is affixed to them, testifying to their legitimacy. R’ Tzadok’s use: the “precious and exalted souls, such as the tribes of Kah,” are the deep souls that come only through the rung of teshuvah (Leah / ima ila’ah) — not the “ordinary children of the world.”

paragraphs.text: Izhbitz-Radzin and Chiddushei HaRim parallel — Sha’ar HaEmunah VeYesod HaChasidut, Entrance to the Gate of Beit Yaakov 24:3–4; Chiddushei HaRim on Torah, Chayei Sara 1: The Izhbitz-Radzin identification of complete teshuvah with Binah sheds light on R. Tzadok's claim that Leah's power of "birth" is rooted in teshuvah and inner thought. Sha'ar HaEmunah teaches that when a person returns fully to the place of Binah he rises above ordinary time, and therefore can "heal the earlier" - the past is no longer a sealed block that can only be regretted. Chiddushei HaRim expresses the same transformative power more existentially: through teshuvah, "in one hour and one moment," past days can be repaired as though they had been filled with mitzvos and good deeds. This makes R. Tzadok's language of holadah particularly apt. Teshuvah is not only erasure; it is generative. From the very place in which a life seemed to have been diminished, new Torah, new avodah, and even a new reading of the past can be born. Leah, the hidden Binah-world, thus represents the womb of spiritual renewal.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 10b initially transmits: “wherever it says va-yehi, it denotes distress.” After counterexamples, Rav Ashi qualifies this: “כָּל וַיְהִי אִיכָּא הָכִי וְאִיכָּא הָכִי; וַיְהִי בִּימֵי אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן צַעַר” — “va-yehi can have either sense; va-yehi bimei denotes only distress.” The complementary contrast used by R’ Tzadok appears in Bereishis Rabbah 42:3: R’ Shmuel bar Nachman says that va-yehi serves for distress and ve-hayah for joy. R’ Tzadok reads the latter’s future sense as pointing toward the Future to Come, in contrast to the revealed-world past tense “and Hashem saw.”

paragraphs.text: Taanis 2a: “R’ Yochanan said: Three keys are in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, that are not given over to a messenger — the key of rain, the key of the woman in childbirth mafteach shel chayah, and the key of the resurrection of the dead.” (So the ending of barrenness — the ‘opening of the womb’ — is in His hand alone.) The Gemara’s explicit prooftext is the opening of Rachel’s womb (Bereishis 30:22); R’ Tzadok applies the principle to the present explanation of Leah.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Leah’s holiness is in purity of thought (cleaving to the Divine “thought”). Every “birth” and increase of souls in Israel comes only through the teshuvah that follows sin — which bursts one’s allotted boundary and turns zdonos into zechuyos. Hence Rachel and Yehoshua bin Nun (perfect-tzaddik line) were barren; the deepest souls come through Leah — ima ila’ah, “the mother of the children.”

p: (יא): — וּלְפִי שֶׁהָיָה מִצַּד הָרְאִיָּה, נולד רְאוּבֵן עַל שֵׁם הָרְאִיָּה
And because this unfolded through the perspective of sight, Reuben was born and named after vision:
(בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, לב): "כִּי רָאָה ה' בְּעָנְיִי",
Genesis 29:32: 'Because Hashem has looked upon my affliction,'.
וְכִי שְׂנוּאָה אָנֹכִי
and because I was hated.
וּבוֹ נִתְגַּלָּה דָּבָר זֶה
And through him this principle was unveiled,
שֶׁהוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן מִזֶּרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמְקוּדָּשִׁים שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה חֵטְא עָצוּם כָּזֶה
in that he was the very first of the sanctified seed of Israel concerning whom an immense sin is recorded in the Torah.
וְנִתְגַּלָּה תֵּיכֶף עַל יָדוֹ מַדְרֵגַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה בָּעוֹלָם שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהּ בְּלֹא חֵטְא
and immediately through him was revealed the spiritual degree of repentance in the world, which cannot exist without prior sin.
וְתַלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁחָטָא אַל תְּהַרְהֵר אַחֲרָיו בַּיּוֹם דְּוַדַּאי עָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה מִיָּד (בְּרָכוֹת יט עַמּוּד א),
And if you see a Torah scholar commit a sin by night, do not entertain doubts after him by day, for he certainly repented immediately (Berakhot 19a),
וְנֶאֱמַר מִיָּד (בְּרֵאשִׁית לה, כב): "וַיִּהְיוּ בְנֵי יַעֲקֹב שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר", דְּנִתְקַבְּלָה תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ.
and Scripture immediately states (Genesis 35:22): 'Now the sons of Jacob were twelve,' showing that his repentance was accepted.
וְאַף שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת נה עַמּוּד ב):
And even though our Sages of blessed memory declared (Shabbat 55b):
כָּל הָאוֹמֵר רְאוּבֵן חָטָא אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא טוֹעֶה, רַק מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב
Whoever asserts that Reuben sinned is nothing other than mistaken, Scripture merely holding him accountable,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֲרֵי הַכָּתוּב חָפֵץ בְּטוֹבַת וּבִשְׁבַח כָּל הַבְּרִיּוֹת
nonetheless Scripture desires the welfare and praise of all creatures,
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן שִׁבְטֵי יָ"הּ,
and all the more so the holy tribes of God,
וְלָמָּה יְסַפֵּר בִּגְנוּתָן מַה שֶּׁלֹּא חָטְאוּ
and why would it recount their disparagement regarding that which they did not commit,
וְיִתְלֶה בּוֹ חֵטְא עָצוּם כָּזֶה לִהְיוֹת מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִלּוּ עָשָׂה
ascribing to him such a severe transgression so that Scripture reckons it as though he had done it,
וּבִפְרָט שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת שָׁב אַחַר כָּךְ?!
and especially when he truly repented afterward?!
רַק לְפִי שֶׁכָּל חֶטְאוֹ הָיָה לְגַלּוֹת מַדְרֵגַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה וּלְהוֹדִיעַ תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ,
Rather, because his entire sin occurred to reveal the spiritual degree of repentance and make known its power,
אִם כֵּן בְּהֶכְרֵחַ הָיָה לְגַלּוֹת הַחֵטְא וְעוֹד לְהַגְדִּילוֹ כְּדֵי לְהַגְדִּיל כֹּחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה
if so it was necessary to expose the sin and even magnify it in order to aggrandize the potency of repentance.
וְזֶהוּ שִׁבְחוֹ: שֶׁאַחַר הַתְּשׁוּבָה שָׁב הַחֵטְא עַצְמוֹ לִהְיוֹת שְׁבָח וּזְכוּת
and this constitutes his praise: that after repentance the sin itself is transformed into glory and merit.
וְכֵן בִּיהוּדָה – מֵאִתּוֹ יָצְאוּ כְּבוּשִׁים לִבְרוֹא אוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ,
And likewise with Judah—from him emerged hidden, veiled events to generate the light of the Messiah,
וּבוֹ נִתְגַּלָּה תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת שֶׁל הַתִּיקּוּן
and through him was revealed the ultimate perfection of rectification;
דְּאַף שֶׁהָיָה נִרְאֶה כְּחֵטְא וּבִיאַת זְנוּת
for even though it appeared outwardly as a transgression and an act of harlotry,
בֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה דָּבָר קָדוֹשׁ מְאֹד
in truth it was an exceedingly sacred occurrence.
דְּמֵאַרְיָא בִּישָׁא וּפוֹעֵל רַע גּוּרְיָא טָבָא לָא נָפֵיק
for from an evil lion and a wicked agent a noble lion cub does not emerge.
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁמִּזֶּה יָצָא שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת בֵּית דָּוִד וּמָשִׁיחַ שֶׁהֵם נְפָשׁוֹת הַיּוֹתֵר קְדוֹשׁוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
And since from this union issued the royal dynasty of David and the Messiah, the most sanctified souls in Israel,
עַל כֵּן הָיָה הָעִנְיָן קְדוּשָּׁה יְתֵירָה מְאֹד
therefore the matter was imbued with extraordinary sanctity,
שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה עֲדַיִן כָּזֹאת, וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה רָאוּי לָזֶה
such as had never yet existed, making it worthy of such a lineage.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלְּמַרְאִית הָעַיִן אֵין כֵּן
even though to outward appearance it was not so.
וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת דַּרְגָּא דְּלֵאָה
And this is the pinnacle of the spiritual degree of Leah,
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרָה אָז (בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, לה): "הַפַּעַם אוֹדֶה אֶת ה
'", which is why she proclaimed then (Genesis 29:35): 'This time I will praise Hashem,'
שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְבָּרֵר עִנְיָנָהּ וּמַעֲלָתָהּ.
for her spiritual station and supreme virtue were now fully clarified.
וְאָז "וַתַּעֲמֹד מִלֶּדֶת"
And at that point 'she ceased from bearing',
עַד מַעֲשֵׂה הַדּוּדָאִים
until the incident of the mandrakes,
שֶׁאָז נִתְחַדֵּשׁ גִּלּוּי עִנְיָן נוֹסָף בְּמַעֲלַת לֵאָה בְּהוֹלָדַת יִשָּׂשׂכָר וּזְבוּלוּן
at which time a further revelation of Leah's greatness was renewed through the birth of Issachar and Zebulun.
שֶׁהֵם לוֹמְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה וְתוֹמְכֵי אוֹרַיְיתָא
who are the students of the Torah and the supporters of the Torah.
וְהַתּוֹרָה נוֹבְלוֹת חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה יז, ה),
And the Torah is a diminished reflection of Supernal Wisdom, as our Sages of blessed memory taught (Bereishit Rabbah 17:5),
וְהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגַת הַבִּינָה שֶׁמִּשָּׁם הַתְּשׁוּבָה, דַּרְגָּא דְּלֵאָה מִצַּד עַצְמָהּ.
and this transcends the level of Binah whence teshuva derives, which is Leah's attribute intrinsically.
וּכְשֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנָּה שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת הַגֶּבֶר שֶׁהֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה כְּבָר נִשְׁלַם מַדְרֵגָתָהּ בִּשְׁלֵימוּת
And when from her emerged the lineage of the man who raised the yoke of repentance, her own intrinsic level was completed in perfection.
אֲבָל מִצַּד מַדְרֵגָה גְּדוֹלָה יוֹתֵר, חִיבּוּרָהּ עִם יַעֲקֹב
Yet from the perspective of an even loftier rung, her union with Jacob,
שֶׁבְּחִיבּוּרוֹ עִם לֵאָה גַּם הוּא נִתְעַלָּה לְמַדְרֵגַת חָכְמָה
– wherein through his union with Leah he too was elevated to the level of Chokhmah—

paragraphs.text: Sefat Emet parallel — Vayeshev 33:4: Sefat Emet develops precisely the paradox R. Tzadok sees in Reuven. On "ha-yeled einenu va-ani anah ani va," he cites the Midrash that Reuven was the first to open the path of teshuvah and that Hoshea, descended from Reuven, therefore opened his prophecy with "Shuvah Yisrael." He defines complete teshuvah as the state in which, because of the sin, the person finds no place or independent existence for himself; only then does Hashem give him a new "place" of refuge. He adds that Reuven was in truth a tzaddik and that the very occurrence of his failing served so that he could teach teshuvah for the generations. This is an exceptionally close complement to R. Tzadok's "kol ha-omer Reuven chata eino ela to'eh" together with Reuven's being the first recorded Israelite paradigm of return. The point is not to deny the moral seriousness of what required teshuvah. Rather, the revealed fall and the hidden purity coexist in such a way that the fall itself becomes the occasion through which the world learns a form of return that could not have been taught by an untouched tzaddik.

paragraphs.text: Bava Kama 92b gives the related proverb that a bad palm goes to a grove of barren trees, and the maxim that creatures attach to their own kind. The specific “good cub” proverb appears in Rashi to Megillah 11b: “מִכַּלְבָּא בִּישָׁא גּוּרְיָא טָבָא לָא נָפִיק” — “from a bad dog a good cub does not issue.” R’ Tzadok’s use is by inversion: precisely because the House of David — “the holiest souls in Israel” — did issue from the Yehudah–Tamar union, that union, though “to the eye’s view” it looked like “a sin, a union with a harlot,” was “in truth a most holy matter”; the holy “cub” proves the holiness of its root.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Reuven, born “for the seeing,” is the first of Israel’s holy ones recorded with a grave “sin” — precisely to reveal the level of teshuvah (impossible without sin). “Whoever says Reuven sinned is mistaken” — yet Scripture magnifies it to magnify teshuvah, so the sin itself becomes praise. So too Yehudah/Tamar → the House of David. Leah’s rung culminates; joined with Yaakov she rises to Chochmah.

until the coming of the Messiah from her seed, speedily in our days.
וְכָל לֵידַת הַשְּׁבָטִים הֵם הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשָּׁרָשִׁים לְבַד בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And all the births of the tribes represent merely the unveiling of the roots in this world.
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ רְאוּבֵן וְשִׁמְעוֹן הוּא רַק תִּיקּוּן הָרְאִיָּה וְהַשְּׁמִיעָה
And the root of Reuben and Simeon is the rectification of sight and hearing,
דְּמִצַּד עַיִן רוֹאָה בָּא הַחֲמָדוֹת
for through the seeing eye come covetous desires,
וּמִצַּד אֹזֶן שׁוֹמַעַת בָּא קַבָּלַת הַתּוֹכָחָה וְהַתְּשׁוּבָה
and through the hearing ear comes the acceptance of rebuke and repentance,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (דְּבָרִים רַבָּה י, א). — הָאֹזֶן הַזֶּה כַּקַּנְקַל לַגּוּף
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Devarim Rabbah 10:1): this ear is like a funnel to the body.
וְכָל חֵשֶׁק לֵאָה לְהַרְבּוֹת שְׁבָטִים
And all of Leah's passion was to multiply tribes,
וְזֶה עִיקַּר מַעֲלָתָהּ מִצַּד הַחֶמְדָּה וְהַחֵשֶׁק
and this was her primary virtue through sacred longing and desire,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּל חֵשֶׁק הוּא מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
even though all physical passion is associated with the inclination in this world,
שֶׁהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (סט עַמּוּד ב); — דִּבִּכְבִישַׁת הַיֵּצֶר לָא אִשְׁתֲּכַח בֵּיעֲתָא בַּת יוֹמָא וְנִמְנַע הַהוֹלָדָה
for they stated in Yoma (69b) that upon the suppression of the inclination not a fresh egg could be found and reproduction ceased;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא בִּקְדוּשָּׁה אֵין קְדוּשָּׁה לְמַעְלָה הֵימֶנּוּ
nevertheless when desire is sanctified there is no holiness higher than it
וְנִקְרָא "טוֹב מְאֹד",
and it is designated 'very good',
דְּ"לֹא תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ לָשֶׁבֶת יְצָרָהּ" (יְשַׁעְיָה מה, יח),
for 'He created it not a waste, He formed it to be inhabited' (Isaiah 45:18),
וְרָצָה שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִבְרָאִין הַמַּכִּירִין כֹּחַ מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and He willed that creations exist who recognize the power of His sovereignty, blessed be He.
וְהִיא לֹא רָצְתָה לְהַעֲמִיד תּוֹלָדוֹת רַק מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And she refused to raise offspring from anyone other than our father Jacob, peace be upon him.
שֶׁיָּדְעָה דְּכוּלּוֹ זֶרַע אֱמֶת
knowing that his seed is entirely the seed of truth.
וּמִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִרְאֶה זֶה חִסָּרוֹן בְּעַיְינִין
And from the perspective of this world this appeared as a blemish in the eyes.
וּבֶאֱמֶת זֶה הָיָה עִיקַּר הַמַּעֲלָה
yet in truth this was the very pinnacle of virtue.
וּלְכָךְ רְאוּבֵן הוּא "רֵאשִׁית אוֹנִי" דְּיַעֲקֹב (בְּרֵאשִׁית מט, ג),
And therefore Reuben is 'the beginning of my strength' of Jacob (Genesis 49:3),
וְיָדוּעַ דְּמַעֲלַת הַבְּכוֹר דְּבוֹ נִכְלָל כָּל הַנּוֹלָדִים אַחֲרָיו
and it is known that the virtue of the firstborn is that in him are included all who are born after him,
דְּזֶה טַעַם חִיּוּב כִּבּוּד אָחִיו הַגָּדוֹל כַּנּוֹדָע מִטַּעַם הָאֲרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
this being the reason for the obligation to honor one's older brother as known from the holy Ari of blessed memory,
וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּלַל מַדְרֵיגוֹת הָאֲמִיתִיּוֹת לְיַעֲקֹב
and this is the root of the collective genuine levels of Jacob.
הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא
which expands into this world, the World of Falsehood.
וְעִיקַּר שַׁקְרָנוּת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא מַה שֶּׁכָּל הֲנָאוֹתָיו הוּא רַק כְּרֶגַע
And the foundational falsehood of this world is that all its pleasures last but a fleeting moment,
כְּמִדַּת לְשׁוֹן שֶׁקֶר
mirroring the character of a lying tongue (Proverbs 12:19).
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן שְׂפַת אֱמֶת הוּא מַה שֶּׁתִּכּוֹן לָעַד
whereas the lip of truth is that which is established forever.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 49:31 (cf. 50:13): “שָׁמָּה קָבְרוּ אֶת אַבְרָהָם וְאֵת שָׂרָה אִשְׁתּוֹ… וְשָׁמָּה קָבַרְתִּי אֶת לֵאָה” — “there they buried Avraham and Sarah his wife… and there I buried Leah.” In his charge, Yaakov asks to be buried in Me’aras HaMachpelah beside Leah — not Rachel, who was buried “on the road to Efras” (Bereishis 35:19) — and Yaakov himself is laid there (50:13). R’ Tzadok’s use: Yaakov’s love of Rachel belonged only to “this world” and its outward manifestation; but for eternity — the World to Come — his rest is with Leah, “in the secret of Abba and Ima that never part,” his level raised to the root of supernal Chochmah.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — structural parallel (Sichat Shedim 2:1): in his discussion of the configurations of the sitra achra, he uses the names Abba and Ima for the hidden roots that produce lower male and female configurations, and explains: “ר״ל יְצִיאַת כֹּחַ הַחָכְמָה וּבִינָה לַפּוֹעַל עַל יְדֵי הַז׳ תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת” — “that is, the emergence of the power of Chochmah and Binah into actuality through the seven lower powers.” He adds that Chochmah and Binah are hidden, whereas the seven lower powers are clothed in bodily organs. This illustrates the distinction between hidden intellectual roots and their manifested powers. In the present passage, R’ Tzadok locates Yaakov and Leah’s World-to-Come bond at the supernal root of Chochmah and Binah, beyond the limits of their manifestation in this world.

paragraphs.text: Zohar (a recurring dictum; cf. Zohar III 4a, and the Idra): Chochmah and Binah — “Abba and Imma” — are “trein re’in de-la mitpar’shin,” “two companions that never part,” ever joined in perfect union. R’ Tzadok’s use: Leah’s own rung is Binah (the source of teshuvah), but “from a still-higher level” she is joined with Yaakov and rises with him to Chochmah (the rung of “Yisrael,” the talmid chacham); and since Chochmah and Binah “never part,” the union of Yaakov and Leah is the deepest bond of all.

paragraphs.text: Shem MiShmuel and Sefat Emet parallel — Shem MiShmuel, Vayetzei 9:15; Sefat Emet, Vayechi 22:3: The Rachel-Leah polarity here is illuminated by Shem MiShmuel's formulation that Rachel corresponds to alma d'isgalya while Leah corresponds to alma d'iskasya. The revealed world displays beauty, deed, and ordered attainment; the hidden world contains heights whose value is not immediately visible and is reached through inward separation from evil. This helps explain why Yaakov's attachment to Rachel belongs to the structure of this world while Leah becomes his enduring partner at the root. Sefat Emet adds that "Yaakov Avinu did not die" means that Yaakov deposited his whole power within the collective of Israel, which can awaken it in every generation. R. Tzadok's point is thus not simply biographical - that Yaakov happened to be buried with Leah. At the level of eternal Israel, Yaakov's abiding force is joined to the hidden world from which teshuvah and inner renewal emerge. Rachel represents visible perfection; Leah represents the concealed source that can regenerate life after visible perfection has failed.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 69b: after the inclination to illicit relations was delivered into the Sages’ hands, they were warned that killing it would end the world. “חַבְשׁוּהוּ תְּלָתָא יוֹמֵי, וּבְעוֹ בֵּיעֲתָא בַּת יוֹמָא בְּכָל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלָא אִשְׁתְּכַח” — “They imprisoned it for three days, and sought a freshly laid egg throughout Eretz Yisrael, but none was found.” They therefore blinded its eyes and released it; this diminished desire for close relatives. R’ Tzadok uses the interruption of procreation to show that the power of desire sustains generation, and that Leah’s desire for holy offspring can therefore become a supreme holiness.

paragraphs.text: Yeshayahu 45:18: “כִּי כֹה אָמַר ה׳ בּוֹרֵא הַשָּׁמַיִם… לֹא תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ, לָשֶׁבֶת יְצָרָהּ” — “He did not create it the world a tohu (wasteland); He formed it to be inhabited.” The Sages derive from “la-sheves yetzarah” the worth of settling and populating the world — the ground of the mitzvah of procreation (cf. Gittin 41b). R’ Tzadok’s use: desire, when channeled in holiness (as Leah’s yearning to raise up tribes), is “very good,” for “He did not create it a wasteland” — “He desired that there be creatures who recognize the power of His kingship.”
