paragraphs.text: Kesuvos 103a: in the exposition of “Honor your father and your mother” (Shemos 20:12), “את אביך” includes one’s father’s wife and “ואת אמך” includes one’s mother’s husband; “וָיו יְתֵירָה — לְרַבּוֹת אֶת אָחִיךָ הַגָּדוֹל” — “the extra vav includes your older brother.” See also Rambam, Hilchos Mamrim 6:15. The Arizal gives the mystical ground: the souls of the later children are “included” within the firstborn, who is their root — so honoring him is honoring the root that contains them. R’ Tzadok’s use: “the virtue of the firstborn is that all born after him are included within him” — Reuven the bechor comprising all the levels of Yaakov.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Yaakov’s love of Rachel belongs only to olam ha-zeh; in the World to Come he is buried with Leah, at the root of supernal Chochmah (Abba and Ima that never part). Reuven and Shimon are the tikkun of seeing and hearing. Leah’s longing to bear tribes — desire channeled into holiness — is “very good.” This world is alma d’shikra: its pleasures last but a moment; only “the lip of truth is established forever.”

p: (יג); — וְכָל הַתַּאֲווֹת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִקְרָא (מִשְׁלֵי כ, יז): "עָרֵב לְאִישׁ לֶחֶם שָׁקֶר וְגוֹמֵר" מֵהַאי טַעְמָא
And all lusts of this world are titled (Proverbs 20:17): 'Bread of deceit is sweet to a man, etc.' for this reason;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶאֱמַר (בַּמִּדְבָּר כג, י): "וּמִסְפָּר אֶת רֹבַע יִשְׂרָאֵל",
whereas regarding the children of Israel it is said (Numbers 23:10): 'or count the stock (rova / seed) of Israel'.
כִּי הֵם קַיָּימִים לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד
for they endure for all eternity.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (הוּבָא בְּחַסְדֵי אָבוֹת לְהָרַב חִידָ"א)
And as they stated in the Zohar (cited in Chasdei Avot by the Chida)
עַל פָּסוּק (יְשַׁעְיָה מט, כא): "אֵלֶּה מִי יָלַד לִי",
on the verse (Isaiah 49:21): 'Who has begotten me these?'
דְּגַם מִכָּל טִפִּין שֶׁאֵין נוֹלָד בַּפּוֹעַל אֵינָם לְבַטָּלָה
that even from all seminal drops that did not produce living offspring in actuality, none were in vain.
וְיִהְיוּ מֵהֶם תּוֹלָדוֹת לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא
and from them will issue progeny in the World to Come.
וְזֶה מִדַּת הָאֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב שֶׁאֵינוֹ לֶחֶם שֶׁקֶר
And this is the attribute of Truth to Jacob which is not bread of falsehood,
אֶלָּא שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין בֵּירוּר גָּמוּר בָּזֶה אֲפִילּוּ לַחֲסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים
except that in this world there is no complete clarification of this even for the most pious among the pious,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה יד, ה) עַל פָּסוּק "בְּעָווֹן מָלֵא",
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded in Vayikra Rabbah (14:5) on the verse 'in iniquity,' with 'iniquity' written in full,
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן הַפְּחוּתִים עַד סוֹף כָּל הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת מִזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב
and all the more so the lowest down to the end of all levels from Jacob's seed,
דְּכֻלָּם לֹא יִדַּח מֵהֶם נִדָּח
that from all of them none shall be utterly cast away.
דִּלְעוֹלָם אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא וּבְשָׁרְשׁוֹ דָּבוּק בֶּאֱמֶת
for forever 'even though he has sinned, he remains Israel' and in his root clings to Truth.
וְזֶה "רֵאשִׁית אוֹנוֹ" דְּיַעֲקֹב
– And this is 'the beginning of his strength' of Jacob—,
הִתְגַּלּוּת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה דְּעַיִן רוֹאָה שֶׁמֵּחֲמָתוֹ הַלֵּב חוֹמֵד
the revelation of holiness within the seeing eye on account of which the heart covets.
דְּגַם זֶה כֻּלּוֹ זֶרַע אֱמֶת
showing that this too is entirely the seed of truth.
וּמַה שֶּׁנִּגְלָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לֹא כֵן
And that which appeared in this world to be otherwise,
הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַמְּהִירוּת
stems merely from undue haste,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קז עַמּוּד א) בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "אֲכָלָהּ פַּגָּה",
along the lines of what is taught in Sanhedrin (107a) concerning King David: 'he ate it while unripe',
וְזֶהוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מט, ד): "פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם",
and this is (Genesis 49:4): 'Unstable as water',
(וּמַיִם מוֹרֶה תַּאֲוָה כַּנּוֹדָע).
(water denoting physical desire, as is known).
וּלְכְשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה וְיִתְבָּרֵר דְּהַכֹּל דְּבַר מִצְוָה
And when it will be revealed and clarified that everything was at its core a matter of mitzvah,
הֲרֵי זֶה מְהִירוּת לְמִצְוָה וְ"זָרִיז וְנִשְׂכָּר" קָרֵינַן לֵיהּ.
behold this constitutes swiftness toward a mitzvah and is termed 'diligent and rewarded.',
דְּאֵין לְךָ גָּרוּעַ מִבְּנוֹת לוֹט
For you have nothing seemingly more degraded than the daughters of Lot,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּנָזִיר (כג עַמּוּד ב):
and nonetheless our Sages of blessed memory stated in Nazir (23b):
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקְּדָמַתָּה לְמִצְוָה קְדָמַתָּהּ אַרְבָּעָה דּוֹרוֹת לַמַּלְכוּת
because the older daughter preceded the younger toward the mitzvah, she preceded her by four generations into kingship.
וְהַיְינוּ אַחַר שֶׁיָּצָא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַטּוֹב שֶׁהָיָה בָּהּ וְנִקְלַט בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
And that occurred once the good root within her emerged and was absorbed into Israel,
וְנִתְגַּלָּה הַקְּדוּשָּׁה הַגְּנוּזָה בְּדָבָר זֶה
– and the holiness concealed within that event was unveiled—;
מִצַּד הַקְּדוּשָּׁה נִקְרָא קְדִימָה לְמִצְוָה
from the perspective of holiness it is designated precedence toward a mitzvah;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשָּׁם רוּבּוֹ כִּכֻלּוֹ מַמָּשׁ הָיָה כָּלוּל בְּמַחֲשָׁבוֹת רָעוֹת
even though in that historical act virtually its entire exterior was wrapped in dark thoughts.
שֶׁהֲרֵי לֹא נִבְחַר מִכָּל אַחַת מֵהֶם אֶלָּא פְּרֵידָה אַחַת טוֹבָה
for from each of them nothing was extracted except a single good dove/mule (pereidah tovah).
וְנִקְרָא "פְּרֵידָה" בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (לח עַמּוּד ב)
And it is termed pereidah in Bava Kamma (38b),
לְשׁוֹן יוֹנָה וּלְשׁוֹן פֶּרֶד
denoting both a dove and a mule,
דְּהָא וְהָא אִיתֵיהּ:
for both meanings are present:
כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְיוֹנָה אִמְתִּילָא (בְּרָכוֹת נג עַמּוּד ב),
the Community of Israel is compared to a pure dove (Berakhot 53b),
וְאֵל אַחֵר דְּאַסְטְרִים נִמְשָׁל לְפֶרֶד שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹלִיד
while the alien god of sterilities is likened to a sterile mule that does not bear offspring,
וּמוֹרֶה עַל זִמָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (תְּהִלִּים לב, ט): "כְּסוּס כְּפֶרֶד אֵין הָבִין",
and signifies wanton licentiousness as it is written (Psalms 32:9): 'Be not as the horse, or as the mule, which have no understanding,'.
וְהוּא מַמְזֵר וְכִלְאַיִם מִסּוּס וַחֲמוֹר
and the mule is a hybrid crossbred from a horse and a donkey.
וְכֵן הֵם מִצַּד שָׁרְשָׁם כֵּן
And they were initially so from the side of their pagan root;
רַק אַחַר שֶׁנִּפְרְדָה מִשָּׁרְשָׁהּ,
yet once Ruth was separated from her root,
דְּגֵר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר כְּקָטָן שֶׁנּוֹלַד דָּמֵי (יְבָמוֹת כב עַמּוּד א),
for a convert who embraces Judaism is like a newborn child (Yevamot 22a),
יָצָא מֵהֶם מַלְכוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנִמְשַׁל לְיוֹנָה
there emerged from them the royalty of Israel, the root of the Community of Israel compared to a dove,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין צה עַמּוּד א)
as our Sages stated in Chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 95a);
בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּעוּבְדָא דְּיִשְׁבִּי
concerning King David, peace be upon him, in the episode of Yishbi-benob;
וְקַל וָחֹמֶר בֶּן בְּנוֹ שֶׁל קַל וָחֹמֶר
and it is an a fortiori argument to the utmost degree.
לְכָל הַתַּאֲווֹת שֶׁבְּזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלָּם – שֶׁהֵם כֻּלָּם זֶרַע אֱמֶת
regarding all desires found within the seed of Israel—that they are all entirely the seed of truth.

paragraphs.text: Mishlei 20:17: “עָרֵב לָאִישׁ לֶחֶם שָׁקֶר, וְאַחַר יִמָּלֵא פִיהוּ חָצָץ” — “Sweet to a man is the bread of falsehood, but afterward his mouth is filled with gravel.” Rashi / Metzudos: illicit or false gain is sweet at first taste but ends in bitterness (gravel). R’ Tzadok’s use: all the desires of “this world” are “lechem sheker” — their pleasure lasts only a moment and then turns to gravel; this is the mark of alma d’shikra, over against the enduring “seed of truth” of Israel.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §60): “‘sweet to a man is bread of falsehood’ — but its reverse is truth, the rung of Yaakov, and it is what brings life, as in Perek Chelek: ‘from the place whose name is truth.’” This is §6-13’s measure exactly — worldly desire is “bread of falsehood,” fleeting; but “the trait of truth to Yaakov” is no bread of falsehood, for it is drawn “from the place whose name is truth,” and so it endures and gives life, while the seed of Israel “endures for all eternity.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §18): “התאוה נקרא שקר ... אחר שמלא תאותו היא נמאסת וכן בסוף הכל בימי הזקנה בטלים כל התאות. ושקר הוא דבר הפוסק” — “Desire is called falsehood … after a person has satisfied his desire it becomes repulsive; likewise, in the end, in old age, all the desires cease. Falsehood is something that comes to an end.” He explicitly cites “ערב לאיש לחם שקר ואחר ימלא פיהו חצץ” and applies Israel’s remorse after sin to the rainbow and the promise that “לא ידח ממנו נדח” — “none of His banished ones will remain banished.” This illuminates the complete contrast here between desire that expires and Israel’s enduring attachment to truth, even after sin. The source later distinguishes the defeat of Edom from rule over it: “ולכך הניצוח אז לאדום שהוא מקור הקנאה ורציחה ... ונפילה שלו הוא ביד זרעו של יוסף ... מה שאין כן דוד המלך ע״ה הוא אחר הניצוח למשול עליו” — “Therefore the victory then is over Edom, which is the source of envy and murder … and its downfall is at the hand of the seed of Yosef … whereas David the king comes after the victory, to rule over it.” The latter distinction is preserved as part of the cited teaching; it is not an explanation of Shlomo’s particular position within Malchus.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 58: “והוא מדת האמת ליעקב שכולו זרע אמת דזהו מדת האמת כאשר כולו כך מבריח מקצה אל הקצה ואין בו דבר מלבר כי שפת אמת תכון לעד.” — “This is the attribute of truth belonging to Jacob, who is entirely seed of truth; for this is the attribute of truth when it is entirely so, passing through from end to end, with nothing in it from outside, for the lip of truth is established forever.” This parallels the claim that Israel’s enduring root remains truth even where its present appearance is otherwise.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 49:4: “פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם אַל תּוֹתַר, כִּי עָלִיתָ מִשְׁכְּבֵי אָבִיךָ…” — “Impetuous as water, you shall not have superiority, for you ascended your father’s bed…” — Yaakov’s words to Reuven. Rashi: “pachaz ka-mayim” — the haste and impetuosity with which you acted. R’ Tzadok’s use (with the known reading that “water denotes desire”): Reuven’s “impetuousness” is only the outward “haste”; once it is clarified that all was “a matter of mitzvah,” the same haste becomes zeal toward a mitzvah — “zealous and rewarded.”

paragraphs.text: Nazir 23b-24a: “לְעוֹלָם יַקְדִּים אָדָם לִדְבַר מִצְוָה, שֶׁבִּשְׂכַר לַיְלָה אַחַת שֶׁקְּדָמַתָּה בְּכִירָה לִצְעִירָה, זָכְתָה וְקָדְמָה אַרְבָּעָה דּוֹרוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לַמַּלְכוּת.” — “A person should always precede in a matter of mitzvah, for as reward for the one night by which the elder preceded the younger, she merited to precede by four generations in Israel in kingship.” The parallel in Bava Kama 38b names Oved, Yishai, David, and Shlomo, while the younger’s line reaches Rechavam through Naamah. R’ Tzadok applies this only after the good root has emerged into Israel and the hidden holiness is revealed; he immediately qualifies that the original act was overwhelmingly mixed with evil thoughts, with only one good offshoot selected from each line.

paragraphs.text: Bava Kama 38b: the Holy One restrained Israel from warring with Moav and Ammon, saying, “two good peridos I have to bring forth from them — Rus the Moabite and Naamah the Ammonite.” A “perida” is a precious offshoot. R’ Tzadok expounds the word doubly — from yonah (dove) and from pered (mule): Knesses Yisrael is likened to a dove, while the “other god,” barren like a mule, “does not reproduce”; the single good “perida” (Rus / Naamah) had to be separated from its impure root before the royalty of Israel could issue from it.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 32:9: “אַל תִּהְיוּ כְּסוּס כְּפֶרֶד אֵין הָבִין, בְּמֶתֶג וָרֶסֶן עֶדְיוֹ לִבְלוֹם” — “Be not like a horse or a mule, without understanding, whose adornment must be curbed with bit and bridle.” Meforshim: do not let yourself be governed like a brute beast. R’ Tzadok’s use: the pered (mule) — a sterile kilayim of “horse and donkey” — is the emblem of the “other god” that “does not reproduce” and “denotes lewdness”; hence “k’sus k’fered,” over against the fruitful “dove” of Knesses Yisrael.

paragraphs.text: Yevamos 22a: “A convert who converts is like a newborn child ger she-nisgayer k’katan she-nolad.” (Severed from his former, impure root.) Sefat Emet parallel - Vayera 30:3: Sefat Emet's explanation of "zera emes" strongly complements the discussion of enduring seed and the bris. He writes that the souls of Israel extend "from beginning to end," and that truth requires the body itself to become a fitting vessel for the light of the neshamah. Bris milah removes the "sefas sheker," the false covering introduced through sin, so that the child is born as "zera emes." Emes, in this account, is continuity: the Divine root, the embodied middle, and the final destiny must belong to one unbroken line. This gives depth to R. Tzadok's contrast between transient desire - "the bread of falsehood" - and Israel's seed of truth. Taavah seeks an immediate experience cut off from enduring purpose; bris gathers the power of desire into a line that reaches beyond the moment and bears fruit. Even where there has been failure, the root of Israel remains oriented toward that continuity, which is why teshuvah can reclaim what appeared wasted and return it to the line of emes.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Worldly desire is “the bread of falsehood” — fleeting; but Israel’s “seed of truth” endures forever, and even the “drops” that bore no child are not wasted. Reuven’s “impetuousness” (David’s “eating the unripe fig”) is, once clarified, a zealous haste toward a mitzvah — like the daughters of Lot, from whose one good “perida” royalty issued. Every desire within Israel’s seed is, at root, “seed of truth.”

p: (יד) — וְעַל כֵּן בִּרְכַּת רְאוּבֵן (דְּבָרִים לג, ו): "יְחִי רְאוּבֵן וְאַל יָמֹת",
Therefore, the blessing of Reuben is (Deuteronomy 33:6): 'Let Reuben live, and not die,'
שֶׁהַמִּיתָה נִמְשָׁךְ מֵהַתַּאֲוָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל דְּזֶהוּ עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ;
since physical death is drawn from bodily lust, as I wrote above that this is the counsel of the Serpent;
אֲבָל שְׁלֵימוּת הַבְּרָכָה בְּדַרְגָּא דִּרְאוּבֵן הִיא הַמְּבִיאָה חַיֵּי עַד
yet the consummation of blessing on the level of Reuben is what brings eternal life.
וְסִיֵּים: "וְאַל יָמֹת",
And Moses concluded: 'and not die,'
דְּבֶאֱמֶת הֲרֵי יֵשׁ חַיֵּי עוֹלָם נָטוּעַ בְּכָל זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל
for in absolute truth, eternal life is firmly planted within all the seed of Israel.
וְהַמִּיתָה רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְבַד
and mortality applies strictly to this physical world alone.
וּכְמוֹ דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא מֵת
And just as our father Jacob, peace be upon him, did not die (Ta'anit 5b).
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת מִיתָה וּקְבוּרָה
yet nonetheless there was in outward manifestation physical death and burial.
אֲבָל מִצַּד הַבְּרָכָה הוּא הַבֵּירוּר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן דְּלֹא יָמוּת כְּלָל
However, from the vantage point of the blessing, the clarification is reached in this world as well that he does not die at all,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בִּימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ.
just as will be in the days of the Messiah.
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הִתְגַּלּוּת "רֵאשִׁית אוֹנוֹ" דְּיַעֲקֹב
And this proceeds from the revelation of the 'beginning of his strength' of Jacob,
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָאֱמֶת דְּתִכּוֹן לָעַד
which is the primordial root of Truth that is established forever.
וְאֵין שָׁם מִיתָה וּבִיטּוּל כְּלָל, דְּאִם כֵּן אֵינוֹ לָעַד
and therein exists no death or nullification whatsoever, for if it did, it would not endure forever.
וְהִתְגַּלּוּת זֶה רַק עַל יְדֵי דַּרְגָּא דְּלֵאָה
And this revelation is possible solely through the spiritual degree of Leah,
דְּהַיְינוּ לְאַהְפָּכָא וְלֹא לְאַכְפַּיָּא
which means to transmute into holiness (le'ahpacha) and not merely suppress (le'akpaya).
וּמִזֶּה נִשְׁלַם הָרְאִיָּה שֶׁהוּא מֵעִנְיָנִים שֶׁחוּץ לַגּוּף
and through this is perfected the faculty of sight, which perceives matters outside the body.
וַעֲדַיִן קְרָאָהּ שִׁמְעוֹן (בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, לג): "כִּי שָׁמַע ה' כִּי שְׂנוּאָה אָנֹכִי",
Yet she still named him Simeon (Genesis 29:33): 'Because Hashem has heard that I was hated,'.
דַּעֲדַיִן לֹא נִתְבָּרֵר בִּפְנִימִיּוּת
for this truth was not yet clarified in the inward depths.
דְּיָדוּעַ דְּהָרְאִיָּה הוּא הַשָּׂגַת הָאָדָם בְּדָבָר שֶׁחוּצָה לוֹ,
For it is known that sight is a person's perception of that which remains external to him,
וְהַשְּׁמִיעָה הוּא קַבָּלַת הַדָּבָר שֶׁחוּצָה לוֹ לְגוּפוֹ,
whereas hearing is the internal absorption of the external word into his bodily essence,
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא כַּקַּנְקַל לַגּוּף
whereby the ear serves as a funnel to the body,
דְּכָל הַגּוּף מְקַבֵּל חַיִּים עַל יָדוֹ,
for the entire body receives life through it.
וְעַל יָדוֹ הוּא הַכְּנִיסָה לַגּוּף
and through it is the entry-point into the body.
וְכֵן הֵם סֵדֶר הַתְחָלַת הַשְּׁלֵימוּיּוֹת
And such is the orderly progression of the dawning of spiritual perfections:
בַּתְּחִלָּה בִּרְאִיָּה
initially in sight,
לִהְיוֹת כָּל מַה שֶּׁרוֹאֶה מֵעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַכֹּל הִסְתַּכְּלוּתוֹ וּרְאִיָּתוֹ
such that everything a person perceives among the affairs of this world, his entire gaze and vision,
הוּא רַק לְכֹחַ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַגָּנוּז בְּגַוָּום
is directed solely toward the power of Hashem, blessed be He, concealed within them,
דְּ"אַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם" (נְחֶמְיָה ט, ו).
as in 'You preserve them all' (Nehemiah 9:6).
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִמֵּילָא, כָּל מַה שֶּׁהוּא מְקַבֵּל מֵהָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְגוּפוֹ
And through this automatically, whatever he receives from this world into his body,
הוּא מְקַבֵּל מִמְּקוֹר חַיּוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמְחַיֶּה אוֹתָם
he receives directly from the Source of His vitality, blessed be He, Who animates them.
וּמִמֵּילָא גַּם גּוּפוֹ מִתְקַדֵּשׁ עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּכָל כֹּחוֹתָיו הַפְּנִימִיִּים
and automatically his physical body too is sanctified through this across all its inward faculties.
וְאָז מִסְתַּלֵּק הַשִּׂנְאָה דִּלְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן גַּם כֵּן
And then the apparent 'hatred' of external appearance is removed as well,
וְגוֹרֵם הַדְּבֵיקוּת הַגָּמוּר דְּ"הַפַּעַם יִלָּוֶה אִישִׁי" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, לד),
generating the absolute cleaving of 'this time my husband will be joined unto me' (Genesis 29:34),
שֶׁכְּבָר נַעֲשָׂה כָּל גּוּפוֹ מֶרְכָּבָה וּמִשְׁכָּן לִכְבוֹד שָׁמַיִם
in that his entire physical body has already become a chariot and tabernacle for the glory of Heaven.
וְזֶהוּ כָּל חֶלְקָהּ שֶׁל לֵאָה בַּבָּנִים
and this represents Leah's entire portion in the procreation of the tribes.
אַךְ חֵלֶק זֶה אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד דַּרְגָּא דְּאַכְפַּיָּא
Yet this measure can likewise be attained through the method of suppression (le'akpaya),
לִהְיוֹת צַדִּיק בְּכָל דְּרָכָיו
to be righteous in all of one's ways,
הוּא חֵלֶק הַמַּגִּיעַ לְרָחֵל גַּם כֵּן
which is the allotted portion that reaches Rachel as well;
אֲבָל עַל יְדֵי דַּרְגָּא דִּתְשׁוּבָה יֵשׁ הוֹסָפָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
yet through the spiritual degree of Teshuva there exists boundless addition, as mentioned above.
וּבִיהוּדָה הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת דַּרְגָּא דִּתְשׁוּבָה
And in Judah occurs the overt disclosure of the degree of Teshuva,
וּבִרְכָתוֹ הוּא (דְּבָרִים לג, ז): "שְׁמַע ה' קוֹל יְהוּדָה",
and his blessing is (Deuteronomy 33:7): 'Hear, Hashem, the voice of Judah,'
דְּכָל מַדְרֵגָתוֹ בְּהַשָּׂגַת הַקּוֹל: "הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כז, כב),
for his entire level lies in grasping the Voice: 'the voice is the voice of Jacob' (Genesis 27:22),

only that with him it is the voice of prayer—the rung of David.

whereas 'the voice of Jacob' is essentially the voice of Torah.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 145:17: “צַדִּיק ה׳ בְּכָל דְּרָכָיו, וְחָסִיד בְּכָל מַעֲשָׂיו” — “Hashem is righteous in all His ways, and kind in all His deeds” (from Ashrei). The phrase “tzaddik b’chol drachav” names a divine attribute in its biblical setting. Rav Tzadok draws an analogy to the human tzaddik gamur, one who keeps his paths righteous. The analogy helps distinguish the rung of subduing (achpaya) — “to be a tzaddik in all his ways”—the ethical discipline that Rachel’s rung too can attain. The additional level Rav Tzadok ascribes to Leah is transformation through teshuvah, beyond restraint alone. This is an interpretive echo of the Psalm, not the verse’s plain subject.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 27:22: “הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב וְהַיָּדַיִם יְדֵי עֵשָׂו” — “the voice is the voice of Yaakov, but the hands are the hands of Esav.” Bereishis Rabbah 65:20 (cf. Gittin 57b): “kol Yaakov” is the voice of Torah and prayer in the synagogues and study-halls — when it is heard, “the hands of Esav” have no power. R’ Tzadok’s use: “the voice of Yaakov” is essentially the voice of Torah; Yehudah’s (David’s) “voice” is its counterpart in prayer — “prayer being the mode by which the fallen self reaches upward, as Torah is the mode by which the Divine reaches down.” Sefat Emet and Chiddushei HaRim parallel - Sefat Emet, Vayeshev 33:4; Chiddushei HaRim on Torah, Chayei Sara 1: Two Ger sources bring out the life-giving character of Reuven's teshuvah. Sefat Emet says that Reuven "opened teshuvah" and thereby became the model from whom Hoshea could proclaim "Shuvah Yisrael." The complete baal teshuvah feels that sin has left him with no independent "place," and it is precisely then that Hashem grants him a new place. Chiddushei HaRim adds that teshuvah can repair past days "in one hour and one moment" as though they had been filled with mitzvos. This combination closely fits the blessing "yechi Reuven ve-al yamus" as R. Tzadok reads it. Reuven's life is not guaranteed because no breakdown occurred; rather, his distinct contribution to Israel is that breakdown need not become death. Teshuvah can supply a new place from which life begins again and can even restore life to the days that seemed already forfeited.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Toldos §5): “שבא״א ע״ה לא מצינו שהתפלל על עצמו ואף על בנים לא התפלל ... ורק על סדום התפלל ונקרא תפלתו עמידה ... והוא מפני שעמד בכח כיון שאינו נוגע בדבר וכמו ויעמוד פינחס ויפלל” — “We do not find that Avraham Avinu prayed for himself; he did not even pray for children … he prayed only for Sedom, and his prayer is called ‘standing’ … because he stood forcefully, since he was not personally concerned in the matter, as in ‘Pinchas stood and prayed.’” Yitzchak, by contrast, prayed for himself, pouring out his suffering and the bitterness of his heart. The source then identifies the two voices explicitly: “וז״ש הקל קול יעקב קל ה׳ קל תפלה שהיא משם אדנ״י ... קל ו׳ קול תורה ו׳ דאיקרי אות אמת ... אמת זו תורה” — “This is ‘the voice is the voice of Yaakov’: kol with the heh is the voice of prayer, which is from the name Adonai … kol with the vav is the voice of Torah; the vav is called the letter of truth … ‘truth’ is Torah.” This directly illuminates the author’s completed distinction here between the voice of prayer and Yaakov’s voice of Torah. The opening passage says that Avraham did not pray for himself; it does not establish a limitation of Moshe’s halachic reach to his own portion.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Reuven’s blessing “yechi ve-al yamus” — deathlessness, since death flows from desire; the teshuvah-rung of Leah transforms (not merely subdues) and completes the “seeing.” Shimon = the reception of “hearing” (reproof); Levi = “this time my husband will be joined.” The order of the soul’s perfections: first the eye, then the ear. Yehudah = the “voice of prayer” (David’s rung).

And the consummation of Torah likewise resides exclusively within the seed of Leah,
דְּלֵיכָּא צוּרְבָא מֵרַבָּנַן דְּמוֹרֵי אֶלָּא מִלֵּוִי וּמִיִּשָּׂשׂכָר .
for there is no seasoned Torah scholar who issues authoritative halakhic rulings unless he descends from Levi or from Issachar (Yoma 26a).
וְעִיקַּר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הוּא מִלֵּוִי
And the primary transmission of the Torah stems from Levi,
שֶׁמִּזַּרְעוֹ הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַתּוֹרָה לַפּוֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם
for from his lineage proceeds the manifest revelation of the Torah into actuality within the world:
מַתַּן תּוֹרָה עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
the Giving of the Torah through Moses our teacher, peace be upon him,
וְהַכֹּהֲנִים בָּהֶם נֶאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים לג, י): "יוֹרוּ מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ לְיַעֲקֹב וְגוֹמֵר"
and the priests concerning whom it is said (Deuteronomy 33:10): 'They shall teach Your judgments to Jacob, etc.'
(וְעַיֵּין בְּסֵפֶר יוּחֲסִין דְּגַם בְּדוֹרוֹת תַּנָּאִים וַאֲמוֹרָאִים
(and see in Sefer Yuchasin that even throughout the generations of the Tannaim and Amoraim
הָיוּ עִיקַּר מְיַסְּדֵי הַתּוֹרָה כֹּהֲנִים בְּכָל דּוֹרָן).
the primary founders of Torah in each era were priests).
וְזֶהוּ חָכְמָה הַמִּתְגַּלֵּית בָּעוֹלָם
And this is the wisdom that becomes revealed in the world,
שֶׁהוּא נוֹבְלוֹת חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה
which is the unripe fruit of the Supernal Wisdom;
אֲבָל הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבְּלֵב כָּל חָכָם
however, the intuitive wisdom residing in the heart of each sage,

which he cannot overtly articulate and bring forth from potential into actuality,
זֶה נִקְרָא "בִּינָה"
this is termed Binah (Understanding),
שֶׁזָּכוּ לָהּ בְּנֵי יִשָּׂשׂכָר (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א יב, לב): "יוֹדְעֵי בִינָה לַעִתִּים לָדַעַת מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה יִשְׂרָאֵל",
which the sons of Issachar merited (I Chronicles 12:32): 'men who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do',
לֹא לְלַמֵּד וּלְהוֹרוֹת מַה יַּעֲשׂוּ,
not to teach and codify what they should do,
רַק לָדַעַת בִּידִיעָה לְבַד
rather to know through inward comprehension alone;
וְעַל יְדֵי הַיְדִיעָה שֶׁלָּהֶם יָדְעוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן מַה יַּעֲשׂוּ.
and through their inward knowing, the children of Israel likewise intuitively knew what to do.
כִּי "לַעִתִּים" הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁהוּא "עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת" וְדָבָר שֶׁל שָׁעָה
For 'of the times' refers to that which is 'a time to act' and an emergency measure for the hour.
כִּי הַתּוֹרָה הוּא חוּקִים קְצוּבִים וּגְדֵרִים שָׁוִים תָּמִיד דְּלֹא יִשְׁתַּנֶּה כָּל יְמֵי עוֹלָם
for the statutory Torah consists of fixed laws and unchanging fences that never alter throughout the history of the world.
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת בַּפּוֹעַל
And this reflects reality from the perspective of manifest deed;
אֲבָל בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב דְּהוּא עָקֹב מִכֹּל הוּא מִשְׁתַּנֶּה בְּכָל רֶגַע
yet in the depths of the heart, which is 'deceitful/deep above all things' (Jeremiah 17:9), it shifts every single moment,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יֵשׁ לִפְעָמִים (תְּהִלִּים קיט, קכו): "עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה' הֵפֵרוּ תוֹרָתֶךָ".
and through this dynamic there arises at times: 'It is time to act for Hashem; they have voided Your Torah' (Psalms 119:126).
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה פָּרָשַׁת נְדָרִים
And regarding this the Torah set forth the section of vows,
וְנִקְרָא (בַּמִּדְבָּר ו, ב): "אִישׁ כִּי יַפְלִא",
and it is stated (Numbers 6:2): 'When a man shall utter a singular vow (yafli),'
וְלֹא נִיתְּנָה נְזִירוּת אֶלָּא לְהַפְלָאָה (נָזִיר לד עַמּוּד א)
and a Nazirite vow takes effect only through explicit declaration (hafla'ah),
וְיָדוּעַ דְּהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּחָכְמָה
and it is known that this corresponds to the level of Chokhmah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה כט, יד): "הִנְנִי יוֹסִף לְהַפְלִיא וְגוֹמֵר וְאָבְדָה חָכְמַת וְגוֹמֵר".
as it is stated (Isaiah 29:14): 'Behold, I will proceed to do a marvelous work (lehafli)... and the wisdom of their wise men shall perish.'
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ (שָׁם י, לג): "מְסָעֵף פֻּארָה",
And this operates in the linguistic manner of (ibid. 10:33): 'shall lop the bough' (mesa'ef, removing the branch),
וּ(בְּאִיּוֹב לא, יב): "וּבְכָל תְּבוּאָתִי תְשָׁרֵשׁ",
and (Job 31:12): 'and would root out all my increase' (tesharesh, removing the root),
דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר הֲסָרַת הַסָּעִיף וְהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
meaning the excision of the branch and the eradication of the root.
וְכֵן "לְהַפְלִיא" רָצָה לוֹמַר הֲסָרַת הַהַפְלָאָה
and so 'lehafli' denotes removing the hiddenness and revealing the wonder.
וְכָל שׁוֹרֶשׁ בִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ מוֹרֶה עַל דָּבָר וְהֶפְכּוֹ כַּנּוֹדָע
For every root in the Holy Tongue can denote both an action and its polar opposite, as is known.
וּ"פֶלֶא" הוּא לְשׁוֹן הֶעְלֵם
And pele (wonder) is an expression of deep concealment,
כִּי חָכְמָה עֶלְיוֹנָה נֶעְלֶמֶת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
for the Supernal Wisdom is hidden within this physical world.
רַק רְשִׁימוּ שֶׁלָּהּ מוּשָּׂג בַּבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב
its impression alone being perceived through Binah in the heart.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה "לֵב יוֹדֵעַ מָרַּת נַפְשׁוֹ" (מִשְׁלֵי יד, י)
And through this 'the heart knows its own bitterness' (Proverbs 14:10),
יוּכַל לְהַגְדִּיר גְּדֵרִים לְעַצְמוֹ
and a person is able to erect custom fences for himself.
כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁרָאוּי לוֹ לְאוֹתוֹ נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִי וּלְאוֹתוֹ זְמַן פְּרָטִי
according to what is necessary for that unique individual soul and for that specific hour.
וְאֵינָם עִנְיָנִים כּוֹלְלִים לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁתִּגְזוֹר עֲלֵיהֶם הַתּוֹרָה
And these are not universal dictates across all Israel upon which the Torah would decree,
רַק מְסָרָתַם לְמִי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לְהַפְלִיא
rather the Torah entrusted them to one who knows how to pierce the hidden
וּלְהַשִּׂיג הַפֶּלֶא הַנֶּעְלָם בְּהַרְגָּשַׁת הַבִּינָה לַעִתִּים
and grasp the concealed wonder through intuitive understanding calibrated to the times,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה מַה שֶּׁרָאוּי בְּאוֹתוֹ עֵת וּבְאוֹתוֹ רֶגַע
discerning thereby what is proper at that hour and in that fleeting instant.
מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ כְּפִי מִשְׁפָּט הַכּוֹלֵל שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
which may not accord with the general, codified baseline of the statutory Torah.

paragraphs.text: Divrei HaYamim I 12:33: “וּמִבְּנֵי יִשָּׂשכָר יוֹדְעֵי בִינָה לַעִתִּים לָדַעַת מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה יִשְׂרָאֵל, רָאשֵׁיהֶם מָאתַיִם וְכָל אֲחֵיהֶם עַל פִּיהֶם” — “And of the sons of Yissachar, men of understanding for the times, to know what Israel should do; their chiefs were two hundred, and all their brethren acted at their word.” R’ Tzadok’s use: Yissachar’s rung is Binah — the wisdom held within the heart that a sage cannot fully draw out into actuality. They “knew what Israel should do” not in order to teach and rule it as fixed law, “but to know by knowledge alone”; and through their knowing, all Israel too knew what to do “according to the times.”

paragraphs.text: Yeshayahu 10:33: “הִנֵּה הָאָדוֹן ה׳ צְבָאוֹת מְסָעֵף פֻּארָה בְּמַעֲרָצָה, וְרָמֵי הַקּוֹמָה גְּדוּעִים וְהַגְּבֹהִים יִשְׁפָּלוּ” — “Behold, the Master, Hashem of Hosts, lops off the bough with terrible force; the tall of stature are hewn down and the lofty laid low.” The verb mesa’ef is built on sa’if (a bough), yet here it means to strip the boughs away. paragraphs.text: Yeshayahu 29:14: “הִנְנִי יוֹסִף לְהַפְלִיא אֶת הָעָם הַזֶּה הַפְלֵא וָפֶלֶא, וְאָבְדָה חָכְמַת חֲכָמָיו וּבִינַת נְבֹנָיו תִּסְתַּתָּר” — “Behold, I will further do wondrously with this people, wondrous upon wonder — and the wisdom of its wise shall perish, and the discernment of its prudent shall hide itself.” Here the same root pele denotes not revelation but withdrawal — wisdom “perishing” and “hiding.” R’ Tzadok’s use: “pele is a term of concealment”; the supernal Chochmah is hidden in this world, and only its “impression” is grasped in the heart’s Binah — the very word that names the nazir’s “wondrous setting-apart” also bespeaks the hiddenness of that wisdom.

paragraphs.text: Mishlei 14:10: “לֵב יוֹדֵעַ מָרַת נַפְשׁוֹ, וּבְשִׂמְחָתוֹ לֹא יִתְעָרַב זָר” — “The heart knows its own bitterness, and in its joy no stranger may share.” Each heart’s inner state is known to it alone. R’ Tzadok’s use: because “the heart knows its own bitterness,” it “can set bounds for itself according to what is fitting for that particular soul and that particular time” — the personal, non-universal measure of Binah, entrusted to the one who can grasp the hidden “wonder according to the times.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §22): “And this is "of the sons of Yissachar, who know understanding for the times, to know what Israel should do" — that they have no fixed matter, but rather gaze at every time with the Binah that is in the heart, to know what the will of Hashem is at that time, what Israel should do.” Exactly the se’if: the written Torah has “rates and bounds that never change,” but Yissachar’s rung reads, out of the heart’s Binah, what this soul and this hour require. Izhbitz-Radzin parallel - Sha'ar HaEmunah VeYesod HaChasidut, Entrance to the Gate of Beit Yaakov 24:3-4: This source is almost a direct commentary on R. Tzadok's Yissachar-Binah structure. Sha'ar HaEmunah cites "u-miBnei Yissachar yodei binah la'itim" and explains that the possessors of Binah know how to "heal the earlier" - to heal time itself. Complete teshuvah returns a person to Binah, a level above the ordinary sequence of time, where past, present, and future are not experienced as mutually sealed compartments. From there, what preceded can be repaired. This complements R. Tzadok's distinction between revealed Chochmah and the wisdom hidden in the heart. Yissachar does not merely know more information; his Binah is a faculty for penetrating the inward meaning of the time and discovering what the present moment asks of Israel. That is why his Torah belongs naturally to Leah, the mother of teshuvah. The heart that understands the time can also reinterpret the past and direct the future.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The perfection of Torah, too, is in Leah’s seed (Levi and Yissachar). Chochmah is the wisdom revealed into the world (“ripened fruit of the supernal Wisdom”); Binah is the wisdom hidden in the heart — Yissachar’s “understanding of the times.” The written Torah is fixed and unchanging, but in the depths of the heart there is sometimes “a time to act for Hashem” — the domain of hafla’ah (the nazir), grasped through the Binah of the heart.

p: (טז), — וְדָבָר זֶה נִקְרָא "דַּעַת" שֶׁהוּא הַמְחַבֵּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה
And this capacity is titled Da'at (Knowledge), which unites Chokhmah and Binah,
וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י בְּפָרָשַׁת כִּי תִשָּׂא (שְׁמוֹת לא, ג) דְּדַעַת הוּא רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
and Rashi explains in Parashat Ki Tisa (Exodus 31:3) that Da'at is the Holy Spirit (Ruach HaKodesh),
וְהַיְינוּ דְּדָבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג כְּלָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מֵעַצְמוֹ,
meaning that this perception cannot be attained independently in this world from mortal intellect alone.
רַק עַל יְדֵי הַמְשָׁכַת רוּחַ מִקּוֹדֶשׁ הָעֶלְיוֹן בְּרָזָא דְּחָכְמְתָא
rather solely through drawing down a spirit from the Supernal Sanctuary within the mystery of Wisdom.
וּכְנוֹדָע בָּרַמְבַּ"ן בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (יב עַמּוּד א)
And as is known in the Ramban in Bava Batra (12a)
דְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ הוּא הַשָּׂגַת חָכְמָה הַבָּאָה בְּלֵב הָאָדָם מַה שֶּׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת שִׂכְלוֹ.
that Ruach HaKodesh is the flash of wisdom entering man's heart transcending the analytical grasp of his intellect.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה הִיא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת שֵׂכֶל הָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And this is because the Supernal Wisdom towers far above the reach of human intellect in this world,
וְהַשָּׂגָה זוֹ אֵינוֹ בָּא לָאָדָם מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ כְּלָל
and this perception does not reach man through rational brain intellect at all,
רַק מִצַּד הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב
rather from the perspective of Binah in the heart.
וְהַיְינוּ הַהַרְגָּשָׁה, דְּבַלֵּב הוּא כֹּחַ הַהַרְגָּשָׁה
which is intuitive feeling, for in the heart resides the faculty of feeling.
וְכָל חָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁל דּוֹאֵג מִשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ ,
And all the wisdom of Doeg was 'from the lip outward' (Sanhedrin 106b),
הַיְינוּ דְּלֹא נִכְנַס לַלֵּב וְלֹא פָּעַל הֶרְגֵּשׁ בּוֹ,
meaning it never penetrated his heart and produced no inner feeling within him.
דְּאָז הַמָּאוֹר מַחֲזִירוֹ לַמּוּטָב
for had it penetrated, the light within the Torah would have restored him to the good.
כִּי חָכְמָה הַנִּגְלֵית אֶפְשָׁר לְכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל לְהַשִּׂיג מִצַּד הַנִּגְלֶה
For revealed external wisdom can be comprehended by any Jew on a manifest level;
אֲבָל עַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק בַּמֶּה מַדְלִיקִין (שַׁבָּת לא עַמּוּד ב): מוּטָב שֶׁלֹּא הֶעֱלֵיתָ,
yet concerning this they stated in Shabbat (31b): 'Better had you not brought it up!',
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (עב עַמּוּד ב) דְּלַמַּשְׂמְאִילִים וְכוּלֵי
and as they said in Yoma (72b) that for those who treat it with the left hand it becomes a potion of death, etc.
וְאֵין זֶה חָכְמָה בֶּאֱמֶת
and this is not authentic wisdom at all,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (מִשְׁלֵי יז, טז): "לָמָּה זֶּה מְחִיר בְּיַד כְּסִיל לִקְנוֹת חָכְמָה וְלֶב אָיִן".
and as it is stated (Proverbs 17:16): 'Why is there a purchase price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?',
דְּהָעִיקָּר הוּא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ לֵב כְּלִי קִבּוּל לַחָכְמָה שֶׁהוּא הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב
For the foundational requirement is that he possess a heart serving as a receptive vessel for wisdom, which is reverence in the heart,
דְּאָז הוּא סַמָּא דְּחַיֵּי לַמַּיְמִינִים לִהְיוֹתָהּ חַיֵּי עוֹלָם
for then it is an elixir of life for those who hold it with the right hand, conferring eternal life;
אֲבָל הַחָכְמָה שֶׁל הַמַּשְׂמְאִילִים אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מְחִיר לִקְנוֹת חָכְמָה, וְלֹא חָכְמָה בֶּאֱמֶת
whereas the wisdom of those who treat it with the left is merely a purchase price to acquire wisdom, but not real wisdom,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ קַיָּים לָעַד בּוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּדוֹאֵג דְּמַלְאָךְ הִשְׁכִּיחוֹ .
since it does not endure within him forever, as they said of Doeg that an angel caused him to forget it (Sanhedrin 106b).
אֲבָל לַמַּיְמִינִים אָמְרוּ בְּהֵיפֶךְ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (וְהוּבָא בְּתַשְׁבֵּ"ץ קָטָן)
However, for those who hold it with the right, our Sages stated conversely in the Midrash (cited in Tashbetz Katan).
דְּמַלְאָךְ מַזְכִּירוֹ הַכֹּל
that an angel reminds him of everything.
וּפֵירוּשׁ "מַלְאָךְ" הוּא הַנּוֹצָר מִן הַלִּימּוּד
And the meaning of 'angel' is the spiritual entity created from the study itself,
דְּמִכָּל מִצְוָה נוֹצָר מַלְאָךְ,
for from every mitzvah an angel is created (Avot 4:11),
רָצָה לוֹמַר כֹּחַ רוּחָנִי הַמִּתְקַיֵּים בְּדָבָר זֶה שֶׁהוּא עוֹסֵק בְּתוֹרַת ה
', meaning a transcendent spiritual power generated through this matter wherein he occupies himself with the Torah of Hashem.
דְּמִדִּבּוּרֵי תּוֹרָה הוּא עִיקַּר קִיּוּם הַמַּלְאָכִים
for from utterances of Torah derives the essential sustenance of angels.
וְאוֹתוֹ מַלְאָךְ עַצְמוֹ הוּא שֶׁהִשְׁכִּיחוֹ,
And that very angel was the one who caused Doeg to forget,
כְּטַעַם סַמָּא דְּמוֹתָא שֶׁהִיא עַצְמָהּ נַעֲשֵׂית מִשּׁוּם דְּ"פוֹשְׁעִים יִכָּשְׁלוּ בָם" (הוֹשֵׁעַ יד, י);
mirroring the lethal potion which itself forms because 'transgressors shall stumble therein' (Hosea 14:10);
וְאִלְמָלֵא תּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל דּוֹאֵג
and were it not for Doeg's vast Torah learning,
לֹא הָיָה בָּא לְכָל מַה שֶּׁבָּא נֶגֶד דָּוִד וְנוֹב
he would never have arrived at all that he perpetrated against David and the city of Nob.
דְּהַכֹּל גָּרַם לוֹ מַה שֶּׁהָיָה אַבִּיר הָרוֹעִים וְרֹאשׁ סַנְהֶדְרִין
since everything was facilitated by his being the chief of the herdsmen and head of the Sanhedrin.
וְעַל כֵּן זֶה עַצְמוֹ הִשְׁכִּיחוֹ,
Therefore, that very entity caused him to forget;
אַף שֶׁהָיָה מַלְאָךְ טוֹב הַנּוֹצָר מִמִּצְוָה
for even though it was originally a holy angel formed from a mitzvah,
דְּ"אֵין עֲבֵירָה מְכַבָּה תוֹרָה" ,
since 'a sin cannot extinguish Torah' (Sotah 21a),
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהָיָה מַשְׂמְאִיל בָּהּ,
nonetheless, because he treated it with the left hand,
הַטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ גָּרַם לְהַשְׁכִּיחוֹ.
the very spiritual potency within it caused him to forget it.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּמַּיְמִין
In contrast, for one who holds it with the right,
עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הָרוּחָנִי שֶׁבְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה הוּא נִזְכָּר הַכֹּל
through the spiritual force embedded within words of Torah he remembers everything
אַחַר שֶׁנִּפְשַׁט מֵהַגַּשְׁמִי וְחֹמֶר הַמַּשְׁכִּיחַ.
after shedding the physical corporeality and materiality that induces forgetfulness.
וְהַשִּׁכְחָה הוּא רַק בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִבְלָע בַּלֵּב
And forgetfulness occurs only regarding that which was never absorbed into the heart,
דְּמַה שֶּׁעוֹשֶׂה רוֹשֶׁם בַּלֵּב אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁכָּח
for that which engraves an impression upon the heart can never be forgotten;
אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הַכֹּל נִבְלָע מִיָּד בַּלֵּב לִהְיוֹת מוּרְגָּשׁ בְּכָל אֵיבָרִים
only that not everything is absorbed immediately into the heart to be felt throughout all the limbs.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ לֵב מֵבִין אֲפִילּוּ רַק בְּדָבָר אֶחָד
Yet nonetheless, as long as a person possesses an understanding heart even in a single concept,
שֶׁנִּפְתְּחוּ שַׁעֲרֵי הַלֵּב כְּחֻדָּהּ שֶׁל מַחַט
wherein the gates of the heart are opened like the eye of a needle,
הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא פּוֹתֵחַ כְּפִתְחוֹ שֶׁל אוּלָם ,
the Holy One, blessed be He, opens for him an entrance like the portal of the Hall (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2),
דְּרוּחַ אַמְשֵׁיךְ רוּחַ,
for spirit draws down spirit,
וְעִיקַּר מִשְׁכַּן הָרוּחַ הוּא בַּלֵּב
and the primary dwelling place of the spirit is in the heart,
וּבוֹ הוּא כֹּחַ הַהַמְשָׁכָה לְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא
and within it lies the drawing power for supernal awakening from Above,
כְּטַעַם (תְּהִלִּים עג, כו ): "צוּר לְבָבִי",
mirroring (Psalms 73:26): 'the rock of my heart'.
דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
for the Holy One is the heart of Israel.
וְהַפֶּתַח כְּחֻדָּהּ שֶׁל מַחַט הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב
And that opening like the eye of a needle is achieved through reverence in the heart,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּיַד הָאָדָם וּמַה שֶּׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׁוֹאֵל מֵעִמּוֹ;
which is within human capacity and what the Holy One asks of him;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַה שֶּׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא פּוֹתֵחַ
and afterward, that which the Holy One opens,

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah §5): “this alluded to the light of the holy Torah that was then bestowed — precisely that which the Greeks sought, "to make them forget Your Torah."” The se’if’s forgetting is here given its historical form: an enemy can reach only Torah that has not been absorbed inward, for what the heart has taken in cannot be made to be forgotten. Sefat Emet parallel - Eikev 24:3: Sefat Emet's treatment of moach, lev, and yirah closely parallels R. Tzadok's description of da'as as wisdom that truly enters the heart. He writes that the essential recognition of the Creator is in the moach and lev, and that yirah is the outer key that opens both; once the covering of the heart is removed, the Divine attachment already planted in the Jewish soul becomes revealed. He therefore calls yirah "re'iyah" - the capacity to see the truth. This helps distinguish the Torah that remains "from the lips outward" from Torah that becomes da'as. Information can be present in the intellect and even on the tongue without reorganizing the inner person. Yirah gives the knowledge existential weight: it opens the heart to receive what the mind knows, so that the Torah becomes part of the person's own inward reality. R. Tzadok's critique of Doeg is therefore not anti-intellectual. It is a demand that chochmah pass through the gate of yirah and enter the lev, where Chochmah and Binah are joined as da'as.

paragraphs.text: Yirmeyah 31:34: “וְלֹא יְלַמְּדוּ עוֹד אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ וְאִישׁ אֶת אָחִיו לֵאמֹר דְּעוּ אֶת ה׳, כִּי כוּלָּם יֵדְעוּ אוֹתִי לְמִקְּטַנָּם וְעַד גְּדוֹלָם” — “and no longer shall a man teach his fellow or his brother, saying, Know Hashem — for they shall all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.” The preceding verse (Yirmeyah 31:33) promises “וְעַל לִבָּם אֶכְתְּבֶנָּה” (“I will write it on their hearts”), and verse 34 describes universal knowledge of Hashem. R’ Tzadok interprets future reward as the complete, limitless absorption of the words of Torah into the heart — that which is fully absorbed needs no “angel to remind” it, for one never forgets what one has wholly become.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Da’as joins Chochmah and Binah — ruach ha-kodesh, wisdom that enters the heart beyond the intellect. Torah “from the lips outward” (Doeg) does not endure — even the “good angel” it created made him forget; but Torah absorbed in the heart cannot be forgotten. The needle-point opening is yirah (man’s task); Hashem then opens it “like the Ulam-hall” and pours in longing without limit — the reward of the Future.

p: (יז) — וְהַיִּרְאָה הוּא (תְּהִלִּים קיח, כ): "הַשַּׁעַר לַה' צַדִּיקִים יָבֹאוּ בוֹ",
And awe is (Psalms 118:20): 'the gate of Hashem, into which the righteous shall enter',
דַּרְגָּא דְּיוֹסֵף דִּ"ירֵא אֱלֹהִים" (בְּרֵאשִׁית מב, יח),
the spiritual degree of Joseph who was 'a God-fearing man' (Genesis 42:18),
וְהִיא תַּרְעָא לְדַרְתָּא לְבַד
and it serves as the outer gate to the courtyard alone;
אֲבָל הַדַּרְתָּא הוּא בְּזַרְעָא דְּלֵאָה עַל יְדֵי תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק
whereas the inner courtyard is entered within the seed of Leah through the intensity of passionate yearning.
וּלְפִי שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁקַט מִמֶּנָּה הַחֵשֶׁק לְהַעֲמִיד שְׁבָטִים
And because the desire to establish holy tribes was never extinguished within her,
שֶׁעִנְיַן חֵשֶׁק זֶה הוּא מַמָּשׁ מַה שֶּׁאָמַר הַכָּתוּב (תְּהִלִּים מב, ג): "צָמְאָה נַפְשִׁי לֵאלֹהִים לְאֵל חָי",
this yearning being literally what Scripture proclaims (Psalms 42:3): 'My soul thirsts for God, for the living God',
כִּי צוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם חֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
for the form of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, is engraved upon the Throne of Glory.
וּשְׁבָטִים הֵם כְּלַל הַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים
and the tribes embody the collective dwelling of His Shechinah among the lower creations.
וְגַם אַחַר שֶׁבֵּירְרָה כָּל שְׁלֵימוּת מַדְרֵיגוֹתֶיהָ וְעָמְדָה מִלֶּדֶת בַּפּוֹעַל
And even after she had clarified the full perfection of her rungs and ceased from actual bearing,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁבַּלֵּב לֹא נִשְׁקַע עֲדַיִן
nonetheless the burning yearning in her heart had not subsided,
כִּי זֶה תַּכְלִית תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שְׂבִיעָה כְּלָל
for such is the utmost intensity of divine love which knows no satiation at all.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל פָּסוּק (קֹהֶלֶת ה, ט): "אֹהֵב כֶּסֶף" – אוֹהֵב מִצְווֹת לֹא יִשְׂבַּע
as they expounded on the verse (Ecclesiastes 5:9): 'He who loves silver'—he who loves mitzvot is never satisfied.
וּשְׂכָרַתּוּ בְּדוּדָאֵי בְּנָהּ רְאוּבֵן
And she hired him with the mandrakes of her son Reuben,
הַיְינוּ מִמַּדְרֵגָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁבַּהַתְחָלָה
which is drawn from that first spiritual level of the beginning,
דְּאַחַר הַשְּׁלֵימוּת חוֹזֵר לַהַתְחָלָה
for after completion one returns to the beginning.
כְּמוֹ אָדָם שֶׁסִּיֵּים לִימּוּדוֹ כָּל הַשַּׁ"ס וְחוֹזֵר לַהַתְחָלָה לִלְמוֹד פַּעַם שְׁנִיָּה בְּעִיּוּן עָמֹק יוֹתֵר
like a man who has finished learning the entire Talmud and returns to the beginning to study a second time with deeper analysis.
וְדָבָר זֶה דַּחֲזָרָה אַחַר שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם
And this recurrence after having achieved completion,
הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַטְעִים לָאָדָם שֶׁטּוֹב מִפְּרִי מַעֲשָׂיו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
is how Hashem gives man a foretaste of the good fruit of his actions in this world.
וְהוּא קִבּוּל שָׂכָר
which is the reception of reward.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמְרָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל, יח): "נָתַן (אֱלֹהִים) שְׂכָרִי אֲשֶׁר נָתַתִּי שִׁפְחָתִי (לְאִישִׁי)",
And this is why she said (Genesis 30:18): 'God has given me my hire (sekhari), because I gave my maidservant to my husband',
זֶהוּ הַתְחָלַת הַצִּמָּאוֹן שֶׁלָּהּ אַחַר הַהַשְׁלָמָה
which marked the dawn of her renewed thirst following the initial completion
לְהַרְבּוֹת שְׁבָטִים עַל כָּל פָּנִים מִשִּׁפְחָתָהּ וְיִהְיוּ נִקְרָאִים עַל שְׁמָהּ.
to multiply tribes at least through her handmaid, so that they be named after her.
וְדוּדָאִים אָמְרוּ דִּמְסֻגָּלִים לְהֵרָיוֹן
And concerning mandrakes our Sages taught that they are auspicious for conception,
הַיְינוּ דִּמְעוֹרְרִים חֵשֶׁק – לְשׁוֹן "דּוֹדִים",
meaning that they awaken desire—from the linguistic root dodim (love).
כִּי פְּעָמִים מְנִיעַת הַהֵרָיוֹן מִצַּד מִיעוּט הַחֵשֶׁק וְהַתַּאֲוָה
for sometimes the prevention of conception is caused by a diminishment of passionate desire.
וּרְאוּבֵן, שֶׁהוּא בֵּירוּר נִקְיוֹן הָרְאִיָּה דְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב
And Reuben, who embodies the clarification of the purity of sight belonging to the seed of Jacob,
בַּמַּה שֶּׁעַיִן רוֹאָה וְלֵב חוֹמֵד הוּא הַכֹּל לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
wherein whatever the eye sees and the heart covets is entirely directed toward the sake of Heaven,
מָצָא הַדּוּדָאִים בַּשָּׂדֶה מְקוֹם הֶפְקֵר שֶׁלֹּא בְּאִיסּוּר
found the mandrakes in the open field—an ownerless area, free of any hint of prohibition (Sanhedrin 99b).
כִּי כָּל חֵשֶׁק לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם צָרִיךְ שְׁמִירָה שֶׁלֹּא יַחְשׁוֹק בַּמַּה שֶּׁאֵין שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹ,
For all desire for the sake of Heaven requires meticulous vigilance lest one lust after what does not belong to him.
דְּעַל זֶה אַזְהָרַת "לֹא תַחְמֹד" שֶׁהִיא אַחֲרוֹנָה בַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת
and upon this stands the prohibition of 'You shall not covet,' the final of the Ten Commandments.
וְנָעוּץ סוֹפָן בִּתְחִלָּתָן
And their end is wedged into their beginning,
דְּמִי שֶׁמַּכִּיר דְּ"אָנֹכִי ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ"
for whoever truly recognizes 'I am Hashem your God'
אֵינוֹ חוֹמֵד וּמִתְאַוֶּוה בַּמַּה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ,
does not covet or lust after that which is not his,
כִּי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁמִּשֶּׁלְּךָ יִתְּנוּ לְךָ (יוֹמָא לח עַמּוּד ב)
knowing that from what is designated as your own they will give you (Yoma 38b),
וְאֵין אָדָם נוֹגֵעַ בַּמּוּכָן לַחֲבֵירוֹ ,
and no person touches that which is prepared for his fellow (Yoma 38b),
מֵאַחַר דַּה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ מַנְהִיגְךָ.
inasmuch as Hashem your God is your personal Guide.
וְהָא בְּהָא תַּלְיָא
And the two are interdependent,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ דְּהַחוֹמֵד סוֹף לַעֲבוֹר עַל כָּל עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת (מְכִילְתָּא יִתְרוֹ),
for our Sages stated that he who covets will ultimately violate all Ten Commandments (Mekhilta, Yitro),
כִּי עִיקַּר חֲטָאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא בַּתַּאֲווֹת
because the primary stumble of Israel's sins occurs in physical desires,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין סג עַמּוּד ב.): — לֹא עָבְדוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֶלָּא לְהַתִּיר עֲרָיוֹת
as they said (Sanhedrin 63b): they served idols solely to permit illicit relations.
וַחֲמָדָה הָאֲסוּרָה הוּא כְּשֶׁחוֹמֵד מַה שֶּׁאֵין רָאוּי לוֹ;
And forbidden coveting occurs when one lusts after that which is not fit for him;
וְאַף מַה שֶּׁרָאוּי לוֹ, אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין רָאוּי עַכְשָׁו רַק לְאַחַר זְמַן
and even after that which is destined for him, but which is not yet fitting now, only after time,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קז עַמּוּד א) שֶׁאָכְלָהּ פַּגָּה
as our Sages stated in Sanhedrin (107a) regarding King David that he ate the fruit while still unripe,
הוּא דּוּגְמַת נִדָּה דְּגַם כֵּן עַכְשָׁו אֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לוֹ,
which resembles the state of a menstruant woman who is likewise temporarily forbidden to him now.
וְדוּגְמַת חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁלֹּא יָכוֹל לְהַמְתִּין
and resembles the sin of Adam the First concerning which our Sages stated that he could not wait until the Sabbath.
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן רְאוּבֵן "פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם",
And this is the inner significance of Reuben's rebuke 'unstable as water' (Genesis 49:4),
שֶׁהוּא רֵאשִׁית הַחֶמְדָּה וּבֵירוּרָהּ בְּתִיקּוּן חֵטְא דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
representing the very inception of desire and its clarification within the rectification of the sin of Adam the First
עַד שֶׁיְּתוּקַּן וִיבוּלַּע הַמָּוֶת וְ"אַל יָמֹת";
until it is perfected and death is swallowed up and 'he shall not die';
וְזֶהוּ "דּוּדָאִים בַּשָּׂדֶה",
and this is 'mandrakes in the field',
דְּאַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוּא הֶפְקֵר יוּכַל לַחְמוֹד לוֹ.
for even though it was not his own, nonetheless since it was ownerless he could rightfully desire it.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 42:18: Yosef to his brothers — “זֹאת עֲשׂוּ וִחְיוּ, אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים אֲנִי יָרֵא” — “do this and live: I fear God.” R’ Tzadok’s use: Yosef, of whom “I fear God” is said, is the rung of yirah — the “gate” through which the righteous enter, the safeguard that precedes the inner service of longing.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 42:3: “צָמְאָה נַפְשִׁי לֵאלֹהִים לְאֵל חָי, מָתַי אָבוֹא וְאֵרָאֶה פְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים” — “my soul thirsts for God, for the living God; when shall I come and appear before God?” R’ Tzadok’s use: this “thirst” is the very cheishek that never subsided in Leah — the longing to raise up tribes; it is the ultimate intensity of longing “which has no satiety at all,” ever renewing from the first rung, like one who finishes the whole Shas and returns to its beginning.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 68:12 (and Chullin 91b): “you are the one whose icon is engraved on high” (at hu she-ikonin shelcha chakukah le-maalah) — the “form of Yaakov” is engraved beneath the Throne of Glory, and the angels “ascend and gaze upon his image above.” R’ Tzadok’s use: because Yaakov’s form is engraved on the Throne, the tribes are “the sum of the resting of the Shechinah among the lower worlds”; so Leah’s unquenchable longing to bear tribes is a longing to extend that indwelling into this world.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §248): “The essence of man is the longing cheishek in the heart, in which lies his superiority over the angels; and it is what is called ‘yetzer’ — both the good inclination and the evil inclination. When he strengthens his longing toward the good, this is good; and if not, toward evil. And the Sages said (Sukkah 52a), ‘the greater a person, the greater his inclination’ — for the greatness of one over another is only according to the greatness of his longing for the good, that is, the power of the inclination; for the good and evil inclinations are ‘this-opposite-that’ in the two chambers of the heart, according to the longing in his heart.”

paragraphs.text: Shem MiShmuel parallel - Vaetchanan 4:15, citing Rambam, Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 2:2: Shem MiShmuel brings the Rambam's classic description of the path to love and fear: contemplation of Hashem's wondrous works first produces love, praise, and an intense desire to know Him - the state expressed by David's "tzamah nafshi l'Elokim l'El chai" - and the very same contemplation then causes the person to recoil in awe, recognizing his smallness before the Perfect Knower. This complements R. Tzadok's presentation of yirah as a gate into Leah's inward world of unending longing. The two movements are not contradictory. True longing grows precisely because the object of longing cannot be possessed or exhausted, while true yirah prevents longing from collapsing into self-satisfaction. One approaches and discovers distance; the distance itself increases thirst; the renewed thirst drives a deeper approach. That circular movement explains R. Tzadok's language that after a person reaches completion he returns again to the beginning. The "gate" is not a threshold crossed once but a permanent protection of the infinitude of the relationship.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Yirah is the gate; the inner courtyard is Leah’s — through the intensity of cheishek (longing), which never satiates (“my soul thirsts for the living God”). After completion one returns to the beginning (like re-learning Shas more deeply) — this is receiving reward. The dudaim arouse longing. “Lo sachmod” (last commandment) is rooted in “Anochi” (first): one who knows all is from Hashem does not covet what is not his.

p: (יח) — וְרָחֵל קִנְּאָה בַּאֲחוֹתָהּ,
And Rachel envied her sister,
וְיָדוּעַ קִנְאָה הוּא הֵיפֶךְ תַּאֲוָה וְחֶמְדָּה
and it is known that envy is the polar opposite of lust and desire,
וְהִיא קִנְּאָה בְּחֶמְדָּה זוֹ וּבִקְּשָׁה לָקַחַת דּוּדָאֵי בְּנָהּ.
and she envied this sacred desire and sought to take the mandrakes of her son.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת זֶה לֹא הָיָה שַׁיָּיךְ לָהּ,
Yet in truth this did not belong to her spiritual realm,
וְזֶהוּ חֶמְדָּה בַּמַּה שֶּׁאֵין שַׁיָּיךְ לָהּ.
and that constitutes coveting that which does not belong to her.
וּלְפִי שֶׁהִיא בִּקְּשָׁה חֶמְדָּה וְאֵין זֶה מִדָּתָהּ,
And because she reached for desire while this was not her native attribute,
וְלֹא יָדְעָה דְּאֶצְלָהּ הַחֶמְדָּה הוּא שֶׁאֵין שַׁיָּיךְ לָהּ וְאָסוּר
and did not realize that for her, this desire was inapplicable and illicit,
גָּרַם לָהּ לְזַלְזֵל עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּמִשְׁכָּבוֹ שֶׁל צַדִּיק
this caused her through this to treat lightly the conjugal bed of the righteous one.
שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ הַחֶמְדָּה לְגַמְרֵי
which was the complete antithesis of holy longing.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא (סוֹטָה ט עַמּוּד א) דְּגַם מַה שֶּׁהָיָה לוֹ נִיטַּל
And this follows what is taught in Sotah (9a) that even what one already possessed is taken from him;
אֶלָּא דְּשָׁם הוּא עֹנֶשׁ בְּעַל כָּרְחוֹ,
except that there it is a punitive stripping against his will,
אֲבָל כָּאן דְּהִיא כִּיוְּונָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
whereas here, where she intended purely for the sake of Heaven,
וְחָלִילָה לֹא חָמְדָה מַה שֶּׁאֵין רָאוּי לָהּ בֶּאֱמֶת
and Heaven forbid that she actually coveted what was truly unbefitting for her,
דַּהֲרֵי הִיא נְתָנָתַם לָהּ,
for Leah consented to give them to her,
רַק דְּלֹא הָיָה רָאוּי לָהּ בְּחִנָּם אֶלָּא בִּשְׂכַר
save that it was not fitting for her to acquire them for free but only through hire,
הִיא בְּעַצְמָהּ נָתְנָה שֶׁלָּהּ מִדַּעְתָּהּ.
she voluntarily yielded of her own with full awareness.
וְזֶהוּ תִּיקּוּן קִנְאָתָהּ,
And this was the rectification of her envy;
דְּיָדוּעַ מִדַּת הַקַּנַּאי יַסְכִּים לְסַלֵּק טוֹבָה מֵאֲחֵרִים
for it is known that the base envious person would rather remove good from others;
אַף שֶׁגַּם לוֹ לֹא יִהְיֶה וְיִגָּרַע עוֹד יוֹתֵר
even though he himself will gain nothing and lose even more;
אֲבָל הִיא הָיָה לָהּ טוֹבַת עַיִן לָתֵת לְלֵאָה שֶׁתֵּלֵד יוֹתֵר
yet she possessed a generous eye to afford Leah the opportunity to bear further,
רַק שֶׁגַּם הִיא יִהְיֶה לָהּ עַל כָּל פָּנִים
provided that she too would eventually bear,
וּבִשְׂכַר זֶה קָנְתָה הַדּוּדָאִים
and as a reward for this she acquired the mandrakes.
הַיְינוּ הַחֶמְדָּה עַל יְדֵי סִילּוּק הַקִּנְאָה מִלֵּאָה
namely holy desire achieved through removing envy from Leah.
וּבָזֶה זָכְתָה לֵאָה לְיִשָּׂשׂכָר
And through this Leah merited Issachar,
שֶׁהוּא קִבּוּל הַשָּׂכָר
who represents the receiving of reward (sekhar),
אַחַר שֶׁסִּילְּקָה רָחֵל קִנְאָתָהּ מִמֶּנָּה
once Rachel had removed her envy from her,
דִּבְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּתְנוּ חֲכָמִים עֵינֵיהֶם וְכוּלֵי (בָּבָא קַמָּא קיז עַמּוּד א),
for wherever the sages cast their eyes, death or poverty follows, etc.
שֶׁזֶּה מוֹנֵעַ הַטּוֹב
for such an eye obstructs the flow of good,
וּ"בִּרְצוֹת ה' דַּרְכֵי אִישׁ גַּם אוֹיְבָיו יַשְׁלִם אִתּוֹ" (מִשְׁלֵי טז, ז)
and 'When a man's ways please Hashem, He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him' (Proverbs 16:7)
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר רַבִּי עַל רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּמוֹעֵד קָטָן (טז עַמּוּד ב).
as Rebbe said concerning Rabbi Chiyya in Moed Katan (16b).
וְנִתְבָּרֵר אָז טָהֳרַת לְבָבָהּ
And at that moment the purity of her heart was clarified
בַּמַּה שֶּׁאָמְרָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל, טז): "אֵלַי תָּבוֹא",
in that she said (Genesis 30:16): 'You must come in unto me,'
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר יַעֲקֹב (שָׁם כט, כא): "הָבָה אֶת אִשְׁתִּי",
just as Jacob had said (ibid. 29:21): 'Give me my wife,'
לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה כַּוָּונָתוֹ אֶלָּא לְהַעֲמִיד תּוֹלָדוֹת לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בּוּשָׁה
– since his intention was solely to raise up holy generations, shame was irrelevant—,
אַף הִיא כֵּן
she likewise was animated by this pure intent,
וּתְבָעַתּוּ בְּפֶה שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּבְּרוּת הַחֵשֶׁק לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם גָּמוּר
and solicited him openly, which marks the ascendance of desire purely for the sake of Heaven (Eruvin 100b).
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכְתָה לְבָנִים דַּאֲפִילּוּ בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה לָא אִשְׁתֲּכַח כְּוָותַיְיהוּ
And through this she merited sons such that even in the generation of Moses none were found like them,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה עב, ה).
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded in Bereishit Rabbah (Parashah 72:5).
דְּחָכְמָתָם הוּא מֵחָכְמָה עֶלְיוֹנָה הַנּוֹטֶפֶת לַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁבּוֹ הַיְדִיעָה
For their wisdom stems from the Supernal Wisdom that distills into Binah in the heart wherein knowledge resides,
רָצָה לוֹמַר הַהַרְגָּשָׁה כְּטַעַם (שְׁמוֹת ב, כה): "וַיֵּדַע אֱלֹהִים".
meaning felt intuitive perception, mirroring (Exodus 2:25): 'and God knew.'

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 30:1: “וַתֵּרֶא רָחֵל כִּי לֹא יָלְדָה לְיַעֲקֹב, וַתְּקַנֵּא רָחֵל בַּאֲחֹתָהּ, וַתֹּאמֶר אֶל יַעֲקֹב הָבָה לִּי בָנִים וְאִם אַיִן מֵתָה אָנֹכִי” — “and Rachel saw that she had borne Yaakov no children, and Rachel envied her sister, and said to Yaakov, ‘Give me children — and if not, I am as dead.’” R’ Tzadok’s use: envy is the very opposite of coveting, yet Rachel “envied” this coveting — desiring the dudaim, which in truth did not belong to her; this is “coveting what is not one’s own,” and it is precisely her rectification of it (ceding the tzaddik’s couch, a “good eye”) that is the subject of this se’if.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §31): “envy is toward those who are not his beloved, yet in any case toward those of his acquaintance and the people of his land — for one is envious only of one who resembles him, and not of a stranger.” This sharpens the se’if’s difficulty and its answer: Rachel could envy only Leah, her very sister and like — which is why the rectification had to come by giving her what was hers.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §190): “In this, Yaakov Avinu’s bed was ‘complete’ and all his seed was truth. And in the language of the Sages, a ‘fine eye’ or a ‘good eye’ ayin tovah means generosity of heart and not being jealous — and so in the language of Scripture, ‘the good of eye shall be blessed, for he has given of his bread to the poor’ (Mishlei 22:9); and its opposite is the ‘evil eye.’” (This defines the very rectification of the se’if: Rachel’s ceding of the couch converts jealousy into the ayin tovah — the open-handed eye that begrudges nothing to another.)

paragraphs.text: Izhbitz–Radzin textual parallel (Mei HaShiloach, Chelek I, Nitzavim §6) on Devarim 30:6, ‘וּמָל ה׳ אֱלֹקֶיךָ אֶת לְבָבְךָ’: “הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁהָיָה אֶצְלְךָ לִדְבָרִים אֲשֶׁר אֵינָם טוֹבִים בְּעֵינֵי הַשֵּׁם, יִתֵּן הַשֵּׁם אֶת הַחֵשֶׁק הַזֶּה וִיתַקֵּן אוֹתוֹ בְּעֵת אֲשֶׁר תָּשׁוּב בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה, וְאָהַבְתָּ אֶת הַשֵּׁם וְתַחְשֹׁק לְדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה” — “The very longing once directed toward things displeasing to Hashem will be taken and rectified by Hashem through complete repentance, so that one will love Hashem and yearn for Torah.” The passage continues that the person redirects that longing “לַעֲשׂוֹת בּוֹ כָּל מִצְווֹתָיו וְחֻקּוֹתָיו” — “to fulfill all His commandments and statutes.” This is a documented parallel to Rachel’s transformation of misplaced envy into a generous, holy longing; it does not retroactively approve wrongful desire.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach §4): “the yetzer hara was created for the good, only that man ruins it and makes it evil. For the root of the yetzer hara is envy, desire and honor — and all of them are needed in holiness as well: envy we find, "the envy of scribes increases wisdom"…” Exactly the se’if: Rachel’s rectification shows how the force of envy can be turned to holy use — jealousy turned into the intensification of longing, wholly for Heaven.

paragraphs.text: Nedarim 7b: “וְתַנְיָא: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּתְנוּ חֲכָמִים עֵינֵיהֶם — אוֹ מִיתָה אוֹ עוֹנִי” — “and it is taught: wherever the Sages set their eyes in reproach, there follows either death or poverty.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the “eye” of the Sages, cast in disfavor, withholds good and brings harm — the “evil eye”; over against it stands Rachel’s “good eye,” which let Leah bear more, and it is by removing that envy that Leah merited Yissachar, “the receiving of reward.”

paragraphs.text: Mishlei 16:7: “בִּרְצוֹת ה׳ דַּרְכֵי אִישׁ, גַּם אוֹיְבָיו יַשְׁלִם אִתּוֹ” — “when Hashem favors a man’s ways, even his enemies make peace with him.” R’ Tzadok’s use (with what Rebbi said of R’ Chiya, Moed Katan 16b): once Rachel’s envy was removed and a “good eye” prevailed, the way was open for blessing — “even his enemies make peace with him” — and Leah could bear Yissachar, free of the “evil eye” that withholds the good.

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 100b: R’ Shmuel bar Nachmani in R’ Yochanan’s name teaches that a woman who initiates closeness with her husband for a mitzvah merits unusually discerning children. He cites Leah’s “אֵלַי תָּבוֹא” (Bereishis 30:16) and the sons of Yissachar who “יֹדְעֵי בִינָה לָעִתִּים” (I Divrei HaYamim 12:33). The same sugya says “הָאִשָּׁה תּוֹבַעַת בַּלֵּב וְהָאִישׁ תּוֹבֵעַ בַּפֶּה” and resolves the apparent tension with “דִּמְרַצְיָא אַרְצוּיֵי קַמֵּיהּ”: a tactful invitation rather than an unqualified overt verbal demand. Rav Tzadok interprets Leah’s words as the expression of pure, holy longing and relates it to the unique wisdom of Yissachar; the Gemara’s qualification should not be omitted.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rachel “envied” — desiring the dudaim not truly hers; this led her to cede the tzaddik’s couch (the very opposite of coveting), rectifying the trait of jealousy: not the “evil eye” that would deny others, but a “good eye” letting Leah bear more. Leah’s pure-hearted “you shall come to me” (like Yaakov’s “give me my wife”) won her the sons of Yissachar — wisdom dripping from Chochmah into the Binah of the heart (“va-yeda Elokim”).

p: (יט), — וּבִרְאוּבֵן נִתְבָּרֵר הָרְאִיָּה
And in Reuben was clarified the faculty of sight,
וּבְיִשָּׂשׂכָר הַיְדִיעָה בְּלֹא רְאִיָּה
and in Issachar the knowledge without outward sight,
דְּזֶהוּ הַיְדִיעָה דְּבִינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְאִיָּה נִגְלֵית כְּלָל
which is the cognition of Binah in the heart without physical sight at all,
רַק עַל דֶּרֶךְ (קֹהֶלֶת א, טז): "וְלִבִּי רָאָה הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה",
rather along the lines of (Ecclesiastes 1:16): 'and my heart had great experience of wisdom'.
שֶׁהִיא הַהַתְחָלָה שְׁנִיָּת דְּקִבּוּל שָׂכָר בִּשְׁלֵימוּת הָרְאִיָּה רוּחָנִית
which is the second beginning of receiving reward in the perfection of spiritual perception.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ זְבוּלוּן (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל, כ): "הַפַּעַם יִזְבְּלֵנִי אִישִׁי",
And following this Zebulun (Genesis 30:20): 'Now will my husband dwell with me',
קִבּוּל שָׂכָר נֶגֶד לֵוִי: "הַפַּעַם יִלָּוֶה אִישִׁי" (שָׁם כט, לד).
the receiving of reward corresponding to Levi: 'Now this time will my husband be joined unto me' (ibid. 29:34).
וְ"יִלָּוֶה" הַיְינוּ דְּבֵיקוּת בִּשְׁעַת חִיבּוּר
And 'joined' denotes cleaving at the specific time of union;
וְ"יִזְבְּלֵנִי" הַיְינוּ דְּבֵיקוּת גַּם שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת חִיבּוּר, כִּמְעָרַת אִישׁ וְלִוְיָתוֹ,
whereas 'dwell with me' denotes continuous cleaving even when not actively conjoined, like the cherubic embrace.
רַק דִּירָה תְּמִידוּת עַל דֶּרֶךְ אַבָּא וְאִימָּא תְּרֵין רֵעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין
being rather an enduring dwelling in the manner of Father and Mother, two companions who never part.
וְזֶהוּ תּוֹמְכֵי דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דְּחָכְמָה עִילָּאָה
And this is the role of the supporters of the Torah of Supernal Wisdom,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָהּ דִּירָה קְבוּעָה וְקַיֶּימֶת בְּחַדְרֵי לִבּוֹ,
so that it possess a permanent, enduring habitation within the chambers of his heart,
כְּעִנְיַן (מְלָכִים א ח, יג): "בָּנֹה בָנִיתִי בֵּית זְבֻל לָךְ מָכוֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ עוֹלָמִים".
in the spirit of (I Kings 8:13): 'I have surely built You a house to dwell in, a settled place for You to abide in forever.'
וְהוּא (בְּרֵאשִׁית מט, יג): "לְחוֹף יַמִּים יִשְׁכֹּן",
And he (Genesis 49:13): 'shall dwell at the haven of the sea',
דְּיָדוּעַ יָם מוֹרֶה תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שְׂבִיעָה
for as is known, the sea symbolizes the surging force of desire that has no satiation,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (קֹהֶלֶת א, ז): "כָּל הַנְּחָלִים הֹלְכִים אֶל הַיָּם וְהַיָּם אֵינֶנּוּ מָלֵא",
as it is written (Ecclesiastes 1:7): 'All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full',
וְהַיְינוּ חֵשֶׁק דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא טְרָדוֹת
namely worldly desire which is full of preoccupations.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה דְּכָל יוֹרְדֵי יָם אֵין לָהֶם נַיָּיחָא עַד שֶׁיַּעַמְדוּ בַּיַּבָּשָׁה
and as our Sages of blessed memory noted, all who go down to the sea find no rest until they stand upon dry land.
וְזֶהוּ הֲמוֹן הָאוּמּוֹת שֶׁהוּא כִּשְׁאוֹן יַמִּים
And this is the turbulent tumult of the nations which is like the roaring of the seas (Isaiah 17:12).
בִּשְׁקִיעָה יְתֵירָה בְּכָל חֲמוּדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם קֵץ
in boundless sinking into all the physical delights of this world.
וְעַל כֵּן: "הַיָּם רָאָה אֲרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף",
Therefore: 'The sea saw the coffin of Joseph',
שֶׁהוּא הַהַגְדָּרָה מֵחֲמוּדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which embodies strict boundary against the lusts of this world,
"וַיָּנֹס" וְנַעֲשָׂה יַבָּשָׁה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פז, ח).
'and fled' (Psalms 114:3) and became dry land (Bereishit Rabbah 87:8).
אֲבָל זְבוּלוּן הוּא לְחוֹף הַחוֹל אֲשֶׁר כִּגְבוּל יַמִּים
However, Zebulun dwells on the shore of sand which serves as the boundary of the seas,
וְהוּא גְּבוּרָה דִּמְאָרָךְ,
and this is the might of your Master,
דִּכִּמְלֹא חוּטָא דְּחוֹל אֵין יָכוֹל לַעֲבוֹר כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (עג עַמּוּד א)
, in that beyond a strand of sand the sea cannot pass, as they stated in Bava Batra (73a).
דְּזֶהוּ מִצַּד מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה הַמְצַמְצֶמֶת לַתַּאֲווֹת וּמַשְׁבִּית שְׁאוֹן יַמִּים
for this stems from the attribute of Gevurah which contracts desires and stills the roaring of the seas.
וּמֵאוֹתוֹ חוֹל נַעֲשֶׂה זְכוּכִית לְבָנָה
And from that sand white glass is produced (Megillah 6a),
הוּא אַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא הַמְּאִירָה
which is the luminous looking-glass (aspaklaria ha-me'irah)

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §43): “a sage is greater than a prophet — he can attain more, only that it is not a revealed and clear attainment like the attainment of prophecy, which is called "the seer," for it is like seeing through glass and a speculum; but then it was reversed from seeing to light, as they said, "the Jews had light" — this is Torah — that the Torah should be light illumining their eyes without seeing at all.” Resisei Layla’s historical contrast concerns the Purim acceptance of Oral Torah: prophetic seeing through a speculum gave way to inward reception of light without direct prophetic sight. This illuminates the present distinction between external vision and understanding in the heart.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Chalomot §23): “וכן בחכמה שבלב נאמר ולבי ראה הרבה חכמה כי מה שמרגיש בלב הוא כמו שרואה בעיניו” — “Of the wisdom that is in the heart it says, ‘And my heart saw much wisdom,’ for what one senses in the heart is as though he sees it with his eyes.” The source explicitly continues: “וכן במתן תורה בתורה שבכתב אף שהוא נתונה מן השמים נאמר וכל העם רואים את הקולות שהיו רואים את הנשמע דשמיעה הוא הידיעה שבמוח הדבר ששומע אבל ראיה הוא על ידי ההרגשה שבלב. וזהו עיקר מתן תורה לישראל שיהיה נבלע בלבם” — “Likewise at the Giving of the Written Torah, although it is given from Heaven, it says, ‘All the people saw the sounds’: they saw what is heard. Hearing is the knowledge in the mind of the thing one hears, whereas seeing is through the feeling of the heart. This is the essential purpose of the giving of Torah to Israel: that it should be absorbed in their hearts.” It also identifies the Oral Torah as wisdom flowing from the hearts of Israel’s sages. The passage thus directly illuminates the author’s completed account here of inward understanding as spiritual sight. It distinguishes kinds of apprehension and their internalization, rather than simply erasing the difference between the senses.

paragraphs.text: Izhbitz-Radzin and Sefat Emet parallel - Sha'ar HaEmunah VeYesod HaChasidut 24:3-4; Sefat Emet, Eikev 24:3: The combination of Yissachar, Binah, and a form of knowledge deeper than ordinary sight is developed in Sha'ar HaEmunah, which explains "yodei binah la'itim" as the power to grasp and even "heal" time from the place of Binah. This is a knowing that does not depend on visible surface alone; it reads the inward demand of the moment. Sefat Emet adds that yirah is itself a form of re'iyah: by removing the covering from moach and lev, fear enables a person to see the Divine truth concealed within his own soul. These two formulations help clarify R. Tzadok's sequence of Reuven, Yissachar, and Zevulun. Reuven begins with rectified seeing; Yissachar reaches an inward understanding that can know what is not visible; Zevulun carries that inward bond into the changing movements of "going out" and worldly encounter. Mature avodah does not depend on constant visionary clarity. Once the heart has become a dwelling for the Divine, a person can move through concealment and still remain joined to the inner truth that Binah has taught him to recognize.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Yisrael Kedoshim §3): “קדושים תהיו פרושים תהיו” — “‘You shall be holy’: you shall be separate.” Citing the same formulation in Toras Kohanim on “והייתם לי קדושים,” he observes: “והנה דחשיב בתרתי פרושים וקדושים אלא שמכל מקום כיילינהו תרווייהו בקדושים דקרא” — “It counts two expressions, ‘separate’ and ‘holy,’ although Scripture includes them both under ‘holy.’” He distinguishes the restraint a person can achieve by effort from “שלימות הקדושה מה שמקדשין אותו מלמעלה” — “the completion of holiness, when he is sanctified from Above.” The qualification is essential: “דצריך שישתדל בפרישות וחסידות בדבר המותר כדי לזכות לשמירה וסיוע שמלמעלה במה שהוא אין יכול להעזר מעצמו גם אחר כל השתדלותו בפרישות וחסידות האפשר. אז השם יתברך שולח עזרו מקודש ... ואת רוחו יתן בקרבו” — “He must strive in separation and piety concerning what is permitted, in order to merit guarding and assistance from Above in that for which he cannot help himself, even after all the possible effort in separation and piety. Then Hashem sends His help from the sanctuary … and puts His spirit within him.” This supplies a parallel for the author’s completed account of reward here: the human work of restraint culminates in a perfection bestowed from Heaven. Here the author specifies fear of Heaven itself as that gift.
