inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Reuven = seeing clarified; Yissachar = knowing without seeing; Zevulun (“yizbeleini”) = a permanent indwelling, not only at the moment of union — “Abba and Ima that never part.” The sea = unquenchable longing (of olam ha-zeh), stilled by the sand-boundary (Gevurah); from that sand comes clear glass (the aspaklaria), so that in the Future even yirah — man’s own task — is granted from Heaven without effort.

p: (כ), — וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת זַרְעָא דְּלֵאָה
And this is the ultimate perfection of the seed of Leah,
שֶׁהֵם עִיקַּר עֲבוֹדָתָם בְּאַהֲבָה וְחֵשֶׁק
whose primary divine service is anchored in love and longing.
וְזוֹכִים גַּם לְיִרְאָה שֶׁהוּא עֲבוֹדַת זַרְעָא דְּרָחֵל
and who merit awe as well, which is the service of the seed of Rachel.
וְחוּט דִּתְכֵלֶת דְּצִיצִית, הַיְינוּ הִתְעוֹרְרוּת יִרְאָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
And the thread of techelet in tzitzit represents the awakening of awe directly from Heaven,
דְּ"וּרְאִיתֶם אֹתוֹ וּזְכַרְתֶּם" (בַּמִּדְבָּר טו, לט).
as in 'that you may look upon it, and remember' (Numbers 15:39).
דְּהַשִּׁכְחָה בָּאָה מִצַּד הֶעְדֵּר הַיִּרְאָה
For forgetfulness arises through the absence of awe,
וְזֶה אַתְחַלְתָּא דְּכָל רָע
and this is the inception of all evil,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים ח, יט): "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁכֹחַ תִּשְׁכַּח וְגוֹמֵר וְהָלַכְתָּ אַחֲרֵי אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים".
as it is stated (Deuteronomy 8:19): 'And it shall be, if you do at all forget, etc. and walk after other gods.'
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהַיִּרְאָה תַּרְעָא לְדַרְתָּא דְּצַדִּיקִים
Just as awe is the outer gateway to the courtyard of the righteous.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַיִּרְאָה בָּא הַזְּכִירָה
And through awe comes remembrance,
כִּי דָּבָר שֶׁאָדָם יָרֵא הוּא נִקְבָּע בַּלֵּב
for a matter of which a person stands in dread becomes permanently fixed in the heart;
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (עב עַמּוּד ב) "וְלֶב אָיִן" עַל הֶעְדֵּר הַיִּרְאָה
which is why they expounded in Yoma (72b) 'and has no heart' as referring to the lack of fear,
וְדָבָר שֶׁהוּא בַּלֵּב תָּמִיד אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִשְׁכּוֹחַ בּוֹ.
and a matter that is in the heart constantly cannot possibly be forgotten.
וְזֶה טַעַם מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה כ, א)
And this explains what our Sages of blessed memory stated in Vayikra Rabbah (Parashah 20:1)
עַל פָּסוּק (שְׁמוּאֵל א טז, יב): "וְטוֹב רֹאִי"
– on the verse (I Samuel 16:12): 'and goodly to look upon'—
כָּל הָרוֹאֶה דָּוִד נִזְכָּר לְתַלְמוּדוֹ.
whoever looked upon David was reminded of his Torah study.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּעִנְיַן צִיוּוּי הַתּוֹרָה בְּמֶלֶךְ: "שֶׁתְּהֵא אֵימָתוֹ עָלֶיךָ" (סַנְהֶדְרִין כב עַמּוּד א),
Which means that the Torah's command concerning a king: 'that his dread be upon you' (Sanhedrin 22a),
אֵין הַכַּוָּונָה אֵימַת בָּשָׂר וָדָם כִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ,
does not mean dread of mere flesh and blood in its simple sense,
דְּעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה נא, יב): "מִי אַתְּ וַתִּירְאִי מֵאֱנוֹשׁ יָמוּת וְגוֹמֵר".
for concerning this it is said (Isaiah 51:12): 'Who are you, that you should be afraid of a man that shall die, etc.',
רַק דְּמֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַלְכוּתוֹ נִמְשֶׁכֶת מִמַּלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם
Rather, a Jewish king has his sovereignty drawn directly from the Sovereignty of Heaven;
וְכַיָּדוּעַ דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת
and as is known, the spiritual rung of King David, peace be upon him, is the attribute of Malchut,
דְּהָיָה דָּבוּק בְּמִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
in that he clung unto the attribute of His Sovereignty, blessed be He,
וּכְטַעַם (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כט, כג): "וַיֵּשֶׁב שְׁלֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּא ה
'". mirroring (I Chronicles 29:23): 'And Solomon sat on the throne of Hashem.',
וְעַל כֵּן מְבָרְכִין "שֶׁחָלַק מִכְּבוֹדוֹ לִירֵאָיו" עַל כָּל מֶלֶךְ מִמַּלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יִהְיֶה אֵיזֶה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה
Therefore we recite the blessing 'Who has imparted of His glory to those who fear Him' over every king of Israel whoever he may be (Berakhot 58a),
דִּבְהֶכְרֵחַ מִצַּד הַמַּלְכוּת, שֶׁשּׁוֹפֵעַ עָלָיו מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ אֲשֶׁר בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה
for perforce by virtue of the kingship, where there rests upon him the attribute of His Sovereignty which rules over all,
דְּמִכֹּחָהּ זָכָה לַמַּלְכוּת
by whose power he merited the throne.
מַקֶּפֶת אוֹתוֹ יִרְאָה גְּדוֹלָה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִמִּדָּה זוֹ כַּיָּדוּעַ בַּזֹּהַר
a great awe surrounds him drawn from this attribute, as is known in the Zohar.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל (סִימָן ב) דְּעַל כֵּן מֶלֶךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁכָּרַע בִּתְפִלַּת עֲמִידָה שׁוּב אֵינוֹ זוֹקֵף
And as I wrote above (Section 2), therefore a king, once he has bowed in the Amidah, does not straighten up

(בִּבְרָכוֹת לד עַמּוּד ב.
) מִצַּד תּוֹקֶף הַיִּרְאָה
(Berakhot 34b) on account of the intense overwhelming awe.
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא רֶגֶל רְבִיעִית דְּמֶרְכָּבָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְמִידָּה זוֹ,
And King David, peace be upon him, who is the fourth leg of the divine Chariot and the seminal root of this attribute.
כָּל הָרוֹאֵהוּ מִסְתַּלֵּק מִמֶּנּוּ הַשִּׁכְחָה לְגַמְרֵי
anyone who gazed upon him had forgetfulness entirely banished from him.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁ"נִזְכָּר לְתַלְמוּדוֹ" דְּדָרְשׁוּ מִמִּלַּת "וְטוֹב",
And this is why 'he is reminded of his Torah study,' which they expounded from the word ve-tov ('and goodly'),
דְּאֵין טוֹב אֶלָּא תוֹרָה
for there is no 'good' other than Torah (Avot 6:3),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְנָחוֹת (נג עַמּוּד ב) מִקְּרָא דְּ(מִשְׁלֵי ד, ב): "לֶקַח טוֹב נָתַתִּי לָכֶם",
as they stated in Menachot (53b) from the verse: 'For I give you good doctrine (lekach tov)',
דִּמְשְׁלֵי דִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם גִּילָּה שֵׁם זֶה לַתּוֹרָה
in that the Proverbs of King Solomon revealed this designation for the Torah,
וְכֵן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר (תְּהִלִּים קיט, עב): "טוֹב לִי תוֹרַת פִּיךָ".
and likewise King David said (Psalms 119:72): 'The law of Your mouth is better (tov) unto me.',
דְּעִיקַּר שֵׁם "טוֹב" רָמוּז לְצַדִּיק כְּטַעַם (יְשַׁעְיָה ג, י): "אִמְרוּ צַדִּיק כִּי טוֹב" כַּנּוֹדָע
For the primary term 'good' is allusive to the tzaddik, as in 'Say of the righteous that he is good' as is known.
וְהַיְינוּ בַּעַל מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים וְגָדוּר בְּיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
meaning one who possesses good deeds and is fenced in with the fear of Heaven.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §16): “And for this purpose is the mitzvah of tzitzis in practice — ‘that you may remember and do all My commandments and not stray after your own heart’ (Bamidbar 15:39) — which does not remove the desire entirely, so that it should not enter the heart at all; rather, it enjoins one not to stray after cravings and the willfulness of his heart, but to thrust it away from his heart at once. And this comes by way of the remembrance that the tzitzis brings — like that student in Menachos (44a) whose very tzitzis ‘slapped him across the face’ and stopped him from sin.” (R’ Tzadok makes explicit the mechanism of the techeiles-thread that this se’if invokes: it is not the uprooting of desire but the instant refusal to pursue it.)

paragraphs.text: Devarim 8:19: “וְהָיָה אִם שָׁכֹחַ תִּשְׁכַּח אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ, וְהָלַכְתָּ אַחֲרֵי אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים…” — “and it shall be, if you forget Hashem your God and go after other gods…” R’ Tzadok’s use: forgetting stems from the absence of fear, and it is “the beginning of all evil” — the slide to “other gods”; hence the techeiles-thread (“you shall see it and remember”) arouses the fear that fixes a thing in the heart, whence it can never be forgotten.

paragraphs.text: Sefat Emet parallel - Eikev 24:3: Sefat Emet's phrase "yirah otiyot re'iyah" gives a precise Chassidic frame for R. Tzadok's use of techeiles, seeing, remembering, and fear. He explains that the bond with Hashem is already planted within Israel, but the physical covering blocks its disclosure; yirah is the key that opens the gates of moach and lev and allows a person to see the truth. This makes "u-re'isem oto u-zekhartem" more than a mnemonic technique. Holy sight generates yirah, and yirah in turn fixes what is seen within the heart so that it is not lost to forgetfulness. R. Tzadok's claim that what truly enters the heart is not forgotten follows naturally: forgetting is a sign that the knowledge remained external, while yirah converts perception into an inward orientation. The techeiles-thread thus stands at the boundary between revealed sight and hidden memory. One sees a finite physical sign, but the purpose is to awaken a fear that opens the heart to the infinite Divine reality toward which the sign points.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Hashanah §17): “"Zachor" corresponds to the brain on the right, and there is the place of remembering — yet even in the brain, in which there is memory, forgetting can still occur at distant intervals. But "Zachor" that is the rung beyond — "in which there is no forgetting and forgetting does not abide" — as it says, "there is no forgetting before the Throne of Your glory"… then there is no forgetting at all whatsoever.” Exactly the se’if: ordinary memory can lapse, but what is fixed by fear is bound to a rung where forgetting has no foothold.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Leah’s seed (love/longing) also attain yirah — the techeiles-thread (“you shall see it and remember”), for forgetting stems from the absence of fear. Fear fixes a thing in the heart, and what is in the heart cannot be forgotten. Hence “whoever saw David recalled his learning”: a king’s awe is not that of flesh-and-blood but of Malchus drawn from the Kingship of Heaven — David being the “fourth leg of the Merkavah.”

p: (כא), — וְנוֹדַע דַּחֲלוּקִים בְּכָל מָקוֹם בַּעֲלֵי תוֹרָה וּבַעֲלֵי מִצְווֹת
And it is known that in all teachings there is a distinction between masters of Torah and masters of mitzvot;
כִּי הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לִהְיוֹת כָּל כָּךְ בַּעַל מִצְווֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים
for one immersed in Torah cannot engage as expansively in the performance of practical mitzvot and good deeds,
מִפְּנֵי שְׁקִידָתוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה
on account of his unbroken diligence in Torah;
אֶלָּא דְּהַתּוֹרָה עַצְמָהּ הִיא כּוֹלֶלֶת כָּל טוֹב
only that the Torah itself inherently encompasses all goodness.
וְאוּלָם עִנְיַן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת "תּוֹרַת ה
'" However, the nature of the Written Torah which is called 'the Torah of Hashem',
אֵינָהּ אֶלָּא לִימּוּד הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
is strictly instruction toward practical action;
וּמִצַּד זֶה: מַעֲשֶׂה גָּדוֹל שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר הַמְכֻוָּון
and from this perspective, physical deed is paramount, being the ultimate objective.
אֲבָל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַנִּקְרָא "תּוֹרָתוֹ"
However, the Oral Torah which is called 'his own Torah' (Avodah Zarah 19a)—
זֶהוּ עִיקַּר גְּדוּלַּת הַתּוֹרָה דְּ"כָל חֲפָצִים לֹא יִשְׁווּ בָהּ" (מִשְׁלֵי ח, יא),
this is the quintessential greatness of Torah, where 'all things desirable cannot compare to it',
אֲפִילּוּ חֶפְצֵי שָׁמַיִם – מִצְווֹת (מוֹעֵד קָטָן ט עַמּוּד ב);
even the heavenly desires—practical mitzvot (Moed Katan 9b);
וְ"אֹהֵב ה' שַׁעֲרֵי צִיּוֹן הַמְצוּיָּינִים בַּהֲלָכָה מִכָּל מִשְׁכְּנוֹת יַעֲקֹב" (בִּבְרָכוֹת ח עַמּוּד א)
– and 'Hashem loves the gates of Zion that are distinguished in Halakhah more than all the dwellings of Jacob' (Berakhot 8a)—,
הַכֹּל הוּא עַל חִדּוּשִׁין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
all refers specifically to the original insights and novel interpretations of the Oral Torah,
שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמַר (מִשְׁלֵי ד, ב): "לֶקַח טוֹב נָתַתִּי לָכֶם",
concerning which Scripture proclaimed (Proverbs 4:2): 'For I have given you good doctrine',
הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁנִּיתַּן בְּמַתָּנָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל דְּ"לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִיא" מֵעַתָּה (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא נט עַמּוּד ב).
meaning that which was conferred as an outright gift unto Israel, such that 'it is not in heaven' any longer (Bava Metzia 59b).
וּמְתִיבְתָּא דִּרְקִיעָא נֶחְלְקוּ עִם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בַּהֲלָכָה בְּפֶרֶק הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַפּוֹעֲלִים (שָׁם פו עַמּוּד א),
And the Heavenly Academy disputed with the Holy One, blessed be He, over a halakhic ruling in the chapter HaSokher et HaPo'alim (ibid. 86a),
וּפָסַק הָרַמְבַּ"ם שָׁם הֲלָכָה כִּמְתִיבְתָּא דִּרְקִיעָא
and Maimonides ruled there the halakhah in accordance with the Academy of Heaven,
וְלָקְחוּ לְוִיכּוּחַ רַבָּה בַּר נַחְמָנִי חָכָם מֵהַאי עָלְמָא דַּוְוקָא
and they summoned for arbitration Rabbah bar Nachmani, an earthly sage specifically,
כִּי כְּבָר נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לַתַּחְתּוֹנִים מַתָּנָה גְּמוּרָה שֶׁנִּקְרָא "תּוֹרָתָם".
because the Torah was already granted to mortal dwellers of earth as an absolute gift such that it is titled 'their Torah.'
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה הוּא נִקְרָא "טוֹב",
And from this vantage point it is called 'good'.
דְּהוּא עֶצֶם הַטּוֹב הַכּוֹלֶלֶת כָּל טוֹב שֶׁבְּכָל מִינֵי מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים
for it is the quintessential Good that encompasses all good present across every variety of worthy deeds.
וְזֶה טַעַם "טוֹב לִי תוֹרַת פִּיךָ מֵאַלְפֵי זָהָב וָכָסֶף" (תְּהִלִּים קיט, עב),
And this explains 'The law of Your mouth is better unto me than thousands of gold and silver' (Psalms 119:72),
הֵם אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה כַּנּוֹדָע
which correspond to love and fear (silver and gold), as is known;
וְ"אַלְפֵי" הוּא תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and 'thousands' represents the pinnacle of completion in this world,
דְּכָל בִּרְכָאן דְּהַאי עָלְמָא הוּא בְּמִסְפַּר אֶלֶף שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד עוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה
for all blessings of this world are bounded within the number one thousand, which corresponds to the World of Action (Asiyah),
כִּי הַמִּסְפָּרִים: יְחִידוֹת, עֲשָׂרוֹת, מֵאוֹת, אֲלָפִים
since the numeric orders: units, tens, hundreds, thousands.
הֵם נֶגֶד אַרְבַּע עוֹלָמוֹת אֲבִיעָ״ה: אֲצִילוּת, בְּרִיאָה, יְצִירָה, עֲשִׂיָּה
correspond to the four cosmic worlds of ABYA: Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah.
וְ"תוֹרַת פִּיךָ" הַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
And 'the law of Your mouth' denotes the Oral Torah,
דְּמַלְכוּת פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ,
for Malchut is the mouth, and we call it the Oral Torah,
וְהַיְינוּ "טוֹב לִי" דַּוְוקָא שֶׁזֶּהוּ דַּרְגָּא דִּילֵיהּ,
and this is 'better unto me' specifically, for that was David's intrinsic spiritual rung.
וְהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ לַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
he being the root of the Oral Torah.
וְזֶה טוֹב מִכָּל עֲבוֹדַת הָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּאַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה שֶׁהֵם רַק גַּדְפִין
And this is superior to all mortal service in this world through love and fear, which serve merely as the two wings;
אֲבָל מַאן דְּאָחֵיד בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא שֶׁהוּא גּוּפָא דְּמַלְכָּא אָחֵיד בְּכוּלָּא (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, נג עַמּוּד ב).
whereas one who holds onto the Torah, which is the very body of the King, grasps everything (Zohar Part III, 53b).
וַאֲחִיזָה הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
And grasping is possible solely through the Oral Torah,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הִתְאַחֲדוּת הָאָדָם בַּתּוֹרָה
which is the authentic unification of man within the Torah,
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִקְרָא "תּוֹרָתוֹ" – הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁהוּא מְחַדֵּשׁ,
whereby it becomes designated as 'his own Torah'—namely that which he innovates,
דְּזֶהוּ עִיקַּר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה: מַה שֶּׁכָּל תַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
for this is the very essence of the Oral Torah: whatever a seasoned disciple is destined to innovate in words of Torah.
וּכְשֶׁמַּשִּׂיג הַחִדּוּשִׁים הַשַּׁיָּיכִים לְחֶלְקוֹ הֲרֵי זֶה אָחֵיד בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא
and when he attains the insights appropriate to his allotted portion, he is holding fast to the Torah.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּרוּת רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ה, טו)
And therefore our Sages of blessed memory expounded in Ruth Rabbah (Parashah 5:15)
עַל פָּסוּק (רוּת ג, ז): "וַיִּיטַב לִבּוֹ" בְּבֹעַז
– on the verse (Ruth 3:7): 'and his heart was merry' concerning Boaz—

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Toldos §8): “ואב ואם המולידים התחדשות הד״ת הוא מקרא ומשנה שהם טל השמים ומשמני הארץ. וז״ש מטל השמים זו מקרא שהוא מן השמים מהקב״ה שנתן התורה ולא מצד יגיעת האדם” — “The father and mother that give birth to the renewal of Torah are Scripture and Mishnah, which are ‘the dew of heaven and the fat of the earth.’ Thus, ‘from the dew of heaven’ means Scripture, which is from Heaven, from the Holy One who gave the Torah, and not from the side of a person’s toil.” He continues: “וכמו כן משנה כתיבא ומנחא שכתבו בסדר ההלכות מכל התורה והדינים הכוללים כל המשפטים. ותלמוד היא ארוכה מארץ מדה שצריכים יגיעה להתחדשות רוב החכמה. ומצד התחדשות החכמה משיגים חיי עולם החכמה תחיה בעליה” — “Likewise Mishnah is written and laid before us: they recorded in the ordered laws all the Torah and the laws encompassing all the judgments. Talmud, however, is longer than the earth in measure, requiring toil for the renewal of abundant wisdom; through the renewal of wisdom one attains eternal life — ‘wisdom gives life to its possessors.’” This illuminates the completed claim here that a person’s own new insights in Oral Torah are how he takes hold of Torah. The given text is the parent of the renewal, and the renewal calls for human toil; the source does not derive judicial garments from Moshe’s upbringing in Midyan.

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 86a: They were disputing in the Heavenly Academy: “if the bright spot baheres preceded the white hair — impure; and if the white hair preceded the bright spot — pure. In a case of doubt — the Holy One says ‘pure,’ and all the Heavenly Academy say ‘impure.’” They said, “who shall decide? — Rabbah bar Nachmani, for he declared, ‘I am unique in the laws of nega’im, I am unique in the laws of ohalos.’” They sent the Angel of Death to bring him — For the Torah’s ruling belongs to the sages of this world. Rabbah’s final utterance is “pure, pure.” Mishneh Torah, Defilement by Leprosy 2:9 rules: “If it is doubtful whether the white hair preceded or the bright spot preceded, this is impure,” and adds, “It appears to me that its impurity is doubtful.” Rav Tzadok invokes this earthly ruling alongside the heavenly narrative as part of his account of the Torah’s complete gift to Israel.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Ki Tisa §3): “שבשעת מתן תורה כל ישראל ראוים לכתר כהונה ... באו מלאכים וקשרו להם ב׳ כתרים א׳ כנגד נעשה וא׳ כנגד נשמע” — “At the Giving of the Torah all Israel were fit for the crown of priesthood … angels came and bound upon them two crowns, one corresponding to ‘we shall do’ and one corresponding to ‘we shall hear.’” He explains the two: “כתר נעשה היינו כתר כהונה דמעשה עבודה וכתר נשמע כתר תורה והיה כתר תורה כולל גם כתר מלכות עדש״נ בי מלכים ימלוכו” — “The crown of ‘we shall do’ is the crown of priesthood, the performance of the service; the crown of ‘we shall hear’ is the crown of Torah, and the crown of Torah included the crown of kingship as well, as it says, ‘Through me kings reign.’” The source thus supplies a distinct parallel for the connection made here between Torah and kingship: the Torah crown itself includes kingship. Its two-crown account does not establish a hierarchy of three separate crowns.

paragraphs.text: Yerushalmi Peah 2:4: “Even that which a seasoned student talmid vasik is destined to teach one day before his master was already said to Moshe at Sinai.” Kedushas Levi — the Oral Torah is the gift of Israel’s own chiddush: Kedushas Levi, Yisro §22, describes the two Torahs in a manner remarkably close to this se’if. Torah shebiksav was entrusted through Moshe in fixed written form, whereas Torah shebe’al peh includes the interpretation transmitted to Moshe together with “כל שתלמיד ותיק עתיד לחדש.” He then draws the consequence: Hashem gave Israel such authority out of His love and choice of them that, according to the Torah as the tzaddikim of the generation truly interpret it, so the Divine order is conducted. This does not mean that a chacham invents a second Torah detached from Sinai; the very novelty he uncovers was rooted at Sinai, yet it becomes “his Torah” only through the labor of his own mind and heart. That formulation sharpens R’ Tzadok’s distinction here. The greatness of Torah shebe’al peh is precisely that the received Divine word becomes a personal acquisition without ceasing to be Divine. “Lo bashamayim hi” is therefore not a distancing of Torah from Heaven but the completion of the matanah: Heaven wills that the earthly chacham grasp, interpret, and decide. In this sense the talmid’s chiddush is the point at which the gift is fully received — the Torah is no longer merely before him as Toras Hashem, but lives within him as toraso.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 49:10: “לֹא יָסוּר שֵׁבֶט מִיהוּדָה וּמְחֹקֵק מִבֵּין רַגְלָיו, עַד כִּי יָבֹא שִׁילֹה” — “the scepter shall not depart from Yehudah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh comes” (Yaakov’s blessing to Yehudah). R’ Tzadok’s use: the “mechokek” of Yehudah is the attainment of the Oral Torah, whose root was in the seed of Yehudah — the line that produced Boaz, Rus (“the mother of royalty”), and David.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The Written Torah (“Toras Hashem”) is the “study of the deed”; the Oral Torah (“toraso — his own Torah”) is the essence of Torah’s greatness — chiddushei Torah, which Hashem “loves — the gates of Zion distinguished in halachah.” Given as an outright gift (“no longer in Heaven”), it lets a person grasp the “body of the King.” Its root is in Yehudah/David (“Malchus = the mouth = Torah she-be’al peh”); hence Boaz/Rus and the “mechokek.”

p: (כב) וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁעָשָׂה אָזְנַיִם לַתּוֹרָה
And King Solomon, peace be upon him, was the first who fashioned handles ('ears') for the Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֵירוּבִין כא עַמּוּד ב):
as our Sages of blessed memory taught (Eruvin 21b):
דְּהָיְתָה כְּקֻפָּה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ אָזְנַיִם
that it was previously like a basket without handles.
הַיְינוּ בֵּית אֲחִיזָה לִהְיוֹת אָחִיד בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא
Meaning a handle-grip to hold fast to the Torah,
דְּזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק עַל יְדֵי הַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב וְהַשָּׂגָתוֹ בְּבִינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַתּוֹרָה
for this is possible only through the sensation of the heart and its grasp with intuitive understanding in the heart into the depths of the Torah,
וְלֹא מִצַּד יְדִיעַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב לְבַד דִּכְתִיבָה וּמַנָּחָא
and not merely from knowing the Written Torah alone which is transcribed and deposited.
דְּהִיא גָּלוּי וְסָתוּם
for it is both revealed and concealed.
הַיְינוּ גִּילּוּי מִצַּד הַנִּגְלֶה
Namely, revealed from the perspective of overt text,
אֲבָל מַעֲמַקֶּיהָ סְתוּמִים וַחֲתוּמִים מְאֹד
yet its depths are exceedingly sealed and hidden,
וְרַק "אִישׁ תְּבוּנָה יִדְלֶנָּה" (מִשְׁלֵי כ, ה),
and only 'a man of discernment will draw it out' (Proverbs 20:5),
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ בִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב לְסַפֵּק חֶבֶל בְּחֶבֶל
meaning one who possesses understanding in the heart to tie rope to rope,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (עֵירוּבִין שָׁם).
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded concerning King Solomon, peace be upon him (Eruvin ibid.).
וְכָל תּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הֶבֶל הוּא עֲדַיִן לִפְנֵי תּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ
And all the Torah of this world is still vanity before the Torah of the Messiah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (קֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה יא, ח).
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Kohelet Rabbah 11:8).
לְשׁוֹן "הֶבֶל" אֵינוֹ גְּנַאי
The expression 'vanity' (hevel - vapor/breath) is not derogatory,
כִּי הוּא בְּסוֹד שִׁבְעָה הֲבָלִים שֶׁאָמַר קֹהֶלֶת עַל כָּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כֻּלָּם
for it is rooted in the esoteric mystery of the seven vapors that Kohelet pronounced upon all affairs of this world,
הַנִּכְלָלִים בְּשֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת וְשִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן
which are subsumed within the seven sefirotic attributes and the seven days of cosmic Building,
וְהַכֹּל הוּא דּוּגְמַת הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא הַקַּיָּים לָעַד
and everything is an earthly reflection of the World to Come which endures forever;
רַק שֶׁעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא דּוּגְמַת הֶבֶל הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַקְּדֵירָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ טַעַם הַתַּבְשִׁיל
except that this world is comparable to the vapor emerging from a cooking pot which contains the aroma and flavor of the stew,
אוֹ הֶבֶל הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַפֶּה בְּעֵת הַדִּבּוּר
or the breath emerging from the mouth during speech,
דְּגַם בַּהֶבֶל כָּלוּל אוֹתִיּוֹת הַדִּבּוּר
since within the raw breath the letters of articulation are also latently included.
אֲבָל בְּהֶעְלֵם עָצוּם מְאֹד שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה כְּלָל
yet in tremendous concealment such that it is not manifest at all.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא עוֹלָם הַנִּגְלֶה וְנִרְאֶה לָעַיִן וּמַרְאִין עָלָיו בְּאֶצְבַּע בְּמִלַּת "זֶה",
And even though this world is the realm of the manifest, visible to the eye where one points with a finger using the demonstrative word 'this' (zeh),
הִנֵּה מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁלּוֹ נִקְרָא עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ שְׁקָרִים
behold, from the perspective of its outward disclosure it is called the World of Falsehood, which is entirely false.
וְהָאֱמֶת שֶׁבּוֹ שֶׁהִשְׁלִיךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אַרְצָה הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם
and the Truth within it which Hashem, blessed be He, cast down to the earth remains in ultimate concealment.
וְאַף אַחַר שֶׁנָּתַן "אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב"
– And even after He granted 'Truth unto Jacob'—,
הַתּוֹרָה דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ אֱמֶת
the Torah, concerning which Truth is inscribed—;
הָאֲמִיתּוּת הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם
its absolute inner veracity remains in ultimate hiddenness;
וּמַה שֶּׁמִּתְגַּלֶּה לְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָאֲמִיתִיִּים בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר
and whatever is revealed to the authentic sages of Israel in each and every generation
אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דּוּגְמַת הֶבֶל הַיּוֹצֵא מִתּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ
is merely comparable to the warm breath emanating from the transcendent Torah of the Messiah.
שֶׁהוּא יִהְיֶה שְׁלֵימוּת הַדִּבּוּר דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
which will constitute the consummate articulated speech of the Oral Torah.

The metaphor means a workable way to grasp the Torah; Shlomo also ordained practices such as eruvin and handwashing.

paragraphs.text: Tanya — the Written Torah is revealed, yet its inner will remains sealed until Torah shebe’al peh: Tanya, Iggeres HaKodesh §29, explains that the ratzon ha-elyon clothed in the mitzvos of the Written Torah is itself “מופלא ומכוסה, טמיר ונעלם,” and becomes disclosed only through Torah shebe’al peh. His example is tefillin: the written verse commands “ukeshartam” and “totafos,” but leaves the concrete form, location, materials, dimensions, and details concealed until the Oral Torah interprets them. The same is true, he says, of all positive and negative commandments. This is a precise Chabad parallel to R’ Tzadok’s phrase that Torah shebiksav is at once “galui v’sasum.” Its words are exposed to every reader, yet the Divine will embedded in those words is not exhausted by their surface. Torah shebe’al peh supplies the “handle” by which the hidden content can actually be grasped and lived. The comparison also clarifies R’ Tzadok’s use of hevel. The revealed word is not false or deficient; like breath carrying unarticulated letters, it bears within itself an abundance not yet unfolded. The future Torah of Mashiach is therefore not a replacement of the present Torah, but the fuller disclosure of what its present letters already contain in concealment — the truth cast into this world becoming transparent rather than hidden beneath its outward form.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 8:5: “נטל אמת והשליכו לארץ” — “He took Truth and cast it to the earth”. The Midrash brings Daniel 8:12, “and it cast truth to the ground,” as its prooftext, and the angels ask that Truth rise again, citing “Truth shall sprout from the earth.” In the plain vision in Daniel the action belongs to the hostile horn; God’s casting Truth to earth is the Midrash’s reading. Rav Tzadok uses that Midrashic image for truth concealed within the visible world.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas Shabbos §2): discussing Temple building, he cites: “אין ביהמ״ק נבנה בידו של אדם אלא בידו של הקב״ה שנא׳ כוננו ידיך. ומדמייתי אקרא דאהלי שודד מבואר דקאי אביהמ״ק א׳ שנחרב דע״כ נקרא אהלי” — “The Beis HaMikdash is built not by the hand of man but by the hand of the Holy One, as it says, ‘Your hands established it.’ Since it brings this in connection with ‘My tent is despoiled,’ it is clear that it refers to the First Beis HaMikdash, which was destroyed; that is why it is called ‘My tent.’” The source reconciles divine building with the human builders: the decisive question is whether God’s action through their hands becomes the abiding reality. It then turns expressly to the present contrast in Torah: “וכן ... התורה דחיי עולם הנגלות דד״ת המתלבש בעוה״ז בכשר ופסול אסור ומותר כו׳ ... היא מסט׳ דעה״ד טוב ורע שמצד עוה״ז. וע״ז ארז״ל תורתו של עוה״ז הבל בפני תורתו של משיח כי הוא יגלה הפנימיות” — “Likewise … the revealed Torah, which is eternal life — the words of Torah clothed in this world in valid and invalid, forbidden and permitted, and so on … is from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, on the side of this world. Of this the Sages said, ‘The Torah of this world is vapor before the Torah of Mashiach,’ for he will reveal the inward dimension.” It continues that Israel’s toil in Torah throughout this world prepares them to hear Mashiach’s Torah. This supplies the explicit parallel to the author’s completed claim here about present Torah and the full disclosure of Oral Torah by Mashiach.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Shlomo first made “handles” for the Torah — a handhold to grasp its depths through the Binah of the heart, not the Written Torah’s surface alone (“revealed and sealed”). All the Torah of this world is still “hevel” before the Torah of Mashiach — not disparagement, but the “seven hevalim”: like the vapor that carries the taste of the dish, or the breath that holds the hidden letters of speech. Olam ha-zeh is the revealed “world of falsehood”; its truth is utterly concealed.

p: (כג) וְעַל כֵּן אַחַר לֵוִי
And therefore following Levi,
שֶׁבּוֹ כָּלוּל כֹּחַ הוֹרָדַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב לָאָרֶץ עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
within whom was embedded the spiritual potency of bringing down the Written Torah to the earth through Moses our teacher, peace be upon him,
נוֹלַד יְהוּדָה שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה עַל יְדֵי הַמָּשִׁיחַ,
Judah was born, who embodies the ultimate perfection of the Oral Torah through the Messiah.
וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת כֻּלּוֹ כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד
and this constitutes the summit of all perfection as it will be manifested in the ultimate future.
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא "יְהוּדָה מְחֹקְקִי" (תְּהִלִּים ס, ט)
– Therefore it is said: 'Judah is my lawgiver' (mechokeki; Psalms 60:9)—,
כִּבְיָכוֹל מְחוֹקֵק אוֹתִי
as though to say: he engraves Me.
כִּי אוֹרַיְיתָא וְקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא חַד
for the Torah and the Holy One, blessed be He, are one.
וְהַחִיקּוּק דְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה בְּלִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
And this engraving of the words of Torah into the hearts of the children of Israel,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לֶעָתִיד: "עַל לוּחַ לִבָּם אֶכְתֲּבֶנָּה" (יִרְמְיָה לא, לב) שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁכְּחוּ עוֹד
as prophesied for the future: 'upon the tablet of their heart I will write it' so that they shall never forget it again.
זֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי יְהוּדָה
this is achieved through Judah.
אֲבָל אַסּוּקֵי שְׁמַעְתָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּהִלְכְתָא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְהִילוּךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם
However, arriving at the clear halakhic conclusion in this world to guide human conduct,
דְּ"בְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ" הַיְינוּ טִרְדָּא דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
wherein 'when you walk along the way' refers to the mundane preoccupation of this world,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה כא עַמּוּד א,) — עַל פָּסוּק "בְּהִתְהַלֶּכְךָ תַּנְחֶה" – דְּהַיְינוּ הִילוּךְ דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Sotah 21a) on the verse 'when you walk it shall guide you'—referring to the path of this world,
וְזֶהוּ לְשׁוֹן הֲלָכָה שֶׁהוּא הַנְהָגַת הַהִילוּךְ,
and this is the linguistic meaning of halakhah, which signifies practical path-walking.
הוּא בְּלֵוִי וְיִשָּׂשׂכָר
this is situated in Levi and Issachar.
הַיְינוּ הַנְהָגָה דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְשֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַמּוּשָּׂגִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
Namely, the governance of the Written and Oral Torah comprehended in this physical world.
לְצוֹרֶךְ הַנְהָגַת אָדָם בּוֹ כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא כְּצֵל יָמֵינוּ עֲלֵי אָרֶץ
for the necessity of guiding mortal man within it according as 'our days upon earth are like a shadow.'
כְּמוֹ הַצֵּל שֶׁהוּא דּוּגְמָא וְגָוֶון לְבַד מִצּוּרַת אָדָם הָאֲמִיתִּי
Just like the shadow which is merely an outline and impression of the authentic human form,
שֶׁהוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַנִּשְׁאֶרֶת קַיֶּימֶת לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
which is the transcendent soul that endures for the World to Come,
כַּנּוֹדָע דְּעָלֶיהָ הוּא עִיקַּר חָלוּת שֵׁם אָדָם
as is known that upon the soul rests the primary application of the title 'Adam' (man),
אֲבָל הַגּוּף דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִקְרָא רַק "בְּשַׂר אָדָם" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, כה),
whereas the physical body of this world is merely termed 'the flesh of man' as stated in the Zohar.
וְהוּא הַצָּרִיךְ הַגְדָּרָה
and it is what requires moral boundaries and restraint.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְצַדִּיקִים יֵלְכוּ בָם" (הוֹשֵׁעַ יד, י),
And as it is written: 'and the righteous shall walk in them' (Hosea 14:10).
דְּהַהֲלִיכַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לַצַּדִּיקִים הַמּוּגְדָּרִים בְּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם
meaning that walking in this world through words of Torah belongs exclusively to the righteous who are disciplined and bounded in their deeds.
וּבִזְמַן הַבַּיִת הָיָה עִיקַּר הַהַנְהָגָה עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וּנְבִיאִים
And in the era of the First Temple, the primary direction operated via the Written Torah and the Prophets.
דְּהַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן הִתְגַּלּוּת מִשָּׁמַיִם
which was likewise overt revelation directly from Heaven.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבָּאוּ דָּוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה וְחִדְּשׁוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כַּמָּה דְּבָרִים
And even though David and Solomon came and innovated numerous teachings of the Oral Torah,
עֲדַיִן הָיָה בְּמַדְרֵגַת כְּתוּבִים
it was still on the sanctified level of the Holy Writings (Ketuvim),
כִּי הַשָּׂגָה שֶׁלָּהֶם הוּא רְשִׁימוּ מִתּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
for their perception was a foretaste and imprint of the Torah of the Messiah within this world,
דְּאָז: "יַעֲשֶׂה אֱלֹהִים חֲדָשָׁה בָּאָרֶץ – נְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵב גָּבֶר" (יִרְמְיָה לא, כא).
wherein: 'God will create a new thing on earth—a female shall encompass a man' (Jeremiah 31:21).
הַיְינוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה יִהְיֶה גַּם כֵּן מוּרְגָּשׁ לָעַיִן דְּהַכֹּל מִשָּׁמַיִם
Namely, the spiritual rung of the Oral Torah will likewise be visibly felt as flowing directly from Heaven,
לֹא כְּמוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם
unlike in this world where it operates in concealment
וְהָאָדָם חוֹשֵׁב שֶׁהוּא מְחַדֵּשׁ דָּבָר בְּחָכְמָתוֹ,
and man imagines that he innovates insight by his own mortal wisdom,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא בֶּאֱמֶת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ כָּל מַה שֶּׁהוּא מְחַדֵּשׁ דִּבְרֵי אֱמֶת
even though whatever he innovates of true words is authentically divine inspiration (Ruach HaKodesh),
דְּאִתְאֲמַרָא הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי כְּוָתֵיהּ,
for Halakhah transmitted to Moses at Sinai was stated in agreement with him,
וּמִמַּה שֶּׁגִּילָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כָּל מַה שֶּׁתַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ ,
and stems from what Hashem, blessed be He, revealed to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, regarding everything an astute disciple is destined to innovate (Megillah 19b).
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא נֶחְשָׁב לְהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם
nonetheless in this world it is experienced as human attainment.

paragraphs.text: “Oraysa v’Kudsha Brich Hu chad” — the Torah and the Holy One are one (Zohar; cf. Tanya, Likutei Amarim ch. 4): the Torah is not a mere instrument that God fashioned, but an emanation of His own wisdom and will, which are utterly one with Him. Background and meforshim: the Tanya (ch. 4) draws the contrast — a mortal king is grasped only through his garments and decrees, which are separate from him, whereas the Holy One “and His wisdom are one,” so that whoever grasps a halachah of the Torah thereby embraces God Himself; the Nefesh HaChaim (Sha’ar 4) develops the same principle at length. R’ Tzadok’s use: because “Oraysa v’Kudsha Brich Hu chad,” calling Yehudah “mechokeki” (“who inscribes Me”) is no mere figure of speech — to inscribe the Torah on the hearts of Israel is to inscribe the Divine Presence itself within them; this is the ultimate perfection of the Future.

paragraphs.text: Yirmeyah 31:32 (Sefaria 31:33): “כִּי זֹאת הַבְּרִית אֲשֶׁר אֶכְרֹת אֶת בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל אַחֲרֵי הַיָּמִים הָהֵם נְאֻם ה׳, נָתַתִּי אֶת תּוֹרָתִי בְּקִרְבָּם וְעַל לִבָּם אֶכְתְּבֶנָּה” — “for this is the covenant I shall make with the House of Israel after those days, says Hashem: I have set My Torah within them, and upon their heart I will write it.” Background: this is Yirmeyah’s prophecy of the “new covenant” of the Redemption — the Torah so internalized that, as the very next verse says, “they shall no longer teach one another… for they shall all know Me,” never again to be forgotten. Meforshim: R’ Tzadok’s wording “on the tablet of their heart” fuses this verse with Mishlei 3:3, “כָּתְבֵם עַל לוּחַ לִבֶּךָ” — “write them upon the tablet of your heart.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this future inscribing-upon-the-heart is the work of Yehudah/Mashiach — the perfected Oral Torah, engraved so deep within that it can never be forgotten.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §13): “The Oral Torah was not written down, for the Oral Torah is the teacher’s very heart — and what is in the heart cannot be written; as they said in Sanhedrin (35a). Only the mouth is ‘the pen of the heart,’ and by it one is able to bring Torah into the heart of his fellow and his student — for ‘words that come from the heart enter the heart.’” (Precisely the se’if’s picture of Yehudah/Mashiach who “inscribes the Torah on the heart”: the Oral Torah is by nature heart-written, passing living from heart to heart rather than from page to page.)

paragraphs.text: Divrei HaYamim I 29:15: “כִּי גֵרִים אֲנַחְנוּ לְפָנֶיךָ וְתוֹשָׁבִים כְּכָל אֲבֹתֵינוּ, כַּצֵּל יָמֵינוּ עַל הָאָרֶץ וְאֵין מִקְוֶה” — “for we are strangers before You, and sojourners like all our fathers; our days upon the earth are like a shadow, and there is no hope of escaping death.” Background: David’s public confession at the great assembly where Israel donated gold and silver for the future Beis HaMikdash — all wealth is truly God’s, and man is only a passing sojourner. Meforshim: Rashi (citing Midrash Koheles Rabbah 1:2) sharpens the image — our days are not even like the lasting shadow of a tree, nor like the momentary shadow of a bird in flight, but “like the shadow of a bee’s wings, which has wings yet casts no shadow at all”; and “there is no mikveh” means “there is none who has any hope that he will not die.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the shadow is but a “sample” and outline of the true form — the soul that endures into the World to Come; hence the guidance of this shadow-world is “halachah,” the conduct of “walking” through it.

paragraphs.text: Yirmeyah 31:21 (Sefaria 31:22): “עַד מָתַי תִּתְחַמָּקִין הַבַּת הַשּׁוֹבֵבָה, כִּי בָרָא ה׳ חֲדָשָׁה בָּאָרֶץ נְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵב גָּבֶר” — “how long will you hide yourself, O backsliding daughter? For Hashem has created a new thing on the earth: a female shall encircle a male.” Background: the prophet calls wayward Israel (“the backsliding daughter”) to return, promising a “new creation” — a reversal of the natural order. Meforshim: Rashi offers two readings — by the plain sense, the “female” (Israel) will court the “male” (the Holy One), going about to seek Him (in the idiom of Shir HaShirim 3:2, “I will seek him”); and in the name of R’ Yehudah HaDarshan, the “female” who until now takes only a small share like a daughter will in the end inherit everything “like a son who inherits all.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the future revelation in which the Oral Torah (Malchus, the “female”) will “encircle” and openly manifest — the receiving rung rising to be “felt to the eye” like the giver, no longer in concealment.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §77): “for even one who is fit for prophecy and ruach ha-kodesh receives it only by way of the greatest of the generation, as it says of the elders, "and I shall draw from the spirit that is upon you."” The se’if’s paradox exactly: a person’s true chiddushim are concealed ruach ha-kodesh, yet they come through a human channel and are therefore reckoned, in this world, as a human attainment. Kedushas Levi — when prophecy recedes, the light of Torah shebe’al peh begins to shine: Kedushas Levi, Homily for Purim §22, reads “kiyemu v’kiblu” as the historical turning-point from prophecy to the revealed flowering of the Oral Torah. Until Mordechai, he writes, “היה מאיר אור תורה שבכתב”; from Mordechai onward, as prophecy ceased, “התחיל להאיר אור תורה שבעל פה,” and the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah began to establish the order of prayer. His point is not that the earlier generations lacked an Oral tradition. Rather, while nevuah remained openly available, the dominant light descended from Above in a form that could be written as the word of the prophet; when that channel closed, the hidden light began to appear through Israel’s own interpretive labor. This complements R’ Tzadok’s Levi–Yehudah structure exactly. Levi/Moshe represents Torah brought down from Heaven; Yehudah/David/Mashiach represents the Torah engraved into the human heart and spoken from within it. The disappearance of open revelation is therefore also the condition for a new form of revelation: what appears to be the chacham’s own halachic judgment can carry concealed ruach ha-kodesh, while still being reckoned to him as genuine attainment and responsibility. The Divine voice has not vanished; it has entered the human mouth and heart deeply enough that the words can truly be called his Torah.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: After Levi (who brings the Written Torah down through Moshe) comes Yehudah — the perfection of the Oral Torah through Mashiach, who “inscribes it on the heart.” “Halachah” is the guidance of walking in this world (Levi and Yissachar), for a world that is “like a shadow.” In the Bais HaMikdash, conduct was by Torah-and-Prophets (revelation from Heaven); the full Oral Torah unfolds only later — man’s true chiddushim being concealed ru’ach ha-kodesh, yet reckoned as a human attainment.

p: (כד) וְזֶהוּ כָּל עִנְיַן עוֹלָם הַזֶּה דְּ"טוּבֵיהּ גְּנִיז בְּגַוֵּיהּ" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה ,
And this is the entire nature of this world wherein 'its goodness is concealed within it' as expressed in the Kabbalistic tradition,
שֶׁהוּא בִּגְנִיזָה וְהֶעְלֵם
for it abides in hiddenness and concealment.
וְרַק הָאָדָם מִצַּד הִשְׁתַּדְלוּתוֹ בּוֹחֵר בַּטּוֹב
and mortal man through his own spiritual exertion chooses the good.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּזְמַן הַבַּיִת שֶׁהָיָה גִּילּוּי שְׁכִינָה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים
In contrast to the era of the Temple when the divine Presence was overtly revealed in lower realms,
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא הָיָה אָז הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כָּל כָּךְ
and therefore the expansive unfolding of the Oral Torah was not as pervasive then,
עַד אַחַר הַחוּרְבָּן
until after the destruction of the Temple,
דְּ"הִשְׁלִיךְ מִשָּׁמַיִם אֶרֶץ תִּפְאֶרֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל" (אֵיכָה ב, א)
– wherein 'He cast down from heaven unto earth the beauty of Israel' (Lamentations 2:1)—.
הִיא הַתּוֹרָה דְּנִקְרֵאת כֵּן כַּנּוֹדָע
which is the Torah, designated by that title as is known. ",
וְלֹא זָכַר הֲדֹם (רַגְלָיו)" וְגוֹמֵר
And 'He remembered not His footstool, etc.'
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא הַשִּׁכְחָה
for through this catastrophe came forgetfulness.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַשִּׁכְחָה הוּצְרְכוּ לְהַעֲמִיק עִיּוּנָם יוֹתֵר בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה
And by virtue of forgetfulness they were compelled to deepen their analytic contemplation much further into words of Torah.
וְכָל הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת הִתְגַּלּוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי הַשִּׁכְחָה וְהַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁנּוֹסָף בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר
And the entire novel disclosure of the Oral Torah arises solely through the forgetfulness and concealment accumulating in every generation,
וְכָל מַה שֶּׁהַשִּׁכְחָה מִתּוֹסֶפֶת – תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה מִתּוֹסֶפֶת
and in proportion as forgetfulness increases, the Oral Torah expands.
דִּצְרִיכִים לְהַעֲמִיק יוֹתֵר וּלְחַדֵּשׁ יוֹתֵר
because scholars are required to plumb deeper and innovate more.
וְאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה הֵם שֶׁהִתְחִילוּ לְיַיסֵּד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אַחַר חוּרְבָּן רִאשׁוֹן
And the Men of the Great Assembly were the ones who began systematizing the Oral Torah after the destruction of the First Temple;
וְגַם בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי דְּלֹא שָׁרְתָה שְׁכִינָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא ט עַמּוּד ב),
and likewise in the Second Temple era where the Shechinah did not overtly rest as our Sages taught (Yoma 9b),
הָיָה הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה יוֹתֵר מִבְּבַיִת רִאשׁוֹן
the expansion of the Oral Torah was greater than during the First Temple,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּפִרְקֵי הֵיכָלוֹת)
as they stated (in Pirkei Heikhalot),
דְּעִיקַּר זִיוָוהּ דְּתוֹרָה הָיָה בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי
that the primary brilliance of Torah study occurred in the Second Temple period,
וְיְעֻיַּין שָׁם בְּאוֹרֶךְ כָּל לְשׁוֹנוֹ.
and let all its phrasing be examined at length there.
וְאַחַר חוּרְבַּן בַּיִת שֵׁנִי נִתְרַחֲבָה עוֹד יוֹתֵר בְּדוֹרוֹת תַּנָּאִים וַאֲמוֹרָאִים
And following the destruction of the Second Temple, it expanded even further throughout the generations of the Tannaim and Amoraim,
עַד שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה)
until our Sages of blessed memory declared (Vayikra Rabbah 22:1).
דְּרָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וַחֲבֵירָיו מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה
that the eye of Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues saw what the eye of Moses had not seen.
וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הוּא הַמְיַסֵּד כְּלָלֵי וּפְרָטֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אָז כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דִּשְׁקָלִים פֶּרֶק ה הֲלָכָה א),
And Rabbi Akiva was the founder of the general principles and specific details of the Oral Torah at that time, as stated (in the Yerushalmi Shekalim 5:1),
וְהוּא הָיָה נוֹשֵׂא כֵּלָיו דְּבֶן כּוֹזִיבָא
and he was the armor-bearer of Ben Koziva (Bar Kokhba),
כִּי הוּא הַמּוּכָן לִהְיוֹת נוֹשֵׂא כֵּלָיו דְּמָשִׁיחַ,
for he was spiritually primed to be the weapon-bearer of the Messiah,
כִּי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהִשִּׂיג הוּא דּוּגְמַת כֵּלִים לְתוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ.
since the Oral Torah which he attained serves as the spiritual vessels for the ultimate Torah of the Messiah.

paragraphs.text: The phrase “טוביה גניז בגויה” (“its goodness is concealed within”) is a traditional condensation of two passages, not a verbatim quotation from the Zohar. Primary sources: Zohar I, Introduction 3a (letter ט): “דהא טובך סתים בגווך וצפון בגווך … הואיל וגניז בגווך” — “your goodness is concealed and hidden within you … because it is stored within you.” Zohar II, Terumah 168b: “טוב איהו כד כליל כלא בגויה ולא אתפשט לנחתא לתתא” — good is when everything remains contained within it and does not extend downward, contrasted with chesed which flows outward. Rav Tzadok uses the abbreviated expression in Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar 2: “אמנם לאחר הקלקול נעשה טוביה גניז בגויה.” He independently cites Terumah 168b by folio in Pri Tzaddik, Terumah 13. Here the world’s good is concealed and must be uncovered by spiritual effort; this concealment is also the occasion for greater development of Torah shebe’al peh. Cf. Chagigah 12a on the hidden primordial light — a conceptual parallel, not the lexical source.

paragraphs.text: Eichah 2:1: “אֵיכָה יָעִיב בְּאַפּוֹ אֲדֹנָי אֶת בַּת צִיּוֹן, הִשְׁלִיךְ מִשָּׁמַיִם אֶרֶץ תִּפְאֶרֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְלֹא זָכַר הֲדֹם רַגְלָיו בְּיוֹם אַפּוֹ” — “how the Lord in His anger has beclouded Bas Tziyon; He cast down from heaven to earth the glory tiferes of Israel, and did not remember His footstool on the day of His anger.” Background: the opening of the second kinah of Eichah — the churban, in which God hurled Israel’s glory down from its heavenly height. Meforshim: Rashi explains “from heaven to earth” — “after He had raised them up to the heavens, He cast them to the earth all at once, not little by little — from a high roof to a deep pit (mei-igra rama le-vira amikta)”; and “His footstool” is the Beis HaMikdash. R’ Tzadok reads “tiferes Yisrael” as the Torah (which is called tiferes, as is known), so the verse speaks of the Torah “cast down” — the onset of forgetting. R’ Tzadok’s use: the churban’s casting-down of the glory brought forgetting, and precisely that forgetting forced Israel to delve the deeper — so the Oral Torah expands with each generation’s concealment.

” — “after He had raised them up to the heavens, He cast them to the earth all at once, not little by little — from a high roof to a deep pit (
)”; and “His footstool” is the Beis HaMikdash. R’ Tzadok reads “

, as is known), so the verse speaks of the Torah “cast down” — the onset of forgetting. R’ Tzadok’s use: the churban’s casting-down of the glory brought forgetting, and precisely that forgetting forced Israel to delve the deeper — so the Oral Torah expands with each generation’s concealment.

paragraphs.text: Tanya — galus and concealment create the work of halachic birur: Tanya, Iggeres HaKodesh §26, gives a conceptual explanation for the phenomenon R’ Tzadok traces historically. The Alter Rebbe identifies the exile of the Shechinah with Malchus being clothed in kelipas nogah, and says that precisely then “עיקר עסק התורה” is the labor of iyun and pilpul in halachah — separating permitted from forbidden and pure from impure. A halachah whose reason was previously hidden is, through the earthly scholar’s analysis, lifted out of the concealment that covered it. He adds that the supernal beings themselves come to hear the chiddushei Torah of those below, because only embodied human beings can perform this particular birur. Thus the darkness is not merely an unfortunate background against which Torah happens to survive. It creates the very task through which new depths of Torah are disclosed. This closely complements R’ Tzadok’s sequence from churban and forgetting to the increased expansion of Torah shebe’al peh. Forgetting forces a descent into difficulty, machlokes, kushya, and sustained analysis; but those are also the places where hidden chochmah is recovered. R’ Akiva’s superiority in certain depths to what Moshe initially apprehended is not a contradiction to Sinai: the later generation encounters layers of concealment that demand, and therefore elicit, forms of Torah disclosure that the earlier revealed order did not yet require.

paragraphs.text: Heikhalot Rabbati (Wertheimer edition, ch. 28–29; numbering varies by edition): R’ Yishmael said in the name of R’ Akiva citing R’ Eliezer: from the day the Torah was given until the last Temple was built, “the Torah was given, but its splendor was not given” — its radiance, its might, and its glory were not given until the last Temple was built and the Shechinah rested within it. In chapter 29 the Holy One said: “I know what you seek — you seek abundant Torah, and long for a wealth of Talmud and many halachic traditions — to multiply halachos like the sand of the sea — and to establish yeshivos in the gates to expound what is forbidden and permitted” — and in the end the Holy One consented to their request. The Torah’s full “radiance,” its Oral expansion, was granted with the Second Temple and increased in the generations after.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: This world’s good is “stored away within it,” attained only through effort. In the Bais HaMikdash, with the Shechinah revealed, the Oral Torah did not yet spread; but the churban “cast down the glory of Israel,” bringing forgetting — and precisely through forgetting they had to delve deeper. So the Oral Torah expands with each generation’s concealment: Anshei Knesses HaGedolah, the greater spread of Bayis Sheni, and after its churban the Tannaim — “R’ Akiva’s eye saw what Moshe’s did not,” he being the “armor-bearer of Mashiach.”

p: (כה) וּלְכָךְ לֵאָה גַּם כֵּן עָמְדָה מִלֶּדֶת אַחַר לֵידַת יְהוּדָה
And therefore Leah likewise ceased bearing children after the birth of Judah,
וְעַל יְדֵי זוֹ הָעֲמִידָה מִלֶּדֶת נַעֲשָׂה הֲכָנָה לְלֵידַת יִשָּׂשׂכָר
and through this cessation from childbearing the preparation was established for the birth of Issachar,
שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בְּבִינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב לְהִילוּךְ שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
who embodies the attainment of the Oral Torah through understanding in the heart to guide conduct in this world.
דְּהַיְינוּ אַלִּיבָּא דְּהִלְכְתָא, הִילוּךְ הַלֵּב בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
namely according to halakhic truth—the movement of the heart in this world.
וְכָל לֵידַת שְׁבָטִים הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר
And every birth of the tribal ancestors is a disclosure of celestial light.
וְהָעֲמִידָה מִלֶּדֶת הוּא הֶעְלֵם הַהִתְגַּלּוּת
while the cessation from childbearing represents the concealment of revelation.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַהֶעְלֵם, וּמִצִּמָּאוֹן שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ הַהֶעְלֵם
And through that concealment, and out of the spiritual thirst born of hiddenness.
בָּא גִּילּוּי הַשָּׂגָה זוֹ לָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
comes the revelation of this deep perception into this world.
וְאָז אַחַר כָּךְ מִתְגַּלֶּה אוֹר דִּזְבוּלוּן שֶׁהוּא כְּטַעַם: "בְּצֵל הַחָכְמָה בְּצֵל הַכָּסֶף" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, יב).
And subsequently the illumination of Zebulun is revealed, which is in accordance with: 'In the shadow of wisdom is the shadow of silver' (Ecclesiastes 7:12).
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הִקְדִּים "זְבוּלֻן בְּצֵאתְךָ" לְ"יִשָּׂשׂכָר בְּאֹהָלֶיךָ" (דְּבָרִים לג, יח),
Nonetheless Scripture placed 'Zebulun, in your going out' prior to 'Issachar, in your tents' (Deuteronomy 33:18),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַדְרֵגָה יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה
for that is a loftier spiritual tier:
שֶׁגַּם בְּצֵאתוֹ בְּעִנְיְנֵי הָעוֹלָם יִהְיֶה לְבָבוֹ דָּבוּק בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים וּמֶלֶךְ עוֹלָם
that even when venturing forth into the material affairs of the world, his heart remains cleaving unto the living God and eternal King.
וְאַף עַל פִּי דְּ"טוֹב לִי תוֹרַת פִּיךָ מֵאַלְפֵי זָהָב וָכָסֶף" (תְּהִלִּים קיט, עב),
And even though 'better unto me is the Torah of Your mouth than thousands of gold and silver' (Psalms 119:72),
שֶׁהוּא דַּרְגָּא דִּבְצֵל הַכֶּסֶף דִּזְבוּלוּן
which represents the rung of the shadow of silver of Zebulun,
שֶׁהוּא הַכִּיסּוּפִין לַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ בְּצֵאתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which is the fervent yearning for His divine service when going forth into this world,
דְּזֶהוּ עִסְקָן שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי מִצְווֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כה, ב)):
this being the endeavor of the masters of mitzvot as they taught (Vayikra Rabbah 25:2):
דְּעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַעֲשׂוֹת צֵל וְחֻפּוֹת לְבַעֲלֵי הַמִּצְווֹת אֵצֶל בְּנֵי תוֹרָה בְּגַן עֵדֶן מִמִּקְרָא זֶה
that the Holy One is destined to make shadow and canopies for the masters of mitzvot alongside the disciples of Torah in Gan Eden derived from this verse.
וְהַצֵּל הוּא מִצַּד צֵל יָמֵינוּ דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And the shadow exists from the perspective of our shadowy transient days in this world,
וּבָעוֹלָם הַבָּא דְּנִגְלֶה דְּזֶה צֵל לְבַד
yet in the World to Come where it is revealed that this was mere shadow,
צֵל הַחָכְמָה גָּדוֹל
the shadow of wisdom is paramount.
וְיִחוּס דְּבַעֲלֵי מִצְווֹת הוּא רַק מַה שֶּׁהֵם אֵצֶל בַּעֲלֵי תוֹרָה
and the stature of the masters of mitzvot is only by virtue of their being adjacent to the masters of Torah.
וְזֶהוּ "טוֹב לִי" דַּיְיקָא לְדַרְגָּא דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And this 'better unto me' applies specifically to the elevated level of King David, peace be upon him,
דְּהוּא מָשִׁיחַ בְּעַצְמוֹ
who is the Messiah himself,
וְהִשִּׂיג מַדְרֵגַת גִּילּוּי עֶצֶם הָאָדָם עוֹשֶׂה הַצֵּל
and grasped the level of the revelation of the essential Man who casts the shadow,
דְּהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת צוּרַת אָדָם דְּיָדוּעַ דְּהוּא רָאשֵׁי תֵּיבוֹת: אָדָם, דָּוִד, מָשִׁיחַ.
which is the absolute perfection of the human form, as is known that Adam, David, Mashiach form the acronym ADAM.
אֲבָל מִקְרָא דְּ"שְׂמַח זְבוּלֻן בְּצֵאתְךָ"
However, the verse 'Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out',
שֶׁהוּא הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁמִּצַּד הַגִּלּוּי שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which addresses the celebration arising from manifest endeavor in this world,
עִיקַּר הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב הִיא נֶעְלֶמֶת
in which the essential wisdom within the heart remains hidden,
וְהַגִּלּוּי אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּמַעֲשֶׂה וּפְעוּלָה נִגְלֵית
and manifest expression occurs solely in overt deeds and tangible actions,
אַף מַעֲלַת בַּעֲלֵי תוֹרָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת
even the virtue of the masters of Torah in this world is recognized externally only through manifestation.
דְּעִסְקָם בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא קִיּוּם מִצְוַת תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן אַחַת מִתַּרְיַ"ג מִצְווֹתָיו שֶׁל תּוֹרָה
namely their occupation in Torah being the fulfillment of the commandment of Torah study which is likewise one of the 613 commandments of the Torah.
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַגָּלוּי לְכָל הָעַמִּים שֶׁאֵין קְרוּיִים אָדָם (יְבָמוֹת סא),
And this operates regarding what is visible to the nations who are not termed 'Adam' in the ultimate sense,
דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם הַרְגָּשָׁה בִּפְנִימִיּוּת הַצּוּרַת אָדָם
for Israel possesses an innate perception into the inner essence of the human archetype,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מַדְרֵגָה הַגְּלוּיָה לָעַמִּים
unlike the outward rung apparent to the nations, ".
עַמִּים הַר יִקְרָאוּ" (דְּבָרִים לג, יט) הָעִיקָּר עַל יְדֵי זְבוּלוּן
'they shall call the peoples unto the mountain' achieved primarily through Zebulun.
וְזֶהוּ "הַר יִקְרָאוּ" כְּאַבְרָהָם שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ הַר (פְּסָחִים פח),
And this is 'they shall call unto the mountain' reminiscent of Abraham who called the Temple Mount a mountain,
דְּהוּא "אַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם" (בְּרֵאשִׁית יז, ד),
for he is 'the father of a multitude of nations',
וְהֵם אֵין מַשִּׂיגִים אֶלָּא מַדְרֵגַת הַר
and they comprehend nothing higher than the status of a mountain.
שֶׁהוּא גִּילּוּי רָשׁוּם וּמְצוּיָּן בַּמֶּה שֶׁהוּא גָּבוֹהַּ מִכֹּל
which is a prominent and distinct outer elevation towering above all.
אֲבָל דַּרְגָּא דִּזְבוּלוּן "יִזְבְּלֵנִי" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל, כ) – לְשׁוֹן דִּירָה
However the spiritual level of Zebulun is yizbeleni—denoting an intimate permanent dwelling,

which resides within the home belonging to the seed of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who called it a House,
דְּהַשְּׁבָטִים הֵם תִּקְרָתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תַּנְחוּמָא שְׁמוֹת ג) עַל פָּסוּק "יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקֹרָאִי",
for the tribal ancestors constitute the roof of the cosmos as our Sages expounded on the verse 'Israel whom I have called'.
וְעַל יָדָם נִבְנֶה הַבַּיִת – בֵּית יַעֲקֹב – לִהְיוֹת שְׁכִינָתוֹ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים
and through them the House—the House of Jacob—is erected for His divine Presence to dwell among the lower realms.
דְּזֶהוּ "מְקֹרָאִי" כִּבְיָכוֹל, עֹשִׂים תִּקְרָה עָלָיו, עַל גַּבֵּי שְׁכִינַת כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For this is the mystic meaning of 'My called ones'—as though they construct a roof over Him, over the dwelling of His glory, blessed be He.
כִּי מְקוֹם שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא רַק בְּקִרְבָּם
for the dwelling place of Hashem, blessed be He, is exclusively within their midst.

paragraphs.text: Koheles 7:12: “כִּי בְּצֵל הַחָכְמָה בְּצֵל הַכָּסֶף, וְיִתְרוֹן דַּעַת הַחָכְמָה תְּחַיֶּה בְעָלֶיהָ” — “for to be in the shade of wisdom is to be in the shade of money; and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its possessor.” Background: Koheles teaches that wisdom shelters a person much as wealth does — yet wisdom is the superior shelter, for it “gives life.” Meforshim: the commentators read the two clauses as a comparison — as money casts a protective “shade,” so does wisdom, and wisdom’s advantage is that “techayeh be’aleha,” it keeps its owner alive. R’ Tzadok’s use: the two shades are two rungs — the “shade of money” is Zevulun (the longing to serve God even amid worldly commerce), and the “shade of wisdom” is Yissachar’s Torah, the greater; in the World to Come it is disclosed that the mitzvos-masters’ service was but a “shade” beside the Torah-masters.

paragraphs.text: Devarim 33:18: “וְלִזְבוּלֻן אָמַר: שְׂמַח זְבוּלֻן בְּצֵאתֶךָ, וְיִשָּׂשכָר בְּאֹהָלֶיךָ” — “and of Zevulun he said: rejoice, Zevulun, in your going out, and Yissachar, in your tents.” Background: part of Moshe’s parting blessing to the tribes. Meforshim: Rashi (from Bereishis Rabbah 99) explains that Zevulun and Yissachar formed a partnership — Zevulun dwells at the seashore, sails out for commerce, and “puts food into the mouth of Yissachar,” who sits and toils in Torah; Moshe therefore placed Zevulun first, “for Yissachar’s Torah came about through Zevulun.” R’ Tzadok’s use: Zevulun’s “going out” — remaining cleaved to God even amid worldly affairs — is a greater level than Yissachar’s inwardness, hence its precedence; yet the essential wisdom is Yissachar’s, hidden in the heart, while Zevulun’s is the revealed joy, perceptible even to the nations.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Masei §4): "“for you are coming to the land of Canaan” — in the Midrash: “what is Canaan? A land of commerce perakmatya, in which they trade,” as you say, “whose merchants are princes.”" Exactly the se’if: the Land itself is named for commerce, so Zevulun’s worldly engagement is no descent from Yissachar’s tent but the appointed setting in which cleaving must be achieved. Sefas Emes — Zevulun carries Torah specifically into the place of ‘going out’: Sefas Emes, Sukkos 2:11, asks the obvious question on “שמח זבולון בצאתך”: why should Zevulun rejoice in the very portion that takes him away from the beis midrash into commerce? He answers that the joy and longing for Torah established before the departure protect the person after he has gone out. Even merchants who cannot remain occupied with Torah throughout the year can fix Torah in the heart so deeply that their worldly engagement does not become total forgetfulness. This is an especially apt complement to R’ Tzadok’s elevation of Zevulun above a merely sheltered spirituality. Yissachar’s holiness is visible in the tent; Zevulun’s test is whether the same inward bond survives “betzeisecha,” when attention is dispersed among markets, money, travel, and ordinary responsibility. The Sefas Emes makes the transition itself the avodah: a person goes outward while carrying an inward point that he refuses to abandon. Thus worldly occupation need not be a second, spiritually neutral life alongside Torah. When the departure is governed by prior attachment, the commerce becomes the arena in which Torah proves that it has entered the person rather than remaining only in his surroundings. This gives content to R’ Tzadok’s claim that true deveikus can be greater precisely amid the affairs of olam hazeh.

paragraphs.text: Devarim 33:19: “עַמִּים הַר יִקְרָאוּ, שָׁם יִזְבְּחוּ זִבְחֵי צֶדֶק, כִּי שֶׁפַע יַמִּים יִינָקוּ וּשְׂפֻנֵי טְמוּנֵי חוֹל” — “peoples will call to the mountain; there they will offer righteous offerings; for they draw from the abundance of the seas and from the hidden treasures buried in the sand.” Background: the continuation of Zevulun’s blessing — his sea-trade draws peoples to the mountain (Har HaMoriah). Meforshim: Rashi glosses “amim” as the peoples “of the tribes of Israel” who gather to Har HaMoriah; Rashi also offers another exposition: gentile merchants come through Zevulun’s commerce, visit Jerusalem, and convert after seeing Israel’s unified service. R’ Tzadok here reads “amim” as the nations of the world, who apprehend only the outward “mountain” — a height “marked and conspicuous by being higher than all around it.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the nations reach only the revealed “har” (as Avraham named the place a “mountain”), whereas Israel alone possess the inner “house.”

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 52: “דלאה היא המולידה שבטים בפועל ורחל כל ימיה חמדה וכספה להולדת שבטים ובפועל לא הולידה אלא שנים. אבל החימוד והכיסוף הוא גדול מההתגלות לפועל ועל כן היא נקראת עקרת הבית” — “Leah bears the tribes in actuality, while Rachel all her days desired and yearned to bear tribes and in actuality bore only two. But longing and yearning are greater than actual manifestation; therefore she is called the foundation of the household”. In that passage the title refers to Rachel because the emphasis is hidden yearning. The present discussion assigns the household-building role to Leah through her children. The two passages give different emphases to actual manifestation and concealed longing.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Leah’s ceasing to bear (after Yehudah) is a concealment that prepares a deeper revelation — every birth is light, every pause is thirst. Zevulun (“in your going out”) is even greater than Yissachar: cleaving to Hashem even amid worldly affairs. Bnei mitzvos stand “beside” bnei Torah — a “shade.” David is Adam-David-Mashiach, the essential man who casts the shadow. The nations grasp only “a mountain” (revealed height); Israel is the inner “house” — the “ceiling” over the Shechinah.

p: (כו) וְלֵאָה הִיא עֲקֶרֶת הַבַּיִת, אֵם הַבָּנִים
And Leah is the mainstay of the House, the joyful mother of children,
וּבְגִילּוּי גָּמוּר הוּא בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
and in complete manifest revelation this is the Holy Temple,
וְזֶה עִיקָּרוֹ בִּימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ.
and this belongs in its true essence to the Messianic era.
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הָיָה גִּלּוּי מְעַט בְּבַיִת לְדָוִד שֶׁבָּנָה שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And in this world there was a partial revelation in the Temple of David which King Solomon, peace be upon him, built,
וְהָיָה רַק לְשָׁעָה כִּזְמַנּוֹ דְּהָיָה סִיהֲרָא בְּאַשְׁלָמוּתָא
and it lasted only temporarily during his era when the moon shone in full brilliance,
וְגַם הוּא מֶלֶךְ וְהֶדְיוֹט (סַנְהֶדְרִין כ),
and he was ultimately both king and commoner.
וְתֵיכֶף אַחַר כָּךְ נֶחְלְקָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד
and immediately thereafter the Davidic dynasty was divided.
אֲבָל עִיקַּר גִּילּוּי שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים הוּא בְּחַדְרֵי הַלְּבָבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
However, the essential dwelling of His Shechinah in this lower world is within the inner chambers of the hearts of the children of Israel.
דִּיכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים (בִּבְרָכוֹת ל).
who directs his heart facing toward the Holy of Holies.
וּבְגִילּוּי הוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת ח):
And in outward expression it is what they stated (Berakhot 8a):
"אֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה",
"The Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in His world except the four cubits of Halakhah,"
וְהוּא עַצְמוֹ הָאוֹצָר שֶׁל יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
and that is identical with the treasury of the fear of Heaven:
שֶׁאָמְרוּ גַּם כֵּן דְּאֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ אֶלָּא יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם בִּלְבַד (שַׁבָּת לא).
concerning which they likewise declared that the Holy One has in His world only fear of Heaven alone (Shabbat 31b).
דְּהָא בְּלָא הָא לָא סַגִּי
For neither can endure without the other.
רַק זֶהוּ אוֹצָר הַגָּנוּז בְּחַדְרֵי הַלֵּב
Only that this is a concealed treasury hidden in the chambers of the heart
וּמִתְגַּלֶּה בַּפּוֹעַל בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה
which is actualized in practice within the four cubits of Halakhah,
לְאַסּוּקֵי שְׁמַעְתָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּהִלְכְתָא
in concluding legal discussions according to established halakhah.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַסִּימָן לְמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּקֶרֶב לִבּוֹ אוֹצָר שֶׁל יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
which is the authentic sign for one who holds a treasury of heavenly awe within his heart.
וְ"אִם אֵין יִרְאָה אֵין חָכְמָה" (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ג, יז) הִיא הַתַּרְעָא דְּיִרְאָה שֶׁבְּהִשְׁתַּדְלוּת אָדָם
And 'if there is no fear, there is no wisdom' (Avot 3:17) corresponds to the gateway of awe attained through human effort.
וְ"אִם אֵין חָכְמָה אֵין יִרְאָה" הוּא מוֹרָא שָׁמַיִם שֶׁעָלָיו מֵעַצְמוֹ
While 'if there is no wisdom, there is no fear' refers to the awe of Heaven resting upon him spontaneously,
עַל יְדֵי הַהַכָּרָה בְּחָכְמָתוֹ דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נֶגְדּוֹ תָּמִיד
through the cognitive recognition in his wisdom that Hashem is set before him continuously,
מִמֵּילָא יַגִּיעַ אֵלָיו הַיִּרְאָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב (בְּהַגָּהַת רֵישׁ אֹרַח חַיִּים),
whereby awe inevitably descends upon him as recorded in the gloss at the opening of Orach Chayyim,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא: "וּבְמוֹרָא גָּדֹל" – זוֹ גִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָה (הַגָּדָה שֶׁל פֶּסַח),
and in the manner expounded: 'and with great terror'—this is the revelation of the Shechinah.
דְּעַל יְדֵי הַהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּא תּוֹקֶף הַיִּרְאָה הַנִּקְרָא מוֹרָא גָּדוֹל
for through overt revelation comes the overwhelming intensity of awe termed 'great terror.'
וְיָדוּעַ דְּגָדוֹל מוֹרֶה הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת עַד אֵין קֵץ
And it is known that 'great' denotes infinite expansion without end.
וְהַיְינוּ יִרְאָה שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִשְׁכּוֹחַ מִמֶּנָּה כְּלָל
which signifies an awe so profound that it is utterly impossible ever to forget it.

paragraphs.text: “Sihara b’ashlemusa” — “the moon at its fullness”: a Zoharic idiom. In Kabbalah the moon symbolizes Malchus — the Davidic kingship and the Shechinah — which waxes and wanes like the moon. Background: Shlomo’s reign was the peak of the Jewish monarchy, “the moon at its fullness,” when the Beis HaMikdash stood and the kingdom was whole. R’ Tzadok’s use: yet this fullness lasted only “for a brief time, in his generation” — Shlomo himself became “king and then a commoner” (Sanhedrin 20b), and straightaway the kingship of the House of David was split; the full and enduring indwelling of the Shechinah in the “house” belongs to the days of Mashiach.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Masei §9): “"I have a good gift in My treasury and its name is Shabbos" — and one must understand: did they not say that the Holy One has nothing in His treasury but the treasury of the fear of Heaven alone, and of that it cannot be said that it is a good gift to give to Israel, since the fear of Heaven is in a person’s hand alone, as they said, "all is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven"?” This is exactly the se’if’s two-way link: fear is the one thing left to man’s effort, and yet it is what Heaven keeps in its treasury — so that each side needs the other. Mei HaShiloach — chochmah and yirah must continually generate one another: Mei HaShiloach I, Beshalach §2, explains the Mishnah “אם אין חכמה אין יראה, אם אין יראה אין חכמה” as a dynamic balance. Chochmah gives a person tokef — inner firmness and confidence — but without yirah that very strength can become the delusion that his wisdom stands independently of Hashem. Conversely, a person who possesses only fear without the strengthening clarity of chochmah has not yet reached true yirah; his fear can remain imagination and anxiety rather than awe of God. The Ishbitzer therefore reads “bayam bayabashah” and “bayabashah besoch hayam” as the required interpenetration of the two states: the sea signifies yirah and tefillah, the dry land signifies the firmness of Torah, and each must be found within the other. This deepens R’ Tzadok’s two-directional account here. The first yirah is the human gate — the small opening of submission by which one enters. Chochmah is then given from Above; but that chochmah itself produces a higher yirah, now born from perception rather than mere restraint. The cycle continues. Hence the Shechinah’s dwelling in the heart is neither achieved by human effort alone nor simply imposed from Heaven. The person opens the treasury through yirah; the Divine chochmah that enters enlarges his capacity for awe, and the enlarged awe becomes a still deeper vessel for wisdom.

paragraphs.text: Rema (R’ Moshe Isserles), in his gloss at the opening of Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chayim 1:1, teaches on the verse “I have set Hashem before me always” (Tehillim 16:8) that “this is a great principle in the Torah and among the virtues of the righteous who walk before God.” A person’s conduct when alone in his house is not as it is before a great king; and when one takes to heart that the great King, the Holy One, blessed is He, whose glory fills the whole earth, stands over him and sees his deeds, “immediately the awe and the submission in the fear of Him reach him” (the Rema citing Rambam, Moreh Nevuchim III:52) — the fear that “reaches him of itself” to which R’ Tzadok alludes here.

paragraphs.text: Devarim 26:8: “וַיּוֹצִאֵנוּ ה׳ מִמִּצְרַיִם בְּיָד חֲזָקָה וּבִזְרֹעַ נְטוּיָה וּבְמֹרָא גָּדֹל וּבְאֹתוֹת וּבְמֹפְתִים” — “and Hashem brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great awe, and with signs and wonders.” Background: this verse is from the “Arami oved avi” passage of the first-fruits declaration (Devarim 26:5–10), which the Pesach Haggadah expounds phrase by phrase. Meforshim: the Haggadah (Magid), darshening this verse, teaches “u-v’mora gadol — this is the revelation of the Shechinah,” deriving it from the parallel “great awesome deeds” (mora’im gedolim) said of the Exodus in Devarim 4:34. R’ Tzadok’s use: “great awe” is the fear that descends from a revealed Divine Presence — and since “gadol” (great) connotes a spreading-forth without end, it is a fear from which one can never come to forget, unlike the lesser fear a person must generate by his own effort (“the gate”).

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Leah is the akeres ha-bayis — in full revelation, the Beis HaMikdash (essentially, the days of Mashiach). The main indwelling of the Shechinah is in the chambers of the heart — “the four amos of halachah,” which is the treasury of yiras Shamayim (each needs the other). The two-way link: “if no fear, no wisdom” (the gate, by effort) and “if no wisdom, no fear” (awe drawn from Above) — a “great awe” from which one cannot forget.

p: (כז) וְזֶהוּ הַיִּרְאָה דִּזְבוּלוּן הַבָּא אַחַר הַחָכְמָה דְּיִשָּׂשׂכָר
And this is the awe of Zebulun that succeeds the wisdom of Issachar
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהוּא בֵּית זְבוּל לְגִילּוּי שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
by virtue of his being an exalted dwelling (beit zevul) for the disclosure of His Shechinah.
דְּהַכֹּל צְרִיכִין לוֹ בָּזֶה לִקְלוֹט יִרְאָה זוֹ דִּזְבוּלוּן עַל יְדֵי חִלָּזוֹן הַגּוֹרֵם זְכִירָה
for all require him in this to absorb this awe of Zebulun through the chillazon creature which induces remembrance.
וְהוּא עוֹלֶה מִן הַיָּם
And it ascends from the sea,
וּ"שְׂפֻנֵי טְמוּנֵי חוֹל" וּ"שְׁפַע יַמִּים יִינָקוּ" (דְּבָרִים לג, יט) עַל יְדֵי זֶה
and 'they shall suck the abundance of the seas' through this,
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁפַע כָּל מִינֵי חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה יִינְקוּ הֵם
meaning the influx of all physical delights of this world they will channel.
לִקְלוֹט הַכֹּחַ שֶׁל קְדוּשָּׁה הַמְקַיְּימָם וּמַמְצִיאָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
so as to absorb the holy vital force that sustains them and brings them into existence in this world.
דְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ נִבְרָא בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת אֲלֵיהֶם
For the entire universe was created for the sake of Israel who have an intrinsic bond to it,
אֶלָּא שֶׁאִם יַשְׁקִיעוּ עַצְמָם בָּזֶה לְבַד
except that if they immerse themselves in this material influx alone
יָבוֹאוּ לִיפָּרֵד חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מֵאַחְדוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
they would come to be alienated, Heaven forbid, from His oneness,
כְּטַעַם: "שָׁמַנְתָּ עָבִיתָ וְגוֹמֵר וַיִּטֹּשׁ אֱלוֹהַּ עָשָׂהוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (דְּבָרִים לב, טו),
in the spirit of: 'You grew fat, you grew thick... and he abandoned the God Who made him' (Deuteronomy 32:15),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְרָם לְבָבֶךָ" (שָׁם ח, יד) עַל יְדֵי רִיבּוּי חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, "וְשָׁכַחְתָּ אֶת ה
'". and as written: 'and your heart be lifted up' through the abundance of worldly attractions 'and you forget Hashem.'
וְעִיקַּר דַּרְגָּא דְּיִרְאַת אֱלֹהִים דְּיוֹסֵף
And the essential rung of the fear of God embodied in Joseph,
הוּא לִהְיוֹת צַדִּיק מוּגְדָּר וְנִבְדָּל בְּכָל חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
is to be a righteous person disciplined and detached within all physical worldly attractions.
אֲבָל זֶהוּ בְּיָרֵא שָׁמַיִם שֶׁמִּצַּד בְּחִירָתוֹ כְּיוֹסֵף
yet that belongs to one who fears Heaven through his conscious free choice, like Joseph.
אֲבָל כַּאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִקְבַּע שְׁכִינָתוֹ בְּקֶרֶב לִבּוֹ בְּעִנְיָן שֶׁהַיִּרְאָה מַקֶּפֶת אוֹתוֹ,
However when Hashem, blessed be He, permanently establishes His Shechinah within his heart so that awe encompasses him,
מִמֵּילָא זֶהוּ הַחוּט שֶׁל תְּכֵלֶת דְּחִלָּזוֹן הַגּוֹרֵם זְכִירָה וּמֵסִיר הַשִּׁכְחָה
spontaneously this becomes the thread of blue from the chillazon that induces remembrance and banishes forgetfulness;
אָז יוּכַל לִינוֹק הַקְּדוּשָּׁה לְבַד מִשֶּׁפַע יַמִּים
then he can extract the holy essence alone from the abundance of the seas,
וְלֹא יִדְבַּק בַּקְּלִיפָּה הַסּוֹבֶבֶת לַפְּרִי
and will not cling to the shell (kelipah) enclosing the fruit,
כִּי יַשִּׂיג "שְׂפוּנֵי טְמוּנֵי חוֹל",
because he attains the 'hidden treasures concealed in the sand'.
דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְשְׁלוּ לַחוֹל מִצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם
for Israel are compared to the sand from the aspect of concealment.
דְּמַה שֶּׁהֵם כְּכוֹכְבֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם הוּא מִצַּד הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹרָם לֶעָתִיד לְעֵין כֹּל
For their resemblance to the stars of heaven is from the perspective of their manifest brilliance in the future before the eyes of all,
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁיּוֹרְדִים יוֹרְדִים עַד לֶעָפָר
yet when they descend they descend to the dust,
הֵם כַּחוֹל גְּבוּל לַיָּם
they are like sand serving as a barrier to the sea,
שֶׁלֹּא לְהַנִּיחַ אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם בַּחֶמְדּוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם לִשְׁטוֹף כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ כְּמוֹ בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל
preventing the nations with their base lusts from flooding the entire cosmos as in the Generation of the Flood.
וְהֵם הַגְּבוּל בָּזֶה
and they serve as the restraining boundary in this.
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה הוּא כֹּחַ הַהֶעְלֵם
And from this vantage point operates the power of concealment.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה א, כא) עַל פָּסוּק "וַיִּטְמְנֵהוּ בַּחוֹל" – אֵלּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל
and as our Sages of blessed memory expounded on the verse 'and he hid him in the sand'—this refers to Israel.
הַיְינוּ דְּעִנְיַן הַהַטְמָנָה וְהַהֶעְלֵם הוּא רַק בָּהֶם
Meaning that hiding and concealment exist uniquely within them,
שֶׁמּוֹנִין לַלְּבָנָה שֶׁפְּעָמִים מִתְכַּסֵּית
who reckon their calendar according to the moon which periodically conceals itself.
וְהִיא בְּאִתְכַּסְיָא וְרָזוֹהִי כַּסְיָין כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּסוֹף שַׁבָּת קנו).
abiding in concealment, its mysteries kept hidden, as they taught (Shabbat 156a end).
וְזֶהוּ סוֹד מַה שֶּׁאִיתָא (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ע עַמּוּד א) ): "רוֹב גַּנָּבֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל",
And this is the secret of what is taught (Avodah Zarah 70a): 'most thieves are of Israel,'
דְּמַאן דִּבְלִבְנָה אִי גָּנֵיב מַצְלַח
for one born under the moon, if he steals, he succeeds.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם דְּמוֹנִין לַחַמָּה רָזוֹהִי גַּלְיָין
in contrast to the nations who reckon by the sun whose mysteries are openly displayed.
