paragraphs.text: “The whole world was created for the sake of Israel”: a foundational teaching of Chazal. Rashi, in his opening comment on the Torah (Bereishis 1:1), explains that God created the world “for the sake of Israel, who are called reishis, and for the sake of the Torah, called reishis”; the midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 36:4) likewise teaches that the world endures in the merit of Israel. R’ Tzadok’s use: because the world thus “belongs” to Israel, its abundance is theirs to elevate — to “absorb the power of holiness that sustains it and brings it into being”; but should they sink into it as an end in itself, they sever both it and themselves from its Source.

paragraphs.text: Devarim 32:15: “וַיִּשְׁמַן יְשֻׁרוּן וַיִּבְעָט, שָׁמַנְתָּ עָבִיתָ כָּשִׂיתָ, וַיִּטֹּשׁ אֱלוֹהַּ עָשָׂהוּ, וַיְנַבֵּל צוּר יְשֻׁעָתוֹ” — “and Yeshurun grew fat and kicked — you grew fat, thick, gross — and he forsook the God who made him, and spurned the Rock of his salvation.” Background: from the song of Ha’azinu — Moshe’s warning that material abundance would lead Israel to rebel. Meforshim: the verse itself traces the descent — satiety (“you grew fat”) breeds “kicking” against Heaven, which ends in forsaking God; wealth ungoverned by gratitude produces rebellion. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the danger of “sinking oneself” into the abundance of this world alone — one is thereby “sundered from His unity”; only Zevulun’s fear (the techeiles-thread) lets a person absorb the holiness within the abundance without being severed from its Source. Noam Elimelech — techeiles and the sea teach a yirah that sets a holy boundary: Noam Elimelech, Shelach §18, develops Chazal’s chain “techeiles resembles the sea, the sea the firmament, and the firmament the Throne of Glory.” He reads the sea as yirah: Hashem placed a boundary for it, and despite the force of its waves it does not pass the limit decreed for it. The firmament, by contrast, expresses a joyous love; together the two repair the person’s ‘wings.’ This illuminates R’ Tzadok’s use of Zevulun, the sea, the sand, and the thread of techeiles. The issue is not to destroy the sea’s abundance — desire, commerce, physical vitality, and the wealth of the world — but to give it a boundary that makes its energy serve rather than overwhelm. Yirah is therefore not withdrawal from shefa; it is the capacity to receive shefa without losing the distinction between the gift and its Source. The sand holds back the sea, and the techeiles draws the eye from sea to sky to Kisei HaKavod. In R’ Tzadok’s terms, that is what permits Zevulun to draw from “shefa yamim” while extracting only the kedushah concealed in it. Without the boundary, abundance becomes “vayishman Yeshurun vayiv’at”; with the boundary, the same abundance is absorbed into avodah.

paragraphs.text: Devarim 8:14: “וְרָם לְבָבֶךָ וְשָׁכַחְתָּ אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ, הַמּוֹצִיאֲךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם מִבֵּית עֲבָדִים” — “and your heart grows haughty, and you forget Hashem your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.” Background: Moshe warns that prosperity in the Land — “you shall eat and be satisfied” — can breed a haughty heart. Meforshim: the verse pairs “haughtiness of heart” directly with “forgetting”; the commentators note that self-sufficiency (as the next verses put it, ascribing success to “my own strength and the might of my hand”) is the very root of forgetting God. R’ Tzadok’s use: forgetting is the fruit of a heart “grown haughty” over worldly abundance — the exact opposite of the fear (the techeiles-thread) that “removes forgetting.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Toldos §7): interpreting Yitzchak’s blessing, he distinguishes blessings of this world from the first three, which are “מעלמא דאתי” — “from the World to Come”; “ומדת מלכות מחובר לבראשית כ״ע איהו כתר מלכות. ולכן אמר כנגדן ברכות מעניני עוה״ב” — “The trait of Malchus is joined to the beginning — the supernal Crown is the crown of Malchus — and therefore he stated, corresponding to them, blessings concerning the World to Come.” Its direct explanation of holy abundance is: “ואמר שזה יתן ה׳ שיהיה בקדושה ולא יזיק רוב דגן ותירש” — “He said that Hashem should grant that it be in holiness and that an abundance of grain and wine should not cause harm.” Of “with grain and wine I have sustained him,” he explains: “שסמכתיו שלא יזיקו לו רב דגן ותירש שיהי׳ אכילתו בקדושה” — “I have sustained him so that abundant grain and wine should not harm him, so that his eating should be in holiness.” This directly illuminates the author’s completed qualification here that, once divine fear surrounds the heart, one can receive the holiness of worldly abundance without its husk. The source does not assign the eleven curses to tribes or remove Yehudah from their count.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash §9): after describing the suffering of the Egyptian exile, he explains its “great wealth”: “שיוציאו כל הניצוצות קדושה משם כי בכל ענין קליפה שיש בעולם משוקע בתוכה צד קדושה ... וישראל יוציאו משם כל הנ״ק המשוקע בתוכם” — “They will bring out all the sparks of holiness from there, for in every form of husk in the world an element of holiness is sunk within it … and Israel will bring out all the sparks of holiness sunk within them.” He applies this to “the good of Egypt”: “שיזכו לקלוט כל הטוב שבמצרים הגם שהם מלאים זוהמת תאות והיין נשפע להם למילוי תאותם. יש בו טוב שדעת זקנים שקנו חכמה ונתבטל תאותם נוחה הימנו” — “They will merit to absorb all the good in Egypt, although the Egyptians are full of the filth of desire and wine is supplied to them to satisfy their desires. It contains a good that is pleasing to the understanding of elders who have acquired wisdom and whose desire has been annulled.” This closely illuminates the author’s qualified claim here: once divine fear surrounds the heart, worldly abundance can yield its holiness without its surrounding husk. The same source continues: “ומצד החסד והאהבה שזכו במצרים נמשכו אחר הקב״ה למדבר ולא אמרו מה נאכל שם. והש״י זוכר להם החסד ואהבה הזו לעולמי עד” — “Through the kindness and love they merited in Egypt, they were drawn after the Holy One into the wilderness and did not say, ‘What shall we eat there?’ Hashem remembers that kindness and love for them forever.” That wilderness teaching is a subsequent outcome in the cited passage.

paragraphs.text: Yirmeyah 5:22: “הַאוֹתִי לֹא תִירָאוּ נְאֻם ה׳… אֲשֶׁר שַׂמְתִּי חוֹל גְּבוּל לַיָּם חָק עוֹלָם וְלֹא יַעַבְרֶנְהוּ, וַיִּתְגָּעֲשׁוּ וְלֹא יוּכָלוּ וְהָמוּ גַלָּיו וְלֹא יַעַבְרֻנְהוּ” — “will you not fear Me, says Hashem…? I who set the sand as a boundary for the sea, an eternal decree it cannot pass — though its waves toss, they cannot prevail; though they roar, they cannot pass it.” Background: the prophet rebukes Israel’s lack of fear, pointing to the standing wonder that mere sand holds back the raging sea — a testimony to God’s power that ought to evoke awe (the verse opens, literally, “Me you do not fear?”). Meforshim: the commentators note the marvel that the frailest barrier — loose grains of sand — restrains the mightiest force, by Divine decree alone. R’ Tzadok’s use: Israel are that “sand” — the boundary that keeps the “sea” of the nations’ desires from flooding the world (as it did in the generation of the Flood); their very lowliness and concealment is what holds the line.

paragraphs.text: Shemos Rabbah 1:29 (Sefaria section numbering; other editions may divide this material differently): “וַיִּטְמְנֵהוּ בַחוֹל ... שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה שָׁם אֶלָּא יִשְׂרָאֵל ... שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלוּ לְחוֹל” — “He hid him in the sand ... only Israelites were there ... who were compared with the sand.” On the verse (Shemos 2:12): “these are Israel,” who are likened to the sand of the sea (cf. Bereishis 22:17): the Midrash adds that sand, when shifted, makes no sound, so the hidden deed should remain secret among them. Rav Tzadok’s printed reference is Shemos Rabbah 1:21; the passage appears at 1:29 in the consulted electronic division.

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 29a: in the passage on the significance of eclipses, the Gemara teaches that “Israel reckon their calendar by the moon, while the nations of the world reckon by the sun.” Background: Israel’s festivals follow the lunar cycle — the moon, which waxes, wanes, and is at times wholly covered. R’ Tzadok’s use: the moon is the emblem of Israel’s “concealment” — like the moon that is periodically hidden, Israel’s greatness is veiled in this world and revealed only in the Future; and it is precisely this hiddenness (monin la-levanah) that is their power to draw the holy spark unseen from the “sea” of worldly abundance.

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 70a: “Certain thieves came to Pumbedita and opened many barrels of wine. Rava said: The wine is permitted. What is the reason? Most of the thieves there are Jews rubba ganavei Yisrael ninhu” — so in this particular wine-law case the court does not presume that a non-Jew handled the wine. The Gemara’s statement concerns a local presumption at Pumbedita, not a general characterization of Jews or permission to steal. Rav Tzadok applies its wording homiletically to the concealment theme; the distinct lunar teaching comes from Shabbos 156a.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 156a: “One born under the moon will be a man who bears illnesses, builds and demolishes, demolishes and builds like the waxing and waning moon, eats what is not his and drinks what is not his, and whose secrets are hidden like the moon that does not shine; if he steals, he succeeds — One born under the sun will be a radiant man shining like the sun, who eats of his own and drinks of his own, and whose secrets are exposed; if he steals, he does not succeed.” Israel “count by the moon” — the sign of concealment; the nations “by the sun” — of open revelation.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Zevulun’s “fear” (after Yissachar’s “wisdom”) lets one “absorb” the sea’s abundance — all worldly desire — into holiness, without cleaving to the “husk.” Yosef’s fear is by choice; but when Hashem fixes His Shechinah in the heart, the techeiles-thread encompasses him and he draws only the holiness (“the hidden treasures in the sand”). Israel are “sand” — the boundary of the sea — and “count by the moon,” in concealment (secrets hidden).

p: (כח) וַאֲפִילּוּ עֵשָׂו שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אֲחִיזָה קְצָת בְּיַעֲקֹב דְּיָדוֹ אוֹחֶזֶת בַּעֲקֵבוֹ,
And even Esau, who possesses a tenuous hold on Jacob whose hand grasped his heel.
וְעִיקַּר שְׁמוֹ יַעֲקֹב הוּא עַל שֵׁם אֲחִיזַת הֶעָקֵב דְּעֵשָׂו
and the primary name Jacob was given on account of grasping the heel of Esau.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּעֵשָׂו נִקְרָא (בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּקִדּוּשִׁין יח, א,) — יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר
And this signifies that Esau is termed (Kiddushin 18a) an apostate Israelite,
כִּי מִצַּד שֶׁהָיָה זֶרַע יִצְחָק וְרִבְקָה שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בּוֹ צַד רַע כְּלָל מֵאֲבוֹתָיו כִּבְיִשְׁמָעֵאל
for since he was the biological offspring of Isaac and Rebecca who possessed no taint from his ancestors unlike Ishmael,
וְנִימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה
and was circumcised on the eighth day,
הָיָה מִלֵּידָה חָל עָלָיו שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל
the designation 'Israel' applied to him from birth,
דְּגַם אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק נִקְרְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (נְדָרִים לא, א)).
for Abraham and Isaac were likewise termed Israel as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Nedarim 31a).
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם לֹא זָכוּ עֲדַיִן לְשֵׁם זֶה אֶלָּא לְעַצְמָם לְבַד
Except that they did not yet merit this name except for themselves alone,
אֲבָל שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֵּן קָבוּעַ לְדוֹרוֹת שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְקַלְקֵל כְּלָל
whereas that it remain fixed eternally for generations incapable of being undone—,
זֶה זָכָה רַק יַעֲקֹב שֶׁנִּקְרָא יִשְׂרְאֵלִי בְּעֶצֶם
this was merited uniquely by Jacob who is an Israelite in essential being.
דְּעַצְמוּתוֹ כָּךְ וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת עוֹד
his essence being inherently thus and impossible ever to mutate.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאָדָם שֶׁיּוֹלִיד בְּהֵמָה
And just as it is impossible for a human being to give birth to a beast,
כָּךְ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל מִזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לְהוֹלִיד גּוֹי
so it is impossible for an Israelite from the seed of Jacob, peace be upon him, to father a gentile,
וַאֲפִילּוּ יִשְׁתַּמֵּד עֲדַיִן יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא
and even if he apostatizes he remains an Israelite.
וְזַרְעוֹ שֶׁמִּיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית מְשׁוּמֶּדֶת אַחֲרָיו כֵּן
and his offspring through an apostate Jewish mother remains an Israelite likewise.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן עֵשָׂו הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּד וּלְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת לִהְיוֹת גּוֹי גָּמוּר
In contrast, Esau had the capacity to defect and metamorphose into an absolute gentile.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מַה שֶּׁמִּלֵּידָה הָיָה יִשְׂרָאֵל זֶה לֹא עַל חִנָּם הָיָה
Nevertheless, that he was originally an Israelite from birth was not in vain.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה גָּנוּז בּוֹ הַרְבֵּה נְשָׁמוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת
for in truth many great souls were concealed within him.
וְכַיָּדוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה עַל פָּסוּק "צַיִד בְּפִיו" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כה, כח))
And as is known from the holy Ari, of blessed memory, on the verse 'game in his mouth' (Genesis 25:28).
דְּהָיָה בוֹ נִשְׁמַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, יְסוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
that within him resided the soul of Rabbi Akiva, the foundation of the Oral Torah.
וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר שֶׁבָּא מִנֵּירוֹן קֵיסָר הוּא מִצֶּאֱצָאָיו
And Rabbi Meir who descended from the Emperor Nero was of his lineage (Gittin 56a),
וּסְתָם מִשְׁנָה כְּווֹתֵיהּ
and an anonymous Mishnah follows his view (Sanhedrin 86a).
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה – הַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת שֶׁנִּקְרָא הֲלָכוֹת
which is the core of the Oral Torah—the Mishnayot titled Halakhot.
אֲבָל אֶצְלוֹ הָיָה זֶה רַק בַּעֲקֵבָיו
Yet in Esau himself this holiness was present solely at his heels,
רָצָה לוֹמַר: מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ אֵצֶל הָאָדָם עִיקַּר מְכֻוָּון זֶה נִקְרָא בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁדָּשׁ בַּעֲקֵבוֹ,
meaning: that which is not a person's deliberate spiritual intent is termed everywhere 'what one treads upon with his heel',
וְשָׁם הֵם הַחֲטָאִים כְּטַעַם: "רַגְלֶיהָ יֹרְדוֹת (מָוֶת)" וְגוֹמֵר (מִשְׁלֵי ה, ה),)
and there sins congregate as in: 'her feet go down to death, etc.' (Proverbs 5:5).
וְהוּא הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה שֶׁבְּקוֹמַת אָדָם
and it is the lowest level in the human stature.
וְאֵצֶל קוֹמַת אָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל מְעַט הַטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא בָּעָקֵב
And in the dark stature of the villainous man, the trace of good within him sits at the heel,
כִּי עִיקַּר הַקּוֹמָה שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא הַהֵיפֶךְ מִזֶּה
for the primary mass of his stature is the reverse of goodness;
וְ"סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה",
yet 'the end of action is bonded in the initial thought,'
דְּזֶה הָיָה תְּחִלַּת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה בִּיצִירָתוֹ.
so that this was the primordial inception in his creation.
וְכַנּוֹדָע (מִסֵּפֶר גַּלֵּי רַזְיָא))
And as known (from Sefer Galei Razaya),
דִּתְחִלַּת יְצִירָה הָיָה רָאוּי לָצֵאת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עִם יַעֲקֹב
that at the inception of creation King David, peace be upon him, was originally destined to emerge alongside Jacob,
שֶׁהָיָה גַּם הוּא אַדְמוֹנִי
being likewise of ruddy complexion (admoni),
רַק עִם "יְפֵה עֵינַיִם" שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְקְנוּ בּוֹ הָעֵינַיִן דְּלֵאָה
only with 'beautiful eyes' wherein the weeping eyes of Leah were already repaired in him.

and the ultimate rectification would have arrived immediately.

Except that 'to everything there is a season, and a time to every purpose' (Ecclesiastes 3:1) due to the nature of this world under time,
וְ"יֵשׁ עֵת אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַט הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם ח, ט),)
and 'there is a time wherein one man rules over another to his hurt' (Ecclesiastes 8:9),
דְּהוּא שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל כַּנּוֹדָע (בְּסֵפֶר הַגִּלְגּוּלִים),)
which is the temporary dominion of the degenerate man as known (in Sefer HaGilgulim).
עַל כֵּן לֹא יָצְאָה אָז נִשְׁמַת דָּוִד עֲדַיִן מֵהַטִּיקְלָא וְנֶהְפַּךְ לְעֵשָׂו
therefore the soul of David did not yet emerge then from the cosmic scales and it transposed into Esau.

Nevertheless at his heel shall come the King Messiah who will seize the sovereignty after him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סג, ט) עַל פָּסוּק "וְיָדוֹ אֹחֶזֶת (בַּעֲקֵב עֵשָׂו)",
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded on the verse 'and his hand grasped Esau's heel',
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁשָּׁם בָּעָקֵב גָּנוּז תְּחִלַּת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ דָּוִד
meaning that there within the heel is concealed the primordial thought and the root of David.
שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד עוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה דְּהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
which corresponds to the World of Action (Asiyah), representing consummate physical action.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 25:26: “וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יָצָא אָחִיו וְיָדוֹ אֹחֶזֶת בַּעֲקֵב עֵשָׂו, וַיִּקְרָא שְׁמוֹ יַעֲקֹב” — “and afterward his brother emerged, his hand grasping the heel of Esav, and he called his name Yaakov.” Background: at the twins’ birth Yaakov is named for the “heel” (akev) of Esav that his hand held. Meforshim: the Sages take the grasping hand as a sign that Yaakov would ultimately seize what was Esav’s (as the midrash develops on this very phrase). R’ Tzadok’s use: Yaakov’s very name expresses a “grip” on Esav’s heel — the point at which even Esav has “some hold” within holiness, and conversely the place where the hidden root of Yaakov (and of David) lies.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §13): “And in Kiddushin (18a) it is brought that Esav is a ‘Yisrael mumar’ an apostate Jew — meaning that before he went out to evil ways the name ‘Israel’ rested upon him, and he was circumcised at eight days, except that afterward he apostatized. And although with a Jew, even an apostate, ‘though he has sinned, he is still a Jew’ — this inseverability is only in the seed of Yaakov, in whom the ‘cord of inheritance’ is already fixed with ‘three strands’ the three Avos and can no longer be severed; but in the seed of Yitzchak i.e., Esav, although he was at first called by the name Israel, once he apostatized he was cut off.”

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 25:28: “וַיֶּאֱהַב יִצְחָק אֶת עֵשָׂו כִּי צַיִד בְּפִיו, וְרִבְקָה אֹהֶבֶת אֶת יַעֲקֹב” — “and Yitzchak loved Esav, for game tzayid was in his mouth, and Rivkah loved Yaakov.” Background: by the plain sense, Yitzchak favored Esav because Esav brought him venison. Meforshim (Kabbalah): the Arizal reads “tzayid be-fiv” as a hint that great souls were “trapped” — tzayid, a hunt — within Esav, among them the soul of R’ Akiva, foundation of the Oral Torah. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is why Esav bore the name “Yisrael” from birth — truly great souls were hidden in him; but only “in his heels,” the lowest rung, whereas in Yaakov they are the very essence. Me’or Einayim — Yaakov’s hand on Esav’s heel is a work of extraction, not identification: Me’or Einayim, Toldos §24, citing the Arizal, explains Yitzchak’s perception of “tzayid befiv” as an apprehension of holy souls trapped within Esav — specifically mentioning the soul of R’ Akiva. He then asks why Yaakov and Esav had to be joined so closely from conception. His answer is a principle of birur: to lift something fallen below, one must be able to reach the place where it lies. Yaakov therefore entered the same womb and “his hand grasped the heel of Esav” in order to seize and elevate the sparks of holiness embedded there. The heel is the point of contact, not the definition of Yaakov’s identity. This fits R’ Tzadok’s formulation with unusual precision. Esav can possess a genuine Israelite spark and can even conceal within himself a soul as exalted as R’ Akiva, while still not becoming ‘Yisrael in essence.’ The holy point in Esav is precisely what Yaakov is destined to reclaim. This also explains why the relationship must be spoken of carefully: the existence of a buried spark does not sanctify the shell that imprisons it. On the contrary, Yaakov’s task is to distinguish the two. The future emergence of Torah and Mashiach from places apparently belonging to Esav is therefore the completion of “yado ochezes ba’akev” — the hidden kedushah is extracted from the heel and returned to the root to which it truly belongs.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach §2): “וכמו״כ היה לעשו כח גדול בחכמה שבראשו ... שהוא הכח שיצא ממנו ר״מ שהיה שורש חכמת תושבע״פ. רק הוא בעצמו לא היה שורש בחכמת התורה ... שאין חכמתו מורה ומלמד ללבו שזהו שם תורה” — “Esav likewise had a great power in the wisdom of his head … this is the power from which Rabbi Meir emerged, who was a root of the wisdom of the Oral Torah. But Esav himself had no root in the wisdom of Torah … his wisdom did not instruct and teach his heart, which is what the name ‘Torah’ means.” In contrast: “אמנם חכמה של ישראל הוא בעצם תורה שמורה ומלמד ללבו הדרך ילך בה” — “The wisdom of Israel is Torah in its essence, which instructs and teaches his heart the way he should go.” In this passage, Rabbi Meir’s Oral Torah was hidden in Esav’s head, while Esav’s own wisdom failed to teach his heart. It directly illuminates the completed account here of Rabbi Meir emerging from Esav and his place at the root of the Mishnah and Oral Torah.

paragraphs.text: Gittin 56a: the Gemara relates that Nero Caesar, sent against Yerushalayim, saw omens that he would be held to blame for its destruction, so he fled, converted, “and R’ Meir descended from him.” R’ Tzadok’s use: that R’ Meir — the anonymous voice of the Mishnah, the essence of the Oral Torah — issued from the very line of Rome/Esav shows how the holiest attainment lay hidden in Esav’s “heel,” waiting to be drawn out.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 86a: R’ Yochanan taught that the anonymous rulings of the Oral Torah all stem from R’ Akiva’s school — “an anonymous Mishnah is R’ Meir, an anonymous Tosefta is R’ Nechemiah, an anonymous teaching in Sifra is R’ Yehudah, an anonymous teaching in Sifrei is R’ Shimon — and all of them are according to R’ Akiva.” R’ Tzadok’s use: since “an anonymous Mishnah is R’ Meir” — and R’ Meir sprang from Esav’s line — the very backbone of the Oral Torah (the anonymous Mishnayos, the fixed “halachos”) traces to the great souls hidden within Esav.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayera §9): “דכיון שנצרך להוליד נפש יצחק שנימול לח׳. והיינו שנולד ישראל. הופיע שורש קדושת ישראל שהוא ג׳ האבות. ומיכאל וגבריאל ימינא ושמאלה חסד וגבורה” — “Since it was necessary to bring forth the soul of Yitzchak, who was circumcised on the eighth day — meaning that Israel was born — the root of Israel’s holiness appeared, namely the three Avos. Michael and Gabriel are right and left, Chesed and Gevurah.” The source then explains the otherwise unexpected presence of Raphael alongside the patriarchal roots: Yaakov himself is “שפת אמת תכון לעד,” but the injury to his thigh signifies an opening against descendants who are disconnected from truth. “וע״ז בא דוד המע״ה שהקים עולה של תשובה והוא יתקן הכל. וכנגדו המלאך רפאל ... וזה מורה שנתרפא מצלעתו” — “For this David the king came, who established the yoke of repentance, and he will repair everything. Corresponding to him is the angel Raphael … and this indicates that Yaakov was healed of his limp.” This is a distinct close parallel to David’s root and the final repair discussed here: the perfection of Yaakov’s enduring truth is brought to his descendants through David and repentance. The birth in the opening quotation is Yitzchak’s, with circumcision on the eighth day.

Corresponding to him is the angel Raphael … and this indicates that Yaakov was healed of his limp.” This is a distinct close parallel to David’s root and the final repair discussed here: the perfection of Yaakov’s enduring truth is brought to his descendants through David and repentance. The birth in the opening quotation is Yitzchak’s, with circumcision on the eighth day.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Even Esav had some grip within Yaakov — “his hand grasping the heel of Esav.” Esav is a “Yisrael mumar”: born of Yitzchak and Rivkah with no evil forebear, yet only Yaakov became “Yisrael in essence,” unchangeable. Great souls were hidden in Esav (R’ Akiva — “tzayid be-fiv”), but only “in his heels,” the lowest rung. David was fit to emerge with Yaakov (“ruddy, yet fair-eyed”), but “a time when man ruled man” turned that potential into Esav — and from that heel Mashiach will yet come.

p: (כט) וּמִצַּד זֶה הוּא אֲחִיזַת עֵשָׂו דְּפוֹשֵׁט טְלָפָיו כַּחֲזִיר, דְּהַיְינוּ עֲקֵבוֹ,
And from this vantage point stems the grasping posture of Esau who displays his hooves like a swine, that being his heel,
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה יג, ה.):) — "מַצַּעַת הַבִּימָה", דְּמַרְאֶה עַצְמוֹ כְּצַדִּיק
and our Sages of blessed memory taught (Vayikra Rabbah 13:5): 'he arranges the tribunal platform,' showing himself as righteous.
דְּמִקְצָת מִצְווֹת קַלּוֹת יֵשׁ בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא י:) עַל פָּסוּק "בִּיבֹשׁ קְצִירָהּ",
For a few light commandments exist among the nations of the world as they taught on the verse 'when its boughs wither',
אַף דְּגַם זֶה אֱמֶת דְּ"חֶסֶד לְאֻמִּים חַטָּאת" (מִשְׁלֵי יד, לד) הוּא לָהֶם
even though it is likewise true that 'the kindness of the nations is a sin' unto them,
דְּכָל מַה שֶּׁעוֹשִׂין אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְהִתְיַהֵר כִּדְאִיתָא שָׁם וְלִפְשׁוֹט טְלָפַיִם
for whatever they do is solely to boast, as brought there, and display split hooves,
וּלְגַבֵּי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם נִקְרָא בָּזֶה רָשָׁע כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה ד, א)),
and regarding the nations one is termed wicked through this as they taught (Rosh Hashanah 4a).
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד הַגִּלּוּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין נִיכָּר
nonetheless from the perspective of manifest appearance in this world it is not outwardly discernible.
וְזֶהוּ כֹּחַ עֵשָׂו עַל יְדֵי שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְצָת טוֹב שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ בַּתּוֹלָדָה
And this is the power of Esau through a small root of goodness that he possessed by birth
דְּנַעֲשָׂה לוֹ סַמָּא דְּמוֹתָא וּ"פוֹשְׁעִים יִכָּשְׁלוּ בָם" (הוֹשֵׁעַ יד, י),
which became for him an elixir of death wherein 'transgressors stumble,'
דְּעַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַעֲלִים הַקְּדוּשָּׁה בָּהֶם
for through the power of concealment inherent in Israel to conceal holiness within them,
נִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ הוּא בְּאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ לְהַעֲלִים הָרַע שֶׁבּוֹ,
he utilized that very same power to conceal the evil within him.
וְלִהְיוֹת רָזוֹהִי, דְּהַיְינוּ הָרַע, כַּסְיָין
and to keep his mysteries—meaning his interior malice—hidden.
וּשְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם הָיָה לְרַע לוֹ,
And the rule of one man over another was to his own ruin,
דְּבֶאֱמֶת עַל יְדֵי זֶה קָלַט יַעֲקֹב גַּם כָּל מַה שֶּׁבַּעֲקֵב עֵשָׂו גַּם כֵּן
for in truth through this Jacob absorbed whatever rested within Esau's heel as well,
לְקַבֵּל הַטּוֹב שֶׁבִּפְשִׁיטַת טְלָפָיו
to assimilate the good that underlay the extending of his hooves,
רַק שֶׁאֶצְלוֹ אֵינוֹ דֶּרֶךְ פְּשִׁיטַת טְלָפַיִם, רַק גּוּפוֹ אָחִיד בֵּיהּ.
except that with Jacob it is not by way of hypocritical hoof-extension, but his very core grasps it.
וְדַרְגָּא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר תַּלְמִיד חָכָם דְּאָחִיד בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא
And the high spiritual rung of 'Israel,' which denotes a Torah scholar who holds onto the Torah,
זֶה: "לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי" (תְּהִלִּים קמז, כ).
this: 'He has not dealt so with any nation' (Psalms 147:20).
רַק דַּרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב, שֶׁהֵם עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
Only the rung of 'Jacob,' who are the unlearned of Israel,
בַּעֲלֵי מִצְווֹת לְבַד בְּפוֹעַל מַעֲשֶׂה הַנִּגְלֵית בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
practitioners of practical mitzvot alone in manifest deed in this world,
זֶה יֶשְׁנוֹ גַּם בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וּבְעֵשָׂו מִצַּד הִתְגַּלּוּת לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן
this is present among the nations and in Esau from the standpoint of superficial appearance,
דְּעִיקָּרוֹ הוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּעֵשָׂו, לְשׁוֹן עֲשִׂיָּה
for its core is the rung of Esau, an expression of action (asiyah),
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֶצְלוֹ הוּא רַק בָּעָקֵב וַעֲשִׂיָּה לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן
except that with him it sits merely at the heel as an action for appearances alone.
וְיַעֲקֹב אָחַז גַּם בְּעָקֵב זֶה וּמְשָׁכוֹ אֵלָיו
and Jacob grasped this heel as well and drew it unto himself.
וְעֵשָׂו בֶּאֱמֶת רֵיקָן מִכֹּל
And Esau is in truth empty of everything,
כִּי הוּא מוֹנֶה לַחַמָּה דְּרָזוֹהִי גַּלְיָין
for he counts by the sun whose secrets are exposed,
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "אֵיךְ נֶחְפְּשׂוּ עֵשָׂו נִבְעוּ מַצְפֻּנָיו" (עֹבַדְיָה א, ו),)
and concerning this it is written: 'How are the things of Esau searched out, how are his hidden treasures sought out!',
דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ כֹּחַ הַהַצְפָּנָה
for although he possessed the deceptive power of concealment,
גַּם זֶה הוּא רַק לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן לְבַד נִרְאֶה כְּרָז וְסוֹד נֶעְלָם
this too appeared only to the eye as an enigmatic secret.
וּבֶאֱמֶת גַּלְיָין וְנִבְעוּ לַכֹּל
whereas in truth it was bare and exposed to all.

paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 10b: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai asked his students the meaning of “charity exalts a nation, but the kindness of the peoples is sin” (Mishlei 14:34). The answers held that the charity and kindness the nations perform is “sin” for them, since they do it only for self-aggrandizement; and R’ Nechunya ben HaKanah’s reading was deemed best — that charity and kindness are for Israel, and for the nations a “sin(-offering)” — for “just as the sin-offering atones for Israel, so charity atones for the nations of the world.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Sukkos §21): “for all the force of their generosity and giving is not in the innermost heart, but only to arouse accusation against Israel — "the kindness of the nations is a sin"; unlike Israel, whose… giving is in joy, in the innermost point of the heart, as it says, "and you shall draw water in gladness."” Exactly the se’if: the nations’ mitzvos are real deeds with a hollow interior — done for self-aggrandizement, they become an accusation rather than a merit. Sefas Emes — Esav’s falsehood survives only by borrowing a beginning of truth: Sefas Emes, Toldos 26:3, reads “וידו אוחזת בעקב עשו” through the maxim that falsehood has no legs. A lie that contains no truth at its beginning cannot endure at all; therefore Esav must possess “something at his head,” but his end is “adei oveid.” Yaakov, by contrast, is “Sefas emes tikon la’ad” — truth that reaches and repairs all the way to the heel and the end. This supplies a sharp conceptual complement to R’ Tzadok’s image of the swine stretching out its split hoof. The deception works only because it displays a real-looking point of purity. Similarly, the nations may perform acts that resemble mitzvos or kindness; the outward form can contain enough truth to sustain the claim. The falsehood lies in making that partial truth represent the whole while the hidden interior remains directed to self. Yaakov’s response is not to deny that there is any true point in Esav. His hand takes hold of precisely that point and carries truth through to its conclusion. The distinction between Yaakov and Esav is therefore not simply ‘truth versus zero truth,’ but enduring truth versus borrowed truth that cannot survive to the end. What is holy in Esav is destined to be gathered into Yaakov; what is merely the pose of holiness is ultimately exposed.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 147:20: “לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי, וּמִשְׁפָּטִים בַּל יְדָעוּם, הַלְלוּ יָהּ” — “He has not done so for any other nation; and His statutes — they know them not. Halleluyah.” Background: the closing verse of the psalm — God gave His word, His laws and statutes, to Yaakov/Israel alone; no other nation was granted them. Meforshim: by the plain sense, the Torah’s mishpatim are Israel’s unique portion, and “the nations do not know them” — which is why the verse crowns the psalm with praise. R’ Tzadok’s use: the rung of “Yisrael” — the talmid chacham who “grasps the Torah” from within — is that of which “He has not done so for any nation”; only the outer rung of “Yaakov” (bare mitzvah-deed, seen by the eye) has any counterpart among the nations and in Esav.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Esav’s grip is like the swine “stretching out its hooves” — presenting himself as a tzaddik. The nations do have some light mitzvos, but “the kindness of the nations is a sin,” done only for self-aggrandizement. Esav uses Israel’s “power of concealment” in reverse — to hide his evil. Yet Yaakov grasped even Esav’s “heel” and drew it in; Esav “counts by the sun,” his secrets revealed — “how Esav was searched out, his hidden things laid bare.”

p: (ל) וְלֵאָה הִיא עָלְמָא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא
And Leah embodies the Concealed World (Alma De'itkasya).
וְחָשְׁבוּ: "הַגְּדוֹלָה לַגָּדוֹל" (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכג),)
and people assumed: 'the elder daughter to the elder son'.
דִּלְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן הָיָה נִרְאֶה בְּעֵשָׂו כֹּחַ זֶה
for to superficial sight Esau appeared to embody this hidden power.
וְיַעֲקֹב מִצַּד הַתְּמִימוּת הָיָה נִרְאֶה לְהֵיפֶךְ,
And Jacob, from the vantage point of pure simplicity, appeared the opposite,
דְּהַתָּמִים הוּא שֶׁכְּפִיו כֵּן לִבּוֹ,
for the simple, wholehearted man is one whose speech matches his heart.
וְרַק דַּרְגָּא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מַעֲמַקֵּי הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב – "אִישׁ תְּבוּנוֹת" דְּאֵין נִגְלֶה לַפּוֹעַל
while the higher rung of 'Israel' plumbs the depths of wisdom within the heart—'a man of discernment'—which does not break forth overtly into visible action.
וּבֶאֱמֶת גַּם דַּרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב הוּא כֵּן
And in truth the rung of Jacob is likewise so:
דְּאַף דְּהוּא תָּמִים, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ: "אָחִיו אֲנִי בְּרַמָּאוּת" (מְגִילָּה יג),)
for even though he is wholehearted, our Sages stated he declared: 'I am his brother in outwitting deceit'.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה רִמָּהוּ לָבָן לָתֵת לוֹ לֵאָה דֶּרֶךְ רַמָּאוּת וְלֹא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת
and on this account Laban deceived him, giving him Leah through subterfuge rather than openly.
כִּי מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת הָיָה נִרְאֶה לְעֵינֵי הָעוֹלָם דְּשַׁיָּיכָה לְעֵשָׂו
For from the perspective of outward manifestation it appeared to the eyes of the world that she belonged to Esau,
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת מִצַּד מַדְרֵגָתָהּ בְּאִתְכַּסְיָא
yet in ultimate truth by virtue of her hidden stature.
הִיא עֲקֶרֶת הַבַּיִת – בֵּית יַעֲקֹב – בְּבִנְיַן הַשְּׁבָטִים
she is the mainstay of the House—the House of Jacob—in constructing the holy tribes.
וּמִצַּד הַמַּעֲמַקִּים אֵין לָהּ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְעֵשָׂו כְּלָל
And from the perspective of interior depths she possesses no affinity to Esau whatsoever.
וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת מַדְרֵגָתָהּ שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם בְּלֵידַת זְבוּלוּן לִינוֹק "שְׂפוּנֵי טְמוּנֵי",
And this is the ultimate perfection of her stature which culminated with the birth of Zebulun to suck the 'hidden treasures',
דְּבָרִים יְקָרִים הַטְּמוּנִים בַּשֵּׂכֶל שֶׁיְּצִיאָתָם לַפּוֹעַל הוּא בִּזְבוּלוּן
precious concepts concealed within the intellect whose actualization emerges through Zebulun,
שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא גִּילּוּי הַמַּטְמוֹן הַזֶּה דְּגִילּוּי שְׁכִינָה שֶׁבְּקֶרֶב לִבָּם
wherein resides the revelation of this hidden treasure of the Shechinah within their heart,
וְדֶגֶם הַמּוֹרָא הַגָּדוֹל וְיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
and demonstrating that even the great terror and awe of Heaven,
שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית שְׁאֵלַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵהָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which is the ultimate requirement that Hashem asks of man in this world.
הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת בִּלְבָבָם מֵעַצְמוֹ נִמְשָׁךְ מִמֵּילָא מִגִּילּוּי הַשְּׁכִינָה
abides inherently within their heart, flowing spontaneously from the revelation of the Shechinah.
וְזֶהוּ הַקִּבּוּל שָׂכָר נֶגֶד לֵוִי
And this represents the receipt of spiritual reward corresponding to Levi,
אֲבָל שִׁמְעוֹן נִכְלַל בִּרְכָתוֹ וְנַחֲלָתוֹ בִּיהוּדָה (יְהוֹשֻׁעַ יט, א).
while Simeon had his blessing and heritage subsumed within Judah (Joshua 19:1).
וְהָיְתָה רְאוּיָה לֵאָה לְהוֹלִיד גַּם אֶת יוֹסֵף
And Leah was originally worthy to give birth to Joseph as well,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ס.) דְּנִתְחַלֵּף בְּדִינָה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁדָּנָה לֵאָה דִּין בְּעַצְמָהּ,
as our Sages of blessed memory taught (Berakhot 60a) that he was exchanged for Dinah because Leah judged a judgment within herself,
וְזֶה הָיָה הַקִּבּוּל שָׂכָר נֶגֶד שִׁמְעוֹן וִיהוּדָה
and this was the receipt of reward corresponding to Simeon and Judah,
דִּשְׁלֵימוּת מַדְרֵגַת בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר חֲטָאָם כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית
for the consummate degree of the penitent ba'al teshuvah is reached when his sins become like those solar years arranged and advancing since the six days of Creation.
וְהַכֹּל זְכִיּוֹת וְהוּא שָׁב לִהְיוֹת צַדִּיק גָּמוּר
and all are transformed into merits and he returns to be completely righteous.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 25:27: “וַיִּגְדְּלוּ הַנְּעָרִים, וַיְהִי עֵשָׂו אִישׁ יֹדֵעַ צַיִד אִישׁ שָׂדֶה, וְיַעֲקֹב אִישׁ תָּם יֹשֵׁב אֹהָלִים” — “and the lads grew up, and Esav became a man who knew hunting, a man of the field, while Yaakov was a wholesome man ish tam, dwelling in tents.” Background: the two brothers’ contrasting natures — Esav the hunter of the open field, Yaakov the “tam” who sat in the tents of study. Meforshim: Rashi glosses “tam” — “he was not expert in deceit; as his heart, so his mouth; one who is not sharp to deceive is called tam.” R’ Tzadok’s use: precisely because Yaakov is “tam” — his inner heart matching his outward conduct — he appeared to the world’s eye to lack Esav’s “power,” so that people supposed Leah “belonged” to Esav; yet in the hidden depths Yaakov is inwardly “his brother in cunning,” and the true rung of “Yisrael” is the concealed wisdom of the heart, which no outward eye perceives.

Rather, he said to her, ‘will you marry me?’ She said, ‘yes, but my father is a swindler and you cannot best him.’ He said, ‘I am his brother (equal) in swindling.’ She said, ‘and is it permitted for the righteous to resort to swindling?’ He said, ‘yes — “with the pure be pure, and with the crooked be wily” (II Shmuel 22).’ — He gave her sign-tokens; and in the end, when Leah (was substituted and) Rachel wished that she not be shamed, Rachel gave her the tokens.” (Yaakov’s “cunning” is a hidden depth used only “with the crooked.”)

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayeitzei §10): “"where the birds nest" — in what place? In Lebanon — and these are the two birds spoken of in several places, the upper ones, which issue from Lebanon, which is the concealed world.” The se’if’s alma d’iskasya precisely: Leah’s perfection is rooted in the upper, hidden place from which the revealed pairs issue — never visible in the order the eye reads. Leah and the hidden world — why the baal teshuvah can reveal a root deeper than visible purity: Shem MiShmuel, Vayeitzei 9:15, explicitly identifies Rachel with alma d’isgalya and Leah with alma d’iskasya. He associates Rachel’s revealed illumination with aseh tov and Leah’s higher hidden illumination with sur me’ra. The Ishbitz teaching on Berachos 34b (Mei HaShiloach II) adds the teshuvah dimension: the tzaddik gamur has a more purified body, but the soul of the baal teshuvah is hewn from a higher place; through the cry and broken heart of teshuvah it can reach an ‘omek amok’ beyond ordinary human daas. These sources clarify R’ Tzadok’s paradox that Leah, apparently the side whose affinity was misunderstood and assigned to Esav, is in her depth wholly alien to him and can culminate in the very perfection of teshuvah. Alma d’iskasya means that the decisive truth of the person is not always readable from the visible history. Yet the hidden root is not a shortcut around avodah. It becomes manifest through sur me’ra, brokenhearted return, and transformation. This is why R’ Tzadok can speak of the baal teshuvah’s sins eventually becoming merits without confusing him with Esav’s concealment of evil. Esav hides corruption beneath an outward claim; Leah’s world hides a holiness that is uncovered by genuine correction. One concealment falsifies the surface, while the other reveals that the surface was never the final measure of the soul. In ShemMiShmuel’s own continuation, the two forms of service correspond to the tasks of Jacob and Esav and to the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil. His emphasis is the spiritual tasks and their potential; Rav Tzadok here analyzes their realized inner affinities. The MeiHaShiloachII passage directly distinguishes the righteous person’s purified body from the penitent’s higher soul and its attainment through brokenhearted return.

In ShemMiShmuel’s own continuation, the two forms of service correspond to the tasks of Jacob and Esav and to the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil. His emphasis is the spiritual tasks and their potential; Rav Tzadok here analyzes their realized inner affinities. The MeiHaShiloachII passage directly distinguishes the righteous person’s purified body from the penitent’s higher soul and its attainment through brokenhearted return.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §66): the four classes — wild animals, domestic animals, birds and fish — correspond to Avraham, Yitzchak, Yaakov and David. Of the final two he writes: “אבל עוף אין בו טומאה כמ״ש פי״ז דכלים נגד יעקב. אבל עדיין צריך זביחת היצר אבל דגים גם כן טהורים לגמרי וגם אין בהם טריפות (רצה לומר חסרונות של ישראל עצמם אף על פי ששניהם ישראלים) וא״צ זביחה” — “But a bird does not impart impurity, as stated in chapter seventeen of Kelim; it corresponds to Yaakov. Yet it still requires the slaughter of the inclination. Fish, however, are likewise entirely pure, and they have no tereifos — meaning the deficiencies of Israelites themselves, although both of these classes in the analogy are Israelites — and they do not require slaughter.” This gives a distinct image for the completed perfection described here: David’s fish represent a state in which the defect itself no longer remains, beyond the need continually to slaughter the inclination. This is the book’s symbolic comparison of spiritual ranks through the four classes.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Pinchas §17): “ומה שא׳ ברע״מ מאן דלא יהיה תוכו כברו בכל אברין פנימאין וחיצונין לא ייעול בהיכלא דא” — “As it says in Ra’aya Mehemna: ‘Whoever is not inwardly as he is outwardly, in all his limbs, inner and outer, shall not enter this chamber.’” He explains this through its account of the complete righteous: “ולצדיקים גמורין תרין יצירות דכר ונוקבא תרווייהו טובים כגוונא דחתן וכלה” — “For the completely righteous, the two formations, male and female, are both good, like bridegroom and bride.” Thus “שלא יהיה מסט׳ דטו״ר יצר הרע ויצר טוב רק שיהיה כגונא דחתן וכלה קב״ה ושכינתיה שיהיה תוכו וברו אחד” — “There should no longer be a person’s composition from the side of good and evil, an evil inclination and a good inclination, but it should be like bridegroom and bride, the Holy One and His Shechinah: his inside and his outside should be one.” This supplies a distinct description of the completed righteousness reached at the end of the author’s argument here.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Leah is alma d’iskasya. To the eye Esav seemed to hold that “power,” and Yaakov the tam seemed the reverse — so people thought the elder daughter fit for the elder son. But in her depths Leah has no bond with Esav at all, and Yaakov is inwardly “his brother in cunning.” Her perfection culminates in Zevulun, and she was even fit to bear Yosef — the perfection of the baal teshuvah, whose very sins become merits.

p: (לא) וְעִיקַּר בֵּירוּר זֶה לְעֵין כֹּל יִהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד
And the primary clarification of this before the eyes of all will occur in the ultimate future,
וְאָז יְקָרֵב הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עֵץ יוֹסֵף וִיהוּדָה אֶחָד אֶל אֶחָד לִהְיוֹת חֲבֵרִים (יְחֶזְקֵאל לז, יט).
and then Hashem, blessed be He, will bring together the tree of Joseph and Judah one unto the other to become united comrades (Ezekiel 37:19).
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דַּעֲדַיִן הָאֲמִיתּוּת בְּהֶעְלֵם הֵם הֲפָכִים
In contrast to this world where the inner truth remains in concealment, they appear as conflicting opposites,
כִּי הַתְחָלַת הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת יְהוּדָה בְּצֶאֱצָאָיו
for the initial outward propagation of Judah through his descendants,
שֶׁבָּזֶה הוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כֹּחוֹת אָבוֹת הַנֶּעְלָמִים לַפּוֹעַל
wherein the hidden potentials of the Patriarchs break forth into actualization.
הָיָה בְּעֵר וְאוֹנָן שֶׁהֵם פָּגְמוּ הַבְּרִית בְּמַעֲשֶׂה דְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל
occurred with Er and Onan who blemished the Covenant through the sin of the Generation of the Flood.
וּמִזֶּרַע שִׁמְעוֹן הָיָה הָעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה אֶלֶף שֶׁנָּפְלוּ בַּשִּׁטִּים וְגַם נְשִׂיא שִׁבְטוֹ,
And from the seed of Simeon came the twenty-four thousand who fell at Shittim along with their tribal prince (Numbers 25).
וְהוּא פְּגָם דִּבְעִילַת אֲרַמִּית
and this was the blemish of consorting with a heathen woman.
דִּשְׁנֵי אֵלֶּה לֹא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ אַזְהָרַת אִיסּוּרָן בְּפֵירוּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה רַק עוֹנְשָׁן לְבַד
For regarding both of these, an explicit warning of their prohibition is not spelled out in the Torah, only their punishment alone:
וַהֲרֵי בְּכָל מָקוֹם לֹא עָנַשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִזְהִיר (סַנְהֶדְרִין נו).
and behold everywhere in Halakhah God does not punish unless He first explicitly warned.
וְעַל כֵּן נִתְעַלְּמָה מִמֶּנּוּ הֲלָכָה מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
Therefore the halakhah was concealed from Moses our teacher, peace be upon him.
עַד שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ פִּינְחָס: "כָּךְ לִמַּדְתַּנִי: הַבּוֹעֵל אֲרַמִּית קַנָּאִים פּוֹגְעִין בּוֹ" (סַנְהֶדְרִין פב).
until Phinehas said to him: 'Have you not taught me: He who consorts with an Aramean woman, zealous zealots strike him?!'
דְּבֶאֱמֶת אֵין בּוֹ עוֹנֶשׁ מְפוֹרָשׁ,
For in truth there is no explicit judicial punishment for it,
דְּמִצַּד הָאֲמִיתּוּת אֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת לְזֶרַע דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל עִם בַּת נֵכָר כְּלָל
because from the perspective of ultimate truth the seed of Israel has no metaphysical connection to a foreign woman whatsoever,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיַּחְשׁוֹק בָּהּ וְהִיא בּוֹ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת מַה לָּהּ,
and it is impossible that he should crave her and she him unless he possesses some latent affinity to her,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּאֵשֶׁת פּוֹטִיפַר דְּרָאֲתָה בְּאִצְטַגְנִינוּת כו' (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פה, ב),
and as they expounded regarding the wife of Potiphar that she saw through astrology, etc.
וְהַחִיבּוּר הָיָה עַל יְדֵי בִּתָּהּ,
and the holy union was ultimately realized through her daughter Asenath,
וְכֵן בְּאֵשֶׁת טוּרְנוּסְרוּפּוּס וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כ, א)
And likewise regarding the wife of Turnusrufus and Rabbi Akiva (Avodah Zarah 20a),
דְּלוּלֵי זֶה לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בַּאֲנָשִׁים כָּאֵלּוּ,
for without that root-affinity it would be inconceivable in individuals of such stature.
וְכֵן בְּדוֹר דֵּעָה כְּדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר
and similarly within the Generation of Knowledge such as the Generation of the Wilderness.
דִּלְעוֹלָם הָרַע שׂוֹנֵא אֶת הַטּוֹב וְאֵין אָרוּר מִדַּבֵּק בְּבָרוּךְ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס, ז),
For evil inherently detests good and the accursed never cleaves unto the blessed,
וְשָׁמַעְתִּי מִדִּיּוּק לָשׁוֹן זֶה: וְלֹא אָמַר בְּהֵיפֶךְ "אֵין בָּרוּךְ כו
'", and I heard derived from the precise syntax of this phrase: it did not state the reverse that 'the blessed does not cleave,'.
דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר דְּגַם הָאָרוּר אֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה
signifying that even the accursed harbors no desire for it.
וְכֵן נוֹדָע מֵהָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בִּשְׁכֶם דְּ"חָשְׁקָה נַפְשׁוֹ" וְכוּלֵי (בְּרֵאשִׁית לד, ח),
And so it is known from the holy Ari, of blessed memory, regarding Shechem whose 'soul longed, etc.'
דְּהָיָה לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת וְנִתְגַּלְגֵּל בְּזִמְרִי
that he had a hidden root-affinity and was reincarnated in Zimri.
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִתְגַּיְּירוּ אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת
Except that nevertheless, so long as they have not converted they possess no legitimate connection.
רַק אַחַר כָּךְ "גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר כְּקָטָן שֶׁנּוֹלַד דָּמֵי" (יְבָמוֹת כב).
only afterward is 'a convert who converts like a newborn child'.
וְעַל כֵּן רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רָקַק אַף דְּשָׂחַק וְיָדַע דְּשַׁיָּיכָה לוֹ,
Therefore Rabbi Akiva spat even though he laughed and knew that she was destined for him,
וְעַל כֵּן נִתְעוֹרֵר בָּהּ הַחֵשֶׁק
and for this reason that passionate yearning was stirred within her;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בּוֹ לֹא פָּעֲלָה כְּלוּם לְהַעֲלוֹת אַף הִרְהוּר כָּל שֶׁהוּא בַּלֵּב
nonetheless upon him she exerted no effect whatsoever to awaken even the slightest inappropriate thought in his heart,
וְשֶׁיִּצְטָרֵךְ לְאֵיזֶה כְּפִיַּת יֵצֶר כְּלָל
nor that he need any active suppression of his inclination at all,
כֵּיוָן דִּבְגַיּוּתָהּ אֵין לָהּ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת עִמּוֹ,
since during her state as a gentile woman she had zero affinity with him,
וְדַי הָיָה לוֹ בִּרְקִיקָה לְבַד
and spitting once was entirely sufficient for him.
שֶׁהֻוצְרַךְ לָהּ לִהְיוֹתוֹ בֶּן גֵּרִים
which spitting he required only because he descended from converts.
וְאוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד (בִּמְנָחוֹת מד.) שֶׁהֻוצְרַךְ לְצִיצִיּוֹתָיו שֶׁיִּטְפְּחוּ עַל פָּנָיו וְיִמְנָעוּהוּ,
And regarding that disciple (Menachot 44a) who required his tzitzit to strike him across the face and hold him back,
שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת שְׂפוּנֵי טְמוּנֵי דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל דְּאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם חִיבּוּר עִם גּוֹי
this was the awakening of the hidden spiritual spark of Israel who have no true union with gentiles;
לְפִי שֶׁכְּבָר נִשְׁתַּקַּע קְצָת בַּהוּצֵי דְּסוֹבְבִים לְאָסָא
because he had already become somewhat enmeshed in the thorns encircling the myrtle,
וְהִיא גַּם הִיא נִשְׁתַּקְּעָה בִּזְנוּת
and she too had sunk deep into licentiousness
וְלֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁתִּתְגַּיֵּיר רַק עַל יְדֵי סִבָּה זוֹ שֶׁתַּצִּיעַ מַצָּעוֹת בְּאִיסּוּר
and it was impossible that she convert except through this specific catalyst of arranging beds in forbidden lust,
וְעַד שֶׁיִּתְעוֹרֵר בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם דְּיַהֲדוּת הַגָּמוּר
until the hidden primordial root of absolute Jewish sanctity was awakened within him,
וּבָזֶה מָשַׁךְ גַּם נִיצוֹץ הַטּוֹב דִּגְנִיז בְּגַוָּוהּ שֶׁיִּתְעוֹרֵר בְּקִרְבָּהּ הָרָצוֹן לְהִתְגַּיֵּיר
and through this he drew forth the spark of good hidden within her so that there awoke within her the desire to convert.
וְזָכָה שֶׁתַּצִּיעַ לוֹ הַמַּצָּעוֹת בְּהֶיתֵּר
and he merited that she arrange those beds for him in sanctified permission.
וְלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בָּזֶה לֶאֱכוֹל פַּגָּה
And the concept of 'eating an unripe fruit' (pagah) does not apply here,
דְּרַק בְּזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל שַׁיָּיךְ פַּגָּה
for only within the seed of Israel does the notion of unripe fruit apply,
דְּהוּא אוֹתָהּ הַפְּרִי רַק דְּעַתָּה לֹא הִגִּיעַ הַזְּמָן
since that is the very same fruit, only that its time has not yet arrived;
אֲבָל גּוֹיָה שֶׁנִּתְגַּיְּירָה הִיא בְּרִיָּה חֲדָשָׁה וּפָנִים חֲדָשׁוֹת
whereas a gentile woman who converts is an entirely new creation and a brand new persona.
וְאֵין זֶה אוֹתוֹ הַפְּרִי פַּגָּה כְּלָל
and this is not that original unripe fruit at all.

paragraphs.text: Yechezkel 37:19: “הִנֵּה אֲנִי לֹקֵחַ אֶת עֵץ יוֹסֵף אֲשֶׁר בְּיַד אֶפְרַיִם וְשִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל חֲבֵרָיו, וְנָתַתִּי אוֹתָם עָלָיו אֶת עֵץ יְהוּדָה, וַעֲשִׂיתִם לְעֵץ אֶחָד, וְהָיוּ אֶחָד בְּיָדִי” — “behold, I take the wood of Yosef, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel his companions, and I will set them upon it — the wood of Yehudah — and make them into one wood, and they shall be one in My hand.” Background: from Yechezkel’s prophecy of the “two sticks” (37:15–19) — the prophet takes two pieces of wood inscribed for Yosef (Ephraim) and for Yehudah and joins them into one, a sign of the future reunification of the divided kingdoms of Israel and Judah into one people under one king (Mashiach). Meforshim: the commentators read the two sticks as the two monarchies — the ten tribes under Ephraim/Yosef, and Yehudah — to be reunited in the Redemption; R’ Tzadok’s phrase “one to the other” (echad el echad) is drawn from the adjacent verse (37:17), “and bring them near one to another into one stick.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the full “clarification” that Yosef and Yehudah — who appear as opposites in this world — are truly one root will be revealed “before all eyes” only in the Future, when God joins “the wood of Yosef and Yehudah, one to the other, to be companions.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash §15: “ואת יהודה שלח לפניו אל יוסף להורות לפניו ואי' (במד"ת יא) להתקין לו בית תלמוד וכו'” — “He sent Yehudah ahead of him to Yosef to direct the way; the Midrash explains: to establish a house of Torah study.” Rav Tzadok then explains: “דזה מרמז על תכלית השלימות כשנזדווגו ביחד שני הבחי' של יוסף ויהודה בקדושה ועיקר השלימות נמצא ע"י ד"ת” — “This points to the ultimate perfection when the aspects of Yosef and Yehudah join together in holiness; the essential completion comes through words of Torah.” Thus Yosef's discipline and Yehudah's power of repair achieve their unity through Torah learning. Shem MiShmuel — the future joining of Yosef and Yehudah repairs the root of their apparent opposition: Shem MiShmuel, Korach 2:21, reads Yechezkel’s two sticks — the wood of Yosef and the wood of Yehudah becoming ‘one in My hand’ — as the final tikkun of the root from which later divisions grew. He links that future unity to the healing of the sale of Yosef and cites the parallel promise that Ephraim will no longer envy Yehudah and Yehudah will no longer oppress Ephraim. This is a close complement to R’ Tzadok’s insistence that the two lines are one at their source even though this world presents them as opposites. Yosef is the visibly guarded yesod, the tzaddik whose sanctity is expressed through restraint and purity; Yehudah is the line in which failure, confession, and teshuvah become the road to Malchus. If one judges only by the revealed form, each can seem to invalidate the other. The prophetic future does not erase either model. It makes them ‘one wood’: the tzaddik’s purity and the baal teshuvah’s depth are seen as two expressions of one Divine root. This also frames the difficult material that follows concerning Yehudah, Shimon, and bris. R’ Tzadok is not lowering the Torah’s prohibitions; he is tracing how the very line whose revealed history contains grave failure can, through teshuvah and clarification, disclose a unity with Yosef that was hidden all along.

paragraphs.text: The Gemara establishes a correspondence between a stated punishment and its prior prohibition (cf. Yoma 81a; and the rule is formulated explicitly in Sanhedrin 56b): “וְלֹא עָנַשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִזְהִיר” — “He did not punish unless he first gave a warning.” The Gemara therefore seeks the corresponding azharah when a penalty is explicit. Rav Tzadok sees the scriptural treatment here as a profound challenge, then relates the concealment of the rule recalled by Pinchas to his explanation of these sins. The theological reading does not make the acts permissible and must not be mistaken for an unrestricted rule about zealotry.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 82a: Zimri seized her Kozbi by her forelock and brought her before Moshe. He said, “son of Amram — is this one forbidden or permitted? and if you say forbidden — who permitted the daughter of Yisro to you?” The halachah was hidden from him Moshe — And it is written, “and Pinchas saw” — what did he see? Rav said: “he saw the deed and remembered the halachah.” He said to Moshe, “great-uncle, did you not teach us on your descent from Sinai, ‘one who cohabits with an Aramean woman — zealots may strike him’?” The prohibition was left unstated, and the halachah “was hidden” until Pinchas recalled it.

paragraphs.text: Rav Tzadok begins with “וְשָׁמַעְתִּי” (“I heard”), without naming the speaker; the mere phrase does not prove an oral transmission by R. Mordechai Yosef of Izhbitz. Two independent PRINTED parallels can, however, be cited exactly: Mei HaShiloach, Vol. I, Balak §9 states: “אַף שֶׁתִּרְאֶה כִּי לֶעָתִיד יִהְיֶה טוֹב ... לֹא תֵּדַע בַּמֶּה יִנְהַג ה׳ בַּהוֹוֶה” — “Even when one foresees future good, one does not thereby know how Hashem wishes one to act now.” It distinguishes the present from a future clarification of souls at their root. Mei HaShiloach, Vol. I, Pinchas §2 says: “כִּי הִיא הָיְתָה בַּת זוּגוֹ מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְּרֵאשִׁית, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבוֹאָר בְּכִתְבֵי הָאֲרִ״י ז״ל” — “For she was his predestined mate from the six days of Creation, as explained in the Arizal’s writings.” The Izbizer then describes Pinchas’s understanding and Hashem’s approval of his act. These are verified printed thematic parallels for Rav Tzadok’s discussion of Shechem/Zimri and hidden affinity, not documentation of whom Rav Tzadok heard; neither should be construed as permission to violate the Torah.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 85:2 (on the wife of Potifar): R’ Yehoshua ben Levi said she saw by her astrology that she was destined to raise up a child from Yosef, but did not know whether from herself or from her daughter — and the union was fulfilled through her daughter Osnas. Avodah Zarah 20a (on R’ Akiva): he saw the wife of the wicked Turnusrufus — and he spat, laughed, and wept: spat, for she came from a putrid drop; laughed, for she was destined to convert and he would marry her; and wept, that such beauty would ultimately decay in the dust. R’ Akiva’s reaction shows the “longing” was one-sided and future-oriented — she would convert and marry him.

paragraphs.text: Menachot 44a: A man scrupulous about tzitzit heard of a harlot overseas who charged four hundred gold coins. He sent the money and arranged a time. When he ascended toward her, his four tzitzit struck his face; he slipped down to the ground, and she did likewise. He explained that the mitzvah repeats “I am the Lord your God” twice: God will punish and will reward. “Now they appeared to me like four witnesses.” She obtained his and his teacher’s names and the name of the study house, distributed her possessions, and came to R. Chiya to convert. After she showed the written account, he told her to go and enjoy her acquisition. The same beds she had spread in prohibition she now spread in permission. The Gemara calls this his reward in this world and leaves the measure of his future reward unstated.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The full “clarification” that Yosef and Yehudah are one root awaits the Future (“the wood of Yosef and Yehudah, one to the other”). In this world they appear opposite: Yehudah’s line begins with Er and Onan, Shimon’s with Shittim/Zimri — bris-corruption and cohabiting with a gentile, whose prohibition the Torah left implicit. In truth, the seed of Israel has no connection to a gentile woman; any “longing” is one-sided (Potifar’s wife, Turnusrufus’s wife) — until conversion, when she becomes “a new creature.”

And from among them emerge the converts,
דְּגָלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל זֶה לְהוֹסִיף גֵּרִים
for Israel was exiled precisely for this purpose, to add converts,
עַל יְדֵי שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל דִּקְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ
through the dominion of the base archetype of human wickedness (Adam Belial) of Klipat Nogah.
שֶׁהִיא אֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים הַמְהַלֶּכֶת בָּתַר אֵשֶׁת חַיִל כְּקוֹפָא בָּתַר בַּר נָשׁ כַּנּוֹדָע
who is the harlot woman walking behind the woman of valor like an ape mimicking a human being, as is known.
וְשׁוֹלֶטֶת בְּאֵשֶׁת חַיִל לְרַע לוֹ,
And she dominates the woman of valor to his own ultimate ruin,
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה "וְהוֹצֵאתִי בִלְעוֹ מִפִּיו"
for through this dynamic "and I will bring forth out of his mouth that which he has swallowed up" (Jeremiah 51:44) occurs.
הֵם נַפְשׁוֹת הַגֵּרִים הַנִּקְלָטִים מֵהָרַע לַטּוֹב
these being the souls of converts who are rescued and absorbed from evil into good.
וּשְׁלִיטָתָהּ הֵם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַנִּתְפָּשִׂים בְּרִשְׁתָּהּ
And her outward dominion consists of the Jewish souls who are caught in her net,
לְהִתְגַּלְגֵּל בַּגּוֹיִם וְאֵין מִתְגַּיְּירִים
to be reincarnated among gentiles without converting,
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיהוּ לָא חָזֵי מַזְלֵיהּ חָזֵי
nevertheless, even though he does not consciously see, his spiritual source (mazal) sees.
וְיֵשׁ לוֹ חֵשֶׁק לְהִתְדַּבֵּק בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
and he harbors an inner longing to cleave unto Israel.
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ הָיָה הָעִנְיָן הַזְּנוּת דִּבְנוֹת מִדְיָן
And similar to this was the matter of licentiousness with the daughters of Midian,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בְּסֵפֶר תִּפְאֶרֶת יוֹנָתָן פָּרָשַׁת פִּינְחָס
and as written in the book Tiferet Yonatan on Parashat Pinchas,
דְּחָלִילָה לַחְשׁוֹד זִמְרִי וּשְׁאָר דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר דּוֹר דֵּעָה אוֹכְלֵי מָן שֶׁיֶּחֶטְאוּ בְּתַאֲווֹת מְגוּנּוֹת
that Heaven forbid one should suspect Zimri and the rest of the Generation of the Wilderness—the generation of knowledge who ate the manna—of sinning out of repulsive base lusts,
רַק כָּל חֲטָאִים שֶׁלָּהֶם הָיָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם עַל יְדֵי אֵיזֶה טָעוּת וּשְׁגָגָה שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם
rather, all of their sins were intended for the sake of Heaven, through an error and inadvertence that befell them,
עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּאוֹרֶךְ עַל פִּי דַּרְכּוֹ.
see there at length according to his approach.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הֵם סָמְכוּ עַל זֶה גּוּפֵיהּ,
However, in truth they relied on this very premise,
שֶׁיָּדְעוּ דִּכְבָר גָּדְלוּ אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה עַל הַתּוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה וּבַאֲכִילַת מָן
knowing that they had already matured for forty years upon Torah, divine service, and the eating of the manna,
שֶׁנִּזְדַּכֵּךְ גּוּפָם לְגַמְרֵי
such that their physical body had been completely purified,
וְנִבְלְעוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּגוּפָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
and words of Torah had been absorbed into their very flesh as our Sages of blessed memory taught,
וְהִכִּירוּ בְּעַצְמָם דִּנְקִיִּים מִתַּאֲווֹת לְגַמְרֵי
and they recognized within themselves that they were entirely clear of selfish lust,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּתְאַוּוּ לִזְנוּת לְדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and that it was impossible that they should lust for licentiousness toward something that is not the divine will of Hashem, blessed be He.
וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה נִסְמֵית עֵינוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע שֶׁאָמַר: "וּמִסְפָּר אֶת רֹבַע יִשְׂרָאֵל",
And over this reality the eye of that wicked one (Balaam) was blinded when he uttered: "or number the fourth part of Israel" (Numbers 23:10),
דְּרָאָה שֶׁכָּל תַּאֲוָה שֶׁלָּהֶם גַּם כֵּן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה וְחָבִיב אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
for he perceived that even all of their physical passions were rooted in holiness and cherished by Hashem, blessed be He.

paragraphs.text: Menachos 43b: the source of the morning identity-blessings — the beraisa (R’ Meir / R’ Yehudah) that a person must bless each day “she-asani Yisrael,” and in the accepted nusach “shelo asani goy,” “shelo asani ishah,” “shelo asani bur/aved.” Background: these blessings affirm the distinctiveness of the Jew’s very being. R’ Tzadok’s use: the negative wording “who did not make me a goy” (rather than “who made me a Jew”) already hints at his point — that some Jewish souls do descend, by way of gilgul, into gentiles; hence one thanks God that he was not “made a gentile.”

paragraphs.text: Divrei Chalomot 13: “אין בך פסולת אלא צפורן אצבע קטנה גדול קמעא העבירו ובטל המום” — “There is no defect in you except the nail of a little finger grown slightly; remove it and the blemish is annulled”. R. Tzadok explains that this refers to Abraham before circumcision, first among converts: the nail, though removable, belongs to the body itself. He then contrasts Israel, whose uncircumcised are still called circumcised: their defect is like foul waste within the body, foreign to its essential substance and naturally expelled. The distinction between a bodily attachment and an extrinsic impurity is part of this parallel.

That is a structural parallel to the present extraction of good from a mixed realm; its immediate subject is permitted worldly conduct rather than the origin of converts’ souls.

R’ Tzadok’s use: converts are rooted in kelipas nogah, the “nogah lo saviv” — the shell that surrounds the holy and can be flipped from evil to good.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 87b: “R’ Elazar said: The Holy One, blessed be He, exiled Israel among the nations only in order that converts be added to them ela kdei she-yitosfu aleihem gerim, as it says (Hoshea 2:25), ‘and I will sow her for Me in the land.’”Tanya — kelipas nogah is a mixed middle that can be clarified and raised: Tanya, Likutei Amarim ch. 7, defines kelipas nogah as an intermediate realm between the three completely impure kelipos and kedushah. It contains good mixed with evil; therefore at times it descends and is included with the impure side, and at times its good is separated and it rises into holiness. The Alter Rebbe illustrates this with ordinary permitted physical things: when used merely for bodily appetite they remain in nogah, but when directed to avodas Hashem their vitality can itself ascend. This provides a useful conceptual parallel to R’ Tzadok’s language here about converts and the extraction of holiness from a mixed exterior. The categories should not simply be equated — R’ Tzadok is discussing the origins of souls and geirus, while Tanya is explaining the spiritual status of permitted worldly vitality — but the underlying structure is similar. A mixed domain is not fixed by its present location. Its hidden good can be separated from the evil surrounding it and incorporated into kedushah. That model helps explain why R’ Tzadok can describe a soul or spark as caught in an alien environment without treating the environment itself as holy. The point of the descent is birur: once the good is truly detached from the old identification, it does not remain a sanctified fragment of the shell; it rises into a new belonging.

The Gemara explains that although they themselves did not see, their mazal saw; Ravina infers the general rule, “Even though he does not see, his mazal sees.” Rav Tzadok applies that distinction here to an attraction whose deeper root is not consciously perceived.

paragraphs.text: Tiferes Yehonasan (Parashas Pinchas) — R’ Yonasan Eybeschutz asks why Moav sent the daughters of Midyan to entice Israel rather than their own daughters, and explains (per his approach) that Balak — a greater diviner than Bilaam — foresaw that from a union of an Israelite with a daughter of Moav would issue the one destined to “remove wickedness from the world”: namely Boaz and Ruth the Moabite, from whom came David HaMelech, who would “cast Moav to the ground.” R’ Tzadok cites this to show that even those apparent “sins” were, at root, “for the sake of Heaven” (see there at length).

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: “Shelo asani goy”: some Jewish souls come by reincarnation into gentiles — distinct from a convert’s soul, which is from another chamber. Converts are kelipas nogah, turning from evil to good, extracted from the “woman of harlotry”; and even a soul caught in her net has a hidden longing to cleave to Israel. So too with Midyan: the generation of knowledge, refined by Torah and mann, could not truly lust — which is why Bilaam’s eye was blinded.

And he gave counsel to cause them to stumble through the daughters of Midian,

for only when both the man and woman among the Children of Israel are of holy seed, cleaving unto holiness, and termed 'children of the Living God,'
כָּל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם הֵם פְּעֻלַּת צַדִּיק לְחַיִּים וְדָבוּק בְּחַיּוּת חֵי הָעוֹלָמִים
are all of their conjugal unions the labor of the righteous unto life, bound up with the vitality of the Life of Worlds,
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁיִּדְבַּק בְּבַת אֵל נֵכָר שֶׁהִיא מִסִּטְרָא דְּמוֹתָא
whereas when one cleaves unto the daughter of an alien god who derives from the side of death,
גָּרַם מִיתָה לָהֶם וּלְכ"ד (עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה) אֶלֶף
he brought about death upon themselves and upon twenty-four thousand,
כִּי בִּהְיוֹת וַלְדָהּ כְּמוֹתָהּ
because since her offspring shares her gentile status.
הֲרֵי אֵין זֶה נִקְרָא רֹבַע יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל מַה שֶּׁבָּא לְגוּף הַגּוֹיָה
that which enters the body of the gentile woman is not termed 'the procreative seed of Israel' at all.
הוּא יָדַע זֶה דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּתְחַבְּרוּ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ אֵיזֶה שַׁיָּיכוּת
He (Balaam) knew that it would be impossible for them to connect unless there existed some spiritual affinity,
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "לְכָה אִיעָצְךָ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה הָעָם הַזֶּה לְעַמְּךָ בְּאַחֲרִית וְגוֹמֵר",
and this is what he meant when saying: "Come, I will counsel you what this people shall do to your people in the end of days" (Numbers 24:14),
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה דָּרְשׁוּ: "אִיעָצְךָ" – עֵצָה דִּזְנוּת
and our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded: "I will counsel you" refers to the scheme of licentiousness.
וְלִכְאוֹרָה הֲרֵי סִיּוּם הַכָּתוּב אֵינוֹ כֵּן
yet seemingly the conclusion of that verse does not indicate this.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת "אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה וְגוֹמֵר" הָיָה עַל יְדֵי דָּוִד וּמָשִׁיחַ הַבָּאִין מִזֶּרַע רוּת
However, in truth "what this people shall do, etc." was fulfilled through David and the Messiah who descend from Ruth.
שֶׁהָיָה עַל יְדֵי הִתְחַבְּרוּת עִם בְּנוֹת מוֹאָב
which came about through union with the daughters of Moab.
וְהִתְחַבְּרוּת מַחְלוֹן וְכִלְיוֹן הָיָה קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּתְגַּיְּירוּ,
And the union of Machlon and Chilyon occurred prior to their conversion,
דְּאַחַר כָּךְ הוּא שֶׁנִּתְגַּיְּירָה רוּת
since Ruth converted only afterward,
וְהֵם מֵתוּ בֶּאֱמֶת בְּלֹא בָנִים
and they indeed died childless,
אֲבָל הֵם גָּרְמוּ לְיִבּוּם וּגְאוּלַּת בֹּעַז וְהוֹלָדַת זֶרַע קֹדֶשׁ אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיְּירָה
yet they brought about the levirate redemption of Boaz and the birth of holy seed after she converted,
וְהֵם רָאוּ זֶה מֵאִצְטַגְנִינוּתָם
and they foresaw this through their astrological vision,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בְּסֵפֶר תִּפְאֶרֶת יוֹנָתָן שָׁם
just as written in Tiferet Yonatan there,
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה טָעָה זִמְרִי גַּם כֵּן, עַיֵּין שָׁם עַל פִּי דַּרְכּוֹ.
that through this reasoning Zimri also erred, see there according to his approach.
וּבִלְעָם יָדַע דְּזֶה יִהְיֶה בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים וַעֲדַיִן לֹא הִגִּיעַ עִתּוֹ,
And Balaam knew that this was destined only for the end of days and its time had not yet arrived,
וִיעָצוֹ שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה עַתָּה מַה שֶּׁיַּעֲשׂוּ לְעַמּוֹ וְגוֹמֵר בְּהִתְחַבְּרוּת לִבְנוֹתָיו
so he advised him to enact now prematurely that which they would ultimately do to his nation by uniting with his daughters,
וְעַתָּה שֶׁהוּא פַּגָּה וּבְלֹא גֵּירוּת יִדְבְּקוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּסִטְרָא דְּמוֹתָא
and that now, being unripe and devoid of valid conversion, they would thereby cling unto the realm of death.
וְלֹא הִגִּיעַ עֵת הַתִּיקּוּן עֲדַיִן כְּבִימֵי בֹּעַז
the era of rectification having not yet arrived as it did in the days of Boaz.
וְהֵם טָעוּ בָּזֶה וְלֹא יָדְעוּ דְּיָלְדָהּ כְּמוֹתָהּ,
And they stumbled in this and did not internalize that her child retains her gentile status,
וְחָשְׁבוּ דְּיַכְנִיסוּם לִקְדוּשָּׁה
assuming that they would draw them into holiness.
כְּשֶׁהִרְגִּישׁוּ הַחֵשֶׁק בְּקִרְבָּם עַל יְדֵי רִישׁ אֵיזֶה שַׁיָּיכוּת
when they experienced the passionate desire within them arising from some latent primal connection.
וְכַיָּדוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה דִּבְכָזְבִּי הָיָה נִיצוֹץ דִּינָה
And as is known from the holy Ari, of blessed memory, that within Cozbi resided a spark of Dinah.
וְכֵן מִסְּתָמָא בִּשְׁאָר בְּנוֹת מִדְיָן נִתְחַלְּקוּ עַנְפֵי נִיצוֹץ זֶה וְכַיּוֹצֵא
and so presumably among the rest of the Midianite women branches of this spark and similar sparks were dispersed.
כִּי עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁנִּתְגַּדֵּל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּמִדְיָן
For regarding Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, developing in Midian,
וְנָשָׂא בַּת יִתְרוֹ כֹּהֵן מִדְיָן הָרֹאשׁ וְהַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבָּהֶם
and marrying the daughter of Jethro, priest of Midian, their foremost and greatest leader,
וְהוּא נִתְגַּיֵּיר וְזָכָה שֶׁנִּקְרָא פָּרָשָׁה בַּתּוֹרָה עַל שְׁמוֹ פָּרָשַׁת יִתְרוֹ,
who converted and merited that a parashah in the Torah be named after him—Parashat Yitro.
וּבְאוֹתָהּ פָּרָשָׁה נֶאֶמְרָה מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
and in that very parashah the Giving of the Torah was recounted.
דְּעִנְיַן שֶׁנִּמְכַּר יוֹסֵף לַמִּדְיָנִים
And regarding Joseph being sold to the Midianites,
וְאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (יִתְרוֹ סח עַמּוּד א) מֹשֶׁה וְיוֹסֵף בְּרָזָא חָד
and they stated in the Zohar (Yitro 68a) that Moses and Joseph are of one unified secret.
וְכֹהֵן מִדְיָן רָזָא דְּאֵשֶׁת מִדְיָנִים, עַיֵּין שָׁם
and the priest of Midian embodies the mystery of the 'contentious woman' (eshet medanim), see there.
וְהָעִנְיָן פֵּירֵשׁ בְּלִקּוּטֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד יְסוֹד אַבָּא שֶׁבִּקְדוּשָּׁה
And this concept was explained in Likkutei Torah that it corresponds to the Yesod of Abba (Father/Wisdom) in holiness,
דְּשָׁם תֹּקֶף הָאַהֲבָה דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין
where supreme love abides such that they never part,
וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ בַּקְּלִיפָּה אֵשֶׁת מִדְיָנִים "וְיִתְפָּרְדוּ וְגוֹמֵר", עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּאוֹרֶךְ.
and facing it in the shell is the contentious woman who causes separation, see there at length.

paragraphs.text: Hoshea 2:1: “וְהָיָה מִסְפַּר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּחוֹל הַיָּם… וְהָיָה בִּמְקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם לֹא עַמִּי אַתֶּם, יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם בְּנֵי אֵל חָי” — “and the number of the Children of Israel shall be like the sand of the sea… and it shall be, in the place where it was said to them, ‘you are not My people,’ it shall be said to them, ‘sons of the living God.’” Background: Hoshea’s word of consolation — Israel, though rebuked, will be restored and named “sons of the living God” (the Sages take this as proof that even when called “not My people” they remain His children). R’ Tzadok’s use: only among Israel — both partners “of holy seed,” called “sons of the living God” — is a marital union “the deed of a tzaddik, unto life,” bound to the vitality of the Life of the worlds.

paragraphs.text: Mishlei 10:16: “פְּעֻלַּת צַדִּיק לְחַיִּים, תְּבוּאַת רָשָׁע לְחַטָּאת” — “the wage of a tzaddik is unto life; the produce of a wicked man is unto sin.” Background: Mishlei contrasts the fruits of the righteous (life) with those of the wicked (sin). R’ Tzadok’s use: he reads “peulas tzaddik l’chaim” of the marital act itself — among Israel it is “a deed of a tzaddik, unto life”; but with “the daughter of a foreign god” the same act becomes “tevu’as rasha l’chatas,” bound to the side of death.

paragraphs.text: Malachi 2:11: “בָּגְדָה יְהוּדָה… כִּי חִלֵּל יְהוּדָה קֹדֶשׁ ה׳ אֲשֶׁר אָהֵב, וּבָעַל בַּת אֵל נֵכָר” — “Yehudah has dealt treacherously… for Yehudah has profaned the holiness of Hashem which He loves, and has married the daughter of a foreign god.” Background: Malachi rebukes the returnees for intermarriage — “marrying the daughter of a foreign god.” Meforshim: the Sages apply “bas El neichar” to the gentile woman and to the very charge of the Zimri episode (Sanhedrin 82a). R’ Tzadok’s use: cleaving to “the daughter of a foreign god” is “from the side of death” — it brought death upon the 24,000, for the offspring “is like her” and never counts as the “seed of Israel.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §69): on Rivkah’s “I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Cheis,” he explains the Midrash’s image of their repulsive smell. “דבר שהנשמה נהנית בו זה הריח, ולכך הוא בחוטם ששם משכן הנשמה כמ״ש נשמת חיים באפו” — “What does the soul derive pleasure from? Scent. Therefore it is in the nose, for there is the dwelling of the soul, as it says, ‘the breath of life in his nostrils.’” The source develops the pleasant fragrance of Torah and Israel — even Israel’s sinners — as a sign of true life, and contrasts it with the spiritual stench of promiscuity. It ends: “וזהו אם לוקח יעקב שהוא החיים הנצחיים כמ״ש יעקב לא מת אשה מבנות כו׳ רק מחרן כי שם היו שמורים מזנות” — “This is Rivkah’s objection: if Yaakov, who is eternal life, as they said, ‘Yaakov did not die,’ takes a wife from the daughters of Cheis … he should take one only from Charan, because there they were guarded from promiscuity.” This is a distinct parallel to the completed contrast here between Israel’s attachment to the Life of the worlds and a union that produces attachment to the side of death. It makes no claim that Tzipporah conveyed a faint external vitality to Moshe.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §45): “"it is the way of the man to conquer and not the woman"… and therefore the entire building of the House of David came about through an arousal from the woman — like the daughters of Lot, and Tamar, and Rus, and the wife of Yishai.” Exactly the se’if’s hidden truth: the very “joining” Bilaam exploited is the channel through which the House of David was in fact destined to be built — only that he forced the hour before its time.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §52): “"and Rus the Moaviah her daughter-in-law with her, who returned" — regarding her the term "returned" is not apt but "came"; only that the intensity of her righteousness made her equal to Naomi, and "returned" — as though she had been an Israelite from birth, from the womb.” Exactly the se’if’s “after she had converted”: what Bilaam sought prematurely, Rus attained in its time — so completely that Scripture speaks of her as a returner, not a newcomer.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 106a: “‘Come, I will counsel you what this people will do to your people’ (Bamidbar 24:14) — Bilaam advised Balak: the God of these Israel hates immorality; set out women before them in harlotry and they will stumble.” (The “counsel of harlotry” — the daughters of Moav and Midyan.)  Mei HaShiloach — a holy potential does not become permissible before its proper time, person, and place: Mei HaShiloach I, Shemini §5, formulates a principle especially important for this se’if: a person must discern “העת והנפש והמקום” so that an act is aligned with the will of Hashem, because a middah or act that is right in one setting is not thereby fit at all times. He illustrates this from Pinchas: the law of kana’in pog’in bo applied only at the exact moment of the act; had the circumstances changed, the legal and spiritual judgment would have changed with them. The Ishbitzer therefore demands not only intensity but exact timing, and the ability to leave a middah immediately when its proper moment passes. This is a powerful safeguard for R’ Tzadok’s discussion of Bilaam’s counsel. Bilaam perceived a future truth — that kedushah, Davidic kingship, and ultimately Mashiach would emerge through Moav — and weaponized that truth by forcing it into the wrong time and form, before conversion and outside the Torah’s permitted order. The later holiness of Rus does not retroactively make the earlier union permissible. It proves the opposite: a potential that belongs to Divine purpose must still arrive through the divinely appointed gate. In Ishbitz terms, knowing a hidden root is never enough; one must also know the et, nefesh, and makom. Otherwise a glimpse of future holiness becomes precisely the temptation by which a person attaches himself to the side of death.
