paragraphs.text: Zohar, Yisro 68a: R’ Abba said: it is not written of Yisro “priest of On” but “priest of Midyan” — it is all one; at first he was called “priest of On” Yosef’s father-in-law, and afterward “priest of Midyan” — and “priest of Midyan” hints at the secret of “the woman of strife eishes medanim.” Likkutei Torah (of the Arizal), beginning of Parashas Yisro: Know that there is in the Sitra Achra a “priest of Midyan,” corresponding to Yesod Abba of holiness; for there in holiness it is love, but in the kelipah it is enmity and strife — and no light was granted to unite them, and they remained in separation — this is “the workers of iniquity shall be scattered”; whereas above, in the secret of Abba and Imma, “they never part.” Yesod Abba is the root of undivided love; its counterfeit in the kelipah is “the woman of strife,” whose “workers of iniquity are scattered.”

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 92:10: “כִּי הִנֵּה אֹיְבֶיךָ ה׳, כִּי הִנֵּה אֹיְבֶיךָ יֹאבֵדוּ, יִתְפָּרְדוּ כָּל פֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן” — “for behold, Your enemies, Hashem, for behold, Your enemies shall perish; all evildoers shall be scattered.” Background: from the Psalm of the Shabbos day — the wicked, though they flourish for a time, are ultimately scattered and destroyed. R’ Tzadok’s use: the “husk” opposite Yesod Abba is the “woman of strife” (eishes medanim) — where the holy “love that never parts” becomes its very opposite, “yispardu kol po’alei aven,” a scattering; the intensity that binds inseparably in holiness is, in the shell, a strife that divides.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Bilaam’s counsel to entice via the daughters of Midyan rested on a hidden truth: the very “joining with the daughters of Moav” would one day yield David and Mashiach (through Rus, after conversion). Bilaam knew the time had not come — the women were “unripe,” without conversion — so he induced the union prematurely, cleaving to the “side of death.” Kozbi held a spark of Dinah; Moshe/Yosef and the “priest of Midyan” are the secret of Yesod Abba vs. its “husk,” the “woman of strife.”

p: (לד) וְאַחַר שֶׁזָּכְתָה לֵאָה לִזְבוּלֻן דְּ"יִזְבְּלֵנִי",
And after Leah merited Zebulun of whom she said "he will dwell with me (yizbeleni),"
אִלּוּ הוֹלִידָה אַחַר כָּךְ גַּם אֶת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא הַיְסוֹד דִּקְדוּשָּׁה
had she subsequently also given birth to Joseph who is the Yesod of holiness,
וּמִצַּד חִבּוּר לֵאָה עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה נִקְרָא יְסוֹד אַבָּא
and from the perspective of Leah's union with Israel would have been termed the Yesod of Abba,
הָיָה תַּכְלִית הַתִּיקּוּן דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין לְגַמְרֵי
there would have been the ultimate rectification of never being separated at all,
וְתֹקֶף הָאַהֲבָה דְּגַם כָּל הַשְּׁבָטִים הָיוּ אוֹהֲבִים אוֹתוֹ,
and the intensity of love such that all the tribes would likewise have loved him.
וְהָיוּ מִתְאַחֲדִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד
and they would have unified as is destined for the future.
כִּי יְסוֹד אַבָּא נִקְרָא הַיּוֹצֵא מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה
For the Yesod of Abba is that which emanates from the realm of Chokhmah (Wisdom),
לֹא כִּיסוֹד זְעֵיר שֶׁהוּא שֵׁשׁ קְצוֹת דְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
unlike the Yesod of Zeir Anpin which comprises the six spatial extremities corresponding to the six days of action.
שֶׁיּוֹצֵא מִצַּד כֹּחַ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה לְבַד
emanating strictly from the power of practical deed.
דְּזֶהוּ עִנְיַן צַדִּיק שֶׁעִיקָּרוֹ בְּמַעֲשֶׂה וְהַגְדָּרָה
For this is the concept of a tzaddik whose primary service lies in action and moral boundaries,
כְּיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁעִיקַּר מַדְרֵגָתוֹ הַגְדָּרַת הַמַּעֲשִׂים
like Joseph the Righteous whose core spiritual level was the restraint and guarding of deeds,
וְעַל כֵּן הֵבִיא דִּבַּת הַשְּׁבָטִים רָעָה
and therefore he brought the evil report of the tribes
שֶׁאֵינָם מוּגְדָּרִים בְּמַעֲשֶׂה כָּמוֹהוּ.
for not appearing as rigorously guarded in outward deed as he was.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הֵם דְּבוּקִים בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים וְכָל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
Yet in truth they were inseparably bound to the living God and all their deeds were for the sake of Heaven,
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּגְלֶה שֶׁל הַמַּעֲשֶׂה לֹא כֵן
and even though the outward appearance of the action did not seem so,
הַמַּשְׂכִּיל יָבִין דְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבָם בֶּאֱמֶת דָּבוּק בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
the discerning person will understand that the deep recesses of their heart were truly cleaving to Him, blessed be He.
וְזֶהוּ דְּרָשַׁת דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק
And this is the exposition of the interpreters of esoteric traces (dorshei reshumot) in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 104b),
דְּכוּלָּם יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
that all of them possess a share in the World to Come.
כָּל אוֹתָם שֶׁהֵם מִזֶּרַע אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב חוּץ מִבִּלְעָם
namely all those of the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, excluding Balaam.
וּ"רְשׁוּמוֹת" נִקְרָא דַּרְגָּא דְּחָכְמָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִבִּינָה שֶׁהוּא עוֹלָם הַבָּא כַּנּוֹדָע
And 'reshumot' refers to the rung of Chokhmah which transcends Binah (the World to Come), as is known,
וְהוּא לִבָּא דְּשָׁם הַהַרְגָּשָׁה
while Binah is the heart where inner perception resides,
אֲבָל חָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ אֵינָהּ מוּרְגֶּשֶׁת
yet Chokhmah in the mind is not tangibly felt,
רַק הָרְשִׁימוּ מִמֶּנָּה מוּרְגָּשׁ בַּלֵּב
only its subtle impression is felt in the heart.
שֶׁרִשּׁוּמוֹ נִיכָּר מִצַּד חִבּוּר מוֹחָא וְלִבָּא שֶׁהֵם תְּרֵין רֵעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין
whose mark is discernible through the union of mind and heart which are two companions that never separate.
וּמִצַּד הַשָּׂגַת הַחָכְמָה אֵין בְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב שׁוּם פְּסוֹלֶת כְּלָל
And from the perspective of the comprehension of Chokhmah there is no dross whatsoever in the seed of Jacob,
וְאַף דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם תַּקָּנָה בִּתְשׁוּבָה שֶׁרוֹמֶזֶת לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא כַּנּוֹדָע
and even matters that possess no remedy through repentance (which alludes to the World to Come / Binah as is known),
הֵם מִתַּתְקְנִים בִּפְתִיחַת תַּרְעָא דְּחָכְמְתָא
become rectified through the opening of the gate of Chokhmah.
שֶׁהִיא לְמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה
which is higher than the standard level of repentance.
וּמִדַּת יְסוֹד יָדוּעַ שֶׁהוּא הַהִתְקַשְּׁרוּת וְהִתְחַבְּרוּת שֶׁבֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם
And the attribute of Yesod is known to be the bond and union between Israel and their Father in Heaven,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ יְסוֹד הַבְּרִיאָה וְהָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ,
which constitutes the very foundation of Creation and the entire universe.
כְּמוֹ כָּל בִּנְיָן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ יְסוֹד בְּתַחְתִּיתוֹ שֶׁעָלָיו עוֹמֵד כָּל הַבִּנְיָן
like any edifice having a foundation at its base upon which the entire building stands.
וְגַם כָּל בִּנְיַן הַבְּרִיאָה יֵשׁ לוֹ יְסוֹד שֶׁעָלָיו נִתְכּוֹנֵן
And the entire edifice of Creation likewise has a foundation upon which it is established,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם",
as it is stated: "The righteous is the foundation of the world" (Proverbs 10:25),
שֶׁעָלָיו הָעוֹלָם עוֹמֵד
upon whom the world rests,
וְלוּלֵי כֵן הָיָה הָעוֹלָם חוֹזֵר לְתֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ.
and were it not for him, the world would revert to unformed chaos.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל דְּנִשְׁאַר רַק נֹחַ אִישׁ צַדִּיק
And as occurred in the Generation of the Flood when there remained only Noah, a righteous man,
דְּמִמֶּנּוּ הוּשְׁתַּת הָעוֹלָם אַחַר כָּךְ.
from whom the world was subsequently refounded.
וְהוּא הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה כְּלַפֵּי כְּלַל אֲצִילוּת קָדְשׁוֹ,
And he represents the lower level relative to the totality of His holy Emanation (Atzilut).
שֶׁאֵין מוּשָּׂג לָאָדָם אֶלָּא כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּרִיאָה תַּחְתּוֹנָה כְּלַפֵּי נִבְרָאִים עֶלְיוֹנִים
comprehensible to man only in terms of being a lower creature compared to supernal beings.
אֶלָּא שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא הִתְחַבְּרוּת תַּחְתּוֹנִים וְעֶלְיוֹנִים, שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ
Except that within him occurs the union of lower and upper realms, heaven and earth,
עַל יְדֵי חִבּוּר נַפְשׁוֹ וְרוּחוֹ עִם גּוּפוֹ,
through the binding of his soul and spirit with his physical body.
וְכָל הִתְחַבְּרוּת תַּחְתּוֹן בָּעֶלְיוֹן הַיְינוּ בְּמִדָּה אַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁל עֶלְיוֹן
and every union of a lower entity with a higher entity takes place in the final attribute of the higher.
אֶלָּא שֶׁאַחַר הַנְּסִירָה דְּנַעֲשׂוּ פָּנִים בְּפָנִים
Except that following the separation (nesirah) whereby they became face-to-face,
אִלּוּ לֹא חָטָא וְנִכְנַס לְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
had Adam not sinned and entered into the Sabbath day in holiness,
שֶׁאָז עֲלִיַּת הָעוֹלָמוֹת
which is the time of the ascent of the worlds,
הָיָה מִתְעַלֶּה לְגַמְרֵי לִהְיוֹת "נְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵב גָּבֶר" כִּלְעָתִיד
he would have ascended completely to fulfill "a woman shall court a man" (Jeremiah 31:21) as in the future.
שֶׁיִּהְיוּ רֵעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין לְעוֹלָם וּמְחוּבָּרִים לְגַמְרֵי
where they would be companions who never part for all eternity, completely unified.
אֶלָּא שֶׁזֶּהוּ שֶׁפַע הַשָּׂגָה יְתֵירָה שֶׁאֵין הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה רָאוּי לָהּ,
However, this is an excessive overflow of comprehension of which this world is not yet worthy,
שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין
having been created with the attribute of judgment,
רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר מִדַּת צִמְצוּם הָאוֹר מֵהַשָּׂגָה
meaning the contraction of the light from apprehension.
דְּמַה שֶּׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ כְּדַאי לָהּ, נִתְעַלֵּם
such that whatever transcends the grasp of this world, and of which it is not worthy, was concealed.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁדָּנָה לֵאָה דִּין בְּעַצְמָהּ,
And this explains why Leah passed judgment upon herself,
הִכְנִיסָה בָּהּ מִדַּת הַדִּין וְהִתְצַמְצְמוּת הַהַשָּׂגָה
introducing within herself the attribute of judgment and contraction of grasp,
שֶׁמִּצַּד הַדִּין לֹא הָיָה הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אָז כְּדַאי עֲדַיִן לְהִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר הַזֶּה בָּעוֹלָם
that from the perspective of judgment this world was not yet worthy of having this light revealed within it,
שֶׁיּוּגְמַר שְׁלֵימוּת הַתִּיקּוּן דְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב לְגַמְרֵי
whereby the total perfection of the seed of Jacob would be finalized,
אֵיךְ הֵם לֹא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין כְּלָל מִמֶּנּוּ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
revealing how they are never severed from Him, blessed be He.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְהַפֵּךְ לִנְקֵבָה
And through this the fetus was transformed into a female,
שֶׁכָּל מִדַּת הַדִּין הוּא מִסִּטְרָא דְּנוּקְבָּא כַּנּוֹדָע
for the entire attribute of judgment stems from the feminine aspect (Nukva) as is known,
כִּי שֵׂכֶל מִדַּת הַצִּמְצוּם הוּא מִצַּד הַמְקַבֵּל שֶׁהוּא הַכְּלִי לְקִיבּוּל
since the concept of contraction originates from the recipient who is the vessel of reception,
שֶׁהַכְּלִי מְצַמְצֶמֶת שֶׁפַע הַהַשְׁפָּעָה וְלֹא מִצַּד הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ.
for the vessel contracts the flow of divine influx, and not from the Bestower.

But beforehand, when he raised their evil report, he had to descend to Egypt.” This illuminates Rav Tzadok’s distinction between Yosef’s initial judgment of the brothers’ outward deeds and their inner attachment to Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 104b: in Perek Chelek, the “expounders of impressions” (dorshei reshumos) said: “דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים: כּוּלָּן בָּאִין לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא” — “The expounders of hints said: All of them enter the World to Come.” In its context this refers to the named figures under discussion (including Ahab and Menashe), not verbatim to all descendants of the Patriarchs. Rav Tzadok expands the teaching to the seed of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, with his exception for Bilaam, and interprets “reshumot” as the traces of Chochmah; compare the Mishnah’s list of exceptions at Sanhedrin 90a). R’ Tzadok’s use: “reshumos” (impressions) denotes the rung of Chochmah, above Binah — the “World to Come”; the supernal Chochmah of the mind is not itself “felt,” only its “impression” is felt in the heart. From the side of that Chochmah there is no “dross” in Yaakov’s seed at all — the discerning one perceives that, however their deeds appear on the surface, the depths of their hearts cleave wholly to God.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §12): “The elevation of the yesod of the male to Yesod Abba comes afterward, on Sukkos — the culmination of Rosh Hashanah — for from the intensity of fear comes the intensity of the joy of ‘the season of our rejoicing,’ whence they draw ru’ach ha-kodesh at the Simchas Beis HaSho’evah: a spirit from the supernal holiness, which is Chochmah Ila’ah the supernal Wisdom.” (This locates the se’if’s Yesod Abba: it is drawn from Chochmah Ila’ah — the “opening of the gate of Chochmah” that stands above teshuvah — which is why it effects the total, unbreakable union that Yesod Ze’er deed cannot.)

paragraphs.text: Mishlei 10:25: “כַּעֲבוֹר סוּפָה וְאֵין רָשָׁע, וְצַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם” — “when the storm passes, the wicked is no more, but a tzaddik is the foundation of the world.” Background: Mishlei contrasts the fleeting wicked with the enduring righteous. Meforshim: the Sages (Yoma 38b) take “tzaddik yesod olam” to mean that the world stands upon the righteous — even one tzaddik sustains it. R’ Tzadok’s use: the sefirah of Yesod is this very “foundation” — the bond joining Israel to their Father in Heaven, “upon which the whole edifice of creation stands,” just as Noach (“ish tzaddik”) remained to re-found the world after the Flood.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Had Leah then borne Yosef (the Yesod), joined to Yaakov he would be Yesod Abba — total, unbreakable union of all the tribes. Yesod Abba (from Chochmah) transcends “Yesod Ze’er” (deed). Yosef’s “evil report” saw only the surface; in the depths all the tribes cleave to Hashem (“all Israel have a share”). But this “extra” attainment this world — created with Din (contraction) — could not yet bear; so Leah’s self-din turned the fetus into a female (Din is of the “vessel/receiver”).

p: (לה) וְכָל הַגָּלִיּוֹת וְעִכּוּב הַתִּיקּוּן הַגָּמוּר הוּא מִצַּד מִדַּת הַדִּין
And all exiles and the delay of complete rectification stem from the attribute of judgment
וְדִינָא דְּמַלְכוּתָא יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ
and the judgment of the heavenly Sovereignty, blessed be His Name,
הָרוֹמֵז לְשֵׁם הָאֲדֹנוּת בְּאֶחָד מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה צֵירוּפָיו
which alludes to the Name Adonut in one of its twenty-four permutations,
שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמְקַבֶּלֶת עוֹל מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּאַהֲבָה
which is the attribute of the Congregation of Israel who accepts the yoke of His sovereignty with love.
יוֹמָם וָלַיְלָה כָּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חָדְשֵׁי הַשָּׁנָה
day and night throughout all twelve months of the year. (,
וְעַל כֵּן הֵם עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה צֵירוּפִים
(And therefore they comprise twenty-four permutations,),
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה רַק שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר צֵירוּפִים נֶגֶד מִדַּת יוֹם לְבַד
(unlike the Name Havayah which has only twelve permutations corresponding to the daytime attribute alone,)
שֶׁהוּא מִדָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ "שֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן ה
'", (which is His divine attribute, "For a sun and a shield is Hashem" (Psalms 84:12);)
וְסִטְרָא דְּנוּקְבָּא הוּא מִדַּת לַיְלָה
– (whereas the feminine side is the attribute of night—),
שְׁלִיטַת הַלְּבָנָה הַמְקַבֶּלֶת אוֹר הַחַמָּה
(the dominion of the moon that receives the light of the sun,),
וְהוּא חִבּוּר יוֹם וָלַיְלָה
(and it constitutes the union of day and night,),
עַל כֵּן אֶצְלָהּ הַשְּׁנֵים עָשָׂר הֵם עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה
(therefore within her the twelve become twenty-four,)
רָצָה לוֹמַר הַשָּׂגַת עַצְמָהּ וְהַשָּׂגַת הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ,
(meaning the apprehension of herself and the apprehension of the Bestower,)
שֶׁהֵם חָמְרָהּ וְצוּרָתָהּ.
(which are her matter and her form.).
וְעַל כֵּן מַזְכִּירִין מִדַּת יוֹם בַּלַּיְלָה וּמִדַּת לַיְלָה בַּיּוֹם בְּבִרְכַּת קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
And therefore we mention the attribute of day at night and the attribute of night by day in the blessings of the Shema.),
וְנִרְאֶה לִי כִּי הַצֵּירוּפִים אדי"ן ודינ"א שֶׁהֵם אוֹתִיּוֹת "דִּין" סְדוּרִים יַחַד
And it appears to me that the permutations A-D-Y-N and D-Y-N-A, whose letters spell "din" (judgment) arranged together.
וְהָאָלֶ"ף דְּהוּא אַלּוּפוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַגָּנוּז בְּגַוֵּוהּ בִּתְחִלָּתָהּ הוּא נֶגֶד חוֹדֶשׁ אָב
and the Aleph, which represents the Champion (Aluf) of the universe hidden within at its beginning, corresponds to the month of Av.
דְּנִרְאֶה לִי שֶׁנִּקְרָא כֵן לְפִי שֶׁאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בָּחַר הַגָּלִיּוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
For it seems to me that it was named thus because Abraham our father, peace be upon him, chose the exiles as our Sages of blessed memory taught,
וְהַיְינוּ דְּאַבְרָהָם הוֹלִיד אֶת יִצְחָק
which means that Abraham fathered Isaac;
דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ חֶסֶד הוּא הוֹלִיד מִדַּת הַדִּין וְהַצִּמְצוּם
for even though his attribute was Chesed, he fathered the attribute of Din and contraction.
וְכָל הוֹלָדָה הוּא כְּפִי הִשְׁתּוֹקְקוּת הַמּוֹלִיד
and all procreation reflects the spiritual yearning of the progenitor.
וְאַבְרָהָם הוּא הַנִּקְרָא "אַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם",
And Abraham is he who was named "the father of a multitude of nations" (Genesis 17:5),
וּבַתְּחִלָּה "אַב לַאֲרָם" וְאַחַר כָּךְ "לְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ",
at first "father to Aram" and afterward "to the entire world,".
דְּמִלַּת "אַב" הוּא עִיקַּר שְׁמוֹ הַמּוֹרֶה עַל עִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁהוּא אַב הָעוֹלָם וְרֹאשׁ לַאֲבוֹת הָעוֹלָם
for the word Av (father) is the core of his name showing his essence as father and head of the Patriarchs of the world.
דְּמַה שֶּׁיִּצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב גַּם כֵּן אָבוֹת הוּא רַק מִצַּד כֹּחַ אַבְרָהָם הַגָּנוּז בְּגַוָּוהוּ,
And the fact that Isaac and Jacob are also Patriarchs is only through the power of Abraham concealed within them.
כִּי הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְעִנְיַן "אַב" דְּהַיְינוּ הַהוֹלָדָה שֶׁהוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַבָּא מִצַּד הַחֶסֶד
for he is the primal root of the concept of fatherhood, namely procreation which is expansive flow coming from Chesed.
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּצַּד שֶׁפַע הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת אֵין מָקוֹם לְהוֹלָדָה וְהֶבְדֵּל בֵּין אָב לְבֵן
Except that from the unbounded overflow of expansion there is no room for birth and distinction between father and son,
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ "אִלְמָלֵא אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁחָטְאוּ אָנוּ לֹא בָּאנוּ אוֹ כְּמִי שֶׁלֹּא בָּאנוּ לָעוֹלָם"
along the lines of "Had our ancestors not sinned, we would not have come, or would be as those who had not come into the world" (Avodah Zarah 5a).
וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה תְּחִלָּתוֹ עָקָר
Therefore his beginning was barren.
דְּכָל הוֹלָדָה הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַהִתְצַמְצְמוּת שֶׁהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּמִדַּת הַדִּין
for all procreative birth occurs only through contraction which is the rung of Din.
וְאַף דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ הוּא רַב חֶסֶד
And even though Abraham our father, peace be upon him, was intrinsically abundant in lovingkindness,
בָּחַר בַּגָּלִיּוֹת מִצַּד חֵשֶׁק שְׁלֵימוּת מִדָּתוֹ,
he chose the exiles out of a yearning for the perfection of his attribute,
שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת שֵׁם "אָב" שֶׁמּוּכְרָח לְהוֹלִיד בָּנִים
which is the fulfillment of the title Father who must bear children.
וּמוּכְרָח לְהוֹלִיד מִדַּת הַצִּמְצוּם וּלְהָבִיאָהּ לָעוֹלָם
and who must give birth to the attribute of contraction and bring it into the world.
וְעַל כֵּן שֵׁם הַחוֹדֶשׁ אָב הַמּוֹלִיד הַדִּינִין
And therefore the name of the month is Av which generates the judgments,
וּלְהַמְתִּיק הַדִּינִין שֶׁהוּא הַכְנָסָתָן בְּשָׁרְשָׁן קְרָאוּהוּ "אָב",
and to sweeten the judgments by restoring them to their root, they called it Av.
שֶׁהוּא שָׁרְשָׁן הַמּוֹלִידָן, שֶׁהוּא אַדְּרַבָּה רַב חֶסֶד
which is their progenitor root, who is on the contrary abundant in lovingkindness.
כִּי כָּל יִסּוּרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגָלִיּוֹתֵיהֶם הוּא לָתֵת לָהֶם עַל יְדֵי זֶה אַחֲרִית וְתִקְוָה טוֹבָה הַנִּמְשָׁכִים מִמִּדַּת הַחֶסֶד
For all tribulations of Israel and their exiles are intended to grant them through this a hopeful future and good end flowing from the attribute of Chesed.
וְזֶהוּ הָאָלֶ"ף הָרוֹמֶזֶת לְמִדַּת הַחָכְמָה
And this is the letter Aleph which alludes to the attribute of Chokhmah,
שֶׁהוּא חֲסָדִים הַנֶּעְלָמִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַמִּתְחַבְּרוֹת לְאוֹתִיּוֹת דִּי"ן
which represents the concealed kindnesses in this world that unite with the letters D-Y-N.
וּבִתְחִלָּתוֹ הַיְינוּ כְּפִי דֶּרֶךְ יְרִידָתָם מִלְּמַעְלָה שֶׁזֶּהוּ נֶגֶד מִדַּת יוֹם
and at its beginning this reflects the trajectory of their descent from Above, which corresponds to the daytime attribute.
וְאָלֶ"ף בַּסּוֹף הוּא מִדַּת לַיְלָה
And the Aleph at the end (D-Y-N-A) corresponds to the nighttime attribute,
שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַסּוֹף וְהָאַחֲרִית מִזֶּה יִהְיֶה לְטוֹב
which is the comprehension of the Congregation of Israel that the final outcome will be for good.
וּלְהַשָּׂגַת פִּלְאוֹת הַחָכְמָה דִּימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא
and for the apprehension of the wonders of Chokhmah in the messianic era and the World to Come.
וְעַל כֵּן יְצִירַת הַחוֹדֶשׁ בְּאוֹת הַטֵּי"ת דְּטוֹבֵיהּ גָּנוּז בְּגַוֵּוהּ,
Therefore the creation of the month of Av was formed through the letter Tet, whose goodness is hidden within it,
וּמַזָּלוֹ אַרְיֵה
and its zodiac sign is Leo (the lion),
וְנִרְאֶה לִי שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד שֵׁבֶט דָּן
and it appears to me that it corresponds to the tribe of Dan (,
וְאַף שֶׁכְּפִי מַה שֶּׁקִּבַּלְתִּי סִדְרָן שֶׁל שְׁבָטִים נֶגֶד חָדְשֵׁי הַשָּׁנָה אֵינוֹ כֵן
(and even though according to the tradition I received the order of the tribes corresponding to the months is different,).
בֶּאֱמֶת יֵשׁ כַּמָּה נוּסְחָאוֹת שׁוֹנוֹת בָּזֶה, עַיֵּין בִּמְפָרְשֵׁי סֵפֶר יְצִירָה
(in truth there are various differing traditions regarding this, see the commentators on Sefer Yetzirah.),
וּלְדַעְתִּי אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים
(And in my view, both these and those are the words of the living God,),
כִּי יֵשׁ בֶּאֱמֶת סְדָרִים שׁוֹנִים בָּזֶה וְכֻלָּם אֱמֶת מִצַּד זוּלַת צַד
(for there are genuinely diverse arrangements in this and all are true from different facets,),
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ לֹא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה עַצְמוֹ סֵדֶר הַשְּׁבָטִים לִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר פְּשׁוּטוֹת
(and perforce the exact order of the tribes for the twelve simple letters was not explicitly detailed in Sefer Yetzirah itself,).
וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹם בֵּיאוּר זֶה
and this is not the place to elaborate on this.) ",
גּוּר אַרְיֵה" שֶׁהוּא הַיָּרוּד שֶׁבַּשְּׁבָטִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
Dan is termed a lion's whelp, being the lowliest of the tribes as our Sages of blessed memory noted,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְרָא אַרְיֵה כִּיהוּדָה
yet nonetheless he is called a lion just like Judah,
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם מְחוּבָּר לִיהוּדָה כַּנּוֹדָע בִּמְלֶאכֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְהַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
and in every place he is joined with Judah, as is known regarding the construction of the Tabernacle and the Temple.
וְגַם לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר
and likewise regarding the days of the Messiah, as they stated in the Zohar.
וְהוּא מִצַּד מִדַּת הָעִגּוּלִים דְּהָרֹאשׁ וְהַסּוֹף מְחוּבָּר יַחַד
And this stems from the circular dimension (Iggulim) wherein the head and the end are joined together,
וְגַם זַנְבָא דְּאַרְיֵה אַרְיֵה הוּא
and even the tail of a lion is still a lion,
וְ"דָן יָדִין עַמּוֹ כְּאַחַד וְגוֹמֵר"
– and "Dan shall judge his people as one, etc." (Genesis 49:16)—.
מְיוּחָד שֶׁבַּשְּׁבָטִים זֶה יְהוּדָה
as the unique one among the tribes, who is Judah.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 44:21: “אָמַר לוֹ בַּמֶּה אַתָּה רוֹצֶה שֶׁיֵּרְדוּ בָנֶיךָ, בַּגֵּיהִנֹּם אוֹ בַּמַּלְכֻיּוֹת? רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר: אַבְרָהָם בֵּרַר לוֹ אֶת הַמַּלְכֻיּוֹת.” — “He said to him: ‘Into which do you wish your children to descend: Gehinnom or the kingdoms?’ Rabbi Chanina bar Papa said: ‘Avraham chose the kingdoms for himself.’” The Midrash contrasts subjection to the kingdoms with Gehinnom. Rav Tzadok explains the choice here as fatherly Chesed expressed through contraction, with exile ultimately returning to its good root. This is Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa’s position, which Rav Tzadok follows here. The same Midrash also records Rabbi Yudan, Rabbi Idi and Rabbi Chama bar Chanina as saying: “אַבְרָהָם בֵּרַר גֵּיהִנֹּם וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בֵּרַר לוֹ אֶת הַמַּלְכֻיּוֹת” — “Abraham chose Gehinnom and the Holy One chose the kingdoms for him.” The alternative opinion must not be hidden when identifying the source.

paragraphs.text: Yirmeyah 29:11: “כִּי אָנֹכִי יָדַעְתִּי אֶת הַמַּחֲשָׁבֹת אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי חֹשֵׁב עֲלֵיכֶם נְאֻם ה׳, מַחְשְׁבוֹת שָׁלוֹם וְלֹא לְרָעָה, לָתֵת לָכֶם אַחֲרִית וְתִקְוָה” — “for I know the thoughts that I think toward you, says Hashem — thoughts of peace and not of evil — to give you a future and a hope.” Background: from Yirmeyah’s letter to the Babylonian exiles — the exile itself is purposed toward a good end. R’ Tzadok’s use: all Israel’s sufferings and exiles are “to give them a good end and hope,” drawn from Chochmah — the hidden chasadim joined to the letters of “din,” whose “end” turns to the wonders of the days of Mashiach.  Shelah — the din of exile is rooted in rescue and a road toward life: Shelah, Aseres HaDibros, Pesachim, Matzah Ashirah 4:46, states the principle “אין רע יורד מלמעלה”: even what appears as evil can be a rescue from a harsher consequence for which the person is otherwise exposed. He cites the Midrashic teaching that Avraham chose subjection to the kingdoms for his descendants so that they be spared Gehinnom, and then links suffering itself to “דרך חיים תוכחות מוסר.” The Shelah does not call pain pleasant, nor does he deny that it must be experienced as judgment. His point is that the judgment can be ordered toward preservation and life. This fits R’ Tzadok’s insistence that the dinim of galus are born from a root of Chesed — Av, the fatherly source, ‘begetting’ contraction precisely for the sake of an achris v’tikvah. The contraction is real: exile limits, separates, and obscures. Yet if its root is chesed, then the final meaning of the contraction is not destruction but formation. A child can exist as a distinct child only because unlimited expansion makes room for boundary; similarly, Israel’s history can pass through din in order to emerge with a clarified and enduring form. The sweetness of the din is therefore not found by denying the darkness, but by returning it to the Av-source from which its good purpose descends. [Original source: Shelah, Matzah Ashirah 4:46]

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar §5: “תיכף בשעת החורבן כשראו ישראל שנכנסו אויבים להיכל אשר לא האמינו מקודם מיד עשו כולם תשובה ... ובירושלמי (ברכות פ״ב ה׳ ד) ובמ״ר (איכה א׳ ע) איתא שבט״ב ביום החורבן נולד תיכף משיח והוא מטעם הנ״ל. רק לא היה עדיין הזמן להיות התיקון כהוגן אבל עכ״פ היו ישראל בגדר עושין רצונו של מקום.” — “Immediately at the time of the destruction, when Israel saw that enemies had entered the Sanctuary, which they had not believed beforehand, they all immediately repented. ... In the Yerushalmi (Berachos 2:4) and the Midrash (Eichah 1:70) it is stated that on Tishah B’Av, on the day of the destruction, Mashiach was immediately born, for the reason just given. Only, the time had not yet come for the repair to be as it should; but in any event Israel were then in the category of those who do the will of the Omnipresent.” This illuminates Av’s hidden good without treating the destruction itself as the completed redemption.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar §2: “ובס׳ יצירה איתא דחודש אדר נוצר באות ק׳ וחודש אב באות ט׳ ואיתא בזוהר הקדוש (תרומה קנב א) טי״ת נהירו דחיין בכל אתר ... וכן חודש אב היה מוכן בעצם להתגלות אור הזה ... אמנם לאחר הקלקול נעשה טוביה גניז בגויה ... שהוא בהסתר ובהתכסות עד עת קץ לע״ל.” — “In Sefer Yetzirah it is stated that the month of Adar was formed with the letter kuf and the month of Av with the letter tet; and in the holy Zohar (Terumah 152a) it is stated: ‘Tet is the light of life everywhere.’ ... The month of Av likewise was inherently prepared for the revelation of this light. ... But after the corruption, its good became hidden within it ... for it is in concealment and covering until the final time in the future.” This directly illuminates Rav Tzadok’s reading of Av’s tet as goodness concealed within judgment.

It is therefore not established that the information came orally from the Ishbitzer. Compare Rav Tzadok’s own Resisei Layla §39: “וְסִדְרָן שֶׁל י״ב שְׁבָטִים נֶגֶד י״ב חֳדָשִׁים יֵשׁ כַּמָּה דֵעוֹת בִּמְפָרְשֵׁי סֵפֶר יְצִירָה וַאֲנִי קִבַּלְתִּי סִדְרָן ...” — “There are several opinions among the commentators on Sefer Yetzirah about the twelve tribes opposite the twelve months, and I received their order…” This is an exact printed parallel, not evidence of whom he heard. Rav Tzadok also expressly distinguishes alternate arrangements in the present se’if. [Original source: Resisei Layla 39]

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 49:16: “דָּן יָדִין עַמּוֹ, כְּאַחַד שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל” — “Dan shall judge his people, as one of the tribes of Israel.” Background: Yaakov’s blessing to Dan. Meforshim: Rashi reads “k’echad” as “like the singular k’meyuchad of the tribes” — i.e., Dan’s judge (Shimshon) will be like David, of Yehudah. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is why Dan, though the “tail” and rearmost of the camp, is bound to Yehudah the “head” — as in the Mishkan (Betzalel of Yehudah, Oholiav of Dan) — the “circle” in which beginning and end are joined as one.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The exiles and the delay of the rectification are from Din — the Name A-D-N-Y (Malchus/Knesses Yisrael), with its 24 permutations (12 “day,” 12 “night”). The month Av “begets the judgments,” yet its name (Av = father) is their sweetening root — abundant Chesed: Avraham “chose the exiles,” for every begetting requires contraction. Israel’s sufferings yield “a good end and hope.” Dan’s mazal is Aryeh, joined to Yehudah (“beginning and end joined as one”).

p: (לו) וְשִׁמְשׁוֹן וּשְׁלֹמֹה שְׁנֵיהֶם נָשְׂאוּ נָשִׁים נָכְרִיּוֹת
And Samson and Solomon both married foreign women.
וְעַיֵּין בָּרַמְבַּ"ם הִלְכוֹת אִיסּוּרֵי בִּיאָה (פֶּרֶק יג הֲלָכוֹת יד – טז) שֶׁגִּיְּירוּם, עַיֵּין שָׁם
and see Maimonides, Laws of Forbidden Intercourse (13:14–16), that they converted them, see there.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּכָל כַּוָּונָתָם הָיָה לְהַכְנִיעָם עַל יְדֵי זֶה וּלְהַכְנִיסָם לִקְדוּשָּׁה
Which means that their entire intention was to subdue them through this and bring them into holiness,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה דְּמָשִׁיחַ יָבוֹא לְלַמֵּד תּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
and as our Sages of blessed memory said that the Messiah will come to teach Torah and commandments to the nations of the world,
אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יִצְטָרְכוּ לוֹ דְּיִלְמְדוּ מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה
whereas Israel will not need him, for they will learn directly from the mouth of the Almighty.
וְאָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ מֶלֶךְ אֶלָּא אָתָּה
and we have no King but You.
וְכָל מַלְכוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מַלְכוּתָם עַל הָאֻמּוֹת
And the entire kingship of Israel is their sovereignty over the nations.
וּמַה שֶּׁיַּכְנִיסוּם גַּם כֵּן לִמְקוֹם הַגֵּרִים תַּחַת כַּנְפֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה
and that which they will bring them likewise into the station of converts beneath the wings of the Shechinah.
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד מַדְרֵגָה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה שֶׁבְּמִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁהִיא מַלְכוּתָא תַּתָּאָה
And this is from the lower level of the attribute of Malchut which is the lower sovereignty,
וְהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּאַרְיֵה מֶלֶךְ בַּחַיּוֹת
and it is the rung of the lion as king over beasts,
הֵם אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הַנִּמְשָׁלִים לְחַיְתוֹ יַעַר
these being the nations of the world who are compared to beasts of the forest.
שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם צוּרַת אָדָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְבָמוֹת סג:) דְּאֵין קְרוּיִים אָדָם
who lack the true spiritual form of Adam, as our Sages taught (Yevamot 63b) that they are not called Adam.
וּלְפִי שֶׁ"רַגְלֶיהָ יֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת" כַּנּוֹדָע
And because "her feet go down to death" (Proverbs 5:5) as is known,
וְכָל שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל הוּא רַק בְּרַגְלִין וּמַדְרֵגָה תַּחְתּוֹנָה
and all dominion of the base archetype of Belial is only in the feet and the lowest level,
שָׁם הוּא מִתְהַפֵּךְ לְרַע לוֹ,
there it turns to his own destruction.
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִכְלֶה הָרַע וּמְעַט הַנִּשְׁאָר יִתְהַפֵּךְ לְטוֹב
so that through this evil will perish and the remaining remnant will invert into good.
וּמָשִׁיחַ יִהְיֶה סוֹף הָרַגְלִין דְּהוּא מַלְכוּת שֶׁבְּמַלְכוּת
And the Messiah will be the culmination of the feet, which is Malchut of Malchut,
וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה יְסוֹד שֶׁבְּמַלְכוּת
and King Solomon, peace be upon him, was Yesod of Malchut.
וְהוּא זַנְבָא דְּאַרְיֵה מִצַּד מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁבְּאַרְיֵה
and he is the tail of the lion from the aspect of kingship within the lion.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁ"מֶּלֶךְ בְּמִשְׁפָּט יַעֲמִיד אָרֶץ",
And even though "A king by justice establishes the land" (Proverbs 29:4),
וְכָל מִדַּת מַלְכוּת הִיא מִדַּת הַדִּין וְדִינָא דְּמַלְכוּתָא לִשְׁפּוֹט תֵּבֵל בְּצֶדֶק
and the whole attribute of Malchut is the attribute of judgment and royal statute to judge the world in righteousness,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם זֶהוּ רַק לְהַעֲמָדַת אֶרֶץ וְהַנְהָגַת הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא מִדַּת מַלְכוּת
nonetheless, this is solely for establishing the land and royal governance which is termed the attribute of Malchut.
אֲבָל עֶצֶם הַמֶּלֶךְ אַדְּרַבָּה מָלֵא רַחֲמִים
whereas the essence of the King is, on the contrary, full of mercy.
וְעַל כֵּן מַלְכוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִשֵּׁבֶט יְהוּדָה
Therefore the kingship of Israel is from the tribe of Judah,
דְּנִקְרָא כֻּלּוֹ עַל שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה שֶׁהוּא עֶצֶם הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהוּא מִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים
which is entirely named after the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, the Name Havayah which is the essence of the King and the attribute of Mercy,
וְהוּא נִקְרָא מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי אָנוּ בָּנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ.
and He is called the King of Israel because we are His children, blessed be His Name.
וְהַמֶּלֶךְ בְּבֵיתוֹ אֵין שַׁיָּיךְ הַנְהָגַת הַמְּלוּכָה
And for a king in his own home, the external governance of monarchy does not apply,
דְּכָל אִישׁ שׂוֹרֵר בְּבֵיתוֹ,
for every man is ruler in his home,
וְהַנְהָגַת מַלְכוּת הוּא רַק עַל זוּלָתוֹ,
and royal administration applies only toward external subjects,
אֲבָל בְּבֵיתוֹ הוּא כְּכָל אָב לְבָנָיו וּדְבוּקָם בְּעֶצֶם הַמֶּלֶךְ.
but in his home he is like any father to his children, who cling to the essence of the king.
אֲבָל מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁהוּא הַנְהָגַת הַמְּלוּכָה מִתְפַּשֵּׁט בִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לִהְיוֹת מוֹשֵׁל בַּגּוֹיִם
However, the attribute of Malchut which is monarchical governance expands into the Congregation of Israel to rule over the nations
וְלִשְׁפּוֹךְ חֲמָתוֹ עֲלֵיהֶם, "חֲמַת מֶלֶךְ מַלְאֲכֵי מָוֶת".
and to pour out His wrath upon them, "The wrath of a king is as messengers of death" (Proverbs 16:14).
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּהַיִּסּוּרִין רַק כְּאָב הַמְיַסֵּר אֶת בְּנוֹ
This is not so with the children of Israel, where tribulations are merely as a father chasteneth his son.
לְהַחֲיוֹתוֹ וּלְהֵיטִיב אַחֲרִיתוֹ עַל יְדֵי זֶה
to vivify him and do good unto his latter end through this.

paragraphs.text: Rambam, Hilchos Issurei Biah 13:14–16: the Rambam cautions, “Let it not enter your mind that Shimshon the savior of Israel, or Shlomo king of Israel who was called ‘beloved of Hashem,’ married gentile women in their gentile state” — rather, these women were converted (13:16: “Shlomo converted women and married them, and so too Shimshon converted and married”). Background: the Rambam (13:14–15) explains that a beis din did not accept converts throughout the days of David and Shlomo — suspecting ulterior motives — yet many converted before laymen, and the great court “neither pushed them away nor drew them close, until their end be seen.” Yet the Rambam immediately adds that the conversions were prompted by worldly motives and subsequent conduct led Scripture to treat the women as though they still stood in their former non-Jewish status. This is a substantive warning, not an unqualified approval of those marriages. Rav Tzadok is explaining their intended spiritual project; that interpretation must be distinguished from the Rambam’s legal and moral qualifications.  Be’er Mayim Chaim — drawing the distant good into kedushah: Be’er Mayim Chaim, Bereishis 1:2:7, explains Chazal’s statement that Israel were exiled among the nations in order that converts be added to them as a process of birur: holy sparks situated in foreign environments are themselves in exile, and when Israel reaches those places the concealed holiness is drawn toward its own kind — ‘מצא מין את מינו וניעור.’ He reads ‘עת אשר שלט האדם באדם לרע לו’ in the familiar Lurianic sense that the apparent dominion of the other side ultimately becomes ‘to its own detriment,’ because Israel departs carrying out the vitality that had been trapped there. This supplies an illuminating conceptual background to R’ Tzadok’s reading of Shimshon and Shlomo. Their aim, as he has grounded it in the Rambam’s insistence that the women were converted, was not to blur Israel’s boundary but to draw what could genuinely enter beneath the wings of the Shechinah. The Be’er Mayim Chaim makes the direction of the movement decisive: holiness may descend into a distant place in order to extract what belongs to it, but it must return with the spark rather than become absorbed by the shell. That distinction is exactly what keeps R’ Tzadok’s account from becoming a license for assimilation. The future conquest of evil by Malchus is not a sanctification of foreignness as foreignness; it is the disclosure and ingathering of whatever can truly be converted into service of Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Mishlei 29:4: “מֶלֶךְ בְּמִשְׁפָּט יַעֲמִיד אָרֶץ, וְאִישׁ תְּרוּמוֹת יֶהֶרְסֶנָּה” — “a king establishes the land through justice, but a man of exactions tears it down.” Background: kingship rightly exercised — through mishpat — gives a land its stability. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the “trait of Malchus,” which is Din — “the law of the kingdom, to judge the world with righteousness”; yet, he stresses, this judging function is only the outward “conduct of the kingdom,” not the essence of the King, who is “on the contrary, full of mercy.”

paragraphs.text: Esther 1:22: Achashverosh’s decree, sent to every province, that “…לִהְיוֹת כָּל אִישׁ שֹׂרֵר בְּבֵיתוֹ וּמְדַבֵּר כִּלְשׁוֹן עַמּוֹ” — “…that every man should rule in his own house and speak the tongue of his people.” Background: the edict issued after Vashti’s fall (the Sages, Megillah 12b, note how petty it seemed). R’ Tzadok’s use: he draws on the verse’s plain phrase — that “every man rules in his own house” — to explain that a king exercises “kingship” (the conduct of Din) only over others; within his own home he is merely a father, and there his children “cleave to the very essence of the King,” untouched by the ruling-rod of Malchus.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Shimshon and Shlomo married “foreign women” whom, per the Rambam, they converted — aiming to subdue the nations and draw them beneath the wings of the Shechinah, which is the future work of Mashiach. This is Malchus Tata’ah, the lowest rung, where “her feet descend to death” and evil is consumed. But Malchus judges only outward: the essence of the King is full of mercy, and Israel’s sufferings are a father chastening a son for his good.

And even though the soul in its own essence is pure,

However, the eye seeing, through which the heart covets, are psychic faculties drawn from the soul.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעִיקַּר רְאִיַּת הַנְּשָׁמָה הוּא בְּטָהֳרָה וּקְדֻשַּׁת הָרְאִיָּה
And even though the primary vision of the soul is in purity and holiness of sight,
לִהְיוֹת רוֹאֶה רַק מַרְאוֹת אֱלֹהִים גַּם בְּכָל דָּבָר גַּשְׁמִי שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה

וְזֶה הָרְאִיָּה הַנִּמְשֶׁכֶת מֵהַיִּרְאָה דַּרְגָּא דְּאַרְיֵה (אַתְוָון דְּדִין כְּאַתְוָון דְּדִין)

שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהוּא קְבִיצַת נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל
which is the root of the sanctity of the Congregation of Israel, the assembly of Jewish souls.
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד הַהִתְחַבְּרוּת הַגּוּף הַחָמְרִי
Nonetheless, from the union with the material body,
שֶׁהוּא הָרַגְלִין דְּעַל יְדֵי שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם
which represents the feet through which the dominion of man over man occurs.
שׁוֹלֵט גַּם בְּמִדַּת הָרְאִיָּה לִהְיוֹתָהּ מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת אֶל חֶמְדַּת הָרָעוֹת לְהַכְנִיסָם לַלֵּב
it rules also over the faculty of sight, causing it to minister unto wicked desires to introduce them into the heart.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 107a: in the same sugya, after the episode of Bas Sheva, when David pleaded to be wholly forgiven, “the Holy One said to him: Accept sufferings upon yourself — and he accepted them upon himself” (kabel alecha yissurin — kibel alav); and Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav that “for six months David was afflicted with tzara’as, the Shechinah departed from him, and the Sanhedrin withdrew from him.” Background: the daf opens with the warning that “a person should never bring himself to a test,” for David had asked, “Examine me, O Hashem, and test me” (Tehillim 26:2), and stumbled. The actual source of the strap statement is Midrash Tehillim 26:2: “למה הרצועה תלויה הכוני בה” — “Why does the strap hang? Strike me with it,” expressly said of David; see also Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 905:1 and Rav Tzadok’s own citation in Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 3. Takanas HaShavin uses the variant “הלקיני.” Sanhedrin 107a is a RELATED account of David accepting suffering, not the source of the exact strap wording. Rav Tzadok reads it as David’s willing embrace of yissurin as the very price of “life”: for as the root of Malchus — Knesses Yisrael “poor and lowly,” who owns nothing of herself — his own “side” is to receive suffering and thereby merit the World to Come. Source: Midrash Tehillim 26:2. Source: Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 905:1. Source: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 3.

paragraphs.text: Rav Tzadok’s wording here, “כל זה בחרתי מעוני,” echoes Job 36:21, whose text reads “כי על זה בחרת מעוני”; his first-person wording here is adapted rather than verbatim. R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §44): “כל דבר אחר התכלית כמו רופא המקיז דם נקרא רפואה אף על פי שהיא מכה לפי שתכליתה רפואה” — “A thing is named for its purpose: drawing blood counts as healing despite the wound, because the goal is healing.” Rav Tzadok contrasts Ruth’s troubles, which led to the eventual Davidic redemption, with Iyov’s blows, which were not themselves instruments of the good end. This printed comparison distinguishes purposeful affliction from suffering without such a healing consequence; it clarifies David’s acceptance of discipline, without claiming that every blow is good in itself.

paragraphs.text: Chagigah 9b: Eliyahu said to Bar Hei Hei (another reading: to Rabbi Elazar): what is the meaning of “behold, I have refined you, but not with silver; I have chosen you in the crucible of affliction” (Yeshayah 48:10)? It teaches that the Holy One went through all the good traits to give to Israel, and found none as fitting as poverty — as people say, “poverty befits Israel like a red trapping on a white horse.” Berachos 5a: It was taught, R’ Shimon ben Yochai says: three good gifts did the Holy One give Israel, and all of them He gave only through afflictions — these are: the Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 91a–b: Antoninus said to Rebbi that body and soul could each escape judgment — the body pleading, “the soul sinned, for from the day it left me I lie still as a stone,” and the soul, “the body sinned, for from the day I left it I fly in the air like a bird.” Rebbi answered with a parable: a king set two watchmen over his orchard, one lame and one blind. The lame said, “I see fine figs — carry me and we will bring them”; the lame rode upon the blind, and they brought and ate. When the owner demanded the figs, the lame said, “have I legs?” and the blind, “have I eyes?” — so he set the lame upon the blind and judged them as one. So too the Holy One brings the soul, casts it into the body, and judges them together. Mei HaShiloach — the neshamah remains pure, while bechirah operates in the embodied person: Mei HaShiloach, Anthology, Collectanea, Siddur §1, explains the daily declaration ‘נשמה שנתת בי טהורה היא’ by distinguishing nefesh, ruach, and neshamah. ‘לנשמה אין שום חטא ופגם מגיע’ — no sin or blemish reaches the neshamah itself; nefesh remains bound to the body, while ruach signifies the human power of bechirah, through which one can choose good and reject evil. This is a precise Izhbitz complement to R’ Tzadok’s use of the blind-and-lame parable. The purity of the soul does not acquit the person, because the moral subject in this world is the joined human being: the soul supplies life and vision, the body supplies the instruments of action, and ruach is the arena in which choice is exercised. Thus R’ Tzadok can simultaneously maintain that the deepest Jewish soul is intrinsically pure and that the embodied person is fully answerable for what he does. The distinction is especially important in this siman, where retrospective descriptions of an unblemished root could otherwise be misunderstood as denying responsibility. Izhbitz itself preserves both truths: the neshamah is never transformed into evil, but the person’s bechirah remains real precisely in the level through which that holy life is translated into action. Yissurin can therefore refine the embodied partnership without implying that the essential soul had ceased to be holy.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §175): “As the Sages said of David HaMelech, ‘your hands are sharp and decisive, to rule with them over His world’; and it says of him ‘admoni’ (ruddy) — like Esav — ‘but with beautiful eyes’ yefeh einayim: he shed blood only by the ruling of the Sanhedrin (Bereishis Rabbah 63); and therefore he merited kingship. And Shaul was removed because he became ‘merciful to the cruel’ — for the trait of Malchus is that of stern judgment.” (This is the se’if’s David: ‘ruddy’ like Esav yet ‘of beautiful eyes’ — his sight is rectified, seeing not by his own craving but by the da’as of the Sanhedrin, which is why ‘poverty’ of the eye does not apply to him.)

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: David — root of Malchus — asked to be “flogged,” accepting yissurin as the price of life; he is the dalet of Yehudah, Knesses Yisrael “poor and lowly,” who owns nothing of herself. Suffering earns Olam Haba (the “three good gifts” via yissurin). The soul, pure in itself, is bound to evil through the body — the parable of the chiger (soul, “lame,” no feet here) riding the suma (body, “blind,” mere instrument). Even holy “sight” can be pressed into the coveting of evil through the body’s dominion.

p: (לח) וְהִתְעַלּוּת קְדֻשַּׁת הָרְאִיָּה נֶאֱמַר בַּכָּתוּב בְּלֵידַת רְאוּבֵן: "כִּי רָאָה יְהוָה בְּעָנְיִי" עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת הָעוֹנִי

And the elevation of the sanctity of vision is stated in Scripture at the birth of Reuben: "Because Hashem has looked upon my affliction (be'onyi)" (Genesis 29:32), through the attribute of poverty (oni),
כִּי לְתַקֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתְחָלַת הַחֵטְא וְהַתְחָלַת שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל שֶׁהוּא בָּרְאִיָּה
for rectifying the root inception of sin and the beginning of the dominion of the wicked archetype in vision.
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה תָּשׁוּב הַנְּשָׁמָה טְהוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיְתָה, הִיא בְּעוֹנִי
whereby the soul returns to being pure as it was, occurs through poverty.
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה טוֹב רֹאִי קָרָא לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ עָנִי בְּרָזָא דִּ"תְּפִלָּה לְעָנִי"
And King David, peace be upon him, who was of beautiful appearance, called himself poor in the mystery of "A prayer of the afflicted" (Psalms 102:1)
כְּשֶׁרָאָה רְשָׁעִים יוֹצְאִין מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁפָּגְמוּ מִדָּתוֹ,
when he saw wicked descendants emerging from him who blemished his attribute,
וְאָמַר עַל עַצְמוֹ: "הֲכִינוֹתִי בְעָנְיִי",
and he stated of himself: "In my poverty I have prepared" (I Chronicles 22:14).
כִּי הוּא קִבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ יִסּוּרִין דְּעוֹנִי
for he accepted upon himself the afflictions of poverty.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה עָשִׁיר גָּדוֹל וּמֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּלָא שַׁיָּיךְ עֲנִיּוּת בִּמְקוֹם עֲשִׁירוּת
And even though he was exceedingly wealthy and king of Israel where poverty does not apply in the place of riches,
אֵין הַכַּוָּונָה עַל עֲנִיּוּת בַּפּוֹעַל גּוּפָנִי
the intention is not physical poverty in concrete actuality,
דִּכְבָר אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (אָבוֹת ד, א): "אֵיזֶהוּ עָשִׁיר? הַשָּׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ".
for our Sages of blessed memory already taught (Avot 4:1): "Who is rich? He who rejoices in his portion.",
וְיֵשׁ עָנִי הַשָּׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ וּמִתְעַנֵּג בְּכָךְ וְאֵין חָסֵר כְּלוּם
And there is a poor person who rejoices in his portion and delights in it and lacks nothing.
וְזֶהוּ מִדָּתָן שֶׁל חֲסִידֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְלָא שַׁיָּיךְ גַּבַּיְיהוּ עֲנִיּוּת אֶפֶס כְּלָל
and this is the trait of the pious of Israel like King David, peace be upon him, with whom no lack of poverty applies at all.
וְעִיקַּר עֲנִיּוּת הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר לָרָשׁ אֵין כֹּל וְחָסֵר הַכֹּל
And the essence of poverty is when the pauper has nothing and lacks everything,
וְעֹנִי גּוּפָנִי הוּא מִדָּה רָעָה
and bodily poverty is a distressing trait,
וְהָרְשָׁעִים אַף שֶׁהֵם עֲשִׁירִים אֵינָם בְּשַׁלְוָה
and the wicked, even when wealthy, lack tranquility,
דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ מָנֶה רוֹצֶה מָאתַיִם וְהֵם עֲנִיִּים גְּדוֹלִים
for one who has a hundred desires two hundred and they are profoundly poor.
וְזֶהוּ עֲנִיּוּתָא דְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
and that is the poverty of the nations of the world.
אֲבָל עַנְיוּתָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא כְּבַרְזָא סוּמָּקָא לְסוּסְיָא חִיוָּרָא
However, the poverty of Israel is like a red strap upon a white horse (Chagigah 9b),
שֶׁהוּא יֹפִי הֵיפֶךְ הָעֲנִיּוּת שֶׁהוּא נִיוּוּל
which is an ornament, the antithesis of poverty that defaces,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל נָאוֹת אֶלָּא שֶׁעֲנִיּוּת מְנַוַּלְתָּן"
as they said: "The daughters of Israel are beautiful, but poverty makes them uncomely" (Nedarim 66a).
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּנֵי מְלָכִים
For in truth all Israel are royal princes,
וְכְלוּם חָסֵר מִבֵּית הַמֶּלֶךְ,
and does anything lack in the king's palace?
וְזֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב שֶׁאָמַר: "יֶשׁ לִי כֹל" דְּאֵין חָסֵר כְּלוּם
and this is the rung of Jacob who said "I have everything" (Genesis 33:11), lacking nothing,
לֹא כְּעֵשָׂו שֶׁאָמַר "יֶשׁ לִי רָב" וְלֹא כֹל דַּעֲדַיִן חָסֵר
unlike Esau who said "I have much" and not all, for he still felt lack.
דְּבֶטֶן רְשָׁעִים לְעוֹלָם תֶּחְסָר
for the belly of the wicked shall forever lack (Proverbs 13:25).
אֲבָל צַדִּיקִים שְׂמֵחִים בְּחֶלְקָם וּשְׂבֵעִים וְאֵין חָסֵר לָהֶם כְּלוּם
However, the righteous rejoice in their portion and are satisfied, lacking nothing.
וְזֶהוּ "סוּסְיָא חִיוָּורָא",
And this is the "white horse",
שֶׁהַסּוּס הוּא הַגּוּף שֶׁעָלָיו רוֹכֶבֶת הַנְּשָׁמָה
for the horse represents the physical body upon which the soul rides,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתִיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר עַל פָּסוּק "עֲבָדִים רֹכְבִים עַל סוּסִים",
and as they expounded in Tikkunei Zohar on the verse "slaves riding upon horses" (Ecclesiastes 10:7).
וּכְשֶׁהוּא לָבָן הַיְינוּ נָקִי וּמָלֵא חֲסָדִים
and when it is white it is pristine and full of lovingkindnesses.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם הַטּוֹב שֶׁבַּסּוּסִים צָרִיךְ לְשֵׁבֶט וּרְצוּעָה לְאַלְקָאָה
Nonetheless, even the finest of horses requires a rod and a strap for lashing,
וְהִיא סוּמָּקָא וּמִדַּת הַדִּין
and it is red, reflecting the attribute of judgment.
וּכְשֶׁהִיא יוֹרֶדֶת עַל הַסּוּס יֵשׁ בָּהּ נוֹי וְיֹפִי לְפִי שֶׁהִיא רְצוּעָה אֲדוּמָה
and when it descends upon the horse it possesses elegance and beauty because it is a red strap.
וְאֵינוֹ כְּשׁוֹט לַסּוּס הַנִּמְשָׁל לְשֵׁבֶט לְגֵו כְּסִילִים
And it is not like a whip for a horse that is compared to a rod for the back of fools,
דְּהַשּׁוֹט עָשׂוּי לְהַכּוֹת לְבַד
for a whip is designed solely to strike,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הָרְצוּעָה שֶׁל עוֹר עָשׂוּי לְנוֹי גַּם כֵּן
unlike a leather strap which is made for ornamentation as well,
וּכְשֶׁמּוּנַּחַת עַל הַגּוּף יֵשׁ בָּהּ נוֹי לְמַרְאִית עֵינֵי אֲחֵרִים
and when resting upon the body it appears beautiful to the sight of onlookers.
רַק הַסּוּס עַצְמוֹ לְבַדּוֹ הוּא שֶׁמַּרְגִּישׁ הַהַכָּאָה וְשֶׁהִיא רְצוּעָה לְאַלְקָאָה
only the horse itself feels the sting of the blow and knows it is a chastising strap.
וְכֵן עֲנִיּוּתָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינוֹ חִסָּרוֹן גּוּפָנִי הַנִּרְאֶה לַכֹּל שֶׁהוֹמֶה וּמְהַמֶּה אַחַר חֶסְרוֹנוֹ
And so the poverty of Israel is not a physical lack apparent to all, roaring and lamenting over its deficit,
רַק חִסָּרוֹן נַפְשִׁי, דְּרַק הַלֵּב יוֹדֵעַ מָרַּת נַפְשׁוֹ,
rather an internal soul-deficiency, for the heart alone knows its own bitterness.
וְהוּא עֹנִי רוּחָנִי דְּנֶפֶשׁ שֶׁמַּכִּיר בְּחֶסְרוֹנוֹ דְּלֵית לֵיהּ מִגַּרְמֵיהּ כְּלוּם
and it is spiritual poverty of soul recognizing its total lack, having nothing of its own.
וּבָזֶה אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם עֲשִׁירִים
And in this regard the nations of the world consider themselves wealthy,
דִּמְדַמִּים בְּנַפְשָׁם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם כֹּחַ וְעֹצֶם יָד לַעֲשׂוֹת חַיִל
imagining in their souls that they possess the personal power and might of hand to generate wealth,
וְעַל כֵּן הֵם מִתְפָּאֲרִים בְּעָשְׁרָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּהָמָן שֶׁסִּפֵּר כְּבוֹד עָשְׁרוֹ
and therefore they boast of their riches, as stated of Haman who recounted the glory of his wealth (Esther 5:11).
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁאָמַר דִּבְכֹחוֹ אָסַף לוֹ עֹשֶׁר רַב כָּזֶה
namely claiming that by his own strength he accumulated such vast wealth.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כְּפִי הָאֱמֶת דְּהַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם וְנִגְזַר קוֹדֶם יְצִירַת הַוָּלָד
This is not so according to the truth that everything is in the hands of Heaven and decreed before conception,
נֶאֱמַר: "אַל יִתְהַלֵּל וְגוֹמֵר, כִּי אִם בְּזֹאת וְגוֹמֵר"
Scripture declaring: "Let not the wise man glory, etc. but let him that glorieth glory in this, etc." (Jeremiah 9:22–23),
הוּא דַּרְגָּא דִּירֵא שָׁמַיִם הָרָמוּז בְּמִלַּת "זֹאת",
which is the rung of the God-fearing person alluded to in the word "zot",
דְּזֶהוּ בִּידֵי אָדָם
for this alone is placed in the hands of man,
וְהוּא "הַשְׂכֵּל וְיָדֹעַ אוֹתִי" לְהַכִּיר אֶת קוֹנוֹ דְּהַכֹּל מִמֶּנּוּ
and it is "to understand and know Me", recognizing one's Creator that all derives from Him
וְהַחָכְמָה וְהַגְּבוּרָה וְהָעֹשֶׁר מִמֶּנּוּ.
and that wisdom, might, and wealth are exclusively from Him.
וַאֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ לוֹ אוֹצְרוֹת מְלָכִים מַכִּיר דְּאֵין לוֹ מִגַּרְמֵיהּ כְּלוּם
And even if he possesses the treasures of kings, he recognizes that he has nothing of his own,
וְאִם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא יִרְצֶה שֶׁיֵּהָנֶה מֵהֶם הוּא כְּאִלּוּ אֵין לוֹ כְּלוּם
and if Hashem, blessed be He, does not will that he enjoy them, it is as though he possesses nothing,
וְרַק מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִתֵּן לוֹ הוּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ,
and only that which Hashem grants him is what he truly has,
וְהוּא אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם כֹּחַ וְשׁוּם סִבָּה מִגַּרְמֵיהּ לַעֲשׂוֹת חַיִל כְּלָל
and he has no power and no self-derived agency to achieve success whatsoever,
וְאַל יַאֲמִין בְּעַצְמוֹ עַד יוֹם מוֹתוֹ,
and let him not believe in himself until the day of his death.
דְּכָל יְמֵי חַיָּיו הוּא בְּעֹנִי זֶה כִּי לֹא יֵדַע מַה יֵּלֶד יוֹם
for all the days of his life he abides in this humble poverty, knowing not what a day may bring forth.

paragraphs.text: I Divrei HaYamim 22:14: “וְהִנֵּה בְעָנְיִי הֲכִינוֹתִי לְבֵית ה׳…” — “and behold, in my affliction b’onyi I have prepared for the House of Hashem…” — David’s words as he readied the gold, silver, and materials for the Temple that Shlomo would build. Meforshim: the commentators ask how David, of vast wealth, could speak of “my affliction,” and explain “onyi” as travail and toil, or (as here) an inner “poverty.” R’ Tzadok’s use: David “took upon himself the sufferings of the poor man,” calling even his Temple-preparations “b’onyi” — the affliction of the soul that recognizes it has nothing of its own.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 102:1: “תְּפִלָּה לְעָנִי כִי יַעֲטֹף, וְלִפְנֵי ה׳ יִשְׁפֹּךְ שִׂיחוֹ” — “a prayer of the poor man ani when he faints, and pours out his plea before Hashem.” Background: the superscription of the psalm — the archetypal prayer of the “poor man.” R’ Tzadok’s use: David HaMelech, though a wealthy king, “called himself ani,” in the secret of “a prayer of the poor man” — the inner poverty of one who knows he owns nothing of his own, and therefore “pours out his plea” before God. Yismach Moshe — David’s poverty is the consciousness that everything is received: Yismach Moshe, Re’eh 16:1, asks how a person should understand giving tzedakah and answers that no one should imagine that he gives from property that is independently ‘his.’ Every human being enters the world empty-handed, and the Creator sustains all creatures through His tzedakah; the wealthy person is therefore a messenger through whom what Hashem has already designated reaches the recipient. He then explains David’s repeated self-description as ‘עני ואביון’: David could say this even as a king because he understood himself as one who only receives a greater measure of the Divine gift. This is almost a prose commentary on R’ Tzadok’s definition of oni in this se’if. The poverty that rectifies sight is not necessarily absence of possessions. It is the collapse of the illusion of autonomous ownership — the inner opposite of ‘כחי ועוצם ידי עשה לי את החיל הזה.’ A person may possess wealth, power, vision, or kingship, yet remain an ani when he sees all of it as entrusted rather than self-generated. In that state the eye no longer converts Divine gifts into grounds for self-expansion. It looks upward to the Giver. David’s poverty therefore belongs intrinsically to Malchus: the king who holds everything can still know that nothing is ‘from himself,’ and this recognition is itself the tikkun of the faculty that otherwise covets and claims. Source: Yismach Moshe, Re’eh 16:1.

paragraphs.text: II Shmuel 12:3: in Nathan the prophet’s parable, “וְלָרָשׁ אֵין כֹּל, כִּי אִם כִּבְשָׂה אַחַת קְטַנָּה” — “but the poor man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb.” Background: Nathan’s rebuke of David after the episode of Bas Sheva — the rich man who seizes the pauper’s single lamb. R’ Tzadok’s use: “the essence of poverty is when ‘the pauper has nothing’ and lacks everything” — real, bodily destitution, which is “a bad trait” — as opposed to Israel’s spiritual “poverty,” which lacks nothing but knows that all it has is from the King.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Kometz HaMinchah I §15: “ג׳ עזין הן, ישראל באומות (ביצה כ״ה:) לכן יאי עניותא לישראל להתיש כח עזותן, אבל אמרו תורה מתשת כח עזותן. וזהו לולי תורתך שעשועי אז אבדתי בעניי (תהלים קי״ט.) או ע״ד מאמרו רבותינו ז״ל (שבת קי״א:) צורבא מרבנן לא מיעני, או יאמר כמו שאמרו ז״ל (עירובין מא:) עניות מעביר על דעת קונו כמ״ש לאו עניותא דגרמא (קידושין מ׳) שהובאו לידי נסיונות על ידי עניות. אבל הסגולה לזה אם פגע בך מנוול משכהו לבית המדרש.” — “There are three brazen ones: Israel among the nations (Beitzah 25b). Therefore poverty befits Israel, to weaken the power of their brazenness; but they said that Torah weakens the power of their brazenness. This is: ‘Had Your Torah not been my delights, I would then have perished in my affliction’ (Psalms 119). Or it follows our Sages’ statement (Shabbos 111b) that a Torah scholar does not become impoverished. Or one may explain it as the Sages said (Eruvin 41b): poverty makes a person transgress his Maker’s will, as it says, ‘Was it not poverty that caused it?’ (Kiddushin 40), for poverty brought them to trials. But the remedy for this is: if this scoundrel confronts you, draw him to the house of study.” The passage preserves both the disciplining function of poverty and its spiritual danger; it clarifies why Rav Tzadok here distinguishes holy inward poverty from harmful material destitution.

paragraphs.text: Nedarim 66a: a man vowed against benefiting from his unattractive niece; they brought her into R’ Yishmael’s house and beautified her, and R’ Yishmael — seeing the vow thereby void — “wept and said: the daughters of Israel are comely, only that poverty disfigures them” (banos Yisrael na’os hen, ela she-ha-aniyus menavaltan). Background: the Gemara’s poignant teaching that the true beauty of Israel’s daughters is merely masked by want. R’ Tzadok’s use: Israel’s poverty is no true blemish but “like a red trapping on a white horse” — a beauty; the “disfigurement” is only the outward want, while inwardly “the daughters of Israel are comely.”

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 33:11, 33:9: Yaakov pressed his gift upon Esav, saying “כִּי חַנַּנִי אֱלֹהִים וְכִי יֶשׁ לִי כֹל” — “for God has favored me, and because I have everything kol” (33:11) — whereas Esav had said only “יֶשׁ לִי רָב,” “I have much rav” (33:9). Meforshim: Rashi contrasts them — Yaakov says “all my need,” the tzaddik content with his portion, while Esav’s “much” is the boast of one still lacking. R’ Tzadok’s use: “yesh li kol” is the rung of Yaakov, who lacks nothing; Esav’s “rav” betrays that he “still lacks” — “and the belly of the wicked shall want” (Mishlei 13:25) — for the righteous are satisfied with their portion, but the wicked, however rich, are “great paupers.”

paragraphs.text: Mishlei 26:3: “שׁוֹט לַסּוּס, מֶתֶג לַחֲמוֹר, וְשֵׁבֶט לְגֵו כְּסִילִים” — “a whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of fools.” Background: Mishlei’s image of the instruments of discipline. R’ Tzadok’s use: he distinguishes the whip — “made only to strike,” a bare blow (the “rod for the back of fools”) — from the leather strap, “which is also made for adornment”; Israel’s chastening is the beautifying red strap, not the fool’s whip.

R’ Tzadok’s use: Haman typifies the nations’ “wealth” — the conceit that “my strength and the might of my hand made this valor,” boasting of riches as self-made — whereas in truth “all is in the hands of Heaven,” decreed before one is even formed.

paragraphs.text: Mishlei 27:1: “אַל תִּתְהַלֵּל בְּיוֹם מָחָר, כִּי לֹא תֵדַע מַה יֵּלֶד יוֹם” — “do not boast about tomorrow, for you know not what a day may bring forth.” Background: Mishlei’s caution against presuming upon the future. R’ Tzadok’s use: joined to “let a person not trust in himself until the day of his death” (Avos 2:4), this seals the point — the God-fearing man lives “all the days of his life in this affliction oni,” owning nothing and presuming nothing, “for he knows not what a day may bring forth.”

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The rectification of sight comes through oni, affliction — “Hashem saw my affliction.” David, “goodly to look upon,” called himself poor and accepted yissurin. This poverty is not material lack but the recognition that one owns nothing of himself: “poverty befits Israel like a red trapping on a white horse.” The nations say “my strength made this wealth”; the God-fearing man knows that all is in Heaven’s hands.

paragraphs.text: Devarim 17:20: among the laws of the king — “לְבִלְתִּי רוּם לְבָבוֹ מֵאֶחָיו, וּלְבִלְתִּי סוּר מִן הַמִּצְוָה יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאול” — “that his heart not be raised above his brothers, and that he not turn aside from the commandment, right or left.” Background: the Torah’s charge to the king, who writes and carries a Sefer Torah “to learn to fear Hashem” and remain humble despite his power. Meforshim: the Sifrei and Rashi stress that even a king may not lord himself over “his brothers.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this is “the essence of the kingship of Israel” and “the perfection of the king” — the mitzvah unique to a king is precisely the guard against “raising of the heart”; hence David, root of Malchus, is the dalet of lowliness, who “recognizes his lowliness and lack.”

paragraphs.text: Shemos 26:28: of the Mishkan’s wall-boards — “וְהַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכֹן בְּתוֹךְ הַקְּרָשִׁים, מַבְרִחַ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה” — “and the middle bar, within the boards, shall reach from end to end.” Background: the central crossbar running the full length of the Mishkan’s wall, binding all the boards together (per the Midrash, miraculously bending around all three sides). Meforshim: in Kabbalah this “middle bar” that “reaches from end to end” is Tiferes — the trait of Yaakov, “truth,” which mediates and joins the extremes. R’ Tzadok’s use: the vav in the middle of “David” is this “letter of truth” that “reaches from end to end” — the rung of Yaakov, “whose form is engraved on the Throne of Glory,” through whom the trait of Malchus is drawn only by cleaving to the very essence of the King. Sod Yesharim — the two dalets of David enclose the vav of connection: Sod Yesharim, Hoshana Rabbah 13:2, gives an unusually direct parallel to R’ Tzadok’s letter-symbolism. The name דוד, he writes, begins with a dalet because David knew ‘דלית ליה מגרמיה כלום’ — he possessed nothing from himself. The vav signifies the explicit connection Hashem then illuminates to the one who recognizes that dependence; precisely because David knows he has no independent power, Hashem shows him the bond through which all blessing reaches him. Yet after all his victories and revelations David still says ‘כי עני ואביון אנכי’ and ‘ה׳ לא גבה לבי ולא רמו עיני’; this continued self-nullification is the second dalet. The Sod Yesharim thus sharpens R’ Tzadok’s point that the vav of emes stands between two dalets. The first lowliness is not merely the condition before receiving Divine abundance, to be discarded once a person succeeds. The second dalet proves that even after the vav — after connection, strength, kingship, and salvation — the recipient has not converted the gift into self-possession. That is why Davidic Malchus can receive endlessly without becoming a rival sovereignty. Its greatness is real, but its truth is the knowledge that every greatness flowing through it remains the King’s. The structure of the name itself becomes a discipline of teshuvah: lack, connection, and then renewed lack even after illumination.

The first lowliness is not merely the condition before receiving Divine abundance, to be discarded once a person succeeds. The second dalet proves that even after the vav — after connection, strength, kingship, and salvation — the recipient has not converted the gift into self-possession. That is why Davidic Malchus can receive endlessly without becoming a rival sovereignty. Its greatness is real, but its truth is the knowledge that every greatness flowing through it remains the King’s. The structure of the name itself becomes a discipline of teshuvah: lack, connection, and then renewed lack even after illumination.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The purpose of yissurin is the reward of Olam Haba — “the righteous sit with their crowns,” delighting in the Shechinah’s radiance as companions that never part. This is the dalet of Yehudah: lowliness, eyes lifted on high, owning nothing but what is received from Above. After salvation the dalet becomes a hei; and “David” is a dalet at either end with a vav between — the king who knows his own lowliness.

p: (מ) וְדָן הוּא זַנְבָא דִּכְלָלוּת הָאַרְיֵה
And Dan is the tail of the collective lion,
וְהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ מִדַּת הַדִּין כִּשְׁמוֹ.
and he is the root of the attribute of judgment (din), as his name indicates.
וְעַל כֵּן שִׁמְשׁוֹן הָיָה שׁוֹפֵט וְיָדִין עַמּוֹ, לֹא מֶלֶךְ,
And therefore Samson was a judge who would judge his people, not a king.
וְעַל כֵּן בְּבִרְכַּת יַעֲקֹב נִמְשַׁל לְנָחָשׁ לֹא לְאַרְיֵה
and therefore in the blessing of Jacob he was compared to a serpent, not to a lion.
וְנוֹדַע דִּכְעַס הָאֲרִי מְעוֹרָב בְּרַחֲמָנוּת גַּם כֵּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ הַטִּבְעִיִּים
And it is known that the anger of the lion is intermingled with mercy as well, as the naturalists have stated,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן חֲמַת זוֹחֲלֵי עָפָר וּנְחָשִׁים
unlike the venomous wrath of the crawlers of the dust and serpents.
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא נָאָה לוֹ הַמְּלוּכָה
and therefore monarchy is not fitting for him.
כִּי מֵהַכַּעַס בָּא לְגַסּוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל דִּשְׁנֵיהֶם חַד
For from anger one comes to haughtiness, as I wrote above that both are one,
וְהֵם עַנְפֵי יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
and they are branches of the inclination toward idolatry,
דְּעַל כֵּן שָׂם יָרָבְעָם הָאֶחָד בְּדָן
which is why Jeroboam placed one of the golden calves in Dan,
וְשָׁם הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ לִמְצִיאוּת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
and there lies the root for the existence of idolatry in Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסִפְרֵי עַל פָּסוּק "פֶּן יֵשׁ בָּכֶם מִשְׁפָּחָה אוֹ שֵׁבֶט" – זֶה שֵׁבֶט דָּן
as they expounded in the Sifrei on the verse "Lest there be among you a family or tribe" (Deuteronomy 29:17)—this refers to the tribe of Dan,
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק  — דְּפֶסֶל מִיכָה עָבַר בַּיָּם
and that aligns with what they taught in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 103b) that the idol of Micah crossed the Red Sea.
וּבְתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ דְּמִיכָה בָּעַט בְּ"אָנֹכִי",
And in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu it is stated that Micah rebelled against the first commandment, "I am Hashem",
וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
which is the core foundation of the Jewishness of Israel,
דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא אָמַר "אָנֹכִי" בִּלְשׁוֹן צִיוּוּי
which is why He did not formulate "I am" in the imperative language of a command,
כִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים
for the root of Israel consists of believers, children of believers,
וְגַם עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּכְלָל זֶה
and even the idolaters of Israel are included in this,
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּבַעֲטִים בְּ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" מִכָּל מָקוֹם שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְבָבָם נִקְשָׁר בֶּאֱמוּנַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and even though they kick against "You shall have no other gods," nonetheless the root of their heart remains bound to faith in Hashem, blessed be He.
רַק מִיכָה שֶׁנִּתְמַכְמַךְ בַּבִּנְיָן
Only Micah who was crushed into the brick building of Egypt,
כִּי אוֹתָם שֶׁשָּׂמוּ בִּמְקוֹם לְבֵנִים בַּבִּנְיָן הוּא כְּאִלּוּ אֵין בָּהֶם אֶלָּא חֹמֶר הָעַפְרִי לְבַד
for those whom the Egyptians placed instead of bricks into the building were reduced to being as though they had nothing in them except crude earthly matter alone,
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב יֵשׁ בָּהֶם חֵלֶק אֱלֹהִי מִמַּעַל
and even though all the seed of Jacob possess a divine portion from Above,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לְעֹצֶם הַהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בְּמִצְרַיִם
nevertheless, owing to the immense immersion and sinking in Egypt,
יֵשׁ שֶׁהָיָה גּוּפָם חוֹמְרִי כָּל כָּךְ
there were those whose physical body became so coarsened and material,
עַד שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ הִתְחַבְּרוּת כְּלָל עִם נַפְשׁוֹ הָרוּחָנִית
that it had no connection whatsoever with its spiritual soul,
עַד שֶׁגַּם בְּחַיָּיו הָיָה כְּאִלּוּ נִפְרָד מִמֶּנּוּ
to the extent that even during his lifetime it was as though it were detached from him.
וְעוֹמֵד עֲלֵיהֶם בְּסוֹד מַקִּיף לְבַד
and hovered over them solely in the mystical mode of an external encompassing light (makif).
וְזֶה טַעַם "וְתַחַת רַגְלָיו כְּמַעֲשֵׂה לִבְנַת הַסַּפִּיר",
And this is the inner reason for the verse "And under His feet was like a paved work of sapphire stone" (Exodus 24:10),
שֶׁהוּא לְמַטָּה מִכָּל הַקּוֹמָה
which is beneath the entire stature of the holy realm.
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם בְּסוֹד מַקִּיף הָיָה מְזַכְּכָם עַד שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ סַפִּירִיִּים
except that nonetheless, in the mystery of the surrounding light, He would purify them until they became radiant as sapphire.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Parshas Shekalim §4): “and among the tribes too we find Shemos Rabbah 40, “אין לך גדול משבט יהודה ואין לך ירוד משבט דן” — “No tribe ranks greater than Yehudah, nor lower than Dan.” Rav Tzadok cites this contrast in Pri Tzaddik, Parshat Shekalim 4 and here uses it to explain Dan as the rear of the tribal body and Shimshon as judge, not king. The original Midrash in Shemot Rabbah 40:4 continues that Betzalel of Yehudah and Oholiav of Dan collaborated in building the Mishkan: “הגדול והקטן שוים לפני המקום” — great and small are equal before Hashem. The hierarchy therefore describes contrasting tribal functions and a test of humility, not a blanket dismissal of Dan or his descendants.

paragraphs.text: Devarim 32:24: in Ha’azinu — “וְשֶׁן בְּהֵמֹת אֲשַׁלַּח בָּם, עִם חֲמַת זֹחֲלֵי עָפָר” — “and the teeth of beasts I will send against them, with the venom of crawlers of the dust.” Background: among the punishments Moshe foretells — the “crawlers of the dust” are serpents. R’ Tzadok’s use: he contrasts the “wrath of the lion,” which “the naturalists said” is mingled with mercy (and so befits kingship), with the pure venom of the serpent, the “crawler of the dust” — and since Dan is likened in Yaakov’s blessing to a serpent, “kingship does not befit him,” only judgeship.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §23): he distinguishes the opposing inclinations of anger and desire, and relates Yosef’s restraint of desire to the particular danger of anger and idolatry: “דבגלעד ושכם שכיחי רוצחים שהם מקומות דזרעא דיוסף דשם יש עצירת תאוה וכן עיקר עבודה זרה התחיל מירבעם כי בדרז״ל הם קוראים שני יצרים דזנות ודעבודה זרה רק אחר שביטלו יצרא דעבודה זרה אין משמש אלא בכעס ורציחה אבל השורש הוא עבודה זרה” — “Murderers are common in Gilead and Shechem, places of Yosef’s offspring, where there is restraint of desire. Likewise the principal beginning of idolatry was with Yerovam. In the words of the Sages the two inclinations are called those of sexual immorality and idolatry; after the inclination to idolatry was abolished, it operates only through anger and murder, but its root is idolatry.” This is a close parallel to the completed sequence here from anger and pride to the root of idolatry and Yerovam’s idol in Dan. The original quoted sentence belongs to the source’s warning about the combined faults: “אבל בצירוף שניהם מתגבר ביותר חס ושלום” — “But in the combination of the two together it prevails all the more, God forbid.” The two there are idolatry/anger and desire; their combination strengthens the evil adversary. The full accurate sentence is preserved without turning it into praise of Rashbi’s hidden power.

paragraphs.text: Rav Tzadok attributes to Sifrei a derashah on Devarim 29:17: the Torah warns, “פֶּן יֵשׁ בָּכֶם… מִשְׁפָּחָה אוֹ שֵׁבֶט אֲשֶׁר לְבָבוֹ פֹנֶה הַיּוֹם מֵעִם ה׳” — “lest there be among you… a family or a tribe whose heart turns away this day from Hashem” — identifying the verse with this is the tribe of Dan.” A parallel appears in Midrash Tehillim 101:2, which explicitly associates the tribe of Dan, Michah’s image, and this verse. The precise wording was not independently located in the accessible Sifrei Devarim edition, so the attribution remains Rav Tzadok’s, not a separately certified Sifrei quotation. Danite idolatry is also discussed in Bamidbar Rabbah 2:10 in connection with Yerovam’s calf. Rav Tzadok’s use: Dan, as the “root of Din,” is likewise the “root of the existence of idolatry in Israel” — for “from anger one comes to coarseness,” and the two are “branches of the drive for idolatry.” Tanya — anger becomes a form of avodah zarah when it attributes independent power to the event: Tanya, Iggeres HaKodesh §25, returns explicitly to Chazal’s statement that anger is ‘as though one worshipped idolatry.’ The Alter Rebbe explains that in ordinary worldly matters the root error of anger is failure to recognize that ‘הכל בידי שמים חוץ מיראת שמים’: the circumstance that provoked the person did not acquire an independent sovereignty outside Divine providence. He carefully limits this principle, noting that in matters of Heaven one may indeed protest wrongdoing in order to separate someone from an issur, as Moshe himself became angry. This distinction complements R’ Tzadok’s movement from Dan’s Din to anger, coarseness, and avodah zarah. Anger becomes spiritually related to idolatry when it experiences the offending person or event as an autonomous force that has displaced Hashem from the field. The issue is not that all forcefulness is forbidden; Din itself is holy, and zeal for Torah can be required. The corruption begins when gevurah ceases to be an instrument of yiras Shamayim and becomes the assertion of a separate center of power. This also explains why R’ Tzadok can trace idolatry to a distortion of Din rather than to an intellectual doctrine alone: the emotional act of rage can already enact the same metaphysical falsehood — treating a created force as though it stood on its own. [Primary-source link: Midrash Tehillim 101:2]

paragraphs.text: Shemos 24:10: at the vision of the elders at Sinai — “וַיִּרְאוּ אֵת אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְתַחַת רַגְלָיו כְּמַעֲשֵׂה לִבְנַת הַסַּפִּיר, וּכְעֶצֶם הַשָּׁמַיִם לָטֹהַר” — “and they saw the God of Israel, and beneath His feet was like the work of a sapphire brick livnas ha-sapir, and like the very heavens in purity.” Meforshim: Rashi (from the Midrash) explains that this “brick” recalled the bricks of Israel’s Egyptian bondage — set before Him throughout the enslavement as a remembrance of their affliction. R’ Tzadok’s use: the “brick,” “beneath His feet,” is “below the entire stature” — the lowest, most material rung (Michah, “pressed into the building”); yet “in the secret of an encompassing light” it is refined until it becomes “sapphirine,” translucent.
