inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Dan is the “tail” of the collective lion and the root of Din — so Shimshon was a judge and not a king, and is likened to a serpent, whose venom does not befit kingship. From anger comes coarseness, the branches of the drive for idolatry; hence Yerovam set a calf in Dan. Even Israel’s idolaters keep faith at their root — only Michah was so material that his spiritual soul barely connected to him at all.

p: (מא) וּלְפִי שֶׁחֵשֶׁק מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה תִּיקּוּן הַגָּמוּר בְּיָמָיו
And because the passionate yearning of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was that the complete final rectification should take place in his days,
כִּי לֹא חָשַׁב שֶׁיְּקוּלְקַל עַל יְדֵי הָעֵגֶל
for he did not imagine that it would become ruined through the Golden Calf,
דְּעַל כֵּן קִבֵּל הַגֵּרִים דְּעֵרֶב רַב
which is why he accepted the converts of the mixed multitude (erev rav),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד גֵּרִים גְּרוּרִים
just as in the ultimate future there will be attached converts (gerim gerurim),
אַף דְּאֵין מְקַבְּלִים גֵּרִים בִּימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ,
even though prospective converts are not accepted in the days of the Messiah,
וְכֵן רָצָה לְתַקֵּן גַּם אֵלּוּ,
and so he desired to rectify these as well.
וְכָל מַה שֶּׁאֶפְשָׁר לָבוֹא בַּסּוֹף לִידֵי תִּיקּוּן חָשַׁב שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֵּן בְּיָמָיו
and whatever could possibly arrive at the end of time unto rectification, he thought would occur right then in his days.
וְצִיוָּהוּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהוֹצִיא מִיכָה לְפִי שֶׁאֵלָיו הָיָה לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת
And Hashem, blessed be He, commanded him to bring forth Micah from the brickwork because Moses had a direct affinity with him,
שֶׁהֲרֵי נִתְחַבֵּר אֵלָיו יְהוֹנָתָן מִזַּרְעוֹ,
since Jonathan, of the descendants of Moses, ultimately attached himself unto him as an idolatrous priest,
וְעַל יָדוֹ נִתְבָּרֵר שׁוֹרֶשׁ טָעוּתוֹ
and through him the exact root of Micah's theological error was clarified
בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמַר: "עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יֵיטִיב ה' לִי וְגוֹמֵר".
in what Micah proclaimed: "Now know I that Hashem will do me good, etc." (Judges 17:13).
דְּנִרְאֶה לִי דְּמִכָּתוּב זֶה לָמְדוּ שֶׁבָּעַט בְּ"אָנֹכִי" וְלֹא בְּ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ"
For it appears to me that from this verse the Sages derived that he rebelled against "I am" and not against "You shall have no other gods",
מַה שֶּׁאָמַר "יֵיטִיב ה'" – שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה
from the fact that he said "Hashem will do good"—using the ineffable Name Havayah,
וְלֹא נִמְצָא כֵּן בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּשׁוּם מָקוֹם כַּיָּדוּעַ,
and we do not find such usage in the context of pagan idolatry anywhere, as is known,
דְּעַל שֵׁם זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וּכְבוֹדִי לְאַחֵר לֹא אֶתֵּן",
concerning which it is declared: "and My glory I will not give to another" (Isaiah 42:8),
אֲבָל זֶה מוֹרֶה עַל גַּסּוּת חָמְרוֹ שֶׁהָיָה מְרוּחָק לְגַמְרֵי מֵרוּחָנִיּוּת
rather this demonstrates the coarse density of his physical nature, being completely distant from spirituality.
וְלֹא הֵבִין עִנְיַן הָרוּחָנִית כְּלָל
and failing to understand the true essence of spirituality at all.
וְאַף הוּא הָיָה מִכְּלַל הַמַּאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים וְהֶאֱמִין בַּה
', And he too was among the collective of believers, children of believers, and believed in Hashem.
אֲבָל דִּמָּה שֶׁעַל הַפֶּסֶל שֶׁלּוֹ גַּם כֵּן חָל שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה
yet he imagined that upon his sculptured idol the Name Havayah likewise rested.
וְזֶהוּ הַבְּעִיטָה בְּ"אָנֹכִי",
And this constitutes kicking against the declaration "I am",
דְּלֹא עָבַד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה לְהַמְצִיא אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים כְּלָל
in that he did not serve idolatry to invent other competing deities at all,
דְּהֶאֱמִין בַּהֲוָיָ"ה
for he believed in Havayah,
רַק שֶׁהִגְשִׁים כְּפִי חָמְרִיּוּתוֹ,
only that he corporealized and materialized God according to his dense materiality,
וַהֲרֵי כָּפַר בַּאֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּבָעַט בְּ"אָנֹכִי" לֹא בְּ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ".
and thereby denied the transcendent true reality of Hashem, blessed be He, rebelling against "I am" rather than "You shall have no other gods".
וְכָל מַאֲמִינֵי הַהַגְשָׁמָה כֵּן
And all who subscribe to corporealizing God are in this category,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָרַאֲבַ"ד בְּהִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה (פֶּרֶק ג הֲלָכָה ז) קְרָאָם "גְּדוֹלִים וְטוֹבִים",
even though the Ra'avad in the Laws of Repentance (3:7) termed them "greater and better than him",
הַיְינוּ לְפִי שֶׁהָיוּ שׁוֹגְגִים בָּזֶה
meaning because they were inadvertent in this error.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם מוֹדֶה דְּשָׁגוּ בָּזֶה
yet he nonetheless admits that they gravely erred in this.
וְאַף דְּגַם הַשּׁוֹגֵג צָרִיךְ כַּפָּרָה
And even though the inadvertent sinner likewise requires atonement,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא נִקְרָא רָשָׁע כְּלָל
nonetheless he is not designated wicked at all.
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הִכִּיר כָּל יָמָיו בְּשִׁגְגָתוֹ וְלֹא שָׁב מִמֶּנָּה
even though he never recognized his inadvertent error throughout his life and never repented from it.
וְאַף מִיכָה וַדַּאי מוּטְעֶה הָיָה
And even Micah was certainly under a delusion,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְרָא "בָּעַט" לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ לִלְמוֹד וְלֹא לָמַד
yet he is nonetheless termed one who "kicked", because he ought to have learned and failed to learn,
וְהָיָה קָרוֹב לְמֵזִיד בָּזֶה
and he bordered on willful intent in this
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁעָבַר תְּחִלָּה עַל שְׁתֵּי דִּבְּרוֹת: "לֹא תִגְנֹב" וְ"לֹא תִשָּׂא",
by having transgressed beforehand two commandments: "You shall not steal" and "You shall not take (the Name in vain)",
שֶׁשָּׁמַע אָלָה וְקִבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ וְלֹא הוֹדָה
in that he heard his mother's curse and accepted it upon himself without confessing,
וְעַל כִּבּוּד אֵם
and also transgressed the honor of his mother.
וּבִתְלָתָא הָוֵי חֲזָקָה שֶׁבָּא לְטַמֵּא לִהְיוֹת פּוֹתְחִין
and upon three transgressions there is an established presumption that when one comes to defile himself, openings are cleared for him to fall further.

paragraphs.text: Yevamos 24b: “the Sages taught: we do not accept converts in the days of the Mashiach — just as they accepted no converts in the days of David or of Shlomo.” Background: formal conversion is suspended in eras where ulterior motive is suspected. R’ Tzadok’s use: yet in the Future there will be “self-attached converts gerim gerurim,” who join of their own accord; Moshe, longing for a complete tikkun already in his own days, “accepted the converts of the erev rav” in that very spirit — reaching to rectify even them.

But Avraham Avinu taught the nations of the world; for of all the converts he made and ‘the souls they made in Charan,’ none remained reckoned among Israel — since there was not yet a ‘name of Israel’ such that ‘a convert who converts is like a newborn child’ into Jewishness.” (This is why, as the se’if says, Moshe could take in the erev rav: through Moshe the Torah ‘establishes’ even the attached converts within Israel — the very work Moshe hoped would bring a complete tikkun in his days.)

paragraphs.text: Shoftim 18:30: of Michah’s idol among the Danites — “וִיהוֹנָתָן בֶּן גֵּרְשֹׁם בֶּן מְנַשֶּׁה, הוּא וּבָנָיו הָיוּ כֹהֲנִים לְשֵׁבֶט הַדָּנִי” — “and Yehonasan son of Gershom son of Menasheh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan.” Meforshim: the nun of “Menasheh מנשה” is written suspended (nun teluyah), and the Sages (Bava Basra 109b) read the name as “Moshe” — Yehonasan was in truth the grandson of Moshe, the nun inserted only to shield Moshe’s honor. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is Moshe’s “connection” to Michah — since Yehonasan, of Moshe’s own seed, later served as Michah’s priest — which is why Hashem bade Moshe “bring out Michah” from the Nile mud.

paragraphs.text: Yeshayah 42:8: “אֲנִי ה׳ הוּא שְׁמִי, וּכְבוֹדִי לְאַחֵר לֹא אֶתֵּן, וּתְהִלָּתִי לַפְּסִילִים” — “I am Hashem, that is My Name, and My glory I will not give to another, nor My praise to idols.” Background: God declares that the honor of His Name belongs to Him alone, never to idols. R’ Tzadok’s use: precisely because the Name Havayah is never “given to another” — never found applied to idolatry anywhere — Michah’s applying it to his own idol was not the “invention of other gods” but the corporealizing of the true God: a “kicking at Anochi.”

paragraphs.text: Shoftim 17:13: Michah’s words when a wandering Levite became his priest — “עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יֵיטִיב ה׳ לִי, כִּי הָיָה לִי הַלֵּוִי לְכֹהֵן” — “now I know that Hashem will do me good, for the Levite has become my priest.” Background: Michah’s private idol-shrine gains a Levite officiant. Rav Tzadok writes “ונראה לי דמכתוב זה למדו” — “It appears to me that from this verse they inferred” — proposing his own explanation of the tradition that Michah “kicked at Anochi,” not at “no other gods” — for he said “Hashem Havayah will do me good,” a Name never applied to idolatry; he did believe in Havayah, only he “corporealized” Him upon his idol. Tanya — the basic error is imagining a created thing as possessing existence apart from the Divine power within it: Tanya, Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah ch. 2, describes the ‘root of the error’ of those who deny continuous Divine providence as the comparison of creation to a human artisan. Once a craftsman finishes a vessel, the vessel can remain after his hands leave it; but creation ex nihilo is entirely different. Were the Creator’s power to withdraw for an instant, the created being would return to absolute nothingness. Therefore ‘כח הפועל בנפעל תמיד’ — the creative force must continuously be present within the creature to sustain it. This provides a useful conceptual complement to R’ Tzadok’s diagnosis of Michah. Michah did not simply erase the Name of Hashem; he could still say ‘ייטיב ה׳ לי.’ His corruption lay in fastening Divine presence to a separate corporeal object, as though the physical form could be a self-standing bearer or localization of God. The Tanya’s account explains why such corporealization is so profound a mistake: the creature has no independent ontological platform upon which God could later ‘rest’ as an added presence. Its entire being at every moment is only the effect of the Divine word sustaining it. Thus even when the language of faith remains on the lips, treating a created thing as an autonomous locus of power already fractures yichud. R’ Tzadok’s category of Michah as gravely mistaken rather than simply atheistic becomes more intelligible against this distinction. The identification of Judges 17:13 as the specific proof is Rav Tzadok’s inference, not an independently located quotation in the Gemara.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas Shabbos §1: “כי אפי׳ פושעי ישראל שא׳ דמלאים מצות כרימון היינו במצות הצדקה וגמ״ח בפרט דבזה אפי׳ פושעי ישראל בגופן קרקפתא דלא מנח תפילין ושאר רשעי ישראל היותר גדולים שאין בה שום לחלוחית של מצוה מ״מ הם מלאים ג״כ במצות הצדקה וגמ״ח שישנו בכל זרע ישראל שהם רחמנים וגומלי חסדים כמשרז״ל אם לא אותן דמערב רב קאתו כמ״ש (בביצה לב:) וע״כ לא ידח נדח מזרע ישראל אפי׳ מהיותר גרועים בתכלית יש בהם איזה שורש טוב בהעלם הנטוע מאבותם בהיותם זרע אברהם יצחק ויעקב.” — “For even the sinners of Israel, of whom it is said that they are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate, are so particularly in the mitzvos of charity and kindness. In this, even Israel’s bodily sinners, the head that has not worn tefillin, and the greatest other wicked people of Israel, in whom there is no moisture of a mitzvah, are nevertheless also full of the mitzvos of charity and kindness. These exist in all the seed of Israel, who are merciful and do kindness, as our Sages said—except those who come from the mixed multitude, as stated in Beitzah 32b. Therefore no outcast of the seed of Israel will be cast off: even the utterly worst have some concealed good root planted by their fathers, as the seed of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov.” This distinguishes a surviving good root from the culpable actions Rav Tzadok has just traced; it does not erase those actions or extend this particular proof to the erev rav.

paragraphs.text: Be’er Moshe (R’ Moshe Yechiel Epstein of Ozherov), Neviim — Shoftim, p. 246 (inherited print-edition reference, not independently checked), cites Sanhedrin 103b: “מפני מה לא מנו את מיכה? מפני שפתו מצויה לעוברי דרכים” — “Why was Michah not included among those enumerated? Because his bread was readily available to wayfarers.” The Gemara also reports that God restrained the angels from pushing him away on account of this hospitality. This establishes that Michah was not included in that specified group on account of a genuine merit; it does NOT declare that the idol was permissible or that Michah was without culpability. Its relevance here is limited to the coexistence of a significant good deed with grievous theological error, while Rav Tzadok independently argues that his initial confusion involved mistaken corporeal conceptions. [Primary-source link: Sanhedrin 103b]

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Kometz HaMinchah I §66: “שכר עבירה עבירה, ע״ד שאמרו (שבת ק״ה) דרכו של יצר הרע היום אומר וכו׳ ועבירה גוררת עבירה וכל עבירה גוררת דוגמתה ממינה ולכן לא תרוי בתאות אכילה ולא תחטא בתאות עריות.” — “The reward of a transgression is a transgression, in the manner of what they said (Shabbos 105): such is the way of the evil inclination—today it says, and so forth. A transgression draws a transgression, and every transgression draws its like, of its own kind. Therefore do not satiate yourself with the desire for eating, and you will not sin with the desire for forbidden relations.” This directly illuminates Rav Tzadok’s account of Michah’s earlier transgressions forming the pattern through which a more serious error became culpable.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Moshe longed for a complete tikkun in his own days, and therefore accepted the erev rav. He was told to raise Michah from the Nile mud, since Michah was connected to him. Michah’s error was corporealizing Hashem: he believed in the Name, but imagined it rested upon his idol — “kicking at Anochi” rather than at “you shall have no other gods.” Believers in corporeality are mistaken rather than wicked, yet he was close to deliberate.

p: (מב) וְהוּא הָיָה מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף
And Micah was from the seed of Joseph,
וְנִתְגַּלְגֵּל פִּסְלוֹ לִבְנֵי דָן
and his sculpted idol rolled over to the children of Dan,
שֶׁהֵם הַתְחָלַת גִּילּוּי זַרְעָא דְּרָחֵל עַל יְדֵי בִּלְהָה שִׁפְחָתָהּ
who represent the initial manifestation of the seed of Rachel through Bilhah her handmaid.
שֶׁרָצְתָה לְהִבָּנוֹת מִמֶּנָּה בְּעוֹד שֶׁהָיָה עֲדַיִן מִדַּת הַדִּין נוֹתֶנֶת שֶׁלֹּא תִּפָּקֵד רָחֵל
who desired to be built up through her while the attribute of strict judgment still dictated that Rachel herself not be remembered with child.
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרָה "דָּנַנִּי אֱלֹהִים",
Which is why Rachel said: "God has judged me (danani)" (Genesis 30:6),
רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר עַל שֶׁמָּנַע הַהוֹלָדָה מִמֶּנָּה הִצְדִּיקָה הַדִּין
meaning that over His withholding childbearing from her, she justified the divine verdict,
וְגַם "שָׁמַע בְּקוֹלִי" לְהִבָּנוֹת מִשִּׁפְחָתָהּ.
and also "He heard my voice" to be built up through her handmaid.
וּקְרָאַתּוּ דָּן עַל שֵׁם מִדַּת הַדִּין בָּהּ,
And she named him Dan after the attribute of judgment in her case,
כִּי עַל יָדוֹ נִתְגַּלָּה לָהּ שֶׁהַכֹּל בַּדִּין
for through him it was revealed to her that all is executed through strict judgment;
כִּי בְּלֵידַת כָּל שֵׁבֶט וִיצִיאָתוֹ לַאֲוִיר הָעוֹלָם נִתְגַּלָּה אוֹרוֹ בָּעוֹלָם
for upon the birth of each tribe and its emergence into the atmosphere of the world, its distinct light was unveiled in the cosmos,
וְנוֹדַע לִמְבִינֵי מַדָּע כָּאָבוֹת וְאִמָּהוֹת כָּל מַעֲלוֹת וְחֶסְרוֹנוֹת שֶׁבּוֹ.
and all virtues and deficiencies within it became known to those of spiritual discernment, like the Patriarchs and Matriarchs.
וְהִרְגִּישָׁה בְּיִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכַעַס הַנִּמְצָא בוֹ
And she sensed the inclination toward idolatry and anger that existed within him,
וְהַתְחָלָתָם בְּזַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף
and their prospective origin within the seed of Joseph,
וְהֵבִינָה מִזֶּה הַצְדָּקַת דִּינָהּ.
and she understood from this the justice of her personal judgment.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם "שָׁמַע בְּקוֹלָהּ" גַּם כֵּן דְּתוּכַל לְהִבָּנוֹת עַל יְדֵי זֶה
And nonetheless "He heard her voice" likewise that she could be built up through this.
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה נֶחְלַשׁ כֹּחַ אוֹתוֹ יֵצֶר
for through this externalization the force of that base inclination was weakened.
דְּ"כָּל הַגָּדוֹל מֵחֲבֵירוֹ יִצְרוֹ גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ"
For "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than he" (Sukkah 52a),
דִּכְפִי תֹּקֶף הַמַּעֲלָה כָּךְ תֹּקֶף הַחִסָּרוֹן מִסִּטְרָא דְּעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע
for commensurate with the intensity of spiritual virtue is the severity of deficiency stemming from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil,
שֶׁהֵם זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה הָרַע נֶגֶד הַטּוֹב וּמַקְבִּיל לְעֻמָּתוֹ כַּיָּדוּעַ.
which stand one opposite the other, evil facing good and mirroring it symmetrically, as is known.
וְדָן שֶׁהוּא יָרוּד שֶׁבַּשְּׁבָטִים מִצַּד הַמַּעֲלָה
And Dan who is the lowliest of the tribes in terms of stature,
גַּם הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁבּוֹ יָרוּד וְאֵין הַיֵּצֶר תַּקִּיף כָּל כָּךְ בּוֹ,
the deficiency in him is likewise lower, and the inclination is not so acutely potent within him,
וּלְפִי שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְחַלֵּק מִמֶּנּוּ לְדָן שֶׁיָּצָא תְּחִלָּה
and because a portion of it was already siphoned off unto Dan who was born first,
נֶחְלַשׁ גַּם בְּיוֹסֵף אַחַר כָּךְ.
it was subsequently mitigated and weakened within Joseph as well.
וְאַף שֶׁבּוֹ עִיקַּר תָּקְפּוֹ וְהַתְחָלָתוֹ בִּיצִיאָה לַפּוֹעַל
And even though within Joseph lay its primary potential intensity and initial emergence into actuality,
דְּמַה שֶּׁהָיָה בְּדָן הָיָה עַל יְדֵי יָרָבְעָם
for what manifested in Dan occurred through the agency of Jeroboam.
וְכֵן בְּנֵי דָן לָקְחוּ מִמִּיכָה
and likewise the sons of Dan took the idol from Micah,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם שׁוֹרֶשׁ יוֹסֵף הוּא עִיקַּר תּוֹלְדוֹת יַעֲקֹב זֶרַע אֱמֶת
nevertheless the essential root of Joseph is the primary offspring of Jacob, seed of truth,
וְאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת בֶּאֱמֶת לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְלֹא לַגּוֹיִם כְּלָל
and he holds no true intrinsic affinity to idolatry or to the gentiles at all,
וּמִמֶּנּוּ קָמוּ מְלָכִים
and from him kings arose
דְּגַם בָּהֶם יֵשׁ בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ תֹּקֶף הַיִּרְאָה וְהַכָּרַת הַחִסָּרוֹן וּלְבִלְתִּי רוּם לְבָבוֹ,
who likewise retain within their root the intensity of divine awe, the perception of personal lack, and not exalting the heart.
וְהַגֵּיאוּת הוּא רַק בַּהוּצֵי הַסּוֹבְבִים לַאָסָא וְלֹא חִסָּרוֹן בְּעֶצֶם
and any haughtiness is merely among the briers surrounding the myrtle, not an essential defect in his core.
אַךְ דָּן שֶׁהוּא הַיָּרוּד וְ"רַגְלֶיהָ יֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת" רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן
However, Dan who is the lowliest and aligns with "her feet go down to death" (Proverbs 5:5), may the Merciful One spare us.
נֶחְשָׁב אֶצְלוֹ זֶה כְּחִסָּרוֹן בְּעֶצֶם שֶׁלְּבָבוֹ פּוֹנֶה וְגוֹמֵר
this is deemed within him an essential deficiency, where his heart turns away, etc.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 30:3: Rachel, still barren, gave her handmaid Bilhah to Yaakov — “הִנֵּה אֲמָתִי בִלְהָה בֹּא אֵלֶיהָ… וְאִבָּנֶה גַם אָנֹכִי מִמֶּנָּה” — “behold my handmaid Bilhah, come to her… and I too shall be built up through her.” Background: as Sarah had done with Hagar, Rachel seeks to be “built up” through her maidservant’s children. R’ Tzadok’s use: Bilhah’s sons are “the beginning of the emergence of Rachel’s seed” — Rachel “wishing to be built up” through her handmaid while Din still decreed that she herself not yet bear; and indeed “He heard her voice,” for the harsh drive was thereby drawn off and weakened.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 30:6: at the birth of Bilhah’s first son — “וַתֹּאמֶר רָחֵל, דָּנַנִּי אֱלֹהִים וְגַם שָׁמַע בְּקֹלִי וַיִּתֶּן לִי בֵּן, עַל כֵּן קָרְאָה שְׁמוֹ דָּן” — “and Rachel said: God has judged me danani, and He has also heard my voice and given me a son; therefore she called his name Dan.” Rashi reads “דנני וחיבני וזכני” — “He judged me, found me culpable, and then granted me merit/vindication.” This differs from Rav Tzadok’s homiletic explanation. R’ Tzadok’s use: Rachel named him for “the trait of Din in her” — sensing at his birth (as the Imahos could) the “drive for idolatry and anger” whose beginning lay in her own line (Yosef’s), and thereby “justifying the judgment” that had kept her barren; yet “He heard my voice,” for through this very child the power of that drive was weakened. Be’er Mayim Chaim — ‘Dan’ itself is remembered by Chazal as a point where avodah zarah obstructs holy advance: Be’er Mayim Chaim, Bereishis 12:8:6, cites Chazal’s derashah on “וירדוף עד דן” as a place-name associated with idolatry, which “strikes before and behind,” and interprets Avraham’s altar between Beis-El and Ai as an attempt to interrupt that spiritual danger. This source does not explicitly establish the specific Rachel-through-Bilhah genealogy proposed by Rav Tzadok. This does not supply R’ Tzadok’s specific genealogy from Rachel through Bilhah, but it gives a striking Chassidic echo to the very association on which he builds: the name and place of Dan stand in Chazal as a frontier at which the power of avodah zarah becomes capable of arresting even Avraham’s forward movement. R’ Tzadok’s contribution is to locate that danger within the inner structure of the shevatim and to explain why it appears specifically at the ‘lowest’ end of Rachel’s extension. The Be’er Mayim Chaim helps frame the severity of the point without making Dan himself synonymous with evil. Avraham’s response is to build a mizbe’ach — to establish an opposing orientation toward Hashem. So too in R’ Tzadok, the very force that can descend into Din and anger is not discarded; it must be weakened, redirected, and ultimately restored to the service of the one God.

rich.text: : at the birth of Bilhah’s first son — “
וַתֹּאמֶר רָחֵל, דָּנַנִּי אֱלֹהִים וְגַם שָׁמַע בְּקֹלִי וַיִּתֶּן לִי בֵּן
and Rachel said: God has judged me danani, and He has also heard my voice and given me a son

; therefore she called his name Dan.” Rashi reads “דנני וחיבני וזכני” — “He judged me, found me culpable, and then granted me merit/vindication.” This differs from Rav Tzadok’s homiletic explanation. R’ Tzadok’s use: Rachel named him for “the trait of

in her” — sensing at his birth (as the Imahos could) the “drive for idolatry and anger” whose beginning lay in her own line (Yosef’s), and thereby “justifying the judgment” that had kept her barren; yet “He heard my voice,” for through this very child the power of that drive was weakened. Be’er Mayim Chaim — ‘Dan’ itself is remembered by Chazal as a point where avodah zarah obstructs holy advance: Be’er Mayim Chaim,

, cites Chazal’s derashah on “וירדוף עד דן” as a place-name associated with idolatry, which “strikes before and behind,” and interprets Avraham’s altar between Beis-El and Ai as an attempt to interrupt that spiritual danger. This source does not explicitly establish the specific Rachel-through-Bilhah genealogy proposed by Rav Tzadok. This does not supply R’ Tzadok’s specific genealogy from Rachel through Bilhah, but it gives a striking Chassidic echo to the very association on which he builds: the name and place of Dan stand in Chazal as a frontier at which the power of avodah zarah becomes capable of arresting even Avraham’s forward movement. R’ Tzadok’s contribution is to locate that danger within the inner structure of the shevatim and to explain why it appears specifically at the ‘lowest’ end of Rachel’s extension. The Be’er Mayim Chaim helps frame the severity of the point without making Dan himself synonymous with evil. Avraham’s response is to build a mizbe’ach — to establish an opposing orientation toward Hashem. So too in R’ Tzadok, the very force that can descend into Din and anger is not discarded; it must be weakened, redirected, and ultimately restored to the service of the one God.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Michah was of Yosef’s seed, yet his idol “rolled” to the children of Dan — the first emergence of Rachel’s line, through Bilhah. Rachel named him Dan, sensing in this child the drive for idolatry and anger whose beginning lay in her own line. “The greater the man, the greater his drive”: Dan, lowest of the tribes, has a lesser though real one, while Yosef’s root has no connection to idolatry at all.

p: (מג) וְעַל כֵּן לֹא נָפַל לַשֵּׁבֶט הַדָּנִי נַחֲלָה בְּתוֹךְ שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד פֶּסֶל מִיכָה
And therefore an allotted inheritance did not settle for the Danite tribe among the tribes of Israel until the episode of Micah's idol,
שֶׁהָיוּ מְבַקְשִׁים אָז עֲדַיִן נַחֲלָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּעִנְיָן בְּסֵפֶר שׁוֹפְטִים (יח, א).
for they were still seeking an inheritance at that time, as stated in the context in the Book of Judges (18:1).
דְּנַחֲלַת הָאָרֶץ לְזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא יְרוּשָּׁה מֵאָבוֹת
For the inheritance of the Land to the seed of Israel is an ancestral patrimony,
מוֹרָה עַל שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִתּוֹלַדְתָּם
pointing directly to the root sanctity of Israel from their birth,
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִקְרָא "אֱלֹהֵי הָאָרֶץ",
because Hashem, blessed be He, is called "the God of the Land".
וְכֵן הַתּוֹרָה עִיקָּרָהּ בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ן
and similarly the Torah has its primary existence in the Land of Israel, as the Ramban wrote.
וְזֶהוּ קְדֻשַּׁת הָאָרֶץ שֶׁהֵקִיאָה כָּל הַגּוֹיִם
And this is the sanctity of the Land that vomited out all the gentiles
וְלֹא קִבְּלָה אֶלָּא בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
and accepted none other than the children of Israel.
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת אֲבוֹתָם שֶׁזָּכוּ עַל יָדָם לְהַבְטָחַת נַחֲלַת הָאָרֶץ
who retain within them the root holiness of their Patriarchs through which they merited the promise of inheriting the Land.
וּמַה שֶּׁלֹּא נִכְבַּשׁ הַכֹּל בִּימֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עַד יְמֵי דָּוִד
And the fact that the entire territory was not conquered in the days of Joshua until the days of David,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִתְבָּרְרָה קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲדַיִן לְגַמְרֵי
was because the sanctity of Israel was not yet fully elucidated.
עַד דּוֹר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
until the generation of King David, peace be upon him, who represents the culmination of the Congregation of Israel.
וּבְנֵי דָן שֶׁלֹּא נִתְבָּרֵר חֶלְקָם וְנַחֲלָתָם בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
And the Danites whose portion and inheritance in the Land of Israel remained unclarified,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִתְבָּרֵר עֲדַיִן שׁוֹרֶשׁ מַעֲלַת קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּקִרְבָּם עַד אָז
signified that the root of Israel's lofty sanctity within them had not been clarified until then.
כִּי נִתְבָּרֵר מַעֲלָתָם
for only then was their true stature elucidated.
וּלְעוֹלָם הַמַּעֲלָה מוֹשֶׁכֶת הַחִסָּרוֹן עִמָּהּ,
And spiritual stature perpetually draws the corresponding deficiency along with it,
וְנִתְגַּלָּה אָז גַּם כֵּן חֶסְרוֹנוֹ שֶׁמַּחֲמָתוֹ לֹא מָצְאוּ נַחֲלָה עַד אָז
and there was likewise revealed at that moment his deficiency on account of which they had not found an inheritance until then.
וּלְפִי שֶׁזֶּה חִסָּרוֹן בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת עַל כֵּן אֵחֲרוֹ הַכָּתוּב
and because this touched upon a flaw in the very root of Jewishness, Scripture placed it later in the narrative.
וְסִדֵּר סִפּוּר זֶה אַחַר סִפּוּרֵי שִׁמְשׁוֹן אַף שֶׁקָּדַם לוֹ הַרְבֵּה
And it arranged this account after the narratives of Samson even though it preceded him chronologically by far,
כְּמִדַּת הַכְּתוּבִים לְהַקְדִּים הָרְפוּאָה לַמַּכָּה
in keeping with the biblical practice of placing the remedy before the affliction.
כִּי שִׁמְשׁוֹן הוּא הָיָה הַיּוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל שֶׁבְּשֵׁבֶט דָּן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וּבוֹ הָיָה תִּיקּוּנָם
for Samson was the greatest figure of the tribe of Dan in this world, and in him lay their rectification.
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגַּם הוּא בָּחַר בִּבְנוֹת הָעֲרֵלִים
For even though he too chose from among the daughters of the uncircumcised,
וְנִרְאָה כְּאִלּוּ יֵשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת עִם עֲרֵלִים
and appeared as though he held an affinity with the uncircumcised,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַכָּתוּב הֵעִיד עָלָיו כִּי מֵאֵת ה' הָיְתָה זֹאת
nonetheless Scripture testified concerning him that "it was of Hashem" (Judges 14:4),
לִנְקוֹם אַדְּרַבָּה עַל יְדֵי זֶה מֵהֶם וּלְהַכְנִיעָם
in order, on the contrary, to take vengeance through this upon them and subdue them.
וּלְרַע לוֹ לָאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל
and to bring ruin unto the corrupt archetype of Belial.
וְנֶאֱמַר שָׁם בְּעִנְיַן מִיכָה
And it is stated there in the narrative of Micah,
וְכֵן כְּעִנְיַן הַתְחָלַת סִפּוּר דִּבְנֵי דָן אַחַר כָּךְ:
as well as at the outset of the subsequent narrative of the Danites:
"בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם אֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל".
"In those days there was no king in Israel" (Judges 17:6, 18:1).
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי מִצַּד מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת הוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
And this means that from the perspective of the attribute of Malchut (monarchy) lies the total perfection of the Congregation of Israel,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת חִסָּרוֹן בָּזֶה בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת
and it is impossible for a defect in the essential root of Jewishness to occur
רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר עֲדַיִן אֵין מֶלֶךְ
except when there is as yet no king.
וְלֹא נִשְׁלַם עֲדַיִן בִּנְיַן קוֹמַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁלֵימוּת
and the construction of the spiritual stature of the Congregation of Israel is not yet culminated.
וְעַל כֵּן עָמַד פֶּסֶל מִיכָה רַק כָּל זְמַן הֱיוֹת בֵּית אֱלֹהִים בְּשִׁילֹה
And therefore the idol of Micah endured only so long as the House of God stood in Shiloh,
שֶׁהוּא בְּשֵׁבֶט אֶפְרַיִם אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִבְחַר בּוֹ לְנַחֲלָה
which was situated in the territory of Ephraim whom He did not choose for an enduring heritage.
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִבְחַר יְרוּשָׁלַיִם שֶׁהוּא הַנַּחֲלָה
and all the while Jerusalem, which is the eternal heritage, had not yet been chosen.
הַיְינוּ שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא נִתְבָּרֵר בְּחִירַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְגַמְרֵי
That is, the absolute chosenness of Israel had not yet been finalized,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּתוֹכָם לְנַחֲלָה קְבוּעָה וְקַיָּימָא
such that His Shechinah would abide amidst them as a permanent, immutable heritage,
וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה אָז מְצִיאוּת פֶּסֶל מִיכָה
and therefore there was room then for the phenomenon of Micah's idol.
שֶׁהוּא הַבְּעִיטָה בְּ"אָנֹכִי" שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל
which was the rebellion against "I am", the foundation of Israel's sanctity.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §37): “שזכו לא"י על ידי יסורים שממתקין את הבשר רצה לומר חלק גופני באדם” — “they merited Eretz Yisrael through suffering that refines the flesh, meaning the bodily aspect of the human being.” He relates the sanctity of the Land to the domain of action and refinement of embodied deeds. In this se’if, the distribution of tribal inheritance reflects the disclosure of a tribe’s covenantal root, rather than an arbitrary allocation; this is a directly relevant Rav Tzadok parallel. The Land is not merely acquired — it is accepted only by those in whom the bodily portion has been made fit to hold it.

paragraphs.text: Ramban, Vayikra 18:25 (on “וַתָּקִא הָאָרֶץ אֶת יֹשְׁבֶיהָ,” “and the Land vomited out its inhabitants”): Ramban writes “כי עקר כל המצות ליושבים בארץ ה׳” — “for the primary setting of all the commandments is for those who dwell in the Land of Hashem.” He cites the obligation to maintain the commandments in exile as signs to preserve their familiarity until return. Background: the verse warns that the Land itself expels those who defile it. R’ Tzadok’s use: since “the inheritance of the Land is a bequest from the Avos,” the Land “spewed out all the nations and accepted only” Israel, who bear “the root of the holiness of their fathers”; hence Dan’s late inheritance signals that the root of his holiness (and its shadow-deficiency) surfaced only later. Sefas Emes — return is possible because the sin is accidental to the inherited root of Israel: Sefas Emes, Nitzavim 5:2, reads ‘אתם נצבים היום כולכם’ as describing an eternal standing of Klal Yisrael before Hashem. The work of each individual is to nullify himself to that whole. Because the Torah’s statement is itself enduring — ‘שפת אמת תכון לעד’ — even the wicked can return: ‘החטא רק במקרה שנפרש מכללות ישראל ולכן יכול לחזור לשורשו, כמאמר לירושת אבותי אני חוזר.’ Sin is a contingent separation from the collective; teshuvah is a return to the inherited root of the fathers. This is an exceptionally close complement to R’ Tzadok’s language in the present se’if. The Land is not merely territory distributed by lot but ‘ירושת אבות,’ a bequest whose reception reflects the underlying covenantal root. Dan’s delayed inheritance can therefore symbolize a delayed clarification of how his particular place belongs within that inherited holiness. The Sefas Emes also guards against reading R’ Tzadok’s discussion as though a tribe’s historical failures could erase its essential share. If sin is a separation from the klal rather than a destruction of the root, the final movement must be return — to the Avos, to the klal, and to the place that expresses that root. Eretz Yisrael can ‘vomit out’ impurity precisely because its deepest relationship to Israel is prior to and more enduring than any particular failure.

paragraphs.text: Shoftim 14:4: of Shimshon’s marriage to a Philistine woman — “וְאָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ לֹא יָדְעוּ כִּי מֵה׳ הִיא, כִּי תֹאֲנָה הוּא מְבַקֵּשׁ מִפְּלִשְׁתִּים” — “his father and mother did not know that it was from Hashem, for He was seeking a pretext against the Philistines.” Background: Scripture testifies that Shimshon’s seemingly wayward choice was providential. R’ Tzadok’s use: though Shimshon “chose the daughters of the uncircumcised” and seemed to have a “connection” with them, “it was from Hashem” — to the very opposite end: to take vengeance upon them and subdue them, “to the detriment of the base man” — the pattern of Malchus Tata’ah, which consumes evil from within.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: No settled inheritance fell to Dan until the era of Michah’s idol — for the Land is a bequest from the Avos, accepted only by those with the root of holiness. Israel’s holiness was fully clarified only in David’s generation, and Dan’s late inheritance reflects that. Scripture places the account after Shimshon — the remedy before the blow — and keeps noting that “there was no king in Israel.”

p: (מד) וְחוּרְבַּן הַנַּחֲלָה וּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ דִּירוּשָׁלַיִם הָיָה גַּם כֵּן בְּחֹדֶשׁ אָב שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד דָּן
And the destruction of the heritage and the Holy Temple in Jerusalem likewise occurred in the month of Av which corresponds to Dan,
שֶׁמִּצִּידּוֹ הוּא זֶה
for this destruction stemmed from his spiritual aspect,
כִּי כָּל הַשְּׁבָטִים כְּלוּלִים זֶה בָּזֶה
because all the tribes are mutually integrated one within the other,
וְהַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁבּוֹ יֶשְׁנוֹ גַּם כֵּן בִּכְלַל הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
and the deficiency present in Dan exists within the collective of the Congregation of Israel as well,
רַק שֶׁבּוֹ נִתְגַּלָּה בְּיוֹתֵר
only that in him it became manifest to the greatest degree.
כִּי כָּל הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל קוֹמָה אַחַת שְׁלֵימָה
for the entirety of the Congregation of Israel constitutes one unified, complete stature.
וּמִשֶּׁנִּכְנַס אָב מְמַעֲטִין בְּשִׂמְחָה (תַּעֲנִית כו),
And "when Av enters we diminish joy" (Ta'anit 26b),
וְכֵן בְּנֵי דָן נִקְרְאוּ שָׁם בַּכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר שׁוֹפְטִים (יח, כה) "מָרֵי נֶפֶשׁ",
and likewise the sons of Dan are described there in the text in the Book of Judges (18:25) as "bitter of soul",
שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם לֵב שָׂמֵחַ הַגּוֹרֵם טוֹבַת נֶפֶשׁ.
lacking a joyful heart that generates spiritual well-being.
כִּי שִׂמְחַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא רַק לִפְנֵי ה
' For the rejoicing of the children of Israel exists solely before Hashem,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וּשְׂמַחְתֶּם שָׁם לִפְנֵי ה
'", as it is stated: "And you shall rejoice there before Hashem" (Deuteronomy 12:7),
וְנֶאֱמַר: "שִׂמְחוּ בַה' וְגוֹמֵר",
and stated: "Be glad in Hashem, etc." (Psalms 32:11).
וְכֵן בְּהַרְבֵּה מִקְרָאוֹת
and so in numerous scriptural verses.
וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה גּוֹרֶמֶת עַצְבוּת וּמְרִירוּת נֶפֶשׁ
And idolatry causes melancholy and bitterness of soul.
לְנֶפֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁמְּרוּחֶקֶת בֶּאֱמֶת מֵהֶם
to the inner Jewish soul which is truly estranged from such pagan folly.
וְשִׁמְשׁוֹן סוֹפוֹ גַּם כֵּן גָּרַם גָּלוּת לְעַצְמוֹ בֵּין הָעַמִּים
And Samson's end likewise brought exile upon himself among the nations
וְעַד שֶׁמָּאַס בְּחַיָּיו וְאָמַר: "תָּמוֹת נַפְשִׁי וְגוֹמֵר",
to the point that he grew weary of his life and declared: "Let my soul die (with the Philistines), etc." (Judges 16:30),
שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד מְרִירוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ עַל מַה שֶּׁרָאָה עַצְמוֹ כָּבוּשׁ תַּחַת יָדָם
which stemmed from anguish of soul over seeing himself subjugated under their hand,
וְהוּא טוֹחֵן בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִים
as he was grinding in the prison house,
כִּדְרָשַׁת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה י עַמּוּד א) שֶׁאֲנָסוּהוּ לָבוֹא עַל בְּנוֹתֵיהֶם וְשֶׁיּוֹלִידוּ מִמֶּנּוּ בָּנִים עֲרֵלִים
in accordance with the exposition of our Sages of blessed memory (Sotah 10a) that they forced him to consort with their women so they might bear uncircumcised children from him.
וּמִצַּד מְרִירוּתוֹ הֶעָצוּם עַל זֶה נִתְרַצָּה בְּמִיתַת נַפְשׁוֹ עִם פְּלִשְׁתִּים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
And from his intense bitterness over this, he consented to the death of his soul along with the Philistines, Heaven forbid.
כְּאִלּוּ חָשַׁב חַס וְשָׁלוֹם חֶלְקוֹ עִמָּהֶם עַל יְדֵי מַעֲשָׂיו
as though he considered, Heaven forbid, that his eternal portion was bound with them through his actions.
דְּעַל כֵּן הוּצְרַךְ יַעֲקֹב לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עָלָיו: "לִישׁוּעָתְךָ קִוִּיתִי",
Which is why Jacob was required to pray over him: "For Your salvation I wait, Hashem" (Genesis 49:18),
שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת לֹא נִשְׁתַּקַּע כְּלָל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בֵּינֵיהֶם
that in internal truth he was not submerged at all among them, Heaven forbid.
וְלֹא נִשְׁאַר מִזַּרְעוֹ כְּלוּם
and no offspring of his remained among them.
וְאַדְּרַבָּה, עַל יְדֵי גָּלוּתוֹ זֶה וּכְבוּשָׁתוֹ בְּיָדָם כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁהֻוצְרַךְ לְהָמִית אֶת עַצְמוֹ
And on the contrary, through this exile of his and his utter subjugation in their hands to the point of bringing death upon himself,
זֶה גָּרַם לְהַכְנִיעָם בְּיוֹתֵר
this brought about their profound defeat,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי רַבִּים אֲשֶׁר הֵמִית בְּמוֹתוֹ וְגוֹמֵר",
as it is stated: "So the dead which he slew at his death were more (than they which he slew in his life)" (Judges 16:30).
דְּכָל שְׁלִיטָתָם לְרַע לָהֶם
for all their fleeting dominion over Israel turns to their own ultimate ruin.
וְלֹא נִתְגַּלָּה בְּיָמָיו עֲדַיִן הָאָלֶ"ף שֶׁבְּסוֹף הַדִּינָא דְּמַלְכוּתָא
And in his days the Aleph at the end of the permutation D-Y-N-A
(דינ"א)
was not yet revealed,
וְגַם יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא גִּלָּהוּ.
nor did Jacob our father, peace be upon him, reveal it.
רַק מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּבִרְכָתוֹ, שֶׁהוּא הַבְּרָכָה דִּלְעָתִיד לָבוֹא
Only Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, in his blessing—which constitutes the blessing for the ultimate future—
קְרָאוֹ אַרְיֵה
called him a lion,
מִצַּד הִתְגַּלּוּת מַדְרֵגַת הָעִגּוּלִים כְּשֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָחוֹל לַצַּדִּיקִים לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא
from the perspective of the revelation of the rung of Circles when the Holy One, blessed be He, makes a circular dance for the righteous in the World to Come.
וְיִהְיֶה דָּן מְחוּבָּר יַחַד עִם יְהוּדָה לִהְיוֹת נָעוּץ הַסּוֹף בַּתְּחִלָּה
and Dan will be joined together with Judah so that the end is wedged in the beginning.
וְזֶהוּ הַיּוֹם טוֹב דְּטַ"ו בְּאָב שֶׁבּוֹ הוּתְּרוּ שְׁבָטִים לָבוֹא זֶה בָּזֶה
And this is the holiday of the Fifteenth of Av on which the tribes were permitted to intermarry,
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא הִתְאַחֲדוּת כָּל הַשְּׁבָטִים יַחַד
for through this unfolds the complete unification of all the tribes together,
דְּמוֹרֶה הֱיוֹת כֻּלָּם עַם אֶחָד וְלֹא כָּל שֵׁבֶט עַם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ,
demonstrating that all constitute one single nation, and not each tribe an independent entity.
וּמִמֵּילָא כּוּלָּא חַד וְגַם זַנְבָא דְּאַרְיֵה אַרְיֵה הוּא
and consequently all is one, and even the tail of the lion is a lion.
וְאָז יִהְיֶה גַּם תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לְשָׂשׂוֹן וּלְשִׂמְחָה וְלֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד מָרֵי נֶפֶשׁ כְּלָל
And then the Ninth of Av will likewise be transformed into gladness and joy, and there will be no bitterness of soul whatsoever.

paragraphs.text: Shoftim 18:25: when Michah pursued the Danites to reclaim his idol, they warned him off — “פֶּן יִפְגְּעוּ בָכֶם אֲנָשִׁים מָרֵי נֶפֶשׁ, וְאָסַפְתָּה נַפְשְׁךָ וְנֶפֶשׁ בֵּיתֶךָ” — “lest men bitter of soul marei nefesh fall upon you, and you gather in your life and the life of your household.” Background: the migrating Danites, bearing Michah’s graven image, are called “bitter of soul.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this “bitterness” is the mark of Dan — “for the joy of Israel is only before Hashem,” and idolatry, “in truth distanced” from the Jewish soul, breeds sadness and bitterness of soul; hence the churban itself fell in Av, “opposite Dan.”

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 49:18: “לִישׁוּעָתְךָ קִוִּיתִי ה׳” — “For Your salvation I hope, Hashem.” Rashi there: “נִתְנַבֵּא שֶׁיְּנַקְּרוּ פְּלִשְׁתִּים אֶת עֵינָיו, וְסוֹפוֹ לוֹמַר זָכְרֵנִי נָא וְחַזְּקֵנִי נָא אַךְ הַפַּעַם וְגוֹ׳.” — “He prophesied that the Philistines would gouge out his eyes, and that he would eventually say: ‘Remember me, please, and strengthen me, please, just this once,’ and so forth.” Bereishis Rabbah 98:14 adds: “לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ רוֹאֶה אוֹתוֹ וְסָבוּר בּוֹ שֶׁהוּא מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ, כֵּיוָן שֶׁרָאָה אוֹתוֹ שֶׁמֵּת, אָמַר אַף זֶה מֵת: לִישׁוּעָתְךָ קִוִּיתִי ה׳.” — “For Yaakov our father saw him and thought that he was the King Mashiach. When he saw that he died, he said: ‘This one too dies—for Your salvation I hope, Hashem.’” These sources distinguish Shimshon’s providential defeat of the Philistines from the final salvation that Yaakov awaited.

paragraphs.text: Devarim 33:22: in Moshe’s blessing of the tribes — “וּלְדָן אָמַר, דָּן גּוּר אַרְיֵה, יְזַנֵּק מִן הַבָּשָׁן” — “and of Dan he said: Dan is a lion’s whelp, that leaps forth from the Bashan.” Background: where Yaakov had likened Dan to a serpent, Moshe calls him a lion. R’ Tzadok’s use: only Moshe — whose blessing is “the blessing of the Future to Come” — names Dan “Aryeh,” from the revelation of the rung of “circles,” when Dan will be rejoined to Yehudah the lion, “the end fixed in the beginning,” so that even the “tail of the lion” is itself the lion.

paragraphs.text: Taanis 31a: “R’ Elazar said: In the Future the Holy One will make a circle-dance machol for the righteous, and He will sit among them in Gan Eden, and each one will point with his finger and say, ‘Behold, this is our God, for whom we hoped.’” Background: the closing aggadah of Taanis — the righteous encircling the Divine Presence. R’ Tzadok’s use: in this “circle” (igulim), where beginning and end join as one, Dan is “joined together with Yehudah” — the very theme of the fifteenth of Av, when “the tribes were permitted to intermarry,” all becoming “one people”; and then “there will no longer be ‘bitter of soul’ at all.”

paragraphs.text: Taanis 26b (Mishnah): “When the month of Av enters, we diminish in joy mishe-nichnas Av mema’atin b’simcha.” Mei HaShiloach — the last camp of Dan is bound to the first camp of Yehudah: Mei HaShiloach II, Bamidbar §2, explains the order of the degalim by focusing on the apparent inequality between Yehudah in the east and Dan, who traveled last in the north. Yet Betzalel of Yehudah and Oholiav of Dan were both filled with wisdom for the Mishkan. The lesson of ‘איש על דגלו,’ he writes, is that each person’s true honor is to stand in the place where Hashem wills his particular revelation to occur, without jealousy. He then cites the Zohar on Moshe’s blessing ‘דן גור אריה’: Dan is deliberately tied to Yehudah so that ‘the beginning and the end’ of the four camps are bound in one place — Yehudah is ‘גור אריה יהודה,’ and Dan too becomes ‘גור אריה.’ This is a direct Izhbitz parallel to R’ Tzadok’s closing movement in the se’if. Dan’s present position as the tail is not his final definition. Precisely the last camp must eventually reveal its bond with the first, and the tribe associated with Shimshon’s serpent-like Din is destined to receive the leonine title of Yehudah. The future tikkun is therefore not the abolition of Dan’s distinct place but the revelation that the lowest edge of the camp was always organically attached to Malchus. The bitterness and distance of the present are healed when the ‘end’ knows itself as part of the same one body as the ‘beginning.’ Exact primary wording from Mei HaShiloach II, Bamidbar 2: “ובכל מקום הוא כבודי ... וזה שהיה שבט דן מתקשר ביהודה” — “And in every place is My glory ... and this is why the tribe of Dan was joined to Yehudah.” It cites Zohar, Vayechi 244b: “למהוי שירותא וסופא קטיר בחד אתר” — “so that beginning and end be bound together in one place.” Source: Mei HaShiloach II, Bamidbar 2.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The churban fell in Av, which stands opposite Dan: his deficiency belongs to all Israel, one complete stature, but shows most in him. The Danites are “bitter of soul,” for Israel’s joy is only “before Hashem,” and idolatry breeds bitterness. Shimshon’s bitter end required Yaakov’s prayer, yet his death subdued them all the more — and only Moshe’s blessing for the future calls Dan “Aryeh,” when he rejoins Yehudah.

p: (מה) וּמִשֶּׁנִּכְנַס אֲדָר שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד יוֹסֵף עַל שֵׁם "וְיִדְגּוּ לָרֹב",
And "when Adar enters", which corresponds to Joseph on account of "and let them grow into a multitude like fish" (Genesis 48:16),
וְכֵן הֵם שְׁנֵי אֲדָרִין שֶׁכֵּן יוֹסֵף נִמְנֶה שְׁנֵי שְׁבָטִים
and similarly there are two Adars in a leap year just as Joseph is enumerated as two tribes.
מַרְבִּין בְּשִׂמְחָה (תַּעֲנִית כט).
"we increase in joy" (Ta'anit 29a).
כִּי בוֹ הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַשִּׂמְחָה בַּה
', For in him resides the root of rejoicing in Hashem,
דְּעַל יָדוֹ הוּא יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ
for through him occurs the supernal union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah.
וְחִבּוּר כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם עַל יְדֵי הַצַּדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם
and the binding of the Congregation of Israel to their Father in Heaven through the Tzaddik, the Foundation of the World.
שֶׁיּוֹסֵף לֹא סָבַל שׁוּם הִתְחַבְּרוּת עִם גּוֹיָה
For Joseph could not endure any attachment with a gentile woman,
וְהוֹצִיא דִּבַּת אֶחָיו שֶׁנּוֹשְׂאִין עֵינֵיהֶם בִּבְנוֹת הָאָרֶץ
and he brought an evil report of his brothers that they cast their eyes upon the daughters of the land,
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד גּוֹדֶל רִיחוּקוֹ בָּזֶה
and this was likewise out of the magnitude of his extreme detachment in this matter,
שֶׁזֶּה כָּל קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם מוּבְדָּלִים מֵהָעַמִּים
for this constitutes the whole sanctity of Israel: that they are segregated from the nations.
וּקְדוּשָּׁה הוּא לְשׁוֹן הַבְדָּלָה
and kedushah (holiness) is intrinsically a term of separation.
וְכָל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב מוּבְדָּלִים מֵהֶם לְגַמְרֵי בְּעֶצֶם
And all the seed of Jacob are completely separated from them in their fundamental essence.
אֲבָל בַּפּוֹעַל וּמַעֲשֶׂה הַנִּגְלֶה אֵצֶל בְּנֵי אָדָם הָיָה יוֹסֵף מוּגְדָּר יוֹתֵר מִכֻּלָּם
yet in concrete actuality and visible deed before human eyes, Joseph was guarded more than all of them.
וְכֵן זַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו אֲפִילּוּ הַגְּרוּעִים
And so too his offspring after him, even the lowest among them,
דְּעַל כֵּן יָרָבְעָם הֵרִים יָד בִּשְׁלֹמֹה עַל שֶׁנָּשָׂא בַּת פַּרְעֹה וְעָשָׂה הַמִּילּוֹא בִּשְׁבִילָהּ.
which is why Jeroboam lifted a hand against Solomon because he took Pharaoh's daughter and closed the Millo rampart for her.
וַעֲדַיִן לֹא נִתְבָּרֵר אָז דָּבָר זֶה
And it was not yet elucidated at that time,
דְּגַם שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה מְרוּחָק מֵהֶם בְּתַכְלִית
that King Solomon, peace be upon him, was likewise completely distanced from them in ultimate reality.
וּדְכָל כַּוָּונָתוֹ הָיָה לְהַכְנִיסָם תַּחַת כַּנְפֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה מַה שֶּׁאֶפְשָׁר לְהַכְנִיס מֵהֶם וּלְהוֹצִיא בִּלְעָם מִפִּיהֶם
and that his entire holy intent was to bring under the wings of the Shechinah whatever could be gathered of them and extract what was swallowed from their mouth.
כִּי לְפִי הַנִּגְלֶה לֹא הָיָה כֵן
For according to the external appearance it did not seem so.
וְלֹא לְפִי הַנִּגְלֶה לְעֵינֵי בָּשָׂר לְבַד שֶׁהֲרֵי גַּם הַכָּתוּב סִפֵּר בִּגְנוּתוֹ בָּזֶה
and not merely to the sight of mortal flesh alone, for Scripture itself recounted this to his criticism.
וְאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה בִּקְשׁוּ לִמְנוֹתוֹ מֵאוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
And the Men of the Great Assembly sought to number him among those who have no share in the World to Come, Heaven forbid,
עַד שֶׁהוֹדִיעוּם מִשָּׁמַיִם דְּלֹא מַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵיהֶם
until they were informed from Heaven that His thoughts, blessed be He, are not their thoughts,
דְּאַף שֶׁכְּפִי הַנִּגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְעוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה שָׁפְטוּ עָלָיו מַה שֶּׁשָּׁפְטוּ,
for even though according to the visible realm of this world and the World of Action they judged him as they did,
זֶהוּ כְּפִי הַחָכְמָה וְהַיְדִיעָה הַמִּתְגַּלֵּית לַחֲכָמִים וּנְבִיאִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
this was solely according to the wisdom and knowledge revealed to sages and prophets in this world,
וְלֹא כְּפִי אֲמִיתַּת חָכְמָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא
and not according to the ultimate truth of His divine wisdom that will be unveiled in the days of the Messiah and the World to Come.
שֶׁאָז יִהְיֶה חִבּוּר אַבָּא וְאִמָּא בִּיסוֹד אַבָּא וְיַשִּׂיגוּ חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה
when the union of Abba and Imma will occur within Yesod of Abba and all will attain the Supernal Wisdom.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Ki Seitzei §10): “and on that day was the creation of the fish, and the blessing of the fish, in which the multiplication is very great, for they are hidden from the eye; and as they said Taanis 8b, that blessing is found only in a thing hidden from the eye.” Exactly the se’if’s “may they multiply like fish”: Yosef’s blessing is of the kind that increases precisely by being unseen — the very opposite of a blessing that must be displayed.

paragraphs.text: Taanis 29a: “אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמִּשֶּׁנִּכְנַס אָב מְמַעֲטִין בְּשִׂמְחָה — כָּךְ מִשֶּׁנִּכְנַס אֲדָר מַרְבִּין בְּשִׂמְחָה.” — “Rav Yehudah son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat said in Rav’s name: just as, when Av enters, we diminish in joy, so, when Adar enters, we increase in joy.”

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 48:16: in Yaakov’s blessing of Ephraim and Menashe — “וְיִדְגּוּ לָרֹב בְּקֶרֶב הָאָרֶץ” — “and may they multiply like fish v’yidgu in the midst of the land.” Meforshim: Rashi — like the fish of the sea, which the waters cover so that the evil eye has no dominion over them, so may Yosef’s seed increase. R’ Tzadok’s use: the month Adar is “opposite Yosef,” “on account of ‘may they multiply like fish’”; and just as Yosef is counted as two tribes (Ephraim and Menashe), so there are two months of Adar — for in Yosef is “the root of joy in Hashem,” and therefore “when Adar enters, we increase in joy.” Zohar, Vayeshev 3:29, states: “דשכינתא לא שריא באתר עציבו אלא באתר דאית ביה חדוה” — “The Shechinah does not dwell in a place of sorrow, but in a place where joy is present.” It applies this directly to Yaakov: “דבגין דהוה עציב עליה דיוסף אסתלקת שכינתא מניה, כיון דאתא ליה חדוה דבשורה דיוסף מיד ותחי רוח יעקב אביהם” — “Because Yaakov grieved for Yosef, the Shechinah departed from him; when the joy of the news of Yosef arrived, immediately the spirit of Yaakov their father revived.” This exact primary parallel explains why, for Rav Tzadok, Yosef’s recovered presence and Adar’s joy are linked to renewed capacity for Shechinah, rather than to ordinary personal happiness alone. Source: Zohar, Vayeshev 3:29.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayechi §9): “"and the name of my fathers, Avraham and Yitzchak" — this is the aspect of good deeds, and it is the totality of the aspect of the "field of apples," which has the aspect of taste and fragrance — for the supernal fathers desired it and rectify it.” The se’if’s tzaddik exactly: Yosef is the point at which the fathers’ rectifying desire reaches the field below — which is how Knesses Yisrael is joined, through him, to her Father.

paragraphs.text: Vayikra 20:26: “וִהְיִיתֶם לִי קְדֹשִׁים כִּי קָדוֹשׁ אֲנִי ה׳, וָאַבְדִּל אֶתְכֶם מִן הָעַמִּים לִהְיוֹת לִי” — “and you shall be holy to Me, for I, Hashem, am holy, and I have separated you from the peoples to be Mine.” Meforshim: Rashi (on Vayikra 19:2, “kedoshim tihyu”) — “be separated perushim”; holiness is an expression of havdalah, of separation. R’ Tzadok’s use: “this is the whole holiness of Israel — that they are separated from the peoples”; and Yosef, who “could bear no joining with a gentile,” embodied that separation most of all “in the revealed act,” bounded-in more than all his brothers.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Yisrael Kedoshim §2): “ומה שאמר חד מאן דאמר בויקרא רבא ... ובירושלמי ... איש קדוש הוא שלא הביט בה” — “As one opinion in Vayikra Rabbah and in the Yerushalmi says, ‘He is a holy man’ — he did not gaze at her.” The discussion concerns Elisha’s exceptional holiness, including avoiding even an unintentional sight of a woman’s face; it does not merely redescribe an ordinary prohibition. The source sets out degrees of holiness: “ונגד כלל האומות שבעולם נקראו כלל ישראל כולם שקיבלו התורה קדושים” — “In relation to all the nations of the world, all Israel who accepted the Torah are called holy”; “ובין כשרי ישראל נקרא קדוש מי שגודר עצמו עוד במותר ... וכמו שאלישע נקרא איש קדוש בדורן של נביאים” — “Among observant Israelites, one who further fences himself off in permitted things is called holy … as Elisha was called a holy man in a generation of prophets.” It likewise identifies Rabbi’s distinct holiness with his exceptional guarding of the covenant. This illuminates the author’s completed distinction here: all Yaakov’s offspring are separate from the nations at their root, while Yosef was distinguished in the visible practice of restraint.

paragraphs.text: Yeshayah 55:8: “כִּי לֹא מַחְשְׁבוֹתַי מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵיכֶם, וְלֹא דַרְכֵיכֶם דְּרָכָי, נְאֻם ה׳” — “for My thoughts are not your thoughts, nor your ways My ways, says Hashem.” Background: God’s assurance that His designs transcend human reckoning. R’ Tzadok’s use: when the Men of the Great Assembly “wished to count Shlomo” among those without a share in the World to Come (Sanhedrin 104b), Rav Tzadok uses Isaiah’s teaching to explain the heavenly rebuke to the sages, distinguishing their judgment “according to the revealed” of this world from the higher Divine wisdom. The actual heavenly voices in Sanhedrin 104b cite Proverbs 22:29, “חזית איש מהיר במלאכתו”, and Job 34:33, “המעמך ישלמנה כי מאסת כי אתה תבחר ולא אני”; they do not quote Isaiah 55:8 verbatim. In Rav Tzadok’s interpretation, Shlomo’s inward purpose is understood in the light of Divine wisdom that surpasses outward appearances; the Gemara itself should not be presented as explicitly endorsing every detail of that interpretation. Source: Job 34:33. Source: Proverbs 22:29.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Adar stands opposite Yosef — “may they multiply like fish,” two Adars answering his two tribes — and “when Adar enters we increase in joy,” for Yosef is the root of joy in Hashem. Yosef could bear no union with a gentile, holiness being separation itself, and he was the most “bounded-in” in the revealed act. So even Shlomo’s marriages were in truth utterly distant, aimed only at drawing converts in.

p: (מו) וְאִלּוּ זָכוּ וְנוֹלַד יוֹסֵף מִלֵּאָה
And had they merited that Joseph be born of Leah,
כְּבָר הָיָה אָז כֵּן תִּיקּוּן כָּל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב בִּשְׁלֵימוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד
there would already have been then the complete rectification of all the seed of Jacob as in the future.
וְזַרְעָא דְּרָחֵל הָיָה בִּנְיָמִין לְבַד
and the offspring of Rachel would have been Benjamin alone.
וּלְפִי שֶׁרִחֲמָה עַל רָחֵל וְרָצְתָה לְהַשְׁלִים קוֹמָתָהּ שֶׁהִיא קוֹמַת הַשְּׁכִינָה שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה דִּינָא קַשְׁיָא
And because Leah took pity on Rachel and desired to complete her stature which is the stature of the Shechinah whence harsh judgment (dina kashya) emanates,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה דָּנָה דִּין בְּעַצְמָהּ
through this she passed judgment upon herself,
וְהוֹדֵית דְּמִצַּד מִדַּת הַדִּין הַקָּשָׁה עֲדַיִן לֹא הִגִּיעַ זְמַן הַתִּיקּוּן הַגָּמוּר
and conceded that from the vantage point of harsh judgment the time of total rectification had not yet arrived,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְהַפֵּךְ לְדִינָה
and through this the embryo was transformed into Dinah,
אוֹתִיּוֹת "דִּין" עַל מִדָּתָהּ,
spelling the letters of "din" (judgment) corresponding to her attribute.
וְהַהֵ"א בַּסּוֹף הִיא הֵ"א אַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁבַּשֵּׁם שֶׁרוֹמֶזֶת לְנוּקְבָּא וּשְׁכִינָה
and the Hei at the end is the final Hei of the Tetragrammaton alluding to the feminine aspect and the Shechinah.
רַק שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה אֶצְלָהּ בְּסוֹף וְאַחֲרִית
Only that this divine illumination was present in her case at the end and culmination,
וּכְלָלוּתָהּ הוּא "דִּין" הַקָּשֶׁה וְצִמְצוּם גָּמוּר מֵהִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר הַשְּׁכִינָה
while her collective state represented harsh judgment and total contraction from the revelation of the light of the Shechinah,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה גָּרַם מַעֲשֵׂה שְׁכֶם שֶׁנִּדְבְּקָה בּוֹ
which brought about the incident of Shechem wherein she was attached to him,
עַד שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה מִמֶּנָּה דְּהַנִּבְעֶלֶת לְגוֹי קָשֶׁה לִפְרוֹשׁ.
to the extent that our Sages of blessed memory remarked concerning her that one who cohabits with a gentile finds it difficult to separate.
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ עַל "בֶּן הַכְּנַעֲנִית" – זוֹ דִּינָה שֶׁנִּבְעֲלָה לִכְנַעֲנִי
And likewise they expounded on "the son of a Canaanitish woman" (Genesis 46:10)—this refers to Dinah who cohabited with a Canaanite (Bereishit Rabbah 80:11),
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה גַּם הִיא כְּנַעֲנִית כְּאִלּוּ נִדְבְּקָה בּוֹ לְגַמְרֵי לִהְיוֹת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כָּמוֹהוּ.
and through this she was termed Canaanitish as though she had cleaved to him completely to become like him, Heaven forbid.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה: "חֲדָא הֲוֵי לֵיהּ וְהַלְּוַאי קְבָרָהּ",
And therefore they stated in Bereishit Rabbah: "He had one daughter, and would that he had buried her!",
דִּלְמַרְאִית עַיִן בְּעוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה הָיָה נִרְאָה כֵּן וְעַל כֵּן הַלְּוַאי קְבָרָהּ,
for to the superficial eye in the World of Action it appeared so, hence 'would that he had buried her',
וְאַחַר הַקְּבוּרָה וְהִסְתַּלְּקוּתָהּ מֵעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא נִתְגַּלָּה הָאֱמֶת
– yet following her burial and departure from this world which is the World of Falsehood, the truth was unveiled—
הֵ"א אַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁבָּהּ,
namely the final Hei within her name.
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר "ה' בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ" וְאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת וְחִבּוּר לִבְנֵי נֵכָר כְּלָל
which is the root of the Congregation of Israel concerning whom it is said "Hashem alone led him" (Deuteronomy 32:12), possessing no affinity or union with aliens at all.
וּבַת אַחַת שֶׁהָיְתָה לוֹ לְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִצַּד מִדַּת הָאֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב
And the single daughter that our father Jacob, peace be upon him, had from the quality of truth to Jacob.
וַדַּאי הִיא שׁוֹרֶשׁ נוּקְבָּא דִּקְדוּשָּׁה
was certainly the holy feminine root.
רַק לְפִי שֶׁהָאִשָּׁה הֵבִיאָה מִיתָה לָעוֹלָם
Only that because woman originally brought death into the world,
דְּבָהּ אֲחִיזַת הַחִיצוֹנִים כַּנּוֹדָע דְּ"רַגְלֶיהָ יֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת",
in her lies the grip of the external forces, as is known that "her feet go down to death",
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (יז, ח) דְּאֵין סָמֶ"ךְ בְּפָרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית עַד בְּרִיאַת הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁנִּבְרָא הַשָּׂטָן עִמָּהּ,
and as they said in Bereishit Rabbah (17:8) that there is no letter Samekh in Parashat Bereishit until the creation of woman, where Satan was created with her,
וְהוּא יֵצֶר הָרַע וְהוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת
and he is the evil inclination and he is the angel of death (Bava Batra 16a),
שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הָרַע שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִצַּד מִדַּת הַדִּין שֶׁבָּהּ,
the root of all evil in this world drawn from the attribute of judgment within her,
רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר כֹּחַ הַצִּמְצוּם שֶׁהוּא מִסִּטְרָהּ,
meaning the power of contraction which stems from her side,
שֶׁהִיא הַכְּלִי קִיבּוּל לְצַמְצֵם הָאוֹר וּלְהַעֲלִימוֹ.
she being the receptive vessel that contracts the light and conceals it.
וְאֵין בָּהֶם שׁוּם הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר דְּתוֹרָה רַק מִצַּד חִבּוּרָן לְבַעְלֵיהֶן וּלְבָנֵיהֶן
And women have no independent revelation of the light of Torah except through their connection to their husbands and sons,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (יז.): "הָנֵי נָשֵׁי בְּמַאי זָכְיָין וְכוּלֵי",
as they stated in Berakhot (17a): "Whereby do women merit (the World to Come)? By sending their sons to study, etc.",
דְּרַק עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִזְדַּכְּכוֹת
for only through this do they become purified.
אֲבָל מִצַּד עַצְמָן אֵין בָּהֶם הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר מֵאִיר
whereas from their own independent aspect there is no shining light manifest within them.
וּמִצַּד גּוֹדֶל הַהֶעְלֵם עַל יְדֵי זֶה אֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים מִתַּתְקְנָא בְּרָזָא דְּאֵשֶׁת חַיִל כַּיָּדוּעַ בַּזֹּהַר
And on account of the vastness of this concealment, the harlot woman (eshet zenunim) mimics and adorns herself in the secret guise of the woman of valor, as is known in the Zohar.
וְיֵשׁ אֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים וְאֵשֶׁת מִדְיָנִים וְהֵם הַקְּלִיפּוֹת שֶׁנֶּגֶד רָחֵל וְלֵאָה
And there exist the 'harlot woman' and the 'contentious woman' who are the corrupt husks confronting Rachel and Leah,
כִּי "זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה עָשָׂה אֱלֹהִים",
for "God has made one corresponding to the other" (Ecclesiastes 7:14),
וְאֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים הוּא הֶפֶךְ רָחֵל
and the harlot woman is the counterfeit antithesis of Rachel,
וְאֵשֶׁת מִדְיָנִים הוּא הַהֵיפֶךְ מִלֵּאָה
and the contentious woman is the counterfeit antithesis of Leah.
וְזֶה מְבוֹאָר מִתּוֹךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְמַעְלָה
and this is clear from what I have written above.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הָיָה הָרָצוֹן לְהִתְגַּלּוּת יְסוֹד דְּאַבָּא בָּעוֹלָם
And when the supernal will was to reveal the Yesod of Abba in the world,
אֶלָּא שֶׁדָּנָה דִּין וְהִתְעוֹרֵר קִטְרוּג מִדַּת הַדִּין
except that Leah exercised judgment and the prosecution of the attribute of judgment was stirred,
גָּרַם הִתְעוֹרְרוּת אָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל בְּאוֹתָהּ מַדְרֵגָה
it caused an awakening of the corrupt archetype of Belial on that exact spiritual level,
כַּיָּדוּעַ דִּלְעוֹלָם שְׁלִיטַת אָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל בְּאָדָם דִּקְדוּשָּׁה
for as is known, the dominion of the wicked archetype over the holy human stature
הוּא בְּאוֹתוֹ אֵיבָר עַצְמוֹ וְאוֹתָהּ מַדְרֵגָה עַצְמָהּ שֶׁהוּא בוֹ כְּנֶגְדּוֹ וּלְעֻמָּתוֹ,
occurs in that very same limb and that very same spiritual level that stands facing and corresponding to it,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְעוֹרֵר כֹּחַ אֵשֶׁת מִדְיָנִים
and through this was stirred the force of the contentious woman (eshet medanim).
שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ קְצָת שַׁיָּיכוּת בְּאוֹתִיּוֹת "דִּין" שֶׁבְּדִינָה
who held some slight attachment in the letters of "din" (judgment) embedded within Dinah.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 80:11: “הנבעלת לערל קשה לפרש” — The Midrash says that a woman who was with an uncircumcised man has difficulty separating; it also connects “שאול בן הכנענית” to Dinah and records the view that Shimon buried her in Canaan. Bereishis Rabbah 84:21: “כמה בנות היו לו חדא הות והלואי קברה” — “How many daughters did he have? One; would that he had buried her.” This second, distinct passage is the precise origin of Rav Tzadok’s “הלואי קברה”; it is not part of 80:11. Rav Tzadok contrasts these harsh judgments about her visible history with the holiness he holds was revealed after her death.

paragraphs.text: Rav Tzadok, Tzidkas HaTzadik §164: “התשובה נקרא עלמא דאתכסיא ואינו נגלה לבני אדם היקרות והיופי שבה ... אבל מכל מקום עיקר תולדות משל לאה.” — “Repentance is called the hidden world; its preciousness and beauty are not apparent to people ... yet the principal offspring are from Leah.” This is an exact parallel for Leah’s concealed spiritual root and its ability to generate Torah and souls. It does not explicitly identify Dinah as the feminine root; that further application here is Rav Tzadok’s own interpretation.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 17a: “גדולה הבטחה שהבטיחן הקדוש ברוך הוא לנשים יותר מן האנשים” — “Greater is the promise the Holy One made to women than to men.” Rav asks, “נשים במאי זכיין?” and the answer is “באקרויי בנייהו לבי כנישתא, ובאתנויי גברייהו בי רבנן, ונטרין לגברייהו” — by bringing their children to Torah learning, enabling their husbands to study, and awaiting their return. The Gemara affirms the women’s distinct merit; it does not state Rav Tzadok’s later metaphysical claim about independent revelation of Torah light. That claim is his kabbalistic reading of the receiving-vessel symbolism in this paragraph.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Had Yosef been born to Leah, the tikkun would already have been complete. But Leah, wishing to complete Rachel’s stature, rendered judgment upon herself — and the fetus “turned into Dinah,” the letters of Din. Her totality is harsh Din and contraction, whence the affair of Shechem; yet after death the truth emerged, that she is the root of the Nukva of holiness.

p: (מז) וְהַמִּדְיָנִים הֵם זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִבְּנֵי קְטוּרָה
And the Midianites are the seed of Abraham our father, peace be upon him, from the sons of Keturah,
וְעַל כֵּן נִכְלָלִים בִּכְלַל יִשְׁמְעֵאלִים בְּסִפּוּר מְכִירַת יוֹסֵף
and therefore they are subsumed under the general category of Ishmaelites in the narrative of Joseph's sale,
וְיֵשׁ בָּהֶם גַּם כֵּן זוּהֲמָא דְּיִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּתַאֲווֹת רָעוֹת וְזִימָּה
and they likewise contain the defilement of Ishmael in evil lusts and licentiousness.
שֶׁהוּא הַפְּסוֹלֶת דְּמִדַּת הַחֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which is the dross of the attribute of Chesed (Lovingkindness) of Abraham our father, peace be upon him.
רַק לְפִי שֶׁהֵם יָצְאוּ מֵאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אַחַר שֶׁנִּימּוֹל וְאַחַר לֵידַת יִצְחָק וְהָעֲקֵידָה
Only that because they issued from Abraham our father, peace be upon him, after he was circumcised, and after the birth of Isaac and the Binding (Akeidah),
דְּאִתְכְּלִילוּ אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק
wherein Abraham and Isaac became mutually integrated,
וְזָכָה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם גַּם לְדַרְגָּא דְּיִצְחָק כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה",
and Abraham merited also the spiritual rung of Isaac as it is said: "for now I know that you fear God" (Genesis 22:12),
וּלְצַמְצֵם הַחֲסָדִים שֶׁלֹּא יִתְפַּשְּׁטוּ לְמָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ,
and to contract lovingkindness so it would not expand unto an unwarranted realm,
עַל כֵּן נִקְרְאוּ מִדְיָן שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן דִּין וּמְדָנִים
therefore they were named Midian, which is an expression of judgment (din) and contention (medanim).
הַמּוֹרֶה פְּסוֹלֶת גְּבוּרָה רָעָה וְהֵיפֶךְ הַתַּאֲוָה
indicating the dross of corrupt Gevurah (severity) and the antithesis of lust.
כִּי תַּאֲוָתָם הָיְתָה מְצוּמְצֶמֶת קְצָת לֹא בְּהֶפְקֵר גָּמוּר כְּיִשְׁמָעֵאל
For their lust was somewhat constricted, not in total lawless abandon like Ishmael,
רַק כִּזְנוּת בֵּית מִדְיָן שֶׁהָיָה רַק לְעוֹרֵר מְדָנִים בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם עַל יְדֵי זֶה
rather like the licentiousness of the house of Midian which was solely intended to incite contention between Israel and their Father in Heaven through it.
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרְאוּ מִדְיָן דְּזֶה כָּל יִשְׁעָם וְחֶפְצָם
which is why they were named Midian, for this was their whole ambition and desire.
כִּי יְסוֹד אַבָּא רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר הִתְקַשְּׁרוּת גָּמוּר דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין
For the Yesod of Abba denotes an absolute bond that never parts,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְהַפְרִיד חִבּוּר זֶה לְגַמְרֵי עַל יְדֵי הֲסָתַת אֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים בִּזְנוּת
and it is impossible for the base force to sever this union completely through the seduction of the harlot woman in outright immorality,
שֶׁהוּא דָּבָר הַמַּפְרִיד וְגוֹרֵם שִׁילּוּחַ וְגָלוּת
which is an act that sunders and brings expulsion and exile,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הֲסָתַת אֵשֶׁת מִדְיָנִים
unlike the incitement of the contentious woman.
הוּא רַק בִּדְבָרִים הַמְּעוֹרְרִים קְטָט כְּרֶגַע וְרַק לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן
which operates solely through matters that arouse momentary dispute and only to external appearances.
כִּי מִצַּד אוֹתָהּ מַדְרֵגָה אֵין עוֹד מָקוֹם לִזְנוּת גָּמוּר
For from the vantage point of that elevated rung there is no longer room for absolute licentiousness,
שֶׁהוּא הַפְרָדָה "כִּי תִשְׂטֶה אִשָּׁה אִישָׁהּ",
which is total severance when "a woman goes astray from her husband".
דְּזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּדוֹר דֵּעָה כְּדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר
for this is impossible in a generation of supernal knowledge like the Generation of the Wilderness.
רַק שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת מַה
Only that they retained a certain affinity.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה אַחַר כָּךְ דְּאוֹתָם שֶׁלֹּא יָדְעוּ אִישׁ הֶחֱיוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לָהֶם וְנִדְבְּקוּ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
and as occurred subsequently when those young Midianite maidens who had not known man carnally were spared alive by Israel and became attached unto Israel.
וְאִלּוּ גַּם הֵם לֹא יָדְעוּ תְּחִלָּה בִּזְנוּת וְאִיסּוּר
And had they likewise not engaged at first through illicit immorality,
הָיוּ נִדְבָּקִים אַחַר כָּךְ בָּהֶם בְּהֶיתֵּר
they would have subsequently attached themselves unto them in a permissible holy manner,
דְּמִצַּד הֱיוֹתָם זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם אַחַר שֶׁזָּכָה לְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל וּלְהִקָּרֵא אֶזְרָחִי
for by virtue of their being the seed of Abraham after he merited the name Israel and was called an Ezrachi (native citizen).
יֵשׁ לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת וְחֵשֶׁק לִדְבַּק בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
they possess an intrinsic affinity and passionate desire to cleave unto Israel.
אֶלָּא שֶׁחֶשְׁקָם לִהְיוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל נִדְבָּקִים בָּהֶם כְּמוֹת שֶׁהֵם בְּגַיּוּתָם
Except that their corrupt desire was that Israel should cleave unto them as they are in their unrefined gentile state.
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה יָדָם עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנָה
so that their hand should have the upper hand.
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן אֵשֶׁת מִדְיָנִים הָרוֹצָה לִמְשׁוֹל בְּבַעְלָהּ,
And this is the secret of the contentious woman who seeks to dominate her husband.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מְעוֹרֶרֶת מְדָנִים וּקְטָטוֹת
and through this stirs up strife and contentions.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 22:12: at the Akeidah, the angel stays Avraham’s hand — “כִּי עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה, וְלֹא חָשַׂכְתָּ אֶת בִּנְךָ” — “for now I know that you are one who fears God, and you have not withheld your son.” Meforshim: Rashi — “now I know” means “now I have made it known to all” that you love Me; the Ramban explains that the trial brought Avraham’s latent fear “from the potential into the actual,” so that it be rewarded as a deed and not as intention alone. R’ Tzadok’s use: through the Akeidah “Avraham merited also the rung of Yitzchak” — the trait of yirah and Gevurah — learning “to contract the chasadim so they not spread to a place where they are not needed”; hence the sons of Keturah, born to him only afterward, bear a contracted desire, called “Midyan” (from din), unlike Ishmael’s unbounded lust.

They passed them before the tzitz, and the face of one fit for intercourse turned green.” This is Rashi’s eligibility distinction; Rav Tzadok develops the verse’s opening toward a later permitted attachment to Israel, contrasting it with prior prohibited attachment.

paragraphs.text: Tiferes Shlomo, Purim §99: “ויצאו הנצוצות האלו שבלעו מהם ויבאו בכם ... לכך עתה בא להזהירם להשמר מהנצוצות האלה” — “The sparks they had absorbed depart from them and come among you; therefore Israel is warned to guard against these sparks.” He expounds Devarim 12:30 and insists on following the Torah’s commands without addition or subtraction. This is a complementary caution about separating a holy element from its forbidden setting, not an original report about the specific Midianite encounter. It illuminates Rav Tzadok’s distinction between Midyan’s latent affinity with Israel and Midyan’s unacceptable attempt to preserve its present form.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The Midianites are Avraham’s seed through Keturah, carrying off the “dross” of his Chesed. But since they issued after the circumcision, Yitzchak’s birth and the Akeidah, that Chesed was already constrained toward Din — hence the name Midyan, from strife. Unlike the “woman of harlotry,” who separates entirely, the “woman of strife” can only stir surface friction; and as Avraham’s seed they even long to cleave to Israel, but on their own terms.

p: (מח) וְזֶה הָיָה כָּל עֲצַת אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע שֶׁנִּקְרָא מַחֲלִיק לָשׁוֹן
And this was the entire wicked strategy of that evil one who was termed a flatterer of tongue.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּדְבָרִים רַבָּה (א, ב) דְּזֶה בִּלְעָם שֶׁהֶחֱלִיק לָשׁוֹן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּדֵי לְטוֹרְדָן מֵהָעוֹלָם
as they stated in Devarim Rabbah (1:2) that this was Balaam who spoke smoothly to Israel in order to banish them from the world.
רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר, גִּלָּה לָהֶם מַעֲלָתָם הָעֲצוּמָה בָּאַחֲרִית
Meaning, he revealed to them their immense, invincible stature in the End of Days,
שֶׁשּׁוּם חֲטָאִים לֹא יַפְרִידוּם וְחֹשֶׁךְ לֹא יַחְשִׁיכֵם
that no sins could ever sunder them and no darkness could obscure them,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הִכְנִיס בְּלִבָּם לַעֲשׂוֹת כָּל מַה שֶּׁבִּלְבָבָם
and through this he implanted in their heart the reckless urge to execute whatever was in their heart,
וְאַף אִם לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן הוּא נֶגֶד הַתּוֹרָה
even if to outward appearances it ran counter to the Torah,
לְפִי שֶׁבִּלְבָבָם יָדְעוּ שֶׁהֵם דְּבוּקִים בְּכָל מַעֲמַקֵּיהֶם בֶּאֱמֶת בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים
because in their heart of hearts they knew they were truly bound in all their depths to the living God.
וְוַדַּאי כָּל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם אֵינֶנּוּ מִתְנַגֵּד זֶה
and surely none of their actions could contradict this.
וְהַתּוֹרָה הִיא נוֹבְלוֹת חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה וְיוֹצֵאת מִיְסוֹד אַבָּא
And the Torah is the unripe fruit of Supernal Wisdom and emanates from Yesod of Abba,
וְכַאֲשֶׁר עוֹבֵר עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן אַף שֶׁבְּלִבּוֹ לַשָּׁמַיִם
and when a person transgresses the words of Torah to outward appearances, even if his inner heart is toward Heaven.
מְעוֹרֵר מְדָנִים וּקְלִיפָּה דְּאֵשֶׁת מִדְיָנִים שֶׁנֶּגֶד יְסוֹד אַבָּא
he arouses contention and the shell of the contentious woman which opposes Yesod of Abba.
וְעַל כֵּן מִדְיָן וַעֲמָלֵק מְחוּבָּרִים כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים כִּמְבוֹאָר בַּמִּקְרָאוֹת
And therefore Midian and Amalek are joined together several times as explicitly demonstrated across Scripture,
כִּי גַּם עֲמָלֵק מִתְעוֹרֵר נֶגֶד זֶה כַּיָּדוּעַ,
for Amalek likewise awakens against this, as is known.
וּמְבוֹאָר אֶצְלֵנוּ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר בְּסוֹד הַפּוּרִים
and it is explained by us elsewhere in the mystical secret of Purim.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה קִטְרוּג הָמָן עַל מַה שֶּׁלֹּא עָשׂוּ אֶלָּא לִפְנִים בְּהִשְׁתַּחֲוָיָה לַצֶּלֶם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה ,
And just as Haman's prosecutorial accusation concerned that they had only bowed to the idol superficially as our Sages of blessed memory noted (Megillah 12a),
כִּי הוּא רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם
for Amalek is the first of nations,
וּתְחִלַּת הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הוּא מִדְיָן
and the beginning of outward expansion is Midian.
וְזֶהוּ הַתְחָלַת הָרָע
and that is the inception of evil.
וַעֲמָלֵק הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע
And Amalek is the very root of evil,
וְכָלוּל בּוֹ כָּל מִינֵי רַע שֶׁל כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת כּוּלָּם
and within him are contained all varieties of evil belonging to all the nations collectively,
עַל כֵּן אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא רֵאשִׁיתָם וּפוֹשֵׁט טְלָפַיִם אַחֲרִיתוֹ עֲדֵי אוֹבֵד לְגַמְרֵי
therefore even though he is their first and deceitfully extends his hooves, his end is utter destruction,
וּשְׁאָר כָּל אוּמּוֹת כָּל אַחַת כּוֹלֵל רַע מְיוּחָד לְבַד שֶׁבּוֹ שָׁרְשׁוֹ וְעִיקַּר אֲחִיזָתוֹ.
while each of the other nations embodies a single, specific evil wherein lies its distinct root and primary grip.
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ מִדְיָן הוּא לְעוֹרֵר מְדָנִים נֶגֶד שׁוֹרֶשׁ וִיסוֹד יִשְׂרָאֵל
And the root of Midian is to stir up contentions against the primordial root and foundation of Israel.
דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וְיִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלָּא חַד הַיּוֹצֵא מִיְסוֹד אַבָּא וְיִשְׂרָאֵל סָבָא
for the Torah and Israel are completely one, emerging from Yesod of Abba and Yisrael Saba.

paragraphs.text: Devarim Rabbah 1:2: “ממחליק לשון, זה בלעם, שהחליק בנבואותיו וגבה לבם ונפלו בשטים” — “The smooth-tongued one is Bilaam: through his prophecies he flattered Israel, their hearts became proud, and they fell at Shittim.” This is the Midrash’s explicit wording. Rav Tzadok goes further and describes Bilaam’s flattery as a theological pretext for violating Torah; that fuller strategy is his interpretation, not a verbatim statement in Devarim Rabbah. Mei HaShiloach I, Korach 2: “השי״ת הסתיר דרכו מבני אדם כי יחפוץ בעבודת האדם” — “Hashem concealed His way from humanity because He desires human service.” The Izhbitzer’s discussion of Korach’s all-techeiles argument explains why the concealed truth of Divine providence cannot cancel the obligations of mitzvos and human avodah in this world.

: “השי״ת הסתיר דרכו מבני אדם כי יחפוץ בעבודת האדם” — “Hashem concealed His way from humanity because He desires human service.” The Izhbitzer’s discussion of Korach’s all-techeiles argument explains why the concealed truth of Divine providence cannot cancel the obligations of mitzvos and human avodah in this world.

paragraphs.text: Rav Tzadok, Pri Tzaddik, Bo 12: “בלעם שהיה כעין קליפת עמלק כנודע לא יכול להבין שיהיה קדושה בענין זה” — “Bilaam, who resembled the husk of Amalek, could not understand that there could be holiness in this matter.” There Rav Tzadok specifically discusses holiness extending even to Israel’s animals; this is an analogy for Bilaam’s inability to comprehend holiness, not a direct account of his counsel at Shittim. It complements, but does not substitute for, Divrei Soferim 15 as the exact parallel to his strategy.

paragraphs.text: Rav Tzadok, Divrei Soferim 15: “ואע״פ שידע דעת עליון שאוהב ישראל ושהם קיימים לעולמי עד עכ״ז לא חדל מלייעץ עצות להכשילם נגד רצון השם יתברך” — “Although he knew through supernal knowledge that Hashem loves Israel and that they endure forever, he nevertheless did not desist from devising schemes to make them stumble against the Divine will.” Rav Tzadok contrasts knowledge merely “משפה ולחוץ” — on the lips alone — with wisdom absorbed into the heart. This is a precise original-text parallel to the misuse of knowledge described in this se’if.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh §12: “אך כיון שבו כ׳ חטא ישראל ללמד דאף על פי שחטא ישראל הוא באו חז״ל להורות דכל שהוא ישראל אף אם הרבה לפשוע והגדיל עונות עד לשמים מכל מקום ישראל הוא ואסא קרו ליה רק דקאי ביני חילפי ... וכל שהוא מזרע יעקב לא ידח ממנו נדח.” — “But since of him it is written, ‘Israel has sinned,’ to teach that even though he sinned he is Israel, the Sages came to teach that whoever is Israel—even if he has greatly transgressed and increased sins to the heavens—is nevertheless Israel, and they call him a myrtle; only, he stands among thorns. ... Whoever is of Yaakov’s seed, no outcast from him will be cast off.” This affirms the continuing root that Bilaam exploits. The present paragraph insists that this truth gives no permission to violate the Torah.
