paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Pri Tzaddik, Tazria §11: “ואמרנו דלא כתיב ובמעשיך דגמר המעשה הוא מהשי״ת והשי״ת רוצה מהאדם שיתעורר באתערותא דלתתא ... שגם במעשה אף שגמר המעשה מהשי״ת מ״מ אין לאדם לסמוך על זה רק צריך לגדור עצמו להשמר מכל רע בכל כחו.” — “We have said that it does not say ‘and in your deeds,’ for the completion of the deed is from Hashem, and Hashem desires that a person awaken with an awakening from below. ... Even in action, although the completion of the deed is from Hashem, a person may nevertheless not rely upon this; rather, he must fence himself in, guarding himself from every evil with all his strength.” This directly excludes the false permission that Bilaam draws from divine governance and Israel’s holy root.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: This was Bilaam’s whole counsel — “the smooth-tongued,” who flattered Israel in order to drive them from the world. He revealed their immense future elevation and thereby instilled a license to do whatever the heart wished, reasoning that a depth which cleaves to God cannot be contradicted by any deed. But the Torah issues from Yesod Abba, and transgressing it outwardly, even for Heaven’s sake, arouses the eishes medinim.

p: (מט) וְעַל כֵּן "לְעֶבֶד נִמְכַּר יוֹסֵף" (תְּהִלִּים קה, יז) לָהֶם
And therefore "Joseph was sold as a slave" (Psalms 105:17) unto them.
דְּעִנְיַן מְכִירָתוֹ
– For the inner meaning of his selling was:
שֶׁהַשְּׁבָטִים לֹא יָדְעוּ דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה
that the tribal Patriarchs did not know that our father Jacob, peace be upon him, had a bed that was entirely whole,
וְחָשְׁבוּ דְּגַם בּוֹ יָצָא פְסוֹלֶת כְּמֵאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק
and they imagined that from him too dross had emerged just as occurred with Abraham and Isaac.
וְדִמּוּ עַל יוֹסֵף כִּי רָאוּהוּ חָפֵץ לִמְשׁוֹל בָּהֶם
and they suspected this concerning Joseph because they observed him desiring to rule over them.
וְחָשְׁבוּ דְּזֶהוּ פְּסוֹלֶת מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם קַו הָאֶמְצָעִי הַמְּחוּבָּר מֵחֶסֶד וּגְבוּרָה
And they reasoned that this was the corrupted dross of the attribute of our father Jacob, peace be upon him—the Middle Line synthesized from Chesed and Gevurah;
כִּי גֵּיאוּת הוּא מִתַּאֲוָה וַחֲשָׁקוֹת רָעוֹת וּמִכַּעַס וּגְבוּרוֹת רָעוֹת
for haughty arrogance is compounded from base desire and evil passions, as well as from anger and corrupt severities.
וּלְפִי שֶׁכָּל מִינֵי רַע מְחוּבָּרִים יַחַד
And because all varieties of evil are inherently intertwined with one another,
וּמִי שֶׁשָּׁרְשׁוֹ בְּאֵיזֶה רַע פְּרָטִי יֵשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְכָל מִינֵי רַע
and whoever is rooted in any particular evil retains an affinity with every category of evil.
עַל כֵּן אַף שֶׁהִכִּירוּ בוֹ שֶׁהוּא מוּגְדָּר מִתַּאֲווֹת חָשְׁבוּ דְּאֵין זֶה בֶּאֱמֶת
therefore, even though they recognized that he appeared guarded against bodily lusts, they assumed that this was not authentic.
וּבְסִטְרָא דְּרַע אִם נִרְאֶה בְּגַוְונוֹ אֵיזֶה דָבָר טוֹב
And on the side of evil, if some virtuous thing appears on its outward surface,
יָדוּעַ דִּפְנִימִיּוּתוֹ הוּא מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ,
it is known that its inner core is quite the contrary;
וּלְפִי שֶׁבְּדָבָר זֶה הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הָרוֹעַ
and because in this matter evil is at its absolute nadir.
הוּא חָפֵץ לְהַעֲלִים כְּדֶרֶךְ עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא שֶׁמַּרְאֶה הַכֹּל הֵיפֶךְ הָאֱמֶת
it seeks to conceal itself after the manner of the World of Falsehood, which portrays everything upside down from the truth.
וְעַל כֵּן חָשְׁבוּ לְמָכְרוֹ לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִים שֶׁהֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרַע דְּתַאֲוָה
Therefore they intended to sell him to the Ishmaelites who represent the root of evil lust,
וְלֹא עָלְתָה בְיָדָם שֶׁנִּמְכַּר לַמִּדְיָנִים
yet this did not materialize in their hand, as he was sold instead to the Midianites
שֶׁהֵם הַחֲפֵצִים בְּכָךְ לְעוֹרֵר מְדָנִים נֶגֶד יְסוֹד קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל
who passionately desire this: to stir up strife and contention against the essential foundation of Israel's holiness.
לוֹמַר שֶׁגַּם בָּהֶם יֵשׁ פְּסוֹלֶת וְשֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם חִבּוּר לָעַמִּים
asserting that among them too resides dross, and that they hold an intrinsic attachment unto the pagan nations.
וְעַל כֵּן הֵם חָזְרוּ וּמְכָרוּהוּ לְמִצְרַיִם עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ
And therefore the Midianites in turn sold him down to Egypt, the unchaste "nakedness of the land",
לוֹמַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ חִבּוּר לִיסוֹד הָרַע גַּם כֵּן
alleging that he was bonded unto the very foundation of evil as well;
כִּי הֵם נֶגֶד הַתְחָלַת הַהֶבְדֵּל שֶׁבֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים
since the Egyptians stand directly opposing the initial demarcation separating Israel from the nations.
וּבִהְיוֹת הַשְּׁבָטִים שִׁבְטֵי יָ"הּ וְתִקְרָתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
And as the tribal Patriarchs are the tribes of God and the celestial roof of the universe,
וַדַּאי אֵין מַחְשְׁבוֹתָם מַחְשְׁבוֹת הֶבֶל וּפְעֻלָּתָם מִקְרִיִּים
their thoughts were certainly not vain illusions nor their actions incidental,
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה עד, יז): "כְּשֶׁרָצִיתָ נָתַתָּ בְּלִבָּם לִשְׂנֹא".
all the more so in light of what our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 74:17): "When You willed it, You placed hatred in their hearts.",
כִּי הָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת עֲדַיִן דָּבָר זֶה צָרִיךְ לְבֵירוּרִים
For in ultimate truth, this spiritual status still required extensive clarification,
כִּי עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לֹא הָיָה עֲדַיִן בְּחִירָה גְּמוּרָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
since prior to the Giving of the Torah, Israel's chosenness had not yet been fully finalized in the cosmos.
וְלֹא נִתְבָּרֵר עֲדַיִן שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם פְּסוֹלֶת
nor had it been clarified beyond all doubt that there was no dross within them.
וְהַבֵּירוּר הָיָה הָעִיקָּר עַל יְדֵי הַבְדָּלָתָם מֵהָעַמִּים
And that essential clarification was achieved primarily through their total separation from the nations,
וְהַתְחָלַת הַבֵּירוּר בָּזֶה הָיָה צָרִיךְ בְּיוֹסֵף
and the initiation of this clarification had to occur specifically within Joseph.
שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ הַפְּרָטִית הַכְּלוּלָה בִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִדָּה זוֹ דְּהַגְדָּרָה מִבְּנוֹת הָאָרֶץ
whose unique personal attribute integrated within the Congregation of Israel is this very trait: moral boundaries guarding against the daughters of the land.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר נִתְבָּרֵר הוּא בָּזֶה בְּאֵשֶׁת פּוֹטִיפַר
And when he was tested and clarified in this through the trial of Potiphar's wife,
נִתְבָּרֵר דְּ"מַחְשַׁבְתָּם לְרָעָה אֱלֹהִים חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטֹבָה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית נ, כ),
it was elucidated that "their thought for evil, God intended it for good" (Genesis 50:20),
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְבָּרֵר קְדֻשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב וְזַרְעוֹ,
for through this trial, the absolute holiness of Jacob and his seed was demonstrated,
וְגָרַם בָּזֶה לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לָהֶם מָזוֹן וְקִיּוּם הַחַיּוּת
and he thereby channeled unto them sustenance and preservation of life.
לִקְלוֹט מְעַט הַחַיּוּת שֶׁבְּמִצְרַיִם עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ נֶגֶד הַיְסוֹד דְּצַדִּיק
gathering up the sparks of vitality embedded in Egypt, the nakedness of the earth, facing the sefirah of Yesod of the Tzaddik.
וְעַד שֶׁלְּבַסּוֹף עֲשָׂאוּהָ כִּמְצוּלָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דָּגִים (בְּרָכוֹת ט),
Until at the end they left Egypt like a net-depth without fish (Berakhot 9b),
אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְבָּרְרוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁנוֹת הַשִּׁעְבּוּד שֶׁהָיוּ גְּדוּרִים בַּעֲרָיוֹת וּבְחִבּוּר עִם מִצְרַיִם
after all of Israel were thoroughly clarified during the years of bondage as having remained scrupulously guarded against immorality and assimilation with Egypt.
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לִגְאוּלָּה
and through this boundary they merited redemption.
דְּרַק אַחַת הָיְתָה מִשִּׁבְטוֹ שֶׁל דָּן שֶׁפִּירְסְמָהּ הַכָּתוּב
For only a single woman (Shelomit bat Dibri) belonged to the tribe of Dan whom Scripture publicized.
דְּאוֹתוֹ שֵׁבֶט הָיָה עֲדַיִן צָרִיךְ לְבֵירוּרִים קְצָת עַד שִׁמְשׁוֹן
because that particular tribe still required further clarifications until the era of Samson.
וְעַל כֵּן מַחֲשֶׁבֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים הוּא שֶׁגָּרְמָה מְכִירַת יוֹסֵף וְהַצְרָכַת הַבֵּירוּרִים
Therefore, the initial suspicion of the tribes was what brought about the sale of Joseph and necessitated the prolonged process of purification.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה גָּרְמוּ הַתְחָלַת הִתְעוֹרְרוּת שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל שֶׁהוּא בַּמִּדְיָנִים
And through this they inadvertently stirred the inception of the dominion of the base archetype of Belial, which resides in the Midianites.
וְעַל כֵּן גָּרְמוּ גַּם כֵּן עוֹנֶשׁ לְעַצְמָם בַּעֲשָׂרָה הֲרוּגֵי מְלוּכָה
And on this account they brought retribution upon themselves in the ten martyr-sages (Asarah Harugei Malchut),
שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם לְרַע לוֹ,
which was likewise the tragic temporal dominion of man over man to his own ultimate ruin.
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוֹצִיאוּ נִיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת הַרְבֵּה כַּנּוֹדָע
for through their martyrdom they extracted many holy sparks as is known.
וְכֵן הַתְחָלַת שְׁלִיטַת אָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל אַחַר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
And similarly, the initial dominion of the archetype of Belial following the Giving of the Torah,
הָיָה עַל יְדֵי בְּנוֹת מִדְיָן שֶׁהֵם הַתְחָלַת הָרָע
was enacted through the daughters of Midian who embody the primal inception of contention,
וְעַל כֵּן מִיתַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיְתָה תְּלוּיָה בְּנִקְמַת הַמִּדְיָנִים
and therefore the passing of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was made contingent upon the vengeance against the Midianites.
כִּי הוּא בְּסוֹד הַדַּעַת הַמְחַבֵּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה כַּנּוֹדָע
for Moses is the mystery of Da'at (Knowledge) unifying Chokhmah and Binah, as is known.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 105:17: of the descent to Egypt — “שָׁלַח לִפְנֵיהֶם אִישׁ, לְעֶבֶד נִמְכַּר יוֹסֵף” — “He sent a man before them; Yosef was sold as a slave.” Meforshim: Rashi and Radak — God “sent” Yosef ahead by means of his sale, to prepare sustenance for the family’s descent; the very selling “as a slave” was the providential instrument. R’ Tzadok’s use: Yosef was sold specifically “as a slave” — “the dominion of man over man to his detriment” — for the brothers, supposing that Yaakov’s line bore “dross” as Avraham’s and Yitzchak’s had, sold him to be subdued; yet this very subjugation set the “clarification” of Israel’s holiness in motion.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Dover Tzedek, Mishlei 10:7, §7 (Har Bracha edition, printed p. 97)): “The Name Havayah is the essential Name of Hashem, comprising all the vitality bestowed into creation — which is the ‘middle line’ kav emtzai of all creation. And Yosef, too, holds fast to this rung, for ‘the radiance of his countenance resembled his father’s’; and the tzaddik is the ‘guardian of the covenant,’ the rung of Yosef, in whom the Divine Name prevails.” (This is why the brothers’ suspicion in the se’if fell on Yosef in particular: he embodies Yaakov’s own ‘middle line’ — the tzaddik-Yesod whose face mirrors his father’s — so that in him, of all the sons, they thought to detect the ‘dross’ of that very trait.)  Original Hebrew (Dover Tzedek, Mishlei 10:7, §7): "שזהו קו האמצעי של כל הבריאה כנודע. ויוסף אחיד גם כן בדרגא זו כנודע שזיו איקונין שלו דומה לשל אביו ... וצדיק הוא שומר הברית דרגא דיוסף". This confirms the parallel to Yaakov’s middle line; the quoted words are Rav Tzadok’s, not a Har Bracha editorial note.  Read the original Hebrew in the Akiva Rav Tzadok Library.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 50:20: Yosef reassures his brothers after Yaakov’s death — “וְאַתֶּם חֲשַׁבְתֶּם עָלַי רָעָה, אֱלֹהִים חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטֹבָה, לְמַעַן עֲשֹׂה כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה לְהַחֲיֹת עַם רָב” — “and you intended evil against me, but God intended it for good, to bring about, as this day, the saving of many lives.” Meforshim: the Ramban — the brothers’ deed and the Divine plan coincided, each bearing its own reckoning, so that Yosef holds them accountable while affirming the good that came of it. R’ Tzadok’s use: once Yosef was “clarified” through the trial of Potifar’s wife, it emerged that “their thoughts for evil, God intended for good” — the sale that seemed to “connect” Yaakov’s seed to the nations in truth proved their utter separateness and holiness. Beis Yaakov — ‘God intended it for good’ is a retrospective clarification, not the brothers’ prospective license: Beis Yaakov on Torah, Vayeitzei 67:3, distinguishes two modes that are indispensable for reading ‘ואתם חשבתם עלי רעה, אלהים חשבה לטובה.’ Yaakov’s own middah is ‘לפני’: he seeks to see the will of Hashem within the act before doing it and refuses to rely on a later heavenly clarification that an outwardly troubling act will somehow be repaired. David’s line can reveal an ‘אחרי’ — a later clarification in which Hashem shows how even what was not consciously ordered can be brought into good. Yosef, whose countenance resembled Yaakov’s, therefore tells his brothers ‘התחת אלהים אני’: according to Yosef’s own path, the act as it appeared at the time was not something he could have chosen on the strength of a future tikkun; only afterward did Hashem reveal how their intention and the event were woven into life-saving good. This is a precise Izhbitz complement to R’ Tzadok’s account of the sale. Providence can take a deed born from error and make it the instrument of the Egyptian descent, Yosef’s test, and Israel’s clarification. But that retrospective Divine good does not collapse the distinction between good and evil at the moment of choice. The brothers remain accountable for what they thought, while Hashem remains sovereign over what their deed ultimately became.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 9b: on “and Hashem gave the people favor in the eyes of Egypt” (Shemos 12:36), the Gemara teaches that at the Exodus Israel so emptied Egypt of its wealth that “they made it like a depth in which there are no fish ki-metzulah she-ein bah dagim.” Meforshim: Rashi — they drained Egypt of its treasures so completely that nothing of worth remained, like a deep that has been fished out. R’ Tzadok’s use: this was the culmination of the “clarification” — after Israel were “fenced-in from immorality” through the years of servitude, they “extracted” the last vitality from Egypt, “the nakedness of the land,” leaving the husk empty, “a depth without fish,” and thereby “merited redemption.”

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar 31:2: God commands Moshe — “נְקֹם נִקְמַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאֵת הַמִּדְיָנִים, אַחַר תֵּאָסֵף אֶל עַמֶּיךָ” — “avenge the vengeance of the Children of Israel against the Midianites; afterward you shall be gathered to your people.” Meforshim: Rashi — although Moshe heard that his death was “bound up” with this act, he carried it out “with joy, without delay”; and it was Midyan, not Moav, that was punished, for they “stirred the strife” through their daughters. R’ Tzadok’s use: Moshe’s death hinged upon avenging Midyan because he is “in the secret of Daas,” which joins Chochmah and Binah — and Midyan, the “woman of strife,” assails precisely that inner union (Yesod Abba); hence the “beginning of the base man’s dominion” after Sinai came through “the daughters of Midyan,” the “beginning of evil.”

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Why Yosef was sold “as a slave”: the tribes did not yet know that Yaakov’s bed was whole, and seeing Yosef “desiring to rule” they suspected the dross of the middle-line trait. They meant to sell him to the Ishmaelites, but he passed to the Midianites and then to Egypt. Yet “their thought was for evil, and God intended it for good” — his test with Potifar’s wife clarified Israel’s holiness and separateness.

p: (נ) וְעַל כֵּן כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲדַיִן בְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם
And therefore, all the while that Israel was still in the Egyptian exile,
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרַשׁ תְּהִלִּים – שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב קיד) עַל פָּסוּק "גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי" (דְּבָרִים ד, לד)
and our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Shocher Tov, Psalm 114) on the verse "a nation from the midst of another nation" (Deuteronomy 4:34)
שֶׁהָיוּ בְּקִרְבָּם מַמָּשׁ מוּקָּפִים מֵהֶם לְגַמְרֵי כְּעֻבָּר בְּיֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חַיּוּת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ,
that they were literally embedded within them, completely encircled like an embryo in the thigh of its mother possessing no independent life of its own,
הוּכְרַח הוּא לִהְיוֹת בְּמִדְיָן
Moses was compelled to abide in Midian,
שֶׁהִיא הַקְּלִיפָּה הַמַּקֶּפֶת יְסוֹד אַבָּא, שֶׁבּוֹ חִבּוּר אַבָּא וְאִמָּא
which is the corrupt husk encompassing Yesod of Abba wherein the union of Father and Mother takes place,
שֶׁשָּׁם הִיא הַעֲלָמַת חִבּוּר זֶה
and where the concealment of this supernal union occurs;
וּמִשָּׁם הָיָה חַיּוּתוֹ עַל יְדֵי צִפּוֹרָה
and from that source his earthly livelihood was sustained through Zipporah.
שֶׁחָמְדָה בוֹ כְּחֵשֶׁק בְּנוֹת מִדְיָן לִדְבַּק בְּזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל
who cherished him, parallel to the deep-seated yearning of the daughters of Midian to cleave unto the seed of Israel.
וְיִתְרוֹ הוּא הַכֹּהֵן וְהָרֹאשׁ שֶׁבָּהֶם שֶׁבּוֹ עִיקַּר כֹּחַ הָאֻמָּה
And Jethro was the priest and paramount leader among them in whom the primary spiritual potency of the nation was concentrated,
אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּתְנַדָּה אָז מֵאֶצְלָם עוֹד טֶרֶם בָּא מֹשֶׁה אֵלָיו
except that he had already been excommunicated by them prior to Moses arriving at his house.
וּכְבָר נִתְרַחֵק מֵהָרַע אֶלָּא שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא נִתְקָרֵב אֶל הַטּוֹב
and had thus broken away from evil though not yet brought near unto the good.
וְהוּא הָיָה בְּאוֹתָהּ עֵצָה דְּפַרְעֹה לְעַכֵּב יְצִיאַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעַם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָם אֶלָּא שֶׁבָּרַח
And he had originally been in that royal council of Pharaoh to prevent Israel's emergence into an independent nation, but he fled.
וְ"שִׂים בַּסֶּלַע קִנֶּךָ" (בַּמִּדְבָּר כד, כא) "אֵיתָן מוֹשָׁבֶךָ",
And "firm is your dwelling place, and your nest is set in the rock" (Numbers 24:21),
רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר נִתְעוֹרֵר בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקָּבוּעַ בּוֹ מִשָּׁרְשׁוֹ שֶׁיָּצָא מֵאֵיתָן זֶה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ,
signifying that there was stirred within him the root implanted from his origin who issued from Ethan—this being Abraham our father.
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן אֲבִיהֶם שֶׁל כָּל הַגֵּרִים
who is likewise the universal father of all proselytes.
וְיִתְרוֹ הוּא הָיָה הָרֹאשׁ לְגֵרֵי הַצֶּדֶק
And Jethro was the foremost prototype of righteous converts,
שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִזַּרְעוֹ,
being likewise of Abraham's biological seed,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין נִקְרָא זַרְעוֹ אֶלָּא יַעֲקֹב
even though Scripture designates that his chosen seed is recognized in Jacob alone;
זֶה נִתְבָּרֵר אַחַר שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם וְנִבְחֲרוּ לְעַם מְיוּחָד
yet this distinction was established only after they went forth from Egypt and were chosen as a consecrated people,
אֲבָל בִּהְיוֹתָם בְּמִצְרַיִם כְּעֻבָּר בְּבֶטֶן אִמּוֹ
whereas while they lingered in Egypt like an embryo in its mother's womb,
הָיָה עֲדַיִן שֵׁם זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם עַל כָּל מִי שֶׁהָיָה מִזַּרְעוֹ.
the encompassing title of 'seed of Abraham' still hovered over all who were biologically descended from him.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין זֶה בֶּאֱמֶת
And even though this was not ultimate enduring truth,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ שְׂפַת אֱמֶת אֲשֶׁר תִּכּוֹן לָעַד
meaning it was not the lip of truth that endures forever,
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה לוֹ מְצִיאוּת גָּמוּר עַד אַרְגִּיעָה
nonetheless it possessed a functional cosmic reality for the interim,
שֶׁהֲרֵי הָיָה אָז מְצִיאוּת לְגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם
for the reality of the Egyptian exile was then in effect;
וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה מָקוֹם לְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת אוֹר בְּיִתְרוֹ מֵאַחַר שֶׁנִּתְרַחֵק מֵהֶם עוֹד קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
and therefore there was spiritual ground for an awakening of light within Jethro, since he withdrew from them even prior to the Giving of the Torah.
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא רֹאשׁ הַגֵּרִים שֶׁבָּא מִכֹּחַ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם שֶׁהָיָה תְּחִלָּה לַגֵּרִים
And therefore he stands as the head of converts who emerged from the potency of Abraham who was the first of all converts,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא זָכָה לִהְיוֹת אַחַר כָּךְ אֶזְרָח בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָב לָאֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית
only that Abraham subsequently merited to become an indigenous citizen in Israel and father to the Jewish nation.
וְיִתְרוֹ נִשְׁאַר בְּמַדְרֵגַת תְּחִלָּה לַגֵּרִים
while Jethro remained at the spiritual tier of the archetype of converts.
וְהָיָה יוֹשֵׁב בְּתוֹךְ עֲמָלֵק כִּמְפוֹרָשׁ בְּעִנְיַן שָׁאוּל (שְׁמוּאֵל א טו, ו),
And he dwelt in the midst of Amalek as explicitly stated in the narrative of Saul (I Samuel 15:6),
כִּי סְמוּכִים בְּמַדְרֵגָתָם
because they are adjacent in their spiritual rank:
זֶה רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם
this one (Amalek) is the first among the nations,
וְזֶה רֵאשִׁית גֵּרִים צַד הַטּוֹב שֶׁבַּגּוֹיִם כַּאֲשֶׁר בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יִכָּנוּ.
and this one (Jethro) is the first of converts, representing the potential spark of good among the nations when they align under the name of Israel.
כִּי הַתְחָלַת הַתּוֹרָה וְהָאֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית הוּא יוֹצֵא מִיְסוֹד אַבָּא
For the genesis of the Torah and the Jewish nation proceeds from the Yesod of Abba,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ "יִשְׂרָאֵל עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה",
in accordance with "Israel arose in the Primordial Thought".
וְכָל יְצִיאָה לַפּוֹעַל הוּא דֶּרֶךְ הַיְסוֹד כַּנּוֹדָע
and all emergence into external manifestation passes through the channel of Yesod, as is known.
וּמִשָּׁם גַּם כֵּן זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה הַתְחָלַת הָרָע
And from that same realm, symmetrically confronting it, emerges the inception of evil;
וּכְשֶׁהַטּוֹב מִתְבָּרֵר הוּא קוֹלֵט עִמּוֹ גַּם מִן הָרַע מַה שֶּׁאֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת נִקְלָט מִמֶּנּוּ וּלְהִתְחַבֵּר אֶל הַטּוֹב
and as the good is clarified, it gathers along with it from the realm of evil whatever can possibly be reclaimed and unified with the holy.
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא : "לֹא גָּלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶלָּא לְהוֹסִיף עֲלֵיהֶם גֵּרִים",
And along the lines of the Talmudic dictum (Pesachim 87b): "Israel was exiled solely to add converts unto them",
כִּי זֶה כָּל צֹרֶךְ הַגָּלִיּוֹת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם לְרַע לוֹ,
for this is the entire underlying purpose of the exiles: that the dominion of man over man should turn out to his own ruin,
שֶׁבְּצֵאתוֹ יוֹצִיא עִמּוֹ כָּל נִיצוֹץ טוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ
so that in departing, Israel draws out every holy spark embedded within him.
וְיַשְׁאִירוּ כִּמְצוּלָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דָּגִים
and leaves that nation like an oceanic abyss stripped of fish.

paragraphs.text: Shemos Rabbah 1:32: Yisro was a priest of idolatry who “saw there was no substance in it,” rejected it, and resolved to repent even before Moshe came. He told his townsmen, “until now I served you as priest; now I am old — choose another,” and handed over the idolatrous vessels. They ostracized him — that none should associate with him, work for him, or shepherd his flocks — “therefore he sent out his daughters to shepherd.” Sotah 11a: R’ Chiya bar Abba said in the name of R’ Simai: three were party to that counsel of “let us deal wisely with them” — Bilaam, Iyov, and Yisro. Bilaam, who advised it, was slain; Iyov, who kept silent, was sentenced to sufferings; and Yisro, who fled, merited that among his descendants were those who sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone the Sanhedrin.

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar 24:21: beholding the Keini (the descendants of Yisro), Bilaam lifts his parable — “אֵיתָן מוֹשָׁבֶךָ, וְשִׂים בַּסֶּלַע קִנֶּךָ” — “firm eisan is your dwelling-place, and set your nest in the rock.” Meforshim: Rashi — the “Keini” are the children of Yisro, and Bilaam marvels at their good fortune, that they came to be “set” so firmly among Israel (some seated in the Chamber of Hewn Stone); “eisan” bespeaks strength and permanence. R’ Tzadok’s use: “his dwelling is eisan” means that there was aroused in Yisro “the root fixed in him from his origin” — that he issued from “Eisan,” Avraham Avinu (Eisan ha-Ezrachi), “the father of all converts”; hence Yisro is the “head of the righteous converts.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Sivan §4): “and Avraham our father fulfilled the whole Torah before it was given.” Exactly the se’if’s Yisro: the “priest and head” who is drawn near belongs to a world in which the name of Avraham still reaches — for a rung of Torah existed and was recognizable before Sinai, outside the camp.  Further original Hebrew (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Sivan 4): "אברהם אבינו ע״ה קיים כל התורה כולה עד שלא נתנה ... ולימד לכל העולם כולו"; later in the same passage: "ואז נבחרו ישראל והייתם לי סגולה מכל העמים". The parallel concerns the transition from Avraham’s universal teaching before Sinai to Israel’s distinct selection at Sinai, not an explicit statement about Yisro in that source.

paragraphs.text: I Shmuel 15:6: before striking Amalek, Shaul warns the Keini — “לְכוּ סֻּרוּ רְדוּ מִתּוֹךְ עֲמָלֵקִי פֶּן אֹסִפְךָ עִמּוֹ, וְאַתָּה עָשִׂיתָה חֶסֶד עִם כָּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל” — “‘Go, depart, go down from among the Amalekite, lest I sweep you away with him’ — for you did kindness with all the Children of Israel.” Meforshim: Rashi — the “Keini” here are the descendants of Yisro, who “dwelt within Amalek”; Shaul spared them for the kindness Yisro had shown Moshe. R’ Tzadok’s use: Yisro, “the first of converts,” and Amalek, “the first of the nations,” are “adjacent in their rung” — the good and evil sides of the nations set side by side; so Yisro “dwelt within Amalek,” the good side waiting to be “extracted” and brought “beneath the wings of the Shechinah.” Mei HaShiloach — converts are still received because the cosmic birur is not yet complete: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Talmud, Berachos 27b:3, reads the dispute over whether Ma’ariv is optional or obligatory through the unfinished work of galus. He notes that when an Ammonite convert came before the sages and was ruled eligible to enter the congregation, the very ruling demonstrated that ‘עדיין לא נגמר הבירור’ — the clarification is not yet complete. In the days of Mashiach converts will no longer be accepted, whereas now they are accepted because ‘עדיין יש ניצוצות קדושה הצריכים להתלקט,’ holy sparks still remain to be gathered. This is an exact Izhbitz parallel to R’ Tzadok’s explanation of Yisro as ‘ראשית גרים’ and of exile as the setting in which the good side of the nations can be extracted and brought beneath the wings of the Shechinah. Yisro’s adjacency to Amalek is therefore not accidental symbolism. So long as the birur is unfinished, good and evil can stand in unnerving proximity; the task is to separate them without confusing them. Yisro leaves the counsel of Pharaoh, leaves Midyan’s idolatrous priesthood, and ultimately comes to Torah. The very possibility of such movement testifies that the nations are not yet a closed, final category. Galus persists while sparks remain outside; geulah corresponds to the completion of that gathering, when the lines are finally clarified and no further conversion is needed.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: While Israel were in Egypt — a nation within a nation, like a fetus with no vitality of its own — Moshe had to be in Midyan, the husk surrounding Yesod Abba, drawing his vitality through Tzipporah. Yisro, the priest and head of Midyan, had already distanced himself from evil. He is the head of righteous converts; and Israel is exiled “to add converts,” the good extracted and the husk left empty.

p: (נא) וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עַל יְדֵי גָּלוּתוֹ בְּמִדְיָן קָלַט עִמּוֹ אֶת יִתְרוֹ
And Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, through his exile in Midian, reclaimed Jethro with him,
שֶׁהוּא מִכֹּחַ הַפְּסוֹלֶת שֶׁנֶּגֶד יְסוֹד אַבָּא
who derived from the opposing dross confronting the Yesod of Abba,
שֶׁאֵין מַנִּיחַ לָצֵאת לַפּוֹעַל מַה שֶּׁבְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹי אֶחָד
which seeks to prevent the realization of what is in His divine thought—to fashion Israel as one singular nation,
וְלָתֵת לָהֶם תּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת שֶׁהוּא הַמְחַבַּרְתָּם יַחַד
and to give them Torah and commandments which bind them into unity,
וְהֵם חֲפֵצִים לְעוֹרֵר מְדָנִים וְלִמְנוֹעַ חִבּוּר זֶה
while the Midianites yearn to stir up strife and prevent this holy union.
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה יָרְדָה חוּרְבָּה וְשִׂנְאָה לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא (שַׁבָּת פט).
whereby ruin and hatred descended upon the pagan nations, as they taught in chapter Rabbi Akiva (Shabbat 89a).
וּלְפִי שֶׁהָאֻמּוֹת גַּם כֵּן בְּרִיּוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And because the nations are likewise His divine creations.
עַל כֵּן יֵשׁ בְּאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ גַּם כֵּן צַד מַה הַטּוֹב שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הַגֵּרִים בְּאוֹתָהּ אֻמָּה הַנִּקְלָטִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
therefore within that very power there resides some element of good from which prospective converts in that nation are absorbed into Israel.
וְהַטּוֹב שֶׁבְּמִדְיָן
And the redeeming good latent within Midian,
שֶׁהוּא הַכֹּחַ שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִהְיוֹת פֵּירוּד וּמְדָנִים וְלֹא חִבּוּר וְגוֹי אֶחָד מְיוּחָד לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם
which corruptly seeks separation and contention rather than unified attachment to their Father in Heaven.
קָלַט מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לְעוֹרֵר מְדָנִים בֵּין הָאֻמּוֹת לַאֲבִינוּ שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם
Moses our teacher reclaimed in order to turn it holy: stirring up decisive contention and rupture between the pagan nations and our Father in Heaven.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ז.): בִּקֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא תִשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָה עַל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
And as they stated (Berakhot 7a): Moses requested that the Shechinah never rest upon the nations of the world,
וְהוֹרִיד חוּרְבָּה וְשִׂנְאָה לָהֶם
and he brought down desolation and permanent division upon them,
וְשֶׁאֲפִילּוּ יִרְצֶה גּוֹי לְהֵיטִיב מַעֲשָׂיו לְגַמְרֵי לֹא יוּכַל כְּלָל
so that even should an uncircumcised gentile desire to rectify his deeds entirely, he cannot do so,
דַּאֲפִילּוּ חֲסִידֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת שֶׁמֶץ וְאֶפֶס קָצֵהוּ לִקְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל
for even the pious of the nations hold no trace or fractional inkling of the essential holiness of Israel,
אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יִתְגַּיְּירוּ וּבְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יִתְכַּנּוּ,
unless they undergo full conversion and are designated by the name of Israel;
וְזֶהוּ הַטּוֹב שֶׁבְּכֹחַ מְדָנִים זֶה לְעוֹרְרוֹ נֶגֶד אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
and this is the holy utility of this contentious power: to wield it against the idolatrous nations.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְעוֹרֵר יִתְרוֹ וּבָא לַמִּדְבָּר
And through this divine impetus, Jethro was aroused and journeyed to the wilderness,
שֶׁנִּתְעוֹרֵר בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחַ דְּמִדְיָן מִצַּד הַבְּרִיאָה
whereby the pure root of Midian's primal energy was awakened within him,
שֶׁהוּא הָרִיחוּק הַגָּמוּר לְכָל מִינֵי כֹּחוֹת דְּאֻמּוֹת
which is absolute detachment from all mundane forces of the nations.
שֶׁהֵם כֹּחוֹת גּוּפָנִיִּים דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לִקְדוּשָּׁה כְּלָל
these being physical, bodily drives of this world holding no intrinsic connection to holiness at all.
וּמַה שֶּׁהֵם חָשְׁבוּ שֶׁכְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל
And whereas the nations presumed that the House of Israel is just like all other peoples,
אַדְּרַבָּה, עַל יָדָם הוּא עִיקַּר בֵּירוּר הַהֶבְדֵּל וְהָרִיחוּק בֵּינֵיהֶם
on the contrary, through converts unfolds the definitive clarification of the unbridgeable gulf between them,
וְשֶׁאֵין לְשׁוּם אֻמָּה וְלָשׁוֹן אֶפְשָׁרוּת לִדְבַּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּלָל אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יִתְיַהֲדוּ.
and that no nation or tongue has any possibility of cleaving to Hashem, blessed be He, unless they become fully Jewish.
וְעַל כֵּן הוּכְרַח לַעֲזוֹב מִשְׁכָּנוֹ בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
And therefore Jethro was compelled to abandon his station at the peak of the civilized world,
רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר שֶׁהָיָה בְּעֵינֵי עַצְמוֹ כְּבָר בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת מִתְרוֹמֵם מִכָּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
meaning that he had considered himself already at the height of perfection, transcending all worldly matters,
דְּעַל כֵּן נִדּוּהוּ וְרִחֲקוּהוּ בְּנֵי מִדְיָן דְּהָיָה מְרוּחָק מֵהֶם
which is why the Midianites ostracized him, as he had grown distant from them;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הִשִּׂיג כִּי עֲדַיִן אֵין זֶה כְּלוּם
nonetheless he realized that this was still utterly nothing
אִם לֹא יֵלֵךְ לְהִתְחַבֵּר עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל דַּוְוקָא כְּדֵי לְהַשִּׂיג מִקְּדֻשָּׁתָם שֶׁ"לֹּא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי" (תְּהִלִּים קמז, כ).
unless he went specifically to attach himself unto Israel to draw from their holiness, for "He did not do so unto any nation" (Psalms 147:20).
וְזֶהוּ כֹּחַ הַטּוֹב שֶׁבְּמִדְיָן לְהַכִּיר רִיחוּק הָאֻמּוֹת וְשֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהִתְגַּיֵּיר
And this is the redeemable power within Midian: to recognize the inherent distance of the nations and the absolute necessity of converting.
אִם כֵּן הוּא הַגֵּר הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה וְשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קֵרְבוֹ,
Thus he was the primary convert at the time of the Giving of the Torah whom Hashem brought near.
כִּי בוֹ, בְּכֹחוֹ שֶׁבְּתוֹלַדְתּוֹ, הוּא הַתְחָלַת עִנְיַן הַגֵּירוּת
for in him and in his innate constitutional makeup lay the inception of conversion.
רַק שֶׁבְּכֹחַ הָרַע רוֹצִים לְדַמּוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל לָהֶם
Except that in the power of evil, they seek to assimilate Israel to themselves.
וּבְכֹחַ הַטּוֹב הוּא שֶׁיַּכִּירוּ רִיחוּקָם וְיִרְצוּ לְהִכָּלֵל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
whereas in the power of holiness, they recognize their spiritual distance and seek to be subsumed within Israel.
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיְסוֹד וְהִתְקַשְּׁרוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם בְּקֶשֶׁר אַמִּיץ וּדְלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין לְעָלְמִין
And Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who is the root of Yesod and the unbreakable, eternal bond of Israel to their Father in Heaven,
נִתְגַּדֵּל בְּמִדְיָן לְבַטֵּל הַקְּלִיפָּה הַסּוֹבֶבֶת לְהַעֲלִים וּלְהִתְנַגֵּד קֶשֶׁר זֶה
developed in Midian precisely to dissolve the surrounding husk that conceals and opposes this covenantal bond;
וְהוּא הִתְאַמֵּץ נֶגֶד זֶה לִהְיוֹת "חַרְבָּם תָּבוֹא בְלִבָּם" (תְּהִלִּים לז, טו) וּלְרַע לוֹ.
and he exerted his spiritual might against it so that "their sword shall enter into their own heart" (Psalms 37:15) and turn to their destruction.

R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Shemos §1): “he mentions there the names of the tribes on account of their allusion to the redemption, which is the purpose of the exile — and all of it a preparation for the Giving of the Torah; and as in Berachos, that three gifts come through sufferings.” The se’if’s Midyan exile exactly: the sojourn among the nations is not an interruption of Moshe’s mission but its preparation — the exile is how the gift is acquired. Izhbitz parallel - Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Yitro 3; Yitro 2: The Ishbitzer gives a particularly close explanation of the same 'good power' that can be extracted from Yisro's Midyanite root. On the Midrash's contrast, 'strike the scoffer' - Amalek, but 'the simple one will become wise' - Yisro, he explains that both traits begin as deficiencies: the leitz mocks every truth, whereas the peti is open to every influence. Yet the latter defect can itself be redirected, because one who is open can eventually receive the truth and repair the root of his deficiency. Yisro therefore moves from having experimented with avodah zarah to 'atah yadati ki gadol Hashem' and conversion. In a second teaching the Ishbitzer says that even Yisro's first 'hearing' was sent to him by Hashem; nevertheless, because Yisro recognized that 'la-Hashem ha'aretz u-melo'ah' and yearned to cleave to Israel, Heaven credited the hearing to him as though it had begun from his own initiative. This closely complements R' Tzadok here: the power of Midyan is not redeemed by blurring the distinction between Israel and the nations. Its good is extracted precisely when the outsider recognizes the distinction and converts the very power of separation into a movement toward joining Israel. 
Ishbitz parallel, Mei HaShiloach II, Yitro §3: "לֵץ תַּכֶּה" זֶה עֲמָלֵק "וּפֶתִי יַעְרִים" זֶה יִתְרוֹ — “Strike the scoffer” means Amalek, and “the simple will become prudent” means Yisro. 
Ishbitz parallel, Mei HaShiloach II, Yitro §2: אַף שֶׁהַתְחָלַת הַשְּׁמִיעָה לֹא הָיָה מִצִּדּוֹ רַק הַשי"ת שָׁלַח לוֹ זֶה הַשְּׁמִיעָה — Although the beginning of the hearing did not arise from him, the Blessed Name sent him that hearing.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 37:15: of the wicked who plot against the righteous — “חַרְבָּם תָּבוֹא בְלִבָּם, וְקַשְּׁתוֹתָם תִּשָּׁבַרְנָה” — “their sword shall enter their own heart, and their bows shall be broken.” Background: David’s psalm, in which the schemes the wicked draw against the just recoil upon themselves. Meforshim: Rashi and the Radak — the very weapon the wicked unsheathe to harm the righteous turns back and pierces their own heart, their bows shattered. R’ Tzadok’s use: Moshe, root of the Yesod and of Israel’s unbreakable bond to their Father, “prevailed against” the surrounding husk of Midyan — turning its own power of strife back upon it, “their sword shall enter their own heart,” so that “all their dominion is to their own detriment.”

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Through his Midyan exile Moshe absorbed Yisro — the power set against Yesod Abba, which resists Israel’s becoming one nation, and which Sinai turned into the nations’ hatred. Yet since the nations too are His creatures, that power has a good side: the converts. Yisro, feeling himself elevated, still recognized that it was nothing without joining Israel — and so became the first convert.

p: (נב) וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְעוֹרֵר שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַגֵּרִים
And through this the root of converts was awakened.
וְלָכֵן קִבֵּל הָעֵרֶב רַב שֶׁהֵם הַגֵּרִים מֵאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁרָצוּ לְהִתְרַחֵק מֵהָאֻמּוֹת וּלְהִתְחַבֵּר עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל
and therefore Moses accepted the mixed multitude (erev rav) who were converts from the nations desiring to abandon the pagans and unite with Israel.
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קְרָאָם "עַמְּךָ" (שְׁמוֹת לב, ז),
And Hashem, blessed be He, called them "your people" (Exodus 32:7),
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אֵינָם בִּכְלַל עַם ה
' for in ultimate truth they were not part of Hashem's authentic core nation;
רַק כֹּחַ זֶה שֶׁל קִבּוּל גֵּרִים קָלַט מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִמִּדְיָן עַל יְדֵי בַּת יִתְרוֹ
rather this capacity to accept converts was absorbed by Moses our teacher from Midian through the daughter of Jethro.
וְהוּא רַק כֹּחַ טוֹב שֶׁבָּאֻמּוֹת
it being merely the positive potential embedded within the nations.
וְהֵם שֶׁעָשׂוּ הָעֵגֶל
And it was they who made the Golden Calf,
שֶׁאֵינָם חֲפֵצִים בַּשְּׁלֵימוּת הַגָּמוּר כִּלְעָתִיד
because they do not truly desire that complete, unmediated perfection destined for the World to Come.
דְּאָז "ה' בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ" (דְּבָרִים לב, יב) וְלֹא יִהְיֶה גֵּרִים כְּלָל
when "Hashem alone will lead him" and no converts will be received at all.
וְעִיקַּר הִתְעוֹרְרוּת מְדָנִים דְּמִדְיָן שֶׁבַּבְּרִיאָה הוּא נֶגֶד הַגֵּרִים
And the primary inciting of contentions (medanim) of Midian within Creation is directed against converts,
דְּהַשָּׂגַת הָאֻמּוֹת הוּא רַק בָּהֶם וְהֵם יֵשׁ לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת עֲדַיִן עִמָּהֶם
for the spiritual reach of the nations extends only unto them, and converts still retain an affinity with their former origins,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ : "גִּיּוֹרָא עַד עֲשָׂרָה דָרֵי לָא תִבְזֵי כוּלֵי",
as they stated (Sanhedrin 94a): "Do not insult an Aramean in the presence of a convert down to ten generations",
כִּי אֵין לָהֶם דְּבֵקוּת גָּמוּר בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים
for converts do not possess an absolute, essential cleaving unto the living God from birth;
וְעַל כֵּן הֵם גַּם כֵּן חֲפֵצִים לְעוֹרֵר מְדָנִים וּלְבַטֵּל הַדְּבֵקוּת הַגָּמוּר מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
and therefore they too unconsciously tend to arouse contention and dilute Israel's absolute cleaving.
וּשְׁלֵימוּתָם הוּא רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר יִרְצוּ לְהִתְדַּבֵּק בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְגַמְרֵי
And their rectification occurs only when they desire to dissolve and attach themselves totally within Israel;
וְאָז "קָשִׁים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּסַפַּחַת" (יְבָמוֹת מז)
yet even then "converts are as troublesome to Israel as a scab (sapachat)" (Yevamot 47b),
שֶׁהוּא נֶגַע הַדְּבוּקָה בְּעוֹר הַבָּשָׂר
which is an external cutaneous blemish attached merely to the outer skin,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה "מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה מוֹשָׁבוֹ" (וַיִּקְרָא יג, מו),
and through this "his dwelling shall be outside the camp" (Leviticus 13:46),
כִּי גּוֹרְמִים לְרִיחוּק שְׁכִינָה דְּאֵינָהּ שׁוֹרָה אֶלָּא עַל מִשְׁפָּחוֹת הַמְיוּחָסוֹת ,
because they cause a distancing of the Shechinah which rests only upon pure-lineage families (Kiddushin 70b),
וּמְבַטְּלִים גַּם כֵּן הַדְּבֵיקוּת הַגָּמוּר
and disrupt that absolute pristine communion.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא רַק לְשָׁעָה דְּמִיָּד נִרְפָּא הַנֶּגַע
except that this is merely temporary, for the affliction will ultimately heal.
וְזֶה הָיָה אוֹת רִאשׁוֹן דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּנִגְעֵי יָדוֹ וְשֶׁשָּׁבָה כִּבְשָׂרוֹ (שְׁמוֹת ד, ו–ז),
And this was the inner meaning of the sign given to Moses our teacher in his hand becoming leprous and then restoring like his flesh (Exodus 4:6–7);
וּדְעַל יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁאָמַר "הֵן לֹא יַאֲמִינוּ לִי" (שָׁם ד, א),
namely, because he uttered: "Behold, they will not believe me",
שֶׁחָשַׁד חִסָּרוֹן אֱמוּנָה בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגַם הוּא בִּכְלַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
thereby suspecting a lack of faith within the children of Israel while he himself was included among them,
וּלְפִי שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ חִסָּרוֹן אֱמוּנָה בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם מַאֲמִינִים
and because he lacked faith in Israel's innate faith,
גָּרַם לְחָשְׁדָם בְּחִסָּרוֹן אֱמוּנָה בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
it caused him to suspect them of a deficiency of faith in Hashem, blessed be He.
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַקְּלִיפָּה דְּמִדְיָן
And this defect derived from the husk of Midian,
שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ אָז מִמֶּנָּה לְגַמְרֵי
from which Moses had not yet completely separated at that juncture,
שֶׁהֵם הַחוֹשְׁדִים כֵּן לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
who chronically harbor such cynical suspicions against Israel.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה חָשַׁב גַּם כֵּן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לַגֵּרִים חִבּוּר עִם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
and through this he presumed that proselytes could be fully integrated with Israel.
וְעַל כֵּן הֶרְאָה לוֹ הַנְּגָעִים בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁהִיא הַמְקַבֶּלֶת הַגֵּרִים
Therefore Hashem showed him the leprosy upon his hand, which represents the hand that receives converts,
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם הַקִּבּוּל מְיוּחָס לְיָד וּכְמוֹ "אַתָּה נוֹתֵן יָד לַפּוֹשְׁעִים".
for in all contexts reception is associated with the hand, as in "You extend a hand to transgressors".
וְהֶרְאָה לוֹ אַחַר כָּךְ שָׁבָה לִבְשָׂרוֹ,
And Hashem subsequently showed him that his hand restored as his healthy flesh,
דִּבְסוֹף לֹא יַזִּיק כְּלוּם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וְכָל מַה שֶּׁקִּלְקְלוּ הַגֵּרִים הָיָה רַק לְשָׁעָה
showing that ultimately the converts will cause no lasting damage to Israel and whatever they spoiled was only temporary.
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא חָשׁ וְקִבְּלָם
and therefore Moses did not hesitate and accepted them.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas Shabbos §6: “ובמ״ת שפסקה זוהמתן זכו לחבה ראשונה מנשיקות פיהו בי׳ הדברות שהיו בפרסום כמ״ש בסוף זבחים דגם או״ה הרגישו איזה הרגש מזה וא״ל בלעם ה׳ עוז לעמו יתן. וכ״ש הערב רב אף שהיו חוץ לענן מ״מ שלט עין הרע שלהם והם שורש זוהמת הנחש שמהם לא פסק. כי גירותים לא הי׳ לש״ש.” — “At the Giving of the Torah, when their defilement ceased, they merited the original affection from the kisses of His mouth, in the ten commandments that were given publicly, as stated at the end of Zevachim: even the nations felt something of this, and Bilaam told them, ‘Hashem will give strength to His people.’ All the more so the mixed multitude: although they were outside the cloud, their evil eye nevertheless took effect; they were the root of the serpent’s defilement, which had not ceased from them, for their conversion was not for the sake of Heaven.” This specifies the incomplete clarification behind the erev rav’s harmful influence, while the present paragraph explains why its effect on Israel was temporary. Source scope: this Hebrew is Rav Tzadok’s own discussion of the particular erev rav at Sinai; it is not a halachic statement about every convert.

paragraphs.text: Shemos 4:1 (and Shabbos 97a): Moshe demurred — “וְהֵן לֹא יַאֲמִינוּ לִי, וְלֹא יִשְׁמְעוּ בְּקֹלִי” — “but behold, they will not believe me, nor heed my voice.” Meforshim: Reish Lakish (Shabbos 97a) — “one who suspects the worthy is smitten in his body,” for God had already attested that Israel are “believers, children of believers”; Moshe, doubting their faith, was answered, “they will believe… but you, in the end, will not believe” — and forthwith his hand turned “leprous as snow.” R’ Tzadok’s use: Moshe’s very suspicion of a “lack of faith” in Israel arose “from the husk of Midyan,” from which he had not yet fully parted — the husk whose way is precisely to suspect Israel — and from this came, too, his thought that “the converts have a connection with the Children of Israel.”

paragraphs.text: Shemos 4:6–7: the sign of Moshe’s hand — “וַיּוֹצִאָהּ וְהִנֵּה יָדוֹ מְצֹרַעַת כַּשָּׁלֶג… הָשֵׁב יָדְךָ אֶל חֵיקֶךָ… וְהִנֵּה שָׁבָה כִּבְשָׂרוֹ” — “he brought out his hand, and behold, it was leprous as snow… then ‘return your hand to your bosom’… and behold, it had returned like his own flesh.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Sages read the leprous hand as a rebuke — Moshe was stricken with tzara’as, the affliction of the slanderer (for having “slandered” Israel by doubting their faith), and its healing bespoke forgiveness. R’ Tzadok’s use: the sign was shown “in his hand” — “that which accepts the converts,” for “acceptance is attributed to the hand”; the hand made leprous and then “returned like his flesh” taught that the converts, like a passing lesion, “harm Israel only for a moment” and leave no lasting wound — “and therefore he did not worry, and accepted them.”

paragraphs.text: Yevamos 47b: “R’ Chelbo said: Converts are as hard for Israel as a sapachas a skin-affliction/scab kashim gerim l’Yisrael k’sapachas.” Izhbitz parallel - Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Berakhot 27b:3; cf. Tiferet Shlomo, Purim 99: The Ishbitzer's reading of the dispute over Ma'ariv gives a conceptual background to R' Tzadok's treatment of gerim and the erev rav. He explains that before the final birur, when the world is not yet completely clarified, converts are still accepted because 'there are still holy sparks that must be gathered'; only in the Messianic future, when the clarification is complete, will converts no longer be accepted. Thus gerus itself belongs to an unfinished world in which holiness remains intermingled outside Israel and must still be drawn home. Tiferet Shlomo develops the same language of nitzotzos but adds an important caution: when holy sparks emerge from the nations, their surrounding admixture can also accompany them, and Israel must guard itself so that the alien element is not absorbed together with the holy spark. That balance fits the present se'if with unusual precision. Moshe's acceptance of the erev rav was not a mistake in recognizing that something holy sought attachment to Israel; the danger lay in the incompleteness of the birur, so that attachment to Israel could coexist with a residue that later sought the Golden Calf. R' Tzadok's 'sapachas' image therefore describes not gerus itself, God forbid, but the danger of an incompletely clarified attachment that clings externally before the inner root has been fully transformed. Legal/source distinction: Yevamos 47b also explicitly teaches “טבל ועלה הרי הוא כישראל לכל דבריו” — after conversion and immersion the convert is Jewish in every respect. Rav Tzadok’s symbolic discussion of this specific erev rav episode must not be taken as a contrary halachic ruling or a general assertion about converts.

Rav Tzadok’s symbolic discussion of this specific erev rav episode must not be taken as a contrary halachic ruling or a general assertion about converts.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Through this Moshe accepted the erev rav — converts who wished to leave the nations for Israel, whom Hashem called “your people.” Yet they made the Calf, not desiring a future in which Hashem alone guides and there are no converts at all. Converts are “hard for Israel as a sapachas,” clinging like a lesion and briefly distancing the Shechinah — which is just what Moshe’s first sign, the hand made leprous and then restored, was showing him.

p: (נג) וְיִתְרוֹ בָּא מֵעַצְמוֹ מֵהִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁקֵּרְבוֹ,
And Jethro came of his own accord from the heavenly awakening of Hashem Who drew him near;
כִּי כְּמוֹ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה בָּאֻמּוֹת שֶׁהֲרֵי יֶשְׁנָם בָּעוֹלָם מִפְּנֵי אֵיזֶה נִיצוֹץ טוֹב שֶׁבָּהֶם
for just as Hashem desired the existence of the nations—who remain in the world solely on account of some holy spark within them—
כָּל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁרָצָה בַּגֵּרִים מִפְּנֵי אֵיזֶה נִיצוֹץ טוֹב שֶׁבָּהֶם וְהוּא יִתְרוֹ.
all the more so did He desire converts on account of the distinct good spark within them, which was Jethro.
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה קְלִיפָּה הַסּוֹבֶבֶת לַפְּרִי
For Hashem willed that in this world there exist a protective husk surrounding the fruit,
וְתַכְלִית הַקְּלִיפָּה מִפְּנֵי אֵיזֶה טוֹב הַנִּקְלָט מֵהֶם לִקְדוּשָּׁה
and the purpose of the shell is to preserve that good which is reclaimed from them into holiness,
הֲרֵי יֵשׁ בָּהֶם אֵיזֶה דָבָר טוֹב הַנִּטְפָּל לִקְדוּשָּׁה
meaning that there exists within them an auxiliary good attached to holiness.
וְזֶהוּ נֶפֶשׁ הַגֵּר שֶׁרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּקְּלִיפָּה שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ יִהְיֶה הַעֲלָמַת הַפְּרִי
and this is the soul of the convert which Hashem willed within the shell to bring about the temporary concealment of the fruit.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לְיִתְרוֹ: "וְהָיִיתָ לָּנוּ לְעֵינָיִם" (בַּמִּדְבָּר י, לא),
And this is what Moses said to Jethro: "and you shall be to us as eyes" (Numbers 10:31),
כִּי הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין נִקְרְאוּ עֵינֵי הָעֵדָה
for the Sanhedrin are designated the 'eyes of the congregation',
וְכֵן אִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה סג) עַל פָּסוּק "עִם יְפֵה עֵינַיִם" – מִדַּעַת סַנְהֶדְרִין
and so it is stated in Bereishit Rabbah (Parashah 63) on the verse "with fair eyes"—from the wisdom of the Sanhedrin,
וּמִזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל יִתְרוֹ יָשְׁבוּ בְּלִשְׁכַּת הַגָּזִית וְהָיוּ רָאשֵׁי סַנְהֶדְרָאוֹת ,
and from the descendants of Jethro scholars sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone and were leaders of Sanhedrins (Sanhedrin 104a).
וְגַם הוּא יִתֵּר פָּרָשָׁה אַחַת בַּתּוֹרָה וְהוּא פָּרָשַׁת סַנְהֶדְרִין וְהַמְנָאַת שׁוֹפְטִים
and he likewise appended an entire section to the Torah, namely the appointment of judges and courts.
כִּי הָעַיִן מוֹרֶה בְּכָל מָקוֹם עַל הַהַשְׁגָּחָה וְשִׂימַת לֵב עַל הַדָּבָר
For the eye everywhere denotes watchful supervision and applying deliberate care to a matter.
כְּמוֹ "וַאֲשִׂימָה עֵינִי עָלָיו" (בְּרֵאשִׁית מד, כא), "עֵינֵי ה' אֶל צַדִּיקִים" (תְּהִלִּים לד, טז) וְכַדּוֹמֶה
such as "that I may set my eye upon him" (Genesis 44:21), "The eyes of Hashem are toward the righteous" (Psalms 34:16), and the like.
וְהַסַּנְהֶדְרִין הֵם הַמַּשְׁגִּיחִים עַל הָעֵדָה
And the Sanhedrin are the overseers supervising the congregation:
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "יָדֵינוּ לֹא שָׁפְכוּ וְגוֹמֵר" – "שֶׁלֹּא רְאִינוּהוּ וְהִנַּחְנוּהוּ כוּלֵי" (סוֹטָה מו),
as it is stated: "Our hands have not shed this blood, etc."—"we did not see him and leave him without food or escort, etc." (Sotah 46b).
כִּי עַל הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין לְהַשְׁגִּיחַ בְּכָל דָּבָר
for it rests upon the Sanhedrin to supervise every communal affair.
וְדָבָר זֶה חִדֵּשׁ יִתְרוֹ שֶׁאָמַר "נָבֹל תִּבֹּל וְגוֹמֵר" (שְׁמוֹת יח, יח),
And this principle Jethro introduced when saying: "You will surely wear away, etc." (Exodus 18:18);
דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא רָצָה לְהַמְנוֹת סַנְהֶדְרִין
for Moses our teacher did not wish to appoint a tiered judiciary;
אַף דְּיָדַע שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְבַד לְהַשְׁגִּיחַ עַל שִׁשִּׁים רִיבּוֹא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל פְּרָטֵי עִנְיְנֵיהֶם
even though he knew that he alone could not possibly arbitrate for six hundred thousand of Israel in all their minute affairs,
הוּא רָצָה לְהַנְהִיגָם בְּעִנְיָן זֶה שֶׁיָּאִיר עֵינֵיהֶם
he wished rather to guide them in such a way that their own spiritual eyes would be illuminated
שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לִרְאוֹת כָּל אֶחָד נִגְעֵי עַצְמוֹ בְּעַצְמוֹ,
so that every individual could perceive his own inward blemishes by himself,
וְיִהְיֶה כָּל אֶחָד "עֵינָיו בְּרֹאשׁוֹ" (קֹהֶלֶת ב, יד)
and each would have "his eyes in his head" (Ecclesiastes 2:14).
וְלֹא יִצְטָרְכוּ לְעֵינֵי הָעֵדָה כְּלָל
and they would not require external eyes of the congregation at all.
וְזֶהוּ אוֹר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד: "דְּלֹא יְלַמְּדוּ עוֹד אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ" (יִרְמְיָה לא, לג),
And this is the transcendent illumination of the future: "And they shall teach no more every man his neighbor" (Jeremiah 31:34);
וְזֶהוּ שְׁלֵימוּת מִדַּת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא רַבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
and this was the perfection of the attribute of Moses our teacher, the Master of Israel.
שֶׁרָצָה לְלַמְּדָם בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת עַד שֶׁלֹּא יִצְטָרְכוּ לְרַב עוֹד
who sought to instruct them with such ultimate perfection that they would never need a teacher again.
אֲבָל אוֹר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר אֶלָּא לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
Yet this internalized light is accessible solely to the native children of Israel,
אֲבָל הַגֵּרִים בְּהֶכְרֵחַ לָהֶם לְקַבֵּל מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
whereas proselytes must perforce receive guidance externally from Israel;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ דְּלֶעָתִיד מָשִׁיחַ יָבוֹא רַק לְלַמֵּד לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם דְּהֵם יִצְטָרְכוּ לִמּוּד גַּם אָז
and as our Sages noted, in the future the Messiah will come to teach only the nations of the world, for they will still require instruction even then.
וּלְפִי שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין הִתְגַּלּוּת הַפְּרִי אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ הַקְּלִיפָּה
And because in this temporal world the revelation of the fruit occurs only through the shell,
עַל כֵּן נֶעְלַם כֹּחַ זֶה גַּם בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְעַל כֵּן הִסְכִּים לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
therefore this unmediated capacity was obscured even within the children of Israel, and Hashem concurred with Jethro's counsel.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְרָא שֶׁהוּא יִתֵּר הַפָּרָשָׁה בַּתּוֹרָה
Nonetheless, it is considered that Jethro appended this section to the Torah;
כִּי אֵין זֶה מִצַּד עֶצֶם הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא מִצַּד עֶצֶם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
for this institutional system does not stem from the essential core of the Torah which mirrors the intrinsic souls of Israel,
רַק מִצַּד הַיִּתּוּר וְהַתּוֹסֶפֶת שֶׁיֵּשׁ עַל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּגֵּרִים
rather from the superfluous addition that attaches to the souls of Israel through converts.
נִתְיַיְתַּר וְנוֹסַף גַּם כֵּן פָּרָשָׁה בַּתּוֹרָה
was an extra, externalized section added to the Torah.

paragraphs.text: Sotah 45b–46b (the declaration and its Gemara interpretation): In the declaration of the eglah arufah, the elders say: “‘our hands did not spill this blood, nor did our eyes see’ (Devarim 21:7)” — the Gemara (Sotah 46b) explains, “he did not come into our hands and we sent him off without food, and we did not see him and leave him without escort.” (The elders are “the eyes of the congregation,” answerable for what they “see.”) Original Gemara (Sotah 46b): “לא בא לידינו ופטרנוהו בלא מזונות, ולא ראינוהו והנחנוהו בלא לויה.” The provision of food and escort is the Gemara’s interpretation, not wording in the verse itself. paragraphs.text: Bamidbar 10:31: Moshe urges Chovav (Yisro) to remain — “אַל נָא תַּעֲזֹב אֹתָנוּ… וְהָיִיתָ לָּנוּ לְעֵינָיִם” — “please do not leave us… and you shall be for us as eyes.” Rashi on Bamidbar 10:31 gives both readings: “you shall be as beloved to us as our own eyes” and “whatever is hidden from our eyes, you shall illuminate for us.” Rashi expressly identifies this material with the Sifrei tradition. R’ Tzadok’s use: “the Sanhedrin are called ‘the eyes of the congregation’” — those who supervise the people; from Yisro’s seed came heads of Sanhedrins seated in the Chamber of Hewn Stone, and it was fitting that he “be for us as eyes,” for the convert’s sight is a light received from without.

paragraphs.text: Shemos 18:18: Yisro’s counsel to Moshe — “נָבֹל תִּבֹּל, גַּם אַתָּה גַּם הָעָם הַזֶּה אֲשֶׁר עִמָּךְ, כִּי כָבֵד מִמְּךָ הַדָּבָר” — “you will surely wear away — both you and this people that is with you — for the matter is too heavy for you.” Meforshim: Rashi — “navol tibol” means you will wither as a leaf wilts in the heat; you cannot bear it alone, so appoint judges beneath you. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the “portion Yisro added” — the appointing of judges (the Sanhedrin). Moshe, of himself, “did not wish to appoint a Sanhedrin”; he would rather “illumine every Jew’s eyes,” that each see his own faults — the light of the Future, when “no longer will each man teach his fellow.” But that inner sight is possible only for Israel; the convert must “receive from Israel,” and so this “increment” entered the Torah through Yisro. Izhbitz parallel - Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Yitro 1; cf. Kedushat Levi, Yitro 22: On 'Moshe listened to the voice of his father-in-law and did all that he said,' the Mei HaShiloach remarks that Yisro himself did not know the full depth of what his own counsel contained; the words were, as it were, spoken through him, while Moshe perceived their true reach. This is an especially fitting complement to R' Tzadok's 'you shall be for us as eyes.' Yisro can introduce the counsel that produces the system of judges, but its Torah-depth is grasped and established through Moshe. Kedushat Levi adds a second dimension: Torah shebe'al peh includes 'all that a seasoned student will one day innovate,' and Hashem entrusted Israel with the extraordinary power that the Torah as interpreted by the righteous sages of the generation becomes the operative halachic word. The two sources together sharpen R' Tzadok's distinction. Yisro's contribution is neither accidental nor merely administrative; it becomes a vessel for the 'eyes of the congregation.' Yet the 'eye' is not an autonomous wisdom imported from outside. The counsel is absorbed into Moshe's Torah, and from there into the Sanhedrin, whose vision is the Torah's own inner perception. This explains how the good spark of a convert can genuinely add to the revealed structure without becoming an independent source alongside Sinai.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Yisro came drawn by Hashem for the sake of a “good spark,” which is the whole purpose of the husk. “You shall be our eyes”: the Sanhedrin are the eyes of the congregation, and Yisro’s descendants sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone. Moshe had not wanted to appoint a Sanhedrin at all — he wished to illumine every Jew’s own eyes — but that inner light is Israel’s alone, so the appointing of judges entered the Torah through a convert.

p: (נד) וְנִרְאֶה לִי כִּי שָׁרְשֵׁי נַפְשׁוֹת הַגֵּרִים בַּתּוֹרָה הוּא בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ דְּיִתְרוֹ,
And it appears to me that the roots of the souls of converts within the Torah are anchored in this Parashat Yitro,
וְהוּא גָּרַם כִּסּוּי עֵינַיִם דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
and he caused the covering of the spiritual eyes of Israel,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיָה רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כֵּן
except that such was the divine will of Hashem, blessed be He,
וּלְרוֹמֵם עַל יְדֵי זֶה נְפָשׁוֹת מְיוּחָדוֹת לִהְיוֹת לְעֵינַיִם לָעֵדָה
in order to elevate through this structure unique souls who serve as eyes unto the congregation.
וְעַל יָדָן זָכָה גַּם הוּא לָזֶה
and through them Jethro likewise merited this role.
וְעַל כֵּן נִכְתַּב מַתַּן תּוֹרָה בַּפָּרָשָׁה הַנִּקְרֵאת עַל שְׁמוֹ,
Therefore the Giving of the Torah was inscribed in the very weekly portion named after him.
וְהַשֵּׁם "יִתְרוֹ" הוּא עַל יִתּוּר פָּרָשָׁה שֶׁהִיא חוּץ לַתּוֹרָה
the name Yitro alluding to the 'surplus' (yittur) section that stands external to the essential core of the Torah.
וַהֲרֵי מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הוּא עִיקַּר הַתּוֹרָה
And yet the Revelation at Sinai is the absolute heart of the Torah;
רַק עִנְיַן סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה הַכְּתוּבָה בִּדְיוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי קְלָף
except that the tangible Torah scroll written in ink upon parchment,
זֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן רַק מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַמַּעֲלִים וּמַסְתִּיר אוֹר הָאֲמִיתִּי
is likewise a concession to this physical world which veils and shrouds the pristine spiritual light,
דִּלְעָתִיד לָבוֹא נֶאֱמַר: "וְעַל לִבָּם אֶכְתְּבֶנָּה" (יִרְמְיָה לא, לב),
for in the ultimate future it is said: "and upon their heart I will write it" (Jeremiah 31:32).
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא יִצְטָרְכוּ לִמְלַמֵּד
and therefore they will not require an external instructor.
וְרַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁנִּתְחַלֵּף "עוֹר" בְּעַד "אוֹר",
And only in this world, where skin
(עוֹר)
was substituted for light (,
אוֹר), כְּמוֹ כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן תְּמוּר כָּתְנוֹת אוֹר שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ קוֹדֶם הַחֵטְא
like the garments of skin given to Adam the First in place of the garments of light he possessed prior to the fall,
כֵּן הַתּוֹרָה דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁמִּסִּטְרָא דְּעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע טָמֵא וְטָהוֹר כָּשֵׁר וּפָסוּל
so the Torah of this world, operating from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil—defining impure and pure, fit and unfit—.
מְלוּבֶּשֶׁת בְּכָתְנוֹת עוֹר וּקְלָף
is enclothed in skins of parchment.
וְכֵן כָּל מִצְווֹתָיו מְלוּבָּשִׁים בְּעִנְיָנִים מַעֲשִׂיִּים דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַגּוּפָנִי
And so too all its commandments are enclothed in physical, practical actions of this bodily world,
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַתּוֹרָה וְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם שֶׁנָּטַע בְּתוֹכֵנוּ.
and this constitutes the accessible Torah and the eternal life implanted within us.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא רַק לְבוּשׁ לַפְּנִימִיּוּת
And even though it is merely a garment for the inner transcendent essence,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהָאָדָם בִּלְבוּשׁ
nevertheless in this world where man himself is enclothed in flesh,
נַעֲשָׂה גַּם זֶה הַלְּבוּשׁ מִצַּד הַתּוֹרָה
this outer garment is likewise consecrated through the Torah.
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַקְּלִיפָּה הַסּוֹבֶבֶת לַפְּרִי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and this reflects the necessary shell that surrounds the fruit in this world.
וְעַל כֵּן נִכְתַּב בְּפָרָשַׁת יִתְרוֹ,
Therefore Sinai was inscribed in the portion of Jethro,
שֶׁמִּצַּד הַזֶּה שֶׁבָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דָּבָר יִתּוּר הַמְּקַיֵּים לַדָּבָר הָעִיקָּר
for through this principle wherein Hashem created in this world a supportive shell that preserves the core fruit,
מִצַּד הַזֶּה נִתְלַבְּשָׁה הַתּוֹרָה גַּם כֵּן בִּלְבוּשִׁים הַלָּלוּ,
from that exact perspective the Torah enclothed itself in these external garments.
וְהַגֵּרִים אֵין מַשִּׂיגִים אֶלָּא הַלְּבוּשִׁים
and proselytes apprehend only these external garments.
וּבַהֲלִיכָה בַּמִּדְבָּר, שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעוּ עֲדַיִן לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁשָּׁם יִזְכּוּ לְבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְהַשָּׂגַת הַפְּנִימִיּוּת
And during the wandering in the desert, having not yet arrived in the Land of Israel where they would merit the Temple and internal illumination,
הָיָה הוּא לָהֶם לְעֵינַיִם מִצַּד הַשָּׂגַת הַלְּבוּשׁ.
Jethro served as eyes unto them from the perspective of external, institutional garments.
וְעַל כֵּן זָכָה לְדֻשְׁנָהּ שֶׁל יְרִיחוֹ (סִפְרֵי בַּהֲעֲלֹתְךָ פא) עַד זְמַן בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
Therefore his lineage merited the fertile pasture of Jericho until the construction of the Temple,
שֶׁאָז הֵאִיר אוֹר דְּגִילּוּי שְׁכִינָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנִתְרַחֲקוּ הַגֵּרִים מִנַּחֲלָתָהּ.
at which point the direct revelation of the Shechinah radiated in the Land of Israel and the Kenites withdrew from the royal tribal inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 3:21; Bereishis Rabbah 20:12: after the sin, “וַיַּעַשׂ ה׳ אֱלֹהִים לְאָדָם וּלְאִשְׁתּוֹ כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר וַיַּלְבִּשֵׁם” — “and Hashem God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin or, with an ayin, and clothed them.” Meforshim: the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 20:12) reports that “in R’ Meir’s Torah scroll it was found written ‘kasnos or’ with an alef — garments of light.” The Midrash itself reports the alternate spelling; Rav Tzadok develops the interpretation of luminous garments before the sin, later exchanged for “garments of skin.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this world is one in which “or (skin) was substituted for or (light)”; correspondingly, the Torah of this world — “from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil” — is “clothed in garments of skin and parchment” (a scroll of ink upon hide), its inner light concealed, until the Future, when “upon the tablet of their heart I will write it.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Eruvin, os ו–ז): on the sugya of R’ Meir (Eruvin 13a–b), R’ Tzadok writes: “This is what they said in Bereishis Rabbah 20, that in R’ Meir’s Torah was written ‘kasnos or’ with an alef — for the ‘garments kasnos’ are the clothing that conceals the body, and ‘or’ with an alef means that even through the garment the light illumines and makes the body shine.” And he explains R’ Meir’s very name: he is called “Meir” Hebrew, “illumines” because “he illumines the eyes of the sages in the revealed halachah,” and “Nehorai” Aramaic for the hidden light of Torah, “which the ministering angels do not grasp” — “his name bespeaks the surpassing measure of his radiance, which is in the concealed and the deep.” (Precisely the se’if’s theme: the Torah of this world is clothed in “garments of skin,” yet the one who is himself “full of light” perceives the inner radiance even through the garment.)

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Pri Tzaddik, Beha’alotcha §10: “בזוה״ק פ׳ זו (קנ״ב א׳) ווי לב״נ דאמר דאורייתא אתא לאתחזאה ספורין בעלמא ומלין דהדיוטא ... כה״ג אורייתא אית לה גופא ומלי אורייתא דאקרון גופי תורה ... מתלבשי בלבושין דאינון ספורין דהאי עלמא ... אבל הענין הוא שיש גופי תורה והיינו ההלכות איך להתנהג וזהו גופא. ועל זה אמר האי גופא מתלבשי בלבושין דאינון ספורין וכו׳ שאף בהספורים יש גופי תורה לימודים הליכות עולם.” — “In the holy Zohar on this portion (152a): ‘Woe to the person who says that the Torah comes to show mere stories and ordinary words. ... In this manner the Torah has a body, and the words of Torah that are called the bodies of Torah ... are clothed in garments, which are the stories of this world.’ ... But the explanation is that there are bodies of Torah—namely, the laws of how to conduct oneself—and this is the body. Of this it says that this body is clothed in garments, which are stories, and so forth, for even in the stories there are bodies of Torah: teachings for the conduct of life.” This illuminates the present qualification that the necessary garment itself belongs to Torah in this world.

R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §53): “R’ Meir was able to distinguish and separate the inner kernel from the husk, for he was ‘full of light’ me’ir, as his name implies — which is why in his Torah scroll it was written ‘garments of light’ kasnos ohr with an aleph (Bereishis Rabbah, end of §20): that even the ‘garment of skin’ kasnos or was full of light. And this is like the light of a torch, which draws to itself every small light that comes near it — so R’ Meir could draw toward himself the inner light that was within Acher. Therefore one should contemplate teshuvah before study, for then he is called a tzaddik (Kiddushin 49b) and merits the ‘light sown for the righteous’ — that what he learns be sown within his heart, to sprout abundant light within him.” Further Chassidic context - Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Yitro 5; Tanya, Iggeret HaKodesh 29:22-24: The Ishbitzer explicitly asks why Yisro's arrival is written before Matan Torah even according to the opinion that he actually came afterward. He answers that the Torah wished to demonstrate, before describing Revelation itself, how far the power of Torah can reach: even Yisro, who had been exceedingly distant and had served every form of idolatry, could through genuine longing draw so near that the parashah of Matan Torah bears his name. He reads the name Yisro as a hint to 'chemlah gedolah vi-yeseirah' - an additional compassion by which the Divine light spreads even to the distant. This directly supports R' Tzadok's play on Yisro as 'surplus': the surplus is not extraneous matter alongside Torah, but Torah's capacity to clothe and extend its light to a place that previously stood outside. Tanya supplies the complementary side of the garment metaphor. The Alter Rebbe explains that the supernal Will clothed in the Written Torah is often sealed and hidden until Torah shebe'al peh reveals its concrete form - tefillin, Shabbos labor, and the detailed halachic structure. Thus a garment is not merely a concealment of the light; it is also what makes the hidden will usable and knowable below. R' Tzadok's formulation that gerim attain the 'garments' can therefore be read as a real mode of attachment, while still preserving his distinction between the garment and the innermost root. 
Original Hebrew, Mei HaShiloach II, Yitro §5: לְהַרְאוֹת עַד הֵיכָן כֹּחַ הַתּוֹרָה לְהַחְזִיר לְטוֹב — To demonstrate how far the Torah’s power extends to bring a person back to goodness. 
In the same passage, on the meaning of the name Yisro: וְשֵׁם יִתְרוֹ רוֹמֵז עַל חֶמְלָה יְתֵרָה, שֶׁנִּתְפַּשֵּׁט הָאוֹר לְהָאִיר גַּם לְהָרְחוֹקִים — And the name Yisro alludes to an additional compassion: the light spreads to illuminate even those who are distant.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The root of the converts’ souls in the Torah is Parashas Yisro, who “covered Israel’s eyes” — yet by Hashem’s will, in order to raise distinguished souls as eyes for the congregation. Matan Torah itself was written in a portion bearing his name, Yisro being an expression of “surplus.” For in this world Torah is clothed in garments — ink upon parchment, the mitzvos in physical acts — and converts attain only the garments.

p: (נה) וּמִצַּד הַלְּבוּשִׁים דְּתוֹרָה הֵם כָּל דִּינֵי דִּינִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ,
And from these external garments of the Torah emerge all its rigorous legal strictures.
וְזֶה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי גִּידּוּל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּמִדְיָן
and this was channeled through the development of Moses our teacher in Midian.
וְעַל כֵּן נִתְלָה מִיתָתוֹ בְּנִקְמַת הַמִּדְיָנִים
Therefore his passing was made contingent upon the avenging of the Midianites,
כִּי הֵם גָּרְמוּ כִּסּוּי וְהֶעְלֵם אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
for they caused the concealment and veiling of the light of the Torah in this world,
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
and this was from their holy root in judgment;
אֲבָל מִצַּד הָרַע שֶׁבָּהֶם רָצוּ לְהַעֲלִים לְגַמְרֵי שֶׁיִּתְעָרְבוּ בַּגּוֹיִם
yet from the evil within them, they sought to obliterate the boundary entirely so Israel would assimilate among the nations.
וּפִינְחָס שֶׁבָּא מִיִּתְרוֹ עִכֵּב בְּדָבָר זֶה
And Phinehas, who descended maternally from Jethro, stayed this plague,
וּמִינֵיהּ וּבֵיהּ אַבָּא נֵיזִיל נַרְגָּא ,
fulfilling "from the forest itself comes the axe-handle to fell it" (Sanhedrin 39b),
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַהַעֲלָמָה נִשְׁאַר
yet the root of the cosmic concealment nonetheless endured,
וְזֶה גָּרַם מִיתַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא הֶעְלֵם הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹרוֹ.
and this brought about the death of Moses, which is the setting of his radiant illumination.
וְהֻוצְרַךְ לִצְרוֹר לַמִּדְיָנִים מִקּוֹדֶם
And he was commanded to harass the Midianites beforehand.
שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹאוּ אַחַר זְמַן לְהַעֲלִים לְגַמְרֵי מִצַּד הָרַע שֶׁבָּהֶם
so that they would not return later to extinguish the light completely through the evil within them.
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּהַלְּבוּשׁ הוּא סִטְרָא דְּנוּקְבָּא הַמְסוֹבֶבֶת גֶּבֶר וּמַלְבִּישַׁתּוּ,
For as is known, the garment belongs to the feminine dimension that encompasses man and enclothes him,
וְעַל כֵּן דִּינָה נִתְגַּלְגְּלָה בְּכָזְבִּי בַּת נְשִׂיא מִדְיָן
and therefore Dinah was reincarnated within Cozbi daughter of the prince of Midian
שֶׁכִּזְּבָה בְּאָבִיהָ,
who deceived her father;
שֶׁהָיָה נָשִׂיא וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחַ הָרַע שֶׁבְּמִדְיָן
for Zur was prince and root of the evil contention of Midian.
וְרָצָה לְהַכְשִׁיל יִשְׂרָאֵל וּלְהַמְשִׁיכָם לְמָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת וְלִהְיוֹת כְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם
seeking to make Israel stumble and drag them into a place to which they hold no affinity, rendering them like all the nations.
אֲבָל הִיא לֹא שָׁמְעָה לוֹ וְדָבְקָה רַק בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ שַׁיָּיכוּת (לְשֵׁבֶט שִׁמְעוֹן),
Yet Cozbi did not obey him, cleaving only unto the place where she held an affinity—the tribe of Simeon.
וְהִיא הָיְתָה מִתְרַצֵּית לְהִתְגַּיֵּיר גַּם כֵּן אִלּוּ רָצָה זִמְרִי
and she would have consented to convert as well had Zimri so desired.
וְזֶהוּ טַעַם טַעֲנָתוֹ: "בַּת יִתְרוֹ מִי הִתִּיר לָךְ?" ,
And this is the inner root of Zimri's challenge to Moses: "Who permitted you the daughter of Jethro?" (Sanhedrin 82a).
כִּי גַּם הִיא דּוּגְמָתָהּ חָפְצָה לִדְבַּק בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, לֹא לְהַמְשִׁיךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָהֶם
for Cozbi, like Zipporah, desired to cleave to Israel, not to drag Israel down to the gentiles.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא תְּפָשָׂהּ כִּכְלוֹרִיתָהּ שֶׁהוּא דַּרְכֵי הָאֱמוֹרִי
Only that Zimri seized her illicitly while undisciplined in pagan ways,
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הִיא עֲדַיִן בְּגַיּוּתָהּ.
and while she was still in her uncircumcised gentile state.
כִּי הוּא (זִמְרִי) גִּלְגּוּל שְׁכֶם
For Zimri was the reincarnation of Shechem,
וְהִרְגִּישׁ בְּדָבָר זֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ נַפְשׁוֹת גּוֹיִם מִתְגַּלְגְּלוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְדְיִשְׂרָאֵל בַּגּוֹיִם
and he intuitively sensed that souls of gentiles reincarnate in Israel and souls of Israel among gentiles,
וְדִמָּה מִזֶּה דְּאֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת גַּם כֵּן קְלִיטָה לְנִיצוֹצִין קַדִּישִׁין גַּם בְּעוֹדָן בְּגַיּוּתָן
and he falsely deduced that holy sparks could be absorbed even while they remained in their gentile status.
וּבִפְרָט בְּמִדְיָן שֶׁסָּמוּךְ לַעֲמָלֵק
especially in Midian which borders Amalek.
וּבַעֲמָלֵק בֵּיאַרְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר
And regarding Amalek I have explained elsewhere,
דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִקְלוֹט הַנִּיצוֹצִין קַדִּישִׁין שֶׁבּוֹ אֶלָּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה
that it is impossible to extract the holy sparks within him except through this unusual route,
דְּבוֹ כְּתִיב "תִּמְחֶה" (דְּבָרִים כה, יט)
for concerning him Scripture wrote "you shall blot out",
וְאָמְרוּ בַּמְּכִילְתָּא (פָּרָשַׁת בְּשַׁלַּח) דְּאֵין מְקַבְּלִין גֵּרִים מֵעֲמָלֵק
and they stated in the Mekhilta that converts are never accepted from Amalek,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מִבְּנֵי בָּנָיו שֶׁל הָמָן לִמְּדוּ תִּינוֹקוֹת בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
and nevertheless some of Haman’s descendants taught children in Jerusalem,
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דְּהָיָה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁבָּא גּוֹי אֶחָד מִבְּנֵי בָּנָיו עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
and perforce this occurred through a gentile descendant cohabiting with a Jewish woman,
דְּהַוָּלָד כָּשֵׁר וְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא
whereby the offspring is legitimate and fully Jewish (Kiddushin 68b),
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם קָרוּי גַּם כֵּן בֶּן הַגּוֹי
yet is nonetheless also termed the son of the gentile,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּתּוֹרָה: "וְהוּא בֶּן אִישׁ מִצְרִי" (וַיִּקְרָא כד, י).
as stated in the Torah: "and he was the son of an Egyptian man" (Leviticus 24:10).
וְחָשַׁב דְּגַם בְּמִדְיָן חֲבֵירוֹ, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן הַתְחָלַת הַגּוֹיִם, הַקְּלִיטָה עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה דַּוְוקָא
And Zimri presumed that with Midian his fellow, who is likewise the inception of the nations, the reclamation was specifically through this route.
וְטָעָה בָּזֶה, דְּגַם שָׁם חָלִילָה לִהְיוֹת בְּרָצוֹן
And he erred disastrously in this, for even there it is forbidden to occur through consent;
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִקְלוֹט הַנִּיצוֹצִין קַדִּישִׁין מֵעֲמָלֵק אֶלָּא בְּאֹנֶס וְשֶׁלֹּא בְּמִתְכַּוֵּין
and holy sparks are reclaimed from Amalek solely through coercion or without intent,
וּכְעִנְיַן "לְבַסּוֹמֵי בְּפוּרַיָּא עַד דְּלָא יָדַע" .
akin to the intoxication on Purim "until he knows not" (Megillah 7b).
וְזֶהוּ רַק בְּאִשָּׁה דְּקַרְקַע עוֹלָם הִיא
And this applies only to the woman who is passive "earth of the world" (Sanhedrin 74b),
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אֹנֶס
and what I wrote above regarding coercion,
וְגַם זֶה רַק בְּגוֹי עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּהַוָּלָד כָּשֵׁר
and this holds true only when a gentile lies with a Jewish woman where the child is Jewish;
אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל הַגּוֹיָה הֲרֵי וַלְדָהּ כְּמוֹתָהּ.
whereas when a Jewish man lies with a gentile woman, her offspring shares her gentile status.
וְשָׁרְשׁוֹ שֶׁהָיָה נֶפֶשׁ הַגּוֹי גָּרַם לוֹ טָעוּת זֶה
And Zimri's past soul-root in Shechem caused him this tragic error;
וּלְפִי שֶׁלֹּא אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ חַתְנוּת
and because the Written Torah explicitly prohibited intercourse only via marital alliance,
אַף דְּיָדַע דְּהוּא אִיסּוּר חָמוּר גַּם שֶׁלֹּא דֶּרֶךְ חַתְנוּת
even though he knew it was a severe prohibition even without marriage.
חָשַׁב דִּלְכָךְ לֹא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ הָאִיסּוּר לְפִי שֶׁפְּעָמִים יֵשׁ שֶׁאֵינוֹ אִיסּוּר
he rationalized that the prohibition was not stated explicitly because at times it might not be forbidden.
וּבֶאֱמֶת מַה שֶּׁלֹּא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ הוּא לְפִי שֶׁזֶּה דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת כְּלָל לְזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל
Yet in truth, the reason it was not explicitly spelled out is that this act is so fundamentally alien to the seed of Israel.
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "אָנֹכִי וְגוֹמֵר" שֶׁלֹּא אָמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן צִיוּוּי
just as "I am Hashem" was not formulated as an imperative command.
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם כְּתָבוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה לְפִי שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְחִסָּרוֹן זֶה גַּם כֵּן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּשֵׁבֶט דָּן
Except that it was nonetheless recorded in the Torah because a subtle root of this deficiency existed in Dan,
אַף דְּהוּא רַק מִצַּד עֹבִי הַחוֹמְרִיּוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל
even though it was merely from the density of bodily matter as I wrote above.
סוֹף סוֹף הוּא חִסָּרוֹן לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן וְהֻוצְרַךְ לְהִכָּתֵב
yet ultimately it appeared as a deficiency to external sight and had to be recorded.

paragraphs.text: Vayikra 24:10: of the blasphemer — “וַיֵּצֵא בֶּן אִשָּׁה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית, וְהוּא בֶּן אִישׁ מִצְרִי, בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל” — “and the son of an Israelite woman went out — and he was the son of an Egyptian man — among the Children of Israel.” Meforshim: Rashi (from the Midrash) — he was the son of the Egyptian taskmaster whom Moshe had slain, born to Shelomis bas Divri of the tribe of Dan; the child of a gentile father and a Jewish mother is a kosher Jew, yet Scripture still calls him “son of an Egyptian man.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the one narrow channel by which a holy spark is reclaimed from the nations — “a gentile upon a bas Yisrael,” where “the child is kosher and is a Jew,” yet is “also called the son of the gentile”; whereas “a Jew upon a gentile woman — her child is like her.”
