paragraphs.text:
Sanhedrin 82a–b: Rav Sheishess said: her name was not Kozbi but Shveilnai bas Tzur; why was she called Kozbi? — because she “acted falsely toward her father” — “שֶׁכִּזְּבָה בְּאָבִיהָ”. The tribe of Shimon came to Zimri ben Salu, “we are judged with death-penalties and you sit silent?” He gathered 24,000 and went to Kozbi, saying, “yield to me.” She replied, “I am a king’s daughter; my father commanded me to yield only to the greatest among them.” He said, “I too am a tribal prince, and greater than Moshe.” He seized her forelock and brought her before Moshe: “Ben Amram — is this one forbidden or permitted? and if you say forbidden — who permitted Yisro’s daughter to you?” The halachah “was hidden from him,” and all wept — “and behold they were weeping at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.” “And Pinchas saw” — Rav said: “he saw the deed and remembered the halachah,” and said, “great-uncle, did you not teach me on your descent from Sinai that ‘one who cohabits with a gentile woman — zealots may strike him’?” Moshe answered, “let the reader of the letter be its agent.” And Pinchas was a grandson of Yisro, for Elazar had married a daughter of “Putiel” — Yisro. Izhbitz parallel - Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Matot 6: The Ishbitzer returns to the episode of Midyan and makes the safeguard in R' Tzadok's discussion explicit. When Moshe rebuked Pinchas and the army for keeping the Midianite women alive, the Mei HaShiloach says that Moshe showed Pinchas that he too had momentarily touched the same error as Zimri: perceiving that a soul contains a holy point and therefore concluding that it may already be brought into holiness through one's own present action. Zimri's claim, 'who permitted Yisro's daughter to you?,' was based on his conviction that Kozbi possessed a real root of holiness, just as Moshe had known that Tzipporah belonged to him. The Ishbitzer does not deny the hidden root; he says that in this world 'the Holy One did not choose this matter,' and that Moshe, in the later war, saw that the apparently salvageable Midianite women were forbidden at that moment despite an underlying connection. This is precisely the distinction needed for R' Tzadok's language of the Torah's dinim as garments. The garment of halachah is not a lower truth that may be discarded once a person senses a deeper spark. It is the authoritative disclosure of how the Divine will is to be lived now. Pinchas' greatness was that he remembered the halachah at Shittim; Moshe's rebuke later taught him that even holy perception must remain subordinate to that present halachic boundary. 
Izhbitz parallel — Mei HaShiloach I, Matos §6: בכאן הראה משה רבינו עליו השלום לפינחס שטעה באותו טעות של זמרי — Here Moshe demonstrated to Pinchas that he had fallen into the same error as Zimri. The passage explains the mistake as supposing that a holy point made the present action permitted.

Devarim 25:19: the command against Amalek — “תִּמְחֶה אֶת זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק מִתַּחַת הַשָּׁמָיִם, לֹא תִּשְׁכָּח” — “you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens; do not forget.” Meforshim: because Amalek is “the root of all evil,” his very “memory” must be erased; and the Mechilta teaches that “we do not accept converts from Amalek.” R’ Tzadok’s use: since Amalek’s evil is total, “it is impossible to absorb the holy sparks within him except by compulsion and unintentionally,” never willingly — and only through a woman (“the ground of the world”), where a gentile comes upon a bas Yisrael and the child is kosher, as indeed “of the descendants of Haman, some taught Torah in Bnei Brak” (Gittin 57b).
Scholarly qualification:  — Rav Tzadok cites a midrashic exclusion concerning Amalek; this footnote preserves that attribution without presenting it as an independent universally settled practical ruling about the status of all converts. The connection to extracting holy sparks is Rav Tzadok’s interpretation.

paragraphs.text:
Megillah 7b: Rava’s dictum — “חַיָּיב אִינִישׁ לְבַסּוּמֵי בְּפוּרַיָּא עַד דְּלָא יָדַע בֵּין אָרוּר הָמָן לְבָרוּךְ מָרְדֳּכַי” — “a person is obligated to become intoxicated on Purim until he does not know the difference between ‘cursed is Haman’ and ‘blessed is Mordechai’.” Meforshim: the commentators explain that on Purim one reaches a rung “beyond knowing,” where even Haman’s Amalek’s evil is subsumed within the praise of God. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the sole mode in which the holy sparks may be drawn out of Amalek — “by compulsion and unintentionally,” in a state of “not knowing,” beyond the deliberate mind; Zimri’s error was to imagine that one might reclaim Midyan’s sparks willingly, in full consciousness, which is impossible. 
Scholarly qualification:  — The “beyond knowing” application to Amalek’s sparks is Rav Tzadok’s interpretation of the Purim dictum, not a literal statement of the Bavli.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: From the “garments of Torah” come all its dinim, which reached Israel through Moshe’s development in Midyan — and so his death was bound up with avenging Midyan, who had concealed the Torah’s light. Pinchas, of Yisro’s line, was the one who checked it: “from the forest itself comes the axe-handle.” The garment is the Nukva that clothes the man, which is why Dinah was reincarnated in Kozbi — and where Zimri erred in his inference.

p: (נו) וְכָל תַּרְיַ"ג (שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת וְשָׁלוֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה) מִצְווֹת הַתּוֹרָה הֵם תַּרְיַ"ג עֵיטִין לְזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶגֶד כָּל הַחֶסְרוֹנוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם בְּשָׁרְשָׁם
And all the 613 commandments of the Torah are 613 counsels for the seed of Israel against all deficiencies existing in their roots.
וְכָל שֵׁבֶט יֵשׁ לוֹ חִסָּרוֹן מְיוּחָד
And each tribe has a specific deficiency.
דְּעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר י"א (אַחַד עָשָׂר) אֲרוּרִים נֶגֶד י"א שְׁבָטִים
concerning which eleven curses were uttered in Deuteronomy 27 corresponding to eleven tribes.
וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּהוּא נֶגֶד הַחֶסְרוֹנוֹת שֶׁבְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל שֵׁבֶט
And I heard that these correspond to the root-deficiencies of each tribe,
כִּי "אָרוּר" לְשׁוֹן חִסָּרוֹן
for arur (cursed) denotes lack and diminishments,
וְנֶגֶד שִׁמְעוֹן לֹא כָתוּב אָרוּר לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה לְבָרְכוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַשִּׁ"י פָּרָשַׁת תָּבוֹא (דְּבָרִים כז, כד).
and facing Simeon no curse was formulated, because Moses did not intend to bless him, as Rashi writes on Parashat Ki Tavo (Deuteronomy 27:24).
וְאֵין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בָּאִים בְּמִקְרֶה
And words of Torah never occur by chance,
וְנִרְאֶה מִזֶּה כִּי הוּא דָבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְלַבֵּשׁ בִּכְתָב וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְכָתְבוֹ.
and it appears from this that Simeon's deficiency is something that cannot be enclothed in writing and cannot be recorded.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת חִסָּרוֹן כָּזֶה הַנִּמְצָא בָהֶם בְּמַעֲשֵׂה דִשְׁטִים
For in truth, such a terrible flaw as appeared among them in the incident of Shittim.
אִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלָל לְהַאֲמִין שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב
is utterly impossible to believe could truly reside in the seed of Jacob.
כִּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר בֶּאֱמֶת רַק כְּפִי הַדִּמְיוֹן שֶׁמְּדַמֶּה זֶה לֶאֱלֹהוּת
For idolatry is not an actual biological union, but an erroneous mental projection imagining it as divinity.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא עֵץ וָאֶבֶן בְּעָלְמָא וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּשְׁלוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ עַל הָעֵגֶל לִמְגַפֶּפֶת לְסָרִיס
whereas in truth it is mere wood and stone, like the Midrashic parable comparing the Golden Calf to a woman embracing a eunuch;
אֲבָל הַבָּא עַל בַּת אֵל נֵכָר דְּ"יִהְיוּ לְבָשָׂר אֶחָד" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, כד),
whereas one who cohabits with the daughter of an alien god so that "they become one flesh" (Genesis 2:24),
שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְהוֹלִיד בְּדוֹמֶה לִשְׁנֵיהֶם גּוּף שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם שֻׁתָּפִים בּוֹ,
being able to father a combined body in which both partake.
זֶה חִבּוּר וְדִיבּוּק גָּמוּר
this constitutes a total and absolute physical attachment.
וְכֵן תּוֹרָה כָּתְבָה בּוֹ לְשׁוֹן "וְדָבַק בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ",
And so the Torah used concerning marriage the terminology: "and he shall cleave unto his wife", ".
לְמַטֵּה אֲבוֹתָיו יִדְבָּקוּ" (בַּמִּדְבָּר לו, ז) וְכַדּוֹמֶה
and "shall cleave every one to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers" (Numbers 36:7), and the like.
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל הַדְּבֵקִים בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים אֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לִדְבַּק בְּמַה שֶּׁכְּנֶגֶד זֶה
And how could Israel, who cleave unto the living God, ever cleave unto the polar opposite of holiness?!
וְהַכְּתָב הוּא דָּבָר הַגָּלוּי לַכֹּל
And the Written Torah is that which is openly revealed to all.
וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַחִסָּרוֹן כְּפִי הַנִּגְלֶה מֵהַמַּעֲשֶׂה הוּא דָּבָר שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר
and that the internal deficiency should truly match the horrific outward deed is completely impossible.
אֲבָל יֵשׁ דְּבָרִים בְּגוֹ וְאֵין הַחִסָּרוֹן כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא בַּהִתְגַּלּוּת
Rather, deep esoteric mysteries reside within and the deficiency is not as it appears overtly;
כִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחַ קְדֻשַּׁת שֵׁבֶט שִׁמְעוֹן נֶעְלָם מְאֹד בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
for the root of the holy power of the tribe of Simeon is profoundly concealed in this world.
כִּי הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ עָלְמָא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא הַנֶּעְלָם
for it is the very root of the Primordial Concealed World.
כִּי שֵׁשֶׁת בְּנֵי לֵאָה וּבַת אַחַת הֵם נֶגֶד שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת
For the six sons of Leah and one daughter correspond to the seven lower sefirotic attributes,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכָל דָּבָר שֵׁשׁ קְצוֹת דִּדְכוּרָא וְנוּקְבָּא כַּיָּדוּעַ.
there being within each structure six masculine spatial directions and one feminine aspect, as is known.
וְשִׁמְעוֹן נֶגֶד מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁהוּא מִדָּה הַמְצַמְצֶמֶת וּמַעֲלֶמֶת הַדָּבָר
And Simeon corresponds to Gevurah, the attribute that contracts and veils.
וְעַל כֵּן נוֹסַף בּוֹ הֶעְלֵם עַל הֶעְלֵם
and therefore in him concealment was layered upon concealment.
וְכֵן כֹּחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה אֵין לוֹ תְּפִיסָה בְּדָבָר גַּשְׁמִי וּמַמָּשִׁי כָּרְאִיָּה
Similarly, the faculty of hearing has no grasp upon physical tangible matter like vision.
כִּי הַדִּבּוּר וְהַקּוֹל רוּחָנִי וְאֵינוֹ נִרְגָּשׁ וּמוּחָשׁ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל
for speech and sonic voice are spiritual and imperceptible as physical solid substance in this world.
וְעַל כֵּן חוּשׁ הַשְּׁמִיעָה רוּחָנִי יוֹתֵר מִכָּל הַחוּשִׁים
Therefore the sense of hearing is more spiritual than all other senses.
שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ תְּפִיסָה רַק בְּדָבָר רוּחָנִי וְלֹא בְּגַשְׁמִי כְּלָל
grasping solely that which is spiritual and nothing of material bulk.
וּבִשְׁמִיעָה יוּכַל הָאָדָם לָדַעַת מַטְמוֹנָיו וּסְתָרָיו שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ מַה שֶּׁבְּלִבּוֹ נֶעְלָם וְטָמִיר שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע לוֹ בְּדִבּוּרוֹ,
And through hearing a person can perceive the hidden secrets of his fellow concealed within the heart as conveyed through speech.
מַה שֶּׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר בִּרְאִיָּה וּשְׁאָר חוּשִׁים לְהַשִּׂיג אֶלָּא הַנִּגְלֶה לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which is impossible through vision and the other senses that register only external appearances in this world.
וְלֵידָתוֹ הָיָה עַל יְדֵי "כִּי שָׁמַע ה' וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, לג),
And Simeon's birth was accompanied by: "Because Hashem has heard, etc." (Genesis 29:33).
דְּגַם לְמַעְלָה יֵשׁ כֵּן
for in the supernal realm this distinction likewise exists.
אַף דַּ"ה' יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב"  — וְהוּא רוֹאֶה גַּם הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת
Even though "Hashem looks into the heart" (I Samuel 16:7) and beholds all hidden secrets.
מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ חִלּוּק בֵּין רְאִיָּה לִשְׁמִיעָה
nonetheless a profound qualitative distinction exists between seeing and hearing.
כִּי הָרְאִיָּה הוּא כְּפִי תְּפִיסַת עֵין הָרוֹאֶה בַּדָּבָר הַנִּרְאֶה
For vision corresponds to the objective perspective of the observer beholding the object,
וְהַשְּׁמִיעָה הוּא רַק מַה שֶּׁהַלָּה מַשְׁמִיעַ לוֹ,
whereas hearing is receptive, taking in what the speaker transmits,
וְהַמַּשְׁמִיעַ מַשְׁמִיעַ כְּפִי תְּפִיסָתוֹ וְהַשָּׂגָתוֹ.
and the speaker expresses from the subjective vantage of his own perception.
וְעַל כֵּן בִּרְאִיָּה נֶאֱמַר "כִּי רָאָה ה' בְּעָנְיִי כִּי עַתָּה יֶאֱהָבַנִי" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, לב) וְלֹא נִזְכַּר לְשׁוֹן שִׂנְאָה
Therefore in vision Leah said: "Because Hashem has seen my affliction, for now my husband will love me", omitting the word hatred,
דְּמִצַּד רְאִיַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא הָיָה נִקְרָא שִׂנְאָה
for from Hashem's objective sight it was never called hatred.
רַק חִסָּרוֹן אַהֲבָה וְעוֹנִי
merely a diminution of overt love and poverty.

Rashi, Devarim 27:24 (citing R’ Moshe HaDarshan): “there are here eleven verses beginning with ‘arur cursed’ — corresponding to the eleven tribes; but for Shimon he did not write ‘arur,’ because Moshe did not wish to bless him before his death, when he blessed the other tribes — and so he did not wish to curse him either.” Background: the arurim of Ki Savo (Devarim 27:15–26) number eleven, Shimon alone unmentioned. Meforshim: Rashi elsewhere (Devarim 33:7) gives the reason Moshe withheld Shimon’s blessing — “he held the deed of Shittim against him.” R’ Tzadok’s use: each “arur” marks the root-deficiency of a tribe (as he “heard”); Shimon’s is left unwritten because his deficiency — the deed of Shittim (Zimri) — “is a matter that cannot be clothed in writing,” too concealed to appear on the revealed page. 
Scholarly qualification:  — The 11 tribal curses are distinct from the concluding general curse “ארור אשר לא יקים את דברי התורה הזאת” (Devarim 27:26): there are 12 occurrences of “arur” in verses 15–26, but Rashi counts the 11 preceding specific curses. Pri Tzaddik, Ki Savo §14 explicitly says “י״א ארורים לבד אשר לא יקום”.

Bereishis 2:24; Bamidbar 36:7: the Torah reserves the language of “cleaving deveikus” for a true, bonded union — “וְדָבַק בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ, וְהָיוּ לְבָשָׂר אֶחָד,” “and he shall cleave to his wife, and they shall become one flesh” (2:24); and “אִישׁ בְּנַחֲלַת מַטֵּה אֲבֹתָיו יִדְבְּקוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,” “each shall cleave to the inheritance of his fathers’ tribe” (36:7). R’ Tzadok’s use: union with “the daughter of a foreign god” is a “complete cleaving,” for the two “become one flesh,” a body in which both are partners — unlike idolatry, which “the Midrash likens to one who embraces a eunuch,” a barren act that begets nothing. Hence the deficiency of Shittim, were it truly as it appears, would be an unthinkable “cleaving” of Israel — who cleave to the living God — to its very opposite. Izhbitz clarification - Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Balak 9: On Zimri's challenge to Moshe, the Ishbitzer gives one of the clearest formulations of the prospective/retrospective distinction that is essential when reading this entire passage. Zimri argued that just as Moshe knew Tzipporah had a portion in the World to Come, he too saw that Kozbi had a future holy root. The Mei HaShiloach answers with 'do not boast of tomorrow, for you do not know what a day will bring': even if one perceives that in the future a matter will be clarified for good, one still does not know 'how Hashem conducts the present.' Moshe's union with Tzipporah was permitted because Hashem illuminated for him how to act in the present; Zimri had no such authorization. Only afterward can Heaven disclose that a hidden soul-root was genuinely connected. This exactly complements R' Tzadok's assertion that Shittim cannot represent the true root of Shimon. The hidden holiness explains why the fall is not the tribe's essence; it does not retroactively give a person license to enact the fall. Before and during action the Torah's revealed command and the obligation of bechirah govern absolutely. Only after the fact, and only through Divine clarification and teshuvah, may a deeper providential root be uncovered. The source therefore protects R' Tzadok's very daring language from an antinomian reading while preserving the Izhbitz claim that the outward appearance is not always the final truth.

paragraphs.text: I Shmuel 16:7: as Shmuel comes to anoint David, God warns him not to judge by appearance — “כִּי הָאָדָם יִרְאֶה לַעֵינַיִם, וַה׳ יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב,” “for a person looks at outward appearances, but Hashem looks at the heart.” Meforshim: Rashi — a person perceives only what is outwardly visible, whereas God discerns the inner intent. R’ Tzadok’s use: even though “Hashem sees the heart” and perceives the hidden, “there is still a distinction between seeing and hearing” — sight grasps the visible surface, but hearing reaches “what the heart conceals”; hence at Reuven’s birth, from the side of seeing, only “affliction” and “a lack of love” were named — not “hatred,” which belongs to the deeper realm of hearing (Shimon).

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The 613 mitzvos are 613 “counsels” against each tribe’s root-deficiency — the eleven arurim against eleven tribes, with Shimon alone left neither cursed nor blessed. But a deficiency such as Shittim is unbelievable in Yaakov’s seed: idolatry is no real joining, whereas union with a foreign woman is a real cleaving. So it cannot be as it appears — Shimon’s holy root is deeply concealed, which is why hearing, the sense that grasps the hidden, is his.

כִּי כָּךְ רָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֹּחוֹת נִפְרָדִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
for so Hashem willed that there exist differentiated forces in this world,
הַמַּרְאִים עַצְמָם כְּפִי דִּמְיוֹן עוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְנִפְרָד לְגַמְרֵי
which portray themselves according to worldly illusion as totally autonomous.
שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ כְּלוּם וְעוֹשֶׂה לְעַצְמוֹ מַה שֶּׁחָפֵץ
needing nothing and accomplishing independently whatever they wish.
אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹי אֶחָד מְיוּחָד בָּזֶה שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם כֹּחַ מֵעַצְמָם כְּלָל
However, Israel is one unique nation in that they possess no independent power whatsoever from themselves.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הֵם בְּתַכְלִית הָעֲנִיּוּת וְהַדַּלּוּת בְּכָל עִנְיָנִים הַנַּפְשִׁיִּים אַלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרָם
and through this they exist in total spiritual poverty and dependency unless the Holy One aids them.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּסֻכָּה נ״ב סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳) שֶׁמַּנִּיחַ יֵצֶר הָרָע אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וּמִתְגָּרֶה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
And as they taught (Sukkah 52a) that the evil inclination leaves the nations aside and incites specifically against Israel,
וְהַיְינוּ דְּהַחִסָּרוֹן דְּ"יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו"  — הוּא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹתֵר
meaning that the vulnerability of "the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth" (Genesis 8:21) is acutely felt in Israel,
שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם כֹּחַ עַצְמָן לְנַצְּחוֹ.
who possess no autonomous mortal power to conquer it.
אֲבָל נֶגֶד זֶה אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם עֵזֶר אֱלֹהִי
Yet opposite this, the pagan nations possess no divine assistance,
וְכֹחָם הוּא הַמּוֹרִידָם לִשְׁאוֹל תַּחְתִּית
and their self-reliant strength is what casts them down to the lowest depths;
מֵאַחַר שֶׁסְּבוּרִים שֶׁזֶּהוּ כֹּחָם וְעֹצֶם יָדָם וְנִפְרָדִים מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
since they imagine that their own strength and might achieved this, separating from Hashem,
מִמֵּילָא הֵם בְּתַכְלִית הָרִיחוּק מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
consequently they abide in ultimate estrangement from Him.
אֲבָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּלֵית לְהוֹ מִגַּרְמַיְיהוּ, עֵינֵיהֶם צוֹפוֹת לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
However, the children of Israel who have nothing of their own, their eyes gaze unceasingly unto Hashem, blessed be He.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "אֶל זֶה אַבִּיט אֶל עָנִי (וּנְכֵה רוּחַ וְגוֹמֵר)" (יְשַׁעְיָה סו, ב),
And concerning this it is stated: "Unto this one will I look, unto him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, etc." (Isaiah 66:2),
דְּאֵין הַבָּטַת עֵינֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֶלָּא עֲלֵיהֶם מִפְּנֵי עָנְיָם
for the divine gaze looks upon none other than Israel on account of their conscious poverty,
וְנֶאֱמַר: "דַּלּוֹתִי וְלִי יְהוֹשִׁיעַ" (תְּהִלִּים קטז, ו),
and it is said: "I was brought low, and He saved me" (Psalms 116:6),
דְּמִפְּנֵי כֵן לִי יְהוֹשִׁיעַ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֲנִי דַּלָּה וַעֲנִיָּה
meaning: precisely because I am impoverished and needy, He delivers me.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הָאֻמּוֹת
which is not the case with the self-sufficient nations.
וּבִפְסָחִים (קיח:): "אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדַּלָּה אֲנִי מִן הַמִּצְווֹת לְךָ אֲנִי וְלִי נָאֶה לְהוֹשִׁיעַ",
And in Pesachim (118b): "Even though I am impoverished of mitzvot, I am Yours and it is fitting for You to deliver me",
דְּזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן תֹּקֶף מַעֲלָתָם
for this represents the apex of their spiritual distinction:
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַדַּלּוּת הוּא חִסָּרוֹן
that even though poverty is a deficiency,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא תֹּקֶף הַמַּעֲלָה וְתַכְלִית רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא עוֹלָם הַמָּלֵא חֶסְרוֹנוֹת
nonetheless it is the ultimate virtue and the divine purpose in this world of deficiencies,
וְרָצָה שֶׁיַּכִּירוּ חֶסְרוֹנָם וְשֶׁהוּא הָעוֹזֵר וְהַמּוֹשִׁיעַ.
He desired that they recognize their lack and know that He alone is their Helper and Deliverer.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַדַּלּוּת "לְךָ אֲנִי",
And through this poverty "I am Yours",
דְּמַכִּיר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם יְשׁוּעָה אֶלָּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
recognizing that he has no salvation except from Hashem, blessed be He,
כְּמוֹ הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁעֵינֶיהָ נְשׂוּאוֹת לְבַעְלָהּ וְאֵין לָהּ אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁהוּא מַשְׁפִּיעַ.
like a wife whose eyes are directed toward her husband, possessing only what he bestows.
וְעַל כֵּן "לִי נָאֶה לְהוֹשִׁיעַ"
Therefore "salvation befits me",
שֶׁנּוֹי כָּל דָּבָר הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא כְּמוֹת שֶׁהוּא רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת
for the beauty of every matter is when it stands as it ought to be.
וְנוֹי הַיְשׁוּעָה כְּשֶׁמּוֹשִׁיעַ לְמִי שֶׁהוּא דַּל וְנִצְרָךְ לַהַיְשׁוּעָה
and the true aesthetic beauty of salvation shines when He rescues one who is truly destitute and yearning for deliverance.
וְהַתְחָלַת הִתְקָרְבוּת הָאָדָם לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בָּזֶה שֶׁיַּכִּיר עָנְיוֹ וִיחַכֶּה לַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
And the initial approach of man to Hashem begins when he recognizes his poverty and awaits His service.
וְזֶהוּ הַתְחָלַת הַהִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַבָּא בְּלֵב הָאָדָם עַל יְדֵי בַּת קוֹל הַיּוֹצֵא בְּכָל יוֹם: "שׁוּבוּ בָנִים שׁוֹבָבִים" ,
And this is the initial awakening stirred in human hearts through the daily heavenly voice: "Return, wayward children" (Chagigah 15a).
דִּרְאִיַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מַכִּיר שָׁרְשָׁם דְּעֵינֵיהֶם צוֹפִיּוֹת רַק אֵלָיו
for in Hashem's penetrating vision into the depths of Jewish hearts, He perceives their root whose eyes gaze solely toward Him.
וּ"בְנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל נָאוֹת"  דְּלָהֶם נָאָה לְהוֹשִׁיעַ,
"The daughters of Israel are beautiful" (Nedarim 66a)—for unto them it is fitting to bring salvation,
וְזֶהוּ הַנּוֹי שֶׁלָּהֶם אֶלָּא שֶׁעֲנִיּוּת הַדַּעַת מְנַוַּלְתָּן
this being their true beauty, except that poverty of understanding makes them appear uncomely,
שֶׁגַּם זֶה מִכְּלַל חֶסְרוֹנָם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם כֹּחַ הַמִּתְעוֹרֵר לָזֶה גַּם כֵּן לְהַכִּיר חֶסְרוֹנָם וְלִצְפּוֹת לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
which itself is part of their utter dependency, lacking even the autonomous initiative to recognize their lack and await Hashem.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok, Kometz HaMinchah I §12: “ידוע שאין ללבנה אור משלה והיא גוף עכור רק מקבלת אור החמה ... וזהו פני משה כפני חמה שקיבל מעצמו אור פניו מד׳. פני יהושע כפני לבנה שקיבל ממשה שסמך ידיו עליו. זקינים שבאותו דור אמרו אוי לאותה בושה כמו שאמרו ... דמאן דאכיל דלאו דילי׳ בהית לאסתכולי באפילו.” — “It is known that the moon has no light of its own; it is an opaque body that only receives the sun’s light. ... This is: Moshe’s face was like the face of the sun, for he himself received the light of his face from Hashem; Yehoshua’s face was like the face of the moon, for he received from Moshe, who laid his hands upon him. The elders of that generation said, ‘Alas for that shame,’ as they said ... that one who eats what is not his is ashamed to look in his face.” The present paragraph develops the other side of received light: recognizing one’s lack turns dependence itself into an opening for Hashem’s help.

Bereishis 8:21: after the Flood, God resolves — “לֹא אֹסִף לְקַלֵּל עוֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה בַּעֲבוּר הָאָדָם, כִּי יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו” — “I will not again curse the ground for man’s sake, for the inclination of man’s heart is evil from his youth.” Meforshim: Rashi — “mi-ne’urav” from his youth: from the moment the child stirs to emerge into the world, the yetzer hara is set within him. R’ Tzadok’s use: this “evil inclination” presses upon Israel more than the nations — for the yetzer “leaves the nations and provokes Israel” (Sukkah 52a) — precisely because Israel “have no power of their own to defeat it,” and must look to God’s help alone. 
Exact Bavli wording — Sukkah 52a: שמניח אומות העולם, ומתגרה בשונאיהם של ישראל — It leaves the nations and antagonizes “the enemies of Israel,” the conventional euphemism in this passage for Israel.

paragraphs.text: Yeshayah 66:2: God declares whom He regards — “וְאֶל זֶה אַבִּיט, אֶל עָנִי וּנְכֵה רוּחַ, וְחָרֵד עַל דְּבָרִי” — “but to this one I look: to the poor and broken-spirited, who trembles at My word.” Meforshim: the Radak — of all His creation, God “looks” upon the humble and lowly of spirit, not the mighty. R’ Tzadok’s use: “the gaze of Hashem’s eyes is only upon Israel, on account of their poverty” — for they own nothing of themselves and their “eyes look only to Him,” unlike the nations, whose self-sufficiency turns their gaze away from Heaven.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 116:6: “שֹׁמֵר פְּתָאיִם ה׳, דַּלּוֹתִי וְלִי יְהוֹשִׁיעַ” — “Hashem guards the simple; I was brought low, and He saved me.” Meforshim: Rashi and Radak — because “I was brought low dalosi” and had no strength of my own, “He saved me.” R’ Tzadok’s use: “for this very reason He saves me — because I am lowly and poor,” which is not so with the nations; and the Sages read (cf. the Hallel, Pesachim 118b), “even though I am poor in mitzvos, I am Yours, and it befits me to be saved” — for the very “beauty of salvation” is the saving of one who is lowly and in need of it.

R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §25): “Man’s completion is from Hashem, who created man as a being of deficiency requiring completion. And this is the root of Israel, who ‘count by the moon’ — for they are ‘in a state of deficiency,’ and their completion is upheld from Hashem. But the nations of the world ‘count by the sun,’ which has no deficiency; since they have nothing to complete, it seems to them that they lack nothing — until they say, ‘I will ascend above the heights of the cloud, I will liken myself to the Most High’ (Yeshayahu 14:14), to resemble the sun; and this is the whole craving of the nations.” (This is the se’if’s contrast exactly: Israel are the ‘poor’ moon, owning nothing of themselves and awaiting completion from Hashem, while the nations are the self-sufficient sun that ‘imagines it needs nothing.’)

Yirmeyah 3:14: the call to return — “שׁוּבוּ בָנִים שׁוֹבָבִים נְאֻם ה׳, כִּי אָנֹכִי בָּעַלְתִּי בָכֶם” — “return, O wayward children, says Hashem, for I am your Master.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this daily voice is “the beginning of the arousal that comes into the heart of man” — for God, “seeing into the depths of Israel’s heart,” recognizes their root, “that their eyes look only to Him,” and rouses them “to recognize their affliction and await His service.” Izhbitz-Radzin parallel - Sod Yesharim, Hoshana Rabba 13:2; cf. Yismach Moshe, Re'eh 16:1: Sod Yesharim reads the very name David as a pattern of holy poverty: the dalet signifies 'לית ליה מגרמיה כלום' - that he has nothing of his own - while the vav signifies the explicit bond Hashem illuminates for one who recognizes that nothing is self-generated; remarkably, after all David's victories he still says, 'for I am poor and needy.' The work contrasts this with Gog, whose defining error is to seize strength as self-generated power. This is a striking parallel to R' Tzadok's description of Israel as the moon: their poverty is not spiritual weakness but the truth that all light is received. Precisely that confession can become the source of immense courage, because the person no longer relies on a finite power of his own. Yismach Moshe makes the same point in the practical realm of tzedakah. Even the wealthy giver is fundamentally poor, since no one brought anything into the world; the money destined for the poor was placed in his hands by Hashem, and he is merely the shaliach who transfers it. David could therefore call himself poor while king. Together the sources illuminate the paradox in this se'if: Israel's lack is itself their closeness. 'I am Yours' means that the absence of independent possession turns the eyes upward, making Hashem's salvation not an external rescue but the completion of the very form in which Israel was created. 
Original Ishbitz-Radzin Hebrew — Sod Yesharim, Hoshana Rabba §13:2: כי אותיות דוד רומזין דלית ליה מגרמיה כלום וע״ז רומז אות ד׳ — The letters of David indicate that he possesses nothing of his own; this is symbolized by the letter dalet.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Israel’s root is to be “poor,” owning nothing of themselves — like the woman, and like the moon by which they count, against the nations’ sun. Hence the yetzer provokes Israel most, for they have no power of their own to defeat it, while the nations’ very power drops them into the pit. Israel’s eyes look only to Hashem — and recognizing one’s affliction is itself the beginning of drawing near.

p: (נח) וְהַתְחָלַת הַהִתְעוֹרְרוּת לָזֶה גַּם כֵּן הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי יֵצֶר טוֹב הַנִּיתָּן בָּאָדָם הַמְּעוֹרְרוֹ לְטוֹב
And the very inception of awakening toward this also derives from Hashem through the Good Inclination placed within man stirring him toward good;
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הָרְאִיָּה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and this unfolds through the divine vision of Hashem,
כִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה ( שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב) עַל פָּסוּק " וְלִבִּי עֵר" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ה, ב),
for the Holy One is the heart of Israel, as our Sages taught (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2) on the verse "and my heart is awake" (Song of Songs 5:2),
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הוּא מִתְעוֹרֵר בִּרְאִיַּת עֵינַיִם גַּם לֵב הָאָדָם מִתְעוֹרֵר לְהַכִּיר עָנְיוֹ וּלְבַקֵּשׁ אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וִישׁוּעָתוֹ.
and when He stirs in divine sight, the human heart awakens in turn to recognize its poverty and seek Hashem's love and deliverance.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר מוֹסִיף לְהַעֲמִיק בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּתוֹ וּלְהִתְבּוֹנֵן יוֹתֵר בִּדְרָכָיו
And as he deepens his awakening and meditates further upon his ways,
רוֹאֶה וּמַכִּיר רִיחוּקוֹ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַד שֶׁחוֹשֵׁב עַצְמוֹ שָׂנוּי חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לִפְנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
he sees and feels his vast distance from Hashem, until he considers himself despised, Heaven forbid, before Hashem.
וְדָבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ מִצַּד הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And this painful feeling does not stem from Hashem's awakening,
כִּי דָּבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת כְּלָל
for such alienation is not objective truth at all,
וְגַם כִּי מִצַּד הַהַכָּרָה שֶׁהוּא שָׂנוּי לֹא יָבוֹא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְעוֹרְרוֹ,
and furthermore, from the divine perspective of regarding one as hated, Hashem would never come to awaken him.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִצַּד אַהֲבָה אוֹ מִצַּד רַחְמָנוּת וְהֶעְדֵּר שִׂנְאָה עַל כָּל פָּנִים
for divine awakening springs from love or compassion and the absence of hatred;
אֲבָל הוּא מִצַּד תְּפִיסַת הָאָדָם בְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַכִּיר מַעֲמַקָּיו בֶּאֱמֶת
rather it arises from the person's own subjective perception, failing to grasp his own inner spiritual depths,
וּכְפִי הִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ חוֹשֵׁב עַצְמוֹ לְשָׂנוּי וּמְרוּחָק לְגַמְרֵי מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and according to the outward disclosure of his heart, he considers himself despised and wholly estranged from Hashem;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְעוֹרֵר יוֹתֵר לִצְעוֹק לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהוֹשִׁיעוֹ
and through this despair he is stirred even more urgently to cry out to Hashem to save him,
וְאֵין סוֹמֵךְ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְעוֹרְרוֹ בְּעַצְמוֹ,
not relying passively that Hashem will stir him on His own,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מְעוֹרֵר אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and through that heartfelt cry he actively awakens Hashem's love,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בִּפְסָחִים קיח, ב): "אֵימָתַי אֲנִי אֲהוּבָה? כְּשֶׁיִּשְׁמַע קוֹל תַּחֲנוּנָי".
as they taught (Pesachim 118b): "When am I beloved? When He hears the voice of my supplications".
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִשְׁתּוֹקֵק לִשְׁמוֹעַ הַקּוֹל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב
For Hashem yearns to hear the voice—the voice of Jacob,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "הַשְׁמִיעִינִי אֶת קוֹלֵךְ כִּי קוֹלֵךְ עָרֵב" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ב, יד),
as it is stated: "Let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet" (Song of Songs 2:14),
וְלָמְדוּ מִזֶּה (בִּבְרָכוֹת כד.): "דְּקוֹל בְּאִשָּׁה עֶרְוָה".
and from this verse they derived (Berakhot 24a) that "a woman's voice is ervah (intimately enticing)".
כִּי הַקּוֹל הוּא יוֹצֵא מִפְּנִימִיּוּת וּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב
For the voice emerges from the innermost depths of the heart,
וּלְפִי שֶׁאֵין תְּשׁוּקָתָהּ שֶׁל אִשָּׁה אֶלָּא לְבַעְלָהּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (כ, ז) עַל פָּסוּק " וְאֶל אִישֵׁךְ תְּשׁוּקָתֵךְ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג, טז),
and because a woman's true desire is solely toward her husband as stated in Bereishit Rabbah (20:7) on "and unto your husband shall be your desire" (Genesis 3:16),
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּאָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן (סוֹף פֶּרֶק א) שֶׁכָּל שִׂיחָתָן נִיאוּף
which is why they noted in Avot DeRabbi Natan that all their natural conversation tends toward affection,
לָכֵן כְּמַיִם הַפָּנִים לַפָּנִים קוֹלָהּ מְעוֹרֵר אַהֲבָה וְתַאֲוָה בְּלֵב הָאִישׁ.
therefore, as water reflects face to face, her voice stirs love and desire in the heart of the man.
וְכֵן אֵין תְּשׁוּקָתָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶלָּא לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
And likewise, the ultimate desire of Israel is directed solely toward the Holy One, blessed be He;
עַל כֵּן קוֹלָם מְעוֹרֵר אַהֲבָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לָהֶם
therefore their outcry awakens His divine love for them.
וְאָז הָאַהֲבָה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁגַּם הָאָדָם אֵין חוֹשֵׁב עַצְמוֹ לְשָׂנוּי
and then that love becomes openly revealed, so that the person no longer regards himself as despised.

Izhbitz parallel - Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Yitro 2: The Ishbitzer's explanation of 'Vayishma Yisro' closely parallels R' Tzadok's account of the first stirrings of teshuvah. He says that the initial hearing did not actually originate in Yisro; Hashem sent him that hearing. Yet because Yisro had recognition of Hashem, a powerful desire to cleave to Israel, and the awareness that 'the earth and all it contains belongs to Hashem,' Heaven rewarded him by attributing even the beginning of the hearing to Yisro himself. The source gives a concrete Izhbitz model for the two levels operating in this se'if. The awakening toward good is a gift - the yetzer tov and the bat kol that call the person home. Nevertheless, the human response is real: the person can receive the arousal, deepen it, and turn his desire toward the Source. When he does so, the Divine gift becomes, as it were, his own avodah and receives the name of his act. This also helps define the danger R' Tzadok describes when introspection deepens into the false conclusion 'I am hated.' The true heavenly arousal is the movement toward return; the despairing interpretation is an added human distortion. But because the person continues to cry out rather than sever the bond, even that darkness can become the setting in which the original Divine summons is heard more deeply. 
Mei HaShiloach II, Yitro §2: אַף שֶׁהַתְחָלַת הַשְּׁמִיעָה לֹא הָיָה מִצִּדּוֹ רַק הַשי"ת שָׁלַח לוֹ זֶה הַשְּׁמִיעָה — Although the beginning of hearing did not originate with him, Hashem sent him this hearing. The parallel is not a quotation from Rav Tzadok.

He says that the initial hearing did not actually originate in Yisro; Hashem sent him that hearing. Yet because Yisro had recognition of Hashem, a powerful desire to cleave to Israel, and the awareness that 'the earth and all it contains belongs to Hashem,' Heaven rewarded him by attributing even the beginning of the hearing to Yisro himself. The source gives a concrete Izhbitz model for the two levels operating in this se'if. The awakening toward good is a gift - the yetzer tov and the bat kol that call the person home. Nevertheless, the human response is real: the person can receive the arousal, deepen it, and turn his desire toward the Source. When he does so, the Divine gift becomes, as it were, his own avodah and receives the name of his act. This also helps define the danger R' Tzadok describes when introspection deepens into the false conclusion 'I am hated.' The true heavenly arousal is the movement toward return; the despairing interpretation is an added human distortion. But because the person continues to cry out rather than sever the bond, even that darkness can become the setting in which the original Divine summons is heard more deeply.

אַף שֶׁהַתְחָלַת הַשְּׁמִיעָה לֹא הָיָה מִצִּדּוֹ רַק הַשי"ת שָׁלַח לוֹ זֶה הַשְּׁמִיעָה — Although the beginning of hearing did not originate with him, Hashem sent him this hearing. The parallel is not a quotation from Rav Tzadok.

Bereishis 3:16 (and Bereishis Rabbah 20:7): to Chava, God says — “וְאֶל אִישֵׁךְ תְּשׁוּקָתֵךְ, וְהוּא יִמְשׇׁל בָּךְ” — “and your longing shall be for your husband, and he shall rule over you.” Meforshim: the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah) reads “teshukasech” your longing as directed to her husband alone; Rav Tzadok attributes the parallel teaching to Avos d’Rabbi Nasan; the exact wording is independently located in Tractate Derekh Eretz Rabbah, Chapter 1. R’ Tzadok’s use: because “a woman’s longing is only for her husband,” her voice — issuing “from the innermost depths of the heart” — arouses his love (whence the Sages derived “kol b’ishah ervah”); and just so, “Israel’s longing is only for the Holy One,” so that their crying voice “arouses His love for them,” and the love that had been hidden is at last revealed. 
Source-location qualification — Tractate Derekh Eretz Rabbah 1 says “לא תרבה שיחה עם האשה שכל שיחתה של אשה אינה אלא דברי ניאופים.” This wording appears in the consulted Derekh Eretz Rabbah text, but not in the consulted Avot d’Rabbi Natan Chapter 1 transcription. The Hebrew manuscript’s attribution to Avot d’Rabbi Natan is preserved; the exact relationship between editions remains qualified. Compare Rav Tzadok, Divrei Soferim §36.  [Open source]

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The arousal to recognize one’s poverty comes from Hashem, by way of the good inclination, for He sees the heart of Israel — “my heart is awake.” Deepening it, a person sees his distance until he imagines himself hated, which is not true and does not come from His arousal at all. Yet through that very misperception he cries out all the more, and the cry itself arouses His love.

p: (נט) וּמִתְּחִלָּה הָיָה הָאַהֲבָה בְּהֶעְלֵם
And initially that love resided in concealment,
עַל כֵּן אַף שֶׁאָמְרָה "עַתָּה יֶאֱהָבַנִי אִישִׁי" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, לב) חָזְרָה לוֹמַר "כִּי שְׂנוּאָה אָנֹכִי" (שָׁם לג),
therefore even though Leah declared "now my husband will love me" (Genesis 29:32), she reverted to saying "because I am hated" (v. 33),
לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הִרְגִּישָׁה הִתְגַּלּוּת אַהֲבָה הֲגַם שֶׁיָּלְדָה לוֹ בֵּן
because she did not yet perceive the overt revelation of love even though she had borne him a son.
וְעִם כָּל זֶה חָשְׁבָה כִּי הִיא שְׂנוּאָה בְּתַכְלִית
and notwithstanding this she still considered that she was utterly hated.
וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁל עָלְמָא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא עַד שֶׁהוּא נִדְמֶה מַמָּשׁ בְּהֵיפֶךְ,
And this is the ultimate profundity of concealment of the Hidden World, to the degree that it appears quite the opposite.
וְזֶה גּוֹרֵם שְׁמִיעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צַעֲקַת הָאָדָם כְּפִי דִּמְיוֹנוֹ בְּהֶעְלֵם
and this very dynamic causes Hashem's hearing of man's cry according to his concealed perception.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נוֹלַד שִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא כֹּחַ זֶה דִּשְׁמִיעָה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And through this Simeon was born, in whom resides this spiritual faculty of Hashem's hearing,
כִּי הַקּוֹל עַצְמוֹ הוּא נַחֲלַת וּבִרְכַּת יְהוּדָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "שְׁמַע ה' קוֹל יְהוּדָה" (דְּבָרִים לג, ז),
for the voice itself is the heritage and blessing of Judah, as it is stated: "Hear, Hashem, the voice of Judah" (Deuteronomy 33:7).
וּבָזֶה נִרְמַז בִּרְכַּת שִׁמְעוֹן כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה וּבְרַשִּׁ"י (פָּרָשַׁת הַבְּרָכָה לג, ז) הַיְינוּ שְׁמִיעַת הַקּוֹל
and therein was hinted the blessing of Simeon, as our Sages of blessed memory noted and as Rashi writes on Parashat VeZot HaBerakhah (Deuteronomy 33:7), namely the receptive hearing of that voice.
כִּי הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם חֵלֶק אֱלֹהִי מִמַּעַל
For the souls of the children of Israel are a divine portion from Above,
שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל הַכֹּחוֹת כּוּלָּם הַמִּתְחַלְּקִים בִּפְרָטֵי הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
Who is the Master of all faculties distributed across the individual souls of Israel,
דְּעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, כו).
concerning which it is stated: "in our image, after our likeness" (Genesis 1:26).
וְיָדוּעַ דְּצֶלֶם וּדְמוּת הֵם דְּכַר וְנוּקְבָּא
And it is known that 'image' (tzelem) and 'likeness' (demut) correspond to masculine and feminine.
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ כֹּחוֹת מַשְׁפִּיעִים וּמְקַבְּלִים, כְּמוֹ רְאִיָּה וּשְׁמִיעָה
signifying that there are bestowing and receiving faculties, such as seeing and hearing.
הָרְאִיָּה הוּא כֹּחַ הָרוֹאֶה
Seeing is the active power of the beholder.
וְיוּכַל לִפְעוֹל גַּם כֵּן בְּכֹחוֹ כַּיָּדוּעַ מִכֹּחַ עַיִן הָרָע
and is able to exert effect through its gaze, as is known from the phenomenon of the evil eye;
וּמִדָּה טוֹבָה דְּעַיִן טוֹבָה מְרוּבָּה
and the positive attribute of a benevolent eye is even more abundant.
אֲבָל דָּבָר הַנִּרְאֶה גַּשְׁמִי אֵין פּוֹעֵל בָּרוֹאֶה
yet the physical object beheld exerts no direct active force upon the beholder.
וְכֹחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה הוּא בְּהֵיפֶךְ,
The faculty of hearing, however, is the reverse,
שֶׁהַמַּשְׁמִיעַ פּוֹעֵל בַּשּׁוֹמֵעַ,
for the speaker directly impacts the listener.
וְעִיקַּר לְשׁוֹן שְׁמִיעָה הַיְינוּ קַבָּלַת דְּבָרִים וְהוּא כֹּחַ מְקַבֵּל
and the primary meaning of the word 'hearing' denotes the reception of words, being a receptive capacity.
וְעַל כֵּן בְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית נִזְכַּר רְאִיָּה תֵּיכֶף
Therefore in the Creation narrative, seeing is mentioned immediately:
בִּבְרִיאַת הָאוֹר נֶאֱמַר: "וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ד)
– at the creation of light it is stated: "And God saw, etc." (Genesis 1:4)—.
נֶאֱצַל כֹּחַ הָרְאִיָּה עִמּוֹ, שֶׁהָרְאִיָּה הוּא בָּאוֹר
the faculty of vision being emanated alongside it, for sight exists in light.
אֲבָל שְׁמִיעָה נִזְכַּר רִאשׁוֹנָה בַּתּוֹרָה בְּאָדָם
– However, hearing is first mentioned in the Torah concerning man—
"וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ אֶת קוֹל ה' אֱלֹהִים מִתְהַלֵּךְ וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם ג, ח),
"And they heard the voice of Hashem God walking, etc." (Genesis 3:8),
דְּעִיקַּר יְצִירַת כֹּחַ זֶה הוּא לָאָדָם שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע הַקּוֹל ה
' for the primary formation of this faculty was designated for man to hear the voice of Hashem
וְלִהְיוֹת "שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (דְּבָרִים ו, ד),
and to fulfill "Hear, O Israel, Hashem is our God, etc." (Deuteronomy 6:4),
שֶׁהוּא הַמְקַבֵּל קוֹל ה' הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ.
man being the recipient of the bestowing voice of Hashem.
וְזֶהוּ קוֹל הָרִאשׁוֹן הַנִּזְכָּר בַּתּוֹרָה
And this is the first voice mentioned in the Torah,
כִּי יְצִירַת עִנְיַן הַקּוֹל הָיָה רַק לְהַשְׁמִיעַ לָאָדָם קוֹל ה
', for the very creation of sonic voice was solely to transmit unto man the voice of Hashem;
וּמִצַּד עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע בּוֹ הָיָה הַתְחָלַת קִלְקוּל הָאָדָם
and through the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, man's initial spiritual downfall occurred,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי שָׁמַעְתָּ לְקוֹל אִשְׁתֶּךָ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג, יז),
as it is stated: "Because you listened to the voice of your wife" (Genesis 3:17).
שֶׁרַק עַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה הַחֵטְא
for solely through this inversion did the sin transpire.
וּמַה שֶּׁנּוֹצַר לִהְיוֹת הוּא מְקַבֵּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ מְקַבֶּלֶת מִמֶּנּוּ,
And whereas man was formed to receive from Hashem and his wife from him,
עַל יְדֵי הַנְּטִיָּה לְתַאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הִפֵּךְ הַסֵּדֶר
through leaning toward worldly desires he inverted the cosmic hierarchy;
כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא נִמְשָׁךְ אַחַר הַתַּאֲווֹת הֲרֵי הַתַּאֲוָה מוֹשֶׁלֶת עָלָיו
for when he is drawn after lusts, the desire dominates over him,
וְהִיא מַשְׁפִּיעַ וְהוּא מְקַבֵּל
and the base lust becomes the bestower while he becomes the recipient,
וּכְאִשָּׁה מְקַבֵּל לְקוֹל אִשְׁתּוֹ הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ לוֹ.
and like a woman he becomes passive, receiving from the voice of his wife who now influences him.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הִקְדִּים רְפוּאָה לַמַּכָּה
Except that the Holy One, blessed be He, preceded the cure to the affliction,
הִיא הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁקָּדְמָה לָעוֹלָם ,
this being Repentance which preceded the creation of the world (Pesachim 54a),
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ בָּאָה אֶלָּא אַחַר הַחֵטְא
and even though it comes into expression only after sin,
וְעַל כֵּן שְׁמִיעָה זוֹ בְּקוֹל ה' נֶאֱמַר אַחַר הַחֵטְא
wherefore this hearing of the voice of Hashem is recounted after the fall,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא לְשׁוֹן שְׁמִיעָה הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
nonetheless it stands as the very first instance of hearing in the Torah,
שֶׁנִּכְתַּב בַּתּוֹרָה קוֹדֶם לְשׁוֹן שְׁמִיעָה דְּרַע – "כִּי שָׁמַעְתָּ (לְקוֹל אִשְׁתֶּךָ)".
being inscribed in the Torah prior to the flawed hearing of "because you listened (to the voice of your wife)".
דְּהָאֱמֶת כְּפִי סֵדֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַתְּשׁוּבָה קָדְמָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה
For the truth according to Hashem's order is that Repentance preceded in primordial thought.
כִּי תַּכְלִית הַחֵטְא הָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁאַחֲרָיו
since the ultimate purpose of the sin was for the sake of the profound Repentance that follows it.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזֶּה אֵינוֹ מִצַּד הָאָדָם
And even though this is not from the human perspective,
דְּאַדְּרַבָּה, "הָאוֹמֵר אֶחֱטָא וְאָשׁוּב אֵין מַסְפִּיקִין בְּיָדוֹ" ,
for on the contrary, "one who says: I will sin and then repent, is not granted the opportunity" (Yoma 85b),
וְאָדָם הַחוֹטֵא אֵין דַּעְתּוֹ לָשׁוּב
and a person who sins has no active thought of repenting at that moment,
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ בְּמַעֲשֶׂה הַחֵטְא קָדַם בַּתְּחִלָּה
and perforce in concrete action the sin preceded first.
כְּפִי הָאֱמֶת שֶׁבְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַתְּשׁוּבָה קָדְמָה
yet according to the ultimate truth within His divine thought, Repentance preceded.

paragraphs.text:
Izhbitz-Radzin context - Beit Yaakov on Torah, Vayetzei 63:1: Beit Yaakov identifies Rachel with alma d'isgalya and Leah with alma d'iskasya. Rachel's way is what a person can understand and choose with clarity; Leah represents help that comes 'not by one's knowledge,' in a form whose goodness is not yet visible. He therefore notes that many of Leah's children's defining episodes - Reuven and Bilhah, Yehudah and Tamar, and the path from Yehudah to Malchus Beis David - initially appeared on the surface as matters a person would not willingly choose to enter. Their greatness was disclosed only after Hashem clarified the hidden intention. This is a powerful complement to R' Tzadok's treatment of Leah's 'hatred.' The concealment is so deep that the outer form can seem to say the opposite of the inner love. Yet the point is not that every troubling appearance is secretly good, nor that one may seek such situations. Beit Yaakov stresses that a person naturally wants to walk securely in the revealed good; the hidden mode is what Hashem may send and later clarify. Thus Leah's cry, and Shimon's 'hearing,' belong to a world in which the inner relationship precedes its visible proof. The more the love is hidden, the more the surface can be misread as rejection; the avodah is to cry from within that concealment until the hidden bond becomes audible. 
Original Beit Yaakov, Vayetzei §63: וְעִנְיַן סַיַּיעְתָּא שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעַת הוּא, שֶׁאַף אִם יִדְמֶה לְאָדָם שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה טוֹב, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מִתְבָּרֵר לְטוֹב — Divine help beyond one’s present knowledge can initially appear otherwise, but later be clarified as good. This is an Ishbitz-Radzin parallel; not Rav Tzadok’s own wording.  [Open source]

rich.text: Izhbitz-Radzin context - Beit Yaakov on Torah, Vayetzei 63:1: Beit Yaakov identifies Rachel with alma d'isgalya and Leah with alma d'iskasya. Rachel's way is what a person can understand and choose with clarity; Leah represents help that comes 'not by one's knowledge,' in a form whose goodness is not yet visible. He therefore notes that many of Leah's children's defining episodes - Reuven and Bilhah, Yehudah and Tamar, and the path from Yehudah to Malchus Beis David - initially appeared on the surface as matters a person would not willingly choose to enter. Their greatness was disclosed only after Hashem clarified the hidden intention. This is a powerful complement to R' Tzadok's treatment of Leah's 'hatred.' The concealment is so deep that the outer form can seem to say the opposite of the inner love. Yet the point is not that every troubling appearance is secretly good, nor that one may seek such situations. Beit Yaakov stresses that a person naturally wants to walk securely in the revealed good; the hidden mode is what Hashem may send and later clarify. Thus Leah's cry, and Shimon's 'hearing,' belong to a world in which the inner relationship precedes its visible proof. The more the love is hidden, the more the surface can be misread as rejection; the avodah is to cry from within that concealment until the hidden bond becomes audible.

וְעִנְיַן סַיַּיעְתָּא שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעַת הוּא, שֶׁאַף אִם יִדְמֶה לְאָדָם שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה טוֹב, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מִתְבָּרֵר לְטוֹב — Divine help beyond one’s present knowledge can initially appear otherwise, but later be clarified as good. This is an Ishbitz-Radzin parallel; not Rav Tzadok’s own wording.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 1:26: at the creation of man — “נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ” — “let us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness.” Meforshim: Rashi — “b’tzalmeinu” in Our image means “in the mold prepared for him”; the “image” and “likeness” denote the higher, God-given faculties that set man apart. R’ Tzadok’s use: the souls of Israel are “a portion of God from above,” bearing all His powers; and “tzelem” and “demus” are “male and female” — the “giving powers and the receiving powers,” corresponding to sight (which acts) and hearing (which receives). inlineHeadings.text: The theme: At first the love was hidden — so Leah, having said “now my husband will love me,” returned to “I am hated”: the deepest concealment appears as its own opposite. It is precisely the cry shaped by that imagined concealment that Hashem “hears” — and so Shimon, the power of hearing, was born. Sight acts and hearing receives, which is why sight appears first at the creation of light, and hearing first with man.

p: (ס) וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתְּשׁוּבָה הוּא בְּמִקְרָא זֶה דִּשְׁמִיעַת קוֹל ה' "וַיִּתְחַבֵּא" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג, ח),
And the root of Repentance lies in this verse of hearing the voice of Hashem, "and they hid themselves" (Genesis 3:8),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר הַתְּשׁוּבָה – הַבּוּשָׁה מֵהַחֵטְא
for this is the very essence of Repentance: shame over the sin,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת י״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
and as they stated (Berakhot 12b):
"הָעוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה וּמִתְבַּיֵּישׁ בָּהּ מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ עַל כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתָיו".
"Whoever commits a transgression and feels ashamed of it, all his iniquities are forgiven him".
וְזֶה בָּא עַל יְדֵי הַשְּׁמִיעָה
And this shame enters specifically through hearing;
דְּעַל יְדֵי הַחֵטְא הוּא בְּהֶסְתֵּר פָּנִים
for through sin a person is cast into concealment of the divine countenance
וְאֵין זוֹכֶה לִרְאִיָּה דְּ"שִׁוִּיתִי ה' לְנֶגְדִּי (תָמִיד)" (תְּהִלִּים טז, ח) הַמֵּבִיא גַּם כֵּן בּוּשָׁה
and does not merit that vivid vision of "I have set Hashem before me always" (Psalms 16:8) which likewise induces shame,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּהַגָּהַת שֻׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ אֹרַח חַיִּים רֵישׁ סִימָן א),
(as written in the Gloss of the Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayyim, start of siman 1),
וְגַם הָאָדָם עַל יְדֵי הַכָּרַת הַחֵטְא מַסְתִּיר פָּנָיו
and the person himself, through recognizing his sin, hides his face,
כִּי יָרֵא מֵהַבִּיט וּבָהֵית לְאִסְתַּכָּלוּ בְּאַפֵּיהּ,
being afraid to look and ashamed to gaze into the divine countenance.
וּמִטַּעַם זֶה חוֹשֵׁב כִּי שָׂנוּא הוּא
and on this account he presumes that he is despised.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם זוֹכֶה לִשְׁמִיעַת קוֹל ה' בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים הַמְּעוֹרְרִים בּוּשָׁה בְּלִבּוֹ.
Yet nonetheless he merits hearing the voice of Hashem within words of Torah and the teachings of sages that awaken shame in his heart.
וְלֹא נִכְתַּב תְּחִלָּה שְׁמִיעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה דְּקוֹדֶם שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה שֶׁנּוֹצַר בָּאָדָם
And the initial hearing prior to sin was not written first, which represents the root of hearing as formed in man;
כִּי מִיָּד לְצִיוּוּי רִאשׁוֹן לֹא שָׁמַע
because right at the very first command he failed to listen,
דְּבְכֹחַ זֶה הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחַ הַקִּלְקוּל
since within this faculty lies the root of the breakdown.
דְּכֹחַ זֶה הוּא עִיקַּר כֹּחַ הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים שֶׁהֵם הַמְקַבְּלִים
this power being the essential trait of lower creatures who are recipients.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּעַל הַכֹּחוֹת כּוּלָּם
Except that Hashem, blessed be He, is the Master of all forces,
דְּלָא שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹמַר שֶׁנּוֹצַר כֹּחַ שֶׁחוּץ מִמֶּנּוּ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
such that it is impossible to say any power was created external to Him;
אֲבָל רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֹּחַ מְקַבֵּל הוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ לַכֹּחַ הַמְקַבֵּל
rather His divine will that there exist a receptive power is the metaphysical root of all reception.
שֶׁהֲרֵי יֵשׁ מְצִיאוּת לְכֹחַ זֶה בִּרְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּי הוּא וּרְצוֹנוֹ חַד
for there is existence for this force within His will, since He and His will are One.
וְהַיְינוּ כֵּיוָן דְּרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִבְרָאִים הַמְקַבְּלִים
Which means that because Hashem desired that there be created beings who receive,
וּכְשֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה כֵּן הֲרֵי נַעֲשָׂה רְצוֹנוֹ וְנַחַת רוּחַ הוּא לְפָנָיו שֶׁאָמַר וְנַעֲשָׂה רְצוֹנוֹ (סִפְרֵי פָּרָשַׁת פִּינְחָס קמג),
and when this is fulfilled His will is executed, producing gratification before Him that He spoke and His will was done (Sifrei, Pinchas 143).
הֲרֵי כִּבְיָכוֹל כְּאִלּוּ הוּא מְקַבֵּל מִנִּבְרָאִים שֶׁהֲרֵי יֵשׁ לוֹ נַחַת רוּחַ מִזֶּה
it is as though, so to speak, He receives from created beings, for He derives divine gratification from this.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל פָּסוּק "תְּנוּ עֹז לֵאלֹהִים" (תְּהִלִּים סח, לה)
And this explains what they taught on the verse "Ascribe strength unto God" (Psalms 68:35),
דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְפַרְנְסִים לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם וּמוֹסִיפִים כֹּחַ בַּפַּמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה
that Israel sustains their Father in Heaven and adds strength to the heavenly entourage.
כִּי מֵאַחַר שֶׁהָיָה הָרָצוֹן בַּבְּרִיאָה הֲרֵי קִיּוּם הַבְּרִיאָה הוּא מִילּוּי הָרָצוֹן
for since the original will was invested in Creation, the preservation of Creation fulfills that desire.
אֶלָּא שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַבְּרִיאָה
Except that this dynamic applies solely from the perspective of Creation,
דְּבֶאֱמֶת "אִם צָדַקְתָּ מַה תִּתֶּן לּוֹ" (אִיּוֹב לה, ז).
for in ultimate reality, "If you are righteous, what do you give Him?" (Job 35:7).
וְזֶה עִנְיַן "בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ", שֶׁהֵם כָּל הַכֹּחוֹת מַשְׁפִּיעִים וּמְקַבְּלִים
And this is the meaning of "in our image, after our likeness", representing all faculties, bestowing and receiving.
וְהַהַשְׁפָּעָה שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר כֹּחַ הָעֶלְיוֹנִים נִקְרָא "צֶלֶם",
And bestowing, which is the primary trait of supernal beings, is termed 'image' (tzelem).
אֲבָל כֹּחַ הַקִּיבּוּל הוּא רַק "דְּמוּת" וְדִמְיוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּעֶלְיוֹנִים דְּמוּת זֶה גַּם כֵּן וְלֹא בֶּאֱמֶת
while the faculty of reception is merely 'likeness' (demut) and an analogy, appearing in supernal beings only as a semblance, not in absolute reality.
אֲבָל בָּאָדָם הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת מִצַּד מַה שֶּׁהוּא מְקַבֵּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
However, within man it exists as actual truth, inasmuch as he truly receives from Hashem, blessed be He.
אֶלָּא שֶׁכֹּחַ זֶה הַנֶּאֱצָל לוֹ מִדְּמוּת שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה
Except that because this capacity was emanated to him from the supernal 'likeness',
הַיְינוּ כֹּחַ הַקַּבָּלָה מִתַּחְתּוֹנִים
namely the capacity of receiving from below,
עַל כֵּן נִשְׁרַשׁ בּוֹ כֹּחַ זֶה גַּם כֵּן דְּקַבָּלָה מִשֶּׁלְּמַטָּה הֵימֶנּוּ הָרְאוּיָה לְקַבָּלָתוֹ.
therefore there was rooted within him likewise the tendency to receive from that which is beneath him, adapting to receive from it.

Berachos 12b: “Rabbah bar Chinnana the Elder said in the name of Rav: whoever commits a transgression and is ashamed of it — all his sins are forgiven him, as it says ‘that you may remember and be ashamed — when I have forgiven you for all that you have done, says Hashem God’ (Yechezkel 16:63).” Chassidic parallel - Sefat Emet, Nitzavim 5:2: The Sefat Emet explains 'you are standing today, all of you' as a permanent truth: the collective of Israel always stands before Hashem, and the work of each individual is to nullify himself into that klal. On this basis he writes that even the wicked can return, because the sin is only a contingent separation from the כלל ישראל and the person can return to his root, 'to the inheritance of my fathers I return.' He then reads 've-hasheivosa el levavecha ... ve-shavta' as returning the holy point that exists in every Jew into the heart and body, where the weight of materiality had covered its light. He adds that teshuvah reaches the Kisei HaKavod because the returning person rectifies not only his own crookedness but awakens a return and straightening through the higher worlds. This gives important context to R' Tzadok's 'shame and hiding.' Shame is not proof that the core has been lost. The person hides because the revealed self no longer matches the holy root, but the very pain of that mismatch testifies that the root remains. Hearing the Divine voice from concealment therefore becomes the first movement of reintegration: the sinner does not manufacture a new soul; he returns the ever-present point to the heart. That is why Chazal can speak of forgiveness through genuine shame - the shame is the soul's recognition that its current exterior is foreign to what it truly is. 
Exact Gemara, Berakhot 12b: ואמר רבה בר חיננא סבא משמיה דרב: כל העושה דבר עבירה ומתבייש בו — מוחלין לו על כל עונותיו. — Rabbah bar Chinnana Sava in the name of Rav: whoever sins and is ashamed of it is forgiven all his sins. The earlier English attribution had an extra “bar”.  [Open source]

rich.text: : “Rabbah bar Chinnana the Elder said in the name of Rav: whoever commits a transgression and is ashamed of it — all his sins are forgiven him, as it says ‘that you may remember and be ashamed — when I have forgiven you for all that you have done, says Hashem God’ (

).” Chassidic parallel - Sefat Emet, Nitzavim 5:2: The Sefat Emet explains 'you are standing today, all of you' as a permanent truth: the collective of Israel always stands before Hashem, and the work of each individual is to nullify himself into that klal. On this basis he writes that even the wicked can return, because the sin is only a contingent separation from the כלל ישראל and the person can return to his root, 'to the inheritance of my fathers I return.' He then reads 've-hasheivosa el levavecha ... ve-shavta' as returning the holy point that exists in every Jew into the heart and body, where the weight of materiality had covered its light. He adds that teshuvah reaches the Kisei HaKavod because the returning person rectifies not only his own crookedness but awakens a return and straightening through the higher worlds. This gives important context to R' Tzadok's 'shame and hiding.' Shame is not proof that the core has been lost. The person hides because the revealed self no longer matches the holy root, but the very pain of that mismatch testifies that the root remains. Hearing the Divine voice from concealment therefore becomes the first movement of reintegration: the sinner does not manufacture a new soul; he returns the ever-present point to the heart. That is why Chazal can speak of forgiveness through genuine shame - the shame is the soul's recognition that its current exterior is foreign to what it truly is.

Tehillim 68:35: “תְּנוּ עֹז לֵאלֹהִים, עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל גַּאֲוָתוֹ, וְעֻזּוֹ בַּשְּׁחָקִים” — “give strength to God; over Israel is His majesty, and His strength is in the heavens.” Meforshim: Rav Tzadok expounds “tnu oz l’Elokim” concerning Israel, who, in Rav Tzadok’s formulation, “sustain their Father in Heaven” and “add strength to the Heavenly retinue pamalya shel ma’alah.” Compare the related, non-identical statement in Pesikta de-Rav Kahana, Selichot 25:1, that the righteous “מוסיפין כח בגבורה.” R’ Tzadok’s use: since God “willed” that there be created beings who receive, the very sustaining of Creation “fulfills His will,” so that, “as it were, He receives from the creatures,” having satisfaction from them — the demus below answering the tzelem above. 
Primary-source limitation — Pesikta de-Rav Kahana, Selichot 25:1 (not 26), states “כל זמן שהצדיקים עושין רצונו של הקב״ה הן מוסיפין כח בגבורה” — when the righteous do the will of the Holy One, they add strength to might. This is a relevant parallel, not an exact source for “מפרנסין לאביהם שבשמים” or “מוסיפין כח בפמליא של מעלה.” The distinct original provenance of those expressions remains open. Rav Tzadok immediately limits the concept to the perspective of Creation.

paragraphs.text: Iyov 35:7: Elihu’s words to Iyov — “אִם צָדַקְתָּ מַה תִּתֶּן לוֹ, אוֹ מַה מִיָּדְךָ יִקָּח” — “if you are righteous, what do you give Him? Or what does He take from your hand?” Meforshim: the commentators — a person’s righteousness confers no benefit upon God, who lacks nothing; the whole gain of the mitzvah is the person’s own. R’ Tzadok’s use: Israel’s “sustaining of their Father” holds true “only from the side of the Creation” — from the will God set, that there be receivers; but in absolute truth, “if you are righteous, what do you give Him?” — He needs nothing, and the notion of His “receiving from the creatures” is only “as it were.”  [Open source]

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Teshuvah’s root is in “they hid themselves” — the shame of the sin, of which they said that one who transgresses and is ashamed is forgiven all his sins. It works through hearing: sin brings a hiding of the Face, and a man ashamed to gaze imagines himself hated, yet still merits to hear His voice in Torah and in the words of the Sages. The receiving-power is the root of corruption — yet His willing a receiver is itself that power’s root.

p: (סא) וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְכֹחַ הַחֵטְא דִּשְׁמִיעָה לְקוֹל אִשְׁתּוֹ וְקַבָּלַת הֲנָאָה וְנַחַת רוּחַ מִדְּבָרִים הַשְּׁפֵלִים וְשֶׁלְּמַטָּה הֵימֶנּוּ.
And this is the root of the power of sin: listening to the voice of his wife and receiving pleasure and gratification from lowly things beneath him.
שֶׁבַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה הוּא טוֹב
Whereas in the Supernal Root it is sublime good,
דְּזֶהוּ עִיקַּר כֹּחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה דִּלְמַעְלָה לִשְׁמוֹעַ צַעֲקַת הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים
for this is the essential purpose of the supernal faculty of hearing: to listen to the outcry of earthly creatures,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשׁוֹחֵר טוֹב עַל פָּסוּק "אָזְנַיִם כָּרִיתָ לִּי" (תְּהִלִּים מ, ז)
as they said in Shocher Tov on the verse "Ears You have dug for me" (Psalms 40:7):
אֵין אָזְנַיִם שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה כְּרוּיוֹת אֶלָּא לְצֹרֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל
the supernal ears are hollowed solely for the sake of Israel.
כִּי הָאֹזֶן הוּא כְּלִי הַקִּיבּוּל דְּלָא שַׁיָּיךְ כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה כְּלָל
For the ear is a receptive vessel that does not apply to the Transcendent Realm at all.
אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל הִכְתִּיב הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁהוּא מְקַבֵּל מֵהֶם
except that for the sake of Israel, Hashem wrote concerning Himself that He receives from them.
וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת הַמְקַבֶּלֶת מֵאֵת הַמַּמְלִיכִים אוֹתוֹ,
And this is the attribute of Malchut (Sovereignty) which receives from those who coronate Him,
דְּלוּלֵי הֵם אֵין מָקוֹם לְמִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת
for without subjects there is no arena for kingship,
וְעַל כֵּן "רַגְלֶיהָ יֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת" (מִשְׁלֵי ה, ה).
and therefore "her feet go down to death" (Proverbs 5:5).
רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר, הַיְינוּ מַדְרֵגוֹת הַתַּחְתּוֹנוֹת הַמִּתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת בַּנִּבְרָאִים
Meaning: these are the lowest tiers extending into created beings,
שֶׁבָּהֶם הוּא עֲמִידַת רֶגֶל מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת מַה שֶּׁמַּלְכוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה
within whom rests the foot of Malchut whereby His sovereignty rules over all;
כְּשֶׁבָּהֶם מִתְפַּשֵּׁט כֹּחַ חֵשֶׁק זֶה לְקַבֵּל מִתַּחְתּוֹנִים
when this urge to receive from what is below extends into them,
זֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בְּכָל מִינֵי רַע דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
this becomes the root for sinking into every manner of worldly evil,
שֶׁכְּלָלוּתָן הַמָּוֶת שֶׁהוּא הַסִּילּוּק וּבִיטּוּל מֵעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
the totality of which is death, the removal and nullification from this world.
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה עוֹנֶשׁ חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
which was the penalty of the sin of Adam the First.
דְּעַל יְדֵי הַשִּׁימּוּשׁ בְּכֹחַ זֶה דְּקַבָּלָה מִתַּחְתּוֹנִים
For through employing this power of receiving from below.
בִּהְיוֹתוֹ חֵלֶק נִפְרָד מִשָּׁרְשׁוֹ, יוּכַל לָבוֹא לְפֵירוּד גָּמוּר
being a component detached from its root, one can arrive at complete rupture.
וְתַקָּנָתוֹ שֶׁיִּסְתַּלֵּק וְיוּכְלַל בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ לְמַעְלָה שֶׁשָּׁם הוּא טוֹב
And its rectification is that it ascend and be integrated into its supernal root where it is good.
וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת שְׁכִינָה תַּתָּאָה
And this is the attribute of the Lower Shechinah (Malchut).
הַיְינוּ שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים בְּפוֹעַל גָּמוּר בְּנִגְלוֹת הַמַּעֲשִׂים כּוּלָּם
namely His divine presence dwelling in the lower realm in concrete actuality throughout all revealed deeds.
אֲבָל שְׁכִינְתָּא עִילָּאָה
However, the Higher Shechinah (Binah),
הַיְינוּ שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּהַנִּסְתָּרוֹת וּמַעֲמַקִּים
namely His divine presence within the hidden mysteries and inner depths,
וְהִיא הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁאֵין מִתְגַּלֵּית לַפּוֹעַל
which is Binah in the heart that is not externalized into physical action,
מִצִּידָּהּ הוּא הַתְּשׁוּבָה הַמְהַפֶּכֶת זְדוֹנוֹת לִזְכִיּוֹת
from its vantage point emerges that Repentance which transforms willful sins into merits,
וּדְהַכֹּל הָיָה שְׁמִיעָה בְּקוֹל ה
', revealing that everything was ultimately an answering of the voice of Hashem.
כֵּיוָן שֶׁהַמַּעֲמַקִּים דְּבוּקִים לְעוֹלָם בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הֲרֵי לְעוֹלָם הַחֵלֶק כָּלוּל בַּכֹּל
since the inner depths are eternally bound to Him, the individual part remaining forever subsumed within the Whole.

Tehillim 40:7 (and Midrash Tehillim 116:3, Shocher Tov): David sings — “זֶבַח וּמִנְחָה לֹא חָפַצְתָּ, אָזְנַיִם כָּרִיתָ לִּי” — “sacrifice and offering You did not desire; ears You have dug open for me.” Meforshim: the plain sense — God “opened my ears” to hear and obey His word, for obedience is more desired than sacrifice; the Midrash (Shocher Tov) reads it of the “ears above,” that “the ears on high are opened only for the need of Israel.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the “ear” is the “vessel of receiving,” which “in truth does not apply Above at all” — yet “for the sake of Israel,” Hashem “wrote of Himself” as one who receives their cry; this is the trait of Malchus, which “receives from those who crown Him,” for “without them there is no place for Malchus,” and hence “her feet descend to death.” 
Midrash Tehillim 116:3: אין האזנים של מעלה כרויות אלא לשמוע תפלתי בלבד, שנאמר אזנים כרית לי — “The ears above are opened only to hear my prayer,” spoken by Knesses Yisrael; the Midrash cites Tehillim 40:7. Rav Tzadok’s “לצורך ישראל” is a faithful paraphrase, not its verbatim wording.

their cry; this is the trait of Malchus, which “receives from those who crown Him,” for “without them there is no place for Malchus,” and hence “her feet descend to death.”

אין האזנים של מעלה כרויות אלא לשמוע תפלתי בלבד, שנאמר אזנים כרית לי — “The ears above are opened only to hear my prayer,” spoken by Knesses Yisrael; the Midrash cites Tehillim 40:7. Rav Tzadok’s “לצורך ישראל” is a faithful paraphrase, not its verbatim wording.

paragraphs.text:
R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §29): “the kabbalists wrote that the trait of day is male and the trait of night female; and therefore in the morning we say "emes" and in the evening "emunah"… because she receives the light.” Exactly the se’if: the receiving-power is not a defect introduced by the sin — it is a whole side of the created order, and emunah is its proper name. Izhbitz-Radzin parallel - Sod Yesharim, The Eighth Day of Pesach 2:1: Sod Yesharim describes Malchus as 'לית לה מגרמה כלום' - it possesses nothing of its own - and yet calls it the completion in which all the preceding sefirot are included. Its kingship appears from Israel's side when, within the darkness and concealment of this world, they freely crown Hashem instead of saying 'my power and the strength of my hand.' He then takes the thought one step further: even the human power to recognize and crown Hashem must itself be 'tithed' back to Him, for the deepest recognition is that the very capacity of bechirah and acknowledgment was illuminated by Hashem. This exactly complements R' Tzadok's paradox of the receiving-power. Malchus is not an independent recipient standing over against the Giver; its whole identity is reception, and nevertheless the created recipient contributes something genuinely desired - the freely offered coronation that can occur only in a world of concealment. Hence the language of 'receiving' Above is relational rather than a statement of Divine need. Hashem lacks nothing, yet He willed a created order in which Israel's response is meaningful. The same middah therefore has two edges: separated from its Source it becomes the fantasy of autonomous reception and 'her feet descend to death'; returned to its Source, its very emptiness becomes the vessel through which kingship is revealed. 
Kometz HaMinchah I §29; Sod Yesharim, Acharon Shel Pesach §2: המקובלים כתבו דמדת יום זכר ומדת לילה נקבה; ולכן בשחרית אמת, בערבית אמונה; כי מדת מלכות לית לה מגרמה כלום — Kometz explains day/night as giver/recipient; Sod Yesharim explains Malchus as lacking independent substance while Israel crowns Hashem. These are conceptual parallels, not a claim of literal Divine need.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: This receiving-power is the root of the sin — “hearing the voice of his wife,” taking pleasure in what stands below oneself. But in its root above it is good: the ears of Heaven were opened only for Israel’s need. Receiving does not truly apply Above, yet for Israel’s sake He wrote of Himself as receiving — this is Malchus, which receives from those who crown Him, and therefore “her feet descend to death.”

p: (סב) וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת נֶפֶשׁ שִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּמוּת כֹּחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה
And this is the root of the sanctity of Simeon's soul, which is the root-likeness of the supernal faculty of hearing,
דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשְּׂנוּאָה מִכָּל מָקוֹם שָׁמַע ה
'. for even though she was hated, Hashem nonetheless heard.
דְּמַה שֶּׁשְּׂנוּאָה הוּא רַק לְמַרְאִית עַיִן הַהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
For being hated was only to the outward appearance of manifest reality in this world,
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת "אָהַבְתִּי אֶתְכֶם אָמַר ה'" (מַלְאָכִי א, ב)
whereas in truth, "I have loved you, said Hashem" (Malachi 1:2),
וְלֹא יָרְדָה שִׂנְאָה אֶלָּא לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְאֶת עֵשָׂו שָׂנֵאתִי" (מַלְאָכִי א, ג)
and hatred descended solely upon the nations of the world, as it is said: "and Esau I hated" (v. 3).
וְכֵן אֵצֶל שׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל שְׂנוּאִים מַעֲשֵׂה עֵשָׂו
And likewise at the spiritual root of Israel, the deeds of Esau are abhorred, (.
בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכג),
(Bava Batra 123a),
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה נִדְמֶה לְשָׂנוּא
and on this account a person imagines himself despised,
כְּטַעַם "כָּל הַגָּדוֹל מֵחֲבֵירוֹ יִצְרוֹ גָּדוֹל (הֵימֶנּוּ)" ,
mirroring "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than he" (Sukkah 52a),
דִּכְפִי הַמַּעֲלָה כֵּן הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁבַּלֵּב כְּנֶגְדּוֹ הַמַּעֲלִים הַמַּעֲלָה כִּקְלִיפָּה הַסּוֹבֶבֶת לַפְּרִי
for corresponding to the spiritual stature is the counter-deficiency in the heart that veils the virtue like a shell surrounding the fruit,
דְּ"זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה עָשָׂה אֱלֹהִים" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, יד)
for "God has made the one corresponding to the other" (Ecclesiastes 7:14).
וְכֹחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה שֶׁבּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַטּוֹב שֶׁבָּאָדָם מִצַּד שֶׁהוּא אָדָם הַמְקַבֵּל
And within the faculty of hearing, which contains the root of human good inasmuch as man is a recipient.
בּוֹ הָיָה גַּם כֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחַ הָרָע
resided likewise the root of the power of evil.
וְכָל עֲמַל הָאָבוֹת וְהָאִמָּהוֹת הָיָה לְתַקֵּן חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן כַּיָּדוּעַ,
And the entire toil of the Patriarchs and Matriarchs was to rectify the sin of Adam the First as is known.
וּבְיִחוּד לֵאָה עֲקֶרֶת הַבַּיִת בֵּית יַעֲקֹב, כִּי בָהּ עִיקַּר הַתִּיקּוּן
and especially Leah, the mainstay of the House of Jacob, for in her lay the core of rectification.
דְּתִיקּוּן הַחֵטְא הוּא עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה וְעַל יְדֵי אֲנָשִׁים שֶׁהֱקִימוּ עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה
– For rectifying sin occurs through Repentance and through those who raised up the yoke of Repentance—,
זַרְעָא דְּדָוִד וּמָשִׁיחַ שֶׁהוּא גְּמַר הַתִּיקּוּן
the lineage of David and the Messiah who represents the final rectification.
לֹא עַל יְדֵי צַדִּיק גָּמוּר שֶׁלֹּא חָטָא מֵעוֹלָם
not through the perfectly righteous who never sinned.
וּתְחִלַּת הַתִּיקּוּן צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בְּכֹחַ וְאַחַר כָּךְ בַּפּוֹעַל
And the beginning of rectification must be in potential (be-kho'ach) and only afterward in actualization (ba-po'al),
וְלֵידַת רְאוּבֵן וְשִׁמְעוֹן הוּא הַתִּיקּוּן שֶׁבְּכֹחַ,
and the birth of Reuben and Simeon was the rectification in potential,
וְלֵוִי וִיהוּדָה הוּא בַּפּוֹעַל
while Levi and Judah represented it in actualization,
שֶׁכְּבָר נִסְתַּלֵּק הַשִּׂנְאָה בַּפּוֹעַל גַּם כֵּן דְּ"הַפַּעַם יִלָּוֶה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, לד),
the hatred having been removed in actualization as well, as in "now this time will my husband be joined (yillaveh) to me" (Genesis 29:34),
וּמִשִּׁבְטוֹ הָיָה עַמּוּד הַתּוֹרָה וְהָעֲבוֹדָה בְּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן
and from Levi's tribe arose the pillar of Torah and service in Moses and Aaron,
שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַתִּיקּוּן בַּפּוֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which was the beginning of practical rectification in this world.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַגְּמָר עַל יְדֵי מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד מִיהוּדָה
and subsequently the final completion through Mashiach ben David from Judah.
וְהַכֹּחַ הַהַתְחָלָה הוּא בִּרְאוּבֵן שֶׁהוּא הָרְאִיָּה וְהַהַשָּׂגָה דְּ"שִׁוִּיתִי ה' לְנֶגְדִּי (תָמִיד)",
And the initial potential resides in Reuben who is vision and the perception of "I have set Hashem before me always".
וּמִצִּידּוֹ הַתְחָלַת הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה בַּלֵּב
and from his aspect emerges the initial stirring of Repentance in the heart.
וְהַגְּמָר כְּשֶׁזָּכְתָה לְהוֹלִיד שִׁמְעוֹן
And the culmination of potential occurred when she merited to bear Simeon,
שֶׁהוֹצִיא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נֶפֶשׁ זֶה חֵלֶק אֱלֹהִי וְכֹחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה דְּמִמַּעַל
Hashem bringing forth this soul—a divine portion and the supernal faculty of hearing,
שֶׁכָּל שְׁמִיעוֹתָיו אֵינָן אֶלָּא לְצֹרֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד הַמַּעֲמַקִּים וְלֹא כְּפִי הַהִתְגַּלּוּת
whose listenings are solely for the sake of Israel from the perspective of inner depths rather than outward appearance,
שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל
which is not revealed in this world at all.
דְּאִם כֵּן הָיָה תִּיקּוּן הַגָּמוּר לְחֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן וּבִלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח
for had it been revealed, complete rectification of Adam's sin would have occurred, swallowing up death forever.

paragraphs.text: Malachi 1:3: completing the prophet’s paired word — “וְאֶת עֵשָׂו שָׂנֵאתִי, וָאָשִׂים אֶת הָרָיו שְׁמָמָה, וְאֶת נַחֲלָתוֹ לְתַנּוֹת מִדְבָּר” — “and Esav I have hated, and I made his mountains a desolation, and his heritage a place for the jackals of the wilderness.” Background: the counterpart to Malachi 1:2 (“I loved Yaakov”) — God’s love for Yaakov set against His rejection of Esav. Editorial distinction: Malachi 1:3 contrasts Esav with Yaakov; the extension that apparent rejection within Israel is only a surface phenomenon is Rav Tzadok’s interpretation, not a verbatim statement by the prophet. R’ Tzadok’s use: though Leah “appeared hated” to the outward eye, “in truth, I have loved you, says Hashem”; “hatred descended only to the nations” — “and Esav I have hated” — while within Israel’s own root it is only “the deeds of Esav” that are hated; so Leah’s “hatred” is mere surface, concealing a yet greater love.

R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §8): “They are not outwardly ‘in order,’ yet with all this they cleave to Hashem. And this is the sense of ‘In what way have You loved us,’ etc. — ‘and I loved Yaakov’ (Malachi 1:2) — without any reason at all, only that ‘this one is Mine and My portion.’” (This grounds the se’if’s reading: since ‘I loved Yaakov’ is a bond beyond all reason, the ‘hatred’ of Leah — ‘and Esav I hated’ — is only an outward appearance, belonging to the nations, never touching Israel, whom ‘Hashem heard.’)Chassidic parallel - Noam Elimelekh, Vayeshev 4:5: R' Elimelech of Lizhensk reads Leah's naming of her first four sons as four levels of the tzaddik. Reuven signifies the beloved 'son' who serves Hashem with love; Shimon is the next, more paradoxical level - a righteous person whose rebuke and truthfulness can make him hated by others, and precisely 'because he is hated' Hashem hears all his prayers, as in 'for Hashem has heard that I am hated.' Whatever one makes of that homiletic structure, its use of Shimon's name is directly relevant here: hatred is not evidence of distance from Hashem; it can coexist with, and even become the setting for, an especially intimate Divine hearing. R' Tzadok radicalizes the point by locating the hatred itself only in the outward appearance and by treating Shimon as the faculty of hearing in Knesses Yisrael. The Noam Elimelech helps show the Chassidic background of that move. 'Hearing' belongs exactly where visible approval is absent. Sight can be reassured by what appears before it; hearing must receive a voice from beyond the immediate surface. Thus Leah's 'ki senuah anochi' does not describe the ultimate relation but the condition in which the relation becomes audible. The higher the root, R' Tzadok says, the stronger the opposing shell; the parallel shows how the concealment of love can itself produce the cry and prayer by which the deeper relation is revealed. 
Resisei Layla §8; Noam Elimelech, Vayeshev 4:5: והגם שהן מדלגין ואין מסודר ... עם כל זה דבוקים בהשם יתברך; וזה טעם במה אהבתנו ... בלי שום טעם, רק שזה שלי ולחלקי — Rav Tzadok’s parallel concerns unconditional love despite obscured outward order. Noam Elimelech, in Vayeshev 4:5, speaks of the righteous person who can be hated by others precisely for reproving wrongdoing; the homilies are related but not identical.
