paragraphs.text: Izhbitz parallel - Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Shmini 7: The Ishbitzer warns that there is such a thing as anavah pesulah. He interprets those who left manna overnight as having regarded themselves as especially humble - perhaps, they thought, they were not worthy that Hashem should provide for them again tomorrow. Yet by singling themselves out as less worthy than Klal Yisrael they had actually left the place Hashem assigned them; what appeared to human eyes as modesty was not the humility Hashem desired. He contrasts this with David's 've'anochi tola'as,' a lowliness that did find favor before Hashem. This is an unusually close complement to R' Tzadok's 'nehog nesi'uscha beramim.' Once genuine humility has been clarified, refusing the responsibility and dignity attached to a Divine office can itself become a distorted humility. Rebbi could be 'anav' and still instruct his son to conduct the nesius with force, because anavah does not mean denying the truth of the role Hashem has given. It means that the role does not become a claim about one's independent self. The Ishbitzer's distinction also explains why outward appearances are insufficient: a deferential posture may conceal self-consciousness, while firm leadership may arise from complete bittul to the task. Thus the son can reveal the father's inward truth precisely by joining two qualities that look contradictory in this world - deep humility and unapologetic exercise of nesius - and showing that both can flow from one l'Shem Shamayim center. Source check: Mei HaShiloach I, Shemini, §7, says “וזה הוא ענוה פסולה שלא בחר בה השם יתברך” — “This is a defective humility that Hashem did not choose.” The Ishbitzer criticizes the self-exclusion of the men who kept manna overnight. The connection to Rebbi’s instruction about the Nesius is an editorial analogy, not a direct statement about Rebbi in Mei HaShiloach.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 11a–Sanhedrin 11b: The first letter is attributed to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and says, “it seemed proper to me.” The Gemara then says, “Come and see the difference between the forceful earlier ones and the humble later ones,” and brings Rabban Gamliel’s letter: “it seemed proper to me and to my colleagues.” It finally qualifies: “Perhaps this was after they deposed him.” The comparison concerns Rabban Gamliel and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel; it does not identify Rebbi as the more self-effacing correspondent. The two original forms can now be distinguished exactly: for RaShbaG (Sanhedrin 11a), “ושפרת מילתא באנפאי” — “and it appeared proper to me”; for Rabban Gamliel (11b), “ושפרא מילתא באנפאי ובאנפי חביריי” — “and it appeared proper to me and to my colleagues.” The Gemara itself cautions “דילמא בתר דעברוהו” — “perhaps this was after they deposed him.” These nuances belong to the primary text and must not be flattened into an unqualified contrast.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rebbi, his grandson, held fast to the same humility — “when Rebbi died, humility ceased” — yet told his son to conduct his office with authority, since his humility was already established and all knew his firmness was for Heaven. Through Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel the depths of Rabban Gamliel’s own heart were clarified. So his line’s nesius endured, and his deposition was “only for a moment.”

p: (ע) וְהִנֵּה שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחִסָּרוֹן הַיּוֹתֵר עָצוּם לְמַרְאִית עַיִן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּנַפְשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא הַחִסָּרוֹן דְּשִׁמְעוֹן
Now the most severe apparent deficiency to outward sight existing within Jewish souls is the deficiency of Simeon.
וְעַל הָאֱמֶת הוּא הַחִסָּרוֹן הַיּוֹתֵר קַל
Yet according to ultimate truth, it is the most superficial and lightest deficiency,
דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא נִכְתַּב בַּתּוֹרָה
which is why it was not recorded explicitly in the blessings and curses of the Torah,
כִּי עַל הָאֱמֶת אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה חִסָּרוֹן בָּזֶה בְּנַפְשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל
for in truth it is impossible for such a defect to exist in the souls of Israel at all.
אֶלָּא שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה צָרִיךְ לְבֵירוּרִים גְּדוֹלִים
only that this reality requires monumental spiritual clarifications.
וְעַל כֵּן אֵין מִיתָתוֹ בְּבֵית דִּין אֶלָּא מִקַּנַּאי הַפּוֹגֵעַ בּוֹ
And therefore his capital punishment is not executed by a formal court, but by the zealot who strikes him down (Sanhedrin 82a).
וְהַקַּנַּאי הוּא שֶׁזָּרִיז וּמָהִיר לִנְקוֹם וְאֵין מָתוּן בַּדָּבָר וּמְצַדֵּד לִזְכּוּת וּלְהַצִּיל כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹשִׂין הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין
and the zealot is swift and zealous to avenge without deliberating or seeking arguments for acquittal and rescue as the Sanhedrin would do.
וְהַבֵּירוּר הַשָּׁלֵם הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה "יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן",
And the complete clarification occurs when there arises 'Joseph the son of Simeon',
שֶׁהַבֵּן יְגַלֶּה הַמַּעֲמַקִּים שֶׁבָּאָב
wherein the son unveils the hidden depths within the father,
כַּאֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה הַבֵּן הֵיפֶךְ לוֹ מַמָּשׁ
when the son stands as the exact polar counterpart to him.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא מוּגְדָּר בָּזֶה בְּתַכְלִית
which is the spiritual root of Joseph who is guarded in this boundary with ultimate perfection.
וְעַל כֵּן סְתָם בֵּן הַמְבָרֵר אָבִיו יֵשׁ לִקְרוֹתוֹ עַל דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל "יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן",
Therefore any typical son who clarifies and vindicates his father is appropriately termed parabolically 'Joseph son of Simeon',
כִּי בֵּירוּר זֶה הוּא בֵּירוּר בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל
for this clarification is universal across all Israel.
שֶׁהֲרֵי חִסָּרוֹן זֶה אֵינוֹ בְּעֶצֶם בְּמִי שֶׁהוּא מִשָּׁרְשָׁא וְגִזְעָא קַדִּישָׁא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
since this defect is not essential to anyone who stems from the holy root and stock of Israel.
וְלָכֵן נָקְטוּ לְמָשָׁל הַשֵּׁם "יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן" כְּשֶׁדִּבְּרוּ מִשְּׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם הַשָּׁוִין בִּשְׁמָן
And therefore the Sages selected the name 'Joseph son of Simeon' as their paradigm when discussing two men with identical names.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּשְׁנָה בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (קעב.) וּבַגְּמָרָא שָׁם (קסז:) וּבִבְכוֹרוֹת (מח)
as stated in the Mishnah in Bava Batra (172a), in the Gemara there (167b), and in Bekhorot (48a);
דְּנִרְאָה דְּהוּא שֵׁם הַמָּצוּי
where it appears as though it were a common name;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין זֶה עַצְמוֹ שֵׁם מָצוּי בַּפּוֹעַל
and even though this specific combination was not common in practical reality,
הֵם נָקְטוּ לְמָשָׁל מַה שֶּׁהוּא רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ.
They selected as their paradigm that which is destined and fitting to be in the spiritual root.
וּכְפִי דַּרְכָּם לִתְפּוֹס לְמָשָׁל שְׁמוֹת הַשְּׁבָטִים שֶׁהֵם רָאשֵׁי הָאֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית
And according to their method of adopting the names of the tribes who are the heads of the Jewish nation,
רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת שֵׁם בֵּן וָאָב
it is fitting that the pairing of son and father,
רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר בֵּן הַמְבָרֵר הָאָב שֶׁעַל זֶה הוּא עִיקַּר עִנְיַן הַבָּנִים
meaning the son who vindicates the father, which is the underlying purpose of childbearing,
הַמָּצוּי הַרְבֵּה "יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן",
should be identified recurrently as 'Joseph son of Simeon'.
רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר הַשֵּׁמוֹת יוֹסֵף וְשִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁל הַשְּׁבָטִים יִהְיֶה זֶה בֵּן לָזֶה וּמְבָרֵר אֶת זֶה
meaning the tribal names Joseph and Simeon standing as son to father, the one clarifying the other.
וְלֹא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בַּפּוֹעַל לְדוֹרוֹת שְׁמוֹת בְּנֵי אָדָם כֵּן
And it does not mean that among ordinary people throughout generations their names were always literally so,
דְּלֹא כָּל שִׁמְעוֹן וְיוֹסֵף שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הֵם דּוּגְמַת הַשְּׁבָטִים
for not every Simeon and Joseph in the world mirrors the Patriarchal tribes.
וּפוֹק חֲזֵי כַּמָּה יוֹסֵף אִיכָּא בְּשׁוּקָא שֶׁאֵינָם גְּדוּרִים בַּעֲרָיוֹת כְּיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק
and go forth and see how many Josephs exist in the marketplace who are not guarded against immorality like Joseph the Righteous.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם וַדַּאי שְׁמָא גָּרֵים (בְּרָכוֹת ז:) לִהְיוֹת לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת מַה לְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ שְׁמוֹ,
And even though a name certainly exerts spiritual influence (Berakhot 7b) so that one has an affinity with his namesake's root.
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין הַבֵּירוּר בִּשְׁמוֹת יוֹסֵף וְשִׁמְעוֹן בְּעָלְמָא
nonetheless the essential clarification is not confined to the literal names Joseph and Simeon.
רַק לְדוּגְמָא נְקָטוּהָ מִשְּׁמוֹת הַשְּׁבָטִים
Rather, as an illustrative paradigm they drew it from the names of the tribes,
וְיִהְיוּ הַשֵּׁמוֹת אֵיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שֵׁם הַמָּצוּי
and whatever the names may be in any given era,
דְּהַיְינוּ הַבֵּירוּר הַמָּצוּי בֵּין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
namely that prevalent clarification recurring among the children of Israel,
לִהְיוֹת עַל יְדֵי זֶה מָצוּי שְׁמוֹת אָב וּבֵן שָׁוִין
bringing about identical father-and-son name pairings,
כִּי הַשֵּׁם הוּא עִיקַּר הַנֶּפֶשׁ וְהַחַיּוּת כַּיָּדוּעַ,
for the name is the core of the soul and its vitality as is known,
רָאוּי לְהַמְשִׁילוֹ וּלְכַנּוֹתוֹ.
It is fitting to designate and typify it thus.

paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 172a (Mishnah; the Gemara there 167b; and Bechoros 48a): the Mishnah and Gemara treat the case of two men in one town who bear the same name (and the safeguards required for their documents) — the source for the point that distinct people may share an identical name. Original Mishnah, Bava Basra 172a: “שנים שהיו בעיר אחת, שם אחד יוסף בן שמעון ושם אחר יוסף בן שמעון” — “Two people in one town, one named Yosef ben Shimon and the other likewise named Yosef ben Shimon.” The Mishnah addresses potentially ambiguous legal documents. Rav Tzadok’s explanation of the names’ spiritual significance is his interpretation, not a statement attributed to that Mishnah.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 7b (“shema garim”): amid the Gemara’s expositions of names as portents (Reuven, Ruth, Yehudah), it asks, “from where that the name has an effect shema garim? R’ Eliezer said: the verse states, ‘go, see the works of Hashem, who has set desolations שַׁמּוֹת in the earth’ (Tehillim 46:9) — do not read שַׁמּוֹת shamos, desolations but שֵׁמוֹת sheimos, names” — The Gemara establishes that names can carry meaning, but it does not establish how parents choose every name or itself prove that each naming occurs with ruach hakodesh, which would require separate evidence. For a concrete example of Rabbi Meir examining names see Yoma 83b: Rabbi Meir suspected the innkeeper “Kidor” based on “ki dor tahpuchos heimah” (Devarim 32:20), and proven right. R’ Tzadok’s use: since “the name is the essence of the soul and the vitality,” the Sages’ stock pair “Yosef ben Shimon” is chosen not for its frequency in the market but for its root meaning. Rav Tzadok’s direct parallel follows in Pri Tzadik, Korach 8:4): “והנה בש״ס מצינו (ב״ב קע״ב.) שנים שהיו בעיר אחת שם אחד יוסף בן שמעון ... וזה שתפס למשל יוסף בן שמעון אף דבשבט שמעון היה רוב כ״ד אלף אשר מתו על דבר פעור מכל מקום באמת הוא גם כן נקרא ע״ש יוסף בחינת צדיק.” Translation: “The Talmud’s example is two men named Yosef ben Shimon; even though many from Shimon fell at Peor, Shimon is nonetheless called by Yosef’s name in the aspect of tzaddik.” This is Rav Tzadok’s own direct parallel in Korach §8, not a quotation from Berachos 7b.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Shimon’s deficiency looks the severest in the souls of Israel, yet is truly the lightest — which is why it is unwritten in the Torah, since in truth it cannot exist in a Jewish soul at all. Hence its penalty comes not from a court but from a zealot, who does not deliberate in order to acquit. The complete clarification is “Yosef ben Shimon” — the son revealing his father’s depths precisely by being his opposite.

p: (עא) וְיֵשׁ לְהוֹסִיף דְּמַה שֶּׁאֵין מָצוּי אוֹתָן שֵׁמוֹת בַּפּוֹעַל כָּל כָּךְ,
And it may be added that the reason these names are not so prevalent in actual practice
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבֵּירוּר זֶה בָּרוּר
is because in truth, even though this spiritual clarification is entirely lucid
הַיְינוּ מִצַּד שָׁרְשֵׁי הַנְּפָשׁוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ.
specifically from the perspective of the primordial soul-roots of the children of Israel in ultimate truth;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ גָּלוּי מַמָּשׁ בַּפּוֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
nonetheless it is not openly manifest in concrete actuality within this world.
וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּגֵיהִנָּם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לָא מִבַּשְׁקַר לֵיהּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק ב דְּ
and even in Gehenna Abraham our father, peace be upon him, does not recognize him, as they stated in the second chapter of Eruvin (19a)!
דְּכָל זְמַן שִׁימּוּשׁ הַאי עָלְמָא, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ בְּחִירָה וְשָׂכָר וָעוֹנֶשׁ,
For as long as the temporal function of this world endures, wherein free choice and reward and punishment exist,
מִשְׁפַּט עוֹלַם הַנְּשָׁמוֹת הוּא כְּפִי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
the judgment of the world of souls corresponds to man's active spiritual exertion in this world,
מִצַּד הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת קוֹמַת הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַפּוֹעֶלֶת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁבָּהּ הַבְּחִירָה
from the vantage point of the expansion of the soul's functional stature operating in this world in which free choice resides.
וְלֹא עַל פִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם הַמִּתְגַּלֶּה בַּבָּנִים שֶׁאֵין תָּלוּי בִּבְחִירָה
and not according to the hidden root that becomes unveiled in descendants, which does not depend upon free choice.
אֶלָּא שֶׁבְּכָל עֲוֹנוֹת דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מַצִּילָם
Except that regarding all other transgressions, Abraham our father, peace be upon him, rescues them,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּצַּד שֶׁהוּא נִיכָּר עֲדַיִן לְזֶרַע אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
meaning that inasmuch as he is still visibly identifiable as the seed of Abraham our father, peace be upon him,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ יַהֲדוּת גָּמוּר
which means there abides within him a complete, uncorrupted root of Jewishness,
אֵין לֶעָוֹן תְּפִיסָה בּוֹ בְּעֶצֶם רַק כְּהוּצֵי הַסּוֹבְבִים לַאָסָא
the iniquity has no essential grip upon his core, being merely like briers encircling the myrtle;
עַל כֵּן עַל יְדֵי הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נִיצּוֹל מִדִּינָהּ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם
therefore, through the ancestral root of Abraham our father, peace be upon him, he is delivered from the judgment of Gehenna
גַּם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּשֶׁמִּתְגַּלֶּה וּמִתְבָּרֵר שָׁרְשׁוֹ בִּבְנוֹ.
even in this world when his root is revealed and clarified within his son.
אֲבָל בּוֹעֵל אֲרַמִּית שֶׁקְּשׁוּרָה בּוֹ כַּכֶּלֶב
However, regarding one who cohabits with an Aramean woman, where she clings to him like a dog (Eruvin 19a),
כִּי מִצַּד גִּילּוּי הַחֵטְא נִרְאֶה כִּיצִיאָה מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת
because from the overt manifestation of the sin it appears as an absolute departure from the root of Jewishness,
שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵין זֶה רָאוּי שֶׁיֵּאָרַע לְמִי שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל
for it is entirely unfitting that such an atrocity should ever befall one who stems from the holy root of Israel;
דְּעַל כֵּן אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לָא מִבַּשְׁקַר לֵיהּ שֶׁהוּא מִזַּרְעוֹ כְּלָל
wherefore Abraham our father, peace be upon him, does not recognize him as his seed at all.
וּכְאִלּוּ אֵין בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ נֶעְלָם דְּיַהֲדוּת כְּלָל
as though he possessed no latent, concealed root of Jewishness whatsoever.
עַל כֵּן אֵין מִתְגַּלֶּה בַּפּוֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שָׁרְשׁוֹ הַנֶּעְלָם בִּבְנוֹ גַּם כֵּן
Therefore his hidden root is likewise not revealed in actual practice within this world through his son.
דְּאָז הָיָה גַּם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מַכִּירוֹ בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ וּמַצִּילוֹ מִדִּין שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם
for had that been so, Abraham our father would have recognized him through his root and rescued him from the punishment of Gehenna.
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּצַּד מִשְׁפַּט הַגֵּיהִנָּם בְּגִלּוּי דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ אַחַר פְּעוּלַּת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ נִיכָּר בָּזֶה
Rather, because from the perspective of Gehenna's judgment manifest in this world—which proceeds strictly according to practical worldly deeds—the root is unrecognizable in this state.
אִם כֵּן אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לִהְיוֹת בֵּירוּר גָּלוּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בִּבְנוֹ גַּם כֵּן
consequently it is impossible for him to achieve an overt, visible clarification in this world through his son either.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (פב)
And therefore they stated in Sanhedrin (82a)
דְּעָנְשׁוֹ דְּ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לוֹ עֵר בַּחֲכָמִים וּבֵן מַגִּישׁ מִנְחָה",
that his punishment is: "he shall have neither one waking among the sages nor a son presenting an offering",
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ בֵּן הַמְבָרֵר שָׁרְשׁוֹ וּמְזַכֵּהוּ בְּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים
meaning he shall have no son who vindicates his root and confers merit upon him through good deeds,
"בְּרָא מְזַכֵּי אַבָּא"
'a son confers merit upon a father' (Sanhedrin 104a).
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל זֶה מִצַּד הַנִּגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
Yet nonetheless all of this applies solely from the perspective of the manifest reality in this world;
אֲבָל יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא וְלֹא נִמְנָה בְּאוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
whereas he retains an eternal share in the World to Come and was not enumerated among those who forfeit their portion in the World to Come.
כִּי מִצַּד הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב הַנֶּעְלֶמֶת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אַדְּרַבָּה שָׁרְשׁוֹ מְבוֹרָר לְגַמְרֵי
for from the perspective of Binah in the heart, which remains veiled in this world, his holy root is on the contrary completely elucidated.
וַחֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה דִּבְּרוּ כְּפִי הָאֲמִיתּוּת
And our Sages of blessed memory spoke in accord with ultimate transcendent truth,
וְנָקְטוּ לְמָשָׁל כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא הַבֵּירוּר הַמָּצוּי בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ
and chose as their paradigm that clarification which exists in ultimate truth.
וְלֹא כְּפִי הַבֵּירוּר הַנִּגְלֶה בְּעוֹלַם הַדִּמְיוֹן
and not according to the superficial clarification manifest in the world of illusion.
וְכָל דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים מְלֵאִים חָכְמָה גְּדוֹלָה
And all teachings of the Sages are replete with profound wisdom,
אִם בְּעִנְיַן הַלִּימּוּד וְהַיְדִיעָה לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם וּמֵבִין מִדַּעְתּוֹ,
both regarding conceptual study and insight for a disciple of the wise who understands from his own discernment,
וְאִם לְעִנְיַן הַהַמְתָּקָה בֶּאֱמֶת
and regarding the actual ontological sweetening of stern judgments;
כִּי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה יֵשׁ לָהֶם כֹּחַ הַפּוֹעֵל בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת
for words of Torah possess an active metaphysical power across all realms.
שֶׁכֻּלָּם מִתְנַהֲגִים עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה הַיּוֹצְאָה מִפִּי חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָאֲמִיתִּיִּים
which are all directed according to the Torah issuing forth from the mouth of authentic sages of Israel.
וְעַל כֵּן לְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים מַרְפֵּא וּמַמְתִּיק לְכָל הַדִּינִים עַל פִּי לְשׁוֹנָם לְבַד כִּי כָּל שִׂיחָתָם תּוֹרָה
Therefore the speech of the wise heals and sweetens all severe judgments through their words alone, for all their discourse is Torah;
וְנִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁעַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ אֱמֶת
and it was clarified that according to the Torah concerning which truth is inscribed,
שֶׁבָּהּ נִתְגַּלָּה וְנִתְבָּרֵר הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ הוּא כֵן
wherein ultimate truth is disclosed and substantiated, such is indeed the reality,
וְעַל כֵּן נָקְטוּ גַּם בָּזֶה לְמָשָׁל "יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן" כְּפִי הַבֵּירוּר הָאֲמִיתִּי
and therefore they selected in this context as an illustration 'Joseph son of Simeon' according to authentic clarification.
לְלַמֵּד אַגַּב אוֹרְחָא לַבָּאִים לִלְמוֹד וּלְהַמְתִּיק כָּל חֲטָאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַיּוֹתֵר חֲמוּרִים בְּשָׁרְשָׁן
to teach by the way unto those who come to study how to sweeten all the most severe sins of Israel at their root.

Sanhedrin 82a: “אם תלמיד חכם הוא לא יהיה לו ער בחכמים ועונה בתלמידים אם כהן הוא לא יהיה לו בן מגיש מנחה לה׳ צבאות” — “If he is a Torah scholar, he shall have no awakened one among the sages and none who answers among the students; if he is a priest, he shall have no son offering a meal-offering to the Lord of hosts”. This expounds Malachi 2:12. The adjacent exposition of Deuteronomy 23:18 concerns prostitution; it is not the Gemara’s prooftext identifying this particular act. Rav Tzadok next qualifies the punishment as this world’s revealed order, rather than loss of the ultimate Jewish root.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 104a (“bra mezakeh abba”): explaining why the Mishnah omits the wicked Amon from the kings with no share in the World to Come (out of honor for his righteous son Yoshiyahu), yet lists Menasheh despite his righteous father Chizkiyahu, the Gemara rules: “the son confers merit upon the father bra mezakeh abba, but the father does not confer merit upon the son, as it is written, ‘and none delivers from My hand’ (Devarim 32:39) — Avraham does not deliver Yishmael, and Yitzchak does not deliver Esav, from the judgment.” Meforshim: Rashi — a father is credited for having raised a worthy son, but cannot shield an unworthy one from his own judgment. R’ Tzadok’s use: the punishment of the boel aramis is that he has “no son who offers a meal-offering” — no son to “clarify his root and grant him merit,” for “a son grants merit to a father”; his concealed Jewish root, which would otherwise surface in such a son, cannot be revealed in this world’s outward order — though from the side of the hidden Binah it remains entirely intact.

paragraphs.text: Mishlei 12:18: “יֵשׁ בּוֹטֶה כְּמַדְקְרוֹת חָרֶב, וּלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים מַרְפֵּא” — “there is one whose rash speech is like the piercings of a sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Ralbag — reckless words wound like a blade, whereas the measured speech of the wise soothes and heals; the marpei (healing) is set against the madkros charev (sword-thrusts) of careless talk. R’ Tzadok’s use: since “words of Torah have an efficacious power in all the worlds,” which conduct themselves “according to the Torah that issues from the mouth of the true Sages of Israel,” their very expression “heals and sweetens all the judgments” — so that when the Sages framed even the boel aramis by way of the example “Yosef ben Shimon,” which he treats in terms of ultimate truth rather than visible conduct. Original Izhbitz–Radzin parallel: Tiferet Yosef, Nasso (opening teaching), reporting “כמו שביאר כבוד אזמו״ר זללה״ה”: “כי באדם יש נפש רוח ונשמה, ולהנשמה אין שום חטא ופגם מגיע ... ורוח רומז לכח הבחירה של האדם ... יכול האדם לבחור בטוב ולמאס ברע.” Translation: “A person possesses nefesh, ruach and neshamah; no sin or blemish reaches the neshamah ... but ruach represents the capacity of choice, by which one may choose good and reject evil.” This original explicitly preserves responsibility for choices, while distinguishing them from the soul’s deeper purity. It is a conceptual comparison, not an explanation given by Mishlei itself.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Why the names are not literally common: the clarification is real at the root of the souls, but is not revealed here in fact — even in Gehinnom, Avraham does not recognize one who cohabited with a gentile. This world’s judgment follows a person’s deeds, where choice lies, and not the hidden root revealed in sons. With ordinary sins the Jewish root holds and Avraham saves; this one looks like a departure from Jewishness, so no son emerges here to clarify him.

p: (עב) וּבֶאֱמֶת עִיקַּר שׁוֹרֶשׁ שִׁמְעוֹן הוּא בְּהֵיפֶךְ,
And in truth, the essential root of Simeon is quite the opposite:
תַּכְלִית הַהַבְדָּלָה מִן הָעַמִּים
the ultimate pinnacle of separation from the gentile nations;
דְּעַל כֵּן הוּא נִכְלָל בִּיהוּדָה שֶׁבּוֹ תַּכְלִית הַהַבְדָּלָה
which is why he is subsumed within Judah in whom resides total separation,
דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָאִים כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל "יְהוּדִים",
wherefore all the Jewish people are titled 'Yehudim' (Jews):
וּבְפֶרֶק קַמָּא דִּ
and in the first chapter of Megillah (13a):
"דְּכָל הַכּוֹפֵר בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה נִקְרָא יְהוּדִי".
'Whoever repudiates idolatry is termed a Yehudi.'
וּבְשִׁמְעוֹן הַהַבְדָּלָה עוֹד יוֹתֵר
And within Simeon the separation is even more absolute,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד: "דַּה' בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ וְאֵין עִמּוֹ אֵל נֵכָר" (דְּבָרִים לב, יב),
as it will be in the ultimate future: 'Hashem alone shall lead him, and there is no alien god with Him' (Deuteronomy 32:12).
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא עִיקַּר הַמְקַנֵּא עַל עִנְיַן דִּינָה וְהָרַג לִשְׁכֶם
wherefore he was the primary zealot avenging the defilement of Dinah who slew Shechem.
וְנִטְפַּל אֵלָיו לֵוִי שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן גָּלוּהַּ לְגַמְרֵי לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְשָׁעָתוֹ,
And Levi joined him, who was likewise entirely dedicated unto Hashem, blessed be He, at that hour.
וְלֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי" (תְּהִלִּים קמז, כ) דְּאֵין כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם אֶלָּא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
'He did not do so unto any nation' (Psalms 147:20), for there are no priests and Levites except within Israel.
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֶצְלוֹ הוּא רַק מִצִּידּוֹ,
Except that with Levi this operates exclusively from his distinct tribal role,
שֶׁהוּא נִבְדָּל גַּם מִכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּאֵין כֻּלָּם כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם
being distinguished even from the rest of Israel since not all are priests and Levites.
עַל כֵּן מַדְרֵגָתוֹ גְּלוּיָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
therefore his spiritual level is openly manifest in this world.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן שִׁמְעוֹן דְּהוּא כְּאַחַד שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
Not so Simeon, who is an ordinary one among the tribes of Israel,
וּמַדְרֵגָתוֹ הוּא מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל
and his spiritual level represents that which resides within the root-holiness of all Israel;
וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּבְדָּלִים כָּל כָּךְ לְגַמְרֵי בְּלִי שׁוּם מְצִיאוּת חִבּוּר זֶה אֵינוֹ גָּלוּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and that the collective of Israel should be so utterly detached without any possibility of assimilation is not manifest in this world,
שֶׁהֲרֵי מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִרְאֶה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל לָבוֹא אֶל הַגּוֹיָה וּלְהִתְחַבֵּר עִמָּהּ.
For from the perspective of this world it outwardly appears possible for any Jew to cohabit with a gentile woman and attach himself unto her.
אֲבָל שִׁמְעוֹן הוּא מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחַ זֶה הַמּוּבְדָּל לְגַמְרֵי
However, Simeon stems from the root of this absolute, unbridgeable segregation,
דְּעִיקַּר זֶה הוּא יִחוּד כֹּחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
the essence of which is the exclusive consecration of the faculty of hearing unto Hashem, blessed be He;
דְּעִיקַּר שְׁמִיעָה לְשׁוֹן קַבָּלָה
for the primary meaning of hearing denotes reception,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּתוּרְגָּם כֵּן כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים שְׁמִיעָה בִּלְשׁוֹן קַבָּלַת דְּבָרִים
and as hearing is frequently rendered in the Aramaic Targum as accepting words.
כִּי הָאֹזֶן עָשׂוּי כִּכְלִי קִיבּוּל, וְזֶהוּ לְקַבֵּל בְּתוֹכוֹ מֵהַזּוּלַת
for the ear is structured as a receptive vessel, designed to take in from another.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר אֵין מְקַבֵּל אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְקַבֵּל וּמַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁפִּיעַ
And when a person receives nothing except that which it is Hashem's will that he receive and that which Hashem bestows,
בָּזֶה הוּא נִבְדָּל לְגַמְרֵי מִבְּנֵי נֵכָר
through this he becomes utterly separated from alien peoples,
דְּזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֵשֶׁת חַיִל הַמּוּבְדֶּלֶת מֵאֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים
for this is the root of the Congregation of Israel, the Woman of Valor set apart from the Harlot Woman.
שֶׁאֵין מְקַבֶּלֶת אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁדּוֹדָהּ נוֹתֵן לָהּ, לֹא זוּלַת זֶה כְּלָל
who receives solely that which her Beloved grants her, and nothing whatsoever from another.
וִיהוּדָה שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִצַּד הַקַּבָּלָה הַנִּגְלֵית בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And Judah, from whom descended King David, peace be upon him, who is the root of the Congregation of Israel, embodies reception manifest in this world.
וְעַל כֵּן הֶעֱמִיד מְלָכִים
wherefore he produced monarchs.
וְהַמֶּלֶךְ עִיקָּרוֹ לִהְיוֹת מַשְׁפִּיעַ לָעָם וְהֵם מְקַבְּלִים מִמֶּנּוּ,
And the primary role of a king is to bestow upon the nation while they receive from him,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם הוּא מְקַבֵּל מֵהֶם, כִּי כָּל מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ הוּא מֵהֶם
and nonetheless he too receives from them, for all that he possesses is from them,
וְכֵן עִיקַּר מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ וּכְבוֹדוֹ הוּא מְקַבֵּל מֵהֶם מַה שֶּׁהֵם מַחֲזִיקִים אוֹתוֹ לְמֶלֶךְ.
And similarly the essence of his sovereignty and honor he receives from them through their upholding him as king.
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד דְּבֵיקוּת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת
And this corresponds to the cleaving of the children of Israel unto the attribute of His divine Sovereignty which constitutes Malchut;
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה יֵשׁ מְצִיאוּת לָעַמִּים גַּם כֵּן
and from this perspective there exists a place for the nations as well,
רַק שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִכְנָעִין לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמְקַבְּלִים מֵהֶם
merely that they be subjugated unto Israel and receive from them.
כִּי יֵשׁ לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִדַּת הַהַשְׁפָּעָה גַּם כֵּן לַזּוּלַת וְהַיְינוּ לָעַמִּים הַנַּעֲשִׂים גֵּרִים גְּרוּרִים
for the children of Israel possess the capacity of bestowing unto others as well, namely unto the nations who become attached converts.
אֲבָל שׁוֹרֶשׁ שִׁמְעוֹן הוּא הַקַּבָּלָה לְבַד שֶׁאֵין מוּכָן לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ כְּלָל
However, the root of Simeon is pure reception alone, wholly unsuited to bestow externally.
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם כֵּן לֹא הֶעֱמִיד מֶלֶךְ וְשׁוֹפֵט שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מִדַּת הַהַשְׁפָּעָה גַּם כֵּן
and therefore he likewise produced neither king nor judge, within whom the capacity to bestow must also reside.

It illuminates only Rav Tzadok’s cited principle that a Yehudi rejects avodah zarah.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 34 (Shimon and Levi at Shechem): after Shechem son of Chamor defiled Dinah, “the two sons of Yaakov, Shimon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword and came upon the city unawares, and slew every male” (34:25), “and Chamor and Shechem his son they slew by the sword, and took Dinah from Shechem’s house” (34:26); to Yaakov’s rebuke they answered, “should he treat our sister like a harlot?” (34:31). Meforshim: Rashi — they are called “Dinah’s brothers” because they endangered themselves for her; the Ramban weighs at length the justice of the deed; and Yaakov, on his deathbed, still censures their zeal — “Shimon and Levi are brothers, instruments of violence… cursed be their wrath” (Bereishis 49:5–7). R’ Tzadok’s use: Shimon is “the principal zealot mekane in the matter of Dinah,” for his very soul-root is “the utmost separation from the peoples” — he could not bear that a daughter of Israel be joined to Shechem the Canaanite; and Levi “joined nilveh him,” though Levi’s separateness is “revealed in this world” (Kohanim and Levi’im set apart even from Israel), whereas Shimon’s — the hidden holiness of all Israel’s utter separateness — stays concealed here.

paragraphs.text: Izhbitz–Radzin parallel — Mei HaShiloach I, VeZos HaBerachah §14: “שמע ה׳ קול יהודה ... ושמעון הוא אודני דשכינתא ויהודא הוא ליבא דשכינתא ... ששבט שמעון ישמע לקול יהודה.” Translation: “Hear, Hashem, the voice of Yehudah ... Shimon represents the ears of the Shechinah, Yehudah her heart ... and Shimon must listen to Yehudah’s voice.” The Ishbitzer explains that Shimon continually requires clarification. Here the parallel illuminates Rav Tzadok’s distinction between Shimon’s hidden faculty of receiving and Yehudah’s revealed role. It is an explicit original Izhbitzer parallel, not Rav Tzadok’s own Hebrew formulation.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Shimon’s root is in fact the opposite — the utmost separation from the peoples — and so he is folded into Yehudah, in whom that separation is complete: “whoever repudiates idolatry is called a Yehudi.” In Shimon it is greater still, which is why he was the zealot who slew Shechem. His essence is hearing, which is pure receiving — the ear being a vessel that takes only what is given it.

p: (עג) וְכָל זֶה הוּא הַכֹּל רַק מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דְּיֵשׁ לְאֵיזֶה נֶפֶשׁ הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לַקָּטָן מִמֶּנּוּ,
And all of this applies exclusively from the perspective of this world wherein a soul possesses an elevated rank enabling him to bestow upon one lesser than he;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לֶעָתִיד כְּשֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה מָחוֹל לַצַּדִּיקִים יִתְגַּלֶּה מַדְרֵגַת הָעִגּוּלִים
which will not be so in the future when He forms a circle dance for the righteous (Ta'anit 31a) revealing the dimension of Circles.
שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם הַמָּחוֹל שֶׁעוֹמְדִים הַכֹּל בְּעִגּוּל, לֹא יְהֵא חִלּוּק מַדְרֵגוֹת וְהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת כְּלָל
wherein anywhere in a dance where all stand in an equidistant circle, there are no hierarchical gradations or status-distinctions whatsoever.
כִּי אָז "לֹא יְלַמְּדוּ עוֹד אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ" (יִרְמְיָה לא, לג) וְלֹא יְקַבְּלוּ אֶחָד מֵחֲבֵירוֹ כְּלָל
For then 'they shall teach no more every man his neighbor' (Jeremiah 31:34) and will receive nothing from one another,
רַק כֻּלָּם יְקַבְּלוּ בְּשָׁוֶה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְבַד
rather all will receive equally from Hashem, blessed be He, alone.
וְלֹא יִהְיֶה מְצִיאוּת לְכֹחַ הַהַשְׁפָּעָה לַזּוּלַת
and there will be no role for the power of bestowing unto another.
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא יִהְיֶה מְצִיאוּת לַגּוֹיִם גַּם כֵּן
And therefore there will be no enduring existence for the pagan nations either,
כִּי הֵם אֵין יְכוֹלִים לְקַבֵּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַצְמוֹ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לוֹ,
since they cannot receive directly from Hashem Himself, having no intrinsic connection to Him,
רַק יְכוֹלִים לְקַבֵּל מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
being able to receive only through the mediation of Israel,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרַשׁ תְּהִלִּים – שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב כא) דְּמָשִׁיחַ יָבוֹא לְלַמֵּד וְלִמְסוֹר אֵיזֶה מִצְווֹת לַגּוֹיִם
and as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Shocher Tov, Psalm 21) that the Messiah will come to instruct and transmit certain commandments to the nations,
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה יִהְיֶה לוֹ תֹּאַר מֶלֶךְ.
and from that aspect he will bear the title of king over them.
אֲבָל לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא דְּאָז "ה' בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ" (דְּבָרִים לב, יב) לֹא יִהְיֶה לָהֶם מְצִיאוּת כְּלָל
However, in the World to Come when 'Hashem alone shall lead him' (Deuteronomy 32:12), they will possess no existence whatsoever.
כִּי לֹא יִהְיֶה רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁפִּיעַ וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַבְּלִים
for there will be solely Hashem bestowing and the children of Israel receiving.
וְזֶהוּ כֹּחַ שִׁמְעוֹן הַקַּבָּלָה לְבַד, דְּלֵית לֵיהּ מִגַּרְמֵיהּ כְּלוּם
And this is the distinct power of Simeon: pure reception alone, possessing nothing of his own.
דָּבָר זֶה נִכְלַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בִּיהוּדָה, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ הִתְגַּלּוּת בַּפּוֹעַל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ עֲדַיִן
this reality being subsumed in this world within Judah, having no independent outward manifestation yet.
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא נֶעְלָם מוֹשֵׁךְ אַחֲרָיו חִסָּרוֹן
And from this circumstance—that in this world it is concealed—it draws an apparent deficiency after it,
שֶׁנִּרְאָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הֵיפֶךְ מִכֹּחַ זֶה
appearing in this world as the polar opposite of this holy power;
וְנִמְצָא אֵין הַחִסָּרוֹן נִמְשָׁךְ בְּעֶצֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ שִׁמְעוֹן כְּלָל
and consequently the deficiency does not proceed from the essential root of Simeon at all,
שֶׁהֲרֵי הוּא אַדְּרַבָּה הֵיפֶךְ זֶה
for he is, on the contrary, the absolute antithesis of this.
רַק מִצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁל מַדְרֵגָתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִמְשָׁךְ הַחִסָּרוֹן לְמַרְאִית עַיִן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַנִּגְלֶה
rather, solely from the concealment of his spiritual level in this world does the deficiency project superficially to the sight of this manifest realm.
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לְהִכָּתֵב עָלָיו הַחִסָּרוֹן בַּתּוֹרָה
Therefore it was impossible for the deficiency to be explicitly inscribed against him in the Torah.
שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵין הַחִסָּרוֹן בּוֹ וּמִצִּידּוֹ כְּלָל
since the flaw does not reside within him nor originate from his side at all.
וְנִתְגַּלָּה הַחִסָּרוֹן קוֹדֶם כְּנִיסָה לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
And this deficiency was outwardly revealed prior to the entry into the Land of Israel,
כִּי אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הַהֵיפוּךְ מִזֶּה
because the Land of Israel is the very antithesis of this mixture.
דְּעִנְיַן אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא הַמְיוּחָד לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד בְּלֹא תַּעֲרוֹבוֹת עַמִּים
the essence of the Land of Israel being uniquely designated for Israel alone without any intermingling of the nations.
וְעַל כֵּן הָעוֹלִים בַּתְּחִלָּה לִכְבּוֹשׁ אַחַר מוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
And therefore those who went up first to conquer after the death of Joshua.
שֶׁהוּא הַכּוֹבֵשׁ מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הַהַגְדָּרָה
he being the initial conqueror from the seed of Joseph who operates through moral boundaries.

paragraphs.text: Pri Tzaddik, Korach §1: Rav Tzadok writes, “ולעתיד יתגלה גם כן בחינת עיגולים ... ובבחינת עיגולים שם אין שום מדרגות שהכל שוים כמו עיגול שאין בו ראש וסוף.” Translation: “In the future the aspect of circles will also be revealed ... within circles there are no gradations, for all are equal, like a circle without beginning or end.” He connects this to the future dance in Ta’anis 31a and explains that Korach wrongly treated this future equality as already realized. This illuminates the contrast between present hierarchy and the future circle without erasing their distinction.

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach I, Korach §3 — original Izhbitzer parallel. “שאין שום התנשאות בין ישראל לאחד על חברו ... שהש״י שוכן בתוך כלם שוה בשוה ... ומחול היינו בעגול שאין שום אחד קרוב יותר מחברו. והיה טוען שעתה גם כן הוא כך.” Translation: “No one in Israel has superiority over another ... Hashem dwells in all equally ... a circle means no one is closer than another; Korach claimed it was already so now.” The passage cites Taanis 31a and answers Korach through the distinction between the future circle and present responsibilities (cf. paragraphs.text: Tzidkas HaTzadik §65: “והיינו שידעו כי לעתיד לא ילמדו איש את רעהו ויהי׳ מדרגה זו שכל העדה כולם קדושים וחשבו שכבר הגיעו לכך.” Translation: “They knew that in the future each will not teach the other, and the entire congregation will be holy; they thought they had already arrived at that level.” The passage concerns Korach’s mistake of timing: it explains why the equality of receiving directly from Hashem belongs to the future, rather than already canceling all hierarchy in this world.

paragraphs.text: Verified source: Pri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev 6:3: “ואות סמך מורה כמו לעתיד שישחוט הקב״ה ליצה״ר ... והיינו בלא חילוק מדרגות כמו כל דבר עגול שאין לו ראש וסוף.” Translation: “The letter samekh alludes to the future defeat of the evil inclination ... without differentiation of ranks, like any circle without beginning or end.” More directly on pure reception, Rav Tzadok writes in Resisei Layla §25: “אבל חשק בני ישראל הוא שיצטרכו להשם יתברך והוא יהיה המשלימם ואין חפצים כלל שלימות בלא השם יתברך.” Translation: “Israel longs to need Hashem, that He complete them; they do not desire perfection apart from Him.” This illuminates Shimon’s reception as an analogy, without falsely attributing a separate Shimon-specific quotation to this source. Cf. Taanit 31a.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: All of this — one soul bestowing upon a lesser — belongs to this world alone. In the Future, the “circle-dance for the righteous,” all stand in a circle with no ranks, “no man teaching his fellow,” each receiving equally from Hashem alone. The nations will then have no existence, for they cannot receive from Him directly; and this is precisely Shimon’s power — pure receiving, with nothing of his own.

p: (עד) אֲבָל הַנִּשְׁאָר אַחַר כָּךְ,
However, regarding what remained to conquer afterward,
הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁהָיָה לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם טַעֲנָה דְּגַם יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין מוּגְדָּרִים כָּל כָּךְ,
namely the area where the nations claimed that even Israel in this world are not so strictly guarded,
נֶאֱמַר בְּרֵאשִׁית שׁוֹפְטִים (א, ב) דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָמַר: "יְהוּדָה יַעֲלֶה" בַּתְּחִלָּה
it is stated at the opening of Judges (1:2) that Hashem said: 'Judah shall go up' first,
וִיהוּדָה אָמַר לְשִׁמְעוֹן אָחִיו: "עֲלֵה אִתִּי בְגֹרָלִי" (שָׁם ג).
and Judah said unto Simeon his brother: 'Come up with me into my lot' (v. 3).
כִּי מִצַּד הַגִּלּוּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
For from the perspective of manifest revelation in this world,
שֶׁמִּצִּידּוֹ הַנִּצּוּחַ לָאֻמּוֹת לֹא דֶּרֶךְ הַגְדָּרָה מֵעֲרָיוֹת כְּיוֹסֵף
wherein victory over the nations proceeds not through restraint against sexual sin like Joseph,
רַק דֶּרֶךְ כְּפִירָה בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כִּיהוּדָה
rather through repudiation of idolatry like Judah,
יְהוּדָה הוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן וְהָעִיקָּר הָרָאוּי לְכָךְ.
Judah is the first and primary tribe suited for this mission.
אֶלָּא דְּשָׁם נִצְטַוּוּ "לֹא תְחַיֶּה כָּל נְשָׁמָה" (דְּבָרִים כ, טז),
Except that there they were commanded: 'you shall save alive nothing that breathes' (Deuteronomy 20:16),
שֶׁלֹּא יַשְׁאִירוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ וְעָנָף, כִּי אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת וְחִבּוּר עִמָּהֶם
leaving neither root nor branch, having no affinity or connection with them whatsoever.
דָּבָר זֶה הָעִיקָּר הוּא כֹּחַ שִׁמְעוֹן
and this radical separation is fundamentally the power of Simeon.
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין גָּלוּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
Only that it is not openly revealed in this world.
עַל כֵּן לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לָבוֹא צִיוּוּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עָלָיו בְּפֵירוּשׁ,
Therefore it was impossible for Hashem's explicit command to be addressed to Simeon directly,
רַק יְהוּדָה כְּלָלוֹ עִמּוֹ,
rather Judah included Simeon alongside himself.
כִּי הֵם כְּלוּלִים יַחַד שֶׁיְּהוּדָה הוּא הַנִּגְלוֹת וְשִׁמְעוֹן הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת
for they are integrated together, Judah representing the manifest and Simeon the hidden.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר לוֹ: "וְהָלַכְתִּי גַם אֲנִי אִתְּךָ" (שׁוֹפְטִים א, ג),
And therefore Judah said to him: 'and I likewise will go with you' (Judges 1:3).
כִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן לֹא יָכוֹל לְנַצֵּחַ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת
for Simeon on his own could likewise not triumph in the manifest realm. (,
וְעַל כֵּן הַשֵּׁם שִׁמְעוֹן הָיָה מָצוּי בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל
(And therefore the name Shimon was common in the Land of Israel as I wrote above,).
הַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַמַּעֲלָה שֶׁבְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ שֵׁם זֶה
(namely on account of the sanctity rooted in this name.),
אֲבָל בְּבָבֶל מָצוּי הַשֵּׁם יוֹסֵף
(Whereas in Babylonia the name Yosef was prevalent,)
כִּי כֹּחַ הַהַגְדָּרָה צָרִיךְ לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בּוֹ הָעִיקָּר בִּהְיוֹתָן בֵּין הָעַמִּים
(for the power of moral boundaries must be utilized primarily when dwelling among the nations),
לְבַל יִתְעָרְבוּ בַּגּוֹיִם וְיִלְמְדוּ מִמַּעֲשֵׂיהֶם
(lest they assimilate with the gentiles and learn their deeds,).
וְזֶהוּ כָּל כֹּחַ יוֹסֵף בִּהְיוֹתוֹ לְעֶבֶד נִמְכָּר בֵּין הַמִּצְרִיִּים שְׁטוּפֵי זִימָּה
and this was the singular power of Joseph when sold as a slave among the licentious Egyptians.),
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא הָיָה כְּבִישַׁת הָאָרֶץ עַל יָדוֹ בַּפּוֹעַל
And therefore the conquest of the Land was not achieved through Simeon in practical execution,
רַק בְּכֹחַ הוּא נִכְלָל בִּיהוּדָה
rather in potential he was integrated within Judah.
שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ לְגַמְרֵי אַחַר מוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עַד דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
who was the principal conqueror from the death of Joshua until King David, peace be upon him.
וּבִימֵי שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּקַיְימָא סִיהֲרָא בְּאַשְׁלָמוּתָא (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק א, רכג סוֹף עַמּוּד ב),
And in the days of King Solomon, peace be upon him, when the moon stood in its fullness (Zohar Part I, 223b).
גַּם כֵּן דָּבַק לְאַהֲבָה בִּבְנוֹת גּוֹיִם
he likewise cleaved in love unto the daughters of the nations.?!
אֲבָל עַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (יְבָמוֹת עז.): "אֲנַן מִשְּׁלֹמֹה נֵיקוּם וְנִגְמוֹר",
Yet concerning this the Talmud remarked (Yevamot 77a): 'Shall we establish legal practice from Solomon?!',
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אָז לֹא הָיָה שַׁיָּיכוּת לְחֵטְא זֶה דֶּרֶךְ חֵטְא בַּפּוֹעַל
for in truth at that golden era this sin held no relevance by way of actual transgression;
אֲבָל הוּא לֹא נָסֵיב
indeed Solomon did not marry them for base lust.
רַק שֶׁכְּפִי מַדְרֵגָתוֹ הֶחְשִׁיבוּ זֶה לְחֵטְא וְהַטָּיַת הַלֵּב
only that according to his exalted spiritual level Scripture accounted this as a sin and a turning of the heart.
דְּ"הִטּוּ אֶת לְבָבוֹ" (מְלָכִים א יא, ג),
For 'they turned away his heart' (I Kings 11:3),
דַּוְוקָא לֵב כְּמוֹתוֹ הַדָּבוּק לְגַמְרֵי בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
specifically a heart like his, entirely cleaving unto Hashem, blessed be He,
כַּאֲשֶׁר הֶרְאָה בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים שֶׁשָּׂח בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ הַנּוֹבֵעַ מִלִּבּוֹ,
as he demonstrated in the Song of Songs which he uttered through the Holy Spirit flowing from his heart.
נֶחְשַׁב גַּם זֶה לְהַטָּיָה
even this subtle distraction was accounted as a turning away.

Rav Tzadok’s application is that the radical separation of Israel’s root, specifically at this historical conquest, represents Shimon’s concealed power.

paragraphs.text: Shoftim 1:2–3: “וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ יְהוּדָה יַעֲלֶה ... וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוּדָה לְשִׁמְעוֹן אָחִיו עֲלֵה אִתִּי בְגֹרָלִי ... וְהָלַכְתִּי גַם אֲנִי אִתְּךָ בְגוֹרָלֶךָ.” Translation: “Hashem said: Judah shall go up ... Judah said to Shimon: Come with me into my allotted territory ... I too will go with you into yours.” Original Chassidic parallel: Bnei Yissaschar, Tamuz and Av 1:9:2 associates Nisan with Yehudah and Av with Shimon (“וחדש מנחם א״ב הוא לשמעון”) and interprets this shared ascent as revealed redemption accompanied by a hidden future good. The Bnei Yissaschar does not claim Rav Tzadok’s identical interpretation; both develop the same partnership of the revealed with the concealed.

paragraphs.text: Yevamos 76b: “אמר רב פפא אנן משלמה ליקו ונתיב? שלמה לא נסיב מידי ... מתוך אהבה יתירה שאהבה מעלה עליו הכתוב כאילו נתחתן בה.” Translation: “Rav Pappa said: Shall we arise and draw a conclusion from Solomon? Solomon did not contract a marriage ... out of his exceedingly great love for her, Scripture regards it as though he had married her.” The Gemara is explaining the tension between “cleaved to them in love” (I Melachim 11:2) and “married into Pharaoh’s house” (I Melachim 3:1). Rav Tzadok’s Hebrew manuscript cites Yevamos 77a; the passage itself is on 76b in the archived daf. The Talmud’s formulation is a specific textual explanation, not permission to disregard the marriage prohibitions.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: To the nations’ claim that Israel too are not so “bounded-in,” the answer is “Yehudah shall go up first,” and Yehudah’s word to Shimon, “go up with me in my lot.” The revealed victory comes not through Yosef’s boundedness but through Yehudah’s repudiation of idolatry. Yet the command to leave no root or branch is essentially Shimon’s power — and being unrevealed, it could not be commanded to him directly, so Yehudah included him.

p: (עה) אֲבָל קוֹדֶם הַכְּנִיסָה הָיָה חֵטְא בַּפּוֹעַל
However, prior to the entry into the Land there was sin in concrete actuality,
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּקוֹדֶם כְּנִיסָה לְאֵיזֶה מַדְרֵגָה יֵשׁ נִסְיוֹנוֹת הָרוֹצִים לְעַכֵּב בְּיָדוֹ,
for as is known, prior to entering into any spiritual tier there exist trials seeking to impede a person;
וְהוּא כִּבְרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם לִהְיוֹת "בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא" (שַׁבָּת עז),
and this follows the design of Creation, to be 'first darkness and then light' (Shabbat 77b),
וְהַקַּדְרוּתָא דְּצַפְרָא שֶׁקּוֹדֶם הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר הַבָּהִיר הוּא חֹשֶׁךְ הַיּוֹתֵר עָצוּם
and the predawn blackness preceding the radiant light is the most intense darkness of all.
וְעַל כֵּן אָז הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה דִּשְׁטִים
and therefore right then occurred the incident of Shittim.
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ בְּגָלוּת בָּבֶל בִּשְׁעַת כְּנִיסָה לָאָרֶץ נִכְשְׁלוּ בְּחֵטְא זֶה וְשָׁבוּ,
And similarly in the Babylonian exile at the moment of re-entering the Land, they stumbled in this sin of foreign women (Ezra 9–10) and repented.
וְאָז נִגְלָה תֵּיכֶף הַנְּהוֹרָא שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד חֹשֶׁךְ זֶה
and right then the radiant light opposing that darkness was revealed.
וְהַכְּנִיסָה לָאָרֶץ הָיָה אָז עַל יְדֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן
And the entry into the Land was led then by Joshua son of Nun,
כִּי יוֹסֵף הוּא מַמָּשׁ הֵיפֶךְ זֶה
for Joseph is the exact antithesis of this impurity,
וְעִיקַּר נַחֲלַת הָאָרֶץ הוּא עַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית
and the core inheritance of the Land is attained through guarding the Covenant,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים, לְעוֹלָם יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ" (יְשַׁעְיָה ס, כא),
as it is stated: 'Your people are all righteous, they shall inherit the land forever' (Isaiah 60:21).
אֶלָּא שֶׁעַם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כֻּלָּם כֵּן
except that the entire people of Israel are essentially so.
וְהָרְאָיָה יְהוּדָה שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ,
And the proof is Judah who was the primary conqueror,
הֲרֵי בּוֹ נִמְצָא הַחֵטְא דְּעֵר וְאוֹנָן
behold within his lineage was found the sin of Er and Onan,
שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ צַדִּיקִים וְנִקְרָא רַע
which is the antithesis of the righteous and termed 'evil' in the eyes of Hashem.
אֶלָּא שֶׁכָּל זֶה אֵינוֹ בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ בֶּאֱמֶת
except that all this does not reflect the root in ultimate truth.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (מד רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א):
And along the lines of what is stated in Sanhedrin (44a):
"אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא",
'Even though he has sinned, he remains Israel,'.
דִּקְדֻשַּׁת שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהֵיעָקֵר מִמֶּנּוּ אַף אִם יַרְבֶּה חֲטָאִים עַד לְמַעְלָה
for the sanctity of the name Israel can never be uprooted from him even if he multiplies sins unto the heavens.
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא שָׁם בְּעָכָן דְּעָבַר עַל כָּל חֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה
And as taught there concerning Achan who transgressed all Five Books of the Torah,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיעַ הַחֵטְא כָּל כָּךְ
nonetheless it is impossible for sin to reach so deeply,
לַעֲקוֹר עֶצֶם הַיַּהֲדוּת וְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל
as to eradicate the essential Jewishness and the name Israel,
שֶׁהוּא הַקְּדוּשָּׁה שֶׁבְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל אִישׁ יְהוּדִי מוֹרָשָׁה מֵאָבוֹת וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which is the holiness rooted within every Jewish person, an inheritance from the Patriarchs and our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְשַׁנּוֹת הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ.
and it is impossible to alter this root.
וְאַף שֶׁמַּרְבֶּה חֲטָאִים
And even when a person multiplies transgressions,
הוּא הַכֹּל מִצַּד הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבַּעִיסָה וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת הַמַּקִּיפִים לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת
it is entirely on account of the leaven in the dough and the subjugation of the empires that encompass the root of Jewishness.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בִּבְרָכוֹת (יז):
and as stated in Berakhot (17a):
"גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנְךָ וְכוּלֵי".
'It is revealed and known that our true will is to perform Your will, etc.'
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה בָּרַמְבַּ"ם (סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב מֵהִלְכוֹת גֵּירוּשִׁין הֲלָכָה כ)
And along these lines Maimonides writes (end of chapter 2 of the Laws of Divorce, halakhah 20).
בְּטַעַם "כּוֹפִין עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר רוֹצֶה אָנִי", עַיֵּין שָׁם
regarding the rationale for 'they compel him until he says: I am willing', see there.
וְעַל כֵּן הִמְשִׁילוּ שָׁם בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (מד.) "לְאָסָא דְּקָאֵי בֵּינֵי חִילְפֵי",
Therefore they compared it there in Sanhedrin (44a) 'to a myrtle standing among thorns',
כִּי הַחֲטָאִים הֵם רַק כַּחִילְפֵי הַסּוֹבְבִים לַאָסָא
for sins are merely like thorns surrounding the myrtle.
אֲבָל עֶצֶם הָאָסָא לֹא נִשְׁתַּנָּה
while the essence of the myrtle has not changed at all.

paragraphs.text: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash §5: “אך מכל מקום הוצרכו עוד לגליות עד מה שנאמר כי שבע יפול צדיק וקם והוא שיש ז׳ נפילות שעל ידי זה יתבררו היטב במדה זו.” Translation: “Nevertheless further exiles were required, as it says ‘the righteous falls seven times and rises,’ for through these seven falls they would be clarified in this trait.” The actual context is successive exiles and further clarification, not an instruction to fall or sin deliberately. It is an interpretive parallel to the trials accompanying spiritual ascent.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 77b: In R. Zeira’s questions to R. Yehudah, the goats precede the sheep “כברייתו של עולם, ברישא חשוכא והדר נהורא.” Translation: “As in the creation of the world: first darkness, and afterward light.” Rav Tzadok extends the pattern to trials that precede entry into a higher spiritual state. The Gemara itself explains the order of goats and sheep, not the specific episodes at Shittim or Ezra.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkas HaTzadik §4: “ויליף מברייתו של עולם לענין קבלת עול מלכות שמים דברישא חשוכא צריך קבלת עול מלכות שמים אף מתוך החושך והסכלות והעדר המעשים ואז סופו לקיימה ... נהורא דיממא.” Translation: “The creation teaches acceptance of Heaven’s yoke: at first, when there is darkness, it must be accepted even amid obscurity and lack of deeds; afterward comes the daylight of clear understanding.” This is Rav Tzadok’s own parallel for progress through darkness; it is not a directive to commit a transgression.

paragraphs.text: Kedushat Levi, Likutim §113: “ובכל מקום היראה קודמת לאהבה ... והיראה הוא השער והתחלה לעבודת השם יתברך ואחר כך האהבה.” Translation: “Everywhere awe precedes love ... awe is the gate and the beginning of service of Hashem, and afterward comes love.” R. Levi Yitzchak reads the Gemara’s “darkness before light” as disciplined awe preceding love; this illuminates the order of spiritual preparation without implying that sin is a prescribed means of attaining the light.

paragraphs.text: Rambam, Hilchos Gerushin 2:20: “One whom the law requires to divorce his wife, and who refuses — a Jewish court, in every place and time, beats him until he says ‘I want to,’ and he writes the get, and it is valid.” Why is it not void as coerced? “For we call an act ‘coerced’ only when one is pressed to do a thing he is not obligated in by the Torah — but one whose evil inclination has overpowered him to nullify a mitzvah or commit a transgression, and who is beaten until he does what he is obligated to do — this is not coerced by others; rather he coerced himself by his own evil intent” — for at his core his will is to be a Jew and fulfill the mitzvos.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Before entering a high rung come trials that hold a person back — as in creation itself, “first darkness, then light,” the gloom before dawn being the deepest. Hence the deed of Shittim before entering the Land, and the foreign wives at the return from Bavel, each followed at once by light. The entry came through Yehoshua, of Yosef — for inheriting the Land turns on guarding the bris, and “your people are all righteous.”

p: (עו) וְכָךְ לְעִנְיַן תֹּאַר "צַדִּיק" כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים כֵּן וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּרֵישׁ סִימָן זֶה
And likewise regarding the title 'Tzaddik', all of Israel are designated as such, as I wrote at the beginning of this section,
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחוֹטְאִים וּפוֹגְמִים בַּבְּרִית בַּפּוֹעַל
and even though they sin and blemish the Covenant in concrete action,
הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַחִילְפֵי וְהַחוֹחִים הַסּוֹבְבִים אֶת הַשּׁוֹשַׁנָּה
it is merely from the thorns and briers surrounding the rose.
אֲבָל אֵינוֹ נוֹגֵעַ בְּעֶצֶם הָאָסָא וְהַשּׁוֹשַׁנָּה
yet it does not touch the essence of the myrtle and the rose.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה (א, ו) עַל פָּסוּק "שֶׁשְּׁזָפַתְנִי הַשָּׁמֶשׁ" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים א, ו),
And along the lines of what is stated in Shir HaShirim Rabbah (1:6) on the verse 'because the sun has tanned me' (Song of Songs 1:6).
דְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שְׁחוֹרִים בְּעֶצֶם
that the nations of the world are black in their very essence.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּהֵם שָׁרְשָׁם בְּרַע
Meaning that their root is in evil,
וְעֶצֶם נַפְשָׁם שָׁקוּעַ רַק בְּתַאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁזֶּה כָּל חַיּוּתָם
and their essential soul is submerged solely in worldly desires which constitute their entire life;
וְאִם לֹא יִהְיֶה לָהֶם מִילּוּי תַּאֲוָתָם לָמָּה לָהֶם חַיִּים
and if they are denied the fulfillment of their lust, why should they have life,
כִּי אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם הַרְגָּשַׁת וְהַשָּׂגַת חַיּוּת אַחֶרֶת אֶלָּא חַיּוּת הַגּוּפָנִי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
having no perception or grasp of any other vitality other than physical bodily existence in this world.
וְאֵין מַשִּׂיג עוֹנֶג אַחֵר אֶלָּא עִנּוּגֵי הַתַּאֲווֹת הַגּוּפָנִיּוֹת
and grasping no delight other than bodily pleasures.
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמַר בַּר שֵׁשַׁךְ לְרָבָא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (סה):
Which is why Bar Sheshakh said to Rava in Avodah Zarah (65a):
"אִית לְכוּ כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא לְעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי?"
'Do you have anything like this in the World to Come?',
שֶׁהוּא נַחֲלַת הַצַּדִּיקִים הַפְּרוּשִׁים וּמְרוּחָקִים מִתַּאֲווֹת
which is the heritage of the righteous who are ascetic and detached from lusts,
וּמַה בֶּצַע לָהֶם מִתִּקְוָתָם לְהַשִּׂיג עַל יְדֵי זֶה הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
wondering what profit there was in their hope of attaining the World to Come through this,
וּמַה עוֹנֶג יוּכְלוּ לְהַשִּׂיג שָׁם אִם אֵין לָהֶם עִנּוּגֵי הַתַּאֲווֹת הָאֵלּוּ שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ,
and what pleasure could they possibly enjoy there if they lack those physical gratifications he enjoyed.
כִּי הוּא לֹא הִשִּׂיג כְּלָל עוֹנֶג אַחֵר
because he could not conceive of any other form of delight at all.
וְעַל כֵּן כָּל הַגּוֹיִם עֲרֵלִים בְּעֶצֶם
Therefore all the gentiles are uncircumcised in their very essence,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כָּל בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל "עַרְלֵי לֵב" (יִרְמְיָה ט, כה),
whereas all the House of Israel are merely 'uncircumcised of heart' (Jeremiah 9:25),
מִצַּד מִשְׁכַּן הַיֵּצֶר שָׁם עַל מִפְתְּחֵי הַלֵּב מִנְּעוּרָיו
stemming from the seat of the inclination dwelling at the entrances of the heart from youth,
לֹא עַרְלֵי בָשָׂר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עֶצֶם הַגּוּף בַּפּוֹעַל רַע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
and not uncircumcised of flesh, as though the physical body itself were inherently evil, Heaven forbid,
וְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא לְעִנְיַן קְדֻשַּׁת עֶצֶם הַנֶּפֶשׁ.
and the title Israel applies to the holiness of the soul's essence.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא גָּלוּי בַּפּוֹעַל גָּמוּר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מֵעֵת שֶׁנִּבְחֲרוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעַם מְיוּחָד
And this truth is manifest in complete actuality in this world from the moment Israel was chosen as a consecrated nation.
דְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין נִיתָּק מֵהֶם עוֹד מִצַּד שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשָׁם
for the name Israel is never severed from them in the root of their soul.
כִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מֵחֶדֶר אַחֵר מֵהַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתוֹסָפוֹת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ה. דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "אֵין"),
For the root of the souls of Israel emerges from a separate chamber than the souls of the nations, as Tosafot noted in Avodah Zarah (5a, s.v. "Ein").
וְאֵין לְנֶפֶשׁ זוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת וְחִבּוּר כְּלָל עִם הַנֶּפֶשׁ דְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
and this soul holds no affinity or union whatsoever with the soul of the nations of the world.
וְעַל כֵּן אֲפִילּוּ הֵמִיר לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יֵשׁ לוֹ כָּל דִּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעִנְיַן קִדּוּשִׁין וְגֵירוּשִׁין וְכַיּוֹצֵא
Therefore even if an apostate converts to idolatry, he retains the full status of a Jew regarding betrothal, divorce, and the like,
כִּי קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּנַפְשׁוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּבָר נִתְבָּרְרָה עַל יְדֵי גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם
for the holiness of Israel within their souls was already clarified through the Egyptian exile.
דְּמֵאָז נִבְחֲרוּ לְגוֹי אֶחָד בָּאָרֶץ
since then they were chosen to be one nation in the earth.
אֲבָל הַשֵּׁם "צַדִּיק" הוּא לְעִנְיַן קְדֻשַּׁת הַגּוּף הַבִּשְׂרִי
However, the designation 'Tzaddik' relates to the holiness of the physical body,
כִּי גַּם הַגּוּפוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשׁוּנִּים מִגּוּפוֹת דְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מִלֵּידָה מִבֶּטֶן וְהֵרָיוֹן
for the physical bodies of Israel are likewise distinct from the bodies of the nations from conception and gestation,
זֶה בְּשַׂר קֹדֶשׁ וְזֶה בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹרִים (יְחֶזְקֵאל כג, כ).
this is holy flesh, while that is the flesh of donkeys (Ezekiel 23:20).
וְדָבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ גָּלוּי עֲדַיִן בַּפּוֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And this distinction is not yet openly manifest in actuality in this world,
שֶׁהֲרֵי יֵשׁ עֲדַיִן רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֵין עֲלֵיהֶם שֵׁם צַדִּיק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
since there are still wicked individuals in Israel upon whom the title Tzaddik cannot be placed in this world,
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁהֵם שְׁזוּפִים וּשְׁחוֹרִים עַל זֶה אָמַר: "הֲלוֹא כִבְנֵי כֻשִׁיִּים אַתֶּם לִי וְגוֹמֵר" .
and as long as they appear blackened, concerning this Scripture states: 'Are you not as children of the Ethiopians unto Me, etc.' (Amos 9:7).
וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּמִקְרָא זֶה נֶאֱמַר עַל פְּגַם הַבְּרִית
And I have heard that this verse was uttered concerning the blemish of the Covenant,
שֶׁהַשָּׁמוּר בּוֹ נִקְרָא "יְפֵה תֹאַר וִיפֵה מַרְאֶה" כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּיוֹסֵף (בְּרֵאשִׁית לט, ו),
for one who guards it is called 'fair of form and fair of appearance' as stated of Joseph (Genesis 39:6),
וְכֵן בְּכָל מָקוֹם בַּמִּקְרָא וּבְדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה הַיֹּפִי וְהַכִּיעוּר הוּא בִּקְדֻשַּׁת הַבְּרִית
and so everywhere in Scripture and in the words of our Sages beauty and ugliness pertain to the sanctity of the Covenant.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ יוֹפִי הַבְּשַׂר אָדָם וְהַגּוּף
which constitutes the true aesthetic beauty of the human body.

paragraphs.text: Pri Tzaddik, Shemos §5: Rav Tzadok explains “חצדי חקלא הקוצרים להכרית כל הקוצים והחוחים הסובבים את השושנה העליונה.” Translation: “The reapers of the field cut away the thorns and briars surrounding the supernal rose.” He continues with the rabbinic myrtle-among-thorns image and “even though he sinned, he is Israel.” Thus the blemish is a surrounding growth, not the flower’s inner essence. This is Rav Tzadok’s own direct parallel.

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:6: On “ששזפתני השמש,” the Midrash begins “מעשה בקרתנית אחת שהיה לה שפחה כושית” — “There was a townswoman who had a Kushite maidservant.” The servant imagines that a momentary stain on her mistress’s hands could cause the husband to replace his wife with her; her companion rebukes her. The Midrash applies the parable to peoples who imagine Israel’s temporary wrongdoing cancels the covenant. Rav Tzadok develops the parable as an interpretation of external concealment versus lasting inward holiness. The Midrash’s color imagery is a historical religious metaphor, not a physical or racial fact.

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 65a: Rava found Bar Sheishach immersed up to his neck in rosewater with women standing before him. He asked “אית לכו כהאי גוונא לעלמא דאתי?” — “Do you have anything like this in the World to Come?” Rava answered that the world to come is superior, because there is no fear of earthly government. The text illustrates Bar Sheishach’s limited conception of delight; Rav Tzadok develops his own contrast between passing appetite and spiritual enjoyment. The Gemara concludes that the king summoned Bar Sheishach, and that his eye burst following Rava’s words.

This clarifies how a blemish can arise and require repair; the source does not say that misconduct is harmless or that repair is unnecessary.

paragraphs.text: Yechezkel 23:20: The prophet’s severe marital metaphor says “אֲשֶׁר בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹרִים בְּשָׂרָם וְזִרְמַת סוּסִים זִרְמָתָם.” Translation: “Whose flesh is like the flesh of donkeys, and whose emission is like that of horses.” In Yechezkel the image depicts the illicit desire attributed to Oholivah for Egyptian lovers. Rav Tzadok applies this biblical metaphor to the tension between external appearance and spiritual holiness. His extension must be distinguished from the historical verse’s immediate context; it is not an empirical description of entire populations.

paragraphs.text: Amos 9:7: “הֲלוֹא כִבְנֵי כֻשִׁיִּים אַתֶּם לִי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נְאֻם ה׳.” Translation: “Are you not like the Cushites to Me, O children of Israel? declares Hashem.” The verse continues by mentioning other peoples whom God also brought from their lands, warning against moral complacency. Rav Tzadok interprets the simile as an outward condition rather than loss of Israel’s spiritual root. Cf. Likutei Moharan I 14:3: “גם הפושעי ישראל ... אף על פי שחטא ישראל הוא.” Translation: “Even sinners of Israel ... though he sinned, he is Israel.” This parallel explains the possibility of repentance without denying wrongdoing.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: So too the title “tzaddik”: all Israel are called by it, their sins being only the thorns around the rose, never touching its essence. The nations are “black in essence,” their souls sunk wholly in worldly desire and knowing no other vitality. Hence they are uncircumcised in essence, while Israel are only “uncircumcised of heart” — the name Israel pertaining to a holiness of soul that cannot be severed.

p: (עז) וּמִקְרָא זֶה הוּא הַפְטָרַת פָּרָשַׁת קְדוֹשִׁים הַמְדַבֶּרֶת בִּקְדֻשַּׁת הַבְּרִית
And this verse serves as the Haftarah for Parashat Kedoshim which treats the sanctity of the Covenant,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר הַקְּדוּשָּׁה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ : "כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא גֶּדֶר עֶרְוָה אַתָּה מוֹצֵא קְדוּשָּׁה".
which is the core of holiness, as they said (Vayikra Rabbah 24:6): 'Wherever you find a fence against immorality, you find holiness.',
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים הֵם
For in truth all Israel are holy,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא (שַׁבָּת פו.) וּבְפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּחֻלִּין (י:): "יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים הֵם",
as they stated in Shabbat (86a) and Chullin (10b): 'Israel are holy,'
וְנֶאֱמַר: "קֹדֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל לַה' וְגוֹמֵר" (יִרְמְיָה ב, ג).
and it is said: 'Israel is holy unto Hashem, etc.' (Jeremiah 2:3).
וְרַק לְמַרְאִית עַיִן הֵם כִּבְנֵי כּוּשִׁיִּים בְּכָ״ף הַדִּמְיוֹן עַל יְדֵי שְׁזִיפַת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ,
And only to outward appearance are they like Ethiopians—with the Kaf of comparison—due to the sun's scorching,
וּבִמְעַט רִיחוּץ מִתְרַחֲצִים
and with a brief washing they are cleansed.
רַק כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִתְרַחֲצוּ דּוֹמִים לִבְנֵי כּוּשִׁיִּים
only as long as they remain unwashed do they resemble dark Ethiopians.
וְהַשִּׁפְחָה הַכּוּשִׁית חוֹשֶׁבֶת לְהִתְדַּמּוֹת לָהּ וְלִירַשׁ גְּבִירְתָּהּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
And the maidservant imagines herself equal to her, seeking to supplant her mistress, Heaven forbid.
וְעַל זֶה הוּא כָּל גָּלוּת זֶה לְבָרֵר קְדֻשַּׁת הַגּוּפוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּקְרָאִים כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים
And it is for this that this prolonged exile exists: to clarify the holiness of the physical bodies of Israel who are all termed Tzaddikim,
וְכִדִּמְסַיֵּים הַמִּקְרָא דְּשָׁם: "וַהֲנִיעוֹתִי בְכָל הַגּוֹיִם אֶת בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹמֵר וְלֹא יִפּוֹל צְרוֹר אָרֶץ" .
as the verse there concludes: 'And I will sift the House of Israel among all nations, etc. yet not the least grain shall fall upon the earth' (Amos 9:9).
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין שָׁם אֲפִילּוּ צְרוֹר אֶחָד שֶׁיִּפּוֹל לָאָרֶץ וְלֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ שׁוּם נִדָּח
For in truth not a single grain falls away, and not a single soul shall be cast out,
כַּיָּדוּעַ בְּסוֹד "וְקַבְּצֵנוּ יַחַד מֵאַרְבַּע כַּנְפוֹת וְכוּלֵי"
as is known in the esoteric secret of 'and gather us together from the four corners, etc.',
מְרוּמָּז הַשֵּׁם הַמְּיוּחָד לִקְבִיצַת הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה
wherein is hinted the holy Name designated for gathering the holy sparks dispersed through wasted seed.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר קִיבּוּץ גָּלִיּוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע כַּנְפוֹת הָאָרֶץ
which constitutes the primary gathering of the exiles from the four corners of the earth.
דְּהַנִּידּוּד לְכָל אַרְבַּע כְּנָפוֹת בָּא עַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם קוֹלְטִים הַשֶּׁפַע
For the dispersion to all four corners occurred because the nations absorbed the divine influx
שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹרֵד לָאָרֶץ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה
– which failed to descend into the Holy Land—
"אֶרֶץ אֲשֶׁר ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ דֹּרֵשׁ (אֹתָהּ)" (דְּבָרִים יא, יב),
'a land which Hashem your God cares for' (Deuteronomy 11:12),
הָרוֹמֶזֶת לָאָרֶץ עֶלְיוֹנָה שֶׁהַמָּטָר בַּעְלָהּ דְּאַרְעָא בִּירִידַת הַשֶּׁפַע מוֹלִידָה וּמַצְמִיחָה כְּשֶׁהוּא יוֹרֵד לַמָּקוֹם הָרָאוּי
which alludes to the Supernal Land where the rain—the husband of the earth—through the descent of influx engenders life when falling into its worthy place;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כְּשֶׁשּׁוֹפֵעַ לַחוּץ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְבַטָּלָה
unlike when it spills outward in vain, Heaven forbid,
כְּטַעַם "ה' צִלְּךָ" (תְּהִלִּים קכא, ה),
in the spirit of 'Hashem is your shadow' (Psalms 121:5).
עַל יְדֵי זֶה מוּכְרָחִים בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לָנוּעַ בֵּין הָעַמִּים
through this are the children of Israel forced to wander among the nations.
וְהוּא "עֵת אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַט הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם לְרַע לוֹ" (קֹהֶלֶת ח, ט) – לָאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל
And this is 'a time when man rules over man to his own hurt' (Ecclesiastes 8:9)—to the ruin of the archetype of Belial;
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים וְהֵם חוֹזְרִים וְקוֹלְטִים הַשֶּׁפַע שֶׁלָּהֶם בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא
for in truth Israel are holy, and they retrieve their divine influx wherever it is,
וְאַגַּבָּהּ נִמְשָׁךְ גַּם מְעַט הַשֶּׁפַע שֶׁהָיָה לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מִצַּד עַצְמָם גַּם כֵּן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
and along with it, the sparse vital influx belonging to the nations themselves is also drawn to Israel,
עַד שֶׁהֵם יִשָּׁאֲרוּ כִּמְצוּלָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דָּגִים וְדָגָן
– until the nations are left like an ocean abyss stripped of fish and grain—.
חַיֵּי גוּפָנִי וְנַפְשִׁי בְּחַיֵּי עוֹלָם
stripped of bodily vitality and soul-sustenance in eternal life.
וְאָז יִהְיֶה קִיבּוּץ גָּלִיּוֹת
And then the Ingathering of Exiles will take place,
שֶׁיְּקוּבְּצוּ כָּל הַנִּדָּחִים מִן הַשֶּׁפַע לַחוּץ שֶׁלֹּא נִלְקְטוּ תֵּיכֶף בְּנוּקְבָּא
wherein all dispersed elements of influx that spilled outward and were not immediately gathered into Nukva,
שֶׁהִיא כְּלַל הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל דִּקְדוּשָּׁה
which is the collective Congregation of Israel in holiness.
וְלֹא יִפּוֹל צְרוֹר אָרֶץ
and not a grain shall fall to the earth.
וִיבוֹרַר זֶה דְּ"עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים",
And this reality that 'your people are all righteous' will be fully vindicated,
שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ זֶה בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק חֵלֶק  — עַל חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
which they expounded at the beginning of chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 90a) concerning a share in the World to Come.
כִּי אָז הוּא שֶׁיִּתְבָּרֵר זֶה
for only then will this truth be openly demonstrated.
"לְעוֹלָם יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ",
And 'they shall inherit the land forever' reveals,
דְּיִתְבָּרֵר אַף שֶׁגָּלוּ מִן הָאָרֶץ הָיָה רַק לְשָׁעָה
that even though they were exiled from the Land it was merely temporary.
וּבֶאֱמֶת יְרוּשַּׁת הָאָרֶץ הוּא לָהֶם לְעוֹלָם
and in truth the inheritance of the Land belongs to them for all eternity.
כִּי מַה שֶּׁהָיָה לְשָׁעָה שֶׁפַע יוֹרֵד חוּץ לָאָרֶץ הַמְּיוּחֶדֶת לְקַבָּלַת הַשֶּׁפַע
For the temporary spillage of influx outside the Land designated for reception,
לֹא נִקְבַּע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לִהְיוֹת כֵּן
was never established permanently to remain so, Heaven forbid.
רַק עֲתִידִים לַחֲזוֹר לְקִבְעָא קַמָּא
rather all is destined to return to its pristine state.
וְכֵיוָן דְּעַל פִּי ה' יַחֲנוּ וְעַל פִּי ה' יִסָּעוּ
And since 'at the commandment of Hashem they encamped and at the commandment of Hashem they journeyed' (Numbers 9:20),
כְּסוֹתֵר עַל מְנָת לִבְנוֹת בִּמְקוֹמוֹ הוּא
it is considered like one who dismantles in order to rebuild in its place.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק בַּמֶּה מַדְלִיקִין (שַׁבָּת לא:) גַּבֵּי מִשְׁכָּן
as they stated in chapter Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 31b) regarding the Tabernacle.
וְכֵן בִּכְלַל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ שֶׁהֵם דּוּגְמַת הַמִּשְׁכָּן
And so too with the souls of Israel in the Diaspora who mirror the Tabernacle,
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן אִתָּם בְּתוֹךְ טֻמְאוֹתָם
for Hashem dwells with them in the midst of their uncleanness,
וּשְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּקֶרֶב הַלְּבָבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
and His Shechinah abides within the hearts of the children of Israel,
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁגָּלוּ גָּלְתָה שְׁכִינָה עִמָּהֶם (מְגִילָּה כט.) וְנַעֲשָׂה שָׁם מְקוֹמָם
and wherever they were exiled the Shechinah accompanied them (Megillah 29a) and made their location into her place?!
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּאֵיכָה רַבָּתִי (פְּתִיחָה כה): "וְכִי אִית יְהוּדִי אַכְסְנַאי",
and along the lines of Eichah Rabbah (Petichta 25): 'Is a Jew ever truly a stranger?!'
וְהַיְינוּ דְּעַל יְדֵי הַגָּלוּת, שֶׁהֵם קוֹלְטִים גַּם מְעַט הַטּוֹב שֶׁבָּאֻמּוֹת
meaning that through the exile, wherein they absorb even the spark of good among the nations,
וּמַחֲזִירִים הַכֹּל לִקְדוּשָּׁה
and restore everything unto holiness.
נִתְקַדֵּשׁ גַּם הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא בִּקְדוּשַׁת אֲוִירָא דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
that foreign place is likewise consecrated with the sanctity of the atmosphere of the Land of Israel.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ דַּעֲתִידָה אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לִהְיוֹת כְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ (פְּסִיקְתָּא רַבָּתִי א),
And on this they taught that the Land of Israel is destined to expand over the entire world (Pesikta Rabbati 1),
הַיְינוּ דְּיִתְקַדֵּשׁ כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ בִּקְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
meaning the entire world will be sanctified with the holiness of the Land of Israel,
עַל יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל שָׁם בִּימֵי הַגָּלוּת
by virtue of Israel having dwelled there during the days of exile,
וְנַעֲשָׂה גַּם אוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם שֶׁבְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ מְקוֹמָם מַמָּשׁ,
and that place in the Diaspora becomes literally their own place,
בְּעִנְיָן שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֵם הֵם בִּמְקוֹמָם
in such a manner that wherever they are, they are in their rightful place.
וְאֵין כָּאן יְרִידַת שֶׁפַע לַחוּץ כְּלָל
and there is no spillage of divine influx outward at all.

paragraphs.text: Pri Tzaddik, Purim §2: Quoting Tikunei Zohar, Rav Tzadok writes “דכסי קב״ה באות דיליה על אסתר דאיהי קדושה דיליה.” Translation: “The Holy One covered Esther with His letter, for she is His holiness.” The context treats Esther as a bearer of Divine holiness during concealment. This is an analogy to the hidden holiness disclosed after exile, not a direct interpretation of Amos or of the Kushite maidservant parable.

paragraphs.text: Amos 9:9: “וַהֲנִעוֹתִי בְכָל הַגּוֹיִם אֶת בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּאֲשֶׁר יִנּוֹעַ בַּכְּבָרָה, וְלֹא יִפּוֹל צְרוֹר אָרֶץ.” Translation: “I will shake the house of Israel among all nations as one shakes with a sieve, and no pebble shall fall to earth.” The surrounding prophecy also warns of judgment (9:8, 10). Rav Tzadok extends “no pebble shall fall” to his mystical account of dispersed holy sparks eventually being gathered; this is his interpretation, not the plain sense of every surrounding verse.

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar 9:23: “עַל פִּי ה׳ יַחֲנוּ וְעַל פִּי ה׳ יִסָּעוּ.” Translation: “At Hashem’s word they would camp, and at Hashem’s word they would journey.” The verse describes Israel’s travel according to the cloud of the Mishkan. paragraphs.text: Vayikra 16:16: “הַשֹּׁכֵן אִתָּם בְּתוֹךְ טֻמְאֹתָם.” Translation: “Who dwells with them amidst their impurity.” The Torah describes the Tent of Meeting, and Rav Tzadok extends this to the Shechinah accompanying Israel in exile. A related Chassidic explanation appears in Be’er Mayim Chaim, Bereishis 1:2 (subsection 7): “לא גלו ישראל אלא כדי שיתוספו עליהם גרים ... והם הניצוצות הקדושות” — “Israel was exiled so that converts might be added ... understood there as holy sparks.” This is an interpretive parallel, not an assertion that exile’s suffering is intrinsically desirable.
