inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Even one born wholly clean of desire has, set against it, a deficiency of anger — the two opposite inclinations in man, “the flame of the ever-turning sword,” at times life and at times death. There is an anger of the Sages that is good on every side, the Torah making a man seethe. Yet even he will not escape some deficiency of anger — for otherwise he would live forever, and Hashem created the yetzer “to guard the way to the Tree of Life.”

p: (פה) וְאַף לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: "יֵשׁ מִיתָה בְּלֹא חֵטְא אֶלָּא בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ" (שַׁבָּת נ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳)
And even according to the authority who maintains that there is death without personal sin, but solely through the instigation of the Serpent (Shabbat 55b).
עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ הַיְינוּ חִסָּרוֹן הַתַּאֲוָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּתּוֹלָדָה מֵעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל
the Serpent's instigation denotes that congenital flaw of desire present from birth through the Serpent, as I wrote above.
וְזֶהוּ הַשְּׁמִירָה לְדֶרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים
And this serves as the divine guard over the way of the Tree of Life,
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר דְּאֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה
wherefore they stated in the Zohar that repentance is ineffective,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיּוֹעִיל לְגַמְרֵי כְּמִשְׁפַּט הַתְּשׁוּבָה הַגְּמוּרָה דִּזְדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוּ כִּזְכִיּוֹת
meaning to be completely effective in the full legal status of absolute repentance wherein willful sins turn into merits (Yoma 86b),
שֶׁמְּתַקֵּן הַקּוֹדֵם לְגַמְרֵי וְעַד שֶׁשָּׁב עוֹד לִזְכוּת
rectifying the past entirely until it transforms into credit.
וְעָדִיף מִצַּדִּיק גָּמוּר דִּבִּמְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵי
standing superior to the wholly righteous, as in 'in the place where penitents stand, etc.',
דְּזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּעָוֹן זֶה
For this total inversion is impossible regarding this specific sin,
דְּאִם כֵּן הָיָה מִסְתַּלֵּק מִמֶּנּוּ הַשְּׁמִירָה מִדֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים
for were it so, the guard over the way of the Tree of Life would be removed from him
וְהָיָה אוֹכֵל וָחַי לְעוֹלָם (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג׳:כ״ב)
and he would eat and live forever (Genesis 3:22),
וְאֵין רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בָּזֶה
and such is not the will of Hashem in this temporal world,
וְשָׂם שׁוֹמְרִים שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לְהַגִּיעַ לָזֶה
He having stationed guardians so that man cannot attain this.
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לְתַקֵּן כָּל כָּךְ וְלָשׁוּב לְגַמְרֵי עַד שֶׁיּוּכַל לִחְיוֹת לְעוֹלָם
meaning that he cannot rectify so profoundly and repent so completely as to live forever.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁעוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה
Yet nonetheless, nothing stands in the face of repentance.
וְהַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁבְּמִדַּת הַיְסוֹד בְּרִית קֹדֶשׁ זוֹכֶה מִיהַת לְהַאֲרָכַת יָמָיו וּשְׁנוֹתָיו
and the repentance within the attribute of Yesod, the Holy Covenant, merits at least the lengthening of his days and years.
וְכָל הַבְטָחוֹת הַתּוֹרָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם הוּא עַל הַאֲרָכַת יָמִים
And all the promises of the Torah in every place pertain to length of days,
וְכֵן נֶאֱמַר בַּתּוֹרָה: "אֹרֶךְ יָמִים בִּימִינָהּ" (מִשְׁלֵי ג׳:ט״ז)
and so it is stated: 'Length of days is in her right hand' (Proverbs 3:16),
וְדָבָר אָרוֹךְ יֵשׁ לוֹ סוֹף עֲדַיִן אֶלָּא שֶׁאָרוֹךְ
and that which is long still has an end, except that it is extended.
וְזֶה לֹא כְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁנַּחֲלָתוֹ בְּלֹא מְצָרִים (שַׁבָּת קיח
And this is not like our father Jacob, peace be upon him, whose heritage is boundless (Shabbat 118b),
דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא מֵת כְּלָל (תַּעֲנִית ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
which is why he never died at all (Ta'anit 5b).
וּבֶאֱמֶת הַתּוֹרָה נִקְרָא חַיֵּי עוֹלָם שֶׁנָּטַע בְּתוֹכֵנוּ
And in truth the Torah is designated 'eternal life implanted within us',
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ עֵץ הַחַיִּים זוֹ תּוֹרָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "עֵץ חַיִּים הִיא לַמַּחֲזִיקִים בָּהּ" (מִשְׁלֵי ג׳:י״ח)
and so they said the Tree of Life is the Torah, as it is said: 'It is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon it' (Proverbs 3:18).
וְאוֹכְלֶיהָ חַיִּים לְעוֹלָם
and those who partake of it live forever.
וְכָל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ הַתּוֹרָה עַל הַר סִינַי אֲחִידִין בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא
And all the souls of Israel who received the Torah at Mount Sinai grasp onto the Torah,
וְעַל כֵּן כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
wherefore all Israel possess a share in the World to Come (Sanhedrin 90a).
דְּהַיְינוּ חַיֵּי עוֹלָם
which signifies eternal life.
אַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דְּנִקְרָא עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא
Yet in this world which is termed the World of Falsehood,
שֶׁאֵין הָאֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב נִגְלֶה
where the truth of Jacob is not overtly manifest.
אֵין דָּבָר זֶה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת
this reality is not in visible revelation.
וְכֵן קִבַּלְתִּי בְּפֵירוּשׁ לְשׁוֹן הַתִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר גַּבֵּי אַבְנֵי שַׁיִשׁ טָהוֹר
And so have I received by tradition in explaining the phrase of the Tikkunei Zohar regarding the stones of pure marble (Chagigah 14b),
דִּלְעָתִיד יִתְגַּלֶּה דְּלֹא הָיָה מִיתָה כְּלָל בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב
that in the future it will be revealed that death never existed at all in the root of the seed of Jacob,
וְהַמִּיתָה דְּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and the mortality of this world is merely from the perspective of manifest appearance in this world,
וְלֹא כְּשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ
and not how it stands when ultimate truth is disclosed.
וְעַל כֵּן בַּקְּרָא כְּתִיב: "וּבְשׁוּב רָשָׁע (מֵרִשְׁעָתוֹ וְעָשָׂה מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה) הוּא (עֲלֵיהֶם) יִחְיֶה" (יְחֶזְקֵאל ל״ג:י״ט)
Therefore in the verse it is written: 'And when the wicked turns from his wickedness, and does that which is lawful and right, he shall live thereby' (Ezekiel 33:19),
סְתָם חַיִּים הַיְינוּ חַיֵּי עוֹלָם
unqualified 'life' denoting eternal life,
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה לָמְדוּ מִזֶּה דְּמַאֲרֶכֶת שְׁנוֹתָיו (יוֹמָא פ״ו עַמּוּד ב׳)
and our Sages derived from this that repentance lengthens his years (Yoma 86b),
כִּי עִיקַּר הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא הַהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב בַּנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דְּ"לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִיא" (דְּבָרִים ל׳:י״ב)
for the essence of the Oral Torah is the disclosure of the Written Torah within Jewish souls in this world where 'it is not in heaven'.
וְהַכְּתָב הוּא דִּבְרֵי הַנָּבִיא מִפִּי ה' מְגַלֶּה הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ
And the written text represents the words of the prophet from the mouth of Hashem revealing ultimate truth,
אֶלָּא שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא נֶעְלָם
except that in this world it is veiled,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָדַעַת כְּלוּם מִתּוֹךְ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב רַק עַל יְדֵי פֵּירוּשָׁהּ שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and it is impossible to understand anything from the Written Torah except through its oral exposition.
שֶׁהוּא גִּלּוּי מַה שֶּׁבַּכְּתָב
which is the disclosure of what is written.
וּכְפִי הַגִּלּוּי דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא רַק הַאֲרָכַת שָׁנִים
And according to the manifest reality of this world it amounts only to lengthening of years,
כִּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת יוֹתֵר
for in this world it is impossible for more to be revealed,
שֶׁהֲרֵי אַף יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּלֹא מֵת
since even regarding Jacob our father who never died,
כְּפִי הַנִּגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הֲרֵי קְבָרוּ קָבְרַיָּא וְחָנְטוּ חָנְטַיָּא (תַּעֲנִית ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
according to the visible plane of this world the undertakers buried him and the embalmers embalmed him (Ta'anit 5b).

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 55a–b: Rav Ami said, “there is no death without sin, and no suffering without iniquity,” bringing proofs from Scripture (“the soul that sins — it shall die”). The Gemara challenges: it was taught that “four died only through the counsel of the serpent b’etyo shel nachash, without sin of their own — Binyamin son of Yaakov, Amram father of Moshe, Yishai father of David, and Kilav son of David” — proving that there is death without sin and suffering without iniquity, and refuting Rav Ami.

paragraphs.text: Mishlei 3:16: of Wisdom (the Torah) — “אֹרֶךְ יָמִים בִּימִינָהּ, בִּשְׂמֹאולָהּ עֹשֶׁר וְכָבוֹד” — “length of days is in her right hand; in her left, riches and honor.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Gemara (Shabbos 63a) — to those who engage the Torah for its own sake lishmah she grants “length of days” (her “right”), and even to those who do not, “riches and honor” (her “left”). R’ Tzadok’s use: “all the promises of the Torah are couched as length of days” — for the teshuvah of Yesod (the bris) redeems what would be death into “a lengthening of his days and years”; yet “a long thing still has an end, only that it is long” — unlike Yaakov, whose inheritance is “without bounds bli meitzarim,” and who therefore “did not die at all.”

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 80 (also Tikkun 20); Mei HaShiloach I, Bereishis §6. Tikkun 80 explains “אבני שיש טהור” and says “ולית הפרשה בין מים למים, דכלא יחודא חדא” — “there is no division between water and water, for all is one unity”; in that context it names “אילנא דחיי ... ואכל וחי לעולם” — “the Tree of Life ... he would eat and live forever.” Tikkun 20 also quotes R. Akiva’s warning “כשתגיעו לאבני שיש טהור אל תאמרו מים מים.” Thus the Zoharic phrase and Tree-of-Life context are confirmed. Rav Tzadok writes “וכן קבלתי” about the interpretation that the ultimate truth concerning Yaakov’s seed is concealed in this world, but does not identify the oral transmitter here. For a distinct Ishbitz parallel, Mei HaShiloach I, Bereishis §6 writes “ותשובה מרפאת את הקודם” — “repentance heals what preceded,” even a deficiency from birth. This parallel does NOT prove that the unnamed teaching was conveyed directly by the Ishbitzer.  |  Source links: Pri Tzaddik, Noach §6

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Even for the view that death comes only “through the serpent’s counsel,” that counsel is the inborn deficiency of desire — the guarding of the way to the Tree of Life. So the Zohar’s “teshuvah does not avail” means only that it cannot avail completely, turning sins into merits; for then the guard would be removed. Yet nothing stands before teshuvah: the teshuvah of the bris redeems death into length of days.

paragraphs.text: Kesubos 104a: it is related that at Rebbi’s passing “he raised his ten fingers toward Heaven and said: Master of the Universe, it is revealed and known before You that I toiled with my ten fingers in the Torah, and I derived no benefit from this world even with my small finger; may it be Your will that there be peace in my repose” — whereupon a Divine Voice proclaimed, “he enters in peace” (Yeshayah 57:2). Meforshim: Rashi — despite all his wealth and honor, Rebbi took no personal pleasure from this world; and the earlier commentators note the precision of “even with my little finger” (compare Pesachim 112b, “not all the fingers are alike”). R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the mark of the rung of holiness, which stands above mere piety — Rebbi did not merely restrain pleasure but sanctified it, so that even within his enjoyment “he derived no benefit from this world”; and he was the one who clarified, in this world, the hidden holiness that belongs to all Israel. Chabad parallel - Tanya, Likkutei Amarim, ch. 7: Tanya's treatment of kelipas nogah helps define the kind of kedushah R' Tzadok attributes to Rebbi. The Alter Rebbe distinguishes a permitted physical act performed merely to satisfy the body's appetite from the same physical vitality used 'lehar'chiv da'ato laHashem uleSoraso' or for the mitzvah of Oneg Shabbos and Yom Tov. In the latter case the vitality of the food and wine is itself clarified and rises to Hashem 'ke'olah u'chekorban.' Even an ordinary word of humor can be elevated when its purpose is to open the mind and gladden the heart for Torah and avodah. This is more than abstinence. The physical thing, precisely because it belongs to the mixed and permitted realm, can become a carrier of holiness. That distinction closely complements R' Tzadok's assertion that kedushah is higher than chassidus. Rebbi's statement that he benefited from this world 'not even with the small finger' cannot mean that his wealthy table or bodily life literally did not exist; R' Tzadok reads it to mean that the enjoyment was not appropriated as an independent worldly end. In Tanya's terms, the vitality itself can be taken up into avodah. Thus the fence of the bris and the sanctification of permissible enjoyment are two sides of the same Yesod: first the power is guarded from prohibited dispersion, and then the permitted physical life is joined to its Divine purpose. Rebbi's holiness is therefore not a flight from embodiment but the clarification of embodiment until even pleasure no longer stands opposite avodas Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 112b: “For not all fingers are alike.” The preceding teaching on112a says not to cook in a pot in which another has cooked: it first explains this as a divorcee whose former husband is alive, and alternatively extends the warning to a widow;112b supplies the concluding reason. “Finger” is a sexual euphemism in that local context. Rav Tzadok cites the phrase to explain the early commentators’ reading of Rebbi’s “small finger,” rather than as an unrelated general maxim.

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 84b: Rebbi sent a proposal of marriage to the widow of R’ Elazar b’Rabbi Shimon; she replied, “a vessel that was used for holiness my late husband, shall it now be used for the mundane?” — and the proverb, “in the place where the master of the house hangs his weapons, shall the lowly shepherd hang his satchel?” He sent to her, “granted he was greater than I in Torah — but in good deeds, who is greater than I?” She replied, “in Torah I do not know whether he was greater; in his deeds I do know, for he accepted sufferings upon himself”

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rebbi, of whom the Sages say he “came home after his death,” was a spark of Yaakov, who did not die — but once it became known he came no more, full revelation being impossible in this world. Of the line of David, Hillel and RaShbaG, he rectified teshuvah down to its Yesod — hence “Kadosh,” attained through the fence against immorality. Holiness surpasses piety: it brings holiness into physical pleasure itself.

p: (פז) וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (צ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
And therefore they taught in Sanhedrin (98b):
"אִי מִן חַיַּיָּא הוּא – כְּגוֹן רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ",
"If the Messiah is among the living, he is like Rabbeinu HaKadosh",
וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ (אֵיכָה רַבָּה ד, כב) וִירוּשַׁלְמִי (שַׁבָּת פֶּרֶק ט״ז הֲלָכָה א׳)
and in the Midrash (Eichah Rabbah 4:22) and Yerushalmi (Shabbat 16:1)
אָמְרוּ עָלָיו קְרָא דְּ"רוּחַ אַפֵּינוּ מְשִׁיחַ ה'" (אֵיכָה ד׳:כ׳)
they applied unto him the verse: 'The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of Hashem' (Lamentations 4:20),
שֶׁהוּא הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת דְּחִזְקִיָּה דְּגַם כֵּן בִּקְשׁוּ לַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ מָשִׁיחַ
he being the spiritual extension of Hezekiah whom they likewise sought to make Messiah (Sanhedrin 94a).
וּבְדוֹרוֹ הָיָה הַרְבָּצַת הַתּוֹרָה בְּיוֹתֵר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כַּיָּדוּעַ בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים
And in Hezekiah's generation there was the greatest dissemination of Torah in Israel, as known from our Sages.
וְכֵן בְּדוֹר רַבִּי
and so too in the generation of Rebbe.
וְאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ל״ו עַמּוּד א׳)
And they stated in Sanhedrin (36a):
דְּמִימוֹת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עַד רַבִּי לֹא הָיְתָה תּוֹרָה וּגְדוּלָּה בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד
that from the days of Moses our teacher until Rebbe, we do not find Torah and worldly greatness unified in one place.
וְחִזְקִיָּה לֹא הָיָה כּוּלֵי שַׁנֵּי
And with Hezekiah it was not so across all his years,
דַּהֲוֵי שֶׁבְנָא שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה כָּפוּף לוֹ
for there was Shebna who was not subservient to him,
וְרַבִּי מִשֶּׁנִּתְפַּרְסֵם וְנִתְגַּלָּה קְדוּשָׁתוֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּתְמַנָּה נָשִׂיא הָיָה הוּא הַיּוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל דְּהַכֹּל כְּפוּפִים לוֹ
whereas Rebbe, once his holiness became publicized and he was appointed Nasi, was preeminent and all were subservient to him.
כִּי כֵּן הַדּוֹרוֹת הוֹלְכִים בְּגִילּוּי יוֹתֵר עַד מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּתַכְלִית הַגִּלּוּי בַּפּוֹעַל
For the generations progress toward greater manifestation until the Messiah who will embody ultimate revelation in actuality,
וְאֵצֶל רַבִּי הָיָה גַּם כֵּן תַּכְלִית הַגִּלּוּי בְּכֹחַ
and with Rebbe there was likewise the ultimate revelation in potential.
הַיְינוּ כִּי יָדוּעַ דְּנֶפֶשׁ הַפַּרְנָס וְרֹאשׁ הַדּוֹר הוּא הַכּוֹלֵל כָּל הַדּוֹר
This is because the soul of the leader and head of the generation encompasses the entire generation.
כִּי לְעוֹלָם כָּל דּוֹר הוּא קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה, וְהָרֹאשׁ הוּא הָעִיקָּר וְכוּלָּם עֲנָפָיו
for every generation constitutes a complete stature, the head being primary and all others its branches.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּעֵרָכִין (י״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
Therefore they taught in Arachin (17a): ",
פַּרְנָס לְפִי הַדּוֹר" וְ"הַדּוֹר לְפִי הַפַּרְנָס", וּשְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת
'a leader corresponds to his generation' and 'a generation corresponds to its leader,' both being true,
אַף עַל גַּב דְּמַקְשֶׁה הָתָם מִצִּדְקִיָּה וִיהוֹיָקִים
even though the Gemara challenges there from Zedekiah and Jehoiakim,
הַיְינוּ לְעִנְיַן הַהִתְגַּלּוּת בַּפּוֹעַל בְּמַעֲשֶׂה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
that challenge pertained to manifest actions in this world.
וּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם תּוּקְפָּא וְנִיחוּתָא הַיְינוּ כֹּחוֹת הַלֵּב
and what was described there as firmness or gentleness reflects the inner capacities of the heart.
וּבְדוֹר רַבִּי הָיָה הִתְגַּלּוּת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה בּוֹ הַמְּעִידָה גַּם כֵּן עַל קְדֻשַּׁת כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים שֶׁהֵם עֲנָפָיו
And in Rebbe's generation the revelation of holiness in him attested to the sanctity of all Israel who were his branches:
וְהַקְּדוּשָּׁה הִיא הַמַּדְרֵגָה אַחֲרוֹנָה בְּמַדְרֵגוֹת דְּרַבִּי פִּינְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר בְּסוֹף סוֹטָה (מ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
And Kedushah is the final rung in the ladder of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair at the end of Sotah (49b)
(כְּפִי גִּירְסָא דִּילַן בַּגְּמָרָא וְהִיא הָעִיקָּר וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בָּזֶה בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר
(according to our text in the Gemara, which is primary, as I wrote elsewhere).
בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָדָם הַמְּבִיאָה לִידֵי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ וּבִיאַת אֵלִיָּהוּ וּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים
in human exertion that brings unto the Holy Spirit, the coming of Elijah, and the Resurrection of the Dead.
עַל כֵּן הָיָה מֵעֵין מָשִׁיחַ
Therefore he was a semblance of the Messiah,
אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה הַהִתְגַּלּוּת בַּפּוֹעַל בְּכָל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבַּדּוֹר
only that the revelation was not actualized in all the individual souls of the generation,
עַד שֶׁתָּשׁוּב הַנְּבוּאָה וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
until prophecy and the Holy Spirit return unto Israel.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לֶעָתִיד: "אֶשְׁפּוֹךְ (אֶת) רוּחִי עַל כָּל בָּשָׂר" (יוֹאֵל ג, א) וְיִזְכּוּ לִתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים
as it is said of the future: 'I will pour out My spirit upon all flesh' (Joel 3:1) and they will merit the Resurrection.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא זָכָה לְעַצְמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא מֵת
And nonetheless he merited for himself never to die,
וְזָכָה לְחַבֵּר הַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת חִבּוּר הַכּוֹלֵל כָּל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה עַד זְמַנּוֹ
and merited to compile the Mishnayot, a work encompassing all the Oral Torah which had never existed until his era.
וְהַתְחָלַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא מִדָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And the inception of the Oral Torah was from King David, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהִתְחִיל לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת אוֹר הַמַּלְכוּת פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ
when the light of Malchut began to shine—the mouth, which we title the Oral Torah.
וְתַכְלִיתוֹ בְּמָשִׁיחַ שֶׁאָז יִהְיֶה שְׁלֵימוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
And its culmination will be in the Messiah when the Oral Torah reaches utter perfection,
שֶׁהוּא הַחָכְמָה הַמִּתְגַּלֵּית עַל יְדֵי חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which is the wisdom disclosed through the sages of Israel in this world.
דְּעַד זְמַנּוֹ יִתְגַּלֶּה כָּל מַה שֶּׁמּוּכָן לְתַלְמִיד וָתִיק לְהִתְחַדֵּשׁ וּלְהִתְגַּלּוֹת
for until his time, whatever is destined for a veteran scholar to innovate will be disclosed.
וּבִימֵי רַבִּי הִתְחִיל שְׁלֵימוּת זֶה בְּחִבּוּר הַמִּשְׁנָה
And in Rebbe's days this perfection began through the redaction of the Mishnah,
שֶׁהוּא הַכּוֹלֵל כָּל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
which encompasses all the Oral Torah
וְגַם כָּל מַה שֶּׁתַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ נִכְלָל בָּהּ
and all that a veteran scholar is destined to innovate is contained within it.
אֶלָּא שֶׁעֲדַיִן הַכֹּל בְּכֹחַ לֹא בַּפּוֹעַל
save that it was then all in potential, not yet in actuality.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 98b. “אמר רב: אי מן חייא הוא, כגון רבינו הקדוש; אי מן מתיא הוא, כגון דניאל איש חמודות” — “Rav said: if he is among the living, he is like Rabbeinu HaKadosh; if among the departed, he is like Daniel, the treasured man.” Rav Tzadok calls Rebbi a foreshadowing of Messianic revelation. The Gemara gives a comparison, not a declaration that Rebbi was definitively the Messiah. The separate leader-and-generation analogy is treated at footnote 990 after Rav Tzadok develops it.  |  Source links: Sanhedrin 98b

paragraphs.text: Yerushalmi Shabbos 16:1; Eichah Rabbah ch. 4 (section numbering varies); Eichah 4:20. The Yerushalmi recounts that Rebbi injured his finger after studying Eichah; Rabbi Chiya said “בחובינו מטתך כן, דכתיב רוח אפינו משיח ה׳ נלכד בשחיתותם” — “On account of our sins this befell you, as it is written, ‘The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of Hashem, was caught in their pits.’” The verse’s plain biblical referent is a Davidic king (Rashi applies it to Yoshiyahu); the rabbinic episode applies its language honorifically to Rebbi. Compare the related narrative in Eichah Rabbah, numbered 4:23 in one arrangement. Rav Tzadok draws an interpretive parallel with Chizkiyah; that further connection is his exposition, not wording asserted by the Yerushalmi.  |  Source links: Eichah 4:20

paragraphs.text: Gittin 59a (and Sanhedrin 36a): “from the days of Moshe Rabbeinu until Rebbi we do not find Torah and greatness in one place.” Meforshim: Rashi — Rebbi united consummate mastery of Torah with the wealth and worldly eminence of the Nasi, a pairing unseen since Moshe. R’ Tzadok’s use: once appointed Nasi, Rebbi “was the greatest of all, for all were subordinate to him” — the head of the generation, whose complete “stature” bears the whole generation as its branches.

paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah I §74; Tanya, Likkutei Amarim ch. 2. Rav Tzadok writes in Kometz HaMinchah: “וכן כל צדיק הדור זולת משה עון הדור פוגם בו ... וזהו פרנס לפי הדור” — “Every righteous leader of a generation other than Moshe is affected by the sin of the generation ... and this is ‘the leader according to the generation.’” The distinction follows his description of Moshe’s self-sustaining light as the sun and Yehoshua’s received light as the moon. Tanya ch. 2 offers a complementary analogy: “וכן בכל דור ודור יש ראשי אלפי ישראל, שנשמותיהם הם בחינת ראש ומוח לגבי נשמות ההמון ועמי הארץ” — “In every generation there are leaders whose souls are in the aspect of head and brain relative to the souls of the multitude.” Together they illuminate Rav Tzadok’s developed point that the head and its members form one spiritual body, while the texts retain their respective emphases.  |  Source links: Kometz HaMinchah I §74

paragraphs.text: Erchin 17a: On the verse “this is the generation of those who seek Him, who seek Your face — Yaakov, selah” (Tehillim 24:6), R’ Yehudah Nesi’ah and the Rabbanan disagreed: one said “the generation (is) according to the leader (parnas),” and one said “the leader according to his generation.” The Gemara challenges (that this cannot concern their relative worthiness) — for there was Tzidkiyah, who was worthy though his generation was not, and Yehoyakim, who was not worthy though his generation was; “rather,” it concludes, “we speak with regard to tukfa (severity) and nichusa (mildness).”

paragraphs.text: Yoel 3:1: of the Future — “וְהָיָה אַחֲרֵי כֵן אֶשְׁפּוֹךְ אֶת רוּחִי עַל כָּל בָּשָׂר, וְנִבְּאוּ בְּנֵיכֶם וּבְנֹתֵיכֶם” — “and it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out My spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and daughters shall prophesy.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Radak — in the Messianic era prophecy will be restored, universally, to Israel. R’ Tzadok’s use: Rebbi was “akin to Mashiach,” yet the revelation was not yet “in actuality in all the souls of the generation” — that awaits the Future, when “I will pour out My spirit upon all flesh” and all merit ruach hakodesh and the resurrection of the dead.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rebbi was “akin to Mashiach” — “if he is among the living, it is one such as Rabbeinu HaKadosh” — an extension of Chizkiyah, whom too Hashem sought to make Mashiach. In both their generations Torah and greatness reached their peak; but Chizkiyah was not preeminent throughout, whereas Rebbi, once appointed Nasi, had all subordinate to him. The generations advance toward ever-greater revelation; in Rebbi it was the ultimate revelation in potential.

p: (פח) וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּסוֹף נִדָּה (עג.) שֶׁהוּא סִיּוּם הַשַּׁ״ס
And therefore they stated at the end of Niddah (73a), which concludes the Talmud:
כָּל הַשּׁוֹנֶה הֲלָכוֹת בְּכָל יוֹם מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא
“Whoever reviews halakhot each day is assured that he is a person destined for the World to Come.”
דַּ"הֲלָכוֹת" רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר מִשְׁנָה
For 'halakhot' denotes the Mishnah,
דְּקָרוּ לֵיהּ הֲלָכוֹת וְהִלְכְתָא בְּכָל הַשַּׁ״ס וּמִדְרָשׁוֹת
which is termed halakhot throughout the Talmud and Midrashim.
שֶׁבָּזֶה זוֹכֶה לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם
through which one merits eternal life.
דְּהָאֲחִיזָה בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
For grasping hold of the Torah occurs solely through the Oral Torah,
שֶׁבָּהּ הוּא הַגִּלּוּי דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הַמּוּשָּׂג לַלְּבָבוֹת וְנַפְשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
wherein resides the disclosure of the Written Torah accessible to Jewish hearts and souls.
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
which is impossible to comprehend in the Written Torah save through the Oral.
כִּי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הוּא הוֹפָעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹרוֹ לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
For the Written Torah was the manifestation of Hashem's light unto Israel at the Giving of the Torah,
דְּנַעֲשׂוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה חֵירוּת מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע
whereby they attained liberation from the evil inclination,
וְאָז הָיָה דַּי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב לְבַד
and then the Written Torah alone was sufficient.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּנְדָרִים (כ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
as the Gemara states in Nedarim 22b:
דְּאַלְמָלֵא חָטְאוּ לֹא נִיתְּנָה לָהֶם אֶלָּא הַתּוֹרָה וְסֵפֶר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ – עֶרְכָּהּ שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
had they not sinned, only the Torah and the Book of Joshua—delineating the boundaries of the Land—would have been given.
דְּהַתּוֹרָה הוּא מִצַּד הַזְּמַן וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ וְנִיתְּנָה בַּמִּדְבָּר
For the Torah relates to Time and Soul, given in the wilderness,
דִּקְבִיעוּת הַמָּקוֹם הוּא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ בְּסֵפֶר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
while the fixation of Place was detailed in the Book of Joshua.
וּבֵיאַרְתִּי זֶה בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר
and I explained this elsewhere.
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים הָיָה דַּי לָהֶם לִהְיוֹת מוּבָן הַכֹּל מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב לְבַד
At any rate, it would have been sufficient for them to understand all from the Written Torah alone.
כִּי הָיָה גָּלוּי אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתּוֹרָה הַמֵּאִיר וּמְגַלֶּה כָּל נֶעְלָם
for Hashem's light shone openly in the Torah, illuminating every mystery.
אֲבָל עַל יְדֵי הַחֵטְא נֶעְלַם זֶה
However, through sin this clarity was veiled,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּעְלַם הָאוֹר דְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית שֶׁנִּגְנַז לַצַּדִּיקִים לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא
just as the primordial light of Creation was concealed for the righteous in the World to Come.
שֶׁאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה יב.) דְּנִגְנַז בַּתּוֹרָה
which they taught was hidden within the Torah.
וְהַהִתְגַּלּוּת הוּא עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהוּא תִּיקּוּן הַחֵטְא
And this revelation returns via the Oral Torah which rectifies sin,
כִּי הַתּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין לְיֵצֶר הָרָע
for the Torah is a spice against the evil inclination,
וְלֹא עַל לְהַבָּא לְבַד רַק גַּם עַל מַה שֶּׁעָבַר
and not merely for the future, but also for what is past,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כה, א) בְּתִיקּוּן הָעֲבֵירוֹת לְהוֹסִיף בְּלִמּוּד
and as our Sages taught regarding the remedy for transgressions: to add in Torah study.
וּבָזֶה נִתְתַּבֵּל הַיֵּצֶר
and through this the inclination is seasoned and sweetened.
וּכְפִי הַהַעֲמָקָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
And in proportion to one's depth in words of Torah,
כָּךְ יוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג מַעֲמַקֵּי מַדְרֵגַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה לְתַקֵּן הַקּוֹדֵם
so can he attain the profound depths of Repentance to rectify the past;
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַיְגִיעָה בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה לְהַשִּׂיג מַעֲמַקֵּי הַתּוֹרָה
for through toil in the Oral Torah to reach the depths of the Torah,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְגַּלֶּה לוֹ כָּל אוֹרוֹת הַתּוֹרָה לִהְיוֹת מְאִירִים לוֹ,
all lights of the Torah are unveiled to shine for him.
וּמִמֵּילָא נִדְחֶה כָּל מִינֵי חֶשְׁכוּת
and all forms of darkness are spontaneously dispelled.
וְעַל כֵּן בִּשְׁלֵימוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נִשְׁלַם כָּל תִּיקּוּן הַקּוֹדֵם
Therefore, in the perfection of the Oral Torah the complete rectification of the past is culminated.
וְנִתְגַּלָּה אוֹר הַבָּהִיר שֶׁבִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דַּאֲחִידָא בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וּבְעֵץ הַחַיִּים
and the radiant light within Israel who grasp the Torah and the Tree of Life is disclosed.

Rav Tzadok observes, “ונראה דלשון שונה דייק דמשמע שינון משנה בדינים והלכות” — “The word shoneh is precise, denoting repeated recitation or review of Mishnah in laws and halachos.” His immediate discussion concerns the obligation to remember Shabbos orally, rather than the Niddah teaching itself. inlineHeadings.text: The theme: At the very close of the Talmud: “whoever studies halachos every day is assured a share in the World to Come” — for “halachos” means the Mishnah, and through it one merits eternal life. The grasp of Torah comes only by way of the Oral Torah, which is the revelation of the Written Torah to Israel’s hearts; the Written cannot be grasped except through it. Had they not sinned, the Chumash and the Book of Yehoshua would have sufficed.

p: (פט) וְהִתְחִיל הִתְעוֹרְרוּת גִּלּוּי אוֹר זֶה בִּימֵי רַבִּי בְּחִבּוּר הַמִּשְׁנָה
And the awakening of this revelation began in the days of Rebbe through compiling the Mishnah,
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (ז׳:ג׳)
wherefore they expounded in Vayikra Rabbah (7:3),
דִּבִּזְכוּת הַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת הַגָּלִיּוֹת מִתְקַבְּצִים
that in the merit of the Mishnayot the exiles are gathered,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "גַּם כִּי יִתְנוּ בַגּוֹיִם עַתָּה אֲקַבְּצֵם" (הוֹשֵׁעַ ח׳:י׳)
as it is stated: 'Yea, though they study (yitnu) among the nations, now will I gather them' (Hosea 8:10).
וְהוּא קִבּוּץ הַנִּדָּחִים שֶׁל כָּל הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמְפוּזָּרוֹת
And this is the gathering of all the dispersed sparks of the children of Israel.
שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי עֲוֹן קִלְקוּל הַבְּרִית כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
which were scattered through the blemish of the Covenant as mentioned above.
וְעַל כֵּן לִמּוּד הַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת נִרְאֶה לִי דְּהוּא תִּיקּוּן לַעֲוֹן קֶרִי וְהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה
Therefore, studying the Mishnayot appears to me to be the specific rectification for seminal emission and wasting seed.
וּמוֹעִיל לְקַבֵּץ הַנִּדָּחִים וּלְהַחֲזִירָם לִקְדוּשָּׁה
and is effective to assemble the dispersed and restore them to holiness.
כִּי כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שָׁרְשָׁם בַּתּוֹרָה
For all the souls of the children of Israel are rooted in the Torah,
דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וְיִשְׂרָאֵל חַד
for the Torah and Israel are one (Zohar III, 73a),
בְּסוֹד נֶפֶשׁ דְּדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
in the mystery of the generation of the wilderness, Moses' generation, who received the Written Torah,
שָׁרְשָׁם בְּאוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב כַּיָּדוּעַ.
their roots being inscribed in the letters of the Written Torah as is known.
וּשְׁאָר הַדּוֹרוֹת שֶׁהֵם הָעֲנָפִים הַמִּתְפַּשְּׁטִים מֵאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר
And the subsequent generations who are branches extending from that primal generation.
נִרְאֶה לִי דְּשָׁרְשָׁם בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁהוּא הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
it appears to me that their soul-roots reside in the Oral Torah, which is the unfolding expansion of the Written Torah.
וְלֵיכָּא מִידֵי דְּלָא רְמִיזֵי בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב (תַּעֲנִית ט׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
And there is nothing that is not hinted within the Written Torah (Ta'anit 9a),
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא שָׁם בְּרֶמֶז וְהֶעְלֵם
only that it is there in subtle hint and concealment,
וְכָךְ הָיוּ נַפְשׁוֹת שְׁאָר כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת גְּנוּזוֹת וּכְלוּלוֹת בְּהֶעְלֵם בְּדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר, שֶׁהֲרֵי מֵהֶם יָצְאוּ.
and so the souls of all subsequent generations were concealed and encompassed within the generation of the wilderness, since from them they issued forth.
וּכְפִי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַמִּתְחַדֶּשֶׁת בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר
And corresponding to the Oral Torah innovated in each respective generation.
כֵּן הֵם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר
such are the souls of Israel flourishing in that era.

The passage says: “כל אחד מישראל יש לו אחיזה ודביקות נשמתו בתורה ... אמנם חלק של אחד לא ימצא השני אף שהוא גדול ממנו” — “Every Jew has a hold and cleaving of his soul in Torah ... yet one person’s particular portion cannot be found by another, even someone greater.” It adds that a lesser scholar can uncover the pearl belonging to his own portion. inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The awakening of this revelation began in Rebbi’s days with the composition of the Mishnah — hence “by the merit of the Mishnayos the exiles are gathered in.” Rebbi gathered the outcasts: the scattered sparks of Israel’s souls. So studying Mishnayos, it appears to R’ Tzadok, is itself a rectification for damage to the bris, gathering those outcasts back to holiness — for the Torah and Israel are one.

p: (צ) וְיָדוּעַ דְּעַל יְדֵי עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע
And it is known that through the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil,
דְּגַם תּוֹרָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַמּוּשֶּׂגֶת עַתָּה הוּא מִסִּטְרָא דְּעֵץ הַדַּעַת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּתִּיקּוּנִים
in that even the Torah accessible in this world now operates from the aspect of the Tree of Knowledge as stated in Tikkunei Zohar.
נִמְסְרוּ הַרְבֵּה דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לַחִיצוֹנִים שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהוֹצִיא מֵהֶם
many words of Torah were surrendered unto external forces whence they must be redeemed.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הַרְבֵּה פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת מֵאֻמּוֹת
Just as there exist in the Written Torah many narratives involving foreign nations,
וְדִבְרֵי לָבָן וְעֵשָׂו וּפַרְעֹה וְכַיּוֹצֵא וּפָרָשַׁת בִּלְעָם וּבָלָק וְכַדּוֹמֶה
and the speeches of Laban, Esau, Pharaoh, and the narrative of Balaam and Balak, and the like,
וְהֵם דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁנִּמְסְרוּ מֵחֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן לַמָּקוֹם שֶׁנִּמְסְרוּ.
these being words of Torah surrendered through the sin of Adam the First unto where they fell.
וּבִשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה חָזְרוּ הַכֹּל לִקְדוּשָּׁה
And at the Giving of the Torah all these reverted unto holiness,
וְיָצְתָה כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ מִנְּרָתִיקָהּ לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת לְנַפְשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁלֵימוּתָהּ,
and the entire Torah emerged from its sheath to be revealed unto the souls of Israel in its complete splendor,
עַד שֶׁאִלְמָלֵא זָכוּ הָיָה אָז עֵת קֵץ הַגָּמוּר
to the extent that had they merited, that would have been the ultimate End of Days
לִהְיוֹת חֵירוּת מִמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת וְיֵצֶר הָרָע וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת
to attain freedom from the Angel of Death, the evil inclination, and worldly servitude (Avodah Zarah 5a).
אֶלָּא שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא
except that sin intervened.
וְאַף דְּהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הוּא כְּבָר בִּשְׁלֵימוּתָהּ לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד וְ"לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי" (תְּהִלִּים קמ״ז:כ׳)
And even though the Written Torah stands in its totality for Israel alone, 'He did not do so unto any nation' (Psalms 147:20),
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה עֲדַיִן יֵשׁ בָּהּ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהוֹצִיא מֵהַחִיצוֹנִים
nevertheless, in the unfolding expansion of the Oral Torah there remain sparks that must be extracted from the external realms.
רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר שֶׁנִּמְסַר עַל יְדֵי הַחֲטָאִים דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּבְיִחוּד עָוֹן דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה
meaning that which was surrendered through the sins of Israel, particularly the sin of wasting seed.
אֶלָּא שֶׁזֶּה אֵינוֹ אֶצְלָם דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה גְּלוּיִים בַּפּוֹעַל כְּמוֹ בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
Only that among the nations these do not exist as explicit words of Torah as in the Written Torah.
שֶׁמִּדִּבְרֵיהֶם וְשִׂיחָתָם מַמָּשׁ נַעֲשָׂה דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
where from their actual historical speech scriptural portions were formed.
כִּי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הוּא מַחְשֶׁבֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּבְרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם
For the Written Torah was the thought of Hashem in creating the universe,
דְּעַל כֵּן הוּא דְּפוּס שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית
wherefore it serves as the blueprint of Creation,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה א׳)
as they stated in Bereishit Rabbah (Parashah 1).
שֶׁהִיא הַדִּפְתְּרָאוֹת וּפִנְקְסָאוֹת שֶׁל צִיּוּר כָּל הָעוֹלָמוֹת הַנּוֹצָרִים וְנִבְרָאִים
that it was the parchment and ledger for sketching all worlds formed and created.
וְגַם הָאֻמּוֹת מִכְּלַל בְּרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם וְיֵשׁ גַּם בָּהֶם אוֹתִיּוֹת דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
And the nations are likewise part of the world's creation, containing letters of Torah.
שֶׁמִּזֶּה נִמְשָׁךְ הַנִּיצוֹץ הַמְחַיֶּה אוֹתָם, דְּלוּלֵי כֵן לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם שׁוּם מְצִיאוּת כְּלָל
whence is drawn the spark that animates them, for without it they would possess no existence at all.
וְעַל כֵּן הֶחֱזִיר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הַתּוֹרָה עַל כָּל אֻמָּה וְלָשׁוֹן לְקַבְּלָהּ
Therefore the Holy One offered the Torah to every nation and tongue to receive it (Avodah Zarah 2b).
כִּי הָיָה לָהֶם גַּם כֵּן צַד שַׁיָּיכוּת מַה אֵלֶיהָ כְּפִי הַדִּמְיוֹן שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
because they retained some superficial affinity to it according to the illusion of this world.
אַךְ כְּפִי הָאֱמֶת דְּשָׁרְשָׁם בְּרַע, כָּל מְצִיאוּתָם הוּא בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל וּלְצָרְכָּם
Yet according to the truth that their root is in evil, their whole existence is for the sake of Israel,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהֵם בְּעַצְמָם עֲתִידִים לוֹמַר לֶעָתִיד כְּשֶׁיַּכִּירוּ הָאֱמֶת
as they themselves are destined to acknowledge in the future when they recognize the truth:
דְּהַרְבֵּה כְּרַכִּים וּגְשָׁרִים וּמֶרְחֲצָאוֹת וְכוּלֵי הַכֹּל בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ב׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
'all the market-places, bridges, and bathhouses we built were solely for Israel,' as stated in Avodah Zarah (2b).
וְהַיְינוּ דְּבֶאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ הָיָה הַכֹּל בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל, רַק שֶׁהֵם לֹא כִּיוְּונוּ לָזֶה
Which means that in ultimate truth all was for Israel, only that they did not intend it,
וְעַל כֵּן כָּל הָאוֹתִיּוֹת דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהָיָה בָּהֶם מִצַּד הַשְׁפָּעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּבְּרִיאָה נִיטַּל מֵהֶם
wherefore all letters of Torah within them through divine creation were taken from them,
וְנִיתַּן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹרָשָׁה קְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב
and granted to Israel as an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob,
וְגוֹי הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה חַיָּיב מִיתָה
and a gentile who occupies himself with Torah is liable to death (Sanhedrin 59a).

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Through the Tree of Knowledge, even the Torah as grasped in this world is from that Tree’s side, and many words of Torah were “handed over to the outer forces” to be extracted from them. Hence the Written Torah contains many narratives concerning the nations, including the words of Lavan, Esav, Pharaoh, Bilaam and Balak. At Sinai all of it returned to holiness and the whole Torah came forth from its sheath — had they merited then, it would have been the final End.

p: (צא) אֲבָל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא מַה שֶּׁחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹצְאִים מִלִּבָּם
However, the Oral Torah is that which the sages of Israel draw forth from their heart.
דָּבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּיַד בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
and this spiritual capacity belongs exclusively to the children of Israel.
וְהָאוֹמֵר "יֵשׁ תּוֹרָה בָּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם" – אַל תַּאֲמֵן
And 'if one says to you: there is Torah among the nations—do not believe it',
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ חָכְמָה בָּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם (אֵיכָה רַבָּה ב׳:י״ג)
For although wisdom is found among the nations of the world (Eichah Rabbah 2:13),
מֵחָכְמָתָם אֵין נַעֲשֶׂה דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּלָל
from their secular wisdom words of Torah are never made.
רַק מֵחָכְמָה הַנּוֹבַעַת מִלֵּב בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
only from the wisdom gushing from the holy heart of Israel.
וְלֹא בְּחִנָּם אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה לָשׁוֹן זֶה: "אִם יֹאמַר לְךָ אָדָם יֵשׁ תּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי",
And not without reason did our Sages formulate this precise phrasing: 'If a man says to you there is Torah, etc.';
וּמֵהֵיכָא תֵּיתֵי יֹאמַר כֵּן
for from where would it enter one's mind to say so;
אֲבָל הֵם צָפוּ בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ מַה שֶּׁעֲתִידִין הַמִּתְפַּלְסְפִים שֶׁבַּדּוֹרוֹת אַחֲרוֹנִים לוֹמַר
rather they foresaw through the Holy Spirit what philosophers in later generations would assert,
כִּי חָכְמָה חִיצוֹנִית דִּבְנֵי יָוָן הֵם סִתְרֵי תוֹרָה
claiming that the external philosophy of the Greeks represents the esoteric secrets of Torah.
וְהוֹדִיעוּ לָנוּ שֶׁלֹּא נַאֲמִין
and our Sages warned us never to believe it.
וְלֹא זֶהוּ הַדֶּרֶךְ בְּהוֹצָאַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מֵהַחִיצוֹנִים לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חָכְמָתָם כְּמוֹת שֶׁהוּא
And it is not the legitimate path of redeeming holy sparks to import their pagan philosophy as it stands,
וְלוֹמַר שֶׁזֶּהוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁנִּקְלַט מֵהֶם
and declare that this constitutes words of Torah reclaimed from them,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב פָּרָשַׁת בִּלְעָם
after the model of the Written Torah containing the parashah of Balaam,
דְּהָיָה מִנְּבִיאֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה
for Balaam prophesied to the nations prior to the Torah being given.
וּמִשֶּׁנִּיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה כְּבָר נָטְלוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהָיָה בָּהֶם מֵהֶם
and once the Torah was given, all words of Torah embedded in the nations were reclaimed from them.
וְאָמְרוּ בְּתַנְחוּמָא (כִּי תִשָּׂא ל״ד)
And they taught in Midrash Tanchuma (Ki Sisa 34),
דְּעַל כֵּן נִיתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
that for this reason the Oral Torah was given orally,
שֶׁעֲתִידִין אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לְתַרְגֵּם הַתּוֹרָה יְוָנִית וְלוֹמַר: "אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל",
because the nations of the world were destined to translate the Scriptures into Greek and claim: 'We are Israel',
וְיֹאמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: "מִי שֶׁמִּסְטוֹרִין שֶׁלִּי בְּיָדוֹ וְכוּלֵי".
whereupon the Holy One will declare: 'Only he who holds My intimate mysteries (mysterion) is Israel'.
וְהַיְינוּ דִּלְתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב יֵשׁ גַּם לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת
Which means that to the Written Torah the nations also have some access.
שֶׁגַּם מִדִּבְרֵיהֶם יֵשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה דְּעַל כֵּן נִגְלֵית בִּכְתָב לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם
for their speeches are recorded in Scripture which is displayed openly to all humanity.
אֲבָל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא מִסְטוֹרִין שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
However, the Oral Torah represents the esoteric mystery of the Holy One,
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹתוֹ בִּכְתָב כְּלָל
which cannot be committed to writing at all,
דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא נִכְתַּב בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
wherefore it was not written in the scriptural text,
רַק "סוֹד ה' לִירֵאָיו" (תְּהִלִּים כה, יד)
Rather, ‘the secret of Hashem belongs to those who fear Him’ (Psalms 25:14)—
הֵם כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל "אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה'" (מִשְׁלֵי לא, ל)
these being Knesses Yisrael, ‘a woman who fears Hashem’ (Proverbs 31:30),
דְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבָם צוֹפֶה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
whose innermost heart gazes continuously unto Hashem,
דְּעִיקַּר הַיִּרְאָה בַּלֵּב
for the primary seat of awe is in the heart,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּיוֹמָא (עב:) עַל פָּסוּק "וְלֵב אָיִן" (מִשְׁלֵי יז, טז)
as taught in Yoma 72b concerning ‘when there is no heart’ (Proverbs 17:16),
וְעַל יְדֵי כָּךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן בְּקֶרֶב לְבָבָם
and through this Hashem abides within their heart.
וְלָכֵן יוּכְלוּ לְהַשִּׂיג מִסְטוֹרָיו וְסוֹד ה' הַגָּנוּז בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
and therefore they alone can attain His intimate mysteries and the divine secret hidden in the Written Torah.
וְהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הוּא נוֹבְלוֹת חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה יז, ה)
And the Written Torah is the unripe fruit of Supernal Wisdom, as taught in Bereishis Rabbah 17:5,
וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא נוֹבְלוֹת בִּינָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה
while the Oral Torah is the unripe fruit of Supernal Understanding (Binah),
דְּהִיא לִבָּא וְתַמָּן הַלֵּב מֵבִין
which corresponds to the Heart wherein the heart understands.
וּמִמֶּנָּה נִשְׁפָּע הַבִּינָה לַלְּבָבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהָבִין דָּבָר מִתּוֹךְ דָּבָר שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
and from it understanding flows into Jewish hearts to discern one concept out of another within the Written Torah.
וּבְחָכְמָה שֶׁהוּא רֵאשִׁית הַגִּלּוּי דְּיֵשׁ מֵאַיִן
And within Chokhmah, which is the inception of manifestation of substance from nothingness,
כִּנְקֻדָּה בִּלְבַד בְּלֹא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת לְאֹרֶךְ וְרֹחַב
existing as a mere point without spatial expansion in length and breadth,
דְּעַל כֵּן רְמוּזָה בְּאוֹת יוֹ"ד שֶׁבַּשֵּׁם כַּיָּדוּעַ,
wherefore it is alluded to by the letter Yud of the Tetragrammaton as is known,
יֵשׁ מָקוֹם לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לִטְעוֹת שֶׁגַּם הֵם נִגְלִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְיֵשׁ.
there is room for the nations to mistakenly presume that they too appear in this world as autonomous substance.
וְעַל כֵּן יֵשׁ חָכְמָה בָּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם גַּם כֵּן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
Therefore secular wisdom exists among the nations in this world as our Sages noted,
עַד לֶעָתִיד דְּ"הַאֲבַדְתִּי חֲכָמִים מֵאֱדוֹם" (עֹבַדְיָה א, ח)
until the future when ‘I will destroy the wise men out of Edom’ (Obadiah 1:8),
כִּי אָז "ה' בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ וְאֵין (עִמּוֹ אֵל נֵכָר)" (דְּבָרִים לב, יב)
For then ‘Hashem alone shall lead him, and there is no foreign god with Him’ (Deuteronomy 32:12).
אֲבָל הַבִּינָה שֶׁהוּא הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת רֵאשִׁית הַגִּלּוּי הַסָּתוּם לִהְיוֹת נִגְלֶה מְפוֹרָשׁ בְּלֵב מֵבִין
However, Binah which is the expansion of the hidden primordial revelation into clear disclosure in the discerning heart,
תַּמָּן "נִבְעוּ מַצְפֻּנָיו" (עֹבַדְיָה א, ו) דְּעֵשָׂו וַחֲבֵירָיו כָּל שָׂרֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
there are exposed the hidden treasures of Esau (Obadiah 1:6) and his peers, all the princes of the nations.
שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת אֶל הַקְּדוּשָּׁה
demonstrating that they hold no connection whatsoever unto holiness.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Yisro §3): “"and your ears shall hear a word from behind you" — which is expounded, that a bas kol is made use of; and in the Yerushalmi they learned a halachah from a woman who said something in passing.” The qualification is essential: this passage speaks of speech within Israel, even among those who do not understand its Torah depth, through the covenant of circumcision. R’ Tzadok then contrasts this with “He did not do so for any nation.” The source therefore illuminates §91’s completed distinction: ordinary Israelite speech may unknowingly carry a word of Oral Torah, while one cannot simply declare the nations’ wisdom, as it stands, to be Torah. It is not an example of extracting Torah from gentile conversation. The source states: “והיינו דאף שלא ידעו מה שאומרים מכל מקום מופיע בישראל דבר ה׳ שהוא תורה שבעל פה” — “Even though they did not know what they were saying, the word of Hashem—which is the Oral Torah—nevertheless appears within Israel.”

paragraphs.text: Tanchuma, Ki Sisa 34 (primary source; not Noach 3 for this episode): “וּלְפִי שֶׁצָּפָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם עֲתִידִין לְתַרְגֵּם אֶת הַתּוֹרָה ... וְהֵם אוֹמְרִים אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל” — “The Holy One foresaw that the nations would translate the Torah ... and say, ‘We are Israel.’” The answer is “אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁמִּסְטוֹרִין שֶׁלִּי אֶצְלוֹ, הֵם בָּנַי” — “Only those who possess My mysteries are My children”; the Midrash explicitly identifies these mysteries as the orally transmitted Mishnah. Tanchuma Noach 3 also contrasts Written Torah and Oral Torah, but the actual ‘we are Israel/My mysteries’ dialogue is in Ki Sisa 34. Rav Tzadok uses this contrast to explain why Written Torah can circulate publicly while Oral Torah retains an inward covenantal character.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §26): “In truth they said (Eichah Rabbah 2:13, expounding Eichah 2:9): ‘there is Torah among the nations of the world — do not believe,’ for it is ‘the inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov’ alone. And in the manner they said (Tanchuma, Ki Sisa 34), that ‘in the Future the nations will say, we are Israel,’ etc. — the Torah is ‘My mystery.’ And this is the meaning of the resting of the Shechinah: that they will not attain the wisdom of the Oral Torah.” (Exactly the se’if’s distinction: the Oral Torah is ‘the inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov’ alone — ‘whoever says there is Torah among the nations, do not believe’ — for it is drawn from Israel’s own heart and is in Israel’s hand alone.) Chabad context - Likkutei Torah, Pinchas 4:11: Likkutei Torah gives a precise reason that Torah Shebe'al Peh cannot be reduced to human wisdom. 'Malchus peh Torah Shebe'al Peh karinan lah': the mouth/Malchus is called Oral Torah, and although Malchus 'leis lah migarmah klum,' it is the revelation of the innermost Divine will. Torah and mitzvos, the Alter Rebbe explains, are the pnimiyus ratzono, and that inner will descends all the way into the most physical details of the six orders of Mishnah in order to lift the lower world into its Source. Thus the human mouth and the concrete halachic case are not alternatives to revelation; they are the vessels through which the inner will becomes articulated below. This complements R' Tzadok's distinction between chochmah among the nations and Torah found in the heart of Israel. A philosopher can reach a true intellectual proposition and it remains chochmah. Torah Shebe'al Peh is a different category because its claim is not simply that the conclusion is clever or correct, but that the inward Divine ratzon is being disclosed through the covenantal mouth of Knesses Yisrael. This is also why its apparently mundane discussions do not make it less 'mistorin': the very descent into physical particulars is the form in which pnimiyus ratzon reaches the earthly realm. Likkutei Torah therefore supplies a Chabad parallel to R' Tzadok's Binah/Malchus language: the Oral Torah has no independent 'self' that could be duplicated by foreign philosophy, yet precisely as the receptive mouth of Israel it becomes the place where the hidden Divine will is spoken.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 25:14: “סוֹד ה’ לִירֵאָיו, וּבְרִיתוֹ לְהוֹדִיעָם” — “the secret sod of Hashem is to those who fear Him, and His covenant, to make it known to them.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Radak — God confides His hidden counsel only to those who fear Him. R’ Tzadok’s use: this alone was set (concealed) in the Written Torah — that the Oral Torah, His “mystery,” belongs to Knesses Yisrael, “the woman who fears Hashem” (Mishlei 31:30), who from the depths of the heart look to Him; “the essence of fear is in the heart” (Yoma 72b), so that Hashem dwells within their heart and they can grasp His hidden secret concealed in the Written Torah.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: But the Oral Torah is what Israel’s sages draw from their own heart, and this alone is in Israel’s hand. “Whoever says there is Torah among the nations, do not believe” — there is chochmah among them, but no words of Torah are made from it. The Sages foresaw by ruach ha-kodesh the later philosophizers who would call Greek wisdom “the secrets of the Torah,” and warned us not to believe it.

p: (צב) וְעַל כֵּן בִּינָה וּמַלְכוּת שְׁנֵיהֶם רְמוּזִים בְּאוֹתִיּוֹת הַהֵהִי"ן דַּשֵּׁם כַּיָּדוּעַ.
And therefore Binah (Understanding) and Malchut (Sovereignty) are both alluded to by the two letters Hei of the Tetragrammaton, as is known:
דִּבְהֵ"א נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה (מְנָחוֹת כט:)
For this world was created with the letter Hei (Menachos 29b),
שֶׁהוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כָּל מִינֵי נִבְרָאִים שׁוֹנִים
which is the expansion of all manner of diverse created beings,
וְיֵשׁ מָקוֹם לָצֵאת לְמִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם)
and there is an opening below for whoever wishes to depart, as the Sages explain there,
וְהָאֻמּוֹת הֵם הַיּוֹצְאִים וְלֹא נִשְׁאֲרוּ שָׁם
and the gentile nations are those who depart through that gap and do not remain within.
וְאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְגוּף הַהֵ"א הָרוֹמֵז לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
holding no intrinsic connection to the holy body of the letter Hei which alludes to the Congregation of Israel.
וְקוֹדֶם שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא הוּא הֵ"א תַּחְתּוֹנָה
And prior to sin man resides in the lower Hei (Malchut),
וְאַחַר שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא וְיָשׁוּב – דִּמְעַיְּילָא לֵיהּ בְּהַךְ וְקוֹשְׁרִין לוֹ כֶּתֶר כִּדְאִיתָא הָתָם
– and after he sins and repents—where they re-admit him through the upper opening and tie a crown for him as stated there—
זֶהוּ הֵ"א עֶלְיוֹנָה
this corresponds to the upper Hei (Binah)
הָרוֹמֶזֶת לִתְשׁוּבָה דְּ"לְבָבוֹ יָבִין וְשָׁב" (יְשַׁעְיָה ו, י) כַּיָּדוּעַ.
which alludes to Repentance, in the verse 'and his heart understands, and he returns' (Isaiah 6:10), as is known.
וּבִמְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין וְכוּלֵי (בְּרָכוֹת לד:)
And ‘in the place where penitents stand’ (Berachos 34b),
דְּמִתְעַלִּין עַל צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים שֶׁעוֹלִין דֶּרֶךְ פֶּתַח הָעֶלְיוֹן
for they transcend the wholly righteous by ascending directly through the supernal upper aperture,
וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא קוֹשֵׁר לָהֶם כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן
and the Holy One, blessed be He, binds for them a transcendent crown
לִדְבַּק בְּבִינָה אִמָּא עִילָּאָה
to cleave unto Binah, the Supernal Mother,
שֶׁהִיא לְמַעְלָה מַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגַת צַדִּיק גָּמוּר
which is exalted far above the stature of the wholly righteous.
וְעַל כֵּן רוֹמֶזֶת גַּם כֵּן לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
wherefore it likewise alludes unto the World to Come:
אַף דְּהָעוֹלָם הַבָּא נִבְרָא בְּיוֹ"ד (מְנָחוֹת כט:)
Even though the World to Come was created with the letter Yud (Menachos 29b),
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אוֹתָם הַנּוֹחֲלִים עוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁהֵם כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
nevertheless, those who inherit the World to Come, namely the Congregation of Israel,
דְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ.)
for all Israel have a portion in the World to Come (Sanhedrin 90a),
הַיְינוּ דִּלְעָתִיד יְבוֹרַר דְּכוּלָּם עַיְילֵי בְּהַךְ,
signifies that in the ultimate future it will be clarified that all of them entered through that upper opening.
וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל רְמוּזָה בְּהֵ"א
and the Congregation of Israel is collectively symbolized by the letter Hei.
אֶלָּא דְּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא הֵ"א אַחֲרוֹנָה
Except that in this world she is the lower, final Hei,
וְהַבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה נִרְאֶה גָּרוּעַ מִצַּדִּיק גָּמוּר וּבָא אַחֲרָיו
and the penitent appears inferior to the wholly righteous and comes after him,
אֲבָל לֶעָתִיד ה' עוֹשֶׂה חֲדָשׁוֹת דְּ"נְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵב גָּבֶר" (יִרְמְיָה לא, כא)
Yet in the future Hashem creates a new thing: ‘a woman shall encompass a man’ (Yirmiyahu 31:21).
וְתִתְעַלֶּה בְּסוֹד "אֵשֶׁת חַיִל עֲטֶרֶת בַּעְלָהּ" (מִשְׁלֵי יב, ד) כַּנּוֹדָע
and she ascends in the mystery of 'a woman of valor is a crown to her husband' (Proverbs 12:4), as is known.
הַיְינוּ שֶׁתָּשׁוּב לִהְיוֹת הֵ"א רִאשׁוֹנָה
That is, she will return to be the higher, first Hei (Binah),
עַל יְדֵי שְׁלֵימוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בַּבִּינָה שֶׁבְּלִבָּם
through the culmination of the Oral Torah within the understanding of their heart,
יִזְכּוּ לִדְבַּק בְּמִדַּת הַבִּינָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה
meriting to cleave unto the supernal attribute of Binah Above.
הַיְינוּ הַבִּינָה שֶׁהֶאֱצִיל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ בָּעוֹלָם
namely the divine Understanding that Hashem emanated to channel influx into the universe.
כִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה׳:ב׳)
For the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2),
וְהַשָּׂגַת הַבִּינָה שֶׁבִּלְבָבָם הוּא הַשָּׂגַת הַמִּסְטוֹרִין דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
and the attainment of Binah within their hearts is the apprehension of the intimate mysteries of the Holy One,
וְהַבִּינָה הַגְּנוּזָה דְּאַכַּתֵּי לְפוּמָא לָא גַּלְיָא
and that concealed understanding which has not yet been articulated by the mouth,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהִיא מִתְגַּלֵּית עַל יְדֵי פִּיּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
save that it is gradually disclosed through the mouths of the children of Israel in every generation through the Oral Torah.
עַד עֵת קֵץ שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה גַּם הַקֵּץ הָאֲמִתִּי לְעֵין כֹּל מִלִּבָּא לְפוּמָא דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
until the End of Days when the true End will be revealed before all eyes, flowing from the heart to the mouths of the children of Israel.
וְאָז יִהְיֶה תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
And then will be the ultimate culmination of the Oral Torah,
וְתַכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת מַדְרֵגַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה
and the ultimate perfection of the level of Repentance,
דְּהָא בְּהָא תַּלְיָא
for the one depends directly upon the other:
כְּפִי שְׁלֵימוּת מִדַּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה בְּלִבְבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאֵיזֶה דּוֹר
in proportion to the perfection of the attribute of Repentance in the hearts of Israel in any given generation.
כָּךְ הוּא הַהִתְגַּלּוּת דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁבְּחַכְמֵי אוֹתוֹ דּוֹר
such is the revelation of the Oral Torah manifest among the sages of that generation.
וְעַל כֵּן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה.)
Therefore King David, peace be upon him, who established the path of repentance (Avodah Zarah 5a),
מִמֶּנּוּ הַתְחָלַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת
from him stemmed the overt beginning of the Oral Torah in revelation.
שֶׁהוּא הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבְּיַד הַחֲכָמִים דַּעֲדִיפֵי מִנְּבִיאִים בָּזֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (יב.), עַיֵּין שָׁם בָּרַמְבַּ"ן
which is that wisdom in the hands of the sages who are superior to prophets in this regard, as stated in Bava Batra (12a), see there in the Ramban.
וְנִזְכַּר לְעֵיל (סִימָן ג) דְּהוּא הַשָּׂגַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ דְּנִשְׁאַר גַּם מִשֶּׁנִּסְתַּלְּקָה הַנְּבוּאָה
And it was noted above (siman 3) that this is the attainment of the Holy Spirit which endured even after prophecy ceased,
וְכָל הַשָּׂגַת חָכְמַת הַחֲכָמִים הוּא בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ.
and the entire comprehension of the sages' wisdom operates through the Holy Spirit.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Noach §7): “the utterance”let there be light," which corresponds to Chochmah when it receives from Keser by way of the tip of the upper yud." The passage maps the Divine Name explicitly: yod–heh signify Chochmah and Binah, while vav–heh signify the Holy One and the Shechinah. It then describes the first light passing through Yesod, called kol, to the lower heh, Knesses Yisrael. This clarifies the letter-symbolism at §92’s opening; it does not turn that flow into a rule about the portico or measure the openings by the heart’s longing. The source states: “ושם הוי״ה כולל כל המדות י״ה חו״ב ו״ה קבה״ו” — “The Name Havayah includes all the traits: yod–heh are Chochmah and Binah; vav–heh are the Holy One and His Shechinah.”

paragraphs.text: Menachos 29b: R’ Yehudah Nesi’ah asked R’ Ami about the verse “trust in Hashem forever, for in Kah (the letters yod and heh) Hashem is the Rock of worlds” (Yeshayah 26:4) — why “b’Kah” rather than “Yah”? (The answer, expounded by R’ Yehudah bar R’ Il’ai:) these are the two worlds the Holy One created — one with a heh and one with a yod — derived from “these are the generations of the heavens and the earth b’hibar’am” (Bereishis 2:4): read not b’hibar’am but b’heh bera’am, “He created them with a heh” — hence this world was created with heh and Olam Haba with yod. And why was this world created with a heh? Because it resembles a portico (akhsadra), open below, so that whoever wishes to leave may leave. And why is its (left) leg suspended (not joined to the roof)? Because if one repents, he is brought back in (through the small upper opening). And let him re-enter by the way he left? — that would not avail, as Reish Lakish taught: “if (one comes) to the scoffers, He scoffs at him; but to the humble He gives grace” (Mishlei 3:34) — one who comes to purify himself is assisted; one who comes to defile himself, an opening is made for him. And why does the heh have a crown (taga)? The Holy One says: if he returns, I bind a crown for him. Direct Chabad parallel - Likkutei Torah, Metzora 13: The Alter Rebbe formulates the symbolism of teshuvah in the very letters R' Tzadok is expounding: 'teshuvah' is 'tashuv hei legabei yud,' the return of the heh to the yud, and the 'hei ila'ah' is Binah. Sin produces a separation from the yud, the bittul of supernal Chochmah, and from that separation the chitzonim are able to draw nurture; teshuvah restores the upper heh to its relation with the yud. The immediate context in Likkutei Torah describes an awakening of ratzo and inner fire from mochin de'Imma followed by its reintegration into bittul - a return that is therefore not emotional escape but a repaired joining of Binah to its Source. This is almost the exact kabbalistic vocabulary of the present se'if. R' Tzadok reads Menachos' suspended heh as the architecture of the baal teshuvah: after exiting, he does not simply retrace the lower route but is assisted through the upper opening and crowned, corresponding to the hei ila'ah of Binah, 'libo yavin vashav.' Likkutei Torah gives the inner-letter mechanism for that ascent. The crown is not merely an honor added after repentance; the entire movement is a restoration of a severed higher relation. It also supports R' Tzadok's linking of teshuvah and Torah Shebe'al Peh: if the upper heh is Binah, then the return of the heart and the renewed expansion of Divine understanding are aspects of one repair. The greater the reintegration of Binah, the more the hidden light can flow from heart to articulated Torah rather than feeding what stands outside holiness.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §68): “the completeness of the receiver — as in the Midrash, "and Miriam answered them"… that the completeness of the receiver is like a woman: the bestower returns to be one who receives, as it says, Israel give strength to the heavenly host — as in the Future, "the female shall encompass the male."” Exactly the se’if: the heh that alludes to Knesses Yisrael is the letter of the receiver, and its whole promise is that the receiving side will one day encompass.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Chayei Sarah §5): “that all his treasuries are engraved for him upon his heart — and this is the matter of what is said in the Gemara Bava Basra 12a,”a sage is greater than a prophet“; and this is what the Oral Torah aims at.” The comparison in this passage concerns a sage who reaches the truth of the Oral Torah through ruach ha-kodesh appearing in his heart, even without prophecy. Wisdom is fixed within him as a personal acquisition, “this one has acquired wisdom”; R’ Tzadok connects David in particular to Malchus and the Oral Torah. This is a direct parallel to §92’s completed explanation that the sages’ wisdom is attained through ruach ha-kodesh, which remains after prophecy has departed. The source states: “והיינו מה שמכוין התורה שבעל פה לאמתו והוא על ידי רוה״ק וכמו ש׳ הרבמ״ן. והיינו אף שאין משיגין על ידי נבואה רק שמופיע בלב על ידי רוה״קץ מ״מ בזה עדיף מנביא.” — “This means the one who attains the truth of the Oral Torah, which is through ruach ha-kodesh, as the Ramban wrote. Even though it is not attained through prophecy, but appears in the heart through ruach ha-kodesh, in this respect the sage is nevertheless greater than the prophet.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Noach §3): “for the Written Torah is the ways of the Holy One, who fulfills the mitzvos first, as it says in the Midrash and in the Yerushalmi — "and He commanded us to walk in His ways and to keep His mitzvos and statutes."” R’ Tzadok immediately distinguishes “knowledge of Your ways” as the Oral Torah, which comes through ruach ha-kodesh, citing the Ramban on Bava Basra 12a. He identifies it with Malchus — “the mouth, called Oral Torah” — and explains that the full Oral Torah was originally included in the Written Torah with Moshe. This supplies a direct parallel to §92’s completed account of the sages’ Oral Torah wisdom through ruach ha-kodesh; the source is not asserting that gentile prophetic encounters disclose nothing of God. inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Binah and Malchus are both alluded to in the two heh’s of the Name. This world was created with a heh — a portico open below, from which whoever wishes may exit; the nations are those who exit and do not remain. Before one sins he is the lower heh; after he sins and returns he is brought back through the upper opening and a crown is bound for him — and this is the upper heh, which alludes to teshuvah.

p: (צג) וְיָדוּעַ דִּכְמוֹ דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה רַבָּן שֶׁל כָּל הַנְּבִיאִים
And it is known that just as Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was the master of all prophets,
כֵּן הָיָה דָּוִד רַבָּן שֶׁל כָּל בַּעֲלֵי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ.
so was David the master of all possessors of the Holy Spirit.
וּמִמֶּנּוּ הַתְחָלַת הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַרְבָּצַת הַתּוֹרָה וְהַחָכְמָה בִּישִׁיבוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת וְתַלְמִידִים רַבִּים שֶׁלֹּא עַל יְדֵי נְבוּאָה
And from him began the widespread dissemination of Torah and wisdom across great academies and numerous disciples independent of prophecy,
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב
and this unfolds through the awakening of Binah in the heart.
שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה בָּא לַהֲקָמַת עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה
from which David came to raise up the yoke of Repentance.
וּבְדוֹר רַבִּי נִתְבָּרְרוּ כָּל הַשֵּׁשׁ קְצוֹת דְּמִדַּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה
And in the generation of Rebbe (Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi) all six extremities of the attribute of Repentance were clarified,
שֶׁהֵם כָּל הַכֹּחוֹת שֶׁבַּכֹּחַ כּוּלָּם
these comprising all potential spiritual capacities in their entirety;
וְעַל כֵּן נִתְגַּלָּה אָז כְּלָלוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בְּחִבּוּר הַמִּשְׁנָה
wherefore the totality of the Oral Torah was then revealed in the compilation of the Mishnah
דְּכוֹלֶלֶת בְּכֹחַ גַּם כָּל מַה שֶּׁיִּתְחַדֵּשׁ מֵחַכְמֵי הַדּוֹרוֹת אַחַר כָּךְ.
which encapsulates in potential even everything destined to be innovated by the sages of all subsequent generations.

paragraphs.text: Izhbitz-Radzin context - Tiferet Yosef, Hoshana Rabba 2: Tiferet Yosef develops the distinction between seeing and hearing in a way that directly illuminates R' Tzadok's Davidic model of ruach hakodesh. Sight, he explains, takes in an external surface at once; hearing cannot receive two voices simultaneously, but it can penetrate to the depth of a matter. He reads 'hatu oznechem ulechu elai, shim'u u'sechi nafshechem... chasdei David hane'emanim' as a summons to incline the inner depth of the heart to Hashem and to follow the Divine light from its first ratzon down to the final action. When a person's inward ear is so directed, he can perceive that Hashem is continually occupied with forging an eternal covenant with Israel. He identifies this capacity with 'chasdei David': David's avodah can receive illumination even into actions whose outer garment appeared to lack light, because his inner life is surrendered to Hashem. This closely complements R' Tzadok's claim that after Moshe, master of prophecy, David becomes master of baalei ruach hakodesh and inaugurates a Torah that wells from awakened Binah in the heart. The shift is not from revelation to merely private creativity. It is from the visual clarity of prophecy to a deeper inward hearing that must be drawn through the heart and then articulated by sages. Tiferet Yosef thus helps explain why teshuvah and the growth of Torah Shebe'al Peh advance together from David onward: both require the heart to penetrate beneath the surface garment and receive the hidden Divine intention that can then become speech, teaching and renewed life.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Just as Moshe was master of all the prophets, so David was master of all possessors of ruach ha-kodesh. From him began the spread of Torah and wisdom — in great yeshivos and many disciples, not through prophecy but through the awakening of the Binah in the heart, from which the yoke of teshuvah is raised. In Rebbi’s generation all six extremities of that middah were clarified, and the whole Oral Torah was revealed in the Mishnah.

p: (צד) וְעַל כֵּן נִרְאֶה לִי דְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלוּלוֹת בְּחִבּוּר הַמִּשְׁנָה
Therefore it appears to me that the root of all the souls of the children of Israel is encompassed within the compilation of the Mishnah,
וְכֵן כְּלוּלִים בָּהּ גַּם כָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁיִּקָּלְטוּ עַל יְדֵי הַגָּלִיּוֹת בֵּין אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
and likewise contained within it are all the insights of Torah destined to be gathered through the exiles among the nations,
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא קִיבּוּץ הַגָּלִיּוֹת
for through this reclamation the Ingathering of Exiles is achieved.
דְּכָל הַגָּלִיּוֹת לְאַרְבַּע כַּנְפוֹת הָאָרֶץ הָיָה לְצֹרֶךְ זֶה
since all the dispersions to the four corners of the earth were intended for this very purpose.
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַחֲטָאִים נִקְלְטוּ הַרְבֵּה נִיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת בִּשְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם
For through sins many holy sparks were captured in the temporal dominion of man over man,
וְסוֹפוֹ לְרַע לוֹ כְּשֶׁיּוֹצִיאוּ בִלְעוֹ מִפִּיו בְּקִיבּוּץ גָּלִיּוֹת (יִרְמְיָה נא, מד)
which will ultimately turn to their detriment when the swallowed holiness is extracted from their mouths at the Ingathering of the Exiles (Jeremiah 51:44).
דְּאָז יִהְיוּ כָל הָעַמִּים מִשְׂרְפוֹת סִיד (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ לג, יב)
For then the nations will be as burnings of lime (Isaiah 33:12).
וְהַנִּשְׁאָרִים יֹאחֲזוּ בִּכְנַף אִישׁ יְהוּדִי וְיִהְיוּ גֵּרִים גְּרוּרִים כַּמְבֹאָר בַּכְּתוּבִים וּבְדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
And those who remain will grasp the corner of a Jewish person’s garment and become attached converts, as explained in the verses and in the words of our Sages.
כִּי אוֹתוֹ נִיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ מוֹשֵׁךְ עִמּוֹ כָּל הַחַיּוּת שֶׁבָּהֶם
For that holy spark extracts along with itself all the vitality within them.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה מִיתַת הַבְּכוֹרִים בְּמִצְרַיִם עַל יְדֵי גִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָה
just as the death of the firstborn in Egypt transpired through the direct revelation of the Shechinah.
וְהַרְבֵּה דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִתְחַדְּשִׁים עַל יְדֵי הַהִתְעָרְבוּת בֵּין הָאֻמּוֹת בְּאוֹפַנִּים שׁוֹנִים
And many novel Torah insights are innovated through the diverse interactions of exile among the nations.
וּבְדֶרֶךְ זֶה הוּא קְלִיטַת הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת מֵהֶם
and in this manner the extraction of sparks from them is accomplished.
וְהֵם רְמוּזִים כֻּלָּם בַּמִּשְׁנָה בִּדְרָכִים שׁוֹנִים
And all of these are hinted within the Mishnah through various hermeneutical channels.
וְיֵשׁ בָּזֶה הַרְבֵּה עִנְיָנִים עֲמוּקִים מְאֹד שֶׁאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹם בֵּיאוּרָם בִּפְרָט
there being in this many profound mysteries whose detailed explanation does not belong here.
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים זֶה אֱמֶת דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל דְּכָל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כְּלוּלָה בַּמִּשְׁנָה
At any rate, it is an overarching truth that all of the Oral Torah is encapsulated within the Mishnah,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא בָּהּ בְּכֹחַ וְיוֹצֵאת לַפּוֹעַל בְּמֶשֶׁךְ הַדּוֹרוֹת עַד יְמוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ
except that it resides within it in potential, unfolding into actuality across the generations until the days of the Messiah.
וְכֵן מַדְרֵגוֹת הַתְּשׁוּבָה
And similarly regarding the levels of Repentance:
כָּל אוֹתָם שֵׁשׁ קְצוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ בְּכֹחַ הֵם יוֹצְאִים לַפּוֹעַל בְּמֶשֶׁךְ דּוֹרוֹת הָהֵם
all those six extremities that existed in potential emerge into actuality throughout those generations,
עַד הַמָּשִׁיחַ שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ אָמֵן
until the Messiah who shall be revealed speedily in our days, Amen,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שְׁלֵימוּת מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת הַמּוֹצִיאָה לַפּוֹעַל מַה שֶּׁבְּכֹחַ הַשֵּׁשׁ קְצוֹת כַּיָּדוּעַ
who will embody the perfection of Malchut which brings into actuality all that was latent within the six extremities, as is known.
וְאָז יִתְגַּלּוּ כָּל מַדְרֵגוֹת הַתְּשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲלוֹתֶיהָ בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת גָּלוּי בַּפּוֹעַל
And then all rungs of Repentance and its virtues will be disclosed in fully revealed actualization,
וּמִמַּדְרֵגַת הַאֲרָכַת שָׁנִים נִזְכֶּה וְנִחְיֶה וְכוּלֵי לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ וּלְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא
and from the level of lengthening of years we shall merit to live unto the messianic era and the life of the World to Come,
שֶׁהוּא עוֹלָם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ אָרוֹךְ וְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ אָמֵן
which is the world that is wholly long, the realm of eternal life, speedily in our days. Amen.
וְנִרְאֶה לִי מִזֶּה דְּלִמּוּד הַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת סְגֻלָּה לַאֲרִיכוּת יָמִים
It also appears to me from this that the study of Mishnayos is a segulah for longevity.

R’ Tzadok’s use: in the ingathering, once the holy sparks are reclaimed from the nations, “all the peoples will be ‘burnings of lime’” — drained of the vitality the indwelling spark had lent them — while “those who remain grasp the corner of a Jew’s garment” and become attached converts. Source check: the October 8 Tanach ZIP spells the word שיד in its Isaiah 33:12 text; the manuscript’s סיד represents the same lime imagery. The application to reclaimed holy sparks is Rav Tzadok’s interpretation, not the prophet’s explicit wording.

paragraphs.text: Zechariah 8:23: “כֹּה אָמַר ה’ צְבָאוֹת… אֲשֶׁר יַחֲזִיקוּ עֲשָׂרָה אֲנָשִׁים מִכֹּל לְשֹׁנוֹת הַגּוֹיִם, וְהֶחֱזִיקוּ בִּכְנַף אִישׁ יְהוּדִי לֵאמֹר: נֵלְכָה עִמָּכֶם, כִּי שָׁמַעְנוּ אֱלֹהִים עִמָּכֶם” — “in those days ten men of all the languages of the nations shall take hold of the corner of the garment of a Jewish man, saying: let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Radak — in the Messianic age the nations will cling to Israel, recognizing that the Divine Presence rests upon them. R’ Tzadok’s use: “those who remain of the nations will grasp the corner of a Jewish man’s garment and become ‘attached converts geirim gerurim.’” Textual qualification: Zechariah 8:23 says the nations grasp a Jewish person’s garment and say “Let us go with you.” The term גרים גרורים and an inference concerning their attachment are supplied by Rav Tzadok and are not a verbatim clause of that verse.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Sukkos §34): “the spreading of blessing in all matters — that even a coin becomes blessed, which is a thing outside the way of nature; and it is from the aspect of Aharon, as it says, "the beard of Aharon," which descends according to his measures like the dew of Chermon — "for there Hashem commanded the blessing: life forever."” Exactly the se’if: the ingathering and the length of days are one blessing, commanded where Israel are gathered together — “life forever,” at the place of joining. The same Pri Tzaddik, Sukkot §34, explicitly calls the sixth greatness of rain “כיום קיבוץ גליות,” relating it to the gathering of scattered sparks. Its “חיים עד העולם” phrase is a parallel for blessing and life, not a word-for-word explanation of the final World to Come.

paragraphs.text: Hosea 6:2: “יְחַיֵּנוּ מִיֹּמָיִם בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי יְקִמֵנוּ וְנִחְיֶה לְפָנָיו” — “He will revive us after two days; on the third day He will raise us up, and we shall live before Him”. Rashi reads the two days as the two calamities of the destroyed Temples and the third day as the building of the third Temple. This provides a prophetic comparison for future national revival. Rav Tzadok’s concluding passage moves from length of years to life in the days of Mashiach and the World to Come; the Hosea comparison does not by itself establish that Rashi interprets this verse as bodily resurrection.
