sections.en: The seventh level: when the individual returns, he and all the world are pardoned

items.h: The seventh level: when the individual returns, he and all the world are pardoned
המדרגה השביעית והעליונה שיחיד ששב מוחלין לו ולכל העולם כולו.

p: (א) הַמַּדְרֵגָה אַחֲרוֹנָה וְהַשְּׁבִיעִית בִּגְדוּלַּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה
The final, seventh level in the greatness of Repentance is:
דְּיָחִיד שֶׁשָּׁב מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ וּלְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ (יוֹמָא פו עַמּוּד ב)
When an individual repents, he and the entire world are forgiven (Yoma 86b).
וּבַעֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת (מַאֲמַר חֲקוֹר דִּין חֵלֶק א פֶּרֶק יד) פֵּירֵשׁ עַל חֶלְקָם בַּעֲרֵבוּת, עַיֵּין שָׁם וּבַמְפָרֵשׁ (אוֹת טז)
In Asarah Maamaros (Maamar Chakor Din, Part I, chapter 14), he explained this as referring to their share through mutual responsibility (arevus); see there and the commentary (note 16).
וְאֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה לִי
yet this does not appear correct to me.
וְגַם דִּבְרֵי מַהַרְשָׁ"א בְּחִידּוּשֵׁי אַגָּדוֹת שָׁם דָּחוּק
and the words of the Maharsha in Chiddushei Aggadot there are likewise forced.
אֲבָל לְדַעְתִּי הַפֵּירוּשׁ כִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ
Rather, in my opinion the interpretation is according to its literal meaning,
וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית מַעֲלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה וִיצִיאָתָהּ לַפּוֹעַל גָּמוּר בְּתַכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתָהּ שֶׁהוּא בְּלֹא מְצָרִים
and this represents the ultimate pinnacle of Repentance and its complete emergence into actuality in the boundless perfection of its expansion.
וְאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁעוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה
and nothing can withstand Repentance.
וּלְפִי שֶׁכָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת כּוּלָּן קוֹמָה אַחַת שְׁלֵימָה
And because all human souls constitute one complete, unified stature,
הוּא קוֹמַת אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁבּוֹ נִכְלְלוּ נַפְשׁוֹת כָּל צֶאֱצָאָיו
this being the cosmic stature of Adam the First wherein the souls of all his descendants were contained,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה מ, ג; תַּנְחוּמָא כִּי תִשָּׂא יב)
as our Sages taught (Shemos Rabbah 40:3; Tanchuma Ki Sisa 12)
עַל פָּסוּק "אֵיפֹה הָיִיתָ בְּיָסְדִי אָרֶץ" (אִיּוֹב לח, ד)
on the verse “Where were you when I founded the earth?” (Job 38:4).
וְעַל כֵּן אֲפִילּוּ מִי שֶׁשָּׁב בְּכָל לְבָבוֹ לַה׳
Therefore, even someone who returns to Hashem with all his heart
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְתַקֵּן לְגַמְרֵי כָּל זְמַן שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלָּם לֹא שָׁבוּ כָּמוֹהוּ
cannot achieve complete individual rectification as long as all of Israel have not likewise repented
לִהְיוֹת נִתְקָן כָּל הַקּוֹמָה כֻּלָּהּ
so that the entire collective stature may be healed.
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ נִיצוֹץ אֶחָד מִן הַקּוֹמָה שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַן לְגַמְרֵי
And as long as there remains a single spark of the stature that is not fully rectified,
הֲרֵי חֶסְרוֹנוֹ גּוֹרֵם חִסָּרוֹן לְכָל הַקּוֹמָה
its deficiency induces an impairment across the entire stature,
כְּמוֹ הָאָדָם כְּשֶׁכּוֹאֵב לוֹ צִפֹּרֶן רַגְלוֹ הוּא מַרְגִּישׁ הַכְּאֵב מִכָּל הַגּוּף
just as when a person's toenail aches, he perceives pain throughout the whole body,
וְגַם חָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁבְּמוֹחוֹ וּבִינָתוֹ שֶׁבְּלִבּוֹ אֵבָרִים הָרָאשִׁיִּים שֶׁבּוֹ
and even his wisdom in his mind and understanding in his heart—his primary organs—.
אֵין מְיוּשָּׁבִים עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַכְּאֵב שֶׁבִּקְצֵה אֵיבָר הַיּוֹתֵר קָטָן
are unsettled on account of this localized pain at the tip of the smallest limb.
וְעַל כֵּן "אֵין אָדָם צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה טּוֹב וְלֹא יֶחֱטָא" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כ)
Therefore 'there is not a righteous man upon earth that does good and sins not' (Ecclesiastes 7:20),
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּצִּידּוֹ הָיָה יָכוֹל לְהִשָּׁמֵר לִהְיוֹת צַדִּיק גָּמוּר בְּכָל דָּבָר
for even though from his own individual capacity he could have been guarded as a tzaddik in everything.
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לִהְיוֹת נָקִי לְגַמְרֵי כָּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין הַדּוֹר כֻּלּוֹ כוּלֵי
he cannot remain entirely pristine as long as the generation as a whole is not so.
וְהַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁבַּדּוֹר וּבְכָל אָדָם פְּרָטִי שֶׁבְּזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר הוּא נִרְגָּשׁ גַּם בּוֹ
And the deficiency within the generation and within every individual of Israel's seed in that era is felt within him as well,
וְלֹא דַּוְוקָא שֶׁאוֹתוֹ הָרַע שֶׁל אָדָם הָאַחֵר פּוֹעֵל בּוֹ
and not necessarily that the external evil of the other person acts upon him directly.
רַק שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת יֵשׁ שֶׁמֶץ מֵחִסָּרוֹן זֶה גַּם בּוֹ, מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַכֹּל קוֹמָה אֶחָד
rather that there truly exists a faint trace of that deficiency within him as well, since all are one single organism.

paragraphs.text: Maharsha, Chiddushei Aggados, Yoma 86b (on “on account of an individual who repents they forgive the whole world”): He proposes to explain it as the Gemara says at the end of the first chapter of Kiddushin (40b) — a person should always regard the world as half innocent and half guilty; if he performs one mitzvah, fortunate is he, for he has tipped the whole world to the scale of merit. So here: even if the world is mostly guilty, if this one does complete teshuvah out of love, his willful sins become merits, and he thereby tips the entire world to the scale of merit, so that the whole world is forgiven. R’ Tzadok finds this forced, preferring that the individual penitent’s teshuvah itself — as the “heart” of the collective stature — draws healing to all.

paragraphs.text: “There is nothing that stands before teshuvah” (Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 3:14): having enumerated those who forfeit their share in the World to Come, the Rambam rules that even they — “if he repented from his wickedness and died as a baal teshuvah, he is among the people of the World to Come; for there is nothing that stands before teshuvah she-ein lecha davar she-omed bifnei ha-teshuvah — even one who denied the Ikkar all his days and repented at the last has a share in the World to Come.” Meforshim: the Rambam anchors this in “Peace, peace, to the far and to the near, says Hashem — and I will heal him” (Yeshayah 57:19) — the “far one” being the lifelong sinner whom teshuvah heals and draws near; it is the boundlessness of teshuvah’s reach, halted by no prior sin. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is precisely “the last and seventh rung in the greatness of teshuvah” — teshuvah “in the ultimate perfection of its expansion, which is ‘without bounds’ b’lo meitzarim — evoking the limitless nachalah b’li metzarim of Shabbos 118a” — so potent that when a single individual truly repents, “they forgive him and the whole world with him.”

paragraphs.text: Chabad context - Tanya, Likkutei Amarim, ch. 32: The Alter Rebbe gives a particularly clear Chassidic formulation of the ontological unity that R' Tzadok uses here. All Israel, he writes, are literally brothers because 'kulan mat'imos ve'Av echad lekulanah' - all their souls correspond and share one Father - and therefore 'all Israel are called actual brothers from the root of their souls in Hashem Echad; only the bodies are divided.' The division belongs to bodily embodiment; at the level of shoresh haneshamah the many are already one. He therefore explains that the indwelling of the Divine light in Knesses Yisrael requires the souls to be joined 'lemehevei echad be'echad,' because the Shechinah does not rest in a place of spiritual fracture. This supplies an exact Chassidic background to R' Tzadok's insistence that the souls are not merely a federation of individuals who happen to share responsibility, but one complete komah. If the bodies are the principle, each person appears self-contained; if the soul-root is the principle, another Jew's deficiency is a deficiency in the same living unity. The extraordinary statement that one individual's complete teshuvah can extend forgiveness beyond himself thus begins from a metaphysical premise rather than a legal fiction: the individual who returns is not an isolated point. His movement occurs within the shared root in which Knesses Yisrael is already 'one in One.'

paragraphs.text: Cf. Shevuos 39a (and Sanhedrin 27b): “all Israel are guarantors one for another arevim zeh ba-zeh” — the halachic root of the mutual bond underlying this siman. Maharal reads this principle through the very image R’ Tzadok uses here: Israel “are like a single man, so that if there is a wound in one of his limbs, all the limbs feel it, since they are one body.” Chassidic parallel - Be'er Mayim Chaim, Emor 21:1:2: The Be'er Mayim Chaim states almost the same bodily model as this se'if and pushes it to the same conclusion. 'Kol Yisrael guf echad heim' - all Israel are one body. Some souls function as the head, the 'rashei alfei Yisrael'; some as the eyes; the masses correspond to the lower limbs, legs and heels, but all together form one body of 248 limbs and 365 sinews. From this he draws a striking consequence: so long as the whole of Israel has not reached shleimus, even the choicest souls and the heads of Israel are not themselves complete, because blessing rests only upon a complete thing. He cites Chazal that Shmuel was worthy of a level of Shechinah comparable to Moshe but his generation was not worthy, and reads this literally through the common body: the imperfection of the generation limited the head. Conversely, the good of Israel raises its leaders. The same passage explains arvus from this bodily unity and compares harming another Jew to a hand striking another limb of one's own body. This is an unusually exact complement to R' Tzadok's claim that one unrectified spark leaves a chisaron in the entire komah. The common body means that completion cannot be purely private. It also explains why the ultimate teshuvah of the 'heart' or head can reverberate through the whole organism: the channels of merit and deficiency already run through a single living body before the individual act of return takes place.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The seventh and highest rung: when a single individual repents, he and the whole world with him are forgiven. Because all souls together form one complete “stature” — the stature of Adam HaRishon — no one can be wholly rectified until all Israel are. A single unrectified point is felt throughout, as pain at the tip of the smallest limb is felt by the whole body.

p: (ב) וְהַלֵּב מִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים לְכָל הַגּוּף (מִשְׁלֵי ד, כג)
From the heart flow the springs of life to the entire body (Proverbs 4:23).
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הַלֵּב בִּשְׁלֵימוּת לֹא יִהְיֶה קִלְקוּל בְּשׁוּם אֵיבָר מֵאֵבְרֵי הַגּוּף
and when the heart is in pristine wholeness there will be no defect in any of the body's limbs.
וְאִם יַגִּיעַ אֵיזֶה קִלְקוּל, הַקִּלְקוּל בָּא מִדָּם שֶׁבַּלֵּב
And if any malfunction occurs, the breakdown originates from the blood in the heart,
דְּ"בְּרֵישׁ כָּל מַרְעִין אֲנָא דָם" (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא נח עַמּוּד ב) וְהוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ
For “at the head of all illnesses am I—blood” (Bava Basra 58b), and blood represents the life-soul.
וְכֵן אֲפִילּוּ קִלְקוּל וּכְאֵב הַבָּא מִבַּחוּץ לְאֵיזֶה אֵיבָר עַל יְדֵי הַכָּאָה וְכַיּוֹצֵא שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִמְשָׁךְ מֵהַלֵּב
And so even an external injury and pain befalling a limb through a blow that does not originate from the heart,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַלֵּב מַרְגִּישׁ
nonetheless the heart registers it.
לֹא בִּכְאֵב הָאֵיבָר אֶלָּא שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַכְּאֵב פּוֹעֵל אֵיזֶה שִׁינּוּי בַּדָּם, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא מַרְגִּישׁ בַּלֵּב
not through the limb's local sensation, but because the trauma causes a systemic alteration in the blood, whereby it is felt in the heart.
וְהַתִּיקּוּן אַחַר כָּךְ לְעוֹלָם הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַלֵּב הַמַּמְשִׁיךְ דָּם חָדָשׁ וְחַיּוּת חָדָשׁ לְאוֹתוֹ אֵיבָר שֶׁיּוּכַל לַחֲזוֹר לִבְרִיאוּתוֹ
And subsequent healing is always effected through the heart, which pumps fresh blood and new vitality unto that limb so it may recover its health.
וְהָאֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כט)
“God made the human being upright” (Ecclesiastes 7:29).
אֶלָּא שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא וְנִתְקַלְקֵל כָּל הַקּוֹמָה
only that sin intervened and damaged the entire cosmic stature.
וְעַל זֶה הוּא הַתְּשׁוּבָה לְתַקֵּן לִהְיוֹת יָשָׁר כִּבְרִאשׁוֹנָה
And for this purpose Repentance exists: to restore man to being upright as at the beginning.
וְאָז מִמֵּילָא הוּא בְּתוֹסֶפֶת שֶׁבַח וְהִידּוּר כַּאֲשֶׁר יִתְיַישֵּׁר אַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל
and then it is spontaneously enhanced with greater praise and beauty once straightened after the fall.
וְעִיקַּר הַתְּשׁוּבָה הוּא בַּלֵּב
And the primary seat of Repentance is in the heart,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וּלְבָבוֹ יָבִין וְשָׁב" (יְשַׁעְיָה ו, י)
As the verse says: “Let his heart understand, and let him return” (Isaiah 6:10).
וּמִמֶּנָּה הַתִּיקּוּן לְכָל הָאֵבָרִים
and from the heart proceeds healing for all the limbs.
וּבְכָל דּוֹר יֵשׁ נֶפֶשׁ אֶחָד שֶׁהוּא הַלֵּב שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר
And in every generation there exists a single soul who serves as the heart of that generation,
וּמִמֶּנָּה תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים לְכָל הַדּוֹר
from whom flow the springs of vitality unto the entire generation.
וּבוֹ הוּא הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה לְכָל הַדּוֹר
and within him resides the awakening of Repentance for the whole generation.
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה הוּא הַלֵּב שֶׁל כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
And King David, peace be upon him, who raised up the yoke of Repentance, is the collective heart of all Israel,
וְעַל כֵּן זָכָה לִמְלוּכָה
wherefore he merited monarchy,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה (פֶּרֶק ו מִשְׁנָה ג): "לֵב בַּגּוּף כְּמֶלֶךְ בָּעוֹלָם"
as stated in Sefer Yetzirah (6:3): 'the heart in the body is like a king in the world'.

paragraphs.text: Mishlei 4:23: “מִכׇּל־מִשְׁמָר נְצֹר לִבֶּךָ, כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים” — “above all that you guard, guard your heart, for from it are the issues of life.” Meforshim: Rashi — guard your heart, more than any other watch, from evil thoughts; “for from it are the issues of life,” since the vitality of the whole body depends upon the heart. Metzudas David — the heart is the wellspring of life to all the limbs, and therefore must be guarded above all. R’ Tzadok’s use: the heart is “the wellsprings of life to the whole body,” so that “when the heart is in wholeness there is no spoilage in any limb,” and every healing flows from the heart, which “draws new blood and new vitality” to the ailing limb; and in each generation there is one soul who is “the heart of that generation,” the source of its life and the awakener of its teshuvah — and David, who “raised up the yoke of teshuvah,” is “the heart of the whole of Israel,” and therefore merited kingship.

paragraphs.text: Sefer Yetzirah 6:2: “The Teli in the world is like a king on his throne; the sphere in the year is like a king in a province; the heart in the soul is like a king in battle.” The final comparison is the heart-king image invoked here. Hence David, the “heart” of Israel and the awakener of its teshuvah, is fittingly the bearer of kingship. Direct Chabad parallel - Tanya, Likkutei Amarim, ch. 2: Tanya gives the organic hierarchy that stands immediately behind R' Tzadok's image of one soul as the 'heart' of a generation. Although there are innumerable levels of Jewish souls, the Alter Rebbe says, in every generation there are 'rashei alfei Yisrael' whose souls are literally the aspect of head and brain in relation to the souls of the populace. He then extends the bodily analogy down to the lowest level: even the toenails of a son still derive their vitality from the brain in the head, and likewise the vitality of the souls of ordinary Jews is drawn through the souls of the tzaddikim and sages who are the 'heads of the children of Israel' in their generation. This does not erase the individuality of the limbs; it explains how differentiated members remain one organism and how life can pass from a governing organ to the whole body. R' Tzadok identifies the decisive organ here not simply as the brain but as the heart, because 'mimenu totze'os chayim' and because teshuvah is principally an awakening of the heart. The two formulations therefore complement one another: Tanya provides the Chassidic anatomy of generational interdependence, while R' Tzadok identifies Davidic teshuvah as the pulse by which renewed life enters that organism. When the generational 'heart' returns in completeness, it is not merely setting a public example; it is renewing the flow of chiyus within the body to which all the other souls belong. Edition note: the Hebrew manuscript cites Sefer Yetzirah 6:3; the archived Warsaw 1884 Hebrew edition places the exact “תלי בעולם ... לב בנפש כמלך במלחמה” passage at 6:2, while 6:3 begins “שלשה כל אחד לבדו עומד.” The difference is in citation numbering, not the heart/king teaching.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The heart is the wellspring of life to the whole body: when the heart is whole, no limb is spoiled, and every hurt is felt and healed through it. “God made man upright,” but the sin spoiled the whole stature. Teshuvah works in the same way — the heart draws fresh blood and vitality to the ailing limb, so that it returns to its health and its beauty.

p: (ג) וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַדָּבָר יָדוּעַ שֶׁמִּדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת הִיא הָאַחֲרוֹנָה
And even though it is known that the attribute of Malchut is the last,
וְהַשְּׁמִינִית לְבִינָה לִבָּא
and the eighth in relation to Binah, the heart,
וּבְסוֹד עֲטֶרֶת הַיְסוֹד בִּהְיוֹתָהּ נְקֻדָּה לְבַד
and exists in the mystery of the crown of Yesod when she is merely a dimensionless point;
אֲבָל בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתָהּ לְקוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה – קוֹמַת הַנּוּקְבָּא
yet in her expansive unfoldment into a complete stature—the feminine Stature of Nukva—
עַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה (ג, יא)
Concerning this, the Sages expounded in Shir HaShirim Rabbah (3:11):
לֹא זָז מֵחַבְּבָהּ עַד שֶׁקְּרָאָהּ בִּתִּי וַאֲחוֹתִי וְאִמִּי
He did not cease cherishing her until He called her My daughter, My sister, and My mother.
הַיְינוּ דִּכְלָלוּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנַּפְשָׁם חֵלֶק אֱלֹהִי מִמַּעַל
This means that the collective Congregation of Israel whose souls are a divine portion from Above,
דְּמַאן דְּנָפַח מִתּוֹכוֹ נוֹפֵחַ
for whoever breathes out, breathes from within himself,
וַאֲצוּלִים מֵאֲצִילוּת קָדְשׁוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהֶאֱצִיל בְּעֵת שֶׁעָלָה בִּרְצוֹנוֹ לִהְיוֹת מָקוֹם לִבְרִיאַת עוֹלָמוֹת
emanating from His holy Emanation when it arose in His will to create worlds,
הֵם הַמַּדְרֵגָה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁבַּמַּדְרֵגוֹת הַנֶּאֱצָלוֹת
they constitute the final, lowest rank among the emanated levels,
שֶׁהִיא הַמַּדְרֵגָה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר שֶׁתִּתְלַבֵּשׁ בַּלְּבוּשׁ הַגּוּפָנִי דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which is the exact rung that can enclothe itself in the bodily garments of this physical world.
וְלִהְיוֹת שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַגּוּפָנִי
so that His divine presence may dwell in the terrestrial realm and in this bodily sphere.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא תַּכְלִית וְסוֹף כָּל הִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת הָאֲצִילוּת
And this outcome is the culmination and final end of the entire chain of Emanation.
שֶׁרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹרוֹ גַּם בְּדָרֵי מַטָּה וְזֶה כָּל הַמְּכֻוָּון בַּבְּרִיאָה
for Hashem willed that His light be revealed even among earthly dwellers, this being the overarching purpose of Creation.
וְעַל כֵּן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם הַסּוֹף מִכָּל הַבְּרִיאָה
Therefore, even though Israel stands as the end of all Creation chronologically,
הֵם גַּם כֵּן הָרֹאשׁ וְעִיקָּר לַכֹּל
they are likewise the head and foundation of all,
דְּ"סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה"
for the end of the deed was first in thought,
וְ"יִשְׂרָאֵל עָלוּ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה א, ד)
and Israel arose in the Divine thought before Creation (Bereishis Rabbah 1:4).
וְזֶהוּ "אָחוֹר וָקֶדֶם צַרְתָּנִי" (תְּהִלִּים קלט, ה)
This is the meaning of “Back and front You have fashioned me” (Psalms 139:5).
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אַחַר הַגִּיעָם לִשְׁלֵימוּתָם
for in truth, once they attain their perfection,
שֶׁנִּשְׁלְמָה כַּוָּונַת כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה עַל יְדֵי הָאָדָם
when the purpose of all Creation is brought to fruition through man,
הֲרֵי הוּא קֶדֶם וְרֹאשׁ הַכֹּל
behold he stands prior and foremost to all.
שֶׁעַל זֶה הָיָה רֵאשִׁית הַמְּכֻוָּון בִּבְרִיאַת עוֹלָם
for this was the primary intent at the world's creation.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁקְּרָאָהּ "אִמִּי"
And this is why He called her “My mother”:
שֶׁהִיא הַמָּקוֹר הַמּוֹלִידָה כָּל הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת שֵׁשׁ קְצוֹת הָאֲצִילוּת
she being the motherly source generating the expansion of the six spatial directions of Emanation,
כִּי הָעוֹמֶק אַחֲרִית הוּא עַצְמוֹ הָעוֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית בְּסוֹד נָעוּץ סוֹפָן בִּתְחִלָּתָן (סֵפֶר יְצִירָה א, ז)
For the depth of the end is the very depth of the beginning, in the mystery that “their end is embedded in their beginning” (Sefer Yetzirah 1:7).
דְּכָל הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הָאֲצִילוּת הָיָה כְּדֵי לְהַגִּיעַ לְהַתַּכְלִית
since the entire expansion of Atzilut was designed to reach this ultimate goal,
שֶׁהוּא בִּנְיַן קוֹמַת הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים
which is the construction of the stature of the Congregation of Israel and the dwelling of the Shechinah below.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתְחָלַת הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת
and this very goal is the primordial root inaugurating the expansion.

paragraphs.text: “One who breathes, breathes from within himself” (the Kabbalistic principle; cf. Ramban, Bereishis 2:7): explaining why the neshamah is “a portion of God from above” (Iyov 31:2), the tradition holds “man de-nafach mi-tocheih nafach” — one who blows breathes out from his own inner self; so when “He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life” (Bereishis 2:7), the verse describes the Divine gift of the life-soul; this is a teaching about its spiritual source, not physical breath or substance. Ramban (Bereishis 2:7) writes: “כי הנופח באפי אחר מנשמתו יתן בו” — “One who breathes into another’s nostrils gives him something of his own soul”; and he connects the human soul with the foundation of Binah, “for the breath of Shaddai gives them understanding” (Iyov 32:8). Rav Tzadok describes the souls of Knesses Yisrael as a “portion of God from above” in his theological idiom; their relation to the Divine is an emanational teaching here, not a literal material separation or a direct quotation from the Ramban.

paragraphs.text: Chabad context - Tanya, Likkutei Amarim, ch. 36: The Alter Rebbe formulates the purpose of Creation in terms that are nearly identical to R' Tzadok's description of Malchus as the final rung for whose sake the whole descent exists: 'tachlis bri'as olam hazeh hu shenis'aveh HaKadosh Baruch Hu lihyos lo dirah batachtonim.' The purpose of the entire hishtalshelus, he stresses, is not the higher worlds, for from their perspective every descent is a diminution of revealed light; the purpose is specifically this lowest physical world, the place of the greatest concealment, so that darkness itself may be transformed and the Infinite light revealed precisely there. He then says that the days of Mashiach, and especially techiyas hameisim, are the tachlis and shleimus of the creation of this world 'shelechach nivra mitchilaso' - the consummation for which it was created from the beginning. This provides a powerful parallel to R' Tzadok's 'achor va-kedem' structure. The tachton is chronologically and spiritually last, yet in intention it is first; the lowest point is the destination toward which the entire chain of worlds was ordered. Malchus is therefore precious not in spite of being the final receptacle but precisely because only there does the original Divine desire reach actuality. Teshuvah's seventh rung belongs to Malchus for the same reason: the final rectification is not an escape from the lower world but the disclosure that the lower world and the collective human stature were the intended dwelling from the outset. Original Hebrew in the Chassidus ZIP (Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 36): “שתכלית בריאת עולם הזה הוא ... להיות לו דירה בתחתונים” — “The purpose of creating this world is ... to make for Him a dwelling below.” This is a direct conceptual parallel, not the source of Rav Tzadok’s precise wording.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash §6): “and in the word Bereishis is alluded ‘he shall fear the Shabbos,’ as it says in Tikunei Zohar; and this is because Israel are called, through the guarding of Shabbos, ‘those who fear My Name,’ and they accept the yoke of His kingship.” He immediately continues that through this Hashem is crowned with the supernal crown: “the supernal crown is the crown of Malchus”; “the end of the deed is in thought first.” Shabbos, Israel’s acceptance of kingship, and the first utterance of Creation thus belong to the same beginning-and-end structure developed here: the final revelation of Divine kingship fulfills Creation’s first intention.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 139:5: “אָחוֹר וָקֶדֶם צַרְתָּנִי, וַתָּשֶׁת עָלַי כַּפֶּכָה” — “back and front You have formed me, and laid Your hand upon me.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Radak read it of God’s all-encompassing formation of man — fashioning him “behind and before,” enclosing him on every side. Chazal (Berachos 61a; Eruvin 18a) expound “achor va-kedem” of Adam HaRishon, created “du-partzufin” — with two faces, back and front. R’ Tzadok’s use: he reads it of man’s place in the order of creation — man is “achor,” the last of all creatures (“the end of the deed”), yet also “kedem,” the first and head (“thought first”), “for on this was the first intent in the creation of the world”; when he reaches his perfection, and the whole purpose of Creation is fulfilled through him, he is revealed as its very head.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §58): “‘may you become thousands of myriads’ — as in the Zohar, that the blessing of Hashem is never less than a thousand… and the blessing is the utmost of the multiplication that the vessel can receive, and its filling — as with the oil of Elisha, and in the Sages’ language, ‘a vessel holds blessing.’” He then distinguishes a vessel’s ordinary filling from the complete abundance signified by a myriad, “the rung of the king,” citing David’s being worth ten thousand. The discourse develops this as enduring Davidic kingship and the perfection of the World to Come. Its account of royal fullness offers a parallel to the completed stature of Malchus described here. Har Bracha printed Kometz HaMinchah II §58, pp. 352–353: “והברכה הוא תכלית הריבוי שיוכל הכלי לקבל ומילויו” — “Blessing is the greatest increase and fullness the vessel can receive.” The passage concerns fullness and enduring Davidic kingship; it is a comparison, not an exact exegesis of the preceding line about all the emanated levels.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Malchus is the last of the middos — the “eighth” counting up to Binah, a mere point as the crown of Yesod. Yet in its expansion into a full stature it is so cherished that He calls her “My daughter,” “My sister,” “My mother.” For His dwelling among the lower ones, in this physical world, is the whole intent of Creation — “Israel arose first in thought.”

p: (ד) וְעַל כֵּן אֵשֶׁת חַיִל
Therefore the Woman of Valor (Malchut),
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא אַחַת מִצַּלְעוֹתָיו בְּתַחְתִּית גּוּפוֹ מָקוֹם שֶׁ"הִסְגִּיר בָּשָׂר תַּחְתֶּנָּה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, כא)
Although she was one of his sides, in the lower part of his body, at the place where He closed up flesh beneath it (Genesis 2:21),
אַחַר שֶׁנִּבְנֵית קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה נַעֲשֵׂית "עֲטֶרֶת בַּעְלָהּ" (מִשְׁלֵי יב, ד)
once she is built into a complete stature, she becomes “the crown of her husband” (Proverbs 12:4).
וְהֵם סוֹד שְׁתֵּי הַהֵהִי"ן דְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה
And they embody the mystery of the two letters Hei of the Name Havayah,
דְּהֵ"א אַחֲרוֹנָה בָּאָה אַחַר הַשֵּׁשׁ קְצוֹת
the final Hei following after the six extremities,
וְהָרִאשׁוֹנָה קוֹדֶמֶת לָהֶם
while the first Hei precedes them,
וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד
and all is one unified reality.
רַק זֶה הַסּוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה וְזֶה הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה
only that this is the final deed while that is the initial thought.
וְאַחַר שֶׁמַּגִּיעִים לִשְׁלֵימוּת הַסּוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה
And once the final deed has reached its completion,
אָז מַשִּׂיגִים הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה דְּהֵ"א עֶלְיוֹנָה שֶׁהוּא סוֹד עוֹלָם הַבָּא כַּנּוֹדָע
then they attain the root of the primordial thought in the upper Hei, which is the mystery of the World to Come as is known.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ, א)
And therefore the Sages stated at the beginning of Perek Chelek (Sanhedrin 90a):
כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
All Israel have a share in the World to Come
מִקְּרָא דְּ"יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ" (יְשַׁעְיָה ס, כא)
as derived from “they shall inherit the land” (Isaiah 60:21).
וְיָדוּעַ דְּאֶרֶץ הִיא הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַיּוֹתֵר תַּחְתּוֹנָה
and it is known that 'earth' (eretz / Malchut) is the lowest level.
אֶלָּא שֶׁלֶּעָתִיד אֶרֶץ הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה עַצְמָהּ הִיא עַצְמָהּ מִתְהַפֶּכֶת לִהְיוֹת אֶרֶץ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה
only that in the future the lower earth itself is transformed to become the Supernal Land.
וְהָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עַצְמוֹ מִתְהַפֵּךְ בְּהִתְחַדְּשׁוּת הָעוֹלָם לִהְיוֹת עוֹלָם הַבָּא
And this physical world itself is inverted in the cosmic renewal to become the World to Come,
כַּאֲשֶׁר מִתְעַלִּים הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּהַגִּיעָם לְתַכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּתָם
when the souls of Israel ascend upon reaching their ultimate perfection.
שֶׁיִּתְבַּעֵר הָרַע וְיִכְלֶה מִן הָעוֹלָם לְגַמְרֵי
wherein evil will be eradicated and perish completely from the world.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 2:21: “וַיַּפֵּל ה’ אֱלֹהִים תַּרְדֵּמָה עַל הָאָדָם וַיִּישָׁן, וַיִּקַּח אַחַת מִצַּלְעֹתָיו וַיִּסְגֹּר בָּשָׂר תַּחְתֶּנָּה” — “And Hashem God cast a deep sleep upon the man, and he slept; and He took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.” Meforshim: Rashi — “one of his ribs tzela” means one of his sides, for in the Sages’ reading Adam was created “du-partzufin” (two-faced), and the woman was built from one side; “and closed up the flesh in its place” — over the site of the incision. R’ Tzadok’s use: the “woman of valor” — Knesses Yisrael as Malchus, the Nukva — originates as “one of his ribs, at the lower part of his body, the place where He closed up flesh beneath it,” a low and hidden place; yet once she is “built into a complete stature” she becomes “the crown of her husband” (Mishlei 12:4) — the upper heh of the Name, the secret of Olam Haba.

paragraphs.text: Torah Ohr, Vaera §5 (October 8 Chassidus ZIP) states: “סוף מעשה הוא דוקא במחשבה תחלה ונעוץ תחלתן בסופן ולכן נק׳ המלכות אשת חיל עטרת בעלה ונק׳ ג״כ ארץ חפץ” — “The final deed is precisely first in thought, and their beginning is embedded in their end; therefore Malchus is called Woman of Valor, the crown of her husband, and also a desirable land.” This original Chabad teaching closely parallels Rav Tzadok’s beginning-and-end relationship. The application to the upper Hei and Olam Haba is Rav Tzadok’s further development here.

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Chayei Sarah §1): “and at the entry of Shabbos every one of Israel merits an additional soul, a new soul; and as it says in the Zohar,”a soul in which is all completeness, of the pattern of the World to Come" — and for this reason it is called Shabbos." Exactly the se’if: the first heh, which precedes the six extremities, is the secret of Olam Haba — and its foretaste is precisely the completeness that arrives from above, not from the six days’ labor.

paragraphs.text: Mishnah, Sanhedrin 90a (Perek Chelek): “All Israel have a share in the World to Come, as it says, ‘and your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever’ (Yeshayah 60:21).” R’ Tzadok reads “land eretz” as the lowest rung (Malchus) which, in the Future, is itself transformed into “the upper land” — so that inheriting the land is the inheritance of Olam Haba. Izhbitz-Radzin context - Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 6:1: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin develops Malchus in a way that strikingly complements the present se'if. Malchus is the final middah, he writes, 'shebah nigmar hahavayah mikol seder hahishtalshelus bishleimus hagamur'; it is the last point of concealment, so distant from the source that Creation can appear to possess an independent existence. Precisely that concealment makes bechirah and coronation possible: the creature can stand within apparent independence and nevertheless choose to crown Hashem. Malchus is therefore 'leis lah migarmah klum' and yet the completion of all the middos, because its entire action is an or chozer that recognizes and returns the upper will. Sod Yesharim then explains the moon's claim of two kings using one crown: since the whole Divine intention reaches completion through Malchus, she senses a genuine root-superiority. In the present world, however, evil is not yet fully clarified, so Malchus must accept tzimtzum - 'lechi u'ma'ati es atzmech.' Only in the Future, after the birurim are complete, will 'eishes chayil ateres ba'alah' be openly true and 'Keser Elyon ihu Keser Malchus' become revealed. This distinction is exactly the one R' Tzadok needs. The final heh is rooted above the six middos, but its superiority cannot yet be lived as unrestricted self-assertion. Present avodah requires constriction, humility and Torah-defined bechirah; future shleimus reveals why the lowest, after faithfully completing its task, was rooted in the highest all along.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: “A woman of valor” — though she is one of his ribs, taken from the low part of the body, once built into a full stature she becomes “the crown of her husband.” She and Binah are the two heh’s of the Name: the last heh comes after the six extremities, the first precedes them. That first heh is the secret of Olam Haba, in which evil is wholly removed from the world.

p: (ה) וּמֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ הוּא דָּוִד בְּעַצְמוֹ כַּיָּדוּעַ,
And the King Messiah is David himself as is known,
אֶלָּא שֶׁדָּוִד הָיָה הַתְחָלַת הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת מִצַּד סוֹף הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
save that David represented the beginning of exertion from the aspect of the final deed.
וּמָשִׁיחַ הוּא סִיּוּם שְׁלֵימוּת הַקּוֹמָה כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה
while the Messiah is the culmination of the stature's perfection as it was conceived in primordial thought.
וְהַהַגָּעָה לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה עַצְמוֹ זֶהוּ עוֹלָם הַבָּא
And arriving at the root of the primordial thought itself is the World to Come,
וִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ הֵם קוֹדֶם עוֹלָם הַבָּא
and the messianic era precedes the World to Come,
שֶׁהוּא סוֹף הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ יַגִּיעוּ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
being the culmination of this world through which they will enter the World to Come.
וְתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת הָאֶפְשָׁרִי לְאָדָם לְהַגִּיעַ אֵלָיו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and the pinnacle of perfection attainable for man in this physical world.
וְהָאֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כט),
And 'God made man upright' (Ecclesiastes 7:29),
וְאַלְמָלֵא חָטָא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
and had Adam the First not sinned,
הָיָה הוּא דָּוִד בְּעַצְמוֹ סוֹף הַמַּעֲשֶׂה דִּבְרִיאָה
he would have been David himself as the culmination of Creation's deed,
וּבְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ לְהַגִּיעַ לְתַכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּתוֹ הָאֶפְשָׁרִי לוֹ
and through his spiritual exertion to reach the ultimate perfection possible for him
הָיָה יָכוֹל לוֹ לְהַגִּיעַ גַּם כֵּן אַחַר כָּךְ לְמַדְרֵגַת הַמָּשִׁיחַ,
he could have subsequently attained the level of the Messiah as well,
וְכַיָּדוּעַ דְּהוּא כּוֹלֵל שְׁתֵּי נְפָשׁוֹת אֵלּוּ הָרְמוּזִים בְּרָאשֵׁי תֵיבוֹת שְׁמוֹ (אָדָם, דָּוִד, מָשִׁיחַ)
As is known, Adam encompasses both of these souls, alluded to in the initials of his name: Adam, David, Mashiach.

paragraphs.text: “The King Mashiach is David himself” (Yirmiyah 30:9; Yechezkel 37:24-25): the prophets call the Messianic king simply “David” — “they shall serve Hashem their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up for them” (Yirmiyah 30:9); “My servant David shall be king over them, and one shepherd shall be for them all” (Yechezkel 37:24), “and David My servant shall be prince to them forever” (37:25). Meforshim: the Radak — some hold this is David HaMelech himself, revived to reign; others, a scion of his house called by his name; and the Gemara (Sanhedrin 98b, cited earlier in this volume) likewise weighs whether the Mashiach is “of the living” or “of the dead, like David.” R’ Tzadok’s use: on the deeper plane Mashiach is David, one soul — David being “the beginning of the effort, from the side of the ‘end of the deed,’” and Mashiach “the culmination of the perfection of the stature, as it is in ‘thought first’”; so Adam, had he not sinned, would himself have been David, and could then have risen to the rung of Mashiach — the two souls hinted in his name (Adam-David-Mashiach).

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §51): “It is known that Adam is the acronym of Adam–David–Mashiach, for all is one — since the world is like a sphere (as it says in the Yerushalmi, Avodah Zarah), and in a sphere the beginning and the end are one point; so too Adam and Mashiach, that is, David — all is one.” The “end of the deed” (David) and the “thought that was first” meet: Adam, David, and Mashiach are one root-soul, the beginning embedded in the end. Early Chassidic parallel - Me'or Einayim, Pinchas 13: The Me'or Einayim gives an exceptionally close Chassidic account of the Adam-David-Mashiach structure used here. Citing the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov, he writes that every Jew must 'repair and prepare the portion of the stature of Mashiach that belongs to his soul.' Adam is read as the roshei teivos Adam-David-Mashiach. Adam HaRishon's original stature extended from one end of the world to the other because all the souls of Israel were included within him; after the sin that stature was diminished. Mashiach will once again be 'komah sheleimah mikol nishmos Yisrael,' a complete stature composed of the entirety of Jewish souls, corresponding to Adam before the sin. Consequently, the building of Mashiach is not external to the avodah of ordinary souls: each person must prepare his own chelek until the entire stature is repaired and a permanent universal yichud becomes possible. This sheds unusually direct light on R' Tzadok's statement that Mashiach is David himself at the level of root, while David is the beginning of the effort from 'sof ma'aseh' and Mashiach is its completed form as it stands in 'machshavah techilah.' The continuity is not merely genealogical. Adam, David and Mashiach are names for successive states of one collective human-Jewish komah: primordial inclusion, historical repair through teshuvah, and final reintegration. Me'or Einayim also prevents the doctrine from becoming passive: because every soul constitutes a limb of that future stature, each individual's present avodah literally belongs to the construction of the completed Mashiach. The October 8 ZIP confirms Me’or Einayim, Pinchas §13: “צריך כל א׳ מישראל לתקן ולהכין חלק קומת משיח השייך לנשמתו ... שאדם הוא ר״ת אדם דוד משיח.” — “Every Israelite must repair and prepare the part of Mashiach’s stature belonging to his soul ... for Adam is the initials of Adam, David and Mashiach.” The original R. Tzadok passage in Kometz HaMincha II §51 is also visible in the Har Bracha PDF, printed p. 344.

Early Chassidic parallel - Me'or Einayim, Pinchas 13: The Me'or Einayim gives an exceptionally close Chassidic account of the Adam-David-Mashiach structure used here. Citing the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov, he writes that every Jew must 'repair and prepare the portion of the stature of Mashiach that belongs to his soul.' Adam is read as the roshei teivos Adam-David-Mashiach. Adam HaRishon's original stature extended from one end of the world to the other because all the souls of Israel were included within him; after the sin that stature was diminished. Mashiach will once again be 'komah sheleimah mikol nishmos Yisrael,' a complete stature composed of the entirety of Jewish souls, corresponding to Adam before the sin. Consequently, the building of Mashiach is not external to the avodah of ordinary souls: each person must prepare his own chelek until the entire stature is repaired and a permanent universal yichud becomes possible. This sheds unusually direct light on R' Tzadok's statement that Mashiach is David himself at the level of root, while David is the beginning of the effort from 'sof ma'aseh' and Mashiach is its completed form as it stands in 'machshavah techilah.' The continuity is not merely genealogical. Adam, David and Mashiach are names for successive states of one collective human-Jewish komah: primordial inclusion, historical repair through teshuvah, and final reintegration. Me'or Einayim also prevents the doctrine from becoming passive: because every soul constitutes a limb of that future stature, each individual's present avodah literally belongs to the construction of the completed Mashiach. The October 8 ZIP confirms Me’or Einayim, Pinchas §13: “צריך כל א׳ מישראל לתקן ולהכין חלק קומת משיח השייך לנשמתו ... שאדם הוא ר״ת אדם דוד משיח.” — “Every Israelite must repair and prepare the part of Mashiach’s stature belonging to his soul ... for Adam is the initials of Adam, David and Mashiach.” The original R. Tzadok passage in Kometz HaMincha II §51 is also visible in the Har Bracha PDF, printed p. 344.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: David and Mashiach, “the end of the deed” and “thought first,” and the final perfection of the stature of Malchus.

p: (ו) אֶלָּא שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא וְיָצָא מַה שֶּׁיָּצָא עֶשְׂרִים דּוֹר
Except that sin intervened and there unfolded what unfolded for twenty generations,
עַד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהִתְחִיל לְתַקֵּן וְלִבְנוֹת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל אֻמָּה מְיוּחֶדֶת מִכָּל הָעַמִּים
until Abraham our father, peace be upon him, who began to rectify and build the Congregation of Israel as a distinct nation from all peoples,
שֶׁבָּהֶם בְּיִחוּד יִהְיֶה הִתְגַּלּוּת כְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים
in whom uniquely the revelation of Heaven's glory would abide among earthly dwellers.
וּשְׁאָר אֻמּוֹת הֵם הַפְּסוֹלֶת הַנִּמְשָׁכִים מִצַּד הָרַע דְּחֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
while the other nations are the dross drawn from the evil of Adam's sin.
וְאַחֲרָיו זַרְעוֹ יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב וְיוֹסֵף עִם שְׁאָר שִׁבְטֵי יָ"הּ
After him came his descendants: Yitzchak, Yaakov and Yosef, with the other tribes of God,
וּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן הִשְׁלִימוּ קוֹמַת הַשֵּׁשׁ קְצוֹת
and Moses and Aaron brought to completion the stature of the six extremities,
עַד שֶׁיָּצָא לַפּוֹעַל אֻמָּה שְׁלֵימָה
until there emerged into actuality a complete nation.
כְּנֵסִיָּה שֶׁהִיא לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם מוּכָנִים לְקַבֵּל תּוֹרָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהִיא מִדָּה אַחֲרוֹנָה
an assembly dedicated for the sake of Heaven, prepared to receive the Torah from Hashem which is the final attribute.
וּכְשֶׁטָּעֲנוּ עֲדַת קֹרַח: "כָּל הָעֵדָה כֻּלָּם קְדֹשִׁים וּבְתוֹכָם ה'" (בַּמִּדְבָּר טז, ג)
When Korach’s assembly argued, “For the entire congregation, all are holy, and Hashem is among them” (Numbers 16:3),
וְלֹא הָיָה דְּבַר שֶׁקֶר חָלִילָה דְּלֹא הָיָה נִכְתָּב בַּתּוֹרָה
it was not an outright falsehood, Heaven forbid, or it would not have been inscribed in the Torah.
דְּכֵן הָאֱמֶת שֶׁהָיָה הַשְׁרָאַת הַשְּׁכִינָה אָז בְּתוֹךְ כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר
for such was indeed the truth: that the Shechinah rested then within all the souls of Israel in that generation.
וְאַלְמָלֵא זָכוּ הָיָה אָז תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת
And had they merited, that would have been the ultimate perfection,
שֶׁהָיוּ הֵם כֻּלָּם קוֹמַת מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת דִּקְדוּשָּׁה
wherein they all would have embodied the stature of the holy attribute of Malchut,
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לֶעָתִיד: "וְהָיָה הַנִּכְשָׁל בָּהֶם בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא כְּדָוִיד" (זְכַרְיָה יב, ח)
As it is written concerning the future, “The one who stumbles among them on that day shall be like David” (Zechariah 12:8).
כִּי דָּוִד הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת כַּנּוֹדָע
for David is the root of the holiness of the Congregation of Israel, the attribute of Malchut, as is known.
וְאָז שֶׁיּוּשְׁלְמוּ כָּל נְפָשׁוֹת דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל יִהְיוּ כֻּלָּם בַּשְּׁלֵימוּת הַהוּא
And then, when all the souls of Israel are perfected, they will all abide in that sublime perfection,
אֶלָּא שֶׁבֵּית דָּוִד יִהְיוּ אָז בְּמַעֲלָה יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה
except that the House of David will then occupy an even greater stature,
דִּכְבָר זָכָה דָּוִד בְּכֶתֶר הַמַּלְכוּת וּנְטָלוֹ לִהְיוֹת הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַלֵּב דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
for David has already merited the crown of kingship and received it to be the root of the Congregation of Israel and the heart of the Jewish people.
וְעַל יָדוֹ הוּא שֶׁנִּבְנוּ וְנִתְקְנוּ כֻּלָּם
and through him all were built and rectified.
אֲבָל אַלְמָלֵא אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁחָטְאוּ
But had our forefathers not sinned,
הָיָה אָז בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה גְּמַר הַתִּיקּוּן בִּשְׁלֵימוּת חֵירוּת מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע
the final, complete rectification would already have arrived at the Giving of the Torah in total freedom from the evil inclination,
וְהַדּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר לֹא הָיוּ צְרִיכִים לְמֶלֶךְ כְּלָל
and the Generation of the Wilderness would not have needed an earthly king at all,
רַק מַאן מַלְכֵי – רַבָּנָן (גִּיטִּין סב, א)
but only “Who are kings? The Rabbis” (Gittin 62a).
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא הָיָה אָז מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, would then have been the King Mashiach,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר דְּהוּא יִהְיֶה מָשִׁיחַ
as stated in the Zohar, that he would be Mashiach,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כָּלוּל נַפְשׁוֹ מִשְּׁנֵיהֶם
meaning that his soul will be integrated of both.
שֶׁכֵּן "דָּוִד מֹשֶׁה" בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא "מָשִׁיחַ" עִם הַכּוֹלֵל
For דוד (David) is 14 and משה (Moshe) is 345, together 359; משיח (Mashiach) is 358, plus the kollel of one equals 359.
אֶלָּא שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא
Except that sin intervened.
וְהֻוצְרְכוּ לַהֲקָמַת עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה עַל יְדֵי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לְתַקֵּן הַחֲטָאִים הַקּוֹדְמִים
and they required the raising of the yoke of Repentance through King David, peace be upon him, to rectify the preceding transgressions.
וְהַכֹּל לְטוֹבָה
And all was for the good.
לְהַגִּיעַ עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְמַדְרֵגָה יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה – מְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִים
to attain through this an even greater spiritual height: the place where penitents stand.

paragraphs.text: Pirkei Avos 5:2: “עֲשָׂרָה דוֹרוֹת מֵאָדָם וְעַד נֹחַ… עֲשָׂרָה דוֹרוֹת מִנֹּחַ וְעַד אַבְרָהָם… עַד שֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם וְקִבֵּל עָלָיו שְׂכַר כֻּלָּם” — “ten generations from Adam to Noach… ten generations from Noach to Avraham… until Avraham came and received the reward of them all.” Meforshim: the Bartenura — the Mishnah counts these twenty generations of provocation to make known God’s great patience, until Avraham arose and began the world’s rectification, “receiving the reward of them all.” R’ Tzadok’s use: “the sin caused what it caused — twenty generations until Avraham Avinu, who began to rectify and to build Knesses Yisrael, a nation distinguished from all the peoples”; the other nations remain “the dross drawn from the evil side of Adam’s sin,” while Avraham inaugurates the holy line destined to become the stature of Malchus.

paragraphs.text: Pirkei Avos 4:11 (R’ Yochanan HaSandlar): “כָּל כְּנֵסִיָּה שֶׁהִיא לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, סוֹפָהּ לְהִתְקַיֵּם; וְשֶׁאֵינָהּ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, אֵין סוֹפָהּ לְהִתְקַיֵּם” — “every assembly kenisiyah that is for the sake of Heaven will in the end endure; and one that is not for the sake of Heaven will not, in the end, endure.” Meforshim: the Bartenura — the enduring assembly is one bound together by truth alone; and the classic example of the assembly “not for the sake of Heaven” that did not endure is the assembly of Korach. R’ Tzadok’s use: Israel, forged by the Avos, Moshe, and Aharon into “a complete nation,” is precisely “an assembly for the sake of Heaven,” prepared to receive the Torah — the “last middah”; Korach’s counter-assembly was the “not for the sake of Heaven” that could not stand.

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar 16:3 (Korach’s claim): “וַיִּקָּהֲלוּ עַל מֹשֶׁה וְעַל אַהֲרֹן… רַב לָכֶם, כִּי כָל הָעֵדָה כֻּלָּם קְדֹשִׁים וּבְתוֹכָם ה’, וּמַדּוּעַ תִּתְנַשְּׂאוּ עַל קְהַל ה’” — “they assembled against Moshe and against Aharon, and said to them: You take too much upon yourselves! For the whole congregation are all holy, and Hashem is among them; why then do you exalt yourselves over the assembly of Hashem?” Meforshim: Rashi — the premise was sound (all Israel “heard the words at Sinai from the mouth of the Almighty”), but Korach’s inference — that therefore no leader was needed — was his rebellion and his ruin. R’ Tzadok’s use: the claim “was no word of falsehood, God forbid, for otherwise it would not have been written in the Torah” — “the Shechinah rested then within all the souls of Israel of that generation”; had they merited, this would have been the ultimate perfection, the whole nation as the stature of Malchus of holiness, “like David.”

paragraphs.text: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §18): “As Korach’s assembly claimed, that ‘the whole congregation are all holy’ and worthy of the high priesthood — and Moshe Rabbeinu showed them that it is not so in actuality in this world, where the revelation of their holiness is not yet manifest; and only ‘the one whom Hashem chooses’ is holy in actuality among the souls. So too with the days of the year; and the World to Come is called (end of Tamid) ‘a day that is wholly Shabbos,’ for then there is no division of times, since all is holy.” Korach’s claim was true at the root — the Shechinah did rest in all — but its full manifestation awaits the Future, when the whole nation stands “like David.” Direct Izhbitz source - Mei HaShiloach I, Korach 3: R. Mordechai Yosef addresses Korach's exact claim and makes the temporal distinction that R' Tzadok develops here. Korach argued that there should be no superiority of one Jew over another because 'betocham Hashem' - Hashem dwells within all of them equally. Mei HaShiloach says that this describes the Future, when Hashem will make a machol, a circle, for the tzaddikim: in a circle there is no point intrinsically closer to the center than another. Korach's error was to insist 'she'atah gam kein hu kach' - that the future equality was already the operative order of the present. The Izhbitzer then turns Korach's own history against him: when the crown and distinction of Levi were given to him, he did not protest that Israel admits no hierarchy. This is an extraordinarily precise complement to R' Tzadok's reading. 'Kulam kedoshim' is not dismissed as false; it is a truth of shoresh and destiny. Yet the world of avodah before final birur still contains differentiated offices, chosen vessels and unequal degrees of revealed kedushah. To collapse the future root into the present state is itself a distortion of that root. R' Tzadok can therefore say both that the claim was true enough to be written in Torah and that Moshe's distinction remained necessary. The completed seventh rung of teshuvah is what finally allows the circular truth to become manifest without destroying the ordered avodah through which that completion is reached. Original Hebrew in Machshavos Charutz §18: “וכמו שטענו עדת קרח כי כל העדה כולם קדושים ... ומשרע״ה הראה להם שאינו כן בפעל בעולם הזה עדיין גלוי קדושתם” — “As Korach’s assembly argued that the entire congregation is holy ... but Moshe showed them this holiness is not yet manifest in action in this world.” This is an especially close original Rav Tzadok parallel.

p: (ז) וּבְכָל דָּבָר יֵשׁ שֶׁבַע מַדְרֵגוֹת
And within every reality there exist seven levels:
שְׁלוֹשָׁה אָבוֹת, וְשָׁלֹשׁ תּוֹלָדוֹת כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶן
three primary 'fathers' (primary attributes), and three 'offspring' (secondary attributes) corresponding to them.
וְהַשְּׁבִיעִית הַמּוֹצִיאָה שֵׁשׁ קְצוֹת אֵלּוּ לַפּוֹעַל וְלִהְיוֹת שְׁלֵימוּת כָּל הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת
and the seventh which actualizes these six extremities into deed, serving as the perfection of all the levels.
וְזֶהוּ הַמַּעֲלָה הַשְּׁבִיעִית שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁאָנוּ מְחַכִּים לָהּ בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ
And this is the seventh greatness of teshuvah for which we hope, speedily in our days:
שֶׁיָּבוֹא הַיָּחִיד מִזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁשָּׁב בְּתַכְלִית הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כֹּחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה בְּכָל מַדְרֵגוֹתֶיהָ
that the individual descended from King David, peace be upon him, will come — one whose teshuvah reaches the fullest extension of the power of repentance throughout all its levels;
עַד שֶׁיִּמָּשְׁכוּ מִמֶּנּוּ, בִּהְיוֹתוֹ הַלֵּב דְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל
until, through him — as the heart of all Israel —
תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים לְכָל הַלְּבָבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר וְשֶׁבְּכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת כוּלָּם
the springs of life will be drawn into all the hearts of the children of Israel in that generation and across all generations collectively.
עַד שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִמָּחֲלוּ לְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ, הַחַיִּים וְהַמֵּתִים
through him forgiveness will reach the entire world, the living and the dead.
וּבָזֶה יִהְיֶה נִבְלַע הַמָּוֶת לְגַמְרֵי וְיִכְלֶה הַיֵּצֶר מִן הָעוֹלָם
And through this death will be swallowed up completely and the evil inclination will be eradicated from the world,
וְהוּא הַיּוֹם אֲשֶׁר "יְבֻקַּשׁ אֶת עֲוֹן יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֵינֶנּוּ וְאֶת חַטֹּאת יְהוּדָה וְלֹא תִמָּצֶאנָה וְגוֹמֵר"
And this is the day of which it is said: “Israel’s iniquity shall be sought, but it will not be there; and the sins of Judah shall not be found,” and so forth (Jeremiah 50:20).

Izhbitz–Radzin parallel (Tiferet Yosef, Hoshana Rabbah §4): “שם הוא יכול להעלות כל הבריאה לנוכח השי״ת פנים בפנים” — “there he can raise the entire creation to stand face-to-face before Hashem.” R’ Yosef derives this capacity from David’s refusal to appropriate power even from his own avodah; this is a conceptual parallel, not a direct source for the exact extent of halachic forgiveness.

paragraphs.text: The two expressions in this Hebrew phrase have distinct sources. Yeshayahu 25:8: “בִּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח” — “He will swallow up death forever.” Sukkah 52a: “לעתיד לבא מביאו הקדוש ברוך הוא ליצר הרע ושוחטו” — “In the future the Holy One will bring the evil inclination and slaughter it.” R’ Tzadok further connects the final abolition of the yetzer to the perfected Davidic teshuvah. Compare his own parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah §14): “והמשיחים שיתקנו הלב כסיל שאז ישחוט הקב״ה ליצה״ר” — “the Mashiachs will repair the foolish heart, and then the Holy One will slaughter the evil inclination.” This last explanation is R’ Tzadok’s, not a statement of Sukkah 52a.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: In everything there are seven rungs — three “fathers,” three “offspring” like them, and a seventh that brings the six extremities into actuality and perfects them all. This is the seventh elevation of teshuvah, which we still await: the individual of David’s seed who will repent, and thereby forgive the whole world entire, the living and the dead.

sections.en: Great is teshuvah, for it tears up an evil decree

items.h: Great is teshuvah, for it tears up an evil decree
גדולה תשובה שמקרעת גזר דין.

p: (א) וְעוֹד יֵשׁ מַעֲלָה שְׁמִינִית
Furthermore, there is an eighth virtue,
בַּמֶּה שֶׁגְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה
in the greatness of repentance,
וְלֹא נִזְכַּר בְּיוֹמָא
which was not mentioned in tractate Yoma;
רַק בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (י״ז עַמּוּד ב׳) אִיתָא
rather, Rosh Hashanah (17b) states:
גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמְּקָרַעַת גְּזַר דִּינוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
“Great is teshuvah, for it tears up a person’s decreed verdict,”
וְדָיֵיק מִן: "וּלְבָבוֹ יָבִין וָשָׁב וְרָפָא לוֹ
and it derives the teaching from Isaiah 6:10: “And his heart will understand, and he will return, and he will be healed.”
וּבְיוֹמָא עַל מְבִיאָה רְפוּאָה
whereas Yoma (86a), concerning the teaching that teshuvah “brings healing,”
מַיְיתֵי מִן: "אֶרְפָּא מְשׁוּבָתָם" וְלֹא מֵהַאי
it cites the verse (Hosea 14:5): “I will heal their backsliding,” and not from this verse.
וְאִי מִשּׁוּם דְּהַהוּא רְפוּאָה דִּסְלִיחָה
And if you suggest that this is because that verse refers to the healing of forgiveness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִלָּה (י״ז עַמּוּד ב
as our Sages explain in Megillah (17b),
גַּם "אֶרְפָּא מְשׁוּבָתָם" אֵימָא כֵּן
even for “I will heal their backsliding” let us say so.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל (סִימָן א׳) בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן
and as I wrote above (Section 1), such is indeed the truth.
רַק דְּ"אֶרְפָּא" מַשְׁמַע לְהַבָּא
Rather, “I will heal” (erpa) implies for the future,
וְכִדְדָיֵיק גְּמָרָא שָׁם אַחַר כָּךְ
as the Gemara subsequently infers,
לְפֵירוּשׁ אֶחָד דְּרַשִׁ״י
according to one interpretation of Rashi;
אֲבָל "וְרָפָא" הַיְינוּ לְשֶׁעָבַר שֶׁכְּבָר נִרְפָּא
whereas “and be healed” (verafa) denotes for the past, that it has already been healed.
וְעוֹד, "אֶרְפָּא" מַשְׁמַע מִפְּעֻלַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
Furthermore, “I will heal” implies through the active operation of Hashem, blessed be He;
אֲבָל "וְרָפָא" מַשְׁמַע מֵעַצְמוֹ
whereas “and be healed” denotes occurring spontaneously on its own.
וְזֶה דָּבָר מוּפְלָא
And this is a remarkable concept:
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִרְפָּא מֵעַצְמוֹ עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה
that it should be healed spontaneously through the power of repentance,
וַהֲרֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָדוֹ פְּתוּחָה לְקַבֵּל שָׁבִים
seeing that Hashem’s hand is outstretched to receive the penitent,
מַשְׁמַע דְּצָרִיךְ לְקַבָּלָתוֹ
which implies that it requires His active acceptance.
אֲבָל בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מַיְירֵי
However, the discussion in Yoma’s chapter Yom HaKippurim centers,
בְּעִנְיַן הַכַּפָּרָה שֶׁל הַתְּשׁוּבָה לְהַבָּא וּלְשֶׁעָבַר
upon the theme of the atonement of repentance for both the future and the past.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא הוֹצָאַת עִנְיַן הַתְּשׁוּבָה לַפּוֹעַל
and this matter constitutes bringing the reality of repentance into actuality.
וְכָל דָּבָר הַיּוֹצֵא לַפּוֹעַל
And every entity that emerges into actuality
יֵשׁ בּוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת
contains three primary supernal attributes (Keter, Chokhmah, Binah)
הַמּוֹלִידוֹת דָּבָר הַהוּא בְּכֹחַ
which generate that entity in potential,
שֶׁמֵּהֶם נִמְשָׁכוֹת שֶׁבַע תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת
from which are drawn down the seven lower attributes (Chesed through Malchut).
מִדּוֹת הַבִּנְיָן שֶׁל הַהוֹצָאָה לַפּוֹעַל
the formative attributes through which the potential becomes actual.
כִּי כָּל דָּבָר מוּגְבָּל עַל כָּרְחֲךָ נֶחֱלָק לְשָׁלֹשׁ חֲלוּקוֹת וְהַגְבָּלוֹת
For everything bounded necessarily has three divisions and limits:
רֹאשׁ, תּוֹךְ, סוֹף
beginning, middle, and end,
וְהֵם הַשָּׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת
and these correspond to the three higher attributes;
וּמֵהֶם נִבְנִים הַיְצִיאָה לַפּוֹעַל בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַמָּקוֹם
and through them the emergence into actuality is built out in spatial extension:
שָׁלֹשׁ הַגְבָּלוֹת דְּאֹרֶךְ וְרֹחַב וְגֹבַהּ אוֹ עֹמֶק
the three boundaries of length, width, and height or depth,
שֶׁבָּהֶם הַשֵּׁשׁ קְצָווֹת דְּכָל דָּבָר
within which exist the six spatial extremities of every physical entity,
וְהַשֶּׁבַע הוּא כְּלָלוּת הַשֶּׁטַח כַּיָּדוּעַ
and the seventh is the overall expanse, as is known.
וּמִזֶּה מַיְירֵי בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
And it is concerning this that the Gemara in Rosh Hashanah treats;
דְּזֶהוּ "וּלְבָבוֹ יָבִין
for this is “and his heart will understand” —
הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתְּשׁוּבָה
which is the primordial root of repentance.
בִּהְיוֹתוֹ עֲדַיִן בְּכֹחַ בַּבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב לְבַד
while it still resides in potential within the understanding (Binah) in the heart alone.
וַעֲשֶׂרֶת יְמֵי תְּשׁוּבָה הֵם עֶשֶׂר מִדּוֹת הַקּוֹמָה
And the Ten Days of Repentance are the ten sefirotic gradations of the complete spiritual stature,
וּבְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הוּא הַהַתְחָלָה וְשָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת
and on Rosh Hashanah is the inception and the three supernal attributes,
וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הוּא הַגְּמָר וְהַסִּיּוּם
and on Yom Kippur is the final culmination and completion.
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יִכָּתֵבוּן, וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים יֵחָתֵמוּן
in the manner that we say in liturgy: on Rosh Hashanah they are inscribed, and on Yom Kippur they are sealed.
וְעַל כֵּן בְּמַסֶּכֶת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בֵּאֲרוּ מַעֲלָה זוֹ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה
Therefore in tractate Rosh Hashanah they elucidated this sublime virtue of repentance
שֶׁמִּצַּד עֶצֶם מִדָּתָהּ
which stems from its intrinsic, essential attribute,
שֶׁהִיא מִדָּה הַשְּׁמִינִית מִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָּא
which is the eighth attribute counting from below upward (Malchut to Binah),
כַּנּוֹדָע דְּבִינָה תַּמָּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתְּשׁוּבָה
as is known that in Binah lies the source-root of repentance.
שֶׁאֵינָהּ אֶלָּא בַּלֵּב
which exists solely within the heart.
וְהַיְצִיאָה לַפּוֹעַל הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גּוֹמֵר בַּעֲדוֹ וּמְקַבְּלָהּ
And its actualized realization is what Hashem, blessed be He, completes on his behalf and accepts.
וְאָז יֵשׁ לָהּ שֶׁבַע מַדְרֵיגוֹת וּמַעֲלוֹת דְּיוֹמָא
and then it manifests the seven rungs and greatnesses detailed in tractate Yoma.

Yochanan said: Great is teshuvah, for it tears up a person’s decree.” The proof is Isaiah 6:10, “ולבבו יבין ושב ורפא לו”; the continuation asks whether the decree was already sealed and answers from “ורפא לו,” since a decree needing healing is a finalized decree. Compare Rosh Hashanah 16b: “ארבעה דברים מקרעין גזר דינו של אדם ... ושינוי מעשה” — change of conduct is one of four ways an adverse decree is torn. This note attaches to R. Tzadok’s first citation of the teaching, not his later exposition of Binah.

paragraphs.text: The precise distinction in Megillah 17b is: “ההוא לאו רפואה דתחלואים היא אלא רפואה דסליחה היא” — “That healing is not the healing of illness, but the healing of forgiveness.” The Gemara uses “ושב ורפא לו” in discussing the blessing of forgiveness. R. Tzadok does not deny that “ארפא משובתם” can likewise describe forgiveness; he asks why Yoma cites that expression while Rosh Hashanah cites “ורפא לו,” and then advances his further distinction between future and already-completed healing.

paragraphs.text: Izhbitz parallel — Mei HaShiloach I, Bereishis §6: “ועץ החיים הוא תשובה אמיתית שמרפאת את הקודם” — “The Tree of Life signifies genuine teshuvah that heals what preceded.” The same passage adds: “ותשובה מרפאת את הקודם היינו החסרון שיש לאדם מיום הולדו” — “teshuvah heals what preceded: even a deficiency present from the day of a person’s birth.” The Izhbitzer describes return to one’s earliest source. This directly clarifies R. Tzadok’s “ורפא ... לשעבר שכבר נרפא,” without attributing to the Izhbitzer R. Tzadok’s separate distinction between Divine action and the healing of itself.

paragraphs.text: Rashi on Yoma 86a (on “וכתיב ארפא”) explains: “משמע מכאן ואילך כבעל מום שנתרפא שמקצת שמו עליו” — “‘I will heal’ implies from this point onward, like a person whose blemish was healed but upon whom part of his former designation remains.” Rashi contrasts repentance from love, which uproots the original sin, with repentance from fear. R. Tzadok uses this future-oriented reading of “ארפא” and then makes his own additional grammatical contrast: “ורפא” indicates healing that has already occurred, apparently of itself. That additional distinction is R. Tzadok’s development, not a direct quotation of Rashi.

paragraphs.text: Liturgical source — the closing prayers of Yom Kippur: “אתה נותן יד לפושעים וימינך פשוטה לקבל שבים” — “You extend a hand to transgressors, and Your right hand is open to accept those who return.” This explains R. Tzadok’s question at “צריך לקבלתו”: if Divine acceptance is necessary, in what sense does “ורפא” describe an inward healing that has already happened? He distinguishes the root of teshuvah in the heart from its complete emergence into action through Hashem’s acceptance.

paragraphs.text: R. Tzadok — internal parallel, Kometz HaMinchah II §57: “כי בכל דבר יש ב׳ קצוות ואמצעי” — “In every thing there are two extremes and a middle”; and “הנה הימין עצמו גם כן חלוק לג׳ אלו ככל בעל גבול” — “the right side itself divides into these three, like any bounded thing.” This is a particularly precise parallel to “ראש, תוך, סוף,” the three delimitations of any finite form. It explains the structure of the three upper principles before R. Tzadok turns to the lower seven.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: There is yet an eighth greatness of teshuvah, not listed in Yoma but taught in Rosh Hashanah: teshuvah “tears up a person’s sealed verdict.” R’ Tzadok reads the wordings closely — “and he shall be healed” implies a healing of the past, that he is already healed, and of itself. This is a different matter from “I will heal their backsliding.”

p: (ב) וְאָמְרוּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שָׁם
And they said there in Rosh Hashanah (17b):
גְּזַר דִּין דְּיָחִיד אֵינוֹ נִקְרָע
“An individual’s decreed verdict is not torn up”;
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר : "אֲנִי ה' לֹא שָׁנִיתִי
as the verse says (Malachi 3:6): “For I, Hashem, have not changed.”
כִּי הִנֵּה לְשׁוֹן "נִקְרָע
For behold, the phrasing “is torn up,”
וְכֵן "תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמְּקָרַעַת
and likewise “repentance which tears up,”
וְכֵן לְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב "וְרָפָא" – מֵעַצְמוֹ
and likewise the biblical term “and be healed” — indicating spontaneously on its own.
הַיְינוּ דְּהַתְּשׁוּבָה מֵעַצְמָהּ הִיא הַקּוֹרַעַת וּמְרַפְּאַת
denote that repentance on its own is that which tears up and heals.
כְּמוֹ דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל שֶׁנָּפַל מַיִם עַל נְיָיר כָּתוּב וְנִמְחֲקוּ הָאוֹתִיּוֹת
It is by way of an analogy to water spilling upon an inscribed paper and erasing the letters;
כִּי אוֹתִיּוֹת הַגְּזַר דִּין הוּא מִמַּעֲשֵׂה הָעֲבֵירָה עַצְמָהּ
for the letters of the decreed verdict are generated by the act of the sin itself,
כִּי "חַטָּאִים תְּרַדֵּף רָעָה" (מִשְׁלֵי י״ג, כ״א
for “Evil pursues sinners” (Proverbs 13:21).
וּמִזֶּה נַעֲשָׂה נְיָיר שֶׁל הַגְּזַר דִּין
and from this is fashioned the parchment of the verdict.
דְּהַיְינוּ סִפְרָן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים
namely the book of the wicked.
דְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁהַסֵּפֶר שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים וְשֶׁל רְשָׁעִים וְשֶׁל בֵּינוֹנִים
For it is known that the book of the righteous, of the wicked, and of the intermediate
הוּא לֵב הָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ
is the person’s own heart;
וּכְשֶׁשּׁוֹבֵר לִבּוֹ וְעָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה
and when he breaks his heart and performs repentance,
וְנִשְׁבַּר לִבּוֹ בְּקִרְבּוֹ
and his heart is broken contritely within him.
הֲרֵי נִקְרַע הַסֵּפֶר שֶׁל גְּזַר דִּין
behold, the book of the decreed verdict is torn up.
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם צָרִיךְ עֵזֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
Yet nonetheless, one requires the assistance of Hashem, blessed be He,
שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַשְׁלִים כָּל מַדְרֵיגוֹת הַתְּשׁוּבָה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת
in order to complete all rungs of repentance in perfection.
וְלֹא יִמְנָעֵהוּ יִצְרוֹ הַמִּתְגַּבֵּר בְּכָל יוֹם
and so that his evil inclination, which grows stronger every day, does not prevent him.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֻכָּה (נ״ב עַמּוּד ב
And as they stated in Sukkah (52b):
דְּ"אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ – אֵין יָכוֹל לו
“Were the Holy One, blessed be He, not to assist him, he could not overcome it,”
וְזֶהוּ לְעִנְיַן לְהַבָּא
and this pertains to the future,
דְּעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "אֶרְפָּא
concerning which it is stated: “I will heal” (erpa).
וּמִטַּעַם זֶה אֵין תְּשׁוּבָה מוֹעֶלֶת
And for this reason, repentance does not avail,
לִפְטוֹר מֵעָנְשֵׁי בֵּית דִּין
to exempt an offender from the judicial punishments of an earthly court,
שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי עֲקִירַת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה לְמַפְרֵע
which would operate through uprooting the deed retroactively,
דְּעַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה כְּאִלּוּ לֹא חָטָא
so that through repentance it is as though he never sinned
וְהַזְּדוֹנוֹת כִּשְׁגָגוֹת אוֹ כִּזְכִיּוֹת
and willful sins become like inadvertent errors or like merits,
וְלָמָּה יֵעָנֵשׁ
and why then should he be punished?
אֲבָל כָּל תִּיקּוּנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה – הַכֹּל בַּלֵּב
However, all rectifications of repentance exist strictly within the heart;
אַךְ בַּיְצִיאָה לַפּוֹעַל שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁמְּקַבְּלוֹ
yet regarding the actualized emergence which is from the side of Hashem, blessed be He, Who receives it,
אֲנִי ה' לֹא שָׁנִיתִי
“I am Hashem, I have not changed”;
וּמֵאַחַר דִּגְזַר דִּין כָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְשַׁנּוֹתוֹ
and since the decreed verdict is inscribed in the Torah, it cannot be altered,
דְּתוֹרָה נִקְרָאת "אֱמֶת
for the Torah is designated as “truth,”
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ה׳ רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב
as they said in Berakhot (5b),
וֶאֱמֶת הוּא מַה שֶּׁיִּכּוֹן לָעַד וְלֹא יִשְׁתַּנֶּה לְעוֹלָם
and truth is that which stands firm forever and never changes;
וְכֵן "חוֹתָמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֱמֶת
and likewise, “The seal of the Holy One, blessed be He, is truth,”
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּ
as they stated in Yoma (69b).
וְעַל כֵּן גְּזַר דִּין
Therefore a decreed verdict,
דְּהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁנֶּחְתַּם כִּדְמַשְׁמַע בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (ט״ז עַמּוּד א
meaning when it has been formally sealed, as implied in Rosh Hashanah (16a).
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת
cannot be altered.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (י״ז עַמּוּד א
Therefore they stated in Avodah Zarah (17a)
בְּמִינוּת וּזְנוּת
concerning heresy and illicit relations,
שֶׁאִם יָשׁוּבוּ לֹא יַשִּׂיגוּ אָרְחוֹת חַיִּים
that even if they repent they will not attain the paths of life,
דְּעַל זֶה לֹא יוֹעִיל הַתְּשׁוּבָה
for against this, repentance does not avail,
דּוּגְמַת לִפְטוֹר מִמִּיתַת בֵּית דִּין
parallel to its inability to exempt from execution by a court.
דְּמֵאַחַר דַּאֲדוּק בָּהֶם זֶה מִקְרֵי דְּנֶחְתַּם גְּזַר דִּין
since because he was passionately bound to them, this is considered as a sealed verdict.
כִּמְבוֹאָר בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (י״ח עַמּוּד א
As clarified in Rosh Hashanah (18a)
דְּזֶהוּ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (יִרְמְיָה ב׳, כ״ב): "נִכְתָּם עֲוֺנֵךְ
that this corresponds to what is written (Jeremiah 2:22): “Your iniquity is marked as a stain (nikhtam),”
רָצָה לוֹמַר כְּכֶתֶם הַנִּכְנָס בַּבֶּגֶד בְּחֹזֶק
meaning like a deep-set stain that penetrates a garment with such tenacity,
שֶׁאַף שֶׁיַּעֲבִירוּ כָּל שִׁבְעָה סִימָנִין אֵין עוֹבֵר
that even if they apply all seven chemical cleansing agents, it does not depart,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ סִימַן הַכֶּתֶם הַמְטַמֵּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּנִדָּה
which is the halakhic criterion of a defiling stain as they stated in Niddah;
שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְכַּבֵּס וְעוֹבֵר כְּלָל
that it cannot be washed out or removed at all;
כָּךְ הַשָּׁקוּעַ בֶּעָוֺן וּבְרַע בְּכָל מַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבוֹ
so too one who is immersed in iniquity and evil within all the depths of his heart,
שֶׁלֹּא יָכוֹל לְהִתְכַּבֵּס
cannot be completely laundered;
וְזֶהוּ חֲתִימַת גְּזַר דִּין שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִקְרָע
and this is the sealing of the decreed verdict that cannot be torn up,
דְּ"כָּל בָּאֶיהָ לֹא יְשׁוּבוּן וְגוֹמֵר" (מִשְׁלֵי ב׳, י״ט
mirroring: “All that go unto her shall not return” (Proverbs 2:19).
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁעוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה
And even though nothing can withstand repentance,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בְּעִנְיַן הַיְצִיאָה לַפּוֹעַל בְּמַעֲשֶׂה
nonetheless regarding its emergence into actualized physical deed,
הֲרֵי יֵשׁ אַרְבָּעָה חִלּוּקֵי כַּפָּרָה הַנִּזְכָּר בְּ
behold there are the four divisions of atonement mentioned in Yoma (86a).
דְּצָרִיךְ לְיִסּוּרִין וּמִיתָה מְמָרְקִין
where one still requires afflictions and death to scour.
וְהַיְינוּ כָּל יְמֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And this applies throughout all the days of this world,
שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא הִגִּיעַ לִשְׁלֵימוּת מַדְרֵגָתָהּ
when it has not yet reached the fullness of its ultimate level
שֶׁיַּגִּיעוּ לֶעָתִיד
that will be attained in the future,
דְּ"יְבֻלַּע הַמָּוֶת" (
when “death will be swallowed up forever” (Isaiah 25:8);
וְיִכְלוּ הַיִּסּוּרִין מִן הָעוֹלָם
and suffering will cease entirely from the world;
כִּי יַגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגַת "מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ וּלְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ
because one will then attain the spiritual rank where “he is forgiven, along with the entire world,”
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ
for there will be an awakening of repentance throughout the entire world.

paragraphs.text: R. Tzadok — conceptual parallel, Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah §7: of the decrees restricting Torah and mitzvot he writes: “ועי״ז נתמרמרו וגדלה התשוקה בלבם לעסוק בתורה בסתר” — “through this they were embittered, and their hearts’ longing to study Torah in secret grew greater.” This is an example of pressure giving rise to a deepened movement of the heart. It illuminates the inner change described when the sinner breaks his heart, but it is not an independent source for R. Tzadok’s particular metaphor of the verdict inscribed in the heart.

paragraphs.text: The sugya in Rosh Hashanah 17b–18a distinguishes a communal decree, which may be torn even after sealing, from the more restricted case of an individual. Izhbitz parallel — Mei HaShiloach II, Yonah 4:1: “כאשר יצאה נבואה ומאמר ה׳, היא בהכרח שתפעול מה; ואפילו כשיעשו תשובה, זה המאמר אינו חוזר ריקם” — “When a prophecy and Divine utterance has gone forth, it must accomplish something; even when people repent, it does not return empty.” In the following lines, the destructive effect of Yonah’s prophecy is borne by the kikayon, not by repentant Nineveh. This offers a distinct parallel to R. Tzadok’s claim that Divine truth remains unchanged although the sinner’s relation to the decree can change. It is not a literal interpretation of the Gemara’s legal distinction.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 86a: The “four divisions of atonement” of R’ Yishmael — for a positive commandment, teshuvah alone atones; for a negative, teshuvah suspends and Yom Kippur atones; for sins bearing kareis or court-death, teshuvah and Yom Kippur suspend and sufferings scour; and for one who profanes the Divine Name, only death, together with the others, scours. Hence in this world some sins still require suffering or death to complete the atonement.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: They also taught that an individual’s sealed verdict is not torn — “I, Hashem, have not changed.” R’ Tzadok resolves it from the wordings themselves: “torn,” “teshuvah tears,” “healed of itself” all mean that teshuvah is what does the tearing and the healing, not a change in Him. When it is truly within a person, the “book” of the verdict is torn.

p: (ג) וּבְצִבּוּר נִקְרָע
And in the case of a community the decreed verdict is torn up,
דְּאָז הוּא עֵת רָצוֹן
for that constitutes an acceptable time of divine favor,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ח׳ עַמּוּד א
and as our Sages taught in Berakhot (8a):
אֵימָתַי עֵת רָצוֹן? וְכוּלֵי
“When is an hour of favor?” and so forth;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (י״ח עַמּוּד א
and as they stated in Rosh Hashanah (18a),
דִּבְיָחִיד נִקְרָא "בְּהִמָּצְאוֹ" בַּעֲשֶׂרֶת יְמֵי תְּשׁוּבָה
that for an individual, “while He may be found” applies during the Ten Days of Repentance,
וּבְצִבּוּר "בְּכָל קָרְאֵנוּ אֵלָיו
whereas for a community, it is “whenever we call upon Him.”
וַאֲפִילּוּ לְאַחַר גְּזַר דִּין, עַיֵּין שָׁם
even after the verdict has been decreed; see there.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּרָצוֹן הוּא הַהֵיפֶךְ מֵרֹגֶז וְדִין
And this is because divine favor (ratzon) is the exact antithesis of anger and strict justice;
וְכֵיוָן דְּהַצִּבּוּר מְעוֹרְרִים עֵת רָצוֹן
and since the community awakens an hour of favor,
מִמֵּילָא אֵין מָקוֹם לַדִּין
consequently there remains no room for strict judgment.
וְאֵין כָּאן שִׁינּוּי
And there is no contradiction or mutability here,
שֶׁהַדִּין לֹא נִשְׁתַּנָּה
for the strict judgment has not been altered;
רַק שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה אוֹר חָדָשׁ בָּעוֹלָם
rather a new illumination has been disclosed in the world.
שֶׁהוּא אוֹר רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא לְעוֹלָם לְהֵיטִיב
which is the light of His divine will, blessed be He, which is eternally to bestow goodness.
וּבְהִתְגַּלּוּת עֵת רָצוֹן זֶה
And through the manifestation of this favorable time,
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְרוּצֶּה בְּעוֹלָמוֹ
wherein the Holy One, blessed be He, is pleased with His creation
וּמוֹצֵא נִיחָא מִבְּרִיּוֹתָיו
and derives spiritual satisfaction from His creatures,
עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב וְאוּבַנְתָּא דְּלִבָּא
through the repentance of the heart and the heart's deep understanding,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא נִגְמַר הַיְצִיאָה לַפּוֹעַל
even though the emergence into actuality has not yet been completed,
עַל יְדֵי עֵזֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַד עֵת קֵץ
through the active assistance of Hashem until the End of Days,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּבָר "וְרָפָא" מֵעַצְמוֹ
nonetheless it has already “been healed” spontaneously on its own,
וּמִמֵּילָא נִקְרַע גְּזַר דִּין
and automatically the decreed verdict is torn up
עַל יְדֵי גִּלּוּי מִדַּת רְצוֹנוֹ וְטוּבוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
through the disclosure of the attribute of His divine favor and goodness, blessed be He.

Tzadok — Pri Tzaddik, Bereishis §13: “ואני תפלתי לך ה׳ עת רצון. הורה לנו דוד המע״ה כשנתפלל בעת רצון על מה נתפלל ... שמאחר שנוכל לפעול רב חסד בעת רצון” — “David taught what to request at an hour of favor ... since abundant kindness can be elicited at such an hour.” In that discourse he also requests that kindness be joined by disciplined fear of Heaven, rather than becoming a hindrance to service. paragraphs.text: Talmudic basis — Berakhot 8a: “אימתי עת רצון — בשעה שהצבור מתפללין” — “When is an hour of favor? When the congregation prays.” A particularly close Chassidic explanation appears in Sefat Emet, Chukat, section 4:5: “בני ישראל מעוררין בתפלתם עת רצון” and “התפלה גורמת הרצון” — “Israel awakens an hour of favor through prayer,” and “prayer generates the favor.” The Sefat Emet adds that sometimes Hashem desires Israel to awaken that favor themselves. This directly illuminates R. Tzadok’s phrase “הציבור מעוררים עת רצון,” without treating communal prayer as an automatic exemption from every form of judgment.
