inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok explores how even an involuntary bodily occurrence can leave ritual impurity and a remaining distance from complete inward purity. He connects the historical immersion requirement, the awe appropriate to Torah, and Torah’s power to transform the inclination.

p: וְעַל דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִלְעַאי
And about the generation of Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai
אָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין כ, עַמּוּד א)
they said (Sanhedrin 20a):
“אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה׳ וְגוֹמֵר”
“a woman who fears Hashem,” etc.;
וְעֲדִיפֵי מִדּוֹרוֹ דְּמֹשֶׁה וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ וְדִחִזְקִיָּה,
and they were superior to the generation of Moshe, Yehoshua and Chizkiyah,
שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ חֵן וְיֹפִי,
who were “grace and beauty,”
הַיְנוּ שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ נְפָשׁוֹת נְקִיּוֹת מִתּוֹלָדָה
that is, they were souls clean from birth,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
as it says of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
מִיָּד שֶׁנּוֹלַד “וַתֵּרֶא אֹתוֹ כִּי טוֹב הוּא”,
from the moment he was born, “and she saw him, that he was good,”
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁנּוֹלַד מָהוּל,
and the Sages of blessed memory said he was born circumcised,
וְהַיְנוּ צַדִּיק כִּי טוֹב הֵיפֶךְ הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי ה׳.
meaning righteous, since “good” is the opposite of “evil in the eyes of Hashem.”
וְכֵן יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִזַּרְעָא דְיוֹסֵף.
So too Yehoshua, from the seed of Yosef.
וְחִזְקִיָּה אָמַר עַל עַצְמוֹ
And Chizkiyah said about himself
“זְכֹר נָא אֵת אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר”,
“Remember, what I walked before You,” etc.,
“וְהַטּוֹב בְּעֵינֶיךָ וְגוֹמֵר”
“and the good in Your eyes,” etc.,
שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ הָרַע בְּעֵינָיו,
which is the opposite of “evil in His eyes,”
וְהָיָה בָּטוּחַ בְּעַצְמוֹ
and he was confident about himself
שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה עָלָיו שׁוּם טַעֲנָה מִשֶּׁמֶץ חֵטְא בָּעוֹלָם,
that there was no claim against him of any trace of sin in the world,
דְּגַם מַה שֶׁבִּטֵּל פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה
for even his having neglected procreation
הָיָה בְּתַמִּימוּת וּלְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם כְּפִי דַעְתּוֹ,
was in innocence and for Heaven’s sake, as he understood,
דְּחָמֵי בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְכוּלֵי
for he foresaw through Divine Inspiration, etc.
וְהַגַּם דְּקְרָא צָוַח
and though the verse cries out
“אֵין אָדָם צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה טּוֹב וְגוֹמֵר”,
“there is no righteous man on earth who does good,” etc.,
צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר דְּדַיְיקָא “צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ”,
we must say the verse is precise: “righteous on earth,”
הַיְנוּ שֶׁהוּא שָׁקוּעַ בְּאַרְצִיּוּת גַּם כֵּן,
meaning one who is also immersed in earthliness,
מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן אוֹתָם שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהֶם שׁוּם שַׁיָּכוּת
unlike those who had no connection at all
לְעִנְיְנֵי אַרְצִיּוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל.
to earthly matters of this world.
אֲבָל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִלְעַאי זָכָה עַל יְדֵי יִרְאַת ה׳,
But Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai merited through fear of Hashem,
שֶׁהוּא מַה שֶׁה׳ שׁוֹאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ
which is what Hashem asks of you,
שֶׁהוּא רַק בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם וְלֹא מִצַּד שָׁרְשׁוֹ.
being only through a person’s effort and not from his root.
דְּזֶה נִקְרָא חֵן וְיֹפִי
For “grace and beauty” is called
מִי שֶׁבַּשֹּׁרֶשׁ נָקִי מִתַּאֲוֹת גַּשְׁמִיּוֹת,
one who in the root is clean of bodily lusts,
וְזֶה לֹא יִקְרֶה לוֹ שׁוּם מִקְרֶה גַּם לְאָנְסוֹ
and no mishap will befall him, even involuntarily,
מֵאֵיזֶה חִמּוּם וְטֹרַח דֶּרֶךְ וְכַדּוֹמֶה שֶׁיִּקְרֶה לִבְנֵי אָדָם,
from some heating, travel strain or the like that happens to people,
וְכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יְבָמוֹת עו, עַמּוּד א)
as they said (Yevamos 76a):
“אַטּוּ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ כו׳”
“Is everyone Yaakov Avinu?” etc.
(שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה אֲפִילּוּ לְאָנְסוֹ),
(who never had even an involuntary emission),
“אַטּוּ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בַּרְזִלַּי כו׳”.
“Is everyone Barzilai?” etc.
וְהַגַּם דְּשָׁם מְבֹאָר
And though it is explained there
דְּגַם מִי שֶׁכְּיַעֲקֹב יִפְעַל הַחִמּוּם אַבֵּי פוֹקְרֵי
that even someone like Yaakov would be affected by warmth applied at the opening of the rectum,
שָׁם הוּא בְּהָקִיץ לְרְצוֹנוֹ וְלֹא לְאָנְסוֹ,
there it is when awake, by his will, not involuntary,
וְעוֹשִׂין כְּדֵי לְהוֹלִיד בְּלִבּוֹ הִרְהוּר
and they do it to generate a thought in his heart,
כְּהַאי דִּבְגָדִים צִבְעוֹנִין שָׁם,
like the colored garments there,
וּבְצֵרוּף הִרְהוּר יִפְעַל הַחִמּוּם,
and with the addition of a thought the heating works,
וְלֹא לְמִי שֶׁנִּזְהָר מֵהִרְהוּר וּכְשֵׁנָה.
but not for one who guards against thought, nor in sleep.
אֲבָל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִלְעַאי זָכָה אַחַר כָּךְ לָזֶה
But Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai later merited this
בְּכֹחַ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה,
through the power of his striving in Torah,
עַד שֶׁאָמְרוּ עָלָיו (שַׁבָּת כה, עַמּוּד ב)
until they said of him (Shabbos 25b)
שֶׁהָיָה דּוֹמֶה לְמַלְאַךְ ה׳ צְבָאוֹת,
that he resembled an angel of Hashem of Hosts,
וּמַלְאָךְ הוּא נָקִי מִתַּאֲוָה.
and an angel is clean of lust.
וְזֶה הָיָה בִּלְבִישַׁת סְדִינִין הַמְצֻיָּצִין,
And this was in wearing the sheets with tzitzis,
דְּצִיצִית בְּחוּט שֶׁל תְּכֵלֶת רוֹמֵז לְיִרְאָה כַּיָּדוּעַ.
for tzitzis with a blue thread hints at fear, as is known.
וְאַחַר הָרְחִיצָה לִכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת,
And after the washing in honor of Shabbos,
שֶׁהִתְחִיל לְהִתְנוֹצֵץ הֶאָרָה מִקְּדֻשַּׁת שַׁבָּת
when light began to sparkle from the holiness of Shabbos,
שֶׁהוּא מֵעֵין הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא בְּבִטּוּל הַיֵּצֶר,
which is a taste of the World to Come in the nullification of the inclination,
זָכָה לָאוֹר פָּנִים שֶׁל אָדָם בְּשַׁבָּת,
he merited the facial light of man on Shabbos,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יא)
which they said (Bereishis Rabbah, parashah 11)
דְּבֵרְכוֹ וְקִדְּשׁוֹ.
is the meaning of “He blessed it and sanctified it.”
וְהַיְנוּ בְּאוֹר פָּנִים שֶׁהָיָה לְאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קֹדֶם הַחֵטְא,
That is, the facial light that Adam had before the sin,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם
as they said there
דְּלְמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת נִטַּל זִיווֹ וְנִטְרַד מִגַּן עֵדֶן
that at the close of Shabbos his radiance was taken and he was driven from Gan Eden,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר “מְשַׁנֶּה פָנָיו וַתְּשַׁלְּחֵהוּ”.
as it says, “changing his face, You sent him away.”
וְלֶעָתִיד שֶׁיִּתְתַּקֵּן זֶה יַחֲזֹר זִיווֹ
In the future, when this is repaired, his radiance will return,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם פָּרָשָׁה יב),
as they said (there, parashah 12),
וְזֶהוּ הַמְּאוֹר פָּנִים לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
and this is the facial light of the World to Come
שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ זוּטָא (פֶּרֶק יב)
that they said in Tanna Devei Eliyahu Zuta (chapter 12)
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְכָל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם כְּפִי תּוֹרָתוֹ, עַיֵּן שָׁם.
will be for each Torah scholar according to his Torah; see there.
וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה זָכָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And Rabbi Yehudah merited in this world
לְ"חָכְמַת אָדָם תָּאִיר"
that "a person's wisdom gives light…"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בִּנְדָרִים מט, עַמּוּד ב)
as they said (Nedarim 49b)
עַל יְדֵי שְׁקִידָתוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה מִתּוֹךְ הַדְּחַק
through his diligence in Torah amid poverty
יוֹתֵר מִכָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת כַּנַּ״ל.
more than all generations, as above.
וְהָאוֹר פָּנִים שֶׁאָדָם זוֹכֶה עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה לִשְׁמָהּ
And the facial light a person merits through Torah for its own sake
זֶהוּ זִיוּוֹ דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קֹדֶם הַחֵטְא,
is the radiance of Adam before the sin,
שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְאוֹר פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ חַיִּים.
for he merits the light of the King’s countenance of life.
וְזֶהוּ כְּשֶׁנִּתְעַטֵּף בַּסְּדִינִין הַמְצֻיָּצִין
And this is when he wrapped himself in the sheets with tzitzis,
שֶׁהוּא חִבּוּר אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה,
which is a joining of love and fear,
כִּי סָדִין לָבָן שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן רוֹמֵז לְמִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה,
for a white linen sheet hints at the attribute of love,
וְחוּט שֶׁל תְּכֵלֶת לְיִרְאָה,
and the blue thread to fear,
וְאוֹרַיְתָא בִּדְחִילוּ וּרְחִימוּ פְּרַחָא לְעֵילָּא
and Torah with fear and love flies upward
וְנַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ סַם חַיִּים
and becomes for him an elixir of life
לְהִדָּבֵק עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּחַי הָעוֹלָמִים יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ,
to cling thereby to the Life of the Worlds, blessed be His Name,
דְּאוֹרַיְתָא וְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא חַד.
for Torah and the Holy One, Blessed is He, are one.

It should not be cited as denying the visible event in every sense.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok distinguishes purity present at a soul’s root from fear of God attained through personal effort. He reads Rabbi Yehudah bar Ilai’s angelic appearance and Shabbos radiance as the fruit of strenuous Torah study joined with love and awe.

p: וְזֶהוּ מַדְרֵגַת "עוֹלָמְךָ תִּרְאֶה בְחַיֶּיךָ" שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרָכוֹת יז סוֹף עַמּוּד א],
And this is the spiritual rung of "May you see your world in your lifetime," which they stated in Berakhot (17a),
וּמְסַיֵּים שָׁם: "וּפָנֶיךָ יַזְהִירוּ כְּזֹהַר הָרָקִיעַ",
and it concludes there: "and may your face shine like the brightness of the firmament,"
הַיְינוּ אוֹר הַפָּנִים;
meaning the supernal radiance of the countenance;
"וּפְעָמֶיךָ יָרוּצוּ לִשְׁמוֹעַ דִּבְרֵי עַתִּיק יוֹמִין",
“and may your feet run to hear the words of the Ancient of Days,”
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מִבְּנֵי עֲלִיָּה.
meaning that he be numbered among the elite sons of ascension.
וְהַךְ מֵימְרָא [דְּפָרָשַׁת וַיְחִי רי״ט עַמּוּד ב׳]
And that dictum in Parashat Vayechi (Zohar I, 219b)
דְּ"לֵית לֵיהּ תְּשׁוּבָה"
that for this sin "he has no repentance"
הוּא מִדִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
is from the teaching of Rabbi Yehudah,
דְּדָבָר זֶה (דִּרְאִיַּת פְּנֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה)
in that this sublime attainment (of directly beholding the face of the Shechinah)
זָכוּ לָהּ רַק יְחִידֵי הַדּוֹרוֹת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
was merited only by the rarest unique individuals of the generations in this world,
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחָאי דְּהֵן מוּעָטִים.
which is why Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai remarked that they are few in number.
וּבַגְּמָרָא דְּסֻכָּה הַנִּזְכֶּרֶת לְעֵיל (מה עַמּוּד ב) אִיתָא:
And in the Gemara in Sukkah mentioned above (45b) it is stated:
"אִם שְׁנַיִם [הֵם – אֲנִי וּבְנִי הֵם]",
“if they are two—they are myself and my son,”
וְלֹא אָמַר פָּחוֹת;
and he did not mention a lesser number;
וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה [פָּרָשָׁה ל״ה, ב] אִיתָא:
whereas in Bereishit Rabbah (35:2) it is stated:
"וְאִם חַד הוּא – אֲנָא הוּא".
“and if he is one—it is I.”
וְשָׁם לֵיתָא הַלָּשׁוֹן "רָאִיתִי",
And there in the Midrash the phrasing "I have seen" does not appear,
וְאָמַר כְּפִי הַמְּצִיאוּת
and he formulated it according to ontological reality,
דְּעַל כָּל פָּנִים אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת פָּחוֹת מֵאֶחָד
in that at the very least it is impossible for there to be fewer than one,
שֶׁעָלָיו הָעוֹלָם עוֹמֵד,
upon whom the entire universe stands,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְצַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם" (מִשְׁלֵי י, כה);
as it is stated: “and the righteous is the foundation of the world” (Proverbs 10:25);
וּבַגְּמָרָא אָמַר "רָאִיתִי",
while in the Gemara he said “I have seen,”
דִּכְבָר נִסְתַּכֵּל וְרָאָה בְּאַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא הַמְּאִירָה שֶׁלּוֹ בִּבְנֵי עֲלִיָּה.
for he had already gazed and perceived the sons of ascension through his own luminous mirror.
וְאַף שֶׁלֹּא הִסְתַּכֵּל לִרְאוֹת כַּמָּה הֵם,
And even though he had not looked to calculate how many they were,
דַּהֲרֵי אָמַר "אִם וְכוּלֵי",
since he said conditionally “if, etc.,”
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עַל בְּנוֹ שֶׁהָיָה עִמּוֹ בְּצַוְותָּא תָּמִיד
nonetheless concerning his son who was constantly with him in companionship
כְּבָר רָאָה וְיָדַע שֶׁהוּא מִבְּנֵי עֲלִיָּה,
he had already observed and knew that he was indeed of the sons of ascension,
וְעַל כֵּן סִיֵּים בִּשְׁנַיִם,
and therefore he concluded the lower limit with two,
דִּכְבָר יָדַע שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר יֵשׁ שְׁנַיִם וַדַּאי מִבְּנֵי עֲלִיָּה.
for he already knew that in that generation there were certainly at least two sons of ascension.
וּלְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ הַגְּדוֹלָה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיעַ
And unto this supreme spiritual rung it is impossible to arrive
אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁהוּא צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם,
except for one who is a righteous foundation of the world,
שֶׁלֹּא פָּגַם הַבְּרִית בַּפּוֹעַל מִיהַת מִיָּמָיו בְּאֵיזֶה חֵטְא.
who never in his life blemished the holy Covenant in actual deed through any sin.
וְאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין לח עַמּוּד ב]
And regarding Adam the First, concerning whom they stated in Sanhedrin (38b)
מִקְּרָא דְּ"עָבְרוּ בְרִית" (הוֹשֵׁעַ ו, ז)
from the verse “they have transgressed the covenant” (Hosea 6:7)
שֶׁהָיָה מוֹשֵׁךְ בְּעָרְלָתוֹ,
that he pulled his foreskin to appear uncircumcised,
דְּעַל יְדֵי עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ בַּחֵטְא דְּעֵץ הַדַּעַת
in that through the instigation of the Serpent in the sin of the Tree of Knowledge,
שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לִידִיעַת רַע וְהַרְגָּשַׁת תַּאֲוָה גּוּפָנִית, פָּגַם הַבְּרִית,
wherein he arrived at the experiential knowledge of evil and bodily lust, he blemished the Covenant,
גּוֹרַשׁ מִגַּן עֵדֶן
he was driven out of the Garden of Eden,
וְהוּשַׂמּוּ "הַכְּרֻבִים וְאֵת לַהַט וְגוֹמֵר לִשְׁמֹר אֶת דֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג, כד).
and there were stationed “the cherubim and the flaming sword, etc., to guard the way of the Tree of Life” (Genesis 3:24).
דְּגַם אַחַר כָּל הַתְּשׁוּבָה וְתַעֲנִיּוֹת ק״ל (מֵאָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים) שָׁנָה
For even after all the repentance and fasts of one hundred and thirty years,
וּבִפְרִישָׁה מֵאִשָּׁה וְהַתַּאֲווֹת,
and through ascetic separation from his wife and bodily desires,
לֹא יָכוֹל לְתַקֵּן שֶׁיּוּכַל לָשׁוּב לְגַן עֵדֶן
he could not rectify things to the point of returning to the Garden of Eden
וְלֶאֱכֹל מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים לִזְכּוֹת לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם;
and eating of the Tree of Life to merit eternal life;
כִּי זוּהֲמָא זוֹ, מִשֶּׁנִּקְלְטָה בַּגּוּף,
because this serpent defilement, once absorbed into the physical body,
אֵין לָהּ תַּקָּנָה אֶלָּא קְבוּרָה
has no ultimate remedy except burial
וְשֶׁיָּשׁוּב אֶל הֶעָפָר כְּשֶׁהָיָה.
and returning to the dust as he originally was.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, Vayechi 219b (canonical Vayechi §25): R’ Yehudah teaches, “There is no transgression in the world that has no repentance, except this one; and there are no wicked who do not behold the face of the Shechinah, except this one,” invoking “evil shall not dwell with You.” R’ Yitzchak then praises the righteous in this world and the World to Come and cites “your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.” The speaker attribution in the body is thus explicit.

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 45b: Rashbi says that he has seen the bnei aliyah and they are few: if a thousand or a hundred, he and his son are among them; if two, they are he and his son. The Gemara challenges the small number from eighteen thousand who stand before Hashem and distinguishes the luminous speculum from lesser perception. It then asks about the thirty-six who receive the Shechinah daily and distinguishes entry with permission from entry without permission, according to Rashi.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok relates “seeing one’s world in one’s lifetime” to an exceptional rank of direct divine closeness. He explains the differing descriptions of Rashbi and his son, then returns to Adam’s inability to undo mortality while the serpent’s defilement remained in the body.

p: וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁעָמְדוּ עַל הַר סִינַי
And the children of Israel who stood at Mount Sinai,
פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָתָן כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּשַׁבָּת קמו רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א],
their defilement ceased, as our Sages stated in Shabbat (146a),
וּלְחַד מַאן דְּאָמַר שָׁם פָּסַק מִימוֹת יַעֲקֹב,
and according to one authority there, it ceased already from the days of Jacob,
וְאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים.
and both these and those are the words of the living God.
כִּי יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם פָּסְקָה מִמֶּנּוּ הַזּוּהֲמָא לְגַמְרֵי,
For from Jacob our father, peace be upon him, the defilement ceased entirely,
דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא מֵת,
which is why he did not die,
וְעַל כֵּן בְּזַרְעוֹ לֹא הָיָה שׁוּם דֹּפִי,
and therefore within his seed there was no moral blemish,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁכֻּלָּם מוּכָנִים וּמְעוּתָּדִים גַּם כֵּן
meaning that they were all primed and destined likewise
לְהַגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגַת פְּסִיקַת הַזּוּהֲמָא,
to reach the level of the cessation of defilement,
וְזָכוּ לָהּ בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה לִהְיוֹת כֵּן בַּפּוֹעַל בְּכָל הָאוּמָּה.
and they merited this at the Giving of the Torah so that it was realized in actuality across the entire nation.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק
In contrast, Abraham and Isaac
הוֹלִידוּ עֵשָׂו וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל,
fathered Esau and Ishmael,
שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַזּוּהֲמָא שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִיפָּסֵק מֵהֶם כְּלָל.
the very embodiment of the defilement which can never cease from them at all.
דְּעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁהֶחֱזִיר עֲלֵיהֶם הַתּוֹרָה לֹא רָצוּ לְקַבֵּל,
Therefore, when Hashem offered the Torah around to them, they refused to accept it,
וְאָמְרוּ: "מַה כְּתִיב בָּהּ? לֹא תִרְצַח, לֹא תִנְאָף",
demanding: “What is written in it? You shall not murder; You shall not commit adultery,”
שֶׁהֵם שְׁנֵי שָׁרְשֵׁי כֹּחוֹת הַיֵּצֶר הַיּוֹשֵׁב עַל שְׁנֵי מִפְתְּחֵי הַלֵּב,
which are the two primal source-powers of the evil urge sitting at the two entrances of the heart,
וְהֵם שָׁרְשָׁם בִּשְׁנֵי כֹּחוֹת הָרָע הַלָּלוּ.
and their essential roots are entrenched in these two corrupted forces.
וְהֵם הַכְּרוּבִים וְלַהַט הַחֶרֶב הַשּׁוֹמְרִים דֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים הִיא הַתּוֹרָה,
And these correspond to the cherubim and the flaming sword guarding the path of the Tree of Life, which is the Torah,
שֶׁלֹּא יִגַּע בָּהֶם מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ זוּהֲמַת נָחָשׁ הַקַּדְמוֹנִי,
lest anyone who contains the root defilement of the primordial Serpent touch them,
שֶׁהוּא נִדְבַּק אָז בַּכְּרוּבִים
in that he attaches himself then to the cherubim
שֶׁהֵם "כִּמְעַר אִישׁ וְלֹיוֹת" (מְלָכִים א ז, לו).
which are arranged “like a man embracing his female consort” (I Kings 7:36).
וּבִקְדוּשָּׁה הוּא יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵיהּ,
And in holiness, this symbolizes the sacred union of the Holy One and His Shechinah,
וּדְבֵיקוּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם,
and the absolute cleaving of the Congregation of Israel to their Father in Heaven,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְאַתֶּם הַדְּבֵקִים בַּה' אֱלֹהֵיכֶם חַיִּים כֻּלְּכֶם הַיּוֹם" (דְּבָרִים ד, ד),
as it is stated: “And you who cleave unto Hashem your God are alive every one of you this day” (Deuteronomy 4:4),
דְּזוֹכֶה עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם.
whereby one merits eternal life through this union.
וְ"זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה עָשָׂה אֱלֹהִים" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, יד),
And “God made one corresponding to the other” (Ecclesiastes 7:14),
שֶׁנִּדְבַּק בְּסִטְרָא אָחֳרָא עַל יְדֵי הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה וְנִיאוּף,
in that one attaches to the Other Side through the emission of semen in vain and through adultery,
וְהֵם שְׁתֵּי קְלִיפּוֹת הַטְּמֵאוֹת.
and these correspond to the two totally impure shells.
וּמִילּוּי תַּאֲווֹת בְּהֶיתֵּר שֶׁקּוֹרֵא לוֹ רַמְבַּ״ן [רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת קְדוֹשִׁים] "נָבָל בִּרְשׁוּת הַתּוֹרָה",
And the indulgence of desires within permissible parameters, which the Ramban terms “a scoundrel with the Torah's permission,”
וְשֶׁעַל זֶה נִצְטַוּוּ "קְדֹשִׁים תִּהְיוּ" (וַיִּקְרָא יט, ב),
concerning which we were commanded “You shall be holy” (Leviticus 19:2),
הוּא מִקְּלִיפַּת נֹגַהּ כַּיָּדוּעַ.
stems from the intermediate shell of Nogah, as is known.

pertain to “the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth” (Genesis 8:21) and the sins of youth;

attaches instead to the flaming sword,

which represents murder, bloodshed, jealousy, and anger.

and through this they were unable to attain the path of the Tree of Life and receive the Torah,

paragraphs.text: Yisrael Kedoshim 9:8 is a direct parallel: it quotes the Sinai and Yaakov traditions, reconciles them, and explains that the absence of dross in Yaakov’s descendants still required the refining hardships of Egypt before its public revelation as a nation receiving Torah. inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok reconciles the cessation of defilement in Yaakov’s days with its cessation at Sinai: what was pure in Yaakov’s root became actual throughout Israel at the giving of the Torah. He develops this through the opposing symbols of covenant, desire, the cherubim, and the flaming sword.

p: וְאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן נוֹלַד מָהוּל,
And Adam the First was created already circumcised,
דְּ"הָאֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כט),
for “God made man upright” (Ecclesiastes 7:29),
אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּיתַּן בּוֹ כֹּחַ הַבְּחִירָה לְהִתְפַּתּוֹת
only that he was endowed with the capacity of free choice to be seduced
עַד שֶׁיַּכְנִיס זוּהֲמַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לְלִבּוֹ
until he admitted the contamination of the evil urge into his heart
וְיוּכַל לְהַמְשִׁיךְ עָרְלָתוֹ וְלִהְיוֹת עָרֵל.
and could stretch his foreskin to become uncircumcised.
וְלֹא כְּמָהוּל הַמָּשׁוּךְ דְּאֵין צָרִיךְ לַחֲזוֹר וּלְמוּלוֹ אֶלָּא מִדְּרַבָּנַן מִשּׁוּם מַרְאִית הָעַיִן לְבַד,
And this was not merely like an ordinary circumcised person whose flesh was stretched, who requires recircumcision solely rabbinically for appearances,
אֲבָל הוּא נַעֲשָׂה אַחַר שֶׁחָטָא עָרֵל גָּמוּר בְּהַמְשָׁכָה זוֹ,
rather, after he sinned he became fully uncircumcised through this extension,
וּמִזֶּה נַעֲשָׂה שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְלֵידַת הַגּוֹיִם עֲרֵלִים,
and from this was forged the root for gentiles being born uncircumcised,
שֶׁכֻּלָּם צֶאֱצָאֵי אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן.
for all of them are descendants of Adam the First.
וְזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל, צֶאֱצָאֵי יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
Whereas the seed of Israel, the descendants of Jacob our father, peace be upon him,
שָׁרְשָׁם מִצַּד שׁוֹרֶשׁ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁקּוֹדֶם הַחֵטְא שֶׁזָּכָה לָהּ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
trace their source to the pristine root of Adam prior to the sin, which Jacob our father merited;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה בְּלֹא פְּסוֹלֶת,
and through this his bed was complete without spiritual dross,
שֶׁגַּם עַרְלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים מוּלִים.
such that even uncircumcised Israelites are called circumcised.
וְהַגּוֹיִם בְּהֵיפֶךְ,
The gentiles, however, are the reverse,
שֶׁהֵם מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הֶעָרְלָה וְהַזּוּהֲמָא שֶׁנִּקְלַט וְנִשְׁרַשׁ בּוֹ אַחַר הַחֵטְא.
being rooted in the foreskin and contamination that was absorbed and implanted within Adam after the sin.
וְעַל כֵּן נִמְנַע מִמֶּנּוּ הַתְּשׁוּבָה הַגְּמוּרָה
Therefore there was withheld from Adam that complete, restorative repentance
לְתַקֵּן לְגַמְרֵי לְבַטֵּל גְּזֵירַת הַמִּיתָה;
which could thoroughly rectify the damage so as to annul the decree of mortality;
וְגַם אַחַר תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ הוֹצִיא זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה לְאֹנְסוֹ
and even after his repentance he emitted semen in vain involuntarily
וְהוֹלִיד רוּחוֹת, שֵׁדִים וְלִילִין;
and generated spirits, demons, and night-specters;
וְזֶה מִצַּד שֶׁלֹּא נִטְהַר עֲדַיִן מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַזּוּהֲמָא
and this occurred because he had not yet been purified from the root defilement
דִּידִיעַת רַע וְהֶרְגֵּשׁ תַּאֲוָה גּוּפָנִית כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
of the experiential knowledge of evil and physical bodily lust, as mentioned above,
וְזֶהוּ שְׁמִירַת הַכְּרוּבִים לְדֶרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים.
and this is the guarding of the cherubim over the way of the Tree of Life.
וְקַיִן הָיָה נָקִי מִזֶּה,
And Cain was clear of this sexual lust,
אֲבָל נִדְבַּק בְּלַהַט הַחֶרֶב וּרְצִיחָה,
yet attached himself to the flaming sword and murder,
וְגַם אַחַר תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ לֹא נִטְהַר מִזֶּה לְגַמְרֵי
and even after his repentance he was not completely cleansed of this,
וְנִשְׁאַר קִינָא דִּמְסָאֲבוּתָא כַּנּוֹדָע,
remaining a nest of defilement (kina dimesavuta) as is known,
כִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַזּוּהֲמָא לֹא יָכוֹל לְסַלֵּק.
for he was unable to remove the core defilement.
וְגַם זֶה מִכְּלַל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע
And this too is part of the root of the evil inclination
שֶׁנִּקְרָא "רַע" בַּעֲוֺן דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה,
which is termed "evil" regarding the sin of emitting semen in vain,
שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן כְּאִלּוּ שׁוֹפֵךְ דָּמִים,
for he too is considered as though he sheds blood,
וּמִזֶּה נִמְשַׁךְ אַחַר כָּךְ בְּקַיִן לְשׁוֹפֵךְ דָּמִים.
and from this propensity was subsequently drawn forth in Cain the capacity to literally shed blood.
וְעַל כֵּן הַכְּרוּבִים קוֹדְמִים וְאַחַר כָּךְ לַהַט הַחֶרֶב,
Therefore the cherubim are mentioned first, and only afterward the flaming sword,
כִּי הַתְחָלַת הָרָע הוּא בְּהֶרְגֵּשׁ הַתַּאֲוָה
because the inception of evil lies in the sensation of bodily lust,
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ חֵטְא דְּעֵץ הַדַּעַת בִּידִיעַת הָרָע.
which is the source-sin of the Tree of Knowledge through knowing evil.

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: וְאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן נוֹלַד מָהוּל,

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Noach §5, lists Adam among seven figures created or born circumcised; Koheles 7:29 states that God made man upright. Pri Tzadik, Tzav 7:1, explicitly joins created circumcision, free choice and the later covering of orlah. Pri Tzadik, Shemos 4:1, adds that the event occurred within the six days of Creation and therefore entered the natural pattern of subsequent birth. The Midrash supplies Adam’s original condition; the account of its transmission as a spiritual birth-root is Rav Tzadok’s interpretation.

paragraphs.text: Machshavos Charutz 1:6 discusses the power of choice even in a person who has reached great holiness: the inclination can still suggest a false likeness to the Most High. It treats the serpent’s deception as a continuing danger of imagination. This is a related account of choice and inward corruption; the direct sources for Adam’s created circumcision are given above. Koheles 7:29 independently supplies the words “God made man upright.”

paragraphs.text: Yevamos 72a teaches that a mashuch remains circumcised by Torah law and requires recircumcision rabbinically because he looks uncircumcised; the verse invoked is an asmachta. A later baraisa refutes Rav Huna’s additional claim that he may actually eat terumah under the rabbinic rule. Nimukei Yosef on the Rif, Yevamos 24a, and Sefer HaChinuch, mitzvah 282, expressly describe the requirement as rabbinic. Thus the sugya’s concluding objection should not be mistaken for rejection of the underlying Torah/rabbinic distinction.

Shabbos 146a, Taanis 5b and Pri Tzadik, Pidyon HaBen 1:1, supply the distinct Yaakov/Sinai, enduring-seed and prenatal-purity traditions already discussed there. The present se’if relates that covenantal name to Israel’s root in Yaakov’s restored Adamic condition; it does not remove an individual’s physical obligation of milah.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 3:22–24 guards the Tree of Life after the sin. Bava Basra 17a and Shabbos 55b list those who died through the serpent’s counsel, rather than a personal sin requiring death. Machshavos Charutz 20:13 explicitly says that Adam’s repentance was real but had not reached the completion subsequently attained by David and to be revealed through Mashiach. It includes both those who never sinned and a person who sinned and returned completely. The distinction here concerns complete restoration and mortality, not a denial that Adam repented.

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 18b expressly resolves the apparent contradiction between Adam’s 130 years of separation and the generation of destructive beings by referring to involuntary emission. It also calls him a great chasid. The full passage was given at Se’if 40. Compare Machshavos Charutz 15:10 and 20:13 on the long repair of the covenantal root. The diagnosis that an unremoved bodily mixture underlies the event is Rav Tzadok’s present inference, not an assertion that the involuntary event was a chosen transgression.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 22:13 records different readings of Cain’s departure: evading or deceiving the Divine judgment, and leaving joyfully. In the latter account he tells Adam, “I repented and reached a compromise.” Vayikra Rabbah 10:5 attributes the half-decree account specifically to R’ Yehudah, alongside R’ Yehoshua b’Levi’s broader account of repentance’s power. These are multiple stated views; Cain’s compromised outcome is not the Midrash’s universal limit on repentance.

paragraphs.text: Tomer Devorah 4:2 calls Cain kina d’masavusa, a nest of impurity, yet rejects the claim that someone rooted in evil has no repair. It describes the transformation conditionally: had Cain returned completely, his restoration could even have counted in Adam’s favor; it then says that he did not wish to return. This is a statement of possible complete repair, not a report that Cain achieved it.

paragraphs.text: Niddah 13a’s bloodshed comparison concerns deliberate emission of seed in vain; the passage uses the verse’s destruction-of-offspring image. Rav Tzadok traces from that generative root to Cain’s actual bloodshed. Eruvin’s description of Adam’s event is expressly involuntary, so the two texts cannot be combined into one attribution of deliberate culpability. The shared spiritual root and the later unfolding into murder belong to the present interpretation.

Kometz HaMinchah 2:14 and 2:79:2 supply the paired roots of desire and aggression, with their distinct chesed/gevurah background discussed at Se’if 44. Rav Tzadok reads the order of the cherubim before the sword in that sequence. The narrative and the parallel establish the materials he joins; they do not independently state his whole explanation of the guardians’ order.

Kometz HaMinchah 2:14 and 2:79:2 supply the paired roots of desire and aggression, with their distinct chesed/gevurah background discussed at Se’if 44. Rav Tzadok reads the order of the cherubim before the sword in that sequence. The narrative and the parallel establish the materials he joins; they do not independently state his whole explanation of the guardians’ order.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok reads Adam’s loss of his original circumcision as the entry of bodily desire into creation. He contrasts the spiritual roots traced through Yaakov with the remaining defilement in Adam and Kayin, and connects desire with the subsequent emergence of bloodshed.

p: וְנֶאֱמַר: "וְעַתָּה פֶּן וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג, כב),
And it is stated: “And now, lest, etc.” (Genesis 3:22),
וְאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כא, ו]
and our Sages expounded in Bereishit Rabbah (21:6)
שֶׁפָּתַח לוֹ לִתְשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵי,
that Hashem opened for him an aperture to repent, etc.,
וְאֵין "פֶּן" אֶלָּא לָאו;
and “lest” (pen) denotes nothing other than a negative refusal;
אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: יִשְׁלַח וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
and the Holy One, blessed be He, said: let him put forth, etc., see there.
וְהַדָּבָר זָר
And the matter is grammatically strange:
לִהְיוֹת מְפַסְּקָא קְרָאֵי
to split the flow of the verse in two
לוֹמַר דְּמִלַּת "פֶּן" שֶׁבָּאֶמְצַע הוּא תְּשׁוּבַת אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן עַל זֶה,
to assert that the word “lest” in the middle represents the reply of Adam the First to this,
דָּבָר שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַכְנִיסוֹ בְּמַשְׁמַע הַכָּתוּב;
which is something impossible to fit within the natural syntax of the text;
וְגַם הוּא נֶגֶד הַבָּרַיְיתָא דְּעֵירוּבִין (יח עַמּוּד ב) הַנִּזְכֶּרֶת לְעֵיל שֶׁעָשָׂה בֶּאֱמֶת תְּשׁוּבָה ק״ל שָׁנָה,
and it furthermore contradicts the Baraita in Eruvin (18b) cited above showing that he did indeed repent for 130 years,
וְכֵן הוּא גַּם בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה [סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה כב, יג],
and so it is stated likewise in Bereishit Rabbah (22:13),
וְעַיֵּין לְעֵיל [סִימָן ג].
and see above (Section 3).
אֲבָל וַדַּאי אֵין מִקְרָא יוֹצֵא מִפְּשׁוּטוֹ
However, certainly no biblical verse departs from its plain meaning,
שֶׁהַכֹּל דִּבְרֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
in that the entire passage is the monologue of Hashem, blessed be He;
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַדָּבָר קָשֶׁה:
save that the matter is conceptually difficult:
מֵאַחַר דְּפָתַח לִתְשׁוּבָה,
since He opened the path for repentance,
אֵיךְ אָמַר: "פֶּן יִשְׁלַח וְגוֹמֵר"?
how could He immediately say: “lest he put forth his hand, etc.”?
וְאִם יָשׁוּב, לָמָּה לֹא יִשְׁלַח וְגוֹמֵר?
And if he repents, why should he not put forth his hand, etc.?
וּתְשׁוּבָה מְבַטֶּלֶת הַגְּזֵירָה!
For repentance annuls the decree!
אֲבָל דִּקְדּוּק לְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב שָׁם: "פֶּן יִשְׁלַח יָדוֹ וְלָקַח גַּם מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים וְגוֹמֵר",
However, by examining the exact wording there: “lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the Tree of Life, etc.”
דְּמִלַּת "יִשְׁלַח יָדוֹ" וּמִלַּת "גַּם" יִתּוּר לָשׁוֹן,
in that the phrase “put forth his hand” and the word “also” appear redundant,
וַהֲוָה לֵיהּ לוֹמַר "פֶּן יִקַּח מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים",
since it should simply have stated: “lest he take of the Tree of Life,”
מְבוֹאָר דְּהַכַּוָּונָה בַּמַּה שֶּׁהִסְמִיךְ זֶה לְ"וְעַתָּה"
it is clear that the intent in juxtaposing this to “And now”
שֶׁהוּא הִתְעוֹרְרוּת תְּשׁוּבָה.
which represents the awakening of repentance:
דְּלוּלֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה, וַדַּאי יוֹסִיף לְהִשְׁתַּקַּע בָּרָע
for without repentance, he would certainly sink deeper into evil
וְלֹא יִקְרַב לְעֵץ הַחַיִּים כְּלָל;
and would never draw near to the Tree of Life at all;
רַק כְּשֶׁיִּתְעוֹרֵר לָשׁוּב,
only when he awakens to repent,
אָז אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּקְרַב לְעֵץ הַחַיִּים
is it possible that he will approach the Tree of Life,
וְהוּא הַשָּׂגַת פְּנִימִיּוּת הַתּוֹרָה.
which is the attainment of the inner mysteries of the Torah.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּמִי שֶׁאֵין לְבָבוֹ מְנוּקֶּה מִתַּאֲווֹת גּוּפָנִיּוֹת,
And it is known that one whose heart is not purified of physical lusts,
אִם יִרְצֶה לִכָּנֵס לִפְנִימִיּוּת הַחָכְמָה וְהַשָּׂגָה שֶׁאֵין שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹ,
if he seeks to enter into the esoteric depths of wisdom and perception that do not belong to him,
נַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ סַמָּא דְּמוֹתָא
it turns into a lethal poison for him,
כְּ'אַחֵר' (אֱלִישָׁע בֶּן אֲבוּיָה) שֶׁקִּיצֵּץ בִּנְטִיעוֹת;
like Acher (Elisha ben Avuyah) who chopped down the saplings;
וְאָמְרוּ [בַּחֲגִיגָה]
and they said [in Chagigah]
לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה נָקִי אַגַּב אִימֵּיהּ,
that this occurred because he was spiritually flawed from his mother's womb,
שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ אֵיזֶה רַע בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נִתְנַקָּה מִמֶּנּוּ מִקּוֹדֶם.
there being an element of evil at his root from which he had not been cleansed beforehand.
וְכֵן כַּת שַׁבְּתַי צְבִי, שֵׁם רְשָׁעִים יִרְקָב,
And likewise the sect of Shabbetai Tzvi, may the name of the wicked rot,
נִרְאֶה דְּנַעֲשׂוּ נוֹאֲפִים עַל שֶׁעָסְקוּ בַּנִּסְתָּרוֹת
it appears that they descended into licentious adulterers because they meddled in esoteric Kabbalah
בְּעוֹד לְבָבָם מָלֵא תַּאֲווֹת.
while their hearts were still brimming with base lusts.
וְכֵן אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
And likewise with Adam the First,
אִלּוּ הָיָה מְתַקֵּן לְגַמְרֵי חֵטְא דְּעֵץ הַדַּעַת
had he completely rectified the sin of the Tree of Knowledge
לִהְיוֹת כִּקְדֶם שֶׁחָטָא,
so as to become as he was prior to the sin,
נֶעְדָּר מִמֶּנּוּ יְדִיעַת הָרַע כָּל עִיקָּר,
with the knowledge of evil totally excised from him,
אָז וַדַּאי הָיָה רָאוּי לֶאֱכֹל מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים;
then he certainly would have been worthy to eat of the Tree of Life;
וּלְכָךְ נִבְרָא לְצוֹרֶךְ הָאָדָם,
and for this very purpose it was created for the sake of man,
דְּכָל הַבְּרִיאָה הָיְתָה בִּשְׁבִילוֹ.
since all Creation was fashioned for him.
וְאוֹרַיְיתָא וְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְיִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלָּא חַד,
And the Torah, the Holy One, and Israel are all one,
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָאָדָם שֶׁבִּשְׁבִילוֹ נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם,
and Israel represents the primal archetype of Man for whose sake the universe was created,
וְהוּא אֶחָד וּמִתְאַחֵד מַמָּשׁ עִם עֵץ הַחַיִּים הוּא הַתּוֹרָה,
and he is uniquely and literally unified with the Tree of Life, which is the Torah,
שֶׁהוּא הַנִּשְׁמַת חַיִּים שֶׁנָּפַח בְּאַפָּיו,
which is identical to the breath of life that Hashem breathed into his nostrils,
וְהַכֹּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ אֶחָד שֶׁל חַיִּים:
and all is one single root of transcendent life:
זֶה נִקְרָא "נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים",
this is titled “the breath of life,”
וְזֶה "עֵץ חַיִּים",
and this is “the Tree of Life,”
וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא "אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים".
and the Holy One, blessed be He, is “the living God.”
אֲבָל זֶהוּ כְּשֶׁהוּא בִּשְׁלֵימוּת הַצֶּלֶם אֱלֹהִים שֶׁבִּתְחִלַּת הַבְּרִיאָה,
However, this applies when he abides in the perfection of the divine image present at the dawn of Creation,
וְזֶהוּ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁצּוּרָתוֹ חֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד.
and this is Jacob our father, peace be upon him, whose form is engraved upon the Throne of Glory.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 21:6: R’ Abba bar Kahana reads ve-atah as an opening to repentance, citing Devarim 10:12. It then says, “and he says pen,” treating pen as refusal; Hashem asks whether he should take from the Tree and live forever, and expels him. The question is marked etmaha, “in astonishment.” Rav Tzadok next objects to assigning the middle word to Adam and develops an interpretation that preserves the entire verse as Divine speech.

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 18b and Bereishis Rabbah 22:13 establish Adam’s penitential discipline and his recognition of repentance’s power. Compare Takanas HaShavin §3 and Pri Tzadik, Vayeilech/Shabbos Shuvah §§8, 13 and 17. Those teachings distinguish complete inner abandonment, a beginning through confession, and repentance stirred by suffering. The reality of repentance and the incompleteness of primordial restoration are therefore separate issues. Rav Tzadok’s objection here is to reading the Midrash as a flat refusal of all repentance.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 63a gives the rule that a verse never departs from its plain meaning. Ramban on Bereishis 3:22 preserves the Garden and Tree narrative while affirming both its revealed and concealed meanings. Rav Tzadok likewise retains the verse as Divine speech before interpreting its unusual wording. This shared method does not make Ramban the author of Rav Tzadok’s specific resolution of the Midrash.

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 10:5 and Shir HaShirim Rabbah 8:6 teach the power of repentance to change decrees. Vayikra Rabbah records differing views of half and full cancellation and concludes with the force of repentance even against a decree and an oath, illustrated by Yechonyah. This supports the question Rav Tzadok asks. The distinction between canceled punishment and a body fitted for immortal Torah-life is his ensuing answer, not a limitation supplied by every one of those Midrashic statements.

paragraphs.text: Ramban on Bereishis 3:22 explains that eating from the Tree of Life could annul the decreed death altogether or displace its appointed time; after Adam acquired independent choice, the guarded way became necessary. Rav Tzadok additionally focuses on “send forth his hand” and “also,” which could have been omitted from a shorter formulation. Ramban supplies the stakes of access; the explanation of a penitent’s premature grasp at inward Torah is Rav Tzadok’s following development.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 72b warns that Torah may become a potion of death when a person has not merited its proper reception, and condemns a scholar whose inside differs from the outside. Chagigah 14b–15a supplies Acher’s cutting of the plantings and his thought of two powers. Pri Tzadik, Parshas Zachor 9:1, applies Pardes to seeking an attainment beyond one’s place; Likkutei Maamarim, On Sefer Yehoshua §4 (canonical title: On Book of Joshua), treats Acher and the separation of revealed power from its source. These illuminate Rav Tzadok’s warning; the distinct prenatal tradition is supplied in the following note.

Tosafos attributes a related version to R’ Nasan and expressly mentions eating. These are related formulations, not one verbatim Bavli statement.

paragraphs.text: Machshavos Charutz 1:6 explicitly names Shabtai Tzvi in its warning about the imagination of already holy or ascetic people: the inclination may suggest that they can resemble the Most High, and cast them from a high place to a deep pit. This is a direct internal parallel to Rav Tzadok’s present sectarian example. The imprecation after the name is spelled out there as shem resha’im yirkav, “may the name of the wicked rot.”

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 37a teaches that humanity began with one person and that each person must say, “For my sake the world was created,” alongside its teaching about the value of a single life. This is the direct rabbinic background for creation’s human purpose. It is distinct from the following identification of Israel and Torah as the completed root of that purpose.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 1:4 places Torah and Israel before creation, with different kinds of priority, and makes Israel’s prior thought central to the parable there. Yisrael Kedoshim 10:8 connects every essential soul-root at Sinai with the completeness of Torah’s letters; its continuation distinguishes the holy root and its remaining trace. Resisei Layla 41:1 relates the world’s naming after Yaakov to his accomplished service. These are the specific settings joined by Rav Tzadok here, rather than interchangeable quotations of one formula.

paragraphs.text: Takanas HaShavin 6:77 explains that Israel’s attachment to Torah carries eternal life whose truth is not fully revealed in this world, while preserving the ordinary appearance of death. Kometz HaMinchah 2:77 describes Torah as Yaakov’s Tree of Life and the staff joining Israel to Hashem; approached from the wrong side, the staff becomes the serpent and a potion of death. Divrei Soferim 36:3 likewise relates Yaakov’s enduring life to the living God and Torah. These are specific parallels to the union now developed in the body.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 2:7; Yisrael Kedoshim 8:1 and 10:8; Resisei Layla 41:1. Yisrael Kedoshim distinguishes sanctity through one’s effort, the inherited holy root, and the higher Divine sanctification. Resisei Layla expressly joins the Divine breath, Torah’s illumination of the soul, and “the Holy One, Torah and Israel are all one.” The three-stage scheme is a related framework, not a verbatim identification of each stage with one member of that formula in every passage. Its application to the breath of life here is developed by Rav Tzadok in the body.

Rashi on Bereishis 28:12 instead explains the exchange of escorting angels, not the engraving on the Throne. The engraving and its interpretation are explicit in Pri Tzadik, Vayigash 13:1, and Resisei Layla §§10, 28, 41 and 45. These distinct parallels should not all be assigned to Rashi’s Genesis gloss.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok examines how the opening of repentance to Adam can coexist with exclusion from the Tree of Life. He reads the warning as guarding against entry into esoteric Torah before the heart is purified, illustrating the danger through Acher and later misuse of mystical study.

p: אֲבָל הַחֲשָׁשׁ "פֶּן וְגוֹמֵר גַּם מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים",
However, the apprehension “lest, etc., also of the Tree of Life,”
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בּוֹ עֲדַיִן זוּהֲמַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת דִּידִיעַת רַע שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַן לְגַמְרֵי,
meant that while the defilement of the Tree of Knowledge remained within him unrectified,
וְיִקַּח מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים גַּם כֵּן
he would take from the Tree of Life as well,
מְצוֹרָף לַאֲכִילַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת הַקּוֹדֵם.
combining it with his earlier consumption of the Tree of Knowledge.
וְזֶהוּ לְשׁוֹן "יִשְׁלַח יָדוֹ":
And this is the precise meaning of “put forth his hand”:
שֶׁלֹּא יִתְקָרֵב אֶל עֵץ הַחַיִּים עַצְמוֹ
that he would not intimately draw near to the Tree of Life itself
לְהִתְדַּבֵּק וּלְהִתְאַחֵד עִמּוֹ
to cleave and become one with it,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה רָאוּי לְאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַחֵטְא.
as was originally fitting for Adam prior to the sin.
דְּאַחַר כָּךְ, אַף שֶׁיִּתְעוֹרֵר לָשׁוּב,
For afterward, even when he awakened to repent,
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא יוּפְלַט מִקִּרְבּוֹ יְדִיעַת הָרָע
so long as the knowledge of evil had not been entirely vomited out of him
וְלִהְיוֹת כְּמוֹ קוֹדֶם,
so as to become as he was before,
הֲרֵי הוּא עוֹמֵד מְרוּחָק מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים,
behold he stands far removed from the Tree of Life,
וְלֹא יָכוֹל לִיקַּח מִפִּרְיוֹ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי שְׁלִיחוּת וְהוֹשָׁטַת הַיָּד.
and can take of its fruit only by dispatching and stretching forth his hand.
וְזֶהוּ לְשׁוֹן "יִשְׁלַח יָדוֹ",
And this is the meaning of “put forth his hand,”
שֶׁהוּא כְּלוֹקֵחַ דָּבָר הַמְרוּחָק מִמֶּנּוּ
being like one who grasps an entity spiritually distant from him,
וְאֵין לוֹ חִיבּוּר וְשַׁיָּיכוּת עִמּוֹ,
having no intrinsic union or affinity with it,
רַק שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְהוֹשִׁיט יָד וְלִיקַּח;
merely possessing the reach to stretch out a hand and seize;
וְאֵין הוּא מִתְקָרֵב אֶל הָעֵץ הַחַיִּים,
and he does not elevate himself to the Tree of Life,
אֶלָּא לוֹקֵחַ מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים וּמַפְרִידוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ
rather he tears from the Tree of Life, severing it from its source,
וּמְקָרְבוֹ אֵלָיו.
and drags it down to himself.
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "קִיצוּץ בִּנְטִיעוֹת",
And this is termed “chopping down the saplings,”
וּמַכְנִיס דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לַחִיצוֹנִים רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן,
infusing words of Torah into the external forces of impurity, may the Merciful One preserve us,
כְּעִנְיַן (תְּהִלִּים נ, טז): "וְלָרָשָׁע אָמַר אֱלֹהִים: מַה לְּךָ לְסַפֵּר חֻקָּי וְגוֹמֵר".
in the spirit of: “And unto the wicked God said: What have you to do to declare My statutes, etc.” (Psalms 50:16).
וּבִכְנִיסָה לַפַּרְדֵּ"ס,
And regarding entry into the Pardes,
שֶׁהוּא לִהְיוֹת מִבְּנֵי עֲלִיָּה
which is to become numbered among the sons of ascension
לִהְיוֹת צוֹפֶה בְּנִסְתָּרוֹת חַדְרֵי מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים,
gazing upon the esoteric secrets of the chambers of the King of kings,
אֲפִילּוּ מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָשָׁע
even one who is not wicked,
רַק שֶׁאֵינוֹ נָקִי לְגַמְרֵי מִשָּׁרְשׁוֹ – אֵין זֶה שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹ,
but is merely not thoroughly cleansed at his root—this does not belong to him,
וְאֵין לוֹ לִדְרוֹשׁ וְלַחְקוֹר בַּמֻּפְלָא מִמֶּנּוּ.
and he has no business seeking and probing into that which is beyond him.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר (דָּנִיֵּאל ב, כא): "יָהֵב חָכְמְתָא לְחַכִּימִין",
And on this it is stated: “He gives wisdom unto the wise” (Daniel 2:21),
וְלֹא לְטִפְּשִׁין שֶׁהָיוּ מוֹצִיאִין אוֹתָהּ בִּמְקוֹמוֹת הַמְטוּנָּפִים.
and not unto fools who would drag it out into defiled places.
וְעִנְיַן הַחֲשָׁשׁ זֶה דְּ"פֶן וְגוֹמֵר",
And the nature of this concern of “lest, etc.,”
שֶׁלֹּא יוּסַר שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַזּוּהֲמָא מִלֵּב לְגַמְרֵי;
was that the root of defilement would not be removed from the heart entirely;
כִּי דָּבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for this total eradication is impossible except through Hashem, blessed be He,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לֶעָתִיד (יְחֶזְקֵאל לו, כו): "וַהֲסִרֹתִי אֶת לֵב הָאֶבֶן [מִבְּשַׂרְכֶם] וְנָתַתִּי לָכֶם לֵב בָּשָׂר",
as it is stated regarding the ultimate future: “and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh” (Ezekiel 36:26),
וְאָמְרוּ: "לֵב לְהוֹצִיא בָּשָׂר",
and they expounded: “a heart to bring forth flesh [offspring],”
שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ לֵב הָאֶבֶן הַמְשׁוּקָּע בְּגַשְׁמִיּוּת.
which is the inversion of the stony heart sunk in coarse materialism.
וְכֵן אָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (תְּהִלִּים נא, יב): "לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא לִי [אֱלֹהִים]",
And likewise King David, peace be upon him, pleaded: “Create in me a clean heart, O God” (Psalms 51:12),
וּבְרִיאָה הוּא יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן.
and “creation” (beri'ah) denotes something out of nothing.
שֶׁאַף שֶׁכְּבָר הֲרָגוֹ לַיֵּצֶר הָרָע בְּתַעֲנִית
For even though David had already slain the evil urge through fasting,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר (שָׁם קט, כב): "וְלִבִּי חָלַל בְּקִרְבִּי",
as he said: “and my heart is slain within me” (ibid. 109:22),
אַחַר שֶׁרָאָה בְּאוֹתָהּ מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁאֵינוֹ כֵן
once he observed through that incident with Bathsheba that this was not fully so
(וְהוּא לֹא יָדַע מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ דְּלֹא הָיָה רָאוּי אֶלָּא וְכוּלֵי
(and he was unaware of what our Sages later revealed that he was not personally susceptible, but that it was divinely orchestrated,
וְשֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת רְאוּיָה לוֹ,
and that she was truly designated for him from Creation,
שֶׁהֲרֵי הַנָּבִיא אָמַר לוֹ שֶׁחָטָא וְנֶעֱנַשׁ עַל זֶה),
seeing that the prophet Nathan told him he had sinned and he was punished for it),
וְחָשַׁב שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ רַע מִזּוּהֲמַת עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ
and he reasoned that he contained a root of evil from the defilement of the Serpent's instigation
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִנָּקוֹת מִזֶּה כְּלָל.
from which it was impossible to be cleansed by mortal exertion at all.
וְעַל כֵּן בִּקֵּשׁ עַל בְּרִיאָה חֲדָשָׁה יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן "לֵב טָהוֹר",
Therefore he beseeched a novel ex nihilo creation: “a clean heart,”
וַהֲסָרַת לֵב הַטָּמֵא וְהָאֶבֶן שֶׁמִּכְּבָר בּוֹ.
and the total removal of the impure and stony heart of old within him.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 3:22; Ramban ad loc. The guarded Tree and the consequence of everlasting life were discussed in the preceding se’if. Machshavos Charutz 15:8 explicitly describes Torah’s Tree-of-Life light becoming encountered through the mixed categories of the Tree of Knowledge after Adam’s sin. inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Taking from the Tree of Life while its seeker remains inwardly distant can, in Rav Tzadok’s reading, sever wisdom from its source. He connects the complete removal of the heart’s evil with divine renewal, illustrated by the future heart of flesh and David’s prayer for a newly created clean heart.

p: וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נוֹצַר בְּתוֹלָדָה כֵּן
And Jacob our father, peace be upon him, was formed thus from birth
מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הָאֱמֶת,
from the supernal root of Truth,
שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ כָּל תַּאֲווֹת גּוּפָנִיּוֹת שֶׁנִּקְרָא "לֶחֶם שֶׁקֶר" וְכָזָב דָּבָר הַפּוֹסֵק,
which is the exact antithesis of all physical lusts, termed “bread of deceit” and a transient lie,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן "שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד" (מִשְׁלֵי יב, יט),
in contrast to “the lip of truth shall be established forever” (Proverbs 12:19),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַקַּיָּים לָעַד
which is the source-root of eternal life enduring forever
וְתוֹרָה דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ "אֱמֶת".
and of the Torah concerning which “truth” is inscribed.
שֶׁזָּכָה לָזֶה עַל יְדֵי יְגִיעַת אֲבוֹתָיו אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק בַּהֲסָרַת הַזּוּהֲמָא
He merited this through the strenuous labor of his fathers, Abraham and Isaac, in shedding the defilement
וּלְהָבִיא נֶפֶשׁ נְקִיָּה כָּזוֹ לָעוֹלָם,
and bringing forth such a pristine soul into the world,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִקְרָא הוּא לְבַדּוֹ לָהֶם "זֶרַע".
such that he alone was designated unto them as true “seed.”
וּמִמֶּנּוּ נִבְנֵית הָאוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית,
And from him was constructed the Jewish nation,
שֶׁזָּכוּ כֻּלָּם לָזֶה בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
who all merited this state at the Giving of the Torah
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁבְּדִבּוּר רִאשׁוֹן יָצְתָה נִשְׁמָתָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּפֶרֶק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, שַׁבָּת פח עַמּוּד ב],
in that at the first divine utterance their souls departed, as stated in Shabbat (88b),
וְהוּסַר לֵב הָאֶבֶן מֵהֶם,
and the stony heart was excised from them,
וְעַל יְדֵי טַל שֶׁל תְּחִיָּה שֶׁהוּחְזַר – הוּחְזַר לֵב בָּשָׂר.
and through the dew of resurrection with which they were revived—a heart of flesh was returned.
וְעַל כֵּן הָיוּ רְאוּיִם אָז לִהְיוֹת חֵירוּת מִמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת,
Therefore they were fully worthy then to enjoy emancipation from the Angel of Death,
כִּי נִסְתַּלְּקָה הַזּוּהֲמָא לְגַמְרֵי וּכְלֶעָתִיד אַחַר תְּחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים.
for the defilement had been removed completely, just as will be in the future after the resurrection of the dead.
אֶלָּא שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא,
Except that sin intervened and caused a relapse,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי [אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם וּבְנֵי עֶלְיוֹן כֻּלְּכֶם], אָכֵן כְּאָדָם תְּמוּתוּן" (תְּהִלִּים פב, ו-ז).
as it is stated: “I said: You are godlike beings, and all of you sons of the Most High; nevertheless you shall die like Adam” (Psalms 82:6–7).
וְ"אֱלֹהִים וּבְנֵי עֶלְיוֹן" הַיְינוּ בַּהֲסָרַת הַיֵּצֶר לְגַמְרֵי כַּמַּלְאָכִים;
And “godlike beings and sons of the Most High” refers to the total removal of the evil inclination like the angels;
וּ"כְאָדָם" הַיְינוּ שֶׁחָטְאוּ דּוּגְמַת אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
while “like Adam” means that they sinned in a manner parallel to Adam the First,
שֶׁפָּגְמוּ בַּבְּרִית גַּם כֵּן,
in that they blemished the holy Covenant as well,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל פָּסוּק (שְׁמוֹת לב, ו): "וַיָּקֻמוּ לְצַחֵק" – זֶה גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת,
as our Sages expounded on the verse: “and rose up to make merry” (Exodus 32:6)—this denotes sexual immorality;
דְּכָל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דְּעֵגֶל הָיָה רַק בִּשְׁבִיל תַּאֲוָה זוֹ,
for the entire root of the idolatry of the Golden Calf was solely for the sake of this lust,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין סג עַמּוּד ב]:
as they stated in Sanhedrin (63b):
לֹא עָבְדוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֶלָּא לְהַתִּיר עֲרָיוֹת בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא.
Israel served idols only to permit sexual immorality in public.
אֲבָל אָמַר "כְּאָדָם" בְּכָ״ף הַדִּמְיוֹן,
However, Scripture specifically said “like Adam” with the comparative Kaf,
דְּמוֹרֶה בְּכָל מָקוֹם "לֹא מַמָּשׁ",
which indicates in every context “not literally identical,”
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב [בְּאֵיכָה רַבָּתִי א, א] עַל פָּסוּק "הָיְתָה כְּאַלְמָנָה" (אֵיכָה א, א).
as written in Eichah Rabbah (1:1) on the verse: “she is become like a widow” (Lamentations 1:1)—a widow whose husband is alive afar.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן חָזַר לִהְיוֹת עָרֵל מַמָּשׁ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
And that is: because Adam the First reverted to being literally uncircumcised, as mentioned above;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יִשְׂרָאֵל, גַּם עֲרֵלִים נִקְרָאִים מוּלִים,
in contrast to Israel, where even those physically uncircumcised are still termed circumcised,
וְהֶעָרְלָה הוּא רַק לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן כְּמוֹ בַּמָּשׁוּךְ.
and the uncircumcision is merely to superficial outward appearance, like one with a stretched foreskin.
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דְּ"אָדָם יִרְאֶה לַעֵינַיִם",
And in this world, where “man looks to the eyes,”
נִרְאֶה עָרְלָה וּפְגָם בַּבְּרִית וְנִגְזַר מִיתָה;
there appears foreskin and a blemish in the Covenant, and physical death was decreed;
אֲבָל עַל הָאֱמֶת, "ה' יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב" (שְׁמוּאֵל א טז, ז),
yet in absolute truth, “Hashem looks into the heart” (I Samuel 16:7),
דְּהוּא יִתְבָּרַךְ צוּר לְבָבָם וְחֶלְקָם,
in that He, blessed be He, is the rock of their heart and their portion,
וְכָל הַפְּגָמִים אֵינוֹ מִמַּעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב,
and none of the blemishes originate from the innermost depths of the heart,
רַק מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר הַיּוֹשֵׁב עַל מִפְתְּחֵי הַלֵּב,
rather solely from the evil urge perched at the portals of the heart,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת יז עַמּוּד א):
and as they stated in Berakhot (17a):
"גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ וְכוּלֵי",
“It is revealed and known that our true will is to perform Your will, etc.,”
וְרַק הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה גּוֹרֵם הַכֹּל.
and only the leaven in the dough causes everything.

The direct claim about idolatry serving the permission of arayos is the Sanhedrin teaching quoted next, not merely a deduction from these parallels.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok traces Yaakov’s purity to the labor of the patriarchs and Israel’s renewed life to the giving of the Torah. He distinguishes the later outward blemish and mortality from an innermost will still directed toward God.

p: וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים דְּ"בַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה יְכַפֵּר" (וַיִּקְרָא טז, ל),
And this is the essence of Yom Kippur, that “on this day shall atonement be made,”
שֶׁאָז הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
for then occurs the reawakening of Binah within the heart,
שֶׁהוּא הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אֲכִילָה וְלֹא שְׁתִיָּה,
which is the World to Come wherein there is neither eating nor drinking,
שֶׁאָז "יְבֻקַּשׁ עֲוֺן יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֵינֶנּוּ" (יִרְמְיָה נ, כ).
at which time “the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none” (Jeremiah 50:20).
וְאָז כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And then all Israel possess a portion in the World to Come,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים" (יְשַׁעְיָה ס, כא),
as it is stated: “And your people are all righteous” (Isaiah 60:21),
כִּדִתְנַן [רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק חֵלֶק, סַנְהֶדְרִין צ עַמּוּד א];
as taught in the Mishnah at the beginning of chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 90a);
וְצַדִּיק הַיְינוּ שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית,
and “righteous” (tzaddik) specifically denotes guardian of the Covenant,
וְלֹא הוֹצִיאוּ שָׁם עוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵירָה בִּפְגַם הַבְּרִית מֵחֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
and the Sages did not exclude those who stumbled in blemishes of the Covenant from a portion in the World to Come,
דְּבֶאֱמֶת מִצַּד עֹמֶק הַלֵּב שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה אָז
because in truth, from the perspective of the depth of the heart that will then be revealed,
הֵם כֻּלָּם כֵּן.
they are all fundamentally righteous.
וְכֵן בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת זֶה:
And likewise on Yom Kippur this reality is unveiled:
"וְנָשָׂא הַשָּׂעִיר אֶת עֲוֺנֹתָם [אֶל אֶרֶץ גְּזֵרָה]" (וַיִּקְרָא טז, כב) לַעֲזָאזֵל,
“And the goat shall bear upon him all their iniquities unto a land cut off,” to Azazel,
וְאָמְרוּ [בְּיוֹמָא סז עַמּוּד ב]:
and our Sages stated in Yoma (67b):
לְכַפֵּר עַל מַעֲשֵׂה עוּזָּא וַעֲזָאֵל.
to atone for the deeds of Uzza and Azael.
הֵם גַּם כֵּן "בְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים"
They too were “sons of elohim,”
שֶׁחָטְאוּ וְהֶחֱטִיאוּ בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל
who sinned and caused others to sin in the Generation of the Flood,
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁקִּטְרְגוּ בִּבְרִיאַת אָדָם,
through having challenged the creation of man,
וְהֶרְאָה לָהֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ:
and Hashem showed them:
דְּ"אַל תָּדִין אֶת חֲבֵרְךָ עַד שֶׁתַּגִּיעַ לִמְקוֹמוֹ" (אָבוֹת ב, ד).
“Judge not your fellow until you come into his place” (Avot 2:4).
כִּי הֵם, כְּשֶׁבָּאוּ לָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַגּוּפָנִי,
For they, when they descended into this physical, bodily world,
נַעֲשָׂה מֵהֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע וְכֶתֶר דִּקְלִיפָּה וְסִטְרָא אָחֳרָא;
became the very fountainhead of evil and the crown of the impure shell (Keter de-Klipa) and the Other Side;
וִינִיקַת בִּלְעָם מֵהֶם
and the spiritual nourishment of Balaam derived from them,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בַּזֹּהַר פָּרָשַׁת בָּלָק רח עַמּוּד ב],
as they stated in the Zohar (Parashat Balak 208b),
וְהוּא הַדַּעַת דִּקְלִיפָּה כַּיָּדוּעַ;
and he embodies the Da'at of the impure realm, as is known;
וּמַלְכַּת שְׁבָא שֶׁהִיא הַמַּלְכוּת דִּקְלִיפָּה,
and the Queen of Sheba, who embodies the Malchut of the impure realm,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּתַרְגּוּם אִיּוֹב א, טו] עַל שְׁבָא – לִילִית וְכוּלֵי,
as stated in Targum Iyov (1:15) that Sheba is Lilith, etc.,
בִּקְּשָׁה לַעֲמוֹד עַל הַשָּׂגַת הַדַּעַת דִּקְלִיפָּה דְּבִלְעָם
sought to understand the attainment of the impure Da'at of Balaam,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר [שָׁם קצד עַמּוּד ב],
as recorded in the Zohar (ibid., 194b).
וְאָמַר לָהּ: עַל יְדֵי הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה, עַיֵּין שָׁם,
And he told her: it is achieved through the emission of semen in vain, see there,
הוּא הַיְסוֹד דִּקְלִיפָּה.
which is the Yesod of the impure shell.
וְכֵן הוּא דִּינֵיהּ דְּבִלְעָם בְּגֵיהִנָּם בְּשִׁכְבַת זֶרַע רוֹתַחַת
And likewise is the sentence of Balaam in Gehenna in boiling semen,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּפֶרֶק הַנִּיזָּקִין, גִּיטִּין נז עַמּוּד א],
as stated in chapter HaNizakin (Gittin 57a),
דְּמִשָּׁם שׁוֹרֶשׁ יְנִיקַת הַקְּלִיפָּה שֶׁלּוֹ,
for from there lies the source of the nurture of his impure shell,
מִדּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל דִּבְרוֹתְחִין קִלְקְלוּ
from the Generation of the Flood who transgressed through boiling heat,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יב עַמּוּד א].
as they stated in Rosh Hashanah (12a).
וְהֶרְאָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
And the Holy One, blessed be He, demonstrated
כִּי מֵהֶם (מֵעוּזָּא וַעֲזָאֵל) נִבְנֵית כָּל קוֹמַת הַקְּלִיפָּה
that from them (from Uzza and Azael) was constructed the entire stature of the Klipa
שֶׁמִּשָּׁם הַמְשָׁכַת כָּל שִׁבְעִים אוּמּוֹת שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ רַע גָּמוּר.
whence flows the spiritual vitality of all seventy nations, which is completely unmitigated evil.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּבְנֵי אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ עֵירוּב טוֹב וָרָע,
In contrast to human beings in whom there is an intermingling of good and evil,
אַף דְּיֵשׁ רַע גָּמוּר, יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן טוֹב גָּמוּר,
though there is total evil, there is likewise absolute good,
דְּ"זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, יד),
as “one corresponds to the other,”
וְעַל יְדֵי שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם מְעוֹרָבִים יַחַד.
and through the dominion of man over man they are blended together.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ [בַּחֲגִיגָה טו עַמּוּד א]:
And concerning this they taught in Chagigah (15a):
זָכָה – נוֹטֵל חֶלְקוֹ וְחֵלֶק חֲבֵירוֹ בְּגַן עֵדֶן,
if he is meritorious, he takes his own portion and the portion of his fellow in the Garden of Eden,
וְהַלָּה נוֹטֵל חֵלֶק שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּגֵיהִנָּם;
and that one takes the portion of both of them in Gehenna;
כִּי נִפְרָד הַטּוֹב מִן הָרָע,
for the good is completely separated from the evil,
וְזֶהוּ שִׁבְעִים נֶפֶשׁ דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶגֶד שִׁבְעִים אוּמּוֹת.
and this corresponds to the seventy souls of the children of Israel facing the seventy nations.

Rav Tzadok reads Yom Kippur’s inward disclosure through that future promise.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok describes Yom Kippur as a revelation of Israel’s hidden purity and a separation of good from evil. He connects the scapegoat, the fallen angels, and Bilaam with the return of evil to its root, within this account of the world to come.

p: וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הוּא הַהַפְרָדָה,
And on Yom Kippur this definitive separation takes place,
דְּאַחַר כָּךְ "יַעֲקֹב נָסַע סֻכֹּתָה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לג, יז),
whereby afterward “Jacob journeyed to Sukkot” (Genesis 33:17),
וְנָקַט בַּיָּי"ן בְּיָדוֹ לוֹמַר דְּהוּא נִצַּח [וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ל, ב],
and grasps his palm-branch (lulav) in his hand to proclaim that he has triumphed (Vayikra Rabbah 30:2),
וְשׁוֹלְחִין הָעֲווֹנוֹת לִמְקוֹם שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע,
and they dispatch the sins back to the source-place of evil,
כִּי הַכֹּל מִשָּׁם מֵהַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה,
for everything originates from there, from the leaven in the dough,
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל נִשְׁאֲרוּ נְקִיִּים לְגַמְרֵי כְּמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת.
and Israel remain completely pure like the ministering angels.
וְעַל כֵּן אָז אֵין רְשׁוּת לַשָּׂטָן לְקַטְרֵג
Therefore on that day the Accuser has no permission to prosecute,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּיוֹמָא כ עַמּוּד א],
as they stated in Yoma (20a),
כִּי אָז נִתְגַּלָּה מַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב
because then the deepest depths of the heart are revealed,
דְּהוּא יִתְבָּרַךְ צוּר לְבָבָם וְחֶלְקָם אֱלֹהִים לְעוֹלָם (תְּהִלִּים עג, כו),
for God, blessed be He, is the rock of their heart and their portion forever (Psalms 73:26),
וְשֶׁכָּל הַחֲטָאִים רַק לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and that all sins were merely superficial to the outward sight in this world.
אֲבָל נֶגֶד הִתְגַּלּוּת הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב
However, in the presence of the revelation of Binah in the heart,
אֵין שָׂטָן וְאֵין פֶּגַע רָע,
there is neither adversary nor evil encounter,
וְזֶה הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַמּוּשְׁרָשׁ בְּכָל זַרְעוֹ,
and this is the pristine root of Jacob our father embedded within all his seed,
שֶׁהֵם זֶרַע אֱמֶת שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ לַה' וְאֵין פְּסוֹלֶת וְרַע כְּלָל.
who are a seed of truth, entirely consecrated to Hashem, containing no dross or evil at all.
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתְּשׁוּבָה דְּ"לְבָבוֹ יָבִין וָשָׁב" (יְשַׁעְיָה ו, י),
And this is likewise the root of repentance: “and his heart will understand, and he returns” (Isaiah 6:10),
שֶׁמֵּאִיר מַעֲמַקֵּי הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
which radiates from the depths of Binah within the heart,
וְהוּא הַשָּׂגַת אוֹר עוֹלָם הַבָּא
and this constitutes the perception of the light of the World to Come,
שֶׁהוּא הָעָלְמָא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
which is the concealed supernal realm within this physical world,
וְנִתְגַּלָּה עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמְּשִׁיב כָּל הַדְּבָרִים לְשָׁרְשָׁם.
and is unveiled through repentance, which restores all entities back to their primal source.
וְזֶהוּ "הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִים שֶׁאֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים יְכוֹלִים לַעֲמוֹד" (בִּבְרָכוֹת לד עַמּוּד ב).
And this is “the place where penitents stand, where even the completely righteous cannot stand” (Berakhot 34b).
כִּי צַדִּיק גָּמוּר הוּא הַיְסוֹד עוֹלָם,
For a completely righteous person embodies Yesod of the world,
דְּעַל כֵּן נִבְרָא אָדָם בְּיוֹם שִׁישִּׁי
which is why man was created on the sixth day,
שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת מִדַּת הַיְסוֹד,
which is the manifestation of the sixth attribute, Yesod,
כִּי הוּא הַיְסוֹד שֶׁעָלָיו עוֹמֵד כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ
for he is the foundation upon which the entire cosmos stands,
וְכָל הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁבְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן.
and the whole creation completed across the six days of cosmic structure.
וְאַחַר שֶׁחָטָא וְשָׁב,
And after Adam sinned and repented,
נִיתַּן לוֹ יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
he was granted the Sabbath day, which is likewise a foretaste of the World to Come,
דְּאָז הוּא קִיבּוּל הַתְּשׁוּבָה.
for then occurs the divine reception of repentance.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן "מִזְמוֹר שִׁיר לְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת" (תְּהִלִּים צב, א)
Therefore Adam the First proclaimed “A Psalm, a song for the Sabbath day” (Psalms 92:1)
כְּשֶׁנּוֹדַע לוֹ כֹּחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה
when the transformative power of repentance was made known to him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה כב, יג],
as our Sages stated in Bereishit Rabbah (22:13),
דְּכָל כֹּחָהּ הוּא מִצַּד יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת,
in that its entire efficacy derives from the dimension of the Sabbath day,
דְּ"רָאָה כָל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, לא),
wherein “He saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good” (Genesis 1:31),
דְּגַם הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁהוּא רַע,
in that even the evil urge, which is superficially evil,
הוּא חוֹזֵר לִהְיוֹת "טוֹב מְאֹד" אַחַר הַתְּשׁוּבָה.
returns to become “very good” following repentance.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה "שָׁבַת וַיִּנָּפַשׁ" (שְׁמוֹת לא, יז),
And through this He “ceased from work and was refreshed” (Exodus 31:17),
שֶׁיָּדוּעַ שֶׁהוּא כְּאָדָם הַמִּתְנַפֵּשׁ
which is known to be comparable to a person catching his breath
וּמוֹשֵׁךְ נְשִׁימָתוֹ וְרוּחַ שֶׁבְּאַפָּיו אֵלָיו,
and drawing his breath and the vitality of his nostrils inward back to himself,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עֲלִיַּית הָעוֹלָמוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
this being the cosmic elevation of the worlds on Shabbat,
דְּהוּא גַּם כֵּן הֲשָׁבָה לַמָּקוֹר;
which is likewise a total return to the primal Source;
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים
save that it operates through the dwelling of His Shechinah in the terrestrial realms,
וּ"מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ" (יְשַׁעְיָה ו, ג).
and “the whole earth is full of His glory” (Isaiah 6:3).

paragraphs.text: Shemos 31:17; Rashi ad loc. Rashi directly explains va-yinafash through the person who restores breath after labor, and calls the Divine description language adapted to human hearing. Beitzah 16a separately expounds the additional Shabbos soul and its departure. Machshavos Charutz 10:1 describes completion of the work through the gathering inward of breath and spirit; Resisei Layla 54:2 treats Shabbos’s complete rest in contrast to festivals and human effort. These are the distinct breath, additional-soul and rest strands underlying the ascent-and-return image.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok joins Yom Kippur’s separation of evil with the victory symbolized by Sukkos and the return to the source symbolized by Shabbos. Repentance reveals the deeper heart and transforms what appeared evil into part of the creation’s return to God.

p: וְזֶהוּ יִחוּדָא תַּתָּאָה דְּ"בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד",
And this is the lower unification of “Blessed be the Name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever,”
וְהוּא תְּשׁוּבָה תַּתָּאָה שֶׁזָּכָה לָהּ גַּם אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
and it is the lower repentance that Adam the First likewise merited
עַל יְדֵי הַ"סוּר מֵרָע" לְבַד.
through “turning away from evil” alone
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ [בִּבְרָכוֹת לד עַמּוּד ב]:
And concerning this our Sages said in Berakhot (34b):
כָּל הַנְּבִיאִים לֹא נִתְנַבְּאוּ אֶלָּא לְבַעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה,
all the prophets prophesied only for penitents,
אֲבָל צַדִּיק גָּמוּר – "עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה [אֱלֹהִים זוּלָתְךָ]" (יְשַׁעְיָה סד, ג),
whereas regarding a completely righteous person—“no eye has seen, O God, beside You” (Isaiah 64:3);
וּפְלִיגָא אַדְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
and this disputes the view of Rabbi Abbahu
דְּ"מְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין – אֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים יְכוֹלִים לַעֲמוֹד".
who asserts: “In the place where penitents stand, completely righteous people cannot stand”
וְאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים,
And both these and those are the words of the living God,
וְהַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבִיאִים בְּאַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְאִירָה
and within the prophetic apprehension through the non-luminous looking-glass
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִרְאוֹת אוֹר הַגָּנוּז לַצַּדִּיקִים לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא.
it is impossible to behold the primordial light hidden for the righteous in the time to come
וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְטַעְמֵיהּ שָׁם
And Rabbi Yochanan is consistent with his reasoning there
דְּכָל הַנְּבִיאִים נִתְנַבְּאוּ לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ,
that all the prophets prophesied only concerning the days of the Messiah,
אֲבָל לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא – "עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה",
whereas regarding the World to Come—“no eye has seen”;
דִּלְנָבִיא לְפָנִים יִקָּרֵא "הָרוֹאֶה" (שְׁמוּאֵל א ט, ט),
for the prophet was of old called “the seer” (I Samuel 9:9),
דְּהַשָּׂגָתוֹ עַל יְדֵי עַיִן רוֹאֶה.
since his apprehension occurs through visionary sight
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמַר לִשְׁמוּאֵל רַבָּן שֶׁל נְבִיאִים:
For this reason Hashem said to Samuel, the master of prophets:
"אַל תַּבֵּט [אֶל מַרְאֵהוּ וְאֶל גְּבֹהַּ קוֹמָתוֹ] וְגוֹמֵר,
“Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature, etc.,
כִּי לֹא אֲשֶׁר יִרְאֶה הָאָדָם,
for it is not as man sees,
כִּי הָאָדָם יִרְאֶה לַעֵינַיִם [וַה' יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב]" (שְׁמוּאֵל א טז, ז).
for man looks on the outward eyes, but Hashem looks into the heart” (I Samuel 16:7)
כִּי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא הַגֶּבֶר שֶׁהֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה עִילָּאָה,
For King David, peace be upon him, was the man who raised the yoke of supernal repentance,
שֶׁהוּא מַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב דְּ"לְבָבוֹ יָבִין" (יְשַׁעְיָה ו, י),
which constitutes the deep recesses of the heart of “and his heart will understand” (Isaiah 6:10),
וְזוֹכֶה לְהַשָּׂגַת הַבִּינָה לִבָּא
and one thereby merits the comprehension of Understanding (Binah), the heart,
שֶׁהוּא עָלְמָא עִילָּאָה דְּעַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה,
which is the supernal world that no eye has seen,
דְּאֵין בּוֹ הַשָּׂגָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
wherein there is no conscious grasp in this world
אֶלָּא לְמִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִרְאוֹת עוֹלָמוֹ בְּחַיָּיו,
except for one who merits to see his world in his lifetime,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁכְּבָר תִּיקֵּן הַכֹּל גַּם הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ
meaning that he has already rectified everything, even the deep root of the instigation of the Serpent,
וְזוֹכֶה לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם,
and merits eternal life,
כִּי אֵין מִיתָה בְּלֹא חֵטְא.
for there is no death without sin
וְאַף דְּאִיתּוֹתַב הַךְ מַאן דְּאָמַר [בְּשַׁבָּת נה עַמּוּד ב],
And although that authority was refuted in Shabbat (55b),
הַיְינוּ דְּאֵין צָרִיךְ חֵטְא גָּמוּר בַּפּוֹעַל,
that refutation implies that an overt, actualized sin is not necessary,
וְרַק כָּל שֶׁלֹּא בִּיטֵּל זוּהֲמַת הַיֵּצֶר לְגַמְרֵי
and rather so long as one has not completely neutralized the defilement of the urge,
זֶהוּ עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ דְּמֵתוּ בָּהּ אוֹתָן דְּחָשֵׁיב שָׁם
that constitutes the instigation of the Serpent on account of which died those four righteous individuals enumerated there,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל.
and as I wrote above
וּלְגַבַּיְיהוּ גַּם זֶה נֶחְשָׁב חֵטְא
And relative to their exalted spiritual stature, even this subtle trace is reckoned as a sin,
דְּ"סְבִיבָיו נִשְׂעֲרָה מְאֹד" (תְּהִלִּים נ, ג),
for “round about Him it storms exceedingly” (Psalms 50:3),
וְהַכָּתוּב קְרָאוֹ "בֶּעָווֹן" מָלֵא גַּבֵּי יִשַׁי,
and Scripture spelled it “in iniquity” (be'avon) with a full Vav regarding Jesse (Psalms 51:7),
דִּלְגַבֵּי דִּילֵיהּ נֶחְשָׁב זֶה לְעָוֺן מַה שֶּׁכִּיוֵּון לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ.
since relative to him it was accounted an iniquity that he harbored any intent for personal physical gratification
וּלְגַבֵּי אִמּוֹ
And relative to David's mother,
דְּמִסְּתָמָא הָיְתָה גַּם כֵּן צַדֶּקֶת גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁזָּכְתָה לְבֵן כָּזֶה
who was presumably likewise an illustrious righteous woman to have merited such a son,
נֶחְשָׁב לְחֵטְא,
it was reckoned merely as a light sin (chet),
וְלוֹ שֶׁהָיָה גָּדוֹל יוֹתֵר נֶחְשָׁב לְעָוֺן,
whereas to Jesse who was of even greater stature it was reckoned as an iniquity (avon),
וְנוֹסַף הַוָּא"ו.
and the letter Vav was added
וְיָדוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִיזַ"ל
And it is known from the holy Ari
שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנּוֹסַף אוֹת מֵאוֹתִיּוֹת שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה
that wherever an additional letter of the Tetragrammaton is appended,
מוֹרֶה תּוֹסֶפֶת קְדוּשָּׁה וְדִבּוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
it denotes an accession of holiness and intimate cleaving unto Hashem, blessed be He,
וְשֶׁמֵּאִתּוֹ יָצְאוּ כְבוּשִׁים,
and that from Him emerged hidden divine schemes,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא [בְּסוֹף מַכּוֹת כג עַמּוּד ב] בִּיהוּדָה וְתָמָר
along the lines of what is taught at the end of Makkot (23b) regarding Judah and Tamar,
[וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פה, ח]
and in Bereishit Rabbah (85:8)
דְּרָצָה לֵילֵךְ, וְרָמַז הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַמַּלְאָךְ הַמְמוּנֶּה עַל הַתַּאֲוָה וְכוּלֵי.
that Judah wished to pass by, but the Holy One signaled to the angel appointed over desire, etc.
וְהָיָה דּוֹמֶה שֶׁעָשָׂה עֲבֵירָה וּבָעַל קְדֵשָׁה,
And it outwardly seemed as though he committed a transgression and cohabited with a harlot,
וְעַל כֵּן תְּחִלָּה רָצָה לֵילֵךְ
and therefore he initially wanted to walk away
כִּי יִצְרוֹ הָיָה מָסוּר בְּיָדוֹ,
because his inclination was under his control,
וְלֹא הָיָה רָאוּי לְאוֹתָהּ מַעֲשֶׂה אִלּוּ הָיָה עֲבֵירָה.
and he would never have stooped to that deed had it truly been an autonomous sin
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הָיָה עָסוּק לִבְרוֹא אוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ,
Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, was actively engaged in bringing forth the light of the Messiah,
שֶׁהוּא מִתְגַּלֶּה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which is revealed within this world
עַל יְדֵי הַהֶסְתֵּר וְהֶעְלֵם הַקּוֹדֵם
specifically by means of the antecedent concealment and obscurity
בְּכָל יְמֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַדּוֹמֶה לְלַיְלָה,
throughout all the days of this world which resembles the night,
שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ חֹשֶׁךְ וְהֶעְדֵּר אוֹר
which is entirely darkness and absence of light
מֵרוֹב הִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכוּת.
from the profound immersion caused by the leaven in the dough and the subjugation of kingdoms
וּבְקַדְרוּת דְּצַפְרָא גּוֹבֵר הַחֹשֶׁךְ יוֹתֵר,
And during the darkest gloom just before the dawn, the darkness intensifies all the more,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּעִקְּבָתָא דִּמְשִׁיחָא,
as our Sages of blessed memory noted regarding the final footsteps of the Messiah,
וּמִשָּׁם דַּיְיקָא "יְקַבֶּצְךָ [ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ] וּמִשָּׁם יִקָּחֶךָ" (דְּבָרִים ל, ד).
and precisely from there “Hashem your God will gather you, and from there He will take you” (Deuteronomy 30:4)
כִּי אוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מַעְלָה הוּא אוֹר הַמֵּאִיר גַּם בְּתוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ
For the supernal light is an illumination that shines even within the heart of darkness
וּמְבָרֵר דִּ"לְכָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה אוֹר בְּמוֹשְׁבֹתָם" (שְׁמוֹת י, כג) גַּם בִּימֵי הַחֹשֶׁךְ,
and clarifies that “for all the children of Israel there was light in their dwellings” (Exodus 10:23) even amidst the epochs of gloom,
דְּ"כִּי אֵשֵׁב בַּחֹשֶׁךְ ה' אוֹר לִי" (מִיכָה ז, ח),
for “though I sit in darkness, Hashem is a light unto me” (Micah 7:8),
וְ"גַם כִּי אֵלֵךְ [בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא רָע] כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי" (תְּהִלִּים כג, ד).
and “yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me” (Psalms 23:4)
דְּכָל הַחֲטָאִים יִהְיוּ כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית,
For all sins will be like these years that have been ordered and come since the six days of Creation,
הַיְינוּ דְּהַכֹּל מְסוּדָּר מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁרָצָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֵּן
meaning that everything was orchestrated by Hashem, blessed be He, Who willed that it be so,
וּמִמֶּנּוּ יָצְאוּ כְבוּשִׁים.
and from Him emerged these inscrutable workings
אֶלָּא שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא עוֹלַם הַבְּחִירָה
Except that in this world, which is the theater of free choice,
דָּבָר זֶה הוּא כִּבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא,
this mystery constitutes the hidden secrets of the Merciful One,
שֶׁהוּא טָמִיר וְנֶעְלָם אֵיךְ הַכֹּל מִידִיעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
being concealed and veiled as to how all coexists within the divine foreknowledge of Hashem,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ קוּשְׁיַת הַיְדִיעָה וְהַבְּחִירָה שֶׁכָּתַב רַמְבַּ״ם
which is the classic paradox of Foreknowledge and Free Will regarding which Maimonides wrote
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג יְדִיעָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
that mortal mind cannot comprehend His infinite knowledge,
וּדְבָרָיו חַיִּים וְקַיָּימִים שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲמוֹד עַל זֶה אֵיךְ יִכּוֹנוּ יַחְדָּו.
and his words are living and enduring, for in this world it is impossible to fathom how they align together

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 56a:7–8 relates that Yaakov’s sons told him: “Just as there is only One in your heart, so there is only One in our hearts.” Yaakov then answered, “Blessed be the name of the glory of His kingship forever and ever.” The Gemara next explains the quiet recitation of this response.

Nevertheless: “We know without doubt that a person’s action is in that person’s hands, and the Holy One does not draw him or decree upon him to do thus.” The uncertainty concerns the manner of divine knowing, not the fact of human responsibility.

paragraphs.text: Dover Tzedek adds an exceptional qualification: the unity is not understood by ordinary intellect on its own, but can be attained when Hashem grants an understanding and feeling heart, at the rare level it describes as yechidah. This is not identical to an unqualified claim that no form of attainment is ever possible. Its simultaneous insistence on one’s created place and choice must remain.
