inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok distinguishes lower repentance from the deeper return associated with the hidden heart and the world to come. Through David’s lineage and Yehudah’s encounter with Tamar, he explores divine purpose concealed within darkness, while maintaining that the relation between divine foreknowledge and human choice remains beyond present understanding.

p: וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ [בִּבְרָכוֹת י סוֹף עַמּוּד א] בְּחִזְקִיָּה
And therefore our Sages taught in Berakhot (10a) regarding King Hezekiah
דַּחֲזָא בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ דְּיִהְיוּ לוֹ בְּנִין דְּלָא מַעֲלוּ:
who foresaw by the Holy Spirit that he would father unworthy children:
"בַּהֲדֵי כִּבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא לָמָּה לָךְ?".
“Why do you meddle in the hidden secrets of the Merciful One?”
דְּמֵאַחַר שֶׁרוֹאֶה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ מִקּוֹדֶם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֵּן,
For since he foresees via the Holy Spirit beforehand that it must be so,
אִם כֵּן הַדָּבָר מְסוּדָּר כֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְאֵינוֹ בִּבְחִירָה.
if so, the outcome is orchestrated by Hashem and transcends human choice
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגַּם זֶה אֱמֶת דְּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַבְּחִירָה בְּיַד אָדָם,
And even though it is equally true that in this world free choice is deposited in human hands,
וְעַל כֵּן הָרְשָׁעִים נִידּוֹנִים עַל חֶטְאָם,
and therefore the wicked are judged for their sins,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, מַה שֶּׁהוּא מַשִּׂיג מִצַּד הַיְדִיעָה
nevertheless, what one apprehends from the perspective of divine foreknowledge,
אִם הַיְדִיעָה אֱמֶת, אֵיךְ נֶחְשָׁב לְחֵטְא,
if that foreknowledge is infallible truth, how could it be reckoned as autonomous sin?
אַף שֶׁפְּשַׁט הַדָּבָר נֶעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּ"בַּהֲדֵי כִּבְשֵׁי וְכוּלֵי".
even though the resolution of the matter remains hidden in this world behind “meddling in divine secrets, etc.”
וּמָשִׁיחַ שֶׁיֵּצֵא מֵחֲלָצָיו,
And the Messiah who will emerge from his loins,
הוּא יְגַלֶּה וְיָאִיר אוֹר הַשָּׂגָה זוֹ וְכִבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא הַלָּלוּ
he will reveal and radiate the light of this perception and these divine secrets,
אֵיךְ הַכֹּל מְסוּדָּר מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית.
clarifying how all was prearranged from the six days of Creation.
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרָא יֵצֶר הָרָע וּבָרָא רְשָׁעִים,
For Hashem, blessed be He, created the evil urge and created the wicked,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל יְמֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַבְּחִירָה בִּידֵי אָדָם,
and nevertheless throughout all the epochs of this world choice is in human hands,
וְדָבָר זֶה סָתוּם וְנֶעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and this paradox remains sealed and concealed in this world.
וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר: "מָצָאתִי דָּוִד עַבְדִּי" (תְּהִלִּים פט, כא),
And therefore Scripture declares: “I have found David My servant” (Psalms 89:21),
כִּי הֲקָמַת עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה דְּדָוִד
for the raising of the yoke of repentance by David,
שֶׁזָּכָה לִהְיוֹת חַי וְקַיָּם עַל יְדֵי תִּיקּוּן כָּל הַחַשְׁכוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
who merited to be living and enduring through the rectification of all darkness of this world,
אוֹר זֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא אָבוּד מִכָּל אָדָם
this illumination in this world is lost to all men
וְאֵינוֹ מִתְגַּלֶּה אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ מְצִיאָה.
and is never discovered except by way of an unexpected find (metzi'ah).
וְאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה מא, ה]:
And our Sages expounded in Bereishit Rabbah (41:5):
הֵיכָן מְצָאתִיו? בִּסְדוֹם,
Where did I find him? In Sodom,
דִּכְתִיב (בְּרֵאשִׁית יט, טו): "בְּנֹתֶיךָ הַנִּמְצָאֹת",
as it is written: “your daughters who are found” (Genesis 19:15),
וְאֵין לְךָ בְּנֵי אָדָם גְּרוּעִים בְּשִׁיקּוּעַ בְּכָל מִינֵי תַּאֲווֹת גּוּפָנִיּוֹת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּאַנְשֵׁי סְדוֹם,
and you have no human beings as vilely sunk into all bodily lusts of this world as the men of Sodom,
וְלוֹט בִּשְׁבִיל כֵּן נִתְחַבֵּר עִמָּהֶם.
and Lot deliberately associated with them on that account.
וְאֵין לְךָ מְגוּנֶּה מֵהַבִּיאָה עַל בְּנוֹתָיו
And you have nothing as repugnant as incestuous cohabitation with one's daughters,
שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַשִּׁיקּוּעַ בַּתַּאֲווֹת,
which is the absolute extremity of immersion in lust,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה נא, יא]:
and as they stated in Bereishit Rabbah (51:11):
מִי שֶׁלָּהוּט אַחַר בּוּלְמוּס שֶׁל עֲרָיוֹת,
whoever is consumed by a ravenous craving for forbidden relations,
סוֹף מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ מִבְּשָׂרוֹ.
is ultimately made to consume of his own flesh.
וּלְשׁוֹן "בּוּלְמוּס" הַיְינוּ תּוֹקֶף תַּאֲוָה הַנּוֹגֵעַ עַד חַיּוּתוֹ מַמָּשׁ,
And the term bulmus denotes an uncontrollable craving that touches one's vital life-force,
כְּעִנְיַן "אֲחָזוֹ בּוּלְמוּס" דְּיוֹמָא (פג עַמּוּד א).
similar to the case of “one seized by a ravenous hunger” in Yoma (83a).
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵן כִּוְּונוּ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּנָזִיר כג עַמּוּד א],
However, they intended for the sake of Heaven, as stated in Nazir 23a,
וְעַל כֵּן נְקֵבוֹתֵיהֶם מוּתָּרוֹת
and therefore their female descendants are permitted to marry into Israel,
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ [בְּבָבָא קַמָּא לח עַמּוּד ב]:
and likewise they stated in Bava Kamma (38b):
בְּכִירָה שֶׁקָּדְמָה לִדְבַר מִצְוָה וְכוּלֵי.
the elder daughter who preceded for the purpose of a mitzvah, etc.
וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ אָמְרוּ: בְּכִירָה שֶׁפָּתְחָה בִּזְנוּת פִּרְסְמָהּ הַכָּתוּב,
Yet in the Midrash they said: the elder daughter who initiated the promiscuity was explicitly exposed by Scripture,
וְכֵן בְּרַשִׁ״י [פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּרָא] וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה [סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה נא] פְּלִיגֵי אָמוֹרָאֵי בָּזֶה.
and likewise in Rashi [Parashas Vayeira]; in Bereishis Rabbah [end of section 51] the Amoraim dispute this.
וּבְוַדַּאי כָּל דִּבְרֵיהֶם אֱמֶת,
And certainly all their words are truth,
דִּלְהַיוֹתָן בְּנוֹת לוֹט מִסְּתָמָא הָיוּ מְשׁוּקָּעוֹת בַּתַּאֲווֹת גַּם כֵּן,
for being the daughters of Lot they were naturally tainted by immersion in lusts as well,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם כָּאן מְפוֹרָשׁ בַּכָּתוּב כַּוָּונָתָם לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם גַּם כֵּן,
yet nevertheless here it is explicit in Scripture that their intention was also for Heaven,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "וּנְחַיֶּה מֵאָבִינוּ זָרַע" (בְּרֵאשִׁית יט, לב),
in that they said: “that we may preserve seed of our father” (Genesis 19:32),
שֶׁכִּוְּונוּ לְקִיּוּם עוֹלָם;
having intended for the survival of the human race;
וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה שָׁם אָמְרוּ:
and in Bereishit Rabbah there they expounded:
"זֶרַע הַבָּא מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר – זֶה מָשִׁיחַ", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
“‘seed that comes from another place’—this refers to the Messiah,” see there.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 10a:28–30 reports that Chizkiyahu refrained from procreation because he foresaw unworthy descendants. Yeshayahu answers: “What have you to do with the hidden matters of the Merciful One? What you were commanded, you must do; and what is pleasing before the Holy One, let Him do.”

paragraphs.text: Chizkiyahu then proposes marriage to Yeshayahu’s daughter, hoping their combined merit will produce worthy children. The source’s practical answer is complete before Rav Tzadok proceeds to ask how true foreknowledge and present choice coexist.

paragraphs.text: Cf. Nefesh HaChaim I:22, which cites Chizkiyahu’s case and Yeshayahu’s answer. It asks: “How could the matter be entrusted to a person’s understanding, to change their laws and the order of their times according to the breadth of his knowledge and attainment?” The subject is the binding practical details of Torah, even for a person with lofty insight.

paragraphs.text: The chapter separately recognizes the Torah-authorized temporary instruction of a prophet, such as Eliyahu at Carmel, with its stated limits; it does not authorize a private or permanent rewriting of a command. This is a comparison concerning commanded conduct. It neither supplies a solution to Rav Tzadok’s metaphysical question nor establishes that the two authors formulate all aspects of that question identically.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 94a:4–5: “The Holy One sought to make Chizkiyahu Mashiach and Sancheriv Gog and Magog.” The attribute of judgment objects that David, who offered songs and praises, was not made Mashiach, whereas Chizkiyahu did not offer song for his miracles. The possibility was not realized in that account.

paragraphs.text: Dover Tzedek, Likkutim 4:120, introduces the comparison: “This was revealed to Chizkiyahu, whom the Holy One wished to make Mashiach,” explaining that he too was at the level expressed by “I will sleep upon my bed, and You...” It explains his effort as seeking not to need effort, so that even sleep would be good. The same paragraph then describes the attempted clarification through the Babylonian envoys and its failure. The messianic possibility and its failure remain distinct; the account does not dispense with the duty to perform the commanded act.

paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 16a:12–13 attributes “You created righteous people; You created wicked people” to Iyov’s attempt to exempt the world from judgment. His friends answer that Hashem created the evil inclination and created Torah as its antidote. The attempted exemption is not the accepted answer of the discussion.

paragraphs.text: Cf. Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 5:1: “Permission is given to every person.” 5:2 expressly rejects a decree at creation that a person must be righteous or wicked: “The Creator does not decree upon a person to be good or to be evil.” 5:5 preserves both divine knowledge and responsibility while denying our comprehension of the manner of that knowledge. The Rambam expressly says that He, blessed be His name, and His knowledge are one, unlike a human knower and that person’s knowledge.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 51:8: וַתֹּאמֶר הַבְּכִירָה אֶל הַצְּעִירָה אָבִינוּ זָקֵן וגו' (בראשית יט, לא), שֶׁהָיוּ סְבוּרוֹת שֶׁנִּתְכַּלָּה הָעוֹלָם כְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל. (בראשית יט, לב): לְכָה נַשְׁקֶה אֶת אָבִינוּ יַיִן וגו', רַבִּי תַּנְחוּמָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל (בראשית יט, לב): וּנְחַיֶּה מֵאָבִינוּ זָרַע, וּנְחַיֶּה מֵאָבִינוּ בֵּן אֵין כְּתִיב כָּאן אֶלָּא וּנְחַיֶּה מֵאָבִינוּ זָרַע, אוֹתוֹ זֶרַע שֶׁהוּא בָּא מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר, וְאֵי זֶה זֶה מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ. — “The elder said to the younger: Our father is old”: they thought that the world had been destroyed as in the generation of the Flood. “Come, let us make our father drink wine”: Rabbi Tanchuma said in the name of Rabbi Shmuel: “Let us preserve seed from our father”—it does not say here, “Let us preserve a son from our father,” but “Let us preserve seed from our father”: that seed which comes from another place. What is it? The King Mashiach”. Genesis 19:32 gives the verse. The passage is 51:8 in the consulted electronic division. R’ Tzadok develops the Midrash’s messianic seed into his account of the holy intention within the mixed deed.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The warning to Chizkiyahu to leave divine secrets to God preserves human responsibility despite foreknown outcomes. Rav Tzadok then reads the emergence of David from Lot’s daughters through their mixed motives: desire accompanied a purpose for Heaven, refined over generations into the messianic line.

p: וְנִרְאֶה לִי לְפִי שֶׁהוּא קִיּוּם כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ,
And it appears to me that this is because he embodies the sustenance of the entire world,
שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִילוֹ
for the whole universe was created solely for his sake,
שֶׁיָּבוֹא וִיתַקֵּן הַכֹּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בִּתְחִלַּת הַבְּרִיאָה.
that he come and rectify everything to be as it was at the dawn of Creation.
וְכַוָּונָתָם לְקִיּוּם כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ עַל יָדָן אַחַר שֶׁנֶּחֱרַב,
And their intention was the preservation of the entire world through them after it was destroyed,
שֶׁהָיוּ סְבוּרוֹת שֶׁכָּל הַהַשְׁאָרָה מֵהֶם,
assuming that all surviving humanity was confined to them,
הֲרֵי בָּאוּ לְתַקֵּן כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ אַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל.
so that they sought to restore the entire world after ruin.
וְתִיקּוּן הָעוֹלָם הוּא עַל יְדֵי מָשִׁיחַ,
And the ultimate rectification of the world is through the Messiah,
וּבִשְׁבִיל חֶשְׁקָם זֶה שֶׁהָיָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם זָכוּ לְכָךְ בֶּאֱמֶת,
and on account of this yearning which was for the sake of Heaven they merited this in truth,
לִהְיוֹת אוֹתוֹ זֶרַע מֵהֶם
that that messianic seed emerge from them
אַחַר זִיכּוּךְ הַרְבֵּה דּוֹרוֹת מִפְּסוֹלֶת הַכַּוָּונָה דִּזְנוּת שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם גַּם כֵּן.
after many generations of refinement from the dross of the lustful intent they also harbored
וְכָל הִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת נֶפֶשׁ דְּמָשִׁיחַ בָּעוֹלָם הָיָה עַל יְדֵי עִנְיָנִים כָּאֵלּוּ,
And the entire descent of the soul of the Messiah into the world unfolded through such paradoxical circumstances,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מַחֲשֶׁבֶת תַּאֲוָה, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם,
wherein there is a thought of lust, yet it is simultaneously for the sake of Heaven,
וְזֶה יְבָרֵר מָשִׁיחַ בְּכָל תַּאֲווֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל דְּהַכֹּל מְסוּדָּר מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and this the Messiah will clarify regarding all desires of Israel: that all was orchestrated from Creation by Hashem.
וְזֶהוּ בְּרִיאַת אוֹרוֹ בְּמַעֲשֶׂה דִּיהוּדָה
And this was the creation of his illumination in the incident of Judah
שֶׁהָיָה עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת תַּאֲוָה גּוּפָנִית וְלֹא בְּכַוָּנָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם,
which occurred through the awakening of bodily lust and not with conscious holy intent,
דַּהֲרֵי רָמַז לַמַּלְאָךְ דְּתַאֲוָה.
for behold Hashem signaled to the angel of desire.
אֲבָל גַּם הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַתַּאֲוָה לֹא הָיָה מִצִּידּוֹ,
Yet even that awakening of desire was not of Judah's own making,
רַק מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דְּעוֹרֵר בּוֹ כֹּחַ תַּאֲוָה הַגּוּפָנִית בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה,
rather from Hashem Who stirred within him physical lust at that hour,
וּלְבָרֵר בָּזֶה שֶׁכָּל תַּאֲווֹת גּוּפָנִיּוֹת דְּזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל הַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא רָצָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֵּן.
to demonstrate that all bodily lusts of the seed of Israel are guided by Hashem Who willed it to be so.
וְכֵן בְּיִשַׁי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
And so with Jesse our Sages of blessed memory noted
שֶׁפֵּירַשׁ מֵאִשְׁתּוֹ וְרָצָה לָבוֹא עַל שִׁפְחָתוֹ,
that he separated from his wife and sought to consort with his maidservant,
וּפֵירֵשׁ הָרַמַ״ע בַּ"עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת" לְטַהֵר זַרְעוֹ.
and the Rama of Fano explained in Asarah Ma'amarot that it was to purify his lineage.
וּמִסְּתָמָא לֹא הָיָה דָּוִד "בֶּן תְּמוּרָה" חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
And presumably David was not a child conceived through mistaken identity, Heaven forbid,
וּכְדִבְאַתָה אִשְׁתּוֹ בִּמְקוֹמָהּ בִּשְׁעַת הֶרְגֵּל דָּבָר מִסְּתָמָא הִגִּידָה לוֹ הָאֱמֶת,
and when his wife came in her stead at the moment of intimacy she presumably told him the truth,
כִּי הִיא צַדֶּקֶת וְכַוָּונָתָהּ לַשָּׁמַיִם לְהָקִים הַזֶּרַע שֶׁנִּתְכַּוְּונוּ לוֹ בְּנוֹת לוֹט כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
for she was righteous and intended for Heaven to raise the seed intended by Lot's daughters as noted above,
וּבְוַדַּאי דְּלֹא רָצְתָה דְּיִהְיֶה דַּעְתּוֹ לְאַחֶרֶת.
and she certainly did not want his thoughts directed toward another woman.
וְלִהְיוֹת הוּא צַדִּיק גָּמוּר,
And since Jesse was completely righteous,
וְחָשַׁב אָז אוּלַי הַהֲלָכָה דְּגַם עַמּוֹנִית אֲסוּרָה
and reasoned then that perhaps the halakhah forbids even an Ammonite woman,
וְלֹא רָצָה לְהוֹלִיד עוֹד מִיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית כְּדִבְרֵי הָרַמַ״ע,
and did not want to father further children from an Israelite woman as the Rama writes,
וַדַּאי שֶׁהָיָה רוֹצֶה לִפְרוֹשׁ מִמֶּנָּה.
he surely would have wanted to separate from her.
וּבְוַדַּאי גַּם אָז רָמַז הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַמַּלְאָךְ דְּתַאֲוָה מַה שֶּׁלֹּא פֵּירַשׁ,
And certainly then too the Holy One signaled to the angel of desire, so that he did not separate,
וְזֶהוּ "בֶּעָוֺן" מָלֵא,
and this is the esoteric meaning of “in iniquity” (be'avon) spelled fully with a Vav,
דְּעַל יְדֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּא לוֹ הַתַּאֲוָה לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ אָז,
in that through the Holy One came upon him the desire for physical pleasure then,
דְּכָךְ רָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ כַּוָּנָה לַהֲנָאָתוֹ.
for Hashem so willed that he harbor intent for his pleasure.
וּבֶאֱמֶת גַּם זֶה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And in truth this too was from Hashem,

to extract such a precious soul specifically from such an intention, and to clarify as noted above

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok explores the hidden divine purpose in the difficult beginnings of the messianic line. His readings of Yehudah and Yishai distinguish their apparent human motives from a providential meaning he expects Mashiach ultimately to reveal.

p: וְעַל כֵּן הִזְכִּיר זֶה דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּתְשׁוּבָתוֹ אַמַּעֲשֶׂה דְּבַת שֶׁבַע,
And therefore King David, peace be upon him, mentioned this in his repentance over Bathsheba,
דְּגַם הוּא לֹא הָיָה רָאוּי לְאוֹתָהּ מַעֲשֶׂה,
for he too was not personally susceptible to that deed,
רַק מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיָה לוֹ זֶה שֶׁיִּכָּשֵׁל לְהוֹרוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה.
rather it was brought upon him by Hashem that he stumble in order to teach the path of repentance.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר דְּ"הֵן בְּעָווֹן חוֹלָלְתִּי" (תְּהִלִּים נא, ז) גַּם כֵּן מַמָּשׁ דּוּגְמַת זֶה,
And therefore he declared that “Behold, I was shaped in iniquity” was likewise literally parallel to this,
דְּלֹא הָיָה יִשַׁי רָאוּי לְכָךְ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
for Jesse was not naturally predisposed to this as mentioned above,
דְּהָיָה מְנוּקֶּה בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם מֵהֶרְגֵּשׁ הֲנָאָה כְּלָל,
having been truly cleansed of any sensation of selfish pleasure,
רַק בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה רָצָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַכְנִיס בּוֹ תַּאֲוָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
only that at that hour the Holy One willed to inject lust into him as noted above.
וְזֶהוּ הִתְנַצְּלוּת גַּם כֵּן עַל חֶטְאוֹ דְּדָוִד,
And this serves as the inner defense also for the sin of David,
דְּהוּא גַּם כֵּן כֵּן,
for his case was likewise identical,
דִּכְבָר הֲרָגוֹ לַיֵּצֶר הָרָע בְּתַעֲנִית וְלֹא הָיָה בּוֹ הֶרְגֵּשׁ הֲנָאָה,
having already slain the evil inclination through fasting without experiencing bodily lust,
רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה לְנַסּוֹתוֹ וְהִכְנִיס בְּלִבּוֹ תַּאֲוָה,
only that Hashem willed to test him and placed desire into his heart,
וּכְדֵי לְתַקֵּן אַחַר כָּךְ בִּתְשׁוּבָה וּלְהוֹרוֹת לְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ.
and so that he rectify it afterward through repentance and instruct the entire world.
וְזָכָה לִהְיוֹת "דָּוִד מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל חַי וְקַיָּם" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כה עַמּוּד א],
And he merited to become “David, King of Israel, lives and endures,” as they stated in Rosh Hashanah (25a),
שֶׁלָּזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִזְכּוֹת
which is impossible to merit
אֶלָּא צַדִּיק גָּמוּר כְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְאֵלִיָּהוּ וְכַדּוֹמֶה,
except for a completely righteous person like Jacob our father, peace be upon him, and Elijah and the like,
אוֹ בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה גָּמוּר כְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁתִּיקֵּן גַּם הָעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ,
or an absolute master of repentance like King David who rectified even the instigation of the Serpent,
אַף שֶׁהָיָה עָלָיו טַעֲנָה מִפְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
even though there was a claim against him regarding a blemish of the Covenant,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר: "וְהָרַע בְּעֵינֶיךָ עָשִׂיתִי" (תְּהִלִּים נא, ו),
and as he said: “and done that which is evil in Your sight” (Psalms 51:6),
דְּזֶה נִקְרָא "רַע" בְּעֵינָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ.
for this specific blemish is designated as “evil” in His eyes, blessed be He.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר: "לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא וְכוּלֵי" (שָׁם פָּסוּק יב),
And therefore he pleaded: “Create in me a clean heart, etc.” (ibid. v. 12),
כִּי מִי שֶׁפָּגַם בְּחֵטְא בַּפּוֹעַל
for one who blemished through sin in actual deed
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְתַקֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתַּאֲוָה לְגַמְרֵי,
is unable to rectify the root of lust entirely
שֶׁיֶּאֱחוֹז בְּעֵץ הַחַיִּים לְתַקֵּן גַּם עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ,
so as to lay hold of the Tree of Life and rectify the Serpent's instigation as well,
אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה דַּחֲזְיָא לְחַפְיָא עַל כָּל עוֹבָדוֹי.
except through that consummate repentance that is fit to cover over all his deeds.
הַיְינוּ כְּעֵין תְּשׁוּבַת רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן דּוּרְדְיָא [בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יז עַמּוּד א] שֶׁיָּצְתָה נַפְשׁוֹ מִתּוֹךְ מְרִירוּת לִבּוֹ.
Namely, akin to the repentance of Rabbi Elazar ben Dordia in Avodah Zarah (17a), whose soul departed in the bitter agony of his contrite heart.
וְכֵן מִי שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לָזֶה עַל יְדֵי תּוֹקֶף הָאַהֲבָה כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
And likewise one who reaches this through the sheer intensity of love, like Israel at the Giving of the Torah as noted above.
וְכֵן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגַת אַהֲבָה זוֹ עַד כְּלוֹת הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
And so too King David, peace be upon him, reached this degree of love unto the expiration of the soul,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר: "כָּלְתָה נַפְשִׁי" וְגוֹ׳ (תְּהִלִּים פד, ג).
as he said: “My soul yearns unto expiration,” etc. (Psalms 84:3).
וְנֶאֱמַר: "אֵלֶיךָ ה' נַפְשִׁי אֶשָּׂא" (שָׁם כה, א),
And it is stated: “Unto You, Hashem, do I lift up my soul” (ibid. 25:1),
דִּמְסַר גַּרְמֵיהּ לְמִיתָה מַמָּשׁ
in that he literally yielded himself unto death
עַל יְדֵי דְּבֵיקוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ בִּמְקוֹרָהּ בְּחֵי הַחַיִּים יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ,
through the soul's clinging to its fountainhead in the Life of all life, blessed be His Name,
רַק שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חוֹזֵר לְהַחֲיוֹתוֹ כִּבְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
save that Hashem restored him to life as at the Giving of the Torah,
וְיוּכַל לְהַחֲזִיר לוֹ לֵב טָהוֹר,
and was able to restore to him a clean heart,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה לְסִילּוּק הַזּוּהֲמָא דְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ לְגַמְרֵי.
and through this he merited the total removal of the defilement of the Serpent's instigation completely.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 51:7: “Behold, in iniquity I was formed, and in sin my mother conceived me.” Rashi, ad loc. gives an account of formation through bodily union and an alternative involving male and female who are subject to sin. He also expressly says that there are midrashic readings that do not fit the speaker’s context in this psalm; he does not identify all of their referents here.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: David’s repentance and prayer for a newly created clean heart illustrate, for Rav Tzadok, a return reaching the root of life itself. He compares David’s profound contrition and love with repentance that releases the soul from its former condition and with the renewed life granted at Sinai.

p: וְהֵם בְּנֵי עֲלִיָּה הַמּוּעָטִים שֶׁרָאָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחָאי,
And these are the few sons of ascension whom Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai beheld,
וּרְאִיָּתוֹ וְהַשָּׂגָתוֹ הָיְתָה בְּהַשָּׂגַת הַחָכְמָה דְּעָדִיף מִנְּבוּאָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא יב עַמּוּד א].
and his vision and perception were through the grasp of wisdom, which is superior to prophecy as they said in Bava Batra (12a).
כִּי אֵינוֹ נִקְרָא רְאִיַּת הָעַיִן כִּדְנְבִיאִים,
For it is not titled visual sight as with prophets,
רַק רְאִיַּת הַשֵּׂכֶל,
rather intellectual and spiritual perception,
וּבַשֵּׂכֶל אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג מִי שֶׁרָאוּי לְכָךְ
and through intellect it is possible for one worthy of it to apprehend
גַּם מַה שֶּׁעַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל.
even that which no eye has seen in this world at all.
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא רָאָה מַדְרֵגַת בְּנֵי עֲלִיָּה,
Therefore he beheld the lofty level of the sons of ascension,
אֲבָל הַנְּבִיאִים לֹא רָאוּ בִּנְבוּאָתָם מַדְרֵגַת הַצַּדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים,
whereas the prophets in their prophetic visions did not perceive the level of completely righteous individuals,
הַיְינוּ כְּאֵלִיָּהוּ שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שׁוּם שֶׁמֶץ חֵטְא אֲפִילּוּ מֵעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ,
namely like Elijah in whom there was no trace of sin, not even from the Serpent's instigation,
דְּגַם כֵּן נִקְרָא עָוֺן לְגַבֵּי צַדִּיק גָּמוּר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
which is likewise designated as an iniquity relative to a complete tzaddik, as mentioned above.
וְכָל שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ, עָלָיו נֶאֱמַר: "אֵין אָדָם צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ וְגוֹמֵר" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כ),
And whoever has not attained this pinnacle, concerning him it is said: “there is no righteous man upon the earth, etc.” (Ecclesiastes 7:20),
הַיְינוּ מִי שֶׁהוּא עֲדַיִן שָׁקוּעַ בְּאַרְצִיּוּת וְהֶרְגֵּשׁ הֲנָאוֹת גּוּפָנִיּוֹת
meaning one who is still embedded in earthliness and the sensation of physical pleasures;
אַף שֶׁהוּא צַדִּיק בַּפּוֹעַל וְעוֹשֶׂה טוֹב,
even though he is practically righteous and does good,
אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יֶחֱטָא בְּאֵיזֶה דָבָר מַה,
it is impossible that he not stumble in some slight matter,
אֶלָּא שֶׁשָּׁב וּמִתְחָרֵט מִיָּד וְהוּא בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה,
except that he immediately returns and regrets, being a ba'al teshuva,
וּמִמַּדְרֵגָתָם דִּבְּרוּ נְבִיאִים בְּהַשָּׂגָתָם מִמַּרְאוֹת הַנְּבוּאָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and of their level did the prophets speak in their vision through prophetic sight in this world.
וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן שֶׁהָיָה צַדִּיק גָּמוּר שֶׁלֹּא פָּגַם בַּבְּרִית מֵעוֹלָם,
And Rabbi Yochanan who was a complete tzaddik who never in his life blemished the Covenant,
כִּי הָיָה מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרָכוֹת כ עַמּוּד א],
for he was from the seed of Joseph as our Sages stated in Berakhot (20a),
וְלֹא יָדַע מִמַּדְרֵגַת בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה עִילָּאָה דַּחֲזְיָא לְחַפְיָא וְכוּלֵי,
and did not partake of the experience of the supreme ba'al teshuva that is fit to cover all sins, etc.,
שֶׁיּוּכַל לְתַקֵּן גַּם פְּגַם הַבְּרִית לְגַמְרֵי אַחַר הַחֵטְא
who is able to rectify even a blemish of the Covenant completely following sin
עַד שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לְמַדְרֵגַת צַדִּיק גָּמוּר וּבְנֵי עֲלִיָּה,
until he merits the status of a complete tzaddik and the sons of ascension,
כִּי כָּל אֶחָד מַשִּׂיג רַק כְּפִי מַדְרֵגָתוֹ,
because each sage apprehends only according to his own spiritual vantage point,
וְעַל כֵּן הִשִּׂיג הוּא הַמַּדְרֵגָה דְּ"עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה" רַק לְצַדִּיק גָּמוּר.
and therefore Rabbi Yochanan grasped the level of “no eye has seen” as reserved exclusively for the tzaddik gamur.
אֲבָל רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, אָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי [פֶּרֶק ג דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הֲלָכָה א]
However regarding Rabbi Abbahu, they related in the Jerusalem Talmud (Avodah Zarah 3:1)
דְּהֶרְאוּ לוֹ לִפְנֵי פְּטִירָתוֹ י״ג (שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר) נַהֲרֵי אֲפַרְסְמוֹן,
that before his passing they showed him thirteen rivers of balsam,
וְאָמַר: "אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי לְרִיק יָגַעְתִּי" (יְשַׁעְיָה מט, ד).
and he exclaimed: “I said: I have labored in vain” (Isaiah 49:4).
וְיָדוּעַ [בַּכַּוָּנוֹת] עַל "לֹא נִיגַע לָרִיק"
And it is known in the Kabbalistic kavanot on the liturgy “that we not labor in vain”
שֶׁהוּא אוֹתִיּוֹת קֶרִ"י,
that ריק consists of the same letters as קרי (keri, a seminal emission),
דִּכְזֶה הוּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם יְגִיעַת בָּשָׂר לָרִיק,
for such is, Heaven forbid, the wasted labor of the flesh in vain,
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ עַל זֶה "וְלֹא נֵלֵד לַבֶּהָלָה"
and likewise they expounded upon this: “nor give birth for sudden terror”
הַיְינוּ רוּחוֹת, שֵׁדִים וְלִילִין.
meaning spiritual specters, demons, and nocturnal spirits.
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁנָּתַן לָנוּ תּוֹרַת אֱמֶת וְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם נָטַע וְכוּלֵי,
And through His having given us the Torah of truth and implanted eternal life within us, etc.,
נִזְכֶּה לָזֶה לְעָבְדוֹ בְּלֵבָב שָׁלֵם,
we merit to serve Him with a whole heart,
הַיְינוּ בִּשְׁנֵי הַלְּבָבוֹת,
meaning with both inclinations of the heart,
גַּם בַּיֵּצֶר הָרָע לְאַכְפַּיָּא
even through subduing the evil inclination
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בּוֹ שׁוּם שׁוֹרֶשׁ מִזּוּהֲמַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
so that there remains no root of the evil inclination's defilement within him,
לְמַעַן לֹא וְכוּלֵי,
in order that we not, etc.,
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה יְבוֹעַר רוּחַ הַטֻּמְאָה שֶׁבְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ וּמֵחֲלַל לִבּוֹ לְגַמְרֵי וְלֹא נִיגַע וְכוּלֵי.
whereby the spirit of impurity is eradicated from his root and from the cavity of his heart completely, and we labor not in vain, etc.
וְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ שֶׁחָשַׁב עַל עַצְמוֹ דְּיָגַע לָרִיק,
And Rabbi Abbahu, who thought of himself that he had labored in vain,
עַל כָּרְחֲךָ חָשַׁד עַצְמוֹ מִפְּגַם הַבְּרִית שֶׁלֹּא תִּיקְּנוֹ לְגַמְרֵי.
perforce suspected himself regarding a blemish of the Covenant that he had not rectified it completely
וּבֶאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ [בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא פד עַמּוּד א]
Yet in truth our Sages stated in Bava Metzia (84a)
דְּשׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ מֵעֵין דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
that the radiant beauty of Rabbi Abbahu was a reflection of our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
שֶׁזָּכָה עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה לִמְאוֹר פָּנִים
who merited through the Torah luminous countenance,
דְּ"חָכְמַת אָדָם תָּאִיר פָּנָיו" (קֹהֶלֶת ח, א),
as “the wisdom of a man makes his face to shine” (Ecclesiastes 8:1),
כִּדְקָרֵי עֲלֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי [פֶּרֶק עַרְבֵי פְסָחִים סוֹף הֲלָכָה א].
as Rabbi Yochanan applied to him in the Yerushalmi (Pesachim 10:1).
וּדְיַעֲקֹב מֵעֵין אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
And the beauty of Jacob was a reflection of Adam the First,
הַיְינוּ קוֹדֶם הַחֵטְא.
meaning prior to the sin.
וְאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן הָיָה רָאוּי לִחְיוֹת לְעוֹלָם בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And Adam the First was originally destined to live forever in overt manifestation in this world,
אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּלֹא מֵת,
whereas Jacob our father, who did not die,
הָיָה בְּהֶעְלֵם מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דְּקָבְרוּ קָבְרַיָּא (תַּעֲנִית ה עַמּוּד ב).
was concealed from the perspective of this world, where he was buried (Taanis 5b).
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "מֵעֵין",
And this is why it is called “a reflection” (me'ein),
כְּמוֹ שַׁבָּת "מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא",
just as Shabbat is a reflection/foretaste of the World to Come,
שֶׁהַהֶרְגֵּשׁ בּוֹ בְּתַכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם.
in that the sensation of it remains in ultimate concealment.
וְדְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ מֵעֵין יַעֲקֹב,
And that of Rabbi Abbahu was a reflection of Jacob,
דְּאֵצֶל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִתְגַּלָּה שֶׁיֵּשׁ הֶעְלֵם,
for with Jacob our father it was at least revealed that there is a concealment,
דְּמִדְּרַשׁ הַמִּקְרָא מִיהַת נוֹדַע דְּבֶאֱמֶת לֹא מֵת,
since through the midrashic exposition of Scripture it became known that in truth he did not die,
וְאֶצְלוֹ הָיָה גַּם הַהֶעְלֵם בְּהֶעְלֵם.
whereas with Rabbi Abbahu even the concealment itself was concealed

paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 12a:13–14 teaches that after prophecy was removed from the prophets it was not removed from the Sages, and states, “A sage is greater than a prophet.” Takanas HaShavin 3:3 qualifies the comparison: “This is from the side of depth; but disclosure and sensory seeing are greater in the prophet.”

paragraphs.text: Cf. Resisei Layla 52:7, which distinguishes apprehension of the concealed root from the prophetic vision of the branches. Its warning against seeking that root means “to apprehend it completely through wisdom”; nevertheless, the Sages “have a hold upon it, because the root of their wisdom is from there.” The passage does not grant unrestricted, complete knowledge of the hidden root. Rav Tzadok’s present statement about one who is worthy remains his application of this distinction.

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 45b:5–6 records Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai’s statement: “I have seen the members of the ascent, and they are few.” The discussion distinguishes the illuminating from the non-illuminating partition, and then those who enter with permission from the rare ones who enter without permission. Rashi, ad loc. identifies the members of the ascent as “the company that receives the face of the Shechinah.” These are successive distinctions in the Gemara, not merely a general name for righteous people.

paragraphs.text: Yeshayahu 64:3 says, “No eye has seen, God, besides You.” Berachos 34b:21 states in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: “All the prophets prophesied only concerning penitents; but concerning the completely righteous, ‘No eye has seen, God, besides You.’” The same page separately applies the verse to the World to Come, beyond the Messianic era. The opposing ranking of penitents remains an explicit dispute in the Gemara.

paragraphs.text: Cf. Pri Tzaddik, Shelach 14:3: “There is an aspect in which it is superior, and nevertheless Eden is superior, for it is ‘no eye has seen.’” Its particular account compares Gan, Eden, and Gehinnom subsequently sanctified through repentance; it does not collapse the different levels into one ranking. The prophetic limit is the relevant comparison here.

paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 17a:6 names four who “died through the serpent’s instigation”: Binyamin son of Yaakov, Amram father of Moshe, Yishai father of David, and Kilav son of David. Eliyahu is not one of the four. II Melachim 2:11 separately says that Eliyahu “went up in the whirlwind to heaven.”

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok distinguishes the perception of wisdom from prophetic vision and relates each sage’s teaching to his spiritual attainment. He reads Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Abbahu as representing different paths to divine closeness, with Abbahu’s final vision revealing a repair he had doubted in himself.

p: וּבַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי [עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שָׁם] אָמְרוּ אַהָא דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ דְּי״ג נַהֲרֵי
And in the Yerushalmi (ibid.) they stated regarding this incident of Rabbi Abbahu and the thirteen rivers
הַגִּרְסָא: דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַרְאֶה לָהֶם מַתַּן שְׂכָרָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְהֵן שְׂבֵעִים וִישֵׁנִים.
the reading: that the Holy One shows them the reward due them while still in this world, and they are sated and fall asleep.
דִּרְאִיַּת י״ג נַהֲרֵי הוּא רְאִיַּת עוֹלָמוֹ בְּחַיָּיו בְּעוֹדוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
For the vision of the thirteen rivers represents beholding one's world in one's lifetime while still in this world—
הַשָּׂכָר דְּעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
the spiritual reward of the World to Come,
וְהוּא עִנְיַן הַשְּׂבִיעָה כְּעִנְיַן "אֶשְׂבְּעָה בְהָקִיץ תְּמוּנָתֶךָ" (תְּהִלִּים יז, טו),
and this is the essence of holy satiety, as in “I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with Your likeness” (Psalms 17:15),
דְּעוֹלָם הַבָּא אֵין בּוֹ אֲכִילָה וְכוּלֵי, רַק נֶהֱנִין מִזִּיו הַשְּׁכִינָה,
for the World to Come has neither eating nor drinking, but only delighting in the radiance of the Shechinah,
וְ"אֶשְׂבְּעָה בְהָקִיץ" הוּא הַשָּׂגַת שְׂבִיעָה זוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and “I shall be satisfied when I awake” is the attainment of this very spiritual satiety in this world.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הַמִּיתָה אַחַר כָּךְ רַק כְּשֵׁינָה בְּעָלְמָא,
And through this, physical death afterward is merely like an ordinary sleep,
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן דְּלֹא מֵת,
and he too is of the category who did not die,
אֶלָּא שֶׁגַּם הָא דְּלֹא מֵת הוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם.
save that the fact that he did not die is itself enveloped in concealment.
וּמִסְפַּר י״ג נַהֲרֵי שֶׁנִּמְצָא גַּם בְּתַלְמוּדֵנוּ [תַּעֲנִית כה עַמּוּד א] בִּשְׂכַר עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And the number of thirteen rivers, which is found in our Babylonian Talmud as well (Ta'anit 25a) regarding the reward of the World to Come,
וַדַּאי הוּא נֶגֶד י״ג מִדּוֹת שֶׁל רַחֲמִים,
is certainly corresponding to the Thirteen Attributes of Divine Mercy,
שֶׁזּוֹכִים לָהֶם עַל יְדֵי עֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה בְּי״ג מִדּוֹת שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה נִדְרֶשֶׁת,
which one merits through engaging in the Torah via the thirteen hermeneutical principles by which the Torah is expounded,
דְּהֵם זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה כַּיָּדוּעַ,
for these correspond directly to one another as is known,
וְיָדוּעַ דְּהַיּ״ג מִדּוֹת הֵם י״ג תִּיקּוּנֵי דְּדִיקְנָא.
and it is known that the Thirteen Attributes correspond to the Thirteen Rectifications of the Holy Beard (Tikkunei Dikna).
וּבְבָבָא מְצִיעָא [פד עַמּוּד א] דְּשׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לֹא חָשֵׁיב
And in Bava Metzia (84a) where the beauty of Rabbi Yochanan is omitted from the supreme list
דְּלֹא הָיָה לוֹ הַדְרַת פָּנִים זָקָן,
because he lacked the facial glory of a beard,
הַיְינוּ דְּהַבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה צָרִיךְ לְעוֹרֵר מִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים רַבִּים לְרַחֵם עָלָיו
that is because the ba'al teshuva must arouse the attribute of abundant mercies to have compassion on him
וּלְקַבְּלוֹ בִּתְשׁוּבָה הֲגַם שֶׁחָטָא,
and receive him in repentance even though he sinned;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן צַדִּיק גָּמוּר אֵין לְמִדַּת הַדִּין לְקַטְרֵג עָלָיו,
whereas concerning a complete tzaddik strict justice has no grounds to prosecute him,
וְהוּא מִתְנַהֵג הַכֹּל עַל פִּי מִדַּת הַדִּין,
and he conducts himself entirely by the standard of strict justice,
דְּעַל כֵּן "סְבִיבָיו נִשְׂעֲרָה מְאֹד".
which is why “round about Him it storms exceedingly.”
וְעַל כֵּן רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן שֶׁהָיָה צַדִּיק גָּמוּר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל וִינִיקָתוֹ מֵהַגְּבוּרוֹת,
Therefore Rabbi Yochanan, who was a complete tzaddik as noted above and drew his spiritual nurture from Gevurot,
דְּעַל כֵּן עָנֵישׁ וְקָטֵיל בְּעוֹבָדָא דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא [בְּבָבָא קַמָּא קיז סוֹף עַמּוּד א]
for which reason he punished and caused death in the episode of Rav Kahana in Bava Kamma 117a
וּדְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ [בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא פד סוֹף עַמּוּד א],
and with Reish Lakish in Bava Metzia 84a,
לֹא הָיָה לוֹ זָקָן,
he lacked a physical beard,
דְּהוּא חוֹתָמָיו שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה
which is the signature seal of the masters of repentance
שֶׁזּוֹכִים בִּתְשׁוּבָתָם לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם
who merit through their repentance eternal life
עַל יְדֵי דְּבֵיקוּת הָאַהֲבָה בִּכְלוֹת הַנֶּפֶשׁ
through the cleaving of love unto the expiration of the soul,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה "כַּמַּיִם הַפָּנִים [לַפָּנִים]" מְעוֹרֵר אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵלָיו
whereby “as in water face reflects face” he stirs Hashem's love toward him
מִמִּידַּת רַחֲמָיו וַחֲסָדָיו,
from His attribute of mercy and lovingkindness,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה לְהַדְרַת פָּנִים יוֹתֵר.
and through this he merits an even greater majestic countenance.
וְהוּא "הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵי"
And this is “the place where penitents stand, etc.”
שֶׁהִשִּׂיג רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ עַל פִּי מַדְרֵגָתוֹ,
which Rabbi Abbahu attained according to his spiritual level,
שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לָהּ לִפְנֵי פְּטִירָתוֹ
which he reached before his passing
עַל יְדֵי הַמְּרִירוּת שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ כָּל יְמֵי חַיָּיו עַל יְדֵי מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ דְּ"לְרִיק יָגַעְתִּי".
through the bitter contriteness he bore all the days of his life through his contemplation that “I labored in vain.”
וּמִי שֶׁלֹּא טָעַם טַעַם חֵטְא אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ מְרִירוּת שֶׁל הַבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה,
And one who has never tasted the taste of sin does not know the agonizing bitterness of penitents,
וְאֵין יָכוֹל לְהַשִּׂיג גּוֹדֶל הַמַּדְרֵגָה שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַגִּיעַ עַל יְדֵי זֶה.
and cannot comprehend the immense height of the rung that one is capable of attaining through it.

paragraphs.text: Cf. Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 8:2: “The World to Come has neither body nor bodily form, but only the souls of the righteous without a body.” He explains the radiance as knowing and apprehending divine truth. This is Rambam’s expressly incorporeal account; it is not imposed as the identical explanation of every other source. Rav Tzadok here applies the enjoyment-of-radiance teaching to satisfaction attained while still in this world.

paragraphs.text: Rashi on Psalms 17:15:2: אֶשְׂבְּעָה בְהָקִיץ תְּמוּנָתֶךָ. אֶשְׂבְּעָה מֵרְאִיַּת תְּמוּנָתְךָ בְּהָקִיץ הַמֵּתִים מִשְּׁנָתָם. לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: אֶשְׂבְּעָה מֵרְאוֹת פָּנֶיךָ בְּהָקִיץ הַמֵּתִים מִשְּׁנָתָם, שֶׁהֵם בִּדְמוּת תְּמוּנָתְךָ, שֶׁכֵּן נֶאֱמַר ״כִּי בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם״ (בראשית ט:ו) — “‘I shall be satisfied, when awake, with Your likeness’: I shall be satisfied from seeing Your likeness when the dead awaken from their sleep. Another explanation: I shall be satisfied from seeing Your face when the dead awaken from their sleep, for they have the likeness of Your image, as it says, ‘For in the image of God He made the human being.’” Radak on Psalms 17:15:3: בהקיץ כי לא תמות ותישן נפשי, הפך וישנו שנת עולם (ירמיהו נא לט נז). — “‘When awake’: for my soul will not die or sleep—the opposite of ‘they will sleep an everlasting sleep.’” Radak’s next comment discusses the soul’s intellectual apprehension of Divine glory after separation from the body, and also reports Ibn Ezra’s interpretation as waking intellectual contemplation in this world. Radak’s account of a soul that does not die or sleep thus differs from Rashi’s resurrection reading. Rav Tzadok here reads the satisfaction as attainable before death.

paragraphs.text: Ta’anis 25a:11–14 concerns Rabbi Elazar ben Pedas, not Rabbi Abbahu. After hearing that remaking the world might allow him a favorable birth-hour and that most of his life had passed, he declines. The promise is: “As the reward for your saying, ‘I do not want it,’ I will give you in the World to Come thirteen rivers of pure balsam oil, like the Euphrates and the Tigris, in which you will delight.”

paragraphs.text: Sifra, Baraisa of Rabbi Yishmael §2: “The Torah is expounded through thirteen principles”: an a-fortiori inference; an analogy based on an identical expression; a general principle derived from one verse or two; a general statement followed by a particular; a particular followed by a general statement; general–particular–general, restricted to cases resembling the particular; a general statement requiring a particular and a particular requiring a general statement; a case included in a general category but singled out to teach about the whole category; a case singled out for a different rule of the same kind, to be lenient and not stringent; a case singled out for a different rule not of the same kind, to be lenient and stringent; a case singled out to be governed by a new matter, not restored to its category unless Scripture expressly restores it; a matter learned from its context or conclusion; and two contradictory verses resolved by a third.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 34b:22: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: מָקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין — צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים אֵינָם עוֹמְדִין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שָׁלוֹם שָׁלוֹם לָרָחוֹק וְלַקָּרוֹב״. ״לָרָחוֹק״ בְּרֵישָׁא, וַהֲדַר ״לַקָּרוֹב״. — “This disagrees with Rabbi Abbahu, for Rabbi Abbahu said: In the place where penitents stand, complete righteous people do not stand, as it says, ‘Peace, peace to the distant and to the near’—first ‘the distant’ and then ‘the near.’” Berakhot 34b:23: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר לְךָ: מַאי ״רָחוֹק״ — שֶׁהָיָה רָחוֹק מִדְּבַר עֲבֵירָה מֵעִיקָּרָא. וּמַאי ״קָרוֹב״ — שֶׁהָיָה קָרוֹב לִדְבַר עֲבֵירָה, וְנִתְרַחֵק מִמֶּנּוּ הַשְׁתָּא. — “Rabbi Yochanan would say to you: What does ‘distant’ mean? One who was distant from transgression from the beginning. And what does ‘near’ mean? One who was near transgression and has now distanced himself from it.” Avodah Zarah 17a describes Elazar ben Durdaya’s weeping until his soul departed and the proclamation of his share in the World to Come. Tzidkas HaTzadik 164 contrasts revealed beauty with repentance’s hidden worth; Peri Tzadik, Pesach Sheni 2:2 explains how steady purity and the sudden merciful leap of repentance can each be greater in its own respect. The preceding Takanas HaShavin 15:54–56 supplies the love, restored-life and hidden-attainment context. The present paragraph concludes that one who never tasted sin cannot know the penitent’s bitterness or its resulting height; that is an account of transformation after failure and return.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok interprets the thirteen rivers as a glimpse of the world to come and links them with divine mercy and Torah. He contrasts the strict justice associated with Rabbi Yochanan’s path with the abundant mercy awakened through a penitent’s bitter longing and love.

p: וּבַבָּרַיְיתָא [דְּמַסֶּכֶת גַּן עֵדֶן] בְּמַעֲלַת הַצַּדִּיקִים בְּגַן עֵדֶן אִיתָא:
And in the Baraita of Masekhet Gan Eden regarding the stature of the righteous in Gan Eden it is stated:
"וְהַכִּיעוּר שֶׁבָּהֶם דּוֹמִין פָּנָיו לְיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק וְלִדְמְיוֹן רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
“and the least comely among them has a countenance resembling Joseph the Righteous and the likeness of Rabbi Yochanan,
וּכְפַרְצוּפֵי רִמּוֹנִים בְּכוֹס שֶׁל זָהָב מוּקָּף נְגוֹהַּ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ", עַד כָּאן.
and like pomegranate seeds in a goblet of gold encircled by the sun's brilliance,” until here
וְדוֹמֶה בָּזֶה לְמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ [בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא שָׁם פד עַמּוּד א]:
And this is similar to what they stated in Bava Metzia (84a):
אַמַּאן דְּבָעֵי לְמֶחֱזֵי שׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, נַיְיתֵי כָּסָא דְּכַסְפָּא וְכוּלֵי.
“He who desires to see the beauty of Rabbi Yochanan, let him bring a cup of silver, etc.”
וְכָאן אָמְרוּ "שֶׁל זָהָב",
And here in the Baraita they said “of gold,”
כִּי אָמְרוּ [בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין נב רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב]:
because they stated in Sanhedrin (52b):
תַּלְמִיד חָכָם דּוֹמֶה לִפְנֵי עַם הָאָרֶץ בַּתְּחִלָּה לְקִיתוֹן שֶׁל זָהָב,
a Torah scholar resembles before an ignoramus initially a golden flagon;
סִפֵּר עִמּוֹ – דּוֹמֶה לְקִיתוֹן שֶׁל כֶּסֶף וְכוּלֵי,
once he converses with him—he resembles a silver flagon, etc.,
עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִׁ״י דְּקָאֵי אַעֲדַת קֹרַח הַנִּזְכָּר מִקּוֹדֶם.
see there in Rashi that this refers to the congregation of Korah mentioned beforehand.
וּמַשְׁמַע דְּחָשֵׁיב לְקֹרַח עַם הָאָרֶץ;
And this implies that he considered Korah an ignoramus;
וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ אָמְרוּ דְּחָכָם גָּדוֹל הָיָה וּמִטּוֹעֲנֵי הָאָרוֹן,
yet in the Midrash they said that Korah was an eminent sage and one of the bearers of the Ark,
וְאָמְרוּ: "קֹרַח שֶׁפִּקֵּחַ הָיָה, מָה רָאָה לִשְׁטוּת זֶה? וְכוּלֵי",
and they asked: “Korah, who was astute, what did he see to commit this folly? etc.,”
וּמַשְׁמַע דְּהוּא הָיָה הַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם הַגָּדוֹל בְּכֻלָּם.
which implies that he was the greatest scholar among them all.
אֲבָל הַכַּוָּונָה, דְּיָדוּעַ דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹת כָּל הַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת,
However, the inner meaning is: for it is known that Moses our teacher is the soul-root of all Torah scholars in Israel throughout all generations,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִיזַ"ל עַל לְשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא: "מֹשֶׁה, שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרַתְּ",
and as the Ari wrote on the Talmudic idiom: “Moses, you have spoken well,”
דְּרוֹצֶה לוֹמַר תַּלְמִיד חָכָם.
which signifies any Torah scholar.
וְהֵם בָּאוּ לַחֲלוֹק עַל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And Korah and his assembly came to dispute against Moses our teacher
בְּטַעֲנַת "כָּל הָעֵדָה כֻּלָּם קְדֹשִׁים וּמַדּוּעַ תִּתְנַשְּׂאוּ" (בַּמִּדְבָּר טז, ג),
under the argument: “All the congregation are holy, every one of them... wherefore then lift you up yourselves” (Numbers 16:3),
הַיְינוּ דְּאֵין הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם עַל עַם הָאָרֶץ,
arguing that there is no spiritual superiority of a Torah scholar over an ordinary person,
דְּ"עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים" וְיִירְשׁוּ אֶרֶץ וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
since “Your people are all righteous” and inherit the land and the World to Come.
כִּי גַּם רֵיקָנִים שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים מִצְוֹת כְּרִמּוֹן,
For even the empty ones of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרָכוֹת נז עַמּוּד א] זֶה עַל עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁהוּא רֵיקָן מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
as our Sages stated in Berakhot (57a) regarding an unlearned person who is empty of Torah knowledge,
וּמִילּוּי הַמִּצְוֹת הוּא דּוּגְמַת מִילּוּי הָרִמּוֹן מִפַּרְצִידֵי וּפַרְטוּטָא דְּרוּמָּנָא.
and being filled with mitzvos resembles a pomegranate packed with its individual seeds.
אֲבָל בְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם יְצַפֶּה לַתּוֹרָה
However, regarding a Torah scholar, concerning whom they said there that he should anticipate Torah,
דִּכְתִיב: "מֵעֲסִיס רִמֹּנִי" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ח, ב),
as it is written: “of the juice of my pomegranate” (Song of Songs 8:2),
הוּא הַנִּמְצָץ מִן הָרִמּוֹן.
this is the rich nectar squeezed from the pomegranate.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ [בַּחֲגִיגָה טו עַמּוּד ב] עַל 'אַחֵר' שֶׁהָיָה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם וּבַעַל עֲבֵירוֹת בַּפּוֹעַל,
And therefore they said in Chagigah (15b) regarding Acher who was a scholar yet committed actual sins,
דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר "רִמּוֹן מָצָא: תּוֹכוֹ אָכַל",
that Rabbi Meir “found a pomegranate: he ate its interior,”
הַיְינוּ שֶׁמָּצַץ הֶעָסִיס,
meaning that he extracted its sweet juice,
"וּקְלִפָּתוֹ זָרַק",
“and threw away its rind,”
שֶׁכָּל גּוּף הַפַּרְצִידֵי הַנִּשְׁאָר אַחַר הַמְּצִיצָה הָיָה קְלִיפָּה.
in that the substantive body of the seeds remaining after the extraction was discarded as a husk.
וְעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ בַּעֲלֵי הַמִּצְוֹת אֵין בָּהֶם עָסִיס,
And unlearned masters of mitzvot have no deep juice within them,
אֲבָל הַפַּרְצִידֵי טוֹבִים לְמַאֲכָל.
yet the firm seeds are wholesome for food.
וְתוֹרָה הוּא הַפְּנִימִיּוּת
And Torah is the inner essence
וְשֹׁרֶשׁ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
and root of the souls of Israel,
שֶׁהוּא מֵאוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה,
which derives from the letters of the Torah,
וְעִקָּרוֹ בְּהַשָּׂגַת הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמֹּחַ
its essence being the grasp of wisdom in the mind
וּבִינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
and understanding in the heart,
וְאֵין בָּהּ שַׁיָּכוּת בְּאֵבְרֵי הַגּוּף
with no connection to the limbs of the body
רַק מִצַּד מַה שֶׁמּוֹצִיא בַּפֶּה.
only through what one brings out with the mouth.

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 84a:7: “One who wishes to see Rabbi Yochanan’s beauty should bring a silver cup from the silversmith, fill it with the seeds of a red pomegranate, surround its rim with a wreath of red roses, and set it between sun and shade. That radiance is a likeness of Rabbi Yochanan’s beauty.”

paragraphs.text: The next passage, 84a:8, separately compares Rav Kahana’s beauty with Rabbi Abbahu’s, Rabbi Abbahu’s with Yaakov’s, and Yaakov’s with Adam’s. It then explains Rabbi Yochanan’s omission from that list by his lack of the facial distinction of a beard. The two teachings are not one continuous quotation; the directly relevant contrast here is the silver cup versus Maseches Gan Eden’s gold.

paragraphs.text: Rashi, s.v. Lamah talmid explicitly says that Korach’s assembly “were Torah scholars,” and explains that after they benefited from Korach’s wealth “they became insignificant in his eyes,” enabling him to entice them into supporting the rebellion. Rashi, s.v. Batechillah similarly describes the scholar as precious in the other person’s eyes while he has no need of him. Rashi does not explicitly call Korach an am ha’aretz in this comment. That implication is Rav Tzadok’s inference, which he next tests against the Midrash’s description of Korach’s learning.

paragraphs.text: Cf. Pri Tzaddik, Korach 8:2. After an explanation involving wealth and pride, Rav Tzadok offers another reading: “Korach became proud and disputed Moshe through the power of the Torah that he possessed”; “he thought that he was as great in Torah as Moshe Rabbeinu.” The 250 men are then distinguished as disputing the hereditary priesthood rather than Moshe’s greatness. These are alternative explanations within that work, not a denial of Korach’s real learning. The description of Korach as the greatest scholar among the whole group is Rav Tzadok’s further inference in the present text.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar 17a:17: מוחא חכמה איהו מחשבה מלגו. בינה לבא ובה הלב מבין. ועל אלין תרין כתיב הנסתרות ליי' אלקינו. — “The brain is wisdom; it is inward thought. Binah is the heart, and through it the heart understands. Of these two it is written: ‘The hidden things belong to Hashem our God.’” Berachos 61a likewise gives the heart’s function as understanding. Patach Eliyahu places these two inward powers after its mapping of the seven manifested attributes and the mouth of Oral Torah. That symbolic structure explains the author’s distinction here: Torah’s principal apprehension is wisdom in the brain and understanding in the heart before its outward expression through the mouth.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Images of gold, silver, and pomegranates distinguish spiritual radiance, practical mitzvos, and the inner sweetness of Torah. Rav Tzadok uses these images to explain why Korach’s challenge to Moshe undermined the special role of Torah wisdom despite the holiness shared by Israel.

The theme: Rav Tzadok distinguishes Torah’s inward wisdom from its outward expression in speech, and contrasts this with the bodily action of mitzvos. Shabbos can sanctify both inward Torah delight and bodily enjoyment, while the root holiness of Israel remains even where a person sins.

p: וְזֶהוּ סוֹף כָּל מַדְרֵגוֹת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
This is the end of all levels of action,
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּמַלְכוּת פֶּה,
as is known, that Malchus is “mouth,”
כִּי הַדִּבּוּר אֵינוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה גָּמוּר בְּפֹעַל
for speech is not a complete deed in actuality
בְּגוּף הַדִּבּוּר,
in the substance of the speech,
רַק עִקּוּם שְׂפָתַיִם נֶחְשָׁב מַעֲשֶׂה.
only the movement of the lips counts as a deed.
וּבַתּוֹרָה הוּא רַק הַהוֹצָאָה מִכֹּחַ לַפֹּעַל
In Torah it is only the bringing out from potential to actual
וּבְהִתְגַּלּוּת מַה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹת,
and in revealing what can be revealed,
אֲבָל עִקַּר הַהַשָּׂגָה הוּא בַּלֵּב
but the essence of grasp is in the heart,
בְּחָכְמָה וּבִינָה,
in wisdom and understanding,
שֶׁהֵם לְמַעְלָה מִשִּׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן
which are above the seven days of building,
שֶׁהֵם יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
which are the days of action.
וְשַׁבָּת מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And Shabbos is a taste of the World to Come,
שֶׁהוּא הַשְּׁבִיתָה מִמַּעֲשֶׂה
being cessation from action,
אַף מֵהַדִּבּוּר בַּתּוֹרָה בְּפֹעַל
even from actual speech in Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קיט, עַמּוּד ב),
as they said (Shabbos 119b),
רַק בְּהַשָּׂגַת הָעֹנֶג לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם
only in the Torah scholar’s grasp of delight
בְּהַשָּׂגַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
in grasping words of Torah,
שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם עֹנֶג לְמַעְלָה מִזֶּה,
for which there is no delight higher than this,
וְהַדִּבּוּר בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה עִם חֲבֵרוֹ
while speaking words of Torah with a friend
מַעֲלִים וּמְכַסֶּה הַהַשָּׂגָה בַּלֵּב כַּיָּדוּעַ.
conceals and covers the grasp in the heart, as is known.
וְלַעֲמֵי הָאָרֶץ בַּעֲלֵי מִצְווֹת
And for unlearned people who observe commandments,
שֶׁהוּא בִּיגִיעַת בָּשָׂר וְאֵבְרֵי הַגּוּף,
whose service is by labor of flesh and limbs,
שֶׁכָּל הַמִּצְווֹת בִּפְעֻלַּת הָאֵבָרִים,
for all commandments are through action of the limbs,
עַל זֶה הוּא מִצְוַת שַׁבָּת בְּעֹנֶג הַגּוּף,
for this is the Shabbos commandment of bodily delight,
שֶׁגַּם בָּזֶה יֵשׁ קְדֻשָּׁה גְּדוֹלָה בְּשַׁבָּת,
for in this too there is great holiness on Shabbos,
כִּי הַגּוּף קָדוֹשׁ דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
since the holy body of the children of Israel
גַּם כֵּן דָּבוּק בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
is also attached to Hashem, blessed is He.
וְכָל אֲכִילַת שַׁבָּת כַּאֲכִילַת הַמָּן
Every Shabbos meal is like eating the manna,
שֶׁפּוֹעֵל לְהַכְנִיס דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בַּלֵּב,
which works to bring words of Torah into the heart;
גַּם מִי שֶׁלֹּא זָכָה לְאוֹר תּוֹרָה
even one who did not merit the light of Torah
זוֹכֶה עַל יְדֵי הַנֵּר דְּמִצְוָה גַּם כֵּן
merits, through the mitzvah candle too,
לְהָאִיר לוֹ בַּגּוּף הַחָשׁוּךְ
to have light for him in the dark body
בְּנֵר הָֽשֵׁם נִשְׁמַת אָדָם,
with “the lamp of Hashem, the soul of man,”
שֶׁהוּא נְהוֹרָא זוּטָא דְּיֵשׁ לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
which is the small light that every Jew has,
דְּכֻלָּם קְדוֹשִׁים וּדְבוּקִים בֵּאלֹקִים חַיִּים.
for all are holy and attached to the Living God.
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ
For this reason they said
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא,
“Even though he sinned, he is still a Jew,”
דְּשֹׁרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת הַיַּהֲדוּת שֶׁבּוֹ
since the root of the holiness of Jewishness within him,
שֶׁמִּצַּד שֹׁרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתָן שֶׁל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב
from the root of the souls of Yaakov’s seed,
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְנַתֵּק.
cannot be severed.
וְבַשַּׁבָּת (קה, עַמּוּד ב)
And in Shabbos (105b)
דְּאָדָם מִיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁמֵּת
that a Jew who died
אֲפִילּוּ דְּלָאוּ אָדָם כָּשֵׁר,
even if not a worthy person,
דּוֹמֶה לְסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּשְׂרַף,
is like a Torah scroll that was burned,
וּפִרֵּשׁ רַשִׁ״י
and Rashi explains
דְּאֵין לְךָ רֵיק מִיִשְׂרָאֵל
that there is no empty person among Israel
שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ תּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת,
without Torah and mitzvos in him;
וְמַשְׁמַע דְּאֲפִילּוּ רָשָׁע וּבַעֲל עֲבֵרוֹת נִמֵּי,
implying even a wicked person and a transgressor too,
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים מִצְווֹת כַּרִּמוֹן.
for even the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate.
וְכֵן מַשְׁמַע לְשׁוֹן “דְּלָאוּ אָדָם כָּשֵׁר”
So too the wording “not a worthy person” implies,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא (שָׁם קמט, עַמּוּד ב)
in the manner found (there, 149b):
“אֵין לֹא טוֹב אֶלָּא רָע”.
“not good” means only “bad.”
וְכֵן הוּא בְּהָרַבֵּנוּ אֲשֶׁר (פֶּרֶק אֵלּוּ מְגַּלְחִין, סִימָן נט)
And so it is in Rabbeinu Asher (chapter Eilu Megalchin, siman 59)
בְּשֵּׁם מוֹרֵנוּ הָרַב רַבִּי מֵאִיר מִרוֹטִנְבֶּרְג
in the name of Maharam of Rothenburg
(וּבְדִפּוּס יָשָׁן שֶׁכָּל סִימְנֵי הַמַּסֶּכֶת נִסְמְנוּ יַחַד הוּא בְּסִימָן קו)
(in an old edition where all the tractate’s simanim are numbered together it is siman 106)
מִלְשוֹן רַשִׁ״י הַנַּ״ל,
from Rashi’s wording above,
וּדְמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר “בְּאַבֹּד רְשָׁעִים רִנָּה”
and as for the statement “when the wicked perish there is joy,”
זֶהוּ בְּעוֹבֲדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
it refers to idol worshippers
אוֹ עוֹשִׂים לַהַכְעִיס וּמִינִין.
or those who sin to spite, and heretics.
וְנִדְחָק בְּהֲרוּגֵי בֵּית דִּין
He strains regarding those executed by the court
דְּאֵין מִתְאַבְּלִין דְּ“בְּאַבֹּד וְגוֹמֵר”,
for whom one does not mourn, based on “when perish,” etc.,
דְּהוּא כְּלַהַכְעִיס
claiming it is like sinning to spite
מַה שֶׁמָּסְרוּ עַצְמָם לִמִיתָה כְּשֶׁהתָּרוּ,
that they handed themselves over to death when warned,
עַיֵּן שָׁם.
see there.

paragraphs.text: Compare Shabbos 119b: Reish Lakish in Rabbi Yehudah Nesiah's name says that the world endures through the breath of schoolchildren. When Rav Pappa asks about the sages' own breath, Abaye distinguishes breath containing sin from breath without sin. The passage also says not to interrupt the children even for building the Temple. This direct praise of children's Torah study is a boundary comparison to the exceptional adult Shabbos attainment developed here; it is not itself a teaching to suspend Torah study.

paragraphs.text: Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Vayassa 3:4: מִכָּן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר: לֹא נִתְּנָה תוֹרָה לִדְרֹשׁ אֶלָּא לְאוֹכְלֵי הַמָּן. הָא כֵיצַד? הָיָה יוֹשֵׁב וְדוֹרֵשׁ, וְלֹא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ מֵהֵיכָן אוֹכֵל וְשׁוֹתֶה, וּמֵהֵיכָן הָיָה לוֹבֵשׁ וּמִתְכַּסֶּה. הָא לֹא נִתְּנָה תוֹרָה לִדְרֹשׁ אֶלָּא לְאוֹכְלֵי הַמָּן. וּשְׁנִיִּים לָהֶם, אוֹכְלֵי תְרוּמָה — “From here Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai would say: Torah was given to be expounded only to eaters of the manna. How so? If someone sat and expounded, he would not know from where he would eat and drink, or from where he would obtain clothing and covering. Thus Torah was given to be expounded only to eaters of the manna, and second to them are eaters of terumah.” The same paragraph also recognizes morning and evening study by one who works during the day. Devarim 8:3 locates life in Hashem’s utterance; Yoma 75b describes the manna’s absorption into the body and records differing explanations and later qualifications. Rav Tzadok’s comparison here makes Shabbos eating conducive to Torah entering the heart; it does not identify ordinary food with the miraculous manna.

It also discusses the delay of atonement until the condemned person experiences a little of the grave’s suffering: mourning begins at the closing of the grave, and “since they were excluded, they remain excluded.” This is kept distinct from the following argument: “Those executed by the court are also like those who act to provoke, since they surrender themselves to death when warned and say, ‘On that condition I act.’” The word “like” is part of the source; the inference should not be quoted as if it had already established identical motivation.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The comparison of a person’s death to a burned Torah scroll leads Rav Tzadok to examine the grounds and limits of mourning. He argues from the Torah and mitzvos retained even by sinners, questions the identification of appetite with deliberate defiance, and asks why death resembles a scroll burned “by force.”

p: וְאֵין בּוֹ טַעַם לְהַחֲשִׁיבוֹ לְהַכְעִיס
But there is no reason to consider it spite
בִּשְׁבִּיל קִבּוּל הַהַתְרָאָה,
because of accepting the warning,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַתַּאֲוָה דְּלְהַנָאַת שָׁעָה
rather the lust for momentary pleasure
עִוּוְרָה עֵינָיו
blinded his eyes
שֶׁלֹּא לָחוּשׁ לְמַה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה,
from heeding what will be,
וְכְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר “עָרֵב לָאִישׁ לֶחֶם שֶׁקֶר וְאַחֲרֵיהֵן יִמָּלֵא פִיו חָצָץ”.
as it says, “bread of falsehood is sweet to a man, but afterward his mouth is filled with gravel.”
וּמַתְעֶה נַפְשָׁוֹ שֶׁיוּכַל לִבְרֹחַ וּלִמָּלֵט.
He deceives himself that he can flee and escape.
וְכָּל שֶׁכֵּן בְּרוֹצַח
All the more so a murderer
הַעוֹשֶׂה לְמַלְאוֹת תַּאֲוַת נִקְמָתוֹ בְּאוֹיְבוֹ,
who acts to satisfy his lust for revenge against his enemy,
דְּהוּא אֵינוֹ חוֹשֵׁשׁ אֲפִילּוּ יְמִיתוּהוּ גַּם כֵּן,
who is not concerned even if they also kill him,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יְבָמוֹת קיח, עַמּוּד א)
as they said (Yevamos 118a):
“תָּמוּת נַפְשִׁי עִם פְּלִשְׁתִּים” קָאֲמָרָה.
“Let me die with the Philistines,” she said.
וְגַם הוּא כָּתַב רַק כְּמוֹ לְהַכְעִיס,
He too wrote only “like to spite,”
אֲבָל אֵין בְּזֶה טַעַם
but this has no reason
כִּיוָן דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא עוֹשֶׂה רַק לִמְלוֹא תַּאֲוָתוֹ
since in any case he acts only to fulfill his lust
וְלֹא לַהַכְעִיס יוֹצְרוֹ.
and not to spite his Creator.
וְתוֹ נִרְאָה דְּהַדִּין תָּמוּהּ מִסַנְהֶדְרִין (מג, עַמּוּד ב)
Moreover the ruling seems puzzling given Sanhedrin (43b):
דְּכָּל הַמּוֹמָּתִין מִתְוַּדִּין,
all who are executed confess,
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהִתְוַּדָּה וְשָׁב
and once he confessed and repented,
אַף שֶׁהוּא בְּשָׁעַת מִיתָה
even at the time of death,
וָדַאי דְּאֵין לְהַחֲשִׁיבוֹ עוֹד כְּמוּמָּר לְהַכְעִיס.
surely he should no longer be deemed a spiteful apostate.
וְבְּאֱמֶת לְשוֹן רַשִׁ״י הַנַּ״ל “שֶׁאֵין לְךָ רֵיק כו׳”
In truth Rashi’s wording above, “there is no empty person,” etc.,
מַשְׁמַע דְּעַל כָּל פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַיּוֹתֵר גֵּרוּעִים נִמֵּי קָאֲמַר,
implies it speaks of even the worst sinners of Israel,
וְכְּמוֹ דְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא נֶעֱקַר
just as the name “Israel” is not uprooted
גַּם מִמּוּמָר לְהַכְעִיס וְעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
even from a spiteful apostate and idol worshipper,
דְּגַם בּוֹ מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ גַּם תּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת.
since even in him there is Torah and mitzvos.
וּבְסַנְהֶדְרִין (לט, עַמּוּד ב) אִיתָא
In Sanhedrin (39b) it says
הָא דְּ“בְּאַבֹּד רְשָׁעִים” עַל אַחְאָב,
that “when the wicked perish” refers to Achav,
וְשָׁם (קג, עַמּוּד ב) אָמְרוּ
and there (103b) they said
שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹנֶה שְׁמוֹנִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה פָּנִים בְּתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים,
that he studied eighty-five interpretations of Toras Kohanim,
אִם כֵּן הָיָה מָלֵא תּוֹרָה,
so he was full of Torah,
וְכֵן בְּמִצְווֹת אָמְרוּ (שָׁם קב, עַמּוּד ב)
and regarding mitzvos they said (there, 102b)
שֶׁהָיָה מְפַרְנֵס תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מִנְּכָסָיו
that he supported Torah scholars from his wealth
וְהָיָה וַתָּרָן בְּמָמוֹנוֹ,
and was generous with his money,
וְצְדָקָה נִקְרָאת בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
and charity is called, in the words of our Sages of blessed memory,
בְּכָּמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת בְּשֵּׁם סָתָם “מִצְוָה”
in several places simply “the mitzvah,”
כִּי זֶהוּ הַמִּצְוָה שֶׁעוֹשִׂין בְּכָל עֵת.
for this is the mitzvah done at every time.
אֲבָל בְּלָאוּ הֵיכִי כְּבָר עָמַד הַרַמְבָּ״ן בְּתוֹרַת הָאָדָם
But even otherwise, Ramban already raised in Toras HaAdam,
וּמוּבָא בְּבֵית יוֹסֵף (יוֹרֶה דֵּעָה, סִימָן ש״מ)
and cited in Beis Yosef (Yoreh Deah, siman 340)
מַה שֶׁאָמְרוּ לְחִיוּב קְרִיעָה
regarding the obligation of tearing garments
דּוֹמֶה לְסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּשְׂרַף,
“like a Torah scroll that was burned”:
הָא בְּסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא בְּזְרוֹעַ
for with a Torah scroll, they required this only when it was burned by force,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מוֹעֵד קָטָן כו, סוֹף עַמּוּד א)
as they said (Moed Katan 26a),
וְנִדְחָק דְּמָשָׁל בְּעָלְמָא אָמְרוּ, עַיֵּן שָׁם.
and he strains, saying it was merely a metaphor; see there.
וְעַדַיִּן צָרִיךְ בִּיאוּר,
This still requires clarification,
דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מַה דִּמָּה לְסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
for in any case why compare to a Torah scroll
וּלְלְמוֹד מִשָּׁם לִקְרוֹע,
and learn from it to tear,
וְגַם הָאֲחַרוֹנִים עָמְדוּ בְּזֶה
and the later authorities addressed this too:
עַיֵּן בְּסֵפֶר תִּפְאֶרֶת לְמֹשֶׁה (סוֹף סִימָן ש״מ)
see Tiferes LeMoshe (end of siman 340),
וּבְשַׁבֻוֹת יַעֲקֹב (חֵלֶק א׳, סִימָן פה)
Shevus Yaakov (part 1, siman 85),
וּתְשֻׁבַת חָכָם צְבִי (סִימָן יז)
and the responsum of Chacham Tzvi (siman 17),
וְלֹא הֶעֱלוּ בְּזֶה דָּבָר בָּרוּר
but they brought nothing clear out of it
רַק כְּדִבְרֵי הַרַמְבָּ״ן הַנַּ״ל.
beyond the words of Ramban above.

paragraphs.text: Mishlei 20:17 — “bread of falsehood is sweet to a person, but afterward his mouth is filled with gravel”: The verse contrasts the immediate sweetness of dishonest gain with its bitter end. Rav Tzadok applies that psychology to a sinner who accepts a warning yet proceeds: desire narrows attention to the moment and suppresses the future consequence. This explains the act without excusing it. The offender remains responsible precisely because the warning made the consequence known, even though appetite overwhelmed that knowledge in practice.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 43b:3: מַתְנִי׳ הָיָה רָחוֹק מִבֵּית הַסְּקִילָה כְּעֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת, אוֹמְרִים לוֹ: ״הִתְוַדֵּה״, שֶׁכֵּן דֶּרֶךְ כׇּל הַמּוּמָתִין מִתְוַדִּין. שֶׁכׇּל הַמִּתְוַדֶּה יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בְּעָכָן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: ״בְּנִי שִׂים נָא כָבוֹד לַה׳ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְתֶן לוֹ תוֹדָה״. ״וַיַּעַן עָכָן אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וַיֹּאמַר אׇמְנָה אָנֹכִי חָטָאתִי וְכָזֹאת וְכָזֹאת וְגוֹ׳״. וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁכִּיפֵּר לוֹ וִידּוּיוֹ? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מֶה עֲכַרְתָּנוּ יַעְכֳּרְךָ ה׳ בַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה״. בְּיוֹם הַזֶּה אַתָּה עָכוּר, וְאִי אַתָּה עָכוּר לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא. — “When he was approximately ten cubits from the place of stoning, they would say to him: ‘Confess,’ for it is the way of all who are put to death to confess, since everyone who confesses has a share in the World to Come. So we find with Achan, to whom Yehoshua said, ‘My son, please give honor to Hashem, the God of Israel, and give Him confession.’ Achan answered Yehoshua and said, ‘Indeed, I have sinned, and such and such,’ and the rest of the verse. From where is it known that his confession atoned for him? It says, ‘Yehoshua said: Why have you troubled us? Hashem will trouble you on this day’—on this day you are troubled, but you are not troubled in the World to Come.” Rav Tzadok draws the further inference here that one who confessed and repented at death cannot still be classified as acting from spite toward the Creator. The Mishnah instructs the condemned person to confess; it does not establish that every condemned person actually does so. Rav Tzadok’s ensuing argument is conditional on actual confession and repentance.

So we find with Achan, to whom Yehoshua said, ‘My son, please give honor to Hashem, the God of Israel, and give Him confession.’ Achan answered Yehoshua and said, ‘Indeed, I have sinned, and such and such,’ and the rest of the verse. From where is it known that his confession atoned for him? It says, ‘Yehoshua said: Why have you troubled us? Hashem will trouble you on this day’—on this day you are troubled, but you are not troubled in the World to Come.” Rav Tzadok draws the further inference here that one who confessed and repented at death cannot still be classified as acting from spite toward the Creator. The Mishnah instructs the condemned person to confess; it does not establish that every condemned person actually does so. Rav Tzadok’s ensuing argument is conditional on actual confession and repentance.

It then provides prayer and kindness as further avenues: “One who lacks the means to perform kindness with his money can perform kindness with his body.” Its conclusion is: “Every person of Israel is distinguished from the nations, whether through Torah, prayer or deeds of kindness.” These distinct avenues explain the local mitzvah point; they do not make learning unnecessary or certify identical spiritual attainment. Takanas HaShavin 15:93 adds the later comparison: even at the utmost descent they were not severed from their root in holiness. Its setting is the disclosure of Oral Torah through exile and in the future; it does not independently decide the law of tearing.

And in my opinion it appears
דְּכָל מִיתַת אָדָם נֶחְשָׁב בִּזְרוֹעַ
that every human death is counted as “by force,”
עַל יְדֵי קִטְרוּג הַמְקַטְרְגִים וּמַשְׂטִינִים,
through the prosecution of the heavenly accusers and adversaries;
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ "לֹא יַחְפֹּץ בְּמוֹת הַמֵּת" (יְחֶזְקֵאל יח, לב),
and Hashem, blessed be He, “has no pleasure in the death of him that dies” (Ezekiel 18:32),
רַק מִצַּד מִדַּת הַדִּין הַמְקַטְרֶגֶת
rather it proceeds strictly from the attribute of strict justice prosecuting
עַל יְדֵי הַשָּׂטָן הָעוֹלֶה וּמְקַטְרֵג,
through the Satan who ascends and prosecutes;
וְהוּא עַצְמוֹ הַמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת
and he himself is the Angel of Death
שֶׁבְּכֹחַ קִטְרוּגוֹ זֶה יוֹרֵד וְנוֹטֵל נְשָׁמָה,
who by the leverage of this prosecution descends and takes the soul,
וְהוּא עַצְמוֹ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וְהַמֵּסִית לַהֲעֲבִירָהּ,
and he himself is the evil inclination who incites to transgression,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא טז עַמּוּד א],
as stated in Bava Basra 16a,
וְהַכֹּל מִמֶּנּוּ.
and all of it derives from him.
וְהַיְינוּ "בִּזְרוֹעַ":
And that is the definition of “by violence”:
כָּל שֶׁאֵין מְחוּיָּב מִיתָה בְּבֵית דִּין,
whenever one is not liable to capital execution by an earthly court,
וּבֵית דִּין שֶׁל מַטָּה הָיוּ פּוֹטְרִין אוֹתוֹ,
and an earthly court would have acquitted him;
אַף דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נָתַן רְשׁוּת לַשָּׂטָן לְהַשְׂטִין
even though the Holy One, blessed be He, granted license to the Satan to prosecute
וְלִהְיוֹת "רְשָׁעִים תְּרַדֵּף רָעָה"
and for “evil to pursue the wicked”
וְהַכֹּל בְּמִשְׁפָּט וּבְדִין שֶׁל מַעְלָה,
and everything is governed by supernal law and heavenly judgment;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לְגַבֵּי דִּידַן,
nevertheless relative to us,
מֵאַחַר דִּכְפִי מִשְׁפְּטֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַמְּסוּרִים לָנוּ אֵין עָלָיו מִשְׁפַּט הַמָּוֶת,
since according to the laws of the Torah entrusted to us there is no death sentence upon him,
נֶחְשָׁב כִּבִזְרוֹעַ,
it is considered as having occurred by violence;
וְעַל כֵּן דִּמּוּהוּ לְנִשְׂרָף בִּזְרוֹעַ.
and therefore the Sages compared him to a Torah scroll burned by violence.
אֲבָל הֲרוּגֵי בֵּית דִּין דִּבְדִין קָטְלִינַן לְהוּ,
However, those executed by a court whom we execute according to halakhic law,
וְאַף דְּשָׁב וּמִתְוַדֶּה אֵין בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַטָּה מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ,
and even though he repents and confesses, an earthly court does not remit his penalty,
וְאָנוּ מְמִיתִין אוֹתוֹ בְּיָדֵינוּ עַל פִּי מִצְוַת הַתּוֹרָה,
and we put him to death with our hands in fulfillment of the Torah's commandment,
לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ לְדַמּוֹתוֹ לִכְבִזְרוֹעַ.
it is inapplicable to compare this to a scroll burned “by force.”
וְהָכִי נַמֵּי מוּמָר לְהַכְעִיס וְעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
And likewise an apostate out of defiance and an idolater,
שֶׁהֵם בִּכְלַל הַמִּינִין דְּמוֹרִידִין כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כו עַמּוּד ב],
who are included among the heretics whom one casts into a pit as they stated in Avodah Zarah (26b),
כֵּיוָן דִּבְדִין לְהוֹרִידָן וּלְהַמִּיתָם בַּיָּדַיִם,
since according to law one is mandated to cast them down and execute them with our hands,
גַּם כְּשֶׁמֵּתוּ מֵעַצְמָן לֹא הָוֵי בִּזְרוֹעַ,
even when they die of natural causes it is not considered by violence,
דְּהָא דִּינָא הָכִי
for such is the law,
וְכוּלֵי עָלְמָא מְצֻוִּין לְבַעֲרוֹ.
and everyone is commanded to remove him.
וּבִכְהַאי גַּוְונָא הוּא שֶׁאָמְרוּ:
And regarding such a case it was said (Proverbs 11:10):
דְּ"בַּאֲבֹד רְשָׁעִים רִנָּה",
“when the wicked perish there is joyful singing,”
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם גַּם כֵּן תּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת
and even though they too possess Torah and mitzvot
וְהֵם כְּסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּשְׂרַף,
and resemble a Torah scroll that was burned,
אֵינוֹ כְּנִשְׂרָף בִּזְרוֹעַ,
it is not comparable to one burned by violence;
כֵּן נִרְאֶה בְּעֵינַי בְּטַעַם זֶה.
so it appears in my eyes regarding this reason.

paragraphs.text: Thus lawful royal execution and execution by a Torah court do not receive an identical mourning rule. The present paragraph names harugei beis din specifically; the note must not broaden it to every lawfully imposed death. This is a boundary comparison, not a claim that Rav Tzadok explicitly discusses or rejects the royal case here. The broader mourning references Sanhedrin 46b and Moed Katan 27a remain background, not the precise location of the timing statement.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok interprets a death not imposed under earthly Torah law as “by force” for the burned-scroll analogy, even when heavenly judgment permits it. He contrasts this with the authorized executions discussed in the sources, where the same particular basis for mourning does not apply.

p: וּלְעוֹלָם גַּם כּוּלְּהוּ מְלֵאִים תּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת,
And eternally all of them are likewise full of Torah and mitzvot,
כָּל שֶׁהֵם מִזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב שֶׁמִּטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה,
so long as they stem from the seed of Jacob whose bed was whole,
דְּ"לֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח" (שְׁמוּאֵל ב יד, יד).
for “none of them shall be utterly cast out” (II Samuel 14:14).
וּבְסוֹף חֲגִיגָה (כז עַמּוּד א) אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
And at the end of Chagigah (27a) Rabbi Abbahu said in the name of Rabbi Elazar:
תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אֵין אוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׁוֹלֶטֶת בָּהֶן
Torah scholars—the fire of Gehenna has no dominion over them,
לְפִי שֶׁכָּל גּוּפָן אֵשׁ;
because their entire body is fire;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
and subsequently Reish Lakish said
דְּאֵין אוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׁוֹלֶטֶת בְּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
that the fire of Gehenna has no dominion over the transgressors of Israel,
קַל וָחֹמֶר מִמִּזְבַּח הַזָּהָב
by an a fortiori argument from the golden Altar:
דְּעָלָיו כְּעֹבִי דִינַר זָהָב וְכוּלֵי,
over which was gold merely the thickness of a gold dinar, etc.,
פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דִּמְלֵאִים מִצְווֹת כְּרִמּוֹן וְכוּלֵי.
how much more so the transgressors of Israel who are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate, etc.
וְאָמְרוּ בָּזֶה לְשׁוֹן "אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ"
And here they used the wording “amar Reish Lakish” (“Reish Lakish said”),
וְלֹא "רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר" כְּמִי שֶׁבָּא לַחֲלוֹק,
and not “Reish Lakish amar,” as one introducing a disagreement;
מַשְׁמַע דְּמָר אָמַר חֲדָא וּמָר אָמַר חֲדָא וְלָא פְּלִיגֵי.
implying that one Master stated one truth and the other Master stated another truth, and they do not disagree.
וְזֶה תֵּימַהּ לִכְאוֹרָה:
And this is astonishing at first glance:
דְּאִם גַּם בְּכָל פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין שׁוֹלֵט,
for if the fire holds no dominion over all transgressors of Israel,
מַה צֹּרֶךְ לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ לוֹמַר רַק בְּתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מִפְּנֵי שֶׁגּוּפָן אֵשׁ?
what need was there for Rabbi Abbahu to state this exclusively regarding Torah scholars because their body is fire?
וְתוֹסָפוֹת שָׁם כָּתְבוּ
And Tosafot there wrote
דְּלָאו אַפּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּגוּפָן קָאָמַר,
that Reish Lakish was not speaking of transgressors of Israel who sin with their body,
דַּעֲלֵיהֶם אָמְרוּ [בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יז עַמּוּד א]:
concerning whom they stated in Rosh Hashanah (17a):
גֵּיהִנָּם כָּלָה וְהֵם אֵין כָּלִין, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
“Gehenna is consumed, but they are not consumed,” see there.
וּלְפִי דִּבְרֵיהֶם יֵשׁ לוֹמַר
And according to their words it can be suggested
דִּבְתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, אֲפִילּוּ הֵם פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּגוּפָן,
that regarding Torah scholars, even if they are transgressors of Israel who sin with their body,
גַּם כֵּן אֵין אוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׁוֹלֵט.
the fire of Gehenna likewise has no dominion.
אֲבָל [בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שָׁם] אִיתָא הָא דְּגֵיהִנָּם כָּלָה עַל מַחֲטִיאֵי הָרַבִּים כְּיָרָבְעָם וַחֲבֵירָיו;
However, in Rosh Hashanah there, that fate where Gehenna is consumed was said regarding those who cause the public to sin, like Jeroboam and his peers;
וּבְסַנְהֶדְרִין [קג רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב]
and in Sanhedrin (103b, beginning)
אַהָא דִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְלָכִים שֶׁהֵן יָרָבְעָם וַחֲבֵירָיו
concerning the three kings who are Jeroboam and his peers,
אָמַר רַב אַשִׁי: "נִפְתַּח בְּחַבְרִין",
Rav Ashi said: “Let us open our discourse with our colleagues,”
פֵּירֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י: שֶׁהָיוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים כְּמוֹתֵינוּ,
which Rashi explains: that they were Torah scholars like ourselves,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ: בְּרַבְרְבָתָא;
and afterward: “with our masters”;
הֲרֵי דְּגַם עַל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אָמְרוּ כֵּן.
behold they asserted this harsh judgment regarding scholars as well.
וּמִיהוּ אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר
However, it is possible to suggest
דְּמֵהַהוּא דְּ"הֵם אֵין כָּלִין" אֵין קוּשְׁיָא,
that from that dictum that “they are not consumed” there is no contradiction;
דְּהָא דְּ"אֵין שׁוֹלֵט" וְלֹא אָמְרוּ דְּאֵין נִכְנָסִים כְּלָל
for from the fact that they formulated “has no dominion” and did not say they do not enter at all,
מְבוֹאָר דְּנִכְנָסִים רַק שֶׁהָאוּר אֵין שׁוֹלֵט;
it is clear that they do enter, only that the fire does not consume;
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ [בִּמְנָחוֹת ק רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א]
and so our Sages stated in Menachot (100a)
שֶׁגַּם לַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁהוּא תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הוּכַן.
that even for a king who is a Torah scholar Gehenna was prepared.
וְאִם כֵּן, עַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּאֵין רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין שׁוֹלֵט כְּלָל שֶׁאֵין מַרְגִּישׁ כְּוִיַּית הָאֵשׁ,
And if so, perforce it does not mean that it has no effect whatsoever such that he feels not the scorch of the fire,
דְּאִם כֵּן לְאֵיזֶה צֹרֶךְ נִכְנָסִין וְלָמָּה הוּכַן לוֹ?
for if so, for what purpose do they enter, and why was it prepared for him?
וְגַם אָמְרוּ [בַּחֲגִיגָה טו עַמּוּד ב] בְּ'אַחֵר'
Furthermore they related in Chagigah (15b) regarding Acher
דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר הֶעֱלָה עָשָׁן מִקִּבְרוֹ לְדַיָּינֵיהּ,
that Rabbi Meir caused smoke to rise from his grave so that he be judged;
הֲרֵי דְּשָׁלַט בּוֹ הָאֵשׁ אַף שֶׁהָיָה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם.
behold the fire held sway over him even though he was an eminent Torah scholar.
וּמֵעִיקָּרָא שֶׁאָמְרוּ דְּלָא לְדַיָּינֵיהּ בִּשְׁבִיל הַתּוֹרָה,
And initially when the heavenly court declared that he should not be judged on account of the Torah,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַכְנִיסוֹ כְּלָל בְּגֵיהִנָּם,
this meant not bringing him into Gehenna at all;
דְּמֵאַחַר שֶׁדָּנוּהוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ עוֹלָם הַבָּא
for since they decreed that he should have no portion in the World to Come,
נָתְנוּ לוֹ שְׂכַר תּוֹרָתוֹ, שֶׁאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַפֵּחַ,
they paid him the reward for his Torah—for the Holy One withholds no reward—
שֶׁלֹּא יִדּוֹן וְיִצְטַעֵר כְּלָל בְּצַעַר גֵּיהִנָּם;
by sparing him from being judged and tormented in the suffering of Gehenna;
וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר אָמַר לְדוּנוֹ וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
while Rabbi Meir prayed that he be judged and purged so that he merit the World to Come;
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים חָזֵינַן דְּשָׁלַט אַף שֶׁכָּל גּוּפוֹ אֵשׁ.
and at any rate we observe that the fire held sway over him, even though his body was fire.

paragraphs.text: Chagigah 27a:8 then reports Reish Lakish’s teaching about the sinners of Israel. The golden altar’s covering was only the thickness of a gold dinar, yet fire did not master it; how much more so the sinners who are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate. These are two separately attributed teachings. The inference about how their scopes fit together is developed by Rav Tzadok; the Gemara does not separately formulate his explanation of why both are necessary.
