inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok reexamines which verse establishes the end of Gehinnom and asks what continued existence afterward would mean for the gravest offenders. He considers whether exclusion from the joy of the righteous could itself remain a punishment after the fire ends.

p: אַךְ מִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתַב בַּ"עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת" שָׁם [סוֹף פֶּרֶק א]
However, from what he wrote in Asarah Ma'amarot there (end of chapter 1)
דְּאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר נִצְחִי אֶלָּא בְּמִדַּת הַטּוֹב,
that you have no entity that is eternal except within the attribute of goodness,
וְכֵן כָּתַב [בְּפֶרֶק ה]
and as he likewise wrote in chapter 5
דִּבְהַנְהָגַת עוֹלָם הַבָּא אֵין רַע כָּל עִיקָּר,
that under the governance of the World to Come there is no evil whatsoever,
מַשְׁמַע דִּכְשֶׁיִּכְלֶה גֵּיהִנָּם יִכְלֶה כָּל רַע וְיִהְיֶה רַק טוֹב;
it implies that when Gehenna terminates, all evil will be obliterated and only goodness will exist;
וּמַשְׁמַע לְפִי זֶה
and according to this it implies
גַּם אוֹתָם רְשָׁעִים שֶׁאֵין כָּלִים יִהְיֶה לָהֶם אָז טוֹב.
that even those wicked who are not consumed will then experience goodness.
וְכֵן כָּתַב שָׁם [בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק ה]:
And so he wrote there at the end of chapter 5:
שֶׁרְשָׁעִים עוֹד אֵינָם,
that the wicked no longer exist as wicked,
רַק יֶשְׁנָם בִּמְצִיאוּת שָׁקֵט וְשַׁאֲנָן, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
rather they exist in a serene and tranquil state, see there.
וְצָרִיךְ לוֹמַר,
And one must say:
אַף דְּרַשִׁ״י בְּשַׁבָּת שָׁם פֵּירֵשׁ זֶה לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
even though Rashi in Shabbat there explained this dynamic of hunger and shame as occurring in the World to Come,
וְכֵן בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה אָמְרוּ "מִשְׁלוֹמַת רְשָׁעִים בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא",
and likewise in Bereishit Rabbah they stated “the retribution of the wicked in the World to Come,”
יָדוּעַ דְּכַמָּה מַדְרֵגוֹת בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא יֵשׁ.
it is known that there exist multiple gradations in the World to Come.
וְשָׁם [בְּשַׁבָּת] מַשְׁמַע שֶׁיֵּשׁ אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה,
And there in Shabbat it implies that there is eating and drinking,
וּבִבְרָכוֹת [יז עַמּוּד א] אִיתָא דְּאֵין בּוֹ אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה.
whereas in Berakhot (17a) it is taught that there is neither eating nor drinking.
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ "דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת" [בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין קד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב]
And it can be suggested that what the interpreters of esoteric traces taught in Sanhedrin (104b)
דְּכוּלָּם בָּאִין לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
that all of them eventually enter the World to Come,
שֶׁהֵם הִשִּׂיגוּ אוֹתָהּ מַדְרֵגָה דְּעוֹלָם הַבָּא
was because they apprehended that ultimate level of the World to Come
שֶׁאֵין מְצִיאוּת לָרַע עוֹד כְּלָל,
where there is no longer any ontological existence for evil at all,
וְאָז גַּם כָּל רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַיּוֹתֵר גְּרוּעִים "לֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח",
and then, even regarding the most degraded sinners of Israel, “none of them shall be cast out,”
דְּהֵם אֵין כָּלִים וּבָאִים לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
for they are not destroyed, and they enter the World to Come.

paragraphs.text: The same conclusion distinguishes souls purified through judgment, whom messengers receive for Gan Eden, from already examined souls needing no further purification. Chakor Din V:5, printed p.312, further says that there is no evil at all in the governance of the World to Come. These are stages and distinctions in Rema’s account; the sentence does not say that no persons, but only an abstract attribute, can endure eternally.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The Asarah Maamaros describes an ultimate order in which evil no longer exists and the wicked no longer remain wicked. Rav Tzadok relates this to differing levels of the world to come and to the esoteric interpretation of eventual restoration for the sinners of Israel.

p: וְיֵשׁ לְיַישֵׁב בָּזֶה דִּבְרֵי הָרַאֲבַ״ד בְּפֵירוּשׁוֹ לְעֵדֻיּוֹת [סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב מִשְׁנָה י]
And through this we can reconcile the words of the Ra'avad in his commentary to Eduyot (end of ch. 2),
אַהָא דְּמִשְׁפַּט רְשָׁעִים בְּגֵיהִנָּם מִקְּרָא דְּ"וְהָיָה מִדֵּי חֹדֶשׁ בְּחָדְשׁוֹ וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה סו, כג),
regarding the judgment of the wicked in Gehenna derived from the verse “And it shall come to pass from one New Moon to another, etc.” (Isaiah 66:23),
כָּתַב: "וּבְמִשְׁפַּט רְשָׁעִים מַיְירֵי וְכוּלֵי
where he wrote: “and it is speaking of the judgment of the wicked, etc.,
אוֹתָם שֶׁכָּפְרוּ בָּעִיקָּר וְכוּלֵי,
namely those who denied the fundamental principle of faith, etc.,
דִּינָם י״ב (שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר) חֹדֶשׁ".
their judgment is twelve months”
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּמַהַרְשָׁ״א בְּחִדּוּשֵׁי אַגָּדוֹת תָּמַהּ עַל זֶה מִבָּרַיְיתָא דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
And examine there in the Maharsha in Chiddushei Aggadot who was astonished at this from the Baraita of Rosh Hashanah,
וּבְתוֹסְפוֹת יוֹם טוֹב שָׁם כָּתַב לְהַגִּיהַּ, יְעֻיַּין שָׁם.
and in Tosafot Yom Tov there he proposed to emend the text, examine there.
וּלְפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי יֵשׁ לוֹמַר,
Yet according to what I have written, it can be maintained
דְּמִמַּה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ: "גֵּיהִנָּם כָּלָה",
that from the fact that the Sages stated: “Gehenna is consumed,”
עַל כָּרְחֲךָ הַךְ "לֹא תִכְבֶּה" לָאו לְעוֹלָם הוּא,
perforce this phrase “shall not be quenched” does not denote absolute eternity,
וּמְפָרֵשׁ דְּקָאֵי לְיוֹם הַדִּין הַגָּדוֹל,
and he interprets that it refers to the Great Day of Judgment;
וְאָז כָּל רְשָׁעִים כְּבָר קִבְּלוּ דִּינָם וְאֵשׁ שֶׁלָּהֶם נִכְבָּה,
and then all ordinary sinners have already undergone their sentence and their fire is quenched,
וְאֵלּוּ עֲדַיִן לֹא קִבְּלוּ כָּל עָנְשָׁם
whereas these heretics have not yet received their full punishment,
וְאֵשׁ שֶׁלָּהֶם עֲדַיִן לֹא תִכְבֶּה עַד שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ מִשְׁפָּטָם,
and their fire shall not be quenched until they have undergone their judgment,
וְאָז הֵם יְבַלּוּן הַשְּׁאוֹל,
and then they wear away Sheol,
כִּי בִּגְמַר דִּינָם יִבְלֶה וְיִכְלֶה,
for upon the completion of their sentence it will wear away and terminate,
שֶׁהוּא מְעוּכָּב רַק בִּשְׁבִילָם.
it being prolonged exclusively for their sake.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר כָּאן מִסֵּיפֵיהּ דִּקְרָא
And regarding this the Ra'avad interpreted here from the continuation of the verse
(וְאַף דִּקְרָא דְּ"וְהָיָה" קָדִים,
(and even though the verse “And it shall come to pass” precedes in Isaiah,)
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא נִשְׁנָה גַּם לְאַחֲרָיו
nevertheless it is repeated at the conclusion of the Book
לוֹמַר דְּקָאֵי גַּם עַל זֶה):
to show that it applies likewise to this:
"וְהָיָה מִדֵּי וְגוֹמֵר",
“And it shall come to pass from one New Moon, etc.,”
דְּמִשְׁפָּטָם אָז הוּא רַק י״ב חֹדֶשׁ מֵאוֹתוֹ יוֹם הַדִּין שֶׁאַחַר תְּחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים,
in that their judgment then endures for only twelve months from that Day of Judgment following the resurrection of the dead,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִכְלֶה גֵּיהִנָּם וְכָל הָרַע מִן הָעוֹלָם
and afterward Gehenna and all evil will be eradicated from the world,
וְיִתּוּקְנוּ גַּם הֵם,
and they too will be rectified,
שֶׁיָּבוֹאוּ בִּכְלַל "כָּל בָּשָׂר לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺת לְפָנַי"
so that they enter into the fellowship of “all flesh to worship before Me”
וּכְדוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל.
and in accordance with the interpreters of esoteric traces mentioned above

paragraphs.text: Mishnah Eduyos 2:10 assigns the wicked a twelve-month judgment in Gehinnom, deriving it from ‘from month to month’; Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri gives the period from Pesach to Shavuos, deriving it from ‘from Shabbos to Shabbos.’ Raavad connects ‘in its month’ with returning to the same month, and the invitation of ‘all flesh’ to worship with the following verse concerning the rebels. The received Raavad text identifies the deniers of the essential principle and those guilty of desecrating the Name; it does not contain Tosafos Yom Tov’s bracketed words ‘other wicked.’

paragraphs.text: The Great Day of Judgment after resurrection — Ran, Ramban, and Asarah Maamaros: Ran on Rosh Hashanah 3b identifies the baraisa of the three groups with the judgment after resurrection, ‘the great and awesome day of Hashem.’ Ramban, Sha’ar HaGemul 64, likewise places the universal Day of Judgment and resurrection at the close of the messianic era, before the enduring World to Come. The Asarah Maamaros, Maamar Chikur Din V:1, as explained by Yad Yehuda, further allows for souls not rectified in the judgment following death to return to Gehinnom for the judgment of resurrection. These sources provide the eschatological structure for Rav Tzadok’s phrase ‘from that Day of Judgment’; his additional claim that the final term is exactly twelve months remains his own reconciliation of the Raavad with the baraisa.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 49:15 and Rashi — who ‘consumes’ Sheol?: The phrase ‘ve-tzuram levalos Sheol’ is difficult, and modern translations also note its uncertainty. Rashi, following the Bavli, reads the form of the wicked as outlasting or wearing away Sheol: Gehinnom ends while they do not. Rav Tzadok develops that reading causally — Sheol remains operative only for their sake, and when their sentence is complete they, as it were, bring Sheol itself to its end. This interpretation is deliberately provisional. In the following se’if he cites a Seder Olam wording that can be read as God consuming their form and their form being destined for consumption in Sheol, and he acknowledges that this may overturn the present explanation.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 17a; Pesachim 54a — ‘their fire shall not be quenched’: Rosh Hashanah applies Yeshayahu 66:24 to the exceptional classes, saying that they are judged ‘for generations of generations,’ and then states that Gehinnom is consumed while they are not. Pesachim cites the same unquenched-fire language when teaching that the fire of Gehinnom, created on the second day, has no extinguishing forever. Rav Tzadok’s explanation is a harmonization: the phrase need not mean that each offender’s active sentence is literally endless; it can mean that the fire is not extinguished before the remaining judgment is completed. Neither Gemara explicitly states that the exceptional group receives only twelve months after resurrection; that is the novel reconciliation proposed here.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok proposes a reconciliation of the Raavad’s twelve-month judgment with descriptions of prolonged punishment. He reads the measure as beginning at the final judgment, after which Gehinnom and evil end, and connects this with the esoteric account of ultimate restoration.

p: וּמִיהוּ רָאִיתִי בְּ"סֵדֶר עוֹלָם רַבָּא" [סוֹף פֶּרֶק ג]
However, I saw in Seder Olam Rabbah (end of ch. 3)
דְּשָׁם אִיתָא הַךְ בָּרַיְיתָא,
that there this Baraita is taught,
וְשָׁם אִיתָא: "וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁשְּׁאוֹל בָּלָה
and there it reads: “and not only that, but Sheol wears away
(וְהוּא כִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב: "לְבַלּוֹת")
(matching the phrasing of Scripture: “to wear away”)
וְהֵן וְכוּלֵי,
while they, etc.,
מִזְּבוּל לוֹ – מִזְּבוּלוֹ מְבַלֶּה צוּרָתָם,
from His habitation—from His habitation He wears away their form,
וְצוּרָתָם לְבַלּוֹת לִשְׁאוֹל", עַד כָּאן.
and their form is to wear away Sheol,” until here.
מְבוֹאָר דְּסוֹף צוּרָתָם לְהִתְבַּלּוֹת גַּם כֵּן,
It is clear from this that ultimately their form is to wear away as well,
וְגַם לְשׁוֹן "וְלֹא עוֹד וְכוּלֵי"
and likewise the phrasing “and not only that, etc.”
מַשְׁמַע דְּבָא לְהוֹסִיף בָּזֶה בְּפוּרְעָנוּתָם,
implies that it comes to add an intensification to their retribution,
וְלֹא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי
and not as I wrote
וּלְפִי זֶה מַשְׁמַע:
And according to this reading it implies:
הָא דְּאֵין נִבְלִים מִקּוֹדֶם עַל יְדֵי גֵּיהִנָּם
that the fact that they do not wear away previously through Gehenna
הוּא לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם יְכוֹלָה לִשְׁלוֹט לְבַלּוֹתָם;
is because the fire of Gehenna lacks the dominion to wear them away;
אֲבָל אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם זוֹ הַגִּרְסָא מְדוּקְדֶּקֶת,
however, I do not know if this textual variant is authoritative,
דִּבְתוֹסֶפְתָּא דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין שָׁם הַגִּרְסָא כַּבַּגְּמָרָא,
since in the Tosefta of Sanhedrin there the reading matches our Gemara,
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר: סְמֵי חֲדָא מִקַּמֵּי תַּרְתֵּי.
and one may say: dismiss one isolated text before two authoritative sources.

paragraphs.text: Seder Olam Rabbah 3 first assigns twelve months to ordinary sinners of Israel who transgress Torah and mitzvos; it then introduces a distinct exceptional group with ‘but.’ For the latter it describes Gehinnom as shut upon them and judgment enduring for generations. The words must not be read as though the exceptional group were simply included in the earlier twelve-month sentence.

paragraphs.text: Its concluding exposition says that Sheol comes to an end while they do not, then adds: ‘From His abode He wears away their form, and their form is to be worn away in Sheol.’ The consulted electronic witness has ‘comes to an end’ at the opening, whereas Rav Tzadok’s main quotation has ‘wears away.’ His question turns on the additional form-wearing-away clause, present in Seder Olam but absent from the shorter Bavli and Tosefta formulations.

paragraphs.text: ‘And not only’ — an intensification that reopens Se’if 73: The connective ve-lo od ella normally adds a further and more severe consequence. Rav Tzadok therefore reads the longer Seder Olam wording as increasing the punishment: not only does Gehinnom fail to finish them, but their form is ultimately consumed from the divine abode. That reverses the proposal of the preceding se’if, where the ending of Gehinnom was presented as the stage after which final restoration could occur. His phrase ‘and not as I wrote’ is an explicit provisional retraction; the next se’if continues the investigation through Maharsha rather than treating the issue as closed.

paragraphs.text: Compare Tosafos Yom Tov on Eduyos 2:10, citing Raavad — the proposed emendation and its scope: On the Mishnah’s twelve-month judgment, Tosafos Yom Tov cites Raavad and proposes that Yeshayahu’s final vision concerns those who denied a foundational principle and also bear chillul Hashem, whereas other wicked are judged for twelve months. He says that this emendation is supported by Seder Olam and the opening chapter of Rosh Hashanah. The proposal clarifies which category receives which duration; it does not decide the separate question occupying Rav Tzadok here — whether the terms ‘consumed,’ ‘burned,’ and ‘ash’ describe absolute annihilation or a changed state from which restoration can still occur. This comparative source clarifies the categories and durations without deciding Rav Tzadok’s separate question about the meaning of consumption and ash.

paragraphs.text: Chagigah 27a — when the fire of Gehinnom ‘has no dominion’: Reish Lakish teaches that the fire of Gehinnom has no power over the sinners of Israel because even the ‘empty’ among them are full of mitzvos. That teaching can illuminate Rav Tzadok’s inference that Gehinnom may punish without being able to consume. It should not, however, be transferred mechanically to every person in Rosh Hashanah’s exceptional list, which includes heretics, informers, deniers, and those who caused the public to sin. Rav Tzadok therefore says only ‘according to this it implies’: the inability of Gehinnom to annihilate them is deduced from the disputed Seder Olam reading, not stated directly by Chagigah, and it does not remove judgment or suffering.

paragraphs.text: ‘Sami chada mi-kamei tartei’ — weighing one recension against two: The phrase ‘remove one before two’ is used in Talmudic and later commentary when one report or textual formulation conflicts with two concordant ones; Tosafos on Beitzah 38a is a classic example. Here the Tosefta and the Bavli both preserve the shorter statement ‘Sheol ends and they do not end,’ without Seder Olam’s added clause that God consumes their form. Rav Tzadok therefore considers setting aside the single longer reading before the two matching witnesses. Yet he deliberately writes ‘I do not know whether this reading is precise’: he does not erase Seder Olam’s wording dogmatically, but records the textual tension and leaves the conclusion open for further analysis.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: A variant in Seder Olam challenges Rav Tzadok’s preceding interpretation by describing the eventual wearing away of the sinners’ form as added punishment. He leaves the variant’s authority uncertain because the Talmud and Tosefta preserve a different reading.

p: וְשׁוּב רָאִיתִי בְּמַהַרְשָׁ״א בְּחִדּוּשֵׁי אַגָּדוֹת [בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שָׁם]
And subsequently I saw in the Maharsha in Chiddushei Aggadot (Rosh Hashanah ibid.)
כָּתַב דְּ"הֵם אֵין כָּלִין"
where he wrote that “they are not consumed”
לֹא לִמְעַלְיוּתָא כְּהַאי דְּסוֹטָה,
is not meant to their advantage as in that passage in Sotah,
רַק לִגְרִיעוּתָא,
rather to their detriment,
שֶׁיִּהְיוּ לְחֶרְפּוֹת עוֹלָם,
that they remain as eternal reproaches,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה סו, ה): "וְנִרְאֶה בְשִׂמְחַתְכֶם וְהֵם יֵבֹשׁוּ", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
as it is stated (Isaiah 66:5): “that we may see your joy, but they shall be ashamed,” see there.
וְזֶהוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל מֵהַגְּמָרָא דְּשַׁבָּת (קנג עַמּוּד א)
And this aligns with what I wrote above from the Gemara in Shabbat (153a)
וְלֹא כְּהַ"עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת".
and not as held by the Asarah Ma'amarot.
וּמַה שֶּׁהוּקְשָׁה לֵיהּ שָׁם: הָא דְּ"נִידּוֹנִין לְדוֹרֵי דוֹרוֹת", וְהִנִּיחַ בְּקוּשְׁיָא,
And as for the difficulty he raised there regarding their being “judged for generations of generations,” which he left unresolved,
לֹא קַשְׁיָא כְּלָל,
it is not difficult at all,
דְּהַהִיא כָּל יְמֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה קָאֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם דּוֹרוֹת,
for that phrasing refers to all the epochs of this world wherein successive generations exist,
וְגֵיהִנָּם כָּלָה לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
while Gehenna terminates in the World to Come,
דִּבְעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין לוֹ כְּבִיָּה,
since within this world its fire is unquenched,
וְאָז אֵין פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרָכוֹת יז עַמּוּד א]
and then procreation ceases as our Sages stated in Berakhot (17a)
וְאֵין עוֹד דּוֹרוֹת.
and there are no further generations.
וְעַיֵּין בַּ"עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת" [שָׁם פֶּרֶק א] עַל לְשׁוֹן "דּוֹרֵי דוֹרוֹת",
And see in Asarah Ma'amarot (ibid. ch. 1) on the phrase “generations of generations,”
וּבְפֵירוּשׁ "יַד יְהוּדָה" [אוֹת כה].
and in the commentary Yad Yehudah (sec. 25).
וְעַיֵּין עוֹד שָׁם בְּמַהַרְשָׁ״א לִפְנֵי זֶה,
And examine further there in the Maharsha prior to this,
דְּהָא דְּ"יִהְיֶה אֵפֶר" לֹא אַנְּשָׁמָה קָאֵי אֶלָּא הַגּוּף,
that the prophecy that they “shall be ashes” refers not to the soul but to the body,
דְּאֵין כָּלָה לְגַמְרֵי רַק נַעֲשָׂה אֵפֶר, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
in that it is not totally obliterated but rather reduced to ash, see there.
וּלְפִי דַּעְתִּי יֵשׁ לוֹמַר כְּדִבְרֵי "יַד יְהוּדָה" הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
And in my opinion one can assert like the words of the Yad Yehudah cited above
דְּאֵין נִשְׂרָף לְגַמְרֵי.
that the soul is not burned out of existence completely.
וְסַעַד לְדִבְרֵי מַהַרְשָׁ״א מָצָאתִי בַּתּוֹסֶפְתָּא שָׁם הַגִּרְסָא:
And support for the thesis of the Maharsha I found in the Tosefta there, where the reading is:
"נַפְשָׁן כָּלָה וְגוּפָן נִשְׂרַף וְגֵיהִנָּם פּוֹלְטָתַן וְנַעֲשִׂין אֵפֶר וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם,
“their soul is consumed and their body is burned, and Gehenna expels them and they become ash, etc.,” see there,
וּמִלָּשׁוֹן זֶה מְבוֹאָר דְּאַגּוּף קָאֵי.
and from this formulation it is explicit that turning to ash refers to the body.
וּבְ"סֵדֶר עוֹלָם רַבָּה" [שָׁם] הַגִּרְסָא:
And in Seder Olam Rabbah (ibid.) the reading is:
"נַפְשָׁן כָּלָה וְגוּפָן כָּלָה, וְהֵן נַעֲשִׂין אֵפֶר וְגֵיהִנָּם פּוֹלְטָתַן וְכוּלֵי",
“their soul is consumed and their body is consumed, and they become ash and Gehenna expels them, etc.,”
וְאָמַר בְּתַרְוַויְיהוּ לְשׁוֹן "כָּלָה",
employing for both soul and body the term “consumed,”
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מִדְּאִיחַר לַגּוּף מַשְׁמַע דְּאַגּוּף קָאֵי.
yet since it juxtaposes turning to ash directly after mentioning the body, it implies that it refers to the body.
אֲבָל לְפִי הַגִּרְסָא בְּתַלְמוּדֵנוּ לֹא מַשְׁמַע כֵּן,
However, according to the reading in our Talmud it does not imply this,
וְגַם לַגִּרְסָא דְּשָׁם לְשׁוֹן "כָּלָה" אַנֶּפֶשׁ,
and furthermore according to the reading there, the term “consumed” applies to the soul,
אִי אֵינוֹ אֵפֶר מַשְׁמַע דְּנִכְלָה לְגַמְרֵי.
so that if the soul does not become ash, it would imply that it is completely annihilated.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 153a; Yeshayahu 65:13–14 and 66:5 — survival can itself be deprivation: Rabbi Meir’s teaching in Shabbos does not describe the unprepared servants as annihilated. Both groups remain at the royal feast, but the righteous eat, drink, and rejoice while the others hunger, thirst, and experience shame. This supplies the model Rav Tzadok invokes against the Asarah Maamaros: continued existence may intensify exclusion rather than constitute a benefit. Maharsha’s prooftext, ‘it shall be seen in your joy, and they shall be ashamed,’ similarly defines the punishment through contrast with the joy of the righteous. These are Aggadic images of participation in, or deprivation from, divine delight; they are not a literal claim about physical nutrition in the World to Come.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 17a — ‘no procreation’ and the limit of ‘generations of generations’: Rav teaches that the World to Come has no eating, drinking, procreation, commerce, jealousy, hatred, or rivalry; the righteous instead enjoy the radiance of the Shechinah. Rav Tzadok infers from the absence of procreation that the phrase ‘for generations of generations’ can describe the entire remaining span of this world, while biological generations still succeed one another, without extending beyond the transition to the World to Come. Neither Berachos nor Rosh Hashanah states that reconciliation explicitly. The existing Yad Yehuda note records a different reading, counting four ‘generations’ and allowing repeated cycles of judgment and rectification.

paragraphs.text: Tosefta Sanhedrin 13:1; Seder Olam Rabbah 3; Rosh Hashanah 17a — three textual forms: The Tosefta reads: ‘their soul is consumed, their body is burned, Gehinnom casts them out, they become ash, and the wind scatters them.’ Seder Olam reads: ‘their soul is consumed, their body is consumed, they become ash, Gehinnom casts them out, and the wind disperses them.’ The Bavli reverses the first pair: ‘their body is consumed and their soul is burned,’ then mentions the wind. These changes in verb and sequence are precisely why Rav Tzadok weighs each recension separately. The Tosefta’s placement makes ‘they become ash’ follow the bodily burning most naturally, but the variants do not by themselves settle whether ‘consumed’ means total disappearance, loss of former form, or transformation into a remnant capable of later rectification.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok finds support in the Maharsha for continued existence as disgrace, while restricting “generations of generations” to the order of this world. He then compares textual witnesses to ask whether the ashes describe the body alone or also the soul, leaving a difficulty with the received Talmudic wording.

p: וְעַיֵּין בְּ"תַּנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ" [רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ג] אִיתָא
And see in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (ch. 3) where it is stated
דְּצַדִּיקִים יְלַמְּדוּ זְכוּת אַהָרְשָׁעִים שֶׁעָסְקוּ בְּמִצְווֹת,
that the righteous will advocate merit on behalf of the wicked who engaged in mitzvot,
וְיֹאמַר לָהֶן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: "רַפְּאוּ אוֹתָן",
and the Holy One, blessed be He, will say to them: “Heal them,”
וְהוֹלְכִין וְעוֹמְדִין עַל עַפְרָן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים וּמְבַקְּשִׁין עֲלֵיהֶם רַחֲמִים,
and they go and stand upon the dust of the wicked and plead for mercy upon them,
וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַעֲמִידָן מֵעֲפַר רַגְלֵיהֶם,
and the Holy One raises them up from the dust of their feet,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (מַלְאָכִי ג, כא): "וְעַסּוֹתֶם רְשָׁעִים [כִּי יִהְיוּ אֵפֶר תַּחַת כַּפּוֹת רַגְלֵיכֶם]", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
as it is stated (Malachi 3:21): “And you shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet,” see there.
וּמִדְּקָרֵי "עָפָר" וְלֹא "אֵפֶר" כִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב דְּמַיְיתֵי,
And from the fact that the Midrash terms it “dust” and not “ash” like the verse it cites,
מַשְׁמַע גַּם כֵּן דְּקָאֵי אַגּוּף הַנִּרְקָב וְנַעֲשָׂה עָפָר
it implies likewise that it refers to the physical body decomposing into dust
שֶׁיָּקוּם בִּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים.
which is destined to rise at the resurrection of the dead.
אֶלָּא דְּשָׁם מַשְׁמַע דְּצַדִּיקִים הוֹלְכִים לִמְקוֹמָן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים לִשְׁאוֹל לַעֲמוֹד עַל עַפְרָם,
Save that there it implies that the righteous go to the place of the wicked in Sheol to stand upon their dust,
וּכְגַמְרָא וְתוֹסֶפְתָּא וְסֵדֶר עוֹלָם רַבָּה אָמְרוּ
whereas in the Gemara, Tosefta, and Seder Olam Rabbah they stated
דְּרוּחַ מֵבִיא הָאֵפֶר לִמְקוֹם הַצַּדִּיקִים לְגַן עֵדֶן.
that the wind blows the ash to the dwelling of the righteous in Gan Eden.
וּמִדְּבָרָיו לָמַדְנוּ דְּאַף הֵם אֵין נִשְׁאָרִים וְנִכְלִים,
And from his words we derive that even these sinners do not remain permanently destroyed,
רַק עַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁנִּתְפַּזְּרִים תַּחַת הַצַּדִּיקִים חוֹזְרִים לָקוּם וְלִחְיוֹת.
rather through being scattered under the righteous they return to rise and live.
וְאִם כֵּן לֹא קַשְׁיָא מַה שֶּׁאָמַר דְּשַׁפִּיר עֲדִיפֵי מִמִּינִים,
And if so, it is not difficult why the Talmud considers them superior to heretics,
אֲפִילּוּ אִי גַּם הֵם אֵין כָּלִים אַחַר שֶׁגֵּיהִנָּם כָּלָה.
even if those heretics likewise are not consumed after Gehenna terminates.
וְשׁוּב רָאִיתִי בַּ"עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת" [שָׁם רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ז]
And subsequently I saw in Asarah Ma'amarot (ibid., beginning of ch. 7)
כָּתַב מִדְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּאֵפֶר זֶה בַּר גִּיבּוּל הוּא,
where he wrote on his own insight that this ash can be kneaded and reconstituted,
וַעֲתִידִים לִחְיוֹת עַל יְדֵי דִּמְעוֹת הַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁיַּעַבְרוּ בְּעֵמֶק הַבָּכָא
and they are destined to be revived through the tears of the righteous who pass through the Valley of Weeping
(לֹא יָדַעְתִּי לְאֵיזֶה צֹרֶךְ, לְמַאי דְּאָזֵיל הוּא לְגִרְסַת תַּלְמוּדֵנוּ
(though I do not know why this is necessary according to his following the Talmud's text
דְּרוּחַ מַפְרִיחַ הָאֵפֶר לְגַן עֵדֶן כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל לְהַחֲיוֹתָן),
that the wind blows the ash to Gan Eden as mentioned above to revive them),
יְעֻיַּין שָׁם בְּאֹרֶךְ.
examine there at length.
וְלֹא מַיְיתֵי דִּבְרֵי הַ"תַּנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה" הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל דִּמְפוֹרָשׁ כֵּן,
And he did not cite the words of Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah cited above where this is explicit,
וְזָכָה לְכַוֵּון הָאֱמֶת מֵעַצְמוֹ.
and he merited to hit upon the truth on his own.

paragraphs.text: Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 3 describes the Holy One and the righteous deliberating in Scripture, Mishnah, halachah and aggadah, declaring impurity and purity in their proper places. Offenders are then judged for different terms, with twelve months given as the general limit. The righteous plead that these people attended the synagogue, recited Shema and performed mitzvos. God responds, ‘If they did so, heal them.’ They stand over the offenders’ dust, pray for mercy, and God raises them from beneath their feet, citing Malachi 3:21, ‘You shall trample the wicked, for they shall be ash beneath the soles of your feet.’

paragraphs.text: The concrete mitzvah plea and conditional response belong to the account; it does not expressly promise undifferentiated restoration to every offender. Later in the same chapter, the named kings’ exclusion is repeated and idolatry continuing until death without repentance is distinguished from repentance followed by death, after which the person is like an enduring righteous one. Those qualifications must remain alongside the revival scene.

paragraphs.text: Malachi 3:21 says that the wicked become efer, ash, beneath the feet of the righteous. Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah3 instead describes the righteous standing over their afar, dust, and God raising them from beneath their feet. Rav Tzadok reads the changed noun as suggesting the bodily residue capable of revival. That inference comes from his comparison, not from the plain wording of Malachi alone. The surrounding prophecy contrasts destructive fire with the healing sun of righteousness.

paragraphs.text: Daniel 12:2 describes awakening from earth’s dust, some to everlasting life and others to reproach. Yechezkel37 describes bones reassembled with sinews, flesh, skin and spirit, then identifies the vision with the whole house of Israel and promises the opening of graves. These are qualified biblical comparisons; neither passage itself identifies Rosh Hashanah’s ash with ordinary grave-dust.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 17a; Tosefta Sanhedrin 13:1; Seder Olam Rabbah 3 — beneath the righteous, but not expressly ‘Gan Eden’: The Bavli says that after twelve months a wind disperses the punished beneath the soles of the righteous. The Tosefta adds that Gehinnom casts them out, they become ash, and the wind scatters them; Seder Olam similarly says that Gehinnom expels them and the wind disperses them beneath the righteous. None of these recensions explicitly names Gan Eden. Rav Tzadok’s description of the ash being brought to the righteous ‘in Gan Eden’ interprets the destination from their location. Tanna d’vei Eliyahu presents the complementary spatial image: instead of the remnant being carried to the righteous, the righteous go and stand over the wicked’s dust.

paragraphs.text: Tehillim 84:7–8 gives the Valley of Weeping and ascent from strength to strength. Eruvin 19a:4–5 applies the weeping to the offenders being judged: they shed tears and accept God’s judgment, including the preparation of Gehinnom for the wicked and Gan Eden for the righteous. Eruvin 19a:10 later describes Avraham raising them, with a specified exception involving intercourse with a gentile woman and failure of recognition; 19a:11 records Rav Kahana’s objection to the present-tense derivation about continued rebellion.

paragraphs.text: The waters become a spring, compared with Yechezkel’s water flowing from beneath the Sanctuary and the traditions in Shekalim and Middos; the divine response brings pure waters and the dew of resurrection. Only after a long time do these lost ones come to be counted among the righteous. The process is neither instantaneous nor solely another person’s act.

paragraphs.text: The chapter’s later account of partners in awakening mercy and Yad Yehudah’s explanation of divine prayer are distinguished from the earlier quotation. Rav Tzadok nevertheless retains his spatial question: if the ash was already carried to the righteous, why must they pass through the valley? His praise of independent agreement with Tanna DeBei Eliyahu does not withdraw that question.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Tanna DeBei Eliyahu’s account of the righteous praying over the wicked’s dust provides Rav Tzadok with a model of restoration after punishment. He compares it with the Asarah Maamaros’ reconstitution of the ashes and notes the different locations described by the sources.

p: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מַה דְּאֵין אוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׁוֹלֵט צָרִיךְ בֵּיאוּר,
And nevertheless, that which the Sages asserted—that the fire of Gehenna has no dominion—requires elucidation,
דְּאַף דְּחוֹזְרִין לָקוּם הוּא עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלַּת הַצַּדִּיקִים,
for even though they ultimately return to rise, this occurs through the prayer of the righteous,
אֲבָל אוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׂוֹרַפְתָּן לְגַמְרֵי.
whereas the fire of Gehenna initially burns them up entirely.
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר דִּבְלָאו הָכִי קָשֶׁה מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ [בְּעֵירוּבִין שָׁם יט עַמּוּד א] לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
And it can be said that even aside from this, it is difficult what the Gemara challenged there in Eruvin (19a) against Reish Lakish:
דִּקְרָא "וְאִשָּׁם לֹא תִכְבֶּה" (יְשַׁעְיָה סו, כד) בְּפוֹשְׁעֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
that the verse “and their fire shall not be quenched” (Isaiah 66:24) refers to the transgressors of the nations of the world,
וַהֲרֵי בַּבָּרַיְיתָא [דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שָׁם יז עַמּוּד א] מְפוֹרָשׁ דְּהוּא בְּמִינִין וְכוּלֵי,
seeing that in the Baraita in Rosh Hashanah (17a) it is explicit that this applies to heretics, etc.,
וּכְגוֹן יָרָבְעָם מֵרִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַחוֹטְאִים בְּאוֹתָן דְּבָרִים וְלֹא בָּאֻמּוֹת!
such as Jeroboam among the wicked of Israel who sin in those matters, and not among the nations!
תּוּ יֵשׁ לְדַקְדֵּק מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ [בְּעֵירוּבִין שָׁם]
Furthermore, one must examine why they formulated in Eruvin there
שֶׁהִקְשָׁה דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אַדְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ,
that they challenged the statement of Reish Lakish against the statement of Reish Lakish,
מַה עִנְיָן לְהַעֲמִיד בְּקוּשְׁיָאתָם מִדְּרָשַׁת רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּ"פָּשְׁעֵי וְאָזְלֵי"?
for what point was there in anchoring their objection in Reish Lakish's exposition that “they continue sinning”?
וְאֵין הַקּוּשְׁיָא מִזֶּה, רַק מִגּוּפֵיהּ דִּקְרָא מֵ"אִשָּׁם לֹא תִכְבֶּה",
For the objection arises not from that rabbinic exposition, but from the body of the biblical verse itself, from “their fire shall not be quenched,”
וַהֲוָה לֵיהּ לוֹמַר רַק: קָשֶׁה אַדְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ!
and the Talmud should merely have said: it is difficult against Reish Lakish!
(וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִׁ״י דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: "דְּאִם כֵּן",
(And examine there in Rashi, heading: “De'im ken,”
וְהָא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ בְּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹקֵי וְכוּלֵי,
where he explains that Reish Lakish established his interpretation regarding the transgressors of Israel, etc.,
וְאֵינוֹ מוּבָן, דְּהָא בְּדִבְרֵי רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אֵין רְאָיָה בְּאֵיזֶה פוֹשְׁעִים קָאֵי
and this is incomprehensible, for in the explicit words of Reish Lakish there is no indication which transgressors he is addressing,
אִם הוּא בְּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דַּוְוקָא).
whether it refers specifically to the transgressors of Israel
וְלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ לְהַקְשׁוֹת דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אַדְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
And it is structurally inapplicable to frame a challenge as “Reish Lakish against Reish Lakish”
רַק אִם הַקּוּשְׁיָא מִדְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ.
unless the internal contradiction emerges directly from Reish Lakish's own words.
וְנִרְאֶה דְּפֵירוּשׁ "אֵין שׁוֹלֵט בָּהֶם",
And it appears that the true meaning of “has no dominion over them”
הַיְינוּ בְּעַצְמִיּוּתוֹ וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם שְׁלִיטָה כְּלָל,
is that over his essential being and the primordial root of his soul the fire holds no dominion whatsoever,
וַאֲפִילּוּ לְהַכְאִיב לוֹ.
not even to inflict agonizing pain.
וְעִיקַּר אוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם הוּא לְכַלּוֹת וּלְבַעֵר הָרָע מִן הָעוֹלָם,
And the quintessential purpose of the fire of Gehenna is to consume and eradicate evil from the universe,
וְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם קוֹצִים כְּסוּחִים מִשָּׁרְשָׁם
and the nations of the world are like cut thorns from their very root,
וּבָאֵשׁ יִצַּתּוּ
and are kindled in the fire,
וְ"לִהַט אֹתָם הַיּוֹם הַבָּא" (מַלְאָכִי ג, יט),
and “the day that comes shall burn them up” (Malachi 3:19),
שֶׁלֹּא יִשָּׁאֵר מֵהֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ וְעָנָף,
so that there shall not remain of them root or branch,
שֶׁיִּכְלוּ וִיבוֹעֲרוּ לְגַמְרֵי.
that they be obliterated and purged entirely.
אֲבָל בְּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, "יִתַּמּוּ חַטָּאִים" כְּתִיב וְלֹא "חוֹטְאִים"
However, regarding the transgressors of Israel, “Let sins cease” is written, and not “sinners,”
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרָכוֹת י רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א],
as our Sages stated in Berakhot (10a),
כִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל דְּבוּקִים בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים
because the essential root of all souls of Israel clings unto the living God,
שֶׁ"חֵלֶק ה' עַמּוֹ" (דְּבָרִים לב, ט).
for “Hashem's portion is His people” (Deuteronomy 32:9).
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּקִדּוּשִׁין לו עַמּוּד א]
And as they stated in Kiddushin (36a)
דַּאֲפִילּוּ לֵית בְּהוּ הֵימָנוּתָא וּפָלְחֵי לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
that even when they appear devoid of faith and worship idols,
דְּיֵאָמֵר לָהֶם "לֹא עַמִּי"
such that it is said unto them “you are not My people,”
וּלְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן כְּאִלּוּ אֵינָם עַמּוֹ,
and to outward appearances it seems as though they are not His nation,
שֶׁהֵם חֵלֶק ה', מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים
inwardly they remain Hashem's portion, believers the children of believers,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּשַׁבָּת צז רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א],
as they stated in Shabbat (97a),
וְזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה
and the seed of Jacob whose bed was whole,
שֶׁאֵין בְּלִבָּם אֶלָּא אֶחָד כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּפְסָחִים נו עַמּוּד א].
wherein in their inner heart resides none other than the One, as they stated in Pesachim (56a).
דְּהוֹשֵׁעַ קְרָאָם "לֹא עַמִּי"
For Hosea called them “not My people”
בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: הַחֲלִיפֵם בְּאֻמָּה אַחֶרֶת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [שָׁם פז סוֹף עַמּוּד א],
on account of having urged the Almighty: Exchange them for another nation, as they stated in Pesachim (87a),
שֶׁהָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לְנַתֵּק שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי הַחֲטָאִים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
assuming that it was possible to sever the name of Israel and the root of Jewish identity through the accumulation of sins, Heaven forbid,
עַד שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: "בָּנַי הֵם, בְּנֵי בְּחוּנַי וְכוּלֵי",
until the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: “They are My children, the children of My tested ones, etc.,”
וְשֶׁיְּבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים לְבַטֵּל הַגְּזֵירוֹת שֶׁבִּשְׁבִילוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [שָׁם עַמּוּד ב].
and instructed him to plead for mercy to annul the harsh decrees provoked through him, as they stated there (87b).
כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁבַּדּוֹר לְמַטָּה מַסְכִּים לְמִדַּת הַדִּין הַמְקַטְרֶגֶת,
For when the righteous leader of the generation below consents to the prosecuting attribute of strict justice,
נִסְתַּתְּמוּ טַעֲנַת מִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים וְנִגְמַר הַדִּין,
the arguments of the attribute of mercy are silenced and the harsh sentence is finalized,
וּמִצַּד מִדַּת הַדִּין הָיָה כֵן.
and from the perspective of strict justice it was indeed so.
אֲבָל בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּת מִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים הִשִּׂיג
However, upon the reawakening of the attribute of mercy, Hosea comprehended
דִּ"בִמְקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם לֹא עַמִּי אַתֶּם, יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם בְּנֵי אֵל חָי" (הוֹשֵׁעַ ב, א),
that “in the place where it was said unto them: You are not My people, it shall be said unto them: You are the children of the living God” (Hosea 2:1),
דְּכַאֲשֶׁר יִתַּמּוּ חַטָּאִים, רְשָׁעִים עוֹד אֵינָם
in that when sins cease, the wicked as such no longer exist
וְנִשְׁאָר הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַטּוֹב,
and the pristine, holy root alone endures,
כִּי כָּל חֲטָאֵיהֶם הֵם רַק מִצַּד הַהוּצֵי וְחוֹחִים הַסּוֹבְבִים לְאָסָא וְשׁוֹשַׁנָּה.
for all their sins stem merely from the briars and thorns encircling the myrtle and the rose.
וְיֵצֶר הָרָע יוֹשֵׁב עַל שְׁנֵי מִפְתְּחֵי הַלֵּב בַּפְּתִיחָה וּבַהַתְחָלָה,
And the evil inclination perches upon the two portals of the heart at the opening and threshold,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "לַפֶּתַח חַטָּאת רֹבֵץ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ד, ז);
as it is stated: “at the door sin couches” (Genesis 4:7);
וְהַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁלִּבָּם בִּרְשׁוּתָן
and the righteous who have their heart in their domain
אֵין מַנִּיחִין אוֹתוֹ לִכָּנֵס.
do not permit it to enter.
וְהָרְשָׁעִים הֵן בִּרְשׁוּת לִבָּן,
Whereas the wicked are in the domain of their heart,
שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּכְנַס, אַף שֶׁתְּחִלָּתוֹ הֵלֶךְ וְאוֹרֵחַ,
so that once it has entered, even though initially it arrived merely as a passerby and guest,
בַּסּוֹף נַעֲשָׂה בַּעַל הַבַּיִת שֶׁמְּמַלֵּא כָּל חַדְרֵי הַלֵּב,
in the end it becomes the master of the house, filling all the chambers of the heart,
עַד שֶׁשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַטּוֹב נֶעְלָם לְגַמְרֵי,
until the inner root of good is totally submerged,
וְנַעֲשָׂה הוּא בַּעַל הַבַּיִת וּכְאִלּוּ שָׁרְשׁוֹ רָע.
and the evil inclination reigns as master of the house as though the person's root were intrinsically evil.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 17a:3 first gives the bodily sinners of Israel and of the nations a twelve-month judgment, with bodily consumption, soul-burning and scattering beneath the righteous. It then introduces the exceptional classes separately in 17a:4–5, including those who sinned and caused others to sin ‘such as Yerovam ben Nevat and his companions,’ with judgment for generations and the statement that Gehinnom ends while they do not.

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 19a:6–9 contrasts acceptance of judgment with Reish Lakish’s statement that the wicked do not repent even at Gehinnom’s entrance, deriving continuing rebellion from ‘those who rebel,’ rather than ‘those who rebelled.’ It distinguishes Israel’s sinners from those of the nations and adds that otherwise Reish Lakish would contradict his own teaching about fire’s inability to master Israel’s sinners.

paragraphs.text: Rashi, s.v. de-im ken, explains the conditional contradiction: if Reish Lakish applies the unquenched-fire verse to Israel’s sinners, it conflicts with his other statement. Rav Tzadok asks what establishes that assignment and why the objection is framed between the teachings rather than from the verse alone. The rescue account and Rav Kahana’s subsequent objection in19a:10–11 remain distinct stages of the sugya, not one undifferentiated explanation.

paragraphs.text: Isaiah 33:12 and Malachi 3:19-21 - cut thorns, consuming fire, and 'root and branch': Isaiah describes peoples becoming like burnings of lime and like cut thorns kindled in fire. Malachi depicts the coming day burning the arrogant and evildoers like stubble, leaving neither root nor branch, while the righteous tread the wicked as ash. Rav Tzadok combines these prophetic images into a contrast between evil that is uprooted at its source and the sins of Israel that can be burned away while a good root remains. The verses themselves speak in broad prophetic language; their assignment to the precise metaphysical categories developed here is Rav Tzadok's interpretive construction.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok locates the deepest protection from Gehinnom in the essential root of Israel’s soul, which the fire cannot destroy or pain. Its work removes the evil surrounding and obscuring that root; the account of Hoshea illustrates how mercy reveals the enduring identity hidden by sin.

p: וְהֵן הֵם אוֹתָם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
And these are the archetypes of those who have no portion in the World to Come.
וְ"כָל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And “All Israel have a portion in the World to Come,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים לְעוֹלָם יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ וְגוֹמֵר"
as it is stated: And your people are all righteous, they shall inherit the land forever, etc.” (Sanhedrin 90a),
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ אוֹתָם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
and perforce those who have no portion in the World to Come
הֵם "לֹא עַמּוֹ" וְאֵינָם בִּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
are categorized as “not My people” and are excluded from the collective community of Israel;
דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא אָמְרוּ: "חוּץ מֵאֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם וְכוּלֵי",
which is why the Mishnah did not formulate: “except for those who have no, etc.,”
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּכָל מָקוֹם דְּחָשְׁבִינַן כְּלָל וּמוֹצִיא אֵיזֶה מֵהַכְּלָל.
as our Sages routinely formulate whenever stating an overarching rule and then excepting individuals from that rule.
אֲבָל אֵלּוּ אֵינָם מוּצָאִים מֵהַכְּלָל,
However, these individuals are not formally excepted from the rule,
דְּמִי שֶׁהוּא מִכְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם עַמּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְנַחֲלָתוֹ,
for whoever truly belongs to the body of Israel who are His people and His heritage,
אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
it is impossible that they should lack a portion in the World to Come.
אֲבָל אֵלּוּ, חֲטָאֵיהֶם גָּרְמוּ
However regarding these, their sins caused
דְּ"נֵר ה' נִשְׁמַת אָדָם" (מִשְׁלֵי כ, כז),
that “the candle of Hashem is the soul of man” (Proverbs 20:27),
שֶׁהוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּ"צוּר לְבָבִי וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים עג, כו),
which is the transcendent root of “the rock of my heart, etc.” (Psalms 73:26),
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
in that the Holy One is the innermost heart of Israel,
נֶאֱפַל וְנֶחְשַׁךְ עַל יְדֵי עֲבֵירָה
became eclipsed and darkened through transgression
שֶׁמְּכַבָּה נֵר מִצְוָה הַמְּאִירָה לְהַצִּיל מִן הַחֵטְא.
which extinguishes the candle of the mitzvah that radiates to protect from sin.
כִּי "עֲבֵירָה גּוֹרֶרֶת עֲבֵירָה",
For “one transgression drags another transgression in its wake,”
כְּדַרְכּוֹ שֶׁל יֵצֶר הָרָע: הַיּוֹם אוֹמֵר עֲשֵׂה כָּךְ, וּמָחָר וְכוּלֵי,
such being the crafty method of the evil urge: today he says do this, tomorrow do that,
וְעַד שֶׁאוֹמֵר לוֹ: "לֵךְ עֲבוֹד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה" (שַׁבָּת קה עַמּוּד ב),
until he finally incites him: “Go and serve idols” (Shabbat 105b),
שֶׁהוּא עֲקִירַת הַיַּהֲדוּת לְגַמְרֵי;
which represents the absolute uprooting of Jewish identity;
דִּ"יהוּדִי" נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם הַכְּפִירָה בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
for a “Jew” (Yehudi) is named on account of denying idolatry
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּמְגִלָּה יג רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א],
as our Sages stated in Megillah (13a),
כִּי לָמוּד הוּא אוֹתוֹ הַשֵּׁבֶט לְבַעֵר עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה].
for that tribe is accustomed to eradicate idolatry, as stated in Bereishit Rabbah.
וְעַל כֵּן מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד מִזַּרְעוֹ,
And therefore the Messiah, son of David, emerges from his lineage,
שֶׁהוּא יְבַעֵר כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע מִן הָעוֹלָם,
for he will thoroughly purge every root of evil from the universe,
עַד שֶׁיְּבוּלַּע גַּם הַמָּוֶת הַבָּא מִזּוּהֲמַת נָחָשׁ
until even physical death, which was introduced through the contamination of the Serpent,
שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת שׁוֹרֶשׁ זוּהֲמַת הָרָע בָּאָדָם,
which is the primal source of the contamination of evil in man, will be swallowed up forever,
שֶׁלֹּא יִרְבַּץ עוֹד גַּם אֵצֶל הַפֶּתַח.
so that sin will no longer couch even at the portal.
וְאָז "יְבֻקַּשׁ עֲוֺן יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֵינֶנּוּ" (יִרְמְיָה נ, כ),
And then “the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none” (Jeremiah 50:20),
כִּי כָּל הַחֲטָאִים "כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ" (יְשַׁעְיָה א, יח),
for all sins “shall be as white as snow” (Isaiah 1:18),
כַּאֲשֶׁר יִתְגַּלֶּה שֶׁהַכֹּל הָיָה רַק בְּסִבַּת הַיֵּצֶר וְהַזּוּהֲמָא הַסּוֹבֶבֶת
when it will be overtly disclosed that everything occurred solely through the catalyst of the external urge and surrounding defilement,
וְלֹא מֵעֶצֶם שָׁרְשָׁם.
and did not touch their pristine ontological root.
וּכְשֶׁיְּבוֹעַר זֶה, יַחֲזוֹר לְהָאִיר נֵרוֹ כְּבָרִאשׁוֹנָה,
And when this encrustation is eradicated, his candle will resume shining as in the beginning,
וְהוּא הָאוֹר שֶׁל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית הַגָּנוּז לַצַּדִּיקִים לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא
which is the primordial light of the six days of Creation hidden away for the righteous in the time to come,
שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים,
when all of Israel will be revealed as righteous,
דְּאָז יִתְגַּלּוּ עִנְיָנָם הַכֹּל שֶׁהוּא כֵן.
for then the true inner reality of all their affairs will be revealed as having been holy.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 90a, Mishnah: “All Israel have a share in the World to Come, as it says (Yeshayah 60): ‘and your people are all righteous, they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to glory.’ And these are the ones who have no share in the World to Come: one who says there is no resurrection of the dead from the Torah, and [one who says] there is no Torah from Heaven, and an epikoros. R’ Akiva says: also one who reads the external books, and one who whispers over a wound and says ‘all the illness that I placed in Egypt I will not place upon you, for I am Hashem your healer.’ Abba Shaul says: also one who pronounces the [Divine] Name by its letters.”

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 90a - 'All Israel' and 'these have no share': The Mishnah first states the universal rule, 'All Israel have a share in the World to Come,' and then introduces the listed cases with ve'elu she'ein lahem, 'and these are the ones who have no share.' Rav Tzadok makes a precise inference from the fact that it does not say chutz me'elu, 'except these': the second clause is not a simple external exception cut away from Israel's essential covenant, but describes persons in whom sin has concealed the aspect by which they are counted as His people and inheritance. When that concealment is removed, the universal opening can again be revealed. This grammatical-ontological distinction is Rav Tzadok's interpretation; the Mishnah itself states the rule and the exclusion without explaining their reconciliation.

Rav Tzadok applies the imagery to a lamp obscured by sin while the inward root remains.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok reads the Mishnah’s share in the world to come through the distinction between Israel’s enduring inner root and the identity eclipsed by accumulated sin. In his account of the ultimate future, removal of that covering allows the original light and righteousness to appear again.

p: וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג זֶה,
And in this physical world it is impossible to comprehend this,
שֶׁעֲדַיִן אֵין הִתְגַּלּוּת מֵאוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ;
since the manifest illumination of the Messiah has not yet broken through;
רַק דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת אָמְרוּ שֶׁכֻּלָּם יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
only the interpreters of esoteric traces asserted that all of them possess a share in the World to Come,
(סַנְהֶדְרִין קד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב),
(Sanhedrin 104b),
שֶׁהֵם הִשִּׂיגוּ רְשִׁימוּ הַנִּשְׁאָר מֵאוֹר הַנִּיתָּק מֵהֶם
in that they apprehended the indestructible trace remaining from the light that was superficially detached from them
עַל יְדֵי תּוֹקֶף הַחֲטָאִים הַבָּאִים עַל יְדֵי יֵצֶר הָרָע שֶׁנִּתְגַּבֵּר עֲלֵיהֶם.
through the intensity of sins induced by the evil urge overpowering them.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמִּגּוּף הָאָדָם,
And just as regarding the physical body of a human being,
הֲגַם שֶׁיָּשׁוּב אֶל הָאָרֶץ כְּשֶׁהָיָה וְנַעֲשָׂה תַּרְוַוד רָקָב וְעַפְרָא בְּעָלְמָא,
even though it returns to the earth as it was and decomposes into a ladleful of rot and mere dust,
הוּא חוֹזֵר וְקָם בִּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים אוֹתוֹ גּוּף עַצְמוֹ;
that very same body returns and rises at the resurrection of the dead;
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע:
and concerning this profound mystery did that wicked Balaam declare (Numbers 23:10):
"מִי מָנָה עֲפַר יַעֲקֹב, וּמִסְפָּר אֶת רֹבַע [יִשְׂרָאֵל]",
“Who can count the dust of Jacob, or number the stock of Israel?”
כִּי הוּא הִשִּׂיג מַעֲלַת פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
for he grasped the virtue of the transgressors of Israel and of those who have no portion in the World to Come,
דְּיֵשׁ לָהֶם קְצָת שַׁיָּיכוּת עִם מַדְרֵגָתוֹ,
in that they held a slight, external connection to his own rung,
שֶׁגַּם הוּא נִמְנָה בַּמִּשְׁנָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ עַמּוּד א) עִם אוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
since he too was enumerated in the Mishnah (Sanhedrin 90a) among those who have no portion in the World to Come.
אֲבָל דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת לֹא דָּרְשׁוּ עָלָיו,
However, the interpreters of esoteric traces did not include him in their expounding of eventual redemption,
כִּי הוּא לֹא נִכְלַל עִמָּהֶם;
for he was not integrated with them;
וּבְבַמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה [רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה יד, א] מְפוֹרָשׁ: "חוּץ מִבִּלְעָם",
and in Bemidbar Rabbah (14:1) it is explicit: “except for Balaam,”
כִּי הוּא שָׁרְשׁוֹ רָע
because his essential root is inherently evil,
וְלֹא שֶׁנִּיתַּק מִמֶּנּוּ,
and not merely that good was severed from him,
וְלֹא נִמְצָא בּוֹ רְשִׁימוּ כְּלָל.
and no holy trace exists within him at all.
וְהוּא הִכִּיר מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּזֶה:
And Balaam recognized the unique preeminence of Israel in this regard:
"כִּי מֵרֹאשׁ צֻרִים אֶרְאֶנּוּ" (בַּמִּדְבָּר כג, ט),
“For from the top of the rocks I see him” (Numbers 23:9),
מֵהַתְחָלַת הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּ"צוּר לְבָבִי וְחֶלְקִי [אֱלֹהִים לְעוֹלָם]" (תְּהִלִּים עג, כו),
from the primordial inception of the root of “God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever” (Psalms 73:26),
שֶׁאַף שֶׁהִגְדִּילוּ עֲוֺנוֹת, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ טוֹב לֹא נִיתַּק לְגַמְרֵי.
showing that even when they multiplied iniquities, nonetheless the good root was never completely severed.
וְעַל כֵּן: "מָה אֶקֹּב לֹא קַבֹּה אֵל" (בַּמִּדְבָּר כג, ח),
And therefore: “How shall I curse, whom God has not cursed?” (Numbers 23:8),
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה [בִּבְרָכוֹת ז עַמּוּד א]: אַף בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָיוּ רְאוּיִם לִקְלָלָה.
and our Sages stated in Berakhot (7a): even during the very times when they were deserving of a curse.
כִּי "לֹא הִבִּיט אָוֶן בְּיַעֲקֹב וְלֹא רָאָה עָמָל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל" (בַּמִּדְבָּר כג, כא),
For “He has not beheld iniquity in Jacob, neither has He seen perverseness in Israel” (Numbers 23:21),
דְּזֶהוּ אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם עָמָל וְאָוֶן,
meaning even when there appears within them outward perverseness and iniquity,
וְהוּא כְּשֶׁיּוֹרְדִים עַד לֶעָפָר,
and that is when they descend down to the very dust,
שֶׁהוּא הַיְרִידָה לַמַּדְרֵגָה הַיּוֹתֵר תַּחְתּוֹנָה.
which represents the descent to the absolute lowest tier.
וְגַם זֶה "מִי מָנָה וְסָפַר רְבִיעִיּוֹתֵיהֶם",
And regarding this too: “who can count and number their cohabitations (revi'oteihem),”
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה [בְּנִדָּה לא עַמּוּד א]:
and our Sages expounded in Niddah (31a):
טִיפָּה לְהַצְדִּיק,
a drop [from which] a righteous person [will be formed],
מִצַּד "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים" (יְשַׁעְיָה ס, כא),
from the perspective of “And your people are all righteous” (Isaiah 60:21),
וּבְכָל רֹבַע יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ טִיפָּה הַנִּקְרָא "צַדִּיק",
and within every cohabitation of Israel there is a holy drop termed “tzaddik,”
דְּעַל דָּבָר זֶה נִסְמֵית עֵינוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע וְכוּלֵי.
and over this sublime mystery was the eye of that wicked one blinded, etc.
כִּי זֶהוּ הַהֶבְדֵּל שֶׁבֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים,
For this is the essential difference between Israel and the nations,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה ד עַמּוּד א]
as they stated in Rosh Hashanah (4a)
דְּעוֹשֶׂה מִצְוָה לְקַבֵּל פְּרָס וּלַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ
that one who performs a mitzvah in order to receive a reward and for his own pleasure,
בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָא "צַדִּיק גָּמוּר",
in an Israelite he is termed “completely righteous,”
וּבְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם חָשֵׁיב לֵיהּ הֶחְמִיץ עַל יְדֵי זֶה.
whereas among the nations of the world it is considered corrupted and soured through this self-interest.
וְכֵן [בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא י עַמּוּד ב]
And likewise in Bava Batra (10b)
דְּנֶחְשָׁב חֵטְא לָהֶם כְּשֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין אֶלָּא לְהִתְגַּדֵּר וְכַדּוֹמֶה,
that it is reckoned as a sin to them when they perform charity solely to boast and the like,
שֶׁאֶצְלָם מַחֲשָׁבָה זוֹ הִיא הָעִיקָּר.
because with them this corrupt thought is the primary essence of the act.
דְּמִטַּעַם זֶה בְּהוּ מַחֲשָׁבָה רָעָה מִצְטָרֶפֶת לְמַעֲשֶׂה וְלֹא טוֹבָה,
And for this reason, with the nations a bad thought combines with deed, whereas a good thought does not,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי [פֶּרֶק א דְּפֵאָה] וְתוֹסָפוֹת [קִדּוּשִׁין לט סוֹף עַמּוּד ב],
as they stated in the Yerushalmi (Peah, chapter 1) and Tosafot in Kiddushin (39b),
וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְהֵיפֶךְ.
while in Israel it is the exact reverse.

paragraphs.text: Mishnah Sanhedrin10:2, also Sanhedrin90a:17, lists three kings and four commoners without a share in the World to Come: Yerovam, Achav and Menasheh; Bilaam, Doeg, Achitofel and Geichazi. Rabbi Yehudah disputes Menasheh’s exclusion, citing his prayer and restoration, while the Sages distinguish restoration to kingship from restoration to the World to Come.

paragraphs.text: Berachos7a explains the attempted curse through the moment of divine anger, which did not occur during Bilaam’s mission. Rav Tzadok adds an inward reading: the rocks signify Israel’s root, dust the lowest descent, and the absence of perceived iniquity means that sin does not fully sever the good root. That spiritual synthesis is his, rather than the Bavli’s literal explanation.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah4a:2–3 calls the person giving charity ‘so that my children live’ or ‘so that I merit the World to Come’ completely righteous, and distinguishes Israel from the nations. Rashi explains the Israelite case as a heart directed to Heaven that does not protest against God when adversity comes, but attributes suffering to its own wrongdoing. This qualification prevents turning the saying into a rule that motive never matters.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The interpreters of esoteric traces perceive a remaining holy root even where it is hidden from present sight. Rav Tzadok compares this with bodily resurrection, distinguishes Bilaam from the Israelite figures in that interpretation, and examines how inner intention affects the meaning of mixed deeds.

p: וּפְרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה הוּא מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה,
And procreation is a positive biblical commandment,
אֲבָל מִצַּד זוּהֲמַת הַנָּחָשׁ אֲפִילּוּ חָסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים מִתְכַּוֵּין לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ,
yet through the defilement of the Serpent even the most pious of the pious inadvertently intends for personal physical pleasure,
וּמִצַּד הַמְשָׁכַת הַזּוּהֲמָא לְכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת
and due to the transmission of this defilement to all generations
דְּ"הֵן בְּעָווֹן חוֹלָלְתִּי, וּבְחֵטְא יֶחֱמַתְנִי אִמִּי" (תְּהִלִּים נא, ז).
Scripture laments: “Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity, and in sin did my mother conceive me” (Psalms 51:7).
אֲבָל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אָזְלִינַן בָּתַר הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהוּא מִצְוָה
However, in Israel we evaluate by the essential deed which is a mitzvah,
וְנֶחְשָׁב בָּזֶה "צַדִּיק גָּמוּר",
and he is reckoned through this as “completely righteous,”
וּמִזֶּה נִמְשָׁךְ דְּ"עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים".
and from this emerges that “your people are all righteous.”
וְכָל הַחֲטָאִים שֶׁנִּמְשְׁכוּ מִצַּד הַזּוּהֲמָא
And all sins that are drawn forth from the defilement
הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִצַּד כַּוָּונַת הֲנָאָה לְגַרְמֵיהּ,
which stems from the intention of selfish gratification,
אֵינָן נוֹגְעִים לְהָעֶצֶם וְהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ.
do not touch the pristine essence and root of the soul.
וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה נִקְרָא אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע "מַחֲלִיק לָשׁוֹן",
And concerning this insight was that wicked Balaam called “a flatterer with his tongue,”
שֶׁהִסִּיתָם בָּזֶה לְמַעֲשֵׂה דְּשִׁטִּים,
in that he incited Israel through this truth into the sinful deed of Shittim,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּדְבָרִים רַבָּה [רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה א, ב]
and as our Sages stated in Devarim Rabbah (1:2)
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה כָּל כַּוָּונָתוֹ:
that this was his entire subversive strategy:
לְגַלּוֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ יַגְדִּילוּ חֲטָאִים לֹא יֹאבְדוּ מַעֲלָתָם.
to disclose to Israel that even if they multiply sins they will never lose their exalted status.
וְזֶה הָיָה הָעֵצָה רָעָה שֶׁלּוֹ:
And this was his wicked counsel:
לְהַסִּיתָם עַל יְדֵי זֶה לַחֲטוֹא בִּבְיאַת אֲרַמִּית דִּ"וְלָדָהּ כְּמוֹתָהּ" (קִדּוּשִׁין סח עַמּוּד ב),
to entice them through this to sin in cohabitation with a gentile woman whose offspring bears her gentile status (Kiddushin 68b),
וּמִטִּיפָּה זוֹ לֹא יֵצֵא זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל וְצַדִּיק כְּלָל,
so that from this drop there will emerge no seed of Israel or righteous child at all,
וְאֵין מְקַיֵּים בָּזֶה מִצְוַת פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה,
and he does not fulfill through this the commandment of procreation,
דְּלֹא נִקְרָא זַרְעוֹ.
since the child is not legally designated as his seed.
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן טַעַם דִּ"מִימְשְׁכָא עָרְלָתוֹ" (עֵירוּבִין יט עַמּוּד א),
And this is likewise the spiritual rationale for his foreskin being drawn out (Eruvin 19a),
אֲבָל גַּם זֶה אֶצְלוֹ הוּא רַק דְּ"לָא מִבַּשְׁקַר",
yet even this condition in him is merely that he is not recognized as a Jew,
וְלֹא שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה עָרֵל בֶּאֱמֶת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם;
and not that he has become literally an uncircumcised gentile, Heaven forbid;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם זַרְעוֹ נֶעֱקַר לְגַמְרֵי מִקְּדוּשַׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
yet nonetheless his biological offspring is entirely uprooted from the sanctity of Israel.
וְהוּא הִתְעָם בְּחַלְקוּת לְשׁוֹנוֹ,
And Balaam deceived them with the smooth flattery of his tongue,
שֶׁהוּא חָשַׁב דִּלְעוֹלָם לֹא יֵעָקֵר טִיפָּה הַנִּמְשֶׁכֶת מִקְּדוּשַׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִקְּדוּשָׁתָהּ,
for he reasoned that a seed drawn from the sanctity of Israel can never be uprooted from its holiness,
דְּתָלוּי בְּ"רֹבַע יִשְׂרָאֵל",
arguing that it depends upon the father's seed in “the stock of Israel,”
דְּהָעִיקָּר הוּא מִשְׁפַּחַת אָב,
holding that the primary lineage follows the father's house,
וּדְיִקְלַט קְדוּשָּׁה עַל יְדֵי זֶה גַּם בַּזֶּרַע שֶׁיּוֹלִידוּ בְּנוֹת הַגּוֹיִם מֵהֶם.
and that holiness would thus be absorbed even within the offspring that the daughters of the gentiles would bear from them.
וּבָזֶה הִסִּית גַּם אוֹתָם לְהַפְקִיר בְּנוֹתָם,
And through this he also incited the Midianites to surrender their daughters to promiscuity,
מַה שֶּׁכְּבָר גָּדְרוּ כָּל הָאֻמּוֹת,
a vice which all the nations had previously fenced themselves against,
כְּדֵי לִקְלוֹט עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּזַרְעָם קְדוּשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
in order to absorb through this the holiness of Israel into their own seed,
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ "עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ".
and it was treated as a sort of “transgression for the sake of Heaven.”
וְכֵן זִמְרִי שֶׁטָּעַן: "בַּת יִתְרוֹ מִי הִתִּיר לָךְ?" (סַנְהֶדְרִין פב עַמּוּד א),
And likewise Zimri who challenged Moses: “Who permitted you the daughter of Jethro?” (Sanhedrin 82a),
חָשַׁב שֶׁגַּם הַנּוֹלָדִים מֵאֵלּוּ יֵחָשְׁבוּ עַל זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל,
reasoned that those born from these Midianite women would likewise be accounted as the seed of Israel,
וְהוּא בָּא לְהַכְנִיס גַּם מֵהֶם תַּחַת כַּנְפֵי שְׁכִינָה.
and he sought to bring them too beneath the wings of the Shechinah.
וַ"עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ" הִיא כְּ"מִצְוָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּנָזִיר כג עַמּוּד ב],
And a “transgression for the sake of Heaven” is equivalent to a “mitzvah not for the sake of Heaven,” as our Sages stated in Nazir (23b),
וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל אָזְלִינַן בָּתַר הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה טוֹבָה,
and in Israel we evaluate by the inward good thought,
וּבָאֻמּוֹת אַחַר מַעֲשֵׂה הָרָע,
while in the nations by the outward bad deed,
הֵיפֶךְ מִבְּמִצְוָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ.
the reverse of the dynamic in a mitzvah not for its own sake.
וְהָאֻמּוֹת, הֵם מְקַבְּלִים שְׂכַר מִצְווֹת קַלּוֹת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And the nations receive the reward for superficial, light mitzvot in this world,
וְגַם מַחֲשָׁבָה טוֹבָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ כְּלוּם,
and even for a good thought which is intrinsically hollow,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עַל אוֹתָהּ עֲבֵירָה אֵין נֶעֱנָשִׁים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה רַק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
nonetheless for that transgression they are not punished in this world but only in the World to Come,
וְאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַפֵּחַ שְׂכַר מַחֲשָׁבָה טוֹבָה שֶׁלָּהֶם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִיהַת,
and the Holy One does not withhold the reward for their good thought in this world at least,
כִּבְמִצְוָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ מֵהַמַּחֲשָׁבָה רָעָה בִּשְׁבִיל הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
just as in a mitzvah not for its own sake one is rewarded for the deed despite the corrupt thought.
וְאֵצֶל יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא בְּהֵיפֶךְ:
Whereas with Israel it is the reverse:
דַּעֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ כְּהַאי, עַל הַמַּעֲשֶׂה יֵשׁ עֹנֶשׁ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
for in a transgression for Heaven's sake like this, there is temporal punishment upon the deed in this world.
וְהוּא וְהֵם שֶׁמְּבַקְשִׁים רַק טוֹבַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And Balaam and the Midianites, who sought exclusively the physical advantages of this world,
יְעָצָם עֵצָה זוֹ;
he gave them this subversive counsel;
וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע דְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
and this is the quintessential root of the evil of the nations of the world,
שֶׁהֵם מְבַקְשִׁים רַק טוֹבוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְחַיֵּי שָׁעָה
that they pursue only the transient pleasures of this world and temporary life,
וְלֹא חַיֵּי עוֹלָם.
and not eternal life.
וְאוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע הָיָה מַשִּׂיג מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְשֶׁיֵּשׁ חַיֵּי עוֹלָם,
And that wicked one intellectually comprehended the supreme virtue of Israel and the reality of eternal life,
וְעִם כָּל זֶה לֹא בִּקֵּשׁ הוּא לִדָּבֵק בָּהֶם וּלְהַשִּׂיג חַיֵּי עוֹלָם;
and with all that, he did not seek to attach himself to them and attain eternal life;
כִּי הֵם כָּל קִיּוּמָם רַק בְּחַיֵּי שָׁעָה דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
for their entire ontological existence is rooted solely in the fleeting life of this world,
וְאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם כְּשֶׁיְּבוֹעַר הָרָע,
and they possess no connection to eternal life when evil is eradicated,
כִּי אֵין לָהֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ טוֹב כְּלָל שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִשְׁאָר אַחַר בִּיעוּר הָרָע.
since they hold no intrinsic good root whatsoever that could survive the eradication of evil.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 1:28 commands procreation; Tehillim 51:7 speaks of the frailty accompanying conception. Vayikra Rabbah 14:5, in Rabbi Acha’s exposition, describes even Yishai’s personal pleasure in the act. Yevamos 103b teaches that the serpent’s contamination ceased for Israel at Sinai. Rav Tzadok’s distinction between that purified covenantal root and residual bodily self-gratification is his synthesis: marital procreation remains a positive commandment, and the admixture does not redefine the essential deed or Jewish root.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok distinguishes the holy root of procreation from the selfish intention that can accompany it. He then shows how Bilaam’s counsel and Zimri’s mistaken reasoning exploited teachings about Israel’s enduring holiness, while the actual forbidden deed and its consequences remained significant.

p: וּבַמִּשְׁנָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ עַמּוּד א) מָנוּ שִׁבְעָה דְּאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא:
And in the Mishnah (Sanhedrin 90a) they enumerated seven individuals who have no portion in the World to Come:
שִׁשָּׁה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, וְהַשְּׁבִיעִי בִּלְעָם מֵאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
six from Israel (three kings and three commoners), and the seventh is Balaam from the nations of the world.
וּמִסְּתָמָא שִׁבְעָה אֵלּוּ כּוֹלְלִים כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And presumably these seven archetypes encompass all souls who have no portion in the World to Come,
דְּוַדַּאי הָיוּ יוֹתֵר מִשִּׁבְעָה אֵלּוּ;
for certainly there were historically more individuals than these seven;
רַק שֶׁכָּל דָּבָר חָלוּק לְשֶׁבַע מַדְרֵגוֹת כַּיָּדוּעַ,
only that every structural reality is divided into seven gradations as is known,
וְכָל אַחַת כּוֹלֵל מַדְרֵגָה מְיוּחֶדֶת,
and each archetype embodies a specific spiritual dimension;
וּכְמוֹ שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית:
just like the seven days of Creation:
שִׁשָּׁה יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וְיוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי שַׁבָּת מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
the six days of creative action and the seventh day Shabbat, a foretaste of the World to Come,
וְכֵן שֵׁשֶׁת אַלְפֵי שָׁנִים דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה;
and likewise the six thousand years of this world;
כָּךְ יֵשׁ גַּם בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁהוּא זְמַן הַקִּיבּוּל שָׂכָר עַל הַמַּעֲשִׂים.
so too is it structured in the World to Come which is the epoch of receiving reward for deeds.
דִּימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דְּ"הַיּוֹם לַעֲשׂוֹתָם" (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ג עַמּוּד א) הֵם שֵׁשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת,
For the working days of this world regarding which it is said “today to perform them” (Avodah Zarah 3a) comprise six gradations,
וּמֵאֵלּוּ הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת נִדְחוּ אוֹתָם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
and from these active gradations were banished those who have no portion in the World to Come,
שֶׁמִּצַּד מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם קִיבּוּל שָׂכָר,
for from the perspective of their deeds in this world they possess no reward whatsoever,
וְזֶהוּ גַּם בְּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and this holds true even regarding the transgressors of Israel.
וּמַדְרֵגָה הַשְּׁבִיעִית דְּעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
However, the seventh dimension of the World to Come,
שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which corresponds to the Sabbath day in this world,
שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
which is not a day of action,
רַק מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה שֶׁנָּתַן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
rather a gracious gift that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave unto Israel;
(דְּגוֹי שֶׁשָּׁבַת חַיָּיב מִיתָה,
(for a gentile who observes Shabbat is liable to death,
דְּמֵהֶם אֵין לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִיחָא אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
since from them the Holy One desires satisfaction only through practical manual labor
שֶׁעוֹסְקִים בְּיִשּׁוּבוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם,
wherein they engage in the settlement and cultivation of the world,
דִּלְכָךְ נוֹצְרוּ לִהְיוֹת אִכָּרִים וְכוֹרְמִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל;
having been created for this purpose to serve as farmers and vinedressers for Israel;
וְעַל כֵּן רַק חֲסִידֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
and therefore only the pious of the nations of the world possess a portion in the World to Come,
אוֹתָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם שְׂכַר מַעֲשִׂים שֶׁפָּעֲלוּ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וְלֹא לְגַרְמַיְיהוּ);
namely those who possess the earned reward of deeds that they performed in this world for Heaven and not for selfish vanity);
וּמַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נֶאֱמַר: "הֲלוֹא אָח [עֵשָׂו לְיַעֲקֹב נְאֻם ה'] וָאֹהַב אֶת יַעֲקֹב" (מַלְאָכִי א, ב),
in contrast to Israel concerning whom it is stated: “Was not Esau Jacob's brother? says Hashem, yet I loved Jacob” (Malachi 1:2),
אַף שֶׁהֵם אַחִים דּוֹמִים זֶה לָזֶה בְּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם,
even when they appear as brothers resembling one another in their outward deeds,
זֶה אָהוּב בְּלֹא טַעַם,
this one is unconditionally beloved without rational cause,
כְּעִנְיַן "וְחַנֹּתִי אֶת אֲשֶׁר אָחֹן" (שְׁמוֹת לג, יט)
mirroring “and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious” (Exodus 33:19)
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ הָגוּן וּכְדַאי,
even though he is neither worthy nor deserving,
מֵאוֹצָר שֶׁל מַתְּנַת חִנָּם,
bestowed from the supernal treasury of unearned gifts,
שֶׁאֵינוֹ לְפִי הַמַּעֲשִׂים רַק מִצַּד הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
which is not measured by deeds but emanates from the pristine soul-root,
דְּהוּא רַק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד.
which belongs exclusively to Israel alone.
וּמִצַּד מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא
And from the perspective of this seventh dimension in the World to Come,
אֵין שׁוּם נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל נִדְחָה,
not a single soul from Israel is ever cast out,
אֶלָּא בִּלְעָם שֶׁהוּא מֵאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
save Balaam alone who is from the nations of the world.

paragraphs.text: Mishnah Sanhedrin 10:2, also Sanhedrin 90a:17, lists three kings—Yerovam, Achav and Menasheh—and four commoners—Bilaam, Doeg, Achitofel and Geichazi—as having no share in the World to Come. inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok reads the Mishnah’s seven figures through seven spiritual dimensions. He distinguishes the reward earned by deeds from the seventh dimension, likened to Shabbos and an unearned gift, through which he explains Israel’s enduring portion and Bilaam’s different position.

p: וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק עַל כָּל פָּנִים בְּאוֹצָר זֶה
And all Israel possess an immutable portion at least in this divine storehouse,
שֶׁלֹּא נִתְגַּלָּה גַּם לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֶלָּא הָרְשִׁימוּ מִמֶּנּוּ,
which was not unveiled even to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, in this world except for its imprint,
רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר מַה שֶּׁגִּילָּה לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְצִיאוּת לְאוֹצָר זֶה.
meaning that which the Holy One disclosed to him that there exists reality to this unearned treasury.
וְזֶהוּ הַקֶּשֶׁר שֶׁל תְּפִלִּין שֶׁהֶרְאָה לוֹ בְּמַרְאֵה אֲחוֹרַיִם
And this is the knot of the tefillin which Hashem showed him in the vision of the hind parts (Berakhot 7a),
(דִּתְפִלִּין דְּמָארֵי עָלְמָא כְּתִיב בְּהוּ:
for in the tefillin of the Master of the world it is inscribed:
"וּמִי כְּעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹי אֶחָד בָּאָרֶץ" [דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א יז, כא]).
“And who is like Your people Israel, a nation one in the earth” [I Chronicles 17:21]
וְהַקֶּשֶׁר הוּא הַהִתְקַשְּׁרוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם עִם אֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם
And the knot embodies the unbreakable bond that they possess with their Father in Heaven
גַּם בִּהְיוֹתָם בִּבְחִינַת "אֲחוֹרַיִם",
even when they subsist in the spiritual posture of “backwards,”
שֶׁהוּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם
which is during the era when they fail to perform the will of the Omnipresent,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא צט עַמּוּד א] שֶׁאֵינָם אָז פָּנִים בְּפָנִים;
as our Sages stated in Bava Batra (99a) that they are then not standing face-to-face;
וְהוּא קֶשֶׁר שֶׁל דָּלֶ״ת הַמּוֹרֶה עַל דַּלּוּתָם מֵהַמִּצְווֹת.
and it forms the knot shaped as the letter Dalet which denotes their poverty (dalut) of mitzvot.
וּבִפְנִים בַּבַּיִת הוּא הַשִּׁי״ן מֵהַשֵּׁם
And inward upon the box of the head-tefillin is the letter Shin of the holy Name Shaddai,
הַמּוֹרֶה עַל קְדוּשַּׁת הַבְּרִית כַּנּוֹדָע,
which denotes the sanctified covenant of circumcision as is known,
שֶׁהוּא קְדוּשַׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֵין הָעָרְלָה נִקְרֵאת אֶלָּא לְשֵׁם אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
which is the intrinsic sanctity of Israel, for uncircumcision is attributed by title solely to the nations.
וְהֵם שְׁתֵּי שִׁינִין שֶׁל שְׁלֹשָׁה רָאשִׁים וְאַרְבָּעָה רָאשִׁים,
And these are the two Shins on the tefillin—one of three heads and one of four heads—
נֶגֶד שִׁבְעָה רוֹעִים שֶׁהֵם כּוֹלְלִים כָּל קְדוּשַׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
corresponding to the Seven Shepherds who encompass the totality of Israel's holiness,
וּדְבֵיקוּתָם בְּשֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת הָעֶלְיוֹנוֹת דֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים כַּנּוֹדָע.
and their cleaving unto the seven supernal attributes of the living God, as is known.
אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא הַתְחָלַת בִּנְיַן הָאֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית,
Abraham our father, peace be upon him, represents the inception of the construction of the Jewish nation,
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא מְשִׁיחַ אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב
and King David, peace be upon him, who is the anointed of the God of Jacob,
הוּא סוֹף שְׁלֵימוּתָם בְּבִיעוּר הָרָע וְגִלּוּי דְּבֵיקוּתָם לְגַמְרֵי;
is the final culmination of their perfection in eradicating evil and unveiling their complete cleaving;
וְשִׁי״ן דִּשְׁלֹשָׁה רָאשִׁים הוּא נֶגֶד שְׁלוֹשָׁה אָבוֹת כַּיָּדוּעַ.
and the Shin of three heads corresponds to the three Patriarchs, as is known.
וְ"זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה" הֵם גַּם כֵּן שֶׁבַע מַדְרֵגוֹת בָּרָע:
And corresponding to “one opposite the other” there are likewise seven gradations within evil:
כְּמוֹ שִׁבְעָה שֵׁמוֹת לַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּסֻכָּה נב עַמּוּד א],
such as the seven names for the evil urge expounded in Sukkah (52a),
וְשִׁבְעָה שֵׁמוֹת לְגֵיהִנָּם [בְּעֵירוּבִין יט עַמּוּד א],
and the seven names for Gehenna in Eruvin (19a),
וְשִׁבְעָה מְדוֹרֵי גֵּיהִנָּם הַנִּזְכָּר בַּזֹּהַר וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ.
and the seven compartments of Gehenna mentioned in the Zohar and Midrash.
וְכֵן שִׁבְעָה אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא:
And so too these seven archetypes who have no portion in the World to Come:
שְׁלוֹשָׁה מְלָכִים נֶגֶד שְׁלוֹשָׁה אָבוֹת,
three kings corresponding to the three Patriarchs,
וּבִלְעָם נֶגֶד דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
and Balaam standing opposite King David, peace be upon him, in holiness,
שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הָרָע לְגַמְרֵי בְּלִי שׁוּם טוֹב מֵחַיֵּי עוֹלָם,
Balaam being the embodiment of unmitigated evil devoid of any lingering good from eternal life,
וְזֶה לֹא נִמְצָא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל.
and such irremediable evil is not found within Israel at all.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 6a - what is written in the tefillin of the Master of the world: The Gemara answers with “Who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land,” then explains mutual singularity: Israel declares Hashem One, and Hashem makes Israel a unique nation. Rav Tzadok uses this not merely as praise written inside the tefillin, but as the content of the permanent attachment symbolized by their knot. The Gemara states the reciprocal praise; the extension to Israel’s bond even in an “achorayim” condition is his interpretation.

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 52a names the evil inclination evil, uncircumcised, impure, enemy, stumbling block, stone, and hidden one. Eruvin 19a lists seven names of Gehinnom. Zohar, Pekudei 53:838, aligns seven chambers with seven names, but its lists differ: it includes Satan and combines ‘stone of stumbling’; its Gehinnom list includes Dumah. These are related sevenfold schemes, not identical lists. The precise Midrash intended by the author’s additional general reference has not been identified.
