inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The knot of the divine tefillin symbolizes, in Rav Tzadok’s reading, Israel’s bond with God even when that bond is turned away from open revelation. The signs of the tefillin and the seven shepherds develop the holy pattern against which he sets the seven opposing forms of evil.

p: וּמִמַּדְרֵגָה זוֹ הִשִּׂיגוּ דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת הָרְשִׁימוּ,
And from this lofty level, the interpreters of esoteric traces apprehended the spiritual imprint,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ דְּכוּלָּם יֵשׁ לָהֶם [חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא].
in that they declared that all of them possess a share in the World to Come.
וְהַכֹּל אֱמֶת,
And everything is truth:
דְּמִצַּד מַדְרֵיגוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת אֵין לָהֶם,
for from the perspective of the initial, standard levels they have no share,
וּבְמַדְרֵגַת הַשֶּׁבַע חָשֵׁיב הַתַּנָּא גַּם כֵּן רַק בִּלְעָם,
and within the seventh level the Tanna of the Mishnah likewise enumerated only Balaam,
כִּי יַעֲקֹב נָטַל לְחֶלְקוֹ הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
because Jacob took for his allotted portion the World to Come,
וְעַל כֵּן כָּל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
and therefore all the seed of Jacob possess a portion in the World to Come;
וְאַף אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
and even these individuals who are listed as having no portion in the World to Come,
גַּם הֵם מִצַּד שֶׁהֵם מִזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב וּמִכְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
they too, by virtue of being from the seed of Jacob and of the collective body of Israel, possess a share in the World to Come.
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא אָמְרוּ לְשׁוֹן "חוּץ" כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
Therefore the Mishnah did not use the exclusionary phrasing “except,” as mentioned above,
וְרוֹמֵז גַּם לָזֶה:
which alludes also to this:
דְּאַף אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם,
that even those who ostensibly have no share,
הֵם גַּם כֵּן מִכְּלַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם
are likewise part of the collective whole of Israel who do have a portion,
מִצַּד שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל;
inasmuch as they too are of Israel;
וּמַה שֶּׁאֵין לָהֶם הוּא מִצַּד הִתְגַּבְּרוּת הָרָע בַּחֲלַל הַלֵּב
and that which they lack is solely from the dominance of evil within the cavity of the heart,
עַד שֶׁנֶּעְלַם וְנִתְכַּסָּה שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְגַמְרֵי.
until the pristine root of good within them became totally submerged and concealed in this world.
וְעַל כֵּן מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּבָר יָצָא מִכְּלַל שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל וְזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב,
Therefore, from the vantage point of manifest disclosure in this world, he has departed from the designation of Israel and the seed of Jacob,
כִּי אוֹתוֹ חֵלֶק רָע הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט וּמְמַלֵּא כָּל מַעֲמַקֵּי לִבּוֹ
because that evil component which expands and fills all the depths of his heart
אֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ יַעֲקֹב וְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל;
bears no affinity or connection to the root of Jacob and the name of Israel at all;
וְעַל כֵּן בְּחֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁמִּצַּד הַמַּעֲשִׂים דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין לָהֶם,
and therefore in the share of the World to Come that is earned through worldly actions they have no part,
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ יֵשׁ לָהֶם.
yet nonetheless from the perspective of their essential spiritual root they do have a share.
וּמִצַּד הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַזֶּה קַיְימָא לָן
And by virtue of this inner root we hold as established halakhah
דְּמוּמָר, אֲפִילּוּ נִטְמַע בֵּין הָעַמִּים, קִידּוּשָׁיו קִידּוּשִׁין וְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל עָלָיו.
that an apostate, even if assimilated among the nations, his betrothal is valid and the name of Israel remains upon him.
וְיֵשׁ גְּאוֹנִים סוֹבְרִים דְּאֵין קִידּוּשָׁיו קִידּוּשִׁין
Now there are Geonim who maintain that an apostate's betrothal is invalid,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּטוּר וּבֵית יוֹסֵף [בְּאֶבֶן הָעֵזֶר סִימָן מד],
as cited in the Tur and Beit Yosef (Even HaEzer, sec. 44),
וְהָרַשְׁדָּ״ם [בְּאֶבֶן הָעֵזֶר סִימָן י] הֶאֱרִיךְ לְבָאֵר דְּאֵינוֹ דֵּעָה דְּחוּיָה,
and the Rashdam (Even HaEzer, resp. 10) elaborated to clarify that this is not a rejected opinion,
דְּטַעֲמָם דְּהָא דְּ"אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא – יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא" מֵעָכָן יָלְפִינַן,
arguing that their reasoning is that the principle “even though he has sinned, he remains Israel” is derived from Achan,
וְאֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא דְּכָוָותֵיהּ;
and we may extend it only to one comparable to him;
וְאַף שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין מד רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א] דְּעָבַר עַל חֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה,
and even though they stated in Sanhedrin (44a) that Achan transgressed the Five Books of the Torah,
לָאו דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל הוּא, יְעֻיַּין שָׁם בְּאֹרֶךְ.
this is not the consensus of all authorities, examine there at length.
וּבֶאֱמֶת לֹא נִמְצָא מַאן דְּפָלֵיג עַל זֶה,
Yet in truth, no dissenting authority is found against this Gemara,
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתַב מִלְּשׁוֹן רַשִׁ״י שָׁם דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: "פְּשִׁיטָא", עַיֵּין שָׁם,
and what the Rashdam derived from the wording of Rashi there (heading: “Peshita”), see there,
אֲפִילּוּ יִהְיֶה זֶה דִּקְדּוּק,
even if that textual inference were valid,
קָשֶׁה אַרַשִׁ״י גּוּפֵיהּ: אָנָה מָצָא מַאן דְּפָלֵיג?
it is difficult on Rashi himself: where did he ever find an opposing Tanna?
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת פָּשׁוּט
Rather in truth it is plain:
דְּרַשִׁ״י נָקַט רַבִּי אִילְעָא גּוּפֵיהּ
that Rashi formulated it with Rabbi Il'a himself
מִשּׁוּם דְּאִי לָאו הָכִי, מִכֹּחַ הַקּוּשְׁיָא "פְּשִׁיטָא", הָיִינוּ אוֹמְרִים דְּהַאי מַאן דְּאָמַר פָּלֵיג,
because otherwise, from the force of the Talmud's question “Isn't this obvious?”, we would have presumed that this authority disputes,
וְלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ לְהַקְשׁוֹת כָּל כָּךְ בִּפְשִׁיטוּת "פְּשִׁיטָא",
and it would not be fitting to challenge so simply “Isn't this obvious?”,
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר דְּהוּא רַבִּי אִילְעָא גּוּפֵיהּ וְלֵיכָּא דְּפָלֵיג.
and therefore Rashi noted that it is Rabbi Il'a himself and no one disputes.
וּמֵהֵיכָא תֵּיתֵי לַאֲפוֹשֵׁי פְּלוּגְתָּא
And whence would one needlessly multiply halakhic controversy
וּלְהַמְצִיא דְּלָאו דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל הוּא?
and fabricate that this is not universally accepted?
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתַב דְּהוּא אַסְמַכְתָּא בְּעָלְמָא,
And what the Rashdam wrote, that Achan's sin is a mere asmachta (biblical support),
הוּא זָר בְּעֵינַי לְאָמְרוֹ כָּאן,
is completely foreign in my eyes to assert here;
דְּדָבָר זֶה שַׁיָּיךְ בְּעִנְיַן דִּין,
for the concept of an asmachta applies strictly to a legal ruling,
דְּיֵשׁ שֶׁהוּא מִדְּרַבָּנָן וְאַסְמְכוּהָ אַקְּרָא;
where a decree is rabbinic and they anchored it upon a verse;
אֲבָל יַלְפּוּתָא אַסִּפּוּר עִנְיָן שֶׁהָיָה,
but a derivation clarifying a historical narrative that occurred,
מַה שַּׁיָּיךְ "אַסְמַכְתָּא בְּעָלְמָא" בָּזֶה?
what relevance has the category of a mere asmachta in such an exposition?

paragraphs.text: Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 111:2 portrays Yaakov and Esav dividing the worlds, Yaakov taking the World to Come. Tanchuma, Terumah 9:3, presents a different formulation: Yaakov receives two portions, eating in this world and inheriting the next, while Esav has one. The author extends Yaakov’s portion to an enduring root within all his seed; the accounts themselves do not formulate that universal individual conclusion.

paragraphs.text: Mishnah Sanhedrin 10:1–2 juxtaposes ‘all Israel’ with exclusions and the seven named figures, without using chutz as its grammatical formulation. Sanhedrin 104b:15–105a:1 records the dorshei reshumos’ restoration teaching and identifies six Israelite figures through the verses; Bilaam is not among those identifications. Rav Tzadok reconciles these accounts through a share measured by deeds and a deeper share rooted in Israelite identity. That resolution is his synthesis.

paragraphs.text: Yevamos 47b; Rambam, Hilchos Ishus 4:15; Tur, Even HaEzer 44 - the apostate’s betrothal: Yevamos rules that after a convert has immersed and emerged, he is “like an Israelite in every respect”; even if he later reverts and betroths a Jewish woman, he is called an apostate Israelite and his kiddushin are valid. Rambam states the broader rule that an Israelite apostate who willingly worships idolatry nevertheless effects complete kiddushin and requires a get. The Tur likewise rules that an apostate’s kiddushin are valid, while recording and rejecting a dissenting view concerning public Shabbos desecration and idolatry. Rav Tzadok reads the operative halachah as a legal expression of the enduring Jewish root beneath the person’s revealed conduct.

paragraphs.text: Tur, Even HaEzer 44, records and rejects the dissent concerning a public Shabbos desecrator or idolater. Maharashdam, Even HaEzer 10, argues that the view cannot simply be dismissed: he limits the Achan inference and explores partial reversion or stringent kiddushin. He explicitly submits his discussion to his teachers rather than presenting an independent practical ruling. The case’s appended permission rests on invalid witnesses among forced converts. Beit Yosef 44:14:1, citing the Itur and Rambam, meanwhile emphasizes complete biblical kiddushin, not mere concern. Rav Tzadok contests Maharashdam’s textual arguments below.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok distinguishes loss of an earned share from the enduring share rooted in Israel’s essential identity. He connects this with the validity of an apostate’s betrothal and critically examines the contrary opinion and the proofs attributed to it.

p: אֲבָל יֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּתַלְיָא
However, it can be said that this matter depends
(וְשׁוּב זָכִיתִי וּמָצָאתִי בִּתְשׁוּבוֹת הָרַשְׁבָּ״א [חֵלֶק א סִימָן קצד וְסִימָן רמב]
(and subsequently I merited finding in the Responsa of the Rashba [Part 1, resp. 194 and 242]
שֶׁהֵבִיא גַּם כֵּן לְעִנְיָן זֶה הַךְ פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
who likewise brought in connection to this the dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah,
וּדְקַיְימָא לָן כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר מִשּׁוּם דְּדָיֵיק קְרָאֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם וַאֲהַנְיָן)
and that we rule like Rabbi Meir because he analyzes the verses with precision, see there, and it brought me great joy)
בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּתַנָּאֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר [בְּקִדּוּשִׁין שָׁם לו עַמּוּד א]:
upon the dispute of the Tannaim, Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Meir, in Kiddushin (36a):
דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר הוּא דִּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ דִּלְעוֹלָם נִקְרָאִים "בְּנֵי אֵל חָי",
for Rabbi Meir holds that under all circumstances they are termed “children of the living God,”
אֲבָל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר דִּכְשֶׁאֵין נוֹהֲגִים מִנְהַג בָּנִים אֵין קְרוּיִים בָּנִים.
whereas Rabbi Yehudah says that when they do not conduct themselves as children they are not termed children.
וּבִתְחִלַּת בִּנְיַן הָאוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית,
And at the dawn of the establishment of the Jewish nation,
בִּתְחִלַּת הַשְּׁלִיחוּת לְהוֹצִיאָם מִמִּצְרַיִם,
at the initial mission to take them out of Egypt,
נֶאֱמַר בְּפָרָשַׁת שְׁמוֹת (ד, כב-כג): "בְּנִי בְכֹרִי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שַׁלַּח אֶת בְּנִי וְיַעַבְדֵנִי",
it is stated in Parashat Shemot: “Israel is My son, My firstborn; let My son go, that he may serve Me,”
מְבוֹאָר שֶׁכְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם בָּנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ,
making it clear that the collective community of Israel are His children, blessed be He,
וְדְעַל כֵּן הוֹצִיאָם לִהְיוֹת לוֹ לְעָם וּלְעָבְדוֹ לְפִי שֶׁהֵם בָּנָיו;
and that He brought them forth to be a people unto Him and to serve Him specifically because they are His children;
וְאִם אֵין קְרוּיִים בָּנִים, אִם כֵּן אֵינָם בִּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַם ה'.
and if they are not termed children, if so they are excluded from the community of Israel and the people of Hashem.
וְנִרְאֶה דְּעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר קְרָא דְּ"בָּנִים אַתֶּם לַה' אֱלֹהֵיכֶם" (דְּבָרִים יד, א)
And it appears that on this account the verse “You are children unto Hashem your God” was stated
גַּבֵּי אַזְהָרַת גְּדִידָה וְקָרְחָה עַל מֵת,
specifically in connection to the prohibition against self-gashing and baldness over the dead;
כִּי זֶה שַׁיָּיךְ בָּאֻמּוֹת שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אֶלָּא הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
for such despair applies to the pagan nations who possess only this physical world,
וּבְמוֹתָם יֵלְכוּ לַאֲבַדּוֹן עוֹלָם;
and at their death they depart into eternal oblivion;
אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל, הַמִּיתָה הִיא "טוֹב מְאֹד" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ט, ה],
whereas for Israel, bodily death is “very good,” as our Sages expounded in Bereishit Rabbah (9:5),
כִּי הִיא לְתַכְלִית טוֹב שֶׁיִּתְעַכֵּל הַזּוּהֲמָא
because it serves a constructive ultimate good: that the Serpent's defilement be consumed
וְיִכְלוּ הַחוֹחִים הַסּוֹבְבִים
and the surrounding briars be terminated,
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה יִשָּׁאֵר נָקִי מִכָּל סִיג.
while the pristine root of holiness remains cleansed of all dross.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר לְטַעַם עַל זֶה דְּ"בָּנִים אַתֶּם":
And this is why Scripture cited as the rationale for this: “You are children”—
כְּבֵן הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מֵהָאָב, כֵּן אַתֶּם לֵאלֹהֵיכֶם,
just as a son is organically drawn from the father, so are you unto your God,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּכֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדוּשָּׁה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה שֶׁהִיא מִזְדַּכֵּךְ בְּמוֹתוֹ.
in that you bear the supernal root of holiness which is purged and refined through death.
וּמִזֶּה גַּם כֵּן: דִּכְשֶׁאֵין קְרוּיִים בָּנִים,
And from this it follows likewise: when they are not termed children,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדוּשָּׁה הַקַּיָּים לְעָלְמֵי עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַמִּיתָה לְטוֹבָתוֹ,
it denotes that he lacks that enduring root of holiness whereby death serves for his ultimate good,
רַק כְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם דְּמִיתָתָם אֲבַדּוֹן,
resembling all the gentiles whose demise is total ruin,
זֶה הוּא עֲקִירַת שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל לְגַמְרֵי מֵהֶם.
and this constitutes the absolute uprooting of the name of Israel from them.
וְצָרִיךְ לוֹמַר לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
And one must say according to Rabbi Yehudah
קְרָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּ"וְהָיָה בִּמְקוֹם וְגוֹמֵר בְּנֵי אֵל חָי" (הוֹשֵׁעַ ב, א) לֹא קַשְׁיָא,
that the verse cited by Rabbi Meir, “And it shall come to pass that in the place, etc., they shall be called children of the living God,” is not difficult,
דִּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ דְּתַרְוַויְיהוּ אֱמֶת,
because he holds that both dimensions are truth,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אַמִּשְׁנָה דְּחֵלֶק וְדִבְרֵי דוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת.
and as I wrote above regarding the Mishnah in Chelek and the words of the interpreters of esoteric traces.
דַּהֲרֵי גַּם הָא דְּנֶאֱמַר "אַתֶּם לֹא עַמִּי" דְּנִגְזְרָה מִקּוֹדֶם,
For behold, even that which was declared, “You are not My people,” which was decreed initially,
נֶאֱמַר בַּכָּתוּב דְּלֹא נִתְבַּטֵּל בַּהֹוֶה
is articulated in Scripture as not being annulled in the present era,
רַק בִּלְשׁוֹן עָתִיד "וְהָיָה".
rather in the future tense: “And it shall come to pass” (Vehayah).
דְּמִצַּד הַהַשָּׂגָה שֶׁבְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לֵב הַחֲכָמִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
For from the perspective of the perception revealed to the heart of the sages in this world,
הֲרֵי מָנוּ אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
behold they enumerated these who have no portion in the World to Come
וְנִשְׁנָה בַּמִּשְׁנָה סְתָם;
and it was taught in the Mishnah without qualification;
רַק בַּגְּמָרָא גִּילּוּ הַשָּׂגַת הַדּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת,
only in the Gemara did they unveil the deeper perception of the interpreters of esoteric traces,
שֶׁהַתַּלְמוּד מְגַלֶּה דְּבָרִים שֶׁסְּתָמוּם בַּמִּשְׁנָה,
for the Talmud explicitly reveals matters that were sealed and hidden in the Mishnah,
שֶׁלֹּא רָצוּ לְפָרֵשׁ כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּנְדָרִים כג סוֹף עַמּוּד ב]:
which they deliberately declined to articulate, in the manner stated in Nedarim (23b):
"תַּנָּא מַסְתֵּים לַהּ סְתוֹמֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא קַלּוּת רֹאשׁ",
“The Tanna deliberately sealed the matter lest there be levity,”
וּבַגְּמָרָא שָׁם פֵּירְשׁוּ הַדָּבָר.
and in the Gemara there they expounded the matter fully.
כִּי הַמִּשְׁנָה, שֶׁהוּא הַהֲלָכוֹת בְּקִיצוּר בְּלֹא מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן וּפִלְפּוּל,
For the Mishnah, which contains codified rulings in concise form without dialectical debate and pilpul,
נִסְדַּר לִהְיוֹת מָסוּר לַכֹּל;
was formulated to be transmitted to the broad populace;
וְעַל כֵּן הִסְתִּירוּ שָׁם דְּבָרִים שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ קַלֵּי הַדַּעַת לָבוֹא עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְקַלּוּת רֹאשׁ.
and therefore they concealed therein matters through which the light-minded might arrive at frivolous license.
וְכֵן כָּאן לֹא רָצוּ לְגַלּוֹת זֶה בַּמִּשְׁנָה
And so here, they did not wish to disclose in the Mishnah
שֶׁיֵּשׁ מַדְרֵגָה בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁבָּהּ יֵשׁ חֵלֶק גַּם לְאֵלּוּ,
that there exists a transcendent dimension in the World to Come wherein even these have a portion,
דְּלָא יָבוֹאוּ לְקַלּוּת רֹאשׁ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל בְּבִלְעָם עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהֶחֱלִיק לָשׁוֹן.
lest people come to frivolous antinomianism, as mentioned above regarding Balaam who seduced through slippery flattery.

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 36a: “It was taught: ‘you are children to Hashem your God’ — at the time you conduct yourselves in the manner of children, you are called children; [if] you do not conduct yourselves in the manner of children, you are not called children — the words of R’ Yehuda. R’ Meir says: either way you are called children, as it says (Yirmeyah 4): ‘they are foolish children,’ and it says (Devarim 32): ‘children in whom there is no faithfulness,’ and it says (Yeshayah 1): ‘seed of evildoers, children who deal corruptly,’ and it says (Hoshea 2): ‘and it shall be, in the place where it is said to them, you are not My people, it shall be said to them, children of the living God.’ What is [the point of each] ‘and it says’? [It is necessary:] and if you would say [that] it is [only] the foolish who are called children, [but] when there is no faithfulness in them they are not called children — come and hear, ‘and it says: children in whom there is no faithfulness.’ And if you would say [that] when there is no faithfulness in them they are [still] called children, [but] when they worship idolatry they are not called children — come and hear, ‘and it says: seed of evildoers, children who deal corruptly.’ And if you would say [that] they are called ‘children who deal corruptly,’ [but] fit children they are not called — come and hear, ‘and it says: and it shall be, in the place where it is said to them, you are not My people, it shall be said to them, children of the living God.’”

paragraphs.text: Shemos 4:22-23 - “My firstborn son Israel” and the purpose of redemption: At the opening of Moshe's mission, Hashem commands him to tell Pharaoh, “Israel is My firstborn son,” followed immediately by “send My son that he may serve Me.” The verse therefore joins national sonship, liberation from Egypt, and avodah. Rav Tzadok reads this sequence as the foundation of Israel's identity as Hashem's people: the nation is redeemed for service because it is already called His son. On the plain level, however, the passage speaks about Israel collectively in confrontation with Pharaoh; applying the title to the enduring inner status of every individual is Rav Tzadok's conceptual extension.

paragraphs.text: Hoshea 1:9 and 2:1 - “not My people” and future restoration: Hoshea first names the child Lo-Ammi and declares, “you are not My people.” The very next prophecy reverses that decree: in the place where they were told “not My people,” they will be called “children of the living God.” Kiddushin 36a treats this as R' Meir's strongest proof that even after severe estrangement the title “children” remains recoverable. Rav Tzadok reconciles the verse with R' Yehuda by distinguishing the present, revealed judgment - in which the title can disappear - from the future disclosure of the enduring root. That present/future two-level reading is Rav Tzadok's synthesis, not an explicit explanation stated by R' Yehuda.

paragraphs.text: Nedarim 23b - a true rule deliberately concealed from the public: The Gemara explains that the Mishnah does not state openly that a person may make an annual stipulation voiding future vows. When Rav Huna bar Chinnana wished to teach the rule publicly, Rava objected that the Tanna had concealed it so that people would not treat vows lightly. Rav Tzadok uses this as an analogy for Mishnah Sanhedrin: the Mishnah can state the severe, practical formulation, while the Gemara discloses a deeper qualification to those capable of receiving it without spiritual carelessness. Nedarim establishes the pedagogical principle of concealment; its application to the excluded figures and the World to Come is Rav Tzadok's analogy.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok relates the dispute about Israel being called God’s children to the enduring holy root, drawing support from the Rashba. He also explains why the Mishnah veils teachings about ultimate restoration that could be misused to encourage sin.

p: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם רָמְזוּ זֶה בַּמַּה שֶּׁלֹּא אָמְרוּ "חוּץ" כַּנִּזְכָּר,
And nonetheless they hinted to this truth in that they omitted the word “except,” as noted,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהִסְתִּירוּ הַדְּבָרִים שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹת בַּמִּשְׁנָה בְּפֵירוּשׁ.
save that they veiled the concepts which could not be explicitly published in the Mishnah.
גַּם מִלְּבַד הַטַּעַם הַנִּזְכָּר, יֵשׁ כָּאן עוֹד:
Furthermore, beyond the aforementioned rationale, there is an additional factor here:
כִּי דָּבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ מוּשָּׂג בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת הַלֵּב בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
that this mystery is not consciously grasped in the revealed heart in this world,
רַק בְּדֶרֶךְ רֶמֶז וְרוֹשֶׁם בְּעָלְמָא.
rather merely by way of subtle allusion and an esoteric imprint.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁבַּגְּמָרָא וְכֵן בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי [בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין שָׁם פֶּרֶק י הֲלָכָה ב] פֵּירְשׁוּ דְּבָרִים בְּהֶדְיָא,
And this is why in the Bavli and in the Yerushalmi (Sanhedrin 10:2) they explained matters explicitly;
הֵם גִּילּוּ כָּל הַמִּסְטוֹרִין, שֶׁלְּבַעֲלֵי תַלְמוּד נוֹדַע הַכֹּל.
for they unveiled all the hidden mysteries, so that to masters of the Talmud everything is made known.
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּשָׁלֹשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת הֵם הַנִּזְכָּר בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת:
As is known that three progressive spiritual levels are mentioned in various places:
בַּעֲלֵי מִקְרָא, בַּעֲלֵי מִשְׁנָה, בַּעֲלֵי תַלְמוּד,
masters of Scripture, masters of Mishnah, masters of Talmud,
שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד שָׁלֹשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה שֶׁבָּאָדָם,
which correspond to the three soul-dimensions of Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah in man,
שֶׁמִּשְּׁלֹשָׁה עוֹלָמוֹת בְּרִיאָה, יְצִירָה, עֲשִׂיָּה כַּנּוֹדָע.
emanating from the three worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, as is known.
וּמִצַּד מַדְרֵגַת הָרוּחַ שֶׁבַּלֵּב אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהָבִין וּלְהַשִּׂיג אֶלָּא בְּרֶמֶז,
And from the perspective of the Ruach in the heart it is impossible to understand except via allusion,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִי שֶׁזָּכָה לְמַדְרֵגַת הַנְּשָׁמָה וְחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג יוֹתֵר.
unlike one who has merited the Neshamah and wisdom in the brain, who comprehends far more.
וּבַכָּתוּב נִתְגַּלָּה גַּם כֵּן בְּדֶרֶךְ כְּלָל
And in Scripture it was likewise unveiled in general terms:
דְּ"וְהָיָה בִּמְקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם לֹא עַמִּי אַתֶּם, יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם בְּנֵי אֵל חָי" (הוֹשֵׁעַ ב, א);
“And it shall come to pass that in the place where it was said unto them: You are not My people, it shall be said unto them: You are the children of the living God” (Hosea 2:1);
וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר בַּבָּרַיְיתָא דְּקִדּוּשִׁין פִּרְסְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן,
and Rabbi Meir in the Baraita of Kiddushin publicized this likewise,
שֶׁהוּא הִשִּׂיג כְּלָלוּת אוֹר הַגָּנוּז דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
for he grasped the comprehensive hidden light of the Oral Torah.
דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא "רַבִּי מֵאִיר"
Therefore he was called “Rabbi Meir” (the Illuminator)
עַל שֵׁם שֶׁמֵּאִיר עֵינֵי חֲכָמִים בַּהֲלָכָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּעֵירוּבִין יג עַמּוּד ב],
because he illuminates the eyes of the sages in halakhah, as they stated in Eruvin (13b),
כִּי הוּא הִמְשִׁיךְ הָאוֹר לְכָל חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עֵינֵי הָעֵדָה,
for he channeled the supernal light unto all the sages of Israel who are the eyes of the congregation,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם:
and as they stated there:
דְּגָלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לִפְנֵי מִי שֶׁאָמַר וְהָיָה הָעוֹלָם שֶׁאֵין בְּדוֹרוֹ כְּמוֹתוֹ.
that it is revealed and known before the One Who spoke and the world came into being that in his generation there was none like him.
וְדָיֵיק שֶׁאָמַר "וְהָיָה הָעוֹלָם",
And the Talmud is precise in stating “Who spoke and the world came into being,”
כִּי הוּא הָיָה מַשִּׂיג שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָאוֹר שֶׁבִּתְחִלַּת בְּרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם בְּמַאֲמַר "יְהִי אוֹר",
for Rabbi Meir comprehended the primordial root of the light at the dawn of Creation brought forth by the utterance “Let there be light,”
שֶׁהוּא אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּגְנַז לַצַּדִּיקִים לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא.
which is the light of the Torah that was hidden away for the righteous in the time to come.
דְּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּהִתְלַבְּשׁוּת הָאָדָם בְּכָתְנוֹת עוֹר
For in this world that light was enclothed through man's enclothement in garments of skin (kutnot or with an Ayin),
הַגּוּף הַמַּלְבִּישׁ לַנֶּפֶשׁ,
the physical body that garments the soul,
וּבְתוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָיָה כָּתוּב "כָּתְנוֹת אוֹר" בְּאָלֶ״ף
whereas in Rabbi Meir's Torah it was written “garments of light” (kutnot or) with an Aleph,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב [בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה כ, יב].
as recorded in Bereishit Rabbah (20:12).
וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה יָכוֹל לְהַרְאוֹת פָּנִים עַל טָמֵא טָהוֹר וְעַל טָהוֹר טָמֵא,
And therefore he was able to demonstrate reasons to declare the impure pure and the pure impure,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִצַּד הַשָּׂגַת שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם מִכָּל דָּבָר;
which stems from comprehending the hidden supernal root within every entity;
שֶׁכָּל דָּבָר מְעוֹרָב טוֹב וָרָע,
for every created entity contains an admixture of good and evil,
וְהַנְהָגַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא כְּפִי הִתְלַבְּשׁוּתָהּ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל גְּבוּל וָסוֹף,
and the halakhic conduct of this world operates according to its outward enclothement in this world which is bounded and finite,
אֲבָל הוּא הִשִּׂיג שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָאוֹר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ סוֹף וּגְבוּל,
yet he grasped the primordial root of the light which has neither end nor boundary,
שֶׁשָּׁם בְּכָל דָּבָר יֵשׁ פָּנִים לְכָל צַד.
where within every entity there exist viable faces toward every perspective.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם: "שֶׁלֹּא יָכְלוּ לַעֲמוֹד עַל סוֹף דַּעְתּוֹ",
And this is what they stated there: “that his colleagues could not fathom the ultimate depth of his mind,”
שֶׁאֵין לְחָכְמָתוֹ וְדַעְתּוֹ סוֹף.
in that his wisdom and consciousness had no finite end.
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא קָבְעוּ הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ,
Therefore they did not establish the halakhah according to his stance,
דִּקְבִיעוּת הַהֲלָכָה הוּא הַהִילוּךְ הָרָאוּי לְהִתְנַהֲגוּת הָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
for the codification of halakhah represents the structured path fitting for human conduct in this finite world.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 104b:15–105a:1 and Yerushalmi Sanhedrin 10:2:27 record the dorshei reshumos and identify the six Israelite figures through Tehillim 60:9–10. Both conclude that God can make them friends; the Yerushalmi also speaks of opening their good deeds and includes the Divine Voice’s protest against human certainty. Rav Tzadok reads the contrast with the Mishnah as a disclosure of restorative depth; the literary theory of deliberate concealment is his explanation.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok links different forms of Torah understanding with different powers to perceive a hidden root. Rabbi Meir’s exceptional illumination can reveal many sides of a matter, while the settled law must still provide a definite path for conduct in this world.

p: וְחָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם (עֵירוּבִין יג עַמּוּד ב)
And the wisdom of that disciple concerning whom they stated there (Eruvin 13b)
שֶׁהָיָה מְטַהֵר הַשֶּׁרֶץ בְּק״נ (מֵאָה וַחֲמִשִּׁים) טְעָמִים,
who purified a creeping reptile with one hundred and fifty rational arguments,
אֵינוֹ חֲרִיפוּת שֶׁל הֶבֶל כְּקוּשְׁיַת תּוֹסָפוֹת שָׁם,
is not an exercise in futile dialectical sharpness as Tosafot questioned there,
דְּבֶאֱמֶת אֵין שׁוּם טוּמְאָה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ טַעֲמֵי טָהֳרָה גַּם כֵּן.
for in truth there is no ritual impurity that does not possess reasons for purity as well.
כִּי בְּכָל דָּבָר עַל כָּרְחֲךָ יֵשׁ אֵיזֶה שׁוֹרֶשׁ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
For within every entity there must perforce exist some root in holiness,
דְּאִם לֹא כֵן, לֹא הָיָה לוֹ מְצִיאוּת וַהֲוָיָה וְקִיּוּם כְּלָל.
since otherwise it would possess no existence, being, or endurance whatsoever.
וּכְשֶׁיְּתוּקַּן הָעוֹלָם, שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה מְצִיאוּת רַע עוֹד,
And when the world is fully rectified, so that evil holds no independent existence,
יִהְיֶה הַכֹּל טָהוֹר וְלֹא יִהְיֶה שׁוּם טוּמְאָה.
everything will be pure and no impurity will remain.
וּכְמוֹ כָּל מַה שֶּׁבַּיָּם טָהוֹר,
And just as everything in the sea is ritually pure,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא מִשְּׁמוֹנָה מִינֵי שְׁרָצִים הַטְּמֵאִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּחֻלִּין קכז עַמּוּד א].
even though it mirrors the eight species of creeping things that are impure on land, as stated in Chullin (127a).
וּלְעָתִיד: "מָלְאָה הָאָרֶץ דֵּעָה [אֶת ה'] כַּמַּיִם לַיָּם מְכַסִּים" (יְשַׁעְיָה יא, ט),
And in the ultimate future: “the earth shall be full of the knowledge of Hashem, as the waters cover the sea” (Isaiah 11:9),
שֶׁיִּתְמַלֵּא הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ בְּמֵימֵי הַדַּעַת וְהַתּוֹרָה הַנִּמְשָׁלָה לְמַיִם וְיִהְיֶה כֻּלּוֹ יָם.
in that the entire universe will be filled with the waters of divine knowledge and the Torah which is compared to water, and the whole world will become a sea.
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן הַיָּם שֶׁעָשָׂה שְׁלֹמֹה בְּגוֹדֶל חָכְמָתוֹ,
And this is likewise the inner meaning of the Molten Sea that Solomon constructed in the greatness of his wisdom,
דְּחָשַׁב גַּם כֵּן שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְטַהֵר הַכֹּל.
in that he assumed he had attained this spiritual stature where he was empowered to purify everything.
דְּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהַשֶּׁרֶץ בְּיָדוֹ,
For in this world, so long as one holds the defiling reptile in his hand,
אֲפִילּוּ טָבַל בְּכָל מֵימוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם לֹא עָלְתָה לוֹ טְבִילָה,
even if he immersed in all the waters of the universe his immersion is of no avail,
דְּשֶׁרֶץ אֵין לוֹ טָהֳרָה בְּמִקְוֶוה;
for the carcass of a reptile has no purification in a ritual pool;
וְכֵן כָּל הַנּוֹגֵעַ בּוֹ, בְּעוֹדוֹ נוֹגֵעַ לֹא יָכוֹל לִיטָּהֵר,
and likewise anyone touching it, while still touching it he cannot be purified,
וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּכָל מֵימוֹת –
even in all the waters—
הַיְינוּ רוֹב חָכְמָה וְהַשָּׂגָה
which denotes an abundance of wisdom and mystical comprehension,
כְּ'אַחֵר' רַבּוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר,
like Acher, the master of Rabbi Meir;
שֶׁמִּמַּה שֶּׁזָּכָה לִהְיוֹת רַבּוֹ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר מוּבָן שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן אוֹר גָּדוֹל
for from the fact that he merited to be Rabbi Meir's teacher, it is clear that he too contained vast illumination
שֶׁהָיָה יָכוֹל לְהָאִיר עֵינֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְנִכְנַס לַפַּרְדֵּ״ס;
which was able to illuminate the eyes of Rabbi Meir, and he had entered the Pardes;
וְהַכֹּל לֹא הוֹעִיל לוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְטַהֲרוֹ מִטֻּמְאַת עֲוֺנוֹתָיו,
yet all this availed him not in this world to purify him from the defilement of his sins,
דְּצָרִיךְ תְּשׁוּבָה וַעֲזִיבַת הַחֵטְא דַּוְוקָא.
for one indispensably requires active repentance and abandonment of the sin.
אֲבָל לֶעָתִיד "יִתַּמּוּ חַטָּאִים",
However, in the future “sins shall cease,”
דְּהֵם עַצְמָם "כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ",
in that the sins themselves “shall be as white as snow,”
שֶׁיַּחֲזוֹר הָעוֹלָם לְשָׁרְשׁוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בַּתְּחִלָּה כֻּלּוֹ מַיִם,
for the universe will return to its source as it was at the dawn of Creation, entirely water,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִנְיַן טָהֳרַת הַמִּקְוֶוה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר הַחִנּוּךְ (מִצְוָה קעג).
which is the foundational principle of immersion in a mikveh, as written in Sefer HaChinukh (mitzvah 173).
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא רַק בִּפְרָטֵי פְּרָטוֹת וּלְכָל אֶחָד כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא,
And in this world this purification functions only in individual particulars, to each person according to what he is,
וּלְעָתִיד יִהְיֶה הַתִּיקּוּן בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ,
while in the future the rectification will encompass the entire cosmos,
שֶׁיָּשׁוּב הַיַּבָּשָׁה לְיָם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ טוּמְאָה כְּלָל,
when the dry land will return to be a sea wherein no impurity exists at all,
וְעָדִיף מִכָּל מֵימוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
surpassing all the waters that exist in this physical world.

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 13b reports a distinguished student at Yavneh who gave 150 reasons to purify the sheretz. Ravina proposes an inference from the snake, which kills and increases impurity yet is itself pure. The Gemara rejects it: the snake performs ‘merely the action of a thorn’—causing injury and death does not establish the impurity of its own body. The rejected inference must remain visible alongside the report of the student’s arguments.

paragraphs.text: Tosafos, Eruvin 13b, asks what distinction there is in purifying a sheretz that the Torah expressly declared impure. Rabbenu Tam proposes a narrower issue: exclusion from animal-carcass impurity carried in an olive-bulk. Ri objects that the proposed snake exclusion was not found in the Sifra and that sheratzim are already expressly excluded from carrying impurity. Further difficulties with Ravina’s inference remain. These are proposals and objections; Rav Tzadok offers a different answer through the root of purity.

paragraphs.text: Taanis 16a; Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 2:3 - immersion cannot replace abandonment of sin: Rav Adda bar Ahavah compares one who confesses without turning away from the transgression to a person holding a sheretz: even immersion in all the waters of the world is ineffective until he throws it away; once he does so, forty se’ah suffice. The Rambam codifies the same image and anchors it in “one who confesses and abandons shall obtain mercy.” Rav Tzadok therefore distinguishes vast Torah knowledge from teshuvah. Intellectual access to reasons of purity cannot purify a person who continues to grasp the sin; practical abandonment is indispensable in this world.

paragraphs.text: Chagigah 14b-15b - Acher, the Pardes, and R’ Meir’s separation of Torah from sin: Elisha ben Avuyah is one of the four who entered the Pardes; he “cut the shoots” and became Acher. Yet the same sugya portrays him as R’ Meir’s teacher and records R’ Meir continuing to seek his return. The Gemara explains that R’ Meir could eat the fruit and discard the peel, and later sought that Acher be judged and ultimately brought to the World to Come. This is precisely Rav Tzadok’s distinction: extraordinary light and Torah may remain present, but they do not themselves erase chosen wrongdoing. The stories also resist a final equation of the sinner with his sin, since R’ Meir and R’ Yochanan continue to labor for Acher’s restoration.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Arguments for purity within an impure thing express, for Rav Tzadok, its underlying source of existence in holiness. Yet in the present world, great wisdom cannot replace actual repentance and abandonment of sin; universal purification belongs to the completed future he symbolizes through water and the sea.

p: וְזֶה הָיָה כַּוָּונַת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בַּיָּם שֶׁעָשָׂה,
And this was the intention of King Solomon, peace be upon him, in the Sea that he made,
שֶׁמַּחֲזִיק ק״נ (מֵאָה וַחֲמִשִּׁים) מִקְוֵה טָהֳרָה.
which held one hundred and fifty ritual measures of mikveh.
וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁבְּכָל דָּבָר יֵשׁ מ״ט (אַרְבָּעִים וְתִשְׁעָה) פָּנִים טָהוֹר וְטָמֵא,
And it is known that in every matter there exist forty-nine faces of purity and impurity,
שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
corresponding to the seven structural days of this world,
כָּל אַחַת כְּלוּלָה מִשֶּׁבַע;
each attribute subdivided into seven;
וְשַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים הַנֶּעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and the Fiftieth Gate, which is concealed in this world,
הוּא מַה שֶּׁחוֹזֵר הַכֹּל לַמָּקוֹר לִהְיוֹת כֻּלּוֹ טָהוֹר.
is the reality wherein all returns to the primordial Source to be entirely pure.
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה "פְּנֵי חַמָּה"
And Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who was the “face of the sun”
בְּהַשָּׂגַת עֶצֶם הָאוֹר הַמֵּאִיר,
in grasping the direct essence of the radiant light,
לֹא יָכוֹל לְהַשִּׂיג אוֹר דְּשַׁעַר הַזֶּה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
could not apprehend the illumination of this Fiftieth Gate in this physical world.
אֲבָל עַל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אָמְרוּ [בִּמְנָחוֹת כט עַמּוּד ב וּבְוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה]
However regarding Rabbi Akiva they stated in Menachot (29b) and Vayikra Rabbah
שֶׁנִּגְלָה לוֹ מַה שֶּׁלֹּא נִגְלָה לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
that there was revealed to him that which was not revealed to Moses our teacher,
וּפֵירֵשׁ בִּ"מְגַלֵּה עֲמוּקוֹת"
and the Megaleh Amukot explained
שֶׁנִּגְלָה לוֹ שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים הַנֶּעְלָם מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
that there was unveiled to him the Fiftieth Gate that remained hidden from Moses.
וְלֹא שֶׁהָיָה מַעֲלָתוֹ גְּדוֹלָה מִמֶּנּוּ,
Not that Rabbi Akiva's spiritual stature was greater than Moses',
שֶׁזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר וְ"לֹא קָם כָּמוֹהוּ",
for that is impossible, and “there arose not a prophet like him,”
אֲבָל לְפִי שֶׁהַשָּׂגָתוֹ הוּא מֵאוֹר הַלְּבָנָה הַמְקַבֵּל מֵאוֹר הַחַמָּה,
rather because his perception derived from the light of the moon which receives from the light of the sun,
כִּי הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַמְקַבֵּל מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
being the root of the Oral Torah which receives from the Written Torah,
וְהִיא הַשָּׂגַת הַחָכְמָה דְּחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל זֶה [בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא יב עַמּוּד א] דְּ"עָדִיף מִנָּבִיא",
and this is the comprehension of the sages of Israel concerning which they said in Bava Batra (12a) that “a sage is superior to a prophet,”
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְהַשִּׂיג יוֹתֵר עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהַשָּׂגָתוֹ בְּאוֹר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַבְהִיק וּמַבְרִיק כָּל כָּךְ.
meaning that he can apprehend more because his perception is through a light that is not so dazzling and brilliant.
וְכֵן שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁזָּכָה לְשֶׁפַע חָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה,
And likewise King Solomon, peace be upon him, who merited the abundance of lower wisdom,
דְּקַיְימָא בְּיָמָיו סִיהֲרָא בְּאַשְׁלָמוּתָא – שְׁלֵימוּת הָאוֹר,
such that in his days the moon stood in its full orbital brilliance—the perfection of reflected light,
בִּקֵּשׁ לִהְיוֹת כְּמֹשֶׁה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כא סוֹף עַמּוּד ב].
sought to become like Moses, as our Sages stated in Rosh Hashanah (21b).
וּלְמַאן דְּאָמְרוּ לוֹ "לֹא קָם וְכוּלֵי",
And according to the authority who holds that the heavenly voice answered him “there arose not, etc.,”
הַיְינוּ שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לְהַשִּׂיג אוֹר הַחַמָּה כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
this means that he sought to attain the solar light directly like Moses,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה מִמֵּילָא גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ
and through this he would automatically have surpassed him
כְּשֶׁיַּשִּׂיג הוּא שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁהִשִּׂיג מִצַּד הַבְּהִירוּת מֵאוֹר הַחַמָּה,
were he to grasp the Fiftieth Gate through the pristine solar brilliance,
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר דְּלֹא קָם וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר.
and on this Hashem told him that no man has arisen thus and it is impossible.
וְאִידָךְ מַאן דְּאָמַר: "בִּמְלָכִים קָם",
And the other authority who held: “Among kings he did arise,”
הַיְינוּ מִצַּד מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת פֶּה – תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
means: from the perspective of the attribute of Malchut, the mouth, the Oral Torah,
אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיעַ גַּם לְהַשָּׂגָה יְתֵירָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
it is possible to reach even an added dimension of comprehension like Rabbi Akiva.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 109b:3, in a discussion of immersing the Temple table, quotes Rabbi Chiyya that Shlomo’s Sea held 150 purifying mikvaos. Eruvin 14a:23 gives the same capacity;14b continues the 40-seah calculation and distinguishes liquid from heaped dry contents. The number is a volume statement; three groups of the fiftieth gate are the author’s interpretation.

paragraphs.text: Yerushalmi Sanhedrin 4:2:2 records Rabbi Yannai’s teaching that Torah was not given as a rigidly fixed determination. Moshe is instructed to follow the majority: acquit or convict accordingly, while Torah can be expounded through 49 impure and 49 pure aspects. ‘Refined sevenfold’ (Tehillim 12:7) accompanies the numerical exposition. The text supplies a decision procedure, not unlimited conflicting practice; the author supplies the seven-by-seven cosmological mapping and the further fiftieth gate.

The following accounts about Koheles are separately attributed views.

paragraphs.text: Menachos 29b:3–5 shows Moshe initially unable to understand R. Akiva’s teaching, then reassured when Akiva identifies its Sinaitic transmission. Bamidbar Rabbah 19:6 explicitly speaks of matters revealed to Akiva and his companions but not to Moshe, within its red-heifer discussion. The author additionally cites Vayikra Rabbah generally and reports a fiftieth-gate explanation from Megaleh Amukot; those precise intended passages have not been located here. The moon receiving from the sun expresses his account of received Oral Torah illumination, not a statement by Menachos itself.

paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 75a - sun and moon as direct and received illumination: The elders describe Moshe’s face as the sun and Yehoshua’s as the moon, based on ‘you shall place some of your splendor upon him,’ but not all of it. The Talmudic image concerns Moshe and Yehoshua. Rav Tzadok extends its pattern of direct and reflected light to Written and Oral Torah, and therefore to R’ Akiva’s mode of attainment; the Bavli does not make that latter identification directly.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Vayetzei 8:55–58, connects Shlomo’s perfected wisdom and the Temple with the moon in fullness: he then apprehended wisdom directly without needing a dream. The continuation says that after his sin he again needed dreams and the moon’s light was impaired, relating the decline to failure to guard the covenant. This supplies a parallel for the author’s full-moon image without erasing the source’s subsequent qualification.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok relates the Molten Sea to the hidden fiftieth gate and distinguishes prophetic illumination from the reflected wisdom of the Oral Torah. He examines the limits of Shlomo’s intuitive judgment and looks toward a fuller clarification in Mashiach.

p: וְעַל זֶה בִּקֵּשׁ לָדוּן בְּלֹא עֵדִים וְהַתְרָאָה
And concerning this Solomon sought to adjudicate without witnesses and forewarning,
שֶׁהוּא דָּבָר מְבוֹרָר בַּפּוֹעַל;
which represents a reality clarified in absolute actuality;
אָכֵן הַנְּבוּאָה הוּא דָּבָר מְבוֹרָר לַנָּבִיא בִּשְׁמִיעָה מִפִּי ה',
indeed, prophecy is an absolute certainty clarified to the prophet through hearing directly from Hashem,
אֲבָל הוּא בִּקֵּשׁ לָדוּן עַל פִּי הַשָּׂגַת חָכְמָתוֹ,
whereas Solomon sought to adjudicate through the intuitive grasp of his wisdom,
וְאָמַר לוֹ: "וְכָתוּב וְכוּלֵי",
and the heavenly voice said to him: “and it is written: uprightly, etc.,”
הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין חָכְמָתוֹ מְבָרֶרֶת הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ דְּאֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּטְעֶה.
meaning that human wisdom cannot clarify the absolute ultimate truth in every case, for it remains possible that he might err.
וּבֵירוּר הַהַשָּׂגָה בְּחָכְמָה יִהְיֶה בְּמָשִׁיחַ,
And the ultimate clarification of perception through wisdom will be realized in the Messiah,
שֶׁעָלָיו אָמְרוּ בֶּאֱמֶת דְּנִשָּׂא מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
concerning whom they stated in truth that he will be more exalted than Moses our teacher,
וְ"לֹא לְמַרְאֵה עֵינָיו [יִשְׁפּוֹט] וְלֹא לְמִשְׁמַע אָזְנָיו [יוֹכִיחַ]" (יְשַׁעְיָה יא, ג) מֵעֵדִים יִשְׁפּוֹט,
and “he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither decide after the hearing of his ears” through witnesses,
רַק "מוֹרַח וְדָאֵין" (סַנְהֶדְרִין צג עַמּוּד ב).
rather “he will scent and judge” through the holy sense of smell (Sanhedrin 93b).
וְרֵיחַ הוּא דָּבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה נֶהֱנֵית מִמֶּנּוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרָכוֹת מג עַמּוּד ב],
And fragrance is that entity from which the soul derives pleasure, as stated in Berakhot (43b),
וְהוּא מִקְרָא דְּ"נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים בְּאַפָּיו" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, ז).
and this corresponds to the verse “the breath of life in his nostrils” (Genesis 2:7).
וּמִי שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם בְּכָל שָׁלֹשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת דְּנֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה,
And one who is perfected in all three dimensions of Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah,
זוֹכֶה לְמַדְרֵגוֹת הַדְּבֵיקוּת שֶׁמִּצַּד הַנְּשָׁמָה לַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁבַּאֲצִילוּת,
merits the levels of cleaving that proceed from the Soul of the soul in Atzilut,
דְּתַמָּן אִיהוּ וְגַרְמוֹהִי חַד,
where there He and His vessels are One,
הַכֹּל בְּיִחוּד גָּמוּר,
everything existing in absolute unification,
דְּאֵין מְצִיאוּת לְשׁוּם רַע וְטָעוּת.
where there is no existence of any evil or error whatsoever.

paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 12a:13–14 distinguishes the removal of prophecy from prophets from its continuance among sages; Ameimar says a sage is superior to a prophet. Rosh Hashanah 21b:12–13 then records separate accounts: Koheles sought to equal Moshe, or sought to judge from the heart without witnesses and forewarning; the latter is answered by the requirement of two witnesses. The author explains that subtle apprehension does not eliminate the possibility of error or displace halachic evidence.

Berachos 43b:3 identifies scent as a benefit of the soul rather than the body and adduces ‘let every soul praise’ (Tehillim 150:6). The connection to the breath of life in Adam’s nostrils (Bereishis 2:7) is the author’s additional link.

Rav Tzadok connects that unity with a mode of apprehension without evil or error. This latter account is his development of the formula.

p: וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁכְּבָר הִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ,
And King Solomon, peace be upon him, who assumed that he had already attained this supreme stature,
שֶׁהִשִּׂיג שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים בְּכָל הַשָּׁלֹשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת דְּנֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה,
in that he had attained the Fiftieth Gate across all three dimensions of Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah,
עָשָׂה הַיָּם שֶׁבּוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים חֲמִשִּׁים מִקְוֵה טָהֳרָה.
constructed the Molten Sea which contained three times fifty ritual measures of mikveh.
שֶׁבְּכָל שְׁעָרִים אֵלּוּ עֲדַיִן יֵשׁ מְצִיאוּת לְטוּמְאָה וָרָע שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִיטָּהֵר מִמֶּנּוּ,
For within all these gates there still remains an ontological presence of impurity and evil from which one must be purified,
דְּיוּכַל לִכָּנֵס בְּאוֹתוֹ שַׁעַר;
in order to be empowered to enter through that gate;
וְאַחַר שֶׁעָבַר כָּל הַק״נ (מֵאָה וַחֲמִשִּׁים) שְׁעָרִים שֶׁבִּשְׁלֹשׁ עוֹלָמוֹת בְּרִיאָה, יְצִירָה, עֲשִׂיָּה,
and once one has traversed all one hundred and fifty gates within the three worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah,
שׁוּב אֵין עוֹד מְצִיאוּת לְטוּמְאָה וָרָע.
there is no longer any existence of impurity or evil at all.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ עַל י״ב (שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר) בָּקָר
And this is why he positioned the Sea upon twelve oxen
נֶגֶד י״ב שִׁבְטֵי יָ״הּ,
corresponding to the twelve tribes of God,
שֶׁהֵם כְּלַל הָאוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית,
who constitute the entirety of the Jewish nation,
שֶׁהֵם כְּשׁוֹר לָעוֹל לְקַבֵּל עוֹל מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
who are like an ox to the yoke to accept the yoke of His sovereignty, blessed be He,
שֶׁהוּא הַיָּם שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה לְטַהֵר עַצְמָם מִכָּל רָע.
which is the supernal Sea to purify themselves from all evil.

paragraphs.text: I Melachim 7:23–26; Eruvin 14a — the Sea and one hundred fifty mikvaos: Scripture describes Shlomo’s cast-metal “Sea,” ten cubits across, resting upon twelve oxen, and holding two thousand bath. Eruvin calculates its volume as one hundred fifty standard mikvaos, each of forty se’ah. These sources provide the vessel and the number 150; they do not divide the number into three groups of fifty corresponding to nefesh–ruach–neshamah or Beriah–Yetzirah–Asiyah. That threefold structure is Rav Tzadok’s kabbalistic reading, continuing the preceding discussion of the fiftieth gate.

paragraphs.text: II Divrei HaYamim 4:2–6 — twelve oxen and priestly purification: The parallel account again places the Sea upon twelve oxen, three facing each direction, and adds that “the Sea was for the priests to wash in.” The verses do not explicitly identify the oxen with the twelve tribes or call the vessel the “Sea above.” Rav Tzadok transforms the Temple arrangement into a national symbol: the twelve tribes bear the yoke of divine kingship, while the Sea signifies the supernal source through which Israel is purified.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: The Molten Sea represents, in Rav Tzadok’s exposition, purification across the three dimensions of the soul. He explains Shlomo’s enduring portion through the root of divine love and distinguishes that unearned dimension from the reward assessed according to deeds.

p: וּכְבָר זָכָה הוּא לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ,
And Solomon indeed merited this sublime level personally,
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ: "וַיַּעַשׂ [שְׁלֹמֹה] הָרַע [בְּעֵינֵי ה']" (מְלָכִים א יא, ו)
so that even though it is written of him: “And Solomon did evil in the sight of Hashem” (I Kings 11:6)
וּבִקְּשׁוּ לִמְנוֹתוֹ בְּאוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
and the Sages sought to number him among those who have no portion in the World to Come,
(סַנְהֶדְרִין קד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב),
(Sanhedrin 104b),
יָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל: "הֲמֵעִמְּךָ יְשַׁלְמֶנָּה כִּי מָאַסְתָּ, כִּי אַתָּה תִבְחַר וְלֹא אָנִי" (אִיּוֹב לד, לג).
a heavenly voice came forth: “Should His repayment depend on you, because you reject it? Is it you who chooses, and not I?” (Job 34:33).
דְּגַם מִשְׁפְּטֵי עוֹלָם הַבָּא הַמּוּשָּׂגִים לְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
For even the judgments of the World to Come that are grasped by the sages of Israel in this world,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּנוּ עֲלֵיהֶם חַכְמֵי הַמִּשְׁנָה וְאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה,
as the sages of the Mishnah and the Men of the Great Assembly adjudicated concerning them,
הוּא הַכֹּל עַל פִּי מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּיתְּנָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וְ"לֹא בַּשָּׁמַיִם הִיא".
is entirely according to the jurisprudence of the Torah given to Israel, which “is not in heaven.”
אֲבָל זֶהוּ בְּשִׁילּוּם הַשָּׂכָר שֶׁמִּצַּד הַמַּעֲשִׂים דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּמִצְוֹת הַתּוֹרָה,
However, that judicial jurisdiction applies to the payment of reward earned through worldly deeds in Torah commandments,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַכֹּל עַל פִּי מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּמְסְרָה לְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
all of which is subject to the jurisprudence of the Torah transmitted to the sages of Israel in this world.
אֲבָל מַעֲלַת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ הָיְתָה מִצַּד שׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתוֹ שֶׁדָּבוּק בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
However, the preeminence of King Solomon stemmed from the primordial root of his soul cleaving unto Him, blessed be He,
דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא מִיָּד בְּלֵידָתוֹ עַל פִּי הַנָּבִיא "יְדִידְיָהּ" (שְׁמוּאֵל ב יב, כה),
which is why immediately at his birth he was named by the prophet “Jedidiah” (Beloved of God),
דַּה' אֲהֵבוֹ טֶרֶם הִגִּיעַ לְשׁוּם מַעֲשֶׂה בִּבְחִירָתוֹ,
for Hashem loved him before he ever performed any deed through his free choice,
דְּהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַטּוֹב הַנֶּאֱהָב,
being the intrinsic root of beloved goodness,
כְּעִנְיַן "וָאֹהַב אֶת יַעֲקֹב" (מַלְאָכִי א, ב) בְּלִי שׁוּם טַעַם,
mirroring “Yet I loved Jacob” (Malachi 1:2) without any causal reason,
גַּם בִּהְיוֹתָם אַחִים יַחַד בַּבֶּטֶן שָׁוִים כְּאֶחָד.
even while they were brothers together in the womb, equal with one another.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר "הַמֵּעִמְּךָ וְגוֹמֵר",
And this is what the heavenly voice meant by “Shall it be from you, etc.”:
שֶׁבְּמַדְרֵגַת עוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁלּוֹ אֵינוֹ מֵעִמְּךָ מִצַּד מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁעִמָּךְ,
that his dimension of the World to Come does not derive from you via the statutory Torah law in your hands,
כִּי מַדְרֵגָתוֹ עֶלְיוֹנָה לְמַעְלָה מֵהַבְּחִירָה.
for his root is supernal, far above the realm of free choice.
כַּיָּדוּעַ בְּיִשּׁוּב עִנְיַן הַיְדִיעָה וְהַבְּחִירָה דְּאֵינָם בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד:
As is known in reconciling Foreknowledge and Free Choice, that they do not operate in the same sphere:
וּבַאֲצִילוּת שֶׁשָּׁם הַיְדִיעָה אֵין מָקוֹם לִבְחִירָה,
for in Atzilut where divine Foreknowledge reigns, there is no place for human choice,
וּבִבְרִיאָה, יְצִירָה, עֲשִׂיָּה שֶׁשָּׁם הַבְּחִירָה אֵין מָקוֹם לִידִיעָה.
and in Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah where choice operates, mortal minds cannot fathom foreknowledge.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 104b:13–14 relates the attempt to add Shlomo, his father’s image, the fire, and the Divine Voices. The final voice cites Iyov 34:33. Rashi explains its challenge: ‘Does the choice depend on you rather than Me, to say who has a share?’ Thus ‘is it you who chooses, and not I?’ is a question, not an instruction to choose. Rav Tzadok reads the protest through Shlomo’s root beyond the Sages’ ordinary plane of judgment.

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 59b — “the Torah is not in Heaven” and earthly halachic authority: In the oven of Achnai dispute, R’ Yehoshua rejects even a Heavenly voice because the Torah was already given at Sinai and practical halachah follows the majority. The sugya addresses the authority to decide halachah after revelation; it does not directly define the metaphysics of reward in the World to Come. Rav Tzadok extends its principle to the Sages’ Torah-based judgments concerning reward and punishment, while distinguishing Shlomo’s deeper soul-root from that judicial plane.

paragraphs.text: Rambam, Teshuvah 5:5, says God and His knowledge are one and human understanding cannot comprehend how foreknowledge coexists with freedom. He nevertheless insists that human deeds remain in the person’s hands, without divine compulsion. Rav Tzadok’s placement of knowledge in Atzilus and choice in Beriah–Yetzirah–Asiyah is his kabbalistic model, not a placement stated by Rambam or a denial of practical responsibility.

p: וְזֶהוּ מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְנַתֵּק,
And this is the immutable preeminence of Israel which can never be severed,
שֶׁהֵם חֵלֶק ה' וְשָׁרְשָׁם מֵהָאֲצִילוּת,
for they are Hashem's portion and their root emerges from Atzilut,
דְּשָׁם אֵין מְצִיאוּת רַע וּבְחִירָה כְּלָל.
where there is no reality of evil or autonomous choice whatsoever.
וּלְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ רַק שׁוֹרֶשׁ נֶעְלָם,
And for all Israel this exists as a concealed root,
וְהוּא (שְׁלֹמֹה) הָיָה כֻּלּוֹ דָּבוּק שָׁם;
whereas Solomon was entirely bound up there;
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר: "כִּי אַתָּה תִבְחַר וְגוֹמֵר",
and therefore the heavenly voice said: “Is it you who chooses, etc.,”
דְּשָׁם אֵין מָקוֹם לִבְחִירָה דִּידְכוּ כְּלָל.
for in that supernal altitude there is no jurisdiction for your human choice at all.
וּנְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר הוֹלִיךְ הַיָּם לְבָבֶל,
And Nebuchadnezzar carried the Molten Sea to Babylon,
דְּשָׁם נִתְיַיסֵּד אַחַר כָּךְ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
for there the Oral Torah was subsequently established
בַּתְּחִלָּה עַל יְדֵי הֶחָרָשׁ וְהַמַּסְגֵּר וְאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה,
initially through the craftsmen and smiths (the exiles of Jeconiah) and the Men of the Great Assembly,
וְנִסְתַּיֵּים אַחַר כָּךְ בְּסוֹף הָאָמוֹרָאִים בַּחֲתִימַת הַתַּלְמוּד בַּבְלִי,
and was brought to completion subsequently at the end of the Amoraim with the sealing of the Babylonian Talmud,
שֶׁהוּא כּוֹלֵל כָּל חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כֻּלָּהּ,
which encompasses the entire wisdom of the Oral Torah in its entirety;
וְשָׁם נִתְגַּלָּה הָאוֹר יוֹתֵר,
and there the light was revealed more intensely,
כִּי שְׁלֵימוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נִתְגַּלָּה יוֹתֵר אַחַר הַחֻרְבָּן רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי.
because the ultimate perfection of the Oral Torah was unveiled more following the first and second destructions.
דְּעַל זֶה הָיָה חֻרְבָּן רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי –
For it was toward this purpose that the first and second destructions occurred—
לִהְיוֹת נִבְנֶה אַחַר כָּךְ בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת,
in order that it be built afterward with far greater grandeur,
דְּ"גָּדוֹל יִהְיֶה כְּבוֹד הַבַּיִת הָאַחֲרוֹן" (חַגַּי ב, ט)
as “greater shall be the glory of the latter house” (Haggai 2:9)
וּבִנְיָן הַקַּיָּים לָעַד.
and an enduring structure that stands forever.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (בְּמִדְרַשׁ אֵיכָה וּבַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי בִּבְרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק ב הֲלָכָה ד):
Therefore our Sages expounded (in Midrash Eichah and in the Yerushalmi, Berakhot 2:4):
דִּבְתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב נוֹלַד מָשִׁיחַ,
that on the Ninth of Av the Messiah was born,
כִּי עַל זֶה הָיָה הַחֻרְבָּן:
for the purpose of the destruction was precisely this:
לְהוֹלִיד עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִשְׁמַת מָשִׁיחַ.
to bring forth through it the soul of the Messiah.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא נד עַמּוּד ב)
And therefore they related in Yoma (54b)
דְּמָצְאוּ אָז כְּרוּבִים מְעוֹרִים זֶה בָּזֶה,
that the invading enemies discovered at that very time the cherubim embraced within one another,
שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַדְּבֵיקוּת דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים,
which embodies the absolute zenith of the cleaving of the Congregation of Israel unto the living God,
שֶׁמִּזֶּה נִצְמַח הִתְגַּלּוּת שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה
from which sprouts the ultimate disclosure of the root of holiness
שֶׁיְּבוֹרַר בְּבִיאַת בֶּן דָּוִד בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ, אָמֵן,
that will be clarified with the arrival of the son of David speedily in our days, Amen,
שֶׁגַּם בִּהְיוֹתָם בְּתַכְלִית הַיְרִידָה שֶׁאֵין לְמַטָּה וְעַד לֶעָפָר,
demonstrating that even when they exist at the nadir of descent, lower than which there is none, down to the dust,
לֹא נִיתְּקוּ מִשָּׁרְשָׁם שֶׁבִּקְדוּשָּׁה כְּלוּם.
they were not severed from their holy root in the slightest.

paragraphs.text: II Melachim 25:13–16; Yirmiyahu 52:17–20 — the bronze Sea carried to Bavel: The biblical accounts state that the Kasdim broke the bronze pillars, bases, and Sea of the Temple and carried their bronze to Bavel; they also identify the Sea as one of the vessels made by Shlomo. Strictly speaking, Scripture describes the bronze of the dismantled Sea being transported, not the intact basin itself. Rav Tzadok reads that physical transfer symbolically: the Temple’s “Sea,” developed in the preceding se’if as the source of purification and Torah illumination, is transplanted into the Babylonian exile where Torah she-be’al peh will be developed.

paragraphs.text: II Melachim 24:14–16; Gittin 88a; Avos 1:1 — the charash ve-hamasger and the Men of the Great Assembly: The exile of Yehoyachin included “the craftsman and the smith.” Gittin identifies these titles with the thousand leading Torah scholars: when they opened a matter all others became as though deaf, and once they closed a matter no one could reopen it. The Gemara calls their earlier exile a divine kindness, because they remained in Bavel to guide the later exiles. Avos places the Men of the Great Assembly in the chain of transmission from Moshe through the prophets. Rav Tzadok joins these two stages into the initial institutional foundation of the Oral Torah in exile.

The child is Menachem, son of Chizkiyah; both accounts include hope of rebuilding and his later removal by winds or whirlwinds. R. Avun/R. Bon connects ‘Lebanon’ falling with the shoot from Yishai (Yeshayahu 10:34–11:1). Rav Tzadok draws out the destruction’s redemptive potential; the stories do not say that final redemption was then completed.

paragraphs.text: This festival display is distinct from Reish Lakish’s account on 54b of the invaders finding the keruvim intertwined at the destruction. The first scene expressly presents the embrace as affection; Rav Tzadok applies that image to the catastrophe in the second scene and interprets the holy root’s continuing attachment. The Bavli does not itself state his entire redemptive explanation.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok links the removal of the Molten Sea to Bavel with the fuller development of the Oral Torah in exile. The accounts of the embracing cherubim and the birth of Mashiach express his theme that Israel’s holy root remains present even at the deepest point of destruction.

p: וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן אוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד שֶׁהָיָה בְּיַבְנֶה,
And this is likewise the inner meaning of that disciple who lived in Yavneh,
שֶׁהוּא בְּעֵת הַחֻרְבָּן,
which was at the era of the destruction of the Temple,
שֶׁאָז הָיָה כָּל חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שָׁם.
for then all the wisdom of the Oral Torah was concentrated there.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּהַנִּיזָּקִין, גִּיטִּין נו עַמּוּד ב]
As they related in the chapter HaNizakin (Gittin 56b)
דְּרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי בִּקֵּשׁ מֵאַסְפַּסְיָנוּס
that Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai requested of Vespasian
לִיתֵּן לוֹ יַבְנֶה וַחֲכָמֶיהָ;
to grant him Yavneh and its sages;
וְעַל שֵׁם זֶה נִקְרָא "יַבְנֶה",
and on this account is the city titled Yavneh (from the root 'to build'),
שֶׁהֵם הָעוֹסְקִים בְּבִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם וּבַיִת הַשְּׁלִישִׁי שֶׁיִּבָּנֶה בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ,
in that they are those engaged in the enduring construction of the universe and the Third Temple that will be built speedily in our days,
שֶׁלְּתַכְלִית זֶה הָיָה הַחֻרְבָּן.
for the sake of which ultimate purpose the destruction occurred.
וְאוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד שֶׁהָיָה הַוָּתִיק שֶׁבָּהֶם,
And that disciple who was the most distinguished among them,
זָכָה לְהַשִּׂיג אוֹתוֹ אוֹר
merited to apprehend that very illumination
הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִדְּבֵיקוּת הַגָּמוּר דִּכְרוּבִים מְעוֹרִים שֶׁהָיָה בִּשְׁעַת הַחֻרְבָּן,
drawn forth from the absolute cleaving of the embracing cherubim present at the moment of destruction,
שֶׁהוּא לֵידַת הַמָּשִׁיחַ הַמְטַהֵר וּמְזַכֵּךְ הַכֹּל
which is the birth of the Messiah who purifies and refines all things,
שֶׁ"יְבֻקַּשׁ עֲוֺן יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֵינֶנּוּ" (יִרְמְיָה נ, כ).
so that “the iniquity of Israel shall be sought, and there shall be none” (Jeremiah 50:20).
וְזֶהוּ טָהֳרַת הַשֶּׁרֶץ בְּק״נ (מֵאָה וַחֲמִשִּׁים) טְעָמִים,
And this was his purifying of the creeping reptile with one hundred and fifty rational arguments,
שֶׁהוּא הַק״נ שְׁעָרִים
which correspond to the one hundred and fifty spiritual gates
שֶׁשְּׁלֵימוּת נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה שֶׁלּוֹ
of the total perfection of his Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah
בְּעוֹלָמוֹת בְּרִיאָה, יְצִירָה, עֲשִׂיָּה.
throughout the three worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah.

paragraphs.text: Gittin 56b:5–6: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai asks Vespasian, “Give me Yavneh and its sages, the dynasty of Rabban Gamliel, and physicians to heal Rabbi Tzadok.” The ensuing criticism says that he should have asked that Jerusalem be spared. His reasoning is then given: perhaps so large a request would not be granted, and even the smaller rescue would be lost.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 64a: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מַרְבִּים שָׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְכׇל בָּנַיִךְ לִמּוּדֵי ה׳ וְרַב שְׁלוֹם בָּנָיִךְ״. — “Rabbi Elazar said in Rabbi Chanina’s name: Torah scholars increase peace in the world, as it is said: “All your children are taught by Hashem, and great is your children’s peace.”” Berakhot 64a: אַל תִּקְרֵי ״בָּנָיִךְ״ אֶלָּא ״בּוֹנָיִךְ״. — “Do not read “your children,” but “your builders.”” Rav Tzadok applies the builders image to the sages of Yavneh, the world and the future Temple. The Gemara’s immediate teaching concerns scholars increasing peace.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok reads Yavneh through the language of building and the Oral Torah preserved at the destruction. The disciple’s arguments for purifying the sheretz symbolize his perception of the future purification, corresponding to the one hundred and fifty gates of the soul.

p: וְרָבִינָא, שֶׁהָיָה סוֹף הוֹרָאָה בְּבָבֶל
And Ravina, who represented the end of normative halakhic instruction in Babylon
וּמֵחוֹתְמֵי הַתַּלְמוּד וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
and was among the definitive sealers of the Talmud and the Oral Torah,
הִשִּׂיג גַּם כֵּן שֶׁמֶץ וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ בָּזֶה,
likewise perceived an inkling and inner root of this mystery,
וְאָמַר שָׁם (עֵירוּבִין יג עַמּוּד ב):
and asserted there in Eruvin (13b):
"אֲנִי אָדוּן וַאֲטַהֲרֶנּוּ קַל וָחֹמֶר מִנָּחָשׁ וְכוּלֵי".
“I will analyze and declare it pure via an a fortiori argument from the serpent, etc.”
רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר דְּנָחָשׁ הַקַּדְמוֹנִי
Meaning to say: that the primordial Serpent,
שֶׁהֵבִיא הַמִּיתָה לָעוֹלָם וְהִרְבָּה כָּל עִנְיַן הַטֻּמְאָה בָּעוֹלָם,
who introduced mortality to the universe and multiplied all manner of impurity in the world,
הוּא עַצְמוֹ טָהוֹר;
is himself essentially pure;
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַסַּמֶּ״ךְ-מֵ״ם
as is known that he is the primal root of the arch-adversary Samael
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מַלְאָךְ קָדוֹשׁ לֶעָתִיד בִּזְבִיחַת הַיֵּצֶר,
who will become a holy ministering angel in the World to Come at the slaughter of the evil inclination,
שֶׁיּוּסַר דָּמָיו מִפִּיו וְשִׁיקּוּצָיו מִבֵּין שִׁנָּיו
whereby his bloodshed will be removed from his mouth and his abominations from between his teeth (Zechariah 9:7)
וְיִשָּׁאֵר גַּם הוּא לֵאלֹהֵינוּ.
and he too will remain consecrated unto our God.
כִּי גַּם הוּא בַּהֲסָתוֹתָיו וְקִטְרוּגָיו עוֹשֶׂה רְצוֹן קוֹנוֹ,
For even he, through his deceptive incitements and heavenward prosecutions, executes the ultimate will of his Creator,
דִּלְכָךְ נוֹצַר
having been fashioned for this very purpose,
כְּמִשַׁל הַזּוֹנָה בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשַׁת תְּרוּמָה קסג עַמּוּד א).
as in the parable of the king and the harlot in the holy Zohar (Parashat Terumah 163a).
וּסְתָמָא דִּגְמָרָא דָּחֵי:
And the anonymous voice of the Gemara rejected this argument, stating:
דְּהוּא מַעֲשֵׂה קוֹץ בְּעָלְמָא עָבֵיד,
that the serpent merely executes the natural puncture of an inert thorn,
שֶׁאֵינוֹ בַּעַל בְּחִירָה כְּאָדָם הַחוֹטֵא בִּבְחִירָתוֹ,
in that the serpent is not endowed with free choice like mortal man who sins through his own volition,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הוּא מֵהָעֶלְיוֹנִים שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בְּחִירָה,
whereas the serpent is of the celestial beings who possess no free will,
וְאֵין עוֹשֶׂה בִּבְחִירָתוֹ כְּלָל רַק שֶׁלְּכָךְ נִבְרָא וְנִשְׁתַּלַּח,
and acts with no autonomy whatsoever, having been created and dispatched solely for this task,
וְזֶהוּ מַעֲשֵׂה קוֹץ שֶׁנּוֹקֵב עַל יְדֵי הָאָדָם הַנּוֹקֵב בּוֹ,
and this is like the prick of a thorn which pierces only because a person steps upon it,
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה יט, א]: "אַתָּה עֲשִׂיתוֹ רָע".
and this is what they expounded in Bereishit Rabbah (19:1): “You made it evil.”
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִסְדְּרוּ דִּבְרֵי רָבִינָא בַּתַּלְמוּד,
And nevertheless, the words of Ravina were codified in the sacred text of the Talmud;
וְיָדוּעַ דַּאֲפִילּוּ הַסָּלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דִּגְמָרָא וְהַהֲוָה אָמֵינָא הַנִּדְחֵית
and it is known that even the initial hypothesis of the Gemara and the rejected premise
הִיא אֱמֶת גַּם כֵּן,
are likewise profound truth,
מִצַּד דְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ – לֹא נִזְכַּר בַּתַּלְמוּד שֶׁהוּא תּוֹרַת אֱמֶת,
because an untruth is never permanently recorded in the Talmud which is the Torah of truth,
וְדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֱמֶת אֵינוֹ תּוֹרָה וְאֵין לְהַזְכִּירוֹ בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה.
and that which is not true is not Torah and has no place being cited within words of Torah.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר רְאָיָה
And as I wrote elsewhere a proof
מִמַּה שֶּׁאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (רַבָּה פָּרָשַׁת וַיְחִי ק, ט)
from that which is taught in Midrash Rabbah (Parashat Vayechi 100:9)
לְעִנְיַן לְשַׁנּוֹת מִפְּנֵי הַשָּׁלוֹם,
regarding altering speech for the sake of peace,
דְּהַכְּתוּבִים דִּבְּרוּ דִּבְרֵי בְּדַאי מִפְּנֵי הַשָּׁלוֹם
where the Sages stated that Scripture itself uttered fabricated words for peace
מִקְּרָא דְּ"אָבִיךָ צִוָּה לִפְנֵי מוֹתוֹ וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית נ, טז).
from the verse: “Your father commanded before he died, etc.” (Genesis 50:16).
וַהֲרֵי שָׁם הַכָּתוּב אֵינוֹ מְסַפֵּר שֶׁקֶר,
Yet behold, there Scripture is not relating an inherent lie,
דַּהֲרֵי הֵם אָמְרוּ לוֹמַר כֵּן לוֹ,
since Joseph's brothers truly instructed the messenger to say so to him;
רַק דְּאֵין לְהַזְכִּיר בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא תּוֹרַת אֱמֶת דְּבַר שֶׁל שֶׁקֶר שֶׁהִגִּיד אֵיזֶה אָדָם גַּם כֵּן,
rather the principle is that in the Torah, which is the Torah of truth, one does not mention even a false statement spoken by an individual,
אִם לֹא לְלַמְּדֵינוּ דְּמוּתָּר לְשַׁקֵּר כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא וְאֵין זֶה נֶחְשָׁב לְשֶׁקֶר.
unless it comes to instruct us that it is permissible to deviate under such circumstances and that this is not reckoned as falsehood.
וְהָכִי נַמֵּי בַּתַּלְמוּד שֶׁהִיא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And so too in the Talmud which is the Oral Torah,
וַדַּאי אֵין לְהַזְכִּיר דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֱמֶת אַף שֶׁדְּחָאוּהוּ;
one certainly would never record an assertion that is devoid of truth even if it was formally rebutted;
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ "לֹא הִיא",
and perforce you must say that what the Gemara rebutted: “That is not so,”
הַיְינוּ דְּוַדַּאי כֵּיוָן דְּהַתּוֹרָה טִמְּאַתּוּ
means: certainly, as long as the Torah declared the reptile ritually impure in this world,
עַל כָּרְחֲךָ יֵשׁ טַעַם לִדְחוֹת כָּל ק״נ טַעֲמֵי הַהֶיתֵּר שֶׁלּוֹ.
perforce there exists an overriding reason to set aside all one hundred and fifty arguments for its purity.
אֲבָל לֶעָתִיד, כְּשֶׁיְּבוֹעַר רוּחַ הַטֻּמְאָה מִן הָאָרֶץ,
However in the World to Come, when the spirit of impurity is eradicated from the earth,
יִשָּׁאֲרוּ טַעֲמֵי הַטָּהֳרָה שֶׁלּוֹ לְבַדָּם.
its reasons for purity will stand alone validated.
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ וִיסוֹד כָּל אוֹתָם הַטְּעָמִים הוּא הַטַּעַם שֶׁגִּילָּה רָבִינָא,
And the root and foundation of all those arguments is the profound rationale revealed by Ravina:
דְּכָל הַטֻּמְאוֹת נִמְשָׁכִים מִזּוּהֲמַת הַנָּחָשׁ וּמַשְׁכָּא דְּחִוְיָא
that all impurities are drawn down from the defilement of the Serpent and the serpent's skin
שֶׁבּוֹ נִתְלַבְּשׁוּ גּוּפוֹת בְּנֵי אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
with which human bodies were enclothed in this world
בְּכָתְנוֹת הָעוֹר הַגּוּפָנִי הַמָּלֵא זוּהֲמָא.
in garments of physical skin that are laden with defilement.
וְאִם הַנָּחָשׁ עַצְמוֹ טָהוֹר,
And if the Serpent himself is fundamentally pure,
לְפִי שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה רַק מַעֲשֵׂה קוֹץ וְהוּא כְּגַרְזֶן בְּיַד הַחֹצֵב,
because he merely acts as a passive thorn and is like an axe in the hand of the hewer,
לֶעָתִיד יִתְגַּלֶּה כִּי גַּם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ הֵמָּה רַק כְּגַרְזֶן בְּיַד הַחֹצֵב,
in the World to Come it will be revealed that all our deeds were likewise merely as an axe in the hand of the hewer,
שֶׁהֵם סְדוּרִים וּבָאִים מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית,
having been systematically ordered and progressing since the six days of Creation,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה "כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ" (יְשַׁעְיָה א, יח).
and through this “they shall become as white as snow” (Isaiah 1:18).

paragraphs.text: Zechariah 9:7: “I shall remove his blood from his mouth and his abominations from between his teeth, and he too shall remain for our God; he shall be like a chief in Yehudah, and Ekron like the Yevusi.” The ending about Ekron belongs to the actual verse and preserves its setting among the Philistine cities. The author recasts the first clause passively (“his blood will be removed”); the verse itself says, “I shall remove.”

paragraphs.text: Rav Tzadok applies this removal-and-remnant imagery to the adversary’s future transformation. That is his symbolic application; the verse does not explicitly name Samael. Likewise, Sukkah 52a:4 states that the Holy One brings the evil inclination and slaughters it before the righteous and the wicked; that statement does not itself say that Samael becomes a holy angel.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Terumah 66:673–676—the passage cited as II, Terumah 163a—compares the tempter to a woman whom a king secretly commissions to test his son. The king had expressly commanded his son not to approach her. “If that son is worthy and heeds his father’s command, he rebukes her, does not heed her, and drives her away. Then his father rejoices in his son,” brings him within the palace and gives him gifts and honor.

rich.text: Zohar, Terumah 66:673–676—the passage cited as II, Terumah 163a—compares the tempter to a woman whom a king secretly commissions to test his son. The king had expressly commanded his son not to approach her. “If that son is worthy and heeds his father’s command, he rebukes her, does not heed her, and drives her away. Then his father rejoices in his son,” brings him within the palace and gives him gifts and honor.

paragraphs.text: The Zohar asks whether the testing agent deserves praise: “Certainly she deserves praise in every respect: first, because she carried out the king’s command; and second, because she caused that son all that goodness and all this love of the king toward him.” It calls the angel of death “very good for one who heeds his Master’s commands” and praises those who encounter the accuser and are rescued from him.

paragraphs.text: The two grounds for the agent’s praise remain distinct: performing the assigned commission, and occasioning the obedient son’s reward. The favorable outcome for the son expressly depends on resistance and obedience. The parable does not commend the human being’s yielding to temptation.

rich.text: Eruvin 13b:8–9: Ravina says, “I shall reason and declare it pure: if a snake, which kills and thereby increases impurity, is pure, then a creeping creature, which does not kill and increase impurity, should certainly be pure.” The Gemara rejects the argument: “That is not so; it merely performs the act of a thorn.”

paragraphs.text: The comparison concerns the impurity associated with the creature, not permission to eat a snake. Its killing is an indirect cause of corpse impurity, like a thorn that injures and kills; that fact does not make the snake’s body one of the Torah’s impure creeping creatures. The anonymous rejection remains part of the source. Rav Tzadok’s further interpretation of the thorn analogy follows in the main text.

inlineHeadings.text: The theme: Rav Tzadok reads Ravina’s rejected argument about the serpent as retaining a truth relevant to the completed future. He distinguishes that underlying truth from the decisive impurity of the sheretz in present halachah, and relates the distinction to divine purpose concealed within human acts.

p: וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא כְּשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה אוֹתוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדוּשַׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל
And this realization will emerge when there is revealed that pristine root of Israel's holiness
בִּמְקוֹר מַחְצָבָם שֶׁנֶּעְלַם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
at their primordial quarry which remains concealed in this world,
שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה אֶלָּא לְאוֹתָם שֶׁזָּכוּ לְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּכָתְנוֹת אוֹר
which is revealed only to those who merited to be enclothed in garments of light (with an Aleph)
תַּחַת עוֹר דְּחִוְיָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר.
in place of the serpent's skin, like Rabbi Meir.
וּסְתָם מִשְׁנָה כְּוָותֵיהּ,
And an anonymous Mishnah follows his stance,
וְגַם סְתָם מִשְׁנָה [דְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק חֵלֶק] לֹא פָּלֵיג עָלָיו,
and even the anonymous Mishnah at the beginning of chapter Chelek does not disagree with him,
דְּאַף הֵם נִקְרָאִים בָּנִים וְיֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק,
for even these severe sinners are titled children and possess a portion,
דְּדָא וְדָא אֱמֶת, כָּל אֶחָד בִּשְׁעָתוֹ.
in that both this and that are truth, each in its appointed time.
וּפְלוּגְתַּת רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה (קִדּוּשִׁין לו עַמּוּד א) בִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה:
And the dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah in Kiddushin (36a) concerns their designation in this world:
אִי אָזְלִינַן בָּתַר מֵעִיקָּרָא אוֹ בָּתַר בַּסּוֹף.
whether we evaluate by their primordial inception or by their final outward state.
וְהַסּוֹבְרִים דְּמוּמָר כְּגוֹי
And those authorities who maintain that an apostate is considered like a gentile
(הָרַשְׁדָּ״ם כִּמְבוֹאָר בְּסִימָן קָטָן פג),
(the Rashdam, as cited above in paragraph 83),
סְבִירָא לֵיהּ דִּבְרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה – הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּאֵין נִקְרָאִים בָּנִים;
hold that in the dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah the halakhah follows Rabbi Yehudah that they are not called children;
וְאִם כֵּן הֵם "לֹא עַמּוֹ",
and if so, they are categorized as “not My people,”
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "בִּמְקוֹם וְגוֹמֵר וּקְרָאוּ וְגוֹמֵר",
as it is stated: “in the place, etc., and called, etc.,”
שֶׁהֵם שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים,
which represent two diametrical opposites,
דְּאוֹתָם שֶׁאֵינָם בָּנָיו אֵינָם עַמּוֹ גַּם כֵּן
in that those who are not His children are likewise not His people
וְיָצְאוּ מִכְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and have departed from the collective community of Israel.
וּמֵהָא דְּעָכָן אֵין רְאָיָה,
And from the episode of Achan there is no proof against them,
אַף דְּעָבַר עַל חֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה,
even though he transgressed the Five Books of the Torah,
שֶׁהֲרֵי מְפוֹרָשׁ בַּמִּשְׁנָה [סַנְהֶדְרִין מג עַמּוּד ב]
for behold it is explicit in the Mishnah (Sanhedrin 43b)
דְּהוּא נִתְוַודָּה וְיֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא;
that he confessed and possesses a portion in the World to Come;
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁשָּׁב וְנִתְוַודָּה,
and since he repented and confessed,
הֲרֵי חָזַר לִכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעוֹדוֹ חַי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
behold he returned to the fold of Israel while still alive in this world,
וְאִיגַּלַּאי מִילְּתָא לְמַפְרֵעַ דְּלֹא נִפְקַע מִינֵּיהּ.
and the matter was retroactively revealed that the name of Israel had never departed from him.
וְאַף דְּהַשְׁתָּא הוּא דְּשָׁב בִּתְשׁוּבָה,
And even though it was only then that he repented,
הוּא מְתַקֵּן הַקּוֹדֵם לִהְיוֹת הֶעָוֺן מִתְכַּפֵּר וּכְאִלּוּ לֹא חָטָא.
his repentance rectifies the past so that the iniquity is expiated and it is as though he never sinned.
וְאַף דְּעַתָּה עֲדַיִן בְּרִשְׁעוֹ וְנֶעֶנְשׁוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יָדוֹ,
And even while he still persisted in his sin and Israel was punished on his account,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹמַר דְּנֶעֱקַר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּזֶה,
nonetheless it is inapplicable to say that the name of Israel was uprooted through this,
דְּקַמֵּי שְׁמַיָּא גַּלְיָא דְּסוֹפוֹ לָשׁוּב בְּחַיָּיו,
for before Heaven it was openly revealed that he would ultimately repent in his lifetime,
וְחֶטְאוֹ וְעָנְשׁוֹ רַק לְשָׁעָה.
and his sin and his punishment were only for a temporary hour.
וְאַף דִּקְרָא דְּ"חָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל" (יְהוֹשֻׁעַ ז, יא) נֶאֱמַר קוֹדֶם שֶׁשָּׁב
And even though the verse “Israel has sinned” was uttered prior to his repenting,
וַעֲדַיִן הַבְּחִירָה בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁמָּא לֹא יָשׁוּב;
and free choice was still in his hand lest he might not repent;
וְאַף דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹדֵעַ עֲתִידוֹת,
and even though the Holy One knows all future events,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם "צַדִּיק וְרָשָׁע לָא קָאָמַר" (נִדָּה טז עַמּוּד ב),
nonetheless “whether righteous or wicked He does not dictate” (Niddah 16b),
וְאֵיךְ אָמַר לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ שֶׁהוּא עֲדַיִן בִּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיָּשׁוּב?
and how then could He reveal to Joshua that the sinner was still included in Israel, implying that he would repent?
וּמִשֶּׁגִּילָּה זֶה לַנָּבִיא אִי אֶפְשָׁר עוֹד שֶׁלֹּא יָשׁוּב,
For once He disclosed this to the prophet, it was impossible that he not repent,
וְאֵינוֹ עוֹד שָׁב בִּבְחִירָתוֹ!
and he would no longer be repenting through unforced free will!
יֵשׁ לוֹמַר: מַה בְּכָךְ דְּהָיָה מוּכְרָח לָשׁוּב,
It can be answered: what of it that he was divinely compelled to repent,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם קַמֵּי שְׁמַיָּא גַּלְיָא דְּגַם בִּבְחִירָתוֹ בְּלֹא הֶכְרֵחַ הָיָה שָׁב.
since before Heaven it was revealed that even in his free choice without compulsion he would have repented.
וְהָא דְּגִילָּה לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ זֶה וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה מוּכְרָח,
And as for why Hashem revealed this to Joshua and made it a certainty,
יֵשׁ לוֹמַר מִשּׁוּם דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא רָצָה לְגַלּוֹת לוֹ מִי חָטָא,
it can be said because Hashem did not wish to tell Joshua directly who had sinned,
רַק שֶׁיַּפִּיל גּוֹרָל כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין מג עַמּוּד ב].
rather instructed him to cast lots, as stated in Sanhedrin (43b).
